text: Bui bi ke nninkpan le ye si. Nima kan bi ga cha m li bi, ki ŋa mi tiŋann.”

text: ki maa kitork aabimbiln na. Le u doon Uwumbɔr nima.

ref: At this time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were still living in the same area, and so there wasn't enough pastureland left for Abram and Lot with all of their animals. Besides this, the men who took care of Abram's animals and the ones who took care of Lot's animals started quarreling.
text: Nima chee, le Abram aanib ni Lot aanib bi nan kpaa baawakor ngbaan na piin ki jaa. N‑yoonn ngbaan, Kanaann yaab ni Peris yaab nan beenin bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni.

ref: Abram said to Lot, “We are close relatives. We shouldn't argue, and our men shouldn't be fighting one another.

text: Cha ti yakr tɔb chee. M tii si nsan, pue lee saah gee lipepel li wɔb na. Nima kan, aa ni saanib ga li bi nibaa wɔb, aan m mu ni maanib li bi niken wɔb.”

text: le ki ton Elam, ni Goyim, ni Babiloŋ, ni Elasar aabɔrb butɔb. Bibɔrb biŋmu ngbaan le nan fii sil, ki ton bibɔrb binaa ngbaan butɔb.

text: le ki gaa baah nan yoor tiwan nimɔk na. U nan gaa ni unaal aajapɔɔn Lot, ni waawan mɔmɔk, ki kpee bipiib, ni binib bi bibɔrb ngbaan nan chuu bi na mɔmɔk. Melkisedek aah nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa Abram pu pu na aabɔr

ref: King Melchizedek of Salem was a priest of God Most High. He brought out some bread and wine

text: Saa tii mi ubo, nima pu na, maanaagbiib ponn ni ubaa le ga ji maafaal.”

ref: Abram asked, “Lord God, how can I know the land will be mine?”
text: Le Abram baa ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, m ga ŋa kinye ki bee ke kitiŋ ngbaan ga li ye maatiŋ?”

text: Le Uwumbɔr nan bui u ke, “Ban ni unaa, ni uŋoob, ni upihja, ni mɔmɔk li ye ŋibin ŋitaa aawakor, ni linanjel, ki kpee libɔrnanjel.”

text: Buyoonn nwiin nan lir, ni bɔnn doo na, le kiŋulk ki kpa iŋmanyuu ni mmiigaal na nan nyan ni, ki jer tiwakor na aanann aakaasisik ni.

ref: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.

text: ki kpee Kenn yaab aatim, ni Kenis yaab aatim, ni Kadmonn yaab aatim,

text: ni Hef yaab aatim, ni Peris yaab aatim, ni Refa yaab aatim,

text: ni Amor yaab aatim, ni Kanaann yaab aatim, ni Girgas yaab aatim, ni Jebus yaab aatim mɔmɔk.”

ref: Abram's wife Sarai had not been able to have any children. But she owned a young Egyptian slave woman named Hagar,

text: M ga puu tipuur tii si ke aa ga li kpa yaabitiib pam.”

text: Tɔ, Rachel aa nan ma ubo tii Jakob, nima pu na, u nan kpa ukpel Lea pu lipiipoln, le ki bui uchal Jakob ke, “Aa yaa kaa tii mi mbim kan, m ga kpo.”

ref: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
text: Jakob aaŋuul nan fii Rachel pu pam, le u bui u ke, “Maa ye Uwumbɔr ki gaa waatuln tun tii u. Uma le aa tii si mbim.”

ref: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
text: Le Rachel nan bui uchal ke, “Maanaagbiipii Bilha sɔ. Doon u chee, nima kan, u ga maa ubo tii mi. Aa yaa ŋa kina kan, u ga maa ubo tii mi, le m li kpa mbim.”

ref: and they had a son.
text: Le Bilha nan dek lipuul ki ma ubijabo tii Jakob.

ref: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
text: Rachel nan bui ke, “Uwumbɔr le toor maabɔr tii mi. Uma le ŋun maameel le ki tii mi ubijabo.” Nima pu na, u nan yin u ke Dann.

ref: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
text: Le Bilha nan ki dek lipuul, le ki ki ma ubijabo uken tii Jakob.

ref: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
text: Rachel nan ki bui ke, “M pɔɔn mbaa ki mee Uwumbɔr ki kan mbim ke nkpel aah kan pu na.” Nima pu na, u nan yin u ke Naftali.

ref: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
text: Le Lea kan ke waa ki maa, le u di waanaagbiipiibo Silpa ki di tii uchal Jakob u di u ŋa upuu.

ref: and they had a son.
text: Le Silpa nan ma ubijabo tii Jakob.

ref: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
text: Lea nan bui ke, “M kpa liyimɔɔn.” Nima pu na, u nan yin u ke Gad.

ref: When they had another son,
text: Silpa nan ki ma ubijabo uken tii Jakob.

ref: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
text: Le Lea bui ke, “M kpa mpopiin pam. Dandana wee, bipiib biken ga yin mi ke mpopiindaan.” Nima pu na, u nan yin u ke Aser.

ref: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
text: Lidicheel yoonn nan fuu, le Rubenn buen tisar ponn ni ki ti ban ni ŋisubil ŋibaa, bi yin ŋi ke ngeehm aasubil, le ki joo ni ŋi nan tii una Lea. Le Rachel bui Lea ke, “Tii mi aajapɔɔn aasubil ngbaan ŋibaa.”

ref: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
text: Lea nan giin bui u ke, “Saah gaa m chee nchal pu na aa ŋeer aa? Dandana wee aa ki pɔɔni aabaa ke aa gaa njapɔɔn aasubil mu la aa?” Rachel nan bui u ke, “Aa yaa kii ki ga tii mi ŋisubil ngbaan kan, m ga di nchal tii si kinyeek kee, aa ni u doon.”

ref: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
text: Tɔ, buyoonn Jakob nan nyan ni kisaak ki kun ni kijook wɔb na, le Lea buen u chee ki ti bui u ke, “Kinyeek kee, aa ga koo ni maadiik ni la; ba pu? m di njapɔɔn aasubil pan n‑yɔnn, aa pu a.” Nima pu na, Jakob nan koo Lea aadiik ni kinyeek ngbaan, le ki doon u chee.

ref: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ŋun Lea aameel pu, le u dek lipuul ki ki ma ubijabo ŋmuŋmur tii Jakob.

ref: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
text: Le Lea bui ke, “Uwumbɔr pan mi maapar a, ba pu? m di maanaagbiipiibo tii nchal.” Nima pu na, u nan yin waabo ngbaan ke Isakar.

ref: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
text: ki nan bui ke, “Uwumbɔr tii mi ipiin nyanyaan. Dandana wee, nchal ga nyuŋ mi, ba pu? m ki ma ubijabo loloob tii u.” Nima pu na, u nan yin u ke Sebulunn.

ref: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
text: Le ni joo cha, le u nan ki ma upiibo mu, le ki yin u ke Daina.

ref: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
text: U nan dek lipuul le ki ma ubijabo. Le u bui ke, “Uwumbɔr chuu nyan maanimɔɔn le ki tii mi ubijabo.

ref: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
text: Cha Uwumbɔr ki tii mi ubijabo.” Nima pu le u yin u ke Josef. Jakob ni Labann aah nan kpokl pu na aabɔr

ref: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
text: Rachel aah nan ma Josef na, le Jakob bui Labann ke, “Cha m li chaa kun, ki gir buen ndo.

ref: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
text: Di mpuutiib ni maabim bi m tun tii si bi pu na tii mi aan m kun. Aa nyi maah tun litunyaan pu ki tii si na.”

ref: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
text: Le Jakob bui ke, “Aa nyi maah tun lituln tii si pu, ki joo saapiih i pɔr sakpen pu na.

ref: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
text: Saapiih siib i aa nan kpa aan m fuu ni na, aa kan ke i pɔr sakpen, le m yaa di i buen nimɔk na kan, Uwumbɔr ŋani tinyoor ŋani i pu. Dandana wee, n‑yoonn fuu ni ke m mu ban mbaa yaan.”

ref: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
text: Le Labann baa u ke, “Aa ban ke m pa si ba?” Le Jakob bui u ke, “Maa ban tipar tibaa. M ga li beenin kpaa saapiih ngbaan, see aa ti kii maah ban m kpokl si pu na.

ref: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
text: Cha m lik saapiih ngbaan ponn ni, ki nyan ipiih imɔk kpa mbɔm na, ni imɔk kpa mpem ni mbɔm na, ni iŋoob imɔk kpa mpem ni mbɔm na. Maah ban tipar ti na le na.

ref: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
text: Ni yaa bi cha kan, aa lik ke m ye unibamɔnn aan maa ye. Buyoonn aa ga nan lik i na, aa yaa kan ipiih i kaa kpa mbɔm, bee iŋoob i kaa kpa mpem ni mbɔm na i ponn ni kan, aa bee ke m sun i la.”

ref: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
text: Tɔ, liyaadaal ngbaan le Labann nan nyan iŋoja i ye ichachal na, ni iŋoninkpel i mu ye ichachal, bee i kpa mpem i pu na ibaa. U nan ki nyan ipihbɔn mu mɔmɔk le ki di i mɔmɔk ŋa ujapɔtiib aaŋaal ni,

ref: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
text: ki cha bi chuun iwiin itaa ki buen timoor ni, nin chee daa na. Le Jakob nan gaa Labann aapiih i gur na ki joo i.

ref: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
text: Jakob nan ban isui ibaa aaboln aabon, le ki ban isui i aawon joon na mu aabon, le ki chuu puur tidapɔr i pu.

ref: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
text: U nan di ibon ngbaan le ki bil tiwakor ngbaan aah nyu nnyun nin chee na. U nan di ibon ngbaan di bil nnyun chee, ba pu? buyoonn tiwakor dan ti nan nyu nnyun na kan, le ija dur isal pu.

ref: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
text: Jakob nan ki yakr iŋoob ni ipiih tɔb chee, le ki cha ti sil toŋ Labann aawakor ti ye tichachal ni tibɔmbɔnn na wɔb. U nan ŋa kina ke uma aawakor pɔr kpee, le ki yakr ti Labann yaar chee.

ref: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
text: Tiwakor ti nan kpa laafee na yaa ti ban ti dur tɔb pu kan, le Jakob di ibon ngbaan di bil yaah nyu nnyun nin chee na, nima kan, i ga maa ibɔnbɔn ni ichachal,

ref: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
text: le kaa nan di ibon ngbaan di bil i kaa kpa laafee na aanimbiin ni. Nima pu le Labann aawakor ti nan gur na mɔmɔk aa kpa mpɔɔn, le Jakob yaar mɔmɔk ma nan kpa mpɔɔn.

ref: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
text: Kina le Jakob nan ŋa mpɔɔndaan ki kpa tiwakor, ni binaagbiib, ni laakumii tiib, ni ibon sakpen.

ref: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
text: Le Jakob ŋun ke Labann aajapɔtiib bui ke, “Jakob gaa tite aawan mɔmɔk a. Waah kpa tiwan nimɔk na nyan ni tite yaan ponn ni la.”

ref: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
text: Jakob nan ki kan ke uweeja Labann aa nan ki gee waabɔr ke waah nan gee u njan pu na.

ref: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
text: Le Uwumbɔr nan bui Jakob ke, “Gir kun aate, ni aado yaab aatiŋ ni. M ga li bi aa chee.”

ref: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
text: Nima pu na, Jakob nan tun ti bui Rachel ni Lea ke bi keln ni u waah bi kpaa tiwakor timoor ni nin chee na.

ref: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
text: Baah fuu ni na le u bui bi ke, “M bee ke nite aa ki gee maabɔr ke waah nan gee mi njan pu na; tɔ, nte Aawumbɔr bi m chee.

ref: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
text: Nimi bilee bee, ni nyi ke m tun lituln sakpen tii nite.

ref: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
text: Le n‑yoonn pam, u jin mi pem pem ki kpeln waah ba ga pa mi pu na nfum kipiik pu. Uwumbɔr mu aa kii ke u bii mi.

ref: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
text: N‑yoonn mu nite Labann ti bui ke, ‘Iŋoob i ye ichachal na ye min yee na’ kan, see i mɔmɔk ga maa kina ŋmeen la. U yaa ti ki bui ke, ‘Iŋoob i lul mbɔmbɔm ni mpepem na ye min yee na’ kan, see i mɔmɔk ga maa kina ŋmeen la.

ref: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
text: Ni kan ke nite aah ji mi pem pem pu na, le Uwumbɔr di waapiih ni iŋoob di tii mi.

ref: Once, when the flocks were mating, I dreamed that all the rams were either spotted or speckled.
text: “Buyoonn tiwakor ngbaan nan piin ki bi maa na, le m daŋ tidaŋ, le ki kan ke iŋoja i nan bi dur ininkpel na nan ye i lul mbɔmbɔm ni mpepem na la.

ref: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
text: Le u bui mi ke, ‘Lik, iŋoja i mɔmɔk bi dur ininkpel na ye ibɔnbɔn, ni ichachal la. Min le cha ni ŋani kina, ba pu? m kan Labann aah ŋani si pu na.

ref: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
text: Min le ye Uwumbɔr u nan dan aa chee Betel aatiŋ ni, nin chee aa nan di litakpal ŋum, ki di nkpan kpir li pu ki di tii mi, ke aa li teer mbɔr, ki nan ki puu tipuur tii mi na. Dandana wee, gor saawan mɔmɔk, ki gir buen baah nan ma si kitiŋ ki ponn ni na.’”

ref: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
text: U ŋani ti mu ke taah ye biwɔwɔm le na. U di timi kooh a, le dandana wee u jin tipar ngbaan doo a.

ref: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
text: Le Uwumbɔr aah gaa waawankpal li ki di tii sin Jakob na, ye ti ni timi aabim yaan la. Uwumbɔr yaa bui ke aa ŋa pu na kan, ŋa kina.”

ref: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
text: Labann nan buen waawakor chee timoor ni, u ti chee waapiih aakor pu, le waah kaa bi buyoonn na, Rachel sun waawaa ŋi nan bi lichiln ni na.

ref: long years to earn your two daughters and another
text: Jakob nan ŋmann Labann, le kaa cha u nyi ke u ga nya udo.

ref: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
text: U nan yoor waawan mɔmɔk le ki san mala buen. U nan ti puur Yufrates aamɔɔl, le ki piin ki cha ŋijoo aatiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Gilead na ni. Labann aah paan Jakob pu pu na aabɔr

ref: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
text: Naah ti saa iwiin itaa daal na, le bi tuk Labann ke Jakob san a.

ref: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
text: Le Labann yoor waajab ki paan Jakob pu ki ti saa iwiin ilole daal, le ki ti pii u ŋijoo aatiŋ Gilead ni.

ref: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
text: Kinyeek ngbaan le Uwumbɔr nan dan Labann chee tidaŋ ni, le ki bui u ke, “Aa li nyi ki taa ŋa Jakob nibaa.”

ref: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
text: Jakob ni waanib nan bi lijool libaa paab, le Labann mu ni waajab nan bi liken paab, Gilead aatiŋ ni.

ref: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
text: Le Labann baa Jakob ke, “Ba ŋa aa ŋmann mi, ki yoor mbisatiib ke saah ton butɔb le ki gaa bi na?

ref: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
text: Ba ŋa aa ŋmann mi ki loon san, kaa tuk mi? Aa yaa ba tuk mi kan, m ba ga cha m ni maanib yoor tiwangbaakaan le ki li gaa ilahn ki kpa mpopiin ki cheen nimi.

ref: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
text: Hali, saa cha m moor n‑yaabitiib ni mbisatiib aatakpin ki chɔi bi. Saah ŋa pu na, ni naahn kijɔrk aatuln la.

ref: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
text: M ba kpa mpɔɔn ke m ŋa si bakaa, le kinyeek na, aate Aawumbɔr fe sur mi ke m li nyi m ŋa si bakaa ubaa.

ref: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
text: M bee ke aanimbil man aa gir kun, nima pu le aa san. Ba ŋa aa sun maadichal ni aawaa?”

ref: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
text: Jakob nan giin bui u ke, “M san ijawaan ki dak ke nibaakan aa ga gaa aabisatiib m chee la.

ref: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
text: Aa mu yaa kan unii u joo saawaa na kan, ku udaan ngbaan. Ti mɔmɔk sɔ do, timi aanib bee le ga li ye biseeraadam, lik m ni maanib aawan mɔmɔk ponn ni, ki nyan saawan aah ye ni na mɔmɔk.” Jakob aa nan nyi ke upuu Rachel le sun ute Labann aawaa.

ref: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
text: Le Labann nan koo Jakob aadiik ni ki biln, ki koo Lea mu, ni baanaagbiipiib bilee na aadir ponn ni ki biln, kaa kan waawaa ngbaan. Le u koo Rachel aadiik mu ni.

ref: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
text: Rachel le nan yoor ŋiwaa ngbaan ki di bɔr laakumii aajal taab, waadiik ni, le ki kal li pu. Le Labann nan biln kidiik ponn ni, ni kookoo, kaa kan ŋi.

ref: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
text: Rachel nan bui ute ke, “Uninkpel, taa gee liŋuul m pu, m fu tipiir la, nima pu le maan ŋmaa fii sil aanimbiin ni.” Le Labann nan biln, kaa kan waawaa ngbaan.

ref: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
text: Kina pu na, Jakob aasui nan fii, waa ki ŋmaa chuu ubaa, le ki baa Labann ke, “M tee ŋa si ba aabakaa. M tee bii nkaal mulamu aan aa kpa nsan ke aa paan ni m pu?

ref: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
text: Dandana wee aa biln timi aawan mɔmɔk ni, aa kan saawan nilani? Nyan ni siin, aan saanib ni maanib mɔmɔk kan ni, ki bee u ye mbamɔndaan na.

ref: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
text: N‑yoonn mumɔk tipeewanbir yaa nan ti chuu saawakork kibaa na kan, ni nan ye min le aafalaa. Maa nan yoor taakpab ti mɔk si ke naa ye maataani. N‑yoonn mumɔk unaayuk yaa nan ti sun saawakork kibaa kinyeek, bee nwiin pu na kan, see min le ga teen si.

ref: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
text: N‑yoonn pam le nwiin nan gbaa mi, le tiwoor mu ŋun mi kinyeek, maa ŋmaa geeni.

ref: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
text: Ni yaa kaa ye Uwumbɔr u nte Aisak ni n‑yaaja Abraham nan dii na nan bi m chee kan, kina m ba nyan aado nkuun la. Uwumbɔr aah kan maafalaa ngbaan, ni maah tun tii si pu na, le kinyeek na u fe bui si mbamɔn.” Jakob ni Labann aah puu tipuur tii tɔb pu na aabɔr

ref: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
text: Labann nan bui Jakob ke, “Mpiibim bimina ye mbisatiib la, le min le yeh baabim ni tiwakor timina mɔmɔk. Mbamɔn, tiwan nimɔk bi do na ye maawan la. Le maah kaan ŋmaa gaa mbisatiib ni baabim na kan,

ref: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
text: m gor ke m ni si ŋa kimɔbaan. Cha ti kuun ŋitakpal bil nibaa chee aan ni li teer timi kimɔbaan ngbaan aabɔr.”

ref: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
text: U nan bui waanib ngbaan ke bi kuuni ŋitakpal ki nan di bil libuul libaa ni. Le bi nan kal ŋitakpal ngbaan chee ki jin tijikaar.

ref: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
text: Labann aaliin ponn ni u nan yin nima chee ke, Jegar Sahadufa. Le Jakob mu aaliin ponn ni, u yin nima chee ke Galeed,

ref: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
text: Le Labann bui Jakob ke, “Ŋitakpal ŋi ti kuun bil na le ga cha ti li teer kimɔbaan ngbaan.” Nima le cha bi yin nima chee ke Galeed.

ref: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
text: Le Labann ki bui ke, “Uwumbɔr li lik ti mɔmɔk bilee, taah ga yakr tɔb chee pu na, ubaa taa ŋa uken bakaa.” Nima pu na, bi nan ki yin nima chee ke Mispa.

ref: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
text: Labann nan ki bui ke, “Aa yaa ŋa mbisatiib bee bakaa, bee aa yaa ki yoor bipiib kpee bi pu kan, hali m yaa kaa nyi kan, teer ke Uwumbɔr waa si.

ref: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
text: Tiwan nilee ngbaan le ga li teer timi. M kii ke nwiin mbaa daal, maan lakr ŋitakpal ŋee pu jer ke m nan ban si kijaak, aa mu taa ŋa kina.

ref: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
text: Aayaaja Abraham Aawumbɔr ni n‑yaaja Nahor Aawumbɔr le ga li ye timi aabɔjir.” Le Jakob aate Aisak Aawumbɔr aayimbil pu, u mu nan puu ke u mu ga li joo tipuur ngbaan.

ref: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
text: U nan kɔr kiwakork ki toor kitork, lijool ngbaan paab, le ki nan chɔi waanib ngbaan, le bi dan nan jin tijikaar. Baah jin doo na, le bi mɔmɔk kpaan doon lijool ngbaan paab.

ref: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
text: Naah woln kichakpiik ni na, le Labann moor uyaabitiib ni ubisatiib aatakpin ki ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu, le ki chɔi bi, le ki gir kun udo.

ref: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
text: Jakob mu nan cha, le Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib tooh u nsan ni.

ref: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.

ref: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”

ref: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”

text: Josef nan bui waanib ke, “Puu tii mi man, ke n‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr nyan nimi Ijipt aatiŋ kee ni, aan ni chaa kun Kanaann aatiŋ ni na, ni ga yoor maawon mu buen nima chee.”

text: Bi mɔmɔk nan kpaan ki ti saa binib imonko itaa ni kipiik, le ki nyan ni Jakob aamaal ni. Ujapɔɔn Josef ma nan puun bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni.

text: Tɔ, baah nan nan Israel yaab ki moo ŋani bi falaa sakpen pu na, Uwumbɔr nan cha bi moo pɔr kpee kina la, le ki yaa gbiin Ijipt aatiŋ ponn ni, le Ijipt yaab nan gur san Israel yaab ijawaan,

text: Bimamaam ngbaan aah nan san Uwumbɔr ijawaan na, le u nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu ki cha bi ma mbim pam. Le Israel yaab too pɔr kpae ki kpa mpɔɔn.

text: Buyoonn u ti bee ke waan ki ŋmaa bɔr u na, le u ban kibɔɔkuuk, le ki ban tiwan teŋ ki ponn ni aan nnyun taa koo u chee, ki nan di ubo ngbaan ŋa kibɔɔkuuk ngbaan ponn ni, le ki di u ti bɔr tikal ni, limɔɔl aagbaan.

ref: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
text: Ubɔr aabisal ngbaan nan chuu piir kibɔɔkuuk ngbaan le ki kan ubijabo waatiir ngbaan. Ubo ngbaan nan bi wii, le kinimbaak chuu u, le u bui ke, “Hiibru yaab aabijabo ubaa le na.”

text: Le ubɔr aabisal ngbaan bui upii ngbaan ke, “Gaa ubo umina ki li ŋaani u tii mi, aan m pa si.” Nima le u nan gaa ubo ngbaan, le ki kpiin u.

text: Ubo ngbaan aah lii libiil buyoonn na, le upii ngbaan di u buen ti di u tii ubɔr aabisal ngbaan, le u gaa u ki di ŋa ujapɔɔn. Le ubɔr aabisal bui usui ni ke, “M daa nyan u nnyun ni la, nima pu na, m ga yin u ke Moses.” Moses aah san ŋmar ki buen Midiann aatiŋ ni pu na

ref: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
text: Le uja ngbaan giin bui u ke, “Ŋma ŋa si timi aayidaan ni ubɔjir? Aa ban ke aa ku mi ke saah fe ku Ijipt aaja na pu na la aa?” Nima chee le ijawaan chuu Moses, le u dakl usui ni ke, “Binib bee maah ŋa pu na a.”

ref: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
text: Le bipihkpaab bibaa mu dan nima ki nan san jenn mpiibim ngbaan. Le Moses buen ti ter bi ki lun nnyun tii baawakor ngbaan.

text: Baah gir kun buyoonn na, le bite baa bi ke, “Ba ŋa ni gir ni din mala kina?”

text: Le bi bui u ke, “Ijipt aaja ubaa le gaa timi lii bipihkpaab ngbaan chee, le ki lun nnyun tii timi aawakor mu.”

ref: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
text: Le u baa ubisatiib ke, “Uja ngbaan bi la chee? Ba ŋa ni cha u ka nima chee? Ti chɔi ni u man, aan u nan ji tijikaar ti chee.”

ref: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.

text: le u ma ubijabo tii u. Le Moses bui usui ni ke, “M ye uwɔwɔnja le kitiŋ kee ni, nima pu na, m ga yin ubo ngbaan ke Gesom.”

ref: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,

ref: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
text: Le u dakl ke, “Nimina ye lijinjiir aawan la. Ba ŋa mmii aa wun busub ngbaan? M ga buen ti lik.”

ref: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
text: Buyoonn Uwumbɔr kan ke Moses ŋɔŋ mmii ngbaan chee na, le u yin u mmii ngbaan ni ke, “Moses, Moses.” U nan kii ke, “M sɔ.”

text: Nima pu le m sunn ni ki dan ke m nan gaa bi lii, ki nyan bi Ijipt yaab aatiŋ ni, ki tii bi kitiŋ ki ŋan, ki wiir, ki kpa tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan ni ŋisubil sakpen na; kitiŋ ngbaan le Kanaann yaab, ni Hef yaab, ni Amor yaab, ni Peris yaab, ni Hif yaab, ni Jebus yaab laa bi ki ponn ni na.

ref: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.

ref: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
text: Dandana wee m ban m tun si Ijipt yaab aabɔr chee, nima kan aa ga ŋmaa loln maanib ngbaan pu nsan ki nyan bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni.”

ref: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
text: Moses nan bui Uwumbɔr ke, “Maa ye nibaa, m ga ŋa kinye ki buen ubɔr chee ki ti nyan Israel yaab Ijipt aatiŋ ni?”

ref: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
text: Le Moses giin bui u ke, “M yaa buen Israel yaab chee ki ti bui bi ke, ‘Tiyaajatiib Aawumbɔr le tun ni mi ni chee’ kan, bi ga baa mi ke, ‘Bi yin u kinye?’ Nima pu na, m ga tuk bi kinye?”

ref: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
text: Tuk Israel yaab ke min, U‑ye‑na, u ye niyaajatiib Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob Aawumbɔr na le tun ni si bi chee. Bi ga li yin mi kina le n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Kina le n‑yoonn mu choo na aanib ga li yin mi.

ref: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
text: M dakl ke m ga nyan bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, nin chee bi ŋani bi falaa na, ki di bi buen kitiŋ ki kpa tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan ni ŋisubil sakpen na, kitiŋ ki ye Kanaann yaab, ni Hef yaab, ni Amor yaab, ni Peris yaab, ni Hif yaab, ni Jebus yaab aatiŋ na pu.

ref: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
text: “Maanib ga pel saah ga bui bi pu na. Le aa di baaninkpiib buen Ijipt yaab aabɔr chee ki ti bui u ke, ‘Uwumbɔr, u ye timi Hiibru yaab Aawumbɔr na, uma le di ubaa mɔk timi. text: M ga di maapɔɔn daa Ijipt yaab aatafal, ki ŋa ijawaan aawan baatiŋ ni. Nee aapuwɔb na u ga cha ni buen.

The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
text: Le Israel yaab aapiib mɔmɔk ga mee binaakoontiib bi ye Ijipt yaab, ni bipiib bi koo bi chee ki ye Ijipt yaab na ŋikeken, ni salmaa, ni tikunabr aaleen. Le Israel yaab ga di tiwan nimina peen bijapɔtiib ni bibisatiib aan ki tun Ijipt yaab aawangol buen.”

ref: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
text: Moses nan bui Uwumbɔr ke, “Nibaakan, Israel yaab yaa kaa gaa mi ki kii, kaan pel maah ga len pu na kan, bi yaa bui ke saa dan m chee kan, m ga ŋa kinye?”

text: Le Uwumbɔr baa u ke, “Aa joo ba?” Le u bui ke, “Kijaangbeek.”

ref: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.

ref: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.

ref: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui u ke, “Ti ŋa kina ki mɔk Israel yaab ke Uwumbɔr, u ye niyaajatiib Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob Aawumbɔr na le dan aa chee.”

ref: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ke, “Di aaŋaal ŋa saabɔkul ponn ni.” Le Moses ŋa kina. Waah nyan uŋaal na, le mu kpaln ibusoon.

ref: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui u ke, “Ki giin aaŋaal ŋa saabɔkul ni.” Le u ŋa kina, le n‑yoonn mu u chuu nyan ni mu na, mu ki pɔɔ, ki bi ke uwon tiken aah bi pu na.

ref: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
text: Hali bi yaa kaa ki faar lelee aajinjiir aatuln ngbaan mu, kaa gaa si kii kan, ki yaa yii, ke baan pel saah len pu na kan, buen ti kab Nail aamɔɔl aanyun ki di mu kpir kitiŋ binimbiin ni. Nnyun ngbaan ga kpaln nsin.”

ref: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
text: Moses nan bui ke, “Aayii, Ndindaan, taa tun mi. Maa ŋmaa len tibɔr mbamɔm, le saah piin ki len m chee buyoonn ki nan saa dandana wee na, m beenin bi kina la, maa ŋmaa len mala mala.”

ref: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui u ke, “Ŋma tii unii bumɔb? Ŋma cha unii ye utafakpaa, bee ubir? Ŋma tii unii ŋinimbil, ki ki cha u ŋani ujoon? Min Uwumbɔr le ŋani kina.

ref: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
text: Nima pu na, li cha. M ga ter si aa len, le ki tuk si saah ga len pu na.”

ref: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
text: Moses nan bui ke, “Aayii, Ndindaan, tun ubaa.”

text: Aa ga bui u ke min Uwumbɔr len ke, ‘Israel yaab le ye maajan aabijabo.

text: Nima pu na, u nan di bi mann dii nteersakpiin pu ki toŋ Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem wɔb. Israel yaab nan gor bi to butɔb.

ref: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
text: Moses nan cha bi yoor Josef aakpab ki di buen; ba pu? Josef aah nan ban u kpo na, u nan cha Israel yaab puu tipuur kina. Josef nan bui ke, “N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr nan gaa nimi lii aan ni ban ni nya na kan, ni yoor maakpab nya do ki di buen.”

ref: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
text: Israel yaab nan nyan Sukof le ki sil Etam aapepel, nteersakpiin aagbaan.

ref: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke,

ref: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
text: “Tuk Israel yaab ke bi fenn ki ti kal Pi Hahirof, ni bi Migdol ni Nnyusakpem Mamam aakaasisik ni na, ki gbɔk Baal Sefonn chee na.

ref: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
text: Ubɔr ngbaan ga li dak ke Israel yaab yenn le ki chuun kitiŋ ngbaan ni, ki bi nteersakpiin ni, kaa ŋmaa nya.

ref: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
text: M ga cha usui pɔɔk, le u ga fii paan ni ni pu, le maah ga nyaŋ ubɔr ngbaan pu na, m ga kan kipak kina pu. Le Ijipt yaab ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.” Israel yaab nan ŋa Moses aah tuk bi pu na.

ref: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
text: Buyoonn ubɔr ngbaan ŋun ke binib na san ŋmar na, le u ni waaninkpiib kpeln bisui le ki kpokl ki bui ke, “Ti ŋa ba kina? Ti cha Israel yaab san ŋmar a, le taa ki kpa binaagbiib.”

ref: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
text: Le ubɔr ngbaan yin waajab, le ki ban waatɔb aatɔroku, le ki gor ubaa pu.

ref: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
text: Uwumbɔr nan cha ubɔr ngbaan aasui pɔɔk, le u di paan Israel yaab bi nan nyan buen linyaŋ ni na aapuwɔb.

ref: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
text: Le Ijipt yaab aajab, ni baataan, ni baatɔroku tiib, ni binib bi ŋaal tɔroku tiib na di paan bi pu, le ki ti pii bi, baah nan kal nin chee, Nnyusakpem Mamam mu bi gbɔk Pi Hahirof ni Baal Sefonn chee na.

ref: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
text: N‑yoonn mu Israel yaab kan ubɔr ngbaan ni waajab paa ni bi pu na, le ijawaan chuu bi, le bi wii yin Uwumbɔr ke u ter bi,

ref: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
text: le ki bui Moses ke, “Ŋikaakul aa bi Ijipt aatiŋ ponn ni la aa? Aa nyan ni timi ke ti nan kpo nteersakpiin mue ni la aa? Lik saah ŋa pu na, ki nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni.

ref: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
text: Moses nan giin bui bi ke, “Taa san ijawaan man. Sil chob man, ni ga kan Uwumbɔr aah ga ŋa pu ki gaa nimi lii din wee na. Naan ki kan Ijipt yaab bee daalbaadaal.

ref: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
text: Uwumbɔr le ga to butɔb ngbaan tii nimi, naan li kpa nibaa ni ŋa butɔb ngbaan ni.”

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke, “Ba ŋa ni wii ki ban nterm? Tuk binib ngbaan ke bi li chuun.

ref: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
text: Yoor saajaangbeek paacham ki di mɔk nnyusakpem ngbaan. Nnyun ngbaan ga yakr, le Israel yaab ga ŋmaa chuun kitikuun pu ki jer nnyusakpem ngbaan aasisik ni.

ref: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
text: M ga pɔɔk Ijipt yaab aajab ngbaan aasui, le bi ga paan ni pu, le m ga nyaŋ ubɔr ngbaan, ni waajab, ni waatɔroku tiib, ni bijab bi ŋaal bi na mɔmɔk, ki kan kipak bi pu.

ref: The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
text: N‑yoonn mu m nyaŋ bi na, le Ijipt yaab ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

ref: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
text: Uwumbɔr aatuun, u ba loln Israel yaab pu nsan na gir buen bipuwɔb. Le ntaalangbam na mu buen ki ti sil Ijipt yaab ni Israel yaab aakaasisik ni.

ref: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
text: Ntaalangbam ngbaan nan cha ni bɔnn Ijipt yaab chee, le ki tee ye nwiihn Israel yaab wɔb, nima pu na, kinyeek ngbaan, ŋitimbol ŋilee ngbaan aa nan ŋmaa ŋɔŋ tɔb pu le kitaak ti woln.

ref: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
text: Moses nan yoor uŋaal paacham ki mɔk nnyusakpem ngbaan, le Uwumbɔr cha libuln nyan ni liwipuul wɔb ki daa nnyusakpem ngbaan pu, le ki kiir mu, le mu yakr tɔb chee. Libuln ngbaan nan daa kinyeek ki ti woln kitaak, le ni kuur. Nnyun ngbaan nan yakr tɔb chee,

ref: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
text: le Israel yaab chuun nnyusakpem ngbaan ni, kitikuun pu, le nnyun ngbaan kpaln ŋigon ki sil ŋipepel mɔmɔk ŋilee.

ref: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
text: Naah ti chaa woln ni na, le Uwumbɔr bi ntaalangbam ni, mmii ponn ni, le ki lik waa Ijipt yaab aajab, le ki cha ijawaan chuu bi.

ref: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
text: U nan cha baatɔroku tiib aataa chɔi kitiŋ, le baa ki ŋmaa chuun mala mala. Le Ijipt yaab bui ke, “Uwumbɔr le bi to butɔb ngbaan tii Israel yaab. Cha ti gir nya do chee na man.”

ref: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ke, “Yoor aaŋaal paacham ki mɔk nnyusakpem ngbaan, nnyun ngbaan ga gir kpaan tɔb ni, ki biin Ijipt yaab, ni baatɔroku tiib, ni bijab bi ŋaal bi na pu.”

ref: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
text: Nima pu le Moses nan yoor uŋaal ki di mɔk nnyusakpem na, le lichakpitaawoln wɔb, nnyun ngbaan ki gir kpaan tɔb ponn ni, ki naa tɔb ke mu aah ba bi pu na. Le Ijipt yaab nan ban bi san ŋmar, le Uwumbɔr moo di bi mee lii nnyun ngbaan ni.

ref: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
text: Le nnyun gir biin baatɔroku tiib, ni bijab bi ŋaal bi na, ni Ijipt yaab aajab bi nan paan Israel yaab na pu, ubaa aa nan ki gur.

ref: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
text: Israel yaab ma nan chuun kitikuun pu le nnyusakpem ngbaan ni, le mu kpaln ŋigon ki si ŋipepel mɔmɔk ŋilee.

ref: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
text: Liyaadaal ngbaan le Uwumbɔr nan gaa Israel yaab Ijipt yaab chee lii, le Israel yaab kan baah kpoi ki dɔ nnyun ngbaan aagbaan pu na.

ref: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
text: N‑yoonn mu Israel yaab kan Uwumbɔr aah di waapɔɔn nyaŋ Ijipt yaab na, le ni ŋa bi tifaan Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu na, le bi gaa Uwumbɔr ni waatutunn Moses ki kii.

ref: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
text: Nima chee le Moses ni Israel yaab nan gaa nlahn mumina ki pak Uwumbɔr: “M ga gaa ilahn ki pak Uwumbɔr, ba pu? waah nyaŋ pu na kpa kipak; u di itaan ni bijab bi jak i na mee lii nnyusakpem ponn ni.

ref: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
text: Uwumbɔr le ye u kii mi ki pɔɔ na. Uma le gaa mi lii. Uma le ye Maawumbɔr, le m ga pak u. Uma le ye nte Aawumbɔr, le m ga gaa ilahn ki pak waah kpa mpɔɔn pu na.

ref: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
text: Uwumbɔr ye u ŋmaa to butɔb na la, waayimbil le ye Uwumbɔr.

ref: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
text: U di Ijipt yaab aajab ni baatɔroku tiib ki di mee lii nnyusakpem ponn ni; baaninkpiib nyanyaam mɔmɔk nan bee nnyusakpem ponn ni.

ref: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
text: Uwumbɔr, saaŋangii le tun mpɔɔn aatuln li kpa kipak na; muma le kool saadim aakpab yuk yuk.

ref: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
text: Saanaan mu kpa kipak na ponn ni le aa joo saapɔɔn nyaŋni saadim. Saaŋuul naahn mmii le ki wu bi ke ŋikak na.

ref: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
text: Aa pii libuln lii nnyusakpem pu, le nnyun fii sil paacham, le mu sil ke ligoln na; le nnyusakpem nin chee nyoo sakpen na kpaln nin chee pɔɔ na.

ref: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
text: Timi aadin bui ke, ‘M ga paan bi pu aan ki chuu bi. M ga yakr baawangol le ki nyan maah gee ni na. M ga di maajaak aajuk le ki jenn bi ki gaa baah kpa tiwan ni na mɔmɔk.’

ref: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
text: Uwumbɔr, aa nan fuur lii Ijipt yaab pu nfum mbaa le bi muin ke tikur na, ki bee nnyusakpem ni.

ref: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
text: Uwumbɔr, lilawaal bi ke si na? Ŋma bi ke si na, aan saabimbin bi chain kina? Ŋma ba tee bi ki tun lijinjiir, ni ŋitun sakpiin ke saah tun pu na?

ref: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
text: Sin le taln aaŋangii, le kitiŋ di timi aadim di nab.

ref: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
text: Ŋinibol mɔmɔk ŋun aa pu, le ijawaan chuu bi, le biwon gbaa, ijawaan nan chuu Filistia yaab.

ref: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
text: Ijawaan nan chuu Edom aaninkpiib, le Moab yaab aayidam aawon gbaa, le Kanaann yaab aataakpab yɔl,

ref: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
text: le ijawaan lir bi pu. Uwumbɔr, binib ngbaan kan saapɔɔn, le ijawaan chuu bi, le bi si lik, kaa ŋmaa ŋa nibaa, le saanib bi aa nyan bi tinaagbiir ni na chuun jer.

ref: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
text: Si le di bi kaan saajool pu, sin Uwumbɔr aah nyan nin chee ke ni li ye aado na, saadichal li aa maa li aabaa na ni.

ref: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
text: Sin Uwumbɔr le ga li ye ubɔr ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.” Miriam aalahn

ref: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔnabpii Miriam, u ye Aaronn aaninkpan na nan yoor waachayakrtuun, le bipiib mɔmɔk mu yoor baachayakrtuun ki dii u ki waa liwaal,

ref: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
text: Miriam le nan gaa ilahn ke: “Gaa ilahn ki pak Uwumbɔr man, ba pu? waah nyaŋ pu na kpa kipak; u di itaan ni bijab bi jak i na mee lii nnyusakpem ponn ni.” Nnyun mu cho na

ref: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
text: Moses nan loln binib ngbaan pu nsan ki nyan Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem na chee, ki di bi dii Sur aateersakpiin ni. Bi nan chuun kiteek ngbaan ni, ki ti saa iwiin itaa, le baa nan kan nnyun.

ref: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
text: Le binib ngbaan nan ŋulni Moses pu ki baa u ke, “Ti ga nyu ba?”

ref: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
text: Le Moses mee Uwumbɔr mbamɔm, le Uwumbɔr mɔk u ndɔ mubaa, le u di mu mee lii nnyun ngbaan ponn ni, le nnyun na mɔɔk, bi nyu. Nima chee le Uwumbɔr tii bi ikaal ke bi li joo i, le u ki toŋ bi nima chee mu.

ref: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
text: U nan bui bi ke, “Ni yaa kii tii mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki ŋani maah ban pu na, ki joo maakaal i m di tii nimi na kan, maan cha iween i aaboln m nan cha i lir Ijipt yaab pu na lir ni pu. Min le ye Uwumbɔr u sɔŋni nimi aaween na.”

ref: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
text: Israel yaab mɔmɔk nan nyan Elim ni, ki ti fuu Sinn aateersakpiin mu bi Elim ni Sainai aakaasisik ni na, lelee aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni iŋmu daal, baah nan nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni na aapuwɔb.

ref: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
text: Nima chee, nteersakpiin ngbaan ni, le bi mɔmɔk len tibɔbir ti kaa ŋan na Moses ni Aaronn pu,

ref: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
text: le ki bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr yaa ba ku timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni kan, ti ba ga li gee kina. Ti ba ga li kani tinann ni tijikaar timɔk ti gee na ki ji, le ni joo ni timi nteersakpiin mumina ponn ni ti nan kpo nkon.”

ref: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui Moses ke, “Dandana wee, m ga cha tijikaar nyan ni paacham ki lir ni kitiŋ, ki tii ni mɔmɔk. Tɔ, binib ngbaan ga ban tijikaar ngbaan iwiin mɔmɔk ki ti ŋeer nwiin mubaa aajim. Nimina le ga cha m bee ke binib ngbaan ga joo maakaal aan baan joo.

ref: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
text: Winloob daal kan, bi ban tijikaar ngbaan ki ŋa ti ŋeer iwiin ilee aajim.”

ref: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
text: Le Moses ni Aaronn nan bui Israel yaab tibɔr ngbaan ke, “Kijook kee le ni ga bee ke Uwumbɔr le nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ponn ni ki joo nimi.

ref: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
text: Kichakpiik ni, ni ga kan Uwumbɔr aajinjiir aawiihn. U ŋun naah len tibɔbir u pu pu na. Mbamɔn, ni len uma la, naa ye timi; tima joo waamɔbon le tuk nimi.”

ref: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
text: Le Moses ki bui bi ke, “Ni ye Uwumbɔr ubaa le ga tii nimi tinann kijook kee, le kichakpiik ni u ga tii nimi tijikaar naah ban pu na, ba pu? u ŋun naah len tibɔbir u pu sakpen pu na; n‑yoonn mu ni len tibɔbir ti pu na, ni ye mbamɔn ke ni len Uwumbɔr la.”

ref: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
text: Moses nan bui Aaronn ke, “Tuk binib ngbaan mɔmɔk ke bi dan nan sil Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, ba pu? u ŋun baah len tibɔbir u pu pu na.”

ref: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
text: Aaronn aah bui bi kina na, le bi mɔmɔk fenn binimbil toŋ nteersakpiin wɔb, le libuul ngbaan ni Uwumbɔr aajinjiir aawiihn na nyan bi chee ntaalangbam ni.

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui Moses ke,

ref: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
text: “Israel yaab aah len tibɔbir m pu pu na, m ŋun. Tuk bi ke kijook kee bi ga kan tinann ki ŋmɔ, le fen kichakpiik ni bi ga fe kan tijikaar timɔk bi ban na, le ki ga bee ke min, Uwumbɔr, le ye Bidindaan.”

ref: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
text: Kijook ngbaan le kichakpeepaak fii nan lir ki gbiin linampal, le ni woln kichakpiik ni, le limaln lir goln linampal.

ref: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
text: N‑yoonn mu limaln baal na, le bi kan tijikaar tibaa aaboln nteersakpiin ngbaan ni. Ti nan diin ki soon ki naahn ŋitaatakpal la.

ref: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
text: N‑yoonn mu Israel yaab kan tijikaar ngbaan na, baa nan bee ti, le ki baa tɔb ke, “Ni ye ba?” Le Moses bui bi ke, “Tijikaar ti Uwumbɔr bui ke u ga tii nimi, ni ji na, le na.

ref: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke lidichal mɔmɔk ban tijikaar ngbaan ki ŋeer nwiin mubaa, naah ga ŋmaa ji pu na, kuruwaa ubaa ŋeer unii ubaa.”

ref: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
text: Israel yaab nan ŋa kina la, ngem nan ban tijikaar ngbaan ki jer bibaa, le biken mu nan ban taa fuu bi.

ref: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
text: Le Moses bui bi ke, “Ubaa taa gur tijikaar ngbaan ti woln kitaak.”

ref: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
text: Ngem aa nan ŋun tii Moses, le ki gur tijikaar ngbaan. Naah woln na le tijikaar ngbaan kpaln ŋikpaambil le ki bur ki nu, le Moses gee liŋuul bi pu.

ref: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
text: Kichakpiik mɔmɔk ni, bi mɔmɔk nan ban tijikaar ngbaan ŋeer bibaa la; le nwiin yaa toŋ kan, le tijikaar ti gur dɔ kitiŋ na donn.

ref: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
text: Winloob daal kan, le bi mɔmɔk ban ti nfum mulee pu, ki ŋeer nwiin ngbaan daal ni kitaak ki ga woln na mu, kuruwaa bilee ŋeer unii ubaa. Le binib ngbaan aaninkpiib dan ki nan tuk Moses baah ŋani pu na,

ref: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
text: le u bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr siin nkaal ke fen fe ye lifuur aawiin la, le ki tii u. Din wee, ni ken naah ban ni ken tijikaar ti na, ki ŋaan naah ban ni ŋaan ti na mu. Ti gur na kan, ni di siin kiir fen.”

ref: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
text: Le Moses aah siin bi pu na, bi nan di tijikaar ti gur na siin, le ni woln kitaak, le taa bii, ŋikpaambil mu aa koo ti ponn ni.

ref: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
text: Moses nan bui bi ke, “Din wee, ni li ji tijikaar ti ni kpa na man, ba pu? din ye likpaakool daal, nwiin mu ye lifuur daal ki tii Uwumbɔr na, naan kan tijikaar ngbaan kitiŋ din wee.

ref: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
text: Ni ban tijikaar ngbaan ki ti saa winloob daal, winlole daal ye lifuur daal la, tijikaar tibaa aan li bi, ni ban ti.”

ref: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
text: Winlole daal le binib ngbaan bibaa buen bi ti ban tijikaar ngbaan, le kaa kan nibaa.

ref: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui Moses ke, “Ni ga yunn ki ti saa bayoonn aan nimi maanib ga nin kii tii mi ki joo maakaal?

ref: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”

text: Aa di salmaa aatork aabimbiln li bi seer tulalee aayon li pu na siin Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa chee, aan ki di likekeln gbin Libool ngbaan aabisamɔb.

ref: Set the altar for burning sacrifices in front of the entrance to my tent.
text: Aa di kitork aabimbiln li bi seer ipiin li pu na siin Libool ngbaan aabisamɔb chee.

ref: Put the large bronze bowl between the tent and the altar and fill the bowl with water.
text: Aa di lisambil li bi ŋir biŋaal li ponn ni na siin Libool ngbaan ni kitork aabimbiln aakaasisik ni, ki ban nnyun gbiin li.

ref: Surround the tent and the altar with the wall of curtains and hang the curtain that was made for the entrance.
text: Aa di tiwan gob Libool na, aan ki di likekeln leen naabisamɔb.

ref: Do the same thing with the altar for offering sacrifices and its equipment
text: Ni paa na, di maakpan meen kitork aabimbiln, ni laawan mɔmɔk, aan ni ŋa chain, ki di ni tii mi.

ref: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent and tell them to wash themselves.
text: “Di Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib dan Libool ngbaan aabisamɔb chee ki cha bi fu nnyun.

ref: Dress Aaron in the priestly clothes, then use the sacred olive oil to ordain him and dedicate him to me as my priest.
text: Di utotoor aawanpeenkaan peen Aaronn, ki di maakpan kpir uyil pu. Aa yaa ŋa u kina kan, u ga ŋmaa tun utotoor aatuln ki tii mi.

ref: Put the priestly robes on Aaron's sons
text: Li joo ni ujapɔtiib mu, ki nan di ŋibɔkul peen bi,

ref: And on the first day of the first month of the second year, the sacred tent was set up.
text: Nima pu na, njan aaŋmal aajan aawiin daal libiln leler ni, baah nyan ni Ijipt ponn ni buyoonn na, le bi nan gaa Uwumbɔr Aabool siin.

ref: The stones with the Ten Commandments written on them were stored in the sacred chest, the place of mercy was put on top of it, and the carrying poles were attached.
text: Le u di ŋitakpapapan ŋilee na ki di ŋa Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ni. U nan di ŋidabil na ki di bɔn ibuen i dab baa dakaa ngbaan pu na, li ki di waabiil biin u pu.

ref: The chest was brought into the tent and set behind the curtain in the most holy place. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
text: U nan di dakaa ngbaan siin Libool ngbaan ponn ni, ki di likekeln ngbaan mu di leen kiir. Waah ŋa pu na, le u kiir Nkaal Aadakaa ngbaan ke Uwumbɔr aah nan bui u pu na.

ref: The table for the sacred bread was put along the north wall of the holy place,
text: U nan di teebul ngbaan mu di siin Libool ngbaan ni, ŋŋangan wɔb, likekeln na aapaal wɔb,

ref: then the lamps were attached to it there in the presence of the Lord.
text: nima chee le u see karyaa tiib Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, ke waah bui u ke u ŋa pu na.

ref: The gold incense altar was set up in front of the curtain,
text: U nan di salmaa aatork aabimbiln mu siin Libool ngbaan ni, likekeln ngbaan chee,

ref: and sweet-smelling incense was burned on it. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
text: le ki see tulalee aayon mu nu mɔ na, ke Uwumbɔr aah nan bui u pu na.

ref: The curtain was hung at the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: U nan di likekeln di leen Libool ngbaan aabisamɔb,

ref: Then the altar for offering sacrifices was put in front of the tent, and animal sacrifices and gifts of grain were offered there.
text: nima chee le u di libimbiln li bi toor ipiin aatork na di siin likekeln ngbaan aapaal wɔb. U nan toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, ni njikaabim aapiin li pu, ke Uwumbɔr aah nan bui u ke u ŋa pu na.

ref: The large bronze bowl was placed between the altar and the entrance to the tent. It was filled with water,
text: U nan di lisambil li bi ŋir biŋaal li ponn ni na siin Libool ni kitork aabimbiln ngbaan aakaasisik ni, le ki ban nnyun gbiin li ni,

ref: then Moses and Aaron, together with Aaron's sons, washed their hands and feet.
text: aan Moses, ni Aaronn, ni ujapɔtiib ŋir biŋaal ki finn bitaa

ref: In fact, they washed each time before entering the tent or offering sacrifices at the altar. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
text: buyoonn bi yaa ti ban bi koo Libool ngbaan ni, bee bi yaa ti dan kitork aabimbiln chee na, ke Uwumbɔr aah nan bui u ke u ŋa pu na.

ref: Suddenly the sacred tent was covered by a thick cloud and filled with the glory of the Lord.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan, Uwumbɔr aataalangbam nan biin Libool pu, le waawiihn mu moor ki deer ŋinimbil na gbiin li ponn ni.

ref: And so, Moses could not enter the tent.
text: Nimina pu na, Moses aa nan ŋmaa koo Libool ngbaan ni.

ref: Whenever the cloud moved from the tent, the people would break camp and follow;
text: Buyoonn Uwumbɔr aataalangbam ti biir Libool ngbaan pu nin chee Israel yaab nan ka na, le Israel yaab ti fii nima chee.

ref: then they would set up camp and stay there, until it moved again.
text: N‑yoonn mumɔk ntaalangbam ngbaan si nima chee na kan, baa fii nima.

ref: No matter where the people traveled, the Lord was with them. Each day his cloud was over the tent, and each night a fire could be seen in the cloud.
text: N‑yoonn mu bi nan bi chuun kina na, bi nan kani Uwumbɔr aataalangbam ngbaan biini Libool na pu, nwiin pu, le kinyeek kan, ni ye mmii ki wiin li pu.

ref: Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
text: Udaan ngbaan ga di uŋaal paan unaaja ngbaan aayil pu, le Uwumbɔr ga gaa waatork ngbaan ki di cha pinn waatunwanbir.

ref: After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
text: U ga ku unaaja ngbaan nima chee, le Aaronn aamaal bi ye bitotoorb na ga di waasin tii Uwumbɔr, ki di mu yɔk yɔk kitork aabimbiln li si Libool ngbaan aabisamɔb chee na aapepel mɔmɔk ŋinaa pu.

ref: Skin the bull and cut it up,
text: Le u su kiwakork ngbaan ki geei kaanann.

ref: while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing.
text: Le bitotoorb ga toor idɔ paan libimbiln pu ki see i mmii.

ref: Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Uja ngbaan finn ponn ni aawan ni ŋitaajal, le utotoor u toor kitork na ga see kitork ngbaan mɔmɔk mmii, libimbiln paab. Tijikaar aapiin kina aaboln nu mɔ Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: If you sacrifice a ram or a goat, it must not have anything wrong with it.
text: Ni yaa ye waapiih, bee waaŋoob ponn ni le u ban u di ubaa toor kan, u nyan kijak ki li ŋan.

ref: Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: U ku ki libimbiln paab, ŋŋangan wɔb, le bitotoorb ga di kaasin yɔk yɔk kitork aabimbiln paab, ŋipepel mɔmɔk ŋinaa pu.

ref: Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Uja ngbaan finn ponn ni aawan, ni ŋitaajal, le utotoor ga di kitork ngbaan tii Uwumbɔr, ki see ti mɔmɔk libimbiln paab mmii ni. Tijikaar aapiin kina aaboln nu mɔ Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon.
text: Ni yaa ye waawan ni kpa ifeen na ponn ni le u ban u di toor kan, u nyan linanjel, bee libɔrnanjel.

ref: A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar,
text: Le utotoor ga di li buen kitork aabimbiln pu, ki mur gii liyil aan ki di see mmii ni, libimbiln pu. Bi cha laasin tuu nyan liwon ponn ni ki gbaa libimbiln aagbaan.

ref: remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar.
text: U chuu chee nyan kifileek, ni tijikaar ti bi ki ponn ni na di mee yaa kitork aabimbiln chee, nin chee nfatan dɔ na, liwipuul wɔb.

ref: Finally, he will take the bird by its wings, tear it partially open, and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: U chuu wɔk li, ki taa nyan ŋipue, aan ki di see mmii ni, libimbiln paab. Tijikaar aapiin aatork kina aaboln nu mɔ Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour,
text: N‑yoonn mu unii ubaa yaa ban u tii Uwumbɔr njikaabim aapiin na kan, u pue nan njikaabim ngbaan mu ŋa n‑yon. U ban nkpan ni tulalee aayon paan mu pu.

ref: and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: U yaa ŋa kina doo kan, u li joo ni mu Aaronn aabijabim bi ye bitotoorb na chee. Utotoor u ga gaa ipiin ngbaan na di uŋaal lee n‑yon ni nkpan, ki paar tulalee aayon na mɔmɔk, ki di see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, ni li ye limɔkl ke ni mɔmɔk ye Uwumbɔr aapiin la. Tijikaar aapiin kina aaboln nu mɔ uma Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
text: N‑yon mu gur na ye bitotoorb yaan la. Baah di tijikaar ngbaan tii Uwumbɔr aan ti gur na, ti ye tijikaar ti bi chain na la.

ref: If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
text: Ipiin ngbaan yaa ye boroboro le bi di pun boroboro aadiik ni kan, bi ŋa u ki taa di boroboro aanyɔk ŋmal u ni; bi di olif aakpan ŋmal n‑yon ni, ki ŋa boroboro u filk na, bee bi ŋa u ke maab na, ki di nkpan gbaa u.

ref: If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast.
text: Ipiin ngbaan yaa ye maab u bi ken u limaasambil ni na kan, bi ŋa u ki di olif aakpan ŋmal n‑yon ni, ki taa ŋa nnyɔk u ni.

ref: Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil.
text: Bi yaa ban bi di u tii Uwumbɔr ipiin kan, bi bur bur u ki ban nkpan ŋa u pu.

ref: If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
text: Ipiin ngbaan yaa ye tijikaar ti bi di ŋaan likumbuul ni na kan, bi yaa ban bi ŋa ti kan, bi di olif aakpan ŋmal n‑yon ni.

ref: You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar.
text: Bi li joo ni ipiin ngbaan ki nan di tii Uwumbɔr, aan utotoor gaa ti ki di buen kitork aabimbiln chee.

ref: Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Utotoor ga lee ti ngem ki di see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, ni li ye limɔkl ke ni mɔmɔk ye Uwumbɔr aapiin la. Tijikaar aapiin kina aaboln nu mɔ uma Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
text: Ipiin i gur na ye bitotoorb yaan la. Baah di tijikaar aapiin ngbaan tii Uwumbɔr aan ti gur na, ti ye tijikaar ti bi chain na la.

ref: Yeast and honey must never be burned on the altar, so don't ever mix either of these in a grain sacrifice.
text: Bi yaa ban bi tii Uwumbɔr njikaabim aapiin kan, bi taa ŋa boroboro aanyɔk mu ni, bi yaa ban bi tii kina aapiin kan, bi taa ŋa boroboro aanyɔk, bee tisiir.

ref: You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
text: Libiln mɔk ni, ni yaa chee njan aajikaabim kan, ni ban ti ki nan tii Uwumbɔr ipiin, ni taa see tima mmii ni.

ref: Salt is offered when you make an agreement with me, so sprinkle salt on these sacrifices.
text: Ni ban n‑yaan ŋa nimi aajikaar aapiin mɔmɔk ni, ba pu? n‑yaan le ye tipuur ti bi ni ni Uwumbɔr aasisik ni na aamɔkl. Ni li ŋani n‑yaan nimi aapiin mɔmɔk ni.

ref: Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest.
text: Ni yaa ban ni tii Uwumbɔr naah chee njan aajikaabim mu na kan, ni pu mu, bee ni nan mu, aan mu ŋa n‑yon.

ref: You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice.
text: Ni ban olif aakpan ni tulalee aayon paan mu pu.

ref: A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
text: Le utotoor ga lee n‑yon, ni nkpan, ki kpee tulalee aayon na mɔmɔk, ki di see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, ni li ye limɔkl ke ni mɔmɔk ye Uwumbɔr aapiin la.

ref: When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal.
text: N‑yoonn mu nimi ubaa ban u di unaa toor kitork ki tii Uwumbɔr kimɔbaan aapiin na kan, u li ye unaaja bee unaasal u ŋan na.

ref: Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: Uja ngbaan ga di uŋaal paan unaa ngbaan aayil pu, le ki kɔr u Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee. Le Aaronn aabijabim bi ye bitotoorb na ga di nsin yɔk yɔk kitork aabimbiln aapepel mɔmɔk ŋinaa pu.

ref: Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
text: Le bitotoorb ga di ni mɔmɔk, ki di kpee kitork kiken pu, ki see mmii ni, kitork aabimbiln paab. Tijikaar aapiin kina aaboln nu mɔ Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it.
text: U yaa ban u di upiih, bee uŋoob le toor kimɔbaan aatoor kan, u cha ki li ye kijak, bee kisal ki ŋan na.

ref: Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: u di uŋaal paan uyil pu, ki kɔr u Libool na aabisamɔb chee. Bitotoorb ga di nsin yɔk yɔk kitork aabimbiln aapepel mɔmɔk ŋinaa pu,

ref: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
text: Le utotoor u ŋa kitork ngbaan na di ni mɔmɔk see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, ni li ye tijikaar aapiin ki tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me
text: U yaa ban u di uŋoob le toor kan,

ref: at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: u di uŋaal paan uŋoob ngbaan aayil pu, aan ki kɔr u Libool na aabisamɔb chee. Le bitotoorb di nsin yɔk yɔk kitork aabimbiln aapepel ŋinaa mɔmɔk pu,

ref: One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me. All fat belongs to me.
text: Utotoor ga di ni see mmii ni, kitork aabimbiln paab, ni li ye tijikaar aapiin i nu mɔ Uwumbɔr chee na. Nkpan aawan mɔmɔk ye uma Uwumbɔr yaan la.

ref: So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
text: Israel yaab ubaa taa ji nkpan, bee nsin. Israel yaab mɔmɔk yaa bi nin chee mɔk na kan, bi li joo likoobil ngbaan ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
text: ki di uŋanbik bɔ nsin ngbaan ni, ki di yɔk yɔk chain aakekeln chee, nfum mulole,

ref: This is a sacrifice for sin. So he will lay his hand on the animal's head, before having it killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
text: U di uŋaal paan uyil pu, aan ki kɔr u, kitork aabimbiln aaŋangan wɔb, nin chee bi kɔr kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aawakor na. Ipiin aatork kimina aaboln le nyani titunwanbir.

ref: Then a priest will dip a finger in the blood; he will smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
text: Utotoor di uŋanbik bɔ nsin ni, ki di mu yɔk yɔk libimbiln aalɔlɔ aamɔju mɔmɔk pu, aan ki di nsin mu gur na kpir libimbiln ngbaan aataab.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses

ref: to say to the community of Israel: Offer a sacrifice to ask forgiveness when you sin by accidentally doing something I have told you not to do. When the High Priest Sins The Lord said:
text: ke u tuk Israel yaab ke ubaa yaa kaa nyi ki peln bii Uwumbɔr aakaal kan, waah ga ŋa pu na sɔ:

ref: When the high priest sins, he makes everyone else guilty too. And so, he must sacrifice a young bull that has nothing wrong with it.
text: Utotoorninkpel le yaa tun titunwanbir le ni ga joo ni ntafadaan binib pu kan, u di unaaja u ŋan na toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr, waatunwanbir ngbaan pu.

ref: The priest will lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay his hand on its head, and kill it there.
text: U li joo ni unaaja ngbaan Libool aabisamɔb chee, ki di uŋaal paan uyil pu, aan ki kɔr u Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni.

ref: He will take a bowl of the blood inside the tent,
text: Le Utotoorninkpel na ga ban unaaja ngbaan aasin ngem ki di koo Libool ngbaan ni,

ref: Then, in my presence, he will smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
text: ki ki di nsin ngbaan ngem ŋa tulalee aayon aabimbiln li si Libool ni na aalɔlɔ aamɔju pu. U di nsin mu gur na kpir libimbiln li si Libool aabisamɔb chee aan bi seer kitork aamii li pu na aataab.

ref: The priest will remove the fat from the bull, just as he does when he sacrifices a bull to ask my blessing. This includes the fat on the insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. He will then send it all up in smoke.
text: Le u ga yoor nkpan ngbaan ki di see mmii ni, libimbiln li paab bi seer kitork na, ke waah ŋani kimɔbaan aatoor aawakor aakpan pu na.

ref: The skin and flesh of the bull, together with its legs, insides, and the food still in its stomach, are to be taken outside the camp and burned on a wood fire near the ash heap. When the Whole Nation Sins The Lord said:
text: u ga di ni mɔmɔk nya baah ka ni chee na lipaal, ki di buen baah joo nfatan kpir nin chee aan ni ye chain na, ki see ni mɔmɔk idɔ aamii pu nima chee.

ref: When the nation of Israel disobeys me without meaning to, the whole nation is still guilty.
text: Israel yaab mɔmɔk le yaa tun titunwanbir Uwumbɔr chee ki bii waakaal kaa nyi,

ref: Once you realize what has happened, you must sacrifice a young bull to ask my forgiveness. Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent,
text: le titunwanbir ngbaan yaa nyan aan bi bee ti kan, bi mɔmɔk kpaan ban ni unaaja, ni li ye titunwanbir aachapinn aatork. Bi li joo ni unaaja ngbaan Uwumbɔr Aabool chee unimbiin ni,

ref: where your tribal leaders will lay their hands on its head, before having it killed in my presence.
text: le binib ngbaan aayidam mɔmɔk ga di biŋaal paan uyil pu, le bi kɔr u nima chee.

ref: The priest will take a bowl of the animal's blood inside the sacred tent,
text: Le Utotoorninkpel ga ban unaaja ngbaan aasin ngem buen Libool ni,

ref: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
text: ki di uŋanbik bɔ mu ni, ki di yɔk yɔk likekeln chee nfum mulole.

ref: Then, in my presence, he must smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
text: U ki di nsin ngbaan ngem ŋa tulalee aayon aabimbiln li si Libool ni na aalɔlɔ aamɔju pu, aan ki di nsin mu gur na kpir libimbiln li si Libool aabisamɔb chee aan bi seer kitork aamii li pu na aataab.

ref: After this, the priest will remove the fat from the bull and send it up in smoke on the altar. Finally, he will burn its remains outside the camp, just as he did with the other bull. By this sacrifice the sin of the whole nation will be forgiven. When a Tribal Leader Sins The Lord God said:
text: Le u nin yoor unaaja ngbaan nya lipaal ki ti see u mmii ni, ke waah see ubaa aatunwanbir aapiin aanaaja pu na. Kitork kimina aaboln le ga ŋmaa nyan bi baatunwanbir ponn ni.

ref: Any tribal leader who disobeys me without knowing it is still guilty.
text: Utinjoor le yaa tun titunwanbir ki bii Uwumbɔr aakaal kaa nyi,

ref: As soon as the leader realizes what has happened, he must sacrifice a goat that has nothing wrong with it.
text: le bi tuk u aan u bee ke u tun titunwanbir kan, u li joo ni uŋoja u ŋan na ki nan toor waatork.

ref: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
text: Utotoor ga di uŋanbik bɔ nsin ni, ki di mu yɔk yɔk libimbiln aalɔlɔ aamɔju mɔmɔk pu, ki di nsin mu gur na kpir libimbiln ngbaan aataab.

ref: Then he must send all of the fat up in smoke, just as he does when a sacrifice is offered to ask my blessing. By this sacrifice the leader's sin will be forgiven. When Ordinary People Sin The Lord said:
text: U ga di waakpan ngbaan see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, ke waah see kimɔbaan aatork aawakor aakpan pu na. Utotoor yaa toor kitork kimina aaboln tii utinjoor kan, Uwumbɔr ga di cha pinn u waatunwanbir.

ref: When any of you ordinary people disobey me without meaning to, you are still guilty.
text: Unii u kaa ye utinjoor, bee utotoor na, yaa tun titunwanbir ki bii Uwumbɔr aakaal kaa nyi,

ref: As soon as you realize what you have done, you must sacrifice a female goat that has nothing wrong with it.
text: le bi tuk u aan u bee ke u tun titunwanbir kan, u li joo ni uŋosal u ŋan na ki nan toor waatork.

ref: Lead the goat to the north side of the bronze altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
text: U di uŋaal paan uyil pu, aan ki kɔr u kitork aabimbiln aaŋangan wɔb, nin chee bi kɔr kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aawakor na.

ref: After this, the priest will remove all of the fat, just as he does when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. The priest will then send the fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. This animal is sacrificed so that I will forgive you ordinary people when you sin.
text: U chuu nyan waakpan mɔmɔk, ke waah nyan kimɔbaan aatork aawakor aakpan pu na, ki di mu see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, aan ni li nu mɔ Uwumbɔr chee. Kina le utotoor ga toor uja ngbaan aatunwanbir aatork, le Uwumbɔr ga di cha pinn u waatunwanbir.

ref: If you offer a lamb instead of a goat as a sacrifice for sin, it must be a female that has nothing wrong with it.
text: U yaa joo ni upiih le u nan toor titunwanbir aatork kan, u cha ni li ye upihsal u ŋan na.

ref: Lead the lamb to the altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
text: U di uŋaal paan uyil pu, aan ki kɔr u kitork aabimbiln aaŋangan wɔb, nin chee bi kɔr kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aawakor na.
