ref: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
text: Le utotoor ga di uŋanbik bɔ kiwakork ngbaan aasin ni, ki di mu yɔk yɔk libimbiln aalɔlɔ aamɔju mɔmɔk pu, le ki di nsin mu gur na kpir libimbiln ngbaan aataab.

ref: After this, all of the fat must be removed, just as when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. Then the priest will send it up in smoke to me, together with a food offering, and your sin will be forgiven.
text: U chuu nyan waakpan mɔmɔk ke waah nyan kimɔbaan aatork aapiih aakpan pu na, aan ki di mu see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, ki kpee tijikaar aatork pu, ki tii Uwumbɔr. Kina le utotoor ga toor uja ngbaan aatunwanbir aatork, le Uwumbɔr ga di cha pinn u waatunwanbir.

ref: You are guilty and unfit to worship me, if you accidentally touch the dead body of any kind of unclean animal.
text: Ubaa yaa kaa nyi le ki meeh tiwan ni kaa bi chain na, nibaakan kiwakork ki kpo na, u yaa bee ke waah ŋa pu na aa ŋan kan, u ŋa tijɔŋ aanii, le waabɔr bii.

ref: You are guilty if you find out that you have accidentally touched anything unclean that comes from a human body.
text: Ubaa yaa kaa nyi le ki meeh unibɔn aajɔŋ kan, u yaa nan bee ke waah ŋa pu na aa ŋan kan, waabɔr bii a.

ref: You are guilty the moment you realize that you have made a hasty promise to do something good or bad.
text: Ubaa yaa puu tipuur fam, tipuur ngbaan yaa ye pu na kan, u yaa nan bee ke waah puu pu na aa ŋan kan, waabɔr bii a.

ref: As soon as you discover that you have committed any of these sins, you must confess what you have done.
text: N‑yoonn mu unii bee ke waabɔr bii na kan, ni ŋan ke u kpiir waatunwanbir ngbaan pu.

ref: Then you must bring a female sheep or goat to me as the price for your sin. A priest will sacrifice the animal, and you will be forgiven.
text: Le u ga li joo ni upihsal, bee uŋosal ki nan toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr, waatunwanbir ngbaan pu. Utotoor le ga toor kitork ngbaan, udaan aatunwanbir pu.

ref: Give both birds to the priest, who will offer one as a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness. He will wring its neck without tearing off its head,
text: U li joo ni ŋi utotoor chee, u pue toor titunwanbir aapiin aatork. U mur lisil ki ku li, ki taa daa tukr liyil.

ref: splatter some of its blood on one side of the bronze altar, and drain out the rest at the foot of the altar.
text: U di laasin yɔk yɔk kitork aabimbiln aagbaan. Nsin mu gur na, u cha mu tuu nya ki lir libimbiln aataab. Kitork ngbaan aaboln le nyani titunwanbir.

ref: If you are so poor that you cannot afford doves or pigeons, you may bring one kilogram of your finest flour. This is a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, so don't sprinkle olive oil or sweet-smelling incense on it.
text: U yaa kaa kpa ŋinanjel ŋilee, bee ŋibɔrnanjel ŋilee kan, u ban ni n‑yon kuruwaa ubaa ki nan tii Uwumbɔr waatunwanbir aapiin. U taa di olif aakpan, bee tulalee aayon paan n‑yon ngbaan pu; ba pu? ni ye titunwanbir aapiin la, naa ye tijikaar aapiin.

ref: Give the flour to a priest, who will scoop up a handful and send it up in smoke together with the other offerings. This is a reminder that all of the flour belongs to me.
text: U li joo ni n‑yon ngbaan nan tii utotoor, aan u di uŋaal lee mu gbiin uŋaal, ni li ye limɔkl ke ni mɔmɔk ye Uwumbɔr aapiin la, aan ki di see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, tii Uwumbɔr. Ni ye kitork ki ga nyan titunwanbir na la.

ref: By offering this sacrifice, the priest pays the price for any of these sins you may have committed. The priest gets to keep the rest of the flour, just as he does with grain sacrifices. Sacrifices To Make Things Right (Leviticus
text: Kina le utotoor ga toor kitork tii utunwanbirdaan, le Uwumbɔr ga di cha pinn u waatunwanbir. N‑yon mu gur na ye utotoor na yaan le ke njikaabim aapiin aah ye uyaan pu na. Lipɔln aatork

ref: The Lord told Moses what the people must do to make things right when they find out they have cheated the Lord without meaning to: If this happens, you must either sacrifice a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay the price of a ram with the official money used by the priests.
text: Ni ponn ni ubaa yaa kaa nyi le kaa pan Uwumbɔr tipar ti bi chain na kan, u tun titunwanbir Uwumbɔr chee. Nima pu na, u li joo ni upihja, bee uŋoja u ŋan na, ki nan tii Uwumbɔr lipɔln aatork. Kiwakork ngbaan aadaak li dii Uwumbɔr aakaal aah siin pu na.

ref: The next morning you will dress in your priestly clothes, including your linen underwear. Then clean away the ashes left by the sacrifices and pile them beside the altar.
text: Le utotoor ga peen utotoor aatanyaan aawan, ki chuu nyan nkpan aafatan mu paa kitork aabimbiln paab na, ki di bil li chee.

ref: and told him what sacrifices the priests must offer on the morning and evening of the day they are ordained: It is the same as the regular morning and evening sacrifices—half a kilogram of flour
text: Bundaal ni ban ni kaan Aaronn aajapɔɔn u li ye utotoor na kan, liyaadaal ngbaan, u ban n‑yon kuruwaa ubaa ki nan tii Uwumbɔr ipiin, ke iwiin mɔmɔk aajikaabim aatork aah wiir pu na; u di ligeln tii kichakpiik ni, ki nan di ligeln mu tii kijook wɔb.

ref: In addition, you must either bring to the priest a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay him for one. The priest will then offer it as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven for what you did wrong. Daily Sacrifices (Exodus
text: Le utotoor ga di kiwakork ngbaan toor udaan ngbaan aatunwanbir pu, le Uwumbɔr ga di cha pinn u waatunwanbir. Kitork ki bi ga see ki mmii ni kookoo na aabɔr

ref: This sacrifice is very holy, and only the priests may have any part of it.
text: Bitotoorb aamaal ni aajab mɔmɔk ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ ipiin ngbaan aanann; ti ye chain chain aanann la.

ref: If the meat was cooked in a clay pot, the pot must be destroyed, but if it was cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
text: Ni yaa di tiyakr aakumbuul le ŋaan tinann ngbaan kan, ni gbaa wii li; bee ni yaa di tikur aakumbuul le ŋaan ti kan, ni ŋir ki kɔr li ponn ni mbamɔm aan ki ban nnyun chann li.

ref: The Lord told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons how to offer the daily sacrifices that are sent up in smoke to please the Lord: You must put the animal for the sacrifice on the altar in the evening and let it stay there all night. But make sure the fire keeps burning.
text: ke u di kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aapiin aakaal aabɔr timina tuk Aaronn ni waabijabim. Ni yaa ban ni see kitork mmii ni kan, ni cha ki li paa libimbiln paab aan mmii li gaal kina kitaak ti woln.

ref: Change into your everyday clothes, take the ashes outside the camp, and pile them in the special place.
text: Le u ga kpeln waawanpeenkaan, ki faa nfatan ngbaan ki di nya lipaal, nin chee bi joo nfatan kpir aan ni ye chain na.

ref: The fire must never go out, so put wood on it each morning. After this, you are to lay an animal on the altar next to the fat that you sacrifice to ask my blessing. Then send it all up in smoke to me.
text: Mmii mu bi kitork aabimbiln paab na, ni cha mu li gaal kina cha, ni taa cha mu junn. Kichakpiik mɔmɔk ni kan, utotoor ti ban idɔ kpee mmii ngbaan ni, aan ki di kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na paan libimbiln ngbaan pu, ki di kimɔbaan aapiin aawakork aakpan na see mmii ni.

ref: The altar fire must always be kept burning—it must never go out. Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord The Lord said:
text: Ni cha mmii ngbaan li gaal kina, ki taa cha mu junn. Njikaabim aapiin aabɔr

ref: When someone offers a sacrifice to give thanks to me, the priests from Aaron's family must bring it to the front of the bronze altar,
text: Naah ga li dii pu ki tii njikaabim aapiin na aakaal le na: Aaronn aajapɔtiib le ga li joo njikaabim aapiin aatork tii Uwumbɔr ipiin, kitork aabimbiln taab.

ref: where one of them will scoop up a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense on it. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, he will lay all of this on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: U di uŋaal lee n‑yon, ni nkpan, ni tulalee aayon mu paa mu pu na, ki di see libimbiln paab, mmii ni, ni li ye limɔkl ke u see n‑yon ngbaan mɔmɔk le mmii ni ki tii Uwumbɔr. Ipiin kina aaboln nu mɔ uma Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: The rest of it is to be baked without yeast and eaten by the priests in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent. This bread is very holy, just like the sacrifices for sin or the sacrifices for making things right, and I have given this part to the priests from what is offered to me on the altar.
text: Bitotoorb le ga ji n‑yon mu gur na. Bi di mu ŋa boroboro, ki taa ŋa boroboro aanyɔk u ponn ni, aan bi ŋmɔ u, chain aapepel ni, Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Libool ngbaan aachiln ni. Uwumbɔr le di ni tii bitotoorb ke ni li ye biyaan, tijikaar aapiin ni. Titunwanbir ni lipɔln aatork aah ye chain pu na, kitork ngbaan mu bi kina la.

ref: Only the men in Aaron's family are allowed to eat this bread, and they must go through a ceremony to be made holy before touching it. This law will never change. When Priests Are Ordained
text: N‑yoonn mɔmɔk Aaronn aamaal bi ye bijab na ga ŋmaa ji tijikaar ngbaan, ba pu? Uwumbɔr le yakr waajikaar tii bi. Unii ubaa yaa kaa bi chain kan, u taa mee ti.

ref: The Lord spoke to Moses
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ikaal imina aabɔr:

ref: mixed with olive oil and cooked in a shallow pan. The bread must then be crumbled into small pieces and sent up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
text: Ni ban nkpan ŋmal mu ni, ki di ŋa maab aan ki bur bur u ki di tii Uwumbɔr, ni li ye njikaabim aapiin, le i nu mɔ uma Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: Each of Aaron's descendants who is ordained as a priest must perform this ceremony and make sure that the bread is completely burned on the altar. None of it may be eaten! Sacrifices for Sin (Leviticus
text: Utotoor aah tii ipiin i aan i ye njikaabim aapiin na, ubaa taa ji i, ni see i mɔmɔk mmii ni. Titunwanbir aatork aabɔr

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses

ref: how the priests from Aaron's family were to offer the sacrifice for sin: This sacrifice is very sacred, and the animal must be killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
text: ke u di ikaal imina aabɔr tuk Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib, ki joo cha titunwanbir aatork wɔb. Bi yaa ban bi toor titunwanbir aapiin aatork kan, bi di kiwakork ngbaan paan kitork aabimbiln paab ŋŋangan wɔb, ki kɔr ki nin chee bi kɔr kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aawakor na. Kitork ngbaan ye chain chain aapiin la.

ref: The priest who offers this sacrifice must eat it in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent,
text: Utotoor u ŋa kitork ngbaan na le ga ŋmɔ kiwakork ngbaan aanann, chain aapepel ni, Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Libool ngbaan aachiln ni.

ref: and anyone or anything that touches the meat will be holy. If any of the animal's blood is splattered on the clothes of the priest, they must be washed in a holy place.
text: Unii ubaa, bee tiwan nibaa yaa kaa bi chain kan, u taa meeh kiwakork ngbaan aanann. Kiwakork ngbaan aasin yaa meeh likekeln libaa kan, see ni finn li, chain aapepel ni.

ref: None of the meat may be eaten from the sacrifices for sin that require blood to be brought into the sacred tent. These sacrifices must be completely burned.
text: Tɔ, ni yaa di kiwakork ngbaan aasin buen Libool na ni, ki ti di mu tii ke mu nyan titunwanbir kan, ni taa ŋmɔ kiwakork ngbaan; ni see ki mmii ni.

ref: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke to me.
text: Utotoor di nkpan ngbaan mɔmɔk see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, aan ni li ye tijikaar aatork ki tii Uwumbɔr. Ni ye naah ga gir toor lipɔln pu na aatork la.

ref: Give me one loaf or wafer from each of these four kinds of bread, after which they will belong to the priest who splattered the blood against the bronze altar.
text: U nyan boroboro ngbaan mɔmɔk ubaabaa, ni li ye tootookpaan ki di tii Uwumbɔr. Utotoor u di kitork ngbaan aasin yɔk yɔk kitork aabimbiln pu na le yeh tijikaar aapiin ngbaan.

ref: Don't eat any of the meat that has touched something unclean. Instead, burn it. The rest of the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean and acceptable to me.
text: Tinann ngbaan yaa meeh tiwan ni kpa tijɔŋ na kan, ubaa taa ki ji ti, bi di ti see mmii ni. Unii umɔk bi chain na ŋeer ke u ŋmɔ tinann ti ye chain na.

ref: The sacrifice to make things right is very sacred.
text: Naah ga dii pu ki toor lipɔln aatork na aabɔr sɔ: Kitork ngbaan ye chain aatork la.

ref: The animal must be killed in the same place where the sacrifice to please me is killed, and the animal's blood must be splattered against the four sides of the bronze altar.
text: Ni yaa ban ni kɔr kiwakork ki toor kitork ngbaan kan, ni kɔr ki, kitork aabimbiln aaŋangan wɔb, nin chee bi kɔr kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na. Ni di kaasin yɔk yɔk libimbiln ngbaan aapepel mɔmɔk ŋinaa pu.

ref: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
text: ni ŋipɔɔkpeebil ni nkpan mu bii ŋi pu na, ni lipɔɔl nin chee ŋan na.

ref: This sacrifice for making things right is very holy. Only the priests may eat it, and they must eat it in a holy place.
text: Utotoor aamaal ni aajab mɔmɔk ga ŋmaa ji ti, ni ŋan ke bi ji ti chain aapepel ni la; ba pu? ti ye chain pam.

ref: The ceremony for this sacrifice and the one for sin are the same, and the meat may be eaten only by the priest who performs this ceremony of forgiveness.
text: Titunwanbir aatork, ni lipɔln aapam aatork kpaa nkaal mubaa la: Utotoor u toor kitork ngbaan na le yeh kitork ngbaan aawakor ti bi di toor na aanann.

ref: In fact, the priest who offers a sacrifice to please me may keep the skin of the animal,
text: Utotoor u toor kina aatork na le yeh kiwakork ngbaan aagban.

ref: just as he may eat the bread from a sacrifice to give thanks to me.
text: Njikaabim aapiin i bi di ŋa boroboro na, bee bi di ken ki ŋa maab na, utotoor u di ipiin aatork ngbaan di tii Uwumbɔr na le yeh ni mɔmɔk.

ref: All other grain sacrifices—with or without olive oil in them—are to be divided equally among the priests of Aaron's family. Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing The Lord said:
text: N‑yon mu gur baa di ŋa nibaa na, bi yaa di nkpan ŋmal, bee bi yaa kaa ŋmal kan, Aaronn aamaal bi ye bitotoorb na le yeh mu. Bi yakr mu, mu li ŋak ki tii tɔb. Kimɔbaan aatork aabɔr

ref: Here are the instructions for offering a sacrifice to ask my blessing:
text: Naah ga dii pu ki toor kimɔbaan aatork tii Uwumbɔr na aakaal aabɔr sɔ.

ref: If you offer it to give thanks, you must offer some bread together with it. Use the finest flour to make three kinds of bread without yeast—two in the form of loaves mixed with olive oil and one in the form of thin wafers brushed with oil.
text: Unii yaa ban u toor kitork kina aan ni li ye idoon aapiin ki tii Uwumbɔr kan, u ban tijikaar aapiin imina ki di kpee kitork aawakork pu: Boroboro u baa di boroboro aanyɔk ŋa u ni na, ki di olif aakpan ŋmal waayon ni, bee ni pu maab ki di olif aakpan gbaa u, bee ni di olif aakpan ŋmal n‑yon ni, ki ken maab.

ref: When you offer an animal to ask a blessing from me or to thank me, the meat belongs to you, but it must be eaten the same day.
text: Bundaal bi di kiwakork ngbaan toor kitork na, bi ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan kookoo, ki taa cha ti gur ki woln kitaak.

ref: It is different with the sacrifices you offer when you make me a promise or voluntarily give me something. The meat from those sacrifices may be kept and eaten the next day,
text: Unii yaa nan puu tipuur le ki giin ti, bee u yaa tii ipiin ubaa aageehn pu, le tinann yaa gur ki woln kitaak kan, ni li ŋmɔ man.

ref: but any that is left over must be destroyed. If you eat any of it after the second day, your sacrifice will be useless and unacceptable, and you will be both disgusting and guilty.
text: Ni yaa ŋman ti wintaa daal ngbaan kan, Uwumbɔr aan ki gaa udaan ngbaan aatork. Le kitork ngbaan aan ki ŋmaa nyan udaan ngbaan waatunwanbir ni, ti bii le na, le umɔk ŋman kitork ngbaan aanann na ga kan ntafadaan.

ref: But don't eat any of this meat if you have become unclean by touching something unclean from a human or an animal or from any other creature. If you do, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: Ni ki kpee na, unii umɔk meeh unibɔn aajɔŋ, bee kiwakork ki kaa bi chain na, nee aapuwɔb u yaa ŋman kitork ngbaan aanann kan, waan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa.

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki di ŋikoobil ŋimina tii Moses

ref: to say to the people: Don't eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats.
text: ke u di tuk Israel yaab: Ni taa ŋmɔ unaa, bee upiih, bee uŋoob aakpan.

ref: If one of your animals dies or is killed by some wild animal, you may do anything with its fat except eat it.
text: Kiwakork yaa kpo kibaa pu, bee timoor ni aapeel le yaa chuu ki kan, ni taa ŋmɔ kaakpan. Tɔ, ni yaa ban kan, ni ga ŋmaa di mu ŋa tiwan nibaa.

ref: If you eat the fat of an animal that can be used as a sacrifice to me, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: Bi yaa kɔr kiwakork ki bi ga ŋmaa di ki toor kitork na kan, ubaa taa ŋmɔ kaakpan, u yaa ŋman kan, waan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa.

ref: And no matter where you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal,
text: Israel aanii yaa koo nin chee na kan, u taa ŋmɔ unyoon, bee kiwakork aasin.

ref: or you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
text: Unii umɔk bii nkaal ngbaan na kan, waan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa.

ref: The Lord also told Moses
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki di ikaal imina tii Moses

ref: to say to the people of Israel: If you want to offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, you must bring the part to be burned and lay it on the bronze altar. But you must first lift up the choice ribs with their fat to show that the offering is dedicated to me.
text: U li joo ni tiwan ngbaan uŋaal ponn ni, ni li ye tijikaar aapiin. U li joo ni kiwakork ngbaan aakpan ni libingbaal, ki nan di tii Uwumbɔr ipiinkpaan.

ref: A priest from Aaron's family will then send the fat up in smoke, but the ribs belong to the priests.
text: Utotoor di nkpan ngbaan see mmii ni, libimbiln paab, aan bitotoorb li joo libingbaal libaa.

ref: The upper joint of the right hind leg is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the animal.
text: Le utotoor u di nsin ni nkpan di tii Uwumbɔr aan ni ye kimɔbaan aapiin na le yeh litaajal ngbaan.

ref: I have decided that the people of Israel must always give the choice ribs and the upper joint of the right hind leg to Aaron's descendants
text: Kiwakork ngbaan aabingbaal ni ŋŋangii aataajal ye ipiinkpaan la, le Uwumbɔr gaal i Israel yaab chee ki joo tii bitotoorb. Israel yaab li joo tinann tee tii bitotoorb n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: These are the ceremonies for sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessing or his forgiveness, as well as the ceremonies for those sacrifices that demand a payment and for the sacrifices that are offered when priests are ordained.
text: Kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aapiin, ni njikaabim aatork, ni titunwanbir aatork, ni lipɔln aatork, ni bitotoorb aakaan aatork, ni kimɔbaan aatork aakaal le na.

ref: While Moses and the people of Israel were in the desert at Mount Sinai, the Lord commanded them to start offering these sacrifices.
text: Nteersakpiin ni, Sainai aajool pu, nwiin mundaal Uwumbɔr nan bui Israel yaab ke bi toor kitork tii u na, le u nan di ikaal ngbaan tii Moses ke u di tuk bi.

ref: Moses lifted up the choice ribs of the ram to show that they were dedicated to the Lord. This was the part that the Lord had said Moses could have.
text: Moses nan ki yoor libingbaal, li ye ipiinkpaan na tii Uwumbɔr. Libingbaal aanann ngbaan le nan ye Moses yaan, kitork ngbaan ni. Moses nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aah tuk u pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: The Lord said to Moses:
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke,

ref: Send for Aaron and his sons, as well as their priestly clothes, the oil for ordination, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and a basket of bread made without yeast.
text: “Di Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib buen Libool aabisamɔb chee nnimbiin ni, aan ki li joo ni bitotoorb aawanpeenkaan, ni nkpanmeenkaan, ni titunwanbir aatork aanaaja, ni ipihja ilee, ni boroboro u kaa kpa boroboro aanyɔk na kibɔɔkuuk kibaa,

ref: Then bring the whole community of Israel together at the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: ki yin ni litimbol ngbaan mɔmɔk, bi kuun dan nima chee.”

ref: Moses obeyed the Lord, and when everyone had come together,
text: Moses nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aah tuk u pu na, le litimbol ngbaan mɔmɔk aah kuun ni ti doo na,

ref: he said, “We are here to follow the Lord's instructions.”
text: u bui bi ke, “Maah ban m ŋa tiwan ni na, Uwumbɔr le tuk mi ke m ŋa kina.”

ref: After Moses told Aaron and his sons to step forward, he told them to wash themselves.
text: Moses nan nyan Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib siin, le ki fu bi nnyun.

ref: He put the priestly shirt and robe on Aaron and wrapped the sash around his waist. Then he put the sacred vest on Aaron and fastened it with the finely woven belt.
text: U nan di utotoor aabɔkul, ni kikpalk peen Aaronn, ki di kikekengeŋ buu uchaŋ ni, le ki di libɔkul li kaa kpa iŋaal na mu peen u, ki di laagbapapaln mu buu uchaŋ ni.

ref: Next, he put on Aaron the sacred breastpiece that was used in finding out what the Lord wanted his people to do.
text: U nan di kibiŋ aakekengeŋ gbab u, le ki di tiwan ni bi yin ni ke Urim ni Tumim di ŋa ki ponn ni.

ref: He placed the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban was the narrow strip of thin gold as a sign of his dedication to the Lord.
text: U nan di likekeln jib uyil, le ki di Uwumbɔr aasalmaa aawanyaan ni mɔk ke uma Uwumbɔr le lee u na buu tam likekeln ngbaan aayigbeer pu, Uwumbɔr aah nan tuk u pu na.

ref: Moses then dedicated the sacred tent and everything in it to the Lord by sprinkling them with some of the oil for ordination.
text: Moses nan yoor nkpanmeenkaan, le ki kpir Uwumbɔr Aabool pu, ni tiwan nimɔk bi li ponn ni na. Kina le u nan ŋa, ki di tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: He sprinkled the bronze altar seven times, and he sprinkled its equipment, as well as the large bronze bowl and its base.
text: U nan yoor nkpan ngbaan ngem le ki bar yɔk yɔk kitork aabimbiln, ni laawan mɔmɔk pu, ni lisambil, ni laapɔtaln pu, nfum mulole; u nan ŋa kina ki di ni tii Uwumbɔr la.

ref: He also poured some of the oil on Aaron's head to dedicate him to the Lord.
text: U nan ki di nkpan ngbaan ngem kpir Aaronn aayil pu, ki ŋa u Uwumbɔr aatutunn.

ref: Next, Moses dressed Aaron's sons in their shirts, then tied sashes around them and put special caps on them, just as the Lord had commanded.
text: Ni paa na, Moses nan nyan Aaronn aajapɔtiib siin, le ki di ŋibɔkul peen bi, ki di ŋitan buu bichaŋ ni, ki di tiyikpupur chiŋ biyil, Uwumbɔr aah nan tuk u pu na.

ref: Moses led out the bull that was to be sacrificed for sin, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
text: Moses nan joo ni unaaja u u ga di toor titunwanbir aapiin aatork na, le ki cha Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib di biŋaal paan uyil pu.

ref: After it was killed, Moses dipped a finger in the blood and smeared some of it on each of the four corners of the bronze altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the altar. This purified the altar and made it a fit place for offering the sacrifice for sin.
text: Moses nan kɔr u, le ki teŋ waasin, ki di uŋanbik ŋa nsin ngbaan ni, ki di ŋa kitork aabimbiln na aalɔlɔ aamɔju pu, le ki di li tii Uwumbɔr. U nan di nsin mu gur na kpir libimbiln ngbaan aataab. U nan ŋa kina ki toor li chain, le ki di li tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: Moses then took the fat on the bull's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and sent them up in smoke on the altar fire.
text: Moses nan chuu nyan nkpan mumɔk bii ponn ni aawan pu na, ni lipɔɔl nin chee ŋan na, ni ŋipɔɔkpeebil, ni nkpan mu bii ŋi pu na, ki di mu mɔmɔk see mmii ni, kitork aabimbiln paab, ki tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: Finally, he took the skin and the flesh of the bull, together with the food still in its stomach, and burned them outside the camp, just as the Lord had commanded.
text: U nan di unaaja ngbaan aanann, ki kpee ngban, ni ponn ni aawan, ki di nyan lipaal ki ti see ni mmii, Uwumbɔr aah tuk u pu na.

ref: Moses led out the ram for the sacrifice to please the Lord. After Aaron and his sons had laid their hands on its head,
text: Ni paa na, Moses nan joo ni upihja u u ga di toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, le ki cha Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib di biŋaal paan uyil pu.

ref: Moses killed the ram and splattered its blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: Le Moses kɔr u, ki di waasin mee kpir kitork aabimbiln ngbaan aapepel ŋinaa pu,

ref: Moses had the animal cut up, and he washed its insides and hind legs. Then he laid the head, the fat, and the rest of the ram on the altar and sent them up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. All this was done just as the Lord had commanded.
text: ki geei waanann ŋichek ŋichek, ki finn uponn ni aawan, ni ŋitaajal, nnyun ni, ki see liyil, ni nkpan, ni upihja ngbaan aanann mɔmɔk libimbiln paab mmii ni, ke Uwumbɔr aah nan tuk u pu na. Kitork ngbaan nan ye tijikaar aapiin aatork la, le ki nu mɔ Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: Moses led out the ram for the ceremony of ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head,
text: Moses nan ki joo ni upihja uken na, uma le u nan di toor kitork ki kaan bitotoorb; le ki cha Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib di biŋaal paan uyil pu.

ref: and it was killed. Moses smeared some of its blood on Aaron's right earlobe, some on his right thumb, and some on the big toe of his right foot.
text: Moses nan kɔr u, le ki ban waasin ngbaan ngem ki di ŋa Aaronn aaŋangii aatafalan pu, ni uŋangii aaŋanbijak pu, ni uŋangii aataŋanbijak pu,

ref: Moses did the same thing for Aaron's sons, before splattering the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar.
text: le ki nyan Aaronn aajapɔtiib siin, ki ban nsin ngbaan ngem di ŋa biŋangii aatafalan pu, ni biŋangii aaŋanbijam pu, ni biŋangii aataŋanbijam pu, le ki nan di nsin mu gur na kpir kitork aabimbiln ngbaan aapepel ŋinaa pu.

ref: He took the animal's fat tail, the fat on its insides, and the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right hind leg.
text: U nan yoor nkpan, ni lijuul aakpan, ni nkpan mumɔk bii ponn ni aawan pu na, ni lipɔɔl nin chee ŋan na, ni ŋipɔɔkpeebil ni ŋaakpan, ni ŋŋangii aataajal.

ref: Then he took from a basket some of each of the three kinds of bread that had been made without yeast and had been dedicated to the Lord.
text: U nan ki nyan boroboro kpiln li kaa kpa nnyɔk aan bi di tii Uwumbɔr na kibɔɔkuuk ni, ni boroboro kpiln li bi di olif aakpan ŋa li na libaa, ni maab ubaa, ki di ni paan upihja na aakpan ni litaajal pu,

ref: Moses placed the bread on top of the meat and gave it all to Aaron and his sons, who lifted it up to show that it was dedicated to the Lord.
text: ki di tijikaar ngbaan mɔmɔk ŋa Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib aaŋaal ni, le bi di ti ŋa kitorkpaan tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: After this, Moses placed it on the fires of the altar and sent it up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. This was part of the ordination ceremony.
text: Moses nan ki gaa ti bi chee, ki di paan kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na pu, libimbiln paab, ki see ti mmii, le ni ye baah kaani Uwumbɔr aatotoorb pu na aatork. Kitork ngbaan nan ye tijikaar aatork aapiin la, le ki nu mɔ Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: Finally, Moses sprinkled the priestly clothes of Aaron and his sons with some of the oil for ordination and with some of the blood from the altar. So Aaron and his sons, together with their priestly clothes, were dedicated to the Lord.
text: Moses nan ban Uwumbɔr aakpan, ni nsin mu bi libimbiln pu na ngem, ki di yɔk Aaronn, ni ujapɔtiib, ni baawanpeenkaan pu. U nan ŋa kina ki di bi ni baawanpeenkaan tii Uwumbɔr, bi li ye uyaab la.

ref: Moses said to Aaron and his sons: The Lord told me that you must boil this meat at the entrance to the sacred tent and eat it there with the bread.
text: Moses nan bui Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib ke, “Yoor tinann ngbaan ki di buen Libool ngbaan aabisamɔb chee, Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, ki ŋaan ti nima, ki kpaan ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan ni boroboro u gur kibɔɔkuuk ni na, ke Uwumbɔr aah tuk timi pu na.

ref: and stay near the entrance to the sacred tent until the ordination ceremony ends seven days from now.
text: Ni li bi Libool ngbaan ni, laachiln ni, ki ti saa iwiin ilole, aan ki toor kitork ngbaan aatuln doo.

ref: We have obeyed the Lord in everything that has been done today, so that your sins may be forgiven.
text: Taah toor kitork ki din na, Uwumbɔr le bui ke ti ŋa kina aan ki nyan nimi titunwanbir ni.

ref: The Lord has told me that you must stay near the entrance to the tent for seven days and nights, or else you will die.
text: Ni li bi Libool ngbaan ni, laachiln ni, nwiin pu ni kinyeek, ki ti saa iwiin ilole, aan ki li ŋani Uwumbɔr aah mɔk pu na. Ni yaa yii kan, ni ga kpo. Uwumbɔr aah tuk mi pu na le na.”

ref: Aaron and his sons obeyed everything that the Lord had told Moses they must do.
text: Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib nan ŋa tiwan mɔmɔk, Uwumbɔr aah bui Moses ke u tuk bi pu na.

ref: Eight days later Moses called together Aaron, his sons, and Israel's leaders.
text: Baah kaan bitotoorb doo ki woln kitaak na, le Moses yin ni Aaronn, ni ujapɔtiib, ni Israel yaab aayidam.

ref: Then he said to Aaron: Find a young bull and a ram that have nothing wrong with them. Offer the bull to the Lord as a sacrifice for sin and the ram as a sacrifice to please him.
text: U nan bui Aaronn ke, “Ban ni unaaja ni upihja i ŋan na, ki nan toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr. Aa di unaaja toor titunwanbir aatork, aan ki di upihja toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na,

ref: Tell the people of Israel that they must offer sacrifices as well. They must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to please the Lord. The bull and the ram must be a year old and have nothing wrong with them.
text: ki tuk Israel yaab ke bi li joo ni uŋoja ki nan toor titunwanbir aatork, ki di libiln libaa aanaabo ni libiln libaa aapihbo u kaa kpa iween ibaa na, ki toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na tii Uwumbɔr,

ref: Then the people must offer a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing and also a grain sacrifice mixed with oil. Do this, because the Lord will appear to you today.
text: ki ban unaaja ni upihja ki di toor kimɔbaan aatork aapiin. Bi di olif aakpan ŋmal njikaabim aatork aapiin ni, ki di kpee tiwakor ngbaan mɔmɔk pu, ki di toor tii Uwumbɔr. Bi pɔɔn bibaa ki ŋa kina, ba pu? Uwumbɔr ga di ubaa mɔk bi din.”

ref: After the animals and the grain had been brought to the front of the sacred tent, and the people were standing there in the presence of the Lord,
text: Le bi nan joo ni tiwan nimɔk Moses nan tuk bi ke bi li joo ni na, le binib mɔmɔk nan kuun dan Libool ngbaan aabisamɔb chee, bi nan doon Uwumbɔr.

ref: Moses said: The Lord has ordered you to do this, so that he may appear to you in all of his glory.
text: Le Moses bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr le tuk nimi ke ni ŋa tiwan nee mɔmɔk, aan nima kan, waawiihn mu moor lak lak na ga nyan ni ni chee.”

ref: Aaron, step up to the altar and offer the sacrifice to please the Lord, then offer the sacrifices for the forgiveness of your sins and for the sins of the people, just as the Lord has commanded.
text: Moses nan bui Aaronn ke, “Li cha kitork aabimbiln chee, ki ti toor titunwanbir aatork, ni kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, aan ki nyan aa ni binib ngbaan aatunwanbir. Toor kitork ngbaan tii Uwumbɔr ki nyan binib ngbaan aatunwanbir, ke Uwumbɔr aah mɔk pu na.”

ref: Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the bull that was to be the sacrifice for his sins.
text: Le Aaronn buen kitork aabimbiln chee ki ti kɔr unaaja, u ye uma ubaa aatunwanbir aatork aapiin aawakork na.

ref: His sons brought him the blood. He dipped a finger in it, smeared some on the four corners of the bronze altar, and poured out the rest at its foot.
text: Le ujapɔtiib joo ni kaasin u chee, le u di uŋanbik bɔn mu ni, ki di ngem ŋa libimbiln ngbaan aalɔlɔ aamɔju pu, le ki di mu gur na kpir libimbiln aataab,

ref: But he sent up in smoke the fat, the kidneys, and the lower part of the liver, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
text: le ki see kiwakork ngbaan aakpan, ni ŋipɔɔkpeebil, ni lipɔɔl nin chee ŋan na, mmii ni, libimbiln paab, ke Uwumbɔr aah tuk Moses pu na.

ref: Then Aaron burned the skin and the flesh outside the camp.
text: U nan nyan lipaal le ki ti see tinann, ni ngban, mmii ni.

ref: After Aaron had killed the ram that was sacrificed to please the Lord, Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against all four sides of the altar.
text: U nan ki kɔr kiwakork ki ye uma ubaa aatork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aapiin aawakork. Le ujapɔtiib joo ni kaasin u chee, le u di mu mee kpir libimbiln aapepel mɔmɔk ŋinaa pu.

ref: They brought him each piece of the animal, including the head, and he burned them all on the altar.
text: Bi nan ki di kiwakork ngbaan aayil, ni tinann tiken, ki di tii u, le u see ti mmii ni, libimbiln paab.

ref: He washed the insides and the hind legs and also sent them up in smoke.
text: U nan ki finn ponn ni aawan, ni ŋitaajal, le ki di paan kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na pu, libimbiln paab, ki see mmii.

ref: Next, Aaron sacrificed the goat for the sins of the people, as he had done with the sacrifice for his own sins.
text: Nee aapuwɔb na, u nan di binib ngbaan aatork mu tii Uwumbɔr ipiin. U nan di uŋoob u u ga di toor binib ngbaan aatunwanbir pu na, ki kɔr toor ke waah toor waatunwanbir aatork pu na.

ref: And so, he burned this sacrifice on the altar in the proper way.
text: U nan ki joo ni kiwakork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, le ki di ki mu toor, nkaal aah mɔk pu na.

ref: He also presented the grain sacrifice and burned a handful of the flour on the altar as part of the morning sacrifice.
text: U nan toor njikaabim aatork mu, le ki lee n‑yon paan kitork aabimbiln paab, ki see mu mmii. U nan ŋa nimina mɔmɔk ki di kpee nwiin mɔk aatork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na pu.

ref: Finally, he killed the bull and the ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing on the people. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against the four sides of the altar.
text: U nan kɔr unaaja ni upihja, le ni ye kimɔbaan aatork aapiin, binib ngbaan pu. Le ujapɔtiib joo ni tiwakor ngbaan aasin, le u di mu kpir libimbiln aapepel mɔmɔk ŋinaa pu.

ref: His sons placed all the fat, as well as the kidneys and the lower part of the liver
text: Aaronn nan di unaaja ni upihja aakpan aawan mɔmɔk

ref: Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar and lifted up the ribs and the right hind leg to show that these were dedicated to the Lord. This was done just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
text: le ki di ŋibingbaa ni ŋŋangii aataajal tii Uwumbɔr ipiinkpaan, le ki nin giin ni tii bitotoorb, ke Moses aah nan tuk u pu na.

ref: Aaron held out his hand and gave the people his blessing, before coming down from the bronze altar where he had offered the sacrifices.
text: N‑yoonn mu Aaronn toor kitork mɔmɔk doo na, le u yoor uŋaal paacham ki toŋ binib ngbaan wɔb, ki mee Uwumbɔr, u ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu, le ki nin sunn ni.

ref: He and Moses went into the sacred tent, and when they came out, they gave the people their blessing. Then the Lord appeared to the people in all of his glory.
text: Moses ni Aaronn nan buen Uwumbɔr Aabool ni; baah nyan ni na, le bi mee Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa bi pu, le Uwumbɔr aawiihn mu moor ki deer ŋinimbil na sunn ni bi mɔmɔk pu.

ref: The Lord sent fiery flames that burned up everything on the altar, and when everyone saw this, they shouted and fell to their knees to worship the Lord.
text: Libuul ngbaan ni, le Uwumbɔr cha mmii nyan ni paacham ki nan wun kitork ki bi ban bi di see mmii ni na aapiin, ni nkpan, libimbiln paab. N‑yoonn mu binib ngbaan kan kina na, le bi teen mpɔɔn pu, ki tar lir kitiŋ lichichikr.

ref: Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death.
text: Baah ŋa kina na, libuul ngbaan ni, le Uwumbɔr cha mmii dan le ki nan ku bi, unimbiin ni.

ref: Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said: “I demand respect from my priests, and I will be praised by everyone!” Aaron was speechless.
text: Moses nan bui Aaronn ke, “Kina pu le Uwumbɔr len ki bui ke, ‘Binib bimɔk tun maatuln na, ni ŋan ke bi li pak maah bi chain pu na; le m ga kpiir mɔk maanib maah nyuun sakpen pu na.’” Le ni gar Aaronn; waa ki ŋmaa len tibɔr tibaa.

ref: Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.”
text: Le Moses yin ni Misael ni Elsafann bi nan ye Aaronn aaweeja Usiel aajapɔtiib na, ki nan bui bi ke, “Dan do man ki nan yoor ninaabitiib nya Uwumbɔr Aabool ni, ki di buen lipaal.”

ref: So they dragged the dead men away by their clothes.
text: Moses aah mɔk bi pu na, le bi dan nan chuu baawanpeenkaan ki di bi nyan lipaal.

ref: Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire.
text: Moses nan ki bui Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib bilee bi gur ki bi, aan bi yin bi ke Eleasar ni Itamar na ke, “Ni toor nimi aayikpir, ki taa kar nimi aawanpeenkaan, ki taa cha nisui bii ninaabitiib ngbaan pu. Ni yaa cha nisui bii bi pu kan, ni mu ga kpo; le Uwumbɔr ga gee liŋuul ŋa Israel yaab mɔmɔk pu. Tɔ, nido yaab Israel yaab bi gur na wii baakpuul, Uwumbɔr aah cha mmii ku ninaabitiib na pu.

ref: But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die. Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
text: Nima taa nya Libool ngbaan ni, ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga kpo, ba pu? bi di Uwumbɔr aakpan kpir niyil pu ki di nimi tii uma Uwumbɔr a.” Le bi ŋa Moses aah tuk bi pu na. Bitotoorb aakaal

ref: The Lord said to Aaron:
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Aaronn ke,

ref: When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change.
text: “Aa ni aajapɔtiib yaa nyun ŋisubil aadaan, bee ndaan muken na kan, ni taa koo ni Maabool ponn ni; ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga kpo. Aa ni saamaal li joo nkaal mue kina cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean.
text: Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki li nyi tiwan ni ye min Uwumbɔr aatuln aawan na, ni ni kaa ye maatuln aawan na, ni tiwan ni ye chain na, ni ni kaa ye chain na.

ref: You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
text: Maah di ikaal imɔk tii Moses aan u di mɔk si na, aa di i mɔk Israel aanib mɔmɔk.”

ref: Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar.
text: Moses nan ki bui Aaronn, ni ujapɔtiib Eleasar ni Itamar bi gur na ke, “Ni di njikaabim aatork ti gur ki nyan ni tijikaar aatork ponn ni, aan ni di tii Uwumbɔr na, ki ŋa boroboro u kaa kpa boroboro aanyɔk na, ki ŋmɔ u kitork aabimbiln chee, ba pu? ipiin ngbaan ye i bi chain na la.

ref: The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place.
text: Ni ŋmɔ u chain aapepel ni; tijikaar aapiin ngbaan ye tijikaar ti bi di tii Uwumbɔr aan u mu di tii nimi na la. Uwumbɔr aah tuk mi pu na le na.

ref: But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
text: N‑yoonn mu bi ti ban bi di nkpan see mmii ni ki tii Uwumbɔr aan ni ye tijikaar aatork na, bi li joo ni litaajal ni libingbaal mu. Uwumbɔr aah mɔk pu na, aa ni saamaal le yeh litaajal ni libingbaal aanann, ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”

ref: When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said,
text: Tɔ, Moses nan baa bi uŋoob u bi di toor titunwanbir aatork na aabɔr, le ki bee ke bi di u see mmii ni a. Le waaŋuul fii Aaronn aajapɔtiib Eleasar ni Itamar pu, le u baa bi ke,

ref: “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt.
text: “Ba ŋa naa jin titunwanbir aatork ngbaan aajikaar chain aapepel ni? Kitork ngbaan ye chain aatork la, le Uwumbɔr di tii nimi ke ki nyan Israel yaab mɔmɔk baatunwanbir ni.

ref: Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
text: Naah kaa di kiwakork ngbaan aasin buen Uwumbɔr Aabool ponn ni na, ni ba ga ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan nima, ke maah tuk nimi pu na.”

ref: Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
text: Le Aaronn giin bui Moses ke, “Bi toor titunwanbir aatork, ni kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aapiin din wee, ki tii Uwumbɔr, le tibɔbir tee aaboln dan m pu. M yaa ba ŋman titunwanbir aatork aanann ngbaan kan, ni ba ga li mɔ Uwumbɔr aa?”

ref: Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
text: N‑yoonn mu Moses ŋun kina na, le ni piir usui.

ref: any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud.
text: Tiwan ni aataabuseen yakr, aan ni ŋmɔ timoor ki biir ki ki ŋmɔ na.

ref: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
text: Uwumbɔr nan len Moses ni Aaronn chee tibɔr timina

ref: to say to the community of Israel: You may eat
text: ke bi di tuk Israel yaab, “Tiwakor ni ipeel i ni ga ŋmaa ji i na sɔ:

ref: Eagles, vultures, buzzards, crows, ostriches, hawks, sea gulls, owls, pelicans, storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats are also disgusting, and you are forbidden to eat any of them.
text: “Ni taa ji inyoon imina: Ŋikaagii, ni ifiin, ni kaasaa tiib, ni titakpatoor, ni kaaŋaaŋaa tiib, ni nangba tiib, ni ŋikakaa, ni taataa tiib, ni inyumuil, ni ineepɔɔn, ni inaakpaapiin, ni imɔɔkaa, ni ŋibaa, ni tinanjenn.

ref: Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
text: “Unii umɔk meeh tiwakor ni ipeel nimina aawankpol na aa ki bi chain kina le ki ti saa kijook wɔb: Tiwakor ni ipeel ni kpa ŋitaa ŋinaa ni tinyanyar na, ni tiwakor ni ipeel nimɔk kpa itaabuseen na, see naataabuseen yakr aan ni ŋmɔ timoor ki biir ki ki ŋmɔ na le aa kɔ. Unii umɔk tun tiwakor bee ipeel ni kɔ na aanann na finn waawanpeenkaan; u mu aan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean.
text: “Tiwan ni mu kɔ na le ye ŋinaasɔn, ni ŋisayik, ni ilapol, ni itakpaja.

ref: Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening.
text: Unii umɔk meeh ni, bee naawankpol na, aa ki bi chain kina ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean.
text: Le naawankpol yaa lir libuul ni kan, tiwan nimɔk bi li ponn ni na aa ki bi chain; ni gbaa wii libuul ngbaan.

ref: If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
text: Nnyun mu bi libuul ngbaan ni na yaa kpir ki meeh tijikaar ti ni ga ŋmaa ji ti na kan, taa ki bi chain, le tiwanyukaan ni bi libuul ngbaan ni na mu aa bi chain.

ref: If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed.
text: Tiwan nimɔk pu naawankpol lir ni pu na aa ki bi chain, ni yaa ye tiyakr aafan, bee boroboro aadiik kan, see ni gbaa wii ni.

ref: A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean.
text: Tɔ, ni yaa ye nnyunbun, bee nin chee bi maa ki di nnyun ŋa ni ponn ni na kan, nima aa bii, tiwan niken ma yaa meeh naawankpol ngbaan kan, naa ki bi chain.

ref: If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean.
text: Ni ponn ni nibaa yaa lir njikaabim mu bi ban bi di bu na pu kan, nwanbim ngbaan aa bii.

ref: But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
text: Ni mu yaa di nwanbim ngbaan pɔɔn nnyun ni, le ni lir ni ponn ni kan, nwanbim ngbaan aa ki bi chain.

ref: If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening.
text: “Tiwakor ti ni ga ŋmaa ji ti na yaa kpo aan ni meeh ti kan, naan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
text: Unii umɔk ŋman tinann ngbaan na, see u finn waawanpeenkaan, kaan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. Unii umɔk tun tinann ngbaan na mu finn waawanpeenkaan, kaan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground.
text: I yaa baar, bee i yaa chuun ŋitaa ŋinaa pu, bee i yaa kpa ŋitaa ŋi wiir na kan, ni taa ji i.

ref: If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are.
text: Ni taa ji i aan ki bii nibaa man.

ref: I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures.
text: Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, le ni ŋan ke ni li joo nibaa chain, ba pu? m bi chain la.

ref: I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
text: Min le ye Uwumbɔr u nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni ke m li ye nimi Aawumbɔr na. Ni li bi chain, ba pu? m bi chain la.

ref: I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
text: Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki gann aan ki bee tiwan ni bi chain na, ni ni kaa bi chain na, nima kan, ni ga ŋmaa bee tiwakor ti kɔ na, ni ti kaa kɔ na.”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki len Moses chee

ref: to say to the community of Israel: If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period.
text: ke u bui Israel yaab tibɔr timina: Upii yaa ma ubijabo ki bi ki ti saa iwiin ilole kan, waa bi chain, le ni bi ke waah fuu mpiikpen le na.

ref: Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day,
text: Winiin daal kan, ni gii ubo ngbaan aachakpaln.

ref: Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another
text: Upii yaa ma upiibo ki bi ki ti saa iwiin kipiik ni inaa daal kan, waa bi chain, le ni bi ke waah fuu mpiikpen le na. Nsin aah nyan upii ngbaan ni pu na, see u ki bi ki ti saa iwiin imonko itaa ni iloob kpee, le ki nin ŋa chain.

ref: When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin.
text: Iwiin ngbaan aapuwɔb na, ubo yaa ye ubijabo, bee upiibo kan, upii ngbaan li joo ni libiln libaa aapihbo utotoor chee, Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee, aan ki nan tii Uwumbɔr kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aapiin, ki ki li joo ni libɔrnanjel, bee linanjel, ki nan toor titunwanbir aatork.

ref: After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl.
text: Le utotoor na ga di waapiin ngbaan tii Uwumbɔr, ki toor kitork aan ki nyan u tijɔŋ ni, ki ŋa u chain. Upii yaa ma kan, kina le u ga ŋa.

ref: If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
text: Upii yaa kaa kpa upihbo u toor kan, u li joo ni ŋibɔrnanjel ŋilee, bee ŋinanjel ŋilee, ki di libaa toor kitork ki di see mmii ni, ki di liken mu toor titunwanbir aatork. Utotoor ga toor ki nyan u tijɔŋ ni, aan u ŋa chain.

ref: The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki di ikaal imina di tii Moses ni Aaronn.

ref: If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests.
text: Ni ponn ni ubaa yaa kpa mbuun uwon pu, bee lichakpelar, bee nibaa chee yaa puun ki ga ŋa tiwon aaween i bir na kan, ni li joo ni u utotoor Aaronn, bee waamaal ponn ni ubaa chee.

ref: If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Le utotoor ga lik iween ngbaan, le nima chee aakor yaa piir aan libuul ngbaan nyoo kan, ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la, le utotoor ga len ke waa bi chain.

ref: But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Tɔ, nima chee yaa piir kaa nyoo aan tikor mu aa piir kan, utotoor nyan u ki di u ŋa nibaa chee ki ti saa iwiin ilole.

ref: If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days.
text: Winlole daal kan, utotoor ki ŋaŋ u ki lik, iween ngbaan yaa beenin bi kina, kaa kpee kan, utotoor ki kpee u iwiin ilole.

ref: Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
text: Utotoor ki gir lik u winlole daal ngbaan, u yaa kan ke iween ngbaan bi door, kaa kpee kan, u ga len ke u ye chain, ni ye tilalab la, u finn waawanpeenkaan ki ŋa chain.

ref: Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest.
text: Ni ponn ni ubaa yaa kpa tiwon aaween i bir na kan, ni li joo ni u utotoor chee,

ref: If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white,
text: le u ga lik u. Uwon nibaa chee yaa duun aan nima chee aakor piir ki kpa tinar kan,

ref: But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.”
text: utotoor ki gir lik u. U yaa kan ke iween ngbaan yaa gaa uwon mɔmɔk pu kan, u len ke u bi chain. Uwon mɔmɔk yaa kpar piir kan, u bi chain le na.

ref: However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
text: aan u ki gir lik u. Le ni yaa ye ke mu yann ki piir kan, u ki ŋa chain le na, le utotoor ga len ke u bi chain.

ref: If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest.
text: kina aapuwɔb na, ni yaa ki gir duun ki piin, bee ki man kan, udaan ngbaan ki buen utotoor chee.

ref: If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Le utotoor ga lik u, u yaa kan ke ni ŋa mbuun ki nyoo, le nima chee aakor yaa piir kan, u len ke waa bi chain. Ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na, le ki pue ŋa ke lichakpelar na.

ref: But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Utotoor mu yaa ŋaŋ u aan ki kan ke nima chee aakor aa piir, li mu aa nyoo, kaa man sakpen kan, utotoor nyan u ŋa nibaa chee, u li bi ki ti saa iwiin ilole.

ref: If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.”
text: Ni yaa moo pɔr kpee kan, utotoor len ke waa bi chain le ki kpa tiwon aaween i bir na.

ref: But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
text: Ni yaa kaa moo pɔr kpee le ki yann cha kibuweek kan, utotoor ngbaan len ke u bi chain.

ref: If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white,
text: Tiwantonn le yaa see unii, le mbuun ngbaan yaa piir, bee mu ponn ni man chaun kan,

ref: a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.”
text: utotoor ŋaŋ u. Mbuun ngbaan yaa nyoo, le nima chee aakor yaa piir kan, ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na le koo mu ponn ni, le utotoor ga len ke udaan ngbaan aa bi chain.

ref: But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Mu yaa kaa nyoo, kaa man sakpen, le nima chee aakor aa piir kan, utotoor nyan u ŋa nibaa chee, u li bi ki ti saa iwiin ilole.

ref: On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: Le utotoor ga ki gir lik u winlole daal, mu yaa moo pɔr kpee kan, ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la; utotoor ga len ke udaan ngbaan aa bi chain.

ref: However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
text: Ni yaa kaa pɔr kpee, aan naah man pu na mu yaa kaa kpee kan, naa ye tiwon aaween i bir na. Utotoor ga len ke u bi chain, ba pu? ni ye tiwantonn aah nan see u pu na aabuweek la.

ref: If you have a sore on your head or chin,
text: Ni ponn ni, uja, bee upii yaa kpa mbuun uyil, bee ulangbachuun pu kan,

ref: it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
text: ni cha utotoor lik mu. Mu yaa nyoo aan mu ponn ni aakor yaa bi ke nkonyon na, kaa wiir kan, ni ye tiwon aaween i bir na la, le utotoor bui ke waa bi chain.

ref: On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
text: Tɔ, n‑yoonn mu utotoor lik u, aan mbuun ngbaan aa nyoo, le nima chee aakor aa ŋan na kan, ni nyan udaan, u li bi nibaa chee ki ti saa iwiin ilole.

ref: By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep,
text: Le winlole daal kan, utotoor ki gir lik mbuun ngbaan, le mu yaa kaa ki pɔr kpee, kaa kpa tikor ti bi ke nkonyon na, ki mu aa ki nyoo kan,

ref: you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days.
text: udaan ngbaan kuu tikor ti mann goln mbuun chee na. Le utotoor ga ki gir cha u li bi waah nan koo nin chee na ki ki saa iwiin ilole.

ref: By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
text: Winlole daal kan, utotoor ki gir lik u, mbuun ngbaan yaa kaa pɔr kpee, kaa ki nyoo kan, utotoor len ke u ŋa chain a. Le udaan ga finn waawanpeenkaan aan ki ŋa chain.

ref: Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.”
text: utotoor ki gir lik u. Mu yaa pɔr kan, utotoor taa ki lik ke mu aakor ŋan aan mu aa ŋan; ni ye le ke udaan ngbaan aa bi chain.

ref: If white spots break out on your skin,
text: Uja bee upii yaa kpa uwon nibaa chee ni piin kan,

ref: but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
text: ni cha utotoor lik u. Nima chee yaa kaa piin sakpen kan, ni ye tiwan ni kaa bir na le nyan nima chee, udaan ngbaan bi chain.

ref: If you become bald on any part of your head, you are still clean.
text: Uja aayikpir yaa gui ugbangbataab bee uyigbeer kan, nima aan cha u ŋa tijɔŋdaan.

ref: But if a priest discovers that a reddish-white sore has broken out on the bald spot and looks like leprosy, he will say,
text: Utotoor lik u, aan ki yaa kan ke ni man ki piin ki ye mbuun kan,

ref: If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!”
text: Unii u kpa tiwon aaween i bir na li peeni tikekekpir, ki taa chaa uyikpir, ki di likekeln biin umɔb wɔb, aan ki li tar mpɔɔn pu ke, “Maah bi chain, maah bi chain.”

ref: As long as you have the disease, you are unclean and must live alone outside the camp.
text: Kikɔŋ ngbaan yaa bi u pu ki ti saa buyoonn na kan, waa bi chain, le ni cha u nya linampal biken chee, ki ti li bi ubaa. Lipɔpɔl aabɔr

ref: and if the mildew has spread in that time, he will say, “This is unclean
text: Winlole daal kan, u ki gir lik ni, le lipɔpɔl ngbaan yaa moo kpee kan, tiwan ngbaan aa bi chain.

ref: because the mildew has spread.” Then he will burn the clothing or the piece of leather.
text: Utotoor di ni see mmii ni, ba pu? lipɔpɔl ngbaan ga pɔr, le ni ŋan ke bi di ni see mmii ni.

ref: If the priest discovers that the mildew hasn't spread,
text: Tɔ, u yaa lik tiwan ngbaan, aan lipɔpɔl aa ŋa ni pu kpee kan,

ref: he will tell you to wash the clothing or leather and put it aside for another seven days,
text: utotoor cha bi finn ni, aan u ki di ni bil ki ti saa iwiin ilole.

ref: after which he will examine it again. If the spot hasn't spread, but is still greenish or reddish, the clothing or leather is unclean and must be burned.
text: U yaa ti ki lik ni, aan lipɔpɔl ngbaan yaa kaa kpeln naabimbin, ki mu aa ŋa kpee kan, tiwan ngbaan aa nin bi chain, ni yaa ye ke lipɔpɔl ngbaan piin kinyaan wɔb bee tibir wɔb kan, ni see ni mmii.

ref: Later, if the spot reappears elsewhere on the clothing or the leather, you must burn it.
text: Lipɔpɔl yaa ki gir nyan ni pu kan, ni bi pɔr kpei la, uwandaan see ni mmii ni.

ref: Even if the spot completely disappears after being washed, it must be washed again before it is clean.
text: Tɔ, u yaa finn tiwan ngbaan, aan lipɔpɔl wuur ki nyan doo kan, u ki gir finn ni lelee, le ni ga ki ŋa chain.

ref: The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
text: Uwumbɔr nan di ikaal imina tii Moses

ref: he will order someone to bring out two live birds that are acceptable for sacrifice, together with a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant.
text: utotoor ga cha bi li joo ni ŋinanjel ŋilee ki kpee santina aadɔ, ni ŋŋmin maman, ni nkiisuk pu.

ref: The priest will order someone to kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water.
text: Le utotoor cha bi kɔr linanjel libaa, tiyakr aasambil li nnyunbun aanyunpɔm bi li ponn ni na aapaacham.

ref: Then he will dip the other bird, the cedar, the red yarn, and the hyssop in the blood of the dead bird.
text: U ga di linanjel li gur baa kɔr na, ni santina aadɔ, ni ŋŋmin maman, ni nkiisuk, ki di bɔ baah kɔr linanjel li na aasin ni,

ref: Next, he will sprinkle you seven times with the blood and say, “You are now clean.” Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away.
text: ki di mu yɔk yɔk uweendaan ngbaan pu nfum mulole, ki bui ke u ŋa chain a. Linanjel li gur waa kɔr li na, utotoor di li lii aan li fii buen.

ref: After this you must wash your clothes, shave your entire body, and take a bath before you are completely clean. You may move back into camp, but you must not enter your tent for seven days.
text: Le udaan ngbaan finn waawanpeenkaan, ki kuu waakor mɔmɔk aan ki fu nnyun; le kitork ngbaan ga ŋa u chain. U yaa kun linampal kan, u taa koo waadichal ni, u li bi lipaal ki tii saa iwiin ilole.

ref: Then you must once again shave your head, face, and eyebrows, as well as the hair on the rest of your body. Finally, wash your clothes and take a bath, and you will be completely clean.
text: Winlole daal kan, u ki gir kuu uyikpir, ni ulangbaln, ni tinimbikee, ni tikor timɔk bi uwon pu na; u ki finn waawanpeenkaan mɔmɔk ki fu nnyun le ki nin ŋa chain.

ref: On the eighth day you must bring to the priest two rams and a year-old female lamb that have nothing wrong with them; also bring
text: Winiin daal kan, u li joo ni ipihjabi ilee, ni upihsal, timɔk li ye libiln libaa aawakor ti ŋan na, ni boroboro aayon mu olif aakpan ŋmal mu ponn ni na kuruwaa bitaa, ni olif aakpan likpalbageln.

ref: Then the priest will present you and your offerings to me at the entrance to my sacred tent.
text: Le utotoor ga di uweendaan ngbaan, ni tiwan nimina mɔmɔk buen Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Waabool aabisamɔb chee.

ref: There he will offer one of the rams, together with the oil, as a sacrifice to make things right. He will also lift them up to show that they are dedicated to me.
text: Utotoor nyan upihjabo ubaa ki kpee nkpan pu, ki di toor kitork aan ni li ye lipɔln aapam aatork. U di ni toor, ni li ye ipiinkpaan tii Uwumbɔr aan utotoor li yeh tiwan ngbaan.

ref: This sacrifice is very holy. It belongs to the priest and must be killed in the same place where animals are killed as sacrifices for sins and as sacrifices to please me.
text: U kɔr upiih ngbaan chain aapepel, nin chee bi joo tiwakor toor titunwanbir aatork na, ni kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na wɔb. U ŋa kina, ba pu? lipɔln aatork ye utotoor yaan ki bi chain, ke titunwanbir aatork na.

ref: The priest will smear some of the blood from this sacrifice on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot.
text: Utotoor ban upihbo ngbaan aasin ki di ŋa uweendaan ngbaan aaŋangii aatafalan ni, ni uŋangii aaŋanbijak pu, ni utaagiil aataŋanbijak pu.

ref: He will then pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand,
text: Utotoor ban olif aakpan ngem ŋa uŋangan aaŋaapɔtan ni,

ref: dip a finger of his right hand into the oil, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent.
text: ki di uŋangii aaŋanbik bɔ mu ni, ki di yɔk yɔk Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, nima chee, nfum mulole.

ref: Next, the priest will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot,
text: U ga ki ban nkpan ngem mu bi uŋaapɔtan ni na, ni upihbo ngbaan aasin, ki di ŋa baah bi toor unii u bi ŋa u chain na aaŋangii aatafalan ni, ni uŋangii aaŋanbijak pu, ni utaagiil aataŋanbijak pu.

ref: and he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head. Then he will offer the other two animals—one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice. After this you will be completely clean.
text: ki di tijikaar aatork kpee, ki ŋa ni kitork aabimbiln pu. Kina le utotoor ga toor ki ŋa u chain, le udaan ngbaan ga ŋa chain.

ref: Depending on what you can afford, you must also offer either two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me.
text: U ki li joo ni ŋinanjel ŋilee, bee ŋibɔrnanjel ŋilee. U di libaa toor titunwanbir aatork, ki di liken toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na aatork.

ref: The priest will offer these to me in front of the sacred tent on the eighth day.
text: Winiin daal aan bi ga toor ki ŋa u chain na, u li joo ni tiwan ngbaan utotoor chee, Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee.

ref: The priest will pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand,
text: Le utotoor ga bar nkpan ngem ki di ŋa uŋangan aaŋaapɔtan ni,

ref: then dip a finger of his right hand in the oil and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent.
text: aan ki di uŋangii aaŋanbik bɔ mu ni, ki di yɔk yɔk Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, nima chee, nfum mulole.

ref: He will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, just as he did with the blood of the sacrifice to make things right.
text: U ki di nkpan mu ŋa unii ngbaan nin chee u ba di nsin ŋa na, unii ngbaan aaŋangii aatafalan pu, ni uŋangii aaŋanbijak pu, ni utaagiil aataŋanbijak pu.

One of the birds is the sacrifice for sin, and the other is the sacrifice to please me. After this you will be completely clean.
text: toor titunwanbir aatork, ki di liken toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, ki kpee njikaabim aapiin aatork pu. Kina le utotoor ga ŋa ki toor kitork ki ŋa udaan ngbaan chain.

ref: These are the things you must do if you have leprosy and cannot afford the usual sacrifices to make you clean. When There Is Mildew in a House
text: Nkaal mu uweendaan u ye ugiin aan iween ngbaan doo u pu, u ban ke u toor ki ŋa ubaa chain na, le na. Lidichal ni aapɔpɔl aabɔr

ref: The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki len Moses ni Aaronn chee tibɔr timina:

ref: After I have given you the land of Canaan as your permanent possession, here is what you must do, if I ever put mildew on the walls of any of your homes.
text: Ni yaa ti koo Kanaann aatiŋ ki m ban m di tii nimi ki li ye nimi yaan na kan, lipɔpɔl yaa ŋa unii aadichal ni kan,

ref: First, you must say to a priest, “I think there is mildew on the wall of my house.”
text: u buen utotoor chee ki ti bui u lipɔpɔl ngbaan aabɔr.

ref: If the priest discovers greenish or reddish spots that go deeper than the surface of the walls,
text: ki ti lik lipɔpɔl ngbaan. U yaa kan ke lipɔpɔl ngbaan ŋa tiwan ni wuun ki bi ke liŋaankal, bee nimamann na, ki baa ligoln pu kan,

ref: he will have the house closed for seven days.
text: u nyan lidichal ngbaan ni, ki laŋ li, ki ti saa iwiin ilole.

ref: Then he will return and check to see if the mildew has spread.
text: Winlole daal kan, u ki gir ti lik. U yaa kan ke lipɔpɔl ngbaan kpee kan,

ref: If so, he will order someone to scrape the plaster from the walls, remove the stones covered with mildew, then haul everything off and dump it in an unclean place outside the town.
text: Nee aapuwɔb, u cha bi pɔkr nyan titan mɔmɔk, ponn ni aagon pu, ki di titan ngbaan nya kitiŋ ni, ki di ti mee nin chee aa bi chain na.

ref: Afterwards the wall must be repaired with new stones and fresh plaster.
text: Le bi ki ban ŋifakuu yayan ki di saŋ ŋimana aabuul ni, ki pɔ ponn ni, ni mɔmɔk.

ref: the priest will come and say, “This house is unclean. It's covered with mildew that can't be removed.”
text: utotoor ki gir koo li ponn ni ki ti lik; lipɔpɔl yaa ki nyan kan, lidichal ngbaan aa ki bi chain.

ref: Then he will have the house torn down and every bit of wood, stone, and plaster hauled off to an unclean place outside the town.
text: U cha bi gbaa wii lidichal ngbaan, ki faa laafakuu, ni idɔ, ni titan timɔk bi di pɔn na, ki nyan ni mɔmɔk kitiŋ aagbaan, ki di buen ti mee nin chee aa bi chain na.

ref: Meanwhile, if any of you entered the house while it was closed, you will be unclean until evening.
text: N‑yoonn mu bi laŋ lidichal ngbaan aan unii koo li ponn ni na, waa ki bi chain le ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: And if you either slept or ate in the house, you must wash your clothes.
text: Unii umɔk doon, bee u jin tijikaar lidichal ngbaan ni na, u finn waawanpeenkaan mɔmɔk.

ref: On the other hand, if the priest discovers that mildew hasn't reappeared after the house was newly plastered, he will say, “This house is clean—the mildew has gone.”
text: N‑yoonn mu bi pɔkr ponn ni aagoln ngbaan ki gir pɔn na, nee aapuwɔb, utotoor yaa koo u ti lik, ki kan ke lipɔpɔl aa ki gir nyan kan, u len ke lidichal ngbaan ŋa chain a, ba pu? lipɔpɔl ngbaan aa ki bi, baah pɔkr titan na, bi nyan lipɔpɔl doo a.

ref: Then, to show that the house is now clean, he will get two birds, a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant and bring them to the house.
text: U yaa ban u toor ki ŋa lidichal ngbaan chain kan, u ban ŋinanjel ŋilee, ni santina aadɔ, ni ŋŋmiman, ni nkiisuk.

ref: He will kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water
text: U ga kɔr linanjel ngbaan libaa, tiyakr aasambil li bi di nnyunbun aanyupɔm ŋa li ponn ni na aapaacham,

ref: and let its blood drain into the pot. Then he will dip the cedar, the hyssop, the yarn, and the other bird into the mixture of blood and water. Next, he will sprinkle the house seven times with the mixture, then the house will be completely clean.
text: Kina le u ga di linanjel ngbaan aasin, ni nnyunpɔm, ni linanjel li fu na, ni santina aadɔ, ni nkiisuk na, ni ŋŋmiman na, ŋa lidichal ngbaan chain.

ref: Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away, ending the ceremony for purifying the house.
text: Le u cha linanjel li fu na fii nya kitiŋ ni ki buen timoor ni. U ga ŋa kina le ki toor lidichal ngbaan chain, le li ŋa chain.

ref: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki di ikaal imina tii Moses ni Aaronn

text: ke bi di mɔk Israel yaab. N‑yoonn mu uja aachakpaln ni ti nyan tinar na kan, tinar ngbaan pu na, waa ki bi chain.

text: U yaa doon tiwandookaan ni pu na, bee u kal ni pu kan, tiwandookaan ngbaan aa ki bi chain.

ref: and if you touch either these or him, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
text: Sin umɔk meeh uja u tinar nya u ni na kan, finn saawanpeenkaan mɔmɔk, ki fu nnyun, le saan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: If you are spit on by the man, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
text: Uja u tinar nya u ni na yaa tii timɔɔtan lɔb sin u bi chain na kan, finn saawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun, le saan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: Any saddle or seat on which the man sits is unclean. And if you touch or carry either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
text: Le unii umɔk meeh waah kal tiwan ni pu na kan, udaan aa ki bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb. Unii yaa tun waah kal tiwan ni pu na kan, u finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun mu, kaan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: If the man touches you without first washing his hands, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
text: Uja ngbaan yaa kaa ŋir uŋaal ki meeh unii u na kan, udaan ngbaan finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun, le waan li bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: Any clay pot that he touches must be destroyed, and any wooden bowl that he touches must be washed.
text: Tiyakr aabuul limɔk uja ngbaan meeh na, ni gbaa wii li; le ni yaa ye idɔ aasambil kan, ni ŋir ŋi mɔmɔk.

ref: Seven days after the man gets well, he will be considered clean, if he washes his clothes and takes a bath in spring water.
text: Nee aapuwɔb na, waaween ngbaan yaa doo kan, u li bi ki ti saa iwiin ilole daal, aan ki nin finn waawanpeenkaan, ki fu nnyunbun aanyunpɔm, le u ga ŋa chain.

ref: On the eighth day he must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest.
text: Winiin daal kan, u ban ŋinanjel ŋilee, bee ŋibɔrnanjel ŋilee, ki di buen Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee, ki ti di tii utotoor.

text: N‑yoonn mu upii kan mpiikpen na, waa ki bi chain ki ti saa iwiin ilole. Unii umɔk meeh u na kan, waa ki bi chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.
