ref: so that when the woman drinks this water, the curses will enter her body.
text: Waahr aan upii ngbaan nin nyu nnyun mu ga cha uponn ni li wu na,

ref: He will take the barley offering from her and lift it up in dedication to me, the Lord. Then he will place it on my altar
text: utotoor ngbaan ga chuu gaa n‑yon mu upii ngbaan joo uŋaal ni na, ki li joo mu uŋaal ni, ki di mu tii min Uwumbɔr, kitork aabimbiln paab.

ref: If the woman has been unfaithful, the water will immediately make her unable to have children, and she will be a curse among her people.
text: U yaa tun kidagook aatuln kan, nnyun ngbaan ga cha uponn ni li wu pam, le upuul ga duun, unimbiin ni mu ga bii, waan ki ŋmaa maa ubo. Le binib ga li gur joo waayimbil puuni lir biken pu.

ref: But if she is innocent, her body will not be harmed, and she will still be able to have children.
text: U yaa kaa nyi tibɔr ngbaan kan, nibaa aan ŋa u, le u ga ŋmaa maa mbim.

ref: This is the ceremony that must take place at my altar when a husband suspects that his wife has been unfaithful. The priest must tell the woman to stand in my presence and carefully follow these instructions.
text: “Uja yaa kpa lipiipoln upuu pu, ki dak ke upuu tun kidagook aatuln kan, nkaal mumina le ni ga dii. Utotoor ga cha upii ngbaan dan nan sil min Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, kitork aabimbiln chee, le u dii nkaal ngbaan aah mɔk pu na.

ref: If the husband is wrong, he will not be punished; but if his wife is guilty, she will be punished.
text: Ni yaa ye mbamɔn ke upii ngbaan tun kidagook aatuln kan, uchal aa kpa taani kpala; upii ma yaa galn kan, see u jin falaa ngbaan.”

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses

ref: to say to the people of Israel: If any of you want to dedicate yourself to me by vowing to become a Nazirite,
text: ke u di tibɔr timina tuk Israel yaab. Uja ni upii umɔk puu ke u ga di ubaa tii Uwumbɔr na kan,

ref: you must no longer drink any wine or beer or use any kind of vinegar. Don't drink grape juice or eat grapes or raisins—
text: u taa nyu ŋisubil aadaan, ki mu taa nyu ndaan mubaa. U taa nyu ŋisubil aadaan ki taa ŋmɔ ŋisubil ngbaan, ŋi soon, bee ŋi kuur na.

ref: The hair of a Nazirite is sacred to me, and as long as you are a Nazirite, you must never cut your hair.
text: Buyoonn u ti puu kina aapuur na, u taa kuu uyikpir. Waah puu tipuur ki di ubaa tii Uwumbɔr na, u cha uyikpir ni ulangbaln aakor li bi, u taa kuu ti.

ref: If someone suddenly dies near you, your hair is no longer sacred, and you must shave it seven days later during the ceremony to make you clean.
text: Unii le yaa kpaan kpo kina aanii u di ubaa tii Uwumbɔr na aanimbiin ni, ki cha u kpaln tijɔŋdaan, aan uyikpir bii kan, u li kii ki ti saa iwiin ilole daal aan ki nin kuu uyikpir ni ulangbaln, n‑yoonn ngbaan na, u ki kpaln chain aanii le na.

ref: Then on the next day, bring two doves or two pigeons to the priest at the sacred tent.
text: Winiin daal kan, u li joo ni ŋibɔrnanjel ŋilee, bee ŋinanjel ŋilee utotoor chee, Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Waabool aabisamɔb chee.

ref: He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. You will then be forgiven for being too near a dead body, and your hair will again become sacred.
text: Utotoor ga di libaa toor titunwanbir aatork, ki di liken na toor ki see li mmii ni, ki ŋaŋ u waah meeh linikpol pu na. Liyaadaal ngbaan unii ngbaan ga ki di waayikpir ti ga ki pa na giin tii Uwumbɔr,

ref: But the dead body made you unacceptable, so you must make another vow to become a Nazirite and be dedicated once more. Finally, a year-old ram must be offered as the sacrifice to make things right.
text: ki ki nyan ubaa tii Uwumbɔr. Waah nan nyan ubaa njan pu aan ki meeh linikpol ki bii ubaa na, nima aa ki ye nibaa, ba pu? waayikpir ti u nan di tii Uwumbɔr na nan kpaln tijɔŋ. U ki li joo ni libiln libaa aapihbo ki nan toor lipɔln aatork.

ref: and offer three animals that have nothing wrong with them: a year-old ram as a sacrifice to please me, a year-old female lamb as a sacrifice for sin, and a full-grown ram as a sacrifice to ask my blessing.
text: ki di ti tii Uwumbɔr: ni li ye libiln libaa aapihjabo aan bi di toor kitork ki see ki mmii ni, ni libiln libaa aapihsabo bi di toor titunwanbir aatork, ni upihja bi di toor kimɔbaan aatork;

ref: Wine offerings and grain sacrifices must also be brought with these animals. Finally, you are to bring a basket of bread made with your finest flour and olive oil, but without yeast. Also bring some thin wafers brushed with oil.
text: ki kpee na, u ga ban ni boroboro u gbei ki ŋmar olif aakpan, kaa kpa boroboro aanyɔk na kibɔɔkuuk kibaa, ni maab u bi di olif aakpan ŋmir u na; ki kpee njikaabim ni ŋisubil aadaan pu.

ref: The priest will take these gifts to my altar and offer them, so that I will be pleased and will forgive you.
text: Utotoor le ga di tiwan nimina mɔmɔk tii Uwumbɔr, ki toor titunwanbir aatork, ni kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na.

ref: After that, you will stand at the entrance to the sacred tent, shave your head, and put the hair in the fire where the priest has offered the sacrifice to ask my blessing.
text: Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Waabool aabisamɔb chee, kina aanii ngbaan ga kuu uyikpir ki di ti ŋa kimɔbaan aatork aamii na ponn ni.

ref: Once the meat from the ram's shoulder has been boiled, the priest will take it, along with one loaf of bread and one wafer brushed with oil, and give them to you.
text: Bi yaa ŋaan upihja ngbaan aabook aanann kan, utotoor nyan ti, ki nyan boroboro kpiln li gbei na libaa, ni maab ubaa kibɔɔkuuk na ni, ki di ŋa kina aanii ngbaan aaŋaal ni.

ref: You will hand them back to the priest, who will lift them up in dedication to me. Then he can eat the meat from the ram's shoulder, its choice ribs, and its hind leg, because this is his share of the sacrifice. After this, you will no longer be a Nazirite, and you will be free to drink wine.
text: Ni paa na, utotoor di tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk tii Uwumbɔr, ni li ye ipiinkpaan yaan; ni ye chain aapiin ki ye utotoor yaan, ki kpee upihja ngbaan aabingbaal ni litaajal pu. Ni ye nkaal le ke ni li ye utotoor yaan. Nee aapuwɔb na, kina aanii ngbaan ga ŋmaa nyu ŋisubil aadaan.

ref: The Lord told Moses,
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses

ref: “When Aaron and his sons bless the people of Israel, they must say:
text: ke u tuk Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib ke bi li joo ŋimɔbon ŋimina mee tinyoor ŋani Israel aanib pu:

ref: I pray that the Lord will bless and protect you,
text: Uwumbɔr ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu ki li lik nimi;

ref: and that he will show you mercy and kindness.
text: Uwumbɔr li kpa ni pu tibulchinn ni tiŋann, ki li gee nimi;

ref: May the Lord be good to you and give you peace.”
text: Uwumbɔr lik faar nimi, ki tii nimi nsuudoon.

ref: Then the Lord said, “If Aaron and his sons ask me to bless the Israelites, I will give them my blessing.”
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “Bi yaa di maayimbil mee tinyoor biin Israel yaab pu kina kan, m ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu.”

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Rubenn Sedeur aajapɔɔn Elisur

ref: Whenever Moses needed to talk with the Lord, he went into the sacred tent, where he heard the Lord's voice coming from between the two winged creatures above the lid of the sacred chest.
text: N‑yoonn mu Moses buen Uwumbɔr Aabool ni u ti len Uwumbɔr chee tibɔr na, le u ŋun Uwumbɔr len u chee tibɔr, tiwan ni bi Nkaal Aadakaa pu aapaacham ki kpa ifeen na aakaasisik ni.

ref: The Lord said to Moses,
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke,

ref: “Tell Aaron to put the seven lamps on the lampstand so they shine toward the front.”
text: “Bui Aaronn ke u yaa ban u di karyaa tiib bilole na tɔŋ baawan pu kan, u di bi siin nin chee bi ga li wiin nimbiin ni na.”

ref: The lampstand was made of hammered gold from its base to the decorative flowers on top, exactly like the pattern the Lord had described to Moses. Instructions for Ordaining the Levites
text: Bi nan di ligagaar le gbaa salmaa le ki ŋa karyaa aawan ngbaan mɔmɔk, ki dii Uwumbɔr aah nan mɔk Moses ke bi ŋa pu na. Baah toor ki ŋa Liifai yaab chain ki di bi tii Uwumbɔr pu na

ref: The Lord said to Moses:
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke,

ref: They are to bring a bull and its proper grain sacrifice of flour mixed with olive oil. And they must bring a second bull as a sacrifice for sin.
text: Bi ban unaajabo, ni n‑yon mu bi di olif aakpan buun mu na, ni li ye njikaabim aatork aapiin; le aa ga ban unaaja uken u li ye titunwanbir aatork aapiin.

ref: Then you, Moses, will call together all the people of Israel and send the Levites to my sacred tent,
text: Kuun ni Israel yaab mɔmɔk ki cha Liifai yaab sil Maabool aabisamɔb chee.

ref: where the people will place their hands on them.
text: Cha Israel aanib ngbaan di biŋaal paan Liifai yaab aayil pu,

ref: Aaron will present the Levites to me as a gift from the people, so that the Levites will do my work.
text: le Aaronn ga di Liifai yaab ngbaan tii mi, bi li ye Israel yaab aapiinkpaan tii mi, bi li tun maatuln.

ref: After this, the Levites are to place their hands on the heads of the bulls. Sacrifice one of the bulls for the forgiveness of sin, and the other to make sure that I am pleased. Then the Levites will be acceptable to me.
text: Le Liifai yaab mu ga di biŋaal paan inaaja ilee na aayil pu; ni ga di ubaa toor titunwanbir aatork aapiin, ki di uken toor kitork ki ni ga di see mmii ni na aapiin, aan ni li ye kitork ki ga ŋa Liifai yaab ngbaan chain na.

ref: They will stand at my altar in front of Aaron and his sons, who will dedicate the Levites to me.
text: “Di Liifai yaab ngbaan tii mi, bi li ye ipiinkpaan m chee, aan Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib li joo bi.

ref: This ceremony will show that the Levites are different from the other Israelites and belong to me in a special way.
text: Ŋa kina aan ki yakr Liifai yaab, Israel yaab biken chee, nima kan, bi ga li ye min yaab.

ref: After they have been made acceptable and have been dedicated, they will be allowed to work at my sacred tent.
text: Aa yaa toor ki ŋa Liifai yaab chain ki di bi tii mi kan, bi ga ŋmaa tun Maabool ni aatuln.

ref: They are mine and will take the place of the first-born Israelite sons.
text: M nyan bi ke bi li si Israel yaab aajan aabijabim aasisiiyaan la, aan bi li ye min baanja yaab.

ref: When I killed the oldest sons of the Egyptians, I decided that the first-born sons in each Israelite family would be mine, as well as every first-born male from their flocks and herds.
text: N‑yoonn mu m nan ku njan aabim mɔmɔk Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, m nan nyan Israel yaab aajan aabijabim, ni baawakor aajan aabim, ni li ye maawan la.

ref: But now I have chosen these Levites as substitutes for the first-born sons,
text: Dandana wee, maah ba ga gaa nimi aajan aabijabim pu na, le m nyan Liifai yaab ke bi li ye maanib.

ref: and I have given them as gifts to Aaron and his sons to serve at the sacred tent. I will hold them responsible for what happens to anyone who gets too close to the sacred tent. The Levites Are Dedicated to the Lord
text: M di Liifai yaab tii Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib, bi li ye Israel yaab aapiin tii bi, aan bi li tun Maabool ni lituln tii Israel yaab, bi li kiir Israel yaab tibɔbir ti bi yaa duun Chain Aapepel kan, bi ga kan ti na chee.”

ref: Moses, Aaron, and the other Israelites made sure that the Levites did everything the Lord had commanded.
text: Nima pu na, Moses ni Aaronn, ni Israel yaab mɔmɔk nan di Liifai yaab tii Uwumbɔr, waah nan bui Moses ke u ŋa pu na.

ref: The Levites sprinkled themselves with the water of forgiveness and washed their clothes. Then Aaron brought them to the altar and offered sacrifices to forgive their sins and make them acceptable to the Lord.
text: Liifai yaab nan toor bibaa, ki finn baawanpeenkaan, le Aaronn di bi tii Uwumbɔr, bi li ye ipiinkpaan u chee. U nan ki toor titunwanbir aatork ke bi ŋa chain mbamɔm.

ref: After this, the Levites worked at the sacred tent as assistants to Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had commanded.
text: Binib ngbaan nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aah nan bui Moses ke u ŋa Liifai yaab pu na. Nima pu na, Liifai yaab nan ŋeer ke bi ŋmaa tun, Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib aah tuk bi ke bi ŋa pu na.

ref: The Lord also told Moses,
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ke,

ref: They may help the other Levites in their duties, but they must no longer be responsible for any work themselves. Remember this when you assign their duties.”
text: Nee aapuwɔb na, u ga ŋmaa ter biken baatuln ni, Maabool ni; biken yaa kaa bi kan, waan ki ŋmaa tun lituln ngbaan ubaa baanja. Kina le aa ga mɔk Liifai yaab baatuln mɔmɔk.”

ref: During the first month of Israel's second year in the Sinai Desert, the Lord had told Moses
text: Israel yaab aah nan nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki bi Sainai Aateersakpiin ni, lelee aabiln aajan aaŋmal ni na, le Uwumbɔr nan len Moses chee tibɔr,

ref: in the evening of the fourteenth day of this month and do it by following all the regulations.”
text: ki bui ke, “Uŋmal umina aawiin kipiik ni inaa daal kan, cha Israel aanib piin Lakr‑jer aajim, nwiin aah nan ti lir na, ki ŋa mu, mu aakaal aah mɔk pu na mɔmɔk.”

ref: Moses told the people what the Lord had said, and they celebrated Passover there in the desert in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
text: Njan aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni inaa daal aajook, le bi nan ŋa kina Sainai Aateersakpiin ni. Binib ngbaan nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aah mɔk Moses ke bi ŋa pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: Some people in Israel's camp had touched a dead body and had become unfit to worship the Lord, and they could not celebrate Passover. But they asked Moses and Aaron,
text: Tɔ, binib bibaa nan bi bi ponn ni, ki meeh linikpol ki bii bibaa, kina na, baa nan ŋmaa kpaan biken chee ki ŋa njim ngbaan liyaadaal. Le bi buen Moses ni Aaronn chee le ki ti bui bi ke,

ref: “Even though we have touched a dead body, why can't we celebrate Passover and offer sacrifices to the Lord at the same time as everyone else?”
text: “Ti meeh linikpol le ki bii tibaa, ba ŋa tima aan ŋmaa kpaan Israel yaab biken chee ki toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr?”

ref: Moses said, “Wait here while I go into the sacred tent and find out what the Lord says about this.”
text: Moses nan bui bi ke, “Kiir mi man, aan m mee Uwumbɔr, u mɔk mi maah ga ŋa pu na.”

ref: The Lord then told Moses
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke,

ref: to say to the community of Israel: If any of you or your descendants touch a dead body and become unfit to worship me, or if you are away on a long journey, you may still celebrate Passover.
text: “Tuk Israel aanib ngbaan ke n‑yoonn mu ni ponn ni ubaa, bee niyaabitiib, yaa ti meeh linikpol ki bii ubaa, bee u buen lisachuln kaa bi, ki ban ke u ŋa Lakr‑jer aajim na kan,

ref: But it must be done in the second month, in the evening of the fourteenth day. Eat the Passover lamb with thin bread and bitter herbs,
text: lelee aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni inaa daal kijook wɔb, udaan ngbaan mu ga ŋmaa ji njim ngbaan. Bi di boroboro u kaa kpa nnyɔk na, ni tifar ti cho na kpaan ji njim ngbaan.

ref: and don't leave any of it until morning or break any of the animal's bones. Be sure to follow these regulations.
text: Bi taa ji gur tijikaar ngbaan tibaa ti woln kitaak, ki mu taa wii tiwakor ti bi di jin njim ngbaan na aakpabl libaa. Bi ji Lakr‑jer aajim ngbaan, mu aakaal aah mɔk pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: But if any of you are fit to worship me, and yet refuse to celebrate Passover when you are not away on a journey, you will no longer belong to my people. You will be punished because you did not offer sacrifices to me at the proper time.
text: Tɔ, unii umɔk bi linampal, kaa buen nsan, ki mu bi chain, ki yii kaa jin Lakr‑jer aajim ngbaan na kan, u li nyi ke waa ki ye maanii, ba pu? buyoonn ni ŋeer ke u tii mi ipiin na, waa ŋa kina, le u ga ji falaa kina pu.

ref: Anyone, including foreigners who live among you, can celebrate Passover, if they follow all the regulations. The Cloud over the Sacred Tent (Exodus
text: “Uwɔwɔnja u koo ni chee na mu yaa ban u ji Lakr‑jer aajim ngbaan kan, see u dii mu aakaal aah mɔk pu na mɔmɔk. Utinbo ni uwɔwɔnja mɔmɔk ga dii nkaalbaan la.” Ntaalangbam mu naahn mmii na aabɔr (Nnyam

ref: As soon as the sacred tent was set up, a thick cloud appeared and covered it. The cloud was there each day, and during the night, a fire could be seen in it.
text: Nwiin mundaal bi gaa Uwumbɔr Aabool doo na, le ntaalangbam dan nan biin li pu. Kinyeek kan, mu nan bi ke mmii na la.

ref: whether it was only one night, a few days, a month, or even a year. As long as the cloud remained over the tent, the Israelites stayed where they were. But when the cloud moved, so did the Israelites.
text: Ntaalangbam ngbaan yaa nan sil Uwumbɔr Aabool pu libuul libaa ni, iwiin ilee, bee uŋmal, bee libiln, bee ki yunn ti saa pu na kan, baa nan fii nima; tɔ, mu yaa ti siir kan, le bi mu fii dii mu.

ref: They obeyed the Lord's commands and went wherever he directed Moses.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa nan bui Moses ke u ni binib ngbaan fii, bee bi kal buyoonn na kan, see bi kii tii u.

ref: The Lord told Moses:
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke,

ref: Have someone make two trumpets out of hammered silver. These will be used to call the people together and to give the signal for moving your camp.
text: “Di baah di ligagaar gbaa tikunabr ti na ŋa kakaan tiib bilee, ki li joo pii yin maanib bi kuuni, ki fiini bi baah ka nin chee na mu.

ref: If both trumpets are blown, everyone is to meet with you at the entrance to the sacred tent.
text: N‑yoonn mu bi ti ŋun kakaan bilee ngbaan wii ni yunn na kan, binib ngbaan mɔmɔk kuun ni aa chee, Maabool aabisamɔb chee.

ref: But if just one is blown, only the twelve tribal leaders need to come together.
text: Bi yaa ŋun kakaan ngbaan ubaa wii kan, ntaŋaal aayidam ŋmeen kuun dan aa chee.

ref: Give a signal on a trumpet when it is time to break camp. The first blast will be the signal for the tribes camped on the east side, and the second blast will be the signal for those on the south.
text: N‑yoonn mu bi ki ŋun kakaan wii lelee, naa yunn na kan, linibol li ka ŋŋangii wɔb na mu le ga fii paan. Nima pu na, kakaan yaa wii kaa yunn kan, ni mɔk ke binib ngbaan fii baah ka nin chee na, ki li chuun.

ref: But when you want everyone to come together, sound a different signal on the trumpet.
text: Tɔ, bi yaa ŋun kakaan wii ki yunn kan, binib ngbaan mɔmɔk kuun ni.

ref: The priests of Aaron's family will be the ones to blow the trumpets, and this law will never change.
text: Aaronn ni ujapɔtiib bi ye bitotoorb na le ga li pii kakaan tiib ngbaan. “Ni li joo ikaal i paa ni na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: Whenever you go into battle against an enemy attacking your land, give a warning signal on the trumpets. Then I, the Lord, will hear it and rescue you.
text: N‑yoonn mu ni bi nimi aatiŋ ni, ki buen butɔb ni, ki ban ni gaa nibaa lii nimi aadim bi lir ni pu na kan, ni pii kakaan tiib ngbaan baah ban bi piin butɔb pu na, le min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga ter nimi, ki nyan nimi, nimi aadim aaŋaal ni.

ref: During the celebration of the New Moon Festival and other religious festivals, sound the trumpets while you offer sacrifices. This will be a reminder that I am the Lord your God. The Israelites Begin Their Journey
text: Ni yaa ti ki ye nimi aapopiin aayoonn, mu ye Uŋmapɔɔn aajim, ni nimi aatoorkpaan aajim muken na kan, buyoonn ni ban ke ni toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, ni kimɔbaan aatork tii mi na, ni pii kakaan tiib ngbaan, le m ga ter nimi. Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.” Israel yaab aah nan fii Sainai Aateersakpiin ni pu na

ref: On the twentieth day of the second month of that same year, the cloud over the sacred tent moved on.
text: Israel yaab aah nan nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni aan ni saa ŋibin ŋilee, lelee aaŋmal aawiin moninko daal na, le ntaalangbam mu nan sunni ki nan biin Uwumbɔr Aabool pu na fii paacham.

ref: So the Israelites broke camp and left the Sinai Desert. And some time later, the cloud stopped in the Paran Desert.
text: Le Israel yaab nan piin lisachuln Sainai Aateersakpiin ni. Ntaalangbam ngbaan nan ti sil Parann Aateersakpiin ni la.

ref: This was the first time the Lord had told Moses to command the people of Israel to move on.
text: Bi nan chuun dii, Uwumbɔr aah mɔk Moses pu na la.

ref: Judah and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out first, carrying their banner. Nahshon son of Amminadab was the leader of the Judah tribe,
text: Bi yaa nan chuun cha kan, bi nan paa tɔb pu kina la. Juda aanibol, ni ŋinibol ŋi kpee li pu ki bi baatuutaa taab na, le nan pue loln nsan, ŋigetek ŋigetek, le Aminadab aajapɔɔn Nasonn nan ye usaloln bi pu.

ref: Nethanel son of Zuar was the leader of the Issachar tribe,
text: Suar aajapɔɔn Netanel le nan ye Isakar aanibol yaab aayidaan.

ref: and Eliab son of Helon was the leader of the Zebulun tribe.
text: Le Helonn aajapɔɔn Eliab nan ye Sebulunn aanibol aayidaan.

ref: The sacred tent had been taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites carried it, marching behind the Judah camp.
text: Bi yaa nan ber Uwumbɔr Aabool ngbaan kan, Gesonn ni Merari aataŋaal ni yaab le ga tun tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk le ki chuun.

ref: Reuben and the tribes that camped alongside it marched out second, carrying their banner. Elizur son of Shedeur was the leader of the Reuben tribe,
text: Rubenn aanibol na, ni ŋinibol ŋi kpee li pu ki bi baatuutaa taab na, le nan yakr ŋigetek ŋigetek, ki paan, le Sedeur aajapɔɔn Elisur nan ye usaloln bi pu.

ref: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was the leader of the Simeon tribe,
text: Surisadai aajapɔɔn Selumiel le nan ye Simeonn aanibol yaab aayidaan.

ref: and Eliasaph son of Deuel was the leader of the Gad tribe.
text: Le Dewel aajapɔɔn Eliasaf nan ye Gad aanibol yaab aayidaan, ki loln bi pu nsan.

ref: Next were the Kohathites, carrying the objects for the sacred tent, which was to be set up before they arrived at the new camp.
text: Liifai yaab bi ye Kohaf aataŋaal ni aanib na mu ga paan, ki tu Uwumbɔr aah ŋa tiwan ni chain na. N‑yoonn mu bima ti fuu nkakaa chee na mui bi ki gaa Uwumbɔr Aabool ngbaan a.

ref: Ephraim and the tribes that camped alongside it marched next, carrying their banner. Elishama son of Ammihud was the leader of the Ephraim tribe,
text: Bi paa na le nan ye Efraim aanibol, ni ŋinibol ŋi kpee li pu ki bi baatuutaa taab na, nan yakr ŋigetek ŋigetek, ki paan, le Amihud aajapɔɔn Elisama nan ye usaloln.

ref: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader of the Manasseh tribe,
text: Pedasur aajapɔɔn Gamaliel le nan ye Manase aanibol yaab aayidaan.

text: Sin, ni aajapɔtiib baanja le ga tun Chain Aapepel wɔb, ni kitork aabimbiln pu aatuln. Nima kan, maaŋuul aan ki fii Israel yaab pu.

ref: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
text: Min le ye u nyan aado yaab Liifai aanibol, Israel yaab ponn ni, ke bi li ye ipiin ki tii nimi na. Min le nyan bi ke bi li ye maanib, nima kan, bi ga ŋmaa tun Maabool ni aatuln.

ref: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
text: Aa ni aajapɔtiib baanja le ga tun lituln li ye kitork ni kaabimbiln yaan na, ni Chain Chain Aapepel wɔb ni aatuln. Ŋitun ŋimina mɔmɔk ye nimi yaan la, ba pu? min le di kitork aatuln tii nimi ipiin. Unii u kaa ŋeer ke u tun lituln ngbaan na yaa dan tiwan ni m ŋa ni chain na chee kan, u ga kpo.” Tiwan ni ye bitotoorb yaan na

ref: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
text: Tiwakor ngbaan aanann ti gur na ye sin yaan la, ke libingbaal ni ŋŋangii aataajal, ŋi ye ipiinkpaan aatork na, aah ye sin yaan pu na.

ref: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
text: Ipiinkpaan i ye miyaan ki bi chain, baan di see mmii ni, kitork aabimbiln pu, ki ye saawan na sɔ: njikaabim aatork, ni titunwanbir aatork, ni lipɔln aapam aatork. Tiwan nimɔk bi di tii mi, ni ye chain aapiin na ye aa ni aajapɔtiib yaan la.

ref: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
text: Ni li ji tiwan ngbaan, chain aapepel ni; bijab baanja le ga ŋmaa ji ni. Li nyi ke m ŋa tiwan ngbaan chain la.

ref: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
text: “Ni ki kpee na, Israel yaab yaa ti ki tii ipiinkpaan ibaa kpee kan, i ye saawan la. M joo i tii sin ni aajapɔtiib, ni aabisatiib, ni li ye nimi yaan ki cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Saamaal ni aanii umɔk bi chain ki ŋeer na ga ŋmaa ji ni.

ref: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
text: “M di tiwanyaan ni Israel yaab kan ki nyan baasar ni, ŋibin mɔmɔk ni, aan bi di tii mi na, tii si; tiwan ngbaan sɔ: olif aakpan, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni njikaabim.

ref: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
text: Nimina mɔmɔk ye sin yaan la. Saamaal ni aanii umɔk bi chain ki ŋeer na ga ŋmaa ji ni.

ref: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
text: “Tiwan nimɔk bi Israel aatiŋ ni aan bi di ni tii mi na ye sin yaan la.

ref: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
text: “Njan aabo, ni tiwakor aajan aabo bi di tii mi na, mu ye sin yaan la. Tɔ, ni gaa tipar, njan aabim ni tiwakor ti kaa bi chain na pu.

ref: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
text: Mbim yaa ti saa uŋmal ubaa kan, ni cha bi pa tikunabr aamombil ŋiŋmu, baah siin pu Maabool ni na.

ref: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
text: Tɔ, njan aanaabo, ni upihbo, ni uŋobo ma kan, ni taa cha bi ki gir daa ti; tiwakor ngbaan ye min yaan la, aan bi li joo toor kitork tii mi. Ni di taasin gbaa kitork aabimbiln, aan ki di tiponn ni aakpan see mmii ni, aan ni li ye tijikaar aapiin tii mi; kitork ngbaan nu mɔ m chee.

ref: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
text: “Tootookpaan umɔk Israel yaab di tii mi na le m di tii sin, ni aajapɔtiib, ni aabisatiib, ki cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Maah len pu na ye tipuur ti kaan bii na la.”

ref: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Aaronn ke, “Saa kpa liwangol libaa aayaabitiib ga ji li lifaal, le baan gii Israel yaab aatiŋ nibaa chee tii si. Min Uwumbɔr ŋeer si.” Tiwan ni ye Liifai yaab yaan na

ref: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui ke, “M di tiwan nibaabaa ni Israel yaab nyan kipiik mɔmɔk ni tii mi na, tii Liifai yaab. Baah bi Maabool ponn ni ki tun pu na aapar le na.

ref: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
text: N‑yoonn mue ki joo cha, Liifai yaab baanja le ga li tun Maabool ponn ni aatuln mɔmɔk, ki yeh li ponn ni aatork mɔmɔk. Nkaal mue si kina le ki tii saamaal mu. Le Liifai yaab mu aan li kpa lifaal libaa Israel yaab aatiŋ ni;

ref: The Lord told Moses
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses

ref: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
text: ke u tuk Liifai yaab ke: “Ni yaa gaa Israel yaab chee baah tii mi ipiin i aan m di i tii nimi na kan, ni mu ki nyan i ponn ni nibaabaa kipiik kipiik ni, i li ye ipiinkpaan ki tii mi Uwumbɔr.

ref: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
text: Tootookpaan ngbaan ga li bi ke ukpaal aah kon ki kan njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadapɔm, ki nyan miyaan tii mi pu na la.

ref: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
text: Naah kan tiwan nimɔk na, ni nyan tiwan ni ŋan ki bi chain na tii mi Uwumbɔr.

ref: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
text: Ni yaa di tiwan ni ŋan na tii min Uwumbɔr kan, ni gur na, ni mu li joo, ke ukpaal yaa nyan Uwumbɔr yaan tii u kan, u joo ni gur na pu na.

ref: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
text: Naah bi Maabool ni ki tun maatuln na, aa ni saamaal ga ŋmaa ji ni gur na, naah gee nin chee na; nimi aapar le na.

ref: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
text: Ni yaa di tiwan ni ŋan na tii min Uwumbɔr kan, ni ga ŋmaa ji ni gur na, kaan li kpa ngalm kina pu. Tɔ, ni li nyi man, Israel yaab yaa joo ni ipiin i ye chain na kan, ni taa lik ke i ye fam, ki ji, kaa pue nyan i ŋan na tii mi Uwumbɔr. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga kpo.”

ref: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
text: ke bi di nkaal mumina mɔk Israel yaab. Bi li joo ni unaa u man, kaa kpa iween, ki ŋan, aan baa kee di u tun lituln libaa na.

ref: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
text: Bi di u ŋa Eleasar u ye utotoor na aaŋaal ni. Bi di u nya n‑gbaan nibaa chee ki ti kɔr u, Eleasar aanimbiin ni.

ref: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
text: Le Eleasar ga di uŋanbik bɔ waasin ngbaan ni, ki di yɔk lii Maabool taab nfum mulole.

ref: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
text: Bi di unaamɔn ngbaan: waagban, ni tinann, ni nsin, ni tineer na, ki di u see mmii, utotoor aanimbiin ni.

ref: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
text: Le u ga di santina aadɔ, ni nkiisuk, ni ŋŋmin maman, mee ŋa mmii ngbaan ni.

ref: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
text: Nee aapuwɔb na, u finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun, nima kan, u ga ŋmaa gir kun linampal; u mu beenin ye ujɔŋdaan la, see kijook wɔb le u ga nan ŋa chain.

ref: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
text: Le uja u see unaa ngbaan mmii ni na, mu ga finn waawanpeenkaan, ki fu nnyun, u mu beenin ye ujɔŋdaan la, see kijook wɔb le u ga nan ŋa chain.

ref: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
text: Unii u ye chain na le ga faa unaa ngbaan aafatan ki di mu bil lipaal, nin chee ŋan na, nima chee le mu ga li dɔ, le Israel aanii ubaa yaa kpaln tijɔŋdaan kan, bi ga lee nfatan ngbaan ŋa nnyun ni, le udaan fu mu, aan ki ŋa chain. Bi yaa ŋa kina kan, bi ga nya baatunwanbir ni.

ref: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
text: Uja u faa nfatan ngbaan na mu finn waawanpeenkaan, u mu beenin ye ujɔŋdaan la, see kijook wɔb le u ga nan ŋa chain. Nkaal ngbaan bi kina le ki cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Mu ye nkaal ki tii Israel yaab, ni biwɔwɔm bimɔk koo bi chee na la. Unii u meeh linikpol na

ref: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
text: Unii umɔk meeh linikpol na kan, u kpaln tijɔŋdaan le ki ti saa iwiin ilole.

ref: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
text: See u fu nnyun mu ga cha u li bi chain na, wintaa daal, ni winlole daal, le ki nin ŋa chain. U yaa kaa fu kina aanyun wintaa ni winlole daal ki ŋa ubaa chain kan, waan li bi chain.

ref: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
text: Unii umɔk meeh linikpol, kaa fu kina aanyun ki ŋa ubaa chain na kan, u gaar tijɔŋ ngbaan ni la, ba pu? waa fu kina aanyun. U bii Uwumbɔr Aabool le na, le waa ki waan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa.

ref: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
text: Nibaakan unii ubaa yaa bi waadiik ponn ni, uken kpo leŋ u pu, bee linikpol ngbaan yaa dɔ ki ponn ni, le uken koo li chee kan, u mu kpaln tijɔŋdaan iwiin ilole le na.

ref: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
text: Nibaakan bi yaa ku unii, bee u kpo ubaa pu lipaal, aan uken yaa meeh u, bee unii ubaa yaa meeh unibɔn aakpab, bee likaakul kan, u kpaln tijɔŋdaan iwiin ilole le na.

ref: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
text: Unii u bi chain na yoor nkiisuk bɔ nnyun ngbaan ni, ki di yɔk yɔk kidiik ngbaan pu, ni tiwan nimɔk bi ki ponn ni na, ni binib bi nan bi ki ponn ni na pu. Unii u bi chain na mu di nnyun ngbaan yɔk yɔk uja u meeh unibɔn aakpab, bee linikpol, bee u meeh likaakul na pu.

ref: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
text: Wintaa, ni winlole daal kan, unii u bi chain na di nnyun ngbaan yɔk yɔk unii u kaa bi chain na pu. Winlole daal kan, u toor nyan uja ngbaan aajɔŋ, ki cha u finn waawanpeenkaan ki fu nnyun, le nwiin yaa lir liyaadaal ngbaan kan, u ŋa chain le na.

ref: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
text: Unii umɔk kaa bi chain ki mu yii kaa toor ubaa na kan, u gur ye ujɔŋdaan la, ba pu? waa fu nnyun mu ŋani binib chain na. U bii Uwumbɔr Aabool le na, le waan ki li ye Uwumbɔr aanib ponn ni ubaa.

ref: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
text: N‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, ni li joo nkaal ngbaan. Le unii u di nnyun ngbaan yɔk yɔk ke mu ŋa uken chain na, mu finn waawanpeenkaan; le unii umɔk meeh nnyun ngbaan na, u mu kpaln tijɔŋdaan le ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
text: Unii u kaa ye chain na aah meeh tiwan nimɔk na mu kpaln tijɔŋ aawan la, le umɔk meeh kina aawan na mu aa ki ye chain ki ti saa kijook wɔb.

ref: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
text: Israel yaab aah nan nyan Ijipt aatiŋ ni ki ti saa ŋibin imonko ilee pu na aajan aaŋmal ni, le binib ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti fuu Sinn aateersakpiin ni, le ki kal Kades aatiŋ ni. Nima chee le Miriam nan kpo, le bi sub u.

ref: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
text: Baah nan kal nin chee na, nnyun aa nan bi nima, kina pu na, binib ngbaan nan kuun gob Moses ni Aaronn,

ref: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
text: le ki ŋulni bi pu ki len ke, “Ti yaa ba kpo Uwumbɔr Aabool chee, biken chee kan, ni ba soor.

ref: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
text: Ba ŋa ni joo ni timi nteersakpiin mue ni do? Ni ban ke ti ni timi aawakor kpo do la aa?

ref: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
text: Ba ŋa ni nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki cha ti nan bi falaa ni do; tijikaar tibaa ga ŋmaa ŋa do oo? Njikaabim ni ŋisubil aasui aa bi kpala. Nnyun aa kpaan bi, ti nyu.”

ref: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
text: Le Moses ni Aaronn siir foor binib ngbaan chee, le ki ti sil Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb chee, le ki tar lir kitiŋ bipuu pu, le Uwumbɔr aawiihn mu moor ki deer ŋinimbil na sunn ni bi chee.

ref: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
text: “Ti yoor lidabil li dɔ Nkaal Aadakaa chee na, aan aa ni Aaronn kuun ni binib ngbaan mɔmɔk, ki len litakpal sakpeln limina chee tibɔr, binimbil ni, le nnyun ga nyan ni li ponn ni. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, nnyun ga nyan ni li ponn ni aan binib ngbaan ni baawakor kan nnyun ki nyu.”

ref: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
text: Uwumbɔr aah bui u kina na, le Moses buen ti yoor ni lidabil ngbaan.

ref: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
text: U ni Aaronn nan kuun ni binib ngbaan mɔmɔk, litakpal sakpeln ngbaan aanimbiin ni, le Moses bui bi ke, “Li pel man, nimi tafalaaŋun aanib bee. Ti ga nyan nnyun litakpal lee ni, tii nimi ii?”

ref: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
text: Le Moses yoor lidabil ngbaan ki di faa litakpal ngbaan nfum mulee, le nnyusakpem puu nyan ni, le binib ngbaan mɔmɔk ni baawakor nyun.

ref: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Moses ni Aaronn ke, “Naah kaa gaa mi ki kii mbamɔm, ki yii, kaa ban ni mɔk binib ngbaan maapɔɔn mu bi chain na pu na, maan cha ni di bi koo kitiŋ ki ponn ni m puu ke m ga di tii bi na ni.”

ref: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
text: Nimina mɔmɔk nan ŋa Meriba aatiŋ ni, nin chee Israel aanib nan ŋulni Uwumbɔr pu na la, le u nan mɔk bi ke u bi chain. Edom yaab aabɔr aah kaa nan kii ke Israel yaab jer waatiŋ ni pu na

ref: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
text: Baah nan ka Kades aatiŋ ni na, le Moses nyan ntuuntiib tun Edom yaab aabɔr chee. Bi nan ti bui u ke, “Tibɔr tee nyan ni aanaabitiib Israel yaab chee la. Aa nyi taah ji falaa umɔk na.

ref: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
text: Tiyaajatiib nan buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni, le ki ti koo nima ŋibin pam. Le Ijipt yaab saan tiyaajatiib, ni timi,

ref: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
text: le ti wii yin Uwumbɔr ke u ter timi. U nan ŋun timi aawiil le ki tun ni waatuun, le u nan nyan timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni. N‑yoonn mue ti ka Kades aatiŋ ni la. Kitiŋ ngbaan bi saatiŋ aanaanmɔk la.

ref: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
text: Uninkpel, tiin timi nsan aan ti bɔ dii saatiŋ ni ki jer. Ti ni timi aawakor ga li dii nsan la, taan dii tikpaasar, ni ŋisubil aasui aasar ponn ni, ki mu aan nyu nimi aanyunbun ni aanyun. Ti ga li dii nsanjakpaan la, le ki ti jer saatiŋ ni.”

ref: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
text: Le Edom yaab giin bui bi ke, “Taan cha ni dii timi aatiŋ ponn ni ki jer. Ni yaa ban ni dii kan, ti ga fii ki tak nimi.”

ref: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
text: Le Israel yaab bui ke, “Ti ga dii nsanja pu la, le ti ni timi aawakor yaa nyun nimi aanyun kan, ti ga pa mu pu. Ti ban ti dii jer kakaan la.”

ref: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
text: Le Edom yaab ki gir bui ke, “Taan kii tii nimi.” Le baajab bi pɔɔ ki wiir sakpen na fii ti tak Israel yaab.

ref: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
text: Edom yaab aah kaa nan kii ke Israel yaab dii baatiŋ ni ki jer na, le Israel yaab fenn ki dii niyayan. Aaronn aah kpo pu na

ref: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
text: Israel yaab mɔmɔk nan fii Kades aatiŋ ni le ki ti fuu Hor Aajool chee.

ref: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
text: “Aaronn aan koo kitiŋ ki m puu ke m ga di tii Israel yaab na ni, u ban u kpo la, ba pu? nimi bilee bee nan yii maamɔb Meriba aatiŋ ni.

ref: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
text: Di Aaronn ni ujapɔɔn Eleasar buen Hor Aajool pu.

ref: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
text: Ti chuu peer Aaronn aatotoorbɔkul ki di peen Eleasar. Aaronn ga ti kpo nima chee la.”

ref: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
text: Moses nan ŋa Uwumbɔr aah bui ke u ŋa pu na mɔmɔk. Bi nan buen Hor Aajool pu, binib ngbaan mɔmɔk aanimbil ni.

ref: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
text: Le Moses ti chuu peer Aaronn aatotoorbɔkul le ki di peen Eleasar. Lijool ngbaan aapaacham le Aaronn kpo, le Moses ni Eleasar gir sunn ni.

ref: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
text: Binib ngbaan mɔmɔk aah ŋun ke Aaronn kpo na, le bi mɔmɔk nan wii waakpuul ki ti saa iwiin piitaa.

ref: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
text: Israel yaab nan nyan Hor aajool chee, le ki dii nsan mu cha baah nan puur Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem nin chee na, nima kan, bi ga ŋmaa gɔln Edom aapepel aanaanmɔk. Baah nan cha na, le binib ngbaan aa nan ŋmaa chuu bibaa,

ref: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
text: le ki ŋulni Uwumbɔr ni Moses pu. Bi nan len ke, “Ba ŋa ni nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni ke ti nan kpo nteersakpiin mue ni, nin chee tijikaar ni nnyun aa bi na. Ti nuur tijikaar tichachaan tee pu a.”

ref: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
text: Le Uwumbɔr cha iwaa i kpa liluul na dan nan junn bi, le bi ponn ni pam nan kpoi.

ref: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,

text: Moses nan bui Israel yaab ke, “Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki kii tii ikaal i m bi mɔk nimi na, nima le ga cha ni li bi, ki ti gaa kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr, u ye niyaajatiib Aawumbɔr na, ban u di tii nimi na.

ref: and now he is your God. I am telling you everything he has commanded, so don't add anything or take anything away.
text: Ni taa di nibaa kpee ikaal ngbaan ni, ki taa nyan nibaa i ni. Ni kii tii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aakaal i m joo tuk nimi na mbamɔm.

ref: You saw how he killed everyone who worshiped the god Baal Peor.
text: Ninimbigbaŋ kan Uwumbɔr aah nan ŋa pu Peor Aajool chee na. U nan kuln unii umɔk nan dooni liwaal Baal na;

ref: But all of you that were faithful to the Lord your God are still alive today.
text: le nimi bi nan dii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr na ma laa beenin bi limɔfal ni, ki nan saa din.

ref: You must be very careful not to forget the things you have seen God do for you. Keep reminding yourselves, and tell your children and grandchildren as well.
text: Ni li kii nibaa man. Ni yaa bi limɔfal ni ki ti saa buyoonn na kan, ni taa suln ninimbigbaŋ aah kan tiwan ni Uwumbɔr ŋa na. Ni tuk nimi aabim, ni niyaabitiib,

ref: Do you remember the day you stood in the Lord's presence at Mount Sinai? The Lord said, “Moses, bring the people of Israel here. I want to speak to them so they will obey me as long as they live, and so they will teach their children to obey me too.”
text: tiwan ni nan ŋa, bundaln ni nan sil Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, Sainai Aajool taab na. N‑yoonn ngbaan, u nan bui mi ke, ‘Kuun ni maanib ngbaan. M ban bi ŋun maah ga len pu na la, nima kan, bi ga li nyi baah ga kii maamɔb pu, ki ti saa baamɔfal aadoon na. Nima kan, bi ga mɔk baabim, aan bi mu li san mi ijawaan.’

ref: Mount Sinai was surrounded by deep dark clouds, and fire went up to the sky. You came to the foot of the mountain,
text: “Tuk nimi aabim naah nan sil lijool ngbaan aataab aan iŋmanyuu i bɔn sakpen na biin li pu, le mmii gaal ki fii ti pii kitaapaak pu na.

ref: and the Lord spoke to you from the fire. You could hear him and understand what he was saying, but you couldn't see him.
text: Ni ki tuk bi Uwumbɔr aah nan len tibɔr mmii ngbaan ponn ni pu na; ni ŋun waah len pu na, ki mu aa waa waah bi pu na.

ref: The Lord said he was making an agreement with you, and he told you that your part of the agreement is to obey the Ten Commandments. Then the Lord wrote these Commandments on two flat stones.
text: U nan tuk nimi naah ga ŋa pu aan ki li joo waah nan puu tipuur ti tii nimi na pu na; ke ni pɔɔn nibaa ki kii tii ikaal kipiik i u nan ŋmee paan ŋitakpal ŋilee pu na.

ref: That's when the Lord commanded me to give you the laws and teachings you must obey in the land that you will conquer west of the Jordan River. Don't Worship Idols Moses said to Israel:
text: Uwumbɔr nan tuk mi ke m di ikaal ngbaan mɔmɔk mɔk nimi, aan ni li joo i mbamɔm, kitiŋ ki ni ban ni ti gaa ki koo ki ponn ni na. Moses nan sur binib ngbaan ŋiwaa aabɔr pu

ref: not to commit the sin of worshiping idols. Don't make idols to be worshiped, whether they are shaped like men, women,
text: ki taa tun titunwanbir ke ni di tiwan nibaa ŋa liwaal tii nibaa, aan ni li naahn upii, bee uja,

ref: reptiles, or fish.
text: bee tiwanbaarkaan, bee ujan.

ref: And when you see the sun or moon or stars, don't be tempted to bow down and worship them. The Lord put them there for all the other nations to worship.
text: Ni taa cha nibaa tɔŋ nimi aan ni li dooni tiwan ni ni waa kitaapaak, ni ye nwiin, ni uŋmal, ni iŋmabi na. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le di tiwan nimina mɔmɔk tii binib bi mɔmɔk bi dulnyaa wee ni na.

ref: But you are the Lord's people, because he rescued you from Egypt, that fiery furnace.
text: Nimi ma kan, uma le nyan nimi Ijipt yaab aamuk ni. U nyan ni nimi ke u di nimi ŋa waanib, ke naah ye waanib din wee pu na.

ref: The Lord was angry with me because of what you said, and he told me that he would not let me cross the Jordan River into the good land that he is giving you.
text: Nimi pu le Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aaŋuul nan fii m pu, le u puu ke waan cha m puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ki koo kitinyanyaan ki u ban u di tii nimi na ni.

ref: So I must stay here and die on this side of the Jordan, but you will cross the river and take the land.
text: Mma kan, m ga kpo kitiŋ kee ni, kaan puur limɔɔl ngbaan daalbaadaal. Le ni ma ban ni puur ki ti gaa kitinyanyaan ngbaan.

ref: Always remember the agreement that the Lord your God made with you, and don't make an idol in any shape or form.
text: Ni pɔɔn nibaa, ki taa suln tipuur ti Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan puu tii nimi na. Ni kii waamɔb, ki taa naan liwaal libaa tii nibaa.

ref: The Lord will be angry if you worship other gods, and he can be like a fire destroying everything in its path.
text: Ba pu? Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bi ke mmiigaal na la, le kaa ban ke unibɔn ki dii tiwan nibaa ki kpee u pu.

ref: Soon you will cross the Jordan River and settle down in the land. Then in the years to come, you will have children, and they will give you grandchildren. After many years, you might lose your sense of right and wrong and make idols, even though the Lord your God hates them. So I am giving you fair warning today, and I call the earth and the sky as witnesses. If you ever make idols, the Lord will be angry, and you won't have long to live, because the Lord will let you be wiped out.
text: Ni yaa yii maah tuk nimi pu na kan, paacham ni kitiŋ le ye maaseeraadam din wee, ni ga kpo doo kitiŋ ngbaan pu. Le kina aan cha ni li bi ki yunn, naah ban ni puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ki ti gaa kitiŋ ki na ni. U ga kuln nimi doo.

ref: Only a few of you will survive, and the Lord will force you to leave the land and will scatter you among the nations.
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha ni yaa buen ŋinibol yayan aatim ni, le nimi siib kina le ga ti gur ki ŋmar.

ref: There you will have to worship gods made of wood and stone, and these are nothing but idols that can't see or hear or eat or smell.
text: Nima chee le ni ga ti li dooni unibɔn aah di uŋaal ŋa idɔ ni ŋitakpal aawaa ŋi na. Ŋiwaa ngbaan aa waa, kaa ŋun, kaa ŋmaa ji, kaa ŋun nnun.

ref: In all of your troubles, you may finally decide that you want to worship only the Lord. And if you turn back to him and obey him completely, he will again be your God.
text: N‑yoonn mu ni ti kan limukl, aan tiwanbir ngbaan mɔmɔk pii nimi na, le ni ga fenn ban Uwumbɔr ki kii tii u.

ref: The Lord your God will have mercy—he won't destroy you or desert you. The Lord will remember his promise, and he will keep the agreement he made with your ancestors.
text: Uma le ye Uwumbɔr u kpa linimbaasaln na. Waan di nimi lii, ki mu aan kuln nimi doo, waan suln tipuur ti u nan puu tii niyaajatiib na.

ref: When the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt, you saw how he fought for you and showed his great power by performing terrifying miracles. You became his people, and at Mount Sinai you heard him talking to you out of fiery flames. And yet you are still alive! Has anything like this ever happened since the time God created humans? No matter where you go or who you ask, you will get the same answer. No one has ever heard of another god even trying to do such things as the Lord your God has done for you.
text: Liwaal libaa kee buen litimbol yayan ni, ki ti nyan ni binib, ki di bi ŋa laanib, ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ŋa nimi pu Ijipt aatiŋ ni pu na aa? Ninimbil ni, le u nan di waapɔɔn sakpiin tun, ki joo ni iween, ni butɔb, ki ŋa iwaan, ni lijinjiir aatun, ki cha ijawaan aawan ŋa.

ref: The Lord wants you to know he is the only true God, and he wants you to obey him. That's why he let you see his mighty miracles and his fierce fire on earth, and why you heard his voice from that fire and from the sky.
text: U nan cha ni ŋun waaneel pu paacham, ke u mɔk nimi tiwan, ki cha ni kan waamii mu bi chain na dulnyaa wee ni, le u len ni chee tibɔr, mmii ngbaan ponn ni.

ref: The Lord loved your ancestors and decided that you would be his people. So the Lord used his great power to bring you out of Egypt.
text: Waah gee niyaajatiib pu na, le u lee nimi, ki di waapɔɔn sakpiin na nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni.

ref: Now you face other nations more powerful than you are, but the Lord has already started forcing them out of their land and giving it to you.
text: Naah tur koo binib ngbaan ponn ni na, le u nyaŋni ŋinibol ŋi kpa mpɔɔn jer nimi na, ke u di baatim tii nimi, le kitiŋ ngbaan laa beenin ye nimi yaan ki nan saa din wee.

ref: So remember that the Lord is the only true God, whether in the sky above or on the earth below.
text: Nima pu na, teer din wee man, ki taa suln kpala ke Uwumbɔr le ye Uwumbɔr u joo paacham ni kitiŋ kee na. Uwumbɔr uken aa ki bi.

ref: Today I am explaining his laws and teachings. And if you always obey them, you and your descendants will live long and be successful in the land the Lord is giving you. Safe Towns
text: Ni li joo waakaal imɔk m di tuk nimi din wee na, le tiwan mɔmɔk ga li bi mbamɔm tii nimi, ni niyaabitiib. Nima kan, ni ga li bi kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga di tii nimi na pu, ki li ye nimi yaan ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.” Mbɔbɔryaan aatim mu bi Jɔɔdann aawipuul wɔb na aabɔr

ref: Moses said, “People of Israel, you must set aside the following three towns east of the Jordan River as Safe Towns: Bezer in the desert highlands belonging to the Reuben tribe; Ramoth in Gilead, belonging to the Gad tribe; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to the Manasseh tribe. If you kill a neighbor without meaning to, and if you had not been angry with that person, you can run to one of these towns and find safety.” The Second Speech: Moses Tells What the Lord Demands Israel at Beth-Peor
text: Moses nan nyan Beser aatiŋ ki bi nteersakpiin aajool li bi taar na pu le siin Rubenn aamaal yaab; le ki nyan Ramof aatiŋ ki bi Gilead aapepel ni na siin Gad aamaal yaab; ki nyan Golann aatiŋ ki bi Basann aapepel ni na siin Manase aamaal yaab. Moses aah nan piin ki mɔk bi Uwumbɔr Aakaal pu na

ref: The Israelites had come from Egypt and were camped east of the Jordan River near Beth-Peor, when Moses gave these laws and teachings. The land around their camp had once belonged to King Sihon of Heshbon. But Moses and the Israelites defeated him
text: Baah nan nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki nan fuu Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl, liwipuul wɔb, kifataŋ ki dɔ tok Bef Peor aatiŋ na aapuwɔb, le u nan di ikaal ngbaan mɔk bi. Ni nan ye Amor yaab aabɔr u bi nan yin u ke Sihonn na aapepel ni la, uma le nan bi Hesbonn aatiŋ ni ki joo waanib. Moses ni Israel yaab aah nan nyan ni Ijipt buyoonn na, le bi nan nyaŋ u.

ref: and King Og of Bashan, and took their lands. These two Amorite kings had ruled the territory east of the Jordan River
text: Bi nan gaa waatiŋ ngbaan, ki kpee ubɔr Og u nan joo Basann aatiŋ na, u mu nan ye Amor yaab aabɔr, le ki bi Jɔɔdann aawipuul wɔb.

ref: Their land included the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, as far south as the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
text: Kitiŋ ngbaan nan ki bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl liwipuul wɔb aapepel ni la, le ki yoor kina ti ker N‑yaan Aanyusakpem aaŋangii wɔb, ki dii kina ti saa Pisga Aajool aataab, liwipuul wɔb.

ref: Moses called together the people of Israel and said: Today I am telling you the laws and teachings that you must follow, so listen carefully.
text: Moses nan yin ni Israel aanib ngbaan, le bi kuun ni tɔb chee, le u bui bi ke, “Israel yaab, li pel man ikaal imɔk m ban m di tuk nimi din wee na. Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki bae i, ki li joo i mbamɔm, ki taa yii i.

ref: Do not murder.
text: “‘Aa taa ku unii.

ref: The Lord our God made an agreement with our nation at Mount Sinai.
text: Sainai Aajool pu le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur tii titetiib,

ref: That agreement wasn't only with our ancestors but with us, who are here today.
text: ni mu aa nan ye titetiib baanja le u nan puu tii, tipuur ngbaan ye timi bi laa beenin bi din wee na mu yaan la.

ref: The Lord himself spoke to you out of the fire,
text: Lijool ngbaan pu, Uwumbɔr nan len ni chee tibɔr, mmii ponn ni.

ref: but you were afraid of the fire and refused to go up the mountain. So I spoke with the Lord for you, then I told you that he had said:
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan, min le nan sil nimi ni Uwumbɔr aakaasisik ni, le ki tuk nimi waah len pu na, ba pu? ni nan san mmii ngbaan ijawaan, le kaa kaa ke ni buen lijool ngbaan paab. “Le Uwumbɔr nan bui ke,

ref: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
text: ‘Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr u nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, nin chee ni nan ye binaagbiib na.

ref: Do not worship any god except me.
text: “‘Ni taa doon liwaal libaa ki kpee min Uwumbɔr pu.

ref: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
text: “‘Ni taa naan tiwan nibaa ki di naŋ paacham aawan nibaa, bee kitiŋ aawan nibaa, bee nnyun ni aawan nibaa, ke ni doon ni.

ref: Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me and worship idols, I will punish your families for three or four generations.
text: Ni taa gbaan kitiŋ ke ni doon liwaal libaa, ba pu? min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, le maa ban ke m ni ubaa li kpaan yeh nimi. M ga daa binib bi nan mi na, ni baabim, ni biyaabitiib, ni bi mu aayaabitiib aatafal.

ref: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
text: M ga li gee binib churbakaa bi mu gee mi, ki kii tii maakaal na.

ref: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
text: “‘Ni taa yin maayimbil fam fam; min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga daa unii u yin maayimbil fam fam na aatafal.

ref: You have six days when you can do your work,
text: Ni kpa iwiin iloob le ni di tun nimi aatun,

ref: but the seventh day of the week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your oxen or donkeys or any other animal, not even those foreigners who live in your towns. And don't make your slaves do any work.
text: le winlole daal ye lifuur daal ke ni li joo dooni mi. Nwiin ngbaan daal kan, nimi, ni nimi aabim, ni nimi aanaagbiib, ni nimi aawakor, ni biwɔwɔm bi bi nimi aatiŋ ni na ubaa taa tun lituln. Cha nimi aanaagbiib fuur ke naah fuur pu na.

ref: This special day of rest will remind you that I reached out my mighty arm and rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
text: Teer man ke ni mu nan ye binaagbiib le Ijipt aatiŋ ni, le min, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr di maapɔɔn sakpiin na nyan ni nimi. Nima pu le m bui nimi ke ni li joo Likpaakool daal mbamɔm.

ref: Respect your father and mother, and you will live a long and successful life in the land I am giving you.
text: “‘Aa li pak aate ni aana, ke min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah bui si pu na, nima kan, tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii si, aan aa li bi ki yunn, kitiŋ ki m ga di tii si na ni.

ref: Do not steal.
text: “‘Aa taa su kinaayuk.

ref: When we were gathered at the mountain, the Lord spoke to us in a loud voice from the dark fiery cloud. The Lord gave us these commands, and only these. Then he wrote them on two flat stones and gave them to me. The People Were Afraid (Exodus
text: “Ikaal imina le Uwumbɔr nan di tii ni mɔmɔk, buyoonn ni nan kuun dan lijool ngbaan chee na. Waah nan len ni chee tibɔr nneel sakpiin, mmii ponn ni, ni ntaalangbam bɔmbɔm ponn ni na, le u nan di ikaal imina tii nimi. Waa ki di ibaa kpee i pu. U nan ŋmee i ŋitakpapepee ŋilee pu, le ki di i tii mi. Baah san Uwumbɔr ijawaan pu pu na (Nnyam

ref: When fire blazed from the mountain, and you heard the voice coming from the darkness, your tribal leaders came to me
text: “N‑yoonn mu lijool ngbaan pu nan ye mmii ŋmeen, aan ni ŋun nneel pu mbɔmbɔɔn ponn ni na, le nimi aaninkpiib, ni nimi aanibol aayidam nan dan m chee,

ref: and said: Today the Lord our God has shown us how powerful and glorious he is. He spoke to us from the fire, and we learned that people can live, even though God speaks to them.
text: ki nan bui ke, ‘Tidindaan Uwumbɔr mɔk timi waapɔɔn sakpiin, ni waanyuŋ, buyoonn ti ŋun u len mmii ni na. Din wee, ti kan ke Uwumbɔr yaa len unii chee tibɔr kan, udaan ngbaan ga ŋmaa li beenin fu.

ref: But we don't want to take a chance on being killed by that terrible fire, and if we keep on hearing the Lord's voice, we will die.
text: Tɔ, taa ban ti li gbiir nkun. Mmii mue ga ku timi. Ti yaa ki ŋun Uwumbɔr len ti chee tibɔr lelee kan, ti ga sil kpo.

ref: Has anyone else ever heard the only true God speaking from fire, as we have? And even if they have, would they live to tell about it?
text: Unibɔn ubaa kee ŋun Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na bi mmii ni ki len u chee tibɔr, aan udaan ki bi, ki kpa limɔfal aa?

ref: Moses, go up close and listen to the Lord. Then come back and tell us, and we will do everything he says.
text: Moses, gir buen aan ki ti pel Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ga len tibɔr timɔk na, ki ki gir ni ki nan tuk timi waah len pu na. Ti ga pel ti, ki gaa ti mɔmɔk.’

ref: The Lord heard you and said: Moses, I heard what the people said to you, and I approve.
text: “N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr ŋun kina na, le u bui mi ke, ‘M ŋun binib ngbaan aah len pu na; bi kpa mbamɔn.

ref: I wish they would always worship me with fear and trembling and be this willing to obey me! Then they and their children would always enjoy a successful life.
text: Bima yaa kpa nlandak ngbaan aaboln kina n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, ki yaa ga pak mi ki kii tii maakaal mɔmɔk kan, tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii bi, ni biyaabitiib, ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: Now, tell them to return to their tents,
text: Gir buen ti tuk bi ke bi gir kun bido ŋinampal.

ref: but you come back here to me. After I tell you my laws and teachings, you will repeat them to the people, so they can obey these laws in the land I am giving them. Moses said:
text: Sin Moses ma kan, gaar m chee do, aan m di maakaal, ni maamɔkm mɔmɔk tuk si. Aa di ikaal ngbaan mɔk binib ngbaan, nima kan, bi ga joo i mbamɔm, ki li bi kitiŋ ki m ban ke m di tii bi na ni.’

ref: Follow them, because they make a path that will lead to a long successful life in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
text: Ni li joo i mɔmɔk mbamɔm, aan nima kan, naah ban ni gaa kitiŋ ki aan ki li koo ki ponn ni na, tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii nimi, le ni ga yunn ki ponn ni.

ref: The Lord told me to give you these laws and teachings, so you can obey them in the land he is giving you. Soon you will cross the Jordan River and take that land.
text: “Ikaal imina le Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan bui mi, ke m di i mɔk nimi. Naah chaa koo kitiŋ ki ponn ni, ke ni ti li bi nima na, ni ti li joo i mbamɔm.

ref: And if you and your descendants want to live a long time, you must always worship the Lord and obey his laws.
text: Nimi ni niyaabitiib aah ga li bi limɔfal ni ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu na, ni li pak Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ki li joo waakaal i m di mɔk nimi na mbamɔm, aan ki yunn kitiŋ ngbaan ni.

ref: Pay attention, Israel! Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he promised to give us this land that is rich with milk and honey. Be careful to obey him, and you will become a successful and powerful nation.
text: Nimi Israel yaab, li pel maah ban m di i mɔk nimi pu na, ki li joo i mbamɔm. Le tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii nimi, le ni ga ŋa litimbokpaan, ki li koo kitiŋ ki kpa tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan ni ŋisubil sakpen na ni, ke Uwumbɔr u ye tiyaajatiib Aawumbɔr na aah nan puu pu na.

ref: Listen, Israel! The Lord our God is the only true God!
text: “Israel yaab, teer man tibɔr tee. Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le ye timi Aawumbɔr. Ubaa aa ki bi.

ref: So love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and strength.
text: Ni li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nimi aasui mɔmɔk ni, ni nimi aawiin mɔmɔk, ni nimi aapɔɔn mɔmɔk.

ref: and tell them to your children over and over again. Talk about them all the time, whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning.
text: Ni di i mɔk nimi aabim. Ni yaa ka linampal, bee ni yaa nyan buen nsan, bee ni yaa ka fuur, bee ni yaa bi tun lituln kan, ni li len yaabɔr.

ref: Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and foreheads to help you obey them.
text: Ni di i gbin niŋaal pu, ki ŋmee i paan niyigbeer pu, aan ni li teer nimi.

ref: Write these laws on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates. Worship Only the Lord Moses said to Israel:
text: Ni ŋmee i paan nimi aadir aabisamɔi pu, ni nimi aatiŋ aagon aabisamɔi pu. Limɔyiir aasurm

ref: The Lord promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you this land. Now he will take you there and give you large towns, with good buildings that you didn't build,
text: “Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah nan puu tipuur ti tii niyaajatiib Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob pu na, u ga di kitiŋ ki kpa ntisakpem mu wiir, ki kpa liwangol, aan naa maa mu nibaa na, tii nimi.

ref: and houses full of good things that you didn't put there. The Lord will give you wells that you didn't have to dig, and vineyards and olive orchards that you didn't have to plant. But when you have eaten so much that you can't eat any more,
text: Ŋidichal ga li gbii tiwanyaan ni nimi nibaa aa di ŋa ŋi ponn ni na, inyunbun mu bi nima, ni mu aa ye nimi le gbii i, le ŋisubil aasui, ni olif aakpan aasui aasar ti nimi nibaa aa kon, kaa bun ti na, mu ga li bi nima. N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr ti di kitiŋ ngbaan tii nimi, aan ni kpa tijikaar ki ji babr na kan,

ref: don't forget it was the Lord who set you free from slavery and brought you out of Egypt.
text: ni li nyi ki taa suln Uwumbɔr u nyan nimi Ijipt yaab aaŋaal ni na, nin chee ni nan ye binaagbiib na, aabɔr.

ref: Worship and obey the Lord your God with fear and trembling, and promise that you will be loyal to him.
text: Ni li pak Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki li dooni uma baanja, aan ki li puur nimi aapuur waayimbil baanja pu.

ref: Don't have anything to do with gods that are worshiped by the nations around you.
text: Ni taa ki doon liwaal libaa; ni taa doon binib bi mann goln nima na aawaal libaa.

text: Baah nan bi lijool ngbaan chee na, le Uwumbɔr nan nyan Liifai aanibol ke bi li lik Nkaal Aadakaa ngbaan, ki li tun bitotoorb aatuln tii u, ki li joo waayimbil ŋani tinyoor ŋani waanib pu. Liifai yaab laa beenin tun lituln ngbaan ki nan saa din wee.

ref: Instead, he told me, “Moses, get ready to lead the people into the land that I promised their ancestors.” What the Lord Wants Moses said:
text: U nan bui mi ke m sunn ni, ki nan loln ni pu nsan, aan ni ŋmaa buen ti gaa kitiŋ ki u nan puu ke u ga di tii niyaajatiib na. Uwumbɔr aah ban waanib li bi pu na

ref: People of Israel, what does the Lord your God want from you? The Lord wants you to respect and follow him, to love and serve him with all your heart and soul,
text: “Israel yaab, li pel man Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ban ni li bi pu na: Ni li dooni Uwumbɔr, ki li ŋani waah bui ke ni ŋa pu na. Ni li gee u, ki li joo nisui mɔmɔk tun waatuln.

ref: and to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. Do this, and all will go well for you.
text: Ni li joo waakaal mɔmɔk. Din wee na, m ban m di i tii nimi aan i li kpa tinyoor ki toor nimi.

ref: Everything belongs to the Lord your God, not only the earth and everything on it, but also the sky and the highest heavens.
text: Uwumbɔr le yeh paacham, ni dulnyaa, ni tiwan nimɔk bi u ni na.

ref: Yet the Lord loved your ancestors and wanted them to belong to him. So he chose them and their descendants rather than any other nation, and today you are still his people.
text: Uwumbɔr aah gee niyaajatiib sakpen pu na, le u nyan nimi baanja ŋinibol mɔmɔk ni, le ni beenin ye waanib ki nan saa din.

ref: Remember your agreement with the Lord and stop being so stubborn.
text: Nima pu na, n‑yoonn mue ki joo cha, ni kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, ki di cha nimi aatafalaaŋun ngbaan.

ref: The Lord your God is more powerful than all other gods and lords, and his tremendous power is to be feared. His decisions are always fair, and you cannot bribe him to change his mind.
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le jer dindatiib mɔmɔk, le ki kpa mpɔɔn mu ki jer ipɔɔn mɔmɔk. Waah ye usakpiin ki kpa mpɔɔn na, le ni ŋeer ke ti li san u ijawaan. Waa kpa imaagann, le kaa gaal igaŋgaŋlik.

ref: The Lord defends the rights of orphans and widows. He cares for foreigners and gives them food and clothing.
text: Uma le lik nkpobim, ni bikpopiib, ki gee biwɔwɔm bi koo ti chee na. Uma le tii bi tijikaar ni tiwanpeenkaan.

ref: And you should also care for them, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
text: Nima pu na, ni li gee biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee na; ba pu? ni mu nan ye biwɔwɔm le Ijipt aatiŋ ni.

ref: Offer your praises to him, because you have seen him work such terrifying miracles for you.
text: Ni li pak u. Uma le ye nimi Aawumbɔr, le ninimbil kan waah ŋa lijinjiir aawan nimɔk ki tii nimi na.

ref: The Lord is your God, so you must always love him and obey his laws and teachings.
text: “Ni li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki li joo waakaal n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: Remember, he corrected you and not your children. You are the ones who saw the Lord use his great power
text: Din wee, ni teer naah bee Uwumbɔr aabimbin, waah tun ŋitukpaan ŋi ni chee na pu. Naa ye nimi aabim le kan, nimi le nan kan ŋitukpaan ngbaan.

ref: when he worked miracles in Egypt, making terrible things happen to the king and all his people.
text: Ni nan kan Uwumbɔr aah ye mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, ki tun ŋitukpaan, ni lijinjiir aatun pu na. Ni nan kan waah ŋa Ijipt aabɔr, ni waatiŋ mɔmɔk pu na.

ref: And when the Egyptian army chased you in their chariots, you saw the Lord drown them and their horses in the Red Sea. Egypt still suffers from that defeat!
text: Ni nan kan Uwumbɔr aah nan kuln Ijipt aajab, ni baataan, ni itaan aatɔroku tiib pu na; u nan cha bi bee Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem ni, buyoonn bi nan san paa ni nimi pu na.

ref: You saw what the Lord did for you while you were in the desert, right up to the time you arrived here.
text: Ni ki nyi Uwumbɔr aah nan ki ŋa tiwan nimɔk tii nimi nteersakpiin ni, aan ni nin fuu do na.

ref: And you saw how the Lord made the ground open up in the middle of our camp underneath the tents of Dathan and Abiram, who were swallowed up along with their families, their animals, and their tents.
text: Ni ki teer waah nan ŋa Datann, ni Abiram, bi nan ye Eliab aajapɔtiib, ki nyan ni Rubenn aataŋaal ni aanib pu na. Ni mɔmɔk aanimbil ni, le Uwumbɔr nan cha kitiŋ piir, le bi ni baamaal, ni baakookoo yaan, ni baanaagbiib, ni baawakor mɔmɔk lir ni ponn ni, le kitiŋ ki biin bi pu.

ref: With your own eyes, you saw the Lord's mighty power do all these things.
text: Mbamɔn, nimi bimina le nan kan ŋitukpaan ŋimɔk Uwumbɔr nan tun na. Tipuur aatiŋ aah kpa tinyoor ti na

text: “Ni li joo waakaal i mɔmɔk m di mɔk nimi din wee na mbamɔm. Nima kan, ni ga ŋmaa puur limɔɔl aan ki ti gaa kitiŋ ki ni chaa koo ki ponn ni na.

ref: that the Lord promised your ancestors and their descendants. It's rich with milk and honey, and you will live there and enjoy it for a long time.
text: Le ni ga li bi kitiŋ ki kpa tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan ni ŋisubil sakpen na ni, aan Uwumbɔr nan puu ke u ga di tii niyaajatiib, ni biyaabitiib na pu.

text: Kitiŋ ki ni ban ni gaa ki na aa bi ke Ijipt aatiŋ ki ni nan bi ki ponn ni na aah bi pu na.

ref: because the Lord your God keeps his eye on this land and takes care of it all year long.
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le joo kitiŋ ngbaan, ki lik ki n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: The Lord your God commands you to love him and to serve him with all your heart and soul. If you obey him,

ref: he will send rain at the right seasons, so you will have more than enough food, wine, and olive oil, and there will be plenty of grass for your cattle.
text: Timoor ga li bi, nimi aawakor ŋmɔ. Ni ga kan naah ban tijikaar ti na mɔmɔk.

ref: But watch out! You will be tempted to turn your backs on the Lord. And if you worship other gods,

ref: the Lord will become angry and keep the rain from falling. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will die and disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
text: Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, Uwumbɔr ga gee ni pu liŋuul; waan ki cha utaal nu, le nimi aatiŋ ga kuur ki ti chaar jer, le nimi aajikaar aan ŋmaa ŋa. Hali kitiŋ ngbaan aah ye kitinyaan pu aan u di ki tii nimi na, naan ki yunn le ni ga kpo.

ref: Memorize these laws and think about them. Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and your foreheads to help you obey them.
text: “Ni teer ikaal ngbaan aabɔr, aan ki li joo i mbamɔm. Ni ŋmee i ki di gbin niŋaal pu, ki di buu tam niyigbeer mu pu, aan ki li teer ibɔr.

ref: Teach them to your children. Talk about them all the time—whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning.

ref: Write them on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates.
text: Ni ŋmee i paan nimi aadir aabisamɔi pu, ni nimi aatiŋ aagon aabisamɔi pu.

ref: Then you and your descendants will live a long time in the land that the Lord promised your ancestors. Your families will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.
text: Nima kan, nimi, ni nimi aabim ga li bi kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan puu ke u ga di tii niyaajatiib na pu, ki yunn. Ni ga li bi ki ponn ni n‑yoonn mumɔk paacham ni taab ga li bi na.

ref: Love the Lord your God faithfully and obey all the laws and teachings I'm giving you today. If you live the way the Lord wants,
text: “Ni li nyi ki li joo ikaal i mɔmɔk m di mɔk nimi na mbamɔm. Ni li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki ŋa waakaal aah mɔk nimi pu na, ki li dii uma baanja.

ref: he will help you take the land. And even though the nations there are more powerful than you, the Lord will force them to leave when you attack.
text: Le u ga jenn nyan ŋinibol ŋimɔk ni tur koo ŋi ponn ni na, le ni ga gaa ŋinibol kpaan ŋi kpa mpɔɔn jer nimi na aatiŋ.

ref: You will capture the land everywhere you go, from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains, and from the Euphrates River west to the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Nitaa aah taa kitiŋ ki mɔmɔk pu na ga li ye nimi yaan la. Nimi aatiŋ mɔk ga yoor nteersakpiin aaŋangii wɔb ki ti nya Lebanonn Aajool chee, ŋŋangan wɔb, le ki ga ki yoor Yufrates Aamɔɔl chee, liwipuul wɔb, ki ti ker Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem chee, liwilir wɔb.

ref: No one will be able to stand up to you. The Lord will make everyone terrified of you, just as he promised.
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah nan puu pu na, u ga cha linibol limɔk ni fuu laatiŋ ni na aanib li san nimi ijawaan. Ubaa aa bi ki ga ŋmaa kiir nimi kpala.

ref: You have a choice—do you want the Lord to bless you, or do you want him to put a curse on you?
text: “Lik man, din wee na, m ban ni lee naah gee tiwan ni na la, ni gee tinyoor le aan tibɔbir?

ref: Today I am giving you his laws, and if you obey him, he will bless you.
text: Ni yaa kii, ki joo Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aakaal i m joo tuk nimi din wee na kan, u ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu.

ref: But if you disobey him and worship those gods that have never done anything for you, the Lord will put a curse on you.
text: Ni mu yaa yii waakaal, ki fenn dooni ŋiwaa kan, ni ga kan tibɔbir la. Teer man ke naa kee dii ŋiwaa, ni taa dii ŋi kpala.

ref: After the Lord your God helps you take the land, you must have a ceremony where you announce his blessings from Mount Gerizim and his curses from Mount Ebal.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa joo ni nimi kitiŋ ki ni ban ni gaa ki na ni kan, ni sil Gerisim Aajool paab ki moon tinyoor aabɔr, ki sil Ebal Aajool paab ki moon tibɔbir aabɔr.

ref: Soon you will cross the Jordan River to conquer the land that the Lord your God is giving you. And when you have settled there,
text: Ni ban ni puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl, ki gaa kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ban u di tii nimi na la.

ref: be careful to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
text: Buyoonn ni ti kal ki ponn ni doo na kan, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki li joo waakaal i mɔmɔk m joo tuk nimi din wee na mbamɔm.

ref: Now I'll tell you the laws and teachings that you have to obey as long as you live. Your ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he is giving you this land.
text: “Ni yaa bi kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr, u ye niyaajatiib Uwumbɔr na, ban u di ki tii nimi na ni kan, naah ga li joo ikaal i na sɔ. Li pel man yaah ye pu na:

ref: But the nations that live there worship other gods. So after you capture the land, you must completely destroy their places of worship—on mountains and hills or in the shade of large trees.
text: Ni kuln naah ban ni gaa kitiŋ ki na aanib ngbaan aah dooni baawaa nin chee na, nima le ye ŋijoofɔfɔk pu, ni ŋigongon pu, ni tiwaachur aasui taab.

ref: Wherever these nations worship their gods, you must tear down their altars, break their sacred stones, burn the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and smash their idols to pieces. Destroy these places of worship so completely that no one will remember they were ever there.
text: Ni gbaa wiir baatork aabimbin, ni baawaa aatakpal yak yak, ki see baapiiwaal Asera aanaŋ, aan ki gaa yikr baawaa mɔmɔk, nima kan, baan ki ŋmaa dan ŋaah bi nin chee na ki nan doon ŋi.

ref: Don't worship the Lord your God in the way those nations worship their gods.
text: “Binib ngbaan aah dooni baawaa pu na, ni mu taa li dooni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr kina aaboln.

ref: The Lord has promised that later on he will give Israel more land, and some of you may not be able to travel all the way from your homes to the place of worship each time you are hungry for meat.
