text: Naah dooni Uwumbɔr nin chee na yaa daa sakpen, aan ni yaa gee ke ni kɔr tiwakor ti Uwumbɔr tii nimi na tibaa, ki ŋmɔ linampal na kan, ni ga ŋmaa ŋa kina, maah tuk nimi pu na.

ref: It is the same as eating the meat from a deer or a gazelle that you kill when you go hunting. And in this way, anyone who is unclean and unfit for worship can have some of the meat.
text: Unii umɔk bi chain na, ni u kaa bi chain na ga ŋmaa ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan, ke naah ŋmɔ ipeeman aanann pu na.

ref: But don't eat the blood. It is the life of the animal, so let it drain out on the ground before you eat the meat.
text: Ni taa ji nsin, ni kɔr tiwakor ngbaan ki nyan nsin kpir kitiŋ, ke naah kpir nnyun pu na.

ref: Do you want the Lord to make you successful? Do you want your children to be successful even after you are gone? Then do what pleases the Lord and don't eat blood.
text: Ni yaa joo ikaal ngbaan mbamɔm kan, Uwumbɔr ga li kpa mpopiin ni pu, le ni ga li ŋan tii nimi, ni nimi aamaal.

ref: All sacrifices and offerings to the Lord must be taken to the place where he chooses to be worshiped. If you offer a sacrifice to please the Lord, all of its meat must be burned on the altar. text: Ni di kitork ki ni ga di ki mɔmɔk see mmii ni, Uwumbɔr aabimbiln paab na toor tii u nima chee. Naah ga di tiwakor ti toor kitork na, ni nyan taasin kpir waabimbiln pu, aan ki ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan.

ref: If you obey these laws, you will be doing what the Lord your God says is right and good. Then he will help you and your descendants be successful. Worship the Lord in the Right Way Moses said:
text: Ni li joo ikaal imɔk m di tuk nimi na mbamɔm, le tiwan mɔmɔk ga li ŋan tii nimi, ni niyaabitiib, ki joo cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na, ba pu? ni yaa ŋani tiwan ni ŋan na kan, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga li kpa mpopiin ni pu. Ni taa yii Uwumbɔr ki li dii ŋiwaa

ref: Israel, as you go into the land and attack the nations that are there, the Lord will get rid of them, and you can have their land.

ref: But that's when you must be especially careful not to ask, “How did those nations worship their gods? Shouldn't we worship the Lord in the same way?”
text: Uwumbɔr yaa kuln ŋinibol ngbaan doo aan ni koo ŋaatim ni kan, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki taa li dii baah dooni ŋiwaa ŋi na; ba pu? ni ye nnikun la. Ni taa li ban ni bee baah dooni baawaa pu na aan ki mu li dooni Uwumbɔr kina.

ref: No, you should not! The Lord hates the disgusting way those nations worship their gods, because they even burn their sons and daughters as sacrifices.
text: Ni taa li dooni Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ke baah dooni baawaa pu na, ba pu? bi dooni baawaa ki ŋani tiwan ni kaa ŋan na aabɔŋ, le Uwumbɔr nan kina aabimbin. Hali bi joo baabim le kɔr toor kitork ki seer mmii ni, ŋibimbin paab tii ŋiwaa.

ref: Obey all the laws and teachings I am giving you. Don't add any, and don't take any away.
text: “Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki ŋa maah bui nimi pu na mɔmɔk, ni taa di tiwan nibaa kpee maah mɔk nimi pu na, ki mu taa nyan nibaa mu.

ref: Someday a prophet may come along who is able to perform miracles or tell what will happen in the future. Then the prophet may say, “Let's start worshiping some new gods—some gods that we know nothing about.”
text: ki ban ke u cha ni li dooni ŋiwaa kan, ni taa dii u. Hali waah puu tipuur ti na yaa ŋa kina kan,

text: ni taa kii tii u. Naa kee dii ŋiwaa ngbaan. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ban ke u di unii ngbaan tɔŋ nimi ki lik ke ni gee u nisui mɔmɔk ni aan naa gee u.

ref: You must be completely faithful to the Lord. Worship and obey only the Lord and do this with fear and trembling,

ref: And when the rest of Israel hears about it, they will be afraid, and no one else will ever do such an evil thing again.
text: Israel yaab mɔmɔk yaa ŋun naah ku u pu na kan, bi ga san ijawaan, le ubaa aan ki ŋa titunwanbir ngbaan aaboln.

ref: After the Lord your God gives you towns to live in, you may hear a rumor about one of the towns.

text: nibaakan ni ga ŋun ke titunwanbirdam bi ye nido yaab na mu ŋmann binaabitiib kitiŋ ki ponn ni bi bi na, le ki cha bi dooni ŋiwaa, ŋiwaa ŋi naa kee doon ŋi na,

ref: You must carefully find out if the rumor is true. Then if the people of that town have actually done such a disgusting thing in your own country,
text: ni yaa ŋun bi len kina aabɔr kan, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki fiir lik, ki bee ti mbamɔm; ti yaa ye mbamɔn kan,

ref: you must take your swords and kill every one of them, and their livestock too.
text: ni kpaan ki ku binib bimɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni na, ni baawakor mu. Ni kuln kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk.

ref: Out of all the nations on this earth, the Lord your God chose you to be his own. You belong to the Lord, so don't behave like those who worship other gods. Animals That Can Be Eaten (Leviticus
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le yeh nimi, uma le nyan nimi binib bimɔk bi dulnyaa wee ponn ni na, ke ni li ye waanib. Baah ga li kɔ tiwakor ti na aabɔr (Liifai Yaab

ref: You can eat any clean bird.
text: “Ni ga ŋmaa ji inyoon i kaa kɔ na.

ref: You may eat the meat of cattle, sheep, and goats; wild sheep and goats; and gazelles, antelopes, and all kinds of deer.
text: ni ipeeyun, ni timoor ni aapiih, ni timoor ni aaŋoob, ni ipeeman.

ref: And don't eat pork, since pigs have divided hoofs, but they do not chew their cud. Don't even touch a dead pig!

ref: Swarming insects are unclean, so don't eat them.
text: “Tiwayukaan nimɔk kpa ifeen ki fiir na mu kɔ, ni taa ji ni.

text: Tiwayukaan ni bi, kaa kɔ na kan, ni ga ŋmaa ji ni.

ref: You belong to the Lord your God, so if you happen to find a dead animal, don't eat its meat. ref: People of Israel, every year you must set aside ten percent of your grain harvest.

ref: Also set aside ten percent of your wine and olive oil, and the first-born of every cow, sheep, and goat. Take these to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped, and eat them there. This will teach you to always respect the Lord your God.

ref: But suppose you can't carry that ten percent of your harvest to the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. If you live too far away, or if the Lord gives you a big harvest,

text: “Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa nimi aatuln pu, le ni kan tijikaar gbiin nimi aapil. U ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu, waah ban u di kitiŋ ki tii nimi na ni.

ref: If you follow and obey the Lord, he will make you his own special people, just as he promised.
text: “Ni yaa kii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki ŋa waah len pu na mɔmɔk kan, u ga di nimi ŋa waanib, ke waah nan puu tipuur pu na.

ref: Then everyone on earth will know that you belong to the Lord, and they will be afraid of you.
text: Le binib bi mɔmɔk bi dulnyaa wee ni na ga kan ke Uwumbɔr le nyan nimi ke ni li ye waanib, le bi ga li san nimi ijawaan.

ref: The Lord will give you a lot of children and make sure that your animals give birth to many young. The Lord promised your ancestors that this land would be yours, and he will make it produce large crops for you.
text: Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu, ni li kpa mbim, ni tiwakor, ni tijikaar pam, kitiŋ ki u nan puu tipuur tii niyaajatiib ke u ga di tii nimi na ni.

ref: The Lord will open the storehouses of the skies where he keeps the rain, and he will send rain on your land at just the right times. He will make you successful in everything you do. You will have plenty of money to lend to other nations, but you won't need to borrow any yourself.
text: U ga cha utaal nyan ni paacham ki nan nu n‑yoonn mu ŋeer na, le nimi aatiŋ ga ŋa tijikaar pam, nima kan, ni ga pinn tii ŋinibol pam, le nimi ma aan buen bi chee ke ni ti pinn nibaa.

ref: Obey the laws and teachings that I'm giving you today, and the Lord your God will make Israel a leader among the nations, and not a follower. Israel will be wealthy and powerful, not poor and weak.
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga cha ni li ye ŋinibol ŋiken aasaloln, le ŋima aan ŋmaa loln ni pu nsan. Ni yaa joo ikaal imɔk m joo tuk nimi din wee na kan, naan lann nibaa, ni ga li kani tinyoor n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: and no one will disturb the birds and wild animals while they eat your dead bodies.
text: Ni yaa kpo dɔ kan, inyoon, ni timoor ni aapeel le ga dan ki nan ji nimi aawon, le ubaa aan kan ki jenn i foor.

ref: Then everyone will look at you and your descendants and realize that the Lord has placed you under a curse.
text: Tibɔbir ngbaan ga li ye limɔkl ki tii nimi ni niyaabitiib n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na, ki mɔk ke Uwumbɔr daa nitafal.

ref: Israel, today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. And if you don't obey them all, he will put many curses on you.
text: “Tɔ, ni yaa yii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb, kaa joo waakaal, ni waah bui nimi din wee pu na kan, tibɔbir timina mɔmɔk ga dan ni pu:

ref: Your businesses and farms will fail.
text: “Uwumbɔr ga puun lii nimi aatim, ni tisar pu.

ref: You'll have only a few children, your crops will be small, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats won't produce many young.
text: “Uwumbɔr ga puun lii ni pu, le kaan tii nimi mbim sakpen, tijikaar mu aan li ŋan, le nimi aawakor aan pɔr.

ref: The Lord will make you fail in everything you do.
text: “Uwumbɔr ga puun lii tiwan nimɔk ni ŋani na pu.

ref: No matter what you try to accomplish, the Lord will confuse you, and you will feel his anger. You won't last long, and you may even meet with disaster, all because you rejected the Lord.
text: “Ni yaa tun titunwanbir, ki yii Uwumbɔr kan, u ga cha falaa dan ni pu, le nimi aalandak ŋmal. Tibɔbir ga dan tiwan nimɔk ni ŋani na mɔmɔk ni, le naan yoor n‑yoonn, le ni kuln kookoo.

ref: He will send dust and sandstorms instead of rain, and you will be wiped out.
text: Uwumbɔr aah ba ga cha utaal nu pu na, le u ga cha kitangbaak ni litambol aataabuŋ daa ki kuln nimi doo.

ref: The Lord will let you be defeated by your enemies, and you will scatter in all directions. You will be a horrible sight for the other nations to see,
text: “Uwumbɔr ga cha nimi aadim nyaŋ nimi. Ni ga nya ni lipepel libaa wɔb le ki nan tak bi, le bi nyaŋ nimi ki cha ni san yaa tɔb chee ki buen ŋipepel mɔmɔk. Le dulnyaa ni aanib mɔmɔk yaa kan tiwan ni ŋa nimi na kan, ijawaan ga chuu bi.

ref: The Lord will make you suffer with diseases that will cause oozing sores or crusty itchy patches on your skin or boils like the ones that are common in Egypt. And there will be no cure for you!
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha ŋichakpelar yur nimi, ke waah nan ŋa Ijipt yaab pu na. U ga cha niwon kpaln ibuun ŋmeen. Niwon ga kpaln ligbaln ŋmeen, ki saak, le nnyɔk aa bi ki ga tii nimi laafee.

ref: You will become insane and go blind. The Lord will make you so confused,
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha ni taa ki li kpa nlan, ki cha ni jɔb, le nimi aalandak ŋmal.

ref: that even in bright sunshine you will have to feel your way around like a blind person, who cannot tell day from night. For the rest of your life, people will beat and rob you, and no one will be able to stop them.
text: Ni ga li chuun tuur nwiin pu ke ujoon na, le kaan bee nin chee ni cha na. Ni yaa ŋa tiwan mɔmɔk kan, naan kan tinyoor kpala. Ni ga li bi falaa ni, n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la, le bi ga li su nimi aawan, ubaa mu aan li bi ki ga ter nimi.

ref: A man will be engaged to a woman, but before they can get married, she will be raped by enemy soldiers. Some of you will build houses, but never get to live in them. If you plant a vineyard, you won't be around long enough to enjoy the first harvest.
text: “Aa ga li ban ke aa yoor usapɔɔn, le uniyayan ga yoor u ki cha si. Aa ga maa lidichal, ki mu aan koo li ponn ni. Aa ga ko ŋisubil aasaak, ki mu aan ji ŋisubil ngbaan.

ref: Your cattle will be killed while you watch, but you won't get to eat any of the meat. Your donkeys and sheep will be stolen from you, and no one will be around to force your enemies to give them back.
text: Bi ga ku saanaaja aanimbil ni la, le saan ŋmaa ŋa nibaa, ki mu aan ŋmɔ tinann ngbaan. Bi ga chuu saabon ki dar buen, le aa si lik baah joo i cha pu na, le baan giin ubaa kina tii si. Saadim ga chur saapiih ki dar buen, le ubaa aan ter si ki gaa i tii si.

ref: Your sons and daughters will be dragged off to a foreign country, while you stand there helpless. And even if you watch for them until you go blind, you will never see them again.
text: Bi ga chur saanachipɔm ni saasapɔm tinaagbiir, ki di buen biwɔwɔm aatim ni, le aa ga li si lik baah joo bi cha pu na. Idaa mɔmɔk aa ga li si lik ke nibaakan saabim ga san gir ni le aanimbil ti bii, ubaa kina aan gir ni.

ref: You will work hard on your farms, but everything you harvest will be eaten by foreigners, who will mistreat you and abuse you for the rest of your life.
text: Linibol yayan ga dan nan yoor nimi aajikaar mɔmɔk ti ni jin falaa ki kon na buen, le ni ga kan falaa ni ntafadaan mu pɔɔ na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: What you see will be so horrible that you will go insane,
text: Naah ga ji falaa pu na ga cha naan ki li kpa nlan.

ref: and the Lord will punish you from head to toe with boils that never heal.
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha nitaa wɔb kpaln ibuun i kaan sɔŋ na, i ga li wu pam, le ŋichakpelar ga biin niwon pu, ki yoor niyil ki ti saa nitaafar.

ref: The Lord will let you and your king be taken captive to a country that you and your ancestors have never even heard of, and there you will have to worship idols made of wood and stone.
text: “Uwumbɔr ga cha bi di nimi, ni nimi aabɔr buen biwɔwɔm aatim ni, nin chee niyaajatiib, ni nimi nibaa aa kee buen na. Nima chee le ni ga ti li dooni idɔ ni ŋitakpal aawaa.

ref: People of nearby countries will shudder when they see your terrible troubles, but they will still make fun of you.
text: Ntim mu ponn ni Uwumbɔr ga cha ni yaa ki koo mu ni na, binib ngbaan aapobil ga yuk tiwan ni ŋa nimi na pu, le bi ga ŋa nimi mbɔnyun ki nyei nimi.

ref: You will plant a lot of seed, but gather a small harvest, because locusts will eat your crops.
text: “Ni ga ko tisar pam, le ki mu ga nan chee siib la, ba pu? itoon ga dan ki nan ŋmɔ nimi aajikaar ngbaan.

ref: You will plant vineyards and work hard at taking care of them, but you won't gather any grapes, much less get any wine, because the vines themselves will be eaten by worms.
text: Ni ga bu ŋisubil aasui ki toor i mbamɔm, le ki mu aan nan kan ŋisubil ki ker ki nyu ŋaadaan; ba pu? ŋikpaambil le ga dan nan ŋmɔ tifar ni mpuun mɔmɔk.

ref: Even if your olive trees grow everywhere in your country, the olives will fall off before they are ready, and there won't be enough olive oil for combing your hair.
text: Olif aakpan aasui ga punn nimi aatiŋ ni, ni kookoo, le ni mu aan kan olif aakpan, ba pu? ŋisubil ngbaan ga gbaar lir kitiŋ pel pel.

ref: Locusts will eat your crops and strip your trees of leaves and fruit.
text: Le itoon ga di nimi aasui ni tijikaar ŋmɔ kookoo.

ref: You will be so short of money that you will have to borrow from those foreigners. They will be the leaders in the community, and you will be the followers. More Curses for Disobedience Moses said:
text: Biwɔwɔm ngbaan le ga li kpa ŋimombil bi pinn tii nimi, le naan li kpa nibaa ni pinn tii bi. Le ni yaa bi cha kan, bima le ga ti gaa nimi aasaloln ki li joo nimi.

ref: Israel, if you don't obey the laws and teachings that the Lord your God is giving you, he will send these curses to chase, attack, and destroy you.
text: “Tibɔr ngbaan mɔmɔk ga dan ni pu, le ki li bi kina ki ti kuln nimi, ba pu? ni yii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb, kaa joo waakaal imɔk u di tii nimi na.

ref: If the Lord makes you wealthy, but you don't joyfully worship and honor him,
text: Uwumbɔr le ŋani tinyoor ŋani ni pu tiwan mɔmɔk ni, le ni yii ke naan doon u, kaan li kpa mpopiin ki li mɔɔni u pu.

ref: he will send enemies to attack you and make you their slaves. Then you will live in poverty with nothing to eat, drink, or wear, and your owners will work you to death.
text: Kina pu na, ni ga li tun tii nimi aadim bi Uwumbɔr cha bi nan nyaŋ nimi butɔb ni na la. Nkon ni nnyunyuu ga chuu nimi, le ni ga chuun ni ŋmeen, kaan li kpa nibaa, ki ye bigiim. Uwumbɔr ga daa nitafal pam, le ni ti kuln.

ref: Foreigners who speak a strange language will be sent to attack you without warning, just like an eagle swooping down.
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha linibol li nyan ni dulnyaa aanaanmɔk aan naa nyi baaliin na nan lir ni pu. Bi ga fii nan lir ni pu, ke likaagiil aah booni chur tiwan pu na la.

ref: They won't show any mercy, and they will have no respect for old people or pity for children.
text: Bi ga li kpa ni pu mbiin, le kaan li san nimi bi por na, ni bi ye biwaatiib na kinimbaak.

ref: They will take your cattle, sheep, goats, grain, wine, and olive oil, then leave you to starve.
text: Bi ga di nimi aawakor ni tijikaar ji, le nkon ku nimi. Baan ki gur nimi tijikaar, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan, ni tiwakor, le ni ga kpo.

ref: All over the land that the Lord your God gave you, the enemy army will surround your towns. You may feel safe inside your town walls, but the enemy will tear them down,
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ban u di kitiŋ ki tii nimi na, bi ga tak nimi, nimi aatim mɔmɔk ni. Nimi aagon fɔfɔk ŋi ni maa ki dak ke ŋi pɔɔ na ga lir.

ref: while you wait in horror. Finally, you will get so hungry that you will eat the sons and daughters that the Lord gave you.
text: “Bi yaa lir nimi aatim pu kan, tijikaar aabɔr ga muk nimi, le ni chur nimi aabim bi Nidindaan Uwumbɔr di tii nimi na ŋmɔ.

ref: Because of hunger, a man who had been gentle and kind will eat his own children and refuse to share the meal with his brother or wife or with his other children.
text: Bi yaa lir ni pu kan, hali nimi aaninyuun u nyan ni biyidam do na, tijikaar aabɔr ga muk u, le u chur waabim ku ki ŋmɔ; ba pu? waan ki li kpa tijikaar tibaa. Le waan li gee ke una aabo, bee upuu u u gee u sakpen na, bee waabim bi gur na ubaa kan waah ga ŋmɔ biken na pu na.

ref: A woman may have grown up in such luxury that she never had to put a foot on the ground. But times will be so bad that she will secretly eat both her newborn baby and the afterbirth, without sharing any with her husband or her other children. Disobedience Brings Destruction Moses said to Israel:
text: Upii u mu ye uninyuun, ki nyan ni biyidam do, ki kpa ŋimombil sakpen, kaa nya chuun yɔl yɔl na mu ga ŋa kina la. Nimi aadim yaa lir nimi aatim pu kan, tijikaar aabɔr ga muk upii kina aaboln, le u di waabopɔɔn ni libɔl ŋmɔ. Waan kii ke u tii uchal u u gee u na, bee waabim bi gur na tinann ngbaan bi mu ŋmɔ.

ref: You must obey everything in The Book of God's Law. Because if you don't respect the Lord,
text: “Ni yaa kaa joo mmɔkm mumɔk bi waagbaŋ ni na mbamɔm, ki yaa kaa pak Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aayimbil li kpa kipak ni ijawaan na kan,

ref: Remember! If the Lord decides to destroy your nation, he can use any disease or disaster, not just the ones written in The Book of God's Law.
text: U ga ki cha iween i aaboln baa ŋmee yaabɔr ŋa Uwumbɔr aakaal, ni mmɔkm aagbaŋ ni na, dan ni pu, le ki kuln nimi.

ref: There are as many of you now as the stars in the sky, but if you disobey the Lord your God, only a few of you will be left.
text: Naah wiir ke iŋmabi na, ni ga ti gur siib la, ba pu? ni yii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb.

ref: The Lord is happy to make you successful and to help your nation grow while you conquer the land. But if you disobey him, he will be just as happy to pull you up by your roots.
text: Ni nan mɔ Uwumbɔr le u ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu ki cha ni pɔr, ni ga ki li mɔ u ke u bii ki kuln nimi. Bi ga nyan nimi kitiŋ ki ni ban ni koo ki ponn ni ki gaa ki na ni.

ref: Those of you that survive will be scattered to every nation on earth, and you will have to worship stone and wood idols that never helped you or your ancestors.
text: “Uwumbɔr ga cha ni yaa buen ŋinibol ŋiken mɔmɔk ponn ni, ki di ti nya dulnyaa aapepel libaa ki ti ker liken, nima chee le ni ga doon ŋitakpal ni idɔ aawaa ŋi nimi ni niyaajatiib aa nan nyi dooni ŋi na.

ref: Each morning you will wake up to such terrible sights that you will say, “I wish it were night!” But at night you will be terrified and say, “I wish it were day!”
text: Tiwan nimɔk ninimbil kan ni na ga cha ijawaan chuu nimi. Ni yaa ti joor kijook kan, ni ba ga dakl ke ni li ye kichakpiik ni, le ni yaa woln kichakpiik ni kan, ni ba dak ke ni li ye kijook.

ref: I told you never to go back to Egypt. But now the Lord himself will load you on ships and send you back. Then you will even try to sell yourselves as slaves, but no one will be interested.
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha iŋɔsakpiin giin nimi buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni, nin chee u nan puu ke waan cha ni ki gir buen na. Nima chee le ni ga ti pɔɔn nibaa ke ni di nibaa kooh tii nimi aadim aan ki li ye baanaagbiib, le ubaa mu aan li ban ke u daa nimi.”

ref: So Moses finished telling the Israelites what they had to do in order to keep the agreement the Lord was making with them in Moab, which was in addition to the one the Lord had made with them at Mount Sinai. The Third Speech: Israel Must Keep Its Agreement with the Lord The Lord Is Your God
text: Tipuur timina le Uwumbɔr nan bui Moses ke uma Uwumbɔr puu tii Israel yaab, Moab yaab aatiŋ ni. Tipuur timina le nan ki kpee tipuur ti Uwumbɔr nan puu tii bi Sainai Aajool chee na pu.

ref: Moses called the nation of Israel together and told them: When you were in Egypt, you saw the Lord perform great miracles that caused trouble for the king, his officials, and everyone else in the country.
text: Ninimbil nan kan iween i ku binib na, ni lijinjiir aatuln, ni laasib aawan nimɔk Uwumbɔr nan ŋa na.

ref: When we first camped here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan attacked, but we defeated them.
text: Le taah fuu ni do chee na, Ubɔr Sihonn u nan koo Hesbonn aatiŋ ni na, ni Basann yaab aabɔr u bi nan yin u ke Og na, nyan ni ki nan tak timi.

ref: Then we captured their land and divided it among the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. Keep the Agreement Moses said:
text: Le ti nan nyaŋ bi, ki gaa baatim, le ki yakr baatim ngbaan tii Rubenn aanibol, ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln.

ref: Israel, the Lord has made an agreement with you, and if you keep your part, you will be successful in everything you do.
text: Ni li joo tipuur tee aah mɔk nimi pu na mbamɔm, nima kan, ni ga ŋmaa nyaŋ nimi aatuln mɔmɔk.

ref: In this agreement, the Lord promised that you would be his people and that he would be your God. He first made this promise to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and today the Lord is making this same promise to you. But it isn't just for you; it is also for your descendants.
text: u ban u puu ti tii ti mɔmɔk bi si unimbiin ni do, din wee na, ki kpee tiyaabitiib bi bi taa kee ma bi na mu la.

ref: When we lived in Egypt, you saw the Egyptians worship disgusting idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold. Then as we traveled through other nations, you saw those people worship other disgusting idols.
text: Ni nan kan baawaawanbir ŋi bi di idɔ, ni ŋitakpal, ni tikunabr, ni salmaa ŋa ŋi na.

ref: So make sure that everyone in your tribe remains faithful to the Lord and never starts worshiping gods of other nations. If even one of you worships idols, you will be like the root of a plant that produces bitter, poisonous fruit.
text: Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki taa cha uja, bee upii, bee mmaal, bee linibol li si do din wee na fenn bipuwɔb tii Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ki dooni ŋinibol ngbaan aawaa. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, ni ga li bi ke ulɔnn yaa punn idi ni kan, u ku i pu na la.

ref: You may be an Israelite and know all about the Lord's agreement with us, but he won't bless you if you rebel against him. You may think you can get away with it, but you will cause the rest of Israel to be punished along with you.
text: Ni mɔmɔk ubaa taa ŋmann ubaa ke naah si do din wee ki ŋun tipuur tee na, u ki pɔɔn usui, ki fenn dii ubaa aasan, ki bui ubaa ke nibaa aan ŋa u. Waabimbin ga bii ni mɔmɔk, bi ŋan na, ni bi kaa ŋan na doo.

ref: The Lord will be furious, and instead of forgiving you, he will separate you from the other tribes. Then he will destroy you, by piling on you all the curses in The Book of God's Law, and you will be forgotten forever.
text: Uwumbɔr aah ga ŋa u pu na ga li ye limɔkl, ke Israel yaab aanibol mɔmɔk kan, le tibɔbir timɔk bi tipuur ti ŋmee ki bi Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni na, lir u pu.

ref: The Lord will strike your country with diseases and disasters. Your descendants and foreigners from distant countries will see that your land
text: “Niyaabitiib bi ga paa ni nipuwɔb na, ni biwɔwɔm bi nyan ntim mu daa na ni na, ga nan kan tibɔbir ni falaa u Uwumbɔr di lii nimi aatiŋ pu na.

ref: has become a scorching desert of salt and sulfur, where nothing is planted, nothing sprouts, and nothing grows. It will be as lifeless as the land around the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, after the Lord became angry and destroyed them.
text: Ikpaakon ga kpaln chirbil ni n‑yaan ŋmeen, ubaa aan ŋmaa bu tiwan nibaa ni punn, le timoor mu aan ŋmaa punn. Nima aatiŋ ngbaan ga li bi ke Sodom ni Gomora aatim, ni Adma, ni Seboyim aatim mu Uwumbɔr nan bii mu na la, n‑yoonn mu usui nan fii bi pu sakpen na, le u kuln mu.

ref: People from other nations will ask, “Why did the Lord destroy this country? Why was he so furious?”
text: Le dulnyaa aanib mɔmɔk ga baa ke, ‘Ba ŋa Uwumbɔr ŋa baatiŋ ngbaan kina? Ba ŋa waaŋuul nan fii bi pu sakpen aan u ŋa bi kina?’

ref: And they will be given this answer: Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, but after he brought them out of Egypt and made an agreement with them, they rejected the agreement
text: Le naatataa ga li ye ke, ‘Binib ngbaan bii tipuur ti Uwumbɔr u ye biyaajatiib Aawumbɔr na nan puu tii bi, buyoonn u nan nyan ni bi Ijipt ni na la.

ref: and decided to worship gods that had never helped them. The Lord had forbidden Israel to worship these gods,
text: Bi nan fenn le ki dooni ŋiwaa ŋi baa nan nyi ŋi na. Uwumbɔr nan bui bi ke bi taa doon ŋiwaa.

ref: and so he became furious and punished the land with all the curses in The Book of God's Law. Then he pulled up Israel by the roots and tossed them into a foreign country, where they still are today.
text: Uwumbɔr aaŋuul nan fii bi pu sakpen, le liŋuusakpeln ngbaan ponn ni, u chuu nyan bi baatiŋ ni, ki di bi buen biwɔwɔm aatim ni, le bi bi nima chee din wee.’

ref: The Lord our God hasn't explained the present or the future, but he has commanded us to obey the laws he gave to us and our descendants.
text: “Tiwan ngem bi, le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr di ni bɔr, kaa cha ti nyi ni. Le u tee kpiir Waakaal mɔk timi, ni ŋan ke ti ni timi aabim kii waamɔb, ki li joo i mbamɔm, ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: I have told you everything the Lord your God will do for you, and I've also told you the curses he will put on you if you reject him. He will scatter you in faraway countries, but when you realize that he is punishing you,
text: “Dandana wee, m tii nimi nsan ke ni nyan naah gee tiwan ni na, ni ban tinyoor le aan ni ban ntafadaan la? N‑yoonn mu tiwan nimina mɔmɔk ŋa nimi, aan ni bi ŋinibol ŋiken aatim ni, nin chee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr nan cha nimi aadim chur nimi buen na kan, ni ga teer tibɔr ti m joo tii nimi na.

ref: return to him with all your heart and soul and start obeying the commands I have given to you today.
text: Nimi ni niyaabitiib yaa fenn dan Uwumbɔr chee, ki di nisui mɔmɔk kii waakaal i m joo tii nimi din wee na kan,

ref: Then he will stop punishing you and treat you with kindness. He may have scattered you to the farthest countries on earth, but he will bring you back
text: Hali ni yaa yaa buen dulnyaa aanaanmɔk kan, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga kuun ni nimi tɔb chee ki giin ni nimi,

ref: to the land that had belonged to your ancestors and make you even more successful and powerful than they ever were.
text: le ni ki gaa niyaajatiib aatiŋ. U ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu, ki kpee nimi liwangol, le ni ga moo pɔr ki li wiir jer niyaajatiib aah nan wiir pu na.

ref: You and your descendants are stubborn, but the Lord will make you willing to obey him and love him with all your heart and soul, and you will enjoy a long life.
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ga tii nimi ni niyaabitiib nsui mu kpa limɔkiir na, nima kan, ni ga li gee u nisui ni mbamɔm, ki li bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni.

ref: Then the Lord your God will remove the curses from you and put them on those enemies who hate and attack you.
text: U ga cha ntafadaan ngbaan fenn lir nimi aadim bi nan nimi ki muk nimi na pu.

ref: You will again obey the laws and teachings of the Lord,
text: Le ni ga ki gir kii waah len pu na, ki joo waakaal imɔk m di tuk nimi din wee na.

ref: and he will bless you with many children, large herds and flocks, and abundant crops. The Lord will be happy to do good things for you, just as he did for your ancestors.
text: Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu, nimi aatuln mɔmɔk ni, le ni ga li kpa mbim ni tiwakor pam, le nimi aakpaakon ga ŋa tijikaar pam. U ga li kpa mpopiin ke u tii nimi liwangol, ke waah nan kpa mpopiin ki tii niyaajatiib pu na.

ref: The Lord will listen to you, tribe of Judah, as you beg to come safely home. You fought your enemies alone; now the Lord will help you.

ref: Protecting Israel's agreement with the Lord was more important to you than the life of your father or mother, or brothers or sisters, or your own children.
text: Bi nan mɔk ke bi pak si sakpen, ki jer baah pak bitetiib, ni binatiib, ni binaabitiib, ni baabim pu na. Bi kii saamɔb ki nan joo saah puu tipuur ti na mbamɔm.

ref: You teach God's laws to Israel, and at the place of worship you offer sacrifices and burn incense.
text: Bima le ga mɔk saanib aan bi li joo saakaal mbamɔm; Bima le ga di tiwakor toor kitork saabimbiln paab.

ref: I pray that the Lord will bless everything you do, and make you strong enough to crush your enemies.
text: Uwumbɔr, ter baanibol aan bi li kpa mpɔɔn. Cha aasui li piin baatuln mɔmɔk pu, ki nyaŋ baadim mɔmɔk tii bi, aan bi taa ki ŋmaa ŋa nibaa.”

ref: The Lord Most High loves you, tribe of Benjamin. He will live among your hills and protect you.
text: U nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa Benjaminn aanibol pu ki bui ke; “Linibol limina le Uwumbɔr gee, le ki kii li. Uma le bii bi pu iwiin mɔmɔk, le ki bi bikaasisik ni.”

ref: Descendants of Joseph, the Lord will bless you with precious water from deep wells and with dew from the sky.
text: U nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa Josef aanibol pu ki bui ke; “Uwumbɔr, ŋa tinyoor ŋa baatiŋ pu, ki cha utaal nu, ki cha nnyun mu nyeeni nya kitiŋ aataab na sɔŋ baatiŋ aan ki li kpa tijikaar.

ref: Month by month, your fruit will ripen in the sunshine.
text: Cha nwiin nyii baajikaar pu aan ti biir, aan kitiŋ ngbaan li kpa tijikaar n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: You will have a rich harvest from the slopes of the ancient hills.
text: Uwumbɔr, cha baayaayoonn na aagongon li kpa ŋisubinyaan.

ref: The Lord who appeared in the burning bush wants to give you the best the land can produce, and it will be a princely crown on Joseph's head.
text: Uwumbɔr, cha tiwanyaan mɔmɔk li gbii baatiŋ ni. Uwumbɔr, ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu, ki cha bi kan tiwanyaan mɔmɔk. Sin le nan len tibɔr tisufar ti nan gaal mmii kaa wu na ni. Uwumbɔr cha tinyoor timina mɔmɔk dan Josef aanibol pu, ba pu? uma le ye ukpetiib pu usaloln.

ref: The armies of Ephraim and Manasseh are majestic and fierce like a bull or a wild ox. They will run their spears through faraway nations.
text: Josef aapɔɔn bi le ke unaaja aapɔɔn na, ki pɔɔ ke upɔɔnaa aayiin na, Mubaa le ye Manase aataŋaal ni aanibol aachur na, le muken ye Efraim aataŋaal ni aanibol ŋichur kipiik. U ga di waapɔɔn ngbaan le nyaŋ ŋitimbol ŋi bi na, ki tur ŋi buen dandar.”

ref: The sea will make you wealthy, and from the sandy beach you will get treasure. So invite the other tribes to celebrate with you and offer sacrifices to God.
text: Bi kuuni biwɔwɔm chaa baajool paab, ki ti toor kitork ki Uwumbɔr gee ki na nima chee. Bi kani liwangol sakpen nnyusakpem ni, ni litambol li dɔ kpak nnyusakpem ngbaan na ni.”

ref: Tribe of Gad, the Lord will bless you with more land. So shout his praises! Your tribe is like a lion ripping up its victim.
text: U nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa Gad aanibol pu le ki bui ke, “Pak Uwumbɔr man, uma le tii bi lipepel li wiir na. Gad aamaal gor ki kiir ke uchinn na, ke bi dar par ŋŋaal mubaa, bee liyipaateer paab aagban.

ref: Your leaders met together and chose the best land for your tribe, but you obeyed the Lord and helped the other tribes.
text: Bi nan nyan lipepel li ŋan na, le ki joo bibaa. Bi nan nyan biyidam aasisiiyaan la. Bi nan kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki joo waakaal mbamɔm buyoonn Israel yaab aayidam nan kuun ni na.”

ref: The Lord is pleased with you, people of Naphtali. He will bless you and give you the land to the west and the south.
text: U nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa Naftali aanibol pu le ki bui ke, “Uwumbɔr ŋa tinyoor sakpen ŋa Naftali aanibol pu, ki cha waabulchinn li bi bi chee. Baatiŋ mɔk le yoor ŋŋangii wɔb ki ti ker Galilee Aanyusakpem mɔk.”

ref: The Lord's greatest blessing is for you, tribe of Asher. You will be the favorite of all the other tribes. You will be rich with olive oil
text: U nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa Aser aanibol pu le ki bui ke, “Ŋinibol ngbaan mɔmɔk ni, nimi le kan tinyoor ki jer ŋiken. Uwumbɔr cha ninaabitiib biken li gee nimi, ki cha nimi aatiŋ li kpa olif aakpan aasui sakpen.

ref: and have strong town gates with bronze and iron bolts. Your people will be powerful for as long as they live.
text: Uwumbɔr li kii nimi aatim ke baah di tikur aajaaleŋ tiib le kiir mu na, aan ni li pɔɔ ki ti saa nimi aakundaal.”

ref: Israel, no other god is like ours— the clouds are his chariot as he rides across the skies to come and help us.
text: Israel aanib, ubaa aa ki bi ke nimi Aawumbɔr na, uma le bi paacham, ntaalangbam ni, ki ter nimi.

ref: The eternal God is our hiding place; he carries us in his arms. When God tells you to destroy your enemies, he will make them run.
text: Uwumbɔr le nyaŋni ki kii nimi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. U joo uŋaal mu bi, kaa kpa ndoon na le kii nimi. Naah tur koo nimi aadim ponn ni ki cha na, le u jenn nyan bi tii nimi, le ki bui nimi ke ni kuln bi mɔmɔk.

ref: Israel, you will live in safety; your enemies will be gone. The dew will fall from the sky, and you will have plenty of grain and wine.
text: Nima pu na, le Jakob aayaabitiib bi bibaa pu, ki kpa nsuudoon, ni mpɔɔn, ki bi kitiŋ ki gbii tijikaar, ni ŋisubil aadaan na, nin chee limaln nyani kitaapaak ki sɔŋni kitiŋ ngbaan n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na.

ref: The Lord has rescued you and given you more blessings than any other nation. He protects you like a shield and is your majestic sword. Your enemies will bow in fear, and you will trample on their backs.
text: Israel yaab, ni kpa mpopiin pam. Lilanibol kpa liyimɔɔn ke nimi na? Nimi aatimbol le Uwumbɔr gaa li lii. Uwumbɔr ubaa le ye nimi aakikiir, ki ter nimi, ki ga li kii nimi, ki tii nimi linyaŋ. Nimi aadim ga san nimi ijawaan ki gaŋ nimi ke ni san bi kinimbaak, le ni ga taa taa bi pu.

ref: Sometime later, Moses left the lowlands of Moab. He went up Mount Pisgah to the peak of Mount Nebo, which is across the Jordan River from Jericho. The Lord showed him all the land as far north as Gilead and the town of Dan.
text: Moses nan nyan Moab aateer ni, le ki buen Nebo Aajool wɔb, ki ti jon Pisga Aajool li bi Jeriko aawipuul wɔb na. Lijool ngbaan paab, le Uwumbɔr nan mɔk u kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk; u nan mɔk u Gilead aapepel mɔmɔk, ki yoor kina ki ti ker Dann aatiŋ, ŋŋangan wɔb,

ref: He let Moses see the territories that would soon belong to the tribes of Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Judah, as far west as the Mediterranean Sea.
text: ki mɔk u Naftali aapepel aah di ti ker pu na, ni Efraim, ni Manase aapepel mu aah di ti ker pu na; ki kpee Juda aapepel mu aah yoor pu ki ti ker liwilir wɔb, Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem chee pu na,

ref: The Lord also showed him the land in the south, from the valley near the town of Jericho, known as The City of Palm Trees, down to the town of Zoar.
text: ki di kina ki ti ker Juda aaŋangii wɔb, ki kpee nteer mu dɔ Soar aatiŋ ni, ki ti ker Jeriko aatiŋ aafataŋ ni na; bi yin Jeriko aatiŋ le ke ŋibɔkpal aasui aatiŋ na.

ref: The Lord said, “Moses, this is the land I was talking about when I solemnly promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that I would give land to their descendants. I have let you see it, but you will not cross the Jordan and go in.”
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui Moses ke, “Kitiŋ kee le m nan puu tii Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob, ke m ga di ki tii biyaabitiib na. M cha aanimbil le kan ki, maan cha aa koo ki ni.”

ref: And so, Moses the Lord's servant died there in Moab, just as the Lord had said.
text: Nima pu na, Moses, u nan ye Uwumbɔr aatutunn na, nan kpo Moab yaab aatiŋ ni, Uwumbɔr aah nan siin pu na.

ref: The Lord buried him in a valley near the town of Beth-Peor, but even today no one knows exactly where.
text: Le Uwumbɔr nan sub u Moab yaab aatiŋ aafataŋ ki dɔ tok Bef Peor aatiŋ na ni. Hali ki di nan saa n‑yoonn mue na, ubaa aa nyi Moses aakaakul chee.

ref: The people of Israel stayed in the lowlands of Moab, where they mourned and grieved
text: Israel yaab nan ŋa waakpuul, Moab yaab aafataŋ ngbaan ni, ki ti saa iwiin piitaa la.

ref: Before Moses died, he had placed his hands on Joshua, and the Lord had given Joshua wisdom. The Israelites paid attention to what Joshua said and obeyed the commands that the Lord had given Moses. Moses Was a Great Prophet
text: Le Nunn aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Josua na nan kpa nlan mu nyani Uwumbɔr chee na, ba pu? Moses nan nyan uma le ke u gaa waasisiiyaan. Israel aanib nan kii Josua aamɔb, ki mu joo ikaal imɔk Uwumbɔr nan di mɔk Moses aan u mu di i tii bi na.

ref: There has never again been a prophet in Israel like Moses. The Lord spoke face to face with him
text: Israel yaab aatiŋ ni, Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ubaa aa kee nyan ki bi ke Moses aah nan bi pu na, le Uwumbɔr nan len Moses chee tibɔr.

ref: and sent him to perform powerful miracles in the presence of the king of Egypt and his entire nation.
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ubaa aa kee ŋa iwaan, ni lijinjiir aawan ni Uwumbɔr nan cha Moses ŋa Ijipt yaab aabɔr, ni waayidam, ni waatiŋ mɔmɔk pu na.

ref: No one else has ever had the power to do such great things as Moses did for everyone to see.
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ubaa aa kee ŋa ijawaan aawan ni Moses nan ŋa Israel yaab mɔmɔk aanimbiin ni na.

ref: Moses, the Lord's servant, was dead. So the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, who had been the assistant of Moses. The Lord said:
text: Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses aah nan kpo na aapuwɔb, le Uwumbɔr bui Moses aateter Josua u nan ye Nunn aajapɔɔn na ke,

ref: My servant Moses is dead. Now you must lead Israel across the Jordan River into the land I'm giving to all of you.
text: “Maatutunn Moses kpo a. Gor dandana wee, aa ni Israel yaab ngbaan mɔmɔk, aan ni puur Jɔɔdann aamɔɔl, ki koo kitiŋ ki m ban m di ki tii nimi na ni.

ref: It will reach from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains in the north, and to the northeast as far as the great Euphrates River. It will include the land of the Hittites, and the land from here at the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea on the west.
text: Nimi aatinaanmɔk ga yoor ŋŋangii wɔb aateersakpiin ni, ki ti saa Lebanonn aajoo ŋi bi ŋŋangan wɔb na, ki ki yoor Yufrates Aamɔɔl mɔk, liwipuul wɔb, ki di bɔ dii Hef yaab aatiŋ ni, ki ti saa Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk, liwilir wɔb.

ref: Joshua, I will always be with you and help you as I helped Moses, and no one will ever be able to defeat you.
text: Josua, saah ga li bi limɔfal ni ki ti saa buyoonn na, ubaa aa bi ki ga ŋmaa nyaŋ si. M ga li bi aa chee ke maah nan bi Moses chee pu na; maan di si lii kpala.

ref: Long ago I promised the ancestors of Israel that I would give this land to their descendants. So be strong and brave! Be careful to do everything my servant Moses taught you. Never stop reading The Book of the Law he gave you. Day and night you must think about what it says. If you obey it completely, you and Israel will be able to take this land.
text: Ni yaa ti ban ni doon mi kan, ni chuu nibaa ki li karni ikaal aagbaŋ ngbaan, ki li bae ikaal ngbaan nwiin pu ni kinyeek, ki chuu aabaa ki kii iliin imɔk bi ki ponn ni na. Nima kan, aa ga kan tinyoor ki li nyaŋni tiwan mɔmɔk ponn ni.

ref: I've commanded you to be strong and brave. Don't ever be afraid or discouraged! I am the Lord your God, and I will be there to help you wherever you go. The Eastern Tribes Promise To Help
text: Teer ke m tuk si ke aa pɔɔn aabaa ki li kpa lipobil. Taa san ijawaan, ki taa cha aawon yɔl. Min, Aadindaan Uwumbɔr ma kan, m ga li bi aa chee saah cha nin chee na mɔmɔk.” Josua aah nan bui Israel yaab pu na

ref: Joshua ordered the tribal leaders
text: Le Josua bui Israel yaab aayidam

ref: to go through the camp and tell everyone: In a few days we will cross the Jordan River to take the land that the Lord our God is giving us. So prepare as much food as you'll need for the march into the land.
text: ke bi bɔ dii binib ngbaan ponn ni ki tuk bi ke, “Gor man ki ban tijikaar; ba pu? ni gur iwiin itaa, ti ga puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl, ki koo kitiŋ ki Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ga di tii timi na ni.”

ref: Joshua told the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
text: Josua nan bui Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln libaa ke,

ref: conquer the land that the Lord is giving them. The Lord will give peace to them as he has given peace to you, and then you can come back and settle here in the land that Moses promised you.
text: aan bi ti gaa ki koo kitiŋ ki bi Jɔɔdann aawilir wɔb aan Nidindaan Uwumbɔr di tii bi na. N‑yoonn mu u ti tii Israel aanibol mɔmɔk lifuur na kan, ni ga ŋmaa gir dan ki nan kal nibaa aatiŋ pu, Jɔɔdann aawipuul wɔb, kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses nan di tii nimi na.”

ref: The men answered: We'll cross the Jordan River and help our relatives. We'll fight anywhere you send us.
text: Le bi kii tii Josua ki gar u ke, “Ti ga ŋa saah tuk timi pu na, ki buen saah ga tun timi nin chee na mɔmɔk.

ref: If the Lord our God will help you as he helped Moses, and if you are strong and brave, we will obey you as we obeyed Moses. We'll even put to death anyone who rebels against you or refuses to obey you.
text: Unii umɔk kpak si ki yii saah len pu na kan, udaan ŋeer bi ku u. Pɔɔn aabaa ki li kpa lipobil.”

ref: Joshua chose two men as spies and sent them from their camp at Acacia with these instructions: “Go across the river and find out as much as you can about the whole region, especially about the town of Jericho.” The two spies left the Israelite camp at Acacia and went to Jericho, where they decided to spend the night at the house of a prostitute named Rahab.
text: Baah nan bi Sitim aatiŋ ni na, le Josua tun bipepekr bilee, ke bi buen Kanaann aatiŋ ni, ki loon lik ke Jeriko aatisakpeŋ aanib bi kinye. N‑yoonn mu bi ti fuu kitisakpeŋ ngbaan ni na, le bi buen pateer u bi nan yin u ke Rahab na do.

ref: But someone found out about them and told the king of Jericho, “Some Israelite men came here tonight, and they are spies.”
text: Le Jeriko aabɔr ŋun ke Israel yaab bibaa koo ni waatiŋ ponn ni kinyeek ngbaan ke bi pekr ki,

ref: Rahab went back up to her roof. The spies were still awake, so she told them:
text: Waahr aan bipepekr ngbaan nin doon kinyeek ngbaan na, Rahab nan buen bi chee paacham nima,

ref: I know that the Lord has given Israel this land. Everyone shakes with fear because of you.
text: le ki ti bui bi ke, “M bee ke Uwumbɔr le di kitiŋ kee tii nimi. Unii umɔk bi kitiŋ kee ni na aapobil yuk ni pu la.

ref: We heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea so you could leave Egypt. And we heard how you destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
text: Ti ŋun Uwumbɔr aah cha Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem foor aan ni puur, buyoonn ni nan nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, ki ki ŋun ke ni ku Amor yaab aabɔrb bilee, Sihonn ni Og, Jɔɔdann aawipuul wɔb.

ref: We know that the Lord your God rules heaven and earth, and we've lost our courage and our will to fight.
text: Taah ŋun kina na, le ijawaan chuu timi, ti mɔmɔk aataakpab yɔl ni pu a. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le ye paacham ni kitiŋ mɔmɔk Aawumbɔr.

ref: Please promise me in the Lord's name that you will be as kind to my family as I have been to you. Do something to show
text: Nima pu na, puu man Waayimbil pu ke ni ga ŋa maamaal tiŋann ke maah ŋa nimi pu na. Tii mi limɔkl man, ke ni ga sil ŋa kina.

ref: that you won't let your people kill my father and mother and my brothers and sisters and their families.
text: Puu tipuur ke ni ga gaa nte, ni nna, ni nninjatiib, ni nnaatiib, ni baamaal mɔmɔk lii. Ni taa cha bi ku timi.”

ref: “Rahab,” the spies answered, “if you keep quiet about what we're doing, we promise to be kind to you when the Lord gives us this land. We pray that the Lord will kill us if we don't keep our promise!”
text: Le bijab ngbaan bui u ke, “Aa yaa gaa timi lii kan, ti mu ga gaa nimi lii. Aa yaa kaa tuk unii ubaa taah chuun pu na kan, ti puu ke Uwumbɔr yaa di kitiŋ kee tii timi kan, ti ga ŋa nimi tiŋann.”

ref: Rahab's house was built into the town wall, and one of the windows in her house faced outside the wall. She gave the spies a rope, showed them the window, and said, “Use this rope to let yourselves down to the ground outside the wall.
text: Rahab aadichal nan bi kitiŋ ngbaan aagoln le pu, nima pu na, u nan cha bijab ngbaan di iŋmin le dii takolu nyan.

ref: Then hide in the hills. The men who are looking for you won't be able to find you there. They'll give up and come back after a few days, and you can be on your way.”
text: U nan bui bi ke, “Li cha ŋigongon ŋee ni man. Ni yaa kaa ŋa kina kan, ubɔr aanib ngbaan ga kan nimi. Ni bɔr nima ki ti saa iwiin itaa, aan nima kan, ubɔr aanib ngbaan ga gir ni. Nee aapuwɔb, ni ga ŋmaa nya ki buen.”

ref: “I'll do exactly what you said,” Rahab promised. Then she sent them on their way and tied the red rope to the window.
text: U nan kii baah len pu na, le ki cha bi buen. N‑yoonn mu bi nyan buen na, le u di tikokomann na gbin takolu ngbaan.

ref: The spies hid in the hills for three days while the king's soldiers looked for them along the roads. As soon as the soldiers gave up and returned to Jericho,
text: Le bipepekr ngbaan buen ŋigongon na ni, le ki ti bɔr nima. Ubɔr aajab na nan chuun mann gonni kitiŋ ngbaan aatingbaan iwiin itaa, kaa kan bi, le ki gir kun ni.

ref: the two spies went down into the Jordan valley and crossed the river. They reported to Joshua and told him everything that had happened.
text: Le bipepekr bilee ngbaan nyan ni ŋigongon ngbaan ni, ki puur limɔɔl, le ki buen Josua chee. Bi nan tuk u tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋa na,

ref: “We're sure the Lord has given us the whole country,” they said. “The people there shake with fear every time they think of us.”
text: le ki bui ke, “Ni sil ye mbamɔn, Uwumbɔr le di kitiŋ ngbaan tii timi. Binib bimɔk bi nima na aapobil fii a.”

ref: Early the next morning, Joshua and the Israelites packed up and left Acacia. They went to the Jordan River and camped there that night.
text: Naah woln kichakpiik ni na, Josua ni Israel aanib ngbaan mɔmɔk nan fii lichakpitaawoln, le ki nyan Sitim aatiŋ ni, ki buen Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee. Bi nan bi nima chee ki kii nwiin mu bi ga puur li na.

ref: Two days later their leaders went through the camp,
text: Iwiin itaa aapuwɔb le Israel yaab aayidam nan fii ki moon binib ngbaan mɔmɔk,

ref: shouting, “When you see some of the priests carrying the sacred chest, you'll know it is time to cross to the other side. You've never been there before, and you won't know the way, unless you follow the chest. But don't get too close! Stay about a kilometer back.”
text: Naa nyi do kpala, nima pu na, bima le ga mɔk nimi nsan. Ubaa taa ŋɔŋ Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan chee, ni li paa u pu, ki li daa u ki pii ŋitaa ŋichur ŋitaa.”

ref: Joshua told the people, “Make yourselves acceptable to worship the Lord, because he is going to do some amazing things for us.”
text: Le Josua bui binib ngbaan ke, “Toor nibaa man, ba pu? Uwumbɔr ga fe ŋa lijinjiir aatuln nikaasisik ni.”

ref: Then Joshua turned to the priests and said, “Take the chest and cross the Jordan River ahead of us.” So the priests picked up the chest by its carrying poles and went on ahead.
text: Josua nan bui bitotoorb ke bi yoor Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aan ki loln binib ngbaan pu nsan, le bi ŋa waah len pu na.

ref: The Lord told Joshua, “Beginning today I will show the people that you are their leader, and they will know that I am helping you as I helped Moses.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Josua ke, “Maah ga ŋa tiwan ni din wee na le ga cha Israel aanib ngbaan mɔmɔk piin ki li nyuŋni si ke uyidaan na, bi ga bee ke m bi aa chee ke maah nan bi Moses chee pu na.

ref: Now, tell the priests who are carrying the chest to go a little way into the river and stand there.”
text: Tuk bitotoorb bi tu Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan na ke bi yaa ti fuu limɔɔl ni kan, bi koo nnyun ngbaan ni, ki sil nnyun ponn ni n‑gbaan.”

ref: Joshua spoke to the people: Come here and listen to what the Lord our God said he will do!
text: Josua nan ki bui binib ngbaan ke, “Ni dan ki nan pel Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ban u len pu na man.

ref: The Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites control the land on the other side of the river. But the living God will be with you and will force them out of the land when you attack. And now, God is going to prove that he's powerful enough to force them out.
text: Mbamɔn, naah tur cha pu na, u ga jenn nyan Kanaann yaab, ni Hef yaab, ni Hif yaab, ni Peris yaab, ni Girgas yaab, ni Amor yaab, ni Jebus yaab.

ref: Just watch the sacred chest that belongs to the Lord, the ruler of the whole earth. As soon as the priests carrying the chest step into the Jordan, the water will stop flowing and pile up as if someone had built a dam across the river. The Lord has also said that each of the twelve tribes should choose one man to represent it.
text: N‑yoonn mu bitotoorb bi tu Uwumbɔr u yeh dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk na Aakaal Aadakaa na yaa ti di bitaa ŋa nnyun ponn ni kan, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aanyun ngbaan ga sil libubaan ni.”

ref: until they came to the Jordan River. The water in the river had risen over its banks, as it often does in springtime. But as soon as the feet of the priests touched the water,
text: Ni nan ye tijikaar aacheen yoonn la, le limɔɔl ngbaan nan gbii nnyun, nwam mu nyan. N‑yoonn mu binib ngbaan nan fii ki ban bi puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl na, le bitotoorb loln bi pu nsan, ki tu Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa ngbaan. Bitotoorb ngbaan aataa aah ti koo limɔɔl ngbaan aanyun ni buyoonn na,

ref: the river stopped flowing, and the water started piling up at the town of Adam near Zarethan. No water flowed toward the Dead Sea, and the priests stood in the middle of the dry riverbed near Jericho while everyone else crossed over.

ref: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
text: Josua nan nyaŋ kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk, Uwumbɔr aah nan bui Moses ke u ŋa pu na. Le Josua nan di kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk tii Israel yaab, ki li ye biyaan; u nan yakr ki tii Israel yaab aanibol ngbaan. Le Israel yaab kan lifuur, kaa ki to butɔb.

ref: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
text: Israel yaab nan puen nyaŋ ki gaa kitiŋ ki bi Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl liwipuul wɔb na, ki yoor Anonn Aafataŋ ni ki ti saa Jɔɔdann Aafataŋ, ki ti ker ŋŋangan, Hemonn Aajool wɔb. Bi nan nyaŋ bibɔrb bilee la.

ref: The first king that Moses and the Israelites defeated was an Amorite, King Sihon of Heshbon. The southern border of his kingdom ran down the middle of the Arnon River gorge, taking in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the gorge. The Jabbok River separated Sihon's kingdom from the Ammonites on the east. Then the Jabbok turned west and became his northern border, so his kingdom included the southern half of the region of Gilead.
text: Ubaa le nan ye Amor yaab aabɔr u bi nan yin u ke Sihonn na, uma le nan jin nnaan Hesbonn aatiŋ ni. Waanaan ngbaan le nan ye Gilead aapepel ligeln, ki nyan Aroer aatiŋ ki bi Anonn Aafataŋ aamɔgben na, ni kitiŋ ki bi kifataŋ ngbaan aakaasisik ni na, ki ti ker Jabok Aamɔɔl li ye Amonn yaab aatiŋ mɔk na,

ref: Sihon also controlled the eastern side of the Jordan River valley from Lake Galilee south to Beth-Jeshimoth and the Dead Sea. In addition to these regions, he ruled the town called Slopes of Mount Pisgah and the land south of there at the foot of the hill.
text: ki kpee Jɔɔdann Aafataŋ ni, ki yoor Galilee Aanyusakpem, ŋŋangii wɔb, ki ti ker Bef Jesimof ki bi N‑yaan Aanyusakpem aawipuul wɔb na, ki di toŋ Pisga Aajool aataab na.

ref: Next, Moses and the Israelites defeated King Og of Bashan, who lived in the town of Ashtaroth part of each year and in Edrei the rest of the year. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim.
text: Bi nan ki nyaŋ Basann aabɔr u bi nan yin u ke Og na, uma le nan ye ubɔr u gbeln kookoo, ŋiwɔk Refa yaab ni na. Uma le nan jin nnaan Astarof ni Edrei aatim ni.

ref: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
text: Waanaan ngbaan le nan ki joo Hemonn Aajool, ni Saleka aatiŋ, ni Basann aatim mu, ki yoor kina ki ti ker Gesur ni Maaka aatim mɔk, ni Gilead aapepel ligeln, ki ti saa Hesbonn aabɔr Sihonn aapepel.

ref: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
text: Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses ni Israel yaab le nan nyaŋ bibɔrb bilee ngbaan. Moses nan di baatim ngbaan tii Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln, mu li ye baatim. Josua aah nan nyaŋ bibɔrb bi na

ref: Later, Joshua and the Israelites defeated many kings west of the Jordan River, from Baal-Gad in Lebanon Valley in the north to Mount Halak near the country of Edom in the south. This region included the hill country and the foothills, the Jordan River valley and its western slopes, and the Southern Desert. Joshua and the Israelites took this land from the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. Joshua divided up the land among the tribes of Israel. The Israelites defeated the kings of the following towns west of the Jordan River:
text: Kitiŋ ngbaan le nan ye ŋigongon aatiŋ, ni ŋigongon aataab aatim mu bi liwilir wɔb na, ni Jɔɔdann aafataŋ aatiŋ, ni ntim mu bi kifataŋ ngbaan, ŋigongon aataab, ki chaan cha liwipuul wɔb na, ni nteer aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangii wɔb na. Binib bimina le nan yeh kitiŋ ngbaan: Hef yaab, ni Amor yaab, ni Kanaann yaab, ni Peris yaab, ni Hif yaab, ni Jebus yaab.

ref: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
text: N‑yoonn mue na, Josua nan por pam. Le Uwumbɔr bui u ke, “Aa por pam, ntim laa beenin wiir ke ni gaa mu.

ref: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
text: Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln nan kan kitiŋ ki ga li ye baatiŋ na. Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses nan puen yakr ki tii bi, ki nan bi Jɔɔdann aamɔɔdapuul, liwipuul wɔb la.

ref: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
text: Baatiŋ mɔk nan yoor ki ti ker Aroer aatiŋ mɔk, ki nan bi Anonn Aafataŋ aamɔgben la, ni kitiŋ ki nan bi kifataŋ ngbaan aakaasisik ni na, ki kpee Medeba aatiŋ, ki ti ker Dibonn aatiŋ mɔk na,

ref: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
text: ki ki yoor kina ki ti ker Amonn yaab aatinaanmɔk, ki kpee ntim mu Amor yaab aabɔr u bi nan yin u ke Sihonn na nan joo mu na, waatiyil nan ye Hesbonn la,

ref: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
text: Mbamɔn, Israel yaab aa nan jenn nyan Gesur ni Maaka yaab, bi laa beenin bi Israel aatiŋ ni.

ref: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
text: Moses aa nan yakr kitiŋ tii Liifai aanibol. Uwumbɔr aah nan bui Moses pu na, Liifai yaab le nan yeh tiwan nimɔk binib nan joo toor kitork ki seer mmii ni tii Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr na aanann ngem. Kitiŋ ki bi nan di tii Rubenn aanibol na

ref: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
text: Moses nan yakr kitiŋ ngbaan aapepel nibaa chee tii imaal i ye Rubenn aanibol na, ke ki li ye baatiŋ.

ref: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
text: Baatiŋ nan yoor ki ti ker Aroer mɔk, ki nan bi Anonn Aafataŋ aamɔgben la, ni kitiŋ ki bi kifataŋ ngbaan aakaasisik ni na, le ki kpee ntim mu mann gonn Medeba aatiŋ na,

ref: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
text: ki kpee ntim mu bi lijool li aapaacham bi taarr na, ni Amor aabɔr Sihonn aanaan mu aatiyil nan ye Hesbonn na. Moses le nan nyaŋ u, ki kpee Midiann yaab aabɔrb bi bi nan yin bi ke Efi, ni Rekem, ni Sur, ni Hur, ni Reba na. Bibɔrb ngbaan mɔmɔk nan joo Midiann yaab tii ubɔr Sihonn la.

ref: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
text: Israel yaab aah nan ku bi ponn ni bi na ubaa le nan ye Beor aajapɔɔn Balaam u nan ye ubɔɔ na.

ref: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
text: Jɔɔdann aamɔɔl mɔk le nan ye Rubenn aanibol aatiŋ aawilir wɔb aapepel aanaanmɔk. Ntim ngbaan le bi nan di tii Rubenn aanibol, mu li ye baatim. Kitiŋ ki bi nan di tii Gad aanibol na

ref: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
text: Moses nan ki di kitiŋ ngbaan lipepel libaa di tii Gad aanibol, ki li ye baatiŋ.

ref: It included the town of Jazer, and in the Gilead region their territory took in the land and towns as far east as the town of Aroer just west of Rabbah. This was about half of the land that had once belonged to the Ammonites.
text: Baatiŋ mɔk le nan ye Jaser, ni ntim mu bi Gilead ni na, ni Amonn yaab aatiŋ ligeln ki yoor ti ker Aroer mɔk, ki nan bi Raba aatiŋ aawipuul wɔb la.

ref: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
text: Baatiŋ nan ki yoor ki nyan Hesbonn aatiŋ, ki ti saa Ramaf Mispa, ni Betonim; ki nyan Mahanaim aatiŋ, ki di naa Lodebar aatiŋ mɔk na,

ref: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
text: ki kpaan Jɔɔdann aafataŋ aatim mu bi yin mu ke Bef Haram, ni Bef Nimra, ni Sukof, ni Safonn mɔk, ni nan ye ubɔr Sihonn u nan ka Hesbonn aatiŋ na aanaan mu gur na la. Liwilir wɔb, baatiŋ aanaanmɔk le nan ye Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ki ti ker ŋŋangan wɔb, Galilee Aanyusakpem chee,

ref: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
text: ntim ngbaan le bi nan di tii Gad aanibol aamaal ke mu li ye baatiŋ. Kitiŋ ki bi nan di tii Manase aanibol ligeln li bi liwipuul wɔb na

ref: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
text: Moses nan di kitiŋ ngbaan lipepel libaa wɔb tii Manase aanibol aamaal ligeln li gur na, aan ki li ye baatiŋ.

ref: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
text: ki nan ki kpee Gilead aatiŋ ligeln, ki ti kpaan Astarof ni Edrei aatim, muma le nan ye ntikpaam ubɔr Og aanaan ni, ki bi Basann aatiŋ ni. Bi nan di kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk tii Manase aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Makir na le aamaal ligeln.

ref: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
text: Kina le Moses nan yakr kitiŋ ki nan bi Jeriko aawipuul wɔb, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔdapuul na, n‑yoonn mu u nan bi Moab aateer pu na.

ref: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
text: Moses aa nan tii Liifai yaab ma aanibol kitiŋ kibaa kpala. U nan tuk bi ke baawan le ga li ye ipiin i Israel yaab joo nan tii bima Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr na, bi ga li ji ipiin ngbaan ponn ni la.

ref: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
text: Nwiin mubaa daal le Juda aanibol aanib bibaa nan dan Josua chee, Gilgal aatiŋ ni. Bi ponn ni ubaa le nan ye Jefune aajapɔɔn, u bi nan yin u ke Kaleb na; u nan ye Kenis aanibol ni aanii la, le u bui Josua ke, “Aa teer Uwumbɔr aah nan len pu Kades Banea aatiŋ ni, m ni si aabɔr, ki tuk uma Uwumbɔr aanii Moses pu na.

ref: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
text: Le bijab bi nan dii mi buen na aah nan len pu na cha ijawaan chuu timi aanib, le m ma nan kii Ndindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb mbamɔm.

ref: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
text: Maah nan ŋa kina na, le Moses nan puu ke u ga di kitiŋ ki m nan chuun ki pu na tii m ni maamaal, ki li ye timi aatiŋ.

ref: I'm just as strong today as I was then, and I can still fight as well in battle.
text: le m laa beenin kpa mpɔɔn din ke maah nan kpa pu buyoonn Moses nan tun mi na. M laa beenin kpa mpɔɔn ki ga ŋmaa buen likumbool, ki ga ŋmaa ŋa tiwan mɔmɔk.

ref: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
text: Nima pu na, di ŋigongon pu aatiŋ tii mi, Uwumbɔr aah nan puu tipuur tii mi n‑yoonn ngbaan pu na. Ti nan tuk si liyaadaal ngbaan ke ŋiwɔk aanib, bi bi nan yin bi ke Anak yaab na, nan bi ntisakpem mu aagon fɔk na ni. Uwumbɔr yaa bi m chee ki ter mi kan, m ga jenn nyan bi ke waah nan len pu na.”

ref: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
text: Josua nan mee Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa Jefune aajapɔɔn Kaleb pu, le ki di Hebronn aatiŋ tii u, ke ki li ye waatiŋ.

ref: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
text: Jefune aajapɔɔn Kaleb aamaal beenin yeh Hebronn aatiŋ ngbaan, bi ye Kenis aanibol ni aanib la. Kaleb aah nan kii Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb pu na, le u nyan kitiŋ ngbaan tii u.

ref: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
text: Waahr aan nimina nin ŋa kina na, bi nan yin Hebronn aatiŋ ngbaan ke Aba aatiŋ la. Aba le nan ye ŋiwɔk Anak yaab aanikpaan. N‑yoonn ngbaan le Israel yaab aatiŋ nan kan nsuudoon.

ref: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
text: Kaanaanmɔk, ŋŋangii wɔb, nan yoor N‑yaan Aanyusakpem aaŋangii wɔb,

ref: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
text: ki di nyan ŋŋangii wɔb, Akrabim Aajool aasan chee, ki di buen Sinn Aateersakpiin ni. Kitiŋ ngbaan yoor ki dii Kades Banea aatiŋ ni, ŋŋangii wɔb, ki kpak Hesronn aatiŋ kina, ki ti ker Adar aatiŋ ni, ki fenn di kpaa Kaka wɔb,

ref: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
text: ki di buen Asmonn aatiŋ wɔb, le ki dii mbun mu bi Ijipt aatiŋ mɔk na, ki ti saa Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem nin chee kitiŋ mɔk doo na. Juda yaab aatiŋ, ŋŋangii wɔb aanaanmɔk le na.

ref: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
text: Liwipuul wɔb aanaanmɔk le nan ye N‑yaan Aanyusakpem, ki yoor kina ki dii nnyusakpem ngbaan aagbaan, ki ti saa nin chee Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl puu koo mu ponn ni na. Kitiŋ ngbaan aah piin nin chee ŋŋangan wɔb na yoor Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aah doo nin chee na,

ref: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
text: ki yoor kina ki ti ker Bef Hogla aatiŋ mɔk, le ki dii buen kidunduŋ ki bi Jɔɔdann aafataŋ chee na aaŋangan wɔb, le ki dii kina buen Bohann, u nan ye Rubenn aajapɔɔn na, aatakpal chee,

ref: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
text: ki yoor ni Tibɔbir Aafataŋ mɔk, ki ti nyan Debir aatiŋ pu, le ki fenn ŋŋangan wɔb ki di kpaa Gilgal aatiŋ, ki ni Adumim Aajool Aasan lik tɔb na, ki bi kifataŋ aaŋangii wɔb na, le ki yoor kina ki buen Ensemes aanyunbun wɔb, ki nyan nima ti pii Enn Rogel,

ref: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
text: le ki bɔ nyan Hinom Aafataŋ ki bi ligongoln li Jebus yaab aatiŋ Jerusalem bi li paab na aaŋangii wɔb, le kimɔk ki yoor kina ki di dii ligongoln li bi Hinom Aafataŋ liwilir wɔb na paab, Refaim Aafataŋ aaŋangan wɔb,

ref: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
text: ki nyan nima chee, ki dii kina buen Neftoa Aanyunbun chee, le ki ti ker ntim mu bi Efronn Aajool chee na. Nima chee le ki fenn kpaa Baala aatiŋ ni; bi ki yin ki ke Kiriaf Jearim aatiŋ.

ref: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
text: Nima chee le ki mann gonn Baala aatiŋ liwilir wɔb, ki fenn kpaa ŋigongon aatiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Edom na, le ki di dii buen Jearim, bee Kesalonn, Aajool aaŋangan wɔb, ki di sunn taab ki ti ker Bef Semes, le ki dii Timna aatiŋ ni.

ref: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
text: U nan nyan nima chee le ki buen ti lir Debir aanib pu. Njan bi nan yin kitiŋ ngbaan ke Kiriaf Sefer aatiŋ la.

ref: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
text: Uwumbɔr aah nan bui Josua ke u ŋa pu na, u nan di Juda aatiŋ aapepel nibaa chee tii Jefune aajapɔɔn Kaleb, u nan ye Juda aanibol aanii ubaa na. Bi nan di Hebronn aatiŋ, ki nan ye Aba u nan ye ŋiwɔk Anak yaab aate na aatiŋ le tii u.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
text: Kaleb nan jenn Anak aamaal mɔmɔk nyan kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni, bi nan ye Sesai yaab, ni Ahimann yaab, ni Talmai yaab aanib la.

ref: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
text: Kaleb nan bui ke, “Uja u ga ŋmaa to butɔb ki nyaŋ Kiriaf Sefer aatiŋ na kan, m ga di mbisal Aksa tii udaan ngbaan u di u ŋa upuu.”

ref: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
text: Waah kunn u bundaal na, le Otniel bui upuu Aksa ke u mee ute kitiŋ ki ŋan na. Le Aksa buen ute chee, ki sunn ubon pu, le Kaleb baa u ke u ban ba.

ref: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
text: Le u giin bui u ke, “M ban kitiŋ ki kpa nnyun na la. Saah di kitiŋ ki tii mi na, ki bi nteer pu la.” Nima pu le Kaleb nan di paacham ni taab aanyunbun aatiŋ na tii u. Ntim mu ye Juda aanibol aatim na

ref: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
text: Ntim mu Juda aanibol nan kan aan mu ye baatim na sɔ:

ref: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
text: ni Lebaof, ni Silim, ni Ayinn, ni Rimonn aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti saa moninko ni muwae la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.

ref: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
text: ni Saarayim, ni Aditayim, ni Gedera, ni Gederotayim aatim: ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ti saa kipiik ni munaa, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.

ref: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
text: ni Gederof, ni Bef Dagonn, ni Naama, ni Makeda aatim: ntim ngbaan nan ti saa kipiik ni muloob la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.

ref: The fourth region was located in the central part of the lower foothills, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages: Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah.
text: ni Keila, ni Aksib, ni Maresa aatim: mu nan ti saa ntim muwae la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.

ref: The fifth region was located along the Mediterranean seacoast, and it had the following towns with their surrounding settlements and villages: Ekron and the towns between there and the coast, Ashdod and the larger towns nearby, Gaza, the towns from Gaza to the Egyptian Gorge, and the towns along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Ntim mu nan ki bi na le nan ye Asdod ni Gasa aatim, ni itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na, le ki yoor kina ki ti ker mbun mu ye Ijipt aatiŋ mɔk na, ni Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem aagbaan.

ref: The sixth region was in the southwestern part of the hill country, and it had the following eleven towns with their surrounding villages: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, Dannah, Kiriath-Sannah, which is now called Debir, Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, and Giloh.
text: ni Gosenn, ni Holonn, ni Gilo aatim: mu nan ti saa kipiik ni kibaa la, le ki kpee itingbaan i bi gbɔk mu na.

ref: The seventh region was located in the south-central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages: Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth-Tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath-Arba, which is now called Hebron, and Zior.
