text: Israel yaab aah nan too inaan ki mee Uwumbɔr, aan u mɔk bi baah ga nyan ntim ni timopɔr ki tii Liifai aanibol pu na le na, kina le u nan bui Moses ke bi ŋa.

ref: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
text: Ntim ngbaan mɔmɔk nan kpaan kipiik ni mutaa la, ni mu aamopɔr, bi nan di mu tii bitotoorb bi nan ye Aaronn aayaabitiib na la.

ref: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
text: Uwumbɔr nan di kitiŋ ki u nan puu tii Israel yaab aayaajatiib ke u ga di ki tii bi na tii bi. N‑yoonn mu bi nan gaa kitiŋ ngbaan doo na, le bi nan kal nima chee.

ref: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
text: Uwumbɔr nan tii bi nsuudoon, kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk ni, ke waah nan puu tii biyaajatiib pu na. Le baadim ponn ni ubaa kina aa ŋmaa ŋa bi nibaa, ba pu? Uwumbɔr le nan tii bi linyaŋ baadim mɔmɔk pu.

ref: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
text: Uwumbɔr nan cha tipuur timɔk u nan puu tii Israel yaab na mɔmɔk gbiin.

ref: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
text: Josua nan yin Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln, ŋi ye liwipuul wɔb yaab na, nan kpaan ubaa chee.

ref: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
text: N‑yoonn mumina mɔmɔk, naa san cha nido yaab Israel yaab kpala. Ni pɔɔn nibaa ki kii tii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr mbamɔm.

ref: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
text: Dandana wee, waah nan puu pu na, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr tii niŋeen aatɔtiib Israel yaab biken nsuudoon a. Kina pu na, gir kun kitiŋ ki pu ni nan gaa ki ye nimi yaan na, kitiŋ ki bi liwipuul, Jɔɔdann aamɔɔdapuul wɔb na, kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses nan di tii nimi na.

ref: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
text: Ni chuu nibaa man, ki kii, ki li joo ikaal i Moses nan di mɔk nimi na: ni li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr, ki ŋa waageehn, ki kii tii waakaal, ki li joo waasan mbamɔm, aan ki li dii u nisui ni, ni nimi aawiin mɔmɔk.”

ref: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
text: Tɔ, binib bibaa nan tuk Israel yaab biken na ke, “Li pel man, Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln maa kitork aabimbiln sakpeln libaa Gelilof aatiŋ ni, ni bi timi aapepel wɔb, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl chee.”

ref: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
text: Israel yaab biken na aah ŋun kina na, le bi mɔmɔk kuun dan Silo aatiŋ ni, ke bi buen ti to ŋinibol ngbaan butɔb.

ref: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
text: Le Israel aanib ngbaan nan tun Eleasar aajapɔɔn u bi yin u ke Fineas na, ke u buen Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln na aanib chee, Gilead aatiŋ ni.

ref: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
text: Israel yaab aaninkpiib bi nan ye bisalolm na kipiik le nan kpee Fineas pu, bi nan nyan liwilir wɔb aanibol aaninkpiib ni la, le bi mɔmɔk nan ye biyidam, baataŋaal ponn ni.

ref: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
text: Le bi ti fuu Gilead aatiŋ ni, Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln bi bi liwipuul wɔb na chee.

ref: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
text: Baah nan kpaan ki ye Uwumbɔr aanib aasalolm pu na, le bi bui bi ke, “Ba ŋa ni ŋa titunwanbir timina aaboln timi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr aanimbiin ni? Ni yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, le ki maa kitork aabimbiln limina tii nibaa, kaa di li tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
text: Ni teer taah nan tun titunwanbir ti Peor aatiŋ ni na; n‑yoonn ngbaan Uwumbɔr nan daa timi waanib aatafal ki cha iween lir ti pu, kina pu na, ti laa beenin ji kina aafalaa. Timi aatunwanbir ngbaan aa ŋeer aa?

ref: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
text: Ni yaa yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb din wee kan, u ga gee liŋuul Israel yaab mɔmɔk pu.

ref: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
text: Ni yaa kaan ŋmaa doon Uwumbɔr nimi aatiŋ ni kan, puur dan ti chee man, nin chee Uwumbɔr Aabool bi na, ki nan gaa timi aatim ngem. Ni taa yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, ki taa nya tipuwɔb ki nan ki maa kitork aabimbiln liken ki kpee Tidindaan Uwumbɔr yaan pu.

ref: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
text: Ni teer Sera aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Akann na bɔr, u nan yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb le ki yoor tiwan ni ye Uwumbɔr yaan na, le Uwumbɔr nan daa Israel yaab mɔmɔk aatafal, naa nan ye Akann baanja le nan kpo titunwanbir ngbaan pu.”

ref: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh answered:
text: Le Rubenn ni Gad aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln aanib nan giin bui liwilir wɔb aanibol aaninkpiib ke,

ref: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
text: “Uwumbɔr le ye Mpɔɔndaan. Uma le ye Uwumbɔr. Uwumbɔr le ye Mpɔɔndaan. Uma le ye Uwumbɔr. Uma le nyi tiwan ni pu ti ŋa kina na, le ti ban ni mu bee ni. Ni yaa ye ke ti tun titunwanbir Uwumbɔr chee, kaa kii waamɔb kan, ku timi man, ki taa cha ti ki li bi man.

ref: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
text: Ni yaa ye ke ti yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb, le ki maa kitork aabimbiln ke ti li seer njikaabim aapiin, bee kimɔbaan aapiin kan, cha Uwumbɔr ubaa daa titafal.

ref: We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.” Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord.
text: U di Jɔɔdann aamɔɔl le siin timi aatiŋ, ni nimi bi ye Rubenn, ni Gad aanibol yaab na aatiŋ mɔk. Naan ŋmaa dii Uwumbɔr.’ Nibaakan niyaabitiib ga bui tiyaabitiib kina, ki cha bi taa ki dii Uwumbɔr.

ref: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
text: Nima pu le ti maa kitork aabimbiln ngbaan, naa ye ke ti ban ti see kitork ki tii ipiin li pu la,

ref: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
text: Le utotoor Eleasar aajapɔɔn Fineas nan bui ke, “Dandana wee, ti bee ke Uwumbɔr bi ti chee. Naa yii waamɔb, kina pu le ni nyan Israel yaab mɔmɔk Uwumbɔr aatafadaan ni.”

ref: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
text: Le Fineas ni biyidam ngbaan nan nyan Gilead aatiŋ ni, Rubenn ni Gad aanibol chee, ki gir buen Kanaann aatiŋ ni, ki buen Israel yaab biken chee, le ki ti ŋeer tibɔr ngbaan mɔmɔk tuk bi.

ref: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
text: Le ni mɔɔr Israel yaab mɔmɔk, le bi pak Uwumbɔr. Baa nan ki dak ke bi ga buen ti to Rubenn ni Gad yaab butɔb.

ref: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
text: Rubenn ni Gad yaab nan bui ke, “Libimbiln lee ye seeraa ke Uwumbɔr le ye Tidindaan.” Kina pu le bi nan yin libimbiln ngbaan ke, “Seeraa.”

ref: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
text: Naah bi cha na, le Uwumbɔr tii Israel yaab linyaŋ baadim pu, le bi kan nsuudoon. N‑yoonn ngbaan Josua nan por pam,

ref: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
text: nima pu na, u nan yin ni Israel yaab mɔmɔk, bi nan ye bininkpiib, ni bisalolm, ni bibɔjirb, ni biyidam bi joo binib ngbaan na, le ki nan bui bi ke, “Dandana wee, m por pam.

ref: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
text: Ni mɔmɔk kan Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ŋa ŋitimbol ŋimina mɔmɔk pu na. Nimi pu le u ŋa kina. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le jaa ni pu.

ref: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le ga cha nimi aadim san nimi ijawaan, ki ga jenn nyan bi, le ni ga gaa baatim ke uma Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah puu tii nimi pu na.

ref: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
text: Kina pu na, ni pɔɔn nibaa ki kii waamɔb, ki ŋa Moses aakaal aagbaŋ aah tuk nimi ke ni ŋa pu na. Ni taa yii nkaal ngbaan mubaa,

ref: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
text: nima kan, naan di nibaa ŋmal biniyayam bi gur ki bi ni chee na ni, ki mu taa yin baawaa aayimbil, ki taa di ŋaayimbil puu tipuur, ki taa doon ŋiwaa ngbaan kpala, ki taa gbaan ŋinimbiin ni.

ref: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
text: Ni tee li dii Uwumbɔr mbamɔm, ke naah gaa u ki kii ki nan saa dandana wee pu na.

ref: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
text: Naah piin ki choo na, Uwumbɔr le cha ni nyaŋni ntikpaam, ni mpɔɔndam aanibol, ki nyani bi baatim ni, ubaa aa kee nyaŋ nimi.

ref: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
text: Ni ponn ni unibaan ga ŋmaa nyaŋ binib lichur; ba pu? Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le nyaŋni bi tii nimi, ke waah nan puu pu na.

ref: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
text: Li nyi man, aan ki li gee Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.

ref: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
text: ni li nyi ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aan jenn nyan ŋinibol ngbaan, naah tur koo bi ponn ni pu na. Bi ga tee li ye ntafadaan le ni pu, ki li ye gaawɔb, ni libuul tii nimi. Le baah ga ŋa nimi falaa u na ga li wu nipuwɔb ke mbambaan na la, ki ga ki li wu ke ikokon le aah saar ninimbil ni na. Le ni ga li bi kina hali ki ti saa buyoonn ni ponn ni ubaa aan ti ki gur kitinyaan kimina ponn ni, kitiŋ ki Nidindaan Uwumbɔr di tii nimi na.

ref: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
text: “Dandana wee, ni ŋeer ke m kpo. Ni mɔmɔk nyi nisui ni, ni nimi aawiin ni, ke Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le tii nimi tiwanyaan nimɔk u puu ke u ga tii nimi na. Tipuur timɔk u puu na, u ŋa ti mɔmɔk; tibaa kina aa bee fam.

ref: Yes, when the Lord makes a promise, he does what he has promised. But when he makes a threat, he will also do what he has threatened. The Lord is our God. He gave us this wonderful land and made an agreement with us that we would worship only him. But if you worship other gods, it will make the Lord furious. He will start getting rid of you, and soon not one of you will be left in this good land that he has given you.
text: Ni yaa kaa joo nkaal mu Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bui nimi ke ni li joo mu na, ki yaa dooni ŋiwaa kan, waaŋuul ga fii, le u ga daa nitafal, naan yunn le ni mɔmɔk ubaa kina aan ki gur kitinyaan ki u di tii nimi na ponn ni.”

ref: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
text: Josua nan kuun Israel aanibol ngbaan mɔmɔk dan ubaa chee Sekem aatiŋ ni. U nan yin baaninkpiib, ni baasalolm, ni baabɔjirb, ni baayidam, le bi mɔmɔk kuun ni Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni.

ref: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
text: Le Josua bui bi mɔmɔk ke, “Uwumbɔr u ye timi Israel yaab Aadindaan na aah len pu na sɔ: ‘N‑yoonn mu jer na, niyaajatiib nan bi Yufrates Aamɔɔdapuul le ki dooni ŋiwaa. Niyaajatiib ngbaan ubaa le nan ye Tera, u nan ye Abraham ni Nahor aate na.

ref: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
text: Le min Uwumbɔr nan yin niyaaja Abraham, ki nyan ni u Yufrates Aamɔɔdapuul, le u dan Kanaann aatiŋ kimina ponn ni. M nan tii u yaabitiib pam. Uma le nan ma Aisak,

ref: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
text: le Aisak mu ma Jakob ni Esɔ. Le m nan di ŋigongon aatiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Edom na ki di tii Esɔ, u li joo, le niyaaja Jakob ni waabim nan buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni.

ref: Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea.
text: Maah nan nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, Ijipt yaab nan san paa bi pu, ki joo itaan ni tɔroku tiib, le nitetiib aah ti pii Nnyusakpem Mamam buyoonn na,

ref: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
text: le bi wii ki yin mi ke m nan ter bi, le m cha mbɔmbɔɔn dan bi ni Ijipt yaab aakaasisik ni. M nan cha Ijipt yaab bee nnyusakpem na ni. Ni nyi maah nan ŋa Ijipt yaab pu na mɔmɔk. “‘Ni nan bi nteersakpiin ni, ni yunn pam.

ref: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
text: Le m nan joo ni nimi Amor yaab aatiŋ ni, Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl aawipuul wɔb. Bi nan ton nimi butɔb, le m cha ni nyaŋ bi. Ni nan gaa baatim, le naah tur koo bi ni na, m ku bi.

ref: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
text: Moab yaab aabɔr u bi nan yin u ke Balak, aan ute nan ye Sipor na, nan ton nimi butɔb. U nan tun unii, Beor aajapɔɔn u bi nan yin u ke Balaam na chee, ki bui u ke u puun lii ni pu,

ref: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
text: le maa kii tii Balaam, le u tee ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu. M nan ŋa kina le ki gaa nimi Balak aaŋaal ni lii.

ref: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
text: Le ni nan puur Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ki dan Jeriko aatiŋ ni. Le Jeriko yaab ton nimi butɔb. Nee aapuwɔb, le Amor yaab, ni Peris yaab, ni Kanaann yaab, ni Hef yaab, ni Girgas yaab, ni Hif yaab, ni Jebus yaab mu nan ton nimi butɔb, le m nan cha ni nyaŋ bi mɔmɔk.

ref: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
text: Naah nan tur koo bi ponn ni pu na, m nan cha ijawaan koo bi, aan ni ŋmaa jenn nyan Amor yaab aabɔrb bilee ngbaan. Naa nan ye nimi aajaak aajum ni itɔi pu le ni nan ŋmaa nyaŋ.

ref: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
text: Min le di ikpaakon i naa nan kon i ponn ni kpala na tii nimi, le ki di ntim mu naa nan maa mu na tii nimi. Le dandana wee, ni bi ntim ngbaan ni, ki ji ndaan aasubil, ni olif aakpan aasubil aasui i mu naa nan bun i na.’”

ref: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
text: Josua nan ki bui bi ke, “Kina pu na, ni li nyuŋni Uwumbɔr, ki gaa u iŋaal ilee, ki li dii u mbamɔm. Ni di ŋiwaa ŋi niyaajatiib nan dooni ŋi Mesopotamia, ni Ijipt aatim ni na lii, aan ki dii Uwumbɔr baanja.

ref: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
text: Ni yaa kaa gee ke ni li dooni u kan, din wee, ni nyan naah ga dii u na; ni ga li dooni ŋiwaa ŋi niyaajatiib nan dooni ŋi Mesopotamia aatiŋ ni na aa? bee ni ga li dooni Amor yaab, bi ni bi baatiŋ ponn ni na le aawaa? M ni maamaal ma kan, ti ga li dii Uwumbɔr la.”

ref: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
text: Le binib ngbaan nan giin bui u ke, “Taan di Uwumbɔr lii kpala ki dii liwaal libaa.

ref: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le nan nyan ni titetiib, ni timi, Ijipt yaab aanaagbiir ni, le ti kan lijinjiir aatun ŋi u tun na. Taah nan bi nin chee na mɔmɔk, uma le nan biin ti pu, le ŋinibol ŋimɔk ti koo bi ni na ubaa aa nan ŋa timi nibaa.

ref: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
text: Taah nan tur koo kitiŋ kee ni na, Uwumbɔr jenn nyan Amor yaab bimɔk nan bi do na, kina pu na, ti ga dii Uwumbɔr la, uma le ye Tidindaan.”

ref: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
text: Le Josua bui binib ngbaan ke, “Naan ŋmaa dii Uwumbɔr, ba pu? Uwumbɔr ye chain la, kaan di cha nimi aatunwanbir pinn nimi. U ye lipiipoln Aawumbɔr la,

ref: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
text: le ni yaa yii u, ki ban ni li dooni ŋiwaa kan, u ga daa nitafal. Hali waah nan ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu na, ni yaa dii liwaal libaa kan, u ga kuln nimi.”

ref: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
text: Le binib ngbaan bui Josua ke, “Aayii, ti ga sil li dii Uwumbɔr la.”

ref: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
text: Le Josua bui bi ke, “Nimi le ye nibaa aaseeraadam, ki len mbamɔn ke ni ga li dii Uwumbɔr la.” Le bi giin bui u ke, “Mbamɔn, timi le ye tibaa aaseeraadam.”

ref: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
text: Le Josua bui bi ke, “Ni yaa ye kina kan, ni nyan ŋiwaa ŋi bi ni chee na man, aan ki puu ke ni ga sil dii Uwumbɔr u ye timi Israel yaab Aadindaan na.”

ref: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
text: Le binib ngbaan bui Josua ke, “Ti ga li dii Tidindaan Uwumbɔr la, ki ga kii waah len pu na.”

ref: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
text: Nima pu na, liyaadaal ngbaan le Josua nan cha bi puu tipuur kina, nima chee, Sekem aatiŋ ni, le ki tii bi nsurm ni ikaal, bi li dii.

ref: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem

text: Tɔ, naah ŋa Gideonn ni waadichal din wee pu na yaa ye ibamɔn, ni mbimbinyaan aatuln kan, ni li kpa mpopiin Abimelek pu, aan u mu li kpa ni pu mpopiin.

ref: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
text: Ni mu yaa kaa ye kina kan, mmii nyan ni Abimelek ni, ki wu Sekem aatiŋ aajab, ni Bef Milo aatiŋ aajab. Mmii mu nyan ni Sekem aatiŋ aajab ni, ni Bef Milo aatiŋ aajab ni, ki wu Abimelek.”

text: Nimina nan ŋa kina ke Abimelek ni Sekem aatiŋ aajab bi nan pai u aan u ku Gideonn aajapɔtiib imonko itaa ni kipiik na kan baatunwanbir aatafadaan la.

ref: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
text: Bi mɔmɔk nan nyan buen baasubil aasui aasar ni ki ti ker ŋisubil, le ki di ŋa ndaan, le ki ŋa njim. Bi nan koo baawaal aadiik ni, le ki ti jin ki nyun ndaan nima ki seei Abimelek.

text: Gaal nan bui ke, “Ti ye ba aajab Sekem aatiŋ ni do? Ni ŋa kinye aan ti di Abimelek ŋa timi aabɔr? U mu ye ŋma? Gideonn aajapɔɔn mu. Uma le len, le Sebul keei, waan ŋmaa li ye timi aabɔr. Li dii man niyaaja Hamor u naan nimi aataŋaal na aasan.

text: Sebul u nan ye kitiŋ ngbaan aajojoor na aah ŋun Gaal aah len pu na, le waaŋuul fii.

ref: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
text: Kina pu na, aa ni saajab nya kinyeek ki nan bɔr bukpaab ni.

text: Ni fe fii fen, nwiin aah laa bi puur pu na, ki nan gob kitiŋ ngbaan. Gaal ni waajab yaa nyan ni ke bi nan tak nimi kan, ni cha ni nyan bi mbamɔm.”

text: Kina pu le Abimelek ni waajab nan fii kinyeek ki nan yakr ŋiker ŋinaa pu ki bɔr Sekem aakpaan ngbaan ni.

text: Gaal nan kan bi, le ki bui Sebul ke, “Lik, bijab bibaa le nyan ni ŋijoo paab ki choo na.” Le Sebul gar u ke, “Nima ngbaan aa ye bijab. Ni ye tijunjunn le bi ŋijoo ngbaan pu.”

text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le Sebul bui u ke, “Saapupuk na bi la chee? Naa ye sin le nan baa ke ba ŋa ti di Abimelek ngbaan ŋa timi aabɔr na aa? Bijab bi aa nan bi joo bi seei na le na. Nya li cha aan aa ni bima ti pii tɔb.”

text: Le u ŋa mala ki yin unachipɔɔn u joo waajawan na ki nan bui u ke, “Fuur saajaak aajuk ki di ku mi. Maa ban ke bi nan len ke upii le ku mi.” Kina pu le unachipɔɔn ngbaan nan saa chaar u, le u kpo.

text: Tola aah nan kpo na, le Jair u nyan ni Gilead na paan u pu ki ye usaloln. U nan joo Israel aanib ki ti saa ŋibin moninko ni ŋilee.

text: Bijab bi pɔɔ na aatɔi kool la, le bi kaa kpa mpɔɔn na moo pɔɔk.

ref: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
text: Binib bi nan kpa ki ji babr na gur joo bibaa le kooh ki kpiini bibaa; nkon aah nan joo bi na gur ji gunni la. Upii u nan ye uŋoob na gur kpa mbim mulole la, le upii u nan kpa mbim pam na aa ki kpa ubaa gur.

ref: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
text: Uwumbɔr ku la, le ki ki tii limɔfal; u cha binib chaa kitekpiitiŋ ni, le ki tii binib limɔfal.

ref: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
text: U ŋani binib bibaa bigiim, le ki ŋani biken biwankpadam. U sunni bibaa taab, le ki ŋani biken binikpaam.

ref: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
text: U nyan ni bigiim titan ponn ni, ki nyan ni binib bi kaa kpa na baanimbaak ponn ni. U ŋani bi mbɔrbim aajɔtiib, ki joo bi kaani binikpaam aakakaa chee. Uwumbɔr le naan kitiŋ kee aatinyikl, le ki pɔɔ, litinyikl lee pu le u naan dulnyaa.

ref: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
text: Waanib bi dii u mbamɔm na, u kii baamɔfal, le bibiindam ma beer mbɔmbɔɔn ni. Uja aan ŋmaa di ubaa aapɔɔn kan linyaŋ.

ref: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
text: Uwumbɔr aadim ga kuln; u bi paacham ki ga teen bi pu ke utaal na. Uwumbɔr le ga ji dulnyaa mɔmɔk tibɔr; u ga tii waabɔr mpɔɔn, u ga cha waah lee ubɔr u na kan linyaŋ.”

ref: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
text: Tɔ, Elkana gir kun Rama, le Samuel u laa ye ubo na gaar Silo, ki tun Uwumbɔr aatuln, utotoor Eli chee. Eli aajapɔtiib aah bir pu na

text: kaa nan bi ikaal i nan mɔk utotoor aah ga ban tiwan ni binib chee na ni. Baah nan labr ŋani pu na sɔ: unii yaa nan bi toor waatork kan, le utotoor aatutunn ga dan, ki joo ni nnanmoon mu yakr ŋipan ŋitaa na, buyoonn tinann ngbaan beenin tɔk mmii pu na,

ref: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
text: le u di nnanmoon ngbaan saa tinann ngbaan ponn ni, le nnanmoon ngbaan aah saa tuun tinann timɔk na ye utotoor aanann la. Israel yaab bimɔk choo Silo ki nan toor kitork na, bi nan ŋani bi mɔmɔk kina la;

ref: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
text: ki ki kpee na, waahr aan bi nin di nkpan na pu mmii ni mu ti wu doo na, utotoor aatutunn ngbaan ga dan ki nan bui unii u bi toor kitork ngbaan na ke, “Tii mi tinann tibaa m ti tii utotoor aan u pu; waan gaa saah ŋaa ti na, u ban tinankaab baanja la.”

ref: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
text: Udaan yaa bui ke, “Cha ti ŋa ikaal aah mɔk pu na waahr, ki pu nkpan aan aa nin lee saah ban pu na” kan, le utotoor aatutunn ngbaan ga bui ke, “Aayii. Di ti tii mi dandana wee. Aa yaa yii kan, m ga di mpɔɔn le lee ti.”

ref: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
text: Baah nan lik seen Uwumbɔr aatork pu na, Eli aajapɔtiib aatunwanbir ngbaan nan bir Uwumbɔr chee pam. Samuel aah nan bi Silo ni pu na

text: N‑yoonn mue na Samuel u nan laa ye ubo na nan beenin bi tun Uwumbɔr aatuln, ki pee libɔkul li bitotoorb peeni na.

ref: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.

text: Le Eli ga ŋa Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa Elkana ni upuu pu, ki bui Elkana ke, “Uwumbɔr tii si mbim muken upii wee chee aan bi leŋ naah di ubo u tii u na aaleleŋ.” Nee aapuwɔb le bi gir kun.

ref: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
text: Uwumbɔr mu nan sil ŋa waanyoor ŋa Hana pu, le u nan ki ma mbijabim mutaa, ni mpiibim mulee. Samuel nan fii ki chikr Uwumbɔr aatuln ponn ni la. Eli ni ujapɔtiib aabɔr

text: N‑yoonn mue Eli nan por pam. U nan beenin ŋun ujapɔtiib aah nan ŋani Israel yaab mbiin pu na, ni baah kpaan doo bipiib bi tun lituln Uwumbɔr Aabool aabisamɔb na chee pu na.

ref: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
text: Njapɔtiib, di cha man ni. Tiwan ni Uwumbɔr aanib len naabɔr na aa ŋan kpala.

ref: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
text: Unibɔn yaa tun uŋeen aatɔ taani kan, nibaakan Uwumbɔr ga san u kinimbaak, tɔ, ŋma ga ter unii u tun Uwumbɔr titunwanbir na?” Le baa pel bite aah len pu na, ba pu? Uwumbɔr nan siin ke u ku bi.

ref: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
text: Samuel nan beenin chikr cha, le ki kpa kipak binib ni Uwumbɔr mu chee. Uwumbɔr kpiir Eli aadichal aabɔr len

ref: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ubaa nan dan Eli chee ki joo ni Uwumbɔr aanaŋ yee ke: “Aayaaja Aaronn ni waadichal aah nan ye binaagbiib Ijipt aatiŋ aabɔr Faro chee na, m nan di mbaa mɔk Aaronn.

ref: Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar. But you honor your sons instead of me! You don't respect the sacrifices and offerings that are brought to me, and you've all grown fat from eating the best parts.
text: Ni ki ŋa kinye aan ni ki lik waa kitork ni ipiin i m ban maanib chee na? Eli, ni ŋa kinye aan aa pak aajapɔtiib ki jer mi, ki cha bi ji maanib aatork aanann ti ŋan sakpen aan bi ba ban bi di tii mi na, ki moo filk cha?

ref: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
text: Min, Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr le nan puu n‑yoonn mu jer na ke saadichal ni saamaal le ga li tun maatuln ke bitotoorb na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Le dandana wee m len ke maan ŋa nimi kina. Maah ga ŋa pu na sɔ, m ga nyuŋ binib bi nyuŋni mi na la, le ki lik seen binib bi lik mi fam na.

ref: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
text: Li pel, n‑yoonn choo le m ga ku binachipɔm bimɔk bi saadichal, ni saamaal ponn ni na, le uja ubaa taa ki li bi saadichal ni ki ti por.

ref: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
text: Ni ga li muk si le aa lik ki neen tinyoor ti m ga di tii Israel yaab biken na, le ubaa aan ki li bi saadichal ponn ni ki ti por.

ref: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
text: Tɔ, m ga cha aayaabitiib ponn ni ubaa gur, ki li tun maatuln ke utotoor na, le u mu ga nan jɔb aan utaakpab yɔl, le aayaabitiib bi gur na ga kpo mpɔɔnkun.

ref: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
text: Tiwan ni ga mɔk si ke maah len pu na ga gbiin na le ye ke aajapɔtiib bilee na, Hofni ni Fineas, ga kpaan kpo liwinbaal la.

ref: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
text: Le m ga lee utotoor u ga dii mi mbamɔm, ki ŋani tiwan nimɔk m ban na. M ga tii u yaabitiib bi ga li tun maatuln, maabɔr u m lee u na chee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
text: Aayaabitiib ponn ni u ŋmar na ga li chaa utotoor ngbaan chee le ki ti mee ŋimombil, ni tijikaar, le ki gaŋ u ke u cha u ter bitotoorb baatuln ni, aan ki kan nibaa ki ti kpiin ubaa.”

ref: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
text: le Samuel mu dɔ nin chee Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa nan bi na. Waahr aan ni nin woln na, buyoonn karyaa aa nan kee junn na,

text: le Uwumbɔr yin Samuel. Samuel nan kii ke, “Maaninkpel, m sɔ,”

text: le ki san buen Eli chee ki ti bui ke, “Saah yin mi na, le m dan.” Le Eli bui u ke, “Maa yin sin, gir ti doon.” Le Samuel gir buen ti doon.

ref: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
text: Le Uwumbɔr ki yin Samuel taataa, le u fii, ki ki buen Eli chee, ki ti ki bui u ke, “Saah yin mi na, le m dan.” N‑yoonn ngbaan le Eli bee ke ni ye Uwumbɔr le yin ubo ngbaan,

text: le u ki bui u ke, “Gir ti doon; u yaa ki yin si kan, bui ke ‘Uwumbɔr, li len, saatutunn pel la.’” Le Samuel ki gir ti doon.

text: Le Uwumbɔr dan nan sil nima, ki yin ke waah ti yin pu na ke, “Samuel, Samuel.” Le Samuel kii ke, “Li len; saatutunn pel la.”

text: Le Uwumbɔr bui u ke, “Nwiin mubaa daal m ga ŋa Israel aanib tiwan nibaa, ni ga li kpa ijawaan, le unii umɔk ŋun ni pu na ga bir, kaan ŋmaa len tibaa.

ref: I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised.
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal le m ga ŋa Eli aadichal tiwan nimɔk m bui ke m ga ŋa li na.

ref: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.

ref: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
text: Kina pu na, min le bui Eli ni waadichal ke kitork bee ipiin ibaa aa bi ki ga ŋmaa nyan titunwanbir timina aatafadaan.”

ref: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.

ref: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
text: Eli nan yin u ke, “Maabo Samuel.” Le Samuel kii ke, “Maaninkpel, m sɔ.”

ref: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
text: Le Eli baa u ke, “Uwumbɔr tuk si ke ba? Taa di tibaa bɔr mi. Aa yaa kaa bui mi waah tuk si pu na mɔmɔk kan, Uwumbɔr ga daa aatafal pam.”

ref: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
text: Kina pu le Samuel bui u ti mɔmɔk; waa nan di tibaa bɔr u. Le Eli bui ke, “Uma le ye Uwumbɔr. Cha u ŋa waah ban pu na.”

ref: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
text: Samuel aah chikr cha na, le Uwumbɔr nan bi u chee ki cha Samuel aah len pu na mɔmɔk gbiini kina.

text: Kina pu le Israel aanib mɔmɔk, bi bi Israel aatiŋ ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni na bee ke Samuel nan sil ye Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr la.

ref: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.

text: Uja ngbaan aah pur Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa aabɔr na, le Eli nyan lijal pu ki lir upuwɔb, mbisamɔb chee. U nan por pam, ki filk mu, le waah lir kina na usil koo, le u kpo. U nan ye Israel aayidaan ki ti saa ŋibin imonko ilee la. Fineas aakpopii mu aah kpo pu na

text: ki len ke, “Taa san ijawaan. Nte Sɔɔl aan ŋmaa ŋa si nibaa. U nyi gbingbin ke sin le ga ŋa Israel aabɔr, le m li paa aa pu.”

ref: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul

text: Sif aanib bibaa nan buen Sɔɔl chee, Gibea aatiŋ ni, ki ti bui u ke, “David bɔr timi aapepel ponn ni, Hores ni, Hakila Aajool li bi Juda yaab aateersakpiin mu bi ŋŋangii wɔb na ni.

text: Bee man libuul li ni chob u bɔr na, ki gir nan tuk mi man mala. Le m ni nimi dii buen, le u yaa beenin bi nima kan, m ga tee mban kan u. Hali ni yaa ye ke m ban u Juda aatiŋ mɔmɔk ni kan, m ga ban kan u.”

ref: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
text: Le bi loln Sɔɔl pu nsan gir kun Sif. David ni waajab nan bi Maonn aateersakpiin ni, kifataŋ ki kaa kpa nibaa, ki bi Juda yaab aapepel aaŋangii wɔb na ni la.

ref: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
text: Sɔɔl ni waajab nan nyan ke bi ban David chee, le u ŋun kina, le ki buen ŋitakpal aagongoln paab, Maonn aateersakpiin ni, ki ti bi nima. Sɔɔl aah ŋun ke u bi nima na, le u paan u pu nima chee.

ref: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
text: Sɔɔl ni waajab nan bi ligongoln ngbaan aapepel libaa, le David ni waajab mu bi lipepel liken. Bi nan ŋani mala, ke bi san cha Sɔɔl ni waajab bi nan ŋɔŋ bi pu ke bi chuu bi na.

text: Kina pu le Sɔɔl di cha, kaa ki dii David, ki buen, u ni Filistia yaab ti jan. Kina pu le bi yin nima chee ke N‑yakr Aagongoln.

text: David nan siir le ki buen Enn Gedi aapepel, nin chee u nan ti bɔr na.

ref: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
text: Sɔɔl aah nyan ni u ni Filistia yaab aatɔb ki gir ni na, le bi bui u ke, “David bi nteersakpiin mu bi Enn Gedi chee na ni.”

ref: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
text: U nan ti fuu kitakpaluŋ kibaa chee, ki nan bi ipiih aabɔkpenn tibaa chee la, le ki koo ki ponn ni ke u ti sɔnn. Kitakpaluŋ baan ngbaan ponn ni, le David ni waajab mu nan bɔr ponn ponn ni.

ref: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
text: Bi nan bui David ke, “Saayoonn le na. Uwumbɔr nan bui si ke u ga di saadin ŋa saapɔɔn ni, le aa ŋa u saah gee pu na.” David nan loon buen u chee, le ki ti chuu gii waabɔkul pu upuwɔb, aan Sɔɔl aa nyi ke u gii.

ref: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le naa ki piir David aasui.

text: Le David paan u pu ki yin u ke, “Mpɔɔndaan.” Le Sɔɔl fenn, le David gbaan ki tii u kipak,

text: Aa kan ke dandana wee Uwumbɔr di si ŋa maapɔɔn ni kitakpaluŋ ngbaan ni. Maajab bibaa bui mi ke m ku si, le m san si kinimbaak, ki bui bi ke maan ŋa si taani siib kina; ba pu? Uwumbɔr le lee si ke aa li ye ubɔr.

text: Lik, nte, lik saabɔkul aageln le m joo na. M ba ga ŋmaa ku si, le m tee gii nimina. Nima le ga ŋmaa mɔk si limɔkl ke maa si aa pu, kaa kpak si, ki mu aa ban m ku si. Aa bi tee mban ki ban mi ke aa ku mi, le maa kpaan ŋa si nibaa.

ref: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
text: Uwumbɔr ga ji timi aabɔr ki lik u aabɔr bii na. Saah ŋani mi pu na, uma le ga daa aatafal; ba pu? maa ban m ŋa si nibaa kpala.

ref: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
text: Aa nyi liyataŋakl na ke, ‘Titunwanbirdam baanja le ŋani titunwanbir.’ Kina pu na, maan ŋa si nibaa.

text: Lik man Israel yaab aabɔr aah bi ban u ku tiwan ni na. Lik man waah bi san dii tiwan ni na. Libɔkpol aa? kibabr aa?

text: Uwumbɔr ga ji timi aabɔr, le ki bee u aabɔr bii na. Cha u lik tibɔr ngbaan ponn ni, ki sil mpuwɔb, ki gaa mi lii.”

text: David aah len doo na, le Sɔɔl bui ke, “Sin maabo David sil ye ee?” le ki piin ki bi wii.

text: Dandana wee na, m bee ke aa ga ŋa Israel yaab aabɔr, le nnaan ngbaan li bi saajoom ni.

text: Mpɔɔndaan, li pel maah kpa pu m tuk si na. Ni yaa ye Uwumbɔr le cha aa ban mi kan, kitork le ga cha u kpeln waalandak; tɔ, ni yaa ye binib kan, Uwumbɔr aapuun li dii bi; ba pu? bi jenn nyan mi Uwumbɔr aatiŋ ni, ki bui mi ke m li cha ki ti li dooni ŋiwaa.

text: Sɔɔl nan kii u ke, “M tun taani. Maabo David, gir ni. Maan ki tun si taani ubaa; ba pu? aa gaa maamɔfal lii kinyeek kee. M ŋa mbaa ujɔr la. M tun titunwanbir sakpen.”

text: Le David mu tun Isbosef chee ke, “Giin mpuu Mikal tii ni mi. M nan di Filistia yaab aajawan aagban nkub le pan u pu ki yoor u.”

text: Ahas nan yoor Uwumbɔr Aadichal, ni libɔrdichal aakunabr ni salmaa, ki di tun ti tii Siria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan ngbaan ipiin.

ref: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
text: Ahas aagaŋ ngbaan pu, le Tiglaf Pileser nan di waajab buen Damaskus aatiŋ pu, le ki ti nyaŋ ki, le ki ku Ubɔr Resinn, le ki chur kaanib tinaagbiir buen Kir aatiŋ ni.

ref: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
text: Ubɔr Ahas aah nan buen Damaskus aatiŋ ni, u ti kan Ubɔrkpaan Tiglaf Pileser na le u nan ti kan kitork aabimbiln nima, le ki di laanaŋ ti mɔk utotoor Uria. Ni nan naahn ke naah ye foto le na.

ref: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
text: Le Uria maa kina aatork aabimbiln, aan li ni lima ngbaan ye tiwanbaan, le ki maa li doo le Ahas nin gir kun ni.

ref: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
text: Ahas aah nyan ni Damaskus aatiŋ ni ki gir ni na, le u kan ke kitork aabimbiln ngbaan maa a,

ref: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
text: kina pu le u nan see tiwakor ni njikaabim aapiin mmii ni li pu. U nan ki di ndaan aapiin, ni kimɔbaan aapiin aasin kpir li pu.

ref: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
text: Tikumann aatork aabimbiln li bi nan di tii Uwumbɔr na nan si libimbipɔln ngbaan ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal aasisik ni la. Kina pu le Ahas nan yoor li ti siin waabimbipɔln ngbaan aaŋangan wɔb,

ref: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
text: le ki bui Uria ke: “Li gur seer kichakpiik ni aatork, ki li toor kijook aajikaabim aatork maabimbiln li wiir na pu, ki li joo min ubɔr, ni binib aatork seer mmii ni li pu, ki li toor baajikaabim aapiin li pu, ki li joo binib aadaan aapiin mu kpir li pu. Li joo baah kɔr tiwakor ti mɔmɔk na aasin kpir li pu. Tɔ, tikumann aabimbiln na ma kan, aa cha li li si m li joo buu tibɔɔr.”

ref: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
text: Ubɔr Ahas nan chuu bii tikumann aatɔroku tiib bi bi nan joo tun lituln Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni na, le ki nyan tisapar ti nan tɔk bi pu na; u nan ki nyan tikumann aakin na mu tikumann aanaaja naankee kipiik ni ilee na pu, le ki di mu tɔŋ ŋitakpal pu.

ref: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
text: Ahas nan ki nyan libɔrjal aah tɔk paangara u pu na Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni, ke ni piir Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan ngbaan aasui, le ki laŋ ubɔr aah diir nin chee koo Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni na.

ref: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
text: Ubɔr Ahas aah nan ki tun ŋitun ŋi mɔmɔk na bi Juda Aabɔrb Aatun Aagbaŋ ni la.

ref: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
text: Juda yaab aabɔr Ahas aanaan ni aabin kipiik ni lileler ni, le Ela aajapɔɔn Hosea jin Israel aanaan, le ki nan bi Samaria aatiŋ ni ki joo waanib ki ti saa ŋibin ŋiwae.

ref: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
text: U nan tun Uwumbɔr titunwanbir, u mu aa nan tee pii Israel yaab aabɔrb bi nan puen u kal lijal ngbaan pu na.

ref: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
text: Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan Salmaneser nan faa u butɔb; le Hosea nan di ubaa tii u ke u nyaŋ u le ki pa tipar tii u libiln mɔmɔk.

ref: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
text: Tɔ, libiln libaa ni, le Hosea nan tun Ijipt yaab aabɔr So chee, ke u nan ter u, le kaa ki pa libiln libiln aapar tii Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan. Salmaneser aah ŋun kina na, le u cha bi chuu Hosea ti laŋ kiyondiik ni. Samaria aatiŋ aah ber pu na

ref: Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years,
text: Salmaneser nan di waajab koo Israel aatiŋ ni, le ki ti gob Samaria aatiŋ. Bi nan bi nima ki ti saa ŋibin ŋitaa,

ref: before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
text: nima le nan ye Hosea aanaan aabiwawaer ni, le Siria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan ti nyaŋ Samaria aatiŋ, le ki chur Israel aanib tinaagbiir buen Asiria aatiŋ ni, le ki ti di bi ponn ni bibaa kaan Hala aatiŋ ni, le ki kaan biken Habor Aamɔɔl chee, Gosann aapepel ni, le ki kaan biken mu Media aatim ni.

ref: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
text: Israel yaab aah nan tun Bidindaan Uwumbɔr titunwanbir na le nan cha Samaria aatiŋ ber. Uwumbɔr nan gaa bi Ijipt yaab aabɔr aaŋaal ni ki nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, le bi nan dooni ŋiwaa,

ref: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
text: le ki dii Uwumbɔr aah nan jenn nyan binib bi baatiŋ pu buyoonn Israel yaab choo na aakaal, le ki gaa ikaal i Israel aatiŋ aabɔrb nan naan tii bi na.

ref: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
text: Israel aanib nan tun ŋitun ŋi Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aa nan gee na la. Bi nan maa tiwaadir baatim mɔmɔk ni, bi nan maa ti ntiwaatiir ni, le ki maa ti ntikpaam mu ni.

ref: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
text: Bi nan siin siin ŋigongon mɔmɔk, ni busub bumɔk kpa mboon na taab ŋiwaabimbin ni liwaapii Asera aanaŋ,

ref: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
text: le ki seer nnyɔknii ŋiwaabimbin mɔmɔk pu, ki dii binib bi Uwumbɔr nan jenn nyan bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu na aasan. Bi nan di baabiin aatun fiin Uwumbɔr aaŋuul,

ref: Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway.
text: le ki yii Uwumbɔr aah nan bui bi ke bi taa li dooni ŋiwaa pu na.

ref: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
text: Uwumbɔr nan tun ni waatuun, ni waabɔnabr ke bi nan sak Israel ni Juda aanib ke: “Di cha man nimi aatunwanbir aasan, ki kii maakaal i bi ikaal i m nan di tii niyaajatiib na, ni maah di i tii ni maatutum bi ye maabɔnabr na.”

ref: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
text: Le baan kii tii u; bi nan kpa tafalaaŋun ke biyaajatiib bi kaa nan di naadii tii Bidindaan Uwumbɔr na la.

ref: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
text: Bi nan yii kaa kii waamɔkm, baa nan joo tipuur ti u nan puu tii biyaajatiib na, le kaa di waah nan sak bi pu na yin nibaa. Bi nan dooni waafam tiib, le ki mu ŋa fam bibaa, le ki nan dii ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln bi na aakaal ki yiil Uwumbɔr aah bui ke bi taa li ŋani ŋitimbol ngbaan aah ŋani pu na.

ref: The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal.
text: Bi nan bii Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aakaal mɔmɔk, le ki naan tikur aanaajabi ilee ki dooni i; bi nan ki naan liwaapii Asera aanaŋ mu, ki dooni iŋmabi, le ki dii liwaal Baal.

ref: They used magic and witchcraft and even sacrificed their own children. The Israelites were determined to do whatever the Lord hated.
text: Bi nan kɔr bijapɔtiib ni bibisatiib ki joo seer mmii ni tii ŋiwaa; bi nan buu tibɔɔr bibɔɔb, ni bipɔnijoob chee, le ki di bibaa tii tiwan ni kaa ŋan Uwumbɔr chee na pel pel, le ki fiin waaŋuul.

ref: The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners. Only the people living in Judah were left,
text: Uwumbɔr aaŋuul nan fii Israel yaab pu, le u nyan bi ubaa chee, ki di cha Juda aanaan baanja.

ref: but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites.
text: Tɔ, Juda aanib mu aa nan kpaan kii Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aakaal; bi mu nan gaa Israel aanib aah nan naan ikaal i na la.

ref: So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
text: Le Uwumbɔr nan yii Israel aanib mɔmɔk, ki daa bitafal ki di bi tii baadim bi kpa mbiin sakpen na, le ki ti baan nyan bi ubaa chee.

ref: Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord.
text: Uwumbɔr aah yakr Israel yaab, Juda yaab chee doo na, le Israel yaab di Nebat aajapɔɔn Jeroboam ŋa baabɔr. Jeroboam nan cha bi suln Uwumbɔr bɔr, le ki di bi koon titunwanbir kpaan ni.

ref: The people kept on sinning like Jeroboam,
text: Bi nan dii Jeroboam le ki tun titunwanbir ti mɔmɔk u tun na,

ref: until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets. That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained. Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
text: le Uwumbɔr ti baan nyan bi ubaa chee, ke waatutum bibɔnabr aah sak bi ke u ga ŋa pu na. Kina pu le Asiria aajab nan chur Israel aanib tinaagbiir buen Asiria aatiŋ ki pu bi beenin bi na. Asiria yaab aah maa kal Israel aatiŋ ni pu na

ref: The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
text: Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan nan nyan binib Babiloŋ, ni Kuf, ni Ifa, ni Hamaf, ni Sefafaim aatim ni, le ki di bi kaan Samaria aatim ni, waah nan chur Israel aanib bi tinaagbiir nima chee na pu. Bi nan gaa ntim ngbaan le ki koo nima.

ref: At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them.
text: Baah nan puen kal nima chee na, baa nan dooni Uwumbɔr, kina pu le u nan cha ichinn dan ki nan ku bi ponn ni bibaa.

ref: A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
text: Bi nan bui Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan ngbaan ke waah di binib bi ti kaan kaan Samaria aatim ni na aa nyi kitiŋ ngbaan Aawumbɔr aakaal, kina pu na, Uwumbɔr ngbaan cha ichinn bi ku bi.

ref: The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.”
text: Le ubɔrkpaan ngbaan bui ke: “Giin man taah chur bitotoorb bi tinaagbiir na ubaa; cha u gir nima, ki ti li koo nima, aan ki li mɔk binib ngbaan kitiŋ ngbaan Aawumbɔr aakaal.”

ref: One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
text: Kina pu le baah nan jenn Israel yaab aatotoor u Samaria aatiŋ pu na gir ki ti koo Betel aatiŋ ni, le ki bi nima ki mɔk binib ngbaan baah ga li dooni Uwumbɔr pu na.

ref: But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines.
text: Tɔ, binib bi nan koo Samaria ni na nan beenin naani baawaa, le ki di ŋi ŋa Israel yaab aah nan maa tiwaadir ti na ponn ni. Linibol mɔk nan naan laawaa laah koo ntim mu ni na la:

ref: The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima;
text: Babiloŋ aanib nan naan baawaal Sukof Benof la; le Kuf aanib naan Negal aawaa; le Hamaf aanib naan Asima aawaa;

ref: those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
text: le Ifa aanib naan Nibhas, ni Taatak aawaa; le Sefafaim aanib kɔr baabim ki seer mmii ni tii baawaa Adramelek, ni Anamelek.

ref: They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines.
text: Kina pu na, bi nan dooni Uwumbɔr, le ki mu ki dooni baawaa baah nyan ni ntim mu ni na aakaal aah mɔk pu na.

ref: Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel.
text: Bi beenin joo baakaal le ki nan saa din na. Baa dooni Uwumbɔr, kaa kii tii ikaal, ni mmɔkm mu u nan di tii Jakob aayaabitiib na. Jakob le Uwumbɔr nan ki yin ke Israel na.

ref: At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them: Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice.
text: Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur tii Israel yaab, le ki bui bi ke: “Taa ki dooni ŋiwaa man; ni taa gbaan ŋinimbiin ni, ki taa dii ŋi, ki taa toor kitork tii ŋi.

ref: Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices.
text: Ni li kii min u di mpɔɔn ni liyabr nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na aamɔb; ni li gbaani nnimbiin ni, ki toor kitork tii mi.

ref: Never worship any other god, always obey my laws and teachings,
text: Ni li joo ikaal ni mmɔkm mu m ŋmee tii nimi na. Ni taa ki kii tii ŋiwaa,

ref: and remember the solemn agreement between us. I will say it again: Do not worship any god
text: ki taa suln maah puu tipuur ti tii nimi na bɔr.

ref: except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
text: Ni kii min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb, le m ga gaa nimi, nimi aadim chee lii.”

ref: But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs.
text: Le binib ngbaan aa nan kpa ŋuntii, le ki yii ki beenin dii baabimbikpok aasan.

ref: They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
text: Kina pu na, binib ngbaan nan dooni Uwumbɔr le ki mu ki dooni baawaa; le biyaabitiib beenin ŋani kina ki nan saa din.

ref: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you.
text: U sur nimi ke ni taa cha Hesekia ŋmann nimi. Hesekia aan ŋmaa gaa nimi lii.

ref: Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
text: Taa pel Hesekia aah len pu na man. Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan bui ke ni nyan ni kitiŋ ngbaan ni, aan ki kii ke u nyaŋ nimi. U ga cha ni mɔmɔk moo ŋisubil nimi aasar ni, ki ŋmɔ nimi aakakan, ki nyu nimi aanyunbun ni aanyun,

ref: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
text: Ni dak ke m di mbaa aapɔɔn le ki nan tak nimi aatiŋ ki kuln ki, kaa ye Uwumbɔr aaterm aa? Uwumbɔr ubaa le bui mi ke m nan tak ki, ki kuln ki.”

ref: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
text: U nan dii uyaaja Ubɔr David aasan, le ki tun Uwumbɔr aageehn.

ref: He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
text: U nan ber tiwaadir mɔmɔk, ki gbaa wiil ŋiwaabimbin, ki gaa gii liwaapii Asera aanaŋ. U nan ki gbaa wii tikumann aawaa u Moses nan naan, aan bi nan yin u ke Nehustann na. Ki nan saa n‑yoonn ngbaan na, Israel aanib nan seer nnyɔknii ki nyuŋni uwaa ngbaan la.

ref: Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him.
text: Hesekia nan tii Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr naadii; Juda aatiŋ aa kee kan ubɔr ubaa aan u nan bi ke uma na, ubaa aa nan puen u bi, le ubaa aan ki li bi upuwɔb.

ref: He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people.
text: U nan tii Uwumbɔr naadii le kaa kee yii umɔb daalbaadaal, le ki nan tee joo ikaal i Uwumbɔr nan di tii ni Moses na mbamɔm.

ref: The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant.
text: Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr nan bi u chee, le u nan nyaŋni tiwan ni mɔmɔk u nan ŋa na ni. U nan nyan Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan aapuwɔb, ki yii kaa di ubaa tii u.

ref: Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
text: U nan nyaŋ Filistia yaab le ki loon baatiwaatiir ni ntikpaam mɔmɔk. Gasa aatiŋ ni kaapepel mu nan bi waah nan loon ntim mu na ni.

ref: During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked
text: Hesekia aanaan aabinanar ni, Israel yaab aabɔr Hosea aanaan aabilolole ni le bi na, le Asiria aatiŋ Aabɔrkpaan Salmaneser nan ti tak Israel aatiŋ, le ki gob Samaria aatiŋ.

ref: and captured it three years later, in the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule and the ninth year of Hoshea's rule.
text: Bi nan bi nima ki ti saa ŋibin ŋitaa, le Samaria aatiŋ nan lir; Hesekia aanaan aabin ŋiloob ni le nan bi na, le ki ye Hosea aabiwawaer ni.

ref: The king of Assyria took the Israelites away as prisoners; he forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
text: Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan ngbaan nan chur Israel aanib tinaagbiir buen Asiria aatiŋ ni, le ki ti di bibaa kaan Hala aatiŋ ni, ki kaan biken Habor Aamɔɔl chee, Gosann aapepel ni, ki kaan biken mu Media aatim ni.

ref: All of that happened because the people of Israel had not obeyed the Lord their God. They rejected the solemn agreement he had made with them, and they ignored everything that the Lord's servant Moses had told them. King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah (
text: Israel yaab aah kaa nan kii Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb, ki bii tipuur ti u nan puu tii bi na, ki yii ikaal i mɔmɔk Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses nan di tii bi na pu le Samaria aatiŋ nan ber. Baa nan ŋun kaa kii tii u. Asiria yaab aah nan faan Jerusalem aatiŋ pu na (

ref: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there. Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him.
text: ki ti saa buyoonn Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan ga ki gir kaan nimi litingbaln li bi ke nimi yaan na, nima chee ndaan aasui aasar bi, ni ga kan ndaan ki nyu, ni nin chee njikaabim bi ni ga kan tijikaar ji na; nima chee le olif aasui bi, olif aakpan ni tisiir bi nima. Ni yaa ŋa waah len pu na kan, naan kpo, ni ga li kpa limɔfal. Taa cha Hesekia ŋmann nimi aan ni li ka dak ke Uwumbɔr ga gaa nimi lii.

ref: One of the Assyrian commanders told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.
text: Le Asiria aajab aaninkpiib ni ubaa nan bui bi ke baabɔrkpaan ban u bee tiwan ni cha Ubɔr Hesekia mak sakpen kina na.

ref: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
text: Asiria aajab aaninkpel ngbaan nan ki len ke, “Bee ni ga bui ke ni lik Nidindaan Uwumbɔr na pu la? Uwumbɔr uchachaan ngbaan aawaachur, ni kitork aabimbin le Hesekia nan ber ki bui Jerusalem ni Juda aanib ke bi li chaa ti dooni Uwumbɔr kitork aabimbiln libaa baanja chee, Jerusalem aatiŋ ni na.

ref: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem.
text: Hesekia aanaan aabin kipiik ni linanar ponn ni, le Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrkpaan Senakerib nan ti tak Juda aatim mu bi maa ŋigon kiir mu, aan mu kpa tijawan na, ki nyaŋ mu.

ref: Ezrah was the father of Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered was married to Bithiah the daughter of the king of Egypt. They had a daughter named Miriam and two sons: Shammai and Ishbah.
