Jered settled the town of Gedor; Heber settled the town of Soco; and Jekuthiel settled the town of Zanoah.
text: Esra nan ma mbijabim munaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Jeter, ni Mered, ni Efer, ni Jalonn. Mered nan yoor Ijipt aabɔr aabisal u bi nan yin u ke Bitia na, le bi nan ma upiibo, ki yin u ke Miriam. Bi nan ma mbijabim bilee mu. Baayimbil le ye Samai ni Isba. Isba le nan naan Estemoa aatiŋ. Mered mu nan yoor Juda aanibol ni aapii la, le bi ma mbijabim bitaa. Baayimbil sɔ: Jered, u nan naan Gedor aatiŋ na, ni Heber, u mu nan naan Soko aatiŋ na, ni Jekutiel, u nan naan Sanoa aatiŋ na.

ref: A man named Hodiah was married to the sister of Naham. Hodiah's descendants included Keilah of the Garmite clan and Eshtemoa of the Maacathite clan.
text: Hodia le nan yoor Naham aaninkpan. Biyaabitiib le naan Gaam aataŋaal mu nan koo Keila aatiŋ ni na, ni Maakaf aataŋaal mu nan koo Estemoa aatiŋ ni na.

ref: Shimon was the father of Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. Ishi was the father of Zoheth and Benzoheth.
text: Simonn nan ma mbijabim munaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Amnonn, ni Rina, ni Ben‑Hanann, ni Tilonn. Isi nan ma mbijabim mulee la. Baayimbil le nan ye Sohef ni Ben‑Sohef. Sela aayaabitiib aayimbil

ref: The members of these clans were the potters who lived in the towns of Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king. The Descendants of Simeon
text: Bi nan ye ubɔr aayamaab, le ki koo Netayim ni Gedera aatim ni. Simeonn aayaabitiib aayimbil

ref: Simeon had five sons: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
text: Simeonn nan ma mbijabim biŋmu la. Baayimbil sɔ: Nemuel, ni Jaminn, ni Jarib, ni Sera, ni Saul.

ref: The descendants of Shaul included his son Shallum, his grandson Mibsam, and his great-grandson Mishma.
text: Saul le nan ma Salum, le uyaabil nan ye Mibsam, le uyaabisɔsɔk nan ye Misma,

ref: The descendants of Mishma included his son Hammuel, his grandson Zaccur, and his great-grandson Shimei.
text: le ki nyan Misma chee na, mmaal ngbaan nan dii kina le ti saa Hamuel, ni Sakur, ni Simei mɔk.

ref: They also lived in the five villages of Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan,
text: Bi nan ki koo ntim muŋmu mumina; Etam, ni Ayinn, ni Rimonn, ni Tokenn, ni Asann ponn ni,

ref: as well as in the nearby villages as far as the town of Baal. These are the places where Simeon's descendants had settled, according to their own family records.
text: ni ntimbim mu bi gob ki ti saa Baalaf aatiŋ ki bi liwilir aaŋangii wɔb na ni. Baah nan ŋmee baadichal, ni baah nan koo koo ntim mu ponn ni na aabɔr pu na sɔ:

ref: As their families and clans became larger, the people of Simeon had the following leaders: Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah, Joel, Jehu, Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah, and Ziza.
text: Bijab bi aayimbil paa na le nan ye bidichadam: Mesobab, ni Jamlek, ni Amasia aajapɔɔn Josa, ni Joel, ni Jehu, ni Eliwenai, ni Jaakoba, ni Jesohaya, ni Asaya, ni Adiel, ni Jesimiel, ni Benaya, ni Sisa, . Baamaal aah nan moo kpae na,

ref: When the people needed more pastureland for their flocks and herds, they looked as far as the eastern side of the valley where the town of Gerar is located,
text: le bi nan yaa koo liwilir wɔb ki bi ban bi koo Gerar aatiŋ ni le baapiih ji kitiŋ ngbaan aah bi kifataŋ ki ni na aawipuul wɔb.

ref: and they found a lot of good pastureland that was quiet and undisturbed. This had once belonged to the Hamites,
text: Bi nan kan mmoŋmɔpaan nima le mu dɔ waa cha, ki bi suuna, kaa kpa tibaa. Ham aanib le nan puen koo nima chee.

ref: but when Hezekiah was king of Judah, the descendants of Simeon attacked and forced the Hamites and Meunites off the land, then settled there.
text: Ubɔr Hesekia aanaan yoonn, le bijab bi aayimbil ŋmee paacham na nan buen Gerar aatiŋ ni ki ti ber Ham aanib ni Meunn aanib bi koo nima na aaboo. Ipiih aamoŋmɔpaan aah nan bi nima sakpen na, le bi nan jenn nyan binib ngbaan ki gaa nima.

ref: They killed the last of the Amalekites and lived there from then on.
text: Bi nan ku Amalek yaab bi nan gur na nima chee la, le ki gur koo nima ki nan saa din.

ref: Reuben was the oldest son of Jacob, but he lost his rights as the first-born son because he slept with one of his father's wives. The honor of the first-born son was then given to Joseph,
text: Jakob aajapɔpol Rubenn aayaabitiib aayimbil sɔ: Rubenn aah nan gaa ute aapuu waatiir ubaa na, waa nan ki kpa nsan u ji tininkpir aafaal ute chee. Unaal Josef le nan gaa kina aasan.

ref: Reuben had four sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
text: Jakob aajapɔpol Rubenn nan ma mbijabim binaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Hanok, ni Palu, ni Hesronn, ni Kami.

ref: The descendants of Joel included Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, Baal, and Beerah, a leader of the Reuben tribe. Later, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria took Beerah away as prisoner.
text: Joel aayaabitiib ni uyaabisɔsɔk aayimbil sɔ: Semaya, ni Gog, ni Simei, ni Maika, ni Reaya, ni Baal, ni Beera. Asiria aabɔrkpaan, u bi nan yin u ke Tiglaf Pileser na, nan chuu Beera, u nan ye binib ngbaan aasaloln na, ki nyan u baatiŋ ni.

ref: The family records also include Jeiel, who was a clan leader, Zechariah, and Bela son of Azaz and grandson of Shema of the Joel clan. They lived in the territory around the town of Aroer, as far north as Nebo and Baal-Meon,
text: ni Bela u aate nan ye Asas na. Uyaaja le nan ye Sema, u ye Joel aataŋaal ni aanii na. Ntaŋaal mue nan koo Aroer aatiŋ, ni lipepel li bi ŋŋangan wɔb ki ti saa Nebo ni Baal Meonn aatim ni na la.

ref: and as far east as the desert just west of the Euphrates River. They needed this much land because they owned too many cattle to keep them all in Gilead.
text: Bi nan kpa tiwakor sakpen Gilead aatiŋ ni, le ki gaa kitiŋ ngbaan ki nyan nteersakpiin mu bi liwipuul wɔb ki ti saa Yufrates Aamɔɔl chee na.

ref: When Saul was king, the Reuben tribe attacked and defeated the Hagrites, then took over their land east of Gilead. The Descendants of Gad
text: Ubɔr Sɔɔl aayoonn na, Rubenn aanibol nan tak Hagar yaab, ki ku bi butɔb ni, le ki gaa baatiŋ ki bi Gilead aawipuul wɔb na. Gad aayaabitiib aayimbil

ref: The tribe of Gad lived in the region of Bashan, north of the Reuben tribe. Gad's territory extended all the way to the town of Salecah.
text: Gad aanibol nan bi Rubenn aanibol aaŋangan wɔb, Basann aatiŋ pu, le ki yoor kina ti saa liwipuul wɔb Saleka aatiŋ ni.

ref: Their relatives included Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber.
text: Linibol ngbaan aataŋaal ilole imina aanib sɔ: Mikael, ni Mesulam, ni Seba, ni Jorai, ni Jakann, ni Sia, ni Eber.

ref: They were all descendants of Abihail, whose family line went back through Huri, Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz.
text: Bi nan ye Abihail, u aate ye Huri na aayaabitiib la. Biyaajatiib le nan ye Abihail, ni Huri, ni Jaroa, ni Gilead, ni Mikael, ni Jesisai, ni Jado, ni Bus.

ref: Ahi, the son of Abdiel and the grandson of Guni, was the leader of their clan.
text: Abdiel aajapɔɔn Ahi, u aayaaja nan ye Guni na, le nan ye itaŋaal imina aasaloln.

ref: The people of Gad lived in the towns in the regions of Bashan and Gilead, as well as in the pastureland of Sharon.
text: Bi nan koo Basann, ni Gilead aapepel ni, ni ntim mu bi nima chee na ni, ni mmoŋmɔpaan aatiŋ ki bi Saronn aafataŋ ni na la.

ref: Their family records were written when Jotham was king of Judah and Jeroboam was king of Israel.
text: Juda Aabɔr Jotam, ni Israel Aabɔr Jeroboam uken aayoonn, le bi nan ŋmee nimina mɔmɔk bil. Liwipuul wɔb aanibol aajab

ref: They fought against the Hagrites and the tribes of Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
text: Bi ni Hagar aanibol ŋimina, Jetur, ni Nafis, ni Nodab yaab nan too tɔb butɔb.

ref: Whenever these soldiers went to war against their enemies, they prayed to God and trusted him to help. That's why the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh defeated the Hagrites and their allies.
text: Bi nan di baanaadii tii Uwumbɔr la, le ki mee u ki ban nterm. Le Uwumbɔr nan kii baameel ki cha bi nyaŋ Hagar yaab ni bimaantɔtiib.

ref: Many of the Hagrites died in battle, because God was fighting this battle against them. The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh lived in that territory until they were taken as prisoners to Assyria. The Tribe of East Manasseh
text: Butɔb ngbaan aah nan ye Uwumbɔr aageehn na, bi nan ku baadim pam. Bi nan gur koo lipepel ngbaan ni le ki ti saa buyoonn baadim nan nyaŋ bi, ki di bi buen kitiyayan ni. Manase yaab bi bi liwipuul wɔb na aabɔr

ref: East Manasseh was a large tribe, so its people settled in the northern region of Bashan, as far north as Baal-Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
text: Manase yaab bi nan bi liwipuul wɔb na nan koo Basann aapepel ni, ki di ti saa ŋŋangan wɔb Baal Hemonn, ni Senir, ni Hemonn Aajool mɔk. Bi nan pɔr sakpen.

ref: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel were their clan leaders; they were well-known leaders and brave soldiers. The Tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh Are Defeated
text: Baataŋaal aasalolm sɔ: Efer, ni Isi, ni Eliel, ni Asriel, ni Jeremia, ni Hodafia, ni Jadiel. Bi mɔmɔk nan ye butɔb aajakpaam la, le ki ye baataŋaal aanikpaam. Uwumbɔr aah nan daa liwipuul wɔb aanibol aatafal pu na

ref: The people of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh were unfaithful to the God their ancestors had worshiped, and they started worshiping the gods of the nations that God had forced out of Canaan.
text: Tɔ, binib ngbaan nan yii Uwumbɔr u biyaajatiib nan dii na, le ki dii ŋitimbol ŋi aanib Uwumbɔr jenn nyan bi baatiŋ pu na aawaa.

ref: So God sent King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria to attack these Israelite tribes. The king led them away as prisoners to Assyria, and from then on, he forced them to live in Halah, Habor, Hara, and near the Gozan River.
text: Kina pu le Uwumbɔr nan cha Asiria yaab aabɔrkpaan Pul bɔ baatingbaln ni. U nan chur Rubenn, ni Gad, ni Manase yaab bi bi liwipuul wɔb na tinaagbiir ki di bi ti kaan Hala, ni Habor, ni Hara aatim ni, ni Gosann Aamɔɔl chee.

ref: Kohath was the father of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
text: Kohaf mu nan ma mbijabim munaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Amram, ni Isar, ni Hebronn, ni Usiel.

ref: Amram was the father of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
text: Amram nan ma mbijabim mulee la. Bima le nan ye Aaronn ni Moses. Bininkpan le nan ye Miriam. Aaronn mu nan ma mbijabim binaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Nadab, ni Abihu, ni Eleasar, ni Itamar.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia took Jehozadak to Babylon as prisoner when the Lord let the people of Judah and Jerusalem be dragged from their land.
text: Ubɔr Nebukadnesar nan chur Jehosadak, ni Juda, ni Jerusalem aanib biken buen tinaagbiir ni. Uwumbɔr le nan cha u ŋa kina. Liifai aayaabitiib biken aayimbil

ref: Levi's three sons had sons of their own.
text: Liifai nan ma mbijabim mutaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Gesonn, ni Kohaf, ni Merari.

ref: Gershon was the father of Libni and Shimei.
text: Bi mɔmɔk mu nan ma mbijabim. Gesonn le nan ma Libni ni Semei,

ref: Kohath was the father of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
text: le Kohaf nan ma Amram, ni Isar, ni Hebronn, ni Usiel,

ref: Kohath's descendants included Amminadab, Korah, Assir, Elkanah, Ebiasaph, Assir, Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul.
text: ni Tahaf, ni Uriel, ni Usia, ni Saul.

ref: Elkanah was the father of Amasai and Ahimoth.
text: Elkana nan ma mbijabim mulee la. Bima le nan ye Amasai, ni Ahimof.

ref: Ahimoth's descendants included Elkanah, Zophai, Nahath, Eliab, Jeroham, and Elkanah.
text: ni Eliab, ni Jeroham, ni Elkana.

ref: Samuel was the father of Joel and Abijah, born in that order.
text: Samuel nan ma mbijabim mulee la. Bima le nan ye Joel, u nan ye upol na, ni Abija, u nan ye uwaatiir na.

ref: Merari's descendants included Mahli, Libni, Shimei, Uzzah, Shimea, Haggiah, and Asaiah. The Temple Musicians
text: ni Simea, ni Hagia, ni Asaya. Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aalahngaab ni biwangbaab aayimbil

ref: After King David had the sacred chest moved to Jerusalem, he appointed musicians from the Levi tribe to be in charge of the music at the place of worship.
text: Baah nan yoor Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aadakaa di buen Jerusalem ponn ni na, bijab bimina le Ubɔr David nan cha bi ye bilahngaab ni biwangbaab nin chee bi dooni Uwumbɔr Jerusalem ni na.

ref: These musicians served at the sacred tent and later at the Lord's temple that King Solomon built.
text: Waahr aan Ubɔr Solomonn nin maa Uwumbɔr Aadichal na, bi nan yakr le ki tun lituln Uwumbɔr Aabool ponn ni.

ref: The rest of the Levites were appointed to work at the sacred tent. The Descendants of Aaron
text: Biŋeen aatɔtiib Liifai yaab biken le nan tun ŋitun ŋi mɔmɔk gur ki bi, baah dooni Uwumbɔr nin chee na. Aaronn aayaabitiib aayimbil

ref: Only Aaron and his descendants were allowed to offer sacrifices and incense on the two altars at the sacred tent. They were in charge of the most holy place and the ceremonies to forgive sins, just as God's servant Moses had commanded.
text: Aaronn, ni ujapɔtiib, ni uyaabitiib le nan seer tulalee aayon, ki toor kitork ki joo seer mmii ni, kitork aabimbiln paab. Bima le nan yeh Chain Chain Aapepel ni aadoon, ki toor kitork ki ga cha Uwumbɔr di cha pinn Israel yaab aatunwanbir na. Bi nan ŋani nimina mɔmɔk, Uwumbɔr aatutunn Moses aah nan mɔk pu na la.

ref: Aaron's descendants belonged to the Levite clan of Kohath, and they were the first group chosen to receive towns to live in.
text: Aaronn aayaabitiib bi nan ye Kohaf aataŋaal pu aanib na le nan puen gaal kitiŋ, baah di nin chee tii Liifai yaab na.

ref: They received the town of Hebron in the territory of Judah and the pastureland around it.
text: Baapepel le nan ye Hebronn, ni bi Juda aatiŋ pu na aapepel, ni tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan i maln goln nima chee na.

ref: But the farmland and villages around Hebron were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
text: Le Jefune aajapɔɔn Kaleb nan tee yeh ikpaakon ni ntimbim mu bi nima chee na.

ref: From the Benjamin tribe they were given the towns of Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth and the pastureland around them. Thirteen towns were given to Aaron's descendants.
text: Baatim mu nan bi Benjaminn aapepel ni na mu sɔ: Geba, ni Alemef, ni Anatof, ni mu aamoŋmɔpaan. Baatim mu ponn ni bi ni baadichal nan koo na, nan ti kpaan ntim kipiik ni mutaa la.

ref: The rest of the Levite clan of Kohath received ten towns from West Manasseh.
text: Bi nan too inaan le ki yakr ntim kipiik Manase aanibol ligeln li bi liwilir wɔb na aapepel ni, ki tii Kohaf aataŋaal i gur na aadichal.

ref: The Levite clan of Gershon received thirteen towns from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and East Manasseh in Bashan.
text: Bi nan yakr ntim kipiik ni mutaa le tii Gesonn aataŋaal aadichal, Isakar aanibol, ni Aser aanibol, ni Naftali aanibol, ni Manase aanibol ligeln li bi liwipuul wɔb Basann aatiŋ ni na aapepel ni.

ref: The Levite clan of Merari received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
text: Bi nan ki yakr kina le tii Merari aataŋaal aadichal ntim kipiik ni mulee, Rubenn, ni Gad, ni Sebulunn aapepel ni.

ref: So the people of Israel gave the Levites towns to live in and the pastureland around them.
text: Kina le Israel yaab nan yakr ntim, ni mu aamoŋmɔpaan tii Liifai yaab, ke bi li koo mu ponn ni.

ref: All the towns were chosen with the Lord's help, including those towns from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
text: Bi nan ki too inaan le ki yakr ntim mu bi Juda, ni Simeonn, ni Benjaminn aapepel aan ŋaayimbil ŋmee paacham na mu ki tii Liifai yaab.

ref: Some of the families of the Kohath clan received their towns from the tribe of Ephraim.
text: Bi nan tii Kohaf aataŋaal pu aadichal ŋibaa ntim ni mu aamoŋmɔpaan Efraim aapepel ni. Ntim ngbaan aayimbil sɔ:

ref: And from West Manasseh they received Aner and Bileam, together with their pastureland.
text: Manase aanibol ligeln li bi liwilir wɔb na ponn ni mu, bi nan di Aner, ni Bileam aatim, ni mu aamoŋmɔpaan le tii bi.

ref: The Gershonite clan received two towns from the tribe of East Manasseh: Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth, including the pastureland around them.
text: Baah nan tii Gesonn aataŋaal aadichal ntim mu ni mu aamoŋmɔpaan na aayimbil sɔ: Golann ki bi Basann ni na, ni Astarof aatim mu bi Manase aanibol ligeln li bi liwipuul wɔb aapepel ni na.

ref: The Gershonites also received four towns from the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh, Daberath, Ramoth, and Anem, including the pastureland around them.
text: ni Ramof, ni Anem aatim mu bi Isakar aapepel ni na.

ref: Finally, the Gershonites received three towns from the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim, including the pastureland around them.
text: Naftali aapepel mu ni, baatim le nan ye Kedes, ki bi Galilee ni na, ni Hamonn, ni Kiriataim.

ref: The rest of the Merari clan received the towns of Rimmono and Tabor and their pastureland from the tribe of Zebulun.
text: Merari aataŋaal pu aadichal ŋi gur na aatim, ni mu aamoŋmɔpaan le paa na. Sebulunn aapepel ni, baatim le nan ye Rimono ni Tabor:

ref: Issachar was the father of four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
text: Isakar nan ma mbijabim munaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Tola, ni Pua, ni Jasub, ni Simronn.

ref: Tola was the father of Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, who were all brave soldiers and family leaders in their clan. There were
text: Ujapɔɔn Tola nan ma mbijabim muloob la. Baayimbil sɔ: Usi, ni Refaya, ni Jeriel, ni Jamai, ni Ibsam, ni Semuel. Bima le nan ye Tola aataŋaal aadichadam, le ki nan ye butɔb aajakpaam. Ubɔr David aayoonn na, biyaabitiib nan ti saa binib ŋichur moninko ni ŋilee ni ikui iloob la.

ref: Ephraim mourned for his sons a long time, and his relatives came to comfort him.
text: Bite Efraim nan wii baakpuul ni ti yunn sakpen, le unaabitiib buen ti sɔŋ usui.

ref: Uzzi was the father of Izrahiah and the grandfather of Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, who were also family leaders.
text: Usi nan ma Israhia baanja la. Israhia nan ma mbijabim munaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Maikel, ni Obadia, ni Joel, ni Isia. U ni bi mɔmɔk nan ye bidichadam la.

ref: Zophah was the father of Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
text: Sofa aayaabitiib aayimbil sɔ: Sua, ni Hanefer, ni Sual, ni Beri, ni Imra,

ref: In fact, according to family records, the tribe of Issachar had a total of
text: Baah nan ŋmee Isakar aanibol aadichadam bi ga ŋmaa buen butɔb na, bi nan ti kpaan bijab ŋichur imonko inaa ni ŋilole la. Benjaminn ni Dann aayaabitiib aayimbil

ref: Benjamin was the father of three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
text: Benjaminn nan ma mbijabim bitaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Bela, ni Beker, ni Jediael.

ref: Bela was the father of Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were all brave soldiers and family leaders in their father's clan. The number of soldiers in their clan was
text: Bela nan ma mbijabim muŋmu la. Baayimbil sɔ: Esbonn, ni Usi, ni Usiel, ni Jerimof, ni Iri. Bi nan ye bidichadam le baataŋaal ni. Bi nan ki ye butɔb aajakpaam la. Biyaabitiib bi nan ye butɔb aajab na nan ye binib ŋichur moninko ni ŋilee ni bijab piitaa ni binaa la.

ref: Becher was the father of Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth.
text: Beker nan ma mbijabim muwae la. Baayimbil sɔ: Semira, ni Joas, ni Elieser, ni Eliwenai, ni Omri, ni Jeremof, ni Abija, ni Anatof, ni Alemef.

ref: Ephraim was the father of Shuthelah and the ancestor of Bered, Tahath, Eleadah, Tahath,
text: Efraim aayaabitiib ki ti saa uyaabisɔsɔk aayimbil sɔ: Sutela, ni Bered, ni Tahaf, ni Eleada, ni Tahaf,

ref: Jediael was the father of Bilhan and the grandfather of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
text: Jediael nan ma Bilhann baanja la, le Bilhann ma nan ma mbijabim mulole. Baayimbil sɔ: Jeus, ni Benjaminn, ni Ehud, ni Kenaana, ni Setann, ni Tasis, ni Ahisahar.

ref: Ulam was the father of Bedan. These were all descendants of Gilead, the son of Machir and the grandson of Manasseh.
text: Ulam mu nan ma ubijabo le ki yin u ke Bedann. Manase aajapɔɔn Makir mu aajapɔɔn Gilead aayaabitiib le nan ye bi mɔmɔk.

ref: Ir was the father of Shuppim and Huppim, who also belonged to this clan. Dan was the father of Hushim. The Descendants of Naphtali
text: Supim ni Hupim mu nan ye linibol limina aanib la. Dann nan ma Husim baanja la, le u ye ubijabo. Naftali aayaabitiib aayimbil

ref: Naphtali's mother was Bilhah, and he was the father of Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. The Descendants of Manasseh
text: Naftali nan ma mbijabim munaa la. Baayimbil sɔ: Jasiel, ni Guni, ni Jeser, ni Salum. Bi nan ye Bilha aayaabitiib la. Manase aayaabitiib aayimbil

ref: Manasseh and his Syrian wife were the parents of Asriel and Machir the father of Gilead.
text: Manase nan ma unaagbiipii u nyan ni Aram aatiŋ ni na chee mbijabim mulee la. Bima le nan ye Asriel ni Makir. Makir le nan ma Gilead.

ref: Machir found a wife for Huppim and one for Shuppim. Machir had a sister named Maacah. Zelophehad was also a descendant of Manasseh, and he had five daughters.
text: Makir le nan chɔi bipiib tii Hupim ni Supim. Uninkpan aayimbil le nan ye Maaka. Makir aajapɔleler le nan ye Selofehad. Uma nan ma mpiibim ŋmeen la.

ref: Machir and his wife Maacah were the parents of Peresh and Sheresh. Peresh was the father of Ulam and Rekem.
text: Makir aapuu Maaka nan ma mbijabim mulee la. Bi nan yin bi ke Peres ni Seres. Peres nan ma mbijabim mulee la. Bima le nan ye Ulam ni Rakem.

text: U nan bui Juda aanib ke, “Cha ti maa ŋigon ni tidir ti fɔk na, ni ibisamɔi i ga li laŋni na kiir timi aatim. Taah tun Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aageehn na le ti kpa mpɔɔn kitiŋ kee pu. U kii timi ki tii timi lifuur ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu.” Kina pu na, bi nan maa, ki kan nkam.

text: N‑yoonn baan ngbaan le Filistia yaab mu nan bi looni ntim mu bi liwilir wɔb aagongon ŋi bi taab na, ni Juda aaŋangii wɔb. Bi nan gaa Bef Semes, ni Aijalonn, ni Gederof aatim, ni Soko, ni Timna, ni Gimso aatim ni itingbaan i bi mu chee na, ki kal mu ni kookoo.

text: Ubɔr Ahas aah kaa nan tii waanib baabamɔn ki bii Uwumbɔr aakaal na, le Uwumbɔr cha tibɔr dan nan lir waatiŋ Juda pu.

text: Kina pu le Ahas yoor Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni, ni libɔrdichal ni, ni binib ngbaan aasalolm aadichal ni aasalmaa ki ti di tii ubɔrkpaan ngbaan. Tɔ, nimina mɔmɔk aa nan tii u nterm mubaa. Ahas aatunwanbir aabɔr

text: Waatunwanbir aah nan ti moo bi nyaŋ ni na, le uja Ahas moo tun titunwanbir ti ubaa aa kee tun na.

ref: He said to himself, “The Syrian gods must have helped their kings defeat me. Maybe if I offer sacrifices to those gods, they will help me.” That was the sin that finally led to the downfall of Ahaz, as well as to the destruction of Judah.
text: U nan toor kitork tii Siria yaab bi nyaŋ u na aawaa. U nan bui ke, “Siria aawaa le ter Siria aabɔrb, kina pu na, m mu yaa toor kitork tii ŋi kan, nibaakan ŋi ga ter m mu.” Le kina aatuln joo ni tibɔbir nan lii u ni waatimbol pu.

ref: Ahaz collected all the furnishings of the temple and smashed them to pieces. Then he locked the doors to the temple and set up altars to foreign gods on every street corner in Jerusalem.
text: Ni nan ki kpee na le ye ke u yoor Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aawanbankaan le ki gbaa wiil ni mɔmɔk yuk yuk. U nan laŋ Uwumbɔr Aadichal le ki maa ŋiwaa aatork aabimbin Jerusalem aatiŋ ni, ni kookoo.

ref: In every city and town in Judah he built local shrines to worship foreign gods. All of this made the Lord God of his ancestors very angry.

text: Waanaan yoonn aatun mɔmɔk, ki nyan mu aapiin ki ti saa ndoon na, bi Juda ni Israel Aabɔrb Aatun Aagbaŋ ni la.

text: Le Ubɔr Hesekia ni binib ngbaan mɔmɔk gbaan kitiŋ ki doon Uwumbɔr.

ref: Then he called the priests and Levites to the east courtyard of the temple
text: U nan kuun bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab bibaa Uwumbɔr Aadichal aachiln li bi liwipuul wɔb na ni,

text: Nima pu le Uwumbɔr gee liŋuul Juda ni Jerusalem pu, le waah ŋa bi tiwan ni na cha ijawaan chuu unii mɔk ki yuk bipobil. Ni nyi nimina mɔmɔk.

text: Bi ku titetiib butɔb ni, le ki yoor tipuutiib ni timi aabim buen tinaagbiir ni.

ref: So I have decided to renew our agreement with the Lord God of Israel. Maybe then he will stop being so angry with us.

ref: Let's not waste any time, my friends. You are the ones who were chosen to be the Lord's priests and to offer him sacrifices.
text: Njapɔtiib, taa taan man. Nimi le Uwumbɔr lee ke ni li seer tulalee aayon tii u, ki li lolni binib nsan waadoon ni.”

ref: When Hezekiah finished talking, the following Levite leaders went to work: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the Kohath clan; Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel from the Merari clan; Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah from the Gershon clan; Shimri and Jeuel from the Elizaphan clan; Zechariah and Mattaniah from the Asaph clan; Jehuel and Shimei from the Heman clan; Shemaiah and Uzziel from the Jeduthun clan.

Jedutunn aataŋaal pu yaab le nan ye Semaya ni Usiel.

ref: These leaders gathered together the rest of the Levites, and they all went through the ceremony to make themselves clean. Then they began to purify the temple according to the Law of the Lord, just as Hezekiah had commanded.

ref: The priests and Levites began their work on the first day of the first month. It took them one week to purify the courtyards of the temple and another week to purify the temple. So on the sixteenth day of that same month
text: Bi nan piin lituln ngbaan njan aaŋmal aawiin mbaa daal la; le ki joo cha winiin daal na bi doo li mɔmɔk, ki kpee Uwumbɔr Aadichal aanaakook mu. Le bi nan beenin tun kina ki ti ki saa iwiin iniin, uŋmal ngbaan aawiin kipiik ni iloob daal le nan bi na. Bi nan di iwiin ngbaan le toor Uwumbɔr Aadichal ke bi ki piin idoon li ponn ni. Baah nan ki giin Uwumbɔr Aadichal ŋa uŋaal ni pu na

ref: And we have brought back all the things that King Ahaz took from the temple during the time he was unfaithful to God. We purified them and put them back in front of the altar. Worship in the Temple
text: Ti ki giin ni tiwan nimɔk Ubɔr Ahas nan yoor ŋibin ŋi waa nan ki dii Uwumbɔr na, ki ki di ni mu ŋa Uwumbɔr Aaŋaal ni. Ni mɔmɔk si Uwumbɔr aatork aabimbiln chee.”

ref: At once, Hezekiah called together the officials of Jerusalem, and they went to the temple.
text: Ubɔr Hesekia aa nan taan le ki kpaan kuun bijab bi ye bisalolm na mɔmɔk, le bi mɔmɔk buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni.

ref: They brought with them seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as sacrifices to take away the sins of Hezekiah's family and of the people of Judah, as well as to purify the temple. Hezekiah told the priests, who were descendants of Aaron, to sacrifice these animals on the altar.
text: Bi nan joo inaaja ilole, ni ipiih ilole, ni ipihbi ilole, ni iŋoob ilole le ke bi ti toor chapinn aatork, nnaan aadichal ni Juda aanib pu, ki kpaan toor nyan Uwumbɔr Aadichal mu aajɔŋ. Ubɔr nan bui Aaronn aayaabitiib bi ye bitotoorb na ke bi di tiwakor ngbaan toor kitork aabimbiln paab.

ref: The priests killed the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, then splattered the blood on the altar.
text: Bitotoorb ngbaan nan pue kɔr inaaja la, le ki paan ipiih, le ki di ipihbi paan; ki joo kitork mɔk aasin yaani kitork aabimbiln pu.

ref: They took the goats to Hezekiah and the worshipers, and they laid their hands on the animals.
text: Kookoo na, bi nan di iŋoob na buen ubɔr ni bimɔk nan dan kina aadoon ni na chee, le bi di biŋaal paan i pu.

ref: The priests then killed the goats and splattered the blood on the altar as a sacrifice to take away the sins of everyone in Israel, because Hezekiah had commanded that these sacrifices be made for all the people of Israel.
text: Le bitotoorb kɔr i, ki di yaasin kpir kitork aabimbiln pu, ke ni li ye kitork ki ga nyan binib ngbaan mɔmɔk aatunwanbir na. Ubɔr ngbaan nan bui ke bi toor kitork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, ni titunwanbir aachapinn aatork tii Israel yaab mɔmɔk.

ref: The Levites were ready to play the instruments that had belonged to David; the priests were ready to blow the trumpets.

ref: As soon as Hezekiah gave the signal for the sacrifices to be burned on the altar, the musicians began singing praises to the Lord and playing their instruments,
text: Hesekia nan tii nsan ke bi piin kitork ki bi ga di see mmii ni na. Baah piin na, le binib ngbaan gaa ilahn ki pak Uwumbɔr, le biwangbaab gbaa tiwan ki pii kakaan tiib.

ref: Then Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing the songs of praise that David and Asaph the prophet had written. And so they bowed down and joyfully sang praises to the Lord.

ref: Hezekiah said to the crowd, “Now that you are once again acceptable to the Lord, bring sacrifices and offerings to give him thanks.” The people did this, and some of them voluntarily brought animals to be offered as sacrifices.
text: Hesekia nan bui binib ngbaan ke, “Naah finn nibaa chain kaa ki kpa tijɔŋ na, li joo ni man idoon aapiin ki nan toor tii Uwumbɔr.” Bi nan kii waamɔb, le biken mu nyan sil ki joo ni tiwakor ki nan toor kitork ki bi ga di see mmii ni na aatork.

ref: There were not enough priests to skin all these animals, because many of the priests had not taken the time to go through the ceremony to make themselves clean. However, since all the Levites had made themselves clean, they helped the priests until the last animal was skinned.

ref: Besides all the sacrifices that were burned on the altar, the fat from the other animal sacrifices was burned, and the offerings of wine were poured over the altar. So the temple was once again used for worshiping the Lord.
text: Bitotoorb le nan ki yeh ke bi di baah nan di tiwakor ti toor ke binib ngbaan ŋmɔ na aakpan see mmii ni, ki ki toor tiwakor ti bi ga di see mmii ni timɔnn na aatork tii Uwumbɔr. Bima le nan ki yeh ndaan mu dii ni mmii ni aatork na aabarn. Kina le bi nan ki piin ki doon Uwumbɔr, Waadichal ni.

ref: Hezekiah and the people of Judah celebrated, because God had helped them make this happen so quickly.
text: Ubɔr Hesekia ni binib ngbaan nan kpa mpopiin, Uwumbɔr aah ter bi pu aan bi tun lituln limina mɔmɔk doo mala na pu.

ref: Everyone from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north was invited. This was the largest crowd of people that had ever celebrated Passover, according to the official records.
text: le bi yin Israel yaab mɔmɔk ki nyan Dann aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangan wɔb na ki ti saa Beerseba ki bi ŋŋangii wɔb na, ke bi dan Jerusalem ni ki nan ji Lakr‑jer aajim, nkaal aah mɔk pu na, ki li wiir jer baah ti puun ji pu na.

ref: Hezekiah's messengers went everywhere in Israel and Judah with the following letter: People of Israel, now that you have survived the invasion of the Assyrian kings, it's time for you to turn back to the Lord God our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob worshiped. text: Ubɔr ni waaninkpiib nan cha ituun nyan buen Juda ni Israel yaab aatim mɔmɔk ki joo nnyim aabɔr tee: “Israel aanib, ni ŋmar Asiria yaab aah gaa kitiŋ pu na ni. Tɔ, gir ni man Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob Aadindaan Uwumbɔr chee, le u mu ga gir ni ni chee.

ref: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. Decide now to obey the Lord our God! Come to Jerusalem and worship him in the temple that will belong to him forever. Then he will stop being angry,
text: Taa li kpa tafalaaŋun ke baah nan kpa pu na man, ni tee kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb. Dan man Uwumbɔr Aadichal li Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ŋa li chain n‑yoonn mɔmɔk aan li bi Jerusalem ni na ni, ki nan doon u aan waaŋuul sɔŋ ni pu.

ref: and the enemies that have captured your families will show pity and send them back home. The Lord God is kind and merciful, and if you turn back to him, he will no longer turn his back on you.
text: Ni yaa gir ni Uwumbɔr chee kan, le binib bi chur nimi aanib buen tinaagbiir ni na ga san bi kinimbaak ki cha bi gir kun ni. Nidindaan Uwumbɔr kpa tiŋann le ki san kinimbaak. Ni yaa fenn gir u chee kan, u ga gaa nimi.”

ref: Only a few people from the tribes of Asher, West Manasseh, and Zebulun were humble and went to Jerusalem.
text: Bibaa mu nan tee nyan ni Aser, ni Manase, ni Sebulunn aanibol ni ki gee ke bi dan Jerusalem aatiŋ ni.

ref: God also made everyone in Judah eager to do what Hezekiah and his officials had commanded. Passover Is Celebrated
text: Uwumbɔr nan bi tun waatuln Juda aapepel ni, le ki cha binib ngbaan ŋa kimɔbaan baah pɔɔni bibaa pu ke bi kii waageehn ki dii ubɔr ni waaninkpiib aah len pu na. Baah jin Lakr‑jer Aajim pu na

ref: In the second month, a large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread.
text: Kinipaak sakpeŋ le nan kuun Jerusalem ponn ni, ŋmalee ni, ke bi ji boroboro u kaa kpa boroboro aanyɔk na aajim.

text: Uwumbɔr nan kii Hesekia aameel; u nan di cha pinn binib ngbaan, kaa ŋa bi nibaa.

ref: Hezekiah thanked the Levites for doing such a good job, leading the celebration. The worshipers celebrated for seven days by offering sacrifices, by eating the sacred meals, and by praising the Lord God of their ancestors.
text: Hesekia nan pak Liifai yaab ngbaan baah nan di nlan mu tun baatuln ki joo cha Uwumbɔr aadoon chee na pu. Lelee aajim Iwiin ilole i ponn ni bi nan toor kitork ki pak biyaajatiib Aadindaan Uwumbɔr na aah jer na,

ref: It was the biggest celebration in Jerusalem since the days of King Solomon, the son of David.
text: Ki nyan David aajapɔɔn Ubɔr Solomonn aayoonn na kina aawan aa kee ŋa; kina pu na, Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni nan ye mmɔɔn ŋmeen la.

ref: The priests and Levites asked God to bless the people, and from his home in heaven, he did.
text: Bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab nan mee Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa binib ngbaan pu. Le Uwumbɔr nan bi udo paacham ki ŋun baah mee u pu na le ki kii ŋi.

ref: Hezekiah divided the priests and Levites into groups, according to their duties. Then he assigned them the responsibilities of offering sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. He also appointed people to serve at the temple and to sing praises at the temple gates.

ref: The official records also included their wives and children, because they had also been faithful in keeping themselves clean and acceptable to serve the Lord.
text: Naah nan ye ke bi gor ki li bi chain aatuln ni n‑yoonn mumɔk bi yin bi na, bi nan ŋmee bi ni bipuutiib, ni baabim, ni bi mɔmɔk koo bi chee na aayimbil bil la.

ref: He told the people of Jerusalem to bring the offerings that were to be given to the priests and Levites, so that they would have time to serve the Lord with their work.
text: Ubɔr nan ki tuk Jerusalem aanib ke bi li joo ni ipiin i ye bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab yaan na, aan bi ŋmaa kan mpaan ki li ŋani Uwumbɔr Aakaal aah ban pu na.

ref: After the Festival, the people went to every town in Judah and smashed the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. text: Njim ngbaan aah jer doo na, Israel aanib mɔmɔk nan buen Juda aatiŋ mɔk ni, le ki ti gbaa wiil ŋiwaatakpal, ki gbaa wɔi liwaapii Asera aanaŋ, ki ber ŋiwaa aatork aabimbin ni tiwaachur mɔmɔk. text: U nan nyani ubaa aawakor le tii aan bi joo toor kichakpiik ni, ni kijook mɔk aatork ki bi joo seer mmii ni na, ki kpee Likpaakool daal, ni Uŋmapɔɔn Aajim aatork, ni njim muken na aatork, Uwumbɔr Aakaal aah mɔk pu na.

ref: As soon as the people heard what the king wanted, they brought a tenth of everything they owned, including their best grain, wine, olive oil, honey, and other crops.
text: Ubɔr aah tii limɔboln ngbaan na, libuul ngbaan ni, le binib ngbaan di baajan aajikaabim, ni ndaan, ni olif aakpan, ni tisiir, ni tisar aajikaar tiken na, ni baah kpa tiwan ni mɔmɔk, ki yakr ni kipiik kipiik ki nyan nibaabaa tii Uwumbɔr na buen.

ref: The people from the other towns of Judah brought a tenth of their herds and flocks, as well as a tenth of anything they had dedicated to the Lord.
text: Binib bi mɔmɔk nan koo Juda aatim ni na nan joo ni baanaa ni ipiih mu yaan kina la, le ki ki joo ni ipiin i wiir sakpen na, ki nan di i tii Bidindaan Uwumbɔr.

ref: The people started bringing their offerings to Jerusalem in the third month, and the last ones arrived four months later.
text: Ŋmataa ponn ni le ipiin ngbaan nan piin ki fuur ni, ki joo kina ki ti saa iŋmal inaa i paan na.

ref: When Hezekiah and his officials saw these offerings, they thanked the Lord and the people.
text: Ubɔr Hesekia ni waaninkpiib aah kan ke bi tii sakpen na, le bi pak Uwumbɔr, ki pak waanib Israel yaab mu.

ref: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the large amount of offerings.
text: Ubɔr nan baa bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab ipiin ngbaan pu,

ref: The high priest at the time was Azariah, a descendant of Zadok, and he replied, “Ever since the people have been bringing us their offerings, we have had more than enough food and supplies. The Lord has certainly blessed his people. Look at how much is left over!”
text: le Utotoorninkpel Asaria, u nan ye Sadok aayaabil na bui u ke, “Binib ngbaan aah piin ki joo ni ipiin ngbaan Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni na, tijikaar pam bi le ti ji, le ti gur na wiir sakpen a. Uwumbɔr aah ŋa tinyoor ŋa waanib pu na le cha ti kpa nimina mɔmɔk.”

ref: So the king gave orders for storerooms to be built in the temple, and when they were completed,
text: Ubɔr nan cha bi toor tijikaar aadir Uwumbɔr Aadichal aapaan ni,

text: Pesia aabɔrkpaan Ataksekes mu aayoonn, le Bislam, ni Mitredaf, ni Tabeel, ni biŋeen aatɔtiib, mu ki ŋmee kigbaŋ tii ubɔrkpaan ngbaan. Bi nan ŋmee kigbaŋ ngbaan Aram yaab aaliin ni, le bi ti karni ki ki nabr tii u.

ref: This letter said: Your Majesty King Artaxerxes, we are your servants from everywhere in Western Province, and we send you our greetings.
text: Kigbaŋ ngbaan aabɔr sɔ: “Ubɔrkpaan Ataksekes, timi saanaagbiib, bi bi Yufrates aamɔɔl aawilir aapepel na le ŋmee kigbaŋ kee tii si.

text: “Naah ŋmee kigbaŋ ki tii ni mi na, bi nabr ki, ki karn ki tii mi.

text: Juu yaab aayidam ngbaan nan maa Uwumbɔr Aadichal ngbaan mala, le Hagai ni Sekaria bi nan ye Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr na nan pɔɔk bitaakpab. Israel yaab Aawumbɔr, ni Pesia aabɔrkpaam Sairus, ni Darius, ni Ataksekes aah nan bui bi pu na, bi nan doo Uwumbɔr Aadichal ngbaan aamaam.

ref: Ezra was a priest and an expert in the laws and commands that the Lord had given to Israel. One day King Artaxerxes gave Ezra a letter which said:
text: Ubɔrkpaan Ataksekes le nan di kigbaŋ kimina tii Esra, u ye utotoor ni ugbanbae, u nyi ikaal i Uwumbɔr nan di tii Israel yaab mbamɔm na ke:

ref: Greetings from the great King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and expert in the teachings of the God of heaven.
text: “Kigbaŋ kee nyan ni ubɔrkpaan Ataksekes chee la, le ki cha Esra u ye utotoor, ni ugbanbae, u nyi Uwumbɔr u bi Paacham na Aakaal na chee.

ref: Any of the people of Israel or their priests or Levites in my kingdom may go with you to Jerusalem if they want to. My seven advisors and I agree that you may go to Jerusalem and Judah to find out if the laws of your God are being obeyed.
text: Min, ni maasusurb bilole na, le tun si ke ni ti lik ke Jerusalem, ni Juda aatim yaab joo Saawumbɔr Aakaal mu u di ŋa aaŋaal ni na aan baa joo mu.

ref: When you go, take the silver and gold that I and my advisors are freely giving to the God of Israel, whose temple is in Jerusalem.
text: Aa ga li joo salmaa ni tikunabr aapiin i m ni maasusurb ban ke ti di tii Israel yaab Aawumbɔr, u Waadichal bi Jerusalem ni na.

ref: Take the silver and gold that you collect from everywhere in Babylonia. Also take the gifts that your own people and priests have so willingly contributed for the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
text: Aa ga ki li joo salmaa, ni tikunabr ti aa ga gaa Babiloŋ aapepel mɔmɔk ni aapiin i Israel aanib ni bitotoorb ga tii Baawumbɔr, u Waadichal bi Jerusalem ni na.

ref: Use the money carefully to buy the best bulls, rams, lambs, grain, and wine. Then sacrifice them on the altar at God's temple in Jerusalem.
text: “Aa taa ji ŋimombil ngbaan yɔl yɔl, aa di ŋi daa inaaja, ni ipihja, ni ipihbi, ni njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ki di ni toor kitork, Uwumbɔr Aadichal aatork aabimbiln pu, Jerusalem ni.

ref: If any silver or gold is left, you and your people may use it for whatever pleases your God.
text: Aa ga ŋmaa di salmaa ni tikunabr ti gur na ŋa nimi Aawumbɔr aah ban ke ni di tun pu na.

ref: Give your God the other articles that have been contributed for use in his temple.
text: Aa ti di ŋisambil ŋi bi di tii si ke bi li joo tun Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aatuln na, ŋa Uwumbɔr aaŋaal ni Jerusalem ni.

ref: If you need to get anything else for the temple, you may have the money you need from the royal treasury.
text: Aa yaa ki ban tiwan nimɔk bi di tun Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aatuln na kan, aa ga ŋmaa di nnaan ni aamombil daa ni.

ref: Ezra, you are a priest and an expert in the laws of the God of heaven, and I order all treasurers in Western Province to do their very best to help you.
text: “M siin Yufrates aamɔɔl aawilir aapepel aaninkpiib bi tun nnaan aamombil aatuln na, ke bi tii Esra, u ye ugbanbae ki nyi Uwumbɔr u bi Paacham na Aakaal mbamɔm na, tiwan ni mɔmɔk u ban na,

ref: They must provide whatever the God of heaven demands for his temple, so that he won't be angry with me and with the kings who rule after me.
text: Aa tii tiwan ni mɔmɔk Uwumbɔr u bi Paacham na ban Waadichal ni na, ki taa cha waaŋuul fii m pu, bee bi ga nan paan m pu na.

ref: We want you to know that no priests, Levites, musicians, guards, temple servants, or any other temple workers will have to pay any kind of taxes.
text: Aa taa gaa bitotoorb, ni Liifai yaab, ni biwangbaab ni bilahngaab, ni bikikiib, ni bitutum, ni unii umɔk tun Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aatuln na ubaa lampoo.

ref: Ezra, use the wisdom God has given you and choose officials and leaders to govern the people of Western Province. These leaders should know God's laws and have them taught to anyone who doesn't know them.
text: “Le sin Esra, di nlan mu Uwumbɔr tii si na ban binib bi ga li lik ŋitun aabɔŋ na, ni bibɔjirb bi ga li joo Yufrates Aamɔɔl Aawilir aapepel aanib bi mɔmɔk bi Saawumbɔr aakaal ponn ni na. Aa mɔk unii umɔk aa nyi Nkaal ngbaan na.

ref: Everyone who fails to obey God's Law or the king's law will be punished without pity. They will either be executed or put in prison or forced to leave their country, or have all they own taken away. Ezra Praises God
text: Unii umɔk yii Saawumbɔr aakaal, bee nnaan mue aakaal na kan, bi daa utafal libuul ngbaan ni. Bi ku u, bee bi jenn nyan u kitiŋ ngbaan ni, bee bi gaa waawangol, bee bi di u ŋa kiyondiik ni.” Esra aah pak Uwumbɔr pu na

ref: Because King Artaxerxes was so kind, Ezra said: Praise the Lord God of our ancestors! He made sure that the king honored the Lord's temple in Jerusalem.
text: Le Esra bui ke, “Pak Uwumbɔr, u ye tiyaajatiib Aadindaan na man. U cha ubɔrkpaan kpa mpopiin ke u nyuŋ uma Uwumbɔr Aadichal li bi Jerusalem ni na kina.

ref: God has told the king, his advisors, and his powerful officials to treat me with kindness. The Lord God has helped me, and I have been able to bring many Jewish leaders back to Jerusalem.
text: Uwumbɔr aageehn pu le ubɔrkpaan ngbaan, ni waasusurb, ni waaninkpiib bi kpa mpɔɔn sakpen na lik faar mi. Ndindaan Uwumbɔr pɔɔk ntaakpab, le m ŋman ki cha Israel yaab aataŋaal pam aayidam nyan Babiloŋ ki dii mi gir Jerusalem ni.”

ref: Artaxerxes was king of Persia when I led the following chiefs of the family groups from Babylonia to Jerusalem:
text: Itaŋaal imina aayidam le nan bi tinaagbiir ni Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni, le ki nan dii min Esra ki gir Jerusalem ni, buyoonn ubɔrkpaan Ataksekes nan ye Pesia aabɔr na:

ref: I said to the priests: You belong to the Lord, the God of your ancestors, and these things also belong to him. The silver and gold were willingly given as gifts to the Lord.
text: M nan bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr u ye niyaajatiib Aawumbɔr na le nyan nimi, kina le ye tikunabr ni salmaa aasambil ŋi bi joo tii u ipiin na mu.

ref: I brought everyone together by the river that flows to the town of Ahava where we camped for three days. Not one Levite could be found among the people and priests.
text: M nan kuun binib ngbaan mɔmɔk nnyunsan mu aanyun puu cha Ahafa aatiŋ ni na chee, le ti nan doon nima chee iwiin itaa. M nan kan ke bitotoorb bi binib ngbaan ni, le Liifai yaab ma aa bi.

ref: So I sent for the leaders Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. I also sent for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were very wise counselors.
text: Le m nan tun yin ni biyidam ngbaan biwae: Elieser, ni Ariel, ni Semaya, ni Elnatann, ni Jarib, ni Elnatann, ni Natann, ni Sekaria, ni Mesulam, ni bimɔmɔkb bilee, Joyarib ni Elnatann.

ref: Then I sent them to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, and I told them to ask him and his temple workers to send people to serve in God's temple.
text: M nan tun bi Ido, u ye binib ngbaan aayidaan na chee, Kasifia aatiŋ ni, ke bi ti bui u ke u ni uŋeen aatɔtiib bi tun Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aatuln na tii ni timi binib aan bi nan li tun Uwumbɔr aatuln Waadichal ni.

ref: God was kind to us and caused them to send a skillful man named Sherebiah, who was a Levite from the family of Mahli. Eighteen of his relatives came with him.
text: Uwumbɔr aageehn pu le bi nan di Liifai aanii u nyi lituln ki nyan ni Mali aataŋaal ni aan bi yin u ke Serebia na tun ni, le ujapɔtiib ni ukpetiib ni unaatiib, binib kipiik ni biniin dii ni u.

ref: We were also sent Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from the family of Merari along with
text: Bi nan ki cha Merari aataŋaal ni yaab, Hasabia ni Jesaya, ni baamaal binib moninko mu dan.

ref: Beside the Ahava River, I asked the people to go without eating and to pray. We humbled ourselves and asked God to bring us and our children safely to Jerusalem with all of our possessions.
text: Ahafa Aanyunsan ngbaan chee le m nan siin ke ti mɔmɔk lul bumɔb ki sunn tibaa taab, timi Aawumbɔr chee, ki mee u aan u cheen timi lisachuln ngbaan ni, ki li kii timi, ni timi aabim, ni timi aawan mɔmɔk.

ref: So we went without food and asked God himself to protect us, and he answered our prayers. The Gifts for the Temple
text: Ti nan lul bumɔb ki mee Uwumbɔr ke u li kii timi, le u kii timi aameel ngbaan. Uwumbɔr Aadichal aapiin

ref: I chose twelve of the leading priests—Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their relatives.
text: M nan nyan bitotoorb bi ye bisalolm na ponn ni Serebia, ni Hasabia, ni kipiik biken,

ref: Then I weighed the gifts that had been given for God's temple, and I divided them among the twelve priests I had chosen. There were gifts of silver and gold, as well as the articles that the king, his advisors and officials, and the people of Israel had contributed. In all there were:
text: Maah nan tii bi pu na sɔ: tikunabr ti aanyunyuun ga pii njikaabim bɔtɔ tiib ikui iŋmu na, ni tikunabr aasambil nkub, ŋi aanyunyuun ga pii njikaabim kuruwaa ŋichur ŋitaa ni ikui inaa na, ni salmaa ti aanyunyuun ga pii njikaabim bɔtɔ imonko itaa ni kipiik ni biŋmu, ni salmaa aasambil moninko, ŋi aanyunyuun ga pii njikaabim kuruwaa biniin ni siib na, ni tikumann aasambil ŋilee, ŋi aadaak ni salmaa aasambil na ye tiwanbaan na.

ref: Be sure to guard them and keep them safe until you reach Jerusalem. Then weigh them inside God's temple in the presence of the chief priests, the Levites, and the heads of the Israelite families.
text: Ni li kii ŋi mbamɔm aan ŋi ti fuu Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni. Ni ti ŋaŋ ni mɔmɔk bitotoorb aadir ni, nima chee, ki di tii bitotoorb aayidam ni Liifai yaab, ni Israel yaab aayidam Jerusalem ni.”

ref: The priests and Levites then took charge of the gifts that had been weighed, so they could take them to the temple of our God in Jerusalem. The Return to Jerusalem
text: Le bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab nan kii tikunabr, ni salmaa, ni ŋisambil ngbaan, ke ni ti fuu Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni, Jerusalem ponn ni. Binib ngbaan aah nan gir Jerusalem pu na

ref: On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River and started for Jerusalem. Our God watched over us, and as we traveled along, he kept our enemies from ambushing us.
text: Ti nan nyan Ahafa Aanyunsan ngbaan chee njan aaŋmal aawiin kipiik ni ilee daal, le ki cha Jerusalem. Timi Aawumbɔr nan bi ti chee, le ki kii timi bidim, ni binib bi ga keln timi nsan ni na chee.

ref: After arriving in Jerusalem, we rested for three days.
text: Taah nan ti fuu Jerusalem na, le ti nan di iwiin itaa fuur.

ref: Then on the fourth day we went to God's temple, where the silver, the gold, and the other things were weighed and given to the priest Meremoth son of Uriah. With him were Eleazar son of Phinehas and the two Levites, Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
text: Le ti nan buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni winaa daal, le ki ti ŋaŋ tikunabr, ni salmaa, ni ŋisambil ngbaan, le ki di ŋi tii Uria aajapɔɔn Meremof u nan ye utotoor na. Binib bi nan kpee u pu na le nan ye Fineas aajapɔɔn Eleasar, ni Liifai yaab bilee, bima le nan ye Jesua aajapɔɔn Josabad, ni Binui aajapɔɔn Noadia.

ref: Some of those who had returned took the king's orders to the governors and officials in Western Province. Then the officials did what they could for the people and for the temple of God.
text: Bi nan ki nyan ubɔrkpaan ngbaan aah nan tii bi kigbaŋ ki na ki di tii Yufrates Aamɔɔl aawilir aapepel aayidaan ni waaninkpiib, le bi nan tii bi nterm, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aadoon aaterm.

ref: Later the Jewish leaders came to me and said: Many Israelites, including priests and Levites, are living just like the people around them. They are even guilty of some of the horrible sins of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
text: Nimina mɔmɔk aah ŋa doo na, le Israel yaab aayidam bibaa dan nan bui mi ke binib ngbaan, ni bitotoorb, ni Liifai yaab aa yakr binib bi koo gbɔk bi ki ye Amonn yaab, ni Moab yaab, ni Ijipt yaab, ni Kanaann yaab, ni Hef yaab, ni Peres yaab, ni Jebus yaab, ni Amor yaab na chee. Bi tun inimɔɔn, ni tijɔŋ aatun ŋi binib ngbaan tun na la.

ref: Some Israelite men have married foreign women and have let their sons do the same thing. Our own officials and leaders were the first to commit this disgusting sin, and now God's holy people are mixed with foreigners.
text: Bi yoor biwɔwɔmpiib la, le bima Uwumbɔr aanib bi bi chain na kpaln tijɔŋ aanib. Biyidam ni bininkpiib na le nan ye biyikpaadam.

ref: This news made me so angry that I ripped my clothes and tore hair from my head and beard. Then I just sat in shock
text: Maah ŋun kina na, le m daa kar maawanpeenkaan, ni n‑yikpir, ni nlangban, mpombiin pu.

ref: until the time for the evening sacrifice. Many of our people were greatly concerned and gathered around me, because the God of Israel had warned us to stay away from foreigners. Ezra's Prayer
text: M nan ka nima, kinimbaak ni, le kijook aatork nan fuu, le binib kuun ni m chee, binib bi ijawaan nan chuu bi, bima Israel yaab Aawumbɔr aah nan len pu, binib bi nan nyan ni tinaagbiir ni ki gir ni na aatunwanbir pu na.

ref: At the time of the evening sacrifice, I was still sitting there in sorrow with my clothes all torn. So I got down on my knees, then lifted my arms,
text: Kijook aatork aayoonn aah nan fuu ni na, le m fii maah ka nin chee ki wii na, ki beenin pee maawankpir na, le ki gbaan, ki yoor ŋŋaal paacham, ki mee Ndindaan Uwumbɔr.

ref: and prayed: I am much too ashamed to face you, Lord God. Our sins and our guilt have swept over us like a flood that reaches up to the heavens.
text: M nan bui ke, “Uwumbɔr, inimɔɔn sakpiin pu, le maa ŋmaa yaar n‑yil paacham aanimbiin ni. Timi aatunwanbir muun ti nyaŋ, ki fɔk jer timi, ti fɔk ti pii kitaapaak.

ref: Since the time of our ancestors, all of us have sinned. That's why we, our kings, and our priests have often been defeated by other kings. They have killed some of us and made slaves of others; they have taken our possessions and made us ashamed, just as we are today.
text: Ki nyan tiyaaja tiib yoonn ki nan saa din, timi saanib tun titunwanbir sakpen. Timi aatunwanbir pu le timi, ni timi aabɔrb, ni timi aatotoorb koo ntiyayam aabɔrb aaŋaal ni, le bi ku timi, ki sun timi aawangol, ki di timi buen tinaagbiir ni. Ti kpaln binimɔɔnib le ki nan saa din wee.

ref: But for now, Lord God, you have shown great kindness to us. You made us truly happy by letting some of us settle in this sacred place and by helping us in our time of slavery.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, le aa san timi kinimbaak, ki cha ti ponn ni siib nyan tinaagbiir ngbaan ponn ni, ki ti koo nsuudoon ni, kitiŋ ki bi chain na ponn ni. Aa nyan timi tinaagbiir ngbaan ni, le ki tii timi limɔfapɔln.

ref: We are slaves, but you have never turned your back on us. You love us, and because of you, the kings of Persia have helped us. It's as though you have given us new life! You let us rebuild your temple and live safely in Judah and Jerusalem.
text: Ti nan ye binaagbiib la, le aa nyan timi tinaagbiir ngbaan ni. Aa cha Pesia aatiŋ aabɔrb san timi kinimbaak, ki tii timi nsan ke ti li bi limɔfal ni, ki ki gir maa Saadichal li nan ber na, ki cha ti kan nsuudoon, Jerusalem ni Juda aatim muken ni.

ref: Our God, what can we say now? Even after all this, we have disobeyed the commands
text: “Uwumbɔr, ti ga ki len ke ba, tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋa na pu? Ti ti ki gir yii ikaal ngbaan,

ref: that were given to us by your servants the prophets. They said the land you are giving us is full of sinful and wicked people, who never stop doing disgusting things.
text: ikaal i aa nan di tii saabɔnabr bi ye saatutum na, ke bi di tii timi na. Aa nan bui timi ke kitiŋ ki ti ban ti koo ki ponn ni na aa ŋan, ba pu? binib bi bi ki pu na di inimɔɔn ni tijɔŋ aatuln le gbiin kaapepel mɔmɔk.

ref: And we were warned not to let our daughters and sons marry their sons and daughters. Your prophets also told us never to help those foreigners or even let them live in peace. You wanted us to become strong and to enjoy the good things in the land, then someday to leave it to our children forever.
text: Bi nan bui timi ke ti yaa ban ke ti li kpa mpopiin kitiŋ ngbaan pu, aan ki nan kpaln tiyaabitiib aatiŋ kan, ti taa yoor baapiibim, ki taa ter bi aan bi kan tinyoor baatun ni.

ref: You punished us because of our terrible sins. But you did not punish us nearly as much as we deserve, and you have brought some of us back home.
text: Timi Aawumbɔr, saah ŋa timi tiwan mɔmɔk ki daa titafal pu na, ti nyi ke saa daa titafal ki ŋeer timi aatunwanbir, le ki cha ti ponn ni siib ŋmar.

ref: Why should we disobey your commands again by letting our sons and daughters marry these foreigners who do such disgusting things? That would make you angry enough to destroy us all!
text: Kina kan, ti ga ŋa kinye ki suln saakaal bɔr, ki ki gir yoor bibiindam ngbaan aapiibim? Ti yaa ŋa kina kan, saaŋuul ga fii ti pu sakpen, le aa ga kuln ti mɔmɔk aan ubaa taa ŋmar.

ref: Lord God of Israel, you have been more than fair by letting a few of us survive. But once again, our sins have made us ashamed to face you.
text: Uwumbɔr, Israel yaab Aadindaan, aa ye ubamɔndaan la, le ki tee cha ti ŋmar. Ti kpiir timi aataani tuk si; taa kpa nsan ke ti dan nan sil aanimbiin ni.”

ref: While Ezra was down on his knees in front of God's temple, praying with tears in his eyes and confessing the sins of the people of Israel, a large number of men, women, and children gathered around him and cried bitterly.
text: Esra aah nan gbaa kitiŋ ki mee limeel, Uwumbɔr Aadichal aabisamɔb chee, ki wii ki kpiir titunwanbir timina na, le Israel yaab aanipaak, bijab, ni bipiib, ni mbim dan nan mann goln u, ki wii pam.

ref: Shecaniah son of Jehiel from the family of Elam said: Ezra, we have disobeyed God by marrying these foreign women. But there is still hope for the people of Israel,
text: Le Elam aataŋaal ni aanii u bi yin u ke Jehiel na aajapɔɔn Sekania, bui Esra ke, “Ti nyan Uwumbɔr aapuwɔb, ki yoor biwɔwɔm aapiib, tɔ, nimina mɔmɔk mu na, Israel yaab beenin kpa limakl.

ref: if we follow your advice and the advice of others who truly respect the laws of God. We must promise God that we will divorce our foreign wives and send them away, together with their children.
text: Taah ban pu dandana wee na le ye ke ti ga puu tipuukpaan tii timi Aawumbɔr, ke ti ga di bipiib ngbaan ni baabim lii. Ti ga ŋa aa ni binib bi nyuŋni Uwumbɔr aakaal na aah sur timi ke ti ŋa pu na. Ti ga ŋa Uwumbɔr aakaal aah len pu na.

ref: Ezra, it's up to you to do something! We will support whatever you do. So be brave!
text: Ni ye sin aatuln le ke aa fii sil. Ti si aachaŋ ni, kina pu na, fii sil ki cha kina ŋa.”

ref: Ezra stood up and made the chief priests, the Levites, and everyone else in Israel swear that they would follow the advice of Shecaniah.
text: Le Esra nan piin ki cha bitotoorb aayidam, ni Liifai yaab aayidam, ni binib bi gur na puu tipuur ke bi ga ŋa Sekania aah len pu na.

ref: Then Ezra left God's temple and went to spend the night in the living quarters of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He felt sorry because of what the people had done, and he did not eat or drink a thing.
text: Nee aapuwɔb le u siir Uwumbɔr Aadichal aabisamɔb chee, ki koo Eliasib aajapɔɔn Jehohanann aadiik ni, ki ti dɔ nima ki wii, binib bi nyan tinaagbiir ni ki gir ni na aah tun titunwanbir ti na pu. Waa nan jin, kaa nyun mu.

ref: The officials and leaders sent a message to all who had returned from Babylonia and were now living in Jerusalem and Judah. This message told them to meet in Jerusalem within three days, or else they would lose everything they owned and would no longer be considered part of the people that had returned from Babylonia.
text: Bi nan bui ke joo cha ni iwiin itaa daal na, unii umɔk yii kaa dan na, bi ga gaa waawangol mɔmɔk, le waan ki li kpa nsan ke u ye binib ngbaan ponn ni ubaa.

ref: Three days later, on the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone from Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem and sat in the temple courtyard. It was a serious meeting, and they sat there, trembling in the rain.
text: Joo cha ni iwiin itaa daal ngbaan, ŋmawae aawiin moninko daal na, bijab bi mɔmɔk koo Juda ni Benjaminn aapepel ni na nan kuun ni Jerusalem ni, Uwumbɔr Aadichal aapaan ni. Utaal nan bi nu sakpen, ki kpee nkuun ngbaan aanyunyuun pu na, unii mɔk nan si jii la.

ref: Ezra the priest stood up and said: You have broken God's Law by marrying foreign women, and you have made the whole nation guilty!
text: Utotoor Esra le nan fii sil ki len bi chee tibɔr. U nan bui bi ke, “Naah yoor biwɔwɔmpiib pu na, le ni nyan Uwumbɔr aapuwɔb, ki joo ni tibɔbir Israel aanib mɔmɔk pu.

ref: Now you must confess your sins to the Lord God of your ancestors and obey him. Divorce your foreign wives and don't have anything to do with the rest of the foreigners who live around here.
text: Dandana wee na, kpiir nimi aatunwanbir tuk Uwumbɔr u ye niyaajatiib mu Aawumbɔr na, ki ŋa tiwan ni ga piir usui na. Taa ki kpaan biwɔwɔm bi bi timi aatiŋ pu na chee man, ki di naah joo nwɔwɔmbim mu na lii.”

ref: Everyone in the crowd shouted: You're right! We will do what you say.
text: Le binib ngbaan teen mpɔɔn pu ke, “Ti ga ŋa saah len pu na la,”

ref: But there are so many of us, and we can't just stay out here in this downpour. A lot of us have sinned by marrying foreign women, and the matter can't be settled in only a day or two.
text: le ki tee ki len ke, “Kinipaak ngbaan wiir sakpen a, le utaal mu ki nu sakpen. Taan ŋmaa li si lipaal do kina. Timi bi bi titunwanbir timina ponn ni na wiir sakpen, tibɔr ngbaan mu aa ye liwinbaal aabɔr.

ref: Why can't our officials stay on in Jerusalem and take care of this for us? Let everyone who has sinned in this way meet here at a certain time with leaders and judges from their own towns. If we take care of this problem, God will surely stop being so terribly angry with us.
text: Cha timi aaninkpiib gaar Jerusalem ni do, ki lik tibɔr ngbaan ponn ni, le ki nin cha unii umɔk joo uwɔwɔnbo na, ni waayidam, ni waatiŋ ni aabɔjirb dan nwiin mundaal aa ga siin udaan na. Kina le ga cha Uwumbɔr nyan waaŋuul ti pu, tibɔr tee pu.”

ref: Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were the only ones who objected, except for the two Levites, Meshullam and Shabbethai.
text: Binib bimina baanja le aa nan kii kina: bima le ye Asahel aajapɔɔn Jonatann, ni Tikfa aajapɔɔn Jaseya, le Mesulam, ni Liifai aanii Sabetai mu sil bipuwɔb.

ref: Everyone else who had returned from exile agreed with the plan. So Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of the families, and he listed their names. They started looking into the matter on the first day of the tenth month,
text: Binib bi nan nyan tinaagbiir ni ki gir ni na biken mɔmɔk nan kii utotoor Esra aah ban pu na, le u nan nyan biyidam, itaŋaal ngbaan ni, le ki ŋmee baayimbil ŋa kigbaŋ ni. Ŋmapiik aajan aawiin daal, le bi nan piin baatuln ki bi fiir lik,

ref: and they did not finish until the first day of the first month of the next year. The Men Who Had Foreign Wives

ref: I am Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and in this book I tell what I have done. During the month of Chislev in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes ruled Persia, I was in his fortress city of Susa,
text: Ataksekes aah nan ye Pesia aabɔrkpaan ki ti saa ŋibin moninko pu na aaŋmal u bi yin u ke Kislef na ponn ni, le min, Nehemia, nan bi litiyil Susa ponn ni.

ref: when my brother Hanani came with some men from Judah. So I asked them about the Jews who had escaped from being captives in Babylonia. I also asked them about the city of Jerusalem.
text: Le nna aabo ubaa, bi yin u ke Hanani, nan nyan ni Juda ki fuu ni, ki joo ni bijab bibaa, le m baa bi Jerusalem aatiŋ, ni ndo yaab, Juu yaab bi nyan ni tinaagbiir ni, Babiloŋ ponn ni, ki gir ni na aabɔr.

ref: They told me, “Those captives who have come back are having all kinds of troubles. They are terribly disgraced, Jerusalem's walls are broken down, and its gates have been burned.”
text: Le bi bui mi ke siib bi ŋmar ki bi linampal na bi limukl ni la, le biwɔwɔm bi bi ki duun bi na lik seen bi. Bi ki bui mi ke baah nan gbaa wii Jerusalem aagon ŋi na, baa kee ki maa ŋi, le ibisamɔi aajaaleŋ tiib bi mu bi nan see mmii na mu aa toor.

ref: When I heard this, I sat down on the ground and cried. Then for several days, I mourned; I went without eating to show my sorrow, and I prayed:
text: Maah ŋun tibɔr ngbaan mɔmɔk na le m kal ki wii pam. Iwiin pam nan jer le m bi wii ikpowiil, kaa ji nibaa. M nan mee Uwumbɔr ke,

ref: Lord God of heaven, you are great and fearsome. And you faithfully keep your promises to everyone who loves you and obeys your commands.
text: “Uwumbɔr u ye Paacham Aadindaan na, aa ye unikpaan la, le ti san si ijawaan. Binib bi gee si ki ŋani saakaal aah len pu na, aa joo saah puu tipuur ti tii bi na mbamɔm.

ref: I am your servant, so please have mercy on me and answer the prayer that I make day and night for these people of Israel who serve you. I, my family, and the rest of your people have sinned
text: Uwumbɔr, san mi kinimbaak, ki ŋun maameel, maah mee si pu nwiin pu ni kinyeek ki tii saanaagbiib, Israel yaab aanib, bi tun titunwanbir na pu na. M kii ke m ni n‑yaajatiib mɔmɔk tun titunwanbir la.

ref: by choosing to disobey you and the laws and teachings you gave to your servant Moses.
text: Ti ŋa si mbiin sakpen ki yii kaa ŋa saah bui timi pu na. Taa joo ikaal i aa nan di tii saatutunn Moses ke u di nabr tii timi na.

ref: Please remember the promise you made to Moses. You told him that if we were unfaithful, you would scatter us among foreign nations.
text: Teer saah nan bui Moses pu na ke: ‘Nimi Israel yaab yaa kaa kii tii mi kan, m ga cha ni yaa ki koo ŋinibol yayan ponn ni.

ref: But you also said that no matter how far away we were, we could turn to you and start obeying your laws. Then you would bring us back to the place where you have chosen to be worshiped.
text: Le ni yaa fenn ki gir ni m chee ki ŋa maah bui nimi pu na kan, m ga giin ni nimi nin chee m lee ke ni li dooni mi na; le ni yaa po yaa yaa ki koo kitiŋ kee aadoon mɔk nin chee na kan, m ga giin ni nimi.’

ref: Our Lord, I am praying for your servants—those you rescued by your great strength and mighty power.
text: “Uwumbɔr, binib bee ye saanaagbiib la, le ki ye sin aabaa aanib. Aa di saapɔɔn sakpiin gaa bi lii.

ref: Please answer my prayer and the prayer of your other servants who gladly honor your name. When I serve the king his wine today, make him pleased with me and let him do what I ask.
text: Li pel maameel, ni saanaagbiib bimɔk ban ke bi nyuŋ si na mu aameen. Tii mi maah ban pu na din wee ki cha ubɔrkpaan ngbaan san mi kinimbaak.” N‑yoonn ngbaan, min le nan ye ubɔrkpaan ngbaan aadaan aaninkpel.

ref: During the month of Nisan in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king, I served him his wine, as I had done before. But this was the first time I had ever looked depressed.
text: Iŋmal inaa aah jer na aawiin mubaa daal, le Ubɔrkpaan Ataksekes nan bi ji tijikaar, le m di ndaan buen ti tii u. Waa nan kee kan nsui aah bii pu aan nnimbil wɔb ŋa gbilngbiln pu na,

ref: So the king said, “Why do you look so sad? You're not sick. Something must be bothering you.” Even though I was frightened,
text: le u baa mi ke, “Ba ŋa aa lik gbilngbiln din kina? Saa bun, kina pu na, aasui le ga li bii.” Ijawaan nan chuu mi,

ref: I answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! I feel sad because the city where my ancestors are buried is in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”
text: le m bui ke, “Uwumbɔr tii sin mpɔɔndaan limɔfal li fɔk na. M ga ŋa kinye ki taa li lik gbilngbiln buyoonn n‑yaajatiib aakpab aah dɔ nin chee na ber doo aan kitiŋ ngbaan aabisamɔi aajaaleŋ tiib wun mmii doo na?”

ref: The king asked, “What do you want me to do?” I prayed to the God who rules from heaven.
text: Le ubɔrkpaan ngbaan ki baa mi ke, “Ni ye ba le aa ban?” Le m mee Uwumbɔr u bi Paacham na,

ref: Then I told the king, “Sir, if it's all right with you, please send me back to Judah, so that I can rebuild the city where my ancestors are buried.”
text: le ki bui ubɔrkpaan ngbaan ke, “Ni yaa mɔ sin mpɔɔndaan aan aa ga tii mi maah ban pu na kan, aa cha m buen Juda aatiŋ pu, kitiŋ ki ponn ni n‑yaajatiib aakpab dɔ na, aan m ti ki gir maa kitiŋ ngbaan.”

ref: The queen was sitting beside the king when he asked me, “How long will it take, and when will you be back?” The king agreed to let me go, and I told him when I would return.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan na ubɔrpii mu nan ka gbɔk u; le u nan kii tii mi. U nan baa mi maah ga yunn pu na, ni buyoonn mu m ga ki gir ni na; le m bui u.

ref: Then I asked, “Your Majesty, would you be willing to give me letters to the governors of the provinces west of the Euphrates River, so that I can travel safely to Judah?
text: Le m ki gaŋ u ke u tii mi tigbann m ti tii biyidam bi bi Yufrates aamɔɔl aawilir wɔb aapepel na ke bi tii mi nsan m ti fuu Juda aatiŋ pu.

ref: I will need timber to rebuild the gates of the fortress near the temple and more timber to construct the city wall and to build a place for me to live. And so, I would appreciate a letter to Asaph, who is in charge of the royal forest.” God was good to me, and the king did everything I asked.
text: M nan ki bui u ke u tii mi kigbaŋ m ti tii Asaf u kii ubɔr aachook na kigbaŋ ki ga cha u tii mi idɔ m ti toor kidifɔfɔk ki kii Uwumbɔr Aadichal na aajaaleŋ tiib, ni ligoln li mann goln kitiŋ ngbaan na aabisamɔi, ni mbaa aadichal li ponn ni m ga li koo na. Uwumbɔr aaŋaal aah nan paa m pu na, ubɔrkpaan ngbaan nan tii mi maah ban pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: The king sent some army officers and cavalry troops along with me, and as I traveled through the Western Provinces, I gave the letters to the governors.
text: Ubɔrkpaan ngbaan nan cha waajab aaninkpiib ni bitandam bibaa cheen mi, le m buen Yufrates aamɔɔl aawilir wɔb Juda aatiŋ pu. Nima chee le m ti di ubɔrkpaan aagbann ngbaan tii biyidam ngbaan.

ref: But when Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about what had happened, they became very angry, because they didn't want anyone to help the people of Israel. Nehemiah Inspects the Wall of Jerusalem
text: Le Sanbalat, u nyan ni Bef Horonn na, ni Tobia, u ye uninkpel ubaa ki bi Amonn aapepel na, ŋun ke unii ubaa dan u nan ter Israel aanib, le baaŋuul fii sakpen.

ref: I got up during the night and left my house. I took some men with me, without telling anyone what I thought God wanted me to do for the city. The only animal I took was the donkey I rode on.
text: kaa bui unii ubaa Uwumbɔr aah bui mi ke m nan tun pu ki tii Jerusalem aatiŋ na. Le m nan fii kinyeek kibaa kitaasiik, ki ban njɔtiib siib kpee mbaa pu. Maah nan dik ubon u pu na baanja le nan ye kiwakork ki dii timi na.

ref: I went through Valley Gate on the west, then south past Dragon Spring, before coming to Garbage Gate. As I rode along, I took a good look at the crumbled walls of the city and the gates that had been torn down and burned.
text: Ni nan beenin ye kinyeek le m dii mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Kifataŋ Aabisamɔb na, ki nyan kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni, ki di toŋ liwilir wɔb, ki fenn toŋ ŋŋangii wɔb ki ti nyan nnyunbun mu bi yin mu ke Kipeewanbiik aanyunbun na chee, ki ti saa mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Litapuln Aabisamɔb na chee. Maah cha na, le m moo lik ŋigon ngbaan nin chee wii wii na, ni ibisamɔi aajaaleŋ tiib bi mmii wun bi na.

ref: So I went down to Kidron Valley and looked at the wall from there. Then before daylight I returned to the city through Valley Gate.
text: kina pu le m sunn koo Kidronn aafataŋ ni ki cha, ki lik ligoln ngbaan, le ki ki gir dii maah ba nyan niwɔb na, ki dii Kifataŋ Aabisamɔb na ki koo kitiŋ ponn ni.

ref: None of the city officials knew what I had in mind. And I had not even told any of the Jews—not the priests, the leaders, the officials, or any other Jews who would be helping in the work.
text: Lituln aaninkpiib bi bi Jerusalem ni na aa nan nyi ke m buen nibaa chee, kaa ki nyi maah bi tun pu na mu. Ki ti saa liyaadaal ngbaan maa bui Juu yaab biken tibaa, bitotoorb, ni kitiŋ ni aaninkpiib, ni ŋitun aaninkpiib, ni unii umɔk nan bi tun lituln ngbaan na, maa nan bui ubaa tibaa.

ref: But when I got back, I said to them, “Jerusalem is truly in a mess! The gates have been torn down and burned, and everything is in ruins. We must rebuild the city wall so that we can again take pride in our city.”
text: Le m nin bui bi ke, “Jerusalem aah bii doo pu na, ni mɔmɔk kan taah bi tibɔr ti ponn ni na. Cha man ti ki gir maa kitiŋ ngbaan aagon man, aan timi aanimɔɔn yee doo.”

ref: Then I told them how kind God had been and what the king had said. Immediately, they replied, “Let's start building now!” So they got everything ready.
text: Le m bui bi Uwumbɔr aah bi m chee ki ter mi pu na, ni ubɔrkpaan na mu aah bui mi pu na. Le bi kii ke, “Cha ti piin ki li maa man.” Le bi gor bibaa ke bi piin lituln ngbaan.

ref: When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab heard about our plans, they started insulting us and saying, “Just look at you! Do you plan to rebuild the walls of the city and rebel against the king?”
text: Le Sanbalat, ni Tobia, ni Arab aanii u bi yin u ke Gesem na aah ŋun taah bi kpokl ke ti ŋa pu na, bi nan laa timi, le ki bui ke, “Ni dak ke ni bi ŋani ba na? Ni ban ni fii sil ubɔrkpaan pu la aa?”

ref: I answered, “We are servants of the God who rules from heaven, and he will make our work succeed. So we will start rebuilding Jerusalem, but you have no right to any of its property, because you have had no part in its history.”
text: Le m gar bi ke, “Uwumbɔr u bi paacham na ga tii timi taah ban pu na. Timi le ye waanaagbiib, le ki ga piin ki maa. Le nimi aa kpa nsan ni ji Jerusalem aafaal libaa, kaa bi kaakaal mu ni.”

ref: These are the people who helped rebuild the wall and gates of Jerusalem: The high priest Eliashib and the other priests rebuilt Sheep Gate and hung its doors. Then they dedicated Sheep Gate and the section of the wall as far as Hundred Tower and Hananel Tower.
text: Kina le bi nan ki gir maa Jerusalem aagoln: Eliasib u ye utotoorninkpel na, ni bitotoorb biken le nan maa mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Ipiih Aabisamɔb na, ki di mu tii Uwumbɔr, ki di mu aajaaleŋ laŋ. Bi nan di ligoln ngbaan mu ki nyan mbisamɔb ngbaan chee ki ti saa bikikiib aadifɔfɔk ki bi yin ki ke Nkub Aadifɔfɔk na, ni ki mu bi yin ki ke Hananel Aadifɔfɔk na mu tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: The people of Jericho rebuilt the next section of the wall, and Zaccur son of Imri rebuilt the section after that.
text: Jeriko aajab mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na. Imri aajapɔɔn Sakur mu le nan maa ligeln li paa Jeriko aajab pu na.

ref: The family of Hassenaah built Fish Gate. They put the beams in place and hung the doors, then they added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
text: Hasenaa aamaal mu le nan maa mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Ijan Aabisamɔb na. Bi nan ŋa jaaleŋ tiib aadɔ ki di jaaleŋ ŋa, le ki ŋa tikur ti mu bi ga li joo laŋni na.

ref: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, completed the next section of the wall. Meshullam, son of Berechiah and grandson of Meshezabel, rebuilt the next section, and Zadok son of Baana rebuilt the section beside that.
text: Hakos aayaabil, Uria aajapɔɔn Meremof mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na. Mesesabel aayaabil, Berekia aajapɔɔn Mesulam mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na. Baana aajapɔɔn Sadok mu le nan paan ki maa ligeln li paa na.

ref: The next section was to be repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their town leaders refused to do the hard work they were assigned.
text: Tekoa yaab le nan paan ki maa ligeln li paa na, le baatiŋ ni aaninkpiib ma nan yii, kaa tun lituln li bininkpiib bi chuun lik lituln ngbaan na nan di tii bi ke bi tun na.

ref: Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah restored Ancient Gate. They put the beams in place, hung the doors, and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
text: Pasea aajapɔɔn Joyada, ni Besodeya aajapɔɔn Mesulam mu le nan maa Jesana Aabisamɔb. Bi nan di jaaleŋ aadɔ ŋum ki di jaaleŋ ŋa, le ki ŋa tikur ti bi ga li joo laŋni na.

ref: Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and the men from Gibeon and Mizpah rebuilt the next section of the wall. This section reached as far as the house of the governor of West Euphrates Province.
text: Melatia u ye Gibeonn aatiŋ aanii na, ni Jadonn u mu ye Meronof aatiŋ aanii na, ni Gibeonn ni Mispa aajab mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na, ki ti saa Yufrates aamɔɔl aawilir wɔb aapepel aayidaan aadichal chee.

ref: Uzziel son of Harhaiah the goldsmith rebuilt the next section. Hananiah the perfume maker rebuilt the section next after that, and it went as far as Broad Wall.
text: Hahaya aajapɔɔn Usiel, u ye salmaa aachaa na, mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na. Hanania, u ŋani tulalee tiib na mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na, ki ti saa ligoln li bi yin li ke Ligoln li Waa na chee.

ref: Rephaiah son of Hur ruled half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall.
text: Hur aajapɔɔn Refaya, u nan ye Jerusalem aageln libaa aaninkpel na, mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na.

ref: The section after that was close to the home of Jedaiah son of Harumaph, and he rebuilt it. Hattush son of Hashabneiah constructed the next section of the wall.
text: Harumaf aajapɔɔn Jedaya mu le nan maa ligeln li bi duun udo na. Le Hasabneya aajapɔɔn Hatus mu maa ligeln li paa na.

ref: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath Moab rebuilt the section after that, and they also built Oven Tower.
text: Harim aajapɔɔn Malkija ni Pahaf Moab aajapɔɔn Hasub mu nan maa ligeln li paa na, ni kidifɔfɔk ki chee bi ŋani boroboro na.

ref: Shallum son of Hallohesh ruled the other half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. Shallum's daughters also worked with him.
text: Halohes aajapɔɔn Salum, u ye Jerusalem aageln li gur na aaninkpel na, mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na. Ubisatiib le nan ter u lituln ngbaan ni.

ref: Hanun and the people who lived in the town of Zanoah rebuilt Valley Gate. They hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. They also rebuilt the wall for
text: Le Sanoa aatiŋ yaab ni Hanunn mu ki gir toor mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Kifataŋ Aabisamɔb na. Bi nan toor mbisamɔb ngbaan doo ki ŋa tikur ti bi ga li joo laŋni mu na ŋa, le ki gir maa ligoln ngbaan ki ti saa mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Litapuln Aabisamɔb na.

ref: Malchijah son of Rechab ruled the district of Beth-Haccherem, and he rebuilt Garbage Gate. He hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
text: Rekab aajapɔɔn Malkija, u ye Bef Hakerem aapepel aaninkpel na mu le nan toor Litapuln Aabisamɔb. U nan ŋa mu, le ki ŋa tikur ti bi ga li joo laŋni na mu.

ref: Shallum son of Colhozeh ruled the district of Mizpah, and he rebuilt Fountain Gate. He put a cover over the gateway, then hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. He also rebuilt the wall at Shelah Pool. This section was next to the king's garden and went as far as the stairs leading down from David's City.
text: Kolhose aajapɔɔn Salum, u ye Mispa Aapepel aaninkpel na, mu le nan ki gir maa mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Nnyunbun Aabisamɔb na. U nan toor mbisamɔb ngbaan ki ŋa jaaleŋ, ni tikur ti bi ga li joo laŋni na. Waah ti fuu Sela Aabukpiik chee na, u nan maa ligoln li paa libɔrchiln aakpifar aasaak pu na, ki ti saa ŋibimbin ŋi sunn nyan ni David Aatiŋ ni na.

ref: Nehemiah son of Azbuk ruled half of the district of Beth-Zur, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. It went as far as the royal cemetery, the artificial pool, and the army barracks. Levites Who Worked on the Wall
text: Asbuk aajapɔɔn Nehemia u ye Bef Sur Aapepel libaa aaninkpel na, le nan maa ligeln li paa na, ki ti saa David aakaakul chee, ni kibukpiik, ni butɔb aajab do chee. Liifai yaab bi nan maa ligoln ngbaan na sɔ

ref: The Levites who worked on the next sections of the wall were Rehum son of Bani; Hashabiah, who ruled half of the district of Keilah and did this work for his district;
text: Binib bimina le nan ye Liifai yaab bi nan maa ligoln ngbaan aagen ŋibaa ŋi gur ki paa na: Bani aajapɔɔn Rehum le nan puen maa ligeln li paa na. Le Hasabia, u ye Keila Aapepel libaa aaninkpel na, mu nan maa ligeln li paa na tii waapepel aanib:

ref: Binnui son of Henadad, who ruled the other half of the district of Keilah;
text: Henadad aajapɔɔn Bafai, u mu nan ye Keila Aapepel li gur na aaninkpel na mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na:

ref: Ezer son of Jeshua, who ruled Mizpah, rebuilt the section of the wall that was in front of the armory and reached to the corner of the wall;
text: Jesua aajapɔɔn Eser, u ye Mispa aaninkpel na mu le nan maa ligeln li bi tijawan aadiik chee na, ki ti saa ligoln ngbaan aah fenn nin chee na:

ref: Baruch son of Zabbai eagerly rebuilt the section of the wall that went all the way to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest;
text: Sabai aajapɔɔn Baruk mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na, ki yoor ti saa Utotoorninkpel Eliasib aadichal aabisamɔb chee:

ref: Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, built up to the far end of Eliashib's house. Priests Who Worked on the Wall
text: Hakos aayaabil Uria aajapɔɔn Meremof mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na, ki nyan nima ki ti saa Eliasib aadichal aah ti doo nin chee na. Bitotoorb bi mu nan maa ligoln ngbaan na sɔ

ref: Here is a list of the priests who worked on the wall: Priests from the region around Jerusalem rebuilt the next section of the wall.
text: Bitotoorb bi mu nan ki maa ligoln ngbaan aagen ŋi gur na sɔ: Bitotoorb bi bi ki maa goln Jerusalem aapepel na le nan maa ligeln li paa Liifai yaab pu na:

ref: Benjamin and Hasshub rebuilt the wall in front of their own houses. Azariah, who was the son of Maaseiah and the grandson of Ananiah, rebuilt the section in front of his house.
text: Benjaminn ni Hasub mu le nan paan ki maa ligeln li bi baadichal chee na: Anania aayaabil, Maaseya aajapɔɔn Asaria mu le nan paan ki maa ligeln li bi udo chee na:

ref: Binnui son of Henadad rebuilt the section of the wall from Azariah's house to the corner of the wall.
text: Henadad aajapɔɔn Binui mu le nan piin Asaria do chee ki ti saa ligoln ngbaan aalɔlɔŋ ni:
