ref: The men from Tekoa rebuilt the next section of the wall, and it was their second section. It started at a place across from the large tower that guarded the Temple, and it went all the way to the wall near Ophel.
text: Tekoa aajab le nan ki maa ligeln li paa na, lima le nan kpee baah maa pu na nlee, ki nyan bikikiib bi kii Uwumbɔr Aadichal na aadifɔfɔk chee ki ti saa ligoln ngbaan nin chee bi gbɔk Ofel na.

ref: Some priests rebuilt the next section of the wall. They began working north of Horse Gate, and each one worked on a section in front of his own house.
text: Bitotoorb bibaa mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na, ki di toŋ ŋŋangan aasikakl wɔb, mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Utaan Aabisamɔb na chee, bi mɔmɔk nan maa nin chee duun baadichal na la.

ref: Zadok son of Immer rebuilt the wall in front of his house. Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, who looked after the East Gate, rebuilt the section after that.
text: Imer aajapɔɔn Sadok mu le nan maa ligeln li paa ki duun udo na. Sekania aajapɔɔn Semaya, u nan ye mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Liwipuul Aabisamɔb aakikiir na, mu le nan maa li paa na.

ref: Hananiah and Hanun rebuilt the next section, which was the second section for them. Meshullam son of Berechiah rebuilt the next section, which happened to be in front of his house.
text: Selemia aajapɔɔn Hanania, ni Salaf aajapɔɔn uloloob Hanunn na, mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na, lima le nan ye lelee aageln li bi maa na. Berekia aajapɔɔn Mesulam mu le nan paan ki maa ligeln li paa na, li nan bi gbɔk udo la.

ref: Malchijah, a goldsmith, rebuilt the next section, as far as the house used by the temple workers and merchants. This area was across from Gathering Gate, near the room on top of the wall at the northeast corner.
text: Malkija, u nan ye salmaa aachaa na, mu le nan maa ligeln li paa na, ki yoor ki ti saa lidichal li ponn ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal aatutum, ni binib bi tiir kitiirk na koo, aan li bi mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Mifkad Aabisamɔb na chee, ki bi kidiik ki tɔk ligoln ngbaan aapaacham liwipuul ni ŋŋangan aalɔlɔŋ ni na chee.

ref: The goldsmiths and merchants rebuilt the last section of the wall, which went from the corner room all the way to Sheep Gate.
text: Salmaa aachaab, ni binib bi tiir kitiirk na mu le nan maa ligeln li gur na, ki nyan kidiik ki bi kilɔlɔŋ ni na chee na ki di ti saa mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Ipiih Aabisamɔb na.

ref: When Sanballat, the governor of Samaria, heard that we were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, he became angry and started insulting our people.
text: Sanbalat aah ŋun ke timi Juu yaab ki bi maa ligoln ngbaan na, le liŋuul chuu u pam, le u piin ki bi ŋani timi mbɔnyun.

ref: In front of his friends and the Samaritan army he said, “What is this feeble bunch of Jews trying to do? Are they going to rebuild the wall and offer sacrifices all in one day? Do they think they can make something out of this pile of scorched stones?”
text: U nan sil uŋeen aatɔtiib ni Samaria aajab aanimbiin ni ki len ke, “Juu yaab, bifalaadam bee, dak ke bi bi ŋani ba na? Bi ŋa nlandak ke bi ki gir maa kitiŋ ngbaan aa? Bi dak ke baah toor kitork ki na ga ŋmaa cha bi doo lituln ngbaan liwinbaal la aa? Bi ga ŋmaa di ŋilangbentanjal ŋi ber ki dɔ ki wun mmii na maa aa?”

ref: Tobiah from Ammon was standing beside Sanballat and said, “Look at the wall they are building! Why, even a fox could knock over this pile of stones.”
text: Tobia nan si gbɔk u, le ki mu len ke, “Ba aagoln aan bi ga ŋmaa maa? Hali uŋɔk ga ŋmaa tur li lii kitiŋ.”

ref: But I prayed, “Our God, these people hate us and have wished horrible things for us. Please answer our prayers and make their insults fall on them! Let them be the ones to be dragged away as prisoners of war.
text: Le m mee Uwumbɔr ke, “Uwumbɔr, li pel baah ŋani timi mbɔnyun pu na. Cha baabɔnyun ngbaan gir kan bi. Cha bi lann baah kpa tiwan ni mɔmɔk na, ki cha bi kpaln biyom kitiyayaŋ ponn ni.

ref: Don't forgive the mean and evil way they have insulted the builders.”
text: Taa suln baatunwanbir pu ki di cha pinn bi baataani; ba pu? bi sii timi bi bi maa na la.”

ref: The people worked hard, and we built the walls of Jerusalem halfway up again.
text: Le ti bi maa ligoln ngbaan. Binib ngbaan aah nan gee lituln ngbaan sakpen pu na, naa nan yunn le ti maa fuu sisik ni.

ref: But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people from the city of Ashdod saw the walls going up and the holes being repaired. So they became angry
text: Sanbalat, ni Tobia, ni binib bi nyan ni Arabia, ni Amonn, ni Asdod aatim ni na aah ŋun ke ligoln ngbaan aamaam moo cha mɔb aan nimɔk nan war lir na bi ŋeeb na, le baaŋuul fii sakpen.

ref: and decided to stir up trouble, and to fight against the people of Jerusalem.
text: Kina pu le bi kpokl ke bi mɔmɔk kpaan ki nan tak Jerusalem aan ki cha timi aalan ŋmal.

ref: But we kept on praying to our God, and we also stationed guards day and night.
text: Le ti mee timi Aawumbɔr, ki ban bijab kaan kiir kinyeek ni nwiin pu.

ref: Meanwhile, the people of Judah were singing a sorrowful song: “So much rubble for us to haul! Worn out and weary, will we ever finish this wall?”
text: Juda aanib nan gaa nlahn ke: “Ti tun ŋitun ki ti bak. Tibir pam le dɔ ke ti yoor ti mee. Ti ga ŋa kinye aan ki maa ligoln ngbaan din wee?”

ref: Our enemies were saying, “Before those Jews know what has happened, we will sneak up and kill them and put an end to their work.”
text: Timi aadim nan dak ke bi yaa choo bi nan ku timi aan ki cha timi aatuln ngbaan sil kan, taan kan bi, kaan li nyi mu, aan bi nan kpaan gob timi.

ref: On at least ten different occasions, the Jews living near our enemies warned us against attacks from every side,
text: Le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk mu Juu yaab bi koo timi aadim ngbaan chee na choo ki nan tuk timi baah bi kpokl ti pu pu na.

ref: and so I sent people to guard the wall at its lowest places and where there were still holes in it. I placed them according to families, and they stood guard with swords and spears and with bows and arrows.
text: Kina pu le m nan tii maanib kijaak aajum, ni tikpaatunn, ni itɔi ki yakr bi siin siin mmaal mmaal nin chee mɔk aa nan kee maa doo na.

ref: Then I looked things over and told the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don't be afraid of your enemies! The Lord is great and fearsome. So think of him and fight for your relatives and children, your wives and homes!”
text: M nan kan ke ilandak le joo maanib; le m bui bi ni baayidam, ni baaninkpiib ke, “Taa san man timi aadim ijawaan. Teer Uwumbɔr aah pɔɔ ki kpa ijawaan pu na, ki jan man nimi aanib ni nimi aabim, ni nipuutiib, ni nimi aadichal pu.”

ref: Our enemies found out that we knew about their plot against us, but God kept them from doing what they had planned. So we went back to work on the wall.
text: Timi aadim nan ŋun ke ti ŋun baah bi kpokl ti pu pu na, le bi bee ke Uwumbɔr nyaŋ baalandak. Le ti mɔmɔk gir ti bi maa ligoln ngbaan.

ref: From then on, I let half of the young men work while the other half stood guard. They wore armor and had spears and shields, as well as bows and arrows. The leaders helped the workers
text: Ki nyan n‑yoonn ngbaan ki joo cha m nan yakr maanib ngbaan nfum mulee pu la, bibaa bi tun, le bima na mu si kii, ki pee kijaak aabɔkul, ki joo tikpaatunn, ni kijaak aapen, ni itɔi. Le timi aayidam fii sil binib bi bi maa ligoln ngbaan na aachaŋ ni.

ref: who were rebuilding the wall. Everyone who hauled building materials kept one hand free to carry a weapon.
text: Hali binib bi nan tui titan ni tidimaawan na nan joo ŋŋaal mubaa le tun, le muken mu joo tijawan,

ref: Even the workers who were rebuilding the wall strapped on a sword. The worker who was to blow the signal trumpet stayed with me.
text: le bimɔk mu nan maa na nan maa le njum tab bichakpok. Uja u nan ga pii ukpiin na nan si gbɔk mi la.

ref: I told the people and their officials and leaders, “Our work is so spread out, that we are a long way from one another.
text: Le m bui binib ngbaan ni baaninkpiib, ni baayidam ke, “Lituln ngbaan yaa, ki daa tɔb, kina le ti mu daa tɔb chee.

ref: If you hear the sound of the trumpet, come quickly and gather around me. Our God will help us fight.”
text: Kina pu na, ni yaa ŋun ukpiin wii kan, ni mɔmɔk kuun dan m chee. Timi Aawumbɔr le ga jan tii timi.”

ref: Every day from dawn to dark, half of the workers rebuilt the walls, while the rest stood guard with their spears.
text: Kina pu na, iwiin mɔmɔk ki nya kichakpinaanyeek ni ki ti saa buyoonn iŋmabi ga nyan ni kinyeek na, timi bibaa bi maa la, le bima na mu si kii ki joo tikpaatunn.

ref: I asked the men in charge and their workers to stay inside Jerusalem and stand guard at night. So they guarded the city at night and worked during the day.
text: N‑yoonn mumina le m nan bui bijab bi ye biyidam na, ni binib bi ter bi na, ke bi mɔmɔk gaar Jerusalem ponn ni kinyeek, aan ti ŋmaa kiir kitiŋ ngbaan kinyeek, ki tun lituln mu nwiin pu.

ref: I even slept in my work clothes at night; my relatives, the workers, and the guards slept in theirs as well. And we always kept our weapons close by.
text: Hali kinyeek kan, m ni ŋŋeen aatɔtiib, ni maatutum, ni uja u si kii mi na aa nan peer timi aawanpeenkaan bilni. Le ti mɔmɔk aajawan ŋub tiŋaal ni.

ref: Some of the men and their wives complained about the Jews in power
text: Naah ŋa iwiin ilee na le binib pam, bijab ni bipiib mɔmɔk, piin ki ŋulni Juu yaab biken aah ŋani bi pu na.

ref: and said, “We have large families, and it takes a lot of grain merely to keep us alive.”
text: Bibaa nan len ke, “Ti kpa ŋidichal ŋi wiir na la, le ki ban tijikaar ti kpiin tibaa.”

ref: Others said, “During the famine we even had to mortgage our fields, vineyards, and homes to them in order to buy grain.”
text: Le biken mu len ke, “Ti gur joo timi aakpaakon, ni ŋisubil aasar, ni timi aadichal le siini lipɔln pu ki kani tijikaar ti ga nyan timi likpasiil ponn ni na.”

ref: Then others said, “We had to borrow money from those in power to pay the government tax on our fields and vineyards.
text: Le biken mu ki len ke, “Ti pinni ŋimombil le ki pa timi aakpaakon, ni ŋisubil aasar aalampoo pu.

ref: We are Jews just as they are, and our children are as good as theirs. But we still have to sell our children as slaves, and some of our daughters have already been raped. We are completely helpless; our fields and vineyards have even been taken from us.”
text: Ti mu ye Juu yaab ke tiŋeen aatɔtiib na la. Tijapɔtiib mu bi ke bi yaab na la. Le tima joo timi aabim kooh ŋani tinaagbiir ni. Ti puun di tibisatiib bibaa kooh ŋa tinaagbiir ni a. Baah chuu gaa timi aakpaakon ni ŋisubil aasar pu na, ti bee fam a.”

ref: When I heard their complaints and their charges, I became very angry.
text: Maah ŋun tibɔr ngbaan kina na, le maaŋuul fii,

ref: So I thought it over and said to the leaders and officials, “How can you charge your own people interest?” Then I called a public meeting and accused the leaders
text: le m fii ki sil ti pu. M nan len binib ngbaan aaninkpiib ni baayidam chee kaa di bɔr, le ki bui bi ke, “Nimi le bi muk nibaa aana aabim.” M nan kuun binib mɔmɔk ke m lik tibɔr ngbaan,

ref: by saying, “We have tried to buy back all of our people who were sold into exile. But here you are, selling more of them for us to buy back!” The officials and leaders did not say a word, because they knew this was true.
text: le ki len ke, “Ti pɔɔk tibaa le ki ki bi daa tinaabitiib Juu yaab bi nan di bibaa kooh tii biwɔwɔm na la. Le nimi le ki muk nimi nibaa aanaabitiib Juu yaab, ke bi di bibaa kooh tii nimi.” Biyidam ngbaan nan ka ŋmin chii, kaa ŋmaa gar tibaa.

ref: I continued, “What you have done is wrong! We must honor our God by the way we live, so the Gentiles can't find fault with us.
text: Le m ki bui bi ke, “Naah ŋani pu na aa ŋan. Ni ba ga li san Uwumbɔr ki ŋa ni ŋan na. Nima kan, timi aadim bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aan ŋmaa kan nsan ki ŋa timi mbɔnyun.

ref: My relatives, my friends, and I are also lending money and grain, but we must no longer demand payment in return.
text: M cha binib pinn m chee ŋimombil ni tijikaar, le ŋŋeen aatɔtiib ni bijab bi tun m chee lituln na mu ŋa kina. Kina pu na, ti taa ki gaa taah pinn bi tiwan ni na man.

ref: Now give back the fields, vineyards, olive orchards, and houses you have taken and also the interest you have been paid.”
text: Bi yaa pinn nimi ŋimombil, bee tijikaar, bee olif aakpan kan, ni di ni mɔmɔk tii bi; ki giin baakpaakon, ni ŋisubil aasar, ni nkpan aasui aasar, ni baadichal dandana wee tii bi.”

ref: The leaders answered, “We will do whatever you say and return their property, without asking to be repaid.” So I made the leaders promise in front of the priests to give back the property.
text: Le biyidam ngbaan gar ke, “Ti ga ŋa saah len pu na. Ti ga giin baawangol tii bi, kaan ki cha bi teen timi baah pinn nimɔk na.” Le m yin ni bitotoorb le ki cha biyidam ngbaan puu binimbil ni, ke bi ga sil ŋa baah len ke bi ga ŋa pu na.

ref: Then I emptied my pockets and said, “If you don't keep your promise, that's what God will do to you. He will empty out everything you own, even taking away your houses.” The people answered, “We will keep our promise.” Then they praised the Lord and did as they had promised. Nehemiah Is Generous
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le m chuu gbabr maawundo u m nan gbab nchaŋ ni na ki yɔk yɔk u, ki bui ke, “Kina le Uwumbɔr ga yɔk yɔk unii umɔk kaa joo waah puu pu na. Uwumbɔr ga gaa nimi aadichal, ni naah kpa tiwan nimɔk na, ki cha nimi niŋmeen.” Le binib bimɔk nan bi nima na kii ke, “Amii,” ki nyuŋ Uwumbɔr. Le biyidam ngbaan nan joo baah puu tipuur ti na. Nehemia aah nan ye ubulchinn pu na

ref: I was governor of Judah from the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king until the thirty-second year. And during these entire twelve years, my relatives and I refused to accept the food that I was allowed.
text: Ŋibin kipiik ni ŋilee ŋi ponn ni m nan ye Juda aatiŋ aayidaan, ki nyan Ataksekes aanaan aabiln moninko ki ti saa waabin piitaa ni ŋilee ponn ni na, m ni maadichal aa nan ji tijikaar ti bi nan siin ke ti li ye uyidaan aajikaar na.

ref: Each governor before me had been a burden to the people by making them pay for his food and wine and by demanding forty silver coins a day. Even their officials had been a burden to the people. But I respected God, and I didn't think it was right to be so hard on them.
text: Biyidam bi mɔmɔk nan kal aan m nan paan bi pu na, nan ye limukl le ki tii binib ngbaan, ki nan gaal tikur aamombil imonko ilee le nwiin mubaa, ke baajikaar ni ndaan le na. Hali baatutum mu nan muk binib ngbaan la. Le mma aa nan ŋani kina; ba pu? m san Uwumbɔr la.

ref: I spent all my time getting the wall rebuilt and did not buy any property. Everyone working for me did the same thing.
text: M nan di maapɔɔn mɔmɔk di ŋa ligoln ngbaan aamaam ponn ni la, kaa ban liwangol libaa. Maatutum mu mɔmɔk nan kpee m pu ligoln ngbaan aamaam ni.

ref: Each day one ox, six of the best sheep, and lots of chickens were prepared. Then every ten days, a large supply of wine was brought in. I knew what a heavy burden this would have been for the people, and so I did not ask for my food allowance as governor.
text: Iwiin mɔmɔk m nan kɔr unaaja ubaa, ni ipiih i ye ipiih na iloob, ni ikɔla i wiir na la, le iwiin kipiik mɔk kan see m tii bi ndapɔm. Maah nan nyi binib ngbaan aafalaa aah wiir pu na, maa nan gaal lipal li biyidam gaal na.

ref: I pray that God will bless me for everything I have done for my people.
text: Le m mee Uwumbɔr ke, “Uwumbɔr, teer mbɔr, ki ŋa tinyoor ŋa m pu, maah tun nimɔk tii binib bee na.”

ref: Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and our other enemies learned that I had completely rebuilt the wall. All I lacked was hanging the doors in the gates.
text: Sanbalat, ni Tobia, ni Gesem, ni timi aadim bi gur na ŋun ke ti ki gir maa ligoln ngbaan doo, le nibaa chee aa gur, ki mu aa nan kee di ibisamɔi aajaaleŋ tiib piin.

ref: Then Sanballat and Geshem sent a message, asking me to meet with them in one of the villages in Ono Valley. I knew they were planning to harm me in some way.
text: Kina pu le Sanbalat ni Gesem tun ni ntuun m chee, ke m keln bi kitiwaatiir kibaa ni, Ono aateer pu. Bi nan ban bi ŋmann mi ki ti ku mi la.

ref: So I sent messengers to tell them, “My work is too important to stop now and go there. I can't afford to slow down the work just to visit with you.”
text: Le m mu tun ti bui bi ke, “M bi tun lituln li ye litukpaan na la, kina pu na, maan ŋmaa buen nima. Maan ŋmaa di cha lituln ngbaan ke m dan nan kan nimi.”

ref: They invited me four times, but each time I refused to go.
text: Bi nan tun ni m chee tibɔr tichachaan ngbaan pu ŋitaa ŋinaa la, le m mu giin bi ngarm chachaan ngbaan.

ref: which said: A rumor is going around among the nations that you and the other Jews are rebuilding the wall and planning to rebel, because you want to be their king. And Geshem says it's true!
text: Ki ponn ni nan len ke: “Gesem bui mi ke u ŋun binib len ke sin ni Juu yaab bi kpokl ke ni ban kijaak la. Kina pu le ni ki gir bi maa ligoln ngbaan. U ki len ke aa ban ke aa di aabaa di ŋa ubɔrkpaan,

ref: You even have prophets in Jerusalem, claiming you are now the king of Judah. You know the Persian king will hear about this, so let's get together and talk it over.
text: le ki ban bibɔnabr ke bi moon kina Jerusalem ponn ni ke sin le ye Juda aabɔrkpaan. Tibɔr ngbaan mu ga fuu mpɔɔndaan ubɔrkpaan chee, kina pu le m ban m kan si aan ti kpokl ti.”

ref: I sent a message back to Sanballat, saying, “None of this is true! You are making it all up.”
text: Le m tun ti bui u ke: “Saah len tibɔr timɔk na tibaa aa gbii. Sin le naan kina aabɔr aabaa.”

ref: Our enemies were trying to frighten us and to keep us from our work. But I asked God to give me strength.
text: Bi nan bi pɔɔni bibaa ke bi faan timi le ti di cha lituln ngbaan. Le m mee Uwumbɔr ke, “Tɔ, dandana wee, Uwumbɔr, moo tii mi mpɔɔn.”

ref: One day I went to visit Shemaiah. He wasn't supposed to leave his house, but he said, “Let's hurry to the holy place of the temple and hide there. We will lock the temple doors, because your enemies are planning to kill you tonight.”
text: N‑yoonn mue le m nan buen m ti mann Mehetabel aayaabil Semaya u aate ye Delaya na, aan ki bɔr waadichal ni na. Le u nan bui mi ke, “Ni ŋan ke m ni sin buen ti bɔr lipepel li bi chain na ni, Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni, ki laŋ jaaleŋ tiib; ba pu? bi choo bi nan ku si la. Kinyeek kee ki joo cha bi ga dan nan ku si.”

ref: I answered, “Why should someone like me have to run and hide in the temple to save my life? I won't go!”
text: Le m gar u ke, “Maa ye uja u aaboln san ki ti bɔrni na. Aa dak ke m ga san ti bɔr Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni ke m ŋmar aa? Maan ŋa kina kpala.”

ref: Suddenly I realized that God had not given Shemaiah this message. But Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him to trick me
text: Maah kal ki dakl lik ti ponn ni na, m nan kan ke naa nan ye Uwumbɔr le bui Semaya ke u len kina. Ni nan ye le ke Tobia ni Sanbalat le tii u igaŋgaŋlik ke u bui mi kina.

ref: and to frighten me into doing something wrong, because they wanted to ruin my good name.
text: Bi nan daa u le ke u nan faan mi aan m tun titunwanbir, le bi kan nsan ki bii maayimbil aan bi lik seen mi.

ref: Then I asked God to punish Tobiah and Sanballat for what they had done. I prayed that God would punish the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who, together with her, had tried to frighten me. The Work Is Finished
text: Le m mee Uwumbɔr ke, “Uwumbɔr, teer Tobia ni Sanbalat aah tun pu na ki daa bitafal. Teer upii u bi yin u ke Noadia na, ni bibɔnabr bi mɔmɔk pɔɔn bibaa ke bi faan mi na, ki daa bi mu aatafal.” Lituln ngbaan aah doo pu na

ref: On the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, the wall was completely rebuilt. It had taken
text: Joo cha iwiin piiŋmu ni ilee ti jer, Elul aaŋmal aawiin moninko ni iŋmu daal na, ligoln ngbaan aatuln mɔmɔk nan doo.

ref: When our enemies in the surrounding nations learned that the work was finished, they felt helpless, because they knew that our God had helped us rebuild the wall.
text: Timi aadim bi bi ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln timi na aah ŋun kina na, le bi bee ke bi jin inimɔɔn a, ba pu? unii mɔmɔk nan bee ke Uwumbɔr aaterm le tun kina aatuln.

ref: All this time the Jewish leaders and Tobiah had been writing letters back and forth.
text: N‑yoonn mue mɔmɔk na, Juu yaab aaninkpiib nan tun ti bui Tobia tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋani na.

ref: Many people in Judah were loyal to Tobiah for two reasons: Shecaniah son of Arah was his father-in-law, and Tobiah's son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
text: Juda aanib pam le nan si upuwɔb, ba pu? uchool le nan ye Juu aanii Ara aajapɔɔn Sekania. Ki ki kpee na, ujapɔɔn Jehohanann mu le nan joo Berekia aajapɔɔn Mesulam aabisal.

ref: The people would always tell me about the good things Tobiah had done, and then they would tell Tobiah everything I had said. So Tobiah kept sending letters, trying to frighten me.
text: Binib ga nan sil nnimbiin ni ki bui mi Tobia aah ye unii pu na, le ki ki gir ti bui u maah len pu na mɔmɔk. Le u beenin ŋmee tigbann tii ni mi ke u pɔɔk ubaa ki faan mi.

ref: Although Jerusalem covered a large area, not many people lived there, and no new houses had been built.
text: Jerusalem nan ye kitiŋ ki wiir na la, le binib bi nan koo ki ponn ni na aa tee wiir, le kaadichal mu aa nan kee wiir.

ref: These are the names of the families of temple workers whose descendants returned: Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth, Keros, Sia, Padon, Lebana, Hagaba, Shalmai, Hanan, Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah, Besai, Meunim, Nephushesim, Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur, Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha, Barkos, Sisera, Temah, Neziah, and Hatipha.
text: Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aatutum aamaal bi nan nyan tinaagbiir ponn ni ki gir ni na mu sɔ: Siha, ni Hasufa, ni Tabaof, ni Keros, ni Sia, ni Padonn, ni Lebana, ni Hagaba, ni Salmai, ni Hanann, ni Gidel, ni Gahar, ni Reaya, ni Resinn, ni Nekoda, ni Gasam, ni Usa, ni Pasea, ni Besai, ni Meunim, ni Nefusesim, ni Bakbuk, ni Hakufa, ni Hahur, ni Baslif, ni Mehida, ni Hasa, ni Bakos, ni Sisera, ni Tema, ni Nesia, ni Hatifa.

ref: Here are the names of Solomon's servants whose descendants returned: Sotai, Sophereth, Perida, Jaala, Darkon, Giddel, Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, and Amon.
text: Solomonn aatutum aamaal ponn ni bi mu nan nyan tinaagbiir ponn ni ki gir ni na sɔ: Sotai, ni Soferef, ni Perida, ni Jaala, ni Dakonn, ni Gidel, ni Sefatia, ni Hatil, ni Pokeref‑Hasebaim, ni Amonn.

ref: The families of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai could not prove they were priests. The ancestor of the family of Barzillai had married the daughter of Barzillai from Gilead and had taken his wife's family name. But the records of these three families could not be found, and none of them were allowed to serve as priests.
text: Bitotoorb aamaal i mu aa nan ŋmaa kan kigbaŋ ki ponn ni biyaajatiib aayimbil bi na: ima le ye Hobaya, ni Hakos, ni Basilai aamaal aanib. Basilai aamaal ngbaan aayaaja nan yoor Gilead aatiŋ aaja u bi nan yin u ke Basilai na aabisal, le ki gur joo uchool aayimbil yin ubaa. Imaal ngbaan ponn ni aanib aah kaa kan kigbaŋ ki ponn ni biyaajatiib aayimbil bi na, baa nan kan nsan ke bi li ye bitotoorb.

ref: In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until he lets us know if you really are priests.”
text: Juu yaab aayidaan nan bui bi ke baan ŋmaa ji tijikaar ti bi di tii Uwumbɔr ipiin na, see utotoor u ga ŋmaa di Urim ni Tumim di ŋaŋ ti ki lik na.

ref: And so, by the seventh month, priests, Levites, temple guards, musicians, workers, and many of the ordinary people had settled in the towns of Judah.
text: Bitotoorb, ni Liifai yaab, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal aakikiib, ni bilahngaab, ni biwangbaab, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aatutum, ni binib bibaa, ni Israel yaab bi gur na, nan kal itingbaan, ni ntisakpem mu bi Juda ponn ni na ni la.

ref: From early morning till noon, he read the Law of Moses to them, and they listened carefully.
text: Mbisamɔb ngbaan chee le u nan karn Nkaal Aagbaŋ ngbaan ki nyan kichakpiik ni ki ti saa nwiin pu, le bi mɔmɔk si pel gbimm ke bi ŋun ti mɔmɔk.

ref: Ezra stood on a high wooden platform that had been built for this occasion. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah were standing to his right, while Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash Baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam were standing to his left.
text: Esra nan si tɔk paangara u bi nan paan u kina aatuln pu na pu la. Bijab bimina le nan si uŋangii wɔb: Matitia, ni Sema, ni Anaya, ni Uria, ni Hilkia, ni Maaseya. Le Pedaya, ni Misael, ni Malkija, ni Hasum, ni Hasbadana, ni Sekaria, ni Mesulam mu si uŋangan wɔb.

ref: Ezra was up on the high platform, where he could be seen by everyone, and when he opened the book, all the people stood up.
text: Esra aah nan si tɔk paangara ngbaan pu ki fɔk jer binib ngbaan mɔmɔk na, le bi mɔmɔk di binimbil kaan u pu. N‑yoonn mu u chuu kpar kigbaŋ ngbaan na, le bi mɔmɔk fii sil paacham.

ref: Ezra praised the great Lord God, and they lifted their hands, shouting “Amen! Amen!” Then they bowed with their faces to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
text: Le Esra bui ke, “Pak Uwumbɔr man, u ye Uwumbɔr Sakpiin la.” Le binib ngbaan mɔmɔk yoor biŋaal paacham ki kii ke, “Amii, amii.” Bi mɔmɔk nan gbaan kitiŋ ki doon Uwumbɔr, le binimbil chik kitiŋ.

ref: After this, the Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah went among the people, explaining the meaning of what Ezra had read.
text: Bi nan puen nabr Uwumbɔr Aakaal ngbaan waahr le ki nin bui bi mu aatataa, le binib ngbaan bee mbamɔm.

ref: The people started crying when God's Law was read to them. Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who had been teaching the people all said, “This is a special day for the Lord your God. So don't be sad and don't cry!”
text: Binib ngbaan aah ŋun Nkaal ngbaan aah ban ke bi ŋa pu na, ni nan muk bi sakpen le bi piin ki bi wii. Kina pu na, Nehemia, u nan ye baayidaan na, ni Esra, u nan ye utotoor ki mu bee Nkaal ngbaan mbamɔm na, ni Liifai yaab bi nan tuk binib ngbaan mu aatataa na bui binib ngbaan ke, “Nwiin mumina ye nwiin mu bi chain ki tii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr na la, kina pu na, ni taa wii, ki taa kpeeni mu.

ref: Nehemiah told the people, “Enjoy your good food and wine and share some with those who didn't have anything to bring. Don't be sad! This is a special day for the Lord, and he will make you happy and strong.”
text: Kina pu na, li chaa kun man ki ti ŋa njim ki ji. Yakr man nimi aajikaar ni ndaan ki tii binib bi kaa kpa na. Din aawiin ye chain aawiin le ki tii Uwumbɔr, nima pu na, cha nisui li piin man. Mpopiin mu Uwumbɔr tii na ga tii nimi mpɔɔn.”

ref: The Levites encouraged the people by saying, “This is a sacred day, so don't worry or mourn!”
text: Liifai yaab ngbaan nan pɔɔn bibaa ki chuun sɔŋni binib ngbaan aasui, ki tuk bi ke nwiin mundaal bi chain na, bi taa cha bisui bii.

ref: When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them. Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
text: Kina pu le binib ngbaan mɔmɔk kun bido ki ti jin, ki nyun, ki kpa mpopiin, ki yakr baah kpa pu na tii biken; ba pu? bi bee baah karn pu tii bi na aatataa. Tikakar Aajim

ref: On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law
text: Kitaak aah ki woln na, le imaal ngbaan aaninkpiib, ni bitotoorb, ni Liifai yaab nan buen Esra chee ke bi ti bae Nkaal aabaem.

ref: that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year.
text: Bi nan ti kan ke Nkaal mu Uwumbɔr nan di tii Moses ke u di tii waanib Israel yaab na, nan siin ke bi ŋa tikakar ki li koo ti ponn ni n‑yoonn mu bi ban bi ji Tikakar Aajim na.

ref: They also learned that they were to go into the woods and gather branches of leafy trees such as olives, myrtles, and palms for making these shelters.
text: Kina pu le bi nan siin tibɔr timina ki di tii Jerusalem aatiŋ, ni ntikpaam, ni ntiwaatiir mu gur na ke, “Li cha man ŋigongon pu ki ti gaa tisufar, ni tibɔkpafar, ni isui i aafar nu mɔ na, ki nan ŋa tikakar ngbaan, nkaal ponn ni aah mɔk pu na.”

ref: So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate.
text: Le binib ngbaan ban tisufar ki nan ŋa tikakar baachin ponn ni, ni baadir aapaacham, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal aachiln ponn ni, ni mpaan mu bi mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Nnyun Aabisamɔb na, ni mu bi yin mu ke Efraim Aabisamɔb na chee.

ref: Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
text: Binib bimɔk nan nyan ni tinaagbiir ni na nan ŋa baakakar ki koo ti ponn ni. Ki nya Nunn aajapɔɔn Josua aayoonn ki nan saa liyaadaal ngbaan na, nwiin ngbaan daal le kina aajim nan ki ŋa, kina pu na, binib mɔmɔk aasui nan piin le ni mɔ bi mɔmɔk.

ref: On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
text: Ki nyan njim ngbaan aajan aawiin daal ki ti saa kookoo aawiin daal na, bi nan karni Uwumbɔr Aakaal ngbaan siisii le mu ti doo. Bi nan jin njim ngbaan ki ti saa iwiin ilole, le winiin daal na, bi mɔmɔk nan kuun ki doon Uwumbɔr, le ki ŋa kookoo aatork, Nkaal ngbaan aah mɔk pu na.

ref: For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
text: Bi nan karn Bidindaan Uwumbɔr Aakaal tii bi ki ti saa tikur titaa aah ga yunn pu na, ki ki yoor tikur titaa aah ga yunn pu na le ki di kpiir baatunwanbir pu ki doon Bidindaan Uwumbɔr.

ref: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God.
text: Bi nan ŋa paangara tii Liifai yaab; le Jesua, ni Bani, ni Kadmiel, ni Sebania, ni Buni, ni Serebia, ni Bani, ni Kenani, si tɔk u pu. Bi nan teen mpɔɔn pu ki mee Bidindaan Uwumbɔr.

ref: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said: “Stand and shout praises to your Lord, the eternal God! Praise his wonderful name, though he is greater than words can express.” The People Pray
text: Liifai yaab bimina le nan bui binib ngbaan ke bi doon Uwumbɔr: bima le ye Jesua, ni Kadmiel, ni Bani, ni Hasabneya, ni Serebia, ni Hodia, ni Sebania, ni Petahia. Bi nan len ke: “Fii sil man ki pak Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. Pak u ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na man. Cha unii mɔmɔk pak waayimbil li kpa kipak na, unibɔn mu aapak aa tee nyuun ki ga ŋeer u.” Titunwanbir aakpiirn aameel

ref: You alone are the Lord, Creator of the heavens and all the stars, Creator of the earth and those who live on it, Creator of the ocean and all its creatures. You are the source of life, praised by the stars that fill the heavens.
text: Le Israel aanib mee limeel limina: “Uwumbɔr, sin baanja le ye Uwumbɔr. Sin le naan paacham ni iŋmabi i bi kitaapaak na. Sin le naan kitiŋ, ni nnyusakpem, ni tiwan ni mɔmɔk bi ni ponn ni na; sin le tii ni mɔmɔk limɔfal. Paacham aawan mɔmɔk gbaani le ki dooni si.

ref: You are the Lord our God, the one who chose Abram— you brought him from Ur in Babylonia and named him Abraham.
text: Sin Tidindaan Uwumbɔr le nan lee Abram ki di u nyan ni Ur aatiŋ ki bi Babiloŋ ni na. Sin le nan kpeln waayimbil ki yin u ke Abraham.

ref: Because he was faithful, you made an agreement to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites and Hittites, of the Amorites and Perizzites, and of the Jebusites and Girgashites. Now you have kept your promise, just as you always do.
text: Aa nan kan ke u kpa gaakii tii si, le aa nan puu tipuur tii u. Aa nan puu ke aa ga di Kanaann yaab aatiŋ tii u, ki kpee Hef yaab, ni Amor yaab aatim, ni Peris yaab, ni Jebus yaab, ni Girgas yaab aatim ke mu li ye uyaabitiib aatim. Saah ŋani saah len pu na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, aa joo saah puu pu na mbamɔm.

ref: When our ancestors were in Egypt, you saw their suffering; when they were at the Red Sea, you heard their cry for help.
text: Aa nan kan tiyaajatiib aah jin falaa sakpen pu Ijipt aatiŋ ponn ni na. Baah nan yin si ke aa ter bi buyoonn bi nan bi Nnyusakpem Mamam na chee na, aa nan kii.

ref: You knew that the King of Egypt and his officials and his nation had mistreated your people. So you worked fearsome miracles against the Egyptians and earned a reputation that still remains.
text: Aa nan tun iwaan aatun ki kiir Ijipt aabɔrkpaan, ni waaninkpiib, ni waanib bi bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu na, ba pu? aa nan nyi baah nan muk saanib pu na. Aa nan jin liyimbil li aa beenin kpa dandana wee na.

ref: You divided the deep sea, and your people walked through on dry land. But you tossed their enemies in, and they sank down like a heavy stone.
text: Aa nan naan nsan nnyusakpem ponn ni ki tii saanib, ki cheen bi puur kitikuun pu. Binib bi nan san dii bi na ma nan bee nnyun mu nyoo na ponn ni, ke litakpal aah muini nnyusakpem ponn ni pu na.

ref: Each day you led your people with a thick cloud, and at night you showed the way with a flaming fire.
text: Aa nan cha ntaalangbam loln saanib pu nsan nwiin pu, ki cha mmii wiihn ki loln bi pu nsan kinyeek.

ref: At Sinai you came down from heaven, and you gave your people good laws and teachings that are fair and honest.
text: Aa nan sunn ni bi chee Sainai Aajool chee; nima chee le aa nan len bi chee tibɔr ki tii bi ikaal i ŋan na, ni mbaem mu kpa ntataa na.

ref: You commanded them to respect your holy Sabbath, and you instructed your servant Moses to teach them your laws.
text: Aa nan mɔk bi ke bi li joo Saakpaakool daal mbamɔm; ki nan di saakaal tii saatutunn Moses le u di ŋum bi.

ref: When they were hungry, you sent bread from heaven, and when they were thirsty, you let water flow from a rock. Then you commanded them to capture the land that you had solemnly promised. *
text: Nkon aah nan joo bi na, aa nan tii bi tijikaar ti nyan ni paacham na, ki tii bi nnyun mu nyan ni litakpal ponn ni na, bi nyun. Aa nan bui bi ke bi li joo kitiŋ ki aa nan puu ke aa ga di tii bi na.

ref: not even when they made an idol shaped like a calf and insulted you by claiming, “This is the god who rescued us from Egypt.”
text: Bi nan naan liwaal li bi ke unaajabo na, ki bui ke liwaal ngbaan le nan nyan ni bi Ijipt aatiŋ ponn ni. Uwumbɔr, bi nan seei si ki ti nyaŋ.

ref: Because of your great mercy, you never abandoned them in the desert. And you always guided them with a cloud by day and a fire at night.
text: Le saa nan san cha bi nteersakpiin ngbaan ni, ba pu? saanimbaasaln wiir sakpen. Saa nan cha ntaalangbam mu nan mɔk bi nsan nwiin pu, ni mmii mu nan mɔk bi nsan kinyeek na siir cha bi.

ref: You took good care of them, and for forty years they never lacked a thing. Their clothes didn't wear out, and their feet were never swollen.
text: Aa nan tii bi baah ban pu na nteersakpiin ni, ki ti saa ŋibin imonko ilee. Baawanpeenkaan aa nan kpo, le bitaa mu aa nan duun, kaa wu mu.

ref: You brought them into the land that you had promised their ancestors, and you blessed their nation with people that outnumbered the stars in the sky.
text: Saah nan tii bi mbim mu na nan wiir ke iŋmabi i bi kitaapaak na la, le bi jan, ki gaa ki koo kitiŋ ki aa nan puu ke aa ga di tii biyaajatiib ni bima na ni.

ref: Then their descendants conquered the land. You helped them defeat the kings and nations and treat their enemies however they wished.
text: Bi nan jan ki gaa Kanaann aatiŋ; aa nan nyaŋ binib bi koo nima na tii bi. Aa nan tii saanib mpɔɔn ke bi ŋa Kanaann aatiŋ aanib, ni baabɔrb, baah gee pu na.

ref: They captured strong cities and rich farmland; they took furnished houses, as well as cisterns, vineyards, olive orchards, and numerous fruit trees. They ate till they were satisfied, and they celebrated your abundant blessings.
text: Saanib nan nyaŋ ntim mu bi maa ŋigon gob mu, ki kii mu na, ni ikpaakon i nyuun na, ni ŋidichal ŋi kpa liwangol na, ni inyunbun i binib puen gbii i na, ni nkpan aasui, ni ŋisubil aasui, ni ndaan aasubil aakpaakon. Bi nan jin baah gee pu na ki filk; bi nan jin mmɔɔn mumɔk aa nan di tii bi na.

ref: In spite of this, they rebelled and disobeyed your laws. They killed your prophets, who warned them to turn back to you, and they cursed your name.
text: Le saanib nan yii saamɔb, kaa kii tii si; bi nan fenn bipuwɔb tii saakaal, ki nan ku saabɔnabtiib bi nan sak bi ki bui bi ke bi gir ni aa chee na. N‑yoonn n‑yoonn bi nan seei si;

ref: So you handed them over to their enemies, who treated them terribly. But in their sufferings, they begged you to help. From heaven you listened to their prayers and because of your great mercy, you sent leaders to rescue them.
text: kina pu le aa nan cha baadim nyaŋ bi ki joo bi. Baah nan bi limukl ponn ni na bi nan yin si ke aa ter bi, le aa nan bi paacham ki kii. Saanimbaasaln sakpeln ponn ni le aa tii bi biyidam bi nan gaa bi lii baadim chee na.

ref: But when they were at peace, they would turn against you, and you would hand them over to their enemies. Then they would beg for help, and because you are merciful, you rescued them over and over again.
text: Nsuudoon aah gir ni na, le bi ki tun titunwanbir, le aa ki cha baadim nyaŋ bi. Le baah ki yii baatunwanbir ki fenn gir ni aa chee ke aa ter bi na, aa bi paacham ki ŋun, ki joo saanimbaasaln gaal bi lir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: For years, you were patient, and your Spirit warned them with messages spoken by your prophets. Still they refused to listen, and you handed them over to their enemies.
text: Le ŋibin mɔmɔk aa ji suklaa bi pu ki sak bi, ki cha Saafuur Nyaan gbiini saabɔnabtiib ke bi sak bi, le bi yii ki kpaa bitafal, kina pu le aa cha baadim nyaŋ bi.

ref: But you are merciful and kind, and so you never forgot them or let them be destroyed.
text: Le saanimbaasaln aah ti nyaŋ sakpen pu na, saa nan yii bi, kaa ku doo bi. Aa sil ye unimbaasaln Aawumbɔr u kpa lineen sakpen na la.

ref: Our God, you are powerful, fearsome, and faithful, always true to your word. So please keep in mind the terrible sufferings of our people, kings, leaders, priests, and prophets, from the time Assyria ruled until this very day.
text: Uwumbɔr, timi Aawumbɔr, saapɔɔn wiir sakpen; Unii mɔk san si ijawaan, le saapɔɔn ti nyaŋ. Aa joo saah nan puu tipuur ti na mbamɔm. Ki nyan buyoonn Asiria aatiŋ aabɔrb nan muk timi na, hali ki nan saa din, taah jin falaa u na nyaŋ a. Timi aabɔrb, ni timi aayidam, ni timi aatotoorb, ni saabɔnabtiib, ni tiyaajatiib, ni timi aanib mɔmɔk jin falaa la. Teer taah jin falaa sakpen pu na.

ref: You have always been fair when you punished us for our sins.
text: Saah daa timi aatafal pu na, aa kpa mbamɔn; ti tun titunwanbir, le sin ma ŋani saah len pu na kaa joo cha.

ref: Our kings and leaders, our priests and ancestors have never obeyed your commands or heeded your warnings.
text: Tiyaajatiib, ni timi aabɔrb, ni timi aayidam, ni bitotoorb mɔmɔk yii saakaal. Bi yii kaa pel saah bui bi pu na, ni saah sak bi pu na.

ref: You blessed them with a kingdom and with an abundance of rich, fertile land, but they refused to worship you or turn from their evil.
text: Saanyoor pu, le bibɔrb joo saanib buyoonn bi nan bi kitiŋ ki waa ki nyuun aan aa nan di tii bi na ponn ni, le bi beenin ŋani titunwanbir kaa dii si.

ref: Now we are slaves in this fruitful land you gave to our ancestors.
text: Le ti kpaln binaagbiib kitiŋ ki ponn ni aa nan di tii timi na, kitiŋ ki nyuun ki tii timi tijikaar na.

ref: Its plentiful harvest is taken by kings you placed over us because of our sins. Our suffering is unbearable, because they do as they wish to us and our livestock. The People Make an Agreement
text: Bibɔrb bi aa cha bi joo timi, timi aatunwanbir pu na le gaal kitiŋ ngbaan aah ŋani tijikaar ti na. Bi ŋani timi, ni timi aawakor baah gee pu na la, le ni bii tisui sakpen.” Binib ngbaan ni Uwumbɔr aah ŋa kimɔbaan pu na

ref: And so, a firm agreement was made that had the official approval of the leaders, the Levites, and priests.
text: Tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋa na pu, le timi Israel aanib sil do, ki ban ke ti di ibamɔn ŋmee kimɔbaan aakpaam aagbaŋ kimina; le timi aayidam, ni Liifai yaab, ni timi aatotoorb di biŋaal paan nkpaam ngbaan pu.

ref: All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
text: sil do ki kpaan timi aayidam chee ki puu tipuur timina, ke ti ga gaa Uwumbɔr Aakaal mu u nan di tii ni waatutunn Moses na; ti ki puu tipuur ke ti ga kii Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb mbamɔm, ki ga li joo waakaal ni waah ban pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: We won't let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
text: Taan joo biwɔwɔm bi koo timi aatiŋ ponn ni na aapiib, kaan di tibisatiib mu tii bi.

ref: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
text: Biwɔwɔm yaa joo tijikaar bee tiwan nimɔk Likpaakool daal, bee nwiin mumɔk bi chain na, ke bi nan kooh ti pu na kan, taan daa ni. Libiln lolole mɔk ni kan, ti ga di timi aasar aatim lii ki taa ko mu, ki di cha pinn bi mɔmɔk joo timi aapɔn na mu, bi taa ki pa timi.

ref: Once a year we will each donate a small amount of silver to the temple of our God.
text: Libiln mɔk kan, ti mɔmɔk ga tii tikunabr siib baah nan siin pu na ki di ter Uwumbɔr Aadichal aatoorn pu.

ref: This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
text: Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aadoon pu, ti ga tii tiwan nimina: boroboro u bi joo tii Uwumbɔr na, ni iwiin mɔmɔk aajikaabim aapiin, ni tiwakor ti bi ga di toor kitork ki see mmii ponn ni na, ni Ŋikpaakoo daal aatork ki bi chain na, ni Uŋmapɔɔn daal aatork aajim, ni njim mu gur na, ni ntoorm mɔmɔk mu gur ki bi chain na, ni kitork ki bi toor Israel yaab aatunwanbir pu na pu, ki kpee tiwan nimɔk bi ban Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni na.

ref: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
text: Ti mɔmɔk, bitotoorb, ni Liifai yaab, ni binib mɔmɔk ga too inaan libiln mɔmɔk ponn ni, ki nyan imaal i ga tii idɔ aan bi li joo seer tiwakor ti bi joo toor tii Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, Nkaal aah mɔk pu na.

ref: Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
text: Libiln mɔk ponn ni kan, ti ga di taah puen chee njikaabim mu na, ŋisubil ŋi puen puir timi aasui pu na buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni ki ti di tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
text: Ti ga di taah puen ma njan aabijabo umɔk na buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni, bitotoorb chee, aan bi di u tii Uwumbɔr, Nkaal aah mɔk pu na. Ti ga ki di timi aanaa aah puen ma unaabo u na; ni timi aapiih, ni timi aaŋoob aah puen ma ipihbi ni iŋobi i na mu tii Uwumbɔr, Nkaal aah mɔk pu na.

ref: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
text: Libiln mɔk ponn ni kan, ti ga di taah puen chee njikaabim mu na aayon, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan, ni ŋisubil mɔmɔk aapiin buen bitotoorb chee Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aan bi di tii Uwumbɔr, Nkaal aah mɔk pu na. Ti ga di ni ye Uwumbɔr yaan ki nyan ni timi aasar mu ponn ni na ki di tii Liifai yaab bi gaal kina aawan itingbaan ponn ni na.

ref: A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom,
text: Bitotoorb bi ye Aaronn aayaabitiib na ga li bi Liifai yaab ngbaan chee n‑yoonn mu bi bi gaal tisar aawan ngbaan na, le Liifai yaab ngbaan ga yakr tijikaar ngbaan nfum kipiik kipiik, ki di ligeln libaabaa ŋa Uwumbɔr Aadichal aapil ponn ni, aan ti li ye Lidichal ngbaan aajikaar.

ref: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.
text: Liifai yaab, ni Israel aanib biken le ga di baah too too tijikaar ti na mɔmɔk, njikaabim, ni ndaan, ni olif aakpan, ki di buen nin chee bitotoorb bi bi lituln pu na, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal aakikiib, ni bilahngaab kpa baadir na, Lidichal ngbaan ponn ni aasambil ni tiyir aah bi nin chee na. Taan suln timi Aawumbɔr Aadichal bɔr.

ref: The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there.
text: Binib bi nan ye biyidam na nan kal Jerusalem ponn ni, le binib bi gur na too inaan ke bi lee lidichal libaa ŋidichal kipiik mɔk ponn ni ke bi buen ti li koo Jerusalem aatiŋ ki bi chain na ponn ni, le bi gur na ti li koo ntisakpem ni muwaatiir na ponn ni.

ref: Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
text: Binib ngbaan nan pak unii umɔk nan nyan sil ke u ga li bi Jerusalem ponn ni na.

ref: Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families. The Judah Tribe
text: Israel aanib ngbaan, bitotoorb, ni Liifai yaab, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aatutum, ni Solomonn aatutum aayaabitiib nan ti kal baatim pu, ntisakpem ni muwaatiir mu gur na ponn ni la, le ki kpa bibaa aasar ni ŋidichal. Juda aatiŋ aamaal aaninkpiib bi nan bi Jerusalem ponn ni na sɔ: Juda aamaal yaab aayimbil sɔ:

ref: From the Judah tribe, two leaders settled in Jerusalem with their relatives. One of them was Athaiah son of Uzziah. His ancestors were Zechariah, Amariah, Shephatiah, Mahalalel, and Perez, the son of Judah. From the descendants of Perez,
text: Peres aayaabitiib bi nan ye binikpaam ki koo Jerusalem ponn ni na nan ye binib ikui inaa ni imonko itaa ni biniin la. Benjaminn aamaal yaab mu aayimbil sɔ:

ref: From the Benjamin tribe, three leaders settled in Jerusalem. The first was Sallu son of Meshullam, and the others were Gabbai and Sallai. Sallu's ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah. Altogether, there were
text: Gabai ni Salai, bi ye Salu aanaabitiib na. Benjaminn aamaal aanib bi nan koo Jerusalem ponn ni na, nan ye binib ikui iwae ni moninko ni biniin la.

ref: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command. Priests
text: Sikri aajapɔɔn Joel le nan ye baayidaan, le Hasenua aajapɔɔn Juda nan ye u paa kitiŋ ngbaan aatutum aaninkpel pu na. Bitotoorb bi mu nan koo Jerusalem ponn ni na aayimbil sɔ:

ref: The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest.
text: Hilkia aajapɔɔn Seraya, u aayaaja nan ye Mesulam na. Seraya aayaajatiib biken le nan ye Sadok, ni Merayof, ni Ahitub u nan ye Utotoorninkpel na.

ref: Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
text: Hasub aajapɔɔn Semaya, u aayaaja nan ye Asrikam na. Uyaajatiib biken le nan ye Hasabia ni Buni.

ref: Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
text: Sabetai ni Josabad nan ye Liifai yaab aanikpaam bi nan lik binib bi tun lituln li bi lipaal Uwumbɔr Aadichal chee na la.

ref: Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant. Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
text: Maika aajapɔɔn Matania, u aayaaja nan ye Sabdi, u ye Asaf aamaal ponn ni na. Uma le nan ye bilahngaab ni biwangbaab bi gaa ilahn ki dooni Uwumbɔr na aaninkpel. Bakbukia le nan ye u paa Matania pu na. Samua aajapɔɔn Abda, u aayaaja nan ye Galal u nyan ni Jedutunn aamaal ponn ni na.

ref: One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
text: Akub, ni Talmonn, ni baamaal nan ti kpaan binib nkub ni imonko itaa ni kipiik ni bilee, le ki koo Jerusalem ponn ni.

ref: The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah.
text: Israel yaab bi gur na, ni bitotoorb bi gur na, ni Liifai yaab bi gur na, nan ti kal baalangben pu baatisakpem ni muwaatiir ponn ni Juda aatiŋ pu la.

ref: But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
text: Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aatutum nan koo Jerusalem aapepel li bi yin li ke Ofel na ponn ni la; le Siha ni Gispa nan ye baaninkpiib.

ref: Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services,
text: Uja u nan lik Liifai yaab bi nan koo Jerusalem ponn ni na le nan ye Bani aajapɔɔn Usi, u aayaaja nan ye Hasabia na. Uyaajatiib biken le nan ye Matania ni Maika, le ki ye Asaf aamaal ponn ni aanii. Mmaal ngbaan le nan ye Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aalahngaab ni biwangbaab, n‑yoonn mu bi dooni Uwumbɔr na.

ref: though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
text: Nnaan aakaal nan bi, ki mɔk imaal ngbaan aah ga li gaa ilahn ki gbaa tiwan Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni, iwiin mɔmɔk pu na.

ref: The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe. The People in the Other Towns and Villages
text: Mesesabel aajapɔɔn Petahia, u ye Sera aamaal ponn ni aanii ki ye Juda aanibol aanii na, le nan si Israel yaab aasisii Pesia aabɔr aadichal ni. Binib bi nan bi ntim mu gur na ponn ni na aayimbil

ref: The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages,
text: Binib bi nan ye Benjaminn aanibol yaab na nan kal Geba, ni Mikmas, ni Ai, ni Betel, ni itingbaan i bi gbɔk nima na,

ref: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
text: ni Anatof, ni Nob, ni Anania,

ref: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
text: ni Hasor, ni Rama, ni Gitayim,

ref: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
text: ni Hadid, ni Seboyim, ni Nebalat,

ref: Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley.
text: ni Lod, ni Ono, ni Bikpikpiib Aafataŋ ni la.

ref: Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
text: Bi nan cha Liifai yaab bi nan ka Juda yaab aatiŋ pu na buen ti kal Benjaminn yaab chee la.

ref: Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
text: Bitotoorb bimina, ni Liifai yaab bee le nan nyan ni tinaagbiir ponn ni ki dii ni Sealtiel aajapɔɔn Serubabel ni Utotoorninkpel Josua: Bitotoorb ngbaan aayimbil sɔ:

ref: The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise,
text: Jesua, ni Binui, ni Kadmiel, ni Serebia, ni Juda, ni Matania, le nan ye binib bi gaa ilahn ki dooni Uwumbɔr na aayidam.

ref: while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses. Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
text: Le Bakbukia, ni Uno, ni Liifai yaab biken na nan keei bi. Utotoorninkpel Josua aamaal

ref: Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada.
text: Josua le nan ma Joyakim; le Joyakim mu ma Eliasib; le Eliasib mu ma Joyada;

ref: Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua. Leaders of the Priestly Clans
text: le Joyada mu ma Jonatann; le Jonatann mu ma Jadua. Bitotoorb aamaal ponn ni aayidam

ref: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
text: Buyoonn Eliasib, ni Joyada, ni Jonatann, ni Jadua nan bi limɔfal ni ki ye bitotoorninkpiib na, le bi nan ŋmee Liifai yaab aamaal aadichadam ni bitotoorb aamaal aadichadam aayimbil. N‑yoonn ngbaan le Darius nan ye Pesia aabɔrkpaan.

ref: However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
text: Liifai yaab aamaal aadichadam ma nan ŋmee baayimbil kigbaŋ ponn ni, ki ti saa buyoonn Eliasib aayaabil Jonatann nan bi na la. Baah yakr Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aatuln pu na

ref: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
text: Hasabia, ni Serebia, ni Jesua, ni Binui, ni Kadmiel le nan yakr Liifai yaab ŋigetek, ŋigetek, le bi tun Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aatuln. Ŋigetek ŋilelee le nan kpaani ki pak Uwumbɔr ki dooni u, ke Uwumbɔr aanii, Ubɔrkpaan David aah nan mɔk ke bi li dooni u pu na.

ref: All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest. Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
text: Binib bee nan bi limɔfal ni buyoonn Josua aajapɔɔn Joyakim, u aayaaja nan ye Jehosadak na, ni n‑yoonn mu uyidaan Nehemia, ni utotoor Esra, u nan bee Nkaal mbamɔm na, nan laa bi limɔfal ponn ni na la. Nehemia aah di Jerusalem aatiŋ aagoln ŋa Uwumbɔr aaŋaal ni pu na

ref: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
text: Buyoonn bi nan di Jerusalem aatiŋ aagoln ŋa Uwumbɔr aaŋaal ni na, bi nan yin ni Liifai yaab baah bi nin chee na mɔmɔk, ke bi nan kpaan kitork ngbaan, ki li gaa ilahn ki dooni Uwumbɔr, ki gbaa tibar ni ichayakrtuun.

ref: The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth.
text: ni Bef Gilgal, ni Geba, ni Asmafef aatim ni ki nan kpaan Jerusalem ni.

ref: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
text: Bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab nan toor kitork ki nyan bibaa ni binib ngbaan aatunwanbir, le ki ŋa ibisamɔi ni kitiŋ aagoln ngbaan chain.

ref: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
text: M nan kuun Juda aayidam ki ti tɔŋ ligoln ngbaan paab, ki di ŋigetek sakpiin ŋilee ŋa biŋaal ni ke bi di bi chuun mann ligoln ngbaan, ki li joo idoon tii Uwumbɔr. Njan aagetekr nan di toŋ ŋŋangii wɔb ligoln ngbaan paab ki cha Litapuln Aabisamɔb wɔb.

ref: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them.
text: Hosaya le nan paa bilahngaab pu, le Juda aayidam ligetekr libaa di paan u pu.

ref: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
text: Udo yaab Semaya, ni Asarel, ni Milalai, ni Gilalai, ni Maai, ni Netanel, ni Juda, ni Hanani le nan paa u pu; bi mɔmɔk nan joo tiwangbaakaan ni bi ke tiwangbaakaan ni Uwumbɔr aanii Ubɔrkpaan David nan gbaa na. Le Esra u nyi Uwumbɔr aakaal mbamɔm na nan loln ligetekr ngbaan pu nsan.

ref: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
text: Baah nan ti fuu mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Uyayak Aabisamɔb chee na, le bi jon ŋibimbin ŋi cha David Aatiŋ ni na, ki jer David aabɔrnaakook, le ki ti ki tɔŋ ligoln ngbaan paab Nnyun Aabisamɔb chee, mu bi liwipuul wɔb kitiŋ ngbaan pu na.

ref: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
text: Ligetekr li mu nan ki joo idoon tii Uwumbɔr na mu nan di toŋ ŋŋangan wɔb ligoln ngbaan paab, le m di binib ligetekr liken di paan bi pu. Ti nan chuun ti jer kidifɔfɔk ki chee bi ŋani boroboro na, ki ti saa Ligowawaal na chee,

ref: Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard,
text: ki nyan nima ki ti jer Efraim Aabisamɔb, ni Jesana Aabisamɔb, ni Ijan Aabisamɔb, ni Hananel Aadifɔfɔk, ni Nkub Aadifɔfɔk, ki ti saa Ipiih Aabisamɔb. Ti nan ti doo timi aasachuln ngbaan Uwumbɔr Aadichal aabisamɔb chee la.

ref: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
text: Le Maaseya, ni Semaya, ni Eleasar, ni Usi, ni Jehohanann, ni Malkija, ni Elam, ni Eser nan paa. Jesrahia, u nan ye bilahngaab aaninkpel na, ni waalahngaab nan gaa ilahn mpɔɔn pu.

ref: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
text: Bi nan toor titoor pam liyaadaal ngbaan, le binib ngbaan nan kpa mpopiin sakpen, Uwumbɔr aah nan tii bi mmɔɔn pu na. Bipiib ni mbim mu nan bi njim ngbaan ponn ni, le kifuuk ki bi mɔmɔk nan ŋani na nan buen dandar. Baah tii Uwumbɔr ipiin pu na

ref: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le bi nan ban bijab kaan kiir tidir ti bi joo tijikaar, ni tiwan niken siini na, ni baah di Uwumbɔr Aadichal aajikaar ti bi too too na di ŋa ti ponn ni na; bi nan di ukpaal mɔmɔk aah tii waajikaar aapiin i na, ni libiln mɔk aajikaabim mu puen biir na, ni ŋisubil ŋi mu puen puir na mu di kpee ti pu. Bijab ngbaan le nan ye bi ga li gaal ikpaakon i bi duun ntim mɔmɔk na, bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab aajikaar ti bi too tii bi, Nkaal aah mɔk pu na nan tii bi. Binib mɔmɔk nan kpa mpopiin bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab ngbaan pu;

ref: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
text: ba pu? bi nan toor titunwanbir aachapinn ni titoor timɔk gur na, Uwumbɔr aah mɔk pu na. Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aalahngaab, ni biwangbaab ni bikikiib mu nan tun baatun ki dii ikaal i Ubɔrkpaan David ni ujapɔɔn Solomonn nan siin na.

ref: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
text: Ki nyan Ubɔrkpaan David ni ulahngaar Asaf aayoonn mu jer na, bilahngaab ni biwangbaab ngbaan le lolni nsan ki pak ki joo idoon tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
text: Serubabel aayoonn, ni Nehemia aayoonn na, Israel aanib nan tii iwiin mɔmɔk aajikaar ki joo ter Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aalahngaab, ni biwangbaab, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal aakikiib. Binib ngbaan nan ki di tijikaar tii Uwumbɔr, ti li ye Liifai yaab yaan, le bi mu ki lee tii bitotoorb, nkaal aah mɔk pu na.

ref: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
text: Bi nan karn Moses Aakaal mpɔɔn pu binib ngbaan aanimbiin ni, ki ti saa nin chee len ke Amonn yaab, ni Moab yaab taa kpaan Uwumbɔr aanib Israel yaab chee daalbaadaal na.

ref: This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing.
text: Naah nan ye pu na le ye ke Amonn ni Moab yaab nan yii kaa tii Israel yaab tijikaar ni nnyun n‑yoonn mu bi nan nyan ni Ijipt ni ki choo kuni na. Bi nan tee labr pan ŋimombil tii ubɔɔ Balaam ke u puun lii Israel yaab pu, le timi Aawumbɔr cha tipuur ngbaan kpaln tinyoor ki tii Israel yaab.

ref: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
text: Israel yaab aanib aah ŋun bi karn nkaal ngbaan na, le bi yakr biwɔwɔm mɔmɔk nyan bikaasisik ni. Nehemia aah giin tiwan mɔmɔk siin chob pu na

ref: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
text: Eliasib u ye utotoor, ki nan ye Uwumbɔr Aadichal aadir ti bi joo tijikaar ni tiwan niken siini na aaninkpel na, ni Tobia nan ye tɔb jɔtiib la. Baajɔtiik nan yunn.

ref: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
text: U nan di kidiik ki wiir na tii Tobia. Kidiik ngbaan nan ye kidiik ki ponn ni bi nan siini tijikaar ti binib tii Uwumbɔr na, ni Uwumbɔr aatulalee aayon, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aawan, ni ipiin i binib nan tii bitotoorb na; ni njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan aapiin i bi joo tii Liifai yaab, ni bilahngaab, ni biwangbaab, ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal aakikiib na.

ref: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
text: Nimina aah nan bi ŋani kina na, maa nan bi Jerusalem aatiŋ ni; Babiloŋ aabɔr Ataksekes aanaan aabiln piitaa ni ŋilee ponn ni na, m nan gir buen u chee ke m ti bui u maah tun pu na. N‑yoonn siib aah jer na, le m nan ki mee u nsan

ref: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
text: ki gir ni Jerusalem. Maah nan ti kan ke Eliasib tii Tobia nsan u li koo Uwumbɔr Aadichal aadiik kibaa ponn ni na, ni nan gar mi sakpen.

ref: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
text: Liŋuul nan chuu mi sakpen, le m yoor Tobia aawan mɔmɔk mae lipaal.

ref: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
text: M nan cha bi toor kitork ki ŋa tidir ngbaan chain, ki di Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aawan, ni njikaabim aapiin, ni Uwumbɔr aatulalee aayon ki ki giin ni siin tidir ngbaan ponn ni.

ref: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
text: M nan ki ŋun ke Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni aalahngaab, ni biwangbaab, ni Liifai yaab biken fii Jerusalem ki gir buen baasar ponn ni, ba pu? binib aa nan ki tii bi ni ga ŋeer bi bi kpiin bibaa na.

ref: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
text: M nan galn binib ngbaan aaninkpiib pam, baah nan cha Uwumbɔr Aadichal aatuln bee fam pu na. Le m nan ki giini Liifai yaab ni bilahngaab ni biwangbaab ngbaan baatuln ponn ni, Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni.

ref: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
text: Le Israel aanib mɔmɔk ki piin ki joo ni baajikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni olif aakpan aapiin nan siini tidir ti ponn ni bi joo kina aawan siini na Uwumbɔr Aadichal chee.

ref: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
text: M nan di utotoor Selemia, ni Sadok, u nyi Nkaal mbamɔm na, ni Liifai aanii Padaya le kaan kiir tidir ngbaan, ki lee Sakur aajapɔɔn Hanann, u aayaaja nan ye Matania na ke u li ter bi. M nan kpa gaakii ke bijab ngbaan ga di ibamɔn yakr tiwan tii baatutuŋeertiib.

ref: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
text: Maawumbɔr, teer mbɔr, ki taa suln tiwan nimɔk m ŋa Saadichal ni aan aa kan idoon mbamɔm ki ponn ni na.

ref: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le m kan Juda aanib bibaa mueni nyani ŋisubil aanyun Likpaakool daal. Biken mu joo njikaabim, ni ŋisubil aadaan, ni ŋisubil aabɔŋ, ni tiwan niken paani baabon pu ki joo cha Jerusalem ponn ni, le m sak bi ke bi taa ki kooh tiwan nibaa Likpaakool daal.

ref: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
text: Taya aajab bibaa nan koo Jerusalem ponn ni, le bi mu joo ni ijan ni tiwan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ ki di koo ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni ke bi nan kooh tii timi aanib Likpaakool daal.

ref: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
text: M nan galn Juu yaab aayidam le ki bui bi ke, “Lik man naah bi tun titunwanbir ti na. Ni bi koor Likpaakool daal aakoobil la.

ref: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
text: Tiwanbaan nee pu le Uwumbɔr nan daa niyaajatiib aatafal ki bii kitiŋ kee. Naah bi koor Likpaakool daal aakoobil kina na, le ni beenin ban ke ni moo di Uwumbɔr aaŋuul lii ni Israel pu.”

ref: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
text: Nima pu le m nan siin ke bi laŋ Jerusalem aabisamɔi nwiin mu ga woln Likpaakool daal na, buyoonn bi kan nwiin ban mu lir na, ki taa ki piir i, see Likpaakool daal ti jer. M nan di maajab bibaa le siin ibisamɔi ngbaan chee, ke bi taa cha unii ubaa joo ni tiwan nibaa koo ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni, Likpaakool daal.

ref: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
text: N‑yoonn n‑yoonn biwankoob bi kooh tiwan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ na, nan doo kitiŋ ngbaan aagoln aapuwɔb kinyeek ki ga woln Likpaakool daal na la.

ref: But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath.
text: Le m nan sak bi ke, “Naah ka nima kii ke ni woln na ye fam la. Ni yaa ki ŋa kina daalbaadaal kan, m ga di mpɔɔn le di mɔk nimi.” Ki nyan n‑yoonn ngbaan, baa ki gir ni Likpaakool daal.

ref: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
text: M nan cha Liifai yaab toor kitork ki ŋa bibaa chain ki buen ti kii ibisamɔi ngbaan ke bi taa cha unii ubaa koor Likpaakool daal aakoobil. Uwumbɔr, teer mbɔr nimina mu pu, ki san mi kinimbaak, saageehm sakpem pu.

ref: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le m nan ki kan ke Juu yaab aajab pam nan yoor Asdod, ni Amonn, ni Moab aapiib.

ref: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
text: Baabim ligetekr libaa nan len Asdod aatiŋ aanib aaliin, bee iliin yayan la, kaa nyi timi aaliin.

ref: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
text: M nan galn bijab ngbaan, ki puun lii bi pu, ki gbaa bi, ki dar gui biyikpir; le ki cha bi puu Uwumbɔr aayimbil pu ke bi ni baabim ni biwɔwɔm aan ki mɔn tɔb.

ref: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
text: Ni ban ke ti dii nimi ki yii timi Aawumbɔr aamɔb ki yoor biwɔwɔmpiib la aa?”

ref: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
text: Joyada aate le nan ye utotoorninkpel Eliasib, le Joyada aajapɔɔn ubaa nan tee yoor Sanbalat, u nyan Bef Horonn aatiŋ ponn ni na aabisal. Nima pu le m jenn nyan Joyada Jerusalem ponn ni.

ref: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
text: Uwumbɔr, teer binib ngbaan aah nan bii bitotoorb aatuln, ni tipuur ti aa nan puu ki tii bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab na.

ref: Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites.
text: M nan nyan binib ngbaan tiwan nimɔk ye biwɔwɔm aawan na ponn ni; ki nan ŋa ikaal tii bitotoorb ni Liifai yaab ke unii mɔk li nyi waatuln;

ref: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
text: ki nan ban isan i ga cha idɔ i bi joo pu kitork aanann na aah ga fuu ni n‑yoonn mu na, ni binib mu aah ga li joo ni baajan aajikaabim aapiin ni njan aasubil ŋi puen puir na pu na. Uwumbɔr, teer mbɔr, ki ŋa tinyoor ŋa m pu.

ref: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
text: Waah nan jin nnaan ki nan saa libiln tatar ni na, u nan ŋa njim sakpem tii waaninkpiib bi lik waanaan na. Pesia ni Media aatɔb aajab nan bi nima, ki kpee biyidam ni bininyuum bi bi ŋipepel nkub ni moninko ni ŋilole na mu.

ref: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
text: Nee aapuwɔb na, le ubɔrkpaan ngbaan ki ŋa kina aajim ki tii bijab bi mɔmɔk bi litiyil Susa ni na, bigiim ni biwankpadam mɔmɔk. Njim mue mu nan yunn ki ti saa likpaakool libaa; bi nan ŋa mu libɔrchiln ni, nin chee ŋan sakpen na la.

ref: The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
text: Bi nan di tikokonn aakekenbɔn ni ŋipiin le di toor lichiln ngbaan ni, ki di ŋitan ŋi ye mbɔm ni mmam na di gbin tikunabr aabuen pu ki di chuu ŋitakpanyaan aagon. Bi nan di ncheen ni ŋitakpanyaan aabɔŋ aabɔŋ le di nak lichiln ngbaan ni, ki di ŋiyikukul aajal ŋi fɔk aan bi di salmaa ni tikunabr ŋa ŋi na di siin.

ref: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
text: Bi nan nyu ndaan salmaa aayikur ni la, le ti mɔmɔk bi tibaabaa kaa kpaan; le ubɔrkpaan ngbaan di mbɔrdaan chann tichann.

ref: and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
text: Ndaan aa nan kpa ke ubaa taa nyu waah gee pu na, ubɔrkpaan ngbaan nan bui libɔrchiln ni aatutum ke bi cha unii mɔk nyu waah ga ŋman pu na mɔk.

ref: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
text: Nimina aah bi ŋani na, le Ubɔrpii Fasti mu nan bi kibɔrnaakook ni ki ŋani kina aajim aaboln tii bipiib mu.

ref: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
text: Nwiin lolole daal, le ubɔr nan bi nyu ndaan ki kpa mpopiin, le ki tun ti yin ni waajab bi bi kpaa bi na ponn ni bilole, bi nan ye ubaa aanaagbiib na, Mehumann, ni Bista, ni Habona, ni Bigta ni Abagta, ni Setar, ni Kakas.

ref: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
text: U nan bui bi ke bi ti li joo ni Ubɔrpii Fasti, aan u li chik nnaan aayikpupuk. Ubɔrpii ngbaan nan ye upii u ŋan na la, le ubɔr ngbaan nan ban u di waanyaan di puk kipupuk waaninkpiib ni bimɔk nan dan njim ngbaan ni na chee.

ref: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
text: Binaagbiib ngbaan aah nan ti bui Ubɔrpii Fasti ke ubɔrkpaan yin u na, u nan yii kaa dan. Le ni chuu ubɔrkpaan ngbaan liŋuul pam.

ref: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
text: Bijab bi nan ŋmaa sur u n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, le nan ye Kasena, ni Setar, ni Admata, ni Tasis, ni Meres, ni Masena ni Memukann; Pesia ni Media aaninkpiib bilole bi joo tininkpir ti nyuun nnaan ngbaan ni na le na.

ref: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
text: U nan bui bi ke, “Min Ubɔrkpaan Sekes tun maanaagbiib Ubɔrpii Fasti chee ke u dan, le u yii maamɔb. Nkaal mɔk ke ti ŋa u kinye?”

ref: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
text: Le Memukann bui ubɔr ni waaninkpiib ke: “Ubɔrpii Fasti aa sii ubɔr baanja la, u sii waaninkpiib mu la; mbamɔn, u sii uja umɔk bi nnaan mue taab na la.

ref: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
text: Upii umɔk bi nnaan mue ni na yaa ŋun tibɔr tee kan, u ga piin ki li lik seeni uchal la. Bi ga bui ke, ‘Ubɔrkpaan Sekes tun yin Ubɔrpii Fasti, le u yii kaa buen u chee.’

ref: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
text: Tɔ, Pesia ni Media aanaan ni aaninkpiib aapuutiib yaa ŋun tibɔr timina kan, bi ga piin ki bi tuk bichatiib, nwiin aa kee lir. Bipiib mɔmɔk aan ki li pak bichatiib, le nimina ga cha bichatiib aaŋuul fii bipuutiib pu.

ref: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
text: Mpɔɔndaan, ni yaa ga piir aasui kan, cha ni nyan aamɔb ni ke Fasti taa ki cha aanimbil kan u. Cha bi ŋmee kina ŋa Pesia ni Media aakaal ponn ni, aan ubaa taa ki kpeln ni. Tɔ, aa di Ubɔrpii aajal mu ki di tii upii u ŋeer li na.

ref: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
text: Aa yaa cha bi moon tibɔr tee ni kookoo nnaan sakpiin mue ni kan, upii mɔmɔk ga lik pak uchal, kaan bui ke u ye ugiin bee upɔɔl.”

ref: King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said,
text: Ubɔrkpaan ngbaan ni waaninkpiib nan kii nsurm ngbaan; le ubɔrkpaan ngbaan nan ŋa Memukann aah nan len pu na.

ref: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
text: U nan tun ŋipepel nkub ni moninko ni ŋilole ngbaan ni, lipepel mɔk ni laaliin, ni laaŋmeen ni, ki len ke uja mɔmɔk li ye waadichal ni aayidaan, aan waah len pu na ŋa kina.

ref: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
text: Nee aapuwɔb, ubɔr aaŋuul aah sɔŋ na, u nan beenin dak Fasti aah ŋa u pu na, ni u mu aah siin nkaal mu u pu na.

ref: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
text: Kina pu na, ubɔr aasusurb bi nan ŋɔk u pu sakpen na nan len ke, “Ba ŋa saa cha ti buen ki ti ban upii u ŋan kaa nyi uja na?

ref: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
text: Aa ga ŋmaa ban bininkpiib saanaan aapepel mɔmɔk ni, ki cha bi li joo ni bisapɔm bi ŋan na saapiichiln ni, Susa litiyil ni do. Di bi ŋa Hegai, bijab bi bi kpaa bi na ponn ni ubaa, u lik saapiib na aaŋaal ni, ki cha bi toor bi ki tii bi kinyaan,

ref: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
text: le aa nan nin nyan bi ponn ni usapɔɔn u aa gee u sakpen na ki di u kaan Fasti aajal pu.” Ubɔr nan dakl ke nsurm ngbaan ŋan, le ki dii mu.

ref: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
