text: Susa ponn ni, Juu aanii ubaa nan bi, bi yin u ke Modekai aan ute ye Jair; u nan nyan ni Benjaminn aamaal ponn ni, le ki ye Simei u nan ye Kis aajapɔɔn na aayaabil.

ref: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
text: U nan bi Ubɔrkpaan Nebukadnesar aah nan chur Juda Aabɔrkpaan Jehoyachinn ni waanib bi nyan Jerusalem, ki di buen Babiloŋ ni tinaagbiir na ponn ni.

ref: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
text: U nan kpa weesal ubaa, bi yin u ke Esta, le ki yin u ke Hadasa Hiibru yaab aaliin ni; u nan ye usapɔɔn u ŋan na la, ki kpa tiwon ti ye kinyaan aawon na. Ute ni una aah kpo na, le Modekai kpiin u ki di u ŋa ubisal.

ref: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
text: Ubɔrkpaan aah nan moon ki ban bisapɔm bi ŋan na ke bi li joo ni bi Susa ni na, Esta nan ye bi ponn ni ubaa. Bi nan di u mu di ŋa libɔrchiln ni, Hegai u lik lipiichiln na aaŋaal ni.

ref: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
text: Hegai nan gee Esta, le waanyaan nan chuu Hegai. Kina pu na, u nan piin waanyaan aabimbin aatuln mala, le ki tii u tijikaar ti ŋan na. U nan tii u kidiik ki ŋan jer ti mɔmɔk na lipiichiln ngbaan ni, ki tii u bisapɔm bi bi nyan ni bi libɔrchiln ni na ponn ni bilole, ke bi li tun tii u.

ref: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
text: Modekai aasurm pu na, Esta aa nan cha ubaa bee ke u ye Juu aanii la.

ref: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
text: Iwiin mɔmɔk Modekai nan chuun kpak lipiichiln ngbaan aabisamɔb, ke u lik Esta aah bi pu na, ni tiwan ni ga ŋa u na.

ref: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
text: Kinyaan aabimbin aajoom ngbaan nan yunn ki ti saa libiln libaa la; bi nan joo mir aakpan ŋmir bisapɔm ngbaan ki ti saa iŋmal iloob, le ki di nkpan mu nu mɔ na mu ki ŋmir bi ki ti saa iŋmal iloob. Nee aapuwɔb, le bi ga di usapɔɔn ubaabaa di koon Ubɔrkpaan Sekes chee.

ref: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
text: Waah ga nya lipiichiln ni pu ki buen libɔrchiln ni na, u ga ŋmaa peen waah gee tiwanpeenkaan ni na.

ref: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
text: Usapɔɔn ngbaan ga buen nima kijook la, le kitaak yaa woln kan, bi nyan u buen lipiichiln liken ni, u ti li bi Sasgas, u ye uja u bi kpaa u aan u lik ubɔr aapuutiib na aaŋaal ni. Uma aan ki buen ubɔr chee see ubɔr gee u sakpen aan ki tun yin u waayimbil aah ye pu na ke u dan u chee.

ref: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
text: Ubɔrkpaan nan gee u ki jer bisapɔm biken na mɔmɔk; le u nan kan ubɔr chee ngeehm ki jer biken na. U nan di kibɔryikpupuk chiŋ u ki ŋa u ubɔrpii, Fasti aajal pu.

ref: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
text: Le ubɔr nan ŋa njim sakpem ke u nyuŋ Esta, le ki yin waaninkpiib mɔmɔk. U nan tii waanaan mɔmɔk aanib nwiin mubaa ke ubaa taa tun lituln, le ki tii ipiin pam. Modekai aah gaa ubɔr aamɔfal lii pu na

ref: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
text: N‑yoonn mue na, Modekai nan ye ubɔr aanaan ni aaninkpel ubaa la.

ref: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
text: Esta aa nan kee kpiir tuk ubaa ke u ye Juu aanii la. Modekai nan bui u ke u taa bui ubaa, le u kii waamɔb tibɔr tee pu, ke waah nan laa ye upiibo ki bi u chee ki keei waamɔb pu na.

ref: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
text: Buyoonn Modekai nan bi waatuln ni, libɔrchiln ni na, Bigtana ni Teres, bijab bi bi kpaa bi na ponn ni bilee, bi nan kii Ubɔr Sekes aadir aabisamɔi na, nan gee liŋuul ubɔr pu, ki kpokl ke bi ku u.

ref: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
text: Modekai nan ŋun tibɔr ngbaan le ki bui Ubɔrpii Esta, le u mu tuk ubɔr, ki mu bui u ke Modekai le kpiir ti tuk u.

ref: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
text: Bi nan fiir lik, ki kan ke tibɔr ngbaan nan gbii, kina pu na, bi nan leen bijab bilee ngbaan iŋmin ki ku bi. Ubɔr nan cha bi ŋmee tibɔr ngbaan mɔmɔk ŋa waanaan aagbann ponn ni.

ref: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
text: Tiwan nee mɔmɔk aah ŋa ki jer na, le Ubɔrkpaan Sekes nan tii uja u bi yin u ke Hamann na tininkpir ti paa ubɔr pu na. Hamann aate le nan ye Hamedata, le uyaaja ye Agag.

ref: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
text: Waaninkpir ngbaan pu, ubɔr ngbaan nan siin nkaal ke waaninkpiib bimɔk tun waatuln na li gbaani ki pak u. Bi mɔmɔk nan ŋani kina, see Modekai baanja le nan yii, kaa ŋani kina.

ref: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
text: Ubɔr aaninkpiib bi gur na nan baa u ke ba ŋa u yii ubɔr aamɔb;

ref: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
text: ki nan pɔɔni bibaa iwiin mɔmɔk ke u li gbaani ki pak Hamann, le u yii kaan ŋun tii bi. U nan bui bi ke, “M ye Juu aanii la, kaan ŋmaa gbaan ki pak Hamann.” Kina pu na, bi nan bui Hamann tibɔr ngbaan ke bi lik Hamann aah ga ŋa Modekai aabimbin ngbaan pu na.

ref: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
text: Hamann aah bee ke Modekai aan gbaan ki pak u na, liŋuul nan chuu u pam;

ref: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
text: waah nan ki bee ke Modekai ye Juu aanii na, u nan ŋa nlandak ke waan daa Modekai baanja aatafal; u nan ŋa nlandak ke u ku Juu aanib bi mɔmɔk bi Pesia aanaan ni na.

ref: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
text: Njan aaŋmal, u bi yin u ke Nisann na ni, Ubɔrkpaan Sekes aabin kipiik ni ŋilee waanaan ni, le Hamann nan cha bi too inaan, bi yin inaan ngbaan ke “Purim”, aan u bee nwiin ni uŋmal u ni u ga ku Juu yaab na. Ŋmapiik ni ilee, bi yin u ke Adar na aawiin kipiik ni itaa daal le nan ti jin.

ref: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
text: Le Hamann nan bui ubɔr ke, “Linibol libaa bi ki yaa ki bi saanaan aapepel mɔmɔk ponn ni. Baah joo ikaal i na ni biken aakaal aa kpaa. Ki ki kpee na, baa kii saanaan aakaal; kina pu na, saan li gee ke kina aanib li bi.

ref: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
text: Le ubɔr chuu ŋmaar waabɔmbik ki bi joo nyiir tigbann pu ke ni ye ubɔr aaseeraa na, ki di tii Juu yaab aadin Hamann u ye Hamedata aajapɔɔn, ki mu ye Agag aayaabil na.

ref: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
text: Le ubɔr bui u ke, “Binib ngbaan ni baamombil ye siyaan la; ŋa bi saah gee pu na.”

text: Unibɔn le joo tibɔbir ubaa pu ke mmii aah pool pu na.

ref: Job, if I were you, I would ask God for help.
text: M yaa ba ye sin kan, m ba ga fenn toŋ Uwumbɔr le ki di maabɔr tuk u.

ref: His miracles are marvelous, more than we can count.
text: Taan ŋmaa bee waah ŋani tiwankpaan ni na aatataa, le waajinjiir aawan aa kpa ndoon.

ref: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
text: U cha utaal nu kitiŋ pu le ki tii ikpaakon nnyun.

ref: He protects the sorrowful and lifts up those who have been disgraced. *
text: Mbamɔn, Uwumbɔr le fiini unii u sunn ubaa taab na paacham le ki tii unii u wii ikpowiil na mpopiin.

ref: Darkness is their only companion, hiding their path at noon.
text: hali nwinkapiin pu kan, bi chuun baani mbɔmbɔɔn ni la.

ref: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
text: Le Uwumbɔr nyani ugiin nkun ni, le ki gaal baah muk binib bi aan bi ban nterm na lir.

ref: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
text: U tii bigiim limakl, le ki ŋmini bibiindam chii.

ref: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
text: Uwumbɔr poo ibuun i u tii na; uma aaŋaal le tii si titotonn, le ki ki tii si laafee.

ref: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
text: N‑yoonn n‑yoonn pam le u ga nyan si titotonn ni.

ref: In times of war and famine, God will keep you safe.
text: Likpasiil yaa fuu ni kan, uma le ga tii si limɔfal, le ki kiir si aan butɔb aakun taa ku si.

ref: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
text: Uwumbɔr ga nyan si liyimbibiil ni; le ki ga tii si ŋŋmarm libiil yoonn.

ref: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
text: Aa ga li laa tijar ni nkon le kaan san tipeewanbir ijawaan.

ref: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
text: Saakpaakon i aa ko na aan li kpa ŋitakpal; tipeewanbir aan tak si kpala.

ref: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
text: Saabim ga li wiir ke timoor aah wiir kinaakpaamook ni pu na la.

ref: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
text: Aa ga por ke njikaabim mu biir ki kiir lijikaacheel na la.

ref: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
text: Job, ti di n‑yoonn pam le bae nimina. Ni ye mbamɔn la, kina pu na, gaa ti.

ref: It's impossible to weigh my misery and grief!
text: Bi yaa ba ga ŋmaa ŋaŋ maabɔr ni maapombiin kan,

ref: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
text: ni ba li nyuun jer litambol li bi nnyusakpem aagbaan na, kina pu na, taa cha maabɔfam ŋa si iwaan.

ref: The fearsome arrows of God All-Powerful have filled my soul with their poison.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan di ipiin too chaar mi, le yaaluul yaa koo nwon ni. Uwumbɔr lol waajawaan aawan kiir mi.

ref: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
text: Ubon yaa bi ŋmɔ timoor kan, u kpa mpopiin, le unaa yaa bi ŋmɔ timocheekaan kan, u ŋmin.

ref: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
text: Tɔ, ŋma ga ŋmaa ji tijikaar ti kaa kpa n‑yaan ni mmɔɔn kpala na? Ba aamɔɔn bi nkojekpan mu ye mupipim na ni?

ref: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
text: Kina aajikaar aa kpa mi kikpeek, le tijikaar timɔk m ji na tii mi iween.

ref: How I wish that God would answer my prayer
text: Ba ŋa Uwumbɔr aan tii mi maah mee tiwan ni na? Ba ŋa waan gar maameel?

ref: I am not strong as stone or bronze,
text: Bi di litakpal le naan mi ii? Maawon ye tikumann la aa?

ref: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
text: Maa ki kpa mpɔɔn ki ga di gaa mbaa lii; Maan ŋmaa fenn toŋ nibaa chee ki kan ŋŋmarm.

ref: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
text: Tibɔbir kina aaboln ni kan, m ban jɔtiibamɔm la, M yaa yii Uwumbɔr, bee maa yii u kan, m ban jɔtiibamɔm la.

ref: like streams that swell with melting snow,
text: Ikpen aanyun kpalni ŋitaanal la,

ref: then suddenly disappear in the summer heat.
text: le ntoton yaa fuu ni kan, ŋi wɔŋ, le mbufan foor ki dɔ nkuun.

ref: I am like a caravan, lost in the desert while searching for water.
text: Le biwankoob bi chuun ban nnyun na ti wɔŋ, bi chuun yiini le ki kpo nteersakpiin ni.

ref: Caravans from Tema and Sheba
text: Seba ni Tema aawankoob lik ban nnyun,

ref: thought they would find water. But they were disappointed,
text: le baamakl ti bee fam nkpenkuun chee.

ref: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
text: Ni bi ke nkpen ngbaan na le ki tii mi, ni kan maadoon, le ijawaan pu ni sur nipuwɔb.

ref: Have I ever asked any of you to give me a gift
text: Maa bui nimi ke ni tii mi ipiin ibaa, kaa bui ke ni tii ubaa igaŋgaŋlik m pu,

ref: or to purchase my freedom from brutal enemies?
text: kaa bui nimi ke ni gaa mi udin, bee limukl libaa chee lii.

ref: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
text: Tɔ, mɔk mi, bui mi maataani aah ye pu na. M ga li ŋmin ki pel aa chee.

ref: The truth is always painful, but your arguments prove nothing.
text: Tibɔbamɔnn kpa ŋuntii, le aa ma ka tool.

ref: Here I am desperate, and you consider my words as worthless as wind.
text: Aa dak ke m ka pii libuln baanja la, maa len tibaa; kina kan, ba ŋa aa gar maasuubiin aamɔbon?

ref: Why, you would sell an orphan or your own neighbor!
text: Aa too inaan unaagbiikpobo pu, le ki di aajɔnyaan kan liwankpal.

ref: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
text: Lik mi mbamɔm. Maan gii si nnyamɔn.

ref: Stop accusing me falsely; my reputation is at stake.
text: Aa buen ti chaar jer a. Taa ki tun beebee aatuln. Taa ki bii mi. M kpa mbamɔn.

ref: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
text: Le aa ma dak ke m gii la, aa dak ke maan ŋmaa gann ibamɔn ki cha inyamɔn la.

ref: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
text: ki naahn unaagbiija aah neen mboon mu soon na pu na; ki naahn ututunn aah kii waapar pu na.

ref: God has made my days drag on and my nights miserable.
text: Uŋmal jer le uŋmal paan ni, le maa kpa limakl libaa; tinyer mɔmɔk joo ni mi mpombiin la.

ref: I pray for night to end, but it stretches out while I toss and turn.
text: M yaa doon ke m geen kan, n‑yoonn ngbaan aa cha kpala; m dɔ binni kinyeek mɔk le ki neen kitaak aawoln.

ref: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
text: Ŋikpaambil le gbii nwon ni, nwon ye ŋibukak ŋmeen la; tinar puu nya maabuun ni la.

ref: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
text: Maawiin jer le kaa joo ni limakl, i san mala jer ke ukpaluul aakokonjal na.

ref: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
text: Uwumbɔr, teer ke maamɔfal ye kifuurk kibaa la; maapopiin doo ni yunn a.

ref: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
text: Aa waa mi din, le kaan ki kan mi kpala. Aa yaa ban mi kan, mui m buen a.

ref: And so, I cry out to you in agony and distress.
text: Maan li ka ŋmin; mmɔb ponn ni choŋ, le liŋuul joo mi. M ga len la.

ref: Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you imprison me?
text: Ba ŋa aa ka kii mi? Aa dak ke m ye nnyusakpem ni aawanbiik la aa?

ref: Leave me alone and let me die; my life has no meaning.
text: M di cha a; m bak limɔfal lee ni a. Di cha mi. Maamɔfal aa kpa tinyoor tibaa.

ref: What makes you so concerned about us humans?
text: Ba ŋa unibɔn aabɔr muk aa chee kina? Ba ŋa aa gar waah tun pu na?

ref: Why do you test us from sunrise to sunset?
text: Aa lik waabimbin kichakpiik mɔk ni, le ki tɔŋni u ki lik n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: Won't you look away just long enough for me to swallow?
text: Saan fenn lik nibaa wɔb siib aan m ŋmaa nab timɔɔtan aa?

ref: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
text: Sin kiyondiik aaninkpel, maatunwanbir tii si titotonn la aa? Ba ŋa aa too mi ipiin? M ye litusakpeln le tii si ii?

ref: Does God All-Powerful stand in the way of justice?
text: Uwumbɔr aa fenni ibamɔn; u tun ni ŋan na n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: He made your children pay for their sins.
text: Nibaakan, saabim tun Uwumbɔr taani la, le u daa bitafal ŋeer baah tun pu na.

ref: So why don't you turn to him
text: Tɔ, fenn ki gaŋ Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan;

ref: and start living right? Then he will decide to rescue and restore you to your place of honor.
text: le aa yaa si chob kaa kpa tijɔŋ tibaa kan, Uwumbɔr ga dan ki nan ter si ki giin saadichal siin saabimbinyaan ngbaan pu.

ref: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
text: Saawangol limɔk wɔŋ na aa ye nibaa. Uwumbɔr aah ga tii si li n‑yoonn ngbaan na ga jer lima ngbaan pel pel.

ref: Our ancestors were wise, so learn from them.
text: Lik n‑yaajayoonn na aalan siib na; dakl lik titetiib aah nan bae ibamɔn i na.

ref: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
text: Timi aamɔfal aa fɔk, le taa nyi nibaa kpala; ti chuun jer kitiŋ pu ke tijunjunn na la.

ref: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
text: Nnyun yaa foor kan, tima le puen yɔl, le ki laa par ke bi chee ti ki di tun lituln.

ref: Such is the hopeless future of all who turn from God
text: Binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na bi kina la; bi yaa suln Uwumbɔr bɔr kan, baamakl doo le na.

ref: and trust in something as frail as a spider's web—
text: Bi joo naadii tii nkokongaal la; bi tii nandala aakokonn naadii la.

ref: Sinful people are like plants with spreading roots and plenty of sun and water.
text: Titunwanbirdam bunni ke timoor aah bunni nwindam ni pu na la, bi bunni ke timoor aah bunni kisaak ni pu na la.

ref: They wrap their roots tightly around rocks.
text: Taanyaan fen joo ŋitakpal, le ki bub joo litakpal mɔk kin kin.

ref: But once they are pulled up, they have no more place;
text: Tɔ, chuu daa ŋɔb ti, le ubaa aan ki bee ke ti ba si nima.

ref: their life slips away, and other plants grow there.
text: Mbamɔn, titunwanbir aamɔɔn kookoo le bi na; bibaa le ga dan ki nan gaa baabuu ni.

ref: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
text: Le Uwumbɔr aan siir cha unii u tun ni ŋan na ma, kaan tii titunwanbirdam mu nterm.

ref: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
text: U ga ki cha aa laa ki teen mpɔɔn pu,

ref: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
text: le ki tee ga cha binib bi nan si na ji inimɔɔn, le bibiindam aadichal ga wɔŋ.

ref: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
text: Mbamɔn, m puun ŋun kina aabɔr a. Tɔ, unibɔn ga ŋa kinye aan ki ji tibɔr ki lii Uwumbɔr?

ref: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
text: Ŋma ga ŋmaa kpak u? U ga ŋmaa baa mbaan kina ki ti saa lichur, le ubaa aan ŋmaa giin u kpala.

ref: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
text: Uwumbɔr aalan ni waapɔɔn nyaŋ a, unii ubaa aa bi ki ga ŋman u.

ref: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
text: U cha ŋijoo foor ŋaabuu ni kaa nyi ke ŋi foor, le waaŋuul ponn ni kan, u kuln ŋi.

ref: God can shake the earth loose from its foundations
text: Uwumbɔr cha kitiŋ puul le ki jii; u damni jaatɔlk mam bi joo kitiŋ na.

ref: or command the sun and stars to hold back their light.
text: U ga ŋmaa chuu nwiin ke mu taa ki puu, ki ga ŋmaa chuu iŋmabi ke i taa li wiin kinyeek.

ref: and set the stars in place— the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the stars in the southern sky.
text: Uwumbɔr di iŋmabi i bi yin i ke Ipeel Kpaan, ni Orionn, ni Pleyades, ni i bi ŋŋangii wɔb na leen kitaapaak.

ref: Of all the miracles God works, we cannot understand a one.
text: Taan ŋmaa bee waah ŋani tiwankpaan ni na aatataa, le waajinjiir aatun aa kpa ndoon.

ref: God walks right past me, without making a sound.
text: Uwumbɔr jer m chee, le maa waa u.

ref: And if he grabs something, who can stop him or raise a question?
text: U yoor tiwan ni u ban na la, le ubaa aa ŋmaa chuu u; ubaa aan kaa ki baa u ke, “Aa ŋani ba?”

ref: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
text: Uwumbɔr chur waaŋuul, u kuln waadim bi nan ter nnyusakpem ni aapeewanbiik Rahab ke ki kpak u na.

ref: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
text: Kina pu na, m ga ŋa kinye aan ki kan ŋimɔbon ki di gar u?

ref: And if God came into court when I called him, he would not hear my case.
text: Hali u yaa tii mi nsan ke m len kan, maa dak ke u ga pel m chee.

ref: He would strike me with a storm and increase my injuries for no reason at all.
text: U cha kitaabuŋ daar yoor mi le ki ki tii mi titotonn, le maa nyi maa tun taani u na.

ref: Before I could get my breath, my miseries would multiply.
text: Waa tii mi lifuur; le ki cha maamɔfal ye mi mpombiin ŋmeen.

ref: God is much stronger than I am, and who would call me into court to give me justice?
text: M di linimaln mɔk Uwumbɔr aa? M di u buen bibɔjirb chee ee? Ubaa ga ŋmaa cha u buen aa?

ref: When a good person dies a sudden death, God sits back and laughs.
text: Unii u kaa kpa taani na yaa kpaan lir ki kpo kan, Uwumbɔr laa la.

ref: And who else but God blindfolds the judges, then lets the wicked take over the earth? My Life Is Speeding By
text: Uwumbɔr di dulnyaa wee tii bibiindam la. U cha bibɔjirb mɔmɔk jɔb. Uwumbɔr yaa kaa ŋa kina kan, ŋma ŋa?

ref: My life is speeding by, without a hope of happiness.
text: Maawiin san jer la, le i ponn ni mubaa kina aa ŋan.

ref: Each day passes swifter than a sailing ship or an eagle swooping down.
text: Maamɔfal jer mala ke buŋɔb bu ŋmaa chuun sakpen na la, ki naahn likaagiil aah booni pu ke li ti chuu sandee na la.

ref: but my sufferings frighten me, because I know that God still considers me guilty.
text: M yaa laa limɔmumukl ke m suln maaween bɔr kan, le maafalaa mɔmɔk gir ban ni mi; m nyi ke Uwumbɔr bui ke maabɔr bii a.

ref: So what's the use of trying to prove my innocence?
text: Maabɔr aah bii na, ntafal ki bi bayaar ni?

ref: Even if I washed myself with the strongest soap,
text: Bukiib bubaa aan ŋmaa finn nyan maatunwanbir.

ref: God would throw me into a pit of stinking slime, leaving me disgusting to my clothes.
text: Uwumbɔr di mi mee lii tijɔŋ aatambuuk ni la, le maawanpeenkaan gur san mi maah kpa inimɔɔn pu na.

ref: Can someone snatch away the stick God carries to frighten me?
text: Uwumbɔr, taa ki dar ntafal. Taa ki cha saajawaan sakpiin ngbaan choo m chee.

ref: Then I could speak up without fear of him, but for now, I cannot speak.
text: Maa san ijawaan, maah nyi nsui ponn ni aabɔr na, m ga len.

ref: Don't just condemn me! Point out my sin.
text: Uwumbɔr, taa bui ke maabɔr bii. Bui mi maabɔr aah bii pu na.

ref: Do you look at things the way we humans do?
text: Aa lik tiwan ke taah lik ni pu na la aa?

ref: Is your life as short as ours?
text: Saamɔfal mu aa fɔk ke timi yaan na la aa?

ref: Is that why you are so quick to find fault with me?
text: Kina kan, ba ŋa aa chur maatunwanbir mɔmɔk bilni, ki tee mban ki ban maataani u mɔmɔk m kpa na?

ref: You know I am innocent, but who can defend me against you?
text: Aa nyi ke maabɔr ŋan; aa nyi ke ubaa aan ŋmaa gaa mi aa chee lii.

ref: Remember that you molded me like a piece of clay. So don't turn me back into dust once again.
text: Teer ke tiyakr le aa nan di naan mi; aa ban ke aa ki gbaa wɔi mi ŋa titan la aa?

ref: As cheese is made from milk, you created my body from a tiny drop.
text: Sin le tii nte mpɔɔn le u di kan mi, sin le cha m biir nna aaponn ni.

ref: Then you tied my bones together with muscles and covered them with flesh and skin.
text: Sin le naan nwon le ti kpa ikpab ni ŋigir, le ki di tinann ni ngban biin ikpab ngbaan pu.

ref: You, the source of my life, showered me with kindness and watched over me. You Have Not Explained
text: Aa tii mi limɔfal ni ngeehm mu kaa kpa ndoon na, le saah joo mi pu na cha m fu.

ref: You have not explained all of your mysteries,
text: Le m bee dandana ke aa looni ki ban ke aa ku mi la.

ref: No matter how hard I try, you keep hunting me down like a powerful lion.
text: hali m yaa kan tinyoor kan, see aa taa taa chuu mi ke uchinn na; le ki kpaan tun lijinjiir aatun ke aa di tii mi titotonn.

ref: You never stop accusing me; you become furious and attack over and over again.
text: Aa kpa m pu biseeraadam n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la; le saah kpa liŋuul li m pu na moo kpae cha; n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, aa kpokl m pu isapɔɔn la.

ref: Why did you let me be born? I would rather have died before birth
text: Uwumbɔr, ba ŋa aa cha bi ma mi? M yaa ba nan kpo ubaa aa kee kan mi kan, ni ba ŋan.

ref: I have only a few days left. Why don't you leave me alone? Let me find some relief, *
text: Di cha mi suuna. Maamɔfal aa kuln le na aa? Cha m ji mmɔɔn n‑yoonn mu gur siib na ni.

ref: of darkness and despair, the place of no return.
text: kitiŋ ki ye mbɔmbɔɔn, ni tijunjunn, ni nlanŋmal na ni, nima chee aawiihn mubaa ye mbɔmbɔɔn la.

ref: Your words have silenced others and made them ashamed; now it is only right for you to be put to shame.
text: Job, aa dak ke taan ŋmaa gar si la aa? Aa dak ke saasiibiil ŋee ga cha ti li gur ka ŋmin la aa?

ref: You claim to be innocent and argue that your beliefs are acceptable to God.
text: Aa bui ke saah len pu na ye mbamɔn la; aa bui ke aa ŋan Uwumbɔr chee la.

ref: But I wish God would speak
text: Uwumbɔr yaa ba ga gar si kan, m ba gee kina sakpen.

ref: and let you know that wisdom has many different sides. You would then discover that God has punished you less than you deserve.
text: U ba ga bui si ke nlan aabɔŋ aabɔŋ wiir pam; ke tiwan pam bi aan unibɔn aalan aan ŋmaa bee ni. Uwumbɔr aa daa aatafal ki ŋeer saah tun pu na.

ref: Can you understand the mysteries surrounding God All-Powerful?
text: Aa ga ŋmaa mɔk Uwumbɔr aapɔɔnsakpiin aanaanmɔk aa?

ref: They are higher than the heavens and deeper than the grave. So what can you do when you know so little,
text: Kitaapaak aa ye Uwumbɔr aanaanmɔk, le ki daa aa chee pam. Uwumbɔr nyi bitekpiib do, le aa ma aa nyi nima.

ref: and these mysteries outreach the earth and the ocean?
text: Uwumbɔr aapɔɔnsakpiin pee jer kitiŋ, ki waa jer nnyusakpem.

ref: If God puts you in prison or drags you to court, what can you do?
text: Uwumbɔr yaa chuu si ki di si buen libɔjil kan, ŋma bi ki ga ŋmaa nyii u pu?

ref: God has the wisdom to know when someone is worthless and sinful,
text: Uwumbɔr nyi binib bi kaa bi tibaa ni na; u waa baatunwanbir mɔmɔk.

ref: but it's easier to tame a wild donkey than to make a fool wise. Surrender Your Heart to God
text: Buyoonn timoor ni aabon ti ma aan ubo ngbaan aa bir na, le bilatiirb mu ga kan nlan.

ref: Surrender your heart to God, turn to him in prayer,
text: Job, cha aapobil li si chob. Li ban Uwumbɔr.

ref: and give up your sins— even those you do in secret.
text: Nyan titunwanbir, ni taani saachiln ni,

ref: Then you won't be ashamed; you will be confident and fearless.
text: ki ki di ntaakpab pɔɔn, ni linimaln tii dulnyaa,

ref: Your troubles will go away like water beneath a bridge,
text: le saamuk mɔmɔk ga nya aayil ni, ke nwam mu jer aan bi suln mubɔr na.

ref: You will rest safe and secure, filled with hope and emptied of worry.
text: Aa ga li bi ŋŋmarm ni, ki li kpa limakl; Uwumbɔr ga li kii si, ki tii si lifuur.

ref: You will sleep without fear and be greatly respected.
text: Saan li san saadim; binib pam le ga dan nan ban nterm aa chee.

ref: But those who are evil will go blind and lose their way. Their only escape is death!
text: Le bibiindam ma ga lik ban ni ntaakpayɔl, ki kan ke ŋŋmarm aa bi. Baamakl libaa li bi na le ye ke nkun ga dan.

ref: You think you are so great, with all the answers.
text: Mbamɔn, nimi le ye binib mɔmɔk aaneel. Ni yaa kpo kan, nlan mu kpoi diir nimi la.

ref: But I know as much as you do, and so does everyone else.
text: Le naah kpa nlan sakpen pu na, m mu kpa kina; naa soor mi nibaa chee, unii mɔmɔk nyi naah len pu na.

ref: I have always lived right, and God answered my prayers; now friends make fun of me.
text: Njɔtiib bibaa gur laa mi la; maa kpa taani, le maabimbin ŋan, le bi laa mi. Uwumbɔr nan tee kii maameel n‑yoonn mubaa.

ref: It's easy to condemn those who are suffering, when you have no troubles.
text: Nimi aa kpa ŋimuk, le ki tee ŋani mi mbɔnyun; unii ban u lir la, le ni ki faa u.

ref: Robbers and other godless people live safely at home and say, “God is in our hands!” If You Want To Learn
text: Tɔ, binaayukb ni binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na bi nsuudoon ni, bi bui ke Uwumbɔr bi biŋaal ni.

ref: If you want to learn, then go and ask the wild animals and the birds,
text: Inyoon ni ipeel kpa tiwan sakpen i di mɔk nimi,

ref: Any of them can tell you what the Lord has done.
text: Tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk nyi ke Uwumbɔr aaŋaal le naan ni.

ref: Every living creature is in the hands of God.
text: Uwumbɔr le joo waawanaankaan aamɔfal; unibɔn mɔk aamɔfal bi uma le aapɔɔn ni.

ref: We hear with our ears, taste with our tongues,
text: Tɔ, nilambil aah neen tijikaar aalakm pu na, kina le nitafal mu neen tibɔr aaŋum.

ref: No one can rebuild what he destroys, or release those he has imprisoned.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa gbaa ber bil kan, ŋma ga ŋmaa maa, ŋma ga ŋmaa nyan unii u Uwumbɔr chuu u piin na lii?

ref: God can hold back the rain or send a flood,
text: Uwumbɔr yaa chuu utaal kan, le ntaaweel bi; le u yaa chur nnyun lii ni kan, nwam nya.

ref: God shames counselors, turns judges into fools,
text: U nyani bitinjoob aalan, le ki cha bisalolm tun kijɔrk aatun.

ref: God removes priests and others who have great power—
text: u sunni bitotoorb, ni binib bi bi mpɔɔn ni na taab.

ref: puts mighty kings to shame, and takes away their power.
text: U jinni binib bi bi mpɔɔn ni na inimɔɔn, le ki cha bitinjoob aapɔɔn door.

ref: he makes nations strong, then shatters their strength.
text: U tii ŋitimbol mpɔɔn sakpiin, le ki nan tee nyaŋ ki kuln ŋi.

ref: God strikes their rulers senseless, then leaves them to roam through barren deserts,
text: U cha ŋaasalolm ŋani bijɔrb, le ki cha bilan ŋmalni bi, le bi chuun yiini ki ti wɔŋ;

ref: lost in the dark, staggering like someone drunk.
text: bi chuun baani mbɔmbɔɔn ni, le ki tuul ke bidagbiib na.

ref: None of you are smarter than I am; there's nothing you know that I don't.
text: Naah len pu na mɔmɔk, m puun ŋun kina. M beer ti mɔmɔk aatataa; naah nyi pu na, m mu nyi kina la. Maa ye nimi aamaasoor.

ref: But I prefer to argue my case with God All-Powerful—
text: Tɔ, m ni Uwumbɔr le kpa tibɔr, naa ye nimi; m ban m ni uma le kpak tɔb.

ref: you are merely useless doctors, who treat me with lies.
text: Ni joo inyamɔn le biini nimi aamaanyi pu; ni naahn biteteeb bi kaan ŋmaa cha unii ubaa pɔɔk na la.

ref: The wisest thing you can do is to keep quiet
text: Taa ki len tibaa man, ki cha ubaa dakl ke ni kpa nlan la.

ref: and listen to my argument.
text: Li pel ki cha m ŋeer maabɔr man.

ref: and not telling the whole truth when you argue his case?
text: Ni pɔɔni nibaa ke ni kpee u pu la aa? Nimi le ga ji waabɔr bibɔjirb chee tii u uu?

ref: If he took you to court, could you fool him, just as you fool others?
text: Uwumbɔr yaa lik nimi suuna kan, u ga kan tiwanyaan nibaa ni chee ee? Ni dak ke ni ga ŋmaa ŋmann Uwumbɔr ke naah ŋmanni binib pu na la aa?

ref: If you were secretly unfair, he would correct you,
text: Hali nimi aalandak aah bɔr pu na, u ga sak nimi mbamɔm,

ref: and his glorious splendor would make you terrified.
text: le waapɔɔn ga cha ijawaan sakpiin chuu nimi.

ref: Your wisdom and arguments will blow away like dust. Be Quiet While I Speak
text: Nimi aayataŋak bi fam ke nfatan na la; le nimi aanikpakpak wur lir ke tiyakr na.

ref: Be quiet while I speak, and we'll see what happens.
text: Ŋmin suuna man, ki tii mi nsan aan m len, ki cha tiwan ni ga ŋa na ŋa.

ref: I will be responsible for what happens to me.
text: M kii ke m di maamɔfal paan talmaa.

ref: God may kill me, but still I will trust him and offer my defense.
text: M ki kpa limakl libaa, Uwumbɔr yaa ba ga ku mi kan, ni ba ga li ŋan. M ban m ŋeer maabɔr tuk u la.

ref: This may be what saves me, because no guilty person would come to his court.
text: Nibaakan, maayigbei ga gaa mi lii, ba pu? ubiindaan ubaa aan kaa ki sil Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: Listen carefully to my words!
text: Tɔ, li pel maabɔr aah ye pu na man.

ref: I have prepared my case well, and I am certain to win.
text: M gor ke m ŋeer maabɔr, ba pu? m nyi ke m kpa mbamɔn.

ref: If you can prove me guilty, I will give up and die. Job Prays I Ask Only Two Things
text: Uwumbɔr, aa choo aa nan galn mi la aa? Aa yaa ba ŋa kina kan, ni ŋeer ke m ŋmin ki kpo.

ref: I ask only two things of you, my God, and I will no longer hide from you—
text: Cha m mee tiwan nilee; kii tii mi, aan m taa bɔr si;

ref: Then speak, and I will reply; or else let me speak, and you reply.
text: Uwumbɔr, puen len waahr aan m gar si. Aa yaa ti ki gee kan, aa cha m puen len aan aa gar mi.

ref: Please point out my sins, so I will know them.
text: Maatunwanbir ye ba? M tun ba aataani? Ba aabiil aan aa di bui ke maabɔr bii?

ref: Why have you turned your back and count me your enemy?
text: Ba ŋa aa minn mi? Ba ŋa aa ŋani mi ke maah ye saadin le na?

ref: Why do you accuse me of horrible crimes and make me pay for sins I did in my youth?
text: Aa joo tibɔr ti wu mponn ni na le galni mi, hali maah nan laa ye ubo pu na aatun le aa joo galni mi.

ref: You have tied my feet down and keep me surrounded;
text: Aa di tikululn le baa ntaa; aa lik maah yoor litaal limɔk na, le ki lik ki nyi maataabuu.

ref: We are flowers that fade and shadows that vanish.
text: Ti muuni le ki gbaar mala ke nsupuun na; ti wɔŋni ke tijunjunn na la.

ref: And so, I ask you, God, why pick on me?
text: Uwumbɔr, aa fenn lik mi le ki di mi buen libɔjil ni ke aa ti ji mi tibɔr aa?

ref: There's no way a human can be completely pure.
text: Tiwanyaan nibaa aan ŋmaa nyan ni unibɔn, tijɔŋdaan ni.

ref: Our time on earth is brief; the number of our days is already decided by you.
text: Waamɔfal aafɔfɔk puun ŋaŋ dɔ ni daa, aa nyi iŋmal imɔk u ga li bi limɔfal ni na. Aa ŋaŋ ni siin, le ubaa aan ŋmaa kpeln ni.

ref: Why don't you leave us alone and let us find some happiness while we toil and labor? When a Tree Is Chopped Down
text: Taa ki lik u chee, ki di cha u suuna; u yaa ga ŋman kan, cha u ji waamɔfapɔɔl ngbaan.

ref: When a tree is chopped down, there is always the hope that it will sprout again.
text: Busub bu bi gaa gii bu na beenin kpa limakl; bu ga ki ŋmaa bunn.

ref: Its roots and stump may rot,
text: Nibaakan, bu aasubon ga por, le bu aasukpiil mu kuur sunn taab,

ref: but at the touch of water, it sprouts once again.
text: nnyun yaa bi kan, bu ga ki bunn ke busub bu laa pɔɔn na.

ref: Humans are different— we die, and that's the end.
text: Le unibɔn ma kpo kan, waadoon le na; u kee kpo kan, u ki bi la?

ref: We are like streams and lakes after the water has gone;
text: Ŋimɔɔ aah geei kaan ki puu, aan tibɔr aanyun mu kuur pu na,

ref: we fall into the sleep of death, never to rise again, until the sky disappears.
text: kina le binib mu kpoi, kaan ki fii kpala. N‑yoonn mumɔk kitaapaak ga li bi na, baan ki finn daalbaadaal; baan ki finn baageen pu kpala.

ref: Please hide me, God, deep in the ground— and when you are angry no more, remember to rescue me. Will We Humans Live Again?
text: M ba ga li gee ke aa di mi bɔr bitekpiib do la; cha m li bɔr aan saaŋuul ti sɔŋ waahr, aan ki nin siin n‑yoonn mu aa ga teer mbɔr na.

ref: My Creator, you would want me; you would call out, and I would answer.
text: Le aa yin mi, le m kii, le aasui ga piir min saawanaankaan pu.

ref: You would take care of me, but not count my sins—
text: Le aa ga li lik litaal limɔk m ga yoor na, kaan li chur maatunwanbir ma bilni.

ref: you would put them in a bag, tie it tight, and toss them away.
text: Aa ga di cha pinn mi ki suln tibɔr; aa ga ber taani umɔk m tun na.

ref: But in the real world, mountains tumble, and rocks crumble;
text: N‑yoonn bi, le ŋijoo lir, le ŋijoomɔju ŋi pɔɔ kib na foor ŋaabuu ni.

ref: streams wear away stones and wash away soil. And you destroy our hopes!
text: Nnyun ga ŋmaa cha ŋitakpal donn, le utaal sakpiin ga puu titan buen; kina le aa kuln unibɔn aamakl kookoo.

ref: You change the way we look, then send us away, wiped out forever.
text: Aa nyaŋni unibɔn, le ki jenni u lir kookoo; nkun ni, le unimbil wɔb paa paa igban.

ref: We never live to know if our children are praised or disgraced.
text: Ujapɔtiib kani bunyuŋ, le waa nyi; le ubaa mu aan tuk u buyoonn bi ji inimɔɔn na.

ref: We feel no pain but our own, and when we mourn, it's only for ourselves.
text: Ubaa aawon aaween, ni ubaa aasuubiin baanja pu le u nyi.

ref: Job, if you had any sense,
text: Job, bɔfam, bɔfam.

ref: Your words are enough to make others turn from God and lead them to doubt.
text: Aa yaa ba kpa aabaa aapɔɔn kan, unii ubaa aa ba ga san Uwumbɔr, ubaa aa ba ga li dooni u.

ref: And your sinful, scheming mind is the source of all you say.
text: Saabɔlen le mɔk saah kpa mbiin pu na; aa joo nlan aabɔlen le pɔɔni aabaa ke aa di saabiin bɔr.

ref: I am not here as your judge; your own words are witnesses against you.
text: Maan ki li ka ke m galn si saah len tibɔr timɔk na le galn si.

ref: Were you the first human? Are you older than the hills?
text: Aa dak ke sin le bi nan puen ma aa? Uwumbɔr aah nan naan ŋijoo na, aa nan bi ii?

ref: Have you ever been present when God's council meets? Do you alone have wisdom?
text: Aa nan jer ki ŋun ilandak i Uwumbɔr ŋa na aa? Sin baanja le bi di unibɔn mɔmɔk aalan tii ii?

ref: Do you know and understand something we don't?
text: Tiwan nibaa aa bi aa nyi ni aan tima aa nyi.

ref: And you have been offered comforting words from God. Isn't this enough?
text: Uwumbɔr tii si mmɔɔn; ba ŋa aa beenin yiil mu? Ti di mbɔdiim le len tii u suuna,

ref: Your emotions are out of control, making you look fierce;
text: le aasui fii, le aa lik timi ke saah ban aa nab timi le na.

ref: that's why you attack God with everything you say.
text: Aa gee Uwumbɔr pu liŋuul, le ki bui ke waa ki ye nibaa.

ref: and neither are angels— not in the sight of God. If God doesn't trust his angels,
text: Hali Uwumbɔr aa tii waatuuntiib naadii; bima bibaa aa ŋan u chee ki ti doo.

ref: what chance do humans have? We are so terribly evil that we thirst for sin. Just Listen to What I Know
text: Le unibɔn nyu titunwanbir ke naah ye nnyun le na; mbamɔn, unibɔn bii doo; unibɔn ye fam la.

ref: Just listen to what I know, and you will learn
text: Job, li pel maah nyi pu na.

ref: Those who gained such insights also gained the land, and they were not influenced by foreign teachings.
text: Biwɔwɔm aa nan bi baatiŋ ni; unii u ga nan ŋmann bi aan bi nya Uwumbɔr chee na aa nan bi.

ref: But suffering is in store each day for those who sin.
text: Ubiindaan u muk biken na, ga li bi iween ni le waamɔfal mɔmɔk ni.

ref: Even in times of success, they constantly hear the threat of doom.
text: U ga li ŋun ijawaan aaneel tar utafal ni, le buyoonn u dak ke u fuur na, le binaayukb nan lir u pu.

ref: They scrounge around for food, all the while dreading the approaching darkness.
text: le nangba mam ka kii waawon. U nyi ke waataak ki ga woln na bɔɔn la;

ref: They are overcome with despair, like frightened soldiers facing a fearsome king in battle.
text: tibɔbir ti bi ke ubɔrpɔɔndaan ubaa na dɔ kiir u ke ti tak u la.

ref: This is because they rebelled against God All-Powerful
text: Unii u fik kiŋanbik mɔk ki sii Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan na aadoon le na.

ref: They won't escape the darkness, and the blazing breath of God will set their future aflame. *
text: le waan ŋmaa san ŋmar mbɔmbɔɔn chee. U ga li naahn busub bu aabon wun mmii, aan libuln daa bu aapuun buen na la.

ref: They have put their trust in something worthless; now they will become worthless
text: U yaa jɔr sakpen le ki di naadii tii titunwanbir kan, titunwanbir le ga li ye waapar.

ref: Or like vineyards or orchards whose blossoms and unripe fruit drop to the ground.
text: U ga li naahn ŋisubil aasub bu aasubikar ker lir na la; ki naahn olif aakpan aasub bu aapuun gbaar na.

ref: Yes, the godless and the greedy will have nothing but flames feasting on their homes,
text: Binib bi kaa nyi Uwumbɔr na aan li kpa yaabitiib, le mmii ga wun baah di igaŋgaŋlik maa ŋidichal ŋi na.

ref: because they are the parents of trouble and vicious lies.
text: Kina aanib le kpokl tibɔbir ki tun titunwanbir na; bisui gbii ŋŋmann le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: I have often heard this, and it offers no comfort.
text: M puun ŋun naah len pu na mɔmɔk a; naah sɔŋni nsui pu na ye mi iween la.

ref: So why don't you keep quiet? What's bothering you?
text: Ni ga li len kina kaan ŋmin la aa? Nimi le yeh kookoo aamɔbon aa?

ref: But I would offer hope and comfort instead.
text: M ba ga di nsurm pɔɔk nitaakpab, ki li len sɔŋni nisui.

ref: If I speak, or if I don't, I hurt all the same. My torment continues.
text: Tɔ, maah len pu na ye fam la, le m yaa ka ŋmin mu kan, maaween aa sɔŋni.

ref: God has worn me down and destroyed my family;
text: Uwumbɔr, aa doo mi a; aa cha bi ku maadichal aanib.

ref: God is my hateful enemy, glaring at me and attacking with his sharp teeth.
text: Uwumbɔr aaŋuul ni, le u dar par mi iŋaal ni ŋitaa; u joo kinanaŋ le lik mi.

ref: Everyone is against me; they sneer and slap my face.
text: Binib lik mi mbɔnyun aanimbilikl la; bi lol goln mi le ki yur mi ntapam.

ref: Everything was going well, until God grabbed my neck and shook me to pieces. God set me up as the target
text: M nan bi nsuudoon ni la, le Uwumbɔr nan chib chuu nneen ni, ki di mi yur yur ki kool mi. Uwumbɔr di unimbil kaan mi le pu,

ref: for his arrows, and without showing mercy, he slashed my stomach open, spilling out my insides.
text: ki too mi ipiin i saa chaar mi ki tii mi titotonn ŋipepel mɔmɔk na, le kaa kpaan san mi kinimbaak.

ref: and so, in my sorrow I dress in sackcloth and sit in the dust.
text: M wii ikpowiil ki pee tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na, le ki ka titan ni, kaa ki bi tibaa ni.

ref: My face is red with tears, and dark shadows circle my eyes,
text: M wii le nnimbil wɔb ti mann chaun, nnimbil duun tigbingbinn,

ref: though I am not violent, and my prayers are sincere.
text: m mu aa kpa titunwanbir tibaa aagalm, maameel li chaa Uwumbɔr chee na aa kpa tijɔŋ.

ref: If I should die, I beg the earth not to cover my cry for justice.
text: Kitiŋ, taa di baah tun mi taani pu na bɔr. Taa cha maah yin ki ban mbamɔn pu na ŋmin fam.

ref: Even now, God in heaven is both my witness and my protector.
text: Ubaa bi paacham, ki ga ŋmaa sil nchaŋ ni, ki len tii mi.

ref: My friends have rejected me, but God is the one I beg
text: Njɔtiib laa mi la; le nnimbil bar tinyunyunn tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: to show that I am right, just as a friend should.
text: M ban ke ubaa gaŋ Uwumbɔr tii mi ke unii aah gaŋni ujɔ pu pu na la.

ref: Because in only a few years, I will be dead and gone.
text: Maabin jer cha la, le m chuun nsan mu kaa kpa ngirm na pu.

ref: My hopes have died, my time is up, and the grave is ready.
text: Maamɔfal aadoon peen ni a. Maa ki ŋmaa fuur; likaakul baanja le gur ye maamakl.

ref: All I can see are angry crowds, making fun of me.
text: M ka mpombiin ni, le ki lik binib aah ŋani mi yansara pu na.

ref: If you, Lord, don't help, who will pay the price for my release?
text: Uwumbɔr, m len ibamɔn la. Gaa maamɔboln. Ubaa aa ki bi ki ga sil maah len pu na pu.

ref: My friends won't really listen, all because of you, and so you must be the one to prove them wrong.
text: Aa cha bi ŋa bilatiirb la; taa ki cha bi nyaŋ mi n‑yoonn mue.

ref: They have condemned me, just to benefit themselves; now blind their children.
text: Liyataŋakpokl na ni, unii kooh ujɔtiib ŋimombil pu, le waabim nan ji naafalaa.

ref: You, God, are the reason I am insulted and spit on.
text: Binib gur joo kina aayataŋakl ŋakl mi; bi choo le ki nan tei timɔɔtan ŋani nnimbil wɔb.

ref: I am almost blind with grief; my body is a mere shadow.
text: Maasuugar ti kpaan jɔb mi la; le ŋŋaal ni ntaa gur naahn tijunjunn.

ref: People who are truly good would feel so alarmed, that they would become angry with my worthless friends.
text: Ni ŋa binib bi bui ke bi si chob na lijinjiir la; le bi mɔmɔk bii mi ke maa nyi Uwumbɔr.

ref: They would do the right thing and because they did, they would grow stronger.
text: Binib bi bui ke bi ye kipak aanib na moo kani ntaakpab pɔɔn ke bima le kpa mbamɔn.

ref: My life is drawing to an end; hope has disappeared.
text: Maawiin jer a; le maalandak bee fam; maamakl doo a.

ref: I could tell the world below to prepare me a bed.
text: Kitekpiitiŋ le gur ye maamakl, nima chee le m ga doon ki geen mbɔmbɔɔn ni.

ref: Then I could greet the grave as my father and say to the worms, “Hello, mother and sisters!”
text: M ga yin likaakul ke nte la; le ki yin ŋikpaambil ŋi ŋmɔ mi na ke nna ni nninkpatiib.

ref: But what kind of hope is that?
text: La chee aan maamakl ki bi? Ŋma waa libaa?

ref: Will it keep me company in the world of the dead?
text: M yaa sunn buen kitekpiitiŋ ni kan, limakl aan dii mi buen nima.

ref: Or do you think that we are dumb animals?
text: Ni ye ba cha aa dak ke ti jɔr ke inaa na?

ref: You cut yourself in anger. Will that shake the earth or even move the rocks? *
text: Aa ki joo saaŋuul tii aabaa le titotonn. Saaŋuul ga ŋmaa cha kitiŋ kpaln nkuun aa? Uwumbɔr ga foor ŋijoo ke ni mɔɔr si ii?

ref: The lamps of sinful people soon are snuffed out,
text: Ubiindaan aamii ga sil junn la; mu aamiigaal aan ki gaa daalbaadaal.

ref: Their powerful legs become weak, and they stumble on schemes of their own doing. *
text: U nan si chob la, le dandana ma u chuun gbeer; uma ubaa aasurm pu le u ga lir.

ref: they are trapped in a net,
text: gaawɔb le chuu utaagbeln ki chɔb joo u kin kin.

ref: then afterwards to be eaten alive by death itself.
text: Kiweenwanbiik le yaa gaa uwon mɔmɔk ni, le ki cha uŋaal ni utaa bur.

ref: Those sinners are dragged from the safety of their tents to die a gruesome death.
text: Bi daa nyan u waadichal li ponn ni u nan bi ŋŋmarm ni na, le ki dar u cha ke u ni Ubɔr Nkun ti kan tɔb.

ref: and they are left like trees, dried up from the roots.
text: Waasubon ni ŋipan yɔl ki kuur a.

ref: without any children to carry on their name.
text: Waa kpa yaabitiib, waa kpa ubaa u ŋmar.

ref: Such is the fate of sinners and their families who don't know God.
text: Bibiindam aadoon le na. Binib bi kaa di Uwumbɔr yin nibaa na aadoon le na.

ref: How long will you torture me with your words?
text: Ba ŋa ni joo tibɔr tii mi iween?

ref: Isn't ten times enough for you to accuse me? Aren't you ashamed?
text: Ni seei mi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, le kaa san inimɔɔn naah seei mi pu na pu.

ref: Even if I have sinned, you haven't been harmed.
text: Hali m yaa galn le kan, kina ngbaan ŋa nimi ba?

ref: You boast of your goodness, claiming I am suffering because I am guilty.
text: Ni dak ke ni soor mi la, le ki len ke maabɔbir le ye maagalm aaseeraa.

ref: But God is the one at fault for finding fault with me.
text: Naa waa ke Uwumbɔr le ŋa nimina aa? Uma le pen gaawɔb ke u chuu mi.

ref: Though I pray to be rescued from this torment, no whisper of justice answers me.
text: Maa kii waatunbir ngbaan pu, le ubaa mu aa pel; ubaa aa ŋun maabamɔn aawiil pu.

ref: God has me trapped with a wall of darkness
text: Uwumbɔr le laŋ nsan, le maa ŋmaa jer; u di maasan bɔr mbɔmbɔɔn ni la.

ref: and attacks with fierce anger, as though I were his enemy.
text: Uwumbɔr aaŋuul fii, le u bil ban mi; u ŋani mi ke waadinkpaan na la.

ref: His entire army advances, then surrounds my tent. I Am Forgotten *
text: U cha waajab nan tak mi; bi gbii ŋibuu gob maadichal.

ref: and I am forgotten.
text: Ndoyaab ni njɔtiib mɔmɔk buen a.

ref: My breath disgusts my wife; everyone in my family turns away.
text: Mpuu aa ki ŋman maafuurk aanunun, le nnaabitiib bibaa aa ki ŋɔŋni m chee.

ref: Young children can't stand me, and when I come near, they make fun.
text: Mbim lik seeni mi, le ki yaa kan mi kan, bi laa.

ref: My best friends and loved ones have turned from me.
text: Njɔtiibamɔm gur nan mi la; maah nan gee binib bi sakpen na le fenn lir m pu.

ref: I am skin and bones— just barely alive.
text: Maagban gur lee maakpab pu la; m ŋmar siib kina la.

ref: My friends, I beg you for pity! God has made me his target.
text: Ni ye njɔtiib la. San mi kinimbaak man. Uwumbɔr aaŋaal le faa mi bil.

ref: Hasn't he already done enough? Why do you join the attack?
text: Ba ŋa ni muk mi ke Uwumbɔr aah ŋani pu na? Naah muk mi pu na aa ŋeer aa?

ref: I wish that my words could be written down
text: M ba neen ke ubaa ga ŋmaa teer maabɔr ki ŋmee ti ŋa kigbaŋ ni;

ref: I know that my Protector lives, and at the end he will stand on this earth.
text: Le m tee nyi ke ubaa bi paacham ki nan len maabɔr tii mi.

ref: My flesh may be destroyed, yet from this body I will see God.
text: Hali iween aah di maawon ŋman doo aan m beenin bi na, m ga kan Uwumbɔr.

ref: Yes, I will see him for myself, and I long for that moment.
text: Nnimbil ga kan u gbin gbin, le waan li ye uwɔwɔnja m chee.

ref: My friends, you think up ways to blame and torment me, saying I brought it on myself.
text: Naah bui ke, “Ti ga ŋa kinye ki saan u?” na, le ntaakpab yɔl. Ni ban libɔkpiln le ke ni di tak mi.

ref: Your words are disturbing; now I must speak.
text: Job, aa bii nsui. Tɔ, nsui fii ke m gar si.

ref: You have accused and insulted me, and reason requires a reply.
text: Saah len pu na ye lisiibil la, m mu nyi maah ga giin si pu na.

ref: Since the time of creation, everyone has known
text: Aa nyi gbin gbin ke n‑yaayoonn mu unibɔn nan puen kal kitiŋ pu na,

ref: that sinful people are happy for only a while.
text: ubiindaan ubaa aa nan kani mpopiin ki cha dik dik.

ref: Though their pride and power may reach to the sky,
text: Nibaakan, u ga li ye unikpaan, ki kpa liyimbil sakpen, nibaakan li ga ti tuu ntaalangbam,

ref: they will disappear like dust, and those who knew them will wonder what happened.
text: le libuln ga daa u buen ke titan na. Binib bi nan nyi u na ga li gur baa ke u tee buen la chee?

ref: and vanish from the sight of family and friends.
text: Ubaa aan ki kan u waah nan koo nin chee na;

ref: Their children will have to repay what the parents took from the poor.
text: le waah nan sun tiwan ni bigiim chee na ga kpaln ujapɔtiib aapɔln.

ref: Indeed, the wicked will die and go to their graves in the prime of life. Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
text: Uwon nan ye tinachipɔwon le ki pɔɔ nyaa, le ti ga guun kpaln titan.

ref: But their food will turn sour and poison their stomachs.
text: Le tijikaar ngbaan ti tee toŋ uponn ni ki to ke liluul mɔmɔk aah to pu na.

ref: Then God will make them lose the wealth they gobbled up.
text: Ubiindaan wulni liwangol li u nan sun li na la; Uwumbɔr nyani li uponn ni, le ki gaa li.

ref: and never enjoy rivers flowing with milk and honey.
text: Waan li bi ki kan buyoonn n‑yaan ni nkpan ga nan li wiir ke limɔɔl aanyun na.

ref: because they cheated the poor and took their homes.
text: ba pu? u nan muk bigiim kaa yin bi nibaa, ki gaa ŋidichal ŋi bibaa maa ŋi na.

ref: Greedy people want everything and are never satisfied.
text: Waakumɔŋ ti nyaŋ sakpen a.

ref: But when nothing remains for them to grab, they will be nothing.
text: Waa ji ki gur nibaa lisambil ni, le waawankam doo dandana.

ref: Once they have everything, distress and despair will strike them down,
text: Waakam aah ga nyaŋ buyoonn na, le falaa u bir na ga wɔb u bil.

ref: and God will make them swallow his blazing anger.
text: Cha u ji waah ban pu na mɔmɔk. Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln ni le u ga daa utafal.

ref: While running from iron spears, they will be killed by arrows of bronze,
text: U yaa ban u san ŋmar tikur aajuk chee kan, tikumann aatɔm le ga too chaar u bil.

ref: whose shining tips go straight through their bodies. They will be trapped by terror,
text: Mpiin le saa chaar uwon na; le waasin tuu mu aapinbim pu lir, le ijawaan sakpiin chib chuu upobil.

ref: and what they treasure most will be lost in the dark. God will send flames to destroy them in their tents with all their property.
text: Waah kuun tiwan nimɔk bil na kuln a; mmii mu unibɔn aaŋaal aa tuur mu na le ga wu waadichal.

ref: The heavens and the earth will testify against them,
text: Paacham le kpiir kina aanii aatunwanbir pu, le kitiŋ ji seeraa ke ti gbii.

ref: and all their possessions will be dragged off when God becomes angry.
text: Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln li naahn nwam na le ga kuln waawangol mɔmɔk.

ref: This is what God has decided for those who are evil.
text: Ubiindaan aadoon le na, Uwumbɔr aah di ndoon mu siin u na le na.

ref: If you want to offer comfort, then listen to me.
text: Li pel maah len pu na; maah ban mpopiin mu na le bi na.

ref: And when I have finished, you can start your insults all over again.
text: Tii mi nsan aan m len man, m yaa ti doo aan ni yaa gee kan, ni laa mi.

ref: My complaint is against God; that's why I am impatient.
text: M ni unibɔn u ga kpo na aa kpa kijaak; m kpa nsan ke maasuklaa doo.

ref: Just looking at me is enough to make you sick,
text: Lik mi man. Nimina aa ŋeer ke ni cha ni li si lik ki ŋmin chii ii?

ref: and the very thought of myself fills me with disgust.
text: M yaa dakl tiwan ni ŋa mi na pu kan, nlan mɔk ŋmal la, le nwon gbaa le m jii.

ref: Why do evil people live so long and gain such power?
text: Ba ŋa Uwumbɔr cha titunwanbirdam kpa limɔfal, ki cha bi por ki kani nkam?

ref: Why are they allowed to see their children grow up?
text: Bi kpa mbim ni yaabitiib, le ki bi ki ti kan bi mɔmɔk aah chikr pu na.

ref: They have no worries at home, and God never punishes them.
text: Uwumbɔr aa cha bi kani tibɔbir baadichal ni; le baa nyi ijawaan sakpiin ibaa.

ref: Their cattle have lots of calves without ever losing one;
text: Mbamɔn, baawakor mɔmɔk pɔr le ki maa kaa kani falaa ubaa.

ref: their children play and dance safely by themselves.
text: Baabim san gbiir ke ipihbi na,

ref: These people sing and celebrate to the sound of tambourines, small harps, and flutes,
text: le ki saar dii tibar ni kulufeeŋ mam.

ref: and they are successful, without a worry, until the day they die. Leave Us Alone!
text: Bi bi nsuudoon ni le baamɔfal mɔmɔk ni, le ki nan kpo suuna, kaa jin falaa ubaa.

ref: Those who are evil say to God All-Powerful, “Leave us alone! Don't bother us with your teachings.
text: Bibiindam bui Uwumbɔr le ke u cha bi suuna; baa ban ke bi bee waah ban bi tun pu na.

ref: We succeeded all on our own.” And so, I keep away from them and their evil schemes.
text: Bi dak ke bibaa aapɔɔn pu le bi kpa, le m ma aan kii tii baalandak ngbaan.

ref: How often does God become angry and send disaster and darkness to punish sinners?
text: Ubiindaan aamii kee junn aa? Bi ponn ni ubaa kee kan tibɔbir aa? Uwumbɔr kee daa bibiindam aatafal waaŋuul ni

ref: How often does he strike them like a windstorm that scatters straw?
text: ki daa bi buen ke kimook bee kitaabuŋ aah daar titan cha pu na aa?

ref: You say, “God will punish those sinners' children in place of those sinners.” But I say, “Let him punish those sinners themselves until they really feel it.
text: Ni bui ke Uwumbɔr dar ubo aatafal ute aatunwanbir pu la. M ma bui ke, cha Uwumbɔr daa titunwanbirdam aatafal; cha u mɔk ke baatunwanbir pu le u ŋa kina.

ref: Let God All-Powerful force them to drink their own destruction from the cup of his anger.
text: Cha titunwanbirdam kan bibaa aatafadaan; Cha bi kan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aaŋuusakpeln.

ref: Because after they are dead, they won't care what happens to their children.” Who Can Tell God What To Do?
text: Unii aamɔfal yaa ti doo kan, u ki dak waabim aapopiin pu uu?

ref: Who can tell God what to do? He judges powerful rulers. *
text: Unibɔn ga ŋmaa mɔk Uwumbɔr u ji binikpaam tibɔr na aa?

ref: while others die in poverty, having known only pain.
text: Biken ma aa kpa mpopiin kpala; bi bi le ki ti di mpombiin kpo.

ref: But we all end up dead, beneath a blanket of worms.
text: Le bi mɔmɔk mu tee kpoi le bi sui bi; le ŋikpaambil pɔl bi mɔmɔk pu.

ref: My friends, I know that you are plotting against me.
text: M nyi tilandakwanbir ti ni kpa na.

ref: You ask, “Where is the home of that important person who does so much evil?”
text: Ni baa le ke, “Ujakpaan u nan tun titunwanbir na aadichal ki bi la?”

ref: that those who do wrong never suffer disaster, when God becomes angry.
text: Bundaal aan Uwumbɔr aaŋuul fii aan u dar binib aatafal na, bibiindam le ŋmar n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: No one points out their sin or punishes them.
text: Ubaa aa bi ki ga galn ubiindaan, bee u teen u waah tun pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: Then at their funerals, they are highly praised;
text: Bi yaa nan tu u cha kicheek ni, nin chee bi si kii waakaakul mbamɔm na,

ref: But empty, meaningless words are the comfort you offer me.
text: Le nima pɔɔni nibaa ke ni di bɔfam sɔŋ nsui. Inyamɔn ŋmeen le ni joo giini mi.

ref: What use are we humans to God, even the wisest of us?
text: Unii ubaa bi, hali ulandaan bi ki kpa tinyoor Uwumbɔr chee ee?

ref: If you were completely sinless, that would still mean nothing to God All-Powerful.
text: Saatunyaan tii Uwumbɔr ba? bee saabimbinyaan tii u ba aaterm?

ref: No! It's because of your terrible and endless sins.
text: Naa ye kina, ni ye le ke aa tun titunwanbir sakpen.

ref: To guarantee payment of a debt, you have taken clothes from innocent people.
text: Ke aanaabo pa si waah joo si lipɔln li na, see aa gaa waawanpeenkaan ki cha u uŋmeen.

ref: And you refused bread and water to the hungry and thirsty,
text: Aa yii kaa tii binib bi bak na nnyun, kaa tii nkon aah joo bi na tijikaar.

ref: although you were rich, respected, and powerful.
text: Aa nan di saapɔɔn ni saasisii gaa kitiŋ mɔmɔk.

ref: You have turned away widows and have broken the arms of orphans.
text: Aa nan yii kaa ter bikpopiib le ki nan sun nkpobim aawan ki ŋa bi falaa.

ref: That's why you were suddenly trapped by terror,
text: Kina pu na, ŋibugen le mann gob si na, le ijawaan kpaan chuu si.

ref: blinded by darkness, and drowned in a flood. God Lives in the Heavens
text: Le ni bɔnn sakpen, le saa ki waa, le nwam biin aa pu kookoo.

ref: God lives in the heavens above the highest stars, where he sees everything.
text: Uwumbɔr bi paachapaacham le ki gbuuni lik iŋmabi i bi paacham na.

ref: Do you think the deep darkness hides you from God?
text: Le aa ki baa ke, “Uwumbɔr nyi ba? ke ntaalangbam duk u, u ga ŋa kinye ki ji binib tibɔr?”

ref: Do thick clouds cover his eyes, as he walks around heaven's dome high above the earth?
text: Aa dak ke waah chuun kitaapaak pu na, ntaalangbam mu gbii na duk u la.

ref: Give up those ancient ideas believed by sinners,
text: Aa sil ban ke aa dii isan i titunwanbirdam puen dii na la aa?

ref: who were swept away without warning.
text: Nwam nan di bi puu buen le baayoonn nin fuu.

ref: They rejected God All-Powerful, feeling he was helpless,
text: Binib bee le nan yii Uwumbɔr ki kpa lipobil ke waan ŋmaa ŋa bi nibaa.

ref: although he had been kind to their families. The beliefs of these sinners are truly disgusting.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr mu le nan tee cha bi ŋa biwankpadam, maan ŋmaa bee bibiindam aalandak.

ref: When God's people see the godless swept away, they celebrate,
text: Buyoonn Uwumbɔr daa bibiindam aatafal na, bininyaam kpa mpopiin, le maa‑kpa‑taani‑dam laa.

ref: saying, “Our enemies are gone, and fire has destroyed their possessions.” Surrender to God All-Powerful
text: Bibiindam aah kpa tiwan ni mɔmɔk na kuln a, le mmii wun tiwan ni mɔmɔk gur na.

ref: Listen to his teachings and take them to heart.
text: Gaa waamɔkm mu u tii na; li joo waamɔbon aasui ni.

ref: If you return to God and turn from sin, all will go well for you.
text: Mbamɔn, gbaan aataŋaayil pu ki gir Uwumbɔr chee, ki kuln titunwanbir ti mɔmɔk ŋa saadichal ni na.

ref: So get rid of your finest gold, as though it were sand.
text: Di saasalmaa mae; di saasalmaa u ŋan sakpen na ti mae mbufan ni.

ref: God will answer your prayers, and you will keep the promises you made to him.
text: Aa yaa mee u kan, u ga kii si, le aa ga li joo tipuur ti aa puu na.

ref: He will do whatever you ask, and life will be bright.
text: Le aa ga kan tinyoor saatuln mɔk ni, le nwiihn ga woln saasan ni.

ref: When others are disgraced, God will clear their names in answer to your prayers.
text: Uwumbɔr sunn bigaadam taab le ki gaal binib bi sunn bibaa taab na lir.

ref: Even those who are guilty will be forgiven, because you obey God.
text: Saabɔr yaa ŋan kan, u ga gaa si lii, Saah ŋani pu na yaa tok kan, u ga gaa si lii.

ref: Today I complain bitterly, because God has been cruel and made me suffer.
text: M beenin len Uwumbɔr kaa kii tii u; maan ki ŋmaa joo maawiil.

ref: Then I would discover what he wanted to say.
text: M ban m bee waah ga len pu na la, ki bee waah ga giin mi pu na.

ref: Would he overwhelm me with his greatness? No! He would listen
text: Uwumbɔr aan ŋmaa di waapɔɔn mɔmɔk ban mi. Waan ŋa kina, u ga pel maah len pu na.

ref: because I am innocent, and he would say, “I now set you free!”
text: Maa kpa beebee; m ni Uwumbɔr ga ŋmaa gbaa maabɔr; u ga bui ke m kpa mbamɔn ki nyan mi kookoo.

ref: I cannot find God anywhere— in front or back of me,
text: M ban Uwumbɔr liwipuul wɔb, kaa kan u; maah lik liwilir wɔb na, maa kan u nima chee mu.

ref: to my left or my right. God is always at work, though I never see him.
text: Uwumbɔr tun lituln ŋŋangan, ni ŋŋangii wɔb, le maa ki kan u nima chee mu.

ref: But he knows what I am doing, and when he tests me, I will be pure as gold. *
text: Le Uwumbɔr tee nyi maah yoor litaal limɔk na; u yaa tɔŋ mi kan, u ga kan ke maa kpa tijɔŋ tibaa.

ref: I have never refused to follow any of his commands,
text: M dii nsan mu u lee na mbamɔm, kaa yenn cha lipepel libaa.

ref: But he alone is God, and who can oppose him? God does as he pleases,
text: Waa kpelni. Ubaa aan ŋmaa kpak u, bee u nyii u pu ke u di cha waah ban u ŋa pu na.

ref: Merely the thought of God All-Powerful
text: m san u, le nwon gbaa unimbiin ni.

ref: Why doesn't God set a time for court? Why don't his people know where he can be found?
text: Ba ŋa Uwumbɔr aa siin libɔjil aawiin, ba ŋa waa siin binib bi dii u na aabamɔn aawiin?

ref: Sinners remove boundary markers and take care of sheep they have stolen.
text: Binib yoor upɔnja aatakpal foor ke bi moo kan kitiŋ; le ki su ipiih ti kpae baapiih pu.

ref: They cheat orphans and widows by taking their donkeys and oxen.
text: Bi gaal nkpobim aabon, le ki joo ukpopii aanaa ke see u ti pan waapɔln.

ref: in the desert, where they and their children must live like wild donkeys and search for food.
text: Kina pu na, bigiim chuun ban tijiir kipɔɔkuun ni ke timoor ni aabon na la; baan ki ŋmaa kan tijikaar nibaa chee ki tii baabim.

ref: If they want grain or grapes, they must go to the property of these sinners.
text: Ikpaakon i baa bun na ni, le bi ti chee, le ki ker ŋisubil bibiindam aasui aasar ni.

ref: They sleep naked in the cold, because they have no cover,
text: Bi doo kinyeek kaa kpa nibaa bi di biin bibaa pu, nibaa aa bi, bi di kiir bibaa tiwoor chee.

ref: and during a storm their only shelters are caves among the rocky cliffs.
text: Utaal u nu ŋijoo pu na le gbaa bi, le bi wuŋni ŋijootakpal taab.

ref: Children whose fathers have died are taken from their mothers as payment for a debt.
text: Mbipɔm bi kaa kpa tetiib na le titunwanbirdam chur ŋani baanaagbiib, le ki joo ugiin aabim pa waapɔln.

ref: Then they are forced to work naked in the grain fields because they have no clothes, and they go hungry.
text: See bigiim chuun tiwoor kaa kpa tiwanpeenkaan; bi yaa bi chee tijikaar kan, bi li chee ti nkon.

ref: They crush olives to make oil and grapes to make wine— but still they go thirsty.
text: Bima le gbaa olif aakpan ki ŋmaani ŋisubil ki nyani ŋaanyun, le nnyunyuu tee joo bi.

ref: And along the city streets, the wounded and dying cry out, yet God does nothing. Some Reject the Light
text: Ntim ponn ni le binib bi kan titotonn na, ni binib bi bi kpoi na wii, le Uwumbɔr aa gaal baameel.

ref: Soon after sunset they murder the poor and the needy, and at night they steal.
text: Lichakpitaawoln le unikur finn ki cha u ti ku bigiim, le kinyeek kan, u su.

ref: Others wait for the dark, thinking they won't be seen if they sleep with the wife or husband of someone else.
text: Uja u ye udagoor na ka kii liwimaln la; le u poo biin unimbil wɔb ke ubaa taa bee u.

ref: Robbers hide during the day, then break in after dark because they reject the light.
text: Kinyeek le binaayukb koo ŋidichal ni, le nwiin pu kan, bi bɔrni nwiihn.

ref: They prefer night to day, since the terrors of the night are their friends. Sinners Are Filthy Foam
text: Bi san nwiin pu aawiihn la, le mbɔmbɔɔn ma aa kpa bi ijawaan. Sofar aah len pu na

ref: Those sinners are filthy foam on the surface of the water. And so, their fields and vineyards will fall under a curse and won't produce.
text: Le Sofar bui ke, “Nwam le joo ubiindaan cha, le Uwumbɔr puun lii waatiŋ pu; ubaa aa ki tun lituln waasui aasar ni.

ref: Just as the heat of summer swallows the snow, the world of the dead swallows those who sin.
text: Ŋitaatakpal aah wɔŋni ntoton, ni ntaaweel ni pu na, kina le utunwanbirdaan wɔŋni bimɔfadam aatiŋ pu.

ref: Forgotten here on earth, and with their power broken, they taste sweet to worms.
text: Hali una aa ki teer ubɔr; ŋikpaambil le ŋman kuln u ke busub bu lir na.

ref: But God's mighty strength destroys those in power. Even if they seem successful, they are doomed to fail.
text: Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn ni le u kuln bipɔɔndam; Uwumbɔr tun, le ubiindaan kpo.

ref: God may let them feel secure, but they are never out of his sight.
text: Uwumbɔr ga ŋmaa tii u ŋŋmarm, le ki tee lik u n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: Great for a while; gone forever! Sinners are mowed down like weeds, then they wither and die.
text: Ubiindaan kani nkam ni yunni siib, le naan yunn le u yɔl ke kimook na, ki yɔl ke baah bar likalmaan li na.

ref: If I haven't spoken the truth, then prove me wrong.
text: Ubaa ga ŋmaa nee ke nimina aa ye kina aa? Ubaa ga ŋmaa kpak mi ke maabɔr aa gbii ii?”

ref: God is the one to fear, because God is in control and rules the heavens.
text: Uwumbɔr kpa mpɔɔn sakpen; unii mɔmɔk li san u; U joo waapaacham nsuudoon ni la.

ref: Who can count his army of stars? Isn't God the source of light?
text: Ŋma ga ŋmaa kahn waatuuntiib bi tun tii u na? La chee bi, aan Uwumbɔr aawiihn aa wiin nima?

ref: How can anyone be innocent in the sight of God?
text: Ŋma ye ki kpa mbimbinyaan ki bi chain Uwumbɔr chee?

ref: To him, not even the light of the moon and stars can ever be pure.
text: U chee kan, uŋmal ni iŋmabi aa wiin ki bi chain.

ref: So how can we humans, when we are merely worms?
text: Ŋmaninkabaa unibɔn, u ye tiwanfuurkaan na? Unibɔn aa ye nibaa Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: You have really been helpful to someone weak and weary.
text: Aa ye nterm nyaan le ki tii mi u ye ugiin u kaa kpa mpɔɔn na.

ref: You have given great advice and wonderful wisdom to someone truly in need.
text: Aa tii nsurm mu ŋan na le ki yakr saalan tii mi u ye ujɔr na.

ref: Remember the terrible trembling of those in the world of the dead below the mighty ocean.
text: Bitekpiib aawiin bi nnyun ni, kitiŋ aataab le ki jii.

ref: Nothing in that land of death and destruction is hidden from God,
text: Kitekpiitiŋ dɔ waa chain Uwumbɔr chee la; libiil libaa aa duŋ ki u chee.

ref: who hung the northern sky and suspended the earth on empty space.
text: Uwumbɔr le daa taln ŋŋangan wɔb aataapaak ki di kitiŋ laŋ, nibaa aa joo ki.

ref: God stores water in clouds, but they don't burst,
text: Uwumbɔr le cha nnyun gbiini ntaalangbam, ki cha mu aanyunyuun aa ŋmaa puu mu.

ref: and he wraps them around the face of the moon.
text: Uma le joo uŋmamɔn bɔrni ntaalangbam ni.

ref: On the surface of the ocean, God has drawn a boundary line between light and darkness.
text: U lol nkuul le gonn nnyusakpem paab le ki yakr nwiin ni mbɔmbɔɔn tɔb chee.

ref: By his power and wisdom, God conquered the force of the mighty ocean.
text: Waapɔɔn le u nan di nyaŋ nnyusakpem; U nan di waalan le ku nnyun ni aawanbiik Rahab.

ref: The heavens became bright when he breathed, and the escaping sea monster died at his hands.
text: Waafuurk le woln kitaapaak chain, le waaŋaal ku kiwanbiik ki nan san ki ŋmar na.

ref: These things are merely a whisper of God's power at work. How little we would understand if this whisper ever turned into thunder!
text: Waapɔɔn aabɔr siib le na, tibɔlɔikaan ti ti ŋun na le na. Ŋma ga ŋmaa bee mbamɔm Uwumbɔr aah pɔɔ sakpen pu na?

ref: I am desperate because God All-Powerful refuses to do what is right. As surely as God lives,
text: M puu Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki yii waan tii mi ibamɔn ki cha maamɔfal choŋ na,

ref: and while he gives me breath,
text: ke waah cha m bi limɔfal ni n‑yoonn mumɔk na,

ref: I will tell only the truth.
text: maamɔb aan len tibɔbir daalbaadaal, maalambil aan gii nnyamɔn daalbaadaal.

ref: Until the day I die, I will refuse to do wrong by saying you are right,
text: Maan kii daalbaadaal ke nimi bijab bee kpa mbamɔn; m ga li joo gbin gbin ke maa kpa taani le ki ti saa maakun daal.

ref: because each day my conscience agrees that I am innocent.
text: Maan di cha ki bui ke maabɔr bii daalbaadaal; m nyi ke maa kpa taani.

ref: I pray that my enemies will suffer no less than the wicked.
text: Cha binib bi mɔmɔk kpak mi ki jaa mi kijaak na kan bibiindam ni titunwanbirdam aatafadaan.

ref: Such people are hopeless, and God All-Powerful will cut them down,
text: Uwumbɔr yaa ti ban u gaa binib bi kaa nyi u na aamɔfal kan, ba aamakl aan bi ki kpa?

ref: without listening when they beg for mercy.
text: Uwumbɔr ga ŋun baawiil tibɔbir yoonn aa?

ref: And that is what God should do, because they don't like him or ever pray.
text: Ni ba ŋan ke bi li neen waah tii mpopiin mu na; bi ba ga li mee u n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: Now I will explain in detail what God All-Powerful does.
text: Cha m mɔk si Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn aah nyaŋ pu na, ki moo mɔk si Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aah siin pu na.

ref: All of you have seen these things for yourselves. So you have no excuse. How God Treats the Wicked
text: Aayii, maan mɔk si. Nimi nibaa kan kina; ba pu aan ni ki gbaa bɔfam ngbaan? Sofar aah len pu na

ref: Here is how God All-Powerful treats those who are wicked and brutal.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan dar bibiindam bi aabimbin pɔɔ na aatafal kina la.

ref: They may have many children, but most of them will go hungry or suffer a violent death.
text: Nibaakan bi ga li kpa japɔtiib pam, le bi mɔmɔk ga kpo butɔb ni. Baabim aa kani ki ji babr.

ref: Others will die of disease, and their widows won't be able to weep.
text: Le iween ga ku bi ŋmar na, le baakpopiib aan kpaan wii baakpuu.

ref: The wicked may collect riches and clothes in abundance as easily as clay.
text: Nibaakan bibiindam aan ti ki li nyi baamombil mɔk ki ga li kpa tiwanpeenkaan jer unii aah ban pu na;

ref: But God's people will wear clothes taken from them and divide up their riches.
text: tɔ, uninyaan ubaa le ga nan peen tiwanpeenkaan ngbaan, le ubamɔndaan ubaa nan gaa ŋimombil na.

ref: No homes built by the wicked will outlast a cocoon or a shack.
text: Bibiindam maa ŋidichal ke nandala aadiik na la, ki naahn unaagbiija aah kaa libool li ponn ni kii ikpaakon ni na.

ref: Those sinners may go to bed rich, but they will wake up poor.
text: N‑yoonn mubaa, bi ga li dɔ ki ye biwankpadam la, le ki nan finn kan, bi ga kan ke baawankpal na buen a.

ref: Terror will strike at night like a flood or a storm.
text: Ijawaan sakpiin ga dan mala ke nwam na la; le libuln ga nan daa bi kinyeek buen;

ref: Then a scorching wind will sweep them away
text: liwipuul wɔb aabuln le ga ŋar bi ŋŋaan nyan baadichal ni;

ref: At last, the wind will celebrate because they are gone.
text: Libuln ga li wii yur bi le bi san, le ki joo libiil aapɔɔn faani bi.

ref: the same is done with iron and copper.
text: Unibɔn gbii kitiŋ le nyani tikur, le ki donni nyani tikumann ŋitakpal ni.

ref: Miners carry lanterns deep into the darkness to search for these metals.
text: Unibɔn fikr koo mbɔmbɔɔn sakpiin ni. Bi koo kitiŋ taab taab ki lik, le ki gbii ban ŋitakpal mbɔmbɔɔn ni.

ref: Far beneath the grain fields, fires are built to break loose those rocks
text: Kitiŋ pu le tijikaar nyan, le kitiŋ baan ngbaan aataab ye tikar ki wɔi lir.

ref: that have jewels or gold.
text: Kitiŋ aatakpal kpa ŋitakpanyaan, le kaatan mu kpa salmaa.

ref: Miners go to places unseen by the eyes of hawks;
text: Ukaa ubaa aa kani nsan mu cha ŋitakpanyaan aabuu ni na, le nangba ubaa aa kee fii labr i pu.

ref: they walk on soil unknown to the proudest lions.
text: Uchinn, bee kipeewanbiik kibaa aa kee dii isakuun ngbaan.

ref: With their own hands they remove sharp rocks and uproot mountains.
text: Unibɔn gbii ŋitakpapɔɔl, le ki gbii doo ŋijoo aataab.

ref: They dig through the rocks in search of jewels and precious metals.
text: Baah lokr isan ŋitakpal ni na, le bi kani ŋitakpanyaan.

ref: They also uncover the sources of rivers and discover secret places. Where Is Wisdom Found?
text: Bi gbii ti nya ŋimɔɔyil, le ki nyani tiwan ni bɔr na mpaan pu.

ref: Nor can it be discovered in the deepest sea. *
text: Nnyusakpem aanyonyoon bui ke saan ŋmaa kan nlan nima.

ref: It is worth much more than silver or pure gold
text: Saan ŋmaa di tikunabr ni salmaa daa mu.

ref: Nothing is its equal— not gold or costly glass.
text: Bi ban mu jer salmaa, ki ban mu jer salmaa aasambil bee salmaa aayikuuk.

ref: Wisdom is worth much more than coral, jasper, or rubies.
text: Nlan ŋan jer nleenyaan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ.

ref: All the topaz of Ethiopia and the finest gold cannot compare with it.
text: Litakpanyaan li bi yin li ke topas na, ni salmaa nyaan aan ŋmaa sil nlan chee.

ref: It is hidden from human eyes and even from birds.
text: Tiwanfuurkaan nibaa aan ŋmaa kan mu, hali unyoon u laani na aa waa mu.

ref: Death and destruction have merely heard rumors about where it is found.
text: Hali nkun ni libiil len ke ni ŋun kakaan la.

ref: God is the only one who knows the way to wisdom;
text: Uwumbɔr baanja le nyi nsan ngbaan, uma le nyi nin chee aa ga ban kan nlan na,

ref: When God divided out the wind and the water,
text: N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr nan tii libuln laapɔɔn, ki siin nnyusakpem aawiwiir na;

ref: God told us, “Wisdom means that you respect me, the Lord, and turn from sin.”
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui unibɔn ke, “Aa ga li san Uwumbɔr le ki nin kan nlan. Aa ga fenn aapuwɔb tii titunwanbir le ki bee tiwan aatataa.”

ref: I long for the past, when God took care of me,
text: Maamɔfal yaa ba ki bi ke n‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr nan joo mi na kan.

ref: and the light from his lamp showed me the way through the dark.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bi m chee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk n‑yaayoonn ngbaan, le ki tii mi nwiihn m joo chuun libɔmbɔln ni.

ref: I was in the prime of life, God All-Powerful was my closest friend,
text: N‑yaayoonn ngbaan le m nan ye uwankpadaan na, le Uwumbɔr aajɔtiik nan lik maadichal pu.

ref: and all of my children were nearby.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan nan bi m chee n‑yaayoonn ngbaan, le maabim mɔmɔk mann goln mi.

ref: My herds gave enough milk to bathe my feet, and from my olive harvest flowed rivers of oil. *
text: Maanaa ni iŋoob nan kpa nnaabiin pam, le maakpasɔi aasui nan muuni ŋitakpal ŋmeen aatiŋ pu.

ref: When I sat down at the meeting of the city council,
text: N‑yoonn mumɔk kitiŋ aaninkpiib ti kuun na kan, m nan ka maabuul ni, bikaasisik ni.

ref: while the older ones stood
text: Binib aasalolm ŋmin;

ref: and remained silent. Everyone Was Pleased
text: hali binikpaam ŋmin chii.

ref: When poor people or orphans cried out for help, I came to their rescue.
text: Bigiim yaa nan wii kan, m ter bi la; m nan ter nkpobim bi kaa kpa unii u chee bi ga fenn buen na.

ref: And I was highly praised for my generosity to widows and others in poverty.
text: Binib bi nan bi falaa kpaan ni na nan pak mi la, le m ter bikpopiib le bi kan lifuur.

ref: Kindness and justice were my coat and hat;
text: M tun dii nsan le ki si chob.

ref: I was helpful to the blind and to the lame.
text: M nan ye ŋinimbil le ki tii bijoom, le ki ye ŋitaa ki tii binib bi wɔb na.

ref: I was a father to the needy, and I defended them in court, even if they were strangers.
text: M nan bi ke te na le ki tii bigiim, le ki si biwɔwɔm bi bi tibɔr ni na aapuwɔb.

ref: When criminals attacked, I broke their teeth and set their victims free.
text: M nan kuln bibiindam aapɔɔn le ki gaa baah muk binib bi na lii.

ref: I felt certain that I would live a long and happy life, then die in my own bed.
text: M nan mak n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke m li kpa limɔfafɔfɔŋ le ki nan kpo linampal, mpopiin ni.

ref: In those days I was strong like a tree with deep roots and with plenty of water,
text: M nan bi ke busub bu aasubon kani nnyun n‑yoonn mɔmɔk aan bu aapan soon limaln na.

ref: My words were eagerly accepted like the showers of spring,
text: unii mɔk nan gaa ti iŋaal ilee ke bikpaab aah gaal unaalantaal pu na.

ref: My advice was followed as though I were a king leading my troops, or someone comforting those in sorrow.
text: Min le nan lolni nsan ki siini ni ga ŋa na; m nan joo bi ke ubɔr aah joo waajab pu na la, le ki tii bi mpopiin baasuugar ni.

ref: Young people now insult me, although their fathers would have been a disgrace to my sheep dogs.
text: Le maah kpeln binachipɔm bi na ka ŋani mi yaansara dandana. Bitetiib aa nan bi tibaa ni n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, le maa nan kii ke bi ni maabɔ kpaan ki kpaa maapiih.

ref: They must claw the desert sand in the dark for something to satisfy their hunger.
text: Bi nan ye bigiim kaa kpa tijikaar, le ki nyii isubonkuun kinyeek, limokpalunn libaa ni.

ref: They gather tasteless shrubs for food and firewood,
text: Bi nan dar ŋɔi nteersakpiin ni aasufar ki ŋman ti, bi nan kpaan ŋman tichachabɔnn.

ref: and they are run out of towns, as though they were thieves.
text: Unii mɔk nan joo tijar le jenni bi ke baah tar binaayukb le pu na.

ref: Their only homes are ditches or holes between rocks,
text: Bi nan koo titakpalunn ni la, bi nan koo ibuu i bi gbii ŋijoo aamɔgben na ni la.

ref: And like senseless donkeys they are chased away. Those Worthless Nobodies
text: Maabitibaanidam bi kaa kpa ŋiyimbil na, bi nan jenn nyan bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu la.

ref: Those worthless nobodies make up jokes and songs to disgrace me.
text: Tɔ, dandana le bi choo nan laa mi; m gur ye yaansara aawan le bi chee.

ref: They are hateful and keep their distance, even while spitting in my direction.
text: Bi lik seeni mi la; bi dak ke bi ŋan sakpen ki jer mi, le ki kpaan choo nan tei timɔɔtan ŋani m pu.
