ref: Who can fully understand the thoughts of a ruler? They reach beyond the sky and go deep in the earth.
text: Saan ŋmaa bee ubɔrkpaan aah dak pu na; waalandak daa ti chee ke kitaapaak aah daa kitiŋ pu na, ki nyoo ke nnyusakpem aah nyoo pu na la.

ref: Silver must be purified before it can be used to make something of value.
text: Chuu nyan tijɔŋ ti bi tikunabr ni na aan unii u naani tiwan na di ti ŋa tiwanyaan tii si.

ref: Evil people must be removed before anyone can rule with justice.
text: Chuu nyan titunwanbirdam ubɔrkpaan chee aan bi li nyi waanaan bɔr ibamɔn pu.

ref: Don't try to seem important in the court of a ruler.
text: Taa gii nnyamɔn ke aa ye uninyuun, buyoonn aa si ubɔrkpaan aanimbiin ni na.

ref: It's better for the ruler to give you a high position than for you to be embarrassed in front of royal officials. Be sure you are right
text: Bi yaa tii si uninyuun aajal ke aa kal kan, ni ŋan jer ke bi gaa saajal tii uninyuun.

ref: before you sue someone, or you might lose your case and be embarrassed.
text: Taa di kijejek buen libɔjil ni, tibɔr ti aa kan ti na pu. Useeraadaan ubaa yaa nan len nyaŋ si kan, aa ga ki ŋa kinye?

ref: When you and someone else can't get along, don't gossip about it.
text: Aa ni aaŋeen aatɔ yaa kpak kinikpakpak kan, toor man tii nibaa ki taa kpiir tɔb pu.

ref: Others will find out, and your reputation will then be ruined.
text: Naa ye kina kan, binib mɔmɔk ga bee ke naan ŋmaa joo tibɔbɔrkaan tibaa, le nimi aanimɔɔn aan doo.

ref: The right word at the right time is like precious gold set in silver.
text: Nlandak mu unii len mu ŋan na naahn ke salmaa le baah di tam tikunabr pu na.

ref: Listening to good advice is worth much more than jewelry made of gold.
text: Ulandaan yaa sur unii u kpa ŋuntii na kan, ni kpa tinyoor ki jer salmaa ni ileenyaan i bi di salmaa ŋa i na.

ref: A messenger you can trust is just as refreshing as cool water in summer.
text: Ntuundaan u gbaa ibamɔn na naahn nnyunsoom aah bi pu kitotoŋ aayoonn na la.

ref: Broken promises are worse than rain clouds that don't bring rain.
text: Binib bi puuni tipuur kaa gbiini ti na naahn ntaalangbam ni libuln li kaa joo ni utaal na la.

ref: Patience and gentle talk can convince a ruler and overcome any problem.
text: Limɔr aasurm ŋmaa nyaŋni mbimbin mu pɔɔ na, ki ga ŋmaa nyaŋ binib bi joo kitiŋ na mu.

ref: Eating too much honey can make you sick.
text: Taa ji tisiir ki ti nyaŋ aabaa; ti ga ŋmaa cha aa wuln.

ref: Don't visit friends too often, or they will get tired of it and start hating you.
text: Taa mann aaŋeen aatɔ sakpen; u ga ti nur si ki nann si.

ref: Telling lies about friends is like attacking them with clubs and swords and sharp arrows.
text: Unii yaa gii inyamɔn paan si kan, ni ga ŋmaa ku si ke kijukaan, ni lichakukul, ni nlapiin aah ku pu na la.

ref: A friend you can't trust in times of trouble is like having a toothache or a sore foot.
text: Aa yaa nyu unyamɔndaan pu baala limukl aayoonn kan, ni naahn ke aanyiln le aah ban li fenn aan aa joo ŋmɔ tiwan, bee aataal le aah kpir aan aa joo chuun na.

ref: If your enemies are hungry, give them something to eat. And if they are thirsty, give them something to drink.
text: Nkon yaa joo saadin kan, kpiin u; nnyunyuu yaa joo u kan, tii u nnyun u nyu.

ref: This will be the same as piling burning coals on their heads. And the Lord will reward you.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le inimɔɔn ga ku u, le Uwumbɔr ga ŋa waanyoor ŋa aa pu.

ref: As surely as rain blows in from the north, anger is caused by cruel words.
text: Linibiil joo ni liŋuul ke ntaanjon wɔb aabuln aah joo ni utaal pu na.

ref: It's better to stay outside on the roof of your house than to live inside with a nagging wife.
text: Aa yaa koo kikaafiik ni kan, ni ŋan jer ke aa ni upii u kpa bumɔb sakpen na li kpaan koo.

ref: Good news from far away refreshes like cold water when you are thirsty.
text: Aa yaa ŋun tibɔnyaan ti nyan ni dandar na kan, ni naahn ke saah kan nnyunsoom n‑yoonn mu nnyunyuu joo si na la.

ref: When a good person gives in to the wicked, it's like dumping garbage in a stream of clear water.
text: Uninyaan yaa ti kii utunwanbirdaan aamɔb kan, ni naahn baah di nnyɔk ŋa liboln aanyun ni, bee nnyunbun mu kpa tijɔŋ na la.

ref: Losing self-control leaves you as helpless as a city without a wall.
text: Aa yaa kaa ŋmaa chur saaŋuul kan, aa naahn lidichal li bi maa li kaa maa ŋigon gob li na la.

ref: Expecting snow in summer and rain in the dry season makes more sense than honoring a fool.
text: Kipak aa ŋeer ujɔr, ni naahn utaal u nu tijikaar aacheen aayoonn na, bee tiwoor ti bi kitotoŋ aayoonn na la.

ref: A curse you don't deserve will take wings and fly away like a sparrow or a swallow.
text: Aa yaa kaa tun taani kan, imɔpuur aan ŋmaa chuu si. Ti naahn inyoon i laani kaan kal busub paab na la.

ref: Horses and donkeys must be beaten and bridled— and so must fools.
text: Aa ga loe utaan linaalab, ki di itangar kpom ubon, le ki ga gbaa ujɔr mu.

ref: Don't make a fool of yourself by answering a fool.
text: Aa yaa gar kijɔrk aabaan kan, aa mu jɔr ke unii u baa mu na la.

ref: But if you answer any fools, show how foolish they are, so they won't feel smart.
text: Unii yaa baa si tibɔr ti kaa kpa ŋitaa kan, di tibɔr ti kaa kpa ŋitaa na giin kii u, aan u bee ke waalan aa fuu waah ba dak pu na.

ref: Sending a message by a fool is like chopping off your foot just to spite yourself.
text: Aa yaa di inaŋ di naŋ ujɔr kan, ni naahn ke saah gaa gii aataal le na; aa bi ban tibɔr le na.

ref: A fool with words of wisdom is like an athlete with legs that can't move.
text: Ujɔr yaa ti bi ŋakl ŋiyataŋak kan, li nyi uwɔb mu ga ŋmaa di utaal di chuun.

ref: Are you going to honor a fool? Why not shoot a slingshot with the rock tied tight?
text: Aa yaa pak unii u ye ulatiir na kan, ni bi le ke aa di litakpal ki di kpiin lifulaataln ponn ni ki buu pu na.

ref: A thornbush waved around in the hand of a drunkard is no worse than a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
text: Ujɔr yaa ŋakl si liyataŋakl kan, nima ni udagbiir aah bi nyani nkokon uŋaal ponn ni pu na ye tiwan nibaa la.

ref: It's no smarter to shoot arrows at every passerby than it is to hire a bunch of worthless nobodies.
text: Unii umɔk yoor ujɔr waatuln ni na bi tii binib bi bi nima na iween la.

ref: Dogs return to eat their vomit, just as fools repeat their foolishness.
text: Ujɔr yaa ki gir ŋa kijɔrk aatuln nfum mulee kan, ni naahn ubɔ aah gir ti jin waawuln pu na la.

ref: There is more hope for a fool than for someone who says, “I'm really smart!”
text: Ujɔr sakpiin soor unii u dak ke u chi kaa chi na.

ref: Don't be lazy and keep saying, “There's a lion outside!”
text: Ba ŋa ugbanyakdaan ma aan nya lipaal? Ni ye ba aan u san? U san ichinn la aa?

ref: A door turns on its hinges, but a lazy person just turns over in bed.
text: Ugbanyakdaan ma dɔ tiwandookaan pu le ki labr. U bi le ke jaaleŋ aah bi fiini libubaan ni pu na.

ref: Some of us are so lazy that we won't lift a hand to feed ourselves.
text: Ligbanyakl pu, bigbanyakdam bibaa aa kpaan ŋmaa joo busaa ŋani bimɔi ni.

ref: It's better to take hold of a mad dog by the ears than to take part in someone else's argument.
text: Aa yaa koo kinikpakpak ki kaa kpaa si na ni, ni aa buen ti chuu ubɔ aatafal ki daa na, ni ye tiwanbaan la.

ref: Where there is no fuel a fire goes out; where there is no gossip arguments come to an end.
text: Idɔ yaa kaa ki bi mmii ni kan, mu junni la; le libɔmbɔtukl mu yaa kaa bi kan, kijaak mu door.

ref: Troublemakers start trouble, just as sparks and fuel start a fire.
text: Nkoon le cha mmiiyon bi, le idɔ mu cha mmii gaal, le bibɔbam cha kinikpakpak bi, kaan doo.

ref: There is nothing so delicious as the taste of gossip! It melts in your mouth.
text: Libɔmbɔtukl mɔ pam. Ti gee ti pel li pam.

ref: Hiding hateful thoughts behind smooth talk is like coating a clay pot with a cheap glaze.
text: Ikpatakpaln i bɔrni unii aabimbin na aah bi pu na naahn n‑yam aah bi tiyakr aabukpiik pu pu na la.

ref: The pleasant talk of an enemy hides more evil plans
text: Unii u ŋmanni binib na joo waananaŋ bɔrni waamɔmɔɔn aabɔgbaal ponn ni la.

ref: If you dig a pit, you will fall in; if you start a stone rolling, it will roll back on you.
text: Binib bi pen biken gaawɔb tiib na, gaawɔb tiib ngbaan le ga ki gir chur bi. Aa yaa bil unii litakpal nsan ni kan, sin le ga nan ki gbeer li ki lir.

ref: Watch out for anyone who tells lies and flatters— they are out to get you.
text: Aa yaa gii inyamɔn ki bii unii aayimbil kan, aa nan u le na. Kimɔmɔɔn aa joo ni nibaa see libiil ŋmeen.

ref: Don't brag about yourself— let others praise you.
text: Cha binib biken pak si, ki cha bicham mu pak si, taa pak aabaa.

ref: Stones and sand are heavy, but trouble caused by a fool is a much heavier load.
text: Litakpal ni litambol aah nyuun pu na aan ŋmaa ŋaŋ tibɔr ti kijɔrk ga ŋmaa ban na.

ref: You can trust a friend who corrects you, but kisses from an enemy are nothing but lies.
text: Aajɔ beenin dak aa pu mbamɔm, hali n‑yoonn mu u tii si titotonn na. Saadin ma yaa di uŋaal paan aabɔgbiln pu kan, li nyi.

ref: If you have had enough to eat, honey doesn't taste good, but if you are really hungry, you will eat anything.
text: Aa yaa jin gbiin kan, aa ga ŋmaa yii tisiir, le nkon ma yaa joo si kan, tijikaar ti cho na mɔ la.

ref: When you are far from home, you feel like a bird without a nest.
text: Uja u kaa bi linampal na naahn unyoon u nyan ki cha waadil na la.

ref: The sweet smell of incense can make you feel good, but true friendship is better still.
text: Tulalee ni nkpamɔɔn cha aasui piir la; le aajɔ yaa sur si kan, ni mɔ jer kina la.

ref: Don't desert an old friend of your family or visit your relatives when you are in trouble. A friend nearby is better than relatives far away.
text: Taa suln aajɔtiib ni aate aajɔtiib bɔr. Aa yaa bi tibɔr ni kan, taa ban aate aabo chee nterm; aaŋeen aatɔ u koo gbɔk si na ga ŋmaa ter si ki jer aate aabo u bi dandar na aah ga ter si pu na.

ref: My child, show good sense! Then I will be happy and able to answer anyone who criticizes me.
text: Maabo, li kpa nlan, aan ni li mɔ mi; nima kan, m ga li kpa ngarm ki tii unii u galni mi na.

ref: Be cautious and hide when you see danger— don't be stupid and walk right into trouble.
text: Bilandam waa tibɔr aah choo pu na le ki minn ti, le ujɔr ma ga koo ti ni, le ki nan ki bi wii.

ref: You deserve to lose your coat if you loan it to someone to guarantee payment for the debt of a stranger.
text: Ujɔr u gaa uchaan aapɔln ke u pa na, waawangol le bi ga nan di pa lipɔln ngbaan.

ref: A loud greeting early in the morning is the same as a curse.
text: Aa yaa puun lii aajɔ pu kan, ni soor ni ke aa di kifuuk ti doon u ki finn u kichakpinaanyeek ni.

ref: The steady dripping of rain and the nagging of a wife are one and the same.
text: Upii u kpa bumɔb sakpen na naahn titaapupur la.

ref: Just as iron sharpens iron, friends sharpen the minds of each other.
text: Binib bae biken chee ke tikur aah ga ŋmaa luun tikur pu na la.

ref: Take care of a tree, and you will eat its fruit; look after your master, and you will be praised.
text: Li kii likakaln mbamɔm ki kan ŋikakan ki ŋmɔ. Ututunn u joo udindaan mbamɔm na ga li kpa kipak.

ref: You see your face in a mirror and your thoughts in the minds of others.
text: Saah waa aabaa nnyun ni pu na, kina le aa waa saabimbin mu aapobil ni.

ref: Death and the grave are never satisfied, and neither are humans.
text: Unibɔn aageehn naahn kitekpiitiŋ ni la, mpaan bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk le ki ban bitekpiib biken.

ref: Gold and silver are tested in a red-hot furnace, but we are tested by praise.
text: Mmii le bi joo tɔŋni salmaa ni tikunabr, kina le binib aah pak unii pu na le mɔk waabimbin aah bi pu na.

ref: No matter how hard you beat a fool, you can't pound out the foolishness.
text: Aa ga ŋmaa gbaa ujɔr u ti li ban u kpo, aa mu aan ŋmaa gbaa nyan waajɔrk u ni.

ref: You should take good care of your sheep and goats,
text: Li kii saapiih ni saanaa mbamɔm,

ref: After the hay is cut and the new growth appears and the harvest is over,
text: Aa ga chee titamoor le ki chee timoor lijool taab, le saah chee titamoor nin chee na ki bi bunni.

ref: From the milk of the goats, you can make enough cheese to feed your family and all your servants.
text: Le iŋoob i gur na ga tii aa ni saadichal, ni saanaagbiisapɔm ŋŋobiin.

ref: Wicked people run away when no one chases them, but those who live right are as brave as lions.
text: Ubaa yaa kaa san dii ubiindaan kan, u san la, le uninyaan ma kaar ke uchinn na.

ref: In time of civil war there are many leaders, but a sensible leader restores law and order.
text: Litimbol li tun titunwanbir na aaninkpiib kpelni mala mala la. Le bilandam ni bichiindam aatiŋ ma kpa mpɔɔn ki yunni.

ref: When someone poor takes over and mistreats the poor, it's like a heavy rain destroying the crops.
text: Ugiin yaa ŋa uyidaan ki muk bigiim kan, u naahn utaal u bii tijikaar na la.

ref: Criminals don't know what justice means, but all who respect the Lord understand it completely.
text: Titunwanbirdam aa nyi ibamɔn, le binib bi dii Uwumbɔr na ma beer ibamɔn mbamɔm.

ref: It's better to be poor and live right, than to be rich and dishonest.
text: Aa yaa ye ugiin ni tibulchinn daan kan, ni ŋan jer aa li kpa liwangol ki ye ubeebeedaan.

ref: It makes good sense to obey the Law of God, but you disgrace your parents if you make friends with worthless nobodies.
text: Unachipɔɔn u joo Uwumbɔr aakaal mbamɔm na kpa ichiin. Le u chuun jɔnni maabitibaanidam na tii ute inimɔɔn.

ref: If you make money by charging high interest rates, you will lose it all to someone who cares for the poor.
text: Aa yaa ji binib pem pem ki kan liwangol kan, unii u san bigiim kinimbaak na le ga nan ji saawangol ngbaan.

ref: God cannot stand the prayers of anyone who disobeys his Law.
text: Aa yaa kaa joo Uwumbɔr aakaal kan, waan ŋun saameel.

ref: By leading good people to sin, you dig a pit for yourself, but all who live right will have a bright future.
text: Aa yaa ŋmann unibamɔnn aan u tun titunwanbir kan, aabaa aagaawɔb le ga chuu si. Le maa‑kpa‑taani‑dam ga kan baapar.

ref: The rich think highly of themselves, but anyone poor and sensible sees right through them.
text: Biwankpadam dak n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke bi kpa nlan la, le ugiin u kpa ichiin ki nyi mbimbin na nyi jer bi.

ref: When an honest person wins, it's time to celebrate; when crooks are in control, it's best to hide.
text: Uninyaan yaa bi mpɔɔn ni kan, unibɔn mɔmɔk mɔɔni la, le bibiindam yaa bi mpɔɔn ni kan, unibɔn mɔk bɔrni ubaa la.

ref: If you don't confess your sins, you will be a failure. But God will be merciful if you confess your sins and give them up.
text: Aa yaa joo saatunwanbir bɔrni kan, saan kan tinyoor saamɔfal ni. Kpiir saatunwanbir ki di ti mee aan Uwumbɔr san si kinimbaak.

ref: The Lord blesses everyone who is afraid to do evil, but if you are cruel, you will end up in trouble.
text: Aa yaa ban mpopiin kan, kii tii Uwumbɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Aa yaa kpa tafalaaŋun kan, saamɔfal ga junn.

ref: A ruler who mistreats the poor is like a roaring lion or a bear hunting for food.
text: Ubiindaan yaa bi mpɔɔn ni kan, bigiim aa kani nterm u chee, u bir le ke uchinn na, bee unaamuun na.

ref: A heartless leader is a fool, but anyone who refuses to get rich by cheating others will live a long time.
text: Unii u bi mpɔɔn ni, kaa kpa nlan na ga li ye ubiindaan la. Le unii u kaa gee igaŋgaŋlik na ga yunn nnaan ni.

ref: Don't give help to murderers! Make them stay on the run for as long as they live.
text: Unii u ku uŋeen aatɔ na bi gbii ubaa aabuu la. Taa bui u ke u di cha.

ref: Honesty will keep you safe, but everyone who is crooked will suddenly fall.
text: Li bi mbamɔm ki ŋmar. Aa yaa ye beebeedaan kan, aa ga lir mala la.

ref: Work hard, and you will have a lot of food; waste time, and you will have a lot of trouble.
text: Ukpaal umɔk tun na kpa ki ji gur ni. Le binib bi ka fam, kaa tun nibaa na ga li ye bigiim n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: God blesses his loyal people, but punishes all who want to get rich quick.
text: Binibamɔm ga li kpa limɔfal li fɔk na, ni mpopiin la. Le aa yaa ban mala ke aa kan liwangol kan, Uwumbɔr ga daa aatafal.

ref: It isn't right to be unfair, but some people can be bribed with only a piece of bread.
text: Njinjin aa ŋan; le bibɔjirb bibaa ma pɔɔni bibaa ki gaal igaŋgaŋlik.

ref: Don't be selfish and eager to get rich— you will end up worse off than you can imagine.
text: Bikumɔndam ban ke bi kan liwangol mala, kaa tee nyi buyoonn igiin ga fuu ni bi na.

ref: If you cheat your parents and don't think it's wrong, you are a common thief.
text: Unii u su ute ni una aawan ki dak ke waa tun titunwanbir na ni unaayuk ye tiwan nibaa la.

ref: Selfish people cause trouble, but you will live a full life if you trust the Lord.
text: Kukumɔŋ joo ni tibɔr baanja la. Aa yaa tii Uwumbɔr naadii kan, ni soor.

ref: Only fools would trust what they alone think, but if you live by wisdom, you will do all right.
text: Aa yaa dii aabaa aalandak baanja kan, ni ye kijɔrk la. Li dii bilandam aasurm ki ŋmar.

ref: Giving to the poor will keep you from poverty, but if you close your eyes to their needs, everyone will curse you.
text: Aa yaa tii bigiim kan, saan lann nibaa. Aa yaa kan bigiim ki ŋum aanimbil kan, binib pam le ga puun lii aa pu.

ref: When crooks are in control, everyone tries to hide, but when they lose power, good people are everywhere.
text: Bibiindam yaa bi mpɔɔn ni kan, binib bɔrni la. Le bi yaa nyan mpɔɔn ni kan, mbamɔndam le ga koo mpɔɔn ni.

ref: If you keep being stubborn after many warnings, you will suddenly discover you have gone too far.
text: Buyoonn bi sur si aa yii ki moo ŋani kalmbaani na kan, daalbaadaal aa ga nan lir, kaan ki fii sil.

ref: If you love wisdom your parents will be glad, but chasing after bad women will cost you everything.
text: Aa yaa neen nlan kan, aate ga ŋmaa li kpa limakl aa pu. Aa yaa ji saamombil bipiidagoob pu kan, ni ye kijɔrk la.

ref: An honest ruler makes the nation strong; a ruler who takes bribes will bring it to ruin.
text: Ubɔrkpaan u aatafal bi ibamɔn ni na aatiŋ kpa mpɔɔn, le ubɔr u aatafal bi ŋimombil ni na aatiŋ ga kuln.

ref: Flattery is nothing less than setting a trap.
text: Aa yaa joo kimɔmɔɔn ŋmanni aajɔtiib kan, aa bi pen aabaa gaawɔb la.

ref: Your sins will catch you, but everyone who lives right will sing and celebrate.
text: Titunwanbirdam aagaawɔb le chur bi, le mbimbinyaandam ma kpa mpopiin ki ka fuur.

ref: The wicked don't care about the rights of the poor, but good people do.
text: Uninyaan nyi ugiin aabamɔn, le bibiindam ma aan bee kina aatataa.

ref: Sneering at others is a spark that sets a city on fire; using good sense can put out the flames of anger.
text: Binib bi lik biken fam na ga ŋmaa bii litimbomɔln. Le bilandam ma cha kitiŋ ponn ni bi suuna.

ref: Be wise and don't sue a fool. You won't get satisfaction, because all the fool will do is sneer and shout.
text: Ulandaan yaa di ujɔr buen libɔjil ni kan, ujɔr ngbaan ma laa le ki seei.

ref: A murderer hates everyone who is honest and lives right.
text: Binikurb aa gee binib bi kaa kpa taani na, le uninyaan ga ŋmaa gaa kina aanii lii.

ref: Don't be a fool and quickly lose your temper— be sensible and patient.
text: Ulatiir joo waaŋuul mɔk binib la, le bilandam ma kpa limɔr ki chur bibaa.

ref: A ruler who listens to lies will have corrupt officials.
text: Ubɔr u pel tinyamɔnbɔr na aatutum mɔmɔk ga li ye binyamɔndam la.

ref: The poor and all who abuse them must each depend on God for light.
text: Ugiin ni unii u muk u na mɔmɔk kpaan tiwan nibaa nee la, Uwumbɔr le tii bi mɔmɔk ŋinimbil.

ref: Kings who are fair to the poor will rule a long time.
text: Ubɔrkpaan u jaa bigiim pu ki joo baabamɔn tii bi na aanaan ga yunn pam.

ref: Correct your children, and they will be wise; children out of control disgrace their mothers.
text: Nsurm ni ntafadaan ŋan tii bibilb la. Ubo yaa ŋani waageehn kan, u ga nan tii una inimɔɔn la.

ref: Crime increases when crooks are in power, but law-abiding citizens will see them fall.
text: Titunwanbirdam yaa bi mpɔɔn ni kan, titunwanbir moo kpae la. Le bininyaam ga li bi ki nan kan titunwanbirdam ngbaan aadoon.

ref: If you correct your children, they will bring you peace and happiness.
text: Li dar saabo aatafal ki li kpa u pu limakl n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Waan jinn si inimɔɔn daalbaadaal.

ref: Without guidance from God law and order disappear, but God blesses everyone who obeys his Law.
text: Litimbol li kaa kpa Uwumbɔr aasurm na aa bi mbamɔm. Unii u joo Uwumbɔr aakaal na le kpa mpopiin.

ref: Even when servants are smart, it takes more than words to make them obey.
text: Saan ŋmaa di imɔliin baanja di sur ututunn. Nibaakan u ga bee yaatataa, ki mu aa ŋun tii si.

ref: There is more hope for a fool than for someone who speaks without thinking.
text: Ujɔr sakpiin soor unii u len tibɔr kaa dakl lik na.

ref: Slaves that you treat kindly from their childhood will cause you sorrow.
text: Saanaagbiija yaa ban tiwan waabir ni aan aa tii u n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, daalbaadaal u ga nan gaa saah kpa pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: A person with a quick temper stirs up arguments and commits a lot of sins.
text: Binib bi aasui fiir yɔl yɔl na ban kijaak ni tibɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la.

ref: Too much pride brings disgrace; humility leads to honor.
text: Kigaak le ga joo ni saadoon, le aa yaa sunn aabaa taab kan, aa kani kipak ni lisil.

ref: If you take part in a crime you are your worst enemy, because even under oath you can't tell the truth.
text: Aa yaa ye unaayuk aaŋeen aatɔ kan, aa tii aabaa titotonn la. Aa yaa len mbamɔn libɔjil ni kan, bi ga daa aatafal, le aa yaa nee kan, Uwumbɔr mu puuni lir aa pu.

ref: Don't fall into the trap of being a coward— trust the Lord, and you will be safe.
text: Aa yaa dii binib aah dak aa pu pu na kan, naa ŋan. Aa yaa tii Uwumbɔr naadii kan, le aa ŋmar.

ref: Many try to make friends with a ruler, but justice comes from the Lord.
text: Unii mɔk ban waajojoor chee nterm la, Uwumbɔr mu baanja chee le ibamɔn bi.

ref: Good people and criminals can't stand each other.
text: Unibamɔnn aa gee ubiindaan, le ubiindaan mu aa gee unibamɔnn.

ref: These are the sayings and the message of Agur son of Jakeh. Someone cries out to God, “I am completely worn out! How can I last?
text: Jake aajapɔɔn Agur aabɔkpaan sɔ: “Uwumbɔr aa bi m chee, Uwumbɔr aa bi m chee, le maa kpa nterm.

ref: I am far too stupid to be considered human.
text: M naahn kiwakork ki jer unibɔn, maa kpa nlan mu unibɔn ga li kpa na.

ref: I never was wise, and I don't understand what God is like.”
text: Maa bae nlan daalbaadaal, kaa nyi Uwumbɔr aabɔr tibaa.

ref: Has anyone gone up to heaven and come back down? Has anyone grabbed hold of the wind? Has anyone wrapped up the sea or marked out boundaries for the earth? If you know of any who have done such things, then tell me their names and their children's names.
text: Ŋma kee bee paacham aalan mbamɔm? Ŋma kee chuu libuln ŋa uŋaal ni? Ŋma kee di nnyun poo likekeln ni? Ŋma kee siin kitiŋ aanaanmɔk? Aa yaa nyi kan, ŋma ye udaan, ŋma ye ujapɔɔn?

ref: Everything God says is true— and it's a shield for all who come to him for safety.
text: “Uwumbɔr joo waah puu tipuur ti na mɔmɔk. U kii binib bi mɔmɔk ban waaterm na.

ref: Don't change what God has said! He will correct you and show that you are a liar.
text: Aa yaa bui ke u len tibɔr tibaa aan waa len ti kan, u ga daa aatafal ki mɔk si ke aa ye unyamɔndaan la.” Ŋiyataŋak ŋiken

ref: There are two things, Lord, I want you to do for me before I die:
text: Uwumbɔr, m mee si ke aa cha m kan tiwan nilee nee waahr aan ki nin kpo.

ref: Make me absolutely honest and don't let me be too poor or too rich. Give me just what I need.
text: Nyan mi inyamɔn ni, ki cha m taa li kpa, ki taa li ye ugiin mu. Kina pu na, tii mi maah ban tijikaar pu na mɔk.

ref: If I have too much to eat, I might forget about you; if I don't have enough, I might steal and disgrace your name.
text: M yaa kpa pam kan, nibaakan m ga bui ke maa ki ban si. M yaa ti ki ye ugiin mu kan, nibaakan m ga su kinaayuk ki di inimɔɔn tii si.

ref: Don't tell a slave owner something bad about one of the slaves. That slave will curse you, and you will be in trouble.
text: Taa bii unaagbiija udindaan chee. Unaagbiija ngbaan ga nan puun lii aa pu, le aa ji falaa ti pu.

ref: Some people curse their father and even their mother;
text: Binib bibaa bi, ki puuni lir bitetiib pu, kaa neen binatiib mu.

ref: others think they are perfect, but they are stained by sin.
text: Binib bibaa bi, ki dak ke baabimbin ŋan la, le ki tee kpa tijɔŋ sakpen.

ref: others are so greedy that they gobble up the poor and homeless.
text: Binib bibaa ŋani bigiim ni bifalaadam mbiin ki kuln bi ke bi taa ki li bi na.

ref: Greed has twins, each named “Give me!” There are three or four things that are never satisfied:
text: Kigiik le kpa bisatiib bilee, ki yin bi mɔmɔk ke “Tii‑mi.” Tiwan ninaa nibaa le bi, kaan bab naah kpa tiwan ni na:

ref: The world of the dead and a childless wife, the thirsty earth and a flaming fire.
text: Kitekpiitiŋ, ni upii u kaa kpa ubo na, ni kitiŋ ki kuur ki ban utaal na, ni mmii mu wu mubaa pu na.

ref: Don't make fun of your father or disobey your mother— crows will peck out your eyes, and buzzards will eat the rest of you.
text: Unii umɔk ŋani ute yaansara na, ni unii umɔk lik una fam waapininkpir ni na ŋan ke nangba tiib le ji u, le ikaabɔn mu gaa lokr unimbil.

ref: There are three or four things I cannot understand:
text: Tiwan ninaa nibaa le bi, le maa ŋmaa bee naatataa:

ref: How eagles fly so high or snakes crawl on rocks, how ships sail the ocean or people fall in love.
text: Likaagiil li bi paacham ki laani na, ni uwaa aah chuun litakpal pu pu na, ni buŋɔb sakpem aah kaa wɔŋni nnyusakpem ponn ni pu na, ni uja ni upii aah bɔnni tɔb pu na.

ref: An unfaithful wife says, “Sleeping with another man is as natural as eating.”
text: Upii u nya uchal aapuwɔb na ŋani kina la: u goor kidagook, le ki nan fu nnyun, ki bui ke, “Maa tun titunwanbir.”

ref: There are three or four things that make the earth tremble and are unbearable:
text: Tiwan ninaa nibaa le bi aan kitiŋ kee aa gee ni:

ref: A slave who becomes king, a fool who eats too much,
text: Unaagbiija u nan kpaln ubɔr na, ni ujɔr u kani waah ban tiwan nimɔk u ji na,

ref: a hateful woman who finds a husband, and a slave who takes the place of the woman who owns her.
text: ni upii u aabimbin aa ŋan na, kan uja ki mɔn, ni unaagbiipiibo u nan gaal udindaan aachal na.

ref: On this earth four things are small but very wise:
text: Tiwakor tinaa tibaa le aa filk dulnyaa wee ni, ki mu tee kpa nlan pam:

ref: Ants, who seem to be feeble, but store up food all summer long;
text: Inyann: yaa kpa mpɔɔn, le ki mu tee ban yaajikaar lipeel siin ni.

ref: badgers, who seem to be weak, but live among the rocks;
text: Lijool paab aalapol: yaa kpa mpɔɔn, le ki mu tee lukr waabuu ŋijootakpal ni.

ref: locusts, who have no king, but march like an army;
text: Itoon: yaa kpa ubɔr, le ki mu kpaan le ki dii tɔb.

ref: lizards, which can be caught in your hand, but sneak into palaces.
text: Kijapark: aa ga ŋmaa di kibaa ŋum aaŋaal ponn ni, le ti mu tee koo bibɔrb aanaakɔr ni.

ref: Three or four creatures really strut around:
text: Tiwan ninaa nibaa aasachuln ŋan ke aa li lik ni chuun:

ref: Those fearless lions who rule the jungle,
text: Ichinn; i ye tiwakor mɔk aapɔɔl u kaa san nibaa na,

ref: those proud roosters, those mountain goats, and those rulers who have no enemies.
text: ni iŋoob, ni ikooja aah chuun pu na, ni bibɔrb aah chuun binib ponn ni pu na.

ref: If you are foolishly bragging or planning something evil, then stop it now!
text: Aa yaa jɔr ki kpa kigaak sakpen ki dak ilandak i kaa ŋan na kan, sil ki ki dakl lik.

ref: If you churn milk you get butter; if you pound on your nose, you get blood— and if you stay angry, you get in trouble.
text: Aa yaa di nnaabiin siin nnaabiin aasambil ni kan, aa ga kan nnaabiinkpan la. Aa yaa faa unii aamɔfal kan, nsin le ga nyan ni. Aa yaa bii unii aasui kan, le aa di aabaa koon tibɔr ni.

ref: These are the sayings that King Lemuel of Massa was taught by his mother.
text: Ubɔrkpaan Lemuel aana aabɔkpaan ti u nan tuk u na sɔ:

ref: My son Lemuel, you were born in answer to my prayers, so listen carefully.
text: “Sin le ye njapɔɔn u m gee u na, u Uwumbɔr nan di gaa maameel na. M ga bui si ke ba?

ref: Don't waste your life chasing after women! This has ruined many kings.
text: Taa di saapɔɔn ni saamombil mɔmɔk tii bipiib. Bi puun ku bibɔrb a.

ref: Kings and leaders should not get drunk or even want to drink.
text: Lemuel, li pel. Naa ŋan ke bibɔrkpaam li nyu ndaan, bee bi li neen ndaan sakpen.

ref: Drinking makes you forget your responsibilities, and you mistreat the poor.
text: Bi yaa nyu ndaan kan, bi suln ikaal la, le ki yii binib bi bi limukl ni na, kaa tii bi baabamɔn.

ref: Beer and wine are only for the dying or for those who have lost all hope.
text: Ndaan ye binib bi bi kpoi na aawan la, ni binib bi bi kinimbaak ni na.

ref: Let them drink and forget how poor and miserable they feel.
text: Cha bima li nyu ki suln baagiin ni baapombiin pu.

ref: But you must defend those who are helpless and have no hope.
text: “Len tii binib bi kaa ŋmaa len na. Li kii binib bi kaa kpa nterm na aabamɔn.

ref: Be fair and give justice to the poor and homeless. In Praise of a Good Wife
text: Len tii bi, ki li ye ubɔjirbamɔnn. Li kii bigiim ni bifalaadam aabamɔn.” Upiibamɔnn

ref: A truly good wife is the most precious treasure a man can find!
text: Ni pɔɔ pam ke aa kan upiibamɔnn. U kpa tinyoor jer nleen mu ŋan ki kpa kidaak sakpen na.

ref: Her husband depends on her, and she never lets him down.
text: Uchal joo waamakl ŋani u ni la, le kaan ŋa ugiin daalbaadaal.

ref: She is good to him every day of her life,
text: N‑yoonn mumɔk u bi na kan, u ŋani u ni ŋan na la, kaa ŋani u ni kaa ŋan na.

ref: and with her own hands she gladly makes clothes.
text: N‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, u bi tun la, ki luu ŋikeken.

ref: She is like a sailing ship that brings food from across the sea.
text: U joo ni tijikaar saah kaa nyi nin chee na la, ke uwankooh aaŋɔb aah nya ni dandar pu na.

ref: She gets up before daylight to prepare food for her family and for her servants.
text: U finn ngeen pu lichakpitaawoln le ki ŋa tijikaar siin waadichal ni aanib, le ki mɔk waanaagbiisapɔm baatun.

ref: She knows how to buy land and how to plant a vineyard,
text: Uma le ban kitiŋ ki bi ga ko na, le ki di waamombil daa ki, ki bu tijikaar ki pu.

ref: and she always works hard.
text: U ye ututunn la, ki kpa mpɔɔn ki tun pam.

ref: She knows when to buy or sell, and she stays busy until late at night.
text: U nyi waah ŋani nimɔk na aanyoor, le ki tun ti mue kinyeek.

ref: She spins her own cloth,
text: U fik ubaa aakokonn le ki luu ubaa aawanpeenkaan.

ref: and she helps the poor and the needy.
text: U kpa bigiim ni bifalaadam chee tiŋann.

ref: Her family has warm clothing, and so she doesn't worry when it snows.
text: Tiwoor aayoonn kan, naa muk u, ba pu? waanib mɔmɔk kpa tiwoor aawanpeenkaan.

ref: She does her own sewing, and everything she wears is beautiful.
text: U ŋal ubaa aawandookaan aakeken, le ki peeni ŋitanyaan aawanpeenkaan.

ref: Her husband is a well-known and respected leader in the city.
text: Le unii mɔk nyi uchal bɔr ke u ye uninyuun la.

ref: She makes clothes to sell to the shop owners.
text: Upii ngbaan luu ŋikeken ni ŋigbapapan, le ki joo kooh biwankoob pu.

ref: She is strong and graceful, as well as cheerful about the future.
text: U kpa mpɔɔn, le binib neen u, waa san fen u ga woln na aajawaan.

ref: Her words are sensible, and her advice is thoughtful.
text: Waamɔliin ye nlan ni ngbasoon aabɔr la.

ref: She takes good care of her family and is never lazy.
text: N‑yoonn mɔmɔk u tun le ki tii waadichal aanib baah ban pu na.

ref: Her children praise her, and with great pride her husband says,
text: Le waabim neen u, le uchal pak u.

ref: “There are many good women, but you are the best!”
text: Le uchal bui ke, “Bipiib pam le ye bipiib, le sin ma ti nyaŋ bi mɔmɔk.”

ref: Charm can be deceiving, and beauty fades away, but a woman who honors the Lord deserves to be praised.
text: Ibɔnyɔk ŋmanni, le kinyaan mu door, le upii u san Uwumbɔr ijawaan na ma kpa kipak.

ref: Show her respect— praise her in public for what she has done.
text: Waah ŋani pu na mɔmɔk ponn ni tii u kipak la. U kpa unibɔn mɔmɔk chee kipak la.

ref: When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
text: Ulandaan, u aate nan ye David u nan ye Jerusalem aabɔr na, aah nan len pu na sɔ:

ref: Nothing makes sense! Everything is nonsense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense!
text: Ni mɔmɔk ye fam la, ni ye fam la. Limɔfal ye fam la, ni mɔmɔk ye fam la.

ref: What is there to show for all of our hard work here on this earth?
text: Aa joo saamɔfal mɔmɔk tun lituln la, ki ji falaa, le ni mɔmɔk aapuwɔb na, saa nan kpa nibaa aa di mɔk.

ref: People come, and people go, but still the world never changes.
text: N‑yoonn mue ni mu aanib choo, le n‑yoonn mue ni mu aanib jer, le dulnyaa ma beenin bi waabimbin.

ref: The sun comes up, the sun goes down; it hurries right back to where it started from.
text: Nwiin beenin puur, le ki beenin lir. Mu chuun mala mala le ki cha nin chee mu ga ti ki piin ni na.

ref: The wind blows south, the wind blows north; round and round it blows over and over again.
text: Libuln daar cha ŋŋangii wɔb, le ki daar cha ŋŋangan wɔb, li daar ki manni gonni, le ki ti ki fuu laah piin nin chee na.

ref: All rivers empty into the sea, but it never spills over; one by one the rivers return to their source.
text: Limɔɔl mɔk puu cha nnyusakpem ni la, le nnyusakpem aa kpa ke mu gbiin. Nnyun ngbaan gir cha nin chee ŋimɔɔ ngbaan piin na la, le ki ti ki piin ni.

ref: All of life is far more boring than words could ever say. Our eyes and our ears are never satisfied with what we see and hear.
text: Tiwan mɔmɔk joo cha tibakr ti unii aan ŋmaa len na ni la. Tinimbil aan ŋmaa kan ki ti bab; le titafal mu aan ŋun tiwan pu ki ti bab.

ref: Someone might say, “Here is something new!” But it happened before, long before we were born.
text: Bi len le ke, “Lik, tiwapɔnn nibaa sɔ.” Aayii, ni puun dan n‑yoonn mu jer na. Ni puun dan ni yunn le bi nan nin ma timi.

ref: No one who lived in the past is remembered anymore, and everyone yet to be born will be forgotten too. It Is Senseless To Be Wise
text: Ubaa aa teer tiwan ni nan dan n‑yoonn mu jer na. Le ubaa aan nan teer tiwan ni ŋani dandana na n‑yoonn mu choo na ni. Ulandaan ngbaan aah kan ki nyi pu na

ref: I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel.
text: Min, ulandaan ngbaan nan ye Israel aabɔr le ki ka Jerusalem aatiŋ ni.

ref: With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do.
text: M nan puu ke see m tɔŋ ki bae lik tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋani dulnyaa wee ni na. Uwumbɔr di mbimbin mu kaa kpa tataa na le di tii timi.

ref: If something is crooked, it can't be made straight; if something isn't there, it can't be counted.
text: Saan ŋmaa naar tiwan ni gɔr na. Saan ŋmaa kahn tiwan ni kaa bi na.

ref: I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.”
text: Le m bui mbaa ke, “M kpaln unikpaan la. M kpa nlan jer ubɔr umɔk puen mi joo Jerusalem aatiŋ na. M nyi Uwumbɔr do aalan, ni nlanbaekoo aah ye pu na.”

ref: Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
text: M nan puu ke m ga bae ki bee nlan ni kijɔrk aah kaa kpaa pu na, ki bee Uwumbɔr do aalan mu, ni kiwaatiik aah kaa kpaa pu na, le ki kan ke m bi san dii libuln la.

ref: The more you know, the more you hurt; the more you understand, the more you suffer.
text: N‑yoonn mu aa moo kani nlan na, n‑yoonn ngbaan le ilandak moo kpae. N‑yoonn mu aa moo beer tiwan na, n‑yoonn ngbaan le ni mu tii si iween.

ref: I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense.
text: M nan ŋa nlandak ke m ji mmɔɔn ki lik ke ni kpa mpopiin aan naa kpa, le ki kan ke ni mu ye fam la.

ref: Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do?
text: M nan kan ke tilaar ye kijɔrk la. M nan bee ke mmɔɔn aa tii unii tinyoor tibaa.

ref: I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
text: Maah nan neen ke m kan nlan sakpen pu na, le m nan piin ki nyu ndaan ke nsui li piin. M nan dak ke kina le unii ga ŋmaa ji waamɔfageŋ kimina kitiŋ kee pu.

ref: I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards.
text: M nan ŋa tiwankpaan pam. M nan maa ŋidichal ki ŋum ndaan aasubil aasui.

ref: I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees.
text: M nan naan tisar ni ŋisubil aasui aasar ti kpa ŋisubil mɔmɔk aabɔŋ na.

ref: And I had pools where I could get water for the trees.
text: M nan gbii ŋimɔɔ ke nnyun li puu chaa tisar ngbaan ni.

ref: I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem.
text: M nan daa binaagbiib pam, le binaagbiib nan ma nnaagbiibim maachiln ni. M nan kpa tiwakor ki jer unii umɔk nan puen mi ki koo Jerusalem ni na.

ref: Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
text: M nan ki kuun tikunabr ni salmaa ki nyan ni nnaan mumɔk nan bi maanaan taab na. Bijab ni bipiib le gaa ilahn ke bi tii mi mpopiin. Le m nan kpa bipiib bimɔk uja ga ŋmaa joo na.

ref: I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise.
text: Mbamɔn, m nan ye unikpaan la. M nan ŋa unikpaan ki jer unii umɔk nan puen mi ki koo Jerusalem ni na. Maalan aa nan jinn mi inimɔɔn daalbaadaal.

ref: I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work.
text: M nan kani tiwan nimɔk m ban na. M nan ji mmɔɔn maah gee pu na la. M nan mak maah tun ki kan tiwan ni mɔmɔk na pu. Nimina mɔmɔk nan ye maapar la.

ref: Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble. Wisdom Comes from God
text: Le m nan kal ki dakl lik maah tun pu na mɔmɔk, ni maah di kitotoŋ ki tun kina na, le ki kan ke ni mɔmɔk nan ye fam la. Ni nan bi ke saah bi san dii libuln le na, naa kpa tinyoor kpala.

ref: I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity.
text: Naah ye pu na le ye ke ubɔr tun bibɔrb bi loln u pu nsan na aah nan tun pu lii na pu la. Kina pu le m piin ki bi dakl lik nlan, ni tafalaaŋun aatun, ni kijɔrk aatataa aah ye pu na.

ref: And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
text: M nyi ke nlan ŋan jer kijɔrk, ke nwiihn aah ŋan jer mbɔmbɔɔn pu na la.

ref: Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
text: Bilandam waa baah cha nin chee na, le bijɔrb ma aa waa. Tɔ, m mu tee nyi ke ti mɔmɔk aadoon ye tiwan nibaa la.

ref: Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense.
text: Le m nan kal ki dakl nneen ni ke, “M ga nan doo ke bijɔrb na la. Kina pu na, maalan na tii mi ba aanyoor?” le ki kii mbaa ke, “Fam, naa tii mi nibaa.”

ref: This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
text: Kina pu na, limɔfal aa nan kpa tinyoor tibaa m chee, ba pu? limɔfal lee aawan mɔmɔk joo ni mi tibɔr ŋmeen la. Ni mɔmɔk ye fam la; m nan bi san dii libuln la.

ref: Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all.
text: Maah nan tun ki kan tiwan ni mɔmɔk na aa nan ye m chee nibaa, ba pu? m nyi ke unii u ga nan paan m pu na le ga nan yoor ni.

ref: Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
text: Nibaakan, u ga nan li ye ulandaan, bee ujɔr la, tɔ, ubaa mu aa nyi. Tɔ, maah tun ki kan tiwan ni mɔmɔk na ga nan kpaln uyaan la. Maah di maalan tun ki kan tiwan ni mɔmɔk na ga nan li ye uyaan la. Ni ye fam la.

ref: I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed.
text: Kina pu le m nan bee ke maah nan tun ki kan pu na aa ye maawan, le ni bii nsui.

ref: When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong.
text: Aa ga di saalan, ni saachiin, ni saanyim mɔmɔk tun kan tiwan, le ni nan kpaln unii u aatotoŋ aa nan nyan ni pu na aawan. Ni ye fam la, le kaa ŋan kina.

ref: What do we really gain from all of our hard work?
text: Aa ga muk aabaa le ki tun dulnyaa wee ni, le kaa nan kpa tinyoor tibaa.

ref: Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
text: N‑yoonn mumɔk aa bi limɔfal ni na, saatuln mɔmɔk joo ni limukl ni iyiween la. Hali kinyeek kan, saa ŋmaa doon ki fuur. Ni mɔmɔk ye fam la.

ref: The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us,
text: Tiwan ni ŋan ke unibɔn ŋa na le ye ke u ji, ki nyu, ki li mɔɔni waah tun ki kan pu na pu. Le m ki kan ke nimina mu nyan ni Uwumbɔr chee la.

ref: and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do.
text: Aa ba ga ŋa kinye ki di aabaa aapɔɔn kan tiwan ki ji, ki li mɔɔni ni pu?

ref: If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: Uwumbɔr tii binib bi piir usui na nlan, ni ichiin, ni mpopiin, le ki tee cha titunwanbirdam tun, ki kani ki gur bilni, ke u nan di tii binib bi piir usui na. Ni mɔmɔk ye fam la. Ni bi ke unii aah san dii libuln pu na la.

ref: Everything on earth has its own time and its own season.
text: Tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋani dulnyaa wee ni na ŋani n‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr ban na la.

ref: There is a time for birth and death, planting and reaping,
text: U siin timar aayoonn, le ki siin nkun mu aayoonn, tiwan aabum aayoonn bi la, le tiwan aaŋɔm mu aayoonn bi,

ref: There is also a time for love and hate, for war and peace. What God Has Given Us To Do
text: U siin ngeehm aayoonn, le ki siin kinanaŋ mu aayoonn, butɔb aayoonn bi, le nsuudoon mu aayoonn bi.

ref: What do we gain by all our hard work?
text: Timi aatun ŋee mɔmɔk aanyoor ye tilati?

ref: I have seen what difficult things God demands of us.
text: M nyi Uwumbɔr aah di litusakpeln li tun timi na.

ref: God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future.
text: U siin tiwan mɔmɔk aayoonn dee dee la. U cha ti kpa lineen ke ti li nyi n‑yoonn mu choo na aabɔr, le kaa tee tii timi nsan ke ti bee waah tun pu na aatataa mbamɔm.

ref: I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life,
text: Le m bee ke buyoonn ti laa bi dulnyaa wee ni na, ti li kpa mpopiin ki tun taah ga ŋman pu na.

ref: because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do.
text: Ti mɔmɔk li ji ki nyu, ki li mɔɔni taah tun ki kan tiwan ni na pu. Ni ye Uwumbɔr aapiin la.

ref: Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
text: M nyi ke tiwan ni mɔmɔk Uwumbɔr ŋani na aan li kpa ndoon. Saan ŋmaa di nibaa kpee ni pu, kan ŋmaa bar ni pu. Uwumbɔr ŋani kina ke binib li pak u la.

ref: Everything that happens has happened before, and all that will be has already been— God does everything over and over again. The Future Is Known Only to God
text: Tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋa na, ni tiwan ni ga ŋa na, puun ŋa n‑yoonn mu jer na. Uwumbɔr cha tiwan chachaan ngbaan ŋani le ki gir ŋani. Beebee aatuln li bi dulnyaa ni na

ref: So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good.
text: Le m bui mbaa ke, “Uwumbɔr ga ji binib bi aabimbin ŋan na, ni titunwanbirdam tibɔr la, ba pu? tiwan mɔmɔk, ni lituln mɔmɔk, ga ŋa n‑yoonn mu u siin ni na la.”

ref: I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals.
text: Le m di doo ke Uwumbɔr bi tɔŋni timi ke u mɔk timi ke unibɔn aa jer kiwakork.

ref: All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth.
text: Ni mɔmɔk cha libubaan ni la, nima le ye titan ni. Ni mɔmɔk nan kpaan nyan ni nima la, le ki ki ga kpaan gir nima chee.

ref: Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth?
text: Ubaa aan ŋmaa bee ke unibɔn aawiin le chaa paacham le kiwakork yaan chaa taab.

ref: I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth. They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful.
text: Le m ki fenn lik beebee aatuln li tun dulnyaa wee ni na. Baah muk binib bi na nan wii la, le ubaa aa ter bi. Binib bi muk bi na nan kpa mpɔɔn la, le ubaa aa nan ter bi.

ref: I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living.
text: M kpa lipiipoln binib bi kpoi kaa ki bi na pu. Bi yaan soor binib bi kaa kpo na.

ref: But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
text: Binib bi yaan ŋan sakpen na, le ye baah kaa kee ma bi na. Bima aah kaa kee kan dulnyaa wee ni aabeebee aatuln na, bi yaan soor.

ref: Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: M nan ki bee naah ŋa pu aan binib nyani kitotoŋ sakpen ke bi li kpa na; nima le ye ke bi kpa biŋeen aatɔtiib pu lipiipoln. Tɔ, ni mu ye fam la. Ni bi ke unii aah san dii libuln pu na la.

ref: Yet a very little food eaten in peace is better than twice as much earned from overwork and chasing the wind.
text: Nibaakan ti gbii kina; tɔ, aa yaa kpa siib, aan saalan dɔ suuna kan, ni soor ni ke aa li joo aaŋaal ilee mɔk yanni n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke aa chuu libuln.

ref: Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense.
text: M ki kan tiwan nibaa dulnyaa wee ni, le ni mu ye fam.

ref: For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life! It Is Better To Have a Friend
text: Uja ubaa le bi ki koo ubaa. Waa kpa bo, kaa kpa naal, bee kpel mu, le ki mu tee tun lituln n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Unimbil aa nan gbiin liwangol li u kpa na. U bi tun tii ŋma, kaa tii ubaa mpopiin? Nimina mu ye fam la, kina aabimbin ye falaa la.

ref: You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn.
text: Bilee ŋan jer ubaa; bi yaa kpaan kan, bi ga tun ki nyan tinyoor.

ref: If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble.
text: Ubaa yaa lir kan, uma na ga fiin u. Tɔ, unii yaa bi ubaa ki ti lir kan, naa ŋan kpala, ba pu? ubaa aa bi u chee ki ga ter u.

ref: If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night.
text: Tiwoor yaa bi kan, bilee ga doon ki bub tɔb le biwon toŋ; tɔ, unibaan ga ŋa kinye tiwoor taa ku u?

ref: Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
text: Binib bilee ga ŋmaa nyaŋ kijaak ki ba ga nyaŋ unibaan na. Baah paa ŋŋmin mu ki gir mil mu na aan ŋmaa kii mala.

ref: I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone.
text: M nan kal dakl binib bi mɔmɔk bi dulnyaa wee ni na aabɔr, le ki kan ke bi ponn ni nibaa chee unachipɔɔn bi ki ga ji nnaan.

ref: His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: Ubɔr aah joo binib bi na gee bi li wiir ba pu, u yaa nan kpo kan, ubaa aan teer ki pak u waah nan tun pu na pu. Ni ye fam la. Ni bi ke unii aah san dii libuln pu na la.

ref: Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship.
text: Li nyi saah chaa Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni pu na. Aa yaa buen nima ke aa ti bae kan, ni ŋan ki jer bijɔrb bi kaa ŋmaa ganni tiwan ni ŋan na, ni ni kaa ŋan na ponn ni aah chaa ke bi ti toor kitork pu na.

ref: Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much.
text: Dakl lik waahr ki nin len, ki taa puur tipuur tii Uwumbɔr fam fam. U bi paacham, le aa bi taab, kina pu na, taa len ki jer saah kpa pu na.

ref: If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
text: Aa yaa dak ilandak sakpen kan, aa daŋni tidaŋ sakpen la. Le aa yaa len tibɔr sakpen kan, aa ga ti len kijɔrk aabɔr.

ref: God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God.
text: Kina pu na, aa yaa puu tipuur tii Uwumbɔr kan, li joo ti gbin gbin. Waa kpa ujɔr aayoonn. Ŋa saah puu ke aa ga ŋa pu na.

ref: It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it.
text: Aa yaa kaa puu tipuur kpala kan, ni soor ni ke aa puu kaa ŋa saah puu pu na.

ref: Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
text: Taa cha aabaa aamɔboln di si koon titunwanbir ni, ki taa bui Uwumbɔr aatotoor ke aa ba ŋani yaansara la. Ba ŋa aa ban Uwumbɔr aaŋuul fii aa pu ki bii tiwan ni aa di aaŋaal ŋa na?

ref: Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do.
text: Aa yaa kan ke biyidam muk bigiim, kaa tii bi baabamɔn, ni tiwan ni ŋan na kan, taa cha ni ŋa si iwaan. Uninkpel mɔmɔk aah bi unii u aataab na le kiir u. Le unii u jer bimɔk bilee na kii bi.

ref: And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
text: Baah chee tijikaar ti na pu le ubɔr bi.

ref: If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense.
text: Aa yaa gee ŋimombil kan, saan bab ŋi daalbaadaal. Aa yaa ban ke aa li kpa kan, saan ŋmaa kan saah ban pu na mɔmɔk. Ni ye fam la.

ref: The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you.
text: Liwangol li aa moo kani li na, kina le aa kpa binib pam ke aa kpiin. Tinyoor ti aa kpa na le ye ke aa nyi ke aa kpa liwangol.

ref: If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
text: Nibaakan, unii u tun na ga li kpa ki ji, nibaa mu kan, waan kan ki ji. Tɔ, u mu tee geeni kinyeek. Uwankpadaan ma kan, u kpa sakpen u ji, le kaa tee geeni kinyeek, ki dɔ dak ilandak.

ref: I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good.
text: Kiwanbiik sakpeŋ ki m kan dulnyaa wee ni na sɔ: binib bilni ŋimombil ki kii n‑yoonn mu bi ga nan ban ŋi na la,

ref: Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children.
text: le ki nan lann ŋi kinimbɔŋ kibaa ni, kaa nan ki kpa nibaa baabim nan nab ni pu.

ref: They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work.
text: Ti nya dulnyaa wee ni ke taah koo ni u ponn ni, kaa joo nibaa pu na la. Taah tun lituln li mɔmɔk na aan nan cha ti li joo nibaa cha.

ref: That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind.
text: Naa ŋan. Taah dan pu na, kina le ti ga gir buen. Ti tun, le ki pɔɔni tibaa ke ti chuu libuln. Tɔ, ba aan ti kani?

ref: Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
text: Ti bi limɔfal lee ni, mbɔmbɔɔn ni mpombiin ni la, le ni muk timi, le timi aaŋuul fii, le ti buŋni.

ref: What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do.
text: Maah kan pu na sɔ: tiwan ni ŋan ke unii ŋa na le ye ke u ji ki nyu, ki li mɔɔni waah tun ki kan pu kimɔfageŋ ki Uwumbɔr di tii u na ni. Unibɔn aadoon le na.

ref: Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa tii unii likpal ni liwangol ki cha u ji naamɔɔn kan, u li dooni u, ki ji waah tun ki kan pu na aamɔɔn. Ni ye Uwumbɔr aapiin la.

ref: God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
text: Uwumbɔr aah tii u nsan ke u li kpa mpopiin na, waa ki jaa waah ga yunn dulnyaa wee ni pu na.

ref: There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth.
text: M kan dulnyaa wee ni ke ŋibamɔn gangal sakpiin le bi.

ref: God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
text: Uwumbɔr ga ŋmaa tii unii ubaa ŋimombil ni liyimbil, ni liwangol; mbamɔn, u ga ŋmaa tii u tiwan ni mɔmɔk u ban na, le kaan tee cha u ji tiwan ngbaan aamɔɔn. Unii uken le ga nan ji ni. Ni ye fam la, le kaa ŋan.

ref: You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial.
text: Uja ga ŋmaa li kpa mbim nkub, ki yunn pam, tɔ, u gee u yunn dulnyaa ni ba pu, u yaa kaa jin waamɔɔn, kaa kan likpuul li nyuun na kan, ubo u kpo una aaponn ni ki nyan ni na soor u.

ref: even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
text: Tɔ, u mu tee kan nin chee u ga fuur na, ki jer uja u jin ŋibin ŋichur ŋilee ki mu aa jin limɔfal aamɔɔn na; ba pu? bi mɔmɔk cha libubaan ni la.

ref: We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied.
text: Unii tun waatuln mɔk ke u kan nibaa ki ji la, le ki mu aan ŋmaa kan bab.

ref: We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right.
text: Ulandaan aa soor ujɔr. Ugiin aah ga ŋmaa ŋa pu ki li bi dulnyaa wee ni na, naa kpa u tinyoor tibaa.

ref: It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
text: Ni ye fam la; ni bi ke unii aah san dii libuln pu ke u chuu li na la. Cha aanimbil gbiin saah kpa ni na, ki taa muk aabaa n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke aa ki kan kpee.

ref: Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us.
text: Tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋani na nan kan naasisii n‑yoonn mu jer na la, le ti mɔmɔk nyi ke unii aan ŋmaa kpak unii u pɔɔ jer u na kinikpakpak.

ref: The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk?
text: N‑yoonn mumɔk aa bi kpak na, le ni moo ŋani si yɔli, kaa ter si.

ref: Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
text: Unii aan ŋmaa bee tiwan ni ŋan tii unibɔn, kimɔfageŋ ki kaa kpa tinyoor tibaa ki pinni jer ke kijunjuŋ na ni. Unii aan ŋmaa bee tiwan ni ga ŋa dulnyaa wee ni, waakun aapuwɔb na.

ref: A good reputation at the time of death is better than loving care at the time of birth.
text: Liyimbinyaan ŋan jer tulalee u nu mɔ na, le nwiin mundaal aa ga kpo na mu ŋan jer nwiin mundaal bi ma si na.

ref: Choose sorrow over laughter because a sad face may hide a happy heart.
text: Mpombiin soor ni tilaar, nibaakan mu ga bii aanimbil wɔb, tɔ, ni mu moo kpae si nlan la.

ref: Correction from someone wise is better by far than praise from fools.
text: Binib bi kpa nlan na yaa sak si kan, ni soor ni bilatiirb li gaa ilahn ki pak si.

ref: Foolish laughter is stupid. It sounds like thorns crackling in a fire.
text: Ujɔr yaa laa kan, ni naahn ke ikokon le aah puul mmii ni na. Naa kpa tataa.

ref: Something completed is better than something just begun; patience is better than too much pride.
text: Tiwan mɔmɔk aadoon ŋan jer naapiin. Limɔr ŋan jer kigaak.

ref: Only fools get angry quickly and hold a grudge.
text: Taa gee liŋuul mala mala; aa yaa gee unii pu liŋuul ki yunn kan, ni ye kijɔrk la.

ref: It isn't wise to ask, “Why is everything worse than it used to be?”
text: Taa baa daalbaadaal ke, “Ni ŋa kinye le n‑yaayoonn na aawan nan ŋan ki jer dandana wee aawan?” Naa ye nlan aabaan.

ref: Wisdom will protect you just like money; knowledge with good sense will lead you to life.
text: le mu ga tii si nsisiinyaan ke ŋimombil aah ga tii si pu na. Nlan tii si lifuur la, nlanbaekoo aanyoor le na.

ref: Think of what God has done! If God makes something crooked, can you make it straight?
text: Dakl lik Uwumbɔr aah tun pu na. Ubaa aan ŋmaa naar Uwumbɔr aah gɔr tiwan ni na.

ref: When times are good, you should be cheerful; when times are bad, think about what it means. God makes them both to keep us from knowing what will happen next. Some of Life's Questions
text: Tiwan yaa laa ŋan tii si kan, li kpa mpopiin, le tibɔr yaa nan dan kan, teer ke Uwumbɔr le joo ni mpopiin ni tibɔr mu. Saan ŋmaa bee tiwan ni mu ga ki ŋa na.

ref: I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper.
text: Maamɔfal ye mi fam la, le m mu tee kan tiwan mɔmɔk li ponn ni. Unibamɔnn ga ŋmaa kpo, le ubaa u ye utunwanbirdaan na ga li beenin chuun.

ref: So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart!
text: Kina pu na, taa bui ke aa li kpa tiŋann, bee nlan sakpen, ba ŋa aa bi ku aabaa?

ref: Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool.
text: Aa mu taa tee li kpa mbiin, bee aa li kpa kijɔrk sakpen. Taa ku aabaa ki laa fu.

ref: Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
text: Nyan aabaa nimina mɔmɔk ni. Aa yaa san Uwumbɔr kan, aa ga kan tinyoor.

ref: Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
text: Nlan aah ga ŋmaa tun lituln li na, bitinjoob kipiik aan ŋmaa tun kina.

ref: No one in this world always does right.
text: Ubaa aa bi dulnyaa wee ponn ni ki tun litunyaan n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kaa tun taani ubaa.

ref: Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you.
text: Taa cha aatafal li bi binib aabɔlen mɔmɔk ni, naa ye kina kan, aa ga nan ŋun saatutunn aah seei si pu na.

ref: Haven't you cursed many others?
text: Le aa nyi ke aa mu seei binib biken pam.

ref: I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me.
text: M di maalan le tɔŋ nimina mɔmɔk. M nan puu ke m ban m kan nlan la, le kina nan jer mi.

ref: The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep.
text: Ŋma ga ŋmaa bee limɔfal aatataa aah ye pu na? Naatataa pɔɔ pam ke ti bee ni.

ref: So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
text: Le m nan di maalandak mɔmɔk tii ichiin ni liwanbae; m nan puu ke m kan nlan ni ngarm ki tii mbaan mu m kpa na, ki bae mbiin aah ye kijɔrk ni ilatiir pu na.

ref: Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for.
text: M nan bee ke upii u kaa ŋan na cho jer nkun. Ngeehm mu u ga di tii si na ga chuu si ke gaawɔb, bee kipɔɔk aah ga chuu si pu na la. Le uŋaal aah kpal si pu na ga chuu si ke tikululn na. Uja u Uwumbɔr aasui piin u pu na ga ŋmar u chee, le u ga chuu utunwanbirdaan ma.

ref: With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together,
text: Ulandaan ngbaan len ke, mbamɔn, siib, siib le m ti kan nimina buyoonn m nan bi ban maabaan ngbaan aagarm na.

ref: but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman.
text: M nan ki ban ngarm muken, le kaa kan. M nan kan bijab lichur ponn ni uja ubaa baanja le kpa kipak, le kaa kan upii ma ubaa.

ref: I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
text: Maah nan bae pu na mɔmɔk sɔ: Uwumbɔr ŋa timi ke ti li bi mbimbin mu kaa pɔɔ na, le ti ŋa tibaa tiwan ni pɔɔ na.

ref: Who is smart enough to explain everything? Wisdom makes you cheerful and gives you a smile. Obey the King
text: Ulandaan baanja le nyi tiwan aatataa aah ye pu na. Nlan cha u laa limɔmumukl ki cha unimbil wiin. Kii ubɔr aamɔb

ref: If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise.
text: Ŋa ubɔr aah len pu na; ba pu? Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur tii u.

ref: Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind.
text: Ubɔr ga ŋmaa ŋa waah ban pu na, kina pu na, taa nya upuwɔb, ki taa dii binib bi kpokl u pu na.

ref: The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?”
text: Ubɔr joo mpɔɔn le tun, le ubaa aan ŋmaa kpak u.

ref: If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it.
text: Aa yaa keei waamɔb n‑yoonn mɔmɔk kan, saan li bi tibɔbir ni. Ulandaan nyi ke libɔjil aayoonn le bi.

ref: Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything,
text: Tiwan nimɔk ŋa na kpa naatataa, ki mu kpa n‑yoonn mu ŋeer ni na. Le binib mu kan tibɔr ti wu na.

ref: We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil.
text: Ubaa aan ŋmaa ter ubaa ki taa kpo, bee u kpeln waakun aawiin. Baan kii ke uja san nya butɔb ni, kina le titunwanbir aan nya utunwanbirdaan nkun ni. Bibiindam, ni binib bi aabimbin ŋan na aabɔr

ref: I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another? Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
text: Maah nan kal ki dakl lik tiwan ni ŋani dulnyaa, u ponn ni binib bibaa kpa mpɔɔn, biken mu ji falaa bi chee na ni, le m nan kan nimina mɔmɔk.

ref: I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense.
text: Mbamɔn, m kan bi sub bibiindam baakaakul ni, tɔ, taah nyan kicheek ni ki choo kun ni na le binib pak bi, kitiŋ ki ponn ni bi tun baatunwanbir na. Ni ye fam la.

ref: When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime.
text: Ba ŋa binib gee ki tun titunwanbir? Naah ye pu na le ye ke baa dar titunwanbirdam aatafal mala ke baah tun ti pu na.

ref: They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying: Everyone who lives right and respects God will prosper,
text: Utunwanbirdaan ga ŋmaa bii libiil nfum nkub ki beenin chuun. Mbamɔn, m nyi baah len pu na ke, “Aa yaa kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb kan, aa ŋmar a,

ref: but no one who sins and rejects God will prosper or live very long.
text: bibiindam ma kan aan kan kina. Baamɔfal bi ke kijunjuŋ na la, le baah kaa kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na, bi ga kpo baabiyar ni.”

ref: There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens.
text: Tɔ, nimina aa kpa tataa. Lik tiwan ni ŋani dulnyaa ni na: binib bibaa aabimbin ŋan, le bi kani bibiindam aatafadaan; le bibiindam bibaa mu kani binib bi aabimbin ŋan na aapar. Le m bui ke ni ye fam la.

ref: So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
text: Kina pu na, m kii ke unibɔn li mɔɔni, ba pu? waamɔɔn mu u kpa waamɔfal ni na le ye ke u ji, ki nyu, ki li mɔɔni. Buyoonn u bi nyani waatotoŋ Uwumbɔr aah tii u limɔfal li dulnyaa wee ni na, le u ga ŋmaa ŋa kina.

ref: Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world.
text: N‑yoonn mumɔk m pɔɔni mbaa ke m ŋa nlan ki bae tiwan ni ŋani dulnyaa wee ni na, le m kan ke aa ga ŋmaa li dɔ waa kinyeek ni nwiin pu,

ref: I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
text: kaan ŋmaa bee Uwumbɔr aah ŋani tiwan ni na. Aa gee aa pɔɔn aabaa ba pu, saan bee ni daalbaadaal. Bilandam ga ŋmaa bui ke bi nyi, ki mu aa nyi.

ref: I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad.
text: M nan kal dakl pam le ni ti yunn, ki lik tiwan nimina, le ki ti kan ke Uwumbɔr le joo bilandam ni binib bi aabimbin ŋan na aabimbin mɔmɔk. Uma le joo baageehm ni baananaŋ mu. Ubaa aa nyi tiwan ni dɔ kiir u na.

ref: But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
text: Ni mɔmɔk ye tiwanbaan la. Ubimbinyaandaan ni ubiindaan aadoon ye tiwanbaan la, kina le ye ni ki tii uninyaan ni u kaa ŋan na mu. Binib bi dii Uwumbɔr aasan mbamɔm na, ni bi kaa dii kpala na, ni binib bi toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr na, ni bi kaa toor na mɔmɔk aadoon ye mubaa la. Ubimbinyaandaan aa soor utunwanbirdaan. Unii u puur tipuur na aa soor unii u kaa puur tipuur na.

ref: It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die.
text: Bi mɔmɔk aadoon ye mubaa la, le nimina mu aa ŋan ke tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋani dulnyaa wee ni na aah kaa ŋan pu na. Unibɔn umɔk kpa limɔfal na kpa kiwaatiik ni ilandak i kaa ŋan na la, le nkun piir bi libuul ngbaan ni.

ref: As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
text: Tɔ, unii umɔk kpa limɔfal dulnyaa wee ni na kpa limakl. Ubɔ u fu na soor ni uchinn u kpo na.

ref: We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten.
text: Mbamɔn, umɔfadaan mɔk nyi ke u ga nan kpo, le bitekpiib ma aa nyi nibaa. Baa ki kpa tipar tibaa; binib suln bibɔr kookoo a.

ref: Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
text: Bi ni baageehm, ni baananaŋ, ni lineen kpaan kpo la. Baan ki ŋa tiwan ni ŋani dulnyaa wee ni na nibaa.

ref: So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do.
text: Li ji saajikaar ki li kpa mpopiin; nyu saadaan ki cha aasui li piin. Ni ŋan Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best.
text: Cha aasui li piin n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki di nkpan meen aayil pu.

ref: Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth.
text: Cha aa ni upii u aa gee u na ji mmɔɔn saamɔfal li kaa kpa tinyoor tibaa aan Uwumbɔr di tii si dulnyaa wee ni na. Ji mmɔɔn nwiin mɔk, ba pu? saatotoŋ aanyoor le na.

ref: Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
text: Aa yaa bi tun lituln limɔk na kan, di saapɔɔn mɔmɔk tun li, ba pu? lituln, ni ilandak, ni ichiin, ni Uwumbɔr do aalan aa bi kitekpiitiŋ ni. Nima chee mu le aa cha.

ref: Here is something else I have learned: The fastest runners and the greatest heroes don't always win races and battles. Wisdom, intelligence, and skill don't always make you healthy, rich, or popular. We each have our own share of misfortune.
text: M nan ki kan tiwan niken, nima le ye ke naa ye binib bi ŋmaa san sakpen na le ji litaasaln ni, le bijakaab mu aa nyaŋni butɔb ni n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Bilandam mu aa kpa tijikaar n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, le binib bi bae tiwan ki nyi sakpen na aa kani nkam. Binib bi ŋmaa joo tiwan na aa kani tininkpir n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Kinimbɔŋ kani unii mɔmɔk la.

ref: None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap. Better To Be Wise than Foolish
text: Ubaa aa nyi buyoonn nkun ga pii u na. Nkun bub chur unii ke gaawɔb, bee kipɔɔk aah chur inyoon pu aan yaa nyi na la. Nlan jer mpɔɔn

ref: Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me.
text: Tiwan nibaa mu nan ki bi m kan ni, tiwan ni m ga ŋmaa di ni ŋaŋ baah lik nlan dulnyaa wee ni pu na.

ref: It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls.
text: Kitiŋ kibaa le nan bi, le binib bi nan koo ki ponn ni na aa wiir. Ubɔr mpɔɔndaan ubaa nan ti tak ki. U nan gob ki, ki gor ke u tur kaagon lii.

ref: But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten.
text: Ujagiin ubaa nan koo ki ponn ni, le ki mu nan tee kpa nlan sakpen ki gaa kitiŋ ngbaan lii. Tɔ, ubaa mu aa nan teer ujagiin ngbaan bɔr.

ref: So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
text: M len n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke nlan ŋan jer mpɔɔn, le ubaa aa nyi ke ugiin mu kpa nlan. Ubaa aatafal aa bi waah len pu na ni.

ref: Words of wisdom spoken softly make much more sense than the shouts of a ruler to a crowd of fools.
text: Aa yaa pel ulandaan aalambil li bi suuna na kan, ni ŋan jer ke aa pel uyidaan u bi tar bijɔrb aakuun ni na.

ref: Wisdom is more powerful than weapons, yet one mistake can destroy all the good you have done.
text: Nlan ŋan jer tijawan, le utunwanbirdaan ubaa ga ŋmaa bii tiwanyaan pam.

ref: A few dead flies in perfume make all of it stink, and a little foolishness outweighs a lot of wisdom.
text: Ŋisibikpol ga ŋmaa cha kpalba u gbii tulalee na nuŋ. Le kijɔrk siib kina ga ŋmaa bii nlan sakpem.

ref: Sensible thoughts lead you to do right; foolish thoughts lead you to do wrong.
text: Ni ye Uwumbɔr do aawan le ke ulandaan tun litunyaan, le ujɔr mu tun ni kaa ŋan na.

ref: Fools show their stupidity by the way they live; it's easy to see they have no sense.
text: Ujɔr aah ŋani pu na le mɔk ke waa kpa nlan. Binib mɔmɔk beer ke u ye ujɔr la.

ref: Don't give up your job when your boss gets angry. If you stay calm, you'll be forgiven.
text: Saatindaan yaa gee aa pu liŋuul kan, taa kpaan bui ke saa ki ye waatutunn. Aa yaa sɔŋ aalan kan, taani sakpiin ga ŋmaa kan chapinn.

ref: Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair:
text: Ŋibamɔn gangal i m kan binib bi joo ntim chee na sɔ:

ref: They honor fools, but dishonor the rich;
text: bi joo mpɔɔn aasisii tii bijɔrb, le ki suln biwankpadam bɔr.

ref: they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
text: M kan binaagbiib dik itaan pu, le bipɔɔndam chuun bitaa pu ke binaagbiib na.

ref: If you dig a pit, you might fall in; if you break down a wall, a snake might bite you.
text: Aa yaa gbii libuul bil kan, sin le ga nan lir li ponn ni. Aa yaa saa kar ligoln lii kan, uwaa le ga juu si.

ref: You could even get hurt by chiseling a stone or chopping a log.
text: Aa yaa tun lituln baah kpii ŋifakuu nin chee na kan, aa gbeer ŋifakuu la. Aa yaa lar idɔ kan, nima chee le aa kani titotonn.

ref: If you don't sharpen your ax, it will be harder to use; if you are wise, you'll know what to do.
text: Saachɔk yaa kaa ka, aa yii kaa luun ki kan, aa tun le ki ti bak. Aa yaa puen ŋa ilandak ki nin tun saatuln kan, ni ŋan sakpen.

ref: The power to charm a snake does you no good if it bites you anyway.
text: Aa yaa cha uwaa puen juu si waahr aan aa nin bui ke aa kpa nnyɔk mu ga jɔr u na kan, ni ye fam la.

ref: If you talk sensibly, you will have friends; if you talk foolishly, you will destroy yourself.
text: Ulandaan aamɔliin tii u liyimbil la, le ujɔr ma aamɔliin ku u.

ref: Fools begin with nonsense, and their stupid chatter ends with disaster.
text: U di ilatiir le di piin, le ki ti di kiwaatiik doo.

ref: They never tire of talking, but none of us really know what the future will bring.
text: Ujɔr aabɔr aa kpa ndoon. Ubaa aa nyi tiwan ni ki ga ŋa na. Le ubaa mu aan ŋmaa bui timi tiwan ni ga ŋa timi aakun aapuwɔb na.

ref: Fools wear themselves out— they don't know enough to find their way home.
text: Ulatiir u kaa nyi udo aasan na le ga di lituln ku ubaa.

ref: A country is in for trouble when its ruler is childish, and its leaders party all day long.
text: Kitiŋ ki aabɔr ye unachipɔɔn, aan kaasalolm mu ji njim ki ti woln kitaak na bi tibɔr ni la.

ref: But a nation will prosper when its ruler is mature, and its leaders don't party too much.
text: Tɔ, kitiŋ ki aabɔr ŋani ubaa aalandak, aan kaasalolm mu ji baajikaar tijikaar aajim aayoonn, ki joo bibaa mbamɔm kaa nyu ndaan gbii na, kpa nsisiinyaan.

ref: Some people are too lazy to fix a leaky roof— then the house collapses.
text: Uja yaa kpa ligbanyakl kaan pin waadiik kan, ki ga lun, le ki lir.

ref: Eating and drinking make you feel happy, and money can buy everything you need.
text: Njim tii si mpopiin le ndaan cha aa kpa nsuupiin, aa mu aan ŋmaa kan nimina kaa nya ŋimombil.

ref: Don't let yourself think about cursing the king; don't curse the rich, not even in secret. A little bird might hear and tell everything.
text: Taa loon ki su ubɔr aapuwɔb, ki taa koo saadiik ni ki su unii u ye uwankpadaan na aapuwɔb. Nibaakan, unyoon le ga di tibɔr ngbaan buen ti tuk bi saah len pu na.

ref: Share what you have with seven or eight others, because you never know when disaster may strike.
text: Taa joo saawangol tii lipepel libaa baanja, li tii ŋipepel mɔmɔk, ba pu? saa nyi kinimbɔŋ ki aa ga kan dulnyaa wee ni na.

ref: If you worry about the weather and don't plant seeds, you won't harvest a crop.
text: Aa yaa ka kii ke libuln ni mbimbin ti ŋeer kan, saan bu nibaa, kaan chee nibaa mu.

ref: No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
text: Uwumbɔr le naan tiwan mɔmɔk, le saan ki ŋmaa bee waah tun pu na, ke saah kaan ŋmaa bee ubo aah naani upudaan aapuul ponn ni pu na.

ref: Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce. Youth and Old Age
text: Li bu saajikaabim kichakpiik ni, ni kijook mu. Saan ŋmaa bee ke ni mɔmɔk ga nan ŋa aan naan ŋa, kaan ki ŋmaa bee kichakpiik ni, ni kijook yaan ni ga ŋa jer niken na.

ref: Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun.
text: Ni ŋan ke aa li fu ki kani nwiin aawiihn.

ref: Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
text: Li dooni Uwumbɔr libiln limɔk aa jin na pu. Aa gee aa yunn dulnyaa wee ponn ni ba pu, li nyi ke aa ga nan yunn nkun ni ki jer kina. N‑yoonn mu choo na aabɔr mɔmɔk ye fam la. Binib bi laa diin na aasurm

ref: Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
text: Binib bi laa diin na, li ji tinachipɔnn ni tisapɔnn man. Li kpa mpopiin buyoonn ni laa pɔɔ na. Li ŋani naah ban ni ŋa pu na, ki li ŋani nisui aageehn, ki tee li teer ke Uwumbɔr ga ji nimi tibɔr nimi aatuln mɔmɔk pu la.

ref: Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
text: Taa cha tiwan nibaa li muk si ki tii si iween. Saapɔnn aan ki yunn sakpen.

ref: Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
text: Kina pu na, saah laa pɔɔn na, li teer Uwumbɔr u naan si na bɔr, waahr aan aa nin por, buyoonn aa ga nan bui ke, “Nsui aa ki piin.”

ref: Someday the light of the sun and the moon and the stars will all seem dim to you. Rain clouds will remain over your head.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le nwiin, ni uŋmal, ni iŋmabi aan ki li wiihn aa chee. Utaal aataalangbam mu ga ki gir ni ki ŋa mbɔmbɔɔn.

ref: The noisy grinding of grain and the voices of singers will be shut out by your deaf ears, but even the song of a bird will keep you awake.
text: Aatafal ga kpaa, kaan ki li ŋun kitiŋ ponn ni aafuuk pu. Hali kinaak yaa nan kan, saan li ŋun kaafuuk pu mbamɔm, kaan li ŋun ŋigangan mu pu mbamɔm. Le unyoon aawiil ma ga finn si ngeen pu.

ref: You will be afraid to climb up a hill or walk down a road. Your hair will turn as white as almond blossoms. You will feel lifeless and drag along like an old grasshopper. We each go to our eternal home, and the streets here are filled with those who mourn.
text: Aa ga li san ke aa tɔŋ tiwan ni fɔk paacham na ijawaan, le lisachuln ga li ye tiwan ni bir na le aa chee. Aayikpir ga piir, le saan ki ŋmaa yoor aataa paacham ki chuun. Lineen mɔmɔk ga nya aa chee. Ti cha timi aakookoo aafuur chee la, le ikpowiil ga li bi kitiŋ ponn ni.

ref: The silver cord snaps, the golden bowl breaks; the water pitcher is smashed, and the pulley at the well is shattered.
text: Tikunabr aaneeleen na ga kii, le salmaa aakaryaa na ga lir ki wii. Ŋŋmin mu bi liboln pu na ga kii, le goomaa ga wii yuk yuk.

ref: So our bodies return to the earth, and the life-giving breath returns to God.
text: Timi aawon ga ki gir kpaln kitiŋ aatan, le limɔfal aafuurk ga gir buen Uwumbɔr u di li tii timi na chee.

ref: Nothing makes sense. I have seen it all— nothing makes sense. Respect and Obey God
text: Ulandaan ngbaan bui ke, “Fam, fam, ni mɔmɔk ye fam la.” Kookoo aabɔr

ref: I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied.
text: Tɔ, ulandaan ngbaan aah nan kpa nlan na, u nan beenin joo waah nyi pu na mɔk binib. U nan bae ŋiyataŋak le ki tɔŋ ŋaabamɔn mbamɔm ki lik.

ref: Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
text: Ulandaan ngbaan nan pɔɔn ubaa ke u kan nsuudoon aamɔboln, le waah nan ŋmee pu na ye ibamɔn.

ref: Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together.
text: Bilandam aamɔbon naahn bipihkpaab aah joo ŋidabil ŋi aamɔi ka aan bi joo kiir baapiih na la. Le ŋiyataŋak ŋi bi ŋmee ŋi bil na yunn, ke kipinbik ki bi kpaa ki mbamɔm na. Uwumbɔr u kpaa ti mɔmɔk na le di ŋi tii ni.

ref: My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these. There is no end to books, and too much study will wear you out.
