text: Maabo, tiwan ki bi ke aa li nyi nibɔr. Tigbann aaŋmeen aa kpa ndoon, le aa yaa bae sakpen kan, aa ga ti bak la.

ref: Everything you were taught can be put into a few words: Respect and obey God! This is what life is all about.
text: Nimina mɔmɔk aapuwɔb na, tiwan nibaa baanja le gur ti len naabɔr. Li san Uwumbɔr, ki li dii waakaal, ba pu? kina pu le u nan naan unibɔn.

ref: God will judge everything we do, even what is done in secret, whether good or bad.
text: Uwumbɔr ga ji timi tibɔr, timi aatun mɔmɔk pu. U ga ji timi tibɔr, timi aatunyaan, ni ŋi kaa ŋan na, ni taah tun ŋi libɔɔl ni na pu.

ref: This is Solomon's most beautiful song. She Speaks:
text: Solomonn aalahmɔɔn i kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na. Njan aalahn Upii aalahn

ref: Kiss me tenderly! Your love is better than wine,
text: Aa joo aamɔb moor nwon mɔmɔk la; saabɔngeehm mɔ jer ŋisubil aadaan.

ref: and you smell so sweet. All the young women adore you; the very mention of your name is like spreading perfume. *
text: Saabaan nu mɔ sakpen a; le bi yaa yin saayimbil kan, mbaan ngbaan nyani. Upii mɔk gee si la.

ref: Hurry, my king! Let's hurry. Take me to your home. The Young Women Speak: We are happy for you! And we praise your love even more than wine. She Speaks: Young women of Jerusalem, it is only right that you should adore him.
text: Yoor mi, ki cha ti san; li ye maabɔr, ki di mi buen saadiik ni. Ti ga li kpaan koo le ni mɔ timi, ki ga nyu ndaan taah gee pu na, le ki mɔk tɔb taah gee tɔb pu na. Ni sil ye mbamɔn ke upii mɔk gee si.

ref: My skin is dark and beautiful, like a tent in the desert or like Solomon's curtains.
text: Jerusalem aapiib, m bɔn le ki ŋan, m bɔn ke Kedar aateersakpiin ni aakeken aaboo na la, le ki tee ŋan jer Solomonn aabɔrchiln ni aakeken ŋi lee tidir aabisamɔi na.

ref: Don't stare at me just because the sun has darkened my skin. My brothers were angry with me; they made me work in the vineyard, and so I neglected my complexion.
text: Taa lik seeni mi maabɔmbɔn pu man, nwiin le seer mi, le m bɔnn kina. Nninjatiib le nan gee m pu liŋuul ki cha m tun lituln ŋisubil aasaak ni. Maa nan kpa n‑yoonn ke m di toor mbaa.

ref: My darling, I love you! Where do you feed your sheep and let them rest at noon? Don't let the other shepherds think badly of me. I'm not one of those women who shamelessly follow after shepherds. He Speaks:
text: Mbɔɔn, tuk mi saah ga di saawakor buen nin chee aan ti ti ŋmɔ timoor na. La chee aan saawakor ga nan baŋ nwiin pu? Naa ŋan ke m nan li bi ban si bipihdam biken ponn ni. Uja aalahn

ref: My dearest, if you don't know, just follow the path of the sheep. Then feed your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
text: Upii nyanyaan, saa nyi nima chee ee? Saa nyi kan, li dii tiwakor cha; li kii saaŋoob biwakodam aaboo chee.

ref: You move as gracefully as the pony that leads the chariot of the king.
text: Mbɔɔn, sin le ye upii nyanyaan, ki ŋan ke ijipt aabɔr aataan aah ŋan pu na.

ref: Earrings add to your beauty, and you wear a necklace of precious stones.
text: Tafajɔnjɔn ti bi aatafal pu na cha aa ŋan sakpen, Nleenyaan mu bi aasil pu tii si kinyaan pam.

ref: Let's make you some jewelry of gold, woven with silver. She Speaks:
text: Le ti ga ŋa salmaa aaleen mu ŋmar tikunabr aakur na tii si. Upii aalahn

ref: My king, while you were on your couch, my aroma was a magic charm.
text: Maabɔr nan dɔ waayikukul aajal pu, le maatulalee aanunun gaa ni mɔmɔk.

ref: My darling, you are perfume between my breasts;
text: Mbɔɔn yaa dɔ paa m pu kan, waabaam nu mɔ ke mir aatulalee na la.

ref: you are flower blossoms from the gardens of En-Gedi. He Speaks:
text: Mbɔɔn nu mɔ ke timoor ni aasupuun mu poor ki bi Enn Gedi aasubil aasar ni na la. Uja aalahn

ref: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— your eyes are those of a dove. She Speaks:
text: Mbɔɔn, aa ŋan sakpen a; le aanimbil ponn ni kpa ngeehm. Upii aalahn

ref: My love, you are handsome, truly handsome— the fresh green grass will be our wedding bed
text: Mbɔɔn unyaan, saanyaan nyaŋ a; le aa tii mi mpopiin. Timosɔnn le ga li ye timi aawandookaan,

ref: in the shade of cedar and cypress trees.
text: santina tiib le ye timi aadichal aalɔkdɔ, le lisalaasiil aasui bii ti pu.

ref: I am merely a rose from the land of Sharon, a lily from the valley. He Speaks:
text: M ye Saronn aafataŋ ni aasupuun la, m ye nsupuun le ki bi lijool aafataŋ ni. Uja aalahn

ref: My darling, when compared with other young women, you are a lily among thorns. She Speaks:
text: Mbɔɔn bi bipiib biken ni ke nsupuun aah ŋmal ikokon ni pu na la. Upii aalahn

ref: And you, my love, are an apple tree among trees of the forest. Your shade brought me pleasure; your fruit was sweet.
text: Mbɔɔn unyaan bi bijab biken ni ke linyɔkl aasub aah bi pu kichook aasui ni na la. M gee ke m li kaa bu aaboon ni, le bu aasubil mɔ m chee pam.

ref: You led me to your banquet room and showered me with love.
text: U di mi koon ni waajim aanaakook ni, le ki di waageehm mɔk mi nima.

ref: Put your left hand under my head and embrace me with your right arm.
text: Uŋangan kul n‑yil la, le uŋangii kpaal nwon mɔmɔk.

ref: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles never to awaken love before it is ready. Winter Is Past She Speaks:
text: Jerusalem aapiib, puu tii mi man, puu upeeman ni upeeyun i bi timoor ni na pu ke naan bɔ timi aabɔtiik aabɔr ni. Lelee aalahn Upii aalahn

ref: I hear the voice of the one I love, as he comes leaping over mountains and hills
text: M ŋun mbɔɔn aaneel pu. U nyan ni ŋijoo paab le ki san ni, u san nyan ni ŋigongon ni le ki choo m chee.

ref: like a deer or a gazelle. Now he stands outside our wall, looking through the window
text: Mbɔɔn naahn upeeyun la, u naahn lipeemanbil la. Uma le ti si tab ligoln na. U baani takolu ni le ki lik, le ki biini takolu aakekeln ki lik ni.

ref: and speaking to me. He Speaks: My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
text: Mbɔɔn len m chee tibɔr. Uja aalahn Mbɔɔn, kina kan, dan; mbɔɔn unyaan, cha ti li cha.

ref: Winter is past, the rain has stopped;
text: Libuln aa ki daar; utaal mu fir a;

ref: flowers cover the earth, it's time to sing. The cooing of doves is heard in our land.
text: le nsupuun poor timoor ni. Lilahngaal aayoonn sɔ; ŋinanjel bi gaa ilahn ikpaakon ni la.

ref: Fig trees are bearing fruit, while blossoms on grapevines fill the air with perfume. My darling, I love you! Let's go away together.
text: Ŋikakan bi puir la; ndaan aasubil aanunun gaa ni mɔmɔk a. Mbɔɔn, kina kan, dan; mbɔɔn unyaan, cha ti li cha.

ref: You are my dove hiding among the rocks on the side of a cliff. Let me see how lovely you are! Let me hear the sound of your melodious voice.
text: Aa naahn linanjel li bɔrni litakpal aaloŋ ni na la. Cha m lik aanimbil wɔb, aanimbil wɔb ŋan sakpen. Cha m pel saaneel pu, saaneel mɔ sakpen.

ref: Our vineyards are in blossom; we must catch the little foxes that destroy the vineyards. She Speaks:
text: Chuu iŋɔk, chuu iŋɔk waatiir ngbaan waahr aan i nin bii timi aasubil aasaak ki bi ŋeeni na. Upii aalahn

ref: My darling, I am yours, and you are mine, as you feed your sheep among the lilies.
text: Mbɔɔn ye min yoo la, le m mu ye u yoo. U kpiini waawakor nsupuun ponn ni la,

ref: Pretend to be a young deer dancing on mountain slopes until daylight comes and shadows fade away.
text: le lichakpitaawoln aabuln ti daa ni, le mbɔmbɔɔn mu doo. Mbɔɔn, gir mala ke upeeyun na, gir ni mala ke Beter aajoo pu aapeemanbil na.

ref: While in bed at night, I reached for the one I love with heart and soul. I looked for him, but he wasn't there.
text: Maah doo geeni maawandookaan pu kinyeek mɔmɔk na, m daŋni maah gee u na pu la; m nan bi ban u, le kaa ŋmaa kan u.

ref: So I searched through the town for the one I love. I looked on every street, but he wasn't there.
text: M nan chuun kpak kitiŋ ponn ni, m nan chuun kaasan, ni nsanbim mɔmɔk ni. M nan chuun ban maah gee u na la. M nan ban u, kaa kan u.

ref: I even asked the guards patrolling the town, “Have you seen the one I love so much?”
text: Bikikiib bi nan chuun manni kitiŋ ni na nan kan mi. M nan baa bi ke, “Ni kan mbɔɔn aa?”

ref: Right after that, I found him. I held him and would not let go until I had taken him to the home of my mother.
text: Le maah kpaan siir bi chee na, le m kan u. M nan bub chuu u, kaan ki di u lii, le u ti nin fuu nna aadiik ni, kidiik ki ponn ni bi nan ma mi na.

ref: Young women of Jerusalem, promise me by the power of deer and gazelles, never to awaken love before it is ready. The Groom and the Wedding Party Their Friends Speak:
text: Jerusalem aapiib, puu tii mi man; puu upeeman ni upeeyun i bi timoor ni na pu ke naan bɔ timi aabɔtiik aabɔr ni. Taataa aalahn Upii aalahn

ref: What do we see approaching from the desert like a cloud of smoke? With it comes the sweet smell of spices, including myrrh and frankincense.
text: Ni ye ba ki nyan ni nteersakpiin wɔb ki naahn iŋmanyuu sakpiin, ki kpa tulalee ni mir aatulalee aabaan, ke tulalee u biwantiirb kooh u na?

ref: It is King Solomon carried on a throne, surrounded by sixty of Israel's best soldiers.
text: Solomonn, le bi tu u waabɔrjal pu choo; Israel aajab bi nyi butɔb aabɔr mbamɔm ki ye bijab bi kii u na ponn ni imonko itaa le dii u.

ref: Its posts are silver, the back is gold, and the seat is covered with purple cloth. You women of Jerusalem have taken great care to furnish the inside.
text: Bi di tikunabr le boon idɔ i bi joo tui li na; le ki di salmaa aakokonn gbaŋ likekeln li paa li pu na. Bi di ŋitan ŋi man ki bɔn timm na le di ŋa likekeln gob li, Jerusalem aapiib le gbaŋ li ni kinyaan ŋmeen.

ref: Now come and see the crown given to Solomon by his mother on his happy wedding day.
text: Sionn aapiib, dan nan lik man ubɔr Solomonn. U chik kibɔryikpupuk ki una nan di chiŋ uyil pu waabɔndinn daal, nwiin mu nan ye waapopiin ni mmɔɔn daal na la. Uja aalahn

ref: My darling, you are lovely, so very lovely— as you look through your veil, your eyes are those of a dove. Your hair tosses about as gracefully as goats coming down from Gilead.
text: Mbɔɔn, saanyaan ti nyaŋ sakpen a. Aa di kiyibubuuk biin aanimbil wɔb, le saabɔngeehm beenin kpii ni. Saayikpir gbeeni ke iŋoob le aah san sunn ni Gilead aagongon na.

ref: Your teeth are whiter than sheep freshly washed; they match perfectly, not one is missing.
text: Aanyin piin ke ipiih i bi laa fu i bukiib ni nnyun na la. Ŋi ponn ni libaa aa fenn; ŋi mɔmɔk ŋak tɔb deedee la.

ref: Your lips are crimson cords, your mouth is shapely; behind your veil are hidden beautiful rosy cheeks.
text: Aamɔgban bi ke litamaln na, le aa yaa len tibɔr kan, ŋi ŋan sakpen. Kiyibubuuk bii aanimbil wɔb, le aatakpiln beenin moor ni lak lak.

ref: Your neck is more graceful than the tower of David, decorated with thousands of warriors' shields.
text: Aasil joon ki bi mɔlb ke David aakikiib aadifɔfɔŋ na la, le nneeleen mu bi ke kijaak aapen lichur na gbin mu pu.

ref: Your breasts are perfect; they are twin deer feeding among lilies.
text: Saabii naahn ipeeyun la, ki bi ke ipeeman jaan le aah si nsupuun ponn ni ki ŋmɔ timoor na.

ref: I will hasten to those hills sprinkled with sweet perfume and stay there till sunrise.
text: M ga li bi mir aatulalee aagongoln pu la, le lichakpitaawoln aabuln ti daa ni, le mbɔmbɔɔn mu ti doo.

ref: My darling, you are lovely in every way.
text: Mbɔɔn, saanyaan ti nyaŋ sakpen a; saa kpa ŋeen aatɔ.

ref: My bride, together we will leave Lebanon! We will say goodbye to the peaks of Mount Amana, Senir, and Hermon, where lions and leopards live in the caves.
text: Maabɔndinn, nyan ni Lebanonn Aajoo ni ki dan ti li cha; nyan ni Lebanonn ki dan ti li cha. Sunn ni Amana Aajool paab, nyan ni Senir, ni Hemonn aajoo paab, nin chee ichinn ni inaamuun koo na.

ref: My bride, my very own, you have stolen my heart! With one glance from your eyes and the glow of your necklace, you have stolen my heart.
text: Maabɔngeehn ni maabɔndinn, nlaasaab bi aanimbil, ni nneeleen mu aa gbin na ni la.

ref: Your love is sweeter than wine; the smell of your perfume is more fragrant than spices.
text: Maabɔngeehn ni maabɔndinn, saageehm tii mi mpopiin la. Saageehm mɔ jer ŋisubil aadaan mɔmɔk; le saatulalee nu mɔ jer tulalee mɔmɔk.

ref: Your lips are a honeycomb; milk and honey flow from your tongue. Your dress has the aroma of cedar trees from Lebanon.
text: Mbɔɔn, aamɔgban mirk ke tisiir na la; le aalambil bi ke nnaabiin ni tisiir na m chee. Saawanpeenkaan kpa Lebanonn aatulalee mɔmɔk aanunun.

ref: My bride, my very own, you are a garden, a fountain closed off to all others.
text: Maabɔngeehn ni maabɔndinn ye kisaak ki bɔr na la, u ye kisaak ki bi maa ligoln gob ki na, ki ye unibaan aanyunbun.

ref: You are a spring in the garden, a fountain of pure water, and a refreshing stream from Mount Lebanon. She Speaks:
text: Uyayak aanyunbun le tii kisaak ngbaan nnyun, le nnyun puu nyan ni Lebanonn Aajoo mu ni ki choo ki ponn ni. Upii aalahn

ref: Let the north wind blow, the south wind too! Let them spread the aroma of my garden, so the one I love may enter and taste its delicious fruits.
text: Ŋŋangan wɔb aabuln, finn ngeen pu. Ŋŋangii wɔb aabuln, daa maasaak pu. Cha nnun mu mɔ na gaa ni mɔmɔk. Cha mbɔɔn dan waasaak ni ki nan moo kaasubil ŋi mɔ na. Uja aalahn

ref: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:
text: Maabɔngeehn ni maabɔndinn, m koo maasaak ponn ni la. M bi nyani maatulalee aakpiin ni mir la; m bi ji maasiinyun ni nsiikpan la; m bi nyu maasubil aadaan ni nnaabiin la. Bipiib aalahn Bɔtiib, li ji ki nyu man ki ti saa buyoonn mbɔngeehm ga gbii nimi na. Nanaa aalahn Upii aalahn

ref: I was asleep, but dreaming: The one I love was at the door, knocking and saying, “My darling, my very own, my flawless dove, open the door for me! My head is drenched with evening dew.”
text: Maah nan dɔ geen na, nsui ma nan waa la. M nan daŋ tidaŋ ke mbɔɔn dan nan kpaar maajaaleŋ pu. Uja aalahn Mbɔɔn, maabɔngeehn, ni maananjel, cha m koo ni. Limaln le sɔŋ n‑yil, le likpakpal mu sɔŋ n‑yikpir. Upii aalahn

ref: But I had already undressed and bathed my feet. Should I dress again and get my feet dirty?
text: M puun gbabr maakeken a; maan ki ŋmaa di ŋi gbab. M puun finn ntaa a; maan ki cha ŋi ŋa tijɔŋ.

ref: Then my darling's hand reached to open the latch, and my heart stood still.
text: Mbɔɔn nan di uŋaal meeh jaaleŋ, le ni ŋa mi ke waah duun ni mi le na.

ref: And I yearned for him while he spoke to me, but when I opened the door, my darling had disappeared. I searched and shouted, but I could not find him— there was no answer.
text: M nan chuu piir jaaleŋ ke mbɔɔn koo ni, le ki muin u puun siir a. M nan neen ke m ŋun uneel pu sakpen; m nan ban u, le kaa kan u. M nan yin u, le kaa ŋun u pu.

ref: Then I was found by the guards patrolling the town and guarding the wall. They beat me up and stripped off my robe.
text: Bikikiib bi nan chuun manni kitiŋ ni na nan kan mi; bi nan gbaa mi ki lakr nwon; bikikiib bi nan kii kitiŋ ngbaan aagoln na nan daa per maayibubuuk.

ref: Young women of Jerusalem, if you find the one I love, please say to him, “She is weak with desire.” Their Friends Speak:
text: Jerusalem aapiib, puu tii mi man ke ni yaa kan mbɔɔn kan, ni ga bui u ke maah neen pu ke m kan u na yɔl nwon mɔmɔk a. Bipiib aalahn

ref: Most beautiful of women, why is the one you love more special than others? Why do you ask us to tell him how you feel? She Speaks:
text: Upii u ŋan jer bipiib mɔmɔk na, aabɔɔn aabimbin ni biken yaan aa kpaan la aa? U kpa lijinjiir aawan nilani aan aa bui ke ti puu tii si? Upii aalahn

ref: He is handsome and healthy, the most outstanding among ten thousand.
text: Mbɔɔn ŋan le ki pɔɔ; binib ŋichur kipiik ni kan, aa ga kan waaboln ubaa la.

ref: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy, black as a raven.
text: Unimbil wɔb joon kpal kpal, le ki man chaun ke tikumann na; uyikpir ŋan, le ki bɔn chin chin ke likakaal na.

ref: His face is a garden of sweet-smelling spices; his lips are lilies dripping with perfume.
text: Utakpin ŋan ke kisaak ki ponn ni kpa tulalee aasufabir mɔmɔk aabɔŋ na la. Umɔgban bi ke nsupuun na la, le mir aatulalee sɔŋ ŋi.

ref: His legs are columns of marble on feet of gold. He stands there majestic like Mount Lebanon and its choice cedar trees.
text: Utaapan bi ke ŋitakpanyaan piin aajaatɔlk aah tɔk salmaa pu pu na la. U si chab ke Lebanonn aajoo ŋi kpa santina aasui fɔfɔk na.

ref: His kisses are sweet. I desire him so much! Young women of Jerusalem, he is my lover and friend.
text: M yaa moor umɔb kan, ni mirk la; waawan mɔmɔk cha m moo neen u la. Jerusalem aapiib, mbɔɔn bi kina la. Bipiib aalahn

ref: My bride, my very own, I come to my garden and enjoy its spices. I eat my honeycomb and honey; I drink my wine and milk. Their Friends Speak: Eat and drink until you are drunk with love. Another Dream She Speaks:

text: Nimi aatiŋ kuln a, le mmii wun nimi aatim mɔmɔk. Le ni si lik le biwɔwɔm gaa nimi aakpaakon mɔmɔk, ki gaa nimi aajikaar.

ref: Enemies surround Jerusalem, alone like a hut in a vineyard or in a cucumber field.
text: Jerusalem baanja le gur, le bi gob ki mu, le kaa kpa mpɔɔn mubaa ke kisaak ni aabool na.

ref: Zion would have disappeared like Sodom and Gomorrah, if the Lord All-Powerful had not let a few of its people survive. Justice, Not Sacrifices
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan yaa kaa ba gur binib siib kan, Jerusalem ba ga kuln ke Sodom aatiŋ ni Gomora aatiŋ aah nan kuln pu na la.

ref: You are no better than the leaders and people of Sodom and Gomorrah! So listen to the Lord God:
text: Jerusalem yaab, nimi aayidam ni nimi aanib naahn Sodom ni Gomora yaab la. Li pel man Uwumbɔr aah bi tuk nimi pu na. Pel man mbamɔm Uwumbɔr aah bi mɔk nimi pu na.

ref: “Your sacrifices mean nothing to me. I am sick of your offerings of rams and choice cattle; I don't like the blood of bulls or lambs or goats.
text: U bui ke, “Taa dak man ke m gee nimi aatork ki ni toor tii mi na. Maa ki neen naah kɔr nimi aapiih i ki joo seer mmii ni ki tii mi na, ni nimi aanaa i ŋan na aakpan mu. Maa ki neen nimi aanaasin, ni mpihsin, ni ŋŋosin mu ni tii mi na.

ref: “Who asked you to bring all this when you come to worship me? Stay out of my temple!
text: Ŋma bui nimi ke ni li joo ni nimina mɔmɔk buyoonn ni choo ni nan pak mi na? Ŋma bui nimi ke ni di ŋitaagbindun ŋimina koo ni Maameen Aadichal ni?

ref: Your sacrifices are worthless, and your incense disgusting. I can't stand the evil you do on your New Moon Festivals or on your Sabbaths and other times of worship.
text: Nimi aapiin i ni joo ni na aa kpa tinyoor tibaa. Naah seer tulalee aayon mu na kpa mi liŋuul la. Nimi aaŋmapɔɔn aajim, ni nimi aakpaakool daal aajim, ni naah kuuni pu na, maa gee ni, ni di nimi aatunwanbir bii ni mɔmɔk a.

ref: I hate your New Moon Festivals and all others as well. They are a heavy burden I am tired of carrying.
text: Nimina mɔmɔk ye lituln li m nan bak ki ki bak li pu na la.

ref: Wash yourselves clean! I hate your filthy deeds. Stop doing wrong
text: Kpeln nimi aabimbin man. Di cha man nimi aatunwanbir ti m kan ni ŋani ti na. Mbamɔn, di cha man,

ref: and learn to live right. See that justice is done. Defend widows and orphans and help the oppressed.” An Invitation from the Lord
text: ki bee ni ŋan na ki ŋa kina. Cha ibamɔn ŋa, ki ter bigiim, ki tii nkpobim baabamɔn, ki li kii bikpopiib.”

ref: I, the Lord, invite you to come and talk it over. Your sins are scarlet red, but they will be whiter than snow or wool.
text: Le Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Dandana wee, cha ti toor tibɔr ngbaan man. Nimi aatunwanbir man ni pu ke nsin na, le m ga ŋmaa finn nimi ni nya chain ke nkokoyon na. Nimi aatunwanbir yaa po man ni pu sakpen pu na, m ga finn nimi, ni piir chain.

ref: If you willingly obey me, the best crops in the land will be yours.
text: Ni yaa kii maamɔb kan, ni ga kan tijikaar pam nimi aatiŋ pu.

ref: But if you turn against me, your enemies will kill you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
text: Le ni yaa yii maamɔb kan, ni ga sil kan nkun. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Titunwanbir aatiŋ

ref: Jerusalem, you are like an unfaithful wife. Once your judges were honest and your people lived right; now you are a city full of murderers.
text: Kitiŋ ki nan bi chain kaa kpa tijɔŋ tibaa na le gur tun ke upiidagoor na. N‑yoonn mubaa bininyaam ŋmeen le nan gbii ki ni, le dandana ma binikurb le gur bi ki ni.

ref: Your leaders have rejected me to become friends of crooks; your rulers are looking for gifts and bribes. Widows and orphans never get a fair trial.
text: Saayidam ye binib bi kaa kii maamɔb na la, ki ye binaayukb aajɔtiib, le ki gaal ipiin, ni igaŋgaŋlik n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Baa ter nkpobim buyoonn bi bi tibɔr ni na, kaan pel bikpopiib aabɔr buyoonn bi di ti fuu ni bi chee na.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the mighty ruler of Israel, and I make you a promise: You are now my enemy, and I will show my anger by taking revenge on you.
text: Kina pu na, li pel man Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, Israel yaab Aadindaan u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aah len pu na: “M ga teen nimi maadim, aan naan ki ŋa mi tibɔbir tibaa.

ref: I will punish you terribly and burn away everything that makes you unfit to worship me.
text: M ga fii sil nimi Jerusalem aanib pu. M ga pu nimi mmii ni ke baah pu tikur mmii ni ki nyani tijɔŋ pu na.

ref: Jerusalem, I will choose judges and advisors like those you had before. Your new name will be “Justice and Faithfulness.” The Lord Will Save Jerusalem
text: M ga tii nimi biyidam bi ga li sur nimi ke naah nan puen kpa pu na. N‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ga ki yin Jerusalem aanib ke binib bi ŋan ki dii mi Uwumbɔr baanja na.”

ref: Jerusalem, you will be saved by showing justice; Zion's people who turn to me will be saved by doing right.
text: Uwumbɔr aah ŋan pu na, u ga gaa Jerusalem, ni kaanib bi kpeln baabimbin na lii,

ref: But those rebellious sinners who turn against me, the Lord, will all disappear.
text: le ki kuln umɔk tun titunwanbir ki kpak u na; u ga kuln unii umɔk yii u na.

ref: You will be made ashamed of those groves of trees where you worshiped idols.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le nisui ga gar ke ni nan chuun dii isui ke i gaa nimi lii, ki toor kisamook ke ki ter nimi ni kan tijikaar.

ref: You will be like a grove of trees dying in a drought.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan ni ga gbar ke likpaln li kuur na, ki yɔl ke tijikaar ti utaal aa nu ŋani ti pu na.

ref: Your strongest leaders will be like dry wood set on fire by their idols. No one will be able to help, as they all go up in flames.
text: Ikpakpaabi aah gaal mmii ni pu na, kina le bipɔɔndam mu aatunwanbir ga gaa ki ku bi doo, le ubaa aan ŋmaa gaa bi lii.

ref: This is the message I was given about Judah and Jerusalem:
text: Uwumbɔr aah nan di Juda ni Jerusalem aatim aabɔr ti tuk Amos aajapɔɔn Aisaya na sɔ:

ref: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills; every nation will rush to it.
text: N‑yoonn choo, le lijool li pu Uwumbɔr Aadichal si na ga li ye lijool li paa jer ŋijoo mɔmɔk na, li ga li fɔk chaar jer ŋigongon mɔmɔk, le ŋinibol pam ga dan li chee,

ref: Many people will come and say, “Let's go to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
text: le ŋaanib ga bui ke, “Cha ti jon man Uwumbɔr aajool ki buen Israel yaab Aawumbɔr aadichal ni. U ga mɔk timi waah ban ti ŋa pu na; le ti ga chuun waah lee isan i na pu; Uwumbɔr aamɔkm nyan ni Jerusalem ni la; Sionn pu le u len waanib chee tibɔr.”

ref: He will settle arguments between nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never make war or attack one another.
text: U ga len ŋinibokpaan aabɔr, le bi ga di baajaak aajum mɔɔ ŋikuu, ki di baakpaatunn mɔɔ gɔrk tiib. Ŋinibol aan ki to tɔb butɔb, kaan ki gor bibaa kiir butɔb daalbaadaal.

ref: People of Israel, let's live by the light of the Lord. Following Sinful Customs
text: Nimi Jakob aayaabitiib, cha ti li gur chuun man nwiihn mu Uwumbɔr di tii timi na ni. Kigaak ga kuln

ref: Our Lord, you have deserted your people, Israel, because they follow customs of nations from the east. They worship Philistine gods and are close friends of foreigners.
text: Uwumbɔr, aa yii saanib, Jakob aayaabitiib. Ki nya liwipuul wɔb ki ti saa Filistia aatiŋ ni mɔmɔk ye nin chee inyɔk aatuln gbii na la, le Israel aanib mu dii biwɔwɔm ngbaan aakaal.

ref: They have endless treasures of silver and gold; they have countless horses and war chariots.
text: Salmaa ni tikunabr le gbii kitiŋ ngbaan ni, le ubaa aa nyi baapɔɔn mɔk. Itaan le gbii baatiŋ ngbaan ni, le ubaa aan ŋmaa kahn baataan aatɔroku tiib.

ref: Everywhere in the country they worship the idols they have made.
text: Ŋiwaa le gbii baatiŋ ngbaan ni, le bi chuun toor tiwan ni bi di bibaa aaŋaal ŋa na.

ref: And so, all of them will be ashamed and disgraced. Don't forgive them! A Day of Judgment
text: Bi mɔmɔk ga ji inimɔɔn. Uwumbɔr, taa di cha pinn bi.

ref: Every one of you, go hide among the rocks and in the ground, because the Lord is fearsome, marvelous, and glorious.
text: Bi mɔmɔk ga bɔr titakpalunn ni, ni ŋitakpasakpiin taab, ŋijoo paab, ke bi ŋmar Uwumbɔr aaŋuul, ni waapɔɔn, ni waawiihn sakpiin chee.

ref: When the Lord comes, everyone who is proud will be made humble, and the Lord alone will be honored.
text: Nwiin mubaa choo, buyoonn unibɔn aagaak ga doo aan kalmbaani mu kuln na. N‑yoonn ngbaan le Uwumbɔr baanja ga kan bunyuŋ.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful has chosen a day when those who are proud and conceited will be put down.
text: Liyaadaal ngbaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga sunn mpɔɔndam, ni kalmbaanidam, ni kigaadam mɔmɔk taab.

ref: The tall and towering cedars of Lebanon will be destroyed. So will the oak trees of Bashan,
text: U ga tur Lebanonn ni Basann aasui fɔfɔk na mɔmɔk lii kitiŋ.

ref: all high mountains and hills,
text: U ga ber ŋijoo ni ŋigongon ŋi fɔk na mɔmɔk,

ref: all the seagoing ships, and every beautiful boat.
text: U ga cha iŋɔsakpiin i ŋan na bee nnyun ni.

ref: You had better hide in caves and holes— the Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth.
text: Buyoonn Uwumbɔr ga dan ki nan deŋ kitiŋ na, binib ga bɔr titakpalunn ni, ni ŋitakpasakpiin taab, ŋijoo paab, ke bi ŋmar waaŋuul, ni waapɔɔn, ni waawiihn sakpiin chee.

ref: On that day everyone will throw to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold they made to worship.
text: Nwiin ngbaan yaa fuu ni kan, bi ga di baah di salmaa ni tikunabr maa ŋiwaa ŋi na mee, ki san cha ŋi, ki di ŋi tii ŋinaasɔn ni tinanjenn.

ref: The Lord will be fearsome, marvelous, and glorious when he comes to terrify people on earth— they will hide in caves and in the hills.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa nan dan ke u nan deŋ kitiŋ kan, binib ga bɔr titakpalunn ni, ni ŋitakpasakpiin taab, ŋijoo paab, ke bi ŋmar waaŋuul pu, ki bɔr waapɔɔn ni waawiihn sakpiin chee.

ref: Stop trusting the power of humans. They are all going to die, so how can they help?
text: Aa yaa di aabaa tii unibɔn u ga kpo na kan, ba aanyoor bi kpa?

ref: The mighty Lord All-Powerful is going to take away from Jerusalem and Judah everything you need— your bread and water, *
text: Dandana wee, Tidindaan Uwumbɔr u ye Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan na ban u chuu nyan Jerusalem ni Juda ponn ni tiwan, ni binib bimɔk nan joo ntim ngbaan aanib na. U ban u chuu yoor baajikaar, ni baanyun,

ref: soldiers and heroes, judges and prophets, leaders and army officers,
text: ni bipobidam ni baatɔb aajab, ni baabɔjirb, ni bibɔnabr ni baabɔɔb, ni baaninyuum,

ref: officials and advisors, fortunetellers and others who tell the future.
text: ni baatɔb aajab aaninkpiib, ni baanib aaninkpiib, ni baayidam, ni binib bimɔk joo inyɔk tun lituln na.

ref: He will let children and babies become your rulers.
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha mbijabim waatiib le li joo ntim ngbaan,

ref: You will each be cruel to friends and neighbors. Young people will insult their elders; no one will show respect to those who deserve it.
text: le unii mɔmɔk ŋa uŋeen aatɔ waageehn. Binachipɔm ni bisapɔm aan li pak bininkpiib, le binib bi kaa bi tibaa ni na aan ki li pak binib bi jer bi na.

ref: Some of you will grab hold of a relative and say, “You still have a coat. Be our leader and rule this pile of ruins.”
text: N‑yoonn mubaa choo, le lidichal libaa ni aanib ga nyan bi ponn ni ubaa ki bui u ke, “Aa ma kpa tiwan ki ga peen, kina pu na, li ye timi aaninkpel limukl aayoonn mue ni.”

ref: But the answer will be, “I can't do you any good. Don't make me your leader. There's no food or clothing left in my house.”
text: Le u ga bui ke, “Naa ye min. Maan ŋmaa ter nimi. Maa kpa tijikaar, bee tiwanpeenkaan. Taa di mi ŋa nimi aaninkpel man.”

ref: Jerusalem and Judah, you rebelled against your glorious Lord— your words and your actions, made you stumble and fall.
text: Mbamɔn, Jerusalem sil kuln a. Juda mu bi lir la. Baah ŋani tiwan nimɔk ki len pu na mɔmɔk seei Uwumbɔr binib aanimbil ni la; le bi fii sil uma Uwumbɔr u kpa mpɔɔn mɔmɔk na pu.

ref: The look on your faces shows that you are sinful as Sodom, and you don't try to hide it. You are in for trouble, and you have brought it all on yourselves. The Wrong Kind of Leaders
text: Baa kaa gbaa ibamɔn pu na ga ki gir koon bima le tibɔr ni. Bi tun titunwanbir kaa joo bɔrni ke Sodom aanib aah nan tun pu na la. Bima le joo ni bibaa aadoon, bi kuln a.

ref: Tell those who obey God, “You're very fortunate— you will be rewarded for what you have done.”
text: Binib bi aabimbin bi chain na ga li kpa mpopiin, le baawan mɔmɔk ga li dii nsan. Baah tun ki kan pu na, bi ga ji ni ni mpopiin.

ref: Tell those who disobey, “You're in big trouble— what you did to others will come back to you.”
text: Le titunwanbirdam ga kuln; le baah ŋa biken pu na, Uwumbɔr ga di giin ŋa bi.

ref: Though you are God's people, you are ruled and abused by women and children. You are confused by leaders who guide you down the wrong path.
text: Mbim le joo maanib ki muk bi, baayidam ye bipiib la. Maanib, nimi aasalolm na joo nimi kooni timoor ni la, ki cha ni yenni. Uwumbɔr aah ji waanib tibɔr pu na

ref: The Lord is ready to accuse and judge all nations.
text: Uwumbɔr gor ke u piin waabɔr, u gor ke u ji waanib tibɔr.

ref: He will even judge you rulers and leaders of his own nation. You destroyed his vineyard and filled your houses by robbing the poor.
text: Uwumbɔr kuun bininkpiib, ni binib bi ye bisalolm na ke u ji bi tibɔr. Waah di ngalm mu di bil bi na sɔ: “Ni sun biken aasar mpɔɔn pu, le nimi aadichal ni gbii tiwan ni ni gaa bigiim chee na.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful says, “You have crushed my people and rubbed in the dirt the faces of the poor.” The Women of Jerusalem
text: Naa ŋan ke ni muen maanib ki ji bigiim ke baah ye bigiim na. Min, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.” Jerusalem aapiib aasurm

ref: The Lord says: The women of Jerusalem are proud and strut around, winking shamelessly. They wear anklets that jingle and call attention to the way they walk.
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Lik Jerusalem aapiib aah kpa kigaak pu na. Bi chuun le bimɔfal ŋui paacham ke ibɔ na. N‑yoonn mɔmɔk bi chuun gɔr kidagook la. Bi tai dim dim, le ŋibɔlun ŋi gbin bitaagbin na weeni kiliŋ kiliŋ.

ref: But I, the Lord, will cover their heads with sores, and I will uncover their private parts.
text: Le m ga daa bitafal; m ga kuu baayikpir ki cha ŋiyikun.”

ref: In place of perfume, there will be a stink; in place of belts, there will be ropes; in place of fancy hairdos, they will have bald heads. Instead of expensive clothes, they will wear sackcloth; instead of beauty, they will have ugly scars.
text: Baah ba ga li ŋmir tulalee pu na, bi ga li nu la; baan ki buu ŋigbapapan, bi ga li buu tichɔsɔnn aaŋmin la; baan ki li kpa tiyikpir ti ŋan na, bi ga li gur ye ŋiyikun ŋmeen la; baan ki gbab ŋikekenyaan, tikekekpir le bi ga li gbae; le baanyaan ga kpaln inimɔɔn.

ref: The fighting men of Jerusalem will be killed in battle.
text: Bijab bi bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni na, hali, bi kpa mpɔɔn sakpen na mɔmɔk ga bee butɔb ni.

ref: When this happens, seven women will grab the same man, and each of them will say, “I'll buy my own food and clothes! Just marry me and take away my disgrace.” The Lord Will Bless His People Who Survive
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, bipiib bilole ga buen ti bub chuu ujabaan ki bui u ke, “Ti ga ŋmaa kpiin tibaa ki mu gbab tibaa, aa mu tee cha ti li yin si ke tichal, aan ki nya maakpayal aanimɔɔn ni.” Jerusalem aah ga gir sil pu na

ref: The time is coming when the Lord will make his land fruitful and glorious again, and the people of Israel who survive will take great pride in what the land produces.
text: N‑yoonn choo, le Uwumbɔr ga cha timoor ni isui imɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu na muun ki li ŋan. Tijikaar ti ga ŋa kitiŋ ngbaan pu na ga tii Israel yaab bimɔk ŋmar na mpopiin ni limakl.

ref: after the Lord sends a fiery judgment to clean the city and its people of their violent deeds.
text: Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn pu u ga ji linibol ngbaan tibɔr ki toor bi, ki finn nyan tibɔbir ni nsin mu nan kpir Jerusalem ponn ni na.

ref: Then the Lord will cover the whole city and its meeting places with a thick cloud each day and with a flaming fire each night. God's own glory will be like a huge tent that covers everything.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le Uwumbɔr ga tun ni ntaalangbam mu nan biin Sionn Aajool ni binib bimɔk kuun nima chee na nwiin pu, ki di iŋmanyuu ni mmiigaal mu wiin chain na biin bi pu kinyeek. Uwumbɔr aapak ki ye nwiihn na le ga biin ki kii kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk.

ref: It will provide shade from the heat of the sun and a place of shelter and protection from storms and rain.
text: Waapɔɔn ga tii kitiŋ ngbaan mboon, nwiin taa see ki, ki ŋa ki nin chee lifuur bi na, ni nin chee utaal ni kitaabuŋ aan ŋmaa koo na.

ref: I will sing a song about my friend's vineyard that was on the side of a fertile hill.
text: Le pel man nlahn mu m ban m gaa na. Mu ye njɔ ubaa ni waasaak aalahn la. Udichadaan ubaa le nan bi le ki naan kisaak lijool li aatiŋ ŋan na pu.

ref: My friend dug the ground, removed the stones, and planted the best vines. He built a watchtower and dug a pit in rocky ground for pressing the grapes. He hoped they would be sweet, but bitter grapes were all it produced.
text: U nan kuun ŋitakpal le ki kon ki ŋum isui i lu ŋisubil ŋi ŋan na ki ponn ni, le ki maa libimbifɔfɔŋ ke bi li ka li paab ki kiir kisaak na, le ki gbii libuul litakpasakpeln ni, li bi ga di ŋisubil ŋa li ponn ni na aan ki ŋmaa ŋaanyun nyan na; le ki kii buyoonn ŋisubil ga puir na; le ŋisubil na mɔmɔk nan mɔɔn la.

ref: Listen, people of Jerusalem and of Judah! You be the judge of me and my vineyard.
text: Kina pu le njɔ bui ke, “Nimi bimɔk bi Jerusalem ni Juda na, lik man maasaak ngbaan aabɔr aan ki len ibamɔn.

ref: What more could I have done for my vineyard? I hoped for sweet grapes, but bitter grapes were all that grew.
text: Ni ye ba le maa ŋa ki? Kina kan, ba ŋa ki lun ŋisubil ŋi mɔɔn na ŋmeen, kaa ye ŋi ŋan na?

ref: Now I will let you know what I am going to do. I will cut down the hedge and tear down the wall. My vineyard will be trampled and left in ruins.
text: “Maah ga ŋa maasaak ngbaan pu na sɔ: M ga chuu ŋɔi idɔ i m nan di gob ki aan i kii ki na, le ipeel i bir na nan ŋmɔ ki, ki taa taa bii ki.

ref: It will turn into a desert, neither pruned nor hoed; it will be covered with thorns and briars. I will command the clouds not to send rain.
text: Maan ki kuur ki ponn ni aan timoor muun ki ponn ni. Maan ki per isui ngbaan aan i ki kpenn, kaan ki toor i taab; m ga cha ukokongɔkr ni ikokon gaa ki ni. M ga jenn utaal u taa ki nu ki ponn ni.”

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful! Israel is the vineyard, and Judah is the garden I tended with care. I had hoped for honesty and for justice, but dishonesty and cries for mercy were all I found. Isaiah Condemns Social Injustice
text: Israel ni Juda aanib le ye Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aasaak, bima le ye ŋisubil aasui i u ŋum na. U nan dak ke bi ba ŋa ni ŋan na, le bi yii ki ku binib. U nan dak ke bi ba li ŋani ni tok na, le bi nan ŋani binib mbiin, le bi wii baabamɔn pu. Titunwanbir ti binib tun na

ref: You are in for trouble! You take over house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone else in all the land.
text: Nimi aamɔfal doo a. Ni moo daa ŋidichal ni ikpaakon ki kpei naah puen kpa i na pu. Naan yunn le unii aan ki kan mpaan ki koo nima chee, le nimi baanja le ga gur kitiŋ ngbaan pu.

ref: But the Lord All-Powerful has made this promise to me: Those large and beautiful homes will be left empty, with no one to take care of them.
text: M ŋun Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan len ke, “Ŋidichanyaan sakpiin ŋimina mɔmɔk ga kpaln ŋidichakuun ki lir.”

ref: None of them are tired. They don't sleep or get drowsy, and they run without stumbling. Their belts don't come loose; their sandal straps don't break.
text: Naa ŋuni bi ponn ni ubaa; le bi ponn ni ubaa aa gbeer nibaa. Baa geeni ki yenni kaa geeni kpala. Bi ponn ni ubaa aagbapapaln aa sɔkr; ubaa mu aanaatakl aa kii.

ref: You are in for trouble! The lies you tell are like ropes by which you drag along sin and evil.
text: Nimi aadoon le na. Naan ŋmaa gaa nibaa nimi aatunwanbir na chee.

ref: You are in for trouble! You get up early to start drinking, and you keep it up late into the night.
text: Nimi aadoon le na. Ni fii mala kichakpinaanyeek ni ki piin ndaan aanyum, ki nyu ki ti saa kijook ki nyu ki gbii.

ref: At your drinking parties you have the music of stringed instruments, tambourines, and flutes. But you never even think about all the Lord has done,
text: Nimi aajim ponn ni, ni gbaa tibar ni ichayakrtuun ki pee ŋiwul ki nyu ndaan, le kaa nyi Uwumbɔr aah ŋani pu na.

ref: and so his people know nothing about him. That's why many of you will be dragged off to foreign lands. Your leaders will starve to death, and everyone else will suffer from thirst.
text: Kina pu na, bi ga yoor nimi di buen tinaagbiir ni. Nkon ga ku nimi aayidam, le nnyunyuu ku bigiim na mu.

ref: The world of the dead has opened its mouth wide and is eagerly waiting for the leaders of Jerusalem and for its noisy crowds, especially for those who take pride in that city.
text: Kitekpiitiŋ ka waa bumɔb kii bi la, ki ga nab Jerusalem aaninyuum na, ni baanib, ni binib bi nyu ndaan ki kpa kifuuk na mɔmɔk.

ref: Its citizens have been put down, and its proud people have been brought to shame.
text: Inimɔɔn ga chuu unibɔn mɔk, le bigaadam na ga sunn bibaa taab.

ref: But the holy Lord God All-Powerful is praised, because he has shown who he is by bringing justice.

text: Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr aan cha unachipɔɔn ubaa ŋmar. Waan san nkpobim ni bikpopiib kinimbaak; ba pu? binib ngbaan mɔmɔk aa dii Uwumbɔr aasan; bi kpa mbiin, le baaliin mɔmɔk ye tibɔbir. Nimina aapuwɔb mɔmɔk na, Uwumbɔr aaŋuul aan kee sɔŋ; u ga li beenin ban u moo daa bitafal.

ref: Evil had spread like a raging forest fire sending thornbushes up in smoke.
text: Binib ngbaan aatunwanbir bii tiwan ke mmii aah wu ikokon ni ŋinaabukar pu na la. Baatunwanbir bii tiwan ke kichook ni aamii aaŋmanyuu na la.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful was angry and used the people as fuel for a fire that scorched the land. They turned against each other
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aaŋuul aah fii na, waatafadaan ngbaan ga bii tiwan ni binib mɔmɔk ke mmii aah wu bii tiwan pu na la. N‑yoonn ngbaan kan, ubaa aan ki li nyi uŋeen aatɔ aabɔr.

ref: like wild animals attacking and eating everyone around them, even their own relatives. But still they were not satisfied.
text: Le kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk pu aanib ga li tɔkl tijikaar siib ti bi kan na le ki ji. Nimina mɔmɔk mu aan cha nkon doo. Hali bi ga di baabim ŋa tijikaar.

ref: The tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh turned against each other, then joined forces to attack Judah. But the Lord was still angry and ready to punish the nation even more.
text: Manase aanib ni Efraim aanib ga to tɔb butɔb, le ki ki gir kpaan ki to Juda yaab butɔb. Nimina aapuwɔb mɔmɔk na, Uwumbɔr aaŋuul aan kee sɔŋ; u ga li beenin ban u moo daa bitafal.

ref: You people are in for trouble! You have made cruel and unfair laws
text: Nimi aadoon le na. Nimi bi naani ikaal i kaa ye ibamɔn ki joo muk maanib na aadoon le na.

ref: that let you cheat the poor and needy and rob widows and orphans.
text: Kina le ni gaal bigiim aabamɔn, ni ni ye biyaan na. Kina le ni gaal bikpopiib ni nkpobim aawangol bi chee.

ref: But what will you do when you are fiercely attacked and punished by foreigners? Where will you run for help? Where will you hide your valuables?
text: Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr yaa daa nitafal kan, ni ga ŋa kinye? Uwumbɔr yaa cha tibɔbir nyan ni dandar ki nan lir ni pu kan, ni ga ŋa kinye? La chee aan ni ga san ti ban nterm? La chee aan ni ga ti di nimi aawangol di bɔr?

ref: How will you escape being captured or killed? The Lord is still angry, and he isn't through with you yet! The Lord's Purpose and the King of Assyria
text: Bi ga ku nimi butɔb ponn ni la, bee bi chuu nimi ki dar buen ke binaagbiib na. Nimina mɔmɔk aapuwɔb na, Uwumbɔr aaŋuul aan sɔŋ; u ga li beenin ban ke u moo daa nitafal. Uwumbɔr di Asiria aabɔrkpaan tun waah ban pu na

ref: The Lord says: I am furious! And I will use the king of Assyria as a club
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “Asiria, maaŋuul yaa ti fii unii u pu na, m joo sin Asiria le gbaa u ke baah joo lichakukul jaa kijaak pu na.

ref: to beat down you godless people. I am angry with you, and I will send him to attack you. He will take what he wants and walk on you like mud in the streets.
text: M tun Asiria yaab ke bi ti tak litimbol li kaa dii mi Uwumbɔr aasan na, binib bi cha maaŋuul fii bi pu na. M tun bi ke bi ti jenn ki gaa, ki su baawan, ki taa binib pu ki ŋmal titan ni, kitiŋ ponn ni.”

ref: He has even bigger plans in mind, because he wants to destroy many nations.
text: Le Asiria aabɔrkpaan ngbaan ma tee kpa ubaa aalandak i kaa ŋan na uyil ponn ni. Waalandak le ye ke u bii ŋitimbol pam;

ref: The king of Assyria says: My army commanders are kings!
text: le ki puk kipupuk ke, “Maatɔb aajab aaninkpiib mɔmɔk kpaln bibɔrb la.

ref: They have already captured the cities of Calno, Carchemish, Hamath, Arpad, Samaria, and Damascus.
text: M nyaŋ Kalno ni Kakemis aatim mɔmɔk, ki nyaŋ Hamaf ni Apad aatim mɔmɔk. M nyaŋ Samaria ni Damaskus aatim.

ref: The gods of Jerusalem and Samaria are weaker than the gods of those powerful nations. And I will destroy Jerusalem, together with its gods and idols, just as I did Samaria.
text: M bii Samaria ni baawaa mɔmɔk doo a, le ki ga ŋa Jerusalem ni waawaa mu kina.”

ref: The Lord will do what he has planned against Jerusalem and Mount Zion. Then he will punish the proud and boastful king of Assyria,
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “M yaa doo maah bi tun lituln li Sionn Aajool pu ni Jerusalem ni na kan, m ga daa Asiria aabɔrkpaan ngbaan aatafal, waah puk tipupuur timɔk na, ni waamakl ngbaan pu.”

ref: who says: I did these things by my own power because I am smart and clever. I attacked kings like a wild bull, and I took the land and the treasures of their nations.
text: Asiria aabɔrkpaan ngbaan puk kipupuk ki len ke, “Min le ŋa nimina mɔmɔk mbaa. M kpa Uwumbɔr do aalan ni ichiin le ki pɔɔ. M ŋar ŋitimbol aanaan mɔmɔk ŋŋaan le ki yoor baah kpa ni mɔmɔk ki di siin kiir bibaa na, le ki taa taa ku binib bi bi nima chee na ke unaaja aah taar tiwan pu pu na.

ref: I have conquered the whole world! And it was easier than taking eggs from an unguarded nest. No one even flapped a wing or made a peep.
text: Dulnyaa wee aanibol mɔmɔk nan bi m chee ke unyoon aanyandil na la, le m nan kuun baawangol ke unii aah chuun ki ti pii ŋikpanjen timoor ni pu na. Ubaa aa nan ŋmaa faan mi, ubaa mu aa ki fii ke u faa nkuun.”

ref: King of Assyria, can an ax or a saw overpower the one who uses it? Can a wooden pole lift whoever holds it?
text: Le Uwumbɔr ma bui ke, “Kichɔk ga ŋmaa bui ke ki jer unii u joo ki na aa? Ukpikpiir aah joo kichɔk ki kpii tiwan na aan ŋmaa bui ke ki jer u. Lichakukul aan ŋmaa yoor unii paacham; unii le ga yoor lichakukul paacham.”

ref: The mighty Lord All-Powerful will send a terrible disease to strike down your army, and you will burn with fever under your royal robes.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga di iween di daa binib bi mɔmɔk ji n‑yaan ni nkpan dandana wee na aatafal. Mmii le ga li wu biponn ni, kaan junn.

ref: The holy God, who is the light of Israel, will turn into a fire, and in one day you will go up in flames, just like a thornbush.
text: Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab aawiihn na ga kpaln mmii. Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na ga kpaln mmiigaal mu ga di nwiin mubaa baanja ki di wu tiwan mɔmɔk doo na, hali ikokon ni ŋinaabukar mɔmɔk ga wu.

ref: The Lord will make your beautiful forests and fertile fields slowly rot.
text: Iween i bir na aah ku unii pu na, kina le tikpaatan ti ŋan na ni tipur mu mɔmɔk ga doo.

ref: There will be so few trees that even a young child can count them. Only a Few Will Come Back
text: Ubo waatiir ga ŋmaa kahn isui siib i ga gur na. Israel yaab siib le ga gir ni

ref: A time is coming when the survivors from Israel and Judah will completely depend on the holy Lord of Israel, instead of the nation that defeated them.
text: N‑yoonn choo le Israel aanib bi ŋmar na aan nan ki li dak linibol li nan ban li ku doo bi na pu. Bi ga nan di baalandak mɔmɔk di tii bima Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na la.

ref: There were as many people as there are grains of sand along the seashore, but only a few will survive to come back to Israel's mighty God. This is because he has threatened to destroy their nation, just as they deserve.
text: Dandana, Israel yaab wiir ke nnyusakpem aatambol aah wiir pu na la, le bi ponn ni siib ga gir ni. Uwumbɔr bui ke u ga bii bi; le bi ŋeer kina.

ref: Now the Lord God All-Powerful says to his people in Jerusalem: The Assyrians will beat you with sticks and abuse you, just as the Egyptians did. But don't be afraid of them.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui waanib bi bi Sionn na ke, “Asiria yaab yaa muk nimi ke Ijipt yaab aah nan muk nimi pu na kan, ni taa san bi ijawaan.

ref: Soon I will stop being angry with you, and I will punish them for their crimes.
text: Naan ki yunn le m ga daa nimi aatafal doo; n‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga kuln Asiria yaab kookoo.

ref: I will beat the Assyrians with a whip, as I did the people of Midian near the rock at Oreb. And I will show the same mighty power that I used when I made a path through the sea in Egypt.
text: Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan di maabanbaan loe bi ke maah nan loe Midiann yaab, Oreb aatakpal chee pu na. M ga daa bima Asiria yaab aatafal ke maah nan daa Ijipt yaab aatafal pu na.

ref: Then they will no longer rule your nation. All will go well for you, and your burden will be lifted.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa fuu ni kan, m ga gaa nimi lii, ki nyan nimi Asiria yaab aapɔɔn ni. Baamukl aan ki li bi ni pu.” Bidim fuu ni a

ref: Enemy troops have reached the town of Aiath. They have gone through Migron, and they stored their supplies at Michmash,
text: Nimi aadim aajab nyaŋ Ai yaab a. Bi kpaan jer Migronn a. Bi di baawan bil Mikmas la.

ref: before crossing the valley and spending the night at Geba. The people of Ramah are terrified; everyone in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, has run away.
text: Bi dii kifataŋ kibaa ni ki fuu Geba ki doon nima. Ijawaan chuu Rama aatiŋ aanib sakpen a, le ubɔrkpaan Sɔɔl aatiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Gibea na aanib san.

ref: Loud crying can be heard in the towns of Gallim, Laishah, and sorrowful Anathoth.
text: Nimi Galim aatiŋ aanib, teen mpɔɔn pu man. Li pel man, Laisa aatiŋ aanib. Anatof aatiŋ aanib kpa kinimbaak la.

ref: No one is left in Madmenah or Gebim.
text: Madmena ni Gebim aanib san ban baamɔfal la.

ref: Today the enemy will camp at Nob and shake a threatening fist at Mount Zion in Jerusalem.
text: Din wee bidim ngbaan fuu ni Nob aatiŋ ponn ni, le ki joo biŋaal mɔk Sionn Aajool li Jerusalem bi li paab na.

ref: But the Lord All-Powerful will use his fearsome might to bring down the tallest trees and chop off every branch.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga daa bi lii ni ke baah gaa bar isubon lir ni kitiŋ pu na. Bininyuum ni kigaadam mɔmɔk ga doon kitiŋ le ki kpaln yaansara aanib.

ref: Like a branch that sprouts from a stump, someone from David's family will someday be king.
text: Baah gaa busub lii aan ibonpɔɔn ki kpenn pu na, kina le ubɔrkpaan David aamaal ponn ni bi. Ubɔrkpaan pɔɔn ga ki nyan ni David aayaabitiib ni.

ref: The Spirit of the Lord will be with him to give him understanding, wisdom, and insight. He will be powerful, and he will know and honor the Lord.
text: Uwumbɔr Aafuur nyaan ga tii u nlan, ni ichiin, ni nnyim mu u ga di joo waanib na. U ga li nyi Uwumbɔr aageehn ki ga nyuŋ u,

ref: His greatest joy will be to obey the Lord. This king won't judge by appearances or listen to rumors.
text: le ki ga kii waamɔb ni mpopiin. U ga li joo waanib ibamɔn ni,

ref: The poor and the needy will be treated with fairness and with justice. His word will be law everywhere in the land, and criminals will be put to death.
text: u ga di bigiim ni binib bi kaa kpa biteterb na aabamɔn tii bi. Waamɔliin le ga daa binib aatafal, le titunwanbirdam ga kpo.

ref: Honesty and fairness will be his royal robes.
text: U ga joo waanib mbamɔm ni kinyaan.

ref: Leopards will lie down with young goats, and wolves will rest with lambs. Calves and lions will eat together and be cared for by little children.
text: Ŋisapol ni ipiih ga kpaan koo tɔb chee ni nsuudoon, le inaamuun ni iŋobi ga kpaan doon tɔb chee. Inaabi ni ichinn aabim ga kpaan ji tɔb chee, le mbiwaatiib le ga li kpaa i.

ref: Cows and bears will share the same pasture; their young will rest side by side. Lions and oxen will both eat straw.
text: Inaa ni tipeewanbir ga kpaan ji, le yaabim ga kpaan doon tɔb chee ni nsuudoon. Ichinn ga ŋmɔ timoor ke inaa na.

ref: Little children will play near snake holes. They will stick their hands into dens of poisonous snakes and never be hurt.
text: Hali, ubo yaa gbiir uwaa u kpa liluul na chee kan, waan ŋa u nibaa.

ref: Nothing harmful will take place on the Lord's holy mountain. Just as water fills the sea, the land will be filled with people who know and honor the Lord. God's People Will Come Back Home
text: Uwumbɔr aagongoln Sionn li bi chain na paab nibaa aan li bi nima ki bir. Nnyusakpem ponn ni aah kpa nnyun sakpen pu na, kina le dulnyaa wee ga li nyi Uwumbɔr bɔr. Baah nan chuu bi buen tinaagbiir ni na ga gir ni

ref: The time is coming when one of David's descendants will be the signal for the people of all nations to come together. They will follow his advice, and his own nation will become famous.
text: Nwiin mubaa choo, le ubɔrkpaan pɔɔn ubaa ga nyan ni ubɔrkpaan David aamaal ni, ki fuu ni, ki ga li ye ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aamɔkl. Bi ga kuun waanaan aatiŋ ni ki nyuŋ u.

ref: When that day comes, the Lord will again reach out his mighty arm and bring home his people who have survived in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Ethiopia, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the land along the coast.
text: Nwiin ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, Uwumbɔr ga di waapɔɔn kunn ni waanib bi gaar Asiria, ni Ijipt, ni Patros, ni Kus, ni Elam, ni Babiloŋ, ni Hamaf aatim ni, ni ntim mu bi nnyusakpem aagbaan na ni, ni mu bi ŋidik pu nnyusakpem ni na.

ref: He will give a signal to the nations, and he will bring together the refugees from Judah and Israel, who have been scattered all over the earth.
text: Uwumbɔr ga yoor limɔkl aatuutaa paacham, ki mɔk ke u bi kuuni Israel ni Juda yaab bi nan yaa ki bi ntim yayam ni na, ki nyan ni bi dulnyaa aapepel ŋinaa na mɔmɔk ni.

ref: Israel will stop being jealous of Judah, and Judah will no longer be the enemy of Israel.
text: Israel aanaan ni aanib aan ki li kpa lipiipoln Juda yaab pu, le Juda yaab mu aan ki li ye Israel yaab aadim.

ref: Instead, they will get together and attack the Philistines in the west. Then they will defeat the Edomites, the Moabites, and the Ammonites in the east. They will rule those people and take from them whatever they want.
text: Bi ga kpaan le ki ti tak Filistia yaab bi bi liwilir wɔb na, aan ki kpaan ti jenn gaa binib bi bi liwipuul wɔb na mu aawan. Bi ga nyaŋ Edom ni Moab aanib; le Amonn yaab mu ga kii baamɔi.

ref: The Lord will dry up the arm of the Red Sea near Egypt, and he will send a scorching wind to divide the Euphrates River into seven streams that anyone can step across.
text: Le Uwumbɔr ga cha nnyunsakpem mu bi yin mu ke Sues na aanyun foor, ki ga cha libuln li ton na daa ki foor limɔɔl li bi yin li ke Yufrates na aanyun, ki di cha ibun waatiir ilole baanja aan unii mɔmɔk ga ŋmaa puur jer.

ref: Then for his people who survive, there will be a good road from Assyria, just as there was a good road for their ancestors when they left Egypt.
text: Nsankpaan ga li dɔ ki nyan ni Asiria ni, ki tii waanib bi kaa kpo ki bi nima na, ke mu aah nan dɔ tii biyaajatiib Israel yaab, baah nan nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni pu na.

ref: At that time you will say, “I thank you, Lord! You were angry with me, but you stopped being angry and gave me comfort.
text: Nwiin mubaa ga fuu ni le binib ga gaa nlahn ke, “M pak si Uwumbɔr. Aa nan gee m pu liŋuul, dandana ma kan, aa sɔŋ nsui kaa ki gee m pu liŋuul.

ref: I trust you to save me, Lord God, and I won't be afraid. My power and my strength come from you, and you have saved me.”
text: Uwumbɔr le ye maagaaliidaan; m ga tii u naadii kaan san ijawaan. Uwumbɔr tii mi mpɔɔn; uma le ye maagaaliidaan.

ref: With great joy, you people will get water from the well of victory.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa gaa waanib lii kan, bi kpa mpopiin ke nnyunsoom aah tii unii u nnyunyuu joo u na mpopiin pu na la.”

ref: At that time you will say, “Our Lord, we are thankful, and we worship only you. We will tell the nations how glorious you are and what you have done.
text: Nwiin mubaa ga fuu ni le binib ga gaa nlahn ke, “Doon Uwumbɔr man. Yin u ke u ter nimi man. Tuk ŋitimbol mɔmɔk waah ŋa pu na man. Tuk bi waah kpa liyimbil pu na man.

ref: Because of your wonderful deeds we will sing your praises everywhere on earth.”
text: Gaa ilahn tii Uwumbɔr, waah ŋa tiwankpaan ni tii nimi na pu. Cha dulnyaa mɔmɔk ŋun tibɔpɔnn ngbaan man.

ref: Sing, people of Zion! Celebrate the greatness of the holy Lord of Israel. God is here to help you.
text: Cha unii umɔk bi Sionn na teen ki gaa ilahn ke, Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na ye Uwumbɔrkpaan la, le ki bi waanib chee.”

ref: This is the message that I was given about Babylon:
text: Amos aajapɔɔn Aisaya aah gaa Uwumbɔr chee Babiloŋ aanaŋ i na sɔ:

ref: From high on a barren hill give a signal, shout the orders, and point the way to enter the gates of Babylon's proud rulers.
text: Ligongoln li kaa kpa nibaa na pu le butɔb aatuutaa fii. Teen ki bui butɔb aajab ngbaan, ki yoor aaŋaal paacham ki mɔk bi ke bi ti tak kitisakpeŋ ki kpa kipupuk na aabisamɔi.

ref: The Lord has commanded his very best warriors and his proud heroes to show how angry he is.
text: Uwumbɔr yin waatɔb aajab bi kpa kigaak ki nyi bibaa pu na ke bi nan jan mbamɔn aajaak ki daa waah gee binib bi pu liŋuul na aatafal.

ref: Listen to the noisy crowds on the mountains! Kingdoms and nations are joining forces. The Lord All-Powerful is bringing together an army for battle.
text: Li pel kifuuk ŋijoo ngbaan pu man, ni ye kinipaak sakpeŋ aafuuk; kifuuk ngbaan ye ŋitimbol ni nnaan aanib le bi kuuni tɔb chee. Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le bi gor bijab ke bi buen butɔb.

ref: From a distant land the Lord is coming fierce and furious— he brings his weapons to destroy the whole earth.
text: Bi nyan ni dandar aatimbol ŋi bi kitiŋ kee aadoon chee na la. Uwumbɔr aaŋuul pu le u choo ke u bii kitiŋ mɔmɔk doo.

ref: Cry and weep! The day is coming when the mighty Lord will bring destruction. *
text: Li wii man iween pu. Uwumbɔr aawiin duun ni a, bundaal uma Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga joo ni libiil na duun ni a.

ref: All people will be terrified. Hands will grow limp; courage will melt away.
text: Unibɔn mɔmɔk aawon ga yɔl, le ujakaan mɔmɔk ga san ijawaan.

ref: Everyone will tremble with pain like a woman giving birth; they will stare at each other with horror on their faces. There Will Be No Mercy
text: Ijawaan ga chuu bi mɔmɔk, le iween nyaŋ bi, ke imalween aah nyaŋni upudaan pu na. Bi ga li lik tɔb ki san ijawaan la, le inimɔɔn ga ku bi.

ref: I, the Lord, will show no mercy or pity when that time comes. In my anger I will destroy the earth and every sinner who lives on it.
text: Uwumbɔr aawiin choo, nwiin mu ga joo ni libiil, ni liŋuusakpeln, ni libiil li wu ke mmii na choo. Kitiŋ kee ga kpaln kitiŋ ki kaa kpa nibaa ki pu na la, le titunwanbirdam mɔmɔk ga doo.

ref: Light will disappear from the stars in the sky; the dawning sun will turn dark, and the moon will lose its brightness.
text: Iŋmabi mɔmɔk aan ki li wiin, le nwiin ga bɔln kaan ki li wiin, le uŋmal mu aan ki li wiin.

ref: I will punish this evil world and its people because of their sins. I will crush the horrible pride of those who are cruel.
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “M ga joo ni falaa kitiŋ kee pu aan ki daa titunwanbirdam mɔmɔk aatafal baatunwanbir pu. Umɔk kpa kigaak ni mbiin na, m ga daa utafal ki sunn bigaadam mɔmɔk taab.

ref: Survivors will be harder to find than the purest gold.
text: Binib bi ga ŋmar na aan li ban kani ke salmaa aah kaa ban kani pu na la.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, am terribly angry— I will make the sky tremble and the earth shake loose.
text: Nwiin mundaal aan min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga mɔk maaŋuul na, m ga cha kitaapaak deŋ, le kitiŋ mu ga dam ki nya kaah si nin chee na.”

ref: Everyone will run to their homelands, just as hunted deer run, and sheep scatter when they have no shepherd.
text: “Biwɔwɔm bi bi Babiloŋ ni na ga san gir baatim ni, ki yaa ke upeeman aah san ŋmar ukpan chee pu na, ki mu ga li bi ke ipiih i kaa kpa upihkpaal na aah bi pu na.

ref: Those men who are captured will be killed by a sword.
text: Bi ga di kijuk saa ku unii umɔk bi ga chuu u na.

ref: The Medes can't be bought off with silver or gold, and I'm sending them to attack Babylonia.
text: Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “M bi saar Media yaab ke bi ti tak Babiloŋ yaab la. Bitafal aan li bi tikunabr ni, le salmaa mu aan li mɔ bi.

ref: Their arrows will slaughter the young men; no pity will be shown to babies and children. The Lord Will Destroy Babylon
text: Bi ga di itɔi ni ipiin le ki di ku binachipɔm. Baan san mbipɔm ni mbim kinimbaak.

ref: The city of Babylon is glorious and powerful, the pride of the nation. But it will be like the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah after I, the Lord, destroyed them.
text: Babiloŋ aanaan le ŋan jer nnaan mɔmɔk; le mu aanib kpa kipupuk mu pu. Le min Uwumbɔr ga kuln Babiloŋ ke maah nan ŋa Sodom ni Gomora aatim pu na.

ref: No one will live in Babylon. Even nomads won't camp nearby, and shepherds won't let their sheep rest there.
text: Ubaa aan ki li bi ki ponn ni. Arab yaab bi chuu kpak na ubaa aan ki ŋa waanambuŋ nima, le upihkpaal ubaa mu aan ki di waapiih buen nima i ti ŋmɔ timoor.

ref: Only desert creatures, hoot owls, and ostriches will live in its ruins, and goats will leap about.
text: Ki ga kpaln nin chee timoor ni aapeel, ni ifiin ga li koo na la. Taataa mam ni ipeel ga li san nima la.

ref: Hyenas and wolves will howl from Babylon's fortresses and beautiful palaces. Its time is almost up!
text: Takɔ tiib ni ikakal yaa wii nima kan, ni ga li keei tidir fɔfɔk na, ni ŋibɔrdichal na ni la. Babiloŋ aayoonn fuu ni a. Kaawiin doo a.”

ref: The Lord will have mercy on Israel and will let them be his chosen people once again. He will bring them back to their own land, and foreigners will join them as part of Israel.
text: Uwumbɔr ga ki gir san waanib Israel yaab kinimbaak ki lee bi ke uyaab. U ga ki cha bi ki koo baatiŋ ponn ni, le biwɔwɔm ga dan nan li bi bi chee.

ref: Other nations will lead them home, and Israel will make slaves of them in the land that belongs to the Lord. Israel will rule over those who once governed and mistreated them. Death to the King of Babylonia!
text: Ŋitimbol pam le ga ter Israel yaab aan bi ki gir ni kitiŋ ki pu Uwumbɔr nan di tii bi na, le ŋitimbol pam ga li ye Israel yaab aanaagbiib ki tun lituln tii bi. Israel yaab ga ki nyaŋ binib bimɔk nan nyaŋ bi ki chur bi tinaagbiir na; le Israel yaab ga li gur joo binib bi nan muk bi na. Babiloŋ aabɔrkpaan koo kitekpiitiŋ ni

ref: The Lord will set you free from your sorrow, suffering, and slavery.
text: Uwumbɔr ga nyan Israel yaab baaween, ni baamuk ni, ni ŋitupɔɔl ŋi bi nan muk bi bi tun ŋi na.

ref: Then you will make fun of the King of Babylonia by singing this song: That cruel monster is done for! He won't attack us again.
text: U yaa ŋa nimina kan, u ga cha bi ŋa Babiloŋ aabɔr mbɔnyun ki len ke: “Ubɔrkpaan mbiindaan na lir a. Waan ki muk ubaa.

ref: The Lord has crushed the power of those evil kings,
text: Uwumbɔr kuln bitinjoob titunwanbirdam na aapɔɔn.

ref: who were furious and never stopped abusing the people of other nations.
text: Bi nan joo liŋuul muk binib bi bi nan chur bi tinaagbiir na, ki ŋani bi falaa n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: Now all the world is at peace; its people are celebrating with joyful songs.
text: Dandana ma kan, dulnyaa mɔmɔk kan mpopiin ni lifuur, le unii mɔmɔk gaa mpopiin aalahn.

ref: King of Babylonia, even the cypress trees and the cedars of Lebanon celebrate and say, “Since you were put down, no one comes along to chop us down.”
text: Santina aasui ni isui imɔk ŋan ki bi Lebanonn na kpa mpopiin ubɔrkpaan u lir na pu; ba pu? ubaa aa ki bi ki ga ki gaa i lii, waah kaa ki bi dandana pu pu na.

ref: The world of the dead eagerly waits for you. With great excitement, the spirits of ancient rulers hear about your coming.
text: “Kitekpiitiŋ gor kibaa, ki kii ki nan doon Babiloŋ aabɔrkpaan ngbaan. Bipɔɔndam bi nan bi kitiŋ kee pu na aawiin bi gor ki kii la. Bibɔrkpaam aawiin bi fiir nya baabɔrjal pu la.

ref: Each one of them will say, “Now you are just as weak as any of us!
text: Bi mɔmɔk yin ki bui u ke, ‘Dandana aa diŋ ke timi na la. Aa gur ye ti ponn ni ubaa la.

ref: Your pride and your music have ended here in the world of the dead. Worms are your blanket, maggots are your bed.”
text: Bi nan joo tibar gaa ilahn ki nyuŋni si, le dandana ma aa gur bi ti chee kitekpiitiŋ ni do la. Aa gur dɔ ŋikpaambil aawandookaan pu la, le ŋi bii aawon mɔmɔk pu.’”

ref: You, the bright morning star, have fallen from the sky! You brought down other nations; now you are brought down.
text: Babiloŋ aabɔrkpaan, aa nan ye ke kichakpiik ni aaŋmabil na, le dandana aa nyan kitaapaak ki ker lir ni kitiŋ. N‑yoonn mu jer na, aa nan chur ŋitimbol tinaagbiir, le dandana ma, bi mee si lii kitiŋ.

ref: You said to yourself, “I'll climb to heaven and place my throne above the highest stars. I'll sit there with the gods far away in the north.
text: Aa nan pɔɔni aabaa ke aa jon buen kitaapaak ki ti di saabɔrjal tɔŋ iŋmabi i ti bi paacham paacham na pu. Aa nan dak ke aa ga ti kal lijool li bi nwiin aasikakl wɔb, nin chee ŋiwaa kuun ni na, ke ubɔrkpaan na la.

ref: I'll be above the clouds, just like God Most High.”
text: Aa nan bui ke aa jon ti kal ntaalangbam paab ki bi ke Mpɔɔndaan Uwumbɔr na.

ref: But now you are deep in the world of the dead.
text: Le u tee joo ni si di dan taab taab nin chee nyoo sakpen na, kitekpiitiŋ ni.

ref: Those who see you will stare and wonder, “Is this the man who made the world tremble and shook up kingdoms?
text: Bitekpiib ga li waa bimɔi le ki lik si. Bi ga baa ke, “Naa ye uja wee le nan dam kitiŋ ki cha bibɔrkpaam aawon gbaa na aa?

ref: Did he capture every city and make earth a desert? Is he the one who refused to let prisoners go home?”
text: Uja wee le aa nan bii ntikpaam ki labr dulnyaa di ŋa nteersakpiin nin chee nibaa aan ŋmaa punn na aa? Naa ye uja umina le aa nan kii ke waanaagbiib kun bido na aa?

ref: When kings die, they are buried in glorious tombs.
text: Bibɔrkpaam mɔmɔk dɔ baakaakunyaan ni,

ref: But you will be left unburied, just another dead body lying underfoot like a broken branch. You will be one of many killed in battle and gone down to the deep rocky pit.
text: le aa ma aa kpa likaakul, le bi di si mee ke aa bur. Bi di butɔb aajab bi bi ku bi butɔb ni na aanikpol le di biin aa pu, ki di ni mɔmɔk mee ŋa kitanbuuk ni, ki taa taa ni pu,

ref: You won't be buried with kings; you ruined your country and murdered your people. You evil monster! We hope that your family will be forgotten forever.
text: ba pu? saah kuln saatingbaln ki ku saanib na, nima pu na, baan sub si ke bibɔrkpaam biken na. Saamaal mu ye titunwanbir aamaal na ponn ni ubaa aan ŋmar.

ref: We will slaughter your sons to make them pay for the crimes of their ancestors. They won't take over the world or build cities anywhere on this earth.
text: Cha linikul piin man. Ubɔrkpaan umina aajapɔtiib ga kpo biyaajatiib aatunwanbir pu. Bi ponn ni ubaa aan ki joo kitiŋ kee, ki mu aan maa ntim ki pu.” Uwumbɔr ga bii Babiloŋ aatiŋ

ref: The Lord All-Powerful has promised to attack Babylonia and destroy everyone there, so that none of them will ever be remembered again.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan len ke, “M ga tak Babiloŋ ki kuln ki, kaan di cha nibaa. Maan di cha mbim, ubaa aan ŋmar kpala. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: The Lord will sweep out the people, and the land will become a swamp for wild animals. Assyria Will Be Punished
text: M ga labr Babiloŋ ŋa kipuuk la, ifiin le ga li bi nima. M ga di ŋŋaan mu ŋar tiwan mɔmɔk na le ŋar Babiloŋ aatiŋ. Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.” Uwumbɔr ga kuln Asiria yaab

ref: The Lord All-Powerful has made this promise: Everything I have planned will happen just as I said.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan puu tipuur ke: “Maah ŋa maalandak pu na, kina le ga ŋa. Maah bui ke m ga ŋa pu na, kina le ga ŋa.

ref: I will wipe out every Assyrian in my country, and I will crush those on my mountains. I will free my people from slavery to the Assyrians.
text: M ga kuln Asiria yaab bi bi maatiŋ Israel ni na, ki taa taa bi pu maajoo pu, ki nyan maanib falaa u Asiria yaab ŋani bi na ni, ki gaa bi lii.

ref: I have planned this for the whole world, and my mighty arm controls every nation.
text: Maah ŋa maalandak mu ki tii dulnyaa na le na, le m fii sil ke m daa ŋitimbol aatafal.”

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have made these plans. No one can stop me now! The Philistines Will Be Punished
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan puu ke u ga ŋa nimina; u fii sil ke u daa binib aatafal, le ubaa aan ŋmaa kiir u ke u taa ŋa kina. Uwumbɔr ga kuln Filistia yaab

ref: This message came from the Lord in the year King Ahaz died:
text: Libiln li ponn ni ubɔrkpaan Ahas kpo na le tibɔr tee nan nyan ni.

ref: Philistines, don't be happy just because the rod that punished you is broken. That rod will become a poisonous snake, and then a flying fiery dragon.
text: Filistia yaab, lidabil li bi di gbaa nimi na koo a, ni mu taa tee laa man. Uwaa ubaa yaa kpo kan, u bir jer uma ngbaan na ga dan nan gaa waabuul ni. Uwaa aajeln kaal kiwanbiik la.

ref: The poor and needy will find pastures for their sheep and will live in safety. But I will starve some of you, and others will be killed.
text: Uwumbɔr le ga kpaa waanib bi ye bigiim na, ki tii bi ŋŋmarm. U ga cha nkon lir nimi Filistia yaab pu, le mu aan cha ni ponn ni ubaa ŋmar.

ref: Cry and weep in the gates of your towns, you Philistines! Smoke blows in from the north, and every soldier is ready.
text: Nimi Filistia aatim mɔmɔk, li wii ki gbei ki ban nterm man. Ni mɔmɔk san ijawaan man. Kitangbaak sakpeŋ kibaa nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb ki choo, ni ye bijakaab ŋmeen la, bijawaandam aa bi bi ponn ni.

ref: If a messenger comes from a distant nation, you must say: “The Lord built Zion. Even the poorest of his people will find safety there.”
text: Kinye aan ti ga gar ituun i nyan ni Filistia yaab chee na? Ti ga bui bi ke Uwumbɔr maa Sionn siin, le waanib bi nan ji falaa na ga kan lifuur nima chee.

ref: This is a message about Moab: The towns of Ar and Kir were destroyed in a night. Moab is left in ruins!
text: Moab yaab aanaŋ sɔ. Kinyeek kibaa le Ar ni Kir aatim ga bii, le ni mɔmɔk ga ŋmin chii.

ref: Everyone in Dibon has gone up to the temple and the shrines to cry and weep. All of Moab is crying. Heads and beards are shaved because of what happened at Nebo and Medeba.
text: Dibonn yaab jon ligongoln paab ki ti wii kiwaachuk ni. Moab yaab wii Nebo ni Medeba aatim aanib pu; bi kuu biyikpir ni bilangban mpombiin pu.

ref: In the towns and at home, everyone wears sackcloth and cries loud and long.
text: Binib bi chuun kitiŋ ponn ni na pee tiwan ni saak kuub na la; kitiŋ ponn ni, ni ŋidichal paab mɔmɔk binib kaani le ki wii ikpowiil.

ref: From Heshbon and Elealeh, weeping is heard in Jahaz; Moab's warriors scream while trembling with fear. Pity Moab
text: Hesbonn ni Eleale aanib wii la, le Jahas aatiŋ aanib ti ŋun baawiil pu. Hali butɔb aajab aawon gbaa la, le bitaakpab yɔl.

ref: I pity Moab! Its people are running to Zoar and to Eglath-Shelishiyah. They cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they tell of disasters.
text: Mpobil wu Moab yaab pu la. Binib ngbaan san buen Soar ni Eglaf Selisiya aatim ni. Bibaa san jon Luhif aasan pu, ki wii le ki cha; bibaa mu san ŋmar buen Horonaim, ki wii mpɔɔn pu.

ref: The streams of Nimrim and the grasslands have dried up. Every plant is parched.
text: Nnyun mu nan bi Nimrim aabun ni na foor a, timoor ti si mbun aagbaan na mɔmɔk yɔl a, le tiwasɔnn nibaa aa gur ki si.

ref: The people of Moab are leaving, crossing over Willow Creek, taking everything they own and have worked for.
text: Binib joo baawangol san puur cha Isui aafataŋ ni, ke bi di san ŋmar.

ref: In the towns of Eglaim and of Beerelim and everywhere else in Moab mournful cries are heard.
text: Moab aatiŋ aanaanmɔk mɔmɔk chee ye iwiil, le Eglaim ni Beer Elim aatim ni yaab ŋun iwiil ngbaan pu.

ref: The streams near Dimon are flowing with blood. But the Lord will bring even worse trouble to Dimon, because all in Moab who escape will be attacked by lions.
text: Dibonn aamɔɔl aanyun kpaln nsin la, le Uwumbɔr beenin kpa tibɔbir ti jer kina na ki tii nima aanib. Mbamɔn, ichinn ga ku binib bimɔk gur Moab aatiŋ ni na la.

ref: Send lambs as gifts to the ruler of the land. Send them across the desert from Sela to Mount Zion.
text: Sela aatiŋ ki bi nteersakpiin pu na, le Moab aanib di upihbo tun tichandaan, uja u joo Jerusalem na chee.

ref: The women of Moab crossing the Arnon River are like a flock of birds scattered from their nests.
text: Bi nan si Anonn aamɔɔl aagbaan le ki kii, kaa nyi baah ga ŋa pu na, aan ki di ti nya do, ki nan nya do, ke inyoon i bi jenn nyan i yaanyondil ni na.

ref: Moab's messengers say to the people of Judah, “Be kind and help us! Shade us from the heat of the noonday sun. Hide our refugees! Don't turn them away.
text: Le bi bui Juda yaab ke, “Bui timi taah ga ŋa pu na. Gaa timi lii ke mboon aah gaal unii lir nwiin pu pu na, ki cha ti fuur niŋaal ni. Ti ye bikusam la; bɔr timi nin chee ubaa aan ŋmaa kan timi na.

ref: Let our people live in your country and find safety here.” Moab, your cruel enemies will disappear; they will no longer attack and destroy your land.
text: Cha ti kal nimi aatiŋ pu man. Gaa timi lii binib bi ban bi kuln timi na chee man.” Tɔ, limukl ni mbiin ga doo, le binib bi ban bi kuln kitiŋ ngbaan na mu ga doo.

ref: Then a kingdom of love will be set up, and someone from David's family will rule with fairness. He will do what is right and quickly bring justice. Moab's Pride Is Destroyed
text: Le Ubɔrkpaan David aayaabil ubaa ji nnaan, le ki ga li joo binib ngbaan mbamɔm, ni ngeehm ni. Tiwan ni ye ibamɔn na, u ga ŋa ni mala kaan li taani, ki kan ke ibamɔn le ga li tun lituln.

ref: Tell everyone in Moab to mourn for their nation. Tell them to cry and weep for those fancy raisins of Kir-Hareseth.
text: Moab aanib ga wii baafalaa u bi jin na pu. Bi mɔmɔk yaa teer baah nan ji tijikaar nyaan ti Kir Heres ni na pu kan, bi ga wii. Biwon ga yɔl.

ref: Vineyards near Heshbon and Sibmah have turned brown. The rulers of nations used to get drunk on wine from those vineyards that spread to Jazer, then across the desert and beyond the sea.
text: Tisar ti bi Hesbonn chee na, ni ŋisubil aasui aasar ti bi Sibma na mɔmɔk bii doo; ŋisubil ngbaan aadaan le ŋitimbol aabɔrb nan nyu ki gbii. N‑yoonn mubaa isui imina aabon taln ti nyan Jaser aatiŋ ni, ki taln buen liwipuul wɔb, nteersakpiin ni, ki taln buen liwilir wɔb ki ti saa nnyusakpem aagbaan.

ref: Now I mourn like Jazer for the vineyards of Sibmah. I shed tears for Heshbon and for Elealeh. There will be no more harvest celebrations
text: Dandana m wii Sibma aatiŋ aasui ngbaan pu ke maah wii Jasar aatiŋ pu pu na. M wii tii Hesbonn ni Eleale aatim; ba pu? nibaa aa bi aan binib ngbaan ga chee aan ni mɔɔr bi.

ref: or joyful and happy times, while bringing in the crops. Singing and shouting are gone from the vineyards. There are no joyful shouts where grapes were pressed. God has silenced them all.
text: Ubaa aa ki bi ikpaakon i nan kpa tijikaar na ni ki kpa mpopiin. Ubaa mu aa ki bi ŋisubil aasar ni ki tar ki gaa ilahn. Ubaa aa ki tun ndaan aatuln nima; le mmɔɔn aafuuk na ŋmin.

ref: Deep in my heart I hurt for Moab and Kir-Heres.
text: M ker idun ni mpombiin, Moab ni Kir Heres aatim aanib pu.

ref: It's useless for Moab's people to wear themselves out by going to their altars to worship and pray.
text: Moab aanib ŋani bibaa falaa ki chaa baatingban, ni baameen aadir ni ke bi ti mee baawaa, le naan ŋa bi tinyoor tibaa.

ref: The Lord has already said all of this about Moab.
text: Tibɔr ti Uwumbɔr nan puen di nabr tii ni Moab yaab na le bi na.

ref: Now he says, “The contract of a hired worker is good for three years, but Moab's glory and greatness won't last any longer than that. Only a few of its people will survive, and they will be left helpless.”
text: Le dandana wee Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Joo cha ni ŋibin ŋitaa na Moab aawangol mɔmɔk ga wɔŋ. Kaanipaak na ponn ni siib le ga ŋmar, le ki mu aan li kpa mpɔɔn kpala.”

ref: This is a message about Damascus: Damascus is doomed! It will end up in ruins.
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “Damaskus aan ki li ye kitiŋ sakpeŋ; ki ga li gur ye ŋilangbentanjal ŋmeen la.

ref: The villages around Aroer will be deserted, with only sheep living there and no one to bother them.
text: Binib ga san cha Siria aatim mɔmɔk. Mu ga li gur ye inaa ni ipiih aah ŋmɔ timoor nin chee, aan ubaa aan san jenn i na la.

ref: Israel will lose its fortresses. The kingdom of Damascus will be destroyed; its survivors will suffer the same fate as Israel. The Lord All-Powerful has promised this. Sin and Suffering
text: Israel aatiŋ aan ki li kpa unii u ga li kii ki na, le Damaskus aatiŋ aan ki li bi kibaa pu. Siria yaab bi ŋmar na ga ji inimɔɔn ke Israel yaab aah ji inimɔɔn pu na la. Min, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.”

ref: When that time comes, the glorious nation of Israel will be brought down; its prosperous people will be skin and bones.
text: Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Nwiin mubaa choo, le Israel aapɔɔn ga doo, le kaawangol ga kpaln igiin.

ref: It will be like an olive tree beaten with a stick, leaving two or three olives or maybe four or five on the highest or most fruitful branches. The Lord God of Israel has promised this.
text: Binib siib baanja le ga gur, le Israel aatiŋ ga li gur bi ke baah ker olif aasubil ki cha lisubil libaabaa bu aapaacham pu na, bee siisiib ŋi gur bu aataab aasubon pu pu na la. Min, Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: At that time the people will turn and trust their Creator, the holy God of Israel.
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal yaa fuu ni kan, binib ga fenn ki ban nterm u naan bi na chee; uma le ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na.

ref: They have built altars and places for burning incense to their goddess Asherah, and they have set up sacred poles for her. But they will stop worshiping at these places.
text: Baan ki li lik ban baah nan di biŋaal maa ŋiwaabimbin ŋi na, kaan ki tii bibaa aaŋaal aah ŋa liwaapii Asera ni ŋiwaabimbin nin chee bi seer nnyɔknii na naadii.

ref: Israel captured powerful cities and chased out the people who lived there. But these cities will lie in ruins, covered over with weeds and underbrush.
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal yaa fuu ni kan, ntisakpem mu bi kii mu mbamɔm na ga gur nkuun ni ŋilangben ke ntim mu Hif yaab ni Amor yaab nan san cha buyoonn Israel yaab nan choo na la.

ref: Israel, you have forgotten the God who saves you, the one who is the mighty rock where you find protection. You plant the finest flowers to honor a foreign god.
text: Israel yaab, ni suln Uwumbɔr bɔr; uma le nan nyan ni nimi ki kii nimi ke litakpasakpeln na. Naah tee ŋa pu na le ye ke ni ŋum ŋisubil aasui le ki dooni ŋiwaa.

ref: The plants may sprout and blossom that very same morning, but it will do you no good, because you will suffer endless agony. God Defends His People
text: Hali isui ngbaan yaa punn ki guu ŋeen liwinbaal kan, naan kan nibaa i pu. Naah ga kan pu na le ye falaa ni iween i kaan sɔŋ na. Bidim aatimbol lir a

ref: But even if they roar like a fearsome flood, God will give the command to turn them back. They will be like dust, or like a tumbleweed blowing across the hills in a windstorm.
text: Ŋitimbol san ni ke tinyunkpenn na, le Uwumbɔr teen bi pu, le bi gir bipuwɔb mala ke kitangbaak aah san sunni ligongoln taab pu na, ki naahn kimook aah bi kinaakpaajabuŋ ponn ni pu na.

ref: In the evening their attack is fierce, but by morning they are destroyed. This is what happens to those who raid and rob us.
text: Kijook kan, bi kpa ijawaan, le kichakpiik ni kan, bi buen a. Unii umɔk gaa timi aatiŋ aawan mpɔɔn na aadoon le na.

ref: Downstream from Ethiopia lies the country of Egypt, swarming with insects.
text: Kifuuk ki naahn ifeen aafuuk na nyan ni Kus aamɔɔ aapuwɔb kitiŋ kibaa ni.

ref: Egypt sends messengers up the Nile River on ships made of reeds. Send them fast to Ethiopia, whose people are tall and have smooth skin. Their land is divided by rivers; they are strong and brutal, feared all over the world.
text: Kitiŋ ngbaan ni le bininkpiib bi si baatiŋ aasisiiyaan na nyan ni Nail aamɔɔl ni, ki bi iŋɔi i bi di tikal ŋa i na ni. Ntuun tiib bi ŋmaa chuun mala mala na, gir kun man. Gaa man inaŋ ki di buen nimi aatiŋ ki ŋimɔɔ yakr ki, aan ki ye litimbol li kpa mpɔɔn sakpen, aan kaanib fɔk, aan biwon joon kpal kpal, bi dulnyaa mɔmɔk aanib san bi ijawaan na chee.

ref: Everyone on this earth, listen with care! A signal will be given on the mountains, and you will hear a trumpet.
text: Unii umɔk bi kitiŋ kee pu na, li pel man. Lik ban limɔkl aatuutaa u ga fii paacham ŋijoo pu na man. Li pel man ukpiin aah wii pu na.

ref: The Lord said to me, “I will calmly look down from my home above— as calmly as the sun at noon or clouds in the heat of harvest season.”
text: Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, “M ga li bi kitaapaak ki lik ni suuna ke lijikaacheel yoonn aamaln aah naani kinyeek pu na, ki lik chimm ke nwiin aah wiin nwiin pu pu na.

ref: Before the blossoms can turn into grapes, God will cut off the sprouts and hack off the branches.
text: Waahr aan bi nin ker ŋisubil na, buyoonn mpuun gbar aan ŋi bi puir na, bidim ga kuln Kus aatiŋ yaab mala ke kijuk aah geei nsubon pu na.

ref: Ethiopians will be food for mountain vultures during the summer and for wild animals during the winter.
text: Baatɔb aajab bi kpo butɔb ni na aanikpol ga li dɔ, le inyoon ni ipeel i bir na ji. Kitotoŋ yoonn le inyoon ga ji ŋinikpol ngbaan, le ipeel mu ŋmɔ ŋi kakab yoonn.”
