ref: Those Ethiopians are tall and their skin is smooth. They are feared all over the world, because they are strong and brutal. But at that time they will come from their land divided by rivers, and they will bring gifts to the Lord All-Powerful, who is worshiped on Mount Zion.
text: N‑yoonn choo le Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga nan gaa ipiin nyan ni kitiŋ ki ŋimɔɔ yakr ki na chee, litimbol ngbaan le kpa mpɔɔn ki pɔɔ, le ki kpa binib bi fɔk, aan biwon joon kpal kpal, aan dulnyaa wee aanib san bi ijawaan na. Bi ga li joo ni ipiin ngbaan ki dan Sionn aajool pu, nin chee bi dooni Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan na.

ref: This is a message about Egypt: The Lord comes to Egypt, riding swiftly on a cloud. The people are weak from fear. Their idols tremble as he approaches and says,
text: Ijipt aatiŋ aabɔr sɔ. Uwumbɔr ka ntaalangbam pu ki choo Ijipt aatiŋ ni. Ijipt yaab aawaa aawon gbaa la. Ijipt aanib aataakpab yɔl a.

ref: “Egypt will be discouraged when I confuse their plans. They will try to get advice from their idols, from the spirits of the dead, and from fortunetellers.
text: M ban m bii Ijipt yaab aah kpokl pu na ki yɔl bitaakpab la. Bi ga buen ti bui baawaa ke ŋi ter bi, ki ga buen bipɔnijoob ni bitekpiib chee ke bi mɔk bi baah ga ŋa pu na.

ref: I will put the Egyptians under the power of a cruel, heartless king. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have promised this.” Trouble along the Nile
text: M ga di Ijipt yaab tii ubiindaan ubaa, ubɔrkpaan u kpa mbiin sakpen na, le u li joo bi. Min, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.”

ref: The Nile River will dry up and become parched land.
text: Nail aamɔɔl aanyun ga foor, aan limɔɔl ngbaan ga li ŋani kina le ki ti kuur.

ref: Its streams will stink, Egypt will have no water, and the reeds and tall grass will dry up.
text: Inyunsan ngbaan ga li foor suusuu suusuu, ki nuŋ, le ki ti kuur. Timɔɔmoor ni tikal ga yɔl,

ref: Fields along the Nile will be completely barren; every plant will disappear.
text: le tijikaar ti mɔmɔk bi bun Nail aamɔɔgbaln na ga kuur, le libuln daa ti buen.

ref: Those who fish in the Nile will be discouraged and mourn.
text: Binib bi ye bijanbam ki chur ijan Nail aamɔɔl ni na ga ker idun ki wii; baapɔr ni ijapiin ga bee fam.

ref: None of the cloth makers will know what to do, and they will turn pale.
text: Binib bi mɔmɔk luu agoo aakeken na aasui ga bii;

ref: Weavers will be confused; paid workers will cry and mourn. Egypt's Helpless Leaders
text: bikpaluub ni biwanŋab mɔmɔk aasui ga bii.

ref: The king's officials in Zoan are foolish themselves and give stupid advice. How can they say to him, “We are very wise, and our families go back to kings of long ago?”
text: Soann aatiŋ aaninkpiib ye bijɔrb la. Ijipt aalandam aasurm ye kijɔrk la. Ŋma ŋmann bi ke bi bui ubɔrkpaan ngbaan ke bima le nab n‑yaayoonn na aagbanyib ni bibɔrb na pu?

ref: Where are those wise men now? If they can, let them say what the Lord All-Powerful intends for Egypt.
text: Ijipt aabɔrkpaan, saalandam bi sur si na bi la? Nibaakan bi ga ŋmaa tuk si Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aah ban u ŋa nimi Ijipt yaab pu na.

ref: The royal officials in Zoan and in Memphis are foolish and deceived. The leaders in every state have given bad advice to the nation.
text: Soann ni Memfis aatim aaninkpiib ye bijɔrb la. Baatuln le nan ye ke bi joo litimbol, le bi tee di bi yenn.

ref: No one in Egypt can do a thing, no matter who they are.
text: Ubaa aa bi Ijipt ni, biwankpadam ni bigiim, bininyuum ni baah kaa nyi binib bi bɔr na, aan ŋmaa ter bi. Ijipt yaab ga doon Uwumbɔr

ref: When the Lord All-Powerful punishes Egypt with his mighty arm, the Egyptians will become terribly weak and will tremble with fear.
text: N‑yoonn mubaa choo le Ijipt yaab ga nan li diin ke bipiib na. Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan yaa taln uŋaal ke u daa bitafal kan, biwon ga li gbaa ijawaan pu la.

ref: They will be so terrified of Judah that they will be frightened by the very mention of its name. This will happen because of what the Lord All-Powerful is planning against Egypt. The Lord Will Bless Egypt, Assyria, and Israel
text: Ijipt yaab ga san Juda yaab ijawaan n‑yoonn mumɔk bi teer bi Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aah gor ntafadaan mu kiir bi na.

ref: The time is coming when Hebrew will be spoken in five Egyptian cities, and their people will become followers of the Lord. One of these cities will be called City of the Sun.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, bi ga li len Israel yaab aaliin, Ijipt aatim muŋmu ni la. Nima chee aanib ga li gur puur baapuur Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aayimbil pu la. Ntim ngbaan kibaa aayimbil le ga li ye ke, “Nwiin Aatiŋ.”

ref: In the heart of Egypt an altar will be set up for the Lord; at its border a shrine will be built to honor him.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aatork aabimbiln ga li bi Ijipt aatiŋ pu, le bi ga maa ligoln waayimbil pu Ijipt aatiŋ aanaanmɔk.

ref: These will remind the Egyptians that the Lord All-Powerful is with them. And when they are in trouble and ask for help, he will send someone to rescue them from their enemies.
text: Libimbiln ni ligoln ngbaan ga li ye limɔkl ki mɔk ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bi Ijipt aatiŋ ponn ni la. Limukl yaa pii nima chee aanib aan bi yin Uwumbɔr aayimbil ki ban nterm kan, u ga tun unii aan u ti gaa bi lii.

ref: The Lord will show the Egyptians who he is, and they will know and worship the Lord. They will bring him sacrifices and offerings, and they will keep their promises to him.
text: Uwumbɔr ga di ubaa mɔk Ijipt aanib, le bi ga bee u ki doon u, aan ki joo ni kitork ni ipiin nan tii u. Bi ga puu tipuur bamɔnn tii u le ki ŋa baah puu pu na.

ref: After the Lord has punished Egypt, the people will turn to him. Then he will answer their prayers, and the Egyptians will be healed.
text: Uwumbɔr ga daa Ijipt aanib aatafal, le ki mu ga ki sɔŋ bisui. Bi ga fenn dan u chee, le u ga ŋun baameel, le ki nyan bi baafalaa ni.

ref: At that time a good road will run from Egypt to Assyria. The Egyptians and the Assyrians will travel back and forth from Egypt to Assyria, and they will worship together.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, nsanja ga li bi ki nya Ijipt aatiŋ ni ki cha Asiria aatiŋ ni. Ŋitingbaln ŋilee ŋimina ga chuun koo tɔb ni, ki kpaan tɔb chee ki doon Uwumbɔr.

ref: Israel will join with these two countries. They will be a blessing to everyone on earth,
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, Israel, ni Ijipt, ni Asiria aatingbaln ga kpaan tɔb chee, le ŋitingbaln ŋitaa ngbaan ga li ye tinyoor sakpenn ki tii dulnyaa mɔmɔk.

ref: then the Lord All-Powerful will bless them by saying, “The Egyptians are my people. I created the Assyrians and chose the Israelites.”
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga ŋa waanyoor ŋa ŋi pu, ki bui ke, “M ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa nimi Ijipt yaab bi ye maanib na; ni nimi Asiria yaab bi m naan bi na, ni nimi Israel yaab bi ye maanib na pu.”

ref: King Sargon of Assyria gave orders for his army commander to capture the city of Ashdod.
text: Asiria aabɔrkpaan Sargonn nan cha waatɔb aajab aaninkpel ti tak Filistia aatikpaan Asdod.

ref: About this same time the Lord had told me, “Isaiah, take off everything, including your sandals!” I did this and went around naked and barefoot
text: Ŋibin ŋitaa waahr aan nimina nin ŋa na, Uwumbɔr nan bui Amos aajapɔɔn Aisaya ke u takr waanaatak ki peer tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na. U nan kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki nan gur chuun uŋmeen kaa tak ŋinaatak.

ref: Everyone in these two countries will be led away naked and barefoot by the king of Assyria. Young or old, they will be taken prisoner, and Egypt will be disgraced.
text: Asiria aabɔrkpaan ga di biyom bi u chuu ŋitingbaln ŋilee ngbaan ni na di buen biŋmeen, kaa tak ŋinaatak mu. Mbim ni bininkpiib mɔmɔk ga chuun biŋmeen, kaan li tak ŋinaatak mu, le bimunjal dɔ; nimina le ga joo ni inimɔɔn nan tii Ijipt aatiŋ.

ref: They will be confused and frustrated, because they depended on Ethiopia and bragged about Egypt.
text: Binib bi di naadii tii Kus aatiŋ ki kpa kipupuk Ijipt aatiŋ pu na ga bee ke bi nan di bibaa mee la.

ref: When this happens, the people who live along the coast will say, “Look what happened to them! We ran to them for safety, hoping they would protect us from the king of Assyria. But now, there is no escape for us.”
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, binib bi koo Filistia yaab aatiŋ, nnyusakpem aagbaan chee na, ga bui ke, ‘Lik man tiwan ni ŋa binib bi ti nan di tibaa tii bi ke bi li kii timi Asiria aabɔrkpaan chee na. Ti ga ŋa kinye aan ki tee ŋmar?’”

ref: This is a message about a desert beside the sea: Enemies from a hostile nation attack like a whirlwind from the Southern Desert.
text: Babiloŋ yaab aabɔr sɔ. Kinaakpaajabuŋ aah ŋar nteer pu pu na, kina le tibɔbir ga nyan ni ijawaan aatiŋ kibaa ni ki dan Babiloŋ pu.

ref: What a horrible vision was shown to me— a vision of betrayal and destruction. Tell Elam and Media to surround and attack the Babylonians. The Lord has sworn to end the suffering they caused.
text: M kan libiil aabɔr tibɔkpiirkaan ni, libiil ni ŋŋmannim aabɔr. Elam aajab, ti tak bi man. Media aajab, buen ti gob man ntim ngbaan. Uwumbɔr ga kuln Babiloŋ yaab aah tii nimi falaa u na.

ref: I'm in terrible pain like a woman giving birth. I'm shocked and hurt so much that I can't hear or see.
text: Maah kan ki ŋun tibɔr ti tibɔkpiirkaan ngbaan ponn ni na tii mi ijawaan ni iween, iween i wu ke imalween na.

ref: My head spins; I'm horrified! Early evening, my favorite time, has become a nightmare.
text: N‑yil gaar la, le ijawaan cha nwon gbaa. M nan ka dak ke kijook fuu ni mala, le ni tee joo ni mi ijawaan ŋmeen.

ref: In Babylon the high officials were having a feast. They were eating and drinking, when someone shouted, “Officers, take your places! Grab your shields.”
text: Tibɔkpiirkaan ngbaan ponn ni, bi gor njim aajikaar a, ki di ikan ter ke bicham nan kal i pu. Bi bi ji ki nyu. Libuul ngbaan ni le bi tii nsan: “Butɔb aajab aaninkpiib, gor man nimi aapen ŋi ni joo jaa kijaak na.”

ref: When they see cavalry troops and columns of soldiers on donkeys and camels, tell them to be ready!”
text: U yaa kan bijab jak itaan pu ki dii tɔb bilelee kan, ni bijab dek ibon ni laakumii mam pu kan, u lik bi suuna.”

ref: Then a guard said, “I have stood day and night on this watchtower, Lord.
text: Tɔ, ukikiir ngbaan teen ki len ke, “Maaninkpel, m si maabuul ni, nwiin pu ni kinyeek.”

ref: Now I see column after column of cavalry troops.” At once someone shouted, “Babylon has fallen! Every idol in the city lies broken on the ground.”
text: Libuul ngbaan ni, le bi nyan ni. Bijab jak itaan, ki dii tɔb bilelee. Ukikiir ngbaan tuk mi waah kan pu na, “Babiloŋ lir a. Baah nan dooni ŋiwaa ŋimɔk na lir kitiŋ ki wii a.”

ref: Then I said, “My people, you have suffered terribly, but I have a message for you from the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel.” How Much Longer?
text: Maanib Israel yaab, bi poi nimi ke idi na la, le dandana m ban m moon ki bui nimi tibɔnyaan ti m ŋun Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan chee na; uma le ye nimi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr. Edom yaab aabɔr

ref: This is a message about Dumah: From the country of Seir, someone shouts to me, “Guard, how much longer before daylight?”
text: Edom yaab aabɔr sɔ. Ubaa bi Edom ki baa mi ke, “Ukikiir, bayoonn aan kitaak ga woln? Bui mi naah ga yunn pu aan kinyeek doo na.”

ref: From my guard post, I answered, “Morning will soon be here, but night will return. If you want to know more, come back later.”
text: Le m gar u ke, “Kichakpiik ni choo, le kinyeek mu ga ki gir ni. Aa yaa ki ban aa baa kan, aa gir ni ki nan ki baa.” Arabia yaab aabɔr

ref: This is a message for Arabs who live in the barren desert in the region of Dedan: You must order your caravans
text: Arabia yaab aabɔr sɔ. Nimi Dedann aanib, nimi bi chuun ki tiir kitiirk ki doo Arabia aatingbaln li kaa kpa nibaa na pu na,

ref: to bring water for those who are thirsty. You people of Tema must bring food for the hungry refugees.
text: tiin man binib bi nnyunyuu joo bi na nnyun. Nimi Tema aatiŋ aanib, tiin bikusam na tijikaar man.

ref: They are worn out and weary from being chased by enemies with swords and arrows.
text: Bi san ke bi ŋmar kijaak aajum mu ban mu ku bi na chee, ni itɔi i gor ke i too na, ni butɔb aabɔbir chee la.

ref: Only a few of their warriors will be left with bows and arrows. This is a promise that I, the Lord God of Israel, have made.
text: Bijab bi too itɔi na le kaar sakpen Kedar aajab ni, le bi ponn ni siib le ga gur. Min, Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: This is a message about Vision Valley: Why are you celebrating on the flat roofs of your houses?
text: Tibɔr timina ye kifataŋ ki ponn ni Uwumbɔr kpiir tiwan mɔk waanib na aabɔr la. Ni ye ba bi ŋani? Ba ŋa binib ngbaan mɔmɔk bi ji njim baadichal aapaacham.

ref: Your city is filled with noisy shouts. Those who lie drunk in your streets were not killed in battle.
text: Kitisakpeŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk ponn ni kpa kifuuk la; ki gbii kifuuk ni mpopiin la. Nimi aajab bi kpoi butɔb bue ni na aa bi jaa le ki kpoi.

ref: Your leaders ran away, but they were captured without a fight. No matter how far they ran, they were found and caught.
text: Nimi aaninkpiib mɔmɔk san, kaa kee too mpiin mubaa, le baadim chur bi.

ref: Then I said, “Leave me alone! Let me cry bitter tears. My people have been destroyed, so don't try to comfort me.”
text: Di cha mi man aan m wii maanib bimɔk kpo na pu. Taa sɔŋni nsui man.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful had chosen a time for noisy shouts and confusion to fill Vision Valley, and for everyone to beg the mountains for help.
text: N‑yoonn mumina ye mpobiyuk, ni linyaŋ, ni nlanŋmal le Tibɔkpiirkaan Aafataŋ ngbaan ni. Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le tun ni kina ti chee. Bi gbaa wii timi aatiŋ aagon, le binib aah wii pu ki ban nterm na ti keei ŋigongon paab.

ref: Your most beautiful valleys were covered with chariots; your cities were surrounded by cavalry troops.
text: Juda aafataŋ ki nan ŋa tijikaar n‑yoonn na gbii itaan aatɔroku tiib; butɔb aajab bi dek itaan pu na si Jerusalem aatiŋ aabisamɔi.

ref: Judah was left defenseless. At that time you trusted in the weapons you had stored in Forest Palace.
text: Juda aatim aagon mɔmɔk lir a. Kina yaa nan ŋa kan, le ni buen tijawan aadiik ni, ni ti ban tijawan;

ref: You counted the houses in Jerusalem and tore down some of them, so you could get stones to repair the city wall.
text: ni kan nin chee Jerusalem aagon ban ntoorm na; ni lik Jerusalem aadichal mɔmɔk, ki gbaa wii ŋibaa, ki nyan ŋitakpal ke ni di toor ŋigon ngbaan,

ref: Then you built a large tank between the walls to store the water. But you refused to trust the God who planned this long ago and made it happen. A Time To Weep
text: ni gbii limɔɔl bil kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni ke ni chuu nnyun mu nyan ni kibukpiik kpok na ni, kaa tee dak Uwumbɔr u kpokl tibɔbir timina mɔmɔk n‑yoonn mu jer na ki cha ti ŋa kina na ma bɔr.

ref: When all of this happened, the Lord All-Powerful told you to weep and mourn, to shave your heads, and wear sackcloth.
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, nan bi yin nimi ke ni nan wii, ki wii ikpowiil, ki kuu niyil, ki peen tiwan ni saak kuub na aawanpeenkaan.

ref: But instead, you celebrated by feasting on beef and lamb and by drinking wine, because you said, “Let's eat and drink today! Tomorrow we may die.”
text: Le ni tee laa ki waa kinaachoŋ; ni kɔr ipiih ni inaa ke ni ŋmɔ, ki nyun ndaan; ni bui ke, “Ni ŋan ke ti ji ki nyu mu; ba pu? ti ga fe kpo fen.”

ref: The Lord All-Powerful has spoken to me this solemn promise: “I won't forgive them for this, not as long as they live.” Selfish Officials Are Doomed
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, uma ubaa le len m chee ki bui ke, “Maan di cha tibɔbir timina pinn bi n‑yoonn mumɔk bi bi na. Min, Nidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, le len kina.” Uwumbɔr sak Sebna

ref: The Lord All-Powerful is sending me with this message for Shebna, the prime minister:
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui mi ke m buen libɔrchiln aaninkpel Sebna chee, ki ti bui u ke,

ref: Shebna, what gives you the right to have a tomb carved out of rock in this burial place of royalty? None of your relatives are buried here.
text: “Aa yin aabaa ŋma? Aa kpa ba aasan ke aa gbii likaakul ŋitakpal ni, ligongoln ni, tii aabaa?

ref: You may be powerful, but the Lord is about to snatch you up and throw you away.
text: Nibaakan aa ga li ye uninyuun la, le Uwumbɔr ga yoor si ki di mee.

ref: He will roll you into a ball and throw you into a wide open country, where you will die and your chariots will be destroyed. You're a disgrace to those you serve.
text: U ga yoor si ke litakpal na ki di mee lii litingbaln li wiir sakpen na ni. Aa ga kpo nima chee, itaan aatɔroku tiib bi aa kpa kipupuk bi pu na chee. Aa jinni saadichandaan inimɔɔn la.

ref: The Lord is going to take away your job!
text: Uwumbɔr ga nyan si saaninkpir ni, ki sunn si taab.”

ref: He will give your official robes and your authority to his servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah. Eliakim will be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the royal family of Judah.
text: M ga nan di saaninkpir aabɔkul ni saagbapapaln tii u, ki di mpɔɔn mu aa nan kpa na tii u. U ga li ye Jerusalem ni Juda yaab aate la.

ref: The Lord will put him in charge of the key that belongs to King David's family. No one will be able to unlock what he locks, and no one will be able to lock what he unlocks.
text: M ga di mpɔɔn mɔmɔk tii u, le u li bi ubɔrkpaan u ye David aayaabil na aataŋaal ni. U ga li joo tininkpir aapiin; waah piir nimɔk na, ubaa aan ki di piin, le waah laŋ nimɔk na, ubaa mu aan ki piir.

ref: The Lord will make him as firm in his position as a tent peg hammered in the ground, and Eliakim will bring honor to his family.
text: M ga baa u kaan libuul libaa ni, le u ga li ye waamaal mɔmɔk aapakm.

ref: His children and relatives will be supported by him, like pans hanging from a peg on the wall.
text: “Le waamaal ni aanib bimɔk ji u pu na ga li ye lituln le ki tii u. Bi ga li lun u pu ke ituun ni tiyir aah lun nkpaa pu pu na la.

ref: That peg is fastened firmly now, but someday it will be shaken loose and fall down. Then everything that was hanging on it will be destroyed. This is what the Lord All-Powerful has promised.
text: Kina yaa nan ŋa kan, nkpaa mu bi nan kpaa mpɔɔn pu na ga ŋɔb ki lir. Le tiwan nimɔk nan lun mu pu na doo le na.” Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Mourn in silence, you shop owners of Sidon, you people on the coast. Your sailors crossed oceans, making your city rich.
text: Li wii man, nimi bi tiir kitiirk Saidonn aatiŋ ni na. Ni tun bijab

ref: Your merchants sailed the seas, making you wealthy by trading with nation after nation. They brought back grain that grew along the Nile.
text: ke bi puur nnyusakpem ki ti daa ki kooh ŋikalmaan ŋi nyan Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, ki tiir kitiirk ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ni.

ref: Sidon, you are a mighty fortress built along the sea. But you will be disgraced like a married woman who never had children.
text: Saidonn aatisakpeŋ, inimɔɔn chuu si a. Nnyusakpem, ni tiwan ni bi mu taab na yii si ki bui ke, “Maa ma mbim kpala. Maa kpiin mbijabim ni mpiibim kpala.”

ref: All of you along the coast had better cry and sail far across the ocean.
text: Li wii man mpombiin pu, nimi Fonisia yaab. Pɔɔn man nibaa ki san buen Speenn aatiŋ ni.

ref: Can this be the happy city that has stood for centuries? Its people have spread to distant lands;
text: Mpopiin aatisakpeŋ Taya ki nan bi n‑yoonn mu jer na le na aa? Kitisakpeŋ ki nan tun kaanib ke bi puur nnyusakpem ki ti naan ntipɔm na le bi na aa?

ref: its merchants were kings honored all over the world. Who planned to destroy Tyre?
text: Ŋma nan kal kpokl ke tibɔbir timina dan Taya aatiŋ pu, mpɔɔn aatiŋ ki aawantiirb naahn biyidam, ki nan ye bininyuum kitiŋ kee pu na?

ref: The Lord All-Powerful planned it to bring shame and disgrace to those who are honored by everyone on earth.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le kpokl kina. U kpokl kina ke u kuln baagaak, ni baah tun pu na, ki jinn baaninyuum inimɔɔn.

ref: People of Tyre, your harbor is destroyed! You will have to become farmers just like the Egyptians. Tyre Will Be Forgotten
text: Nimi bi bi ntim mu bi Speenn aatingbaln ni na, buen ti ko kitiŋ ngbaan man. Ubaa aa ki bi ki ga li kii nimi.

ref: The Lord's hand has reached across the sea, upsetting the nations. He has given a command to destroy fortresses in the land of Canaan.
text: Uwumbɔr taln uŋaal paan nnyusakpem pu ki nyaŋ bibɔrb aanaan. U cha bi bii Fonisia aanyam.

ref: The Lord has said to the people of Sidon, “Your celebrating is over— you are crushed. Even if you escape to Cyprus, you won't find peace.”
text: Saidonn aatisakpeŋ, saamɔɔn doo a, le saanib bi limukl ni. Hali bi yaa san buen Saiprus aatiŋ ni kan, bi ga li beenin bi tibɔr ni.

ref: Look what the Assyrians have done to Babylonia! They have attacked, destroying every palace in the land. Now wild animals live among the ruins.
text: Babiloŋ yaab le nan cha tipeewanbir bii Taya aatiŋ, naa nan ye Asiria yaab. Babiloŋ yaab le nan ti gob ki bii Taya aatiŋ aapɔɔn, ki cha tilangbenn ŋmeen.

ref: Not a fortress will be left standing, so tell all the seagoing ships to mourn.
text: Li wii mpombiin pu, nimi bi ŋaal iŋɔi nnyusakpem ponn ni na. Kitisakpeŋ ki ni mak ki pu na kuln a.

ref: You're gone and forgotten, you evil woman! So strut through the town, singing and playing your favorite tune to be remembered again.
text: Yoor saabeek, mann gonn kitiŋ ngbaan, sin udagoorgiin u bi suln u pu na. Li gbaa ki, ki gir gaa saalahn, ki ki gir giin ni bijab aa chee.

ref: but none of what is earned will be kept in the city. That money will belong to the Lord, and it will be used to buy more than enough food and good clothes for those who worship the Lord.
text: Bi ga di ŋimombil ŋi bi kani kitiirk ni na di tii Uwumbɔr. Baan ki di ŋi bil; le binib bi dooni Uwumbɔr na ga gaa baamombil ngbaan ki di daa tijikaar ni tiwanpeenkaan ni bi ban na.

ref: The Lord is going to twist the earth out of shape and turn it into a desert. Everyone will be scattered,
text: Uwumbɔr ga kuln kitiŋ kee aan ki gur nkuun. U ga mur fenn kitiŋ kee, ki yaa kaanib.

ref: The earth will be stripped bare and left that way. This is what the Lord has promised.
text: Kitiŋ kee ga doon nkuun, kaan ki li kpa nibaa. Uwumbɔr le len, le ni ga ŋa kina.

ref: The earth wilts away; its mighty leaders melt to nothing.
text: Kitiŋ kuur ki yɔl a; dulnyaa mɔmɔk aanib aataakpab yɔl; taab ni paacham bur a.

ref: The earth is polluted because its people disobeyed the laws of God, breaking their agreement that was to last forever.
text: Binib ngbaan bii kitiŋ la; bi kool Uwumbɔr aakoobil ki bii tipuur ti u nan puu ke ti li bi ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: The earth is under a curse; its people are dying out because of their sins.
text: Kina pu le Uwumbɔr puun lii kitiŋ pu. Kaanib bi pa baah tun pu na pu la. Bi ponn ni siib le ga gur.

ref: Grapevines have dried up: wine is almost gone— mournful sounds are heard instead of joyful shouts.
text: Ŋisubil ŋi bi joo ŋani ndaan na aasui yɔl a, le ndaan aabɔr pɔɔk. Unii umɔk nan kpa mpopiin na aasui bii dandana,

ref: No one plays tambourines or stringed instruments; all noisy celebrating has come to an end.
text: le mpopiin aabar ni ŋigangan ŋi nan gbaa na ŋmin.

ref: They no longer sing as they drink their wine, and it tastes sour.
text: Baah nan nyu ndaan ki gaa mpopiin aalahn i na doo a, ubaa aan ki lak ndaan aamɔɔn.

ref: Towns are crushed and in chaos; houses are locked tight.
text: Kitiŋ ponn ni aawan mɔmɔk ŋa yɔl yɔl, le binib laŋni bibaa ŋani baadichal ni ke bi ŋmar.

ref: Happy times have disappeared from the earth, and people shout in the streets, “We're out of wine!”
text: Ndaan aah kaa ki bi na, le binib tar kitiŋ ponn ni. Mpopiin doo kookoo a; mu doo kitiŋ kee pu a.

ref: Cities are destroyed; their gates are torn down.
text: Kitisakpeŋ ngbaan gur ŋilangben ŋmeen la, le kaabisamɔi aajaaleŋ mam wiir doo a.

ref: Nations will be stripped bare, like olive trees or vineyards after the harvest season. Praise the God of Justice
text: Kina le ga ŋa dulnyaa aatimbol mɔmɔk ni. Ni ga li naahn tijikaar aacheen yoonn la, buyoonn bi gbaa ker olif aakpan aasubil isui pu doo, ki ker ŋisubil ŋi gur na mu doo pu na.

ref: People in the west shout; they joyfully praise the majesty of the Lord.
text: Le binib bi ŋmar na ga gaa ilahn mpopiin pu. Binib bi bi liwilir wɔb na ga len Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn aah bi pu na,

ref: And so, everyone in the east and those on the islands should praise the Lord, the God of Israel.
text: le binib bi bi liwipuul wɔb na ga nyuŋ u. Binib bi bi nnyusakpem aagbaan na ga nyuŋ Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab Aadindaan na.

ref: From all over the world songs of praise are heard for the God of justice. But I feel awful, terribly miserable. Can anyone be trusted? So many are treacherous! There's No Escape
text: Ti ga ŋun dulnyaa aatingbaan i bi dandar na aanib gaa ilahn ki pak Uwumbɔr u ŋan na. Nee mɔmɔk pu na le m bui ke maa kpa limakl. Nwon kpo doo a. Bibɔmbɔtukb beenin tuk tibɔr, le baabiin moo kpae.

ref: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; if you crawl out of the pit, you will get caught in a trap. The sky has split apart like a window thrown open. The foundations of the earth have been shaken;
text: Unii umɔk pɔɔn ubaa ke u nya ijawaan ni na ga lir libuul ni; le umɔk pɔɔn ubaa ke u nya libuul ni na, gaawɔb ga chuu u. Ntaanyusakpem ga nya paacham ki lir ni, le ŋitinyik ga deŋ.

ref: the earth is shattered, ripped to pieces.
text: Kitiŋ ga taa iween, ki wii, ki puu.

ref: It staggers and shakes like a drunkard or a hut in a windstorm. It is burdened down with sin; the earth will fall, never again to get up.
text: Kitiŋ ga li deŋni ke udagbiir aah chuun gbeer pu na, ki yeŋni ke libool aah yeŋni kitaabuŋ ni pu na. Dulnyaa aatunwanbir nyɔɔn u lii kitiŋ; ki ga lir, kaan ki fii kpala.

ref: On that day the Lord will punish the powers in the heavens and the kings of the earth.
text: N‑yoonn choo, le Uwumbɔr ga daa ipɔɔn i bi paacham na, ni bibɔrkpaam bi bi taab na aatafal.

ref: He will put them in a pit and keep them prisoner. Then later on, he will punish them.
text: Uwumbɔr ga kuun bibɔrkpaam ŋa kiyondiik ni ke biyom aah bi mbuu ni pu na. U ga piin bi kiyondiik ni ki ti saa bundaal u ga daa bitafal na.

ref: Both the moon and sun will be embarrassed and ashamed. The Lord All-Powerful will rule on Mount Zion in Jerusalem, where he will show its rulers his wonderful glory.
text: Uŋmal ga bɔnn, le nwiin aan ki li wiin; ba pu? Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga ŋa ubɔrkpaan. U ga li ye Jerusalem u bi Sionn aajool pu na aabɔr, le binib ngbaan aaninkpiib ga kan waah nyuun sakpen pu na.

ref: You, Lord, are my God! I will praise you for doing the wonderful things you had planned and promised since ancient times.
text: Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, m ga nyuŋ si ki pak saayimbil. Aa ŋa lijinjiir aawan; aa ŋman ki joo saah nan siin n‑yaayoonn na ke aa ga ŋa pu na.

ref: You have destroyed the fortress of our enemies, leaving their city in ruins. Nothing in that foreign city will ever be rebuilt.
text: Aa cha ntisakpem kpaln ŋilangben, ki bii ntim ngbaan aah bi nin chee na. Timi aadim aah nan maa ŋibɔrdichal ŋi na kuln, kaa ki si.

ref: Now strong and cruel nations will fear and honor you.
text: Ŋitimbol ŋi kpa mpɔɔn sakpen na aanib ga pak si; bi ga san si ijawaan bibiindam aatimbol ni.

ref: You have been a place of safety for the poor and needy in times of trouble. Brutal enemies pounded us like a heavy rain or the heat of the sun at noon, but you were our shelter.
text: Bigiim, ni binib bi kaa kpa nterm na san dan aa chee; le aa gaa bi lii baamukl aayoonn. Aa gaa bi lii kibuŋ yoonn, ki tii bi mboon buyoonn nwiin ton sakpen na. Bibiindam tak ke kakab yoonn aabuln na;

ref: Those wild foreigners struck like scorching desert heat. But you were like a cloud, protecting us from the sun. You kept our enemies from singing songs of victory. The Lord Has Saved Us
text: ki naahn ntaaweel aah sil kitiŋ ki kuun na pu na. Uwumbɔr, le sin ma cha timi aadim ŋmin chii; ki cha bibiindam aafuuk mu ŋmin chii, ke ntaalangbam aah tii mboon nwiin mu ton na daal pu na. Uwumbɔr gor njim siin

ref: On this mountain the Lord All-Powerful will prepare for all nations a feast of the finest foods. Choice wines and the best meats will be served.
text: Sionn Aajool pu do, le Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga gor njim siin dulnyaa aatimbol mɔmɔk. Njim mu aajikaar nyuun aan mu aadaan pɔɔ ti nyaŋ na.

ref: Here the Lord will strip away the burial clothes that cover the nations.
text: Nima chee le u ga kpaan nyan mpombiin mu bii ŋitimbol ngbaan mɔmɔk pu na.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful will destroy the power of death and wipe away all tears. No longer will his people be insulted everywhere. The Lord has spoken!
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ga nyaŋ nkun ki kuln mu. U ga per binib mɔmɔk aanimbil tinyunyunn, ki nyan inimɔɔn i waanib jin dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni na. Uma Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: The powerful arm of the Lord will protect this mountain. The Moabites will be put down and trampled on like straw in a pit of manure.
text: Uwumbɔr ga kiir Sionn paab aanib; Moab yaab ma kan, u ga taa diin bi pu, ke inaa aah taa diini likakl tinaanyar ponn ni pu na la.

ref: They will struggle to get out, but God will humiliate them no matter how hard they try.
text: Bi ga taln biŋaal ke baah ban bi wo nnyun le na, le Uwumbɔr ga jinn bi inimɔɔn, le biŋaal ga yɔl lir kitiŋ.

ref: The walls of their fortresses will be knocked down and scattered in the dirt.
text: U ga wii Moab yaab aah maa ŋigofɔfɔŋ ŋi kiir baatiŋ na mɔmɔk, ki taa taa ŋi ŋmal titan ni.

ref: The time is coming when the people of Judah will sing this song: “Our city is protected. The Lord is our fortress, and he gives us victory.
text: Nwiin mubaa choo, le binib ga gaa nlahn mumina Juda aatiŋ pu: Timi aatisakpeŋ pɔɔ. Uwumbɔr ubaa le kii kaagon.

ref: Open the city gates for a law-abiding nation that is faithful to God.
text: Chuu piir man kaabisamɔi aan litimbol li bi mbamɔm na koo, litimbol li aanib ŋani ni ŋan na.

ref: The Lord gives perfect peace to those whose faith is firm.
text: Uwumbɔr, sin le joo nsuudoon mu sil ye nsuudoon na tii binib bi joo baabimbin mbamɔm ki tii si naadii na.

ref: So always trust the Lord because he is forever our mighty rock.
text: Tiin man Uwumbɔr naadii n‑yoonn mɔmɔk; u ga li kii timi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: God has put down our enemies in their mountain city and rubbed it in the dirt.
text: U sunn kigaadam taab, ki kuln baatiŋ ki pɔɔ na, ki gbaa wiil kaagon ŋmal titan ni.

ref: Now the poor and abused trample all over that city.” The Lord Can Be Trusted
text: Baah nan muk bi na le gur chuun ki pu, ki taa ki pu.

ref: Our Lord, you always do right, and you make the path smooth for those who obey you.
text: Uwumbɔr, saa cha bininyaam aasan ponn ni kpa tibɔbir; baah chuun isan i pu na aa kpa ŋibugen.

ref: You are the one we trust to bring about justice; above all else we want your name to be honored.
text: Ti dii saah ban pu na ki kpa limakl aa pu; si le ye taah ban nimɔk na.

ref: Throughout the night, my heart searches for you, because your decisions show everyone on this earth how to live right.
text: Maah gee si pu na, m wii kinyeek ki ban si; aa yaa ji kitiŋ kee ni kaanib tibɔr kan, bi ga bae ibamɔn aah ye pu na.

ref: Even when the wicked are treated with mercy in this land of justice, they do wrong and are blind to your glory, our Lord.
text: Saah po ŋani bibiindam tiŋann na, baa kee bae ke bi ŋa ni ŋan na. Hali nin chee bininyaam bi na, bi beenin ŋani ni kaa ŋan na; bi yii, kaa bee ke aa kpa mpɔɔn sakpen.

ref: Your hand is raised and ready to punish them, but they don't see it. Put them to shame! Show how much you care for us and throw them into the fire intended for your enemies.
text: Saadim aa nyi ke aa ga daa bitafal. Uwumbɔr, jinn bi inimɔɔn ki cha bi ji falaa; cha bi kan ntafadaan mu aa siin bi na. Mɔk bi saah gee saanib sakpen pu na.

ref: You will give us peace, Lord, because everything we have done was by your power.
text: Uwumbɔr, aa ga tii timi nwankam; tiwan nimɔk ti kani na ye saaŋann la.

ref: Others have ruled over us besides you, our Lord God, but we obey only you.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr, dindaayayan le nan joo timi, sin baanja mu le ye Tidindaan.

ref: Those enemies are now dead and can never live again. You have punished them— they are destroyed, completely forgotten.
text: Dandana wee, bi kpo a, kaan ki gir ni; baawiin aan ki fii; ba pu? aa daa bitafal ki kuln bi a; ubaa aan ki teer bi pu daalbaadaal.

ref: Our nation has grown because of you, our Lord. We have more land than before, and you are honored. The Lord Gives Life to the Dead
text: Uwumbɔr, aa cha timi aatimbol moo kpae la, ki kpae ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu, le nimina joo ni si bunyuŋ.

ref: When you punished our people, they turned and prayed to you, our Lord.
text: Uwumbɔr, aa daa saanib aatafal, le baanimbaak ni, bi mee si.

ref: Because of what you did to us, we suffered like a woman about to give birth.
text: Sin Uwumbɔr, aa cha ti wii mpɔɔn pu, ke imalween aah joo upii kan, u wii pu na.

ref: But instead of having a child, our terrible pain produced only wind. We have won no victories, and we have no descendants to take over the earth.
text: Ti nan bi iween ni kinimbaak ni, le kaa nyan nibaa; taa nyaŋ timi aadim ki gaa timi aatiŋ; taa kan nibaa.

ref: Your people will rise to life! Tell them to leave their graves and celebrate with shouts. You refresh the earth like morning dew; you give life to the dead.
text: Tɔ, timi aanib bi kpo na ga ki fikr nkun ni. Biwon ga ki fikr ki li kpa limɔfal. Bimɔk dɔ geen baakaakul ponn ni na ga fii ki gaa mpopiin aalahn. Limaln aah sɔŋni kitiŋ pu na, kina le Uwumbɔr ga fikr binib bi kpo ni yunn na. Ntafadaan ni chapinn

ref: Go inside and lock the doors, my people. Hide there for a little while, until the Lord is no longer angry. The Earth and the Sea Will Be Punished
text: Maanib, koo man nimi aadichal ni, aan ki laŋ nibaa pu. Bɔr man nibaa siib aan Uwumbɔr aaŋuul jer.

ref: The Lord will come out to punish everyone on earth for their sins. And when he does, those who did violent crimes will be known and punished.
text: Uwumbɔr ga nyan ni waakookoo yaan mu bi paacham na, ki nan daa kitiŋ kee pu aanib aatafal baatunwanbir pu. Binib bi, bi nan ku ki di bɔr kitiŋ kee pu na aabɔr ga nyan mpaan pu, kitiŋ kee aan ki bɔr binib bi bi ku bi na pu.

ref: On that day, Leviathan, the sea monster, will squirm and try to escape, but the Lord will kill him with a cruel, sharp sword. Protection and Forgiveness The Lord said:
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal kan, Uwumbɔr ga di waajaak aajuk ki pɔɔ ki ku na, ki di daa kipeewanbiik Lefiatann ki mur guŋ kina ki bi nnyusakpem ni na aatafal, ki ku ki.

ref: At that time you must sing about a fruitful vineyard.
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal Uwumbɔr ga len waasubil aasaak ki ŋan na aabɔr ke,

ref: I, the Lord, will protect it and always keep it watered. I will guard it day and night to keep it from harm.
text: “M lik ki, ki ŋani ki nnyun n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. M kii ki nwiin pu ni kinyeek ke ubaa taa bii ki.

ref: I am no longer angry. But if it produces thorns, I will go to war against it and burn it to the ground.
text: Maa ki gee ki pu liŋuul. Ikokon le yaa ba bi ki ponn ni kan, m ba ga see i mmii ki kuln i.

ref: Yet if the vineyard depends on me for protection, it will become my friend and be at peace with me.
text: Maanib aadim ma yaa tee ban ke m li kii bi kan, cha bi sɔŋ nsui. Mbamɔn, cha bi sɔŋ nsui.”

ref: Someday Israel will take root like a vine. It will blossom and bear fruit that covers the earth.
text: Iwiin i choo na ni, Jakob aamaal, Israel yaab, ga nyal sil ke busub na, ki ŋeen ki lu. Kitiŋ kee ga gbiin baah tun ki kani pu na.

ref: I, the Lord, didn't punish and kill the people of Israel as fiercely as I punished and killed their enemies.
text: Uwumbɔr aa daa Israel yaab aatafal sakpen ke waah daa baadim aatafal pu na, ki mu aanib pam aa kpo ke baadim na.

ref: I carefully measured out Israel's punishment and sent the scorching heat to chase them far away.
text: Uwumbɔr cha waanib aadim chur bi tinaagbiir ki di bi buen ki ti daa bitafal. U cha libuln li pɔɔ ki bir ki nyan ni liwipuul wɔb na le di bi buen.

ref: There's only one way that Israel's sin and guilt can be completely forgiven: They must crush the stones of every pagan altar and place of worship. The Lord Will Bring His People Together
text: Israel yaab yaa nan baawaatakpal ke nfatan na, ki kuln nnyɔknii aabimbin ni liwaapii Asera aanaŋ kan, Uwumbɔr ga di baatunwanbir cha pinn bi.

ref: Fortress cities are left like a desert where no one lives. Cattle walk through the ruins, stripping the trees bare.
text: Kitisakpeŋ ki bi nan maa ŋigon kiir ki na ber doo a. Ki gur nkuun ke nteersakpiin na la. Ki kpaln inaa aamoŋmɔpaan, nin chee i ga fuur ki ki fii ŋmɔ na la.

ref: When broken branches fall to the ground, women pick them up to feed the fire. But these people are so stupid that the God who created them will show them no mercy.
text: Isubon na mɔmɔk kuur ki kool lir a, le bipiib ti peei ti tuur mmii, ba pu? binib ngbaan aa bee nibaa, nima pu na, Uwumbɔr u naan bi na aan di cha pinn bi, kaan san bi kinimbaak mu.

ref: The time is coming when the Lord will shake the land between the Euphrates River and the border of Egypt, and one by one he will bring all of his people together.
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal, ki nya Yufrates aamɔɔl ki ti saa Ijipt yaab aatiŋ aanaanmɔk, Uwumbɔr ga kuun ni waanib ubaabaa, ke unii aah ganni mmuubim ki cha timuupɔkr pu na.

ref: A loud trumpet will be heard. Then the people of Israel who were dragged away to Assyria and Egypt will return to worship the Lord on his holy mountain in Jerusalem.
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal yaa nan fuu ni kan, kakaan ga wii ki yin Israel yaab bi bi Asiria ni Ijipt aatim ni tinaagbiir ni na ke bi gir ni. Bi ga dan ki nan doon Uwumbɔr, Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni, waajool paab.

ref: The city of Samaria above a fertile valley is in for trouble! Its leaders are drunkards, who stuff themselves with food and wine. But they will be like flowers that dry up and wilt.
text: Tibɔbir bi Israel aanaan pu. Kipak ki nnaan ngbaan aaninkpiib nan kpa na bi gbaar lir ke nsupuun mu bi di tuun baabɔryikpupur pu na la; ba pu? bi ye bidagbiib la. Bi di tulalee di gbaa biyil ŋi bi tu ŋi paacham na pu, le ki mu aa ŋmaa buen nibaa chee, bi nyun gbii ki dɔ gbara nima chee.

ref: Only the Lord is strong and powerful! His mighty hand will strike them down with the force of a hailstorm or a mighty whirlwind or an overwhelming flood.
text: Uwumbɔr kpa unii ubaa u kpa mpɔɔn sakpen ki gor ke u ti tak bi na. Udaan ga fuu ni ke kibuŋ ki joo ni ŋitaatakpal na, ni utaasakpiin, ki naahn nwam mu san mala mala ki kpa mpɔɔn na, le ki ga biin kitiŋ ngbaan pu.

ref: Every drunkard in Ephraim takes pride in Samaria, but it will be crushed.
text: Bi ga taa taa bininkpiib bi ye bidagbiib ngbaan na aagaak ŋmal titan ni.

ref: Samaria above a fertile valley will quickly lose its glory. It will be gobbled up like the first ripe fig at harvest season.
text: Kipak ki bininkpiib bi ye bidagbiib na nan kpa na bi gbaar ke baah ker ŋikakan ŋi puen puir na mala pu na la.

ref: When this time comes, the Lord All-Powerful will be a glorious crown for his people who survive.
text: Nwiin mubaa choo, le Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aapak ga li naahn ubɔr aayikpupuk ki tuu nsupuun na aah kpa kipak pu na, ki tii waanib bi ŋmar na.

ref: He will see that justice rules and that his people are able to defend their cities. Corrupt Leaders Will Be Punished
text: U ga tii bibɔjirb ibamɔn aalan, ki pɔɔk bikikiib bi kii kitisakpeŋ ngbaan aabisamɔi na aataakpab n‑yoonn mu binib dan bi nan tak bi na. Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib bi ye bidagbiib na

ref: Their tables are covered, completely covered, with their stinking vomit.
text: Baah ka nin chee nyu ndaan na ye tiwuln ŋmeen la, nibaa chee aa gur ki ŋan.

ref: You don't even listen— all you hear is senseless sound after senseless sound.
text: U pɔɔni ubaa ke u mɔk timi ŋibɔbil ngbaan aatataa aah ye pu na.”

ref: So, the Lord will speak to his people in strange sounds and foreign languages.
text: Tɔ, ni yaa kaan pel ni m chee kan, Uwumbɔr ga di biwɔwɔm bi len ŋitimbol yayan aaliin na ki di mɔk liwamɔkl.

ref: He promised you perfect peace and rest, but you refused to listen.
text: U tii ni mɔmɔk lifuur ni mmɔɔn, le ni yii kaa pel u chee.

ref: Now his message to you will be senseless sound after senseless sound. Then you will fall backwards, injured and trapped. False Security Is Fatal
text: Kina pu le Uwumbɔr ga mɔk nimi ŋibɔbil ngbaan mɔmɔk aatataa aah ye pu na. Le ni yaa yoor litaal limɔk na kan, ni ga gbeer. Ni ga kan iween, gaawɔb mam ga chuu nimi, aan bi di nimi ŋa kiyondiik ni. Sionn aatakpajal

ref: You rulers of Jerusalem do nothing but sneer; now you must listen to what the Lord says.
text: Tɔ, nimi bigaadam bi joo Jerusalem aanib bimina na, li pel man Uwumbɔr aah len pu na.

ref: Do you think you have an agreement with death and the world of the dead? Why do you trust in your lies to keep you safe from danger and the mighty flood?
text: Ni bui ke nimi ni nkun ŋa tɔb kijɔtiik aan ni ni kitekpiitiŋ kpaan a. Ni dii inyamɔn ki dak ke ŋŋmann pu le ni ga ŋmar, ki tii naadii ke tibɔbir yaa fuu ni kan, ni ga nya ti ni.

ref: And so the Lord says, “I'm laying a firm foundation for the city of Zion. It's a valuable cornerstone proven to be trustworthy; no one who trusts it will ever be disappointed.
text: Nima pu le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr len ke: “M bi joo nsisii mu pɔɔ ki si chob na le siini Sionn aatiŋ ni. Mu ponn ni, m ga di litakpal li pɔɔ na ki di siin mu aalɔlɔŋ ni. Unii umɔk gaa u ki kii na aan ji inimɔɔn.

ref: Your agreement with death and the world of the dead will be broken. Then angry, roaring waves will sweep over you.
text: Nimi ni nkun aah kpaan kimɔbaan ki na ga doo, le nimi ni kitekpiitiŋ aakpaam na mu ga doo. Tibɔbir yaa fuu ni kan, ni ga kuln.

ref: Morning, noon, and night an overwhelming flood will wash you away. The terrible things that happen will teach you this lesson:
text: Ni ga yun nimi, ki ki gir yun nimi kichakpiik mɔmɔk ni. Ni ga ji falaa ngbaan nwiin pu ni kinyeek. Tibɔchann timɔk Uwumbɔr ga joo ni na ga li joo ni ijawaan pɔɔn la.

ref: The Lord will fiercely attack as he did at Mount Perazim and in Gibeon Valley. But this time the Lord will do something surprising, not what you expect.
text: Uwumbɔr ga jan ke waah nan jan Perasim aajool pu, ni Gibeonn aafataŋ ni pu na, ke u ŋa waah ban ke u ŋa pu na; waah ga ŋa pu na aatataa ga li pɔɔ ti bee. U ga doo waatuln. U ga doo waatuln li aatataa bɔr na.

ref: So you had better stop sneering or you will be in worse shape than ever before. I heard the Lord All-Powerful threaten the whole country with destruction. All Wisdom Comes from the Lord
text: Taa laa man nsurm mu m joo tii nimi na. Ni yaa laa kan, naah ga ŋa pu aan ki ŋmar na ga moo pɔɔk. Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan tuk mi ke u ga kuln litingbaln ngbaan mɔmɔk. Uwumbɔr aalan

ref: When a field is ready, they scatter the seeds of dill and cumin; they plant the seeds of wheat and barley in the proper places and sow other grains around the edges.
text: U yaa kee beer mpaan doo kan, u bu ŋibaabil aasubil ni ikonjubɔn aasubil la. U bu imuul ni idi aapɔn, le ki bu njikaabim muken mu waakpaab ngbaan aagbaan.

ref: After dill and cumin have been harvested, the stalks are pounded, not run over with a wagon.
text: Waa joo likukul li filk na poi ŋibaabil ni ikonjubɔn aabil, u joo lidabil waatiir le poi.

ref: Wheat and barley are pounded, but not beaten to pulp; they are run over with a wagon, but not ground to dust.
text: Waa gbaa wiir waamuubim ni waadibim, u nyi waah ga di inaaja aatɔroku poi mu pu, kaan taa wiir njikaabim ngbaan na.

ref: Jerusalem, city of David, the place of my altar, you are in for trouble! Celebrate your festivals year after year.
text: Uwumbɔr aatork aabimbiln, li ye Jerusalem na, kuln a. Kitisakpeŋ ki ubɔr David nan koo ki ponn ni na kuln a. Cha libiln libaa bee ŋilee jer, ŋi ni ŋaajim, ni mu aawanpɔɔn aajim,

ref: I will surround you and prepare to attack from all sides.
text: Uwumbɔr ga mann gob kitisakpeŋ ngbaan, ki tak ki.

ref: From deep in the earth, you will call out for help with only a faint whisper.
text: Jerusalem ga li naahn utekpiir aawiin mu bi kitiŋ taab, ki pɔɔni mubaa ke muneel nyan ni titan ni na la.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will come to your rescue with a thundering earthquake and a fiery whirlwind.
text: Libuul ngbaan ni, le Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga gaa nimi lii. U ga cha utaal gben, le kitiŋ mu ga deŋ. U ga cha kibuŋ ki pɔɔ na ni imii dan;

ref: Be shocked and stunned, you prophets! Refuse to see. Get drunk and stagger, but not from wine.
text: Li ye bijɔrb man. Li ye bijoom man. Li ye bidagbiib bi kaa nyun ndaan na man. Li chuun gbeer ke naah nyun ndaan le na.

ref: The Lord has made you drowsy; he put you into a deep sleep and covered your head.
text: Uwumbɔr le cha ni doon ki geen kaan finn mala. Nimi Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr le ba ye binib aanimbil, le Uwumbɔr ŋum ninimbil.

ref: Others say, “We can't read it, because we don't know how to read.”
text: Aa yaa di ki tii unii u kaa nyi tigbann na ke u karn ki tii si kan, u ga bui si ke waa nyi tigbann.

ref: The Lord has said: “These people praise me with their words, but they never really think about me. They worship me by repeating rules made up by humans.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Binib bimina bui ke bi dooni mi la, le baadoon aa kpa tataa, bisui bi nibaa wɔb la. Bi joo biyaajatiib aakaal i bi di ŋa bisui ni ki ŋmaa teer i n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na la, ke ni ye Uwumbɔr aakaal la.

ref: So once again I will do things that shock and amaze them, and I will destroy the wisdom of those who claim to know and understand.”
text: Le m yaa cha tibɔbir tibaa jer kan, tiken ki fuu ni, le ni gar bi. Binib bi kpa nlan na ga kpaln bijɔrb, le baalan ngbaan ga bee fam.” N‑yoonn mu choo na aamakl

ref: You are in for trouble, if you try to hide your plans from the Lord! Or if you think what you do in the dark can't be seen.
text: Binib bi joo baalandak bɔrni Uwumbɔr na aamɔfal junn a. Bi bɔrni le ki ŋani baatunwanbir ki dak ke ubaa aan kan bi, ubaa mu aan li nyi baah ŋani pu na.

ref: You have it all backwards. A clay dish doesn't say to the potter, “You didn't make me. You don't even know how.” Hope for the Future
text: Bi labr tiwan mɔmɔk chiŋni la. Nilani ye tiwankpaan, uyakmaal aan tiyakr? Tiwan ni unii naan ni na aan ŋmaa bui udaan ke, “Sin le aa naan mi,” ni mu aan ŋmaa bui u ke, “Saa nyi saah bi ŋani pu na.”

ref: Soon the forest of Lebanon will become a field with crops, thick as a forest.
text: Liyataŋakl libaa bi ke, naan yunn le kichook kpaln baah ko nin chee na, le baah ko nin chee na ga ki kpaln kichook.

ref: The deaf will be able to hear whatever is read to them; the blind will be freed from a life of darkness.
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal yaa nan fuu ni kan, bitafakpaab ga ŋun baah karni kigbaŋ kibaa pu na, le bijoom bi nan bi mbɔmbɔɔn ni na ga likr binimbil ki li waa.

ref: The poor and the needy will celebrate and shout because of the Lord, the holy God of Israel.
text: Bigiim, ni binib bi sunn bibaa taab na ga ki kan mpopiin mu Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr u bi chain na tii bi na.

ref: All who are cruel and arrogant will be gone forever. Those who live by crime will disappear,
text: Binib bi muk biken ki lik seen Uwumbɔr na aamɔfal ga doo. U ga kuln titunwanbirdam mɔmɔk aamɔfal.

ref: together with everyone who tells lies in court and keeps innocent people from getting a fair trial.
text: Binib bi bii biken ki biini titunwanbirdam aatun pu kaa dar bitafal, ki mu geei inyamɔn aan bibamɔndam aa kani baabamɔn na, Uwumbɔr ga kuln bi.

ref: The Lord who rescued Abraham has this to say about Jacob's descendants: “They will no longer be ashamed and disgraced.
text: Kina pu na, Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr u nan nyan Abraham tibɔr ni na len ke, “Maanib, naan ki ji inimɔɔn; ninimbil wɔb aan ki li kpa inimɔɔn.

ref: When they see how great I have made their nation, they will praise and honor me, the holy God of Israel.
text: Ni yaa nan kan mbim mu m ga tii nimi na kan, le ni ga tii naadii ke m sil ye nimi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na. Ni ga pak mi ki san mi ijawaan.

ref: Everyone who is confused will understand, and all who have complained will obey my teaching.”
text: Bijɔrb ga bae nlan ki bee baah ga dii nsan mu na, le binib bi ŋulni n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na ga li gur kpa mpopiin ki gaa nsurm.”

ref: This is the Lord's message for his rebellious people: “You follow your own plans instead of mine; you make treaties without asking me, and you keep on sinning.
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “Binib bi joo Juda aatiŋ na aamɔfal junn a; ba pu? bi yii maamɔb. Bi dii isan i maa mɔk bi na; le bi ni biken kpaani kimɔbaan ki maa tuk bi ke bi kpaan na, le ki moo joo titunwanbir kpae titunwanbir pu.

ref: You trust Egypt for protection. So you refuse my advice and send messengers to Egypt to beg their king for help.
text: Bi chaa Ijipt aatiŋ ni ti ban nterm kaa puen baa mi waahr. Bi ban ke Ijipt yaab li kii bi, kina pu na, bi di naadii tii Ijipt aabɔrkpaan.

ref: “You will be disappointed, completely disgraced for trusting Egypt.
text: Ubɔrkpaan ngbaan mu aan ŋmaa ter bi, le Ijipt yaab aaterm ngbaan ga ti doo tibɔbir ni la.

ref: The king's power reaches from the city of Zoan as far south as Hanes.
text: Hali baah nyan Juda aaninkpiib bi ke bi ti li bi Ijipt aatisakpem Soann ni Hanes ni na kpaan fuu nima;

ref: Egypt can't help you! That's why I call that nation a helpless monster.” Israel Refuses To Listen
text: Ijipt aaterm aa kpa tinyoor. Kina pu le m naan Ijipt aatiŋ liyimbinaankee ke, ‘Kipeewanbiik ki kaa ŋmaa ŋa nibaa na.’” Binib bi kaa kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na

ref: The Lord told me to write down his message for his people, so that it would be there forever.
text: Uwumbɔr bui mi ke m ŋmee ŋa kigbaŋ ponn ni binib ngbaan aah bi pu na, aan ni li dɔ, kaan li kpa ndoon, baatunwanbir aah bi pu na.

ref: They have turned against the Lord and can't be trusted. They have refused his teaching
text: N‑yoonn mɔmɔk baa keei Uwumbɔr aah tuk bi pu na, ki geei inyamɔn n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, kaa pel Uwumbɔr aah mɔk bi pu na.

ref: and have said to his messengers and prophets: Don't tell us what God has shown you and don't preach the truth. Just say what we want to hear, even if it's false.
text: Bi tuk Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ke bi ŋmin. Bi len le ke, “Taa bui man timi mbimbin mu ŋan na aabɔr. Bui man timi taah ban ti ŋun pu na. Cha ti li joo timi aajoon.

ref: Stop telling us what God has said! We don't want to hear any more about the holy One of Israel.
text: Siir cha timi nsan man. Taa ban ti ŋun Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na aabɔr.”

ref: Now this is the answer of the holy One of Israel: “You rejected my message, and you trust in violence and lies.
text: Tɔ, Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na aah len pu na sɔ: “Nitafal aa bi maah tuk nimi pu na ni, le ki tee kii tii inyamɔn ni kijaak ma.

ref: This sin is like a crack that makes a high wall quickly crumble
text: Ni jin libɔkpol a. Ni naahn ligoln li fɔk ki taa nween ki ti saa kitiŋ na la, libuul lee ni le ni ga lir.

ref: and shatter like a crushed bowl. There's not a piece left big enough to carry hot coals or to dip out water.” Trust the Lord
text: Ni wii yak yak ke tiyakr aabuul na la, ni wii yak yak sakpen le kisanjaŋ aan ki li bi, bi di moo mmii, bee bi di kab nnyun nkin ponn ni.”

ref: The holy Lord God of Israel had told all of you, “I will keep you safe if you turn back to me and calm down. I will make you strong if you quietly trust me.” Then you stubbornly
text: Israel yaab Aadindaan Uwumbɔr u bi chain na le len waanib chee ke, “Gir ni man ki nan kii tii mi suuna, le ni ga kan mpɔɔn ni ŋŋmarm.” Le ni yii kaa ŋa kina.

ref: As few as five of them, or even one, will be enough to chase a thousand of you. Finally, all that will be left will be a few survivors as lonely as a flag pole on a barren hill. The Lord Will Show Mercy
text: Nimi aajab lichur yaa kan nimi aadim aaja ubaa kan, bi ga san, le nimi aadim ngbaan aajab biŋmu ga ŋmaa cha nimi aajab mɔmɔk san. Nibaa aan gur nimi aajab ni, see nimi aatuutaa u ni di ŋum ligongoln paab na baanja.

ref: The Lord God is waiting to show how kind he is and to have pity on you. The Lord always does right; he blesses those who trust him.
text: Nee mɔmɔk pu na, Uwumbɔr beenin si kii ke u san nimi kinimbaak. Waah tun ni ŋan na pu na, u gor ke u san nimi kinimbaak. Binib bi di bibaa tii Uwumbɔr na kpa mpopiin. Uwumbɔr ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa waanib pu

ref: People of Jerusalem, you don't need to cry anymore. The Lord is kind, and as soon as he hears your cries for help, he will come.
text: Nimi binib bi koo Jerusalem ponn ni na aan ki wii iwiil. Uwumbɔr san nimi kinimbaak, le ni yaa wii ki yin u ki ban nterm kan, u ga kii nimi aayim.

ref: The Lord has given you trouble and sorrow as your food and drink. But now you will again see the Lord, your teacher, and he will guide you.
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha ni kan limukl; le uma ubaa ga li bi nima ki mɔk nimi waasan, kaan ki bɔr.

ref: Whether you turn to the right or to the left, you will hear a voice saying, “This is the road! Now follow it.”
text: Ni yaa yenn nsan ki fenn buen ŋŋangii wɔb, bee ŋŋangan wɔb kan, ni ga ŋun waaneel nipuwɔb len ke, “Nsan le na. Dii mu man.”

ref: Then you will treat your idols of silver and gold like garbage; you will throw them away like filthy rags.
text: Ni ga yoor naah di tikunabr naan nimi aawaa ŋi na, ni naah di salmaa naan ŋi na, ki di ti mee ke ŋi ye tijɔŋ la, ki tar ke, “Taa ki ban ti kan nimi.”

ref: The Lord will send rain to water the seeds you have planted—your fields will produce more crops than you need, and your cattle will graze in open pastures.
text: N‑yoonn mumɔk ni bun nimi aajikaabim na kan, Uwumbɔr ga cha utaal nu, aan mu muun ki ŋa mbamɔm, le nimi aawakor mu ga kan timoor pam ki ŋmɔ.

ref: Even the oxen and donkeys that plow your fields will be fed the finest grain.
text: Nimi aanaaja ni ibon i ko nimi aasar na mu ga kan timoor ti ŋan na ki ŋmɔ.

ref: On that day people will be slaughtered and towers destroyed, but streams of water will flow from high hills and towering mountains.
text: Nwiin mundaal ni ti nyaŋ nimi aadim, ki gaa baadifɔfɔŋ, ki ku baanib na, ibun ga puu nnyun ŋijoo, ni ŋigongon mɔmɔk pu.

ref: Then the Lord will bandage his people's injuries and heal the wounds he has caused. The moon will shine as bright as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter than usual. It will be like the light of seven days all at once. Assyria Will Be Punished
text: Uŋmal ga li wiin ke nwiin na, le nwiin ga moo woln ki jer mu aah ti wiin pu na, ki naahn ke iwiin ilole le aah di kpaan ki wiin nwiin mubaa daal na. N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr ga poo waanib aabuun i u tii bi aan i yann na, le nimina mɔmɔk ga ŋa. Uwumbɔr ga daa Asiria yaab aatafal

ref: The Lord is coming from far away with his fiery anger and thick clouds of smoke. His angry words flame up like a destructive fire;
text: Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn ni waapak ga nya ni paacham. Waaŋuul ye mmii ni iŋmanyuu la. U yaa len tibɔr kan, ti seer ke mmii na la.

ref: he breathes out a flood that comes up to the neck. He sifts the nations and destroys them. Then he puts a bridle in every foreigner's mouth and leads them to doom.
text: U yaa chuun kan, libuln lolni u pu nsan ke nwam mu yoor tiwan mɔmɔk na la. Li ŋar ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ŋŋaan ki kuln ŋi, ŋaatunwanbir pu.

ref: The Lord's people will sing as they do when they celebrate a religious festival at night. The Lord is Israel's mighty rock, and his people will be as happy as they are when they follow the sound of flutes to the mountain where he is worshiped.
text: Le nimi Uwumbɔr aanib ga li kpa mpopiin ki gaa ilahn ke naah ŋani pu kinyeek ki ni ji Uwumbɔr aajim mubaa na. Ni ga li kpa mpopiin ke binib bi waa kulufeeŋ aawaal ki cha Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab aakikiir na Aadichal ni na.

ref: The Lord will get furious. His fearsome voice will be heard, his arm will be seen ready to strike, and his anger will be like a destructive fire, followed by thunderstorms and hailstones.
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha unii mɔmɔk ŋun waaneel mu kpa mpɔɔn na pu, ki ŋun waaŋuul mu pu; le imiigaal, ni ŋitaayiyir, ni ŋitaatakpal, ni utaasakpiin ga li bi.

ref: When the Assyrians hear the Lord's voice and see him striking with his iron rod, they will be terrified.
text: Asiria yaab yaa ŋun Uwumbɔr aaneel mu kpa mpɔɔn na pu, ki ŋun waatafadaan aah bir pu na pu kan, ijawaan ga chuu bi.

ref: He will attack them in battle, and each time he strikes them, it will be to the music of tambourines and harps.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa faa bi ki ki gir faa bi kan, waanib ga li waa liwaal ki dii ŋigangan ni tibar aah gbaa pu na. Uwumbɔr ubaa le ga jan Asiria yaab kijaak.

ref: Long ago the Lord got a place ready for burning the body of the dead king. The place for the fire is deep and wide, the wood is piled high, and the Lord will start the fire by breathing out flaming sulfur.
text: N‑yoonn mu jer na, bi nan puen toor libuul li ponn ni bi ga nan di Asiria aabɔrkpaan ngbaan see mmiisakpiin ni na. Li nyoo le ki waa, le bi pii idɔ ti gbiin li; le Uwumbɔr ga fuur mmiigaal mu ti gaa u ni idɔ ngbaan li ponn ni.

ref: You are in for trouble if you go to Egypt for help, or if you depend on an army of chariots or a powerful cavalry. Instead you should depend on and trust the holy Lord God of Israel.
text: Binib bi chaa Ijipt ti ban nterm na aamɔfal junn a. Bi lik Ijipt aajab bi chaa butɔb na, ni baataan ni baataan aatɔroku tiib aawiwiir la. Baa tee fenn lik Uwumbɔr, u ye bima Israel yaab Aadindaan ki bi chain na, ke u ter bi.

ref: The Lord isn't stupid! He does what he promises, and he can bring doom. If you are cruel yourself, or help those who are evil, you will be destroyed.
text: U nyi waah ŋani pu na. Uma le cha tibɔbir choo. U yaa puu ke u daa titunwanbirdam ni binib bi ter bi na aatafal kan, waan di cha.

ref: The Egyptians are mere humans. They aren't God. Their horses are made of flesh; they can't live forever. When the Lord shows his power, he will destroy the Egyptians and all who depend on them. Together they will fall.
text: Ijipt aanib mu po ye binibɔm la, baa ye Uwumbɔr. Baataan mu aa ye lijinjiir aawan nibaa. Uwumbɔr yaa ban u tun waah ban pu na kan, litimbol li kpa mpɔɔn na ga bur, le litimbol li kaa pɔɔ aan li ter li na ga lir. Ŋimɔk ga kuln la.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful said to me, “I will roar and attack like a fearless lion not frightened by the shouts of shepherds trying to protect their sheep. That's how I will come down and fight on Mount Zion.
text: Uwumbɔr bui mi ke, “Uchinn yaa chuu kiwakork, aan bipihkpaab po gee bi li tar mpɔɔn pu sakpen pu na, waan san cha ki; ni mu ga li bi kina le Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan chee, nibaa aan ŋmaa kiir u, aan u taa li kii Sionn aajool.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will protect Jerusalem like a mother bird circling over her nest.” Come Back to the Lord
text: Unyoon aah wuŋni waadil pu ki kii waabim pu na, kina le min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga kiir Jerusalem aatiŋ ki biin ki pu.”

ref: People of Israel, come back! You have completely turned from the Lord.
text: Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “Israel aanib, ni tun mi taani kaa si mpuwɔb; gir ni m chee man.

ref: The time is coming when you will throw away your idols of silver and gold, made by your sinful hands.
text: Naah nan tun mi taani ki di tikunabr ni salmaa di naan ŋiwaa ŋi na, n‑yoonn mubaa choo le ni mɔmɔk ga di ŋi lii.

ref: The Assyrians will be killed, but not by the swords of humans. Their young men will try to escape, but they will be captured and forced into slavery.
text: Butɔb ga bii Asiria aatiŋ, ni mu aan li ye binibɔm aapɔɔn pu. Asiria yaab ngbaan ga san butɔb ngbaan ni, le binachipɔm ga kpaln binaagbiib;

ref: Their fortress will fall when terror strikes; their army officers will be frightened and run from the battle. This is what the Lord has said, the Lord whose fiery furnace is built on Mount Zion.
text: ijawaan pu, le baabɔrkpaan ga san, baaninkpiib aawon ga li gbaa sakpen aan bi di baatuutaa mam di mee.” Uwumbɔr u bi dooni u Jerusalem aatiŋ ni, nin chee waatork aamii gaal na, le len kina.

ref: They will be a place of safety from stormy winds, a stream in the desert, and a rock that gives shade from the heat of the sun.
text: Bi mɔmɔk ga li bi ke mbɔbɔryaan mu ga ŋmaa kiir unii libuln chee, ni nin chee unii ga bɔr ki ŋmar kitaabuŋ chee na la. Bi ga li naahn ibun i puu nteersakpiin pu nin chee nnyun aa bi na, ki ki naahn litakpasakpeln li tii mboon nin chee isui aa bi na.

ref: Then everyone who has eyes will open them and see, and those who have ears will pay attention.
text: Binimbil ni bitafal ga li bi binib bi kaa kpa na ni.

ref: All who are impatient will take time to think; everyone who stutters will talk clearly.
text: Bi ga li bi suuna, ki ga li tun ŋitun ŋi kpa ŋitataa na, ki ga ŋa baah len pu na.

ref: Fools will no longer be highly respected, and crooks won't be given positions of honor.
text: Ubaa aan bui ke ujɔr le kpa kipak, bee ubiindaan le kpa mbamɔn.

ref: Fools talk foolishness. They always make plans to do sinful things, to lie about the Lord, to let the hungry starve, and to keep water from those who are thirsty.
text: Ujɔr le ye unii u len kijɔrk aaliin, ki dakl ilandak i kaa ŋan na. Waah ŋani pu na, ni waah len pu na mɔmɔk ye lisiibil le ki tii Uwumbɔr; waa kpiini nkon aah joo binib bi na, kaa tii binib bi nnyunyuu joo bi na mu nnyun.

ref: Cruel people tell lies— they do evil things, and make cruel plans to destroy the poor and needy, even when they beg for justice.
text: Ulatiir ye unii u bir na, le ki tun titunwanbir; u dakl ke u di inyamɔn di bii bigiim bi taa kan baabamɔn.

ref: But helpful people can always be trusted to make helpful plans. Punishment for the Women of Jerusalem
text: Le unii u kpa kipak na tun lituln li ga joo ni u kipak na, ki si chob buyoonn u kan mbamɔn dɔ na. Ntafadaan ni chapinn aabɔr

ref: Listen to what I say, you women who are carefree and careless!
text: Nimi bipiib bi bi nibaa pu, kaa dak tiwan nibaa pu na, li pel man maah bi len pu na.

ref: You may not have worries now, but in about a year, the grape harvest will fail, and you will tremble.
text: Mbamɔn, ni ji bab dandana wee, tɔ, libiln libaa yaa jer kan, naan li nyi naah bi nin chee na; ba pu? ŋisubil aan ki li bi aan ni chaa ti peei.

ref: Slap your breasts in sorrow because of what happened to the fruitful fields and vineyards,
text: Li gbaa nibiŋ ki wii iwiil man; ba pu? ikpaakon nyaan, ni ŋisubil aasui aasar mɔmɔk bii doo a,

ref: and to the happy homes in Jerusalem. The land of my people is covered with thorns.
text: le ikokon ŋmeen le gur si maanib aakpaakon ni. Li wii man ŋidichal ŋimɔk ponn ni binib nan bi ni mɔ bi na pu, ni kitisakpeŋ ki nan gbii binib na pu.

ref: When the Spirit is given to us from heaven, deserts will become orchards thick as fertile forests.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr ga ki gir tii ni timi Waafuur Nyaan. Ikpaakon i nan bii na ga ki gir ŋa ikpaakon i ŋan na, ki ga ŋa tijikaar sakpen.

ref: Honesty and justice will prosper there,
text: Le ibamɔn ni mbimbinyaan ga gbiin kitiŋ ngbaan ni;

ref: You, the Lord's people, will live in peace, calm and secure,
text: Uwumbɔr aanib ga nya ilandak mɔmɔk ni, le baadichal ni ga li kpa nsuudoon ni lifuur.

ref: You will have God's blessing, as you plant your crops beside streams, while your donkeys and cattle roam freely about.
text: nimi tee ga li kpa mpopiin, nimi aajikaar ga kan nnyun, le timoor mu ga li bi ni kookoo nimi aawakor ŋmɔ.

ref: You defeated my people. Now you're in for trouble! You've never been destroyed, but you will be destroyed; you've never been betrayed, but you will be betrayed. When you have finished destroying and betraying, you will be destroyed and betrayed in return.
text: Timi aadim aamɔfal junn a. Bi sun kinaayuk, ki bii binib, le ubaa ma aa sun bi kinaayuk kaa bii bi mu. Tɔ, baayoonn mu bi joo su ki bii binib na ga doo, le binib mu ga su bi kinaayuk ki bii bi mbamɔm.

ref: Please, Lord, be kind to us! We depend on you. Make us strong each morning, and come to save us when we are in trouble.
text: Uwumbɔr, san timi kinimbaak. Ti di timi aamakl di ŋa aa ni. Li kii timi iwiin mɔmɔk ki gaa timi lii buyoonn ti bi limukl ni na.

ref: You, Lord, are above all others, and you live in the heavens. You have brought justice and fairness to Jerusalem;
text: Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn nyaŋ a. Uma le joo tiwan mɔmɔk. U ga cha binib li kpa mbimbinyaan ki tii tɔb baabamɔn, Jerusalem aatiŋ ni,

ref: you are the foundation on which we stand today. You always save us and give true wisdom and knowledge. Nothing means more to us than obeying you. The Lord Will Do Something
text: le nibaa aan ki ŋmaa dam litimbol ngbaan. U kii waanib n‑yoonn mɔmɔk le ki tii bi nlan ni mbaem. Baawangol li bi gee sakpen na le ye ke bi li pak Uwumbɔr.

ref: Listen! Our bravest soldiers are running through the streets, screaming for help. Our messengers hoped for peace, but came home crying.
text: Bipobidam wii ki ban nterm la. Bitutum bi pɔɔk bibaa bi joo ni nsuudoon na wii iwiil la.

ref: No one travels anymore; every road is empty. Treaties are broken, and no respect is shown to any who keep promises.
text: Isanja ni gbii tibɔbir sakpen le binib aa ki ŋmaa dii i. Mmɔkpaan na mɔmɔk bii le kimɔbaan mu aa ki bi. Unii ubaa aa ki kan kipak.

ref: Fields are dry and barren; Mount Lebanon wilts with shame. Sharon Valley is a desert; the forests of Bashan and Carmel have lost their leaves.
text: Ubaa aa ki ko kitiŋ ngbaan, le ki gur dɔ fam. Lebanonn aachoor na aasui yɔl, le Saronn aafataŋ ki aatiŋ ŋan na gur naahn nteer la, le Basann aatiŋ ni, ni Kamel Aajool pu aasui aafar gbar lir kitiŋ. Uwumbɔr sur waadim

ref: But the Lord says, “Now I will do something and be greatly praised.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ŋitimbol ngbaan ke, “Dandana, m ga fii sil. M ga mɔk maah pɔɔ sakpen pu na.

ref: Your deeds are straw that will be set on fire by your very own breath.
text: Ni kpokl nkpokl mu kaa kpa tinyoor na, le naah ŋani tiwan nimɔk na aa kpa tinyoor. Maawiin naahn mmii mu ga bii nimi doo na la.

ref: Everyone, both far and near, come look at what I have done. See my mighty power!” Punishment and Rewards
text: Cha bimɔk bi kɔnkɔni do na, ni bimɔk bi dandar na mu ŋun maah tun pu na, aan ki bee maapɔɔn aah bi pu na.”

ref: Those terrible sinners on Mount Zion tremble as they ask in fear, “How can we possibly live where a raging fire never stops burning?”
text: Sionn aatunwanbirdam na aapobil yuk, le biwon gbaa. Le bi len ke, “Uwumbɔr aabɔjil naahn mmii mu wu kaan junn na la. Ti ponn ni, ŋma ga ŋmar mmii mumina aaboln ni?”

ref: But there will be rewards for those who live right and tell the truth, for those who refuse to take money by force or accept bribes, for all who hate murder and violent crimes.
text: Ni yaa len ki ŋani ni ŋan na kan, ni ga ŋmar. Taa di man nimi aapɔɔn di ji bigiim, ki taa gaa igaŋgaŋlik. Ni taa kpaani binib bi kpokl ke bi ku unii, bee binib bi tun titunwanbir na chee.

ref: They will live in a fortress high on a rocky cliff, where they will have food and plenty of water. The Lord Is Our King
text: Nima kan ni ga ŋmar; ni ga fuur ke naah bi lijool li pɔɔ ki fɔk na paab le na. Ni ga li kpa tijikaar ni ji, ki kpa nnyun mu ni nyu. Lifuur aayoonn mu choo na
