ref: If you obey me, the kings from David's family will continue to rule Judah from this palace. They and their officials will ride in and out on their horses or in their chariots.
text: Ni yaa sil ŋani maah tuk nimi pu na kan, Ubɔr David aayaabitiib ga li beenin ji nnaan. Le bima, ni baaninkpiib, ni baanib ga li diir ibisamɔi yee, ki bi itaan aatɔroku mam ni, ki dik itaan pu, ki nya libɔrdichal lee ni.

ref: But if you ignore me, I promise in my own name that this palace will lie in ruins.
text: Tɔ, ni yaa kaa ŋani maah tuk nimi pu na kan, m puu tii nimi ke libɔrdichal limina ga ber doo ki kpaln lilangbeln. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Listen to what I think about it: The palace of Judah's king is as glorious as Gilead or Lebanon's highest peaks. But it will be as empty as a ghost-town when I'm through with it.
text: “M chee kan, Juda aanaan aadichal ŋan ke Gilead aatiŋ, ni Lebanonn aajoo na la; le m ga ŋa li nin chee ubaa aan ŋmaa koo na.

ref: People from different nations will pass by and ask, “Why did the Lord do this to such a great city as Jerusalem?”
text: “Nee aapuwɔb le biwɔwɔm pam ga jer, le ki baa tɔb ke ba ŋa min Uwumbɔr ŋa kitisakpeŋ kee kina.

ref: Others will answer, “It's because the people worshiped foreign gods and broke the agreement that the Lord their God had made with them.” King Jehoahaz The Lord said:
text: Le bi ga gar ke ni bii nimi ni nimi Aawumbɔr aamɔbaan, ki dooni ŋiwaa ki tun tii ŋi na le cha u ŋa kina.” Jeremia aah nan di Joahas aabɔr ti len na aabɔr

ref: King Josiah is dead, so don't mourn for him. Instead, mourn for his son King Jehoahaz, dragged off to another country, never to return.
text: Juda aanib, taa wii Ubɔr Josia pu man; taa wii waakpuul man. Li wii ujapɔɔn Joahas pu; bi ga nan chuu u di buen, le waan ki gir ni daalbaadaal, waan ki kan kitiŋ ki pu bi nan ma u na.

ref: Jehoahaz became king of Judah after his father King Josiah died. But Jehoahaz was taken as a prisoner to a foreign country. Now I, the Lord, promise that he will die there without ever seeing his own land again. King Jehoiakim The Lord told me to say: *
text: Baah di u buen kitiŋ ki ni na le u ga ti kpo nima, le kaan ki kan kitiŋ kimina daalbaadaal.” Jeremia aah nan di Jehoyakim aabɔr ti len na sɔ

ref: King Jehoiakim, you are doomed! You built a palace with large rooms upstairs.
text: Uja u di beebee maa waadichal, ki moo maa kpae li pu inyamɔn pu aan waanib tun lituln fam, kaa gaal tipar na aamɔfal junn a.

ref: You put in big windows and used cedar paneling and red paint. But you were unfair and forced the builders to work without pay. *
text: Uja u len ke, “M ga maa lidichasakpeln ki cha paacham aadir li waa pam,” le ki ŋa takolu mam waadichal pu, ki di santina aakpan kpaa bi, le ki di tiwamann boon bi na aamɔfal junn a.

ref: More cedar in your palace doesn't make you a better king than your father Josiah. He always did right— he gave justice to the poor and was honest.
text: Aa yaa di santina maa saadichal ke li li ŋan jer biken yaan kan, kina ga ŋmaa ŋa si ubɔrnyaan ki jer biken aa? Aate nan jin waamɔɔn u nan bi chob ki kpa ibamɔn, le ki nan kan tinyoor waatuln mɔmɔk ni.

ref: That's what it means to truly know me. So he lived a comfortable life and always had enough to eat and drink.
text: U nan jin bigiim aabɔr ibamɔn pu, le waawan mɔmɔk nan kpa nsan. Kina le mɔk ke unii sil nyi Uwumbɔr.

ref: But all you think about is how to cheat or abuse or murder some innocent victim.
text: Le aa ma le ban saakumɔŋ aanyoor baanja; aa ku binib bi kaa kpa taani ubaa na, le ki joo mbimbinpɔɔl muk saanib. Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Jehoiakim, no one will mourn at your funeral. They won't turn to each other and ask, “Why did our great king have to die?”
text: Le Uwumbɔr nan len Josia aajapɔɔn Jehoyakim, u nan ye Juda aabɔr na aabɔr ke, “Ubaa aan wii waakpuul, kaan len ke, ‘Ni kpa mpombiin sakpen, njɔ, ni kpa mpombiin sakpen a.’ Ubaa aan wii u pu, kaan moo u pu ke, ‘Maaninkpel, maabɔr.’

ref: You will be given a burial fit for a donkey; your body will be dragged outside the city gates and tossed in the dirt. I, the Lord, have spoken. King Jehoiachin and the People of Jerusalem The Lord told me to say:
text: Bi ga di ubon aakpuul aanyuŋ le di fuul u di buen ki ti di u mee Jerusalem aabisamɔi aapuwɔb.” Jeremia aah di Jerusalem aalirm aabɔr ti len na sɔ

ref: People of Jerusalem, the nations you trusted have been crushed. Go to Lebanon and weep; cry in the land of Bashan and in Moab.
text: Jerusalem aanib, li cha Lebanonn aatiŋ pu, ki ti li tar man; li cha Basann aatiŋ pu ki li wii man; li bi Moab aajoo pu ki yin man, ba pu? bi nyaŋ nimaantɔtiib a.

ref: When times were good, I warned you. But you ignored me, just as you have done since Israel was young.
text: Naah nan laa kpa liwangol buyoonn na, le Uwumbɔr nan len ni chee le ni yii kaa pel. Nimi aatuln le bi na, nimi aamɔfal aayoonn mɔmɔk ni; naa kee kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb.

ref: Now you will be disgraced because of your sins. Your leaders will be swept away by the wind, and the nations you trusted will be captured and dragged to a foreign country.
text: Naah tun titunwanbir pu na, le libuln ga daa nimi aayidam buen, le bidim ga chur nimaantɔtiib butɔb ni tinaagbiir, le nimi aatiŋ jin inimɔɔn.

ref: King Jehoiachin, son of Jehoiakim, even if you were the ring I wear as the sign of my royal power, I would still pull you from my finger.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Juda Aabɔr Jehoyakim aajapɔɔn Jehoyachinn ke, “Maah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu na, hali aa yaa ba ye kibɔmbik ki ŋmaa ŋŋangii aaŋanbik pu na kan,

ref: I would hand you over to the enemy you fear, to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army, who want to kill you.
text: m ba ga ŋmaar si tii binib bi ban bi ku si, aan aa san bi ijawaan na. M ga di si tii Ubɔr Nebukadnesar ni waajab la.

ref: You and your mother were born in Judah, but I will throw both of you into a foreign country, where you will die,
text: M ga jenn aa ni aana buen tinaagbiir ni. Ni ga buen kitiŋ ki baa nan ma nimi ki ponn ni na la, le ni mɔmɔk ga ti kpo nima.

ref: Jehoiachin, you are unwanted like a broken clay pot. So you and your children will be thrown into a country you know nothing about.
text: Le m bui ke, “Ubɔr Jehoyachinn kpaln libuul li wii aan bi di li mee ubaa aa ki ban li na la aa? Kina pu le u ni waabim bi tinaagbiir ni, kitiŋ ki baa nyi kaabɔr na ni ii?

ref: Land of Judah, I am the Lord. Now listen to what I say!
text: Kitiŋ, kitiŋ, kitiŋ, li pel Uwumbɔr aah len pu na.

ref: Erase the names of Jehoiachin's children from the royal records. He is a complete failure, and so none of them will ever be king. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: M siin ke uja wee lann waabim ki li ye uja u kaan kan tinyoor na. Waan li kpa yaabitiib bi ga nan li joo Juda aatiŋ ke Ubɔr David aah nan ye pu na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: You leaders of my people are like shepherds that kill and scatter the sheep.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa nan jin biyidam bi bii ki yaa waanib na tibɔr kan, naan li ŋan bi pu.

ref: You were supposed to take care of my people, but instead you chased them away. So now I'll punish you severely and make you pay for your crimes!
text: Uwumbɔr, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na aah len biyidam bi aatuln ba ye bi li joo waanib mbamɔm na aabɔr pu na sɔ: “Naa joo maanib; ni yaa bi, le ki jenn bi buen. Tɔ, m ga daa nitafal naah tun titunwanbir ti na pu.

ref: I will bring the rest of my people home from the lands where I have scattered them, and they will grow into a mighty nation.
text: M ga kuun ni maanib bi ŋmar na ki nya ni ntim mu m yaa bi aan bi bi mu ponn ni na, le ki giin ni bi bido aatiŋ pu. Bi ga li kpa mbim pam ki pɔr kpee.

ref: I promise to choose leaders who will care for them like real shepherds. All of my people will be there, and they will never again be frightened.
text: M ga ban biyidam bi ga li joo bi na. Maanib aan ki li san ijawaan, le maan ki daa bitafal. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: Someday I will appoint an honest king from the family of David, a king who will be wise and rule with justice.
text: Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “N‑yoonn choo le m ga nyan Ubɔr David aayaabitiib ponn ni ubɔr u aabimbin ŋan na. Ubɔr ngbaan ga di nlan le joo waanib ki li ŋani tiwan ni ŋan ki tok na kitiŋ ngbaan pu.

ref: As long as he is king, Israel will have peace, and Judah will be safe. The name of this king will be “The Lord Gives Justice.”
text: U yaa nan ŋa ubɔr kan, Juda aanib ga kan lifuur, le Israel aanib kan nsuudoon. Bi ga li yin u ke ‘Uwumbɔr u gaal timi lir na’ la.”

ref: A time will come when you will again worship me. But you will no longer call me the Living God who rescued Israel from Egypt.
text: Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “N‑yoonn choo le binib aan ki li puur tipuur maayimbil pu ke, ‘Uwumbɔr u bi ki nyan ni Israel aanib Ijipt aatiŋ ni na.’

ref: Instead, you will call me the Living God who rescued you from the land in the north and from all the other countries where I had forced you to go. And you will once again live in your own land. Jeremiah Thinks about Unfaithful Prophets
text: Bi ga li gur puur maayimbil pu ke, ‘Uwumbɔr u bi ki nyan ni Israel aanib ŋŋangan wɔb aatiŋ ni, ni ntim mu ponn ni m cha bi yaa ki bi mu ponn ni na la.’ Le bi ga li koo bima bibaa aatiŋ pu.” Jeremia aah nan di Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib aabɔr ti len na sɔ

ref: When I think of the prophets, I am shocked, and I tremble like someone drunk, because of the Lord and his sacred words.

text: Juda aatiŋ aayidam aah ŋun tiwan ni ŋa na pu, le bi san nyan ni nnaan aadichal ni, ki dan Uwumbɔr Aadichal chee, le ki ti kal baakakaa chee, mbisamɔb mu bi yin mu ke Mbisamɔpɔɔn na chee.

ref: While they listened, the priests and the prophets said to the crowd, “All of you have heard Jeremiah prophesy that Jerusalem will be destroyed. He deserves the death penalty.”
text: Le bitotoorb ni bibɔnabr nan bui biyidam ni binib ngbaan ke, “Uja wee ŋeer ke ti ku u, waah len tibɔr ti kitiŋ kee pu na pu. Nimi nibaa aatafal ŋun waah len pu na.”

ref: Then I told the judges and everyone else: The Lord himself sent me to tell you about the terrible things he will do to you, to Jerusalem, and to the temple. But if you change your ways and start obeying the Lord, he will change his mind.
text: Ni kpeln mbimbin mu ni bi mu ni na, ni tiwan ni ni ŋani na, ki kii Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb. Ni yaa ŋa kina kan, u ga kpeln waalandak ki taa ki cha libiil li u bui ke u ga joo ni ni pu na dan.

ref: You must decide what to do with me. Just do whatever you think is right.
text: M ma kan, m bi nimi aapɔɔn ni la. Naah gee pu na kan, ni ŋa mi.

ref: The judges and the other people told the priests and prophets, “Since Jeremiah only told us what the Lord our God had said, we don't think he deserves to die.”
text: Le biyidam ni binib ngbaan bui bitotoorb ni bibɔnabr ngbaan ke, “Uja wee len ti chee tibɔr Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aayimbil pu la; naa ŋan ke ni ku u.”

ref: Then some of the leaders from other towns stepped forward. They told the crowd that
text: Nee aapuwɔb, biyidam ngbaan bibaa nan fii sil le ki bui binib bi kuun ni na ke,

ref: years ago when Hezekiah was king of Judah, a prophet named Micah from the town of Moresheth had said: “I, the Lord All-Powerful, say Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.”
text: “Hesekia aah nan ye Juda aabɔr na, Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Maika u nan bi Moresef aatiŋ ni na nan tuk binib mɔmɔk ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan len ke, ‘Bi ga kpar Sionn ke lisikpel na, le Jerusalem kpaln tilangbenn aakpuk, le Uwumbɔr Aadichal aagongoln ga kpaln kichook.’

ref: Then the leaders continued: No one put Micah to death for saying that. Instead, King Hezekiah prayed to the Lord with fear and trembling and asked him to have mercy. text: Ubɔr Hesekia ni Juda aanib aa nan ku Maika. Hesekia nan labr san Uwumbɔr le ki pɔɔn ubaa ke u kan lineen u chee. Le Uwumbɔr nan kpeln waalandak, kaa ki cha tibɔbir ti u nan bui ke ti ga dan bi pu na dan. Ti bi ban tibɔbir sakpenn le tii tibaa.”

ref: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me: Jeremiah, make a wooden yoke with leather straps, and place it on your neck.
text: ke m di ŋigbapapan ni idɔ, ki ŋa mbaa inaaja i ko na aadɔ i punn isil pu na ki di leen nsil.

ref: Then send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Some officials from these countries are in Jerusalem, meeting with Zedekiah.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke m di inaŋ tii Edom, ni Moab, ni Amonn, ni Taya, ni Saidonn aaninkpiib bi dan Jerusalem ni ke bi nan kan Ubɔr Sedekia na, aan bi ti di i tii baabɔrb.

ref: So have them tell their kings that I have said: I am the All-Powerful Lord God of Israel,
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, nan tuk mi ke m tuk bi ke bi ti bui baabɔrb ke uma Uwumbɔr len ke,

ref: and with my power I created the earth, its people, and all animals. I decide who will rule the earth,
text: “Maapɔɔnsakpiin pu le m naan dulnyaa wee, ni unibɔn, ni tiwakor ti mɔmɔk bi kitiŋ pu na; le ki joo ki tii unii umɔk m gee na.

ref: and I have chosen my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to rule all nations, including yours. I will even let him rule the wild animals. All nations will be slaves of Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his grandson. Then many nations will join together, and their kings will make slaves of the Babylonians.
text: Ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ga tun tii u, ki ga tun tii ujapɔɔn, ni uyaabil ki ti saa buyoonn waatimbol ga lir na. N‑yoonn ngbaan le waatimbol ga li tun tii ŋitimbol ni bibɔrkpaam bi kpa ipɔɔn na.

ref: This yoke stands for the power of King Nebuchadnezzar, and I will destroy any nation that refuses to obey him. Nebuchadnezzar will attack, and many will die in battle or from hunger and disease.
text: “Litimbol, bee nnaan mubaa yaa kaa kii tii u kan, m ga di butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween daa litafal ki ti saa buyoonn m ga cha Nebukadnesar kuln li pel pel na.

ref: You might have people in your kingdom who claim they can tell the future by magic or by talking with the dead or by dreams or messages from a god. But don't pay attention if any of them tell you not to obey Nebuchadnezzar.
text: Taa ŋun tii bibɔnabr man, bee unii umɔk bui ke u ga ŋmaa len tiwan ni ga fe ŋa fen na tidaŋ ni, bee bitekpiib aawiin, bee binib bi joo inyɔk tun na. Bi mɔmɔk tuk nimi le ke ni taa kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr.

ref: If you listen to such lies, I will have you dragged far from your country and killed.
text: Bi ŋmanni nimi la, le kina ngbaan ga cha bi chur nimi buen dandar ki cha nimi aatiŋ. M ga jenn nyan nimi, le bi ku doo nimi.

ref: But if you and your nation are willing to obey Nebuchadnezzar, I will let you stay in your country, and your people will continue to live and work on their farms.
text: Tɔ, litimbol li kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr ki tun tii u na ma kan, m ga cha li li bi laatiŋ pu, ki li koo nima ki ko. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: After I had spoken to the officials from the nearby kingdoms, I went to King Zedekiah and told him the same thing. Then I said: Zedekiah, if you and the people of Judah want to stay alive, you must obey Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians.
text: M nan bui Juda Aabɔr Sedekia tibɔchachaan ngbaan la, “Kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr. Li tun tii u ni waanib, ki li kpa limɔfal.

ref: But if you refuse, then you and your people will die from war, hunger, and disease, just as the Lord has warned.
text: Ba ŋa aa ban aa ni saanib kpo butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween aakun? Kina le Uwumbɔr len ke litimbol li kaa kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr na ga kan.

ref: Your prophets have told you that you don't need to obey Nebuchadnezzar, but don't listen to their lies.
text: Taa ŋun bibɔnabr bi tuk nimi ke ni taa di nibaa tii u na aabɔr. Bi ŋmanni nimi la.

ref: Those prophets claim to be speaking for the Lord, but he didn't send them. They are lying! If you do what they say, he will have both you and them dragged off to another country and killed. The Lord has spoken.
text: Uwumbɔr ubaa le len ke waa tun ni bi, ke bi joo inyamɔn le tuk nimi waayimbil pu. Kina pu na, u ga jenn nyan nimi, le bi ku nimi; nimi ni bibɔnabr bi joo inyamɔn yee tuk nimi na ga kpo.”

ref: When I finished talking to the king, I told the priests and everyone else that the Lord had said: Don't listen to the prophets when they say that very soon the Babylonians will return the things they took from my temple. Those prophets are lying!
text: Le m tuk bitotoorb ngbaan ni binib ngbaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na ke, “Taa ŋun bibɔnabr bi len ke Maadichal ni aawangol ga ki nyan Babiloŋ ni ki gir ni dandana na aabɔr. Bi geei nimi inyamɔn la.

ref: If you choose to obey the king of Babylonia, you will live. But if you listen to those prophets, this whole city will be nothing but a pile of rubble.
text: Taa pel bi chee man. Kii tii Babiloŋ aabɔr ki li kpa limɔfal man. Ba ŋa ni ban ke kitiŋ kee kpaln tilangbenn.

ref: If I really had spoken to those prophets, they would know what I am going to do. Then they would be begging me not to let everything else be taken from the temple and the king's palace and the rest of Jerusalem.
text: Bi yaa sil ye maabɔnabr le ki kpa maabɔr kan, cha bi gaŋ min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ke m taa cha bi yoor liwangol li gur Maadichal ni, ni nnaan aadichal ni na buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni.”

ref: will be taken to Babylonia, where they will remain until I decide to bring them back to Jerusalem. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Bi ga yoor li buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu m ga fenn maalandak toŋ li wɔb na. Le m ga giin ni li ki nan di siin libuul lee ni. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: Later that same year, in the fifth month of the fourth year that Zedekiah was king, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur from Gibeon came up to me in the temple. And while the priests and others in the temple were listening,
text: Libinbaal ngbaan ponn ni, Sedekia aah nan ye ubɔr pu na aabinanar aaŋmaŋmu ni, le Asur aajapɔɔn Hanania u nan ye ubɔnabr Gibeonn aatiŋ ni na nan len m chee tibɔr Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni.

ref: he told me that the Lord had said: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I will smash the yoke that Nebuchadnezzar put on the necks of the nations to make them his slaves.
text: U nan bui mi bitotoorb ni binib ngbaan mɔmɔk aanimbil ni, ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na len ke, “M bii Babiloŋ aabɔr aapɔɔn.

ref: And within two years, I will bring back to Jerusalem everything that he took from my temple and carried off to Babylonia.
text: Joo cha ni ŋibin ŋilee na, m ga giin ni Maadichal ni aawangol li Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar nan yoor di buen na.

ref: King Jehoiachin and the other people who were taken from Judah to Babylonia will be allowed to come back here as well. All this will happen because I will smash the power of the king of Babylonia!
text: M ga giin ni Juda aabɔr Jehoyachinn, u aate ye Jehoyakim na, ni Juda aanib bi mɔmɔk nan buen tinaagbiir ni Babiloŋ ni na. Een, m ga bii Babiloŋ aabɔr aapɔɔn. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: The priests and the others were still standing there, so I said:
text: M nan bui Hanania ni bitotoorb, ni binib bi mɔmɔk nan si Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni na aanimbil ni ke:

ref: Hananiah, I hope the Lord will do exactly what you said. I hope he does bring back everything the Babylonians took from the temple, and that our people who were taken to Babylonia will be allowed to return home.
text: “Mbamɔn, Uwumbɔr ba sil ŋa kina kan, ni ba ŋan. Saabɔkpiirkaan tee ba ga sil gbiin ke u nyan ni Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni, Waadichal ni aawangol ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi tinaagbiir ni nima na kan, m ba ga li gee kina sakpen.

ref: But let me remind you and everyone else
text: Tɔ, tee li pel maah kpa pu m tuk aa ni binib ngbaan na.

ref: that long before we were born, prophets were saying powerful kingdoms would be struck by war, disaster, and disease.
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr bi nan puen len tibɔr n‑yaajayoonn, waahr aan m ni sin nin fuu ni na, nan len ke butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween ga dan ŋitimbol ni bibɔrkpaam pam pu.

ref: Now you are saying we will have peace. We will just have to wait and see if that is really what the Lord has said.
text: Tɔ, ubɔnabr u len ke nsuudoon bi, aan waah len pu na nan gbiin kan, le bi ga bee u ke u sil ye ubɔnabr u Uwumbɔr tun ni u na.”

ref: Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke from my neck and smashed it.
text: Le Hanania chuu inaaja aadɔ i lee nsil na ki kool kool i yuk yuk,

ref: Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.” I left the temple,
text: le ki len binib ngbaan mɔmɔk aanimbil ni ke: “Uwumbɔr bui ke kina le u ga bii Ubɔr Nebukadnesar aadɔ i u di leen ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aasil na; ki joo cha ŋibin ŋilee ponn ni le u ga ŋa kina.” Le m siir.

ref: and a little while later, the Lord told me
text: Nee aapuwɔb, le Uwumbɔr bui mi

ref: to go back and say to Hananiah: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You smashed a wooden yoke, but I will replace it with one made of iron. text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na bui ke u ga di tikur aadɔ kina le leen ŋitimbol ŋee aasil ki cha bi li tun tii Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar. Uwumbɔr ki len ke u ga cha ipeel mu tun tii Nebukadnesar.”

ref: Hananiah, I have never sent you to speak for me. And yet you have talked my people into believing your lies and rebelling against me. So now I will send you—I'll send you right off the face of the earth! You will die before this year is over.
text: Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr ubaa len ke u ga ku si. Saah bui binib ngbaan ke bi yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na, aa ga kpo waahr aan libiln lee nin jer.”

ref: Two months later, Hananiah died.
text: Le Hanania nan kpo libinbaal ngbaan aaŋmalole ponn ni.

ref: I had been left in Jerusalem when King Nebuchadnezzar took many of the people of Jerusalem and Judah to Babylonia as prisoners, including King Jehoiachin, his mother, his officials, and the metal workers and others in Jerusalem who were skilled in making things. So I wrote a letter to the priests, the prophets, the leaders, and the rest of our people in Babylonia.
text: Baah nan chuu Ubɔr Jehoyachinn, ni una, ni libɔrchiln ni aaninkpiib, ni Juda ni Jerusalem aayidam, ni bikpikpiib, ni biwanŋab mɔmɔk di buen tinaagbiir ni na aapuwɔb le m nan ŋmee kigbaŋ ngbaan.

ref: I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote
text: M nan di kigbaŋ ngbaan tii Safann aajapɔɔn Elasa, ni Hilkia aajapɔɔn Gemaria, bi Juda Aabɔr Sedekia nan tun bi Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni, Ubɔr Nebukadnesar chee na la. Kaabɔr sɔ:

ref: that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. Now I tell you
text: “Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, bui binib bi mɔmɔk u nan cha Nebukadnesar chur Jerusalem ni ki di buen tinaagbiir ni, Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni na ke:

ref: to settle there and build houses. Plant gardens and eat what you grow in them.
text: ‘Maa ŋidichal ki kal man. Naan tisar ki ji naah bun tijikaar ti ti ponn ni na.

ref: Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
text: Yoor bipiib ki maa mbim man, ki cha nijapɔtiib mu yoor bipiib, nibisatiib mu mɔn tichar, aan ki mu kan mbim. Ni ŋan ke ni pɔr ki taa seen.

ref: Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
text: Li tun man ki cha ntim mu m cha ni ti bi tinaagbiir ni mu ponn ni na kan tinyoor. Li mee limeel m chee bi pu, ba pu? bi yaa kan liwangol kan, ni mu ga kan.

ref: You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers.
text: Le ni ga yin mi. Ni ga dan ki nan mee limeel, le m ga ŋun nimi aameel.

ref: You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you
text: Ni ga ban mi, le ki ga kan mi, ba pu? ni ga di nisui mɔmɔk le ban mi.

ref: You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
text: “Nimi le bui ke Uwumbɔr tii nimi bibɔnabr Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni.

ref: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now.
text: Nimi bi mɔmɔk m cha ni buen tinaagbiir ni Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni na, li pel man, min Uwumbɔr aah len pu na.’

ref: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, nan tii mi tibɔr ke m di tii Semaya, u ye Nehelam aatiŋ aanii, ki nan di ubaa aayimbil pu ki ŋmee kigbaŋ tii Jerusalem aanib mɔmɔk, ni utotoor Sefania, u aate ye Maaseya na, ni bitotoorb biken na mɔmɔk. Semaya nan ŋmee tibɔr timina le waagbaŋ ngbaan ni tii Sefania:

ref: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars.
text: “Uwumbɔr nan yii Jehoyada le ki di si ŋa utotoor, sin le ye uma Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aayidaan. Ni ye sin le aatuln ke aa chur biwaarb bi mɔmɔk chuun ŋmanni ke bi ye bibɔnabr na, ki di tikur aabuen ŋmaan bisil, ki di tikululn baa bi kaan.

ref: Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him?
text: Ba ŋa saa ŋa Anatof aanii u bi yin u ke Jeremia aan u chuun tuk binib tibɔr ke u ye Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr na kina?

ref: He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
text: U tuk binib bi bi Babiloŋ ni, tinaagbiir ni na, ke bi ga li bi nima aan ni ti yunn, kina pu na, bi maa ŋidichal, ki kal nima, ki naan tisar, ki ji baah ko tijikaar ti na; kina pu na, cha bi chuu u.”

ref: When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me.
text: Sefania nan karn kigbaŋ ngbaan tii mi.

ref: The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you.
text: bui mi ke, “Ŋmee maah tuk si tibɔr ti mɔmɔk na ŋa kigbaŋ ni,

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah: Screams of terror are heard, with no word of peace.
text: “M ŋun ijawaan aawiil pu, iwiil ngbaan ye ijawaan aawiil, kaa ye nsuudoon aawiil.

ref: Can men give birth? Then why do I see them looking so pale and clutching their stomachs like women in labor?
text: Tɔ, sil man ki dakl lik. Uja ga ŋmaa maa ubo oo? Tɔ, ni ŋa kinye aan m waa uja mɔmɔk bub joo upuul ke upii u ban u maa na? Ba ŋa unii mɔk naahn ubun kina?

ref: My people, soon you will suffer worse than ever before, but I will save you.
text: Ijawaan sakpiin aawiin mubaa choo; nwiin ngbaan aaŋeen aatɔ aan li bi, maanib aapombiin aayoonn le bi na, bi mu tee ga ŋmar.”

ref: Now you are slaves of other nations, but I will break the chains and smash the yokes that keep you in slavery.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ki bui ke: “Liyaadaal ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, m ga kool inaaja i ko na aadɔ i bi di leen bisil na ki chuu nyan baakululn na mu, le baan ki li ye biwɔwɔm aanaagbiib.

ref: Then you will be my servants, and I will choose a king for you from the family of David. *
text: Bi ga li gur tun min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aatuln, ni maah ga nyan Ubɔrkpaan David aayaabil u kaan nnaan na aatuln la.

ref: Israel, you belong to me, so don't be afraid. You deserved to be punished; that's why I scattered you in distant nations. But I am with you, and someday I will destroy those nations.
text: Maanib, taa san ijawaan man; Israel aanib, taa cha ijawaan joo nimi man. M ga nyan ni nimi dandar aatiŋ ni, m ga nyan ni nimi kitiŋ ki ponn ni, ni ye binaagbiib na. Ni ga gir ni linampal ki nan li bi nsuudoon ni, ni ga li bi lifuur ni, le ubaa aan ki cha ijawaan chuu nimi.

ref: Then I will bring you and your descendants back to your land, where I will protect you and give you peace. Then your fears will be gone. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
text: M ga dan ni chee ki nan gaa nimi lii. M ga kuln ŋitimbol ŋi mɔmɔk m cha ni yaa ki bi ŋi ponn ni na, maan kuln nimi ma. Maan di cha ki taa daa nitafal; m mu yaa daa nitafal kan, m ga daa ki ŋeer la. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: The Lord said: My people, you are wounded and near death.
text: Uwumbɔr ki bui waanib ke, “Nimi aabuun aa kpa ke i yann, nimi aatotonn aan doo.

ref: You are accused of a crime with no one to defend you, and you are covered with sores that no medicine can cure. *
text: Ubaa aa bi ki ga li joo nimi, nnyɔk aa bi ki ga cha nimi aabuun yann, naa kpa limakl ke ni ga sɔŋ.

ref: Your friends have forgotten you; they don't care anymore. Even I have acted like an enemy. And because your sins are horrible and countless, I will be cruel as I punish you.
text: Nibɔtiib mɔmɔk suln nibɔr a; bitafal aa ki bi ni ponn ni. M tak nimi ke udin na la; nimi aatunwanbir aah wiir aan nimi aabiin nyaŋ sakpen pu na le cha nimi aatafadaan bir.

ref: But if your enemies try to rob or destroy you, I will rob and destroy them, and they will be led as captives to foreign lands.
text: Tɔ, dandana ma kan, binib ga nae bi mɔmɔk nan nae nimi na, bi ga chur nimi aadim tinaagbiir di buen. Bi ga muk binib bi mɔmɔk nan muk nimi na, le ki gaa binib bi mɔmɔk nan gaal nimi aawan mpɔɔn na mu aawan mpɔɔn.

ref: No one wants you as a friend or cares what happens to you. But I will heal your injuries, and you will get well. The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
text: Ni yaa po ye ke nimi aadim len ke, ‘Bi di Sionn mee a; ubaa aatafal aa ki bi u ni’ kan, m ga ki cha ni pɔɔk, m ga cha nimi aabuun yann. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: The Lord said: Israel, I will be kind to you and let you come home. Jerusalem now lies in ruins, but you will rebuild it, complete with a new palace.
text: Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “M ga giin ni maanib baatiŋ pu ki san lidichal mɔmɔk kinimbaak; Jerusalem ga ki gir maa, le kaanaan aadichal ki gir sil.

ref: Other nations will respect and honor you. Your homes will be filled with children, and you will celebrate, singing praises to me.
text: Binib bi koo nima na ga gaa kipak aalahn; mpopiin ga dan le bi li tar. M ga di ŋŋaal biin bi pu le bi pɔr kpee; le kina ngbaan tii bi liyimbil.

ref: It will be just like old times. Your nation will worship me, and I will punish anyone who abuses you.
text: M ga cha litimbol ngbaan ki kan laah nan kpa mpɔɔn mu n‑yaayoonn na, ki cha li ki too nyal sil; m ga daa binib bi mɔmɔk muk bi na aatafal.

ref: Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
text: “Yin mi, le m ga kii si; m ga bui si tibɔkpaan ni iwaan aawan ni saan nyi naabɔr na.

ref: Many of the houses in Jerusalem and some of the buildings at the royal palace have been torn down to be used in repairing the walls to keep out the Babylonian attackers. Now there are empty spaces where the buildings once stood. But I am furious, and these spaces will be filled with the bodies of the people I kill. The people of Jerusalem will cry out to me for help, but they are evil, and I will ignore their prayers.
text: Min Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, bui ke Jerusalem aadichal ni Juda aanaan aadichal ga ber. Naa kpa tinyoor ke ni buen ti jan Babiloŋ yaab bi gob nimi aatiŋ na kijaak. Nimina ga cha maaŋuusakpeln aah fii binib bi pu aan m ban m faa ku bi na aanikpol le gbiin kitiŋ kee ni. Kaanib aah tun titunwanbir ti na pu le m fenn mpuwɔb tii ki.

ref: Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace.
text: Tɔ, m tee ga tii kitiŋ kee, ni kaanib lifuur, ki cha bi ki li kpa laafee. M ga tii bi nsuudoon mu ga yunn na, ni ŋŋmarm.

ref: I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before.
text: M ga cha Juda ni Israel yaab kan nkam, m ga ki gir siin bi ke baah nan bi pu na.

ref: They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt.
text: M ga finn nyan bi titunwanbir ti bi tun mi na ni, le ki di baatunwanbir, ni baah yii maamɔb pu na cha pinn bi.

ref: When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
text: Jerusalem ni le maamɔɔn, ni bunyuŋ, ni limakl ga li nya ni, le dulnyaa wee aatimbol li ŋun maah ŋani tiwanyaan ni tii Jerusalem aanib, ni nkam mu m joo ni kitiŋ ngbaan ni na pu kan, biwon ga li gbaa, le bi san ijawaan.”

ref: Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Binib len le ke do chee na bi ke nteersakpiin ni na la, ke binib ni tiwakor aa koo nima. Ni mu sil ye mbamɔn; Juda aatim ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni ye nkuun la; binib ni tiwakor aa bi nima. Tɔ, ntim ngbaan ni, le ni ga ki ŋun mpopiin,

ref: happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say: “We praise you, Lord All-Powerful! You are good to us, and your love never fails.” The land will once again be productive.
text: ni mmɔɔn, ni tibɔndinn aajim aakuun aafuuk pu. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord's Wonderful Promise
text: Bipihkpaab ga ki kahn baapiih ntim mu bi ŋigongon aatiŋ pu na, ni taab aagongon aatim ni, ni Juda aaŋangii wɔb, ni Benjaminn aapepel ni, ni ntimbim mu bi gbɔk Jerusalem na ni, ni Juda aatim ni. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: The Lord said: I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
text: Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “N‑yoonn choo, le m ga cha maah nan puu tipuur ti tii Israel ni Juda yaab na gbiin.

ref: I promise that the time will come when I will appoint a king from the family of David, a king who will be honest and rule with justice.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga lee Ubɔrkpaan David aayaabil u aabimbin ŋan na ŋa ubɔr. Ubɔr ngbaan ga ti tun ni ŋan ki ye ibamɔn na le kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk pu.

ref: In those days, Judah will be safe; Jerusalem will have peace and will be named, “The Lord Gives Justice.”
text: Le Juda ni Jerusalem aanib ga ŋmar ki li bi nsuudoon ni. Bi ga li yin kitiŋ ngbaan ke, ‘Uwumbɔr u gaal timi lir na.’

ref: The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants,
text: Min Uwumbɔr puu ke Ubɔr David aayaabitiib ga li bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ki ji Israel yaab aanaan.

ref: and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
text: Le bitotoorb mu ga li bi ki nyan ni Liifai aanibol ni ki li tun maatuln, ki joo ni kitork ki ga see mmii ni na, ni njikaabim aapiin, ni titoor ti gur na.”

ref: Then the Lord told me:
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke,

ref: I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them,
text: “M ni nwiin pu ni kinyeek puu tipuur tii tɔb la, ke ni li choo n‑yoonn mu m siin ni na, le tipuur ngbaan aa kpa ke ti bii.

ref: and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel,
text: Kina le m puu tipuur tii maatutunn Ubɔr David ke u ga li kpa yaabil n‑yoonn mɔmɔk aan u li ye ubɔr, le ki puu tii bitotoorb bi nyan ni Liifai aanibol ni na ke bi li tun maatuln n‑yoonn mɔmɔk; le tipuur ngbaan mu aa kpa ke ti bii.

ref: and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
text: M ga cha maatutunn Ubɔr David aayaabitiib ni Liifai aanibol moo too pɔr, le unii aan ŋmaa kahn bi ke unii aah kaa ŋmaa kahn iŋmabi i bi kitaapaak na, ni litambol li dɔ nnyusakpem aagbaan na pu na.”

ref: The Lord also said:
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke,

ref: You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
text: “Saa kan binib aah bi len ke m yii ŋidichal ŋilee, ŋi ye Israel ni Juda aanib bi min mbaa nan lee bi na aa? Kina pu le bi lik maanib fam, kaa ki kahn bi sakni ŋitimbol ni.

ref: Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands.
text: Le min Uwumbɔr puu tipuur tii nwiin pu, ni kinyeek, le ki siin ikaal i joo taab ni kitaapaak na.

ref: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
text: Ni ye mbamɔn ke maah ŋa kina pu na, kina le m ga li beenin joo tipuur ti m puu tii Jakob aayaabitiib, ni maatutunn Ubɔr David na. M ga lee Ubɔr David aayaabitiib ponn ni ubaa le u li joo Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob aayaabitiib. M ga san maanib kinimbaak ki cha bi ki kan nkam.”

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me
text: Buyoonn Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar ni waajab, ki di kpee ŋitimbol ni ŋinibol ŋi mɔmɔk nan bi u taab na aajab, nan bi tak Jerusalem ni ntim mu bi gbɔk ki na, le Uwumbɔr nan ki len m chee tibɔr.

ref: to say to King Zedekiah: I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down.
text: Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, nan bui mi ke m ti tuk Juda Aabɔr Sedekia ke, “Min Uwumbɔr ga di kitiŋ kimina tii Babiloŋ aabɔr, le u see ki mmii.

ref: You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
text: Saan ŋmar; bi ga chuu si le ki di si tii u. Aanimbil ga kan u gbin gbin le aa ni uma len tɔb chee tibɔr; le bi di si buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni.

ref: Zedekiah, I promise that you won't die in battle.
text: Sedekia, li pel maah kpa saabɔr ti m len na. Baan ku si butɔb ni.

ref: You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
text: Aa ga kpo nsuudoon ni la, le binib aah nan seer tulalee aayon pu aan bi sub aayaajatiib bi nan puen ye bibɔrb na, kina le bi ga see tulalee aayon mmii ni tii aa mu. Bi ga wii saakpuul le ki bui ke, ‘Timi aabɔr kpo a.’ Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said.
text: Le m nan di tibɔr ngbaan tuk Sedekia, Jerusalem ni,

ref: Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured. The People Break a Promise
text: buyoonn Babiloŋ aabɔr aajab nan bi tak kitiŋ ngbaan na. Bijab ngbaan ki bi tak Lakis, ni Aseka, Juda aatim mulee mu baanja nan gur ki kpa tijawan aan bi maa ŋigon gob mu na mu. Baah nan ŋmanni binaagbiib pu na

ref: King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
text: Binib ngbaan mɔmɔk ni baayidam nan kii ke bi di baanaagbiib lii ki taa ki gir chuu bi. Bi nan sil di bi lii,

text: le naa woln kitaak le bi ki kpeln baalandak, le ki ki chur bi mpɔɔn ŋa tinaagbiir ni lelee.

ref: I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves.
text: u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, bui mi ke m tuk binib ngbaan ke: “Maah nan gaa niyaajatiib Ijipt yaab chee lii na, m nan puu tipuur tii bi.

ref: As part of this agreement, you must let a Hebrew slave go free after six years of service. Your ancestors did not obey me,
text: M bui bi ke libilolole mɔk ni kan, bi di baanaagbiib bi ye Israel yaab ki tun ŋibin ŋiloob tii bi na lii. Le niyaajatiib aa nan ŋun tii mi, kaa nan pel maah len pu na.

ref: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
text: Tɔ, le ni ki kpeln nimi aalandak ki lik seen mi. Ni mɔmɔk ki gir chur nimi aanaagbiib bi ni nan di lii aan bi gee kina na, le ki ki chuu bi mpɔɔn ŋa tinaagbiir ni lelee.

ref: You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
text: Le min Uwumbɔr bui ke ni yii maamɔboln, ke naan tii nina aabitiib Israel yaab lifuur li bi ban na. Kina pu na, m ga tii nimi lifuur, m ga tii nimi lifuur ke ni kpo butɔb ni, ni iween ni, ni nkon ni. Maah ga ŋa nimi pu na ga cha dulnyaa wee aatimbol mɔmɔk san ijawaan.

ref: These enemies are King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia and his army. They have stopped attacking Jerusalem, but they want to kill King Zedekiah and his high officials. I will also let them destroy the towns of Judah, so that no one can live there any longer.
text: M ga lii bi bumɔb le bi ki gir ni kitiŋ kee pu. Bi ga tak ki, ki nyaŋ ki, le ki see ki mmii. M ga ŋa Juda aatim ke nteersakpiin mu pu ubaa aa koo na la. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: When Jehoiakim was king of Judah, the Lord told me,
text: Josia aajapɔɔn Jehoyakim aah nan ye Juda aabɔr na, le Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke,

ref: “Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
text: “Li cha Rekab aataŋaal yaab chee ki ti li joo ni bi Maadichal ponn ni aadiik kibaa ni, ki nan tii bi ndaan.”

ref: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
text: Le m nan ti yoor ni Rekab aataŋaal ngbaan mɔmɔk, Jeremia uken aajapɔɔn Jaasania, Jeremia ngbaan mu aate le nan ye Habasinia, ni unaatiib, ni waabim,

ref: I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
text: le ki joo ni bi Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni. M nan di bi buen ubɔnabr Hanann, u aate ye Igdalia na aadidiliib aadiik ni la. Kidiik kimina nan bi Salum aajapɔɔn Maaseya, u nan ye Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni aanikpaan ubaa na aadiik aapaacham la, le ki bi duun bininkpiib biken aadir.

ref: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
text: Le m nan di tiyikur ni ŋidabuu siin Rekab yaab ngbaan, le ki bui bi ke, “Nyu ndaan man.”

ref: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
text: Le bi gar mi ke, “Taa nyu ndaan. Tiyaaja Rekab aajapɔɔn Jonadab nan bui timi ke timi ni tiyaabitiib taa nyu ndaan mubaa.

ref: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
text: U nan ki bui timi ke ti taa maa tidir, ki taa ko tisar, ki taa ŋum ndaan aasubil aasui ki taa daa i mu. U nan siin ke ti li koo igban aaboo ni, timi aamɔfal ni, aan ki li ye bicham kitiŋ kee pu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: Our clan has always obeyed Jonadab's command. To this very day, we and our wives and sons and daughters don't drink wine or build houses or plant vineyards or crops. And we have lived in tents,
text: Taa maa tidir ke ti li koo, ti koo igban aaboo ŋmeen ni la, le kaa kpa ndaan aasubil aasar, kaa kpa ikpaakon, ni njikaabim mu. Ti kii tii ikaal i mɔmɔk tiyaaja Jonadab nan siin tii timi na.

ref: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
text: Le Ubɔr Nebukadnesar aah nan di waajab koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni na, ti nan bui ke ti ga dan Jerusalem ni do ki nya Babiloŋ ni Siria aajab ni. Nima pu le ti koo Jerusalem ponn ni do.”

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson
text: Le Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na bui mi ke m ti tuk Juda ni Jerusalem aanib ke, “Min Uwumbɔr baa nimi ke ba ŋa naan ŋun tii mi ki kii maakaal.

ref: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
text: Jonadab aayaabitiib kii tii waakaal kaa nyu ndaan, ki di nan saa din, bi ponn ni ubaa aa nyu ndaan. Le m ma len ni chee ki gir len, le naan kii tii mi.

ref: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
text: M beenin tun ni maatutum bi ye bibɔnabr na ni chee, le bi tuk nimi ke ni di cha nimi aabimbin mu kaa ŋan na, ki tun ni ŋan na. Bi sak nimi ke ni taa tun tii ŋiwaa, ki taa dooni ŋi, aan ki li beenin bi kitiŋ ki m nan di tii niyaajatiib na pu. Le naan ŋun tii mi, kaa pel m chee kpala.

ref: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
text: Jonadab aayaabitiib ma kii tii ikaal i biyaaja Jonadab nan di tii bi na, le nimi ma aa kii maamɔb.

ref: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
text: Kina pu na, min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na ga cha libiil li m puu ke li ga dan na, dan nimi Juda ni Jerusalem aanib pu. Maah len ni chee aan naa pel, ki yin nimi aan naa kii na, le ga cha m ŋa kina.”

ref: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
text: Le m bui Rekab yaab ngbaan ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na len ke, “Ni kii tii ikaal i niyaaja Jonadab nan di tii nimi na; ni dii waamɔkm mɔmɔk, le ki ŋa tiwan nimɔk u siin tii nimi na.

ref: so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
text: Kina pu na, min, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, puu ke Rekab aajapɔɔn Jonadab ga li kpa yaabil u ga li tun maatuln n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na.”

ref: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
text: Josia aajapɔɔn Jehoyakim aah nan ye Juda aabɔr pu na aabinanar ponn ni, le Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke,

ref: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
text: “Ban kigbaŋ ki ŋmee maah tuk si Israel, ni Juda, ni ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aabɔr ti na ŋa ki ponn ni. Ŋmee maah nan piin bundaal ki len aa chee tibɔr na, buyoonn Josia nan ye ubɔr na, ki nan saa din wee na.

ref: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
text: Nibaakan, Juda aanib yaa ŋun libiil li mɔmɔk m ban m joo ni bi pu na kan, bi ga di cha baabimbin mu kaa ŋan na. Le m ga di baatunwanbir ni baabiin aatuln cha pinn bi.”

ref: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
text: Le m yin Neria aajapɔɔn Baruk le ki nan ka len tibɔr ti mɔmɔk Uwumbɔr bui mi na, le u ŋmee. Baruk nan ŋmee ti mɔmɔk ŋa kigbaŋ ngbaan pu.

ref: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
text: Le m nan bui Baruk waah ga tun pu na. M bui u ke, “Baan ki kii ke m koo Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni.

ref: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
text: Tɔ, m ban ke binib ngbaan yaa ki bi lulni bumɔb bundaal na kan, aa buen nima. Aa ti karn kigbaŋ ngbaan mpɔɔn pu, aan bi mɔmɔk ŋun tibɔr ti Uwumbɔr di tuk mi aan m mu cha aa ŋmee ti na. Aa karn ki nin chee bi mɔmɔk ga ŋun na; cha Juda aanib bi nyan ni baatim ponn ni ki dan na mu ŋun.

ref: The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
text: Nibaakan bi ga mee Uwumbɔr ki fenn bipuwɔb tii baatunwanbir, ba pu? Uwumbɔr aaŋuusakpeln ni, le u puu ke u ga daa bitafal pam.”

ref: In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud. This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials.
text: Tɔ, buyoonn binib ngbaan nan bi pel suuna na, le Baruk karn tibɔr ti mɔmɔk m nan tuk u na kigbaŋ ngbaan ni. text: Gemaria, u aate nan ye Safann na aajapɔɔn Mikaya nan ŋun Baruk aah karn kigbaŋ ni, Uwumbɔr aah len pu na.

ref: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
text: Le u fii buen libɔrdichal ni ki ti koo libɔrchiln aagbaŋmeer aadiik ni, nin chee bininkpiib ngbaan mɔmɔk nan ka na. ref: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
text: Mikaya nan tuk bi tibɔr ti mɔmɔk u nan ŋun Baruk karn tii binib ngbaan na.

ref: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
text: Le bi bui ke, “Kal ki karn kigbaŋ ngbaan tii timi.” Le Baruk ŋa kina.

ref: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
text: Waah karn ki ti doo na, le bi fenn lik tɔb, le ijawaan bi binimbil ni, le bi bui Baruk ke, “See ti tuk ubɔr tibɔr tee,”

ref: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
text: Le u bui waabo Jerameel, ni Asriel aajapɔɔn Seraya, ni Abdeel aajapɔɔn Selemia ke bi chuu m ni maagbaŋmeer Baruk. Tɔ, Uwumbɔr nan bɔr timi, baa ŋmaa kan timi. Jeremia aah ki gir ŋmee kigbaŋ kiken pu na

ref: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
text: Ubɔr Jehoyakim aah nan di maah ŋeer tibɔr ti tuk Baruk aan u ŋmee ti na see mmii na aapuwɔb,

ref: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
text: le Uwumbɔr ki bui mi ke m ki ban kigbaŋ ki ŋmee tiwan ni mɔmɔk m nan ŋmee ŋa njan yaak ni na.

ref: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke m tuk ubɔr ke, “Aa see kigbaŋ ngbaan mmii, le ki baa Jeremia ke ba ŋa u ŋmee kigbaŋ ke Babiloŋ aabɔr ga dan ki nan kuln kitiŋ kee ki ku kaanib ni tiwakor.

ref: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
text: Min Uwumbɔr le bui sin Ubɔr Jehoyakim, ke aayaabil ubaa aan kal Ubɔr David aanaanjal pu. Bi ga di saawon mee, le nwiin gbaa ti nwiin pu, le limaln mu gbaa ti kinyeek.

ref: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
text: M ga daa aatafal, ki daa aayaabitiib, ni saaninkpiib aatafal titunwanbir ti ni mɔmɔk tun na pu. Aa ni Jerusalem ni Juda aanib yii kaa pel maah sak nimi pu na, kina pu le m ga cha ni kan tibɔbir ti m puu ke ni ga kan ti na.”

ref: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
text: M nan ki yoor kigbaŋ kiken tii maagbaŋmeer Baruk, le u ŋmee tibɔr ti mɔmɔk m di tuk u na. U nan ŋmee tibɔr ti mɔmɔk nan bi njan aagbaŋ na ponn ni na, ni kina aabɔr ti m nan tuk u ke u ŋmee na.

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
text: Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar nan nyan Jehoyakim aajapɔɔn Jehoyachinn, Juda aanaan ni, le ki di Josia aajapɔɔn Sedekia ŋa ubɔr.

text: Aa yaa nyaŋ Babiloŋ aajab ngbaan mɔmɔk, le bi kan titotonn na baanja gur dɔ baaboo ni kan, bijabaab ngbaan le ga ki fii ki see kitiŋ kee aan ki wu pel pel.” Baah chuu Jeremia laŋ kiyondiik ni pu na

text: Le m gar u ke, “M yaa tuk si mbamɔn kan, aa ga ku mi, m yaa ti ki sur si kan, saan ŋun tii mi.”

text: Le Ubɔr Sedekia nan loon ki puu tii mi ke, “M puu Uwumbɔr u bi, ki tii timi limɔfal na, ke maan ku si, kaan di si tii binib bi ban bi ku si na.”

ref: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
text: Le m bui Sedekia ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na len ke, “Aa yaa ti di aabaa tii Babiloŋ aabɔr aajab aaninkpiib kan, saan kpo, kitiŋ kee mu aan wu mmii. Aa ni saadichal mɔmɔk ga ŋmar.

ref: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”

ref: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.

text: Le m ki len ke, “Saapiib, ni saabim mɔmɔk ga koo Babiloŋ yaab aaŋaal ni, le sin aabaa aan ŋmar bi chee. Babiloŋ aabɔr ga chuu si tinaagbiir, le kitiŋ kimina ga wu mmii pel pel.”

ref: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
text: Bui bi ke aa bi gaŋni mi ke m taa di si giin kiyondiik ni aan aa ti kpo nima la.”

ref: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.

ref: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
text: le ki chur ubɔr aabisatiib ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi Mispa na, aan bijab aayidaan Nebusaradann nan di ŋa Gedalia aaŋaal ni na tinaagbiir. Ismael nan chur bi le ki di toŋ Amonn aapepel wɔb.

ref: Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done.
text: Johanann ni bijab aayidam mɔmɔk nan ŋun Ismael aah bii libiil li na.

ref: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
text: Le bi ni baajab nan di paan u pu ki ti pii u Gibeonn aabukpiik sakpeŋ na chee.

ref: When Ishmael's prisoners saw Johanan and the officers, they were happy
text: Ismael aah nan chur binib bi na aah nan kan Johanann ni waajab aaninkpiib na, le bisui piir,

ref: and turned around and ran toward Johanan.
text: le bi gir ki san choo bi chee.

text: Tɔ, Ismael ni waajab biniin bibaa nan san ŋmar Johanann ni waajab ki buen Amonn aatiŋ ni.

ref: Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon
text: Le Johanann ni waajab bi nan dii u na aaninkpiib gaa binib bi Ismael nan ku Gedalia ki chur bi tinaagbiir ki nyan Mispa aatiŋ ni na, bi nan ye bijab bi jaa kijaak na, ni bipiib, ni mbim, ni baah lee nyan bijab bi aajawan na.

ref: toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar. The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
text: Ismael aah nan ku Gedalia, u Babiloŋ aabɔr nan di ŋa kitiŋ ngbaan aayidaan na, le bi san Babiloŋ yaab ijawaan. Kina pu le bi nan di toŋ Ijipt aatiŋ ni ke Babiloŋ yaab taa pii bi. Baah cha na, le bi nan ti sil Kimham aatiŋ ki bi Betlehem na chee.

ref: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
text: Bijab aasalolm mɔmɔk, ki di kpee Karea aajapɔɔn Johanann, ni Hosaya aajapɔɔn Asaria pu, ni binib mɔmɔk aabɔŋ nan dan m chee,

ref: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
text: le ki nan bui mi, “Ŋaanii ki ŋa taah bui si pu na. Mee Tidindaan Uwumbɔr tii timi. Mee limeel tii timi bi mɔmɔk ŋmar na. N‑yoonn mubaa ti nan ye binib bi wiir na la, tɔ, dandana ma kan, sin aabaa waa ke timi siib kina le gur.

ref: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
text: Mee Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ke u mɔk timi nin chee ti ga buen na, ni tiwan ni ti ga ŋa na.”

ref: “All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
text: Le m gar bi ke, “Tɔ, ni ŋan. M ga mee Tidindaan Uwumbɔr naah len pu na, u yaa kpa timɔk ki len na kan, m ga di tuk nimi. Maan di tibaa bɔr nimi.”

ref: They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says,
text: Le bi bui mi ke, “Ti yaa yii kaa kii Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ga di tibɔr timɔk tuk si ke aa di tuk timi na kan, u li ye useeraadaan bamɔnn ti pu.

ref: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
text: Iwiin kipiik aapuwɔb le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr,

ref: Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together
text: le m kuun Johanann, ni bijab bi bi u chee na aasalolm mɔmɔk, ni binib biken mɔmɔk.

ref: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
text: M nan bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr, Israel yaab Aawumbɔr, u chee ni di nimi aabɔr tun mi na bui ke,

ref: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
text: ‘Ni yaa ban ke ni li beenin bi kitiŋ kimina pu kan, m ga maa nimi ŋidichal ki taa bii nimi, m ga cha ni moo chɔbaan ki taa ki kpokl lir. Maah nan cha libiil li dan ni pu na tii mi mpombiin pam.

ref: Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him,
text: Taa ki san Babiloŋ yaab aabɔr ijawaan. M bi ni chee, ki ga nyan nimi waapɔɔn ni.

ref: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
text: Maah ye unimbaasaln na, m ga cha u san nimi kinimbaak ki cha ni gir kun. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.’

ref: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
text: Binib bi mɔmɔk aanimbil mann ke bi ga buen ti li koo Ijipt aatiŋ pu na, butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween le ga ku bi. Bi ponn ni ubaa aan ŋmar, ubaa aan nya tibɔbir ti m ban m cha ti dan bi pu na.’”

ref: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
text: Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na ki bui ke, “Maah nan cha maaŋuusakpeln dan Jerusalem pu pu na, kina le ni yaa buen Ijipt ni kan, maaŋuul ga dan ni pu. Binib yaa kan nimi kan, ni ga li kpa ijawaan; binib ga lik nimi fam le ki li joo nimi aayimbil puuni lir biken pu. Naan ki kan do kpala.”

ref: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
text: Le m ki moo len ke, “Uwumbɔr bui mi ke m tuk nimi bi gur Juda ni na ke ni taa buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni. Kina pu na, m sur nimi dandana wee ke

ref: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
text: ni bi tun taani sakpiin la. Ni bui mi ke m mee Tidindaan Uwumbɔr tii nimi, le ki puu ke ni ga ŋa waah len pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
text: Tɔ, m bui nimi a, le ni yii tiwan ni mɔmɔk Tidindaan Uwumbɔr tun ni mi ke m nan tuk nimi na.

ref: I told the people everything the Lord had told me.
text: M nan tuk binib ngbaan Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aah bui mi ke m tuk bi pu na doo.

ref: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
text: Le Hosaya aajapɔɔn Asaria, ni Karea aajapɔɔn Johanann, ni bigaadam biken na mɔmɔk bui mi ke, “Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aa tun ni si ke aa nan tuk timi ke ti taa buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni ki ti li koo nima. Aa gii la.

ref: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
text: Neria aajapɔɔn Baruk le saan si lii ti pu, ke Babiloŋ yaab kan ti pu mpɔɔn, ki yaa gee kan, bi ku timi, bee bi chur timi buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni.”

ref: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
text: Kina pu na, Johanann, ni bijab aaninkpiib, ni binib ngbaan ubaa aa kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki gaar Juda aatiŋ pu.

ref: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
text: Le Johanann ni bijab aaninkpiib ngbaan mɔmɔk yoor unii umɔk gur Juda aatiŋ pu na buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni; bi nan di binib bi nyan ni baah nan yaa ki bi ŋitimbol ŋi ponn ni ki gir ni na mu buen:

ref: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
text: bi nan di bijab, ni bipiib, ni mbim, ni ubɔr aabisatiib mu buen. Bi nan yoor bijab aayidaan Nebusaradann aah nan cha binib bimɔk gaar Juda ni ki bi Gedalia aaŋaal ni na, ki di Baruk ni m mu kpee.

ref: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
text: Bi nan yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb le ki di ti fuu Ijipt aatiŋ ki bi yin ki ke Tapanes na ni.

ref: when the Lord told me:
text: Nima chee le Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke,

ref: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
text: “Ban ŋitakpal ŋi filk na, ki di ŋi sub baah chii Ijipt aabɔr aadichal aabisamɔb nin chee na, ki cha Israel yaab bi bi kitiŋ kimina ponn ni na aanimbil kan saah sub ŋi pu na,

ref: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
text: ki bui bi ke min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, ga cha maatutunn u ye Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar na dan do, u ga nan di waabɔrjal siin ŋitakpal ŋi aa di sub na pu, le ki taln nnaan aakekeln biin ŋi pu.

ref: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
text: Uwumbɔr nan len Israel yaab bi nan bi Ijipt aatiŋ pu ki koo Migdol, ni Tapanes, ni Memfis aatim ni, ni Ijipt aaŋangii wɔb aapepel ni na aabɔr.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na bui ke, “Nimi nibaa nan kan tibɔbir ti m nan cha ti dan Jerusalem ni Juda aatim muken mɔmɔk pu pu na. Ki nan saa din wee, mu beenin ye tilangbenn, le unii ubaa aa bi mu ponn ni; ba pu?

ref: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
text: mu aanib nan tun titunwanbir ki ŋa mi liŋuul. Bi nan toor kitork tii ŋiwaa, le ki dii ŋiwaa ŋi bima, ni nimi, ni niyaajatiib aa kee dii ŋi na.

ref: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
text: Le m joo maatutum bi ye bibɔnabr na tuni ni chee, le bi nan bui nimi ke ni taa ŋani tiwan ni sukr ponn ni na maah kaa gee ni na.

ref: but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods.
text: Le ni yii, kaa pel, kaa ŋun tii mi. Naa di cha titunwanbir ti ni tun ke ni toor ŋiwaa na.

ref: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
text: Le m di maaŋuusakpeln lii ni Juda aatim pu, ni Jerusalem ponn ni, le mu wun mmii. Mu nan kpaln tilangbenn, le ki kpa unii ijawaan, ke mu aah beenin bi pu din wee na.

ref: Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies.
text: “Kina pu le min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na baa nimi ke ba ŋa ni bi tun nibaa titunwanbir timina aaboln. Ni ban ke ni joo ni tibɔbir nan lii bijab, ni bipiib, ni mbim, ni mbipɔm pu, le nimi aanii ubaa taa gur aa?

ref: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
text: Ba ŋa ni dii ŋiwaa ki toor kitork tii ŋiwaa Ijipt ni do, nin chee ni dan nan koo na, ki ŋani mi liŋuul? Ni ŋani kina ke ni kuln, aan binib li lik nimi fam ki joo nimi aayimbil puuni lir biken pu la aa?

ref: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
text: Ni suln niyaajatiib, ni Juda aabɔrb, ni bipuutiib, ni nimi, ni nipuutiib aah nan tun mbiin aatun ŋi Juda aatim ni, ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni na pu la aa?

ref: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
text: Le ki nan saa din, naa kee sunn nibaa taab. Naa nyuŋni mi, le kaa joo ikaal i mɔmɔk m di tii nimi ni niyaajatiib na.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have decided to wipe you out with disasters.
text: “Kina pu na, min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, ga fenn lir ni pu ki kuln Juda aatiŋ mɔmɔk.

ref: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
text: Juda aanib bi ma gur aan binimbil man ke bi buen ti li koo Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, see m kuln bi mɔmɔk. Binikpaam ni biwaatiib mɔmɔk ga kpo butɔb ni, ni nkon aakun, Ijipt aatiŋ ni. Binib yaa kan bi kan, bi ga li kpa ijawaan la; binib ga lik bi fam, ki li joo baayimbil puuni lir biken pu.

ref: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
text: Maah nan di butɔb, ni nkon, ni iween daa Jerusalem aatiŋ yaab aatafal pu na, kina le m ga daa binib bi mɔmɔk koo Ijipt ni na aatafal.

ref: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
text: Juda aanib bi gur ki dan nan koo Ijipt ponn ni na ubaa aan san ŋmar ki kan limɔfal. Bi ponn ni ubaa aan ki gir ni Juda, nin chee bi ga ki li gee ke bi nan ki li koo na. Ubaa aan ki gir ni, see bikusam siib kina le ga gir ni.”

ref: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
text: Le bijab bi nyi ke bipuutiib toor kitork tii ŋiwaa na, ni bipiib bi mɔmɔk nan si nima chee na, ki di kpee Israel yaab bi koo Ijipt aaŋangii wɔb ki nan ye kinipaak sakpeŋ na, mɔmɔk bui mi ke,

ref: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
text: “Taan kii saah di Uwumbɔr aayimbil tuk timi tibɔr ti na.

ref: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
text: Ti ga ŋa tiwan ni mɔmɔk ti bui ke ti ŋa na. Ti ga toor kitork tii timi aawaapii, u ye Paacham Aapiibɔr na, ki ga tii u ndaan aapiin, ke timi, ni tiyaajatiib, ni timi aabɔr, ni timi aasalolm aah nan ŋani pu Juda aatim ni, ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni pu na. N‑yoonn ngbaan ti nan kpa tijikaar sakpen, ki nan kpa liwangol, kaa kpa tibɔr tibaa.

ref: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
text: Tɔ, n‑yoonn mu ti di cha kaa ki toor kitork tii Paacham Aapiibɔr kaa ki tii u ndaan aapiin na, taa ki kpa nibaa, le timi aanib kpoi butɔb ni nkon ni.”

ref: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
text: Le bipiib ngbaan ki len ke, “Taah nan ken maab naŋni Paacham Aapiibɔr, ki toor kitork tii u, ki tii u ndaan aapiin na, tichatiib nan kii tii taah ŋani pu na ke ni ŋan.”

ref: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
text: “Ni dak ke nimi, ni niyaajatiib, ni nimi aabɔrb, ni nimi aasalolm, ni kitiŋ ngbaan pu aanib aah nan toor kitork ki tii ŋiwaa, Juda aatim ni, ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni na, Uwumbɔr aa nyi ti pu, bee u suln ti pu la aa?

ref: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
text: Din wee na, nimi aatiŋ dɔ nkuun, le ubaa aa bi ki pu. Binib gur san ki ijawaan la, le Uwumbɔr aah kaa nan ki ŋmaa gaa nimi aabiin ni titunwanbir pu na, le binib gur joo kaayimbil puuni lir biken pu.

ref: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
text: Naah kaa joo Uwumbɔr aakaal ki tun u titunwanbir, ki toor kitork tii ŋiwaa pu na le cha tibɔbir timina dan ni pu.”

ref: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
text: M nan bui binib ngbaan mɔmɔk, ki moo sak bipiib ngbaan, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, aah bi tuk Juda aanib bi koo Ijipt aatiŋ ni na ke, “Nimi ni nipuutiib mɔmɔk puu tipuukpaan tii Paacham Aapiibɔr. Ni nan puu ke ni ga li toor kitork tii u, ki tii u ndaan aapiin, le ki joo naah puu tipuur ti na. Tɔ, ni ŋan. Li joo nimi aapuur man. Tun naah puu pu na man.

ref: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
text: Tɔ, li pel man tipuur ti min Uwumbɔr di maayimbikpaan puu tii nimi Israel yaab bi mɔmɔk koo Ijipt aatiŋ ni na. Maan ki cha ni ponn ni ubaa puu tipuur maayimbil pu ke, ‘M puu Uwumbɔr u bi kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na pu.’

ref: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
text: Maan ki cha ni ponn ni ubaa kan nkam, le ki tee kuln nimi. Ni mɔmɔk ga kpoi, ni ga kpoi butɔb ni, ni iween ni, ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu ubaa aan gur na.

ref: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
text: Tɔ, siib ga nya nkun ni ki gir nya Ijipt ni ki kun ni Juda aatiŋ pu. Binib bi ga ŋmar na ga bee ke min ni biken na, ulau aamɔbon gbiin.

ref: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
text: Min Uwumbɔr ga tii nimi limɔkl ke m ga daa nitafal do, ki ki mɔk ke maah puu ke m ga cha tibɔbir ti dan ni pu na ga gbiin kina.

ref: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
text: M ga di Ijipt Aabɔr Hofra tii waadim bi ban ke bi ku u na, ke maah di Juda Aabɔr Sedekia tii waadin Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar u nan ban ke u ku u pu na la.”

ref: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
text: Josia aajapɔɔn Jehoyakim aah nan ye Juda aabɔr pu na aabinanar ponn ni, le Baruk nan ŋmee maah nan ŋeer tibɔr ti tuk u na bil.

ref: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
text: Le m bui u ke Uwumbɔr, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na bui ke,

ref: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
text: “Baruk, aa bi len ke, ‘M di cha a. Uwumbɔr moo di mpombiin le kpee maabɔr pu. Maah dɔ ŋuuni pu na yɔl nwon a, le maa ŋmaa kan lifuur libaa.’

ref: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
text: “Le min Uwumbɔr bi gbaa wiil maah nan maa ni na, le ki ŋɔi maah nan bun ni na mu. M ga ŋa kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk kina la.

ref: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Aa bi ban ke m ŋa si tiwankpaan la aa? Taa ban kina. M ban m cha tibɔbir dan unibɔn mɔmɔk pu la, le aa ma ga ŋmar nin chee mɔk aa ga li bi na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
text: U nan di Ijipt aatimbol aabɔr le loln nsan. U nan len Ijipt Aabɔr Neko aajab bi Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar nan nyaŋ bi Kakemis aatiŋ ki bi gbɔk Yufrates Aamɔɔl na aabɔr. Ni nan ye Juda aabɔr Jehoyakim aanaan aayoonn aabinanar ni la. U nan len ke,

ref: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
text: “Ijipt aajab aaninkpiib nan tar ke, ‘Ban nimi aajaak aapeln man ki nya buen butɔb ni.

ref: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
text: Di itangar poo nimi aataan man ki diŋ i pu. Lul sil man, ki di nimi aajaak aayikpupur chiŋ. Luun nimi aakpaatunn man. Di nimi aajaak aabɔkul peen man.’”

ref: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
text: Bijab bi ŋmaa san mala na aan ŋmar; bijab ngbaan aan ŋmaa san ŋmar. Ŋŋangan wɔb, Yufrates Aamɔɔl chee, le bi gbeer ki lir.

ref: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
text: Ŋma ye ki fii paacham kina ke Nail aamɔɔl na, ki naahn ke limɔɔl le aah nyan nwam na.

ref: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
text: Ijipt yaab le fii ke Nail Aamɔɔl na, ki naahn limɔɔl le aah nyan nwam na. Ijipt yaab nan bui ke, ‘Ti ga fii ki biin dulnyaa pu; ti ga kuln ntim, ni binib bi koo mu ponn ni na.

ref: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
text: Cha itaan ngbaan siir man ki cha itaan aatɔroku mam li san mala mala. Cha bijab ngbaan li cha man. Cha bijab bi joo kijaak aapeln ki nyan ni Kus ni Libia na, ni Lidia aajab bi ŋmaa too sakpen na li cha.’”

ref: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
text: Din wee le ye Tidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aawiin, din le u ga teen waadim; din le u ga daa waadim aatafal. Waajaak aajuk ga geei bi ki ti bab, le ki nyu baasin ki ti gbii. Din wee le Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ga di waadim toor kitork ŋŋangan wɔb, Yufrates aamɔɔl chee.

ref: Egypt, no medicine can heal you, not even the soothing lotion from Gilead.
text: Ijipt aanib, li cha man Gilead aatiŋ ni ki ti ban inyɔk. Nimi aanyɔk mɔmɔk ye fam la; nibaa aan ŋmaa tii nimi laafee.

ref: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
text: Ŋitimbol ŋun nimi aanimɔɔn ngbaan pu; unii mɔmɔk ŋun naah wii pu na. Uja ubaa gbeer uken, le bi mɔmɔk lir kitiŋ. Nebukadnesar aah choo pu na

ref: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
text: “Moon Ijipt aatim ni, moon Migdol ni, ni Memfis ni, ni Tapanes ni ke, ‘Gor ki kiir nibaa man; naah kpa tiwan ni mɔmɔk na ga bii butɔb ni.

ref: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
text: Ni ŋa kinye aan nimi aawaasakpeln Apis lir? Uwumbɔr le faa li lii.’

ref: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
