text: Nimi aajab gbeer le ki lir; le bimɔk len tɔb chee ke, ‘Ŋa mala, cha ti gir kun tido aanib chee ki ŋmar timi aadim aajaak aajum chee.’

ref: Give the king of Egypt this new name, “Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
text: Tii Ijipt aabɔr liyimbipɔln ke, ‘Kipupukdaan u kpa kifuuk ki bii waasan na.’

ref: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
text: Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le ye ubɔr. Min le ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na. Unii u ga tak si na ga li kpa mpɔɔn ke Tabor Aajool aah paa jer ŋijoo mɔmɔk pu, ki mu ga li kpa mpɔɔn ke Kamel Aajool aah paa jer nnyusakpem pu na la.

ref: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
text: Nimi Ijipt yaab gor nibaa pu aan bi di nimi buen tinaagbiir ni. Memfis aatiŋ ga kpaln nteersakpiin, mu ga li ye nkuun aan ubaa aa koo nima na la.

ref: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
text: Ijipt aatiŋ bi ke unaanyaan u kinaagangaŋ ki nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb na bi juuni u na la.

ref: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
text: Ijipt aajab san, le baadim aajab aah choo na, bi fuuni ke iwaa na. Bi nan di nchɔkm le tak ki ke bijab aah bi gaar isui

ref: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
text: ki bii kichook ki kpa isui sakpen na. Saan ŋmaa kahn baajab; baajab wiir jer itoon.

ref: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
text: Bi jinn Ijipt aanib inimɔɔn; ŋŋangan wɔb aanib le nyaŋ bi. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na len ke, “M ga daa Tebes aawaal Amonn, ni Ijipt aatiŋ, ni kaawaa, ni kaabɔrb aatafal. M ga yoor Ijipt aabɔr ni binib bi mɔmɔk di naadii tii u na,

ref: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
text: ki di bi tii binib bi ban ke bi ku bi na; m ga di bi tii Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar ni waajab. Le puwɔb na, binib ga nan ki li koo Ijipt aatiŋ ponn ni ke n‑yaayoonn na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Uwumbɔr aah ga gaa waanib lii pu na

ref: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
text: “Maanib, taa san ijawaan man, Israel aanib, taa cha ijawaan chuu nimi. M ga nyan ni nimi dandar aatiŋ pu, m ga nyan ni nimi kitiŋ ki pu ni ye binaagbiib na. Ni ga gir kun ni, ki nan li bi nsuudoon ni; ni ga kan lifuur, le ubaa aan faan nimi.

ref: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: M ga dan ki nan gaa nimi lii. M ga kuln ŋitimbol ŋi mɔmɔk m cha ni yaa ki bi ŋi ponn ni na, le kaa kuln nimi ma. M ga daa nitafal; tɔ, m yaa daa nitafal kan, m ga daa ki ŋeer la. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
text: Waahr aan Ijipt aabɔr nin tak Gasa aatiŋ na, Uwumbɔr nan len Filistia yaab aabɔr m chee.

ref: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
text: Bi ga ŋun itaan aataagbendun pu, ki ŋun itaan aatɔroku aawiil pu, ki ŋun baafambann aah weeni pu na. Tetiib aan fenn ban baabim; biwon ga yɔl, le biŋaal gur jɔn kaakaan.

ref: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
text: N‑yoonn fuu ni ke Filistia kuln, n‑yoonn fuu ni ke ki taa ki kan Taya ni Saidonn aaterm mu gur na. Min Uwumbɔr le ga kuln Filistia yaab, bi mɔmɔk nyan ni Krete aanyun aagbaan ni na.

ref: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
text: Mpombiin sakpiin fuu ni Gasa aanib chee a, le Askelonn aanib ŋmin chii. Filistia yaab bi gur na ga wii ikpowiil ti saa bayoonn?

ref: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
text: Ni wii ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aajaak aajuk, saan di cha timi ii? Gir koo saajufuuk ni, ki ti li bi nima ki fuur.’

ref: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
text: Tɔ, maah tii ki lituln li na aah kaa doo na, ki ga ŋa kinye aan ki fuur? Tɔ, m bui ki ke ki tak Askelonn ni binib bi koo nnyusakpem aagbaan na la.”

ref: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aah nan len Moab yaab aabɔr ti na sɔ: “Nebo aanib aatiŋ kuln a, san bi kinimbaak man. Bi nyaŋ Kiriataim aatiŋ a, bi wii kaadir ti pɔɔ ki fɔk na, le kaanib jin inimɔɔn.

ref: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
text: Moab aanyaan doo a. Bidim nyaŋ Hesbonn yaab a, le ki kpokl ke bi ti tak Moab aatimbol. Madmenn aatiŋ ponn ni ga ŋmin chii; bijab ga tak ki.

ref: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
text: Moab aatiŋ kuln a; li pel mbim aah wii pu na.

ref: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
text: Li pel Luhif aasan pu, baah fai pu na ki li pel Horonaim aasan pu nsuugar aawiil.

ref: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
text: Bi len le ke, ‘Mala, li san ban nimi aamɔfal man. Li san man ke nteersakpiin pu aabon u bi timoor ni na.’

ref: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
text: Moab aatiŋ, aa nan mak saapɔɔn ni saawangol pu la, le dandana ma kan, aa ga lir; bi ga yoor saawaal Kemos ni laawaadabim, ni laatotoorb ki di buen.

ref: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
text: Kitiŋ kibaa aan nya libiil ngbaan ni; tifatann, ni ni kaa ye tifatann na ga bii. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
text: Ban likaakul aatakpal bil Moab aatiŋ man; ki ga kuln dandana. Kaatim ga kpaln tilangbenn la, le ubaa aan ki li koo nima.”

ref: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
text: Puun lii unii u kaa joo usui mɔmɔk tun Uwumbɔr aatuln na. Puun lii unii u kaa joo kijaak aajuk gaar ki ku na pu na. Baah kuln Moab aatim pu na

ref: But now, I will send enemies to pour out the wine and smash the jars!
text: “Tɔ, n‑yoonn choo le m ga tun binib bi ti kpenn Moab ke ndaan na. Bi ga kpenn kaadabuu ki wii ŋi yuk yuk.

ref: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
text: Le Moab yaab ga lik baawaal Kemos fam, ke Israel yaab aah nan lik liwaal Betel, li bi nan di naadii tii li na fam pu na.

ref: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
text: Moab aajab, ba ŋa ni bui ke ni ye bijab, le ki kaar butɔb ni?

ref: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
text: Moab ni kaatim kuln a; kaanachipɔm bi ŋan sakpen na kpo a. Min le ye ubɔr, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le ki len kina.

ref: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
text: Moab aadoon peeni a; kaadoon ga fuu ni dandana.

ref: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
text: Nimi bi bi gbɔk litimbol ngbaan, ki nyi laah kpa liyimbil pu na, li wii ki pu man. Bui man ke, ‘Laapɔɔn mu li joo lik laanib na bii doo a; le laayimbil ni mpɔɔn aa ki bi.’

ref: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
text: Nimi bi koo Dibonn aatiŋ ni na, sunn ni kinyuŋ aakakaa chee ki nan kal kitiŋ, titan ni man; unii u ban u bii Moab na fuu ni a, le ki ber kaadir ti fɔk ki pɔɔ ki kpa tijawan na lii.

ref: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
text: Nimi bi koo Aroer aatiŋ ni na, li si kii isan chee man; baa binib bi san na, ki bee tiwan ni ŋa na.

ref: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
text: Bi ga gar ke, ‘Moab aatiŋ lir a, ki jin inimɔɔn a; li wii ki pu man. Moon Anonn Aamɔɔgban ke Moab aatiŋ ber a.’

ref: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
text: “Libɔjil fuu ni ŋijoo ŋi aapaacham bi taar na aatim pu: li fuu ni Holonn, ni Jasa, ni Mefaf,

ref: Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
text: ni Kiriataim, ni Bef‑gamul, ni Bef‑meonn,

ref: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
text: Moab aapɔɔn bii a; kaapɔɔn kuln a. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Baah ga sunn Moab taab pu na

ref: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Moab aatiŋ aah nyan mpuwɔb pu na, cha ki gbii ndaan. Moab aatiŋ ga biln kibaa aawuln ponn ni la, le binib ga laa.

ref: You made fun of my people and treated them like criminals caught in the act.
text: Moab, teer saah nan yuul Israel aanib pu na. Aa nan ŋani bi ke baah ye binaayukb le bi chuu bi na.

ref: But I also know bragging will never save you.
text: Min Uwumbɔr nyi baagaak bɔr. Baapupuk ye fam la, le baah tun ŋitun ŋi na aan yunn.

ref: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
text: Kina pu le m ga wii Moab aatiŋ, ni Kir Heres aatiŋ aanib mɔmɔk pu.

ref: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
text: M ga wii Sibma aanib pu, ki jer maah ga wii Jaser aanib pu pu na. Sibma aatiŋ, aa bi ke ŋisubil aasub bu aabon taln ki ti puur N‑yaan Aanyusakpem ki ti saa Jaser na la. Le saasubil ŋi puir na bii a.

ref: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
text: Mmɔɔn ni mpopiin doo Moab aatiŋ ki kpa tijikaar sakpen na pu. M cha ndaan doo baah ŋaa ndaan nin chee na; ubaa aa ki bi ke u ŋaa ndaan ki faa mpopiin aafuuk.

ref: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
text: “Hesbonn ni Eleale aanib wii la, le baawiil di ti fuu Jahas aatiŋ ni; Soar aanib ŋun i pu la; le Horonaim, ni Eglaf Selisiya aanib mu ti ŋun i pu. Hali Nimrim aabukpiik na aanyun foor a.

ref: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Maan ki cha Moab aanib see kitork mmii ni, baah dooni baawaa nin chee na, ki taa ki toor kitork tii ŋi. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
text: “Kina pu le m wii Moab, ni Kir Heres aanib pu, ke unii u joo kulufeeŋ gaa ikpolahn na, ba pu? bi lann baawangol mɔmɔk a.

ref: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
text: Moab bii doo a. Li wii man. Moab jin inimɔɔn a. Ki ber doo, le ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln ki na yuul ki. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Moab aan san ŋmar

ref: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
text: Uwumbɔr puu ke litimbol ga boon ni nan pee Moab ke likaagiil na,

ref: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
text: le ki nyaŋ kaatim, ni ntim mu bi maa ŋigon gob mu na. Liyaadaal ngbaan kan, Moab aajab ga san ijawaan ke imalween aah joo upii u na.

ref: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
text: Moab aatiŋ aah yii mi pu na, ki ga kuln kaan ki li ye litimbol.

ref: Terror, pits, and traps are waiting for you.
text: Ijawaan, ni ŋibugen, ni gaawɔb mam le dɔ kii Moab aanib. Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Uwumbɔr aah siin n‑yoonn mu ke u kuln Moab na, unii umɔk pɔɔn ubaa ke u san ŋmar ijawaan chee na ga lir ŋibugen ni, le umɔk baar nyan ŋibugen ni na, gaawɔb mam le ga chuu u.

ref: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
text: Bikusam bi kaa kpa nterm na pɔɔni bibaa ke bi ti kan nterm Hesbonn aatiŋ ki Ubɔr Sihonn nan joo ki na ni, tɔ, ki mu gaa mmii a. Mmii wun Moab aanib bi gee butɔb sakpen na aanaanmɔk ni kaajoo paab.

ref: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
text: San Moab aanib kinimbaak man. Binib bi nan dii liwaal Kemos na kuln a, le bi chur bijapɔtiib ni bibisatiib buen tinaagbiir ni.

ref: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: N‑yoonn mu choo na, Uwumbɔr ga nan ki tii Moab nkam. Uwumbɔr aah len ke tiwan ni mɔmɔk ga ŋa Moab aatiŋ na le na.

ref: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
text: Uwumbɔr aah nan len Amonn aatiŋ aabɔr ti na sɔ: “Israel aajab bi la chee? Ubaa aa bi ki kiir baatiŋ aa? Ba ŋa bi cha Amonn aanib bi dii liwaal Milkom na gaa Gad aanibol aapepel ki kal nima?

ref: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
text: Tɔ, n‑yoonn choo, le m ga cha Amonn aatiyil Raba aanib ŋun butɔb aafuuk pu, le ki gur tilangbenn, kaatiwaatiir wu mmii. Le Israel yaab ga ki gaa baatiŋ ki bi nan gaa ki na bi chee.

ref: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
text: Hesbonn aanib, li wii man. Ai aatiŋ kuln a. Raba aapiib, li wii ikpowiil man. Di tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na ki di peen ki li wii. Li san gonni man. Bi ga yoor nimi aawaal Milkom buen tinaagbiir ni, ki kpaan yoor laatotoorb ni laawaadabim mu.

ref: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
text: Ba ŋa nimi binib bi kaa dii Uwumbɔr na kpa kipupuk? Nimi aapɔɔn bi door la. Ba ŋa ni kpa nibaa aapɔɔn pu naadii ki len ke ubaa aan kaa ki tak nimi?

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
text: M ga cha ijawaan nya ŋipepel mɔmɔk ki chuu nimi. Ni mɔmɔk ga san. Unii mɔk ga li san ban ubaa la, le ubaa aan li bi ki ki kuun nimi aajab.

ref: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
text: “Tɔ, m ga nan ki cha Amonn aanib kan nkam. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Uwumbɔr aah ga ji Edom aatiŋ tibɔr pu na

ref: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
text: Dedann aanib, fenn ki li san man. Bɔr man. M ban m kuln Esɔ aayaabitiib la, ba pu? n‑yoonn le fuu ni ke m daa bitafal.

ref: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
text: Binib yaa ker ŋisubil kan, ŋibaa gur la; binaayukb mu yaa dan kinyeek kan, bi yoor tiwan ni bi ban na baanja la.

ref: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
text: Le m ma per Esɔ aayaabitiib pel pel ki per woln baabɔbɔryaan chee, ke bi taa ki ŋmaa bɔr. Edom aanib mɔmɔk kuln a. Bi ponn ni ubaa aa gur.

ref: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
text: Di nimi aakpobim tii mi man, le m ga li kpiini bi. M ga ŋmaa joo nimi aakpopiib mu.

ref: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
text: “Hali binib bi kaa ba ye ke m daa bitafal na yaa ti nyun ntafadaan aayikuuk ni kan, ni dak ke nimi le aan kan ntafadaan aa? Mbamɔn ni ga nyu kiyikuuk ngbaan ponn ni.

ref: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
text: Min mbaa le puu ke Bosra aatiŋ ga kpaln ijawaan aawan ni nteersakpiin; binib ga li yuul ki, le ki joo kaayimbil puuni lir biken pu. Ntimbim mu bi gbɔk ki na ga kpaln tilangbenn ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
text: Le m bui ke, “Edom aatiŋ, Uwumbɔr le di inaŋ tii ni mi. U tun ni ntuun ke mu nan bui ŋitimbol ke ŋi kuun ŋaajab, ki gor, ki ti tak si.

ref: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha aa taa ki li kpa mpɔɔn, le ubaa aan ki li pak si.

ref: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
text: Saagaak le ŋmann si. Ubaa aa san si ke saah dak ke bi san si pu na. Aa bi ŋijootakpal paab la, ki bi ŋijoo aapaachapaacham; tɔ, aa koo paachapaacham ke likaagiil na la, Uwumbɔr mu tee ga sunn si taab. Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: People passing by your country will be shocked and horrified to see a disaster
text: Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “Tibɔbir ti ga dan Edom pu na ga li kpa ijawaan sakpen le unii umɔk jer nima na ga san ijawaan ki jek.

ref: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
text: Tiwan ni nan ŋa Sodom ni Gomora aatim aan mu ni ntim mu nan bi gbɔk mu na kuln na, kina le ga ŋa Edom aatiŋ mu. Ubaa aan ki koo nima kpala. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
text: M ga dan ki nan cha Edom yaab san libuul ni ki nya baatiŋ ni, ke uchinn le aah nyan ni kichook ni ki di bɔ dii Jɔɔdann aagbaan pu ki nan nya timosɔnn ni pu na la, le maah lee usaloln u na ga li joo litimbol ngbaan. M ni ubaa aa ŋak. Ubaa aan ŋmaa kpak mi. Utinjoor ubaa aan ŋmaa kpak mi.

ref: Listen to my plans for you, people of Edom. Your children will be dragged off and your country destroyed.
text: Kina pu na, li pel maah kpokl Edom aanib pu nkpokl mu na, ni maah ban ke m ŋa Temann aatiŋ aanib pu na. Bi ga kpaan dar baabim mu buen, le kina chuu unii mɔmɔk ijawaan.

ref: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
text: Edom yaa nan lir kan, kifuuk ki ga nya na ga cha kitiŋ dam, le kaalirm aawiil ga ti fuu Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem chee.

ref: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
text: Bidim ga boon ni ke likaagiil na le ki nan tak Bosra aatiŋ. Liyaadaal ngbaan kan, Edom aajab ga san ijawaan ke upii u imalween joo u na la.” Uwumbɔr aah ga ji Damaskus aatiŋ tibɔr pu na

ref: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
text: Uwumbɔr aah nan len Damaskus aatiŋ aabɔr ti na sɔ: “Hamaf ni Apad aatim aanib aah ŋun tibɔbir ti na pu le ni tii bi ilandak ki muk bi. Ijawaan gbiin bi ki ti puu kpir ke nnyusakpem na la, le baa ŋmaa fuur.

ref: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
text: Damaskus aanib aawon yɔl le ijawaan cha bi san. Iween ni falaa joo bi ke imalween aah joo upii pu na la.

ref: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
text: Kitisakpeŋ ki ponn ni nan kpa mpopiin na gur dɔ nkuun la.

ref: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
text: Liyaadaal ngbaan kan, bi ga ku kaanachipɔm ki ponn ni, le kaajab mɔmɔk ga doo.

ref: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
text: M ga see Damaskus aatiŋ aagon mmii, ki see Ubɔr Ben‑Hadad aabɔrdichal lii. Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.” Uwumbɔr aah ga ji Kedar aanibol ni Hasor aatiŋ tibɔr pu na

ref: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
text: Uwumbɔr aah nan len Kedar aanibol, ni Hasor aah nan joo ŋipepel ŋi, aan Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar nan nyaŋ, ki gaa ŋi na aabɔr ti na sɔ: “Tak Kedar aanib ki kuln liwipuul wɔb aanibol ngbaan.

ref: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
text: “Hasor aanib, min Uwumbɔr le sur nimi ke ni san buen dandar ki ti bɔr. Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar kpokl ni pu a; waah len pu na sɔ:

ref: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
text: ‘Dan man. Ti ga tak binib bi dak ke bi ŋmar, nibaa aan ŋa bi na. Baatiŋ aa kpa ibisamɔi i laŋni na, le ubaa aa kii ki.’

ref: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
text: “Chur baalaakumii tiib ni tiwakor man. M ga cha binib bi chee biyigbeer pu aayikpir na yaa ni kookoo, ki ga cha tibɔbir nya ni ni kookoo ki nan pii bi.

ref: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
text: U nan bui ke, “M ga ku bijab bi too itɔi ki cha Elam aatiŋ kan mpɔɔnsakpiin na mɔmɔk.

ref: Enemies will attack from all directions, and you will be led captive to every nation on earth.
text: M ga cha libuln nya ni ŋipepel mɔmɔk ki nan daa Elam pu, m ga cha kaanib yaa buen ni kookoo, ki ti saa buyoonn kaakusam ga li bi kitiŋ mɔmɔk ni na.

ref: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: M ga ku baabɔrb ni baasalolm, le ki di maabɔrjal siin nima.

ref: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
text: Puwɔb na, m ga nan ki cha Elam aanib kan nkam. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
text: Uwumbɔr aah nan di Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni kaanib aabɔr ti tuk mi na sɔ:

ref: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
text: “Bui ŋitimbol tibɔchann ngbaan. Moon ti. Tii limɔkl ki moon tibɔchann ngbaan. Taa di ti bɔr. Babiloŋ lir a. Kaawaal li bi yin li ke Maduk na wii yuk yuk a. Babiloŋ aawaa jin inimɔɔn a, kaawaa ŋi sukr ponn ni na wiil a.

ref: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
text: “Litimbol li nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb na dan ke li nan tak Babiloŋ, le ki ga ŋa ki nteersakpiin. Binib ni tiwakor ga san, le ubaa aan ki li koo nima.” Israel yaab aah ga gir ni pu na

ref: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui ke, “N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, Israel ni Juda aanib mɔmɔk ga wii ban mi, Baawumbɔr.

ref: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
text: Bi ga baa Sionn aasan pu le ki di toŋ nima wɔb. Bi ga puu tipuukpaan ti kaa kpa ndoon na tii mi, kaan bii ti.

ref: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
text: “Maanib bi ke ipiih i aapihkpaal cha i wɔŋ ŋijoo ponn ni na la. Bi chuun yenni ki nya lijool libaa paab ki ti saa liken paab, le ki suln bido aah ye nin wɔb na.

ref: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
text: Unii umɔk kan bi na kan, u tak bi la. Baadim len le ke, ‘Bi tun Uwumbɔr le titunwanbir, kina pu na, taah ŋa bi pu na aa bir. Biyaajatiib nan kii tii Uwumbɔr, bi mu ba ga li bi u chee kina.’

ref: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
text: “Israel aanib, san nya Babiloŋ ni man. Nya kitiŋ ngbaan ni man. Li ye njan aanib bi ga puen nya na man.

ref: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
text: M ban m ti saa ŋitimbol ŋibaa ŋŋangan wɔb le ki cha ŋi ti tak Babiloŋ. Bi ga lul butɔb ki nyaŋ Babiloŋ. Bi ye bikpam bi nyi kikpaŋ aabɔr na la, bi yaa too ipiin kan, baa lanni.

ref: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
text: Bi ga gaa Babiloŋ aawangol, le binib bi ga gaa li na ga yoor tiwan ni mɔmɔk bi gee na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Babiloŋ aatiŋ aah lir pu na

ref: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “Babiloŋ aanib, ni nan gaa maatimbol aawangol butɔb ni. Ni kpa mpopiin le ki mɔɔni, le ki chuun ke unaa u bi taa gbaar ŋikalmaan, ni utaan u bi wii na,

ref: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
text: le saatikpaan na ga ji inimɔɔn ki kpaln tilaar aawan. Babiloŋ le ga li gur ye kitiŋ ki kaa kpa liyimbil ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ni na: ki ga kpaln nteersakpiin mu kuun kaa kpa nnyun na.

ref: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
text: Maaŋuul pu le ubaa aan ki li koo Babiloŋ ni; ki ga gur tilangbenn la, le unii umɔk jer nima na, ni ga ŋa u lijinjiir ni iwaan.

ref: Babylon has rebelled against me. Archers, take your places. Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
text: “Bitɔndam, lul goln Babiloŋ butɔb man. Too Babiloŋ nimi aapiin mɔmɔk, ba pu? ki tun min Uwumbɔr titunwanbir.

ref: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
text: Faa butɔb aakuun ki mann Babiloŋ aatiŋ. Babiloŋ aatiŋ di kibaa tii a. Bidim wiil kaagon ki koo ki ponn ni a. M bi teeni Babiloŋ la. Kina pu na, ni mu teen bi, ki ŋa bi ke baah nan ŋa biken pu na.

ref: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
text: Taa cha bi bu lijikaabil, ki taa chee lijikaabol, kitiŋ ngbaan ni. Uchaan umɔk bi ki ponn ni na ga san bidim aah bi tak ki pu na ijawaan, le ki gir kun.” Israel yaab aah ga gir ni pu na

ref: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
text: Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Israel aanib bi ke ipiih i ichinn jenn yaa i na la. Njan na, Asiria aabɔrkpaan le nan puen tak bi, le Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar nan nyir baakpab.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
text: Nima pu le min, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, ga daa Ubɔr Nebukadnesar ni waatiŋ aatafal, ke maah nan daa Asiria aabɔrkpaan aatafal pu na.

ref: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
text: M ga giin Israel aanib baatiŋ pu. Bi ga ji tijikaar ti bi bun Kamel Aajool pu, ni Basann aapepel ni na, le ki ga ji tijikaar ti mɔmɔk bi ban na, Efraim ni Gilead aapepel ni.

ref: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, titunwanbir tibaa aan ki li bi Israel ni, le mbiin mu aan ki li bi Juda ni, ba pu? m ga di cha pinn binib bi m cha bi ŋmar na. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Uwumbɔr aah ga ji Babiloŋ aatiŋ tibɔr pu na

ref: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “Tak Merataim ni Pekod aatim aanib man. Ku bi ki kuln bi mɔmɔk. Ŋa man maah bui nimi ke ni ŋa pu na mɔmɔk. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
text: Bi ŋun butɔb aafuuk pu kitiŋ ngbaan pu, le libiil sakpeln bi.

ref: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
text: Babiloŋ nan di ugagaar gbaa wɔi dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk, le ugagaar ngbaan kool doo. Ŋitimbol mɔmɔk yaa kan tiwan ni ŋa kitiŋ ngbaan na kan, ijawaan ga chuu ŋi.

ref: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
text: Babiloŋ, aa nan jan mi kijaak, le maah nan di gaawɔb u pen si aan saa nyi u bɔr na chuu si.

ref: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
text: M chuu piir maajawan aah bi nin chee na, le maaŋuul ponn ni m yoor ti, ba pu? min Dindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan kpa lituln Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni m tun.

ref: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
text: Tak ki ŋipepel mɔmɔk. Kuun naah gaa kaawangol li na paan tɔb pu ke njikaabim na. Kuln kitiŋ ngbaan man. Taa di cha tiwan nibaa kina.

ref: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
text: Ku baajab mɔmɔk. Kɔr bi man. Babiloŋ aanib aadoon fuu ni a. Baatafadaan aayoonn fuu ni a.”

ref: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
text: Tɔ, bikusam nan san nyan ni Babiloŋ ki dan Jerusalem, ki nan len Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah teen Babiloŋ yaab baah nan tun Waadichal pu pu na.

ref: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
text: “Bui binib bi too itɔi na ke bi tak Babiloŋ aatiŋ. Cha umɔk nyi butɔm ni mpiin aatoom na buen. Gob man kitiŋ ngbaan ki taa cha ubaa ŋmar. Kaah nan di kigaak mɔk min, Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi chain na pu na, teen ki kaah nan tun pu na mɔmɔk, ki ŋa ki ke kaah nan ŋani ntim muken pu na.

ref: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
text: Liyaadaal ngbaan le kaanachipɔm ga kpoi ki ponn ni, le kaajab mɔmɔk ga kuln. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
text: “Babiloŋ, aa kpa kigaak sakpen a, kina pu le min, Dindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan nyan sil aa pu. N‑yoonn fuu ni ke m daa aatafal.

ref: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
text: Saatimbol li kpa kigaak na ga gbeer ki lir, le ubaa aan ter si aa ki fii sil. M ga see saatim mmii, le tiwan nimɔk bi duun mu na ga bii doo.”

ref: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan len ke, “Bi muk Israel ni Juda aanib la. Binib bi mɔmɔk nyaŋ bi, ki chur bi na kii bi gbingbin, kaan cha bi nya biŋaal ni.

ref: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, will rescue and protect them. I will bring peace to their land and trouble to yours.
text: Le u ga gaa bi lii na kpa mpɔɔn, waayimbil le ye Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan. Uma ubaa le ga gaa baabɔr, ki cha nsuudoon dan kitiŋ kee pu, le Babiloŋ aanib ma kpa tibɔbir.”

ref: I have declared war on you, your officials, and advisors.
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “Nkun li bi Babiloŋ aatiŋ aanib, ni kaayidam, ni bilandam pu.

ref: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
text: Nkun li bi bibɔnabr bi ye binyamɔndam na pu, bi ye bijɔrb la. Nkun li bi kaajab pu, ijawaan chuu bi a.

ref: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
text: Kuln kaataan ni yaatɔroku mam. Nkun li bi kaajab bi bi ti pan bi ŋimombil ke bi nan jan tii bi na pu. Baa ki kpa mpɔɔn. Bii kaawangol, gaa ni ki yoor ni mpɔɔn.

ref: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
text: Cha nweel dan kaatiŋ pu, ki foor kaamɔɔ. Babiloŋ ye kitiŋ ki kpa ijawaan aawaa na la, ŋima le ŋmann binib ngbaan.

ref: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
text: Maah nan kuln Sodom ni Gomora aatim, ni ntim mu bi gbɔk mu na pu na, kina le m ga ŋa Babiloŋ mu. Ubaa aan ki koo nima daalbaadaal. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
text: Binib nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb aatiŋ kibaa ni ki choo, ki ye litimbokpaan libaa le ki bi dandar; bibɔrb pam le bi gor kiir butɔb.

ref: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
text: Bi yoor baatɔi ni baajaak aajum; bi kpa mbiin, kaa san kinimbaak. Bi yaa jak baataan kan, yaafuuk naahn nnyusakpem aafuuk la. Bi gor ki ban bi to Babiloŋ butɔb la.

ref: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
text: Babiloŋ aabɔr aah ŋun tibɔr ngbaan na, uwon yɔl le uŋaal gur jɔn kaakaan. Ijawaan sakpiin chuu u, le ki wu ke upii aamalween na.

ref: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
text: “Min Uwumbɔr ga dan ki nan cha Babiloŋ yaab san libuul ni, ki nyan baatiŋ ni, ke uchinn aah nyan ni kichook ni, ki di bɔ dii Jɔɔdann aagbaan pu, ki nan nya timosɔnn ni pu na la. Maah ga lee usaloln u na le ga li joo litimbol ngbaan. M ni ubaa aa ŋak. Ubaa aan kaa ke u kpak mi. Utinjoor ubaa aan ŋmaa kpak mi.

ref: Listen to my plans for you, people of Babylonia. Your children will be dragged off, and your country destroyed.
text: Kina pu na, li pel maah kpokl Babiloŋ aatiŋ pu nkpokl mu na, ni maah ban ke m ŋa kaanib pu na. Bidim ga kpaan dar baabim mu buen, le ni ga chuu unii mɔmɔk ijawaan.

ref: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
text: Babiloŋ yaa nan lir kan, kifuuk ki ga nya na ga cha kitiŋ dam, le ŋitimbol ŋiken ga ŋun kaalirm aawiil.”

ref: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “M ban m cha libuln li bii tiwan na le daa Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni kaanib pu.

ref: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
text: M ga tun ni biwɔwɔm le bi nan bii Babiloŋ ke libuln li daar timoor cha na. Libiil aawiin daal yaa fuu ni kan, bi ga tak ki ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu la, le ki cha ki doon nkuun.

ref: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
text: Taa tii baajab nsan bi too baapiin, ki taa tii bi nsan ke bi peen baajaak aabɔkul. Ku binachipɔm man. Kuln baajab mɔmɔk.

ref: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
text: Bi ga kan titotonn le ki kpoi baatim ponn ni.

ref: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
text: Hali Israel ni Juda yaab aah tun mi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr u bi Chain na titunwanbir na, min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aa yii bi.

ref: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
text: San nya Babiloŋ ni man. Li san ban nibaa man. Taa cha bi ku nimi Babiloŋ aanib aatunwanbir pu. M bi teeni le ki dar bitafal naah ŋeer bi pu na.

ref: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
text: Babiloŋ nan bi ke salmaa aayikuuk na le ŋŋaal ni, ki cha dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk nyun ki ponn ni ki ti gbii. Ŋitimbol nan nyun ki ponn ni aadaan le kaa ki kpa nlan.

ref: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
text: Babiloŋ kpaan lir libuul ngbaan ni le ki kuln. Wii kaakpuul man. Ban nnyɔk ki nan ŋa kaabuun ni, nibaakan, i ga yann.

ref: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
text: Biwɔwɔm bi koo nima na bui ke, ‘Ti nan pɔɔn tibaa ke ti ter Babiloŋ yaab, tɔ, n‑yoonn mu nan jer. Cha ti di cha bi ki gir kun man. Uwumbɔr di waapɔɔn mɔmɔk le daa Babiloŋ aatafal le ki kuln ki kookoo.’”

ref: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
text: Uwumbɔr aah ban u kuln Babiloŋ aatiŋ na, le u ti saa Media aabɔrb. Waah ga leŋ lipɔln Waadichal pu pu na le na. Bijab bi bi tak ki na aayidam teen ke, “Luun nimi aapiin man. Gor nimi aajaak aapen man.

ref: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
text: Kitiŋ ngbaan kpa ŋimɔɔ ni liwangol sakpen, tɔ, kaayoonn mu fuu a, le kaamɔfal doo.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan puu ubaa aamɔfal pu ke u ga cha bijab bi wiir ke itoon na nan tak Babiloŋ, ki ga nyaŋ ki, ki teen mpɔɔn pu. Nlahn mu pak Uwumbɔr na

ref: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
text: Uma le len, le nnyun mu bi kitaapaak na ŋuuni; u cha ntaalangbam nyani kitiŋ aanaanmɔk ki choo. Utaal yaa nu kan, u cha u moor, le ki nyani libuln waah di li siin nin chee na.

ref: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
text: Uwumbɔr di waapɔɔn le naan kitiŋ kee, waalan le u di naan dulnyaa le ki daa taln kitaapaak.

ref: People who make idols are stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods cannot breathe.
text: Unibɔn yaa kan kina kan, le u bee ke u ye ulatiir la, kaa kpa nlan; binib bi naani ŋiwaa ŋi kaa ye nibaa, kaa kpa limɔfal na jin inimɔɔn a.

ref: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
text: Ŋaa kpa tinyoor le ki ŋan ke bi lik seen ŋi; Uwumbɔr yaa nan nyan sil ŋi pu kan, u ga kuln ŋi.

ref: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
text: Uma Uwumbɔr u tiyaaja Jakob nan dii u na aa bi kina; uma le naan tiwan mɔmɔk, le ki lee Israel yaab ke bi li ye uma ubaa aanib. Waayimbil le ye ke Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan. Uwumbɔr aagagaar

ref: Babylonia, you were my hammer; I used you to pound nations and break kingdoms,
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “Babiloŋ, sin le ye maagagaar, sin le ye maajawan ti m joo to butɔb na. M joo sin le wiil ŋitimbol ni nnaan,

ref: But now, my people will watch, while I repay you for what you did to Zion.
text: Uwumbɔr len ke, “Ni ga kan maah ga teen Babiloŋ ni kaanib baah tun Jerusalem titunwanbir ti na mɔmɔk.

ref: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.
text: Babiloŋ, aa naahn lijool li bii dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk na la, le min Uwumbɔr le ye saadin. M ga chuu si, ki ber si bil kitiŋ, ki cha aa kpaln nfatan.

ref: Your stone blocks won't be reused for cornerstones or foundations, and I promise that forever you will be a desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Nations Will Attack Babylon The Lord said:
text: Baan ki di saalangbentakpanjal libaa maa lidichal. Aa ga li gur bi ke nteersakpiin na le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Signal the nations to get ready to attack. Raise a flag and blow a trumpet. Send for the armies of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Choose a commander; let the cavalry attack like a swarm of locusts.
text: “Tii limɔkl ke bi ti tak. Pii ukpiin ki cha ŋitimbol ŋun. Gor ŋitimbol ngbaan ke ŋi ti to Babiloŋ butɔb. Bui Ararat, ni Minni, ni Askenas aanaan ni yaab ke bi ti tak. Ban uninkpel u ga loln bi pu nsan na. Cha itaan dan ke kitoonpaak na.

ref: Tell the kings and governors, the leaders and the people of the kingdoms of the Medes to prepare for war!
text: Gor ŋitimbol ngbaan ke ŋi ti to Babiloŋ butɔb. Tun ti yin ni Media aabɔrb, ni baasalolm, ni baaninkpiib, ni ntim mumɔk bi joo na aajab.

ref: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.
text: Uwumbɔr aah bi tun waatuln ke u ŋa Babiloŋ nteersakpiin, nin chee ubaa aa koo na, le kitiŋ dam ki jii.

ref: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
text: Babiloŋ aajab di cha kijaak le ki gaar baajawan aadir ni. Baa ki kpa lipobil, le ki gur bi ke bipiib na. Bidim gbaa wɔi kitiŋ ngbaan aabisamɔi aajaaleŋ mam, le ki see ŋidichal lii.

ref: One messenger after another announces to the king, “Babylon has been captured!
text: Ituun, ituun le san ti tuk Babiloŋ aabɔr ke bijab diir ŋipepel mɔmɔk le ki koo ni waatiŋ ponn ni.

ref: The enemy now controls the river crossings! The marshes are on fire! Your army has panicked!”
text: Bidim gaa mmɔɔsan a, ki seer tidir ti fɔk ki pɔɔ na mmii lii. Babiloŋ aajab aapobil yuk.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
text: Naan yunn le baadim ga nyaŋ bi ki taa taa bi bil ke baah poi ŋikalmaan lipaal pu pu na. Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan, u ye Israel yaab Aawumbɔr na, le len kina.”

ref: The people of Jerusalem say, “King Nebuchadnezzar made us panic. That monster stuffed himself with us and our treasures, leaving us empty— he gobbled up what he wanted and spit out the rest.
text: Babiloŋ aabɔr nan gii gii Jerusalem le ki di ŋman. U nan chuu kpenn kitiŋ ngbaan chain ke libuul na la; u nan nab ki ke kipeewanbiik aah nae tiwan pu na la. U nan yoor waah gee ni na buen le ki di ni gur na mee.

ref: The people of Babylonia harmed some of us and killed others. Now, Lord, make them pay!” The Lord Will Take Revenge on Babylon
text: Cha Sionn aanib len ke, “Cha bi chuu Babiloŋ taani, taah kan titotonn ti na pu.” Cha Jerusalem aanib len ke, “Cha bi chuu Babiloŋ taani, taah jin falaa u na pu.” Uwumbɔr ga ter Israel yaab

ref: My people, I am on your side, and I will take revenge on Babylon. I will cut off its water supply, and its stream will dry up.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Jerusalem aanib ke, “M ga gaa nimi aabɔr ki cha nimi aadim pa baah ŋa nimi pu na pu. M ga cha Babiloŋ yaab aanyun aah nyan ni nin chee na kuur, ki cha baamɔɔ foor.

ref: Babylon will be a pile of rubble where only jackals live, and everyone will be afraid to walk among the ruins.
text: Kitiŋ ngbaan ga kpaln tilangbenn ti ponn ni ipeel ŋmeen koo na la. Nima chee ga li kpa unii mɔk ijawaan; ubaa aan li koo nima, le ijawaan ga chuu unii umɔk kan kina na.

ref: The Babylonians roar and growl like young lions.
text: Babiloŋ yaab mɔmɔk wii ki ŋuuni ke ichinn ni yaabim na la.

ref: And since they are hungry, I will give them a banquet. They will celebrate, get drunk, then fall asleep, never to wake up!
text: Bi ye bikumɔndam la aa? M ga ŋa njim tii bi ki cha bi nyu ti gbii ki li kpa mpopiin. Bi ga ti doon geen, le kaan ki fii.

ref: I will lead them away to die, like sheep, lambs, and goats being led to the butcher.
text: M ga cha bi kɔr bi ke ipihbi, ni iŋoob, ni ipihja na la. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Babiloŋ aah ga kan tibɔbir ti na

ref: All nations now praise Babylon, but when it is captured, those same nations will be horrified.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki len Babiloŋ aabɔr ke, “Kitiŋ ki dulnyaa mɔmɔk nan pak ki na lir a. Babiloŋ gur ye ijawaan aawan le ŋitimbol chee.

ref: Babylon's enemies will rise like ocean waves and flood the city.
text: Nnyunsakpem di mu aanyunkpenn ti pɔɔ na biin Babiloŋ pu.

ref: Horrible destruction will strike the nearby towns. The land will become a barren desert, where no one can live or even travel.
text: Kaatim gur ye ijawaan aawan la, le ki gur bi ke nteersakpiin mu kaa kpa nnyun na. Ubaa aa koo ki ni kaa chuun nima chee.

ref: I will punish Marduk, the god of Babylon, and make him vomit out everything he gobbled up. Then nations will no longer bring him gifts, and Babylon's walls will crumble. The Lord Offers Hope to His People
text: M ga daa Babiloŋ aawaal Bel aatafal, ki cha li giin laah sun tiwan ni na mɔmɔk; ŋitimbol aan ki li dooni li.

ref: Get out of Babylon, my people, and run for your lives, before I strike the city in my anger!
text: “Babiloŋ aagon lir a. Israel aanib, san nya nima chee man. Li san ban nimi aamɔfal maaŋuusakpeln chee man.

ref: Don't be afraid or lose hope, though year after year there are rumors of leaders fighting for control in the city of Babylon.
text: Taa cha naah ŋun tibɔr ti na yɔl nitaakpab, ki taa san ijawaan. Libiln mɔk aabɔŋunkaan ngbaan bi tibaa la, mbimbin mu pɔɔ na aabɔr, ni ubɔr ubaa ni uken aajaak bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu la.

ref: The time will come when I will punish Babylon's false gods. Everyone there will die, and the whole nation will be disgraced,
text: Kina pu na, n‑yoonn choo, le m ga fii sil Babiloŋ aawaa pu. Kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk ga ji inimɔɔn, le bi ga ku kaanib mɔmɔk.

ref: when an army attacks from the north and brings destruction. Then the earth and the heavens and everything in them will celebrate.
text: Buyoonn Babiloŋ nan koo binib bi ban bi kuln ki na aaŋaal ni na, le taab ni kitaapaak aawan mɔmɔk ga di mpopiin teen mpɔɔn pu.

ref: My people, you escaped death when Jerusalem fell. Now you live far from home, but you should trust me and think about Jerusalem. Leave Babylon! Don't stay!
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui waanib bi bi Babiloŋ ni na ke: “Ni nyan nkun a. Li cha man. Taa ki taan man. Nibaakan, ni ga li dak ke ni daa linampal, li lik min Uwumbɔr pu, ki teer Jerusalem bɔr.

ref: Soon I will send a war to punish Babylon's idols and leave its wounded people moaning everywhere.
text: Kina pu le m bui ke n‑yoonn choo, le m ga fii sil Babiloŋ aawaa pu, le binib bi kan titotonn na ga li ker idun kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk pu.

ref: Although Babylon's walls reach to the sky, the army I send will destroy that city. I, the Lord, have spoken. Babylon Will Be Destroyed The Lord said:
text: Babiloŋ yaa ga ŋmaa jon kitaapaak ki ti maa tidir ti fɔk ki pɔɔ sakpen na kan, m ga sil tun binib bi ti bii ti nima. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Uwumbɔr aah ki ga gir bii Babiloŋ pu kpee na

ref: Listen to the cries for help coming from Babylon. Everywhere in the country the sounds of destruction can be heard.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Li pel man iwiil aafuuk pu Babiloŋ ni, li pel man libiil aakpowiil pu kitiŋ ngbaan pu.

ref: The shouts of the enemy, like crashing ocean waves, will drown out Babylon's cries as I level the city.
text: M ban m bii Babiloŋ la, le ki cha ki ŋmin chii. Bijab berni ke tinyunkpenn na la le ki tar ki tak ki.

ref: An enemy will attack and destroy Babylon. Its soldiers will be captured and their weapons broken, because I am a God who takes revenge against nations for what they do.
text: Bi dan ke bi nan kuln Babiloŋ la; bi nyaŋ kaajab ki chur bi, le ki kool baatɔi. M ye Uwumbɔr u daar unii u tun titunwanbir na aatafal la, le ki ga ŋa Babiloŋ tiwan ni ŋeer ki na.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the true King, promise that the officials and advisors, the governors and leaders, and the soldiers of Babylon will get drunk, fall asleep, and never wake up.
text: M ga cha kaajojoob ni bijab bi kpa nlan, ni bisalolm, ni baajab nyu ki ti gbii. Bi ga ti doon geen le kaan ki fii kpala. Min, Ubɔr ngbaan le len kina, min le ye Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan.

ref: The thick walls of that city will be torn down, and its huge gates burned. Everything that nation worked so hard to gain will go up in smoke. Jeremiah Gives Seraiah a Scroll
text: Babiloŋ, mpɔɔn aatiŋ na aagon lir kitiŋ a, le kaabisamɔi aajaaleŋ mam na gaa mmii. Ŋitimbol aatuln na ye fam la; ŋaapɔɔn mɔmɔk gaa mmii a. Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan na le len kina.” Jeremia aanaŋ aah buen Babiloŋ pu na

ref: During Zedekiah's fourth year as king of Judah, he went to Babylon. And Baruch's brother Seraiah went along as the officer in charge of arranging for places to stay overnight.
text: Ubɔr Sedekia aaninkpel le nan ye Seraya. Seraya aate nan ye Neria, le uyaaja ye Mahseya. Sedekia aah nan ye Juda aabɔr pu na aabinanar ponn ni, le u nan cha Babiloŋ le Seraya dii u. Le m nan di tibɔr tibaa tii u.

ref: Before they left, I wrote on a scroll all the terrible things that would happen to Babylon.
text: M nan ŋmee kigbaŋ ponn ni libiil li mɔmɔk ga dan Babiloŋ pu na, ni Babiloŋ aabɔr tiken.

ref: I gave the scroll to Seraiah and said: When you get to Babylon, read this scroll aloud,
text: M nan bui Seraya ke, “Aa yaa buen Babiloŋ ni kan, aa teer ki karn tiwan ni mɔmɔk bi do na mpɔɔn pu tii binib ngbaan.

ref: then pray, “Our Lord, you promised to destroy this place and make it into a desert where no people or animals will ever live.”
text: Nee aapuwɔb na, mee limeel ke, ‘Uwumbɔr, aa bui ke aa ga bii do, le tiwanfuurkaan, binib ni tiwakor nibaa aan ki li bi ki pu, le ki ga li bi ke nteersakpiin na ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.’

ref: When you finish praying, tie the scroll to a rock and throw it in the Euphrates River. Then say,
text: Seraya, aa yaa ti karn kigbaŋ kee doo kan, aa di ki gbin litakpal pu ki di li mee ŋa Yufrates Aamɔɔl ni,

ref: “This is how Babylon will sink when the Lord destroys it. Everyone in the city will die, and it won't have the strength to rise again.” The End of Jeremiah's Writing Jeremiah's writing ends here.
text: ki bui ke, ‘Kina le bi ga ŋa Babiloŋ, Uwumbɔr aah ban u joo ni libiil li ki pu na, ki ga muin, kaan ki puur ni kpala.’” Jeremia aamɔbon nan doo do la.

ref: then his eyes were poked out. He was put in chains, then dragged off to Babylon and kept in prison until he died.
text: Nee aapuwɔb, le u cha bi chuu lokr Sedekia aanimbil, le ki di tikululn gbin u ki di u buen Babiloŋ ni. Sedekia nan gaar kiyondiik ni Babiloŋ ni le ki ti saa nwiin mundaal u kpo na. Baah nan ber Uwumbɔr Aadichal pu na (

ref: meters around. They were hollow, but the bronze was about
text: ki ti saa Sedekia aanaan aabin kipiik ni libaa ni.

ref: After a year and a half, all the food in Jerusalem was gone. Then on the ninth day of the fourth month,
text: Libiln ngbaan aaŋmanaa aawiin iwae daal, buyoonn nkon nan moo nyaŋ aan tijikaar tibaa aa ki gur binib ji na,

ref: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the Jordan River valley,
text: le Babiloŋ aajab nan wiil kaagon ki koo ni, le ki gob kitiŋ ngbaan ti to, le kitiŋ ngbaan aajab nan loon kinyeek ki nyan. Bi nan dii libɔrdichal aasaak aasan, le ki dii mbisamɔb mu bi ŋigon ŋilee ngbaan aasisik ni na nyan, ki di toŋ Jɔɔdann Aafataŋ wɔb.

ref: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
text: Bi nan di Sedekia buen Ubɔr Nebukadnesar u nan bi Ribla aatiŋ ki bi Hamaf aapepel ni na chee, nima chee le Nebukadnesar nan ti jin u tibɔr ki siin baah ga ŋa u pu na.

ref: Zedekiah's sons and the officials of Judah were killed while he watched,
text: Ribla aatiŋ ni, nima chee, le u nan ku Sedekia aajapɔtiib unimbil ni, le ki ku Juda aaninkpiib mu.

ref: Jerusalem was captured during Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king of Babylonia. About a month later, Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guards arrived in Jerusalem. His name was Nebuzaradan,
text: Ubɔr Nebukadnesar aah nan ye Babiloŋ aabɔr pu na aabin kipiik ni liwawaer aaŋmaŋmu aawiin kipiik daal, le waasusur Nebusaradann, u nan ki ye waajab aayidaan na, nan koo Jerusalem aatiŋ ni.

ref: and he burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in the city, as well as all the houses.
text: U nan see Uwumbɔr Aadichal, ni libɔrdichal, ni binikpaam bi mɔmɔk bi Jerusalem na aadichal lii;

ref: He led away the people left in the city, including everyone who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar, the rest of the skilled workers, and even some of the poor people of Judah.
text: Nebusaradann nan di binib bi gur ki ponn ni na buen Babiloŋ ni, ni biwanŋab bi nyi tiwan mbamɔm ki beenin bi nima na, ni binib bi nan nyan ti di bibaa kpee Babiloŋ yaab pu na.

ref: Only the very poorest were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
text: Tɔ, u nan di cha bigiim bi kaa kpa liwankpal libaa na, le ki cha bi tun lituln ŋisubil aasar, ni tijikaar aakpaakon ni, Juda aatiŋ ni.

ref: Evil Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
text: Efil Merodak nan san u kinimbaak ki tii u nsisii mu kpa kipak ki jer bibɔrb bi mu nan bi Babiloŋ ni tinaagbiir ni na.

ref: Jehoiachin was allowed to wear regular clothes instead of a prison uniform, and he even ate at the king's table every day.
text: Kina pu na, Jehoyachinn nan kan nsan ki kpeln waayondiik ni aawanpeenkaan, ki gur ji ubɔr chee tijikaar le ki ti kpo.

ref: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
text: Waah nan bi limɔfal ni n‑yoonn mumɔk na, bi nan luu u iwiin mɔmɔk aajikaar le ki ti saa waakundaal.

ref: Jerusalem, once so crowded, lies deserted and lonely. This city that was known all over the world is now like a widow. This queen of the nations has been made a slave.
text: Jerusalem, kitiŋ ki nan gbii binib na gur ŋmin chii la. Dulnyaa mɔmɔk aanib nan pak kima la, le ki gur naahn ukpopii; kitiŋ ki nan kpa liyimbikpaan na aanib kpaln binaagbiib.

ref: Each night, bitter tears flood her cheeks. None of her former lovers are there to offer comfort; her friends have betrayed her and are now her enemies.
text: Kinyeek ni kitaak aawoln pu, kaanib wii la; le tinyunyunn puu dii bitakpin. Ubaa aa ki bi kijɔtiib mɔmɔk ponn ni ki ga sɔŋ kisui. Kimaantɔtiib di ki kooh a, le bi mɔmɔk gur ye kaadim.

ref: The roads to Zion mourn because no one travels there to celebrate the festivals. The city gates are deserted; priests are weeping. Young women are raped; Zion is in sorrow!
text: Ubaa aa ki koo Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni ke u nan doon Uwumbɔr njim daal. Bisapɔm bi nan gaa ilahn nima na ji falaa la, le bitotoorb ker idun ŋmeen la. Kitiŋ aagoln aabisamɔi ni gur ye nkuun la, le Sionn aatiŋ aanib bi iween sakpen ni.

ref: Enemies now rule the city and live as they please. The Lord has punished Jerusalem because of her awful sins; he has let her people be dragged away.
text: Kaadim nyaŋ ki; ki gur bi baapɔɔn ni la. Uwumbɔr le cha ki jin falaa kaatunwanbir sakpenn pu; Bi chur kaabim ki di bi buen a.

ref: Zion's glory has disappeared. Her leaders are like deer that cannot find pasture; they are hunted down till their strength is gone.
text: Jerusalem aanyaan gur ye n‑yaayoonn na aawan la. Kaayidam gur naahn ipeeman i nkon joo i na la, i san ke i ŋmar bikpam chee, le yaapɔɔn mɔmɔk ti doo.

ref: Her people recall the good life that once was theirs; now they suffer and are scattered. No one was there to protect them from their enemies who sneered when their city was taken.
text: Jerusalem aatiŋ teer kaayaayoonn na aanyaan bɔr, le ki gur ber ki dɔ suuna. Kaah nan lir kaadim aaŋaal ni na, ubaa aa nan bi ki ter ki. Le binib bi nan nyaŋ ki na laa, kaah nan lir pu na.

ref: Jerusalem's horrible sins have made the city a joke. Those who once admired her now hate her instead— she has been disgraced; she groans and turns away.
text: Kaanyuŋ doo a; ki gur nkuun la, le bi gur lik ki fam. Ki ker idun le ki bɔrni inimɔɔn pu. Jerusalem aatiŋ di titunwanbir le ŋa kibaa tijɔŋ.

ref: Her sins had made her filthy, but she wasn't worried about what could happen. And when Jerusalem fell, it was so tragic. No one gave her comfort when she cried out, “Help! I'm in trouble, Lord! The enemy has won.”
text: Kaajɔŋ aa nan bɔr, le kitafal aa nan bi ntafadaan mu ga pii ki na ni. Kaalirm nan nyaŋ a; ubaa aa ŋmaa sɔŋ kisui. Kaadim nyaŋ ki; le kaanib wii ke Uwumbɔr san bi kinimbaak.

ref: Zion's treasures were stolen. Jerusalem saw foreigners enter her place of worship, though the Lord had forbidden them to belong to his people.
text: Kaadim nan sun kaawangol mɔmɔk; kaanib nan kan baah koo Uwumbɔr Aadichal ponn ni pu na. Uwumbɔr aa tii nsan ke binib bi kaa ye Israel yaab na koo nima chee.

ref: Everyone in the city groans while searching for food; they trade their valuables for barely enough scraps to stay alive. Jerusalem Speaks: Jerusalem shouts to the Lord, “Please look and see how miserable I am!”
text: Kaanib bi ban tijikaar; le ki ker idun. Bi joo baawangol le kpenni tijikaar ki ji ke bi ŋmar. Kitiŋ ngbaan wii le ke, “Uwumbɔr, lik maah bi pu na; lik mi, maanimbaak ni.”

ref: No passerby even cares. Why doesn't someone notice my terrible sufferings? You were fiercely angry, Lord, and you punished me worst of all.
text: Unii umɔk jer na kan, ki wii le ki len ke, “Lik maah bi pu na. Ubaa aa kee kan iween i aaboln m kan na, Uwumbɔr aaŋuul yoonn le u di kina aaween tii ni mi.

ref: From heaven you sent a fire that burned in my bones; you set a trap for my feet and made me turn back. All day long you leave me in shock from constant pain.
text: U cha mmii mu wu nwon ni na nyan ni paacham ki dan m pu. U pen mi gaawɔb ki cha m lir kitiŋ. Le u siir cha mi ki di iween ŋmeen tii mi.

ref: You have tied my sins around my neck, and they weigh so heavily that my strength is gone. You have put me in the power of enemies too strong for me.
text: U ŋmee maatunwanbir mɔmɔk bil le ki buu ti mɔmɔk kpaan tɔb ni. U nan di ti leen nneen ni, le taanyunyuun nyii mi bil kitiŋ. Uwumbɔr di mi tii maadim, le maa nan kpa mpɔɔn mubaa bi chee.

ref: You, Lord, have turned back my warriors and crushed my young heroes. Judah was a woman untouched, but you let her be trampled like grapes in a wine pit.
text: Uwumbɔr nan yuul maajab bi kaar na. U nan tun ni bijab le bi nan kuln maanachipɔm. U nan muen muen maanib ke baah mueni ndaan aasubil pu na la.

ref: Because of this, I mourn, and tears flood my eyes. No one is here to comfort or to encourage me; we have lost the war— my people are suffering. The Prophet Speaks:
text: Kina pu le tinyunyunn nya nnimbil ni ki puu lir. Ubaa aan ŋmaa sɔŋ nsui, ubaa aan ŋmaa pɔɔk ntaakpab. Bidim nyaŋ mi, bi yoor maanib aawan mɔmɔk a.

ref: Zion reaches out her hands, but no one offers comfort. The Lord has turned the neighboring nations against Jacob's descendants. Jerusalem is merely a filthy rag to her neighbors. Jerusalem Speaks:
text: M taln ŋŋaal le ubaa aan ter mi. Uwumbɔr yin bidim bi nyan ŋipepel mɔmɔk na nan lii m pu. Le bi ŋani mi ke maah ye tijɔŋ aawan nibaa le na.

ref: The Lord was right, but I refused to obey him. Now I ask all of you to look at my sufferings— even my young people have been dragged away.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr kpa mbamɔn, min le yii waamɔb. Ŋipepel mɔmɔk aanib, li pel m chee man, lik maah bi iween i ponn ni na man. Bi chur maanachipɔm ni bipiisapɔm tinaagbiir.

ref: I called out to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and my leaders died while searching the city for scraps of food.
text: M yin mmaantɔtiib, le bi yii, kaa dan nan ter mi. Le bitotoorb ni biyidam bi ban tijikaar, kaa kan, ki ti kpoi kitiŋ ponn ni.

ref: Won't you look and see how upset I am, our Lord? My stomach is in knots, and my heart is broken because I betrayed you. In the streets and at home, my people are slaughtered.
text: Uwumbɔr, lik maah bi ntoton mu ponn ni na. Maatunwanbir bii nsui mɔmɔk doo. Bi ku binib kitiŋ ponn ni, hali tidir mu ni, bi ku binib la.

ref: Everyone heard my groaning, but no one offered comfort. My enemies know of the trouble that you have brought on me, and it makes them glad. Hurry and punish them, as you have promised.
text: Li pel maah ker idun pu na; ubaa aa bi ki sɔŋ nsui. Saah di tibɔbir tii ni mi na, le maadim aasui piir. Cha saah nan puu ke nwiin mu ga dan na fuu ni; cha maadim mu ji maah jin falaa u na.

ref: Don't let their evil deeds escape your sight. Punish them as much as you have punished me because of my sins. I never stop groaning— I've lost all hope!
text: Cheer bi baabiin na mɔmɔk pu. Daa bitafal ke saah daa ntafal maatunwanbir pu pu na. Falaa ponn ni le m ker idun, le ni ye nsui ni iween.”

ref: The Lord was angry! So he disgraced Zion though it was Israel's pride and his own place of rest. In his anger he threw Zion down from heaven to earth.
text: Uwumbɔr aaŋuul ponn ni le u di mbɔmbɔɔn biin Sionn pu. U nan kpeln kaanyaan na ŋa tilangbenn. Waaŋuul ngbaan daal le u nan nyan cha Waadichal.

ref: The Lord had no mercy! He destroyed the homes of Jacob's descendants. In his anger he tore down every walled city in Judah; he toppled the nation together with its leaders, leaving them in shame.
text: Uwumbɔr nan kuln Juda aatiwaatiir na mɔmɔk, kaa san mu kinimbaak. U nan tur tijawan aadichal ŋi nan kii Juda aatiŋ na lir kitiŋ. U nan cha nnaan ngbaan ni binib bi joo mu na jin inimɔɔn.

ref: The Lord was so furiously angry that he wiped out the whole army of Israel by not supporting them when the enemy attacked. He was like a raging fire that swallowed up the descendants of Jacob.
text: Waaŋuul ponn ni, le u kuln Israel aajab aapɔɔn. Timi aadim aah nan fuu ni na, u nan yii, kaa ter timi. U nan fii sil ti pu ke mmii na, le ki kuln tiwan mɔmɔk.

ref: He attacked like an enemy with a bow and arrows, killing our loved ones. He has burned to the ground the homes on Mount Zion.
text: U nan di waapɔɔn kaan ti pu ke waah ye timi aadin le na. U nan ku binib bi mɔmɔk nan tii timi mpopiin ni mmɔɔn na. Waaŋuul li ton ke mmii na nan pii ni timi bi bi Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni do na.

ref: The Lord was like an enemy! He left Israel in ruins with its palaces and fortresses destroyed, and with everyone in Judah moaning and weeping.
text: Uwumbɔr kuln Israel aatiŋ ke udin na la. U cha kaabɔrdichal, ni tijawan aadichal na kpaln tilangbenn. U tii Juda aanib mpombiin mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: He shattered his temple like a hut in a garden; he completely wiped out his meeting place, and did away with festivals and Sabbaths in the city of Zion. In his fierce anger he rejected our king and priests.
text: Waadichal li ponn ni ti nan dooni u na, le u gbaa wii li yuk yuk. U kuln ŋikpaakoo, ni iwinyaan daal. Waaŋuul aapɔɔn fuu bibɔrb ni bitotoorb mu chee.

ref: The Lord abandoned his altar and his temple; he let Zion's enemies capture her fortresses. Noisy shouts were heard from the temple, as if it were a time of celebration.
text: Uwumbɔr yii waatork aabimbiln, le ki siir cha Waadichal li bi chain na. U cha bidim kan nsan ki gbaa wii laagon. Nin chee ti nan joo mpopiin dooni u na, le bi kpa linyaŋ aafuuk.

ref: The Lord had decided to tear down the walls of Zion stone by stone. So he started destroying and did not stop until walls and fortresses mourned and trembled.
text: Uwumbɔr puu ke Sionn aagon lir kitiŋ. U nan ŋaŋ ŋi ke u sil kan ŋaalirm. Bikikiib aadir na, ni ŋigon mɔmɔk ber le ki dɔ kitiŋ.

ref: Zion's gates have fallen facedown on the ground; the bars that locked the gates are smashed to pieces. Her king and royal family are prisoners in foreign lands. Her priests don't teach, and her prophets don't have a message from the Lord.
text: Ibisamɔi gur dɔ sub tibir ni, le yaakudɔ kool yuk yuk. Ubɔr ni bininyuum na gur bi tinaagbiir ni la. Ubaa aa ki mɔk binib Uwumbɔr Aakaal Aagbaŋ, le Uwumbɔr aa ki kpiir tibɔr tuk waabɔnabtiib.

ref: Zion's leaders are silent. They just sit on the ground, tossing dirt on their heads and wearing sackcloth. Her young women can do nothing but stare at the ground.
text: Jerusalem aajaninkpiib gur ka kitiŋ le ki ŋmin chii, ki di titan puŋ biyil, ki pee tiwan ni saak kuub na. Bisapɔm ka tii biyil la.

ref: My eyes are red from crying, my stomach is in knots, and I feel sick all over. My people are being wiped out, and children lie helpless in the streets of the city.
text: Iwiil pu le nnimbil ti foor koo; m bi ntoton ni la. Baah ku bii maanib pu na le mpombiin ban mu ku mi. Mbim ni mbipɔm fik le ki dɔ kitiŋ ponn ni.

ref: A child begs its mother for food and drink, then blacks out like a wounded soldier lying in the street. The child slowly dies in its mother's arms.
text: Nkon ni nnyunyuu pu le bi wii ki ban binatiib. Bi chuun kitiŋ ponn ni le ki lir ke titotonn le aah pii bi na. Le bi dɔ binatiib aaŋaal ni ki ti kpo.

ref: Zion, how can I comfort you? How great is your pain? Lovely city of Jerusalem, how can I heal your wounds, gaping as wide as the sea?
text: Jerusalem aatiŋ ki m gee ki na, m ga len ke ba? M ga ŋa kinye ki sɔŋ aasui? Ubaa aa kee jin falaa umina aaboln. Saabɔbir aa kpa timɔk ke nnyusakpem na la; limakl aa ki bi nibaa chee.

ref: Your prophets deceived you with false visions and lying messages— they should have warned you to leave your sins and be saved from disaster.
text: Bibɔnabr nan tuk si inyamɔn ŋmeen la. Baah nan tuk si tibɔr ti na le ŋmann si, ba pu? baa nan kpiir saatunwanbir pu. Bi nan cha aa dak ke saa kpa tibɔbir tibaa aa kpiir.

ref: Those who pass by shake their heads and sneer as they make fun and shout, “What a lovely city you were, the happiest on earth, but look at you now!”
text: Binib bi jer kitiŋ ngbaan chee na lik ki, le ki laa ki. Bi gbakr biyil le ki laa Jerusalem aatiŋ, le ki baa ke, “Kitinyaan na le na aa? Kitiŋ ki nan ye dulnyaa mɔmɔk aamakl na le na aa?”

ref: Zion, your enemies curse you and snarl like wild animals, while shouting, “This is the day we've waited for! At last, we've got you!”
text: Saadim mɔmɔk ŋani si yaansara, le ki gbee si kinanaŋ aaningbee. Bi mul bimɔi le ki bui ke, “Ti kuln ki a. Taah nan kii nwiin mu na le na.”

ref: The Lord has done everything that he had planned and threatened long ago. He destroyed you without mercy and let your enemies boast about their powerful forces.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ŋa waah faan ke u ga ŋa pu na. U kuln timi kaa san timi kinimbaak, ke waah nan sak timi n‑yoonn mu jer na pu na. U tii timi aadim linyaŋ, u cha ti lir le ki tii bi mpopiin.

ref: Zion, deep in your heart you cried out to the Lord. Now let your tears overflow your walls day and night. Don't ever lose hope or let your tears stop.
text: Jerusalem aatiŋ, cha aabaa aagon wii ki ban Uwumbɔr chee nterm. Cha saanyunyunn li puu kinyeek ni nwiin pu ke limɔɔl na. Cha saapombiin ni iwiil tii si tibakr.

ref: Get up and pray for help all through the night. Pour out your feelings to the Lord, as you would pour water out of a jug. Beg him to save your people, who are starving to death at every street crossing. Jerusalem Speaks:
text: Li fiir kinyeek ki wii ban nterm Uwumbɔr chee. Di aasui mɔmɔk wii ki gaŋ u aan u san saabim kinimbaak. Nkon ku mbim bilni kitiŋ ponn ni aalɔlɔnn mɔmɔk ni la.

ref: Think about it, Lord! Have you ever been this cruel to anyone before? Is it right for mothers to eat their children, or for priests and prophets to be killed in your temple?
text: Uwumbɔr, lik binib bi aa bi jinni bi falaa na. Bipiib joo baah gee baabim mu na le ŋmɔ. Bi ku bitotoorb ni saabɔnabtiib Saadichal ni la.

ref: My people, both young and old, lie dead in the streets. Because you were angry, my young men and women were brutally slaughtered.
text: Binib bi por na, ni bi kaa por na mɔmɔk kpoi kitiŋ ponn ni la. Bidim aajaak aajum le ku binachipɔm ni bisapɔm mɔmɔk. Saaŋuul aawiin daal le aa kɔr bi mɔmɔk, kaa san bi kinimbaak.

ref: When you were angry, Lord, you invited my enemies like guests for a party. No one survived that day; enemies killed my children, my own little ones.
text: Aa yin ni maadim ke bi nan ji linikul aajim m chee. Le saaŋuul ngbaan daal ubaa aa ŋmaa ŋmar. Bi ku maabim mu m kpiin mu ki gee mu na.

ref: I have suffered much because God was angry.
text: M ye unii u nyi Uwumbɔr aatafadaan aah bi pu na la.

ref: He chased me into a dark place, where no light could enter.
text: U jenn mi koon mbɔmbɔɔn aakaasisik ni,

ref: I am the only one he punishes over and over again, without ever stopping.
text: le ki gbaa mi kpakpaayuk, kaa san mi kinimbaak.

ref: God caused my skin and flesh to waste away, and he crushed my bones.
text: U gbaa mi le nwon lakr lakr, le ki kool maakpab.

ref: He attacked and surrounded me with hardships and trouble;
text: U di mi ŋa falaa, ni iween aayondiik ni.

ref: he forced me to sit in the dark like someone long dead.
text: U chuu mi mpɔɔn le m ti koo kitekpiitiŋ ni, nin chee ye mbɔmbɔɔn ŋmeen na.

ref: God built a fence around me that I cannot climb over, and he chained me down.
text: U buu mi tikululn kaan, le m kpaln unaagbiija u kaan ki ŋmaa san ŋmar na.

ref: Even when I shouted and prayed for help, he refused to listen.
text: M wii mpɔɔn pu ki ban nterm, le Uwumbɔr yii, kaan pel m chee.

ref: God put big rocks in my way and made me follow a crooked path.
text: M yaa chuun kan, m gbeer la; le baah di ŋitakpal maa ŋigon ŋi na leŋ maasan mɔmɔk.

ref: God was like a bear or a lion waiting in ambush for me;
text: U nan dɔ kii mi ke kipeewanbiik na, le ki nan bib m pu ke uchinn na.

ref: he dragged me from the road, then tore me to shreds.
text: U nan jenn mi koon timoor ni, ki ti daa par mi, ki siir cha mi nima chee.

ref: God took careful aim and shot his arrows
text: U nan taln waapiin mɔk mi ke u too.

ref: straight through my heart.
text: U too waapiin chaar mi.

ref: I am a joke to everyone— no one ever stops making fun of me.
text: Binib laa mi le nwiin ti lir; m gur ye yaansara aanii binib mɔmɔk chee la.

ref: He made me eat gravel and rubbed me in the dirt.
text: U di nnimbil tur buun titan ni, le ki tur mi lii isak pu le nnyin kool.

ref: I cannot find peace or remember happiness.
text: Maa ki nyi ngbapɔɔn ni nsuudoon ni mpopiin aah ye tiwan ni na.

ref: I tell myself, “I am finished! I can't count on the Lord to do anything for me.”
text: Maamɔfal aa ki cha dik dik, maah nan mak Uwumbɔr pu pu na doo a.

ref: Just thinking of my troubles and my lonely wandering makes me miserable.
text: M yaa dak maaween, ni maah kaa ki kpa do pu na kan, ni naahn ke maah nyun liluul le na.

ref: That's all I ever think about, and I am depressed.
text: M dak ni pu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la, le nsui mɔmɔk bii doo.

ref: Then I remember something that fills me with hope.
text: Le m yaa ti teer tiwan nibaa ni paa ni na pu kan, m ki kpa limakl.

ref: The Lord's kindness never fails! If he had not been merciful, we would have been destroyed.
text: Uwumbɔr aageehm ni linimbaasaln li kaa door na beenin bi.

ref: The Lord can always be trusted to show mercy each morning.
text: Waageehm ni linimbaasaln aa door ke kichakpiik ni, bee nwiin aah puur pu na, aah kaa door pu na la.

ref: Deep in my heart I say, “The Lord is all I need; I can depend on him!”
text: Uwumbɔr baanja le m kpa, kina pu le m kpa limakl u pu.

ref: The Lord is kind to everyone who trusts and obeys him.
text: Uwumbɔr kpa tiŋann unii umɔk kii tii u na pu.

ref: It is good to wait patiently for the Lord to save us.
text: Kina pu na, ni ŋan ke ti di limɔr kiir u, aan u nan gaa timi lii.

ref: When we are young, it is good to struggle hard
text: Le ni ŋan ke ti bae limɔr buyoonn ti laa pɔɔn na.

ref: and to sit silently alone, if this is what the Lord intends.
text: Buyoonn ti ji falaa na kan, ni ŋan ke ti li ka tibaa suuna, ki li kpa limɔr.

ref: Being rubbed in the dirt can teach us a lesson;
text: Ni ŋan ke ti kii ke ti tun taani, nibaakan, limakl ga li bi.

ref: we can also learn from insults and hard knocks.
text: Bi gbaa timi, ki seei timi, tɔ, ni ŋan ke ti kii kina.

ref: The Lord won't always reject us!
text: Uwumbɔr san kinimbaak, kaa yii timi kookoo.

ref: He causes a lot of suffering, but he also has pity because of his great love.
text: Nibaakan, u ga joo ni timi falaa, tɔ, waageehm mu u kpa ti pu na bi ki pɔɔ.

ref: The Lord doesn't enjoy sending grief or pain.
text: Ti yaa bi ji falaa kan, naa ye tiwan ni mɔ u na.

ref: Don't trample prisoners under your feet
text: Uwumbɔr nyi buyoonn tisui bii kiyondiik ni kookoo na.

ref: or cheat anyone out of what is rightfully theirs. God Most High sees everything,
text: U nyi n‑yoonn mu bi gaal ti chee timi aabamɔn i u tii timi na.

ref: and he knows when you refuse to give someone a fair trial.
text: Buyoonn bibɔjirb ko biini ibamɔn pu libɔjil aadiik ni na, u nyi.

ref: No one can do anything without the Lord's approval.
text: Uwumbɔr aageehm baanja le tun lituln.

ref: Good and bad each happen at the command of God Most High.
text: Uma le ga len, le ni ŋan na, ni ni kaa ŋan na ga ŋa.

ref: We're still alive! We shouldn't complain when we are being punished for our sins.
text: Taah kpa limɔfal pu na, Uwumbɔr yaa daa titafal kan, naa ŋan ke ti ki len tibaa.

ref: Instead, we should think about the way we are living, and turn back to the Lord.
text: Cha ti lik tibaa aabimbin suuna man ki gir ni Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: When we lift our hands in prayer to God in heaven, we should offer him our hearts and say,
text: Cha ti piir tisui tii Uwumbɔr u bi paacham na ki mee limeel ke,

ref: “We've sinned! We've rebelled against you, and you haven't forgiven us!
text: “Uwumbɔr, ti tun titunwanbir ki yii saamɔb, le saa di cha pinn timi.

ref: Anger is written all over you, as you pursue and slaughter us without showing pity.
text: Aa san dii timi ki ti ku timi; saaŋuul nan di saanimbaasaln na bɔr.

ref: You are behind a wall of clouds that blocks out our prayers.
text: Saaŋuul nan filk sakpen, le timi aameel aa ŋmaa jer ki ti pii si.

ref: You allowed nations to treat us like garbage;
text: Aa di timi le ŋa dulnyaa wee aatapuln.

ref: We are terrified and trapped, caught and crushed.”
text: Ti koo tibɔbir, ni libiil ni, le ki nyan; ti bi linimaln, ni ijawaan ni.

ref: My people are destroyed! Tears flood my eyes,
text: Baah kuln maanib pu na, le cha maanyunyunn puu ke ŋimɔɔ na.

ref: until the Lord looks down from heaven and helps.
text: le Uwumbɔr u bi paacham na ti nin lik kan timi.

ref: I am horrified when I see what enemies have done to the young women of our city.
text: M yaa lik tiwan ni ŋa kitiŋ kee aapiib na kan, le nsui bii.

ref: No one had reason to hate me, but I was hunted down like a bird.
text: Maa tun maadim taani ubaa le bi pen gaawɔb chuu mi ke unyoon na.

ref: Then they tried to kill me by tossing me into a pit and throwing stones at me.
text: Bi di mi mee lii mbuu ni le ki di litakpal leŋ mumɔb pu.

ref: Water covered my head— I thought I was gone.
text: Nnyun nan bi biini m pu, le m dak ke nkun peen ni a.

ref: From the bottom of the pit, I prayed to you, Lord.
text: Uwumbɔr, m nan bi mbuu ngbaan aataab taab, le ki wii yin si.

ref: I begged you to listen. “Help!” I shouted. “Save me!” You answered my prayer
text: Le maah gaŋ si ke aa pel maawiil na, aa ŋun.

ref: and came when I was in need. You told me, “Don't worry!”
text: Aa nan ŋun le ki bui mi ke m taa san ijawaan.

ref: You rescued me and saved my life.
text: Uwumbɔr, aa dan ki nan gaa maamɔfal lii.

ref: You saw them abuse me, Lord, so make things right.
text: Ji tibɔr ter mi, ba pu? aa nyi baah tun mi taani u na.

ref: You know every plot they have made against me.
text: Aa nyi maadim aah nan mi pu ki kpokl ki ban mi pu na.

ref: Yes, you know their insults and their evil plans.
text: Uwumbɔr, aa ŋun baah seei mi pu na; aa nyi baah kpokl pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: All day long they attack with words and whispers.
text: Bi len maabɔr le ki kpokl m pu le nwiin ti lir.

ref: No matter what they are doing, they keep on mocking me.
text: Ki nya kichakpiik ni ki ti saa kijook, bi yuul mi la.

ref: Pay them back for everything they have done, Lord!
text: Uwumbɔr, daa bitafal, baah tun pu na pu.

ref: Put your curse on them and make them suffer.
text: Puun lii bi pu ki cha biwon yɔl.

ref: Get angry and go after them until not a trace is left under the heavens.
text: Ban chuu bi, ki ŋar bi ŋŋaan kitiŋ kee pu.”

ref: The purest gold is ruined and has lost its shine; jewels from the temple lie scattered in the streets.
