text: Timi aasalmaa u nan moor lak lak na gur bɔn timm la. Uwumbɔr Aadichal aagon ŋi wii na aatakpal yaa, le ki dɔ kitiŋ ponn ni, ni kookoo.

ref: These are Zion's people, worth more than purest gold; yet they are counted worthless like dishes of clay.
text: Sionn aanachipɔm nan ye ti chee liwangol ke salmaa na la, le dandana ma kan, bi gur ŋani bi ke tiyakr aabuu na.

ref: Even jackals nurse their young, but my people are like ostriches that abandon their own.
text: Hali takɔ tiib kpiini baabim la, le maanib ma bi ke taataa tiib na, bi ŋani baabim mbiin la.

ref: Babies are so thirsty that their tongues are stuck to the roof of the mouth. Children go begging for food, but no one gives them any.
text: Bi cha baabim kpo nkon ni nnyunyuu la; mbim mee ban tijikaar ti ubaa aan tii bi na la.

ref: All who ate expensive foods lie starving in the streets; those who grew up in luxury now sit on trash heaps.
text: Binib bi nan ji tijikaar ti ŋan sakpen na gur kpoi nkon kitiŋ ponn ni, binib bi nan ji nkpan ni n‑yaan na gur bi ŋitapun pu le ki far ban tijikaar.

ref: My nation was punished worse than the people of Sodom, whose city was destroyed in a flash without the help of human hands.
text: Maanib kan ntafadaan ki jer Sodom yaab bi Uwumbɔr aaŋaal nan dan nan kuln bi liwinbaal na.

ref: The leaders of Jerusalem were purer than snow and whiter than milk; their bodies were healthy and glowed like jewels.
text: Timi aayidam nan ye binib bi kaa kpa tijɔŋ ki piin chain ke nkokoyon na la, bi nan kpa mpɔɔn, ki kpa laafee.

ref: Now they are blacker than tar, and no one recognizes them; their skin clings to their bones and is drier than firewood.
text: N‑yoonn mumina ma kan, ubaa aan ki bee bi, le bi dɔ titan ni, kitiŋ ponn ni, le nkun bɔnn binimbil wɔb; biwon kuur ke ndɔkuun na, le ki faan tam baakpab.

ref: Life in the city is so bad that loving mothers have boiled and eaten their own children.
text: Tibɔbir nan dan maanib pu ki joo ni ijawaan; natiib bi nan gee baabim sakpen na nan di bi ŋa tijikaar ki ŋaan bi.

ref: The Lord was so fiercely angry that he burned the city of Zion to the ground.
text: Uwumbɔr nan buur waaŋuusakpeln lii; U nan tuur mmii Sionn aatiŋ ponn ni le mu wun ki pel pel.

ref: Not a king on this earth or the people of any nation believed enemies could break through her gates.
text: Ubaa aa nan bi nibaa chee, hali ntiyayam aayidam aa nan dak ke udin ga ŋmaa dii Jerusalem aabisamɔi ki koo ki ponn ni.

ref: Jerusalem was punished because her prophets and her priests had sinned and caused the death of innocent victims.
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr bi nan bi ki ponn ni na nan tun titunwanbir, le kaatotoorb mu nan cha binib bi kaa tun taani na kpoi, nima le nan cha kina ngbaan ŋa.

ref: Yes, her prophets and priests were covered with blood; no one would come near them, as they wandered from street to street.
text: Kaasalolm nan chuun kpak kitiŋ ponn ni ke bijoom na, biwon mɔmɔk nan ye nsin, le ubaa aan kii ki meeh bi.

ref: Instead, everyone shouted, “Go away! Don't touch us! You're filthy and unfit to belong to God's people!” So they had to leave and become refugees. But foreign nations told them, “You can't stay here!”
text: Binib nan teen ke, “Li cha man. Ni kpa tijɔŋ. Taa meeh mi.” Kina le ubaa aa nan gaa bi, le bi chuun kpak ki nya litimbol lee ni, ki ti saa lee ni.

ref: The Lord is the one who sent them scattering, and he has forgotten them. No respect or kindness will be shown to the priests or leaders.
text: Uwumbɔr aatafal aa nan ki bi bi ni; uma ubaa le nan yaa bi. Utafal aa nan bi timi aatotoorb ni biyidam ni.

ref: Our eyes became weary, hopelessly looking for help from a nation that could not save us.
text: Ti lik ban nterm mu kaa choo na, le kaa ti ki ŋmaa lik. Ti nan kiir ban nterm litimbol li kaa kpa nterm li tii timi na chee, le kaa kan.

ref: Enemies hunted us down on every public street. Our time was up; our doom was near.
text: Bidim nan bi lik ban timi; le taa nan ti ki ŋmaa chuun kitiŋ ponn ni. Timi aayoonn nan doo; timi aamɔfal nan kuln.

ref: They swooped down faster than eagles from the sky. They hunted for us in the hills and set traps to catch us out in the desert.
text: Bi nan jenn timi sunn mala mala ke likaagiil le aah boon ki nyan ni paacham na. Bi nan ti gob timi ŋigongon pu la; nteersakpiin pu le bi nan loon timi.

ref: The Lord's chosen leader was our hope for survival! We thought he would keep us safe somewhere among the nations, but even he was caught in one of their traps.
text: Bi nan chuu timi aabɔr u ye timi aamɔfal na; uma le Uwumbɔr nan lee, le ti nan kpa limakl u pu ke u ga li kii timi bidim chee.

ref: You people of Edom can celebrate now! But your time will come to suffer and stagger around naked.
text: Edom ni Us aanib, li laa man; buyoonn ni ga ŋman na kan, li kpa mpopiin man. Ni mu aabɔbir choo; ni mu ga li chuun gbeer niŋmeen inimɔɔn ŋmeen.

ref: The people of Zion have paid for their sins, and the Lord will soon let them return home. But, people of Edom, you will be punished, and your sins exposed.
text: Sionn aatiŋ pan kaatunwanbir pu; Uwumbɔr aan ki cha ti li bi tinaagbiir ni. Le sin Edom aatiŋ ma, Uwumbɔr ga daa aatafal; u ga nyan saataani mpaan pu.

ref: Our Lord, don't forget how we have suffered and been disgraced.
text: Uwumbɔr, teer tiwan ni dan ti pu na. Lik ni timi, ki kan timi aanimɔɔn.

ref: Foreigners and strangers have taken our land and our homes.
text: Timi aawangol gur bi biwɔwɔm aaŋaal ni la; bima le koo timi aadichal ni.

ref: We are like children whose mothers are widows.
text: Bidim le ku titetiib, le tinatiib gur ye bikpopiib.

ref: The water we drink and the wood we burn cost far too much.
text: Ti daa nnyun le ki nyu; ti daa idɔ le ki tuur mmii.

ref: We are terribly mistreated; we are worn out and can find no rest.
text: Bi jak timi mpɔɔn ke ibon ni laakumii tiib na la, le ti ti bak, le baan cha ti fuur.

ref: We had to surrender to Egypt and Assyria because we were hungry.
text: Ti chuun mee Ijipt yaab ni Asiria yaab tijikaar ti ti ga ji ki li bi na la.

ref: Our ancestors sinned, but they are dead, and we are left to pay for their sins.
text: Tiyaajatiib le nan tun titunwanbir, le kaa ki bi din wee, le timi le bi ji baatunwanbir ngbaan aafalaa.

ref: Slaves are now our rulers, and there is no one to set us free.
text: Binaagbiib soor binib bi joo timi na, le ubaa mu aan ŋmaa gaa ti bi chee ki lii.

ref: We are in danger from brutal desert tribes; we must risk our lives just to bring in our crops.
text: Binikurb chuun kpak kitiŋ kee pu la; ti joo timi aamɔfal pa talmaa, le ki nya ti ban tijikaar.

ref: Our skin is scorched from fever and hunger.
text: Nkon cha fee fee ti ban u ku timi la, le tiwon ton jer kikpawuŋ.

ref: On Zion and everywhere in Judah our wives and daughters are being raped.
text: Bi chur tipuutiib mpɔɔn ki doo bi chee Sionn Aajool pu; bi chur tibisatiib mpɔɔn ki doo bi chee Juda aatim mɔmɔk ni la.

ref: Our rulers are strung up by their arms, and our nation's advisors are treated shamefully.
text: Bi chur timi aayidam buen le ki ti leen bi iŋmin; ubaa aa ki pak timi aaninkpiib.

ref: Young men are forced to do the work of slaves; boys must carry heavy loads of wood.
text: Bi chur timi aanachipɔm mpɔɔn le bi nan idi ke binaagbiib na; mbijabim tui idɔ i nyuun na le kaa ki ŋmaa chuun.

ref: Our leaders are not allowed to decide cases in court, and young people no longer play music.
text: Bininkpiib aa ki kaa kitiŋ aabisamɔb chee, le binachipɔm ni bisapɔm aa ki waa liwaal.

ref: Our hearts are sad; instead of dancing, we mourn.
text: Taa ki kpa mpopiin; mpombiin cha taa ki waa liwaal.

ref: Zion's glory has disappeared! And we are doomed because of our sins.
text: Taah nan mak tiwan ni pu na aa ki gur. Ti tun titunwanbir, le timi aamɔfal kuln.

ref: We feel sick all over and can't even see straight;
text: Ti gur ye bibum la, le tinyunyunn cha taa ki waa,

ref: our city is in ruins, overrun by wild dogs.
text: ba pu? Uwumbɔr Aadichal Aajool gur nkuun la, le ikakal san nuuni laalangbenn ni.

ref: You will rule forever, Lord! You are King for all time.
text: Uwumbɔr, le aa ma ye ubɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki ga li joo dulnyaa ki ti saa ndoon.

ref: Why have you forgotten us for so long?
text: Aa yii timi ni yunn sakpen a. Saan ki teer timi aabɔr la aa?

ref: Bring us back to you! Give us a fresh start.
text: Uwumbɔr, giin ni timi aabaa chee. Giin ni timi. Taah nan kpa kipak ki n‑yaajayoonn na, giin ki tii timi.

ref: Or do you despise us so much that you don't want us?
text: Aa yii timi kookoo la aa? Saaŋuul aa kpa ndoon la aa?

ref: I saw a windstorm blowing in from the north. Lightning flashed from a huge cloud and lit up the whole sky with a dazzling brightness. The fiery center of the cloud was as shiny as polished metal,
text: M nan waan lik paacham le ki kan kitaabuŋ nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb ki choo. Utaal nan moor ntaalangbam sakpem mubaa ni, le ntaalangbam ngbaan chee nan wiin chain. Utaal ngbaan aah nan moor nin chee na, tiwan nibaa nan moor nima chee ke tikumann na.

ref: and in that center I saw what looked like four living creatures. They were somewhat like humans,
text: M nan waa tiwanfuurkaan ninaa nibaa kitaabuŋ ngbaan aakaasisik ni, ke binib na.

ref: except that each one had four faces and four wings.
text: Ni mɔmɔk nibaabaa nan kpa nimbil wɔb munana, ni ifeen inana la.

ref: Their legs were straight, but their feet looked like the hoofs of calves and sparkled like bronze.
text: Tiwan ngbaan aataa nan tok kaa gɔr nibaa chee, le ni kpa itaabuseen ke unaaja na. Ni nan moor ke tikumann ti bi jɔŋ ti mbamɔm na la.

ref: The four creatures were standing back to back with the tips of their wings touching. They moved together in every direction, without turning their bodies.
text: Nibaa mɔk nan taln naafeen ilee le ki ti ton niken aafeen, le ni di ŋa likpakpaln pu. Ni yaa siir ki cha kan, ni dii tɔb la, kaa fenn niwon.

ref: Each creature had the face of a human in front, the face of a lion on the right side, the face of a bull on the left, and the face of an eagle in back.
text: Tiwanfuurkaan ngbaan nibaabaa aanimbil wɔb munana ngbaan aa nan naahn tɔb; unibɔn aanimbil wɔb le nan bi nimɔb wɔb, le uchinn aanimbil wɔb bi ŋŋangii wɔb, le unaaja aanimbil wɔb bi ŋŋangan wɔb, le likaagiil aanimbil wɔb bi nipuwɔb.

ref: Two wings of each creature were spread out and touched the wings of the creatures on either side. The other two wings of each creature were folded against its body.
text: Nibaabaa mɔk aafeen ilelee nan taln le ki ti ton niken ni si gbɔk ni na aafeen, le ki di ilelee i gur na tam niwon.

ref: The four living creatures went wherever the Spirit led them, and they moved together without turning their bodies, because each creature faced straight ahead.
text: Nibaa mɔk nan kpa nimbil wɔb munana mu lik ŋipepel ŋinaa mɔmɔk pu na, kina pu na, ni mɔmɔk ga nan ŋmaa kpaan ki chuun buen naah gee lipepel li na, kaa fenn niwon.

ref: The creatures were glowing like hot coals, and I saw something like a flaming torch moving back and forth among them. Lightning flashed from the torch every time its flame blazed up.
text: Tiwan nibaa nan bi tiwanfuurkaan ngbaan aakaasisik ni ki naahn mmii, ki chuun n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Mmii ngbaan nan gaa le ki too pelb pelb ke utaal aah moor pu na.

ref: The creatures themselves moved as quickly as sparks jumping from a fire.
text: Tiwanfuurkaan ngbaan mu nan ber ti nya do ki ber ti nya do ki dii mmii ngbaan aah too pelb pelb pu na la.

ref: I then noticed that on the ground beside each of the four living creatures was a wheel,
text: Maah si lik tiwanfuurkaan ngbaan na, le m kan tifambann aataa ŋinaa meehr kitiŋ ki kpak tiwanfuurkaan ngbaan nibaabaa.

ref: shining like chrysolite. Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it,
text: Tifambann aataa ngbaan nan naahn tɔb la; kibaa mɔk nan moor lak lak ke litakpanyaan li kpa kidaak na la, le kibaa mɔk ki kpa kifambaŋ ki puln kiken na,

ref: so that they could move in any direction without turning.
text: kina pu na, tifambann aataa ngbaan mɔmɔk ga ŋmaa buen ŋipepel mɔmɔk wɔb.

ref: The rims of the wheels were large and frightening, and they had eyes all the way around them.
text: Tifambann ngbaan mɔmɔk pu nan ye ŋinimbil ŋmeen la.

ref: The creatures controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the four creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels were beside them.
text: Kina pu na, tiwanfuurkaan ngbaan yaa chuun, bee ni fii paacham kan, kina le ŋitaa ngbaan mu ŋani.

ref: Above the living creatures, I saw something that was sparkling like ice, and it reminded me of a dome. Each creature had two of its wings stretched out toward the creatures on either side, with the other two wings folded against its body.
text: Tiwan ngbaan aataab le tiwanfuurkaan ngbaan nan si ki taln ifeen ilelee ti ton niken ni si gbɔk ni na, le ki di ifeen ilelee mu tam niwon.

ref: Whenever the creatures flew, their wings roared like an ocean or a large army or even the voice of God All-Powerful. And whenever the creatures stopped, they folded their wings against their bodies.
text: M nan ŋun naah fii aan naafeen kpa kifuuk ki na pu; kifuuk ngbaan nan naahn nnyusakpem aafuuk la, ki naahn butɔb aajab bi wiir sakpen na aafuuk, ki ki naahn Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aaneel. Ni yaa kaa ki fiir kan, ni kpab naafeen la,

ref: When the creatures stopped flapping their wings, I heard a sound coming from above the dome.
text: le kifuuk nan tee beenin nya ni tiwan ni bi ke tikur ti bi niyil paab na ni.

ref: I then saw what looked like a throne made of sapphire, and sitting on the throne was a figure in the shape of a human.
text: Tiwan nibaa nan bi tiwan ni naahn tikur na paacham ki naahn libɔrjal li bi di ŋitakpanyaan ŋa li na. Tiwan nibaa nan ka libɔrjal ngbaan pu ki naahn unibɔn.

ref: From the waist up, it was glowing like metal in a hot furnace, and from the waist down it looked like the flames of a fire. The figure was surrounded by a bright light,
text: Tiwan ngbaan nan moor ke tikumann le aah pu mmii aakaasisik ni na. Ni nan moor ki wiin ke nwiihn na,

ref: as colorful as a rainbow that appears after a storm. I realized I was seeing the brightness of the Lord's glory! So I bowed with my face to the ground, and just then I heard a voice speaking to me.
text: ki bi ke waakpimanja aah bi pu na. Nwiihn mu nan deer ŋinimbil ngbaan na le nan mɔk ke Uwumbɔr bi nima chee.

ref: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, I want you to stand up and listen.”
text: Maah kan kina na, le m tar lir kitiŋ lichichikr, le ki ŋun nneel len ke, “Unibɔn, fii sil. M ban m len aa chee tibɔr la.”

ref: After he said this, his Spirit took control of me and lifted me to my feet. Then the Lord said:
text: Nneel ngbaan aah bi len kina na, le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan koo m ni le ki fiin mi siin ntaa pu, le m ŋun nneel na ki len ke,

ref: Ezekiel, I am sending you to the people of Israel. They are just like their ancestors who rebelled against me and refused to stop.
text: “Unibɔn, m tun si Israel aanib chee la. Bi nya mpuwɔb ki nyan sil m pu, ki beenin ye binib bi yiir maamɔb ke biyaajatiib aah nan bi pu na.

ref: They are stubborn and hardheaded. But I, the Lord God, have chosen you to tell them what I say.
text: Bi ye tafalaaŋundam le kaa pak mi, kina pu le m bi tun si bi chee ke aa ti bui bi min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aah bi tuk bi pu na.

ref: Those rebels may not even listen, but at least they will know that a prophet has come to them.
text: Binib bi yii maamɔb ngbaan na yaa ti ŋun tii si, bee baa ŋun tii si kan, bi ga bee ke Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr nan bi bikaasisik ni.

ref: Don't be afraid of them or of anything they say. You may think you're in the middle of a thorn patch or a bunch of scorpions. But be brave
text: “Sin unibɔn, taa li san bi ijawaan, ki taa li san baah len pu na mu ijawaan. Bi ga yii si ki lik seen si; ni ga li bi ke unii aah koo inyoohn chee pu na la. Taa san binib bi yii maamɔb ngbaan na ijawaan, ki taa li san baah len pu na mu ijawaan.

ref: Ezekiel, don't rebel against me, as they have done. Instead, listen to everything I tell you. And now, Ezekiel, open your mouth and eat what I am going to give you.
text: “Unibɔn, li pel maah ga tuk si pu na. Taa li ye umɔyiir ke bima na. Waar aamɔb ki ji tiwan ni m ban m di tii si na.”

ref: Just then, I saw a hand stretched out toward me. And in it was a scroll.
text: M nan kan ŋŋaal mubaa taln mɔk ni mi, ki ŋub kigbaŋ ki bi kpae ki na.

ref: The hand opened the scroll, and both sides of it were filled with words of sadness, mourning, and grief.
text: Ŋŋaal ngbaan nan chuu kpar kigbaŋ ngbaan, le m kan ke ki kpa ŋŋmeen ŋipepel mɔmɔk ŋilee pu, ki ye mpombiin aawiil, ni ikpowiil, ni idun aaŋmeen.

ref: He handed me the scroll and said, “Eat this and fill up on it.” So I ate the scroll, and it tasted sweet as honey.
text: U nan ki bui ke, “Unibɔn, di kigbakpaikee ki m di tii si na ŋmɔ; cha ki gbiin aapuul.” M nan di ki ŋman, le ki mɔ mmɔb ni ke tisiir na.

ref: They are Israelites, not some strangers who speak a foreign language you can't understand. If I were to send you to foreign nations, they would listen to you.
text: M yaa tun si ŋitimbokpaan ŋi aanib len iliyayan i saa ŋun na chee kan, bima le ga pel aa chee,

ref: But the people of Israel will refuse to listen, because they have refused to listen to me. All of them are stubborn and hardheaded,
text: le Israel aanii ubaa aan li ban ke u pel; baan kpaan pel min mbaa chee kpala. Bi mɔmɔk kpa tafalaaŋun le ki ye bimɔyiib.

ref: so I will make you as stubborn as they are.
text: M ga cha aa mu li kpa tafalaaŋun aan saabimbin li pɔɔ ke bima na.

ref: Listen carefully to everything I say and then think about it.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki nab ke, “Unibɔn, pel suuna ki teer maah tuk si pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: Then go to the people who were brought here to Babylonia with you and tell them you have a message from me, the Lord God. Do this, whether they listen to you or not.
text: Li cha aado yaab bi bi tinaagbiir ni na chee, ki ti bui bi min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aah bi tuk bi pu na, hali bi yaa kaan pel aa chee kan, aa len ti mɔmɔk.”

ref: The Spirit lifted me up, and as the glory of the Lord started to leave, I heard a loud, thundering noise behind me.
text: Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan nan yoor mi paacham le m ŋun nneel mu ŋuuni kaakaan na len ke, “Pak Uwumbɔr aanyuŋ paacham man.”

ref: It was the sound made by the creatures' wings as they brushed against each other, and by the rumble of the wheels beside them.
text: M nan ŋun tiwanfuurkaan na aafeen gbaa tɔb paacham, le tifambann aataa na aafuuk bi ke kitiŋ le aah dam ki puu na.

ref: Then the Spirit carried me away. The Lord's power had taken complete control of me, and I was both annoyed and angry.
text: Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn nan di mpɔɔnsakpiin mubaa le dan m pu, le Waafuur Nyaan aah yoor mi buen na, le nsui fii, le liŋuul chuu mi.

ref: When I was back with the others living at Abib Hill near the Chebar River, I sat among them for seven days, shocked at what had happened to me. The Lord Appoints Ezekiel To Stand Watch (Ezekiel
text: M nan ti fuu Tel Abib aatiŋ ki bi Kebar Aamɔɔl chee aan binaagbiib na koo nima chee na, ki koo nima ti saa iwiin ilole, le maah ŋun ki kan pu na nyaŋ mi kookoo. Uwumbɔr aah di Esekiel ŋa ukikiir pu na (Esekiel

ref: Seven days after I had seen the brightness of the Lord's glory, the Lord said:
text: Iwiin ilole ngbaan aah jer na, le Uwumbɔr len m chee tibɔr.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
text: U nan len ke, “Unibɔn, m di si ŋa Israel aatimbol aakikiir la. Aa di nsakm mu m di tii si na nabr bi.

ref: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways so they won't be punished. If you refuse, you are responsible for their death.
text: M yaa len ke utunwanbirdaan ga kpo, le saa sak u ke u kpeln waabimbin aan ki ŋmar kan, u ga kpo, ki beenin ye utunwanbirdaan, le m ga chuu si taani waakun pu.

ref: However, if you do warn them, and they keep on sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent.
text: Aa yaa sak utunwanbirdaan, le u yii, kaa kpeln waabimbin kan, u ga kpo ki beenin ye utunwanbirdaan, le aa ma ga ŋmar.

ref: Now suppose faithful people start sinning, and I decide to put stumbling blocks in their paths to make them fall. They deserve to die because of their sins. So if you refuse to warn them, I will forget about the times they were faithful, and I will hold you responsible for their death.
text: “Unibamɔnn ubaa yaa piin ki bi tun titunwanbir aan m di u siin mbimbin mu bir na ni, aan saa sak u kan, u ga kpo. Waatunwanbir pu le u ga kpo, maan teer waatunyaan na bɔr, le m ga chuu si taani waakun pu.

ref: But if you do warn them, and they listen to you and stop sinning, I will let them live. And you will be innocent. Ezekiel Cannot Talk
text: Aa yaa sak unibamɔnn ke u taa tun titunwanbir aan u yaa ŋun tii si, kaa tun titunwanbir kan, u ga li kpa limɔfal, le aa mu ga ŋmar.” Esekiel aah kaan ki ŋmaa len tibɔr pu na

ref: The Lord took control of me and said, “Stand up! Go into the valley, and I will talk with you there.”
text: M nan bee ke Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn bi m chee le ki ŋun u len ke, “Fii sil ki li cha kifataŋ ni. M ga ti len aa chee tibɔr nima chee.”

ref: I immediately went to the valley, where I saw the brightness of the Lord's glory, just as I had seen it near the Chebar River, and I bowed with my face to the ground.
text: M nan fii buen kifataŋ ni, le ki ti kan Uwumbɔr aanyuŋ wiin chain nima chee, ke maah nan kan Kebar Aamɔɔl chee pu na. M nan tar lir kitiŋ lichichikr,

ref: His Spirit took control of me and lifted me to my feet. Then the Lord said: Go back and lock yourself in your house!
text: le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan koo m ni ki fiin mi siin ntaa pu. Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke, “Li chaa kun ki ti laŋ aabaa pu saadichal ni.

ref: You will be tied up to keep you inside,
text: Unibɔn, m ga ti buu si iŋmin, le saan ki ŋmaa nya binib ni.

ref: and I will make you unable to talk or to warn those who have rebelled against me.
text: M ga cha aalambil kpal aan aa taa ŋmaa sak bimɔyiib ngbaan.

ref: But the time will come, when I will tell you what to say, and you will again be able to speak my message. Some of them will listen; others will be stubborn and refuse to listen.
text: Tɔ, m yaa nan ki len, ki ki lɔkr aalambil ke aa len kan, aa ga bui bi min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aah bi tuk bi pu na. Bi ponn ni ngem ga ŋun, le baah ye litimbol li yii maamɔb na aanib na, ngem mu aatafal aan li bi aa ni.”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, find a brick and sketch a picture of Jerusalem on it.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, ban litambipapaln ki di li bil aanimbiin ni, ki naan Jerusalem aatiŋ aah bi pu na paan li pu.

ref: Then prepare to attack the brick as if it were a real city. Build a dirt mound and a ramp up to the top and surround the brick with enemy camps. On every side put large wooden poles as though you were going to break down the gate to the city.
text: Ŋa ŋibuu, ni ŋibimbin aawan, ki naan butɔb aajab aakpuk, ni ŋidɔgen ŋi bi ga di gbaa wiil kaagon na mann goln saah naan Jerusalem aatiŋ ki na. Nima le ga mɔk ke bijab gob ki a.

ref: The brick stands for Jerusalem, so attack it! Stare at it and shout angry warnings.
text: “Di aanimbil kaan bijab aah ga gor pu ki ti gob Jerusalem aatiŋ pu na. Fik aaŋaal mɔk kitiŋ ngbaan ki di maah tuk si pu na tuk kaanib.

ref: I will tie you up, so you can't leave until your attack has ended.
text: M ga buu si bil, le aa taa ŋmaa fenn doon nsikakl muken pu ki ti saa buyoonn butɔb aajab aah gob Jerusalem aatiŋ pu na ti jer.

ref: Get a large bowl. Then mix together wheat, barley, beans, lentils, and millet, and make some bread. This is what you will eat for the
text: “Ban njikaabim, ni ŋituun, ni iyuu, ni njikaabim muken. Di ni mɔmɔk ŋmal tɔb ni, ki di ŋa boroboro. Nima le aa ga li ji ki ti saa iwiin ikui itaa ni imonko inaa ni kipiik i aa dɔ aaŋangan aasikakl pu na.

ref: Use dried human waste to start a fire, then bake the bread on the coals where everyone can watch you.
text: Aa ga li joo unibɔn aabikuun le tuur saamii, muma pu le aa ga li ŋani saaboroboro, ki ŋmɔ u nin chee binib mɔmɔk ga li waa si na.”

ref: When I scatter the people of Israel among the nations, they will also have to eat food that is unclean, just as you must do.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “Nimina le ga li ye Israel yaab aah ga li ji tijikaar ti Nkaal bui ke ti kɔ na, buyoonn m cha bi yaa ki bi biwɔwɔm aatim ni na.”

ref: I said, “Lord God, please don't make me do that! Never in my life have I eaten food that would make me unacceptable to you. I've never eaten anything that died a natural death or was killed by a wild animal or that you said was unclean.”
text: Le m nan gar ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, maa kii, maa kee bii mbaa daalbaadaal. Maah fii ubo na, maa kee ŋman kiwakork ki kpo na, bee upeel aah chuu ki na. Maa kee jin tijikaar ti kɔ na.”

ref: The Lord replied, “Instead of human waste, I will let you bake your bread on a fire made from cow manure.
text: Kina pu le Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Ni ŋan. M ga cha aa li joo ŋinaabindun le tuur saamii, le aa ga ŋmaa di ŋima ŋa saaboroboro, naan ki li ye unibɔn aabikuun.”

ref: Everyone will be shocked at what is happening, and, because of their sins, they will die a slow death.”
text: Baajikaar ni nnyun ga doo; bitaakpab ga yɔl, le baatunwanbir pu bi ga foor doo.”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, get a sharp sword and use it to cut off your hair and beard. Weigh the hair and divide it into three equal piles.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, ban kijaak aajuk ki ka na ki di ki kuu aayikpir ni aalangbaln mɔmɔk. Aa yaa ŋa kina doo kan, aa ŋaŋ ki bee taanyunyuun, ki yakr ti nfum mutaa pu.

ref: After you attack the brick that stands for Jerusalem, burn one pile of your hair on the brick. Chop up the second pile and let the small pieces of hair fall around the brick. Throw the third pile into the wind, and I will strike it with my own sword.
text: Butɔb aajab aah ŋa tiwan ni mɔmɔk ki gob Jerusalem aatiŋ na yaa nan jer kan, aa di liker libaa ŋa mmii ni, kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni. Di saajaak aajuk chɔi chɔi liker liken buyoonn aa nyan kitiŋ ngbaan ni ki bi chuun na. Di liker li gur na yaa libuln ni, aan m di maajaak aajuk paan ti pu.

ref: Keep a few of the hairs and wrap them in the hem of your clothes.
text: Gur tikor siib ki di gbin saawanpeenkaan aamɔju,

ref: Then pull out a few of those hairs and throw them in the fire, so they will also burn. This fire will spread, destroying everyone in Israel.
text: ki lee ti ponn ni siib ki di ŋa mmii ni ti wu. Tima ngbaan aamii le ga yaa gaa Israel aatimbol mɔmɔk.”

ref: I am the Lord God, and I have made Jerusalem the most important place in the world, and all other nations admire it.
text: Ndindaan Uwumbɔr nan ki len ke, “Lik Jerusalem aatiŋ. M di ki siin dulnyaa aakaasisik ni la, le ntim mu gur na mann goln ki.

ref: But the people of Jerusalem rebelled and refuse to obey me. They ignored my laws and have become even more sinful than the nations around them.
text: Le Jerusalem aatiŋ yii maakaal, ki mɔk ke ki kpa mbiin jer ntim muken, kaa kii maamɔb ki jer ntim mu mann goln ki na. Jerusalem aatiŋ yii maah mɔk pu na, ki yii ke kaan joo maakaal.

ref: So tell the people of Jerusalem: I am the Lord God! You have refused to obey my laws and teachings, and instead you have obeyed the laws of the surrounding nations. You have become more rebellious than any of them!
text: Jerusalem aatiŋ, li pel min Aadindaan Uwumbɔr aah bi len pu na. Saah kaa joo maakaal, ni maah mɔk pu na na, aa ban tibɔbir ti jer ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln si na aabɔbir. Aa dii ŋitimbol ŋiken aakaal la.

ref: Now all those nations will watch as I turn against you and punish you
text: Kina pu na, min Aadindaan Uwumbɔr le len ke aa ye maadin la. M ga ji si tibɔr nin chee ŋitimbol mɔmɔk ga kan si na.

ref: for your sins. Your punishment will be more horrible than anything I've ever done or will ever do again.
text: Jerusalem aanib aah tun lituln li sukr ponn ni na pu, le m ga daa kitafal sakpen, ke maah kaa kee daa bitafal pu na, le kaan ki ŋa kina.

ref: Parents will be so desperate for food that they will eat their own children, and children will eat their parents. Those who survive this horror will be scattered in every direction.
text: Kina pu na, tetiib ni natiib bi bi Jerusalem ponn ni na ga ŋmɔ baabim, le mbim mu ga ŋmɔ tetiib ni natiib. M ga daa nitafal le ki cha bi ŋmar na yaa buen ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni.

ref: Your sins have disgusted me and made my temple unfit as a place to worship me. So I swear by my own life that I will cut you down and show you no pity.
text: “Kina pu na, maah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, ki ye Aadindaan Uwumbɔr, maamɔboln sɔ: naah di titunwanbir, ni tiwan ni sukr ponn ni na bii Maameen Aadichal na, m ga kuln nimi kaan san nimi kinimbaak.

ref: A third of you will die here in Jerusalem from disease or starvation. Another third will be killed in war. And I will scatter the last third of you in every direction, then track you down and kill you.
text: Nimi aanib ŋiker ŋitaa ponn ni aaker libaa ga kpo iween, ni nkon aakun kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni; le liker liken ga bee kijaak aajuk aakun ni, kitiŋ ngbaan aagbaan; le m ga di litatar na yaa tii libuln, ki di maajaak aajuk paan bi pu.

ref: You will feel my fierce anger until I have finished taking revenge. Then you will know that I, the Lord, was furious because of your disobedience.
text: “Nimi le ga gaa maaŋuusakpeln ki ti saa buyoonn m ga bab na. Nimina yaa nan ŋa kan, le ni ga bee ke min Uwumbɔr le di maaŋuusakpeln na len ni chee, naah yii maah mɔk nimi pu na pu.

ref: will insult you and make fun of you, but they will also be shocked and terrified at what I did in my anger.
text: “Maaŋuul yaa fii ni pu sakpen aan m daa nitafal liŋuul pu kan, ijawaan ga chuu ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln nimi na. Biponn ni ga li sukr ni pu, le bi ga li joo nimi ŋani yaansara.

ref: I will destroy your crops until you starve to death, and disasters will strike you like arrows.
text: Maan ki cha ni kan tijikaar, le ni ga kpo nkon aaween pu ke ipiin i ka sakpen na le aah choo i nan kuln nimi na.

ref: Starvation and wild animals will kill your children. I'll punish you with horrible diseases, and your enemies will strike you down with their swords. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: M ga cha nkon ni ipeel i bir na ku nimi aabim, ki cha iween, ni linikul, ni butɔb ku nimi. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: The Lord God said:
text: Uwumbɔr nan yin mi ki len ke,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, face the hills of Israel and tell them:
text: “Unibɔn, lik Israel aajoo wɔb ki len tibɔbir lii ŋi pu.

ref: Listen, you mountains and hills, and every valley and gorge! I, the Lord, am about to turn against you and crush all the places where foreign gods are worshiped.
text: Bui Israel aajoo ke ŋi pel Uwumbɔr aamɔboln, bui ŋi ke ŋi li ŋun min Ŋidindaan Uwumbɔr aah joo pu tuk ŋijoo, ni ŋigongon, ni ŋijoo aasisik ni aafatann, ke m ga di kijaak aajuk nan kuln binib aah dooni ŋiwaa nin chee na.

ref: Every altar will be smashed, and in front of the idols I will put to death the people who worship them.
text: Ŋiwaabimbin ni baah seer nnyɔknii ŋibimbin ŋi pu na ga ber. Bi ga ku binib bi mɔmɔk bi nima chee na, baawaa aataab.

ref: Dead bodies and bones will be lying around the idols and the altars.
text: M ga di Israel yaab aanikpol yaa; m ga di baakpab yaa ŋiwaabimbin ngbaan chee la.

ref: Every town in Israel will be destroyed to make sure that each shrine, idol, and altar is smashed—everything the Israelites made will be a pile of ruins.
text: Israel aatim mɔmɔk ga kuln, aan baawaa, ni ŋiwaabimbin, ni nnyɔknii aabimbin ga wiil yuk yuk, le baah ŋa tiwan ni mɔmɔk na wɔŋ.

ref: All over the country, your people will die. And those who survive will know that I, the Lord, did these things.
text: Bi ga ku binib, ni kookoo, le bi ŋmar na ki len ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.

ref: I will let some of the people live through this punishment, but I will scatter them among the nations,
text: “M ga cha bi nya linikul ngbaan ni ki yaa koo ŋitimbol ŋiken ni,

ref: where they will be prisoners. And when they think of me, they will realize that they disgraced me by rebelling and by worshiping idols. They will hate themselves for the evil things they did,
text: nin chee bi ga li bi tinaagbiir ni na. Nima le bi ga ti teer mbɔr ki bee ke min le daa bitafal ki jinn bi inimɔɔn, bisui i kaa ŋani maah len pu na, ki yii mi ki labr dii ŋiwaa na pu. Baah tun titunwanbir ki ŋani tiwan ni bii binib aayimbil na pu, le biponn ni ga li sukr bibaa pu.

ref: and they will know that I am the Lord and that my warnings must be taken seriously.
text: Bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr, ki bee ke maah nan sak bi pu na aa ye tifaan baanja la.”

ref: The Lord God then said: Ezekiel, beat your fists together and stomp your feet in despair! Moan in sorrow, because the people of Israel have done disgusting things and now will be killed by enemy troops, or they will die from starvation and disease.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr len ke, “Ŋmaan aaŋaal. Di aataa taa kitiŋ mpɔɔn pu. Li wii ni mpombiin Israel yaab aah tun titunwanbir ni tiwan ni sukr ponn ni na pu. Bi ga kpoi butɔb ni, ni nkon, ni iween ni.

ref: Those who live far away will be struck with deadly diseases. Those who live nearby will be killed in war. And the ones who are left will starve to death. I will let loose my anger on them!
text: Binib bi bi dandar na ga buŋ le ki kpo; le binib bi bi duun na ga kpo butɔb ni; le bi gur na ga kpo nkon pu. Bi ga kan maaŋuul aah pɔɔ pu na mɔmɔk.

ref: These people used to offer incense to idols at altars built on hills and mountaintops and in the shade of large oak trees. But when they see dead bodies lying around those altars, they will know that I am the Lord.
text: Ŋinikpol ga li dɔ ŋmal ŋiwaa ni ŋiwaabimbin ni, ki yaa gbiin ligongoln limɔk paa na pu, ni lijool mɔk pu, ni bususoom mɔk, ni likpaln mɔk taab, ni nin chee mɔk bi seer nnyɔknii tii ŋiwaa na. Le unii mɔmɔk ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.

ref: I will make their country a barren wasteland, from the Southern Desert to the town of Diblah in the north. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
text: Mbamɔn, m taln ŋŋaal le ki kuln baatiŋ. M ga cha ki kpaln nkuun, ki nya ŋŋangii wɔb nteersakpiin ni, ki ti saa Ribla aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangan wɔb na, kaan di cha nin chee mɔk Israel yaab koo na. Le unii mɔk ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that I am saying: Israel will soon come to an end! Your whole country is about to be destroyed
text: “Unibɔn, min Aadindaan Uwumbɔr aah len Israel aatiŋ aabɔr ti na sɔ: Kitiŋ ngbaan aadoon le na.

ref: that I will show no pity. I will punish you for the evil you've done, and you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Maan san si kinimbaak, kaan di cha si. M ga daa aatafal saah tun ŋitun ŋi aan ŋi sukr ponn ni na pu, le aa bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

ref: And when it comes, your life will be over.
text: Ni mɔmɔk doo a. Ndoon ngbaan le na. Saabɔr doo a.

ref: You people of Israel are doomed! Soon there will be panic on the mountaintops instead of celebration.
text: Nimi binib bi bi kitiŋ pu na aadoon choo. N‑yoonn peen ni le njim aan ki li bi ŋijoo aawaachur ni, see nlanŋmal ŋmeen.

ref: Your sins are so terrible, that you'll get no mercy from me. Then you will know that I, the Lord, have punished you.
text: Maan san nimi kinimbaak, kaan di cha nimi. M ga daa nitafal, nimi aatun ŋi sukr ponn ni na pu, le ni bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr, ki bee ke min le dar nitafal.”

ref: and violent criminals run free. None of you will survive the disaster, and everything you own and value will be shattered.
text: Mbimbin mu pɔɔ na moo kpae la. Kipupuk nyaŋ sakpen a. Mbimbin mu pɔɔ na joo ni mbiin la. Baawangol, ni baanyaan, ni baanyuŋ nibaa kina aan gur.

ref: and people who sell property will never get it back, because all of you must be punished for your sins. And I won't change my mind!
text: Uwumbɔr aatafadaan aah ga dan unii mɔmɔk pu na, utitiir ubaa aan li bi ki nan kan waah nan lir tiwan ni pu na aanyoor. Binib bi tun titunwanbir na aan ŋmar daalbaadaal.

ref: A signal has been blown on the trumpet, and weapons are prepared for battle. But no one goes to war, because in my anger I will strike down everyone in Israel. Israel Is Surrounded The Lord said to the people of Israel:
text: Ukpiin wii, le unii mɔk gor ubaa pu. Ubaa mu aan fii buen butɔb yaan, ba pu? Uwumbɔr aaŋuul ga dan unii mɔmɔk pu mbaa la. Israel yaab aatunwanbir aatafadaan

ref: War, disease, and starvation are everywhere! People who live in the countryside will be killed in battle, and those who live in towns will die from starvation or deadly diseases.
text: Kijaak bi kitiŋ ponn ni, le iween ni nkon bi ŋidichal ni. Unii umɔk bi timoor ni na ga kpo kijaak ni la, le iween ni nkon ga ku umɔk bi kitiŋ ponn ni na.

ref: Anyone who survives will escape into the hills, like doves who leave the valleys to find safety. All of you will moan because of your sins.
text: Bibaa ga san buen ŋijoo ni ke ŋinanjel ŋi tiwan faani ŋi tifatann ni na la. Bi mɔmɔk ga li du baatunwanbir pu.

ref: Your hands will tremble, and your knees go limp.
text: Unii mɔk aaŋaal aan li pɔɔ, le bitaŋaayil ga li gbaa.

ref: You will put on sackcloth to show your sorrow, but terror will overpower you. Shame will be written all over your faces, and you will shave your heads in despair.
text: Bi ga peen tiwan ni saak kuub na, le biwon gbaa tɔtɔk. Biyil ga li ye ŋiyikun la, le bi mɔmɔk ga ji inimɔɔn.

ref: Your silver and gold will be thrown into the streets like garbage, because those are the two things that led you into sin, and now they cannot save you from my anger. They are not even worth enough to buy food.
text: Bi ga di baasalmaa ni tikunabr mae kitiŋ ponn ni ke timoor na; ba pu? baasalmaa ni tikunabr aan ŋmaa gaa bi lii buyoonn Uwumbɔr di waaŋuusakpeln lii ni bi pu na. Baan ŋmaa di ni kuln baakpeek, bee bi di ni gbiin bipuu. Salmaa ni tikunabr le di bi koon titunwanbir ponn ni.

ref: You took great pride in using your beautiful jewelry to make disgusting idols of foreign gods. So I will make your jewelry worthless.
text: N‑yoonn mubaa bi nan kpa kigaak baatakpanyaan pu la, le bi di ŋi ŋa ŋiwaa ŋi sukr ponn ni na. Nima le cha Uwumbɔr cha baawangol sukr biponn ni.

ref: Your whole country is in confusion! Murder and violence are everywhere in Israel,
text: “Tiwan mɔmɔk gur bi yɔl yɔl la, le linikul gbii kitiŋ pu, le ntim ponn ni ye mbimbin mu pɔɔ na ŋmeen.

ref: so I will tell the most wicked nations to come and take over your homes. They will put an end to the pride you have in your strong army, and they will make your places of worship unfit to use.
text: M ga cha ŋitimbol ŋi tun titunwanbir sakpen na dan do ki nan gaa nimi aadichal. M yaa cha ŋitimbol ngbaan bii naah dooni nimi aawaa ŋi na kan, nimi aajab bi pɔɔ sakpen na aawon ga yɔl.

ref: You will be terrified and will desperately look for peace—but there will be no peace.
text: Tibɔbir choo, le ni ga li ban nsuudoon, kaan kan.

ref: One tragedy will follow another, and you'll hear only bad news. People will beg prophets to give them a message from me. Priests will stop teaching my Law, and wise leaders won't be able to give advice.
text: Tibɔbir tibaa ga dan, le tiken paan ni ti pu, le tibɔbir ga li puu fuur ni nimi ke nkpen aah puu pu na. Ni ga gaŋ maabɔnabtiib ke bi tuk nimi baah kan tibɔr ti ga dan ni pu na. Bitotoorb aan li kpa nibaa bi di mɔk binib, le bininkpiib aan li kpa nsurm mubaa bi tii.

ref: Even your king and his officials will lose hope and cry in despair. Your hands will tremble with fear. I will punish you for your sins and treat you the same way you have treated others. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: Ubɔr ga wii ikpowiil, le kitiŋ aayidaan aamakl ga wɔŋ, le binib aawon ga li gbaa ijawaan pu. M ga daa nitafal naah tun pu na pu, le ki ji nimi tibɔr naah ji biken tibɔr pu na. Nimina le ga mɔk nimi ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.” LELEE AABƆKPIIRKAAN (Esekiel

ref: Six years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the leaders of Judah were meeting with me in my house. On the fifth day of the sixth month, the Lord God suddenly took control of me,
text: Timi aanaagbiir aabiloloob ni aaŋmaloob aawinŋmu daal, le m ni binaagbiib ngbaan aasalolm nan ka maadichal ni. Libuul ngbaan ni le Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn dan nan gbiin mi.

ref: and I saw something in the shape of a human. This figure was like fire from the waist down, and it was bright as polished metal from the waist up.
text: M nan waan lik paacham, le ki kan unibɔn aabimbin aajawaan aawan nibaa. Ki nyan uchaŋ mɔk ki di sunn taab na, uwon nan naahn mmii la, le ki nyan uchaŋ mɔk ki di jon paab na, uwon nan moor lak lak ke baah jɔŋ tikumann ti mbamɔm na.

ref: It reached out what seemed to be a hand and grabbed my hair. Then in my vision the Lord's Spirit lifted me into the sky and carried me to Jerusalem. The Spirit took me to the north gate of the temple's inner courtyard, where there was an idol that disgusted the Lord and made him furious.
text: U nan taln tiwan ni naahn ŋŋaal na ki di chuu maayikpir. Le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan yoor mi paacham ki di mi buen Jerusalem aatiŋ ni. U nan di mi buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal aabisamɔb mu bi ponn ni, ki bi ŋŋangan wɔb nin chee liwaal li fiini Uwumbɔr aaŋuul sakpen na si na.

ref: Then I saw the brightness of the glory of the God of Israel, just as I had seen it near the Chebar River.
text: Nima chee le m kan nwiihn mu deer ŋinimbil ki mɔk ke Israel Aawumbɔr bi nima chee na, ke maah nan kan pu Kebar Aamɔɔl chee na.

ref: God said to me, “Ezekiel, son of man, look north.” And when I did, I saw that repulsive idol by the altar near the gate.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke, “Unibɔn, lik aaŋangan wɔb.” M nan lik, le ki kan ke liwaal li fiini Uwumbɔr aaŋuul sakpen na si gbɔk kitork aabimbiln li bi mbisamɔb ngbaan chee na.

ref: God then said, “Do you see the terrible sins of the people of Israel? Their sins are making my holy temple unfit as a place to worship me. Yet you will see even worse things than this.”
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke, “Unibɔn, aa kan tiwan ni bi ŋani na aa? Lik Israel aanib aah ŋani tiwan ni sukr ponn ni do pu, ki moo jenni mi maabuul li bi chain na chee na. Aa ga kan inimɔɔn aawan ni jer nimina na.”

ref: Next, I was taken to the entrance of the courtyard, where I saw a hole in the wall.
text: U nan di mi nyan ni lichinjal aabisamɔb chee, le ki mɔk mi liboln libaa ligoln ni.

ref: God said, “Make this hole bigger.” And when I did, I realized it was a doorway.
text: U nan ki bui ke, “Unibɔn, wii ligoln ngbaan do chee na.” M nan wii li nima chee, le ki kan jaaleŋ ubaa.

ref: “Go in,” God said, “and see what horrible and evil things the people are doing.”
text: U nan ki bui mi ke, “Koo ki ti lik titunwanbir, ni tiwan ni sukr ponn ni aan bi bi ŋani na.”

ref: Inside, I saw that the walls were covered with pictures of reptiles and disgusting, unclean animals, as well as with idols that the Israelites were worshiping.
text: M nan buen ki ti lik. Bi nan naan ikuub ni tiwakor ti kɔ na ŋmeen, ni Israel yaab aah dooni tiwan niken ni na ŋmeen le gbiin ŋigon ngbaan pu.

ref: Seventy Israelite leaders were standing there, including Jaazaniah son of Shaphan. Each of these leaders was holding an incense burner, and the smell of incense filled the room.
text: Israel yaab aasalolm imonko itaa ni kipiik le nan ka nima; Safann aajapɔɔn Jaasania mu nan bi bi ni. Bi mɔmɔk ubaabaa nan ka joo baah joo nnyɔknii seer tiwan ni ponn ni na, le nnyɔknii aaŋmanyuu fii paacham.

ref: God said, “Ezekiel, do you see what horrible things Israel's leaders are doing in secret? They have filled their rooms with idols. And they say I can't see them, because they think I have already deserted Israel.
text: Uwumbɔr nan baa mi ke, “Unibɔn, aa kan Israel yaab aah looni ki tun ŋitun ŋi libɔɔl ni na aa? Bi mɔmɔk bi kidiik ki ponn ni ye ŋiwaa ŋmeen na, le ki dooni ŋi. Baah len pu na le ye ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aa waa timi. Waa ki bi timi aatiŋ pu.’”

ref: He took me to the north gate of the temple, where I saw women mourning for the god Tammuz.
text: Kina pu na, u nan di mi buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal aaŋangan wɔb aabisamɔb chee ki ti mɔk mi bipiib bi ka wii liwaal Tamus aakpuul na.

ref: God asked me, “Can you believe what these women are doing? But now I want to show you something even worse.”
text: U nan baa mi ke, “Unibɔn, aa kan aa? Aa ga ki kan ŋitun ŋi sukr ponn ni ki jer kina na.”

ref: God said, “Ezekiel, it's bad enough that the people of Judah are doing these disgusting things. But they have also spread violence and injustice everywhere in Israel and have made me very angry. They have disgraced and insulted me in the worst possible way.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki baa mi ke, “Unibɔn, aa kan aa? Juda aanib bimina aa lik faar baah tun ŋitun ŋi sukr ponn ni, ni baah tun mbimbinpɔɔl aatun ŋi kitiŋ kee pu na. Baa lik faar kina, see bi dan nan tun ŋi Maadichal mu ni, ki moo fiini maaŋuul. Lik baah pɔɔn bibaa ki seei mi ŋisiibil ŋi wu sakpen na pu na.

ref: So in my fierce anger, I will punish them without mercy and refuse to help them when they cry out to me.”
text: Bi ga kan maaŋuul aah pɔɔ pu na mɔmɔk. Maan san bi kinimbaak, kaan di cha pinn bi mu. Bi ga li tar mpɔɔn pu sakpen ki mee mi limeel, le maan gar bi.”

ref: After that, I heard the Lord shout, “Come to Jerusalem, you men chosen to destroy the city. And bring your weapons!”
text: M nan ŋun Uwumbɔr teen mpɔɔn pu ke, “Nimi bijab bi ga daa kitiŋ ngbaan aatafal na, dan do man. Li joo ni nimi aajawan man.”

ref: I saw six men come through the north gate of the temple, each one holding a deadly weapon. A seventh man dressed in a linen robe was with them, and he was carrying things to write with. The men went into the temple and stood by the bronze altar.
text: Libuul ngbaan ni le bijab biloob nyan ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal aapaal aabisamɔb mu bi ŋŋangan wɔb na ni, ubaa mɔk joo tijawan. Uja ubaa nan pee ŋitanyaan aawanpeenkaan ki ŋmal bi ni, ki joo tiwan ni u ga di ŋmee na. Bi mɔmɔk nan dan, le ki nan sil tikumann aatork aabimbiln na chee.

ref: The brightness of God's glory then left its place above the statues of the winged creatures inside the temple and moved to the entrance. The Lord said to the man in the linen robe,
text: Le Israel yaab Aawumbɔr aawiihn mu deer ŋinimbil na fii mu aah ba bi ifeen aawan chee ni na paacham, ki di buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal aabisamɔb chee. Uwumbɔr nan yin uja u pee ŋitanyaan aawanpeenkaan na ki nan bui u ke,

ref: “Walk through the city of Jerusalem and mark the forehead of anyone who is truly upset and sad about the terrible things that are being done here.”
text: “Koo Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni, ki daan unii umɔk aasui bii aan ni muk u baah tun ŋitun ŋi sukr ponn ni kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni na aayigbeer pu kidaan.”

ref: He turned to the other six men and said, “Follow him and put to death everyone who doesn't have a mark on their forehead. Show no mercy or pity! Kill men and women, parents and children. Begin here at my temple, but be sure not to harm those who are marked.” The men immediately killed the leaders who were standing there.
text: Ku bijaninkpiib, ni binachipɔm, ni bipiisapɔm, ni bipiib bi joo mbim na, ni mbim man. Ni taa meeh unii umɔk kpa kidaan uyigbeer pu na. Piin Maadichal ni do man.” Kina pu na, bi nan di bisalolm bi si Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni nima chee na le piin.

ref: Then the Lord said, “Pollute the temple by piling the dead bodies in the courtyards. Now get busy!” They left and started killing the people of Jerusalem.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “Koor Maadichal aakoobil man. Cha ŋinikpol gbiin laachiln man. Piin lituln man.” Kina pu na, bi nan piin ki bi ku binib, kitiŋ ngbaan ni.

ref: I was then alone, so I bowed down and cried out to the Lord, “Why are you doing this? Are you so angry with the people of Jerusalem that everyone must die?”
text: Baah bi ku binib kina na, m nan si nima mbaa baanja la. M nan tar lir kitiŋ lichichikr le ki teen ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, saaŋuul fii Jerusalem aatiŋ pu sakpen le aa ban aa ku unii umɔk gur Israel aatiŋ pu na aa?”

ref: The Lord answered, “The people of Israel and Judah have done horrible things. Their country is filled with murderers, and Jerusalem itself is filled with violence. They think that I have deserted them, and that I can't see what they are doing.
text: Uwumbɔr nan gar ke, “Israel aanib ni Juda aanib aabɔr gbii titunwanbir ti bir sakpen na. Bi ku binib kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu, le ki di libiil gbiin Jerusalem aatiŋ ni. Bi bui ke min Uwumbɔr yii baatiŋ, kaa ki waa bi.

ref: And so I will not have pity on them or forgive them. They will be punished for what they have done.”
text: Maan san bi kinimbaak, m ga ŋa bi baah ŋa biken pu na.”

ref: Just then, the man in the linen robe returned and said, “I have done what you commanded.”
text: Uja u nan pee ŋitanyaan aawan na nan gir ni ki nan tuk Uwumbɔr ke, “M tun saah mɔk mi pu na doo a.”

ref: I saw the dome that was above the four winged creatures, and on it was the sapphire throne.
