text: Ki ni kibisatiib nan kpa kigaak baah kpa tijikaar sakpen bi ji pu na pu, aan ki bi nsuudoon, ni lifuur ni na pu; bitafal mu aa nan tee bi bigiim ni binib bi lann na ponn ni.

ref: They thought they were better than everyone else, and they did things I hate. And so I destroyed them.
text: Bi nan kpa kigaak ni tafalaaŋun, le ki ŋani tiwan ni sukr ponn ni na m chee, kina pu le m nan kuln bi, saah nyi pu na.

ref: You people of Jerusalem have sinned twice as much as the people of Samaria. In fact, your evil ways have made both Sodom and Samaria look innocent.
text: “Samaria aatiŋ aa nan tun saah tun titunwanbir ti na aageln libaa. Aa tun ŋitun ŋi sukr ponn ni ki jer Samaria aatiŋ aah nan tun pu na pel pel. Saatun yɔl yɔl ngbaan cha aanaabitiib bi aa chee ke baah kaa tun taani kpala le na.

ref: So their punishment will seem light compared to yours. You will be disgraced and put to shame because of your disgusting sins. Jerusalem Will Be Ashamed The Lord said to Jerusalem:
text: Ni ŋeer ke aa gaa saanimɔɔn. Saatunwanbir ti nyaŋ sakpen na pu le aanaabitiib bi aa chee ke baah kaa tun taani kpala le na. Li joo saanimɔɔn ki cha i koo aasil, ba pu? aa cha aanaabitiib gur naahn bi bi chain na la.” Sodom ni Samaria aatim aah ga ki gir maa pu na

ref: Someday I will bless Sodom and Samaria and their nearby villages. I will also bless you, Jerusalem.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui Jerusalem aatiŋ ke, “M ga ki tii Sodom ni kaatimbim, ni Samaria ni kaatimbim liwangol. Mbamɔn, m ga tii aa mu liwangol.

ref: Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you.
text: Inimɔɔn ga chuu si, le saanimɔɔn ga mɔk aanaabitiib baah soor si pu na.

ref: When that day comes, you and Sodom and Samaria will once again be well-off, and all nearby villages will be restored.
text: Bi ga ki kan liwangol, le aa ni saatimbim mu ga gir maa.

ref: Jerusalem, you were so arrogant that you sneered at Sodom.
text: Saah nan kpa kigaak buyoonn na, aa nan ŋani Sodom aatiŋ mbɔnyun,

ref: But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks.
text: waahr aan saah nan tun titunwanbir ti na nin nyan mpaan pu. Aa mu gur bi ke kima na la, aa gur ye mbɔnyun aatiŋ le Edom yaab, ni Filistia yaab, ni ntim mu bi gbɔk si kaa gee si na chee.

ref: You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem The Lord said:
text: Aa ga ji kininsuŋ ni tiwan ni sukr ponn ni aa tun na aafalaa.” Uwumbɔr le len kina. Tipuur ti bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na

ref: But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever.
text: Saah nan laa diin aan m puu tipuur kpaan ti tii si na, m ga gbiin ti, le m ni si ki puu tipuur ti ga li bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na tii tɔb.

ref: When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement.
text: Aa yaa nan ki gaa aakpel ni aanaal kan, aa ga teer saah nan tun pu na le inimɔɔn chuu si. M ga cha bi li bi ke bisatiib na le ki tii si, kina mu aa nan bi maapuur kpaan ti m nan puu tii si na ni.

ref: I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord.
text: M ga ki gir fikr tipuur ti m nan puu tii si na, le aa bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.

ref: I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: M ga di cha pinn si saah tun taani u mɔmɔk na, aa mu tee ga teer taani ngbaan bɔr, le inimɔɔn ga chuu si sakpen, le saan ki ŋmaa waar aamɔb.” Aadindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story,
text: “Unibɔn, ŋakl Israel yaab liyataŋakl limina,

ref: so they will understand what I am saying to them: A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree,
text: ke bi bee ke min le ye Bidindaan Uwumbɔr le ki tuk bi ke: Likaagiil sakpeln libaa le nan bi ki kpa tikokor ti ŋan sakpen na, le laafeen filk ki pee. Li nan fii buen Lebanonn Aajoo ni le ki ti bar santina aabonja aapaachapaacham,

ref: then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities.
text: le ki di buen kitiŋ ki ponn ni bi kooh tiwan na, ki ti di ni bil biwankoob aatiŋ kibaa ni.

ref: The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream.
text: Li nan ban busub bu laa punn na Israel aatiŋ pu, le ki ti di bu ŋum bukpaab bu aatiŋ nyuun, aan nnyun bi ki ga cha bu muun na ponn ni.

ref: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
text: Busub ngbaan nan filk, ki ye ndaan aasubil aasub bu kaa fɔk ki taln ni mɔmɔk na. Bu aapan nan too paacham ki lik likaagiil ngbaan, le inyaan mu koo kitiŋ mbamɔm. Bu nan kpa ŋipan ni tifar sakpen.

ref: There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil.
text: “Likaagiil sakpeln libaa mu nan ki bi, ki kpa ifeen i filk na, ni tikokor sakpen. Le ndaan aasubil aasub ngbaan nan fenn bu aanyaan, ni bu aafar toŋ likaagiil leler na wɔb, ki dak ke li ga ŋmaa tii bu nnyun sakpen ki jer bu aah si nkpaakon mu ponn ni na.

ref: But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
text: Tɔ, bu mu nan puun si kitiŋ ki nyuun na ni la, le nnyun bi mbamɔm ke bu ŋa tifar, ki lu ŋisubil, ki li ye busukpaam.

ref: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
text: “Le min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr baa ke: ndaan aasubil aasub ngbaan ga li bi ki ŋa busub aa? Njan aakaagiil na aan nan daa ŋɔb bu, ki ker ŋaasubil lir, ki kool kool ŋaapan, ki cha ŋi yɔl aa? Naan li pɔɔ, kaan li pɔɔ ke litimbol li kaa pɔɔ na nan ŋɔb bu lii.

ref: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
text: Mbamɔn, bi ŋum bu a, tɔ, bu ga li bi ki ŋa busub aa? Liwipuul wɔb aabuln yaa daa bu pu kan, bu aan yɔl aa? Bu aan yɔl bu aah si nin chee na aa?” Liyataŋakl ngbaan aatataa aah ye pu na

ref: The Lord said:
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke,

ref: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
text: “Baa bimɔyiib ngbaan ke liyataŋakl ngbaan aatataa ye kinye. Bui bi ke Babiloŋ aabɔr dan Jerusalem aatiŋ ni ki nan yoor Jerusalem aabɔr ni waaninkpiib ki di buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni.

ref: He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens,
text: U nan yoor ubɔr aadichal ni aanii ubaa, le ki cha bi ŋa kimɔbaan, ki cha u puu ke u ga li dii u mbamɔm. U nan chur kaanikpaam buen,

ref: so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
text: ke kitiŋ ngbaan aanib taa ŋmaa nya upuwɔb, ki cha bi li joo kimɔbaan ngbaan mbamɔm.

ref: But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
text: Juda aabɔr nan nyan upuwɔb, le ki buen Ijipt aabɔr chee ti ban itaan, ni butɔb aajab bi wiir na. U ga nyaŋ aa? U ga ŋmaa nya tibɔr ngbaan ni ii? Waan ŋmaa bii kimɔbaan ngbaan kaa kan ntafadaan.”

ref: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “Maah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu, ubɔr ngbaan aah bii waah puu tipuur ti na, ni kimɔbaan ki u ni Babiloŋ aabɔr u di u kaan nnaan na nan ŋa na, u ga kpo Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni.

ref: Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people.
text: Hali Ijipt aatɔb aajab ni baapɔɔnsakpiin aan ŋmaa ter u, u jan Babiloŋ yaab buyoonn bi maa maa ŋibimbin tam Jerusalem aagon ki gbii ŋibuu ke bi ku binib pam na.

ref: The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
text: U bii waah puu tipuur ti na, ni kimɔbaan ki u nan ŋa na. U ŋa tiwan nimina mɔmɔk, le waan ŋmar.”

ref: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Maah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu, m ga daa utafal waah di maayimbil puu tipuur ke u ga joo kimɔbaan ki, ki ki bii ki na pu.

ref: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
text: M ga taln ukpan aapɔɔk ki di chuu u. Waah kaa ŋani maah tuk u pu na pu, m ga di u buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni ki ti daa utafal.

ref: His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Waajab bi nyi butɔb aabɔr mbamɔm na ga bee butɔb ni, le bi ŋmar na ga yaa koo ŋipepel mɔmɔk ni, le ni ga bee ke min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Uwumbɔr aah puu ke limakl bi pu na

ref: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na sɔ: “M ga chuu koo santina aasub bu fɔk na aapaacham, ki chuu koo naah laa bi tukni pu na; m ga ti di ni ŋum lijool li fɔk na aapaacham,

ref: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
text: m ga ti ŋum ni Israel aajool li fɔk jer ŋijoo mɔmɔk na pu. Ni ga ŋa ŋipan ki lu ŋisubil ki kpaln santina sakpiin. Inyoon mɔmɔk aabɔŋ ga li koo bu ni, ki kan lifuur bu aaboon ni.

ref: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
text: Isui i mɔmɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu na ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. Min le ga gaa geei isui i fɔk na, ki cha i kaa fɔk na muun ki li fɔk. Min le ga kuur isusoon ki cha isukuun fikr ki bunn. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina. M ga ŋa maah bui ke m ga ŋa pu na.”

ref: The Lord said:
text: Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr,

ref: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
text: ki bui ke, “Binib aah ŋakl liyataŋakl li ki gir ŋakl Israel aatiŋ pu na ye ba aayataŋakl? ‘Tetiib le ŋman ŋisubil ŋi mɔɔn na, le ni nan tee mɔɔn baabim aamɔi ni.’”

ref: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “Maah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu, naan ki ŋakl liyataŋakl ngbaan Israel aatiŋ pu.

ref: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
text: Unii mɔmɔk aamɔfal ye min yaan la, min le yeh tetiib ni natiib, ni baabim aamɔfal. Unii u tun titunwanbir na, uma le ga kpo.

ref: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
text: “Uninyaan bamɔnn u si chob na yaa ba bi kan,

ref: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
text: waa ba ga li dooni Israel yaab aawaa, kaan ŋmɔ tiwaachur ni aatork aanann. Waan di kimɔmɔɔn gaa uken aapuu, kaan doon upii u bi waapiir ni na chee.

ref: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
text: Waa pinni ŋimombil tii unii ki ban tinyoor. U yiil titunwanbir aatum, le ki len ibamɔn kinikpakpak mɔk ni.

ref: and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
text: Kina aanii joo maah mɔk pu na ki joo maakaal mbamɔm. U ye unii u aabimbin ŋan na, le ki ga li kpa limɔfal;” kina le Dindaan Uwumbɔr len.

ref: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
text: “Kina aaja yaa kpa japɔɔn u su kinaayuk, ki ku binib, ki ŋani tiwan

ref: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
text: ni ute aa kee ŋa na; u ji tiwaachur ni aatork aajikaar, ki joo kimɔmɔɔn gaal biken aapuutiib.

ref: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
text: U ji bigiim pem pem, ki su kinaayuk; unii yaa pinn u chee ŋimombil ki di waawan nibaa siin lipɔln ngbaan pu kan, waa joo giini. U chaa tiwaachur ni, ki dooni ŋiwaa ŋi sukr ponn ni na,

ref: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
text: ki pinni ŋimombil tii binib ki gaal tinyoor. U ga li kpa limɔfal aa? Aayii, waan li kpa. U tun ŋitun ŋi sukr ponn ni na mɔmɔk, kina pu na, u ga kpo. Uma le ku ubaa.

ref: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
text: “Nibaakan, uja leler umina yaa kpa japɔɔn u kani ute aah tun titunwanbir ti mɔmɔk na, ki mu aa dii ute ngbaan aasan:

ref: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
text: waa dooni Israel yaab aawaa, kaa ŋmɔ tiwaachur ni aatork aanann. Waa joo kimɔmɔɔn gaal uja uken aapuu,

ref: He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor
text: kaa muk ubaa, kaa su ubaa aawan. U giini unii u pinn u chee ŋimombil ki di waawan siin ŋi pu na tii uwandaan. U kpiini nkon aah joo bi na, ki tii binib bi chuun biŋmeen na tiwanpeenkaan.

ref: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
text: U yiil, kaa tun titunwanbir, ki pinni ŋimombil tii binib, kaa ban tinyoor. U joo maakaal, ki dii maah mɔk pu na. Waan kpo ute aatunwanbir pu, u ga li kpa limɔfal.

ref: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
text: “Tɔ, le ni baa ke: ‘Ba ŋa ubo ngbaan aa ji ute aatunwanbir aafalaa?’ Ni ye le ke ujapɔɔn ngbaan tun ni ŋan ki tok na la. U joo maakaal ki dii i mbamɔm, kina pu na, u ga li kpa limɔfal.

ref: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
text: Unii u tun titunwanbir na, uma le ga kpo. Japɔɔn aan ji falaa ute aatunwanbir pu, le te mu aan ji falaa ujapɔɔn aatunwanbir pu. Uninyaan ga kan tipar waatunyaan pu, le titunwanbirdaan mu ga ji falaa waah tun titunwanbir ti na pu.

ref: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
text: “Titunwanbirdaan yaa di cha titunwanbir aatum ki joo maakaal, ki yaa tun ni ŋan ki tok na kan, waan kpo; u ga sil li kpa limɔfal.

ref: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
text: M ga di waatunwanbir mɔmɔk cha pinn u, le u ga li kpa limɔfal, waah tun ni ŋan na pu na pu.”

ref: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr baa ke, “Ni dak ke titunwanbirdaan yaa kpo kan, ni mɔ mi la aa? Aayii, m ga li gee ke u ba kpeln waabimbin ki li bi.

ref: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
text: “Tɔ, uninyaan yaa di cha waatunyaan aatum ki piin ki tun titunwanbirdam aatun ŋi mɔmɔk sukr ponn ni na kan, u ga li beenin kpa limɔfal aa? Aayii. Maan ki teer waatunyaan na mɔmɔk libaa bɔr. U ga kpo waah kaa dii maamɔkm pu na ni waatunwanbir pu la.

ref: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
text: Uninyaan yaa di cha litunyaan aatum ki piin ki tun titunwanbir ki yaa kpo kan, waatunwanbir ngbaan pu le u kpo.

ref: And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
text: Titunwanbirdaan yaa di cha titunwanbir aatum, ki piin ki tun ni ŋan na kan, u gaa waamɔfal la.

ref: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
text: U bee waah tun pu na, le ki di cha titunwanbir aatum, kina pu le waan kpo, u ga li kpa limɔfal.

ref: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
text: Nimi Israel yaab le len ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aah ŋani pu na aa ŋan.’ Ni dak ke maah tun maatuln pu na aa ŋan, naa ye kina aa? Nimi le aah tun pu na aa ŋan.

ref: I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished.
text: “Tɔ, min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le tuk nimi Israel yaab ke m ga ji ni mɔmɔk tibɔr udaan aah tun pu na la. Fenn nipuwɔb tii nimi aatunwanbir ti mɔmɔk ni tun na ki taa cha nimi aatunwanbir kuln nimi.

ref: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
text: Di cha titunwanbir ti mɔmɔk ni tun na man, ki ban isuupɔɔn, ni ilandak pɔɔn tii nibaa. Ba ŋa nimi Israel yaab ban ke ni kpo?

ref: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
text: Min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le len ke maa ban ke ubaa kpo. Fenn nipuwɔb tii nimi aatunwanbir ki li bi man.”

ref: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui ke m gaa mpombiin aalahn mumina tii Israel aabɔrbim bilee:

ref: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
text: Aana nan ye uchinnpiikpaan le ichinn ni. U nan kpiin waabim ichinnja i bir na aakaasisik ni la.

ref: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
text: U nan kpiin waabo ubaa, le ki mɔk u kikpaŋ; u nan kpaln uchinn u ŋmɔ binib na la.

ref: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
text: Ŋitimbol nan ŋun u pu, le ki di libugeln pen chuu u. Bi nan di ijapiin le dar u buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni.

ref: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
text: Una nan gur ka kii u, le ki ti bee ke waamakl doo a. Le u nan ki kpiin ubo uken, le uma di ŋa uchinn u bir sakpen na.

ref: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
text: Ŋitimbol nan kuun ke ŋi faa u butɔb; binib nan nyan ni ŋipepel mɔmɔk ki dan. Bi nan taln baapɔr ti bi joo chur tinann na, le ki di ti chuu u.

ref: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
text: Bi nan di u ŋa dakaa u kpa ŋibon na ni, le ki di u buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ aabɔr chee. Bi nan ti kii u nima chee ke bi taa ki ŋun waaŋuun pu Israel aagongon pu daalbaadaal.

ref: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
text: Aana nan naahn ndaan aasubil aasub bu si gbɔk nkpen na la. Nnyun aah bi sakpen na, bu nan kpa tifar ni ŋisubil pam.

ref: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
text: Bu aapan nan pɔɔ pam, le ki muun ki ti ŋa bibɔrb aajaangbeedabil. Busub ngbaan nan muun sakpen ki ti koo ntaalangbam ni; unii mɔmɔk nan waa bu aah fɔk ki kpa tifar sakpen pu na.

ref: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
text: Tɔ, liŋuul aaŋaal nan daa ŋɔb bu, ki di bu mee bil kitiŋ. Liwipuul wɔb aabuln nan daa kuur bu aasubil. Bi nan bar bar bu aapan, le ŋi kuur aan bi di tuur mmii.

ref: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
text: Tɔ, bu gur si nteersakpiin ni la, kitiŋ ki kuun kaa kpa nnyun na ni.

ref: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
text: Mmii nan gaa bu aasupuul. Mmii wun bu aapan ni ŋisubil. Ŋipan ngbaan aan ki pɔɔk daalbaadaal, kaan ki ŋmaa ŋa bibɔrb aajaangbeedabil. Mpombiin aalahn sɔ; bi gaa mu, le ki gir gaa.

ref: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
text: Timi aanaagbiir aabilolole ni aaŋmaŋmu aawiin kipiik daal, le Israel yaab aasalolm bibaa nan dan m chee ke bi nan baa ki bee Uwumbɔr aageehn, le ki nan kal nnimbiin ni.

ref: Just then, the Lord God said:
text: Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
text: U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, len bijab bimina chee tibɔr ki bui ke Bidindaan Uwumbɔr len ke: Ni dan ke ni nan bee maageehn la, naa ye kina aa? Maah ye Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu, maan cha ni baa mi tibaa. Min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
text: Tuk bi maah bi len pu na. Maah nan lee Israel aanibol na, m nan puu tipuur tii bi. M nan di mbaa mɔk bi, Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki bui bi ke: Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.

ref: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le m nan puu ke m ga nyan bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni ki di buen kitiŋ ki kpa tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan ni ŋisubil sakpen na, kitiŋ ki ŋan jer ntim mɔmɔk aan m nyan ke m di tii bi na pu.

ref: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
text: M nan bui bi ke maah ye Bidindaan Uwumbɔr pu na, bi di baah gee ŋiwaa ŋi aan ŋi sukr ponn ni na mee, ki taa di Ijipt aawaa na bii bibaa.

ref: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
text: Tɔ, bi nan lik mi fam ki yii; baan ŋun tii mi. Baa nan di ŋiwaa ŋi sukr ponn ni na ngbaan mee, kaa di cha Ijipt yaab aawaa na mu. Ijipt aatiŋ ni, le m nan gor ke m cha bi bee maaŋuul aah pɔɔ pu na.

ref: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
text: Kina ngbaan aah ba ga nan joo ni maayimbibiil na, maa nan ŋa kina, ba pu? baah nan koo binib bi chee na aanimbil ni le m nan bui Israel yaab ngbaan ke m ga nyan bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni.

ref: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
text: “Kina pu na, m nan di bi nyan Ijipt aatiŋ ni ki di bi koo nteersakpiin ni.

ref: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
text: M nan tuk bi maah ban bi li bi pu na, ki mɔk bi maakaal i tii unii umɔk gaa i ki kii na limɔfal na.

ref: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
text: M nan cha Likpaakool daal aajoom le ye m ni bima aaseeraa, ki li teer bi ke min Uwumbɔr bi chain la.

ref: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
text: Tɔ, nteersakpiin ni, nima chee le bi kpaan yii maamɔb. Bi bii maakaal, le ki yii maamɔkm mu tii unii umɔk gaa mu ki kii na limɔfal na. Bi nan bii Likpaakool daal aajoom pel pel. M nan gor nteersakpiin ni nima ke m cha bi bee maaŋuul aah pɔɔ pu na ki kuln bi.

ref: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
text: Maa nan ŋa kina; ba pu? kina ba ga nan joo ni maayimbibiil, ŋitimbol ŋi kan maah di Israel yaab nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni pu na chee.

ref: Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised.
text: Kina pu le m nan puu tii bi nteersakpiin ni nima chee, ke maan di bi fuu kitiŋ ki kpa tiwakor aamoŋmɔpaan ni ŋisubil sakpen na ki ŋan jer ntim mɔmɔk aan m di tii bi na ni.

ref: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
text: Baah yii maamɔkm, ki bii maakaal, ki koor Likpaakool daal aajoom, ki tee gee baawaa aadoon na pu le m nan puu kina.

ref: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
text: “Tɔ, m nan tee san bi kinimbaak. M nan yii ke maan ku bi nteersakpiin ni nima.

ref: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
text: M nan tee sak binib bi nan laa diin ki bi bi ponn ni na ke: Taa li joo ikaal i niyaajatiib ŋa na; taa dii baakaal man, ki taa di baawaa bii nibaa.

ref: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
text: Min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr. Li joo maakaal ni maamɔkm man.

ref: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
text: Di Likpaakool daal ŋa nimi aafuur daal man, aan ni li ye seeraa taah ŋa kimɔbaan ki na pu, ki li teer nimi ke min le ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr.

ref: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
text: “Tɔ, bima ngbaan aaker mu nan ki yii maamɔb. Bi nan bii maakaal, kaa joo maamɔkm mu tii unii umɔk gaa mu ki kii na limɔfal na. Bi nan bii Likpaakool daal aajoom. Nteersakpiin ni, nima chee, le m nan gor ke bi bee maaŋuul aah pɔɔ pu na, ki kuln bi mɔmɔk.

ref: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
text: Tɔ, maa nan ŋa kina, ba pu? kina ngbaan ba ga nan joo ni maayimbibiil, ŋitimbol ŋi kan maah di Israel yaab nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni pu na chee.

ref: So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations,
text: Kina pu na, m nan ki puu tipuur tiken tii bi nteersakpiin ni, nima chee. M nan puu timm ke m ga cha bi yaa koo dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni.

ref: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
text: Baah yii maamɔkm, ki bii maakaal, ki koor Likpaakool daal aajoom, ki dooni ŋiwaabaan ŋi biyaajatiib nan dooni na pu le m nan ŋa kina.

ref: I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life,
text: “M nan ki di ikaal i kaa ŋan, ni mmɔkm mu kaa tii limɔfal na le tii bi.

ref: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
text: M nan cha bi di bibaa aatork le bii bibaa, le ki cha bi di baajan aabijabim toor kitork tii ŋiwaa. Nimina le ga nan daa bitafal ki cha bi bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.

ref: Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me
text: “Tɔ, unibɔn, tuk Israel yaab ngbaan min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr aah tuk bi pu na. Bitetiib aah nan yii maasan ki sii mi na sɔ:

ref: by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them!
text: M nan di bi fuu ni kitiŋ ki m nan puu ke m ga di tii bi na pu. Baah kan ŋigongon ŋi paa na, ni isusoon na, le bi toor kitork ni mɔmɔk chee tii ŋiwaa. Bi nan cha maaŋuul fii kitork ki bi di see mmii ni na, ni ndaan mu bi nan joo nan tii ŋiwaa ipiin na pu.

ref: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
text: M nan baa bi ke: Naah chaa ŋibuu ŋi paa na paab na ye ba? Nima pu na, le bi gur yin ŋi ke, ‘Ŋibuu ŋi paa na’ ki nan saa din.

ref: by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer.
text: Hali din wee ni beenin tii ipiinbaan la, le ki joo nimi aabim toor kitork ki seer mmii ni tii ŋiwaabaan ŋi bi nan dii na, ki bii nibaa. Le nimi Israel yaab beenin choo ke ni nan baa ki bee maageehn aah ye pu na. Maah ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ki bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na pu, maan cha ni baa mi tibaa.

ref: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
text: Ni nan ŋa nimi aalandak ke ni li bi ke ŋitimbol ŋiken aanib bi koo ntim muken ni ki dooni isui ni ŋitakpal na. Tɔ, kina mu aan ŋa. Uwumbɔr dar binib aatafal le ki ki cha pinni mu

ref: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
text: “Maah ye Nidindaan Uwumbɔr ki bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, m sak nimi ke maaŋuul ponn ni, m ga di maapɔɔn joo nimi, aan ni li pɔɔ ni pu.

ref: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
text: M ga di nimi dan ‘Ŋitimbol Aateersakpiin’ ni, le ki nan daa nitafal.

ref: and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt.
text: Min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bui ke m ga daa nitafal ke maah nan daa nitetiib aatafal Sainai Aateersakpiin ni pu na.”

ref: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
text: “M ga chuu nimi ŋa ŋŋaal ni ki cha ni kii tii taah nan puu tipuur tii tɔb pu na.

ref: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: M ga nyan binib bi bi ni ponn ni ki ye bimɔyiib ni titunwanbirdam na. M ga nyan bi baah koo ntim mu ponn ni dandana na, ki mu aan cha bi gir ni Israel aatiŋ pu; le ni ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

ref: Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me!
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “Tɔ, nimi Israel yaab mɔmɔk, li ŋani naah gee pu na man. Li toor nimi aawaa man. Tɔ, ni mu tee li nyi ke nimina aapuwɔb na, see ni kii maamɔb, ki taa ki toor nimi aawaa le maayimbil aabiim doo.

ref: When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices.
text: Nimi Israel aanib mɔmɔk ga li dooni mi kitiŋ ngbaan pu, maajool li bi chain ki ye Israel aajool li paa na pu nima. M ga li gee nimi, le ni ga joo ni mi nimi aatork, ni nimi aapiinkpaan i bi chain na.

ref: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
text: M yaa nyan ni nimi maah cha ni yaa ki bi ntim mu ni na ki kuun nimi nan kpaan kan, n‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga gaa nimi aatork ki ni di see mmii ni tii mi na, le ŋitimbol ŋiken ga bee ke m ye chain la.

ref: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
text: M yaa nan giin ni nimi Israel aatiŋ ki m nan puu ke m ga di tii niyaajatiib na pu kan, le ni ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.

ref: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le ni ga teer naah nan dii pu ki ŋani tiwan ni tii nibaa tijɔŋ na bɔr. Le niponn ni ga li sukr nibaa pu, naah nan tun titunwanbir ti mɔmɔk na pu.

ref: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
text: M yaa nan fii sil ke m kiir maanyuŋ kan, nimi Israel yaab ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr, ba pu? maa ŋani nimi, nimi aabiin aatunwanbir aah ŋeer pu na.” Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina. Mmii mu bi ŋŋangii wɔb aapepel na aabɔr

ref: “Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests
text: “Unibɔn, lik ŋŋangii wɔb. Len tibɔbir ŋŋangii wɔb aapepel ni laachook pu.

ref: that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path.
text: Tuk ŋŋangii wɔb aachook ke ki li pel min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na ke: Lik, m piin mmii mubaa, le mu ga wu bususoom ni busukuum mɔmɔk aa ponn ni. Tiwan nibaa aan ŋmaa junn mu. Mu ga mar ki nya ŋŋangii wɔb ki ti saa ŋŋangan wɔb, le unii mɔmɔk ga ŋun mu aamiigaal aatoton pu.

ref: Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
text: Bi mɔmɔk ga bee ke min Uwumbɔr le see ki lii, le ubaa aan ŋmaa junn mu.”

ref: But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
text: Le min Esekiel nan bui ke, “Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, taa cha m len ti. Unii mɔmɔk puun len ke m len maabɔr ŋiyataŋak ponn ni la.”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
text: “Unibɔn, lik Jerusalem aatiŋ wɔb, ki len tibɔbir ŋibuu ŋi ponn ni binib dooni ŋiwaa na pu. Sak Israel aatiŋ

ref: that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil.
text: ke min Uwumbɔr len ke: M ye saadin la. M ga fuur maajaak aajuk ki ku ni mɔmɔk, bi ŋan na ni bi kaa ŋan na mɔmɔk.

ref: knowing that my sword will never be put away.
text: Unii mɔmɔk ga bee ke min Uwumbɔr le fuur maajaak aajuk, kaan ki di ki fuu.

ref: When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise! A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
text: Bi yaa baa si ke ba ŋa aa du kan, aa bui bi ke tibɔchann ti choo na pu le aa du. Ti yaa nan fuu ni kan, ijawaan ga gbiin bisui, biŋaal ga yɔl ki jɔnn, baajakaab ga wɔŋ, le bitaŋaayil ga li gbaa. N‑yoonn ngbaan fuu ni a; mu fuu ni do a.” Aadindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: The Lord said:
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui mi ke,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem: I have sharpened my sword to slaughter you; it is shiny and will flash like lightning! Don't celebrate— punishment is coming, because everyone has ignored my warnings.
text: Bi luun ki ke ki ku la, ki duun ki ke ki li moor lak lak. Mmɔɔn aan li bi, ba pu? maanib yii nsurm ni ntafadaan mɔmɔk.

ref: Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel; the sword is drawn against my people and their leaders. They will die! So give up all hope.
text: Unibɔn, wii mpɔɔn pu; Kijaak aajuk kimina ga ku maanib Israel yaab aasalolm mɔmɔk la. Ki ga ku maanib ni baasalolm mɔmɔk. Li gbaa aabiŋ mpombiin pu.

ref: I am testing my people, and they can do nothing to stop me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: M bi tɔŋni maanib la, le bi yaa yii kaan kpeln kan, bi ga kan tibɔbir ngbaan mɔmɔk.

ref: Ezekiel, warn my people, then celebrate my victory by clapping your hands. My vicious sword will attack again and again, killing my people with every stroke.
text: “Tɔ, unibɔn, nabr maabɔr. Kpaar aaŋaal ki cha kijaak aajuk ngbaan gaa, ki gir gaa. Ki ye kijaak aajuk ki ku na la, ki ye kijaak aajuk ki faani sakpen ki kɔr na la.

ref: They will lose all courage and stumble with fear. My slaughtering sword is waiting at every gate, flashing and ready to kill.
text: Ki cha maanib aataakpab yɔl, le bi lir. M joo kijaak aajuk ki moor lak lak ke utaal na, ki gor ke ki ku na le faani baatiŋ.

ref: It will slash right and left, wherever the blade is pointed.
text: Sin, kijaak aajuk ki ka na, gii ŋŋangii ni ŋŋangan. Gii saah fenn lipepel limɔk na.

ref: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
text: M mu ga kpaar ŋŋaal, le maaŋuul ga sɔŋ. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.” Babiloŋ Aabɔr aajaak aajuk

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
text: “Unibɔn, daan isan ilee i pu Babiloŋ aabɔr ga di waajaak aajuk dii ni na. I mɔmɔk ilee ga piin kitinbaan ni la. Ŋmee tiwan aan ki ti di ŋum isan ngbaan aah ti yakr nin chee na.

ref: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
text: Nsan mubaa ga mɔk ubɔr ngbaan Amonn aatiŋ Raba aah bi nin chee na, le muken na mɔk u Juda aatiŋ Jerusalem ki kpa ŋigon ŋi pɔɔ na chee.

ref: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
text: Ubɔr ngbaan ga ti sil isayakr ngbaan. U ga dam tibɔɔr aapiin, ki baa waawaa chee, ki lik baah kɔr kiwakork ki na aapɔɔl, le ki bee waah ga dii nsan mu na.

ref: His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people.
text: Tɔ, uŋangii joo mpiin mu mɔk ‘Jerusalem aatiŋ’ na la. Mu bui u ke u buen ti ban ŋidɔgen ŋi bi ga di wiil kaagon na, ki faa butɔb aakuun, ki di ŋidɔgen baŋ kaabisamɔi, ki kuun titan bil chur chur ki gbii ŋibugen.

ref: Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
text: Jerusalem yaab aah ŋa kimɔbaan ŋitimbol ŋiken chee pu na, baan dakl ke kina ga ŋmaa ŋa. Tɔ, tibɔr timina ga teer bi baatunwanbir pu, le ki sak bi ke bidim ga chur bi tinaagbiir.

ref: Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying: Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
text: Tɔ, min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na sɔ: Nimi aatunwanbir nyan mpaan pu a. Unii mɔmɔk nyi nimi aabɔr aah bii pu na. Nimi aatuln mɔmɔk ni le ni joo nimi aatunwanbir mɔk. Nimi aabɔr bii a, le m ga di nimi tii nimi aadim.

ref: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
text: “Sin Israel yaab aajojoor, mbiindaan, saawiin mu ye saakookoo aatafadaan aawiin na choo.

ref: I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies.
text: Min, Aadindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina. Chuu chikr saabɔryikpupuk, ni likekeln li aa joo buu aayil na. Tiwan nibaa aan ki li bi naabimbin. Fiin bigiim ŋa mpɔɔn ni. Sunn binib bi joo kitiŋ dandana na taab.

ref: I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city. Judgment against Ammon
text: Tɔ, libiil, libiil. Mbamɔn, m ga ŋa kitiŋ ngbaan tilangbenn. Tɔ, nimina mu aan kee ŋa see maah lee unii u ke u nan daa kitiŋ ngbaan aatafal na fuu ni, le m ga di ki tii u. Kijaak aajuk ni Amonn yaab

ref: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying: A sword is drawn, ready to slaughter; it is polished and prepared to kill as fast as lightning.
text: “Unibɔn, nabr maabɔr. Moon min Aadindaan Uwumbɔr aah bi tuk Amonn yaab bi bi seei Israel aatiŋ na. Bui bi ke: ‘Kijaak aajuk gor ke ki kuln nimi; Bi duun ki chain ke ki ku la, le ki moor lak lak.

ref: You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
text: Naah kani tibɔkpiirkaan ti na aa gbii, le naah len ke tiwan ni ga ŋa na ye inyamɔn. Ni ye bibiindam ni titunwanbirdam la, le nimi aawiin mu ye nimi aakookoo aatafadaan aawiin na choo. Kijaak aajuk ga lir nisil pu.

ref: Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth.
text: “‘Giin kijaak aajuk ngbaan fuu. M ga ji nimi tibɔr maah nan naan nimi nin chee na la, kitiŋ ki pu bi ma nimi na le m ga ji nimi tibɔr.

ref: My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing.
text: M yaa fenn maaŋuul lii ni pu ke mmii mu wu sakpen na kan, le ni ga kan maaŋuul aah pɔɔ pu na; le m ga di nimi tii bibiindam bi nyi baah ga kuln binib pu na.

ref: You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Mmii le ga kuln nimi. Nimi aatiŋ ponn ni le nimi aasin ga nya, le ubaa aan ki teer ni bɔr daalbaadaal.’” Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Some time later, the Lord said:
text: Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr le ki bui ke,

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins
text: “Unibɔn, aa gor ke aa ji kitiŋ ki ponn ni gbii binikurb na tibɔr aa? Kpiir tiwan ni mɔmɔk sukr ponn ni aan ki ŋa na tuk ki.

ref: and tell them I am saying: Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished!
text: Bui kitiŋ ngbaan min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na ke: Saah ku saanib sakpen ki di ŋiwaa bii aabaa pu na, saayoonn choo.

text: Aa nan koo Uwumbɔr aasaak Edenn ni la, le ki kpa ŋitakpanyaan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ. Aa nan kpa ŋitakpanyaan ŋi bi yi ŋi ke rubi, ni diamonn, ni topas, ni beril, ni kaneliann, ni jaspa, ni safir, ni emeral, ni ganet na. Aa nan kpa salmaa aaleen. Nwiin mundaal bi naan si na, le bi nan ŋa tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk tii si.

ref: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
text: M nan di maatuun mu ga tii unii ijawaan na siin kiir si nima. Aa nan bi maajool li bi chain na pu, le ki chuun ŋitakpanyaan ŋi moor lak lak na ni.

ref: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
text: Saabimbin nan ŋan sakpen ki nyan nwiin mundaal bi naan si na ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu aa piin titunwanbir aatuln na.

ref: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
text: Aa nan di liwandaal ni liwankooh le muk aabaa, le kina aatuln di si koon mbimbin mu pɔɔ na, ni titunwanbir aatuln ni. Kina pu le maatuun mu nan kii si na jenn nyan si ŋitakpanyaan ŋi moor lak lak na ni.

ref: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
text: Aa nan mak saanyaan pu, le saayimbil nan cha aa bi ke ujɔr na. Nimina pu le m nan mee si lii kitiŋ, ki cha si nima, ke aa li ye nsurm ki tii bibɔrb biken.

ref: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
text: Aa nan di liwandaal ni liwankooh tun titunwanbir, le ki cha saameen aabuu ni kpaln njinjin aabuu ni. Kina pu le m see kitiŋ ngbaan mmii lii, ki cha ki wun ti kpaln nfatan. Unii umɔk yaar lik si na waa si ke aa gur ye nfatan la.

ref: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
text: Aa buen a, aa buen kookoo a, le ijawaan chuu ŋitimbol ŋi nan nyi si na sakpen, ŋi san ijawaan ke ŋi mu ga kan saah kan pu na.” Saidonn aatiŋ aabɔr

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
text: “Unibɔn, lik Saidonn aatiŋ wɔb ki len tibɔbir lii ki pu.

ref: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
text: M ga cha iween dan aa pu, ki cha nsin puu saatiŋ ponn ni. Bi ga tak si ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu, ki ku saanib. N‑yoonn ngbaan le aa ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.” Uwumbɔr aah ga ŋa waanyoor ŋa Israel yaab pu pu na

ref: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “Ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln Israel aatimbol ki nan lik li fam na libaa aan ki li bi ke ikokon na ki ŋa Israel nibaa. Le ŋi ga bee ke min le ye Dindaan Uwumbɔr.”

ref: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr nan ki len ke, “M ga ki nyan Israel yaab maah nan cha bi yaa ki bi ŋitimbol ŋi na ni, ki cha ŋitimbol mɔmɔk bee ke m ye chain la. Israel aanib ga li koo bibaa aatiŋ pu la, kima le ye kitiŋ ki m nan di tii maatutunn Jakob na.

ref: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
text: Bi ga li bi nima lifuur ni la. Bi ga maa ŋidichal ki ko ŋisubil aasar. M ga daa ŋitimbol ŋi nan lik bi fam na aatafal, le Israel aatiŋ ga kan nsuudoon. N‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ga bee ke min le ye Bidindaan Uwumbɔr.”

ref: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
text: Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin kipiik ni aaŋmapiik aawiin kipiik ni mulee daal, le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr ki bui ke,

ref: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
text: Bui ke Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah tuk Ijipt aabɔr pu na sɔ: sin unyiib, kiwanbiik ki dɔ nnyun ni na, m ye saadin la. Aa bui ke Nail Aamɔɔl ye sin yaan la, ki len ke sin le ŋa li.

ref: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
text: M ga di njapiin le saa chaar aalakpak aan ki cha saamɔɔl aajan dab baan si. Le m ga dar nyan si Nail Aamɔɔl ponn ni, aan ijan ngbaan mɔmɔk dab baa si.

ref: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
text: M ga di aa ni ijan ngbaan mɔmɔk mee lii nteersakpiin ni. Aa ga ti lir kitiŋ ki gaar nima, ubaa taa sub si. M ga di si tii inyoon ni ipeel i di ŋa tijikaar.

ref: Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord. You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le Ijipt aanib mɔmɔk ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.” Uwumbɔr nan ki len ke, “Israel yaab nan mak nimi Ijipt yaab pu le ke ni ter bi, ni mu nan bi ke likal li kaa pɔɔ na la.

ref: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
text: Baah nan nyii ni pu na, le ni koo lir ki saa chaar biŋmɔŋ ni, le ki cha bi daa goob bichaŋ.

ref: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
text: Tɔ, min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le bui si ke m ga ban bijab aan bi nan di kijaak aajum tak si, le bi ga ku saanib ni saawakor.

ref: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
text: Ijipt aatiŋ ga kpaln tilangbenkuun la. N‑yoonn ngbaan le ni ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr. “Saah bui ke Nail Aamɔɔl ye sin yaan na pu, ki len ke sin le ŋa li na,

ref: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
text: m ye saadin la, le ki ye saamɔɔl ngbaan mu aadin. M ga ŋa Ijipt aatiŋ mɔmɔk tilangbenkuun, ki nya Migdol aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangan wɔb na ki ti saa Aswann aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangii wɔb na, ki yoor kina ki ti saa Kus yaab aatinaanmɔk.

ref: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
text: Unibɔn, bee kiwakork aan ki chuun nima. Nibaa aan li bi ki pu ki ti saa ŋibin imonko ilee.

ref: They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom
text: le ki ga cha bi ti li koo Ijipt aapepel li bi ŋŋangii wɔb ki ye biyaajatiib aalangbenn na; nima chee le bi ga li bi ki ye nnaan mu kaa kpa mpɔɔn na,

ref: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
text: Israel aatimbol aan ki nyii bi pu daalbaadaal ki ban nterm. Ijipt aabimbin ngbaan le ga teer Israel yaab naah kaa ŋan pu ke bi nyii bi pu ki ban nterm na. N‑yoonn ngbaan le Israel yaab ga bee ke min le ye Bidindaan Uwumbɔr.” Ubɔr Nebukadnesar aah ga nyaŋ Ijipt aatiŋ pu na

ref: Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
text: Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin moninko ni ŋilole aajan aaŋmal aajan aawiin daal, le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr ki bui ke,

ref: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
text: “Unibɔn, Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar fii sil ki tak Taya aatiŋ. U cha waajab tun ŋitun ŋi nyuun sakpen na le biyikpir ti gui, le bibɔgbin mu puun puun, tɔ, ubɔr ngbaan ni waajab mɔmɔk aa kan nibaa nimina pu.

ref: So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops.
text: Tɔ, Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na sɔ: M joo Ijipt aatiŋ tii Ubɔr Nebukadnesar la. U ga koo ki yoor Ijipt aawangol mɔmɔk ke ni li ye waajab aapar.

ref: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Waajab aah nan tun maatun na pu le m ga di Ijipt aatiŋ tii u. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
text: “Kina yaa nan ŋa kan, m ga cha Israel aanib pɔɔk, ki cha sin Esekiel sil unii mɔmɔk aah ga ŋun aa pu nin chee na ki len tibɔr, ki cha bi bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
text: “Unibɔn, nabr ki moon min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na. Aa teen ŋimɔbon ŋimina mpɔɔn pu ke: Ijawasakpiin aawiin mubaa choo,

ref: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
text: Nwiin mundaal Uwumbɔr ga fii sil na duun ni a, mu ga li ye ntaalangbam ni tibɔbir aawiin le ki tii ŋitimbol.

ref: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
text: Butɔb ga li bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni le mpombiin sakpiin ga li bi Kus aatiŋ ni. Bi ga ku binib pam Ijipt aatiŋ ni; bi ga yoor litingbaln ngbaan aawan ki cha ki nkuun.

ref: All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
text: Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Ki nya Migdol aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangan wɔb na ki ti saa Aswann aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangii wɔb na, bi ga ku Ijipt yaab bi kii kitiŋ ngbaan na mɔmɔk. Bi ga kuln Ijipt aatɔb aajab bi kpa kigaak na. Min Dindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
text: Kitiŋ ngbaan le ga doon nkuun ki jer dulnyaa aatim mɔmɔk, le kaatikpaan ga kpaln ŋilangben.

ref: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
text: M yaa moo mmii see Ijipt aatiŋ lii, aan bi ku kaakikiib mɔmɔk kan, bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.

ref: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
text: “Nwiin ngbaan yaa fuu ni aan Ijipt aatiŋ kuln kan, m ga tun binib iŋɔi ni, le bi ti bui Kus yaab bi kaa nyi kina pu na, le ijawaan sakpiin ga chuu bi. Nwiin ngbaan choo.”

ref: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “M ga di Babiloŋ Aabɔr Nebukadnesar le kuln Ijipt aawangol.

ref: He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
text: U ni waajab bi kaa san kinimbaak kpala na ga dan ki nan bii kitiŋ ngbaan. Bi ga di kijaak aajum le tak Ijipt aatiŋ, le kitiŋ ngbaan pu ga li ye ŋinikpol ŋmeen.

ref: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
text: M ga cha Nail Aamɔɔl foor ki kuur, aan ki di Ijipt aatiŋ ŋa bibiindam aaŋaal ni. Biwɔwɔm le ga bii kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk doo. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “M ga kuln ŋiwaa ni inyɔk Memfis aatiŋ ni. Ubaa aan ki li bi ki ye Ijipt aatiŋ aajojoor, le m ga cha ijawaan sakpiin chuu kaanib mɔmɔk.

ref: The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed!
text: M ga cha Ijipt aapepel li bi ŋŋangii wɔb na doon nkuun, ki see Soann aatiŋ ki bi ŋŋangan wɔb na mmii lii. M ga daa kaatiyil Tebes aatafal.

ref: The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
text: M ga cha Ijipt aatikpaan Pelusium ki bi maa ŋigon kiir ki na, kan maaŋuul li pɔɔ na. M ga kuln Tebes aawangol.

ref: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
text: M ga see Ijipt aatiŋ mmii, le Pelusium aatiŋ ga li bi iween kpaan ni. Tebes aagon ga wɔi doon kitiŋ, le kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni kpaln nwam.

ref: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
text: Heliopolis ni Bubastis aatim aanachipɔm ga bee butɔb ni; le bi ga chur binib bi gur na tinaagbiir.

ref: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
text: M yaa nan bii Ijipt aapɔɔn mu bi nan mak mu pu sakpen na kan, mbɔmbɔɔn ga lir Tapanes aatiŋ pu. Ntaalangbam ga biin Ijipt aatiŋ pu, le bi ga chur kaatim mɔmɔk aanib tinaagbiir.

ref: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
text: M yaa daa Ijipt aatiŋ aanib aatafal kina kan, bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.” Ijipt Aabɔr aapɔɔn aah doo pu na

ref: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
text: Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin kipiik ni libaa aajan aaŋmal aawinlole daal, le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword.
text: U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, m koo Ijipt aabɔr aaŋaal a. Ubaa aa di litaln poo mu, kaa di tiwan chuu mu ki di leen usil ke mu sɔŋ ki ki pɔɔk aan u ki di mu chuu kijaak aajuk.

ref: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
text: Tɔ, min Dindaan Uwumbɔr aah len pu na sɔ: M ye Ijipt aabɔr aadin la. M ban m koo uŋaal ilee ngbaan mɔmɔk la, m ga koo mu pɔɔ na ni mu puun koo na, le kijaak aajuk nya uŋaal ni ki lir.

ref: and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
text: M ga cha Ijipt yaab yaa koo dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni.

ref: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
text: Mbamɔn, m ga diŋ u le ki moo pɔɔk Babiloŋ aabɔr ma. M yaa di maajaak aajuk tii u aan u di ki mɔk Ijipt aatiŋ kan, unii mɔmɔk ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.

ref: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
text: M ga cha Ijipt yaab yaa koo dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni. N‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ga bee ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

ref: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
text: Taah nan bi tinaagbiir ni pu na aabin kipiik ni libaa aaŋmataa aajan aawiin daal, le Uwumbɔr nan len m chee tibɔr.

ref: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
text: U nan bui ke, “Unibɔn, tuk Ijipt aabɔr ni waanib mɔmɔk ke: Nimi aapɔɔn nyaŋ a. M ga di nimi ŋaŋ ba?

ref: There was once a cedar tree in Lebanon with large, strong branches reaching to the sky.
text: Ni bi ke Lebanonn aatiŋ aasantina na la, ki kpa mboon aapanyaan, ki ye busub bu fɔk ki ti tuu ntaalangbam na.

ref: This tree had plenty of water to help it grow tall, and nearby streams watered the other trees in the forest.
text: Bu nan kpa nnyun ke bu di muun, le ŋimɔɔ bi kitiŋ taab ki tii bu nnyun. Bi nan kpir nnyun busub ngbaan aah si nin chee na ki ŋa nkpen buen kichook ni aasui mɔmɔk chee.

ref: But this tree towered over those other trees, and its branches grew long and thick.
text: Bu aah nan kpa nnyun na, bu nan muun jer isui mɔmɔk. Bu aapan nan filk ki fɔk.

ref: Birds built nests in its branches, and animals were born beneath it. People from all nations lived in the shade of this strong tree.
text: Inyoon mɔmɔk aabɔŋ nan ter yaadil bu aapan ni; ipeel nan ma yaabim bu aaboon ni; dulnyaa aatimbol nan kaa bu aaboon ni.

ref: It had beautiful, long branches, and its roots found water deep in the soil.
text: Busub ngbaan aanyaan nan ti nyaŋ, Bu nan fɔk, ki kpa ŋipan fɔfɔŋ. Bu aanyaan nan koo taab taab ki ti pii kitiŋ taab aamɔɔ na.

ref: None of the cedar trees in my garden of Eden were as beautiful as this tree; no tree of any kind had such long branches.
text: Santina aa nan bi Uwumbɔr aasaak na ni, aan aa ga di ŋaŋ bu. Busub bubaa aaboln aa kpa kina aapan, bu aasupuul aaboln aa nan bi. Busub bubaa aa nan bi Uwumbɔr aasaak ni ki ŋan kina.

ref: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
text: M nan ŋa bu, bu ŋan ki kpa ŋipan ŋi fɔk na. Busub bumɔk nan bi Uwumbɔr aasaak ni, Edenn aatiŋ ni na, nan kpa bu pu lipiipoln la.

ref: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
text: “Tɔ, min Dindaan Uwumbɔr ga bui si tiwan ni ga ŋa busub bu muun ki ti tuu ntaalangbam na. Bu aah moo muun kpee na, le bu gur kpa kipupuk;

ref: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
text: kina pu na, m yii bu, ki ga di bu tii ujojoor u ye uwɔwɔnja na. U ga di tiwan ni ŋeer busub ngbaan aabiin na tii bu.

ref: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
text: Biwɔwɔm bi kaa san kinimbaak kpala na ga gaa bu lii ki siir cha bu. Bu aapan ni lisupuul ga lir lijool mɔmɔk, ni kifataŋ ki mɔmɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan pu na pu. Ŋitimbol ŋi nan koo bu aaboon ni na ga yaa.

ref: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
text: Inyoon ga dan nan kal busub bu lir ki dɔ na pu, le ipeel ga taa bu aapan pu ki jer.

ref: Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
text: Kina pu na, ki nya n‑yoonn mumina na, busub bubaa aan ki ŋmaa muun ke buma na, bee bu too ti chaar ntaalangbam ni ki ti pii kitaapaak. Hali bu yaa po kan nnyun sakpen pu na kan, bu aan fuu kina. I mɔmɔk ga kpo ke unibɔn na la, i ga buen ti kpee binib bi bi kitekpiitiŋ ni taab na pu.”

ref: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aah ki len pu na sɔ: “Nwiin mundaal busub ngbaan ga buen kitekpiitiŋ ni na, m ga cha kitiŋ taab aanyun biin bu pu aan ni mɔk bu aakpowiil. M ga chuu ŋimɔɔ siin ki taa ki cha ikpen pam na puu nya. Busub ngbaan aah kpo na, m ga cha mbɔmbɔɔn biin Lebanonn Aajoo pu ki cha kichook ngbaan aasui mɔmɔk yɔl.

ref: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
text: M yaa tur bu lii kitekpiitiŋ ni kan, bu aah ga lir pu na ga dam ŋitimbol. Edenn aatiŋ aasui mɔmɔk, ni Lebanonn aachook aasunyaan i mɔmɔk sunn buen kitekpiitiŋ ni na aasui ga piir bu aalirm pu.

ref: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
text: I ga dii bu buen ti kpee isui i puun lir na pu. Le binib bi mɔmɔk ka bu aaboon ni na ga yaa koo ŋitimbol ŋiken ni.

ref: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. text: U nan bui mi ke, “Nnyun mumina puu cha liwipuul wɔb, le ki ti lir Jɔɔdann Aafataŋ ni, ki nyan nima ti koo N‑yaan Aanyusakpem ni. Nima chee le mu ti gaa n‑yaan aanyun mu bi nnyusakpem ngbaan ni na, ki ye nnyunbamɔm.

ref: Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea.
text: Nnyun ngbaan yaa puu nin chee mɔk jer na, ipeel ni ijan mɔmɔk aabɔŋ ga li bi nima. Nkpen ngbaan aanyun ga cha N‑yaan Aanyusakpem ngbaan aanyun ŋa nnyun mu mɔ na, le mu aah puu jer nin chee mɔk na mu ga tii limɔfal.

ref: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.

ref: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
text: Tɔ, nnyun mu bi kipuuk, ni tibɔr ti bi nnyusakpem ngbaan aagbaan na ni ga li beenin kpa n‑yaan. Mu ga bee nima chee ki li ye nin chee n‑yaan nyan ni na.

ref: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
text: Isui mɔmɔk aabɔŋ ga muun ŋimɔɔgban ŋilee ngbaan mɔmɔk pu ki tii tijikaar. Yaafar aan yɔl daalbaadaal, le yaasubil mu aan fir daalbaadaal. Isui ngbaan ga li tii tijikaar, le bi ga li joo yaafar mu ki sɔŋ binib aaween.” Kitiŋ ngbaan aatinaanmɔk

ref: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad,
text: “Ŋŋangan wɔb aatinaanmɔk nyan Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem chee ki di dii liwipuul wɔb ki ti saa Hetlonn aatiŋ, ni Hamaf Aasan chee, ni Sedad aatiŋ chee,

ref: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
text: ki di kpee Berota, ni Sibraim aatim mu bi Damaskus aanaan aapepel ni Hamaf aanaan aakaasisik ni na, ni Tikonn aatiŋ ki bi Haurann aapepel aanaanmɔk na.

ref: So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
text: Kina pu na, ŋŋangan wɔb aatinaanmɔk nan nyan Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk ki di dii liwipuul wɔb ki ti saa Enonn aatiŋ mɔk ki di Damaskus ni Hamaf aatinaanmɔk lii ŋŋangan wɔb.

ref: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
text: “Liwipuul wɔb aatinaanmɔk nan nyan libuul libaa ni Damaskus ni Haurann aapepel chee ki di dii ŋŋangii wɔb, le Jɔɔdann Aamɔɔl ye Israel aatiŋ ki bi liwilir wɔb na, ni Gilead ni bi liwipuul wɔb na aatinaanmɔk, ki yoor kina ti saa Tamar aatiŋ ki bi N‑yaan Aanyusakpem chee na.

ref: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
text: “Ŋŋangii wɔb aatinaanmɔk nan nyan Tamar aatiŋ mɔk ki di dii ŋŋangii wɔb ni liwilir aapepel wɔb ki ti saa Kades Meriba aateersakpiin aanyun na chee, le ki di toŋ ŋŋangan ni liwilir aapepel ki kpak Ijipt aatinaanmɔk ki ti saa Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk.

ref: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
text: “Liwilir wɔb aatinaanmɔk nan nyan Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk ki di dii ŋŋangan wɔb ki ti saa libuul libaa ni, Hamaf Aasan aawilir wɔb.

ref: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
text: “Yakr kitiŋ kimina tii nimi aanibol.

ref: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
text: Ki ga li ye nimi aatiŋ le ki cha n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Ni yaa bi yakr ki kan, ni tii biwɔwɔm bi koo ni chee ki ma mbim do na mu baatiŋ. Ni ŋa bi ke naah ga ŋa Israel aanii pu na, ki cha bi mu kpaan too inaan Israel aanibol chee ki gaa baatiŋ.

ref: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
text: Uwɔwɔnii umɔk koo do na ga gaa waatiŋ waah koo linibol li ponn ni na chee la. Min Nidindaan Uwumbɔr le len kina.”

ref: Each tribe will receive a section of land that runs from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. text: Kitiŋ ngbaan aaŋangan wɔb aatinaanmɔk nan nyan Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk le ki di dii liwipuul wɔb ki ti saa Hetlonn aatiŋ, ni Hamaf Aasan, ni Enonn aatiŋ, ki ti saa Damaskus ni Hamaf aanaan aah ti naa tɔb nin chee na. Mpaan mu bi nyan bil kitiŋ ngbaan aakaasisik ni na aabɔr

ref: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
text: Kitiŋ ngbaan aapaan mu nan paa kaasisik ni na le bi nan nyan siin ŋitun ŋibaa pu na. Mpaan ngbaan aawawaan ki nya ŋŋangan wɔb ki ti saa ŋŋangii wɔb li ye mal kipiik, ki nya liwipuul wɔb ki ti saa liwilir wɔb mu aafɔfɔk li fɔk ŋak ke baah gii pu tii ŋinibol ngbaan na. Mpaan ngbaan ni le Uwumbɔr Aadichal ga sil.

ref: An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
text: Mpaan ngbaan aakaasisik ni ga ki li kpa mpaan mu aafɔfɔk ye mal kipiik, aan nwawaan mu ye biniin na. Muma le ga li ye Uwumbɔr aapaan.

ref: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
text: Bitotoorb ga li kpa mpaan, chain aapepel lee ni. Ki nya liwipuul wɔb ki ti saa liwilir wɔb, baapaan aafɔfɔk li ye mal kipiik, ki nya ŋŋangan wɔb ki ti saa ŋŋangii wɔb mu li ye mal binaa. Uwumbɔr Aadichal ga li bi lipepel limina aakaasisik ni la.

ref: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
text: Sadok aayaabitiib bi ye bitotoorb na yeh chain aapepel ngbaan. Bima le dii mi mbamɔm, kaa nan ŋmal Israel yaab biken ni, baah nan bi tun mi taani buyoonn na, ke Liifai aanibol liken aah nan ŋa pu na.

ref: The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
text: Kina pu na, baapaan ga li paa Liifai yaab biken yaan pu la, le ki ga li bi chain ki jer ŋipepel mɔmɔk.

ref: I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide,
text: Liifai yaab mu aapepel ga li bi libaa la, ki ga li bi bitotoorb aapaan aaŋangii wɔb. Mu mu ga li ye mal kipiik ki nya liwipuul ki ti saa liwilir wɔb, ki li ye mal binaa ki nya ŋŋangan ki ti saa ŋŋangii wɔb.

ref: South of my sacred land will be a section twelve and a half kilometers long and three kilometers wide. It will not be sacred, but will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem, together with its houses and pastureland.
text: Mpaan mumina aapepel li gur ki ye mal kipiik aafɔfɔk, aan nwawaan ye mal bilee aafɔfɔk na aa bi chain, le ki ga li ye binib aawan mɔmɔk aapaan. Bi ga ŋmaa li koo mu pu ki ko mu pu. Kitiŋ ga li bi mu aakaasisik ni,

ref: The city will be a square: Each side will be two kilometers long,
text: le mu aafɔfɔk ni nwawaan li ye tiwanbaan. Ni ga li ye ŋitaa ŋichur ŋilole ni ikui iŋmu ni imonko itaa ŋipepel mɔmɔk pu.

ref: The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide.
text: Mpaan mu gur kitiŋ ngbaan aamaam aapuwɔb ki kpaan bi chain aapepel aaŋangii wɔb na aafɔfɔk ga li ye mal binaa, le nwawaan ye mal bilee liwipuul wɔb, ki li ye mal binaa aafɔfɔk, ni mal bilee aawawaan liwilir wɔb mu. Mpaan ngbaan ga li ye binib bi koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni na aasar la.

ref: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
text: Unii umɔk koo kitiŋ ngbaan ni na ga ko nima chee la. Baan li dii ŋinibol ŋi ponn ni binib ngbaan nyan ni na aasan le ki ko nima.

ref: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
text: Kina pu na, mpaan mu bi nan nyan bil kitiŋ ngbaan aakaasisik ni na aafɔfɔk ni nwawaan ga li ŋak la, ni ga li ye mal kipiik le lipepel mɔmɔk pu, baah maa kitiŋ ki na ga li bi mu ni.

ref: together with the share belonging to the Levites and the city of Jerusalem. The northern border of the ruler's property will be the land that belongs to Judah, and the southern border will be the land that belongs to Benjamin. The Division of Land among Tribes in the South The Lord God said:
text: Mpaan mu gur ki bi Uwumbɔr Aadichal, ni bitotoorb aatiŋ, ni Liifai yaab aatiŋ, ni kitiŋ ki bi nima na aawipuul ni liwilir wɔb na le ye Israel yaab aajojoor na aatiŋ. Ki di toŋ liwipuul wɔb ki ti saa liwipuul aatinaanmɔk, ki di toŋ liwilir wɔb ki ti saa Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk, le ki ti saa Juda aanibol aatinaanmɔk ŋŋangan wɔb, ki di ti saa Benjaminn aanibol aatinaanmɔk ŋŋangii wɔb. Ŋinibol ŋiken na aatim

ref: South of this special section will be the land that belongs to the rest of Israel's tribes.
