text: Lipepel limina aaŋangii wɔb le ŋinibol ŋi gur na mɔmɔk ga kan ntim, ki nya liwipuul aatinaanmɔk ki di toŋ liwilir wɔb, ki ti saa Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk. Ŋinibol ngbaan ga li dii tɔb ki nya ŋŋangan wɔb ki cha ŋŋangii wɔb kina la: Benjaminn aanibol le ga pue gaa, le Simeonn aanibol paan, le Isakar aanibol paan, le Sebulunn aanibol paan, le Gad aanibol ti gbeln puwɔb.

ref: Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
text: Gad aanibol aatiŋ aaŋangii wɔb aatinaanmɔk nyan Tamar aatiŋ mɔk le ki di toŋ ŋŋangii ni liwilir aapepel ki ti saa Kades aateersakpiin aanyun na chee, le ki fenn ŋŋangan ni liwilir aapepel ki di toŋ Ijipt aatinaanmɔk ki ti saa Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem mɔk.

ref: That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Gates of Jerusalem The Lord said:
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr len ke, “Kina le ni ga yakr ki ga gii gii kitiŋ ngbaan tii Israel aanibol aan ni li ye biyaan.” Jerusalem aatiŋ aabisamɔi aabɔr

ref: The city of Jerusalem will have twelve gates, three on each of the four sides of the city wall. These gates will be named after the twelve tribes of Israel. The gates of Reuben, Judah, and Levi will be in the north; Joseph, Benjamin, and Dan will be in the east; Simeon, Issachar, and Zebulun will be in the south; Gad, Asher, and Naphtali will be in the west. Each side of the city wall will be two kilometers long,
text: Jerusalem aatiŋ kpa ibisamɔi kipiik ni ilee la. Ŋigon ŋinaa ŋi gob ki na libaa mɔk aafɔfɔk ye ŋitaa ŋichur ŋilole ni ikui iŋmu ni imonko itaa la, le ibisamɔi itata bi ligoln mɔk ni. Mubaa mɔk kpa ŋinibol kipiik ni ŋilee na libaa aayimbil. Ibisamɔi i bi ŋŋangan wɔb na aayimbil le ye Rubenn, ni Juda, ni Liifai; le i bi liwipuul wɔb aagoln ni na ye Josef, ni Benjaminn, ni Dann; le i bi ŋŋangii wɔb aagoln ni na aayimbil ye Simeonn, ni Isakar, ni Sebulunn; le i bi liwilir wɔb aagoln ni na ye Gad, ni Aser, ni Naftali.

ref: and so the total length of the wall will be ten kilometers. The new name of the city will be “The-Lord-Is-Here!”
text: Ŋigon ŋinaa ngbaan aafɔfɔk nan ti saa ŋitaa ŋichur piitaa ni ikui ilee ni moninko la. Kitiŋ ngbaan aayimbil ki nyan n‑yoonn mue ki joo cha ga li ye ke “Uwumbɔr‑bi‑do.”

ref: In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia attacked Jerusalem.
text: Jehoyakim aah nan ye ubɔrkpaan Juda aatiŋ pu na aabitatar ni, le Babiloŋ Aabɔrkpaan Nebukadnesar nan ti tak Jerusalem ki gob kitiŋ ngbaan.

ref: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim and take away some of the things used in God's temple. And when the king returned to Babylonia, he put these things in the temple of his own god.
text: Uwumbɔr nan cha u nyaŋ Ubɔrkpaan Jehoyakim ki chuu u ki gaa Uwumbɔr Aadichal aawangol libaa ki di bi buen waawaa aadiik, Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni, ki di Uwumbɔr Aadichal aawan ngbaan di bil waawaa aawangol aadiik ni.

ref: One day the king ordered Ashpenaz, his highest palace official, to choose some young men from the royal family of Judah and from other leading Jewish families.
text: Ubɔr ngbaan nan cha waaninkpel u bi yin u ke Aspenas na nyan Israel aanaagbiib bi u nan chur na ponn ni binachipɔm bi nyan ni libɔrdichal ni, ni bininyuum do na bibaa.

ref: The king said, “They must be healthy, handsome, smart, wise, educated, and fit to serve in the royal palace. Teach them how to speak and write our language
text: Bi nan ye binachipɔm bi ŋan, ki kpa nlan, bi bi mɔk bi tiwan mbamɔm na, aan bi ŋmaa bae tiwan mala mala, kaa kpa iween ibaa na, aan bi li bi ubɔr aadichal ni. Aspenas aatuln le nan ye ke u mɔk bi tiwan aan bi li ŋmaa karni ki ŋmaa ŋmee Babiloŋ yaab aaliin.

ref: Four of the young Jews chosen were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, all from the tribe of Judah.
text: Daniel, ni Hanania, ni Misael, ni Asaria, bi mɔmɔk nan ye Juda aanib na, nan ŋmal baah nyan binachipɔm bi na ponn ni.

ref: But the king's chief official gave them Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abednego.
text: Ubɔr aaninkpiib aaninkpel ngbaan nan ki tii bi Babiloŋ yaab aayimbil ŋimina: U nan yin Daniel ke Beltesasar, ki yin Hanania ke Sadrak, ki yin Misael ke Mesak, ki yin Asaria ke Abednego.

ref: Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace.
text: Daniel nan ŋa nlandak ke waan ji tijikaar ti ubɔr aachiln ni aanib ji na, kaan nyu baadaan mu ki bii waah dii nsan mu na; kina pu na, u nan bui Aspenas ke u ter u,

ref: God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel.
text: le Uwumbɔr nan cha Aspenas san Daniel kinimbaak.

ref: But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”
text: Tɔ, Aspenas mu nan tee san ubɔr ijawaan, le ki bui Daniel ke, “Ubɔr mɔk waah ban ni li ji tijikaar ti, ni ndaan mu na, le aa yaa kaa nan gbiin unimbil ke binachipɔm biken na kan, nibaakan u ga ku mi.”

ref: The king's official had put a guard in charge of Daniel and his three friends. So Daniel said to the guard,
text: Le Daniel buen Aspenas aah di ukikiir u tii u ni ujɔtiib bitaa na chee,

ref: When the ten days are up, compare how we look with the other young men, and decide what to do with us.”
text: Iwiin kipiik ngbaan yaa ti jer kan, aa di timi ŋaŋ binachipɔm bi ji ubɔr aachiln ni aanib aajikaar na, ki lik ke ulau jer uken.”

ref: The guard agreed to do what Daniel had asked.
text: U nan kii ke bi ŋa kina ki ti saa iwiin kipiik ki lik.

ref: Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan aah nan fuu ni na, bi nan kan ke bi kpa laafee ki pɔɔ jer bi mɔmɔk nan ji ubɔr aachiln ni aajikaar na.

ref: God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
text: Uwumbɔr nan tii binachipɔm binaa ngbaan nlan, ni ichiin, ni laasaab. U nan ki kpee Daniel nlan mu ga cha u bee tidaŋ ni tibɔkpiirkaan aatataa na.

ref: At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him.
text: Ŋibin ŋitaa ŋi ubɔr nan siin na aah nan saa na, le Aspenas nan di binachipɔm ngbaan buen Nebukadnesar chee.

ref: The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court.
text: Ubɔr nan len bi mɔmɔk chee tibɔr, le Daniel, ni Hanania, ni Misael, ni Asaria nan kan u chee lineen ki jer biken na. Kina pu na, bi nan kpaln ubɔr aachiln ni aanib la.

ref: From then on, whenever the king asked for advice, he found their wisdom was ten times better than that of any of his other advisors and magicians.
text: Mbaan mubaa aa nan bi ubɔr baa, bee limukl libaa dan, aan binachipɔm binaa ngbaan aa ŋmaa gar. Bi nan nyi tiwan ki jer bibɔɔb, ni binib bi joo inyɔk tun iwaan aatuln ki bi nnaan ngbaan ni na.

ref: Daniel served there until the first year of King Cyrus.
text: Daniel nan beenin bi ubɔr aachiln ni le Pesia Aabɔrkpaan Sairus nan nyaŋ Babiloŋ yaab butɔb ni.

ref: During the second year that Nebuchadnezzar was king, he had such horrible nightmares that he could not sleep.
text: Nebukadnesar aah jin nnaan ki nan saa ŋibin ŋilee na, le u nan daŋ tidaŋ. Ti nan muk u sakpen le waa nan geen kinyeek ngbaan,

text: le u bui bi ke, “M daŋ tidaŋ tibaa le ti muk mi. M ban ke m bee taatataa la.”

text: Le bi gar ubɔr ngbaan Aram yaab aaliin ponn ni ke, “Uwumbɔr tii mpɔɔndaan limɔfal li fɔk na. Tuk timi saadaŋ ngbaan, aan ti ti kpiir taatataa tuk si.”

ref: But the king replied, “No! I have made up my mind. If you don't tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be chopped to pieces and your houses will be torn down.
text: Le ubɔr ngbaan ki bui bi ke, “M ŋa nlandak ke nimi le ga tuk mi tidaŋ ngbaan aah ye pu na, ni taatataa mu. Ni yaa kaa ŋman kan, m ga cha bi daa par par nimi ki kuln nimi aadichal mu.

ref: However, if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be greatly rewarded and highly honored. Now tell me the dream and explain what it means.”
text: Tɔ, ni yaa ŋman ki tuk mi tidaŋ ngbaan ni taatataa aah ye pu na kan, m ga tii nimi ipiin ni kipak ki nyuun na. Kina pu na, tuk mi tidaŋ ngbaan ni taatataa aah ye pu na man.”

ref: “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
text: Le bi ki gir gar ubɔr ke, “Mpɔɔndaan yaa ba ga tuk timi tidaŋ ngbaan kan, ti ba ga ŋmaa tuk si taatataa.”

ref: because you know what's going to happen if you don't come up with the answer. You've decided to make up a bunch of lies, hoping I might change my mind. Now tell me the dream, and that will prove that you can interpret it.”
text: naah kan ke m ŋa nlandak ke ni yaa kaa ŋmaa tuk mi tidaŋ ngbaan kan, m ga tii ni mɔmɔk ntafadaan baan na, le cha ni ŋani kina. ref: His advisors explained, “Your Majesty, you are demanding the impossible! No king, not even the most famous and powerful, has ever ordered his advisors, magicians, or wise men to do such a thing.
text: Le bisusurb ngbaan ki gar u ke, “Unii ubaa aa bi kitiŋ kee pu ki ga ŋmaa tuk mpɔɔndaan saah ban aa bee tiwan ni na. Ubɔr ubaa aa bi, hali ubɔr u kpa mpɔɔn sakpen na ubaa aa kee tuk waabɔɔb, ni bimɔk joo inyɔk tun iwaan aatuln na kina aabɔr aaboln.

text: Bi ga jenn nyan si binib chee, le aa ni ipeel ga ti li kpaan koo tɔb chee. Aa ga ŋmɔ timoor ke unaa na ki doo lipaal, nin chee limaln ga li lir aa pu na, ki ti saa ŋibin ŋilole. N‑yoonn ngbaan le aa ga tii naadii ke Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na le kpa mpɔɔn unibɔn aanaan mɔmɔk pu, le ki ga ŋmaa di mu tii unii umɔk u gee na.

ref: But he gave orders not to disturb the stump and roots. This is to show that you will be king once again, after you learn that the God who rules from heaven is in control.
text: Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib nan bui ke bi di cha busub ngbaan aasukpiil li li si kitiŋ. Nimina mɔk ke aa yaa nan tii naadii ke Uwumbɔr le joo dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk kan, aa ga ki gir ji saanaan.

ref: Your Majesty, please be willing to do what I say. Turn from your sins and start living right; have mercy on those who are mistreated. Then all will go well with you for a long time. The Rest of Nebuchadnezzar's Letter about His Second Dream
text: Kina pu na, mpɔɔndaan, li dii maasurm. Di cha titunwanbir aatuln, ŋa tiwan ni ŋan na, ki san bigiim kinimbaak. Le saawangol ga moo kpee.”

ref: About twelve months later, I was walking on the flat roof of my royal palace and admiring the beautiful city of Babylon, when these things started happening to me. I was saying to myself, “Just look at this wonderful capital city that I have built by my own power and for my own glory!”
text: le ki bui ke, “Lik man Babiloŋ aah kpa mpɔɔn pu na. Min le maa ki ke maatiyil, ke m di mɔk maapɔɔn, ni maapak, ni maah kpa liyimbil pu na.”

ref: But before I could finish speaking, a voice from heaven interrupted: King Nebuchadnezzar, this kingdom is no longer yours.
text: Waahr aan u nin len tibɔr ngbaan doo na, le nneel nyan ni paacham ki len ke, “Ubɔrkpaan Nebukadnesar, li pel maah ban m len pu na. M nyan saanaan aapɔɔn aa chee dandana.

ref: You will be forced to live with the wild animals, away from people. For seven years you will eat grass, as though you were an ox, until you learn that God Most High is in control of all earthly kingdoms and that he is the one who chooses their rulers.
text: Bi ga jenn nyan si binib chee, le aa ni ipeel le ga li kpaan koo tɔb chee, le aa li ŋmɔ timoor ke unaa na ki ti saa ŋibin ŋilole. N‑yoonn ngbaan le aa ga tii naadii ke Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na kpa mpɔɔn unibɔn aanaan mɔmɔk pu, ki ga di mu tii unii umɔk u gee u na.”

ref: This was no sooner said than done—I was forced to live like a wild animal; I ate grass and was unprotected from the dew. As time went by, my hair grew longer than eagle feathers, and my fingernails looked like the claws of a bird.
text: Libuul ngbaan ni, le tibɔr ngbaan kpaan ŋa kina. Bi nan jenn Nebukadnesar binib chee, le u ŋman timoor ke unaa na. Limaln nan lir uwon pu, le waakor muun ke likaagiil aakokor na, le waanyanyar mu fɔk ke ukaa aanyanyar na. Nebukadnesar aah pak Uwumbɔr pu na

ref: Finally, I prayed to God in heaven, and my mind was healed. Then I said: “I praise and honor God Most High. God lives forever, and his kingdom will never end.
text: Le ubɔr ngbaan bui ke, “Ŋibin ŋilole ngbaan aah jer na, le m waan lik kitaapaak, le maalan ki gir ni m chee. Le m pak Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na, ki nyuŋ u waah bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na pu. U ga li joo dulnyaa wee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, le waanaan aan li kpa ndoon.

ref: To him the nations are far less than nothing; God controls the stars in the sky and everyone on this earth. When God does something, we cannot change it or even ask why.”
text: U lik binib bi bi taab na ke baa ye nibaa u chee. Waatuuntiib ni binib bi bi taab do na bi uŋaal ni la. Ubaa aan ŋmaa kpak waageehn bee u baa u waah ŋani tiwan ni na pu.

ref: At that time my mind was healed, and once again I became the ruler of my glorious kingdom. My advisors and officials returned to me, and I had greater power than ever before.
text: “Maalan aah ki gir ni m chee na, le bi ki di maapak, ni maapɔɔn, ni maayimbil, ni maanaan tii mi. Maaninkpiib, ni maaninyuum nan ki gaa mi iŋaal ilee, le ki ki di maanaan aapɔɔn tii mi, hali ki pak mi ki jer maah nan bi pu na.

ref: That's why I say: “Praise and honor the King who rules from heaven! Everything he does is honest and fair, and he can shatter the power of those who are proud.”
text: “Le dandana wee, min Nebukadnesar pak ki nyuŋ Paacham Aabɔrkpaan ngbaan ki tii u kipak. Waah ŋani tiwan nimɔk na ye mbamɔn ki tok, le u ga ŋmaa sunn binib bi kpa kigaak na taab.”

ref: One evening, King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his highest officials, and he drank wine with them.
text: Kinyeek kibaa le Ubɔrkpaan Belsasar nan yin ni waaninyuum lichur ke bi nan ji u chee njim sakpem, le bi nan kpaan ki nyun ndaan.

ref: He got drunk and ordered his servants to bring in the gold and silver cups his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. Belshazzar wanted the cups, so that he and all his wives and officials could drink from them.
text: Baah bi nyu ndaan na, le Belsasar nan bui ke bi ti yoor ni salmaa aayikur, ni tikunabr aayikur, ni ŋisambil ŋi ute Nebukadnesar nan yoor nyan Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni, Jerusalem aatiŋ ni na. Ubɔr nan cha bi yoor ni tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk ke u ni waaninyuum, ni upuutiib, ni ubɔtiib nan di ni nyu ndaan la.

ref: When the gold cups were brought in, everyone at the banquet drank from them and praised their idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
text: le ki pak baah di salmaa naan ŋiwaa ŋi na, ni baah di tikunabr, ni tikumann, ni tikur, ni isui, ni ŋitakpal naan ŋi na.

ref: Suddenly a human hand was seen writing on the plaster wall of the palace. The hand was just behind the lampstand, and the king could see it writing.
text: Libuul ngbaan ni, le unibɔn aaŋaal nyan ni ki piin ki bi ŋmee baah nan ligoln li na pu, libɔrdichal ni aadiik ki bi ka na ni, nin chee karyaa aamii wiin sakpen na. Le ubɔr nan kan mu aah bi ŋmee pu na.

ref: He was so frightened that his face turned pale, his knees started shaking, and his legs became weak.
text: Ijawaan nan chuu u, le uwon yɔl, le utaŋaayil gbaa.

ref: The king called in his advisors, who claimed they could talk with the spirits of the dead and understand the meanings found in the stars. He told them, “The man who can read this writing and tell me what it means will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. He will wear robes of royal purple and a gold chain around his neck.”
text: Le u teen ke ubaa yin ni bibɔɔb, ni binib bimɔk joo inyɔk tun lituln na ke bi dan. Baah koo ni na, le ubɔr bui bi ke, “Unii u ŋmaa karn ŋŋmeen mue ki tuk mi mu aatataa na kan, bi ga peen u ŋibɔrbɔkul ŋi ŋmal mmam ni nsiin na, ki gbin u salmaa aaleen mu kpa kipak na uneen ni, aan u li ye unii tatar u aaninkpir paa m pu, nnaan mue ni na.”

ref: All of King Belshazzar's highest officials came in, but not one of them could read the writing or tell what it meant,
text: Libɔrdichal ni aasusurb ngbaan nan foor mal ni, le kaa ŋmaa karn ŋŋmeen ngbaan, kaa ŋmaa tuk ubɔr mu aatataa mu.

ref: and they were completely puzzled. Now the king was more afraid than ever before, and his face turned white as a ghost.
text: Usui aah nan bii sakpen na, uwon nan moo yɔl la, le waaninyuum ngbaan aa nan nyi baah ga ŋa pu na.

ref: When the queen heard the king and his officials talking, she came in and said: Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! Don't be afraid or look so pale.
text: Le ubɔr aana nan ŋun kifuuk ki ubɔr ni waaninyuum nan faa na pu, le ki koo ni bi chee njim aadiik ngbaan ni, le ki bui ke, “Uwumbɔr tii mpɔɔndaan limɔfal li fɔk na. Taa cha ni li muk si sakpen kina aan aawon yɔl.

ref: In your kingdom there is a man who has been given special powers by the holy gods. When your father Nebuchadnezzar was king, this man was known to be as smart, intelligent, and wise as the gods themselves. Your father put him in charge of all who claimed they could talk with the spirits or understand the meanings in the stars or tell about the future.
text: Uja ubaa bi saanaan ni ki kpa Uwumbɔr u bi chain na Aafuur Nyaan u ni. Aate aah nan ye ubɔr pu na, uja ngbaan nan mɔk waalan, ni ichiin ki kpa nlan ke ŋiwaa na. Le Ubɔrkpaan Nebukadnesar nan di u ŋa bibɔɔb, ni binib bimɔk joo inyɔk tun iwaan aatuln na aayidaan.

ref: He also changed the man's name from Daniel to Belteshazzar. Not only is he wise and intelligent, but he can explain dreams and riddles and solve difficult problems. Send for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means.
text: Waalan ni ichiin nyaŋ sakpen le u ŋmaa kpiir tidaŋ aatataa len, ki nyi ŋiyataŋak aatataa, ki ŋmaa kpiir tiwan ni bɔr na mɔk binib, kina pu na, tun yin ni uja u bi yin u ke Daniel na, u ubɔr nan ki yin u ke Beltesasar na, le u ga nan tuk si tiwan nimina mɔmɔk aatataa.” Daniel aah kpiir ŋŋmeen ngbaan aatataa ki len pu na

ref: When Daniel was brought in, the king said: So you are Daniel, one of the captives my father brought back from Judah!
text: Libuul ngbaan ni le bi nan ti joo ni Daniel ubɔr aanimbiin ni, le ubɔr baa u ke, “Sin le ye Daniel, unaagbiija u nte ubɔr nan joo ni si ki nyan ni Juda aatiŋ ni na aa?

ref: I was told that the gods have given you special powers and that you are intelligent and very wise.
text: M ŋun aa pu ke Uwumbɔr u bi chain na Aafuur Nyaan bi aa chee, le aa kpa nlan ki nyi tiwan sakpen.

ref: Neither my advisors nor the men who talk with the spirits of the dead could read this writing or tell me what it means.
text: M yin bisusurb, ni binib bimɔk joo inyɔk tun iwaan aatuln na ke bi nan karn ŋŋmeen mue ki tuk mi mu aatataa, le baa ŋmaa karn, kaa ki bee mu aatataa mu.

ref: But I have been told that you understand everything and that you can solve difficult problems. Now then, if you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. You will wear royal purple robes and have a gold chain around your neck.
text: Tɔ, m ŋun ke aa ŋmaa kani tiwan ni bɔr na aatataa ki kpiir len. Aa yaa ga ŋmaa karn ŋŋmeen mue ki tuk mi mu aatataa kan, bi ga peen si libɔrbɔkul li ŋmal mmam, ni nsiin na, ki gbin si salmaa aaleen mu kpa kipak na aaneen ni, ki li ye nnaan mue ni aaninkpel tatar u paa m pu na.”

ref: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, I will read the writing and tell you what it means. But you may keep your gifts or give them to someone else.
text: Le Daniel gar u ke, “Li joo saapiin aabaa, bee aa ga ŋmaa di i tii ubaa. M ga karn ŋŋmeen ngbaan ki tii mpɔɔndaan, ki kpiir mu aatataa tuk si.

ref: Sir, the Most High God made your father a great and powerful man and brought him much honor and glory.
text: “Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na nan ŋa aate Nebukadnesar ubɔrkpaan, ki tii u liyimbil ni mpɔɔn.

ref: God did such great things for him that people of all nations and races shook with fear. Your father had the power of life or death over everyone, and he could honor or ruin anyone he chose.
text: Waah nan kpa mpɔɔn sakpen pu na, ŋitimbol mɔmɔk, ni ŋinibol mɔmɔk, ni iliin mɔmɔk aanib nan san u ijawaan ki jii unimbiin ni. U yaa nan ban u ku unii u na kan, u ŋani kina la; le u yaa ban unii li kpa limɔfal kan, u cha u bi la. U nan nyuŋni ki jinni binib inimɔɔn waah gee pu na la.

ref: But when he became proud and stubborn, his glorious kingdom was taken from him.
text: Tɔ, u nan di kigaak, ni inimpool, ni mbiin di ŋa waawangol na, nima le Uwumbɔr nan nyan u waanaan ni, ni kipak ni.

ref: His mind became like that of an animal, and he was forced to stay away from people and live with wild donkeys. Your father ate grass like an ox, and he slept outside where his body was soaked with dew. He was forced to do this until he learned that the Most High God rules all kingdoms on earth and chooses their kings.
text: Bi nan jenn nyan u binib chee, le waalandak gur bi ke tiwakor aalandak na. U ni ibon i bi timoor ni na, le nan gur koo tɔb chee, ki ŋmɔ timoor ke unaa na, ki doo timoor ni, nibaa aa bii u pu limaln taa pii u. Gbelngbeln na, le u di naadii tii Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na, ke uma le joo unibɔn aanaan mɔmɔk, ki ga ŋmaa di mu tii unii umɔk u gee u na.

ref: King Belshazzar, you knew all of this, but you still refused to honor the Lord who rules from heaven.
text: “Le sin ujapɔɔn, saa sunn aabaa taab, ki mu nyi tibɔr ngbaan mɔmɔk.

ref: Instead, you turned against him and ordered the cups from his temple to be brought here, so that you and your wives and officials could drink wine from them. You praised idols made of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, even though they cannot see or hear or think. You refused to worship the God who gives you breath and controls everything you do.
text: Aa tun Paacham Aadindaan tiwan ni kaa ŋan na, ki yoor tiyikur ni ŋisambil ŋi nyan ni Waadichal ni na; le sin, ni saaninyuum, ni aapuutiib, ni aabɔtiib nyun ndaan tiyikur ni ŋisambil ngbaan ponn ni, ki pak ŋiwaa ŋi bi di salmaa, ni tikunabr, ni tikumann, ni tikur, ni idɔ, ni ŋitakpal naan ŋi na, ŋiwaa ŋi kaa waa, kaa ŋun tibɔr, kaa nyi nibaa na, kaa tee nyuŋni Uwumbɔr u lik ke aa ga li bi, bee aa ga kpo, ki joo tiwan ni mɔmɔk aa ŋani na.

ref: That's why he sent the hand to write this message on the wall.
text: Kina pu le Uwumbɔr tun ni ŋŋaal ngbaan mu nan ŋmee tibɔr tee.

ref: Belshazzar gave a command for Daniel to be made the third most powerful man in his kingdom and to be given a purple robe and a gold chain.
text: Libuul ngbaan ni le Belsasar bui waatutum ke bi di libɔrbɔkul li ŋmal mmam ni nsiin na peen Daniel, ki di salmaa aaleen mu kpa kipak na gbin uneen ni; le ki di u ŋa waanaan ni aaninkpel tatar u paa u pu na.

ref: That same night, the king was killed.
text: Liyaadaal ngbaan aanyeek le bi ku Belsasar, u ye Babiloŋ aabɔr na;

ref: In order to make sure that his government was run properly, Darius put three other officials in charge of the governors. One of these officials was Daniel.
text: U nan lee binib bilee ki di kpee Daniel pu ke bi li lik biyidam ngbaan aatuln, ni ubɔr mu aageehn.

ref: And he did his work so much better than the other governors and officials that the king decided to let him govern the whole kingdom.
text: Naa nan yunn le Daniel nan mɔk ke u ye unii u nyi waatuln ki jer uŋeen aatɔtiib bilee na, ni biyidam na mu la. Waah nan nyi tiwan ki ti nyaŋ sakpen pu na, ubɔr nan ŋa nlandak ke u di u ŋa waanaan ngbaan mɔmɔk aayidaan.

ref: The other men tried to find something wrong with the way Daniel did his work for the king. But they could not accuse him of anything wrong, because he was honest and faithful and did everything he was supposed to do.
text: Le uŋeen aatɔtiib na, ni biyidam na nan ban isan ke bi bii u waah joo nnaan ngbaan pu na, kaa ŋmaa kan nsan mu pu bi ga di bii u na; ba pu? Daniel nan tun waatuln ni ibamɔn la, kaa kpa beebee.

ref: Finally, they said to one another, “We will never be able to bring any charge against Daniel, unless it has to do with his religion.”
text: Le bi bui tɔb ke, “Taan ŋmaa kan nsan mu pu ti ga ŋmaa di galn Daniel na. Nsan mu diin na le ye waah dii Uwumbɔr aasan mu na.”

ref: They all went to the king and said: “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
text: Kina pu le bi nan buen ti kan ubɔr ki bui u ke, “Ubɔr Darius, Uwumbɔr tii si limɔfal li fɔk na.

ref: Order this to be written and then sign it, so it cannot be changed, just as no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed.”
text: Kina pu na, cha mpɔɔndaan siin nkaal ngbaan ki di saanaŋ nyii mu pu, ki cha mu aatuln piin. Mu li ye Media yaab, ni Pesia yaab aakaal mu kaan ki kpeln na.”

ref: So King Darius made the law and had it written down.
text: Le ubɔr Darius di waanaŋ nyii kina aakaal pu.

ref: Daniel heard about the law, but when he returned home, he went upstairs and prayed in front of the window that faced Jerusalem. In the same way that he had always done, he knelt down in prayer three times a day, giving thanks to God.
text: Daniel aah ŋun ke ubɔr di waanaŋ nyii nkaal ngbaan pu na, le u kun linampal. U nan ti koo paacham aadiik ni, waadichal ponn ni. Kidiik ngbaan aatakolu tiib bibaa nan lik Jerusalem aatiŋ wɔb la. Nima chee, le u nan gbaan ke waah ti ŋani pu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na, takolu tiib bi piir na chee, ki mee Uwumbɔr nfum mutaa nwiin mubaa.

ref: The king was really upset to hear about this, and for the rest of the day he tried to think how he could save Daniel.
text: Ubɔr aah ŋun kina na, usui nan bii pam, le u pɔɔk ubaa ke u kan nsan ki gaa Daniel lii. U nan bi pɔɔni ubaa ki ban kina aasan le nwiin ti lir.

ref: At sunset the men returned and said, “Your Majesty, remember that no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed, not even by the king.”
text: Le bijab ngbaan ki gir buen u chee ki ti bui u ke, “Mpɔɔndaan nyi ke Media ni Pesia yaab aakaal mu ubɔr di waanaŋ nyii mu pu na aan ki ŋmaa kpeln daalbaadaal.”

ref: So Darius ordered Daniel to be brought out and thrown into a pit of lions. But he said to Daniel, “You have been faithful to your God, and I pray that he will rescue you.”
text: Kina pu le ubɔr nan tii nsan ke bi ti chuu Daniel ki di u mee ŋa ichinn aabuu mu ichinn gbii na ni, le ki bui Daniel ke, “Saawumbɔr, u aa di aasui ni saalandak mɔmɔk tii u na gaa si lii.”

ref: A stone was rolled over the pit, and it was sealed. Then Darius and his officials stamped the seal to show that no one should let Daniel out.
text: Le bi di litakpal ŋeeb mbuu ngbaan aamɔb, le ubɔr di uma ubaa aanaŋ ni waaninyuum aanaŋ nyii li pu, ke ubaa taa ŋmaa nyan Daniel.

ref: All night long the king could not sleep. He did not eat anything, and he would not let anyone come in to entertain him.
text: Le ubɔr gir kun, kaa ti ŋmaa geen kinyeek ngbaan, kaa jin tijikaar, kaa cha bi gbiir ngbiir tii u liyaadaal ngbaan.

ref: At daybreak the king got up and ran to the pit.
text: Kichakpinaanyeek ni le ubɔr fii ki ŋa mala ki buen mbuu ngbaan chee.

ref: He was anxious and shouted, “Daniel, you were faithful and served your God. Was he able to save you from the lions?”
text: Waah ti fuu nima chee na, le u yin mala ke, “Daniel, Uwumbɔr u kpa limɔfal na aatutunn, Uwumbɔr u aa dii ni ibamɔn na ŋman ki gaa si lii ichinn ngbaan chee ee?”

ref: Daniel answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever!
text: Le Daniel kii ke, “Uwumbɔr tii mpɔɔndaan limɔfal li fɔk na.

ref: My God knew that I was innocent, and he sent an angel to keep the lions from eating me. Your Majesty, I have never done anything to hurt you.”
text: Uwumbɔr tun ni waatuun le u nan kiir ichinn ngbaan; yaa ŋmaa ŋa mi nibaa. Waah nyi ke maa tun taani ubaa kaa ti ki ŋa mpɔɔndaan mu tibaa na, le u ŋa kina.”

ref: The king was relieved to hear Daniel's voice, and he gave orders for him to be taken out of the pit. Daniel's faith in his God had kept him from being harmed.
text: Ni nan mɔɔr ubɔr ni ti nyaŋ, le u bui ke bi daa nyan ni Daniel mbuu ngbaan ni. Le bi daa nyan ni u ki kan ke nibaa aa ŋa u; ba pu? u nan gaa kii ke Uwumbɔr ga nyan u.

ref: And the king ordered the men who had brought charges against Daniel to be thrown into the pit, together with their wives and children. But before they even reached the bottom, the lions ripped them to pieces.
text: Le ubɔr bui ke bi chur binib bi mɔmɔk nan galn Daniel na, ki nan di bi mɔmɔk, ni bipuutiib, ni baabim mee ŋa mbuu ngbaan ni. Waahr aan bi ti lir mbuu ngbaan aataab na, ichinn ngbaan nan bib chur bi ki nyii kool baakpab.

ref: King Darius then sent this message to all people of every nation and race in the world: “Greetings to all of you!
text: Le Ubɔrkpaan Darius ŋmee kigbaŋ tii ŋitimbol mɔmɔk, ni ŋinibol mɔmɔk, ni iliin mɔmɔk aanib kitiŋ kee pu ke: “M dooni ni mɔmɔk.

ref: I command everyone in my kingdom to worship and honor the God of Daniel. He is the living God, the one who lives forever. His power and his kingdom will never end.
text: Min le len ke maanaan mɔmɔk ni, binib mɔmɔk li san ki pak Daniel Aawumbɔr. U ye Uwumbɔr u kpa limɔfal na la, le u ga li joo dulnyaa ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Ubaa aan ŋmaa bii waanaan, le waapɔɔn mu aan ŋmaa doo.

ref: He rescues people and sets them free by working great miracles. Daniel's God has rescued him from the power of the lions.”
text: U gaal binib lir ki cha bi ŋmar; u tun iwaan, ni lijinjiir aatuln paacham, ni kitiŋ do. U cha ichinn aa ŋmaa ku Daniel.”

ref: All went well for Daniel while Darius was king, and even when Cyrus the Persian ruled.
text: Kina pu na, Daniel nan kan nwankam n‑yoonn mu Darius ni Sairus u nyan ni Pesia aatiŋ ni na nan joo kitiŋ ngbaan. DANIEL AAH ŊEER WAADAŊ AABƆR LEN PU NA (Daniel

ref: Daniel wrote: In the first year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had some dreams and visions while I was asleep one night, and I wrote them down. The four winds were stirring up the mighty sea,
text: Maah nan kan pu kinyeek ngbaan na sɔ: Libuln nan daar ki nyani ŋipepel mɔmɔk ki ti yur nnyusakpem.

ref: when suddenly four powerful beasts came out of the sea. Each beast was different.
text: Le ipeel sakpiin inaa ibaa nyan ni nnyusakpem ni, i mɔmɔk bi ibaabaa kaa naahn tɔb.

ref: The first was like a lion with the wings of an eagle. As I watched, its wings were pulled off. Then it was lifted to an upright position and made to stand on two feet, just like a human, and it was given a human mind.
text: Njan yoo nan naahn uchinn, le ki tee kpa likaagiil aafeen. Maah si lik kina na, le m kan ke ifeen na chuu bar nyan lir kitiŋ. Le bi chuu fiin upeel ngbaan siin utaajal ŋilee pu ke unibɔn na, le ki di unibɔn aalandak tii u.

ref: The second beast looked like a bear standing on its hind legs. It held three ribs in its teeth, and it was told, “Attack! Eat all the flesh you want.”
text: Kipeewanbiik sakpeŋ kiken nan ki nyan ni ki si kitaajal pu. Ki nan kpob isikakpab itaa kimɔb ni, le nneel bui ki ke, “Li ŋmɔ, ŋmɔ tinann saah gee pu na mɔk.”

ref: The fourth beast was stronger and more terrifying than the others. Its huge teeth were made of iron, and what it didn't grind with its teeth, it smashed with its feet. It was different from the others, and it had horns on its head—ten of them.

ref: “This king will speak evil of God Most High, and he will be cruel to God's chosen ones. He will try to change God's Law and the sacred seasons. And he will be able to do this for a time, two times, and half a time.
text: U ga sii Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na, ki muk uma Uwumbɔr waanib. U ga pɔɔn ubaa ke u kpeln baah dii isan i na, ni baajim aakuun mu, le Uwumbɔr aanib ga li bi waapɔɔn ni ki ti saa ŋibin ŋitaa ni ligeln.

ref: But he will finally be judged, and his kingdom completely destroyed.
text: Le paacham aabɔjil ga kal ki ji tibɔr, ki gaa waapɔɔn, ki kuln u kookoo.

text: Kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk aanaan aapɔɔn mɔmɔk ga kpaln Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aanib aanaan la. Baanaan aapɔɔn aan li kpa ndoon, le dulnyaa wee ni aaninkpiib mɔmɔk ga tun baatuln ki kii baamɔi.”

ref: That was what I saw and heard. I turned pale with fear and kept it all to myself.
text: Maah nan ŋmee pu bil na le na. Ijawaan nan chuu mi sakpen, le nwon yɔl, le m nan di tibɔr ngbaan mɔmɔk ŋa nsui ni.

text: Ubɔr Belsasar aah nan ti saa ŋibin ŋitaa nnaan ni na, le m nan ki daŋ tidaŋ ki kan iwaan aawan lelee.

ref: when I looked up and saw a ram standing there with two horns on its head—both of them were long, but the second one was longer than the first.
text: le ki kan upihja u kpa iyiin ilee i fɔk na si gbɔk limɔɔl ngbaan. Waayiin ngbaan mubaa nan fɔk ki pɔɔ jer muken na.

ref: The ram went charging toward the west, the north, and the south. No other animals were strong enough to oppose him, and nothing could save them from his power. So he did as he pleased and became even more powerful.
text: M nan si lik upihja ngbaan aah joo waayiin ngbaan ber toŋ liwilir, ni ŋŋangan, ni ŋŋangii pu na. Le kiwakork kibaa aa nan ŋmaa bui u ke u di cha, bee ki ŋmar waapɔɔn chee. U nan ŋani waah gee pu na ki moo kan mpɔɔn.

ref: I kept on watching and saw a goat come from the west and charge across the entire earth, without even touching the ground. Between his eyes was a powerful horn,
text: Maah nan si dak lik tibɔr tee aatataa aah ye pu na, le uŋoja ubaa nyan ni liwilir wɔb, ki san mala mala le utaa aa ti ki piir kitiŋ. U nan kpa n‑yiin mu fɔk ki gbei na unimbil aakaasisik ni.

ref: and with tremendous anger the goat started toward the ram that I had seen beside the river.
text: U nan san tok upihja u m ba puen kan u si gbɔk limɔɔl na, ki di waapɔɔn mɔmɔk ber toŋ u.

ref: The goat was so fierce that its attack broke both horns of the ram, leaving him powerless. Then the goat trampled on the ram, and no one could do anything to help.
text: M nan kan u buen ti tak upihja ngbaan. Waaŋuul nan fii sakpen, le u ber ti saa upihja ngbaan ki kool waayiin ilee na. Upihja ngbaan aa nan kpa mpɔɔn u sil kiir u. U nan saa u lii kitiŋ ki taa u ŋmal titan ni, le ubaa aa ŋmaa gaa u lii.

ref: After this, the goat became even more powerful. But at the peak of his power, his mighty horn was broken, and four other mighty horns took its place—one pointing to the north and one to the east, one to the south and one to the west.
text: Le uŋoja ngbaan moo pɔɔk ki mak pam, le buyoonn waapɔɔn ti ban mu nyaŋ na, le waayiin ngbaan chuu koo. Mu aah koo na, le iyiin inaa i fɔk ki gbei na nyan mu aabuul ni. I mɔmɔk nan lik yaapepel ibaabaa la.

ref: A little horn came from one of these, and its power reached to the south, the east, and even to the holy land.
text: Iyiin inaa ngbaan ponn ni mubaa pu le n‑yiin waatiir mubaa nan ki nyan ni, le mu aapɔɔn nan ti saa ŋŋangii, ni liwipuul, ni Kitiŋ ki Ŋan na ni.

ref: It became so strong that it attacked the stars in the sky, which were heaven's army. Then it threw some of them down to the earth and trampled on them.
text: Mu nan kan mpɔɔn le ki ti kpaan tak iŋmabi i bi paacham na ibaa, ki ker ibaa lii ni kitiŋ ki taa taa i pu.

text: Binib nan tun titunwanbir li ponn ni, kaa toor iwiin mɔmɔk aatork ki ba ye ke bi toor li ponn ni na, le ki di isan i ye ibamɔn ke bi dii i na lii. Tiwan nimɔk n‑yiin ngbaan nan ŋa na, nan kpa mu tinyoor la.

ref: Then one of the holy angels asked another, “When will the daily sacrifices be offered again? What about this horrible rebellion? When will the temple and heaven's army no longer be trampled in the dust?”
text: Le m ŋun Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib ubaa baa uken ke, “Tiwan ni bi tidaŋ ngbaan ponn ni na ga yunn kinye? Titunwanbir ti gaa iwiin mɔmɔk aatork na ga yunn ki ti saa kinye? Baah taar paacham aaŋmabi ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal pu pu na ga yunn ki ti saa kinye?”

ref: Daniel wrote: I was trying to figure out the meaning of the vision, when someone suddenly appeared there beside me.

text: Waah nan bi len kina na, le nnimbil bɔln, le m lir kitiŋ kaa ki nyi mbaa chee. Le u chuu mi, ki fiin mi siin ntaa pu,

text: “Saah kan upihja u kpa iyiin ilee na ye Media ni Pesia aanaan la.

text: Waah nan jin nnaan ngbaan na aajan aabiln ponn ni, le m nan bi bae Uwumbɔr aagbann ponn ni, ki dakl lik ŋibin imonko itaa ni kipiik ŋi ponn ni Jerusalem ga li bi libiil ni na. Uwumbɔr nan di libiil ngbaan aabɔr kpiir tuk waabɔnabr Jeremia la.

ref: Then, to show my sorrow, I went without eating and dressed in sackcloth and sat in ashes. I confessed my sins and earnestly prayed to the Lord my God: Our Lord, you are a great and fearsome God, and you faithfully keep your agreement with those who love and obey you.

ref: Lord God, you are merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against you
text: Aa ye unimbaasaln la, ki joo cha pinni titunwanbir mu, le tima yii si.

text: Uwumbɔr, ŋun maameel ni maah gaŋni si pu na. Gir maa Saadichal li bi nan ber na. Gir maa li, aan binib mɔmɔk bee ke sin le ye Uwumbɔr.

text: Ubɔr pɔɔl ngbaan ga cha u ni binib pam kpaan kimɔbaan ki pɔɔ na ki ti saa ŋibin ŋilole, le ŋibin ŋilole ngbaan ponn ni yaa nan saa ŋibin ŋitaa ni ligeln na, u ga kuln kitork ni ipiin, Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni. text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le m nan bi mpombiin ni ki ti saa ŋikpaakoo ŋitaa.

text: Maa nan jin tijikaanyaan tibaa, bee tinann, kaa nyun ndaan mu, kaa chaa maayikpir ki ti saa ŋikpaakoo ŋitaa.

ref: Then, on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing on the banks of the great Tigris River,

text: le ki yaar lik paacham ki kan unii ubaa si pee ŋitan ŋi ŋan na aawanpeenkaan, ki buu salmaa aagbapapaln.

ref: His body was like a precious stone, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming fires, his arms and legs like polished bronze, and his voice like the roar of a crowd.
text: Uwon nan moor lak lak ke nleenyaan na. Le unimbil wɔb mu moor ke utaal aah moor pu na, le unimbil bi ke mmii mu gaal na. Uŋaal ni utaa nan moor ke tikumann ti bi pir ti mbamɔm na, le uneel naahn kinipaak aafuuk.

ref: Although the people who were with me did not see the vision, they became so frightened that they scattered and hid.
text: Min baanja le nan kan lijinjiir aawan ngbaan. Bijab bi nan si m chee na aa nan kan nibaa; ijawaan mu nan tee chuu bi, le bi san ti bɔr.

ref: and at the sound of his voice, I fell facedown in a deep sleep.
text: Maah nan ŋun waaneel na, le m fik ki lir kitiŋ mpuul pu ki dɔ chik.

ref: He raised me to my hands and knees
text: Le ŋŋaal mubaa chuu mi ki fiin mi gbaan ntaaŋaayil pu; le nwon beenin gbaa.

ref: and then said, “Daniel, your God thinks highly of you, and he has sent me. So stand up and pay close attention.” I stood trembling, while the angel said:
text: Le Uwumbɔr aatuun ngbaan bui mi ke, “Daniel, Uwumbɔr gee si pam. Fii sil ki pel mbamɔm maah ban m len pu na. Uwumbɔr le tun ni mi aa chee.” Waah len kina na, le m fii sil, le nwon beenin gbaa.

ref: Daniel, don't be afraid! God has listened to your prayers since the first day you humbly asked for understanding, and he has sent me here.
text: Le u ki bui mi ke, “Daniel, taa san ijawaan. Njan aawiin mundaal aa nan sunn aabaa taab ki piin ki bi mee u ke u tii si nlan na, le Uwumbɔr nan ŋun saameel. Saameel ngbaan pu le m dan.

ref: Now I have come here to give you another vision about what will happen to your people in the future.
text: M dan ke m nan cha aa bee tiwan ni ga nan ŋa saanib n‑yoonn mu choo na la. Lijinjiir aawan ngbaan ye n‑yoonn mu choo na aabɔr la.”

ref: While this angel was speaking to me, I stared at the ground, speechless.
text: Waah len kina na, le m si lik kitiŋ, kaa ŋmaa waar mmɔb ki len tibaa.

ref: Then he appeared in human form and touched my lips. I said, “Sir, this vision has brought me great pain and has drained my strength.
text: Le Uwumbɔr aatuun u nan naahn unibɔn na, taln uŋaal ki di mee mmɔgban. Le m bui ke, “Uninkpel, lijinjiir aawan ni m kan tidaŋ ponn ni na tii mi iween ki cha nwon yɔl sakpen.

ref: I am merely your servant. How can I possibly speak with someone so powerful, when I am almost too weak to get my breath?”
text: M gur naahn ke unaagbiija le aah si udindaan aanimbiin ni na. M ga ŋa kinye ki len aa chee tibɔr? Maa ki kpa mpɔɔn, bee kifuurk kibaa nwon ni.”

ref: The angel touched me a second time and said, “Don't be frightened! God thinks highly of you, and he intends this for your good, so be brave and strong.” At this, I regained my strength and replied, “Please speak! You have already made me feel much better.”
text: Le u bui mi ke, “Uwumbɔr gee si, kina pu na, taa cha nibaa li muk si, bee ni faan si.” Waah ki len kina na, le nwon moo pɔɔk sakpen, le m bui ke, “Maaninkpel, tuk mi saah kpa pu aa len na. Aa cha nwon chuu a.”

ref: You also need to know that I protected and helped Darius the Mede in his first year as king. The Angel's Message to Daniel Part One: The Four Kings and Their Successors
text: Min le nan ter u ki tii u mpɔɔn buyoonn Ubɔr Darius nan ye Media yaab aajojoor na aajan aabiln ponn ni na.

ref: What I am going to tell you is certain to happen. Four kings will rule Persia, one after the other, but the fourth one will become much richer than the others. In fact, his wealth will make him so powerful that he will turn everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
text: Maah ban m bui si pu na ye ibamɔn la.” Ijipt ni Siria aanaan aabɔr Uwumbɔr aatuun ngbaan nan ki bui mi ke, “Bibɔrb bitaa ga ki ji nnaan Pesia aatiŋ ni, ki paan tɔb pu, le unanar mu ga paan ni bi pu, uma ga li kpa liwangol ki jer bitaa na. Buyoonn waapɔɔn ni waawangol ngbaan ga ti moo nyaŋ na, le u ga buen ti kpak Griis aanaan.

ref: Then a mighty king will come to power and will be able to do whatever he pleases.
text: “N‑yoonn ngbaan le ubɔr ubaa ga nyan ni ki ga li kaar ki kpa kipak sakpen. Waanaan ga li wiir pam, le u li ŋani waah gee pu na.

ref: But suddenly his kingdom will be crushed and scattered to the four corners of the earth, where four more kingdoms will rise. But these won't be ruled by his descendants or be as powerful as his kingdom.
text: Buyoonn waapɔɔn ti moo nyaŋ na, le waanaan ga bii ki yakr nfum munaa pu. Bibɔrb bi ga ji nnaan waanaan ni na aan li ye waamaal ni aanib, bi mu aan li kpa mpɔɔn mu u nan kpa na.

ref: The king of the south will grow powerful. Then one of his generals will rebel and will rule an even larger kingdom.
text: “Ijipt aabɔr ga li pɔɔ pam. Le waatɔb aajab aaninkpel ubaa ga li pɔɔ jer u, ki ga li joo waanaan ni aapepel li wiir ki jer ubɔr ngbaan aapepel na.

ref: Years later the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom will make a treaty, and the daughter of the king of the south will marry the king of the north. But she will lose her power. Then she, her husband, their child, and the servants who came with her will all be killed. After this,
text: Ŋibin ŋibaa aapuwɔb le Ijipt aabɔr ngbaan ga buen ti ŋa kimɔbaan Siria aabɔr chee, ki ga di ubisal tii u. Kimɔbaan ngbaan mu aan yunn, le bi ga ku upii ngbaan ni uchal, ni ute, ni binaagbiib bi nan dii u nyan ni ute do na, ni unii u sil upuwɔb na.

ref: one of her relatives will become the ruler of the southern kingdom. He will attack the army of the northern kingdom and capture its fortresses.
text: Nee aapuwɔb na, naan yunn le upii ngbaan aado yoo ubaa ga ji nnaan ngbaan. U ga tak Siria aabɔr aajab, ki koo baah maa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na kiir ntim mu na ni, ki nyaŋ bi.

ref: Then he will carry their idols to Egypt, together with their precious treasures of silver and gold, but it will be a long time before he attacks the northern kingdom again. Some years later
text: U ga yoor baawaa, ni salmaa, ni tikunabr aawan ni bi nan di tii baawaa ngbaan na mɔmɔk ki di gir buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni. Ŋibin siib ga jer ki li ye nsuudoon aabin la;

ref: the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom, but he will be forced back to his own country.
text: ŋee aapuwɔb na Siria aabɔr ga buen ti loon tak Ijipt, le Ijipt yaab ga nyaŋ bi, le bi gir kun.

ref: The sons of the king of the north will gather a huge army that will sweep down like a roaring flood, reaching all the way to the fortress of the southern kingdom.
text: “Siria aabɔr aajapɔtiib ga ban bijab pam ki gor kiir butɔb. Bi ponn ni ubaa ga san mala ke nwam na ki ti tak bidim bibaa aatim mu kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na.

ref: But this will make the king of the south angry, and he will defeat this large army from the north.
text: Ijipt aabɔr aaŋuul ga fii pam le u ga ti to Siria aajab butɔb ki nyaŋ bi.

ref: The king of the south will feel proud because of the many thousands he has killed. But his victories won't last long,
text: Waah ga nyaŋ bi ki ku baajab sakpen pu na ga cha u kpaln umakdaan; tɔ, waanyaŋ ngbaan mu aan yunn.

ref: because the king of the north will gather a larger and more powerful army than ever before. Then in a few years, he will start invading other countries.

ref: At this time many of your own people will try to make this vision come true by rebelling against the king of the south, but their rebellion will fail.
text: Le binib pam ga nya Ijipt aabɔr aapuwɔb. Le bijab bibaa ga nyan ni sin Daniel aatimbol ponn ni, ki ga li bir pam ki mu ga nya upuwɔb, ba pu? bi kan tiwan nibaa tidaŋ ponn ni. Bi mu ga lir.

ref: Then the army from the north will surround and capture a fortress in the south, and not even the most experienced troops of the southern kingdom will be able to make them retreat.
text: Kina pu na, Siria aabɔr ga ti loon kitiŋ ki bi maa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ gob ki na ki nyaŋ ki. Ijipt aatɔb aajab ga di cha kaan ki to butɔb; hali bi ponn ni bi kaar sakpen na aan ki li kpa mpɔɔn mubaa bi jan kijaak.

ref: The king who invaded from the north will do as he pleases, and he will even capture and destroy the holy land.
text: Siria aabɔr ngbaan ga ŋa bi waah gee pu na, le ubaa aan ŋmaa sil kiir u. U ga sil Kitiŋ ki Ŋan na ni, ki ga li kpa mpɔɔn ki u kuln ki.

ref: In fact, he will decide to invade the south with his entire army. Then he will attempt to make peace by giving the king of the south a bride from the northern kingdom, but this won't be successful.
text: “Siria aabɔr ga kpokl ke u di waajab mɔmɔk buen butɔb aaban. U ga li ban ke u bii waadin aanaan mɔmɔk, kina pu na, u ga cha u ni uma ŋa kimɔbaan ki di ubisal tii u; le ni mu aan kal kina.

ref: Afterwards, this proud king of the north will invade and conquer many of the nations along the coast, but a military leader will defeat him and make him lose his pride.
text: Nee aapuwɔb, le u ga ti tak ŋitimbol ŋi bi nnyusakpem chee na, ki nyaŋ mu ponn ni pam. Le biwɔwɔm aajab aaninkpel ga nan nyaŋ u ki kuln waamakl ngbaan; mbamɔn, u ga giin Siria aabɔr aamakl ngbaan di ŋa u.

ref: He will retreat to his fortresses in his own country, but on the way he will be defeated and never again be seen.
text: Ubɔr ngbaan ga gir buen waatim mu kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na udo aatiŋ pu; tɔ, nima chee le bi ga ti nyaŋ u, le waamɔfal ga junn.

ref: The next king of the north will try to collect taxes for the glory of his kingdom. However, he will come to a sudden end in some mysterious way, instead of in battle or because of someone's anger. Part Two: The Evil King from the North
text: “Ubɔr uken ga paan ni u pu, uma le ga tun waaninkpel u di mpɔɔn muk binib ki gaa lampoo ke waanaan kan ŋimombil sakpen. Naan yunn le bi ga ku ubɔr ngbaan, le ubaa aan li nyi waakun bɔr; ni mu aan li ye butɔb ponn ni.” Siria yaab aabɔr aah nan ye utunwanbirdaan pu na

ref: The successor of this king of the north will be a worthless nobody, who doesn't even come from a royal family. He will suddenly appear and gain control of the kingdom by treachery.
text: Le Uwumbɔr aatuun ngbaan ki kpiir tuk mi ke: “Siria yaab aabɔr u ga paan ni na ga li bir pam, kaan li kpa nsan ke u ji nnaan, le ki mu tee ga di beebee nyan ni, ubaa aan li nyi u bɔr, le ki nan gaa nnaan ngbaan.

ref: Then he will destroy armies and remove God's chosen high priest.
text: U ga ku unii umɔk nyan sil u pu na, ki kpee Uwumbɔr Aatotoorninkpel mu.

ref: He will make a treaty, but he will be deceitful and break it, even though he has only a few followers.
text: U ga ŋmann ŋitimbol ŋiken, ki cha bi ŋa kimɔbaan, le ki moo kani mpɔɔn kpae; u mu aah joo binib bi na aan li wiir.

ref: Without warning, he will successfully invade a wealthy province, which is something his ancestors never did. Then he will divide among his followers all of its treasures and property. But none of this will last very long.

ref: He will gather a large and powerful army, and with great courage he will attack the king of the south. The king of the south will meet him with a much stronger army, but he will lose the battle, because he will be betrayed
text: “U ga di limakl ki ban bijab bi wiir na ke u ti tak Ijipt yaab aabɔr. Le Ijipt yaab aabɔr ngbaan mu ga gor ni bijab bi wiir ki kpa mpɔɔn jer waajab na ke bi to butɔb. Tɔ, bi ga ŋmann Ijipt yaab aabɔr ngbaan, le u lir.

ref: by members of the royal court. He will be ruined, and most of his army will be slaughtered.

ref: The two kings will meet around a table and tell evil lies to each other. But their plans will fail, because God has already decided what will happen.
text: Le bibɔrb bilee ngbaan ga kpaan kal ke bi ji tijikaar lisambil libaa ni, bi mu aalandak ga li ye titunwanbir aalandak la, le bi mɔnn tɔb inyamɔn. Baan kan baah ban pu na, ba pu? baah ban pu na aayoonn aa kee fuu ni.

ref: Then the king of the north will return to his country with great treasures. But on the way, he will attack the religion of God's people and do whatever else he pleases.
text: Siria yaab aabɔr ga di waah gaa tiwan ni mpɔɔn butɔb ni na gir kun, ki ga pɔɔn ubaa ke u bii Uwumbɔr aanib aah dii nsan mu na. U ga ŋa waah gee pu na, le ki gir kun udo aatiŋ pu.

ref: At the time God has decided, the king of the north will invade the southern kingdom again, but this time, things will be different.
text: “Nee aapuwɔb na, u ga buen ti loon tak Ijipt aatiŋ lelee, le n‑yoonn mumina ma tibɔr ga labr lir u pu.

ref: Ships from the west will come to attack him, and he will be discouraged. Then he will start back to his own country and take out his anger on the religion of God's faithful people, while showing kindness to those who are unfaithful.
text: Rom yaab ga di iŋɔi dan ki nan tak u, le ijawaan ga chuu u. “U ga gee liŋuul ki fenn upuwɔb ki pɔɔn ubaa ke u bii doo Uwumbɔr aanib aasan. U ga ŋa binib bi yii nsan ngbaan na tiŋann.

ref: He will send troops to pollute the temple and the fortress, and he will stop the daily sacrifices. Then he will set up that “Horrible Thing” that causes destruction.
text: Waajab ngem ga bii Uwumbɔr Aadichal. Bi ga kuln iwiin mɔmɔk aatork, ki di tiwanbir ni bii tiwan nimɔk bi chain na siin nima.

ref: The king will use deceit to win followers from those who are unfaithful to God, but those who remain faithful will do everything possible to oppose him.
text: Ubɔr ngbaan ga di kimɔmɔɔn kan binib bi puen yii nsan ngbaan na aaterm, le binib bi dii Uwumbɔr na ga sil kiir bi.

ref: Wise leaders will instruct many of the people. But for a while, some of these leaders will either be killed with swords or burned alive, or else robbed of their possessions and thrown into prison.
text: Binib ngbaan aaninkpiib bi kpa nlan na ga di baalan yakr tii binib pam. Le bi ponn ni bibaa ga kpo butɔb ni; bi ga see bibaa mu mmii ponn ni bi ti kpo, le ki su bibaa mu kinaayuk ki di bi ŋa kiyondiik ni; tɔ, falaa ngbaan mu aan yunn.

ref: They will receive only a little help in their time of trouble, and many of their followers will be treacherous.
text: Buyoonn linikul ngbaan beenin ku na, Uwumbɔr aanib ga kan nterm siib, binib pam le ga kpee bi pu, bi mu ga li ŋani kina ki ban bibaa aajim pu la.

ref: Some of those who are wise will suffer, so that God will make them pure and acceptable until the end, which will still come at the time he has decided.
text: Bi ga ku bilandam ngbaan bibaa, le kina ngbaan ga nyan binib ngbaan baajɔŋ ni. Nimina ga li ŋani kina ki ti saa ndoon, n‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr siin na.

ref: This king will do as he pleases. He will proudly claim to be greater than any god and will insult the only true God. Indeed, he will be successful until God is no longer angry with his people.
text: “Siria aabɔr ga li ŋani waah gee pu na la. U ga li kpa kipupuk ke liwaal libaa aa bi ki pii u, ke u kpaan jer Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na mu. U ga li ŋani kina ki ti saa buyoonn Uwumbɔr ga daa utafal na. Uwumbɔr aah kpokl ke u ŋa pu na, kina le ga ŋa.

ref: This king will reject the gods his ancestors worshiped and the god preferred by women. In fact, he will put himself above all gods
text: Ubɔr ngbaan aatafal aan li bi ŋiwaa ŋi uyaajatiib nan dii na, ni liwaal li bipiib gee na ni. Mbamɔn, utafal aan li bi liwaal libaa, bee Uwumbɔr ni; ba pu? u dak ke u jer ni mɔmɔk.

ref: and worship only the so-called god of fortresses, who was unknown to his ancestors. And he will honor it with gold, silver, precious stones, and other costly gifts.
text: Waah ga ŋa pu na le ye ke u nyuŋ liwaal li kiir ntim mu kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk ki pɔɔ na. U ga di salmaa, ni tikunabr, ni nleenyaan, ni liwangol aapiin tii liwaal li uyaajatiib aa kee dii li daalbaadaal na.

ref: With the help of this foreign god, he will capture the strongest fortresses. Everyone who worships this god will be put in a position of power and rewarded with wealth and land. Part Three: The Time of the End
text: U ga di binib bi dii liwaal yayan na le di kiir waatim mu bi maa ŋigon gob mu na. U ga nyuŋ binib bimɔk tii naadii ke u ye ubɔr na, ki siin bi lituln li kpa kipak na, ki tii bi kitiŋ, ke baapiin le na.

ref: At the time of the end, the king of the south will attack the kingdom of the north. But its king will rush out like a storm with war chariots, cavalry, and many ships. Indeed, his forces will flood one country after another,
text: “Buyoonn Siria aabɔr aayoonn nan ban mu fuu ni na, le Ijipt aabɔr ga ti tak u, le Siria aabɔr ga di waapɔɔn mɔmɔk sil kiir u, u ga di itaan aatɔroku tiib, ni itaan, ni iŋɔi pam jan kijaak ngbaan. U ga loon ntim pam, ke nwam na.

ref: and when they reach the holy land, tens of thousands will be killed. But the countries of Edom and Moab and the ruler of Ammon will escape.

text: U ga loon ntim mumina mɔmɔk ki kpee Ijipt aatiŋ mu.

ref: and he will take its rich treasures of gold and silver. He will also conquer Libya and Ethiopia.
text: U ga yoor Ijipt aatiŋ aawangol li bɔr ki ye salmaa, ni tikunabr, ni liwangol li kpa kidaak na mɔmɔk. U ga nyaŋ Libia ni Kus aatim mu.

ref: But he will be alarmed by news from the east and the north, and he will become furious and cause great destruction.
text: Le tibɔr ti ga nyan ni liwipuul wɔb, ni ŋŋangan wɔb na ga cha ijawaan chuu u, le u moo jan kijaak ke uwaar na, ki ku binib pam.

ref: After this, he will set up camp between the Mediterranean Sea and Mount Zion. Then he will be destroyed, and no one will be able to save him.
text: U ga kpaan gaa waanaan aaboo sakpiin nnyusakpem ni lijool li Uwumbɔr Aadichal si li paab na aakaasisik ni. Tɔ, u mu ga kpo, le ubaa aan li bi nima ke u ter u.”

ref: Many of those who lie dead in the ground will rise from death. Some of them will be given eternal life, and others will receive nothing but eternal shame and disgrace.
text: Bi puen kpo na pam le ga fikr nkun ni: bibaa ga kan limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na, le bibaa mu ji inimɔɔn i kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: Everyone who has been wise will shine as bright as the sky above, and everyone who has led others to please God will shine forever like the stars.
text: Bilandam bi mɔk biken ke bi li tun litulnyaan na ga li wiin chain ke kitaapaak aah wiin pu na, ki wiin ke iŋmabi i bi paacham na, ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: Daniel, I now command you to keep the message of this book secret until the end of time, even though many people will go everywhere, searching for the knowledge to be found in it. The End of Time
text: “Tɔ, Daniel, kpab kigbaŋ ngbaan ki ŋal biin ki pu ki ti saa dulnyaa aadoon; le binib pam ga bii baayoonn ke bi bee tiwan ni bi ŋani na aatataa.”

ref: Daniel wrote: I looked around and saw two other people—one on this side of the river and one on the other side.
text: Le m kan bijab bilee bibaa si gbɔk limɔɔl libaa, ubaa si lidapuul lee, le uken mu si lidapuul liken.

ref: The angel who had spoken to me was dressed in linen and was standing upstream from them. So one of the two beside the river asked him, “How long before these amazing things happen?”
text: Le ubaa baa Uwumbɔr aatuun mu si dandar limɔɔl aapaacham na ke, “Ni ga yunn kinye aan iwaan aawan nimina doo?”

ref: The angel then raised both hands toward heaven and said, “In the name of the God who lives forever, I solemnly promise that it will be a time, two times, and half a time. Everything will be over, when the suffering of God's holy people comes to an end.”
text: Le Uwumbɔr aatuun ngbaan yoor uŋaal ilee paacham; le m ŋun u puu tipuur Uwumbɔr u bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na aayimbil pu ki len ke, “Ni ga li ye ŋibin ŋitaa ni ligeln la. Buyoonn Uwumbɔr aanib aapɔɔn ga kuln na, le tiwan nee mɔmɔk ga ŋa doo.”

ref: I heard what the angel said, but I didn't understand. So I asked, “Sir, how will it all end?” The angel in my vision then replied:
text: M ŋun waah len pu na, ki mu aa bee taatataa. Le m baa ke, “Tɔ, maaninkpel, ni mɔmɔk ga doo kinye?”

ref: Daniel, go about your business, because the meaning of this message will remain secret until the end of time.
text: Le u kii ke, “Daniel, li cha n‑yoonn mue; ba pu? tibɔr timina ye tibɔbɔrkaan la, ki ga li bɔr ki ti saa ndoon aayoonn.

ref: Many people will have their hearts and lives made pure and clean, but those who are evil will keep on being evil and never understand. Only the wise will understand.
text: Uwumbɔr ga toor binib pam ki nya bi tijɔŋ ni aan bi ŋa chain. Binib bi kpa mbiin na aan bee taatataa le ki ga li moo ŋani mbiin; binib bi kpa nlan na baanja le ga bee taatataa.

ref: So, Daniel, be faithful until the end! You will rest, and at the end of time, you will rise from death to receive your reward.
text: “Kina pu na, sin Daniel, li si chob ki ti saa ndoon ngbaan; le aa ga kpo, ki mu tee ga fikr ki ti gaa saapal, ndoon aayoonn ngbaan.”

ref: I am Hosea son of Beeri. When Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah, and when Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel, the Lord spoke this message to me. Hosea's Family
text: Bibɔrb bimina aah nan jin jin nnaan ki paan paan tɔb pu n‑yoonn mu aan Jehoas aajapɔɔn Jeroboam mu nan ye Israel aabɔr na, le Uwumbɔr nan di tibɔr timina tuk Beeri aajapɔɔn Hosea: Juda aabɔrb ngbaan le nan ye Usia, uma le nan puen jin nnaan, le Jotam paan u pu, le Ahas mu nan paan Jotam pu, le Hesekia ti gbeln puwɔb. text: Le n‑yoonn ngbaan m ga bii Israel aajab aapɔɔn, Jesreel aafataŋ ni.”

text: Gomer nan ki ma ubo uken, n‑yoonn mumina ma kan, u nan ye upiibo la. Le Uwumbɔr bui Hosea ke, “Yin u ke ‘Maaneen,’ ba pu? maan ki li neen Israel aanib, kaan ki di cha pinn bi.

ref: But I am the Lord God of Judah, and I will have mercy and save Judah by my own power—not by wars and arrows or swords and cavalry.”
text: Tɔ, m ga li gee Juda yaab ma. Min, Bidindaan Uwumbɔr ga gaa bi lii, m mu aan di kijaak aajum, bee itɔi ni ipiin, bee itaan ni bitandam tun li.”

ref: After Gomer had stopped nursing Lo-Ruhamah, she had another son.
text: Gomer aah lii waapiibo ngbaan na, u nan ki dek, le ki ki ma ubijabo.

ref: Then the Lord said, “Name him Lo-Ammi, because these people are not mine, and I am not their God.” Hope for Israel
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Hosea ke, “Yin u ke ‘Baa‑ye‑maanib,’ ba pu? Israel aanib aan ki li ye maanib, le m mu aan ki li ye Baawumbɔr.” Israel aanaan ga ki gir maa

ref: Someday it will be impossible to count the people of Israel, because there will be as many of them as there are grains of sand along the seashore. They are now called “Not My People,” but in the future they will be called “Children of the Living God.”
text: Israel aanib ga li wiir ke nnyusakpem aatambol na la. Bi ga li wiir jer baah ga kahn, bee bi ŋaŋ bi pu na. Le Uwumbɔr bui bi n‑yoonn mue ke, “Naa ye maanib,” tɔ, n‑yoonn choo le u ga nan bui bi ke, “Ni ye min Uwumbɔr u bi na aabim la.”

ref: Israel and Judah will unite and choose one leader. Then they will take back their land, and this will be a great day for Jezreel.
text: Juda aanib ni Israel aanib ga ki gir kpaan kimɔbaan. Bi ga kpaan le ki ban usaloln ubaa, le bi ga ki pɔr ki kan nkam baatiŋ ni. Een, Jesreel aawiin daal ga li ye nwinkpaan la.

ref: So let your brothers be called “My People” and your sisters be called “Shown Mercy.” The Lord Promises To Punish Israel
text: Kina pu na, ni li yin ninaabitiib Israel yaab ke, “Uwumbɔr Aanib,” ki ki yin bi ke, “Uwumbɔr aah gee bi na.” Gomer ni Israel yaab aah kaa dii mbamɔm pu na

ref: Accuse! Accuse your mother! She is no longer my wife, and now I, the Lord, am not her husband. Beg her to give up prostitution and stop being unfaithful,
text: Maabim, nina aa ki ye mpuu, le u mu aachal aa ki ye mi, tɔ, ni mu tee gaŋ u man. Gaŋ u ke u di cha kidagook.

ref: or I will strip her naked like the day she was born. I will make her barren like a desert, and she will die of thirst.
text: U yaa kaa di cha kan, m ga gbabr u ki cha u uŋmeen ke baah nan ma u nwiin mundaal na. M ga ŋa u nkuun ke kitiŋ ki kaa kpa tijikaar na, le ki cha nnyunyuu ku u.

ref: Your mother was unfaithful. She was disgraceful and said, “I'll run after my lovers. Everything comes from them— my food and drink, my linen and wool, my olive oil and wine.”
text: Maan san waabim kinimbaak; bi ye upiidagoor u kaa san inimɔɔn na aabim la. Uma ubaa le len ke, “M ga buen mbɔtiib chee la, bi tii mi tijikaar ni nnyun, ki tii mi ŋikeken, ni olif aakpan, ni ndaan.”

ref: I, the Lord, will build a fence of thorns to block her path.
text: Kina pu na, m ga di ikokon le gob u ki maa ligoln kiir waasan.

ref: She will run after her lovers, but not catch them; she will search, but not find them. Then she will say, “I'll return to my first husband. Life was better then.”
text: U ga li san paa ubɔtiib pu, le kaan pii bi. U ga ban bi, kaan kan bi, le ki bui ke, “M ga gir nchakpok chee la, nima chee nan soor ni maah gur bi pu na.”

ref: She didn't know that her grain, wine, and olive oil were gifts from me, as were the gold and silver she used in worshiping Baal.
text: Waan kii daalbaadaal ke ni ye mi le tii u tijikaar, ni ndaan, ni olif aakpan, ni tikunabr, ni salmaa u mɔmɔk u joo dooni liwaal Baal na.

ref: So I'll hold back the harvest of grain and grapes. I'll take back my wool and my linen that cover her body.
text: Kina pu na, lijikaacheel yoonn kan, m ga gaa maajikaar ni ndaan, ki gaa ŋikeken ŋi m tii u ke u li joo gbae na.

ref: Then I'll strip her naked in the sight of her lovers. No one can rescue her.
text: M ga gbabr u ki cha u uŋmeen ubɔtiib aanimbil ni, le ubaa aan ŋmaa nyan u maapɔɔn ni.

ref: I'll stop Israel's celebrations— no more New Moon Festivals, Sabbaths, or other feasts.
text: M ga kuln waajim mɔmɔk; m ga kuln libiln libiln, ni uŋmal uŋmal, ni likpaakool daal aajim, ni njim mu u siin na mɔmɔk.

ref: She said, “My lovers gave me vineyards and fig trees as payment for sex.” Now I, the Lord, will ruin her vineyards and fig trees; they will become clumps of weeds eaten by wild animals.
text: M ga bii ndaan aasubil aasui ni ŋisubil ŋiken aasui, i u bui ke waah tun tii ubɔtiib pu na le bi tii u na. M ga cha waadaan aasubil aasui ni ŋisubil ŋiken aasui na kpaln kichook, ipeel le ga bii ni mɔmɔk.

ref: I'll punish her for the days she worshiped Baal and burned incense to him. I'll punish her for the times she forgot about me and wore jewelry and rings to attract her lovers. I, the Lord, have spoken! The Lord Will Help Israel
text: N‑yoonn mu mɔmɔk u nan sulni mbɔr ki seer tulalee aayon tii liwaal Baal ki peeni nleenyaan ki san dii ubɔtiib na pu le m ga daa utafal. Uwumbɔr le len kina. Uwumbɔr aah gee waanib pu na

ref: Israel, I, the Lord, will lure you into the desert and speak gently to you.
text: Kina pu na, m ga ki giin u buen nteersakpiin ni, nima chee le m ga ti ki di tibɔmbɔr gaa u.

ref: I will return your vineyards, and then Trouble Valley will become Hopeful Valley. You will say “Yes” to me as you did in your youth, when leaving Egypt.
text: M ga ki di waah nan kpa ndaan aasubil aasar ti na tii u, ki cha kifataŋ ki bi yin ki ke Tibɔbir aafataŋ na kpaln limakl aabisamɔb. Waah nan laa ye usapɔɔn, ki nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni ki keei mi pu na, kina le u ga ki kii mi,

ref: I promise from that day on, you will call me your husband instead of your master.
text: le ki ga ki yin mi ke uchal, waan ki yin mi waaninkpel ke waah yin liwaal Baal pu na.

ref: I will no longer even let you mention the names of those pagan gods that you called “Master.”
text: Maan ki cha u yin liwaal Baal aayimbil kpala.

ref: And I will agree to let you live in peace—you will no longer be attacked by wild animals and birds or by weapons of war.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ni ipeel, ni inyoon i bir na ga puu tipuukpaan tii tɔb, le ni taa ŋa maanib nibaa. M ga ki nyan butɔb aajawan mɔmɔk ni ye kijaak aajum na, ni itɔi na kitiŋ ngbaan ni, ki cha maanib li bi nsuudoon, ni lifuur ni.

ref: I will scatter the seeds and show mercy to Lo-Ruhamah. I will say to Lo-Ammi, “You are my people,” and they will answer, “You are our God.”
text: M ga maa maanib kaan kitiŋ ngbaan pu ki tii bi liwangol. M ga mɔk baah nan yin bi ke “Maa‑neen” bi na ngeehm, ki ga bui baah yin bi ke “Baa‑ye‑maanib” na ke “Bi‑ye‑maanib” la, le bi ga kii ke, “Aa ye timi Aawumbɔr la.”

ref: Once again the Lord spoke to me. And this time he said, “Hosea, fall in love with an unfaithful woman who has a lover. Do this to show that I love the people of Israel, even though they worship idols and enjoy the offering cakes made with fruit.”
text: Le Uwumbɔr nan bui mi ke, “Gir ki ti di ngeehm tii upii u bi ubɔɔn chee na. Aa li gee u ke maah gee Israel aanib pu na, aa mu tee lik kan, bi di bibaa tii ŋiwaa le ki gee ke bi li joo ŋisubil ŋi kuur na tii ŋiwaa ipiin.”

ref: Then I said, “Now you are mine! You will have to remain faithful to me, though it will be a long time before we sleep together.”
text: M nan bui u ke u ga kal ni yunn pam, ki taa tun kidagook aatuln, ki kiir mi, le n‑yoonn ngbaan na m ga li ka kii u.

ref: It will also be a long time before Israel has a king or before sacrifices are offered at the temple or before there is any way to get guidance from God.
text: Kina le Israel yaab mu ga li gur bi, kaa kpa bibɔrb ni bisalolm, kaan ki li kpa kitork ki toor, kaan li kpa ŋitakpal ŋi bi toor na, kaan li kpa ŋiwaa, bee tiwanaankaan nibaa ke bi li joo buu tibɔɔr.

ref: But later, Israel will turn back to the Lord their God and to David their king. At that time they will come to the Lord with fear and trembling, and he will be good to them.
text: Tɔ, n‑yoonn tee choo, le Israel aanib ga nan ki fenn dan Bidindaan Uwumbɔr chee, ki dan ubɔr David aayaabil chee. Le bi ga li san Uwumbɔr ki gaa waapiin i ŋan na.

ref: And so your land is a desert. Every living creature is dying— people and wild animals, birds and fish. The Lord Warns the Priests
text: Kina pu le kitiŋ ga kuur, le tiwan nimɔk bi ki pu na ga kpoi. Tiwakor, ni inyoon, ni ijan mu ga kpoi.” Uwumbɔr aah galn bitotoorb pu na

ref: Don't accuse just anyone! Not everyone is at fault. My case is against you, the priests.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Ubaa taa galn binib ngbaan ki taa sak bi; nimi bitotoorb chee le maagalm cha.

ref: You and the prophets will stumble day and night; I'll silence your mothers.
text: Kinyeek ni nwiin pu mɔk ni moo bii cha, le bibɔnabr mu bi kina la. M ban m kuln nina Israel la.

ref: You priests have rejected me, and my people are destroyed by refusing to obey. Now I'll reject you and forget your children, because you have forgotten my Law.
text: Maanib aah kaa bee mi na, le baamɔfal ga junn. Nimi bitotoorb yii ke naan bee mi, le ki yii maakaal, kina pu le m mu yii nimi, kaan kii ke nijapɔtiib li ye maatotoorb.

ref: By adding more of you priests, you multiply the number of people who sin. Now I'll change your pride into shame.
text: “Nimi bitotoorb aah wiir pu na, kina le naah tun mi titunwanbir ti na mu wiir, le ki ga cha m kpeln nimi aanyuŋ ŋa inimɔɔn.

ref: You encourage others to sin, so you can stuff yourselves on their sin offerings.
text: Maanib aatunwanbir pu le ni moo kani titunwanbir aatork aawangol, le ki ban ke bi li moo tun titunwanbir.

ref: That's why I will punish the people for their deeds, just as I will punish you priests.
text: Nimi ni binib ngbaan aatafadaan ga li ye tiwanbaan la. M ga daa nitafal ki cha ni pa naah tun titunwanbir ti na pu.

ref: You expect wooden idols and other objects of wood to give you advice. Lusting for sex at pagan shrines has made you unfaithful to me, your God.
text: Lidɔgeln chee le bi chaa ti baa tibɔkpiirkaan. Ndɔ le tuk bi baah ban ke bi li nyi tiwan ni na. Bi di mi Uwumbɔr di mee. Bi di bibaa tii ŋiwaa ke upii u di ubaa ŋa udagoor na la.

ref: You offer sacrifices on mountaintops and hills, under oak trees, and wherever good shade is found. Your own daughters and daughters-in-law sell themselves for sex.
text: Ŋijoo paab le bi toor ŋiwaa, le ki seer nnyɔknii isui sakpiin i aabon taln buen dandar na taab, ŋigongon pu, isui aaboon aah mɔ ni chee na, kina pu le nibisatiib joo bibaa kooh, le nibipuutiib mu kpaln bidagoob.

ref: But I won't punish them. You men are to blame, because you go to prostitutes and offer sacrifices with them at pagan shrines. Your own foolishness will lead to your ruin.
text: Nimi ni bipiib bi bi nimi aawaadir ni na aah tun kidagook aatuln ki toor tijɔŋ aatork na pu, le maan daa nibisatiib ni nibipuutiib aatafal. Liyataŋakl libaa le len ke, ‘Binib yaa bi kaa kpa nlan kan, bi wɔŋ la.’

ref: Israel, you are unfaithful, but don't lead Judah to sin. Stop worshiping at Gilgal or at sinful Bethel. And quit making promises in my name—the name of the living Lord.
text: “Tɔ, nimi Israel aanib aa kii maamɔb, Juda yaab ma taa ji kina aabɔkpol. Ni taa ki buen Gilgal, bee Bef Afenn ki ti doon mi, ki taa puu tipuur nima chee min Uwumbɔr u bi na aayimbil pu.

ref: You are nothing more than a stubborn cow— so stubborn that I, the Lord, cannot feed you like lambs in an open pasture.
text: Israel aanib aatafal pɔɔ ke uŋoob na la. Maan kpiin bi mmoŋmɔpaan ni ke ipihbi na.

ref: You people of Israel are charmed by idols. Leave those people alone!
text: Ŋiwaa le chuu Israel aanib. Cha bi li dii baah gee nsan mu na.

ref: You get drunk, then sleep with prostitutes; you would rather be vulgar than lead a decent life.
text: Bi yaa ti nyun ndaan bab kan, le bi fii lir kidagook pu, le ki neen inimɔɔn n‑yoonn ngbaan ki jer kipak.

ref: And so you will be swept away in a whirlwind for sacrificing to idols.
text: Uwumbɔr ga di bi buen ke kinaakpaajabuŋ le aah daar bi cha na, le inimɔɔn ga chuu bi ŋiwaa aatork pu.

ref: Listen, you priests! Pay attention, Israel! Listen, you members of the royal family. Justice was your duty. But at Mizpah and Mount Tabor you trapped the people.
text: “Nimi bitotoorb, li pel nimina man. Israel yaab, pel man. Nimi bi ye nnaan ni yaab na, li pel man. Nimi aatuln le ye ke ni di ibamɔn ji binib tibɔr, kina pu na, m ga ji nimi tibɔr. Ni kpaln gaawɔb le ki dɔ Mispa, le ki ye kipɔɔk Tabor aajool pu,

ref: At the place of worship you were a treacherous pit, and I will punish you.
text: le ki ye libuusakpeln Sitim aatiŋ ponn ni, le m ga daa ni mɔmɔk aatafal.

ref: Your evil deeds are the reason you won't return to me, your Lord God. And your constant craving for sex keeps you from knowing me.
text: Binib ngbaan aah tun titunwanbir ti na le cha baa ŋmaa gir ni Baawumbɔr chee. Ŋiwaa kpa bi pu mpɔɔn, le baa ki nyi Uwumbɔr.

ref: Israel, your pride testifies to your guilt; it makes you stumble, and Judah stumbles too.
text: Israel yaab aagaak mɔk ke bi kpa ngalm. Baatunwanbir cha bi gbeer le ki lir, le Juda aanib mu lir dii bi.

ref: You offer sheep and cattle as sacrifices to me, but I have turned away and refuse to be found.
text: Bi joo baapiih ni inaa ki ti kɔr toor ke bi tii Uwumbɔr la, le naa ter bi. Waah siir cha bi na, le baa kan u.

ref: You have been unfaithful to me, your Lord; you have had children by prostitutes. So at the New Moon Festival, you and your crops will be destroyed. The Lord Warns Israel and Judah
text: Bi nyan Uwumbɔr aapuwɔb; kina pu le baabim aa ye waabim. Kina pu le naan yunn le baatim ga kuln. Juda ni Israel yaab aatɔb aabɔr

ref: Give a warning on the trumpet! Let it be heard in Gibeah, Ramah, and sinful Bethel. Benjamin, watch out!
text: Pii butɔb aakpiin Gibea aatiŋ ni man. Faa nkuun Rama aatiŋ ni man. Faa butɔb aakuun Bef Afenn aatiŋ ni. Benjaminn aajab, fii buen butɔb ni man.

ref: I, the Lord, will punish and wipe out Israel. This is my solemn promise to every tribe of Israel.
text: Ntafadaan aawiin choo, le Israel aatiŋ ga ber. Israel aanib, nimina ga sil ŋa.

ref: Judah's leaders are like crooks who move boundary markers; that's why I will flood them with my anger.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Juda aanib aayidam aah koo Israel aatiŋ ni ki sun kaatiŋ ngem na, le maaŋuul fii. Kina pu na, m ga cha ntafadaan dan bi pu ke nwam na.

ref: Now I, the Lord, will fill Israel with maggots and make Judah rot.
text: M ga kuln Israel ni Juda yaab.

ref: When Israel and Judah saw their sickness and wounds, Israel asked help from Assyria and its mighty king. But the king cannot cure them or heal their wounds.
text: “Israel aatiŋ nan kan kaah bun pu na, Juda mu kan kibaa aabuun na, le Israel buen Asiria aabɔrkpaan na chee ki ti ban nterm, le waa nan ŋmaa tii ki laafee, bee u yann kaabuun.

ref: So I'll become a fierce lion attacking Israel and Judah. I'll snatch and carry off what I want, and no one can stop me.
text: M ga tak Israel ni Juda aanib ke uchinn na la. Min mbaa le ga daa par par bi, ki siir cha bi. M yaa nan dar bi cha kan, ubaa aan ŋmaa gaa bi lii.

ref: Then I'll return to my temple until they confess their guilt and worship me, until they are desperate and beg for my help.
text: “M ga siir cha maanib, ki ti saa buyoonn bi ga ji falaa u ŋeer baatunwanbir ki gir ban ni mi na. Nibaakan bi ga fenn ban mi limukl ngbaan ni.”

ref: Let's return to the Lord. He has torn us to shreds, but he will bandage our wounds and make us well.
text: Binib ngbaan len ke, “Cha ti gir Uwumbɔr chee man. U tii timi titotonn, le ki ga sil tii timi laafee; u tii timi ibuun, le ki ga sil ban litaln poo biin i pu, u ga sil ŋa kina.

ref: In two or three days he will heal us and restore our strength that we may live with him.
text: U ga ki gaa timi iwiin ilee aakaasisik ni, le ti ga li bi unimbiin ni.

ref: Let's do our best to know the Lord. His coming is as certain as the morning sun; he will refresh us like rain renewing the earth in the springtime. The Lord Speaks to Israel and Judah
text: Cha ti pɔɔn tibaa man ki li nyi Uwumbɔr, ki nyi waah ban pu na. U ga sil dan ti chee ke kitaak aah ga woln pu na, u ga dan ti chee ke unaalantaal u sɔŋni kitiŋ na.”

ref: People of Israel and Judah, what can I do with you? Your love for me disappears more quickly than mist or dew at sunrise.
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Israel ni Juda yaab, m ga ki ŋa nimi kinye? Naah kpa ngeehm mu m pu na fir mala ke kichakpiik ni aakpakpal na la, ki naahn limaln li fir nchakpawiin pu na.

ref: That's why I slaughtered you with the words of my prophets. That's why my judgments blazed like the dawning sun.
text: Kina pu le m di maah ga daa nitafal ki kuln nimi pu na tun ni maabɔnabr. Maah ban pu ni chee na aa duk kpala:

ref: Everyone in Gilead is evil; your hands are stained with the blood of victims.
text: Gilead ye kitiŋ ki gbii titunwanbirdam ni binikurb na la.

ref: You priests are like a gang of robbers in ambush. On the road to Shechem you murder and commit other horrible crimes.
text: Bitotoorb na bi ke kinaayupaak ki ti dɔ nsan ni kiir unii na la. Hali bi yaa cha Sekem aatiŋ ki bi chain na ni kan, bi ku binib nsan ni la. Bi po nyi le ki tun titunwanbir timina mɔmɔk.

ref: I have seen a terrible thing in Israel— you are unfaithful and unfit to worship me.
text: M kan tibɔbir tibaa Israel aatiŋ ni: tima le ye ke maanib Israel yaab bii bibaa le ki dooni ŋiwaa.

ref: People of Judah, your time is coming too. The Lord Wants To Help Israel I, the Lord, would like to make my nation prosper again
text: “Le nimi Juda aanib ma, m siin n‑yoonn mu m ga di daa ni mu aatafal na.

ref: The king and his officials take great pleasure in their sin and deceit.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Binib joo baatunwanbir aakpokl le ŋmanni ubɔr ni waaninkpiib.

ref: On the day their king was crowned, his officials got him drunk, and he joined in their foolishness.
text: Ubɔr aajim daal, le bi cha ubɔr ni waaninkpiib nyu ndaan gbii le ki jɔr.

ref: Their anger is a fire that smolders all night, then flares up at dawn.
text: Mbamɔn, baakpokl wu ke baah pu boroboro nin chee na aamii na la. Kinyeek ni kitaak aawoln pu, baaŋuul nyakr la, le kichakpiik ni kan, li gaa mmii.

ref: They are flames destroying their leaders. And their kings are powerless; none of them trust me.
text: “Baaŋuul aakaasisik ni le bi ku baajojoob. Bi ku baabɔrb paani tɔb pu la. Le ubaa aa tee mee mi ki ban nterm.” Israel ni ŋitimbol ŋiken aabɔr

ref: The people of Israel have mixed with foreigners; they are a thin piece of bread scorched on one side.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Israel aanib bi ke boroboro u bi pun u aan waa biir mbamɔm na la. Bi ka lik ŋitimbol ŋi mann goln bi na pu le ki ban nterm,

ref: They don't seem to realize how weak and feeble they are; their hair has turned gray, while foreigners rule.
text: kaa nyi ke biniyayam aaterm ngbaan gaal baapɔɔn la. Baawiin aa ki daa, le baa kpaan nyi.

ref: I am the Lord, their God, but in all of their troubles their pride keeps them from returning to me. No Help from Foreign Nations The Lord said:
text: Israel aanib aagaak wii ban bi la. Hali tiwan ni mɔmɔk ŋa na pu, baa fenn ki gir ni min Bidindaan Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: But I will catch them in a net as hunters trap birds; I threatened to punish them, and indeed I will.
text: Bi yaa bi jer kan, m ga taln kipɔɔk ki chur bi ke inyoon na. Baah tun titunwanbir ti na pu le m ga daa bitafal.

ref: Trouble and destruction will be their reward for rejecting me. I would have rescued them, but they told me lies.
text: “Baamɔfal junn a. Bi di mi lii le ki nyan mpuwɔb. Bi ga kuln. M ba ban ke m ter bi la, le bi mu aa dii mi mbamɔm.

ref: I taught them what they know, and I made them strong. Now they plot against me
text: Min le nan kpiin bi ki tii bi mpɔɔn, le bi fenn ki kpokl m pu.

ref: and refuse to obey. They are more useless than a crooked arrow. Their leaders will die in war for saying foolish things. Egyptians will laugh at them.
text: Bi nya mpuwɔb n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, le ki dii liwaal li kaa kpa mpɔɔn mubaa na. Saan ŋmaa li kpa bi pu limakl ke butɔm bu gɔr na la. Baasalolm aah len tibɔr kigaak ŋmeen na, le bi ga kpo mpɔɔkun, le Ijipt yaab ga laa bi.”

ref: Sound a warning! Israel, you broke our agreement and ignored my teaching. Now an eagle is swooping down to attack my land.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Faa nkuun man. Bidim boon nan lir maatiŋ pu ke ŋikaagii na la. Maanib bii tipuur ti m nan puu tii bi na, le ki yii maamɔkm.

ref: Israel, you say, “We claim you, the Lord, as our God.”
text: Bi yin mi ke Baawumbɔr la, le ki bui ke bi ye maanib le ki nyi mi,

ref: But your enemies will chase you for rejecting our good agreement.
text: le ki tee yii lituln li ŋan na. Kina pu na, baadim ga li ban bi.
