text: Le Jona nan tee fii ki di toŋ nibaa wɔb ke u bɔr Uwumbɔr. U nan di buen Jopa aatiŋ ni la, nima chee le u ti kan buŋɔb bu cha Speenn aatiŋ ni na. U nan pan le ki koo bu ponn ni, biŋɔŋaab chee, ke bi buen Speenn aatiŋ ni, nin chee Uwumbɔr aan ki kan u na.

ref: But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr nan cha libupɔɔl libaa dan nan lir nnyusakpem ngbaan pu, libuln ngbaan nan bir pam, le buŋɔb ngbaan nan ban bu wii ki muin.

ref: The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter. All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep.
text: Ijawaan nan chuu biŋɔŋaab ngbaan, le bi mɔmɔk wii ki yin baawaa ki ban nterm. Bi nan nyan ŋitun ŋi bi bu ponn ni na mae ŋa nnyun ni ke bu taa ki li nyuun. N‑yoonn mue na, Jona nan dɔ bu ponn ni ki dɔ geen.

ref: The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
text: Le biŋɔŋaab ngbaan aaninkpel nan ti kan u nima chee, le ki baa u ke, “Aa dɔ ŋani ba, aa dɔ geen la aa? Fii sil ki mee saawaal aan li ter timi. Nibaakan, li ga san timi kinimbaak ki gaa timi lii.”

ref: Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
text: Biŋɔŋaab ngbaan nan bui tɔb ke, “Cha ti pul kipulk timi aakaal aah mɔk pu na man, ki lik ke ŋma ye unimbɔŋdaan u joo ni timi linimaln limina na.” Bi nan ŋa kina, le ki kan ke Jona le ye unimbɔŋdaan.

ref: They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
text: Le bi bui u ke, “Tɔ, bui timi, ŋma aan ti ga galn tibɔr timina pu? Aa bi ŋani ba do chee na? Aa nyan ni lilatingbaln ni? Aado ye la chee? Aa ye lilanibol aanii?”

ref: Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
text: Le Jona gar bi ke, “M ye Hiibru aanii la. M dooni Uwumbɔr u ye paacham Aadindaan, ki naan kitiŋ, ni nnyusakpem na la.”

ref: When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
text: Jona nan ki tuk bi ke u bi san bɔrni Uwumbɔr la. Ijawaan nan chuu biŋɔŋaab ngbaan, le bi bui u ke, “Saah ŋa pu na aa ŋan kpala.”

ref: The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
text: Kitaabuŋ ngbaan nan moo pɔɔk kpae la, le biŋɔŋaab ngbaan baa u ke, “Ti ga ŋa kinye aan kitaabuŋ ngbaan di cha?”

ref: Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
text: Jona nan gar bi ke, “Di mi ŋa nnyusakpem ngbaan ni man, le mu ga doon suuna. M nyi ke ni ye maataani pu le ni nan koo kitaabuŋbiik kee ni.”

ref: The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute.
text: Tɔ, biŋɔŋaab ngbaan nan tee pɔɔn bibaa ke bi di buŋɔb ngbaan buen ligbaal, le ki moo ŋaal bu mpɔɔn pu. Tɔ, kitaabuŋ nan moo kpae la, le baa ŋmaa buen nibaa chee.

ref: So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.”
text: Kina pu le bi wii ki yin Uwumbɔr ke, “Uwumbɔr, ti mee si, taa daa titafal ki ku timi uja wee aamɔfal pu. Uwumbɔr, sin le tun nimina mɔmɔk; ni ye saatuln la,”

ref: Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down.
text: le ki yoor Jona di mee ŋa nnyusakpem ngbaan ni. Libuul ngbaan ni le mu doon suuna.

ref: The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
text: Nima le nan cha biŋɔŋaab ngbaan san Uwumbɔr ijawaan ki toor kitork tii u, ki puu tipuur tii u.

ref: The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr nan cha ujan sakpiin ubaa chuu Jona di nab, le u nan bi ujan ngbaan aaponn ni, iwiin itaa ni tinyer titaa.

ref: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
text: Jona nan bi ujan ngbaan aaponn ni taab le ki mee Udindaan Uwumbɔr ke:

ref: When I was in trouble, Lord, I prayed to you, and you listened to me. From deep in the world of the dead, I begged for your help, and you answered my prayer.
text: “Uwumbɔr, buyoonn nsui bii na le m yin si, le aa kii maayim ngbaan. M nan bi kitekpiitiŋ ni taab taab ki wii yin si ki ban nterm, le aa ŋun maah yin pu na.

ref: You threw me down to the bottom of the sea. The water was churning all around; I was completely covered by your mighty waves.
text: Aa di mi mee lii taab taab, nnyusakpem aataab, nin chee nnyun nan mann goln mi na, le saanyunkpenn ti kpa mpɔɔn sakpen na fii labr m pu.

ref: I thought I was swept away from your sight, never again to see your holy temple.
text: M nan nyi ke aa nyan mi aanimbiin ni la, le maan ki kan Saadichal li bi chain na.

ref: I was almost drowned by the swirling waters that surrounded me. Seaweed had wrapped around my head.
text: Nnyun nan biin m pu ki kpar mi, nnyusakpem nan biin m pu kookoo a, le nnyusakpem ponn ni aamoor biin n‑yil pu.

ref: I had sunk down deep below the mountains beneath the sea. I knew that forever, I would be a prisoner there. But, you, Lord God, rescued me from that pit.
text: M nan buen taab taab ŋijoo aataab, ki ti fuu kitiŋ ki aabisamɔi lak n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na ni. Ndindaan Uwumbɔr, sin le giin nyan ni mi taab taab ngbaan, le m beenin kpa limɔfal.

ref: When my life was slipping away, I remembered you— and in your holy temple you heard my prayer.
text: Uwumbɔr, buyoonn m dak ke maamɔfal doo na, le m mee si, le aa bi Saadichal li bi chain na ponn ni ki ŋun maameel ngbaan.

ref: All who worship worthless idols turn from the God who offers them mercy.
text: Binib bi dooni ŋiwaa ŋi kaa po kpa tinyoor tibaa na yii saanimbaasaln.

ref: But with shouts of praise, I will offer a sacrifice to you, my Lord. I will keep my promise, because you are the one with power to save.
text: Le mma ga gaa ilahn pak si, m ga toor kitork tii si, ki ŋa maah puu ke m ga ŋa pu na. Limɔfal nyan ni Uwumbɔr chee la.”

ref: The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui ujan ngbaan ke u ti wuln Jona lii limɔɔtambol pu, le u ŋa kina.

ref: Once again the Lord told Jonah
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki gir len Jona chee tibɔr,

ref: to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
text: ki bui ke, “Li cha kitisakpeŋ Ninefa ni, ki ti di tibɔr ti m di tii si na tuk bi.”

ref: Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it.
text: Jona nan kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki buen Ninefa, kitisakpeŋ ki u nan di iwiin itaa bɔ dii ki ponn ni ki ti saa kimɔk na.

ref: After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
text: Jona nan piin ki bɔ dii kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni, le waah chuun nwimɔn aasachuln na, le u mooni tuk binib ngbaan ke, “Joo cha ni iwiin imonko ilee na, Ninefa aatiŋ ga kuln.”

ref: They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
text: Ninefa aanib nan tii naadii Uwumbɔr aah di tibɔr ti tuk bi na pu, le ki cha unii mɔk lul bumɔb; le binib mɔmɔk, bi ye biwankpadam ni bigiim na mɔmɔk nan peen tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na ki mɔk ke bi kpeln baabimbin la.

ref: When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust.
text: Ninefa aabɔr aah ŋun tibɔr ngbaan na, le u fii libɔrjal pu, ki chuu peer waanaan aawanpeenkaan, le ki di tiwanpeenkaan ni saak kuub na peen, le ki kal nfatan ponn ni.

ref: When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
text: Uwumbɔr nan kan baah ŋa pu na; u nan kan ke bi di cha baabiin aabimbin, kina pu le u kpeln waalandak kaa ki daa bitafal ke waah ba ga daa pu na.

ref: Jonah was really upset and angry.
text: Jona aasui nan bii kina ngbaan pu, le liŋuul chuu u sakpen.

ref: So he prayed: Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
text: Le u mee Uwumbɔr ke, “Uwumbɔr, maah nan laa bi linampal na, m nan len ke kina le aa ga ŋa. Kina pu le m nan pɔɔn mbaa ke m san mala ki buen Speenn aatiŋ ni. M nyi ke aa ye Uwumbɔr u gee binib ki san bi kinimbaak na la, aa kpa limɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki kpa tiŋann n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki ŋmaa kpelni saalandak kaa dar binib aatafal.

ref: The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
text: Le Uwumbɔr nan gar u ke, “Saah gee liŋuul pu na, ni ŋan aa?”

ref: Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
text: Jona nan nyan kitiŋ ngbaan ni, le ki di toŋ liwipuul wɔb ki ti kal nibaa chee. Nima chee le u nan gaa kinambuŋ ki kal kaaboon ni, ki ka kii tiwan ni ga ŋa Ninefa aatiŋ na.

ref: The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine,
text: Le Uwumbɔr cha lipulaajil punn ki jon kinambuŋ ngbaan, ki biin ki pu, ki tii Jona mboon, aan ki sɔŋ uwon. Jona aasui nan piir lipulaajil ngbaan pu sakpen.

ref: but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up.
text: Tɔ, kitaak ki ga woln na aachakpinaanyeek ni, le Uwumbɔr cha likpaambil libaa di lipulaajil ngbaan aafar ŋman, le li kpo.

ref: During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
text: Nwiin aah puu na, le Uwumbɔr cha liwipuul wɔb aabuln li ton na dan, le ki nan see Jona aayil, le u ti ban u fik. Le u mee Uwumbɔr ke u ba kpo. U nan bui ke, “M yaa ba tee kpo kan, ni ba soor ni ke m li kpa limɔfal.”

ref: But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?” “Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
text: Le Uwumbɔr nan ki bui u ke, “Saah gee liŋuul lipulaajil ngbaan aakun pu na, ni ŋan aa?” Le Jona gar ke, “Ni ŋan ke m gee liŋuul. M kpa liŋuul li ga ŋmaa ku mi na.”

ref: But the Lord said: You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui u ke, “Kinyeek kibaa ponn ni le lipulaajil ngbaan punn ki muun, le ki ki kpo kinyeek ki paa na; saa ŋa nibaa tii li, naa ti ki ye sin le cha li punn ki muun, le laah kpo na, aasui bii li pu.

ref: Listen, all of you! Earth and everything on it, pay close attention. The Lord God accuses you from his holy temple.
text: Ŋitimbol mɔmɔk, ŋun tibɔr tee man, binib bimɔk bi kitiŋ kee pu na, li pel man tibɔr tee. Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔndaan ga len ibamɔn, le ki galn nimi. Li pel man. U bi waapaacham aadichal ni le ki len ni.

ref: And he will come down to crush underfoot every pagan altar.
text: Uwumbɔr ga nya ni waabuul li bi chain na ni le ki dan; u ga sunn ni ki nan chuun ŋijoo paab.

ref: Mountains will melt beneath his feet like wax beside a fire. Valleys will vanish like water rushing down a ravine.
text: Le ŋijoo ngbaan ga donn u taab ke tisikakpiin aah donni mmii ni pu na; ŋi ga puu ti lir tifatann ponn ni ke nnyun aah puu sunni ligongoln pu pu na.

ref: This will happen because of the terrible sins of Israel, the descendants of Jacob. Samaria has led Israel to sin, and pagan altars at Jerusalem have made Judah sin.
text: Israel aanib aah tun titunwanbir ki yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na le ga cha nimina mɔmɔk ŋa kina. Ŋma aan bi ga galn Israel yaab aah yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb pu na pu? Ni ye Israel aatiyil Samaria la. Ŋma bi Juda aatiŋ ni ki dii ŋiwaa? Ni ye Jerusalem aatiŋ la.

ref: So the Lord will leave Samaria in ruins— merely an empty field where vineyards are planted. He will scatter its stones and destroy its foundations.
text: Kina pu le Uwumbɔr len ke, “M ga cha Samaria kpaln litakpakpokl le kipɔɔk ni, nin chee bi ga ko ndaan aasubil aasui aasar na. M ga ber kaagon lii, ki faa kaabir ti mee kifataŋ ni.

ref: Samaria's idols will be smashed, and the wages of temple prostitutes will be destroyed by fire. Silver and gold from those idols will then be used by foreigners as payment for prostitutes. Judah Is Doomed
text: Kaawaa ŋi bi gee sakpen na ga wii yɔk yɔk, le baawaadir ni aapiidagoob aawangol wu mmii ni, le kaawaa mɔmɔk ga kpaln litapuln li bi fii cha li na. Samaria yaab nan ban nimina mɔmɔk ke bi pɔr la, le baadim ga yoor ŋi mɔmɔk buen nibaa wɔb ki ti li pa bipiidagoob biken.”

ref: Because of this tragedy, I go barefoot and naked. My crying and weeping sound like howling wolves or ostriches.
text: Le Maika bui ke, “Nimina pu le m ga wii, ki gaa ikpolahn. M ga chuun ŋŋmeen kaan taŋ ŋinaatak, ki mɔk maapombiin aah bi pu na. M ga gbei ke ikakal na, ki wii ke taataa na.

ref: Everyone in Maroth hoped for the best, but the Lord sent disaster down on Jerusalem.
text: Marof aatiŋ aanib ka jek ki kii lifuur; ba pu? Uwumbɔr di tibɔbir ŋɔŋ ni Jerusalem aatiŋ pu a.

ref: Get the war chariots ready, you people of Lachish. You led Jerusalem into sin, just as Israel did.
text: Lakis aatiŋ aanib, di itaan aatɔroku tiib tul itaan pu man. Ni mu tun Israel yaab aatunwanbir, le ki cha Jerusalem yaab tun titunwanbir.

ref: Now you will have to give a going-away gift to Moresheth. Israel's kings will discover that they cannot trust the town of Achzib.
text: Tɔ, Juda aanib, chɔi Moresef Gaf aatiŋ aanib man. Israel aabɔrb aan kan nterm Aksib aatiŋ ni.

ref: People of Mareshah, the Lord will send someone to capture your town. Then Israel's glorious king will be forced to hide in Adullam Cave.
text: Uwumbɔr ga di Maresa aatiŋ aanib tii udin u ga gaa baatiŋ na. Israel aayidam bi kpa kipak na ga buen ti bɔr Adulam aatakpaluŋ ni.

ref: Judah, shave your head as bald as a vulture and start mourning. Your precious children will be dragged off to a foreign country.
text: Juda aanib, kuu nimi aayikpir man ki li wii naah gee nimi aabim bi na pu. Kuu ŋiyikun ke nangba tiib na man, ba pu? bi ga di nimi aabim buen kitiyayaŋ ni ki cha nimi.

ref: Doomed! You're doomed! At night you lie in bed, making evil plans. And when morning comes, you do what you've planned because you have the power.
text: Tibɔbir bi binib bi dɔ dak titunwanbir pu kinyeek na pu. Kitaak yaa woln, aan bi kan nsan siib na, le bi ŋa titunwanbir ti bi kpokl na.

ref: You grab any field or house that you want; you cheat families out of homes and land.
text: Bi yaa ban ikpaakon kan, bi gaal i mpɔɔn la; bi yaa ban ŋidichal kan, bi gaal ŋi mpɔɔn la. Ubaa aadichal bee waawangol aa nyan tibɔr ni.

ref: But here is what the Lord says: “I am planning trouble for you. Your necks will be caught in a noose, and you will be disgraced in this time of disaster.”
text: Kina pu le Uwumbɔr bui ke, “M bi dakl ke m joo ni tibɔbir nan lii ni pu la, le naan ŋmaa nya ti ponn ni. Ni ga kan ke ni bi tibɔr ni la, le naan ki chuun kigaak aasachuln.

ref: When that happens, this sorrowful song will be sung about you: “Ruined! Completely ruined! The Lord has taken our land and given it to traitors.”
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, binib ga di nimi aabɔr le di ŋa tibɔbir aaseeraa, le ki ga gaa nnandalahn mue, naah kan pu na pu: Ti doo a. Uwumbɔr chuu gaa timi aatiŋ ti chee, ki di tii binib bi chur timi tinaagbiir na.”

ref: “Enough of your preaching!” That's what you tell me. “We won't be disgraced, so stop preaching!”
text: Binib mooni m pu ki len ke, “Taa mooni ti chee. Taa mooni tima ngbaan mɔmɔk man. Uwumbɔr aan jinn timi inimɔɔn.

ref: Descendants of Jacob, is it right for you to claim that the Lord did what he did because he was angry? Doesn't he always bless those who do right?
text: Nimi Israel yaab len ke Uwumbɔr aa ki kpa limɔr la aa? U ga sil ŋa tiwan ngbaan mɔmɔk aa? Waa len binib bi ŋani ni ŋan na chee ki san bi kinimbaak aa?”

ref: My people, you have turned against one another! You have even stolen clothes right off the backs of innocent neighbors who pass by in peace.
text: Le Uwumbɔr ga gar ke, “Ni tak maanib ke bidim na la. Bijab nyan ni butɔb ni, ki dak ke baah fuu ni linampal na bi ŋmar la, le ni bi nima chee ke ni nan su baabɔkur.

ref: You take over lovely homes that belong to the women of my nation. Then you cheat their children out of the inheritance that comes from the Lord.
text: Ni jenn nyani maanib aapuutiib ŋidichal ŋi ponn ni bi gee na, le ki gaa baabim chee maanyoor.

ref: Get out of here, you crooks! You'll find no rest here. You're not fit to belong to the Lord's people, and you will be destroyed.
text: Fii ki li cha man; lifuur libaa aa ki bi do. Nimi aatunwanbir kuln do doo a.

ref: The only prophet you want is a liar who will say, “Drink and get drunk!” A Promise of Hope
text: “Binib bee ban bibɔnabr bi chuun ŋmanni ki geei inyamɔn, ki len ke, ‘M nabr ke ni ga gur ndaan la.’

ref: I, the Lord, promise to bring together the people of Israel who have survived. I will gather them, just as a shepherd brings sheep together, and there will be many.
text: “Le m ga kuun ni nimi Israel aanib bi gur na nan kpaan. M ga kuun ni nimi ke ipiih aah kpaan chaa koo yaabool ponn ni pu na la. Nimi aatiŋ ga ki gbiin binib ke kipihkpaamook ki ponn ni gbii ipiih na la.”

ref: Listen to me, you rulers of Israel! You know right from wrong,
text: Nimi bi ye Israel yaab aajojoob na, li pel man. Nimi aatuln le ba ye ke ni li dii ibamɔn,

ref: but you prefer to do evil instead of what is right. You skin my people alive. You strip off their flesh,
text: le ni nan tiwan ni ŋan na, ki tee gee titunwanbir. Maanib aa kee kpoi le ni sun baagban ki dar lui baanann baakpab pu.

ref: break their bones, cook it all in a pot, and gulp it down.
text: Ni ŋmɔ maanib la. Ni lui nyani baagban, le ki kool baakpab, ki chɔi chɔi bi ke baah ban bi di tinann ti ŋaa na.

ref: Someday you will beg the Lord to help you, but he will turn away because of your sins.
text: N‑yoonn choo le ni ga nan wii ban Uwumbɔr chee nterm, le waan gar nimi. Waan ŋun nimi aameel; ba pu? ni tun titunwanbir la.

ref: You lying prophets promise security for anyone who gives you food, but disaster for anyone who refuses to feed you. Here is what the Lord says to you prophets:
text: Baabɔnabr bi gaal tipar na le ŋmann maanib ke nsuudoon bi bi chee, le ki faani binib bi kaa pa bi na ke butɔb choo. Uwumbɔr bui bibɔnabr ngbaan ke,

ref: But the Lord has filled me with power and his Spirit. I have been given the courage to speak about justice and to tell you people of Israel that you have sinned.
text: Tɔ, mma kan, Uwumbɔr le joo Waafuur Nyaan ni waapɔɔn gbiini mi, le ki tii mi ibamɔn aalan, ni ntaakpapɔɔn mu m ga ŋmaa di bui Israel yaab baatunwanbir aah ye pu na.

ref: So listen to my message, you rulers of Israel! You hate justice and twist the truth.
text: Nimi Israel aanib aajojoob, li pel man, nimi bi kaa gee ibamɔn ki kpelni tiwan ni ŋan na ŋani taani na.

ref: You make cruelty and murder a way of life in Jerusalem.
text: Ni bi maa Uwumbɔr aatiŋ Jerusalem nnikum ni mbiin pu la.

ref: You leaders accept bribes for dishonest decisions. You priests and prophets teach and preach, but only for money. Then you say, “The Lord is on our side. No harm will come to us.”
text: Igaŋgaŋlik pu le kitiŋ ngbaan aajojoob joo ki, le bitotoorb tuk binib Uwumbɔr Aakaal ki gaal tipar, le bibɔnabr mu kpiir Uwumbɔr aah len pu na ŋimombil pu, le bi mɔmɔk len ke Uwumbɔr bi ti chee. Bi len le ke, “Tibɔbir tibaa aan dan ti chee. Uwumbɔr bi ti chee.”

ref: And so, because of you, Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.
text: Kina pu na, nimi pu le bidim ga kpar Sionn ke lisikpel na, le Jerusalem kpaln tibir aatapuln, le Uwumbɔr Aadichal aagongoln kpaln kichook.

ref: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills, and every nation will rush to it.
text: N‑yoonn choo, le lijool li pu Uwumbɔr Aadichal si na ga li ye lijool li paa jer ŋijoo mɔmɔk na, li ga chaar ŋigongon mɔmɔk pu. Le ŋitimbol pam ga dan li chee;

ref: People of many nations will come and say, “Let's go up to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
text: le ŋaanib ga bui ke, “Cha ti jon Uwumbɔr aajool ki buen Israel yaab Aawumbɔr Aadichal ni; ba pu? u ga mɔk timi waah ban ti ŋa pu na, le ti ga chuun waah lee isan i na pu. Uwumbɔr aamɔkm nyan ni Jerusalem aatiŋ ni la; Sionn pu le u len ni waanib chee tibɔr.”

ref: He will settle arguments between distant and powerful nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never again make war or attack one another.
text: U ga toor ŋitimbol pam aabɔr; ki toor ŋitimbokpaan ŋi bi duun u na, ni ŋi bi ni daa na aabɔr. Bi ga di baajaak aajum mɔɔ ŋikuu ki di baakpaatunn mɔɔ gɔrk tiib. Ŋitimbol aan ki to tɔb butɔb, kaan ki gor bibaa kiir butɔb daalbaadaal.

ref: Everyone will find rest beneath their own fig trees or grape vines, and they will live in peace. This is a solemn promise of the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Unii mɔmɔk ga li bi nsuudoon ni ubaa aadaan aasubil, ni ŋisubil ŋiken aasui aasar ni, le ubaa aan faan u nima. Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le puu kina.

ref: Others may follow their gods, but we will always follow the Lord our God. The Lord Will Lead His People Home
text: Litimbol mɔk dooni ki keei laawaal aamɔb la, le ti mɔmɔk ga nan doon ki kii Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Israel yaab ga nya tinaagbiir kitiyayaŋ ni ki gir ni

ref: The Lord said: At that time I will gather my people— the lame and the outcasts, and all others into whose lives I have brought sorrow.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “N‑yoonn choo, le m ga kuun ni binib bi m daa bitafal, aan bi jin falaa tinaagbiir ni kitiyayaŋ ni na nan kpaan.

ref: Then the lame and the outcasts will belong to my people and become a strong nation. I, the Lord, will rule them from Mount Zion forever.
text: Binib bi gur na wɔb le ki daa bido, le m ga tii bi mpɔɔn, le bi ga kpaln litimbol kpaan. M ga li bi Sionn Aajool paab le ki joo bi ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”

ref: Jerusalem, why are you crying? Don't you have a king? Have your advisors gone? Are you suffering like a woman in childbirth?
text: Ba ŋa aa wii mpɔɔn pu sakpen kina? Ba ŋa aa ji falaa ke upii u imalween joo u na? Saah kaa kpa ubɔr, aan saasusurb mu kpoi na pu le aa wii ii?

ref: Keep on groaning with pain, you people of Jerusalem! If you escape from your city to the countryside, you will still be taken as prisoners to Babylonia. But later I will rescue you from your enemies.
text: Jerusalem aatiŋ aanib, li mur fenni ki ker idun ke upii u imalween joo u na, ba pu? ni ga nya kitiŋ ponn ni ki ti li koo timoor ni. Ni ga buen Babiloŋ aatiŋ ni; le Uwumbɔr ga ti tee gaa nimi, nimi aadim chee lii nima.

ref: Zion, because of your sins you are surrounded by many nations who say, “We can hardly wait to see you disgraced.”
text: Ŋitimbol pam le kuun ni ke ŋi nan tak nimi. Bi bui ke, “Ti ga bii Jerusalem aatiŋ doo. Ti ga kan ke kitiŋ ngbaan bii doo.”

ref: But they don't know that I, the Lord, have gathered them here to grind them like grain.
text: Tɔ, ŋitimbol ngbaan mu aa tee nyi Uwumbɔr aalandak. Baa nyi ke bi kuun ni tɔb ke Uwumbɔr nan daa bitafal, ke baah kuuni ŋikalmaan bilni pu ke bi poi ŋi na la.

ref: Smash them to pieces, Zion! I'll let you be like a bull with iron horns and bronze hoofs. Crush those nations and bring their wealth to me, the Lord of the earth.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Jerusalem aanib, li cha ti daa nimi aadim aatafal man. M ga cha ni li pɔɔ ke unaaja u kpa tikur aayiin ni tikumann aataabuseen na. Ni ga ber ŋitimbol pam, le baah di mpɔɔn kan liwangol li na, ni ga joo ni li nan tii min, u ye dulnyaa mɔmɔk Aawumbɔr na.”

ref: Jerusalem, enemy troops have surrounded you; they have struck Israel's ruler in the face with a stick.
text: Jerusalem aanib, kuun nimi aajab man. Bi loon timi a. Bi bi tak Israel aayidaan la. Uwumbɔr puu ke ujojoor ga nya ni Betlehem aatiŋ ni

ref: Bethlehem Ephrath, you are one of the smallest towns in the nation of Judah. But the Lord will choose one of your people to rule the nation— someone whose family goes back to ancient times.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Betlehem Efrata, aa ye kitiwaatiir kibaa le Juda aatiŋ pu, le sin ponn ni le m ga nyan ni ujojoor u ga li joo Israel aanib na, u ga nya ni mmaal mu ye n‑yaayoonn na aamaal ponn ni la.”

ref: Like a shepherd taking care of his sheep, this ruler will lead and care for his people by the power and glorious name of the Lord his God. His people will live securely, and the whole earth will know his true greatness,
text: Ujojoor ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, u ga di mpɔɔn sakpiin mu nyan ni Tidindaan Uwumbɔr ubaa chee na le di joo waanib. Waanib ga li bi lifuur ni la; ba pu? kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk aanib ga li nyi waapɔɔn bɔr,

ref: because he will bring peace. Assyria Will Be Defeated Let Assyria attack our country and our palaces. We will counterattack, led by a number of rulers
text: le u ga joo ni nsuudoon. Gaalii ni ntafadaan Asiria yaab yaa nan koo ni timi aatiŋ ni ki nyaŋ binib bi kii timi na kan, le ti ga di timi aayidam bi pɔɔ sakpen na tun aan bi ni bima ti jan.

ref: whose strong army will defeat the nation of Assyria. Yes, our leaders will rescue us, if those Assyrians dare to invade our land. The Survivors Will Be Safe
text: Buyoonn bi koo ni timi aapepel ni na, le bi ga di tijawan ki nyaŋ Nimrod aatiŋ Asiria, le ki gaa timi Asiria yaab chee lii.

ref: A few of Jacob's descendants survived and are scattered among the nations. But the Lord will let them cover the earth like dew and rain that refreshes the soil.
text: Israel aanib bi ŋmar na ga li naahn limaln li Uwumbɔr tun ni li na le ŋitimbol pam chee, ki naahn utaal u pui tijikaar pu na. Bi ga li bi Uwumbɔr pu la, naan li ye unibɔn pu.

ref: At present they are scattered, but later they will attack, as though they were fierce lions pouncing on sheep. Their enemies will be torn to shreds, with no one to save them;
text: Binib bi gur ki ŋmal ŋitimbol ŋiken ni na ga li bi ke uchinn u bi ban tijikaar kichook ni, bee kipihkpaamook ni na la: u ga koo ipiih ni, le ki chur i, le ki daa par par i, le yaan kan nterm nibaa chee.

ref: they will be helpless, completely destroyed. Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
text: Israel yaab ga nyaŋ baadim le ki ku doo bi mɔmɔk.

ref: The Lord said: At that time I will wipe out your cavalry and chariots,
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “N‑yoonn ngbaan kan, m ga gaa nimi aataan ni chee, le ki bii nimi aataan aatɔroku tiib.

ref: I will stop you from telling fortunes and practicing witchcraft.
text: M ga bii nimi aanyɔk i ni joo tun nimi aatun na, ki cha ni taa ki li kpa bibɔɔb.

ref: You will no longer worship the idols or stone images you have made— I will destroy them,
text: M ga bii nimi aawaa, ni nimi aatakpal ŋi ni dooni na; naan ki doon tiwan ni, ni di nibaa aaŋaal naan ni na.

ref: together with the sacred poles and even your towns.
text: M ga ber liwaapii Asera aanann ti ni maa ti nimi aatiŋ pu na, ki bii nimi aatim.

ref: I will become furious and take revenge on the nations that refuse to obey me.
text: Le maaŋuul ponn ni m ga teen ŋitimbol ŋi mɔmɔk yii maamɔb na.”

ref: Israel, I am bringing charges against you— I call upon the mountains and the earth's firm foundation to be my witnesses.
text: Nimi ŋijoo, nimi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na aatinyik, li pel Uwumbɔr aabɔr man. Uwumbɔr ni waanib le kpa tibɔr. U ban ke u joo ni ngalm Israel aanib pu la.

ref: My people, have I wronged you in any way at all? Please tell me.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Maanib, m ŋa nimi ba? Kinye pu aan m ye lituln ki tii nimi? Gar mi man.

ref: I rescued you from Egypt, where you were slaves. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to be your leaders.
text: M nyan ni nimi Ijipt aatiŋ ni; m nyan ni nimi tinaagbiir ni; m nan tun Moses, ni Aaronn, ni Miriam ke bi nan loln ni pu nsan.

ref: Don't forget the evil plans of King Balak of Moab or what Balaam son of Beor said to him. Remember how I, the Lord, saved you many times on your way from Acacia to Gilgal. True Obedience
text: Maanib, teer man Moab aabɔr Balak aah nan kpokl ke u ŋa nimi pu na, ki teer Beor aajapɔɔn Balaam aah nan gar u pu na. Teer man maah nan cha ni puur Jɔɔdann aamɔɔl na, buyoonn ni nan nyan ni Sitim aakakaa chee ki cha Gilgal aatiŋ ni na. Teer man tiwan nimina mɔmɔk ki bee maah nan ŋa pu ke m gaa nimi lii na.” Uwumbɔr aah ban pu na

ref: What offering should I bring when I bow down to worship the Lord God Most High? Should I try to please him by sacrificing calves a year old?
text: Buyoonn m dan ke m nan doon Uwumbɔr u ye paacham Aadindaan na kan, m ga joo ba nan tii u? M ga joo ni inaabi i ŋan sakpen na le nan see mmii ni tii u uu?

ref: Will thousands of sheep or rivers of olive oil make God satisfied with me? Should I sacrifice to the Lord my first-born child as payment for my terrible sins?
text: M yaa joo ni ipiih ŋichur ŋichur, bee olif aakpan mu kaan doo na kan, ni ga piir Uwumbɔr aasui ii? M ga di maajan aabijabo le toor kitork tii u maatunwanbir pu uu?

ref: The Lord God has told us what is right and what he demands: “See that justice is done, let mercy be your first concern, and humbly obey your God.” Cheating and Violence
text: Aayii. Uwumbɔr bui timi tiwan ni ŋan na. Waah ban tiwan ni ti chee na sɔ: ke ti ŋa tiwan ni tok ki ŋan na, ki li kpa ngeehm n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki li bi suuna timi Aawumbɔr chee.

ref: I am the Lord, and you are wise to respect my power to punish. So listen to my message for the city of Jerusalem:
text: Ni ye nlan aawan le ke ti li san Uwumbɔr. U yin kitiŋ ngbaan ni aanib ke, “Li pel man, nimi bi kuun kitiŋ ngbaan ni na.

ref: But I, the Lord, will punish you for cheating with weights and with measures.
text: M ga ŋa kinye aan ki di cha pinn binib bi joo inyamɔn aawan ŋaŋni tiwan na?

ref: You rich people are violent, and everyone tells lies.
text: Nimi aawankpadam ji bigiim pem pem la, le ni mɔmɔk ye binyamɔndam.

ref: Because of your sins, I will wound you and leave you ruined and defenseless.
text: Kina pu na, m puun gor ke m bii doo nimi, nimi aatunwanbir pu.

ref: You will eat, but still be hungry; you will store up goods, but lose everything— I, the Lord, will let it all be captured in war.
text: Ni ga ji, le ki mu aan bab; mbamɔn, nkon ga li joo nimi. Ni ga kuun liwangol di bil, le ki mu aan ŋmaa li joo li; naah ga li kpa tiwan nimɔk na, m ga bii kina aawan butɔb ponn ni.

ref: You won't harvest what you plant or use the oil from your olive trees or drink the wine from grapes you grow.
text: Ni ga bu njikaabim, ki mu aan chee tijikaar. Ni ga nyan nkpan olif aasubil ni, ki mu aan ŋmaa di mu ŋa nibaa. Ni ga ŋaa ndaan, ki mu aan nyu mu.

ref: Jerusalem, this will happen because you followed the sinful example of kings Omri and Ahab. Now I will destroy you and your property. Then the people of every nation will make fun and insult you.
text: Naah dii Ubɔr Omri aajapɔɔn Ubɔr Ahab aatunwanbir aasan na pu, le kina ga ŋa. Ni beenin joo baakaal la, kina pu le m ga bii doo nimi, le unii mɔk ga lik nimi fam. Binib bi bi dulnyaa wee ni na ga lik seen nimi.”

ref: I feel so empty inside— like someone starving for grapes or figs, after the vines and trees have all been picked clean.
text: Maa kpa nsuupiin. M naahn uja u nkon joo u aan lisubil mu aa gur waasui pu, aan ndaan aasubil mu aa bi ŋaasui pu na la. Bi ker ŋisubil mɔmɔɔn ngbaan mɔmɔk a.

ref: No one is loyal to God; no one does right. Everyone is brutal and eager to deceive everyone else.
text: Unii ubaa aa gur kitiŋ ngbaan pu ki bi chob, ubaa mu aa bi ki kii tii Uwumbɔr. Binib mɔmɔk ka kii ke bi ku binib biken la. Unii mɔmɔk dɔ ban udo yoo le u ku.

ref: Don't trust anyone, not even your best friend, and be careful what you say to the one you love.
text: Taa tii aajɔ, bee aa ni unii u koo gbɔk tɔb na naadii. Li nyi saah len pu na, hali aapuu mu chee kan, li nyi.

ref: Sons refuse to respect their own fathers, daughters rebel against their own mothers, and daughters-in-law despise their mothers-in-law. Your family is now your enemy.
text: N‑yoonn mumina ponn ni le mbijabim yin bitetiib bijɔrb, le mpiibim aa keei binatiib aamɔi; le bipiisapɔm ni bichapiitiib jaa; le unii aadim ye udo lichiln ni aanib.

ref: But I trust the Lord God to save me, and I will wait for him to answer my prayer. The Nation Turns to God
text: Le mma ga li lik Uwumbɔr pu; m ga ji limɔr ki li kii Uwumbɔr u ga gaa mi lii na. Maawumbɔr ga ŋun maayim. Uwumbɔr ga gaa timi lii

ref: My enemies, don't be glad because of my troubles! I may have fallen, but I will get up; I may be sitting in the dark, but the Lord is my light.
text: Timi aadim aa kpa nsan ke bi li kpa mpopiin timi aafalaa pu. Ti lir la, le ki mu tee ga ki fii. Ti bi mbɔmbɔɔn ni le dandana, le Uwumbɔr ga tii timi nwiihn.

ref: I have sinned against the Lord. And so I must endure his anger, until he comes to my defense. But I know that I will see him making things right for me and leading me to the light.
text: Ti tun Uwumbɔr titunwanbir, kina pu na, ni ŋan ke ti ji falaa waaŋuul pu. Nee aapuwɔb na u ga sil tipuwɔb ki toor taani u bi ŋa timi na. U ga nyan ni timi dan nwiihn ni; ti ga li bi ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu u ga gaa timi lii na.

ref: You, my enemies, said, “The Lord God is helpless.” Now each of you will be disgraced and put to shame. I will see you trampled like mud in the street. A Bright Future
text: Timi aadim ga kan nimina, le ki ji inimɔɔn, bidimbaam bi nan ŋani timi yaansara ki bui ke, “Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bi la?” na. Ti ga kan binib aah nyaŋ bi pu na, ki taa bi bil kitiŋ ke tikpakpar na.

ref: Towns of Judah, the day is coming when your walls will be rebuilt, and your boundaries enlarged.
text: Jerusalem aanib, n‑yoonn mu ni ga ki gir maa kitiŋ kee aagon na choo. N‑yoonn ngbaan le nimi aapepel ga moo kpee.

ref: Those nations will suffer disaster because of what they did. Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
text: Tɔ, kitiŋ kee tee ga kpaln nteer ŋmeen, binib bi bi ki pu na aatunwanbir pu. Uwumbɔr aah san Israel yaab kinimbaak pu na

ref: Lead your people, Lord! Come and be our shepherd. Grasslands surround us, but we live in a forest. So lead us to Bashan and Gilead, and let us find pasture as we did long ago.
text: Uwumbɔr, li bi saanib bi aa lee na chee ke upihdaan na. Bi yaa, ki bi kipɔɔk ni la, le kitiŋ ki nyuun na bi bi chee. Cha bi buen Basann, ni Gilead aapihkpaamoor ti nyuun na ni, ke baah nan bi n‑yaayoonn na pu na.

ref: I, the Lord, will work miracles just as I did when I led you out of Egypt.
text: Uwumbɔr, tun lijinjiir aatun tii timi saanib, ke saah nan ŋa pu n‑yoonn mu aa nan nyan ni timi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na.

ref: Nations will see this and be ashamed because of their helpless armies. They will be in shock, unable to speak or hear,
text: Ŋitimbol ga kan nimina le bitaakpab yɔl, le baan ki li kpa mpɔɔn. Bitaakpab aah ga yɔl pu na, le bi ga muib bimɔi ki ŋeeb bitafal mu.

ref: because of their fear of me, your Lord and God. Then they will come trembling, crawling out of their fortresses like insects or snakes, lapping up the dust. No One Is Like God The people said:
text: Bi ga baar kitiŋ titan ni, ke iwaa na la; bi ga nyan ni baadichal ŋi kpa ŋigon ŋi fɔk na ni, ki jii ijawaan pu. Ijawaan pu, bi ga fenn ban Tidindaan Uwumbɔr.

ref: Our God, no one is like you. We are all that is left of your chosen people, and you freely forgive our sin and guilt. You don't stay angry forever; you're glad to have pity
text: Uwumbɔr, ubaa aa ki bi ke sin na; aa di cha pinn saanib bi ŋmar na aatunwanbir. Saa joo saaŋuul ni yunni, le ki tee gee ke aa mɔk timi ngeehm n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.

ref: and pleased to be merciful. You will trample on our sins and throw them in the sea.
text: Aa ga ki san timi kinimbaak lelee. Aa ga taa taa timi aatunwanbir ŋmal titan ni, ki di ti buen nnyusakpem aataab.

ref: You will keep your word and be faithful to Jacob and to Abraham, as you promised our ancestors many years ago.
text: Aa ga mɔk saanib, Abraham ni Jakob aayaabitiib, ke saah bi mbamɔm ki kpa ngeehm n‑yoonn mɔmɔk pu na, ke saah nan puu tii tiyaajatiib n‑yaayoonn na pu na.

ref: I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh. The Fierce Anger of the Lord
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Nahum u nyan ni Elkos aatiŋ ni na aah nan kan Ninefa aatiŋ aabɔr ti na sɔ. Uwumbɔr le nan kpiir ti mɔk u. Uwumbɔr aah gee Ninefa aatiŋ pu liŋuul pu na

ref: The Lord God demands loyalty. In his anger, he takes revenge on his enemies.
text: Tidindaan Uwumbɔr aa kii ke unii doon liwaal libaa; u dar binib bi kpak u na aatafal. Waaŋuul ponn ni le u teeni bi baah tun pu na.

ref: The Lord is powerful, yet patient; he makes sure that the guilty are always punished. He can be seen in storms and in whirlwinds; clouds are the dust from his feet.
text: Uwumbɔr aaŋuul aa fiir mala mala, le u tee kpa mpɔɔn sakpen, le ki dar binib bi aabɔr aa ŋan na aatafal, kaa joo cha pinni bi. Kitaabuŋ fii nin chee Uwumbɔr chuun na la; utaa aatangbaak le ye ntaalangbam.

ref: At the Lord's command, oceans and rivers dry up. Bashan, Mount Carmel, and Lebanon wither, and their flowers fade.
text: Uma le len nnyusakpem chee, le mu foor. U cha ŋimɔɔ foor. Basann aatiŋ aakpaakon kuur la, Kamel Aajool mann ke titan na la, le Lebanonn aatiŋ aasupuun gbar lir.

ref: At the sight of the Lord, mountains and hills tremble and melt; the earth and its people shudder and shake.
text: Ŋijoo jii Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni la; le ŋigongon donn unimbiin ni. Kitiŋ yaa kan Uwumbɔr kan, ki deŋni la; dulnyaa, ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi u pu na aawon gbaa la.

ref: Who can stand the heat of his furious anger? It flashes out like fire and shatters stones. The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
text: Uwumbɔr aaŋuul yaa fii kan, ŋma ga ŋmar? Ŋma ga ŋmar waaŋuusakpeln ni? U cha waaŋuul puu nyan ni ke mmiigaal na la; ŋitakpal wur unimbiin ni ki kpaln titan la.

ref: The Lord is good. He protects those who trust him in times of trouble.
text: Uwumbɔr ŋan; waanib yaa bi tibɔr ni kan, u kii bi; le ki lik binib bi fenn buen u chee ki ban nterm na pu.

ref: But like a roaring flood, the Lord chases his enemies into dark places and destroys them.
text: U kuln waadim ke nwam mu san mala mala na la; u ku binib bi kpak u na la.

ref: So don't plot against the Lord! He wipes out his enemies, and they never revive.
text: Ba aan ni bi kpokl Uwumbɔr pu? U ga kuln nimi. Ubaa aan ŋmaa kpak u ki jer nfum mubaa.

ref: They are like drunkards overcome by wine, or like twisted thornbushes burning in a fire.
text: Nimi bidanyurb ga wu mmii ke ikokon i lɔk tɔb ni na, ni timokuun aah wu pu na la.

ref: Assyria, one of your rulers has made evil plans against the Lord.
text: Uja u aasui nan gbii mbiin aalandak na nan nyan ni sin Ninefa aatiŋ ni la, uma le nan kpokl Uwumbɔr pu.

ref: But the Lord says, “Assyria, no matter how strong you are, you will be cut down! My people Judah, I have troubled you before, but I won't do it again.
text: Uwumbɔr aah bui waanib Israel yaab pu na sɔ: “Hali Asiria yaab aah wiir ki kpa mpɔɔn pu na, bi mɔmɔk ga kuln ki wɔŋ. Maanib, min le nan cha ni jin falaa, tɔ, maan ki ŋa kina.

ref: Assyria, this is what else the Lord says to you: “Your name will be forgotten. I will destroy every idol in your temple, and I will send you to the grave, because you are worthless.”
text: Uwumbɔr aah siin pu Asiria aatiŋ pu na sɔ: “Baan li kpa yaabitiib bi ga cha baayimbil li beenin bi na. M ga kuln ŋiwaa ŋi bi baawaadir ni na. M bi gbii likaakul bilni Asiria yaab la, naa ŋan ke bi li kpa limɔfal.”

ref: Look toward the mountains, people of Judah! Here comes a messenger with good news of peace. Celebrate your festivals. Keep your promises to God. Your evil enemies are destroyed and will never again invade your country.
text: Lik man, ntuun nyan ni ŋijoo pu ki joo ni tibɔnyaan. U choo u nan moon linyaŋ aabɔr la. Juda aanib, ji nimi aajim man, ki tii Uwumbɔr naah di nisui mɔmɔk puu ke ni ga tii u ni na. Bibiindam aan ki dan nan jenn gaa nimi aatiŋ daalbaadaal. Bi kuln doo kookoo a.

ref: Nineveh, someone is coming to attack and scatter you. Guard your fortresses! Watch the road! Be brave! Prepare for battle!
text: Ninefa aatiŋ, bi gob si a. Mpɔɔn mu ga wii si yuk yuk na fuu ni a. Ban bijab sil saatiŋ aagon paab. Cha bi kiir nsan ngbaan. Gor ki kiir butɔb.

ref: Judah and Israel are like trees with branches broken by their enemies. But the Lord is going to restore their power and glory. *
text: Uwumbɔr ban u ki giin Israel aatiŋ aapak ki ki nan kpa, aan kaadim nan gaa kaawangol butɔb ni na tii ki la.

ref: An officer gives a command. But his soldiers stumble, as they hasten to build a shelter to protect themselves against rocks thrown down from the city wall.
text: Bi kuun bijab aayidam; le baah tur cha mɔb pu na, bi gbeer. Bidim chii ki buen kitiŋ ngbaan aagoln chee ki gor baajaak aapeln ke baah ga li joo yur tɔb le na.

ref: The river gates fly open, and panic floods the palace.
text: Ibisamɔi i bi limɔɔl wɔb na chuu piir a; le ijawaan gbiin libɔrdichal ni.

ref: Nineveh is disgraced. The queen is dragged off. Her servant women mourn; they moan like doves, and they beat their breasts in sorrow.
text: Bi chuu ubɔrpii a; le waatutum wii ke ŋinanjel na ki joo biŋaal gbaa bibiŋ mpombiin pu.

ref: Nineveh is like a pond with leaking water. Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!” can be heard everywhere. But everyone is leaving.
text: Binib san nyan Ninefa aatiŋ ni ke limɔɔl aah kar kan, laanyun puu nya pu na la. Iwiil nya ni ke, “Sil man. Sil man.” Le ubaa aa fenni upuwɔb ke u lik.

ref: Enemy soldiers shout, “The city is full of treasure and all kinds of wealth. Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
text: Gaa tikunabr ngbaan mpɔɔn man. Gaa salmaa ngbaan mpɔɔn man. Kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni gbii liwangol la.

ref: What happened to this city? They were safer there than powerful lions in a den, with no one to disturb them.
text: Tɔ, kitiŋ ki nan bi ke ichinn aabuu na ki bi la chee? nin chee ichinn aabim ji, aan uchinnja ni uchinnpii nan chaa, aan yaabim bi lifuur ni na, bi la chee?

ref: These are the same lions that ferociously attacked their victims, then dragged away the flesh to feed their young.
text: Uchinn nan chuu tinann le ki daa par par ti ki tii upuu ni waabim; u nan di tinankaab le gbiin waabuu ni.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful is against you, Nineveh. God will burn your chariots and send an army to kill those young lions of yours. You will never again make victims of others or send messengers to threaten everyone on this earth.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui ke, “Saadin ye min la. M ga see saataan aatɔroku tiib mmii. Bi ga ku saajab butɔb ni la, le m ga yoor saah nan gaa tiwan ni biken chee na ki di buen. Ubaa aan ki ŋun saah nan kpa mpɔɔn mu dulnyaa wee ni na pu.”

ref: Doom to the crime capital! Nineveh, city of murder and treachery,
text: Kitiŋ ki gbii inyamɔn, ni linikul, ni liwangol li bidim ga gaa li mpɔɔn na aadoon le na.

ref: here is your fate— cracking whips, churning wheels; galloping horses, roaring chariots;
text: Li pel ŋinaalab aah wii pu na man, ni itaan aatɔroku tiib aah san pu na.

ref: You were nothing more than a prostitute using your magical charms and witchcraft to attract and trap nations.
text: Uwumbɔr daa pateer Ninefa aatiŋ aatafal la. Ki nan ŋan sakpen, le ki kpa ibɔnyɔk i bir na, ki nan ŋmal ŋitimbol ŋiken ibɔnyɔk, ki di mu ŋa tinaagbiir ni.

ref: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, am now your enemy. I will pull up your skirt and let nations and kingdoms stare at your nakedness.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui ke, “M ga daa sin Ninefa aatiŋ aanib aatafal. M ga gbabr si ki cha si aaŋmeen ki cha ŋitimbol ŋiken kan si, ŋi ga kan si saanimɔɔn ngbaan ni.

ref: I will cover you with garbage, treat you like trash, and rub you in the dirt.
text: M ga lik si fam, ki di tijɔŋ biin aa pu. Binib ga lik si ki san ijawaan la.

ref: Everyone who sees you will turn away and shout, “Nineveh is done for! Is anyone willing to mourn or to give her comfort?” Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
text: Binib bimɔk kan si na ga sur bipuwɔb. Bi ga len ke, ‘Ninefa aatiŋ kpaln tilangbenn le ki dɔ. Ubaa aan san ki kinimbaak. Ubaa mu aan li ban ke u sɔŋ kisui.’”

ref: Nineveh, do you feel safer than the city of Thebes? The Nile River was its wall of defense.
text: Ninefa aatiŋ, aa jer Ijipt aatiyil Tebes aa? Ki mu nan kpa limɔɔl li kii ki ke ligoln na. Nail aamɔɔl le nan ye kaakikiir.

ref: Thebes trusted the mighty power of Ethiopia and Egypt; the nations of Put and Libya were her allies.
text: Kima le nan joo Kus ni Ijipt aanib, le ubaa aa nan nyi kaapɔɔn mɔk. Kimaantɔ le nan ye Libia aatiŋ.

ref: But she was captured and taken to a foreign country. Her children were murdered at every street corner. The members of her royal family were auctioned off, and her high officials were bound in chains.
text: Le bi nan yoor Tebes aanib buen tinaagbiir ni. Bi nan gbaa ku baabim bil kitiŋ ngbaan aalɔlɔnn mɔmɔk ni. Bi nan di tikululn le gbin binib bi ye baasalolm na, le ki yakr bi tii binib bi nan nyaŋ bi ki chur bi na.

ref: Nineveh, now it's your turn! You will get drunk and try to hide from your enemy.
text: Sin Ninefa aatiŋ mu ga ŋa ke saah gbii ndaan le na. Aa mu ga pɔɔn aabaa ke aa san ŋmar saadim chee.

ref: Your fortresses are fig trees with ripe figs. Merely shake the trees, and fruit will fall into every open mouth.
text: Saah maa tidir ti fɔk ki pɔɔ kiir aabaa na ga li gur naahn ŋikakan aasui i aasubil puir na la: dam isui ngbaan le ŋikakan ga gbar lir ni aamɔb ni.

ref: Your army is weak. Fire has destroyed the crossbars on your city gates; now they stand wide open to your enemy.
text: Saajab naahn bipiib la, le ubaa aa kii saatiŋ ke saadim taa nyaŋ ki. Mmii le ga wu idɔ i aa di laŋ saabisamɔi na.

ref: You will still go up in flames and be cut down by swords that will wipe you out like a field attacked by grasshoppers. So, go ahead and increase like a swarm of locusts!
text: Ni po gee ni ŋa pu na kan, mmii le ga wu nimi, bee ni bee butɔb ponn ni. Bi ga ŋar nimi ŋŋaan ke itoon aah ŋmɔ tijikaar pu na la. Ni pɔr ke itoon na la.

ref: More merchants are in your city than there are stars in the sky— but they are like locusts that eat everything, then fly away.
text: Nimi aanib bi tiir kitiirk na wiir jer iŋmabi aah wiir kitaapaak pu na. Le dandana ma kan, bi mɔmɔk buen ke itoon i taln ifeen ki fii buen na la.

ref: Your guards and your officials are swarms of locusts. On a chilly day they settle on a fence, but when the sun comes out, they take off to who-knows-where.
text: Saaninkpiib naahn itoon i koo ŋigon ni nwiin mundaal soon na la, le nwiin yaa nyan ni kan, i fii buen, le ubaa aa ki nyi yaa buen nin chee na.

ref: King of Assyria, your officials and leaders are sound asleep, while your people are scattered in the mountains. Yes, your people are sheep without a shepherd.
text: Asiria aabɔrkpaan, saayidam kpoi a, le saanib bi kpa ŋiyimbil na mu geen kaan ki finn kpala. Saanib yaa, ki bi ŋijoo paab, le ubaa aa bi ki ga giin bi kunn ni linampal.

ref: You're fatally wounded. There's no hope for you. But everyone claps when they hear this news, because your constant cruelty has caused them pain.
text: Nnyɔk aa bi ki ga sɔŋ saatotonn ti aa kan na, le saabuun ngbaan aan yann. Binib bi mɔmɔk ŋun saah bii doo pu na gbaa tinyɔpur mpopiin pu la. Unii ubaa nan ŋmaa ŋmar saabiin mu kaa nan kpa ndoon na ni ii?

ref: I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me. Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
text: Uwumbɔr aah nan kpiir tibɔr ti tuk waabɔnabr Habakuk na sɔ. Habakuk aah len waanib aatunwanbir aabɔr pu na

ref: Our Lord, how long must I beg for your help before you listen? How long before you save us from all this violence?
text: Uwumbɔr, ni ga yunn kinye aan aa ŋun maah yin si ki ban nterm pu na, aan ki nyan mi linimaln ni?

ref: Why do you make me watch such terrible injustice? Why do you allow violence, lawlessness, crime, and cruelty to spread everywhere?
text: Ba ŋa aa cha m kani tibɔbir timina aaboln? Ni ga ŋa kinye aan aa li ka lik titunwanbir ki ŋmin? Mbiin ni mbimbin mu pɔɔ na le mann goln mi na, le kijaak ni kinikpakpak bi ni kookoo.

ref: Laws cannot be enforced; justice is always the loser; criminals crowd out honest people and twist the laws around. The Lord Answers Habakkuk
text: Nkaal aa kpa mpɔɔn, le ki bee fam, kina pu na, ibamɔn aa bi. Titunwanbirdam nyaŋ binib bi aabimbin ŋan na, le ki laŋ ibamɔn pu. Uwumbɔr aah gar pu na

ref: I am sending the Babylonians. They are fierce and cruel— marching across the land, conquering cities and towns.
text: M ban ke m di mpɔɔn ŋa Babiloŋ aanib bi kpa mbiin kaa san nibaa na aaŋaal ni la. Bi chuun dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni ki ban ntim ke bi nyaŋ ki gaa mu la.

ref: How fearsome and frightening. Their only laws and rules are the ones they make up.
text: Bi ye binib bi biken san bi ijawaan sakpen na la, le ki kpa kigaak ki ŋani baah gee pu na.

ref: They make fun of rulers and laugh at fortresses, while building dirt mounds so they can capture cities.
text: Bi lik seeni bibɔrb le ki laa baaninkpiib. Baah maa ŋigon kiir ntim mu aan mu pɔɔ na kibaa aa ŋmaa sil kiir bi, bi kuun titan le ti din kaagon, le ki nyaŋ ki,

ref: Then suddenly they disappear like a gust of wind— those sinful people who worship their own strength. Habakkuk Complains Again
text: le ki chuun mala ke libuln na ki jer, titunwanbirdam bi aapɔɔn ye baawaal na le na.” Habakuk aah ki gir bui Uwumbɔr binib aah tun titunwanbir pu na

ref: Holy Lord God, mighty rock, you are eternal, and we are safe from death. You are using those Babylonians to judge and punish others.
text: Uwumbɔr, ki nyan mpiin na, sin le ye Uwumbɔr. Sin le ye Maawumbɔr u bi chain kaa kpa ndoon na. Uwumbɔr, Ndindaan ni maakikiir, sin le lee Babiloŋ yaab ki cha bi kpa mpɔɔn ke bi ŋmaa daa timi aatafal.

ref: But you can't stand sin or wrong. So don't sit by in silence while they gobble up people who are better than they are.
text: Tɔ, ba ŋa saa daa bibiindam ngbaan aatafal? Aanimbil bi chain pam kaan ŋmaa lik titunwanbir, kaan ŋmaa li si lik aan binib ŋani tiwan ni kaa ŋan na. Kina pu na, ba ŋa aa ka ŋmin aan bi bi kuln binib bi aabimbin ŋan jer baabimbin na?

ref: The people you put on this earth are like fish or reptiles without a leader.
text: Binib ye ijan i bi nnyun ni kaa kpa ujojoor na aa?

ref: Then an enemy comes along and takes them captive with hooks and nets. It makes him so happy
text: Babiloŋ yaab ngbaan joo ijapiin le chur binib ke baah ye ijan le na. Bi joo baapɔr le dar bi cha, le ki tar mpopiin pu.

ref: that he offers sacrifices to his fishing nets, because they make him rich and provide choice foods.
text: Bi kpaan dooni baapɔr ngbaan le ki toor kitork tii ti; ba pu? tima le tii bi baah ban tiwanyaan ni mɔmɔk na.

ref: Will he keep hauling in his nets and destroying nations without showing mercy?
text: Bi ga li joo baajaak aajum kuln ŋitimbol, kaa san ŋi kinimbaak kina le ki cha aa?

ref: While standing guard on the watchtower, I waited for the Lord's answer, before explaining the reason for my complaint.
text: M ga jon maakikiib aadifɔfɔk pu, ki ti li ka nima, ki lik Uwumbɔr aah ga bui mi pu ke m len na, ni ngarm mu u ga tii mi maabɔr ti m len na pu.

ref: Then the Lord told me: “I will give you my message in the form of a vision. Write it clearly enough to be read at a glance.
text: Le Uwumbɔr gar mi ke, “Ŋmee tibɔbɔrkaan ti m ga kpiir tuk si na tiyakr aapen pu, aan unii umɔk yaar tuur ti pu na ga ŋmaa karn ti;

ref: At the time I have decided, my words will come true. You can trust what I say about the future. It may take a long time, but keep on waiting— it will happen!
text: ba pu? tibɔkpiirkaan ngbaan aayoonn aa kee ŋeer ke ti gbiin, ti ye ndoon aabɔr la, le ki ga dan mala ki nan gbiin kina. Nibaakan, ti ga yunn siib, aa mu tee li kii ti, ti ga sil dan kaan yunn.

ref: “I, the Lord, refuse to accept anyone who is proud. Only those who live by faith are acceptable to me.” Trouble for Evil People
text: Tibɔr ngbaan sɔ: ‘Utunwanbirdaan aan ŋmar, le uninyaan aah gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii na, u ga li kpa limɔfal.’” Titunwanbirdam aah kuln pu na

ref: Wine is treacherous, and arrogant people are never satisfied. They are no less greedy than death itself— they open their mouths as wide as the world of the dead and swallow everyone.
text: Mbamɔn, liwangol ŋmanni unii la, u kpa kigaak le kaa tee kpa lifuur ma. Waah kpa kikumɔŋ ke likaakul ki bi ke nkun na, waa babr tiwan nibaa, le ki nyaŋni ŋitimbol ki chur binib mɔmɔk tinaagbiir.

ref: But they will be mocked with these words: You're doomed! You stored up stolen goods and cheated others of what belonged to them.
text: Bi mɔmɔk ga ŋa u mbɔnyun ni yaansara ki len ke, “Unii u kuun kinaayuk aawangol ki gaal binib aawan mpɔɔn pu bilni na aamɔfal ga kuln. Kina aatuln ga yunn kinye?”

ref: But without warning, those you owe will demand payment. Then you will become a frightened victim.
text: Libuul ngbaan ni le binib bi ye saapɔndam na ga fii sil. Bi ga finn ngeen pu, le ki cha ijawaan chuu si, le sin aabaa ga kpaln baapɔndaan.

ref: You robbed cities and nations everywhere on earth and murdered their people. Now those who survived will be as cruel to you.
text: Saah gaa ŋitimbol pam aawangol mpɔɔn pu pu na, kina le binib bi ŋmar na mu ga nan gaa saawangol; ba pu? aa ku binib pam ki kuln baatim ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi mu ni na.

ref: You're doomed! You made your family rich at the expense of others. You even said to yourself, “I'm above the law.”
text: Saamɔfal junn a. Aa di mpɔɔn ni beebee le ki di gaa binib aawangol le ki kpaln uwankpadaan, le ki pɔɔn aabaa ke aa maa saadichal paacham ki nya mbiin ni tibɔr ni.

ref: But you will bring shame on your family and ruin to yourself for what you did to others.
text: Aa ban isan ki kuln binib pam aamɔfal, le ki joo ni inimɔɔn nan lii saadichal pu, ki lann aabaa aamɔfal.

ref: The very stones and wood in your home will testify against you.
text: Tidir aagon aatakpal wii saabiin pu la, le ilɔkdɔ ti keei.

ref: You're doomed! You built a city on crime and violence.
text: Saamɔfal junn a. Aa di titunwanbir naan kitiŋ, le ki di linikul maa kitiŋ ngbaan siin.

ref: But the Lord All-Powerful sends up in flames what nations and people work so hard to gain.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le nan siin ke binib ngbaan aatotoŋ li ye idɔ i ga tuur mmii na, ki mɔk ke ŋitimbol nan tun nimina mɔmɔk fam.

ref: Just as water fills the sea, the land will be filled with people who know and honor the Lord.
text: Nnyun aah bi ni kookoo nnyusakpem ponn ni pu na, kina le binib ga li nyi Uwumbɔr aah kpa mpɔɔn sakpen pu na dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni.

ref: Now you will be disgraced instead of praised. The Lord will make you drunk, and when others see you naked, you will lose their respect.
text: Sin le ga kan inimɔɔn, naan li ye kipak. Sin aabaa ga nyu ndaan ki gbii. Uwumbɔr le ga daa aatafal ki cha inimɔɔn biin saapak pu.

ref: You destroyed trees and animals on Mount Lebanon; you were ruthless to towns and people everywhere. Now you will be terrorized. Idolatry Is Foolish
text: Mbiin mu aa nan di ŋa Lebanonn aachook na ga gir ni aa pu, le saah nan ku tiwakor ti na ga cha ijawaan chuu si, ba pu? aa ku binib pam ki kuln baatim ni binib bi mɔmɔk bi mu ponn ni na.

ref: What is an idol worth? It's merely a false god. Why trust a speechless image made from wood or metal by human hands?
text: Liwaal kpa ba aanyoor? Unibɔn le naan li, le li joo inyamɔn baanja tuk si. Unii u naan li na tii li naadii, le li mu aa tee ŋmaa len tibɔr.

ref: What can you learn from idols covered with silver or gold? They can't even breathe. Pity anyone who says to an idol of wood or stone, “Get up and do something!”
text: Saamɔfal junn a; ba pu? aa bui lidɔgeln ke, “Finn ngeen pu,” le ki ki bui litakpal li kaa kpa kifuurk na ke, “Finn ngeen pu.” Liwaal ga ŋmaa kpiir tiwan nibaa tuk si ii? Bi ga di salmaa ni tikunabr le boon li, le li mu aa tee kpa kifuurk.

ref: Let all the world be silent— the Lord is present in his holy temple.
text: Uwumbɔr bi Waadichal li bi chain na ni, cha kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk ŋmin chii unimbiin ni.

ref: This is my prayer:
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Habakuk aameel sɔ:

ref: I know your reputation, Lord, and I am amazed at what you have done. Please turn from your anger and be merciful; do for us what you did for our ancestors.
text: Uwumbɔr, m ŋun saah tun lituln li na pu, le ijawaan chuu mi sakpen. Tɔ, ŋa timi aayoonn mumina ŋitukpaan ŋi aa nan ŋani na. Hali saaŋuul ponn ni kan, san timi kinimbaak.

ref: You are the same Holy God who came from Teman and Paran to help us. The brightness of your glory covered the heavens, and your praises were heard everywhere on earth.
text: Uwumbɔr ki nyan ni Edom aatiŋ ni ki choo; Uwumbɔr u ye chain na nyan ni Parann aagongon pu ki choo. Waanyuun gbiin paacham, le waapak mu gbiin kitiŋ kee pu.

ref: Your glory shone like the sun, and light flashed from your hands, hiding your mighty power.
text: Waah wiin pu na naahn nwiin aah wiin pu na la; uŋaal moor lak lak ke mmii na la, le waapɔɔn ma tee bɔr.

ref: Dreadful diseases and plagues marched in front and followed behind.
text: U cha iween le lolni u pu nsan, le nkun paa upuwɔb.

ref: When you stopped, the earth shook; when you stared, nations trembled; when you walked along your ancient paths, eternal mountains and hills crumbled and collapsed.
text: U yaa sil kan, kitiŋ deŋni la; le u yaa yaar lik kan, ŋitimbol jii. Ŋijoo ŋi bi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk na wur la; le n‑yoonn mɔmɔk aagongon na mu ber lir kitiŋ. Ŋima pu le u nan chuun n‑yaayoonn na.

ref: The tents of desert tribes in Cushan and Midian were ripped apart.
text: M nan kan ke ijawaan nan chuu Kusann aanib, le Midiann aatiŋ aanib aawon gbaa.

ref: Our Lord, were you angry with the monsters of the deep? You attacked in your chariot and wiped them out.
text: Uwumbɔr, ŋimɔɔ pu le saaŋuul nan fii ii? nnyusakpem pu le saaŋuul nan fii ii? Aa nan jak saataan ni yaatɔroku tiib bi ye linyaŋ yaab na.

ref: Your arrows were ready and obeyed your commands. You split the earth apart with rivers and streams;
text: Aa nan gor saatɔm kiir, ki ban ipiin pam; Aa cha ŋimɔɔ puu ki bɔkl kitiŋ.

ref: mountains trembled at the sight of you; rain poured from the clouds; ocean waves roared and rose.
text: Le ŋijoo kan si ki mur fenni. Nnyusakpem nyan ni paacham ki lir ni; le nnyun mu bi kitiŋ na puu mpɔɔn pu, le mu aanyunkpenn fii jon paacham.

ref: The sun and moon stood still, while your arrows and spears flashed like lightning.
text: Nwiin ni uŋmal aah kan saapiin ni saakpaatuŋ aah san mala mala pu na, le ni sil paacham chii.

ref: to rescue your people and save your chosen one. You crushed a nation's ruler and stripped his evil kingdom of its power.
text: Aa nan dan ke aa ti gaa saanib ni saah nyan ubɔr u na lii la. Aa nan kuln titunwanbir aatiŋ aayidaan, aa nan doo u kookoo la.

ref: His troops had come like a storm, hoping to scatter us and glad to gobble us up. To them we were refugees in hiding— but you smashed their heads with their own weapons.
text: Aa di ubaa aakpaatuŋ le too chaar uyil buyoonn waajab chii ni ke bi nan jenn timi, ki mɔɔni ke baah ban bi ti loon le ki ku doo bigiim bi bi limukl ni na.

ref: Then your chariots churned the waters of the sea. Habakkuk's Response to God's Message
text: Aa di saataan taa taa nnyusakpem, ki taa taa nnyun mu ti kpaln tipupur.

ref: When I heard this message, I felt weak from fear, and my lips quivered. My bones seemed to melt, and I stumbled around. But I will patiently wait. Someday those vicious enemies will be struck by disaster. Trust in a Time of Trouble
text: M ŋun timina mɔmɔk pu le mpobil gbaa, le mmɔgban jii ijawaan pu, le nwon mɔmɔk kpo, le ntaa jii. Le m tee ga mɔr ki li kii nwiin mundaal Uwumbɔr ga daa binib bi tak timi na aatafal na.

ref: Fig trees may no longer bloom, or vineyards produce grapes; olive trees may be fruitless, and harvest time a failure; sheep pens may be empty, and cattle stalls vacant—
text: Ŋikakan yaa kaa ŋeen, le ndaan aasubil mu yaa kaa baa isui pu, olif aakpan aasui mu yaa yii kaa lun, le tijikaar mu yaa kaa ŋa ikpaakon ni, ipiih mu yaa kaa bi kibɔkpuk ni, le inaa mu yaa kaa bi tinaabar ni kan,

ref: but I will still celebrate because the Lord God is my Savior.
text: m tee ga li mɔɔni Uwumbɔr pu, m ga li kpa mpopiin Uwumbɔr u gaal mi lir na pu.

ref: The Lord gives me strength. He makes my feet as sure as those of a deer, and he helps me stand on the mountains. To the music director: Use stringed instruments.
text: Ndindaan Uwumbɔr le ye maapɔɔn; u ŋa maataafar ke upeeman aataabuseen na la, le ki kii mi ŋijoo paab.

ref: I am Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah. When Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, the Lord gave me this message. Judgment on Judah
text: Uwumbɔr aah nan di waabɔr ti tuk Sefania, buyoonn Amonn aajapɔɔn Josia nan ye Juda aabɔr na sɔ. Sefania nan ye Kusi aajapɔɔn la. Le Kusi mu aate nan ye Gedalia, u mu aate nan ye Amaria na, le Amaria mu aate nan ye ubɔr Hesekia. Uwumbɔr aabɔjil aawiin daal

ref: I, the Lord, now promise to destroy everything on this earth—
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “M ga kuln tiwan mɔmɔk kitiŋ kee pu,

ref: people and animals, birds and fish. Everyone who is evil will crash to the ground, and I will wipe out the entire human race.
text: m ga kuln binib, ni tiwakor, ni inyoon, ni ijan mɔmɔk. M ga cha bibiindam lir baatun mɔmɔk ni. M ga kuln unibɔn, ubaa aan ŋmar. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: I will reach out to punish Judah and Jerusalem— nothing will remain of the god Baal; nothing will be remembered of his pagan priests.
text: “M ga daa Jerusalem aatiŋ, ni Juda aapepel aanib mɔmɔk aatafal. M ga kuln kookoo aanib bi gur ki dooni liwaal li bi yin li ke Baal na, ki kuln baawaadam bi toor li na.

ref: Not a trace will be found of those who worship stars from their rooftops, or bow down to the god Milcom, while claiming loyalty to me, the Lord.
text: M ga kuln unii umɔk joi ŋidichal aapaacham ki ti dooni nwiin, ni uŋmal, ni iŋmabi na. M ga kuln binib bi mɔmɔk dooni mi ki bui ke bi ga kii maamɔb, ki tee puur liwaal li bi yin li ke Milkom na.

ref: Be silent! I am the Lord God, and the time is near. I am preparing to sacrifice my people and to invite my guests.
text: Uwumbɔr aawiin peen ni a, nwiin mundaal Uwumbɔr ga ji binib tibɔr na peen ni a, kina pu na, li ŋmin suuna man. Uwumbɔr gor ke u kɔr waanib ke kitork aawakor na la, le ki yin baadim ke bi nan yoor baawan.

ref: On that day I will punish national leaders and sons of the king, along with all who follow foreign customs.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Linikul ngbaan daal kan, m ga daa bininkpiib, ni mbɔrbim, ni bi mɔmɔk kaa dii maasan na aatafal.

ref: I will punish worshipers of pagan gods and cruel palace officials who abuse their power.
text: M ga daa binib bi mɔmɔk aa taar mbisamɔb na aatafal. Bi su kinaayuk mu, ki ku binib, ki joo baawan ti bilni baawaadir ni na.”

ref: Everyone in Lower Hollow will mourn loudly, because merchants and money changers will be wiped out.
text: Nimi bi bi kitiŋ ngbaan aanyaŋ ni wɔb na, ni li wii ikpowiil, ba pu? binib bi mɔmɔk chuun daa ki tiir na ga kpo.

ref: I'll search Jerusalem with lamps and punish those people who sit there unworried while thinking, “The Lord won't do anything, good or bad.”
text: “N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga yoor karyaa ki biln Jerusalem aatiŋ ponn ni. M ga daa binib bi lik bibaa ke bi ye bininyuum ki lik pak bibaa na aatafal. Bi len ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aa ŋani nibaa ni ŋan, kaa ŋani ni kaa ŋan na mu.’

ref: Their possessions will be taken, their homes left in ruins. They won't get to live in the houses they build, or drink wine from the grapes in their own vineyards. A Terrible Day
text: Bidim ga yoor baawangol buen, le baadichal ber. Baan koo ŋidichal ŋi bi bi maa na ponn ni, kaan nyu baah bi ŋumni ndaan aasubil aasui i na aadaan kpala.”

ref: The great day of the Lord is coming soon, very soon. On that terrible day, fearsome shouts of warriors will be heard everywhere.
text: Uwumbɔr aawinkpaan ngbaan peen ni, mu peen ni ki choo mala mala. Mu ga li ye mpombiin daal la, hali bijab bi kaar na ga wii itaakpayɔl pu.

Mu ga kpaln baah gbii n‑yaan nin chee na, ni baah kuln nin chee kookoo aan timoor gaa nima chee na la. Maanib bi ŋmar na ga yoor baawan ni baatiŋ mu.”

ref: I will fiercely attack. Then every god on this earth will shrink to nothing, and everyone of every nation will bow down to me, right where they are. Judgment on Ethiopia

ref: Herds of wild animals will live in its rubble; all kinds of desert owls will perch on its stones and hoot in the windows. Noisy ravens will be heard inside its buildings, stripped bare of cedar.
text: Nima chee le ipiih, ni iŋoob, ni inaa, ni tiwakor mɔmɔk aabɔŋ ga li doo. Ifiin ga li koo kaalangbenn ni, le ki wii takolu tiib ni kinyeek. Ikakal ga li tɔk ibisamɔi pu le ki wii nima. Santina tiib aadɔ i bi di maa baadichal na ga nya lir kitiŋ,

text: Kaaninkpiib bi ke ichinn i ŋuuni na la; le kaabɔjirb naahn takɔ tiib bi nkon joo bi na, kaan ŋmaa mɔr ke likpabl li dɔ ki ti woln kitaak.

ref: The Lord wiped out nations and left fortresses crumbling in the dirt. Their streets and towns were reduced to ruins and emptied of people.
text: Uwumbɔr bui ke, “M ŋar ŋitimbomɔn ŋŋaan; m kuln ŋaatim ki cha ŋaagon ni tidifɔfɔŋ na ber doo. Bi fii cha ntim ngbaan a, ubaa aa ki bi mu ponn ni, ubaa aa gur.

text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le m nan dak ke maanib ga san mi ki kii maasurm, aan baatiŋ taa kuln, aan maatafadaan mɔmɔk taa dan bi pu. Tɔ, bi nan beenin neen ke bi li tun beebee aatun baatuln mɔmɔk ni.”

ref: The Lord said: Just wait for the day when I accuse you nations. I have decided on a day, when I will bring together every nation and kingdom and punish them all in my fiery anger. I will become furious and destroy the earth.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ki bui ke, “Ni li kii man. Li ŋmin man ki li kii bundaal aan m ga fii sil ki galn ŋitimbol na. M ŋa nlandak ke m kuun ŋitimbol ni nnaan, ki cha ŋi bee maaŋuul aah pɔɔ pu na. M ga di maaŋuusakpeln li wu ke mmii na le di kuln kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk.

ref: I will purify each language and make those languages acceptable for praising me. Then, with hearts united, everyone will serve only me, the Lord.
text: “N‑yoonn ngbaan le m ga kpeln ŋitimbol ngbaan aanib aabimbin, le bi ga li gur mee min baanja ki taa ki mee liwaal libaa. Bi mɔmɔk ga kii maamɔb.

ref: From across the rivers of Ethiopia, my scattered people, my true worshipers, will bring offerings to me.
text: Hali maanib bi yaa ki bi Kus aatiŋ ni dandar dandar na ga joo ni ipiin nan tii mi.

ref: When that time comes, you won't rebel against me and be put to shame. I'll do away with those who are proud and arrogant. Never will any of them strut around on my holy mountain.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan na, nimi maanib aan ki san inimɔɔn ke ni nan nyan mpuwɔb. M ga nyan binib bi mɔmɔk kpa kigaak ni kipupuk na ni ponn ni, le naan ki li kpa kalimbaani maagongoln li bi chain na pu daalbaadaal.

ref: But I, the Lord, won't destroy any of your people who are truly humble and turn to me for safety.
text: M ga cha binib bi aabimbin ŋan aan bi sunn bibaa taab ki ga dan m chee ki nan ban nterm na le li bi nima.

ref: The people of Israel who survive will live right and refuse to tell lies. They will eat and rest with nothing to fear. A Song of Celebration

ref: Everyone in Jerusalem and Judah, celebrate and shout with all your heart!
text: Israel aanib, li mɔɔni ki tar man. Jerusalem aatiŋ, li mɔɔni sakpen.

ref: Zion, your punishment is over. The Lord has forced your enemies to turn and retreat. Your Lord is King of Israel and stands at your side; you don't have to worry about any more troubles.
text: Uwumbɔr kuln nimi aatafadaan a; u nyaŋ nimi aadim mɔmɔk a. Uwumbɔr u ye Israel yaab aabɔr na bi ni chee; taa ki san ijawaan man.

ref: Jerusalem, the time is coming, when it will be said to you: “Don't be discouraged or grow weak from fear!
text: N‑yoonn choo, le bi ga nan bui Jerusalem aanib ke, “Sionn aanib, taa san ijawaan man. Taa cha niwon yɔl.

ref: The Lord your God wins victory after victory and is always with you. He celebrates and sings because of you, and he will refresh your life with his love.” The Lord's Promise to His People
text: Nidindaan Uwumbɔr bi ni chee; waapɔɔn le tii nimi linyaŋ. Uwumbɔr ga li neen nimi le ki ga tii nimi limɔfapɔln waageehm ni. Nimi pu le u ga gaa ilahn ki li kpa mpopiin,

ref: I will punish those who mistreat you. I will bring together the lame and the outcasts, then they will be praised, instead of despised, in every country on earth.
text: N‑yoonn choo, le m ga daa binib bi muk nimi na aatafal; m ga gaa binib bi mɔmɔk ye biwɔb na lii, ki giin ni binib bi bi tinaagbiir ni kitiyayaŋ ni na linampal. M ga cha baanimɔɔn kpaln nnyuŋ, le dulnyaa mɔmɔk ga li pak bi.

ref: I will lead you home, and with your own eyes you will see me bless you with all you once owned. Then you will be famous everywhere on this earth. I, the Lord, have spoken!
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan choo, le m ga giin ni nimi aanib bi yaa na linampal; m ga cha ni li kpa liyimbil dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni, ki cha ni ki gir kan liwangol.” Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: On the first day of the sixth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak his message to the governor of Judah and to the high priest. So Haggai told Governor Zerubbabel and High Priest Joshua
text: Darius aah nan ye Pesia aabɔrkpaan ki ti saa ŋibin ŋilee pu na aaŋmaloob aawiin mbaa daal, le Uwumbɔr nan cha waabɔnabr Hagai len tibɔr timina. Tibɔr ngbaan nan ye Juda aayidaan Serubabel u nan ye Sealtiel aajapɔɔn na, ni Utotoorninkpel Josua u nan ye Jehosadak aajapɔɔn na aabɔr la.

ref: You harvest less than you plant, you never have enough to eat or drink, your clothes don't keep you warm, and your wages are stored in bags full of holes.
text: Ni bun njikaabim pam, le ki tee nan chee njikaabim pɔkaa kina. Ni kpa tijikaar ni ji, le ki mu aa babr. Ni kpa ndaan ni nyu, le mu aa tee gbii nimi. Ni kpa tiwanpeenkaan, le ni mu aa leer nimi tiwoor. Bijab bi tun lituln ki gaal lipal na aapal aa fuur bi.

text: Ni bee tiwan ni cha nimina mɔmɔk ŋani nimi na aa?

ref: But first, go to the hills and get wood for my temple, so I can take pride in it and be worshiped there.

text: “Ni nan mak ke ni ga nan chee tijikaar sakpen, le naa nan kpann kpala. Le naah di tijikaar ngbaan kun linampal na, m pii ti libuln di buen. Ba ŋa aan m ŋa kina? Unii mɔk aanimbil aah man ubaa aadichal pu aan Maadichal ber ki dɔ na pu le cha m ŋa kina.

ref: That's also why the dew doesn't fall and your harvest fails.
text: Kina pu le utaal aa bi, le tijikaar mu aa ŋmaa ŋa.

ref: Haggai then told them that the Lord had promised to be with them.

text: Naah nan nyan ni Ijipt aatiŋ ni na, m nan puu ke m ga li bi ni chee n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. M beenin bi ni chee, kina pu na, ni taa san ijawaan man.

ref: Soon I will again shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
text: “Naan ki yunn le m ga dam paacham, ni taab, ni kitiŋ, ni nnyusakpem.

ref: I will shake the nations, and their treasures will be brought here. Then the brightness of my glory will fill this temple.

ref: All silver and gold belong to me,
text: Dulnyaa wee aakunabr ni salmaa mɔmɔk ye min yaan la.

ref: and I promise that this new temple will be more glorious than the first one. I will also bless this city with peace. The Past and the Future
text: Maadichapɔln limina ga li ŋan jer likpokl na pel pel, nima chee le m ga tii maanib nwankam ni nsuudoon.” Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina. Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr aah buen ti baa bitotoorb mbaan mu na

text: U nan bui ke, “Baa bitotoorb ki bee mbaan mue aabɔr.

text: Unii yaa lee kitork aanann ti bi chain aan bi di ti tii Uwumbɔr na ki di poo waabɔkul ni; udaan yaa nan cha waabɔkul ngbaan meeh boroboro, bee baah mɔn bisaa bu na, bee ndaan, bee olif aakpan, bee tijikaar tibaa kan, kina ga ŋmaa cha kina aajikaar ŋa chain aa?” Hagai aah baa mbaan ngbaan na, bitotoorb ngbaan nan bui ke, “Aayii.”

ref: But from now on, things will get better. Before you started laying the foundation for the temple,

text: Uŋmal ngbaan aawiin moninko ni inaa daal baan ngbaan,

ref: Today you have completed the foundation for my temple, so listen to what your future will be like.
text: Din wee ye ŋmawae aawiin moninko ni inaa daal la, le ni bil Maadichal aadinyikl aatakpal doo. Tɔ, li lik man tiwan ni ga ŋa n‑yoonn mue ki joo cha na.

ref: Although you have not yet harvested any grain, grapes, figs, pomegranates, or olives, I will richly bless you in the days ahead. God's Promise to Zerubbabel
text: Tɔ, njikaabim mubaa aa gur, le ndaan aasubil ni ŋikakan, ni ŋisubil ŋiken na, ni olif aakpan aasui mu aa kee lun; ki nya din wee ki joo cha, m ga ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu.” Uwumbɔr aah bui ke u ga ter Serubabel pu na

text: le Uwumbɔr nan ki tii Hagai tibɔr tee ke u di tii Juda aayidaan Serubabel ke, “M ban m dam paacham ni kitiŋ

text: ki nyaŋ nnaan yayan mɔmɔk ki kuln mu aapɔɔn. M ga nyaŋ itaan aatɔroku tiib ni binib bi ŋaal bi na; itaan ga kpoi, le binib bi dik i pu na ku tɔb.

ref: But tell my servant Zerubbabel that I, the Lord All-Powerful, have chosen him, and he will rule in my name.
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal le m ga lee sin maatutunn Serubabel, ki ga cha aa di maayimbil joo binib. Sin le ye unii u m lee u na.” Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.

ref: I am the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo. In the eighth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told me to say:
text: Ubɔr Darius aah nan ye Pesia aabɔrkpaan pu na aabileler ni aaŋmaniin ponn ni, le Uwumbɔr nan di tibɔr timina tuk waabɔnabr Sekaria. Sekaria aate le nan ye Berekia, le uyaaja ye Ido.

ref: Israel, I, the Lord All-Powerful, was very angry with your ancestors. But if you people will return to me, I will turn and help you.
text: le m bui nimi dandana wee ke, ‘Gir ni m chee man aan m mu gir ni ni chee.

ref: Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. They were warned by the earlier prophets to give up their evil and turn back to me, but they paid no attention.
text: Ni taa li bi ke niyaajatiib na. N‑yaayoonn na le bibɔnabr nan di maabɔr tuk bi, ki tuk bi ke bi taa ki tun titunwanbir, ki taa ki li bi kinimbɔŋ aabimbin ni. Le baa ŋun tii mi, kaa kii maamɔb mu.

ref: Where are your ancestors now? Not even prophets live forever.
text: Niyaajatiib ni bibɔnabr ngbaan aa ki bi.

ref: But my warnings and my words spoken by the prophets caught up with your ancestors. So they turned back to me and said, “Lord All-Powerful, you have punished us for our sins, just as you had planned.” First Vision: Horses and Riders
text: M nan cha maatutum bi ye bibɔnabr na tii niyaajatiib ikaal ni nsurm, le bi yii i, le ki jin falaa i pu. Le bi bee ke bi tun taani, ki bee ke min, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le daa bitafal ke maah nan puu ke m ga ŋa pu na, ki ŋeer baah tun pu na.’” Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ngbaan aah daŋ tidaŋ ki kan itaan pu na

ref: On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, which was the eleventh month of that same year, the Lord spoke to me in a vision during the night: In a valley among myrtle trees, I saw someone on a red horse, with riders on red, brown, and white horses behind him.
text: M nan kan Uwumbɔr aatuun dik utaman pu. U nan sil ikpasɔi aasui ibaa taab kifataŋ ni, le itaan i nan ye itaman, ni itachachal, ni itapiin na nan paa upuwɔb.

ref: An angel was there to explain things to me, and I asked, “Sir, who are these riders?” “I'll tell you,” the angel answered.
text: Le m baa u ke, “Maaninkpel, itaan yee aatataa ye kinye?” Le Uwumbɔr aatuun mu bi len m chee na gar mi ke, “M ga mɔk si yaatataa aah ye pu na.”

ref: At once, the man standing among the myrtle trees said, “These are the ones the Lord has sent to find out what's happening on earth.”
text: Le Uwumbɔr aatuun u si ikpasɔi aasui ngbaan taab na bui mi ke, “Uwumbɔr le tun i ke i chuun mann kitiŋ.”

ref: Then the riders spoke to the Lord's angel, who was standing among the myrtle trees, and they said, “We have gone everywhere and have discovered that the whole world is at peace.”
text: Tɔ, i nan tuk Uwumbɔr aatuun mu si ikpasɔi aasui taab ngbaan na yaah kan pu na ke: “Ti chuun dulnyaa mɔmɔk ni ki kan ke dulnyaa wee bi suuna la.”

ref: So the angel told me to announce: I, the Lord All-Powerful, am very protective of Jerusalem.
text: Le ntuun ngbaan bui mi ke m di Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aah len pu na moon ke: “M gee Jerusalem sakpen, le ntafal bi maatiŋ ki bi chain na ni,

ref: For a while I was angry at the nations, but now I am furious, because they have made things worse for Jerusalem and are not the least bit concerned.
text: le maaŋuul fii ŋitimbol ŋi kpa kigaak ki bi nsuudoon ni lifuur ni na pu sakpen. Buyoonn m nan laa joo maaŋuul ke li taa pii maanib na, le ŋitimbol ngbaan nan cha maanib aafalaa moo nyaŋ.

ref: And so, I will have pity on Jerusalem. The city will be completely rebuilt, and my temple will stand again.

text: Le ubaa yaa baa u ke, ‘Kina kan, tibuwar ti bi aabiŋ pu na nyan ni la chee’ kan, u ga bui ke, ‘Njɔ ubaa do le m kan ti.’” Uwumbɔr aah bui ke bi ku waapihkpaal pu na
