text: M ga tak maanib, le kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu binib ŋigetek ŋilee kpoi.

ref: Then I will purify them and put them to the test, just as gold and silver are purified and tested. They will pray in my name, and I will answer them. I will say, “You are my people,” and they will reply, “You, Lord, are our God!”
text: Le ligetekr libaa li gur na, m ga tɔŋ bi, ki nyan baajɔŋ, ke baah pu tikunabr mmii ni ki nyani taajɔŋ pu na. M ga tɔŋ bi ke baah tɔŋni salmaa mmii ni pu na. Le bi ga li mee mi, le m ga kii baameel. M ga bui bi ke bi ye maanib la, le bi len bibaa ke min le ye Baawumbɔr.”

ref: The Lord will have his day. And when it comes, everything that was ever taken from Jerusalem will be returned and divided among its people.
text: Nwiin mundaal Uwumbɔr ga kal ki ji binib tibɔr na peen ni a. Le bi ga yoor Jerusalem aawan mpɔɔn buen, ki ga yakr tiwan ngbaan ninimbil ni.

ref: But first, he will bring many nations to attack Jerusalem—homes will be robbed, women raped, and half of the population dragged off, though the others will be allowed to remain.
text: Uwumbɔr ga kuun ŋitimbol mɔmɔk nan kpaan, le ŋi tak Jerusalem. Bi ga nyaŋ kitiŋ ngbaan, le ki yoor ŋidichal ni tiwan mpɔɔn, ki chur bipiib mpɔɔn ki doon bi chee. Bi ga di binib ngbaan ligetekr libaa buen tinaagbiir ni, kitiyayaŋ ni, le ligetekr li gur na ga gaar kitiŋ ngbaan ni.

ref: The Lord will attack those nations like a warrior fighting in battle.
text: Le Uwumbɔr ga nya ki ti tak ŋitimbol ngbaan, ke waah nan ŋani pu n‑yaayoonn na.

ref: He will take his stand on the Mount of Olives east of Jerusalem, and the mountain will split in half, forming a wide valley that runs from east to west.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan kan, u ga ti li si Olif Aasui Aajool li bi Jerusalem aawipuul wɔb na pu la. Le Olif Aasui Aajool ngbaan ga bool nfum mulee, le kifataŋ sakpeŋ doon kaasisik ni, ki nya liwipuul ki ti saa liwilir. Libool libaa ga di toŋ ŋŋangan wɔb, le liken na di toŋ ŋŋangii wɔb.

ref: Then you people will escape from the Lord's mountain, through this valley, which reaches to Azal. You will run in all directions, just as everyone did when the earthquake struck in the time of King Uzziah of Judah. Afterwards, the Lord my God will appear with his holy angels.
text: Kifataŋ ki yakr lijool limina nfum mulee na ponn ni, le ni ga dii ki san ŋmar. Ni ga san ke kitiŋ aah nan puu, Juda aabɔr Usia aayoonn, aan niyaajatiib nan san pu na. Ndindaan Uwumbɔr ga joo ni waatuuntiib mɔmɔk ki dan.

ref: It will be a bright day that won't turn cloudy or cold.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, tiwoor aan ki li bi,

ref: And the Lord has decided when it will happen—this time of unending day.
text: le libɔmbɔln mu aan li bi. Nwiin ga li bi nwiin pu ni kinyeek mu la. Uwumbɔr baanja le nyi buyoonn nimina ga ŋa na.

ref: In both summer and winter, life-giving streams will flow from Jerusalem, half of them to the Dead Sea in the east and half to the Mediterranean Sea in the west.
text: Nwiin ngbaan daal yaa nan fuu ni kan, nnyunpɔm ga li puu nya ni Jerusalem ni. Ligetekr libaa ga li puu cha N‑yaan Aanyusakpem ni, le liken puu cha Kaasisik ni Aanyusakpem ni. Mu ga li puu n‑yoonn mɔmɔk libiln ni la. Mu ga li puu lipeel ni kiseek ni la.

ref: Then there will be only one Lord who rules as King and whose name is worshiped everywhere on earth.
text: Le Uwumbɔr ga li ye kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk aabɔr. Unii mɔk ga li dooni u ke u ye Uwumbɔr, le ki li nyi u liyimbil ngbaan pu.

ref: Here is what the Lord will do to those who attack Jerusalem: While they are standing there, he will make their flesh rot and their eyes fall from their sockets and their tongues drop out.
text: Uwumbɔr ga cha iween i bir na nan lir ŋitimbol ŋi mɔmɔk tak Jerusalem na pu. Ŋaanib aawon ga bur le bi laa fu. Binimbil ni bilambil ga bur lir.

ref: The Lord will make them go into a frenzy and start attacking each other,
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan kan, Uwumbɔr ga ŋmal bilan ki cha ijawaan chuu bi sakpen, le umɔk fenn kan uŋeen aatɔb na kan, u ga tak u.

ref: until even the people of Judah turn against those in Jerusalem. This same terrible disaster will also strike every animal nearby, including horses, mules, camels, and donkeys. Finally, everything of value in the surrounding nations will be collected and brought to Jerusalem—gold, silver, and piles of clothing.
text: Iween i bir na mu ga lir baadim aawakor mɔmɔk pu, baakakaa ni. I ga lir itaan, ni tiwakor ti naahn ibon na, ni laakumii tiib, ni ibon pu.

ref: Afterwards, the survivors from those nations that attacked Jerusalem will go there each year to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful, and to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
text: Le binib bi mɔmɔk ŋmar ŋitimbol ŋi nan tak Jerusalem na ga li chaa nima libiln mɔk ni ki ti dooni Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ke ubɔrkpaan na. Bi ga li chaa ti ji Tikakar mu aajim nima.

ref: No rain will fall on the land of anyone in any country who refuses to go to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Litimbol limɔk yii kaa chaa ti dooni Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ke ubɔrkpaan na kan, utaal aan nu baatiŋ pu.

ref: This horrible disaster will strike the Egyptians and everyone else who refuses to go there for the celebration.
text: Ijipt yaab ni ŋitimbol ŋimɔk yii kaa ji Tikakar aajim na aatafadaan le na.

ref: At that time the words “Dedicated to the Lord” will be engraved on the bells worn by horses. In fact, every ordinary cooking pot in Jerusalem will be just as sacred to the Lord All-Powerful as the bowls used at the altar. Any one of them will be acceptable for boiling the meat of sacrificed animals, and there will no longer be a need to sell special pots and bowls.
text: Ŋikumbuu ŋimɔk bi Jerusalem ni Juda aapepel liken mɔmɔk ni na ga kpaln Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aadoon aawan la. Binib bi toor kitork na ga li joo ŋima le ŋaani kitork aanann. N‑yoonn ngbaan yaa nan fuu ni kan, binib bi tiir kitiirk na aan ki li bi Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan Aadichal ni.

ref: I am Malachi. And this is the message that the Lord gave me for Israel. The Lord's Love for Israel
text: Uwumbɔr aah nan di waabɔr ti tuk waabɔnabr Malakai ke u di tuk Israel yaab na sɔ. Uwumbɔr aah gee Israel yaab pu na

ref: Israel, I, the Lord, have loved you. And yet you ask in what way have I loved you. Don't forget that Esau was the brother of your ancestor Jacob, but I chose Jacob
text: Uwumbɔr bui waanib ke, “M gee nimi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk.” Le bi gar u ke, “Kinye aan aa mɔk timi saah gee timi pu na?” Le Uwumbɔr gar bi ke, “Esɔ ni Jakob nan ye naabitiib la, le m nan tee lee Jakob ni uyaabitiib,

ref: instead of Esau. And I turned Esau's hill country into a barren desert where jackals roam.
text: le ki yii Esɔ ni uyaabitiib. M nan bii Esɔ aatiŋ ki bi ŋigongon ni na, ki cha ki kpaln ipeel aatiŋ.”

ref: Esau's descendants may say, “Although our nation Edom is in ruins, we will rebuild it.” But I, the Lord All-Powerful, promise to tear down whatever they build. Then everyone will know that I will never stop being angry with them as long as they are so sinful.
text: Esɔ aayaabitiib, bi ye Edom aanib na, yaa bui ke, “Bi ber timi aatim a, tɔ, ti mu ga ki gir maa mu” kan, le Uwumbɔr ga gar ke, “Cha bi ki maa mu, m ga ki gir ber mu. Binib ga yin ki ke, ‘Titunwanbir aatiŋ,’ ni ‘Litimbol li Uwumbɔr aaŋuul fii li pu kaan sɔŋ na.’”

ref: Israel, when you see this, you will shout, “The Lord's great reputation reaches beyond our borders.” Judgment against Priests
text: Israel aanib aanimbil ga kan nimina, le ki bui ke, “Hali ni yaa kaa ye Israel aatiŋ pu kan, Uwumbɔr pɔɔ la.” Uwumbɔr aah sak bitotoorb pu na

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something to say to you priests. Children respect their fathers, and servants respect their masters. I am your father and your master, so why don't you respect me? You priests have insulted me, and now you ask, “How did we insult you?”
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui bitotoorb ke, “Japɔɔn nyuŋni ute la, le ututunn mu nyuŋni udindaan. Nite le ye mi, ba ŋa naa nyuŋni mi? Nidindaan le ye mi, ba ŋa naa pak mi? Ni lik mi fam, le ki tee baa ke, ‘Ti lik si fam kinye?’

ref: You embarrass me by offering worthless food on my altar. Then you ask, “How have we embarrassed you?” You have done it by saying, “What's so great about the Lord's altar?”
text: Naah lik mi fam pu na sɔ, ni joo tijikaar ti kaa ŋan na le toor kitork maatork aabimbiln pu. Le ni baa ke, ‘Kinye aan ti yii kaa pak si?’ M ga bui nimi ke naa lik faar maatork aabimbiln.

ref: But isn't it wrong to offer animals that are blind, lame, or sick? Just try giving those animals to your governor. That certainly wouldn't please him or make him want to help you.
text: Buyoonn ni joo ni kiwakork ki jɔb, bee ki bun, bee ki aataal koo na nan toor kitork tii mi na, ni dak ke taani ubaa aa bi ii? Di kina aawakork tii nimi aayidaan man ki lik. Ni dak ke kina aawakork ga li piin usui ii? U ga faar nimi aapiin ngbaan ki ter nimi ii?”

ref: I am the Lord God All-Powerful, and you had better try to please me. You have sinned. Now see if I will have mercy on any of you.
text: Tɔ, nimi bitotoorb, pɔɔn nibaa man ki mee Uwumbɔr ke u li kpa ti pu tiŋann. Waan kii nimi aameel, ba pu? ni tii u ipiin i kaa ŋan na la.

ref: I wish someone would lock the doors of my temple, so you would stop wasting time building fires on my altar. I am not pleased with you priests, and I refuse to accept any more of your offerings.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ki bui ke, “M ba neen ke ni ponn ni ubaa laŋ Maadichal aajaaleŋ tiib, aan ni taa ki ŋmaa koo ki ti tuur mmii mu kaa kpa tinyoor tibaa na maatork aabimbiln paab. Nsui aa piin ni pu; maan gaa ipiin i ni joo nan tii mi na.

ref: From dawn until dusk my name is praised by every nation on this earth, as they burn incense and offer the proper sacrifices to me.
text: Dulnyaa wee aanib mɔmɔk nyuŋni mi la. Bi seer tulalee aayon ni kookoo ki tii mi, ki tii mi ipiin i ŋan na. Bi mɔmɔk nyuŋni mi la.

ref: But even you priests insult me by saying, “There's nothing special about the Lord's altar, and these sacrifices are worthless.”
text: Le nima aa nyuŋni mi, ki bui ke maatork aabimbiln aa ye nibaa, le ki joo ni tijikaar ti ni lik seen ti na nan toor kitork li pu.

ref: You get so disgusted that you even make vulgar signs at me. And for an offering, you bring stolen animals or those that are lame or sick. Should I accept these?
text: Ni bui le ke, ‘Ti kpaan bak nimina pu a,’ le ki fenn nimɔfal toŋ nibaa wɔb. Naah sun kiwakork ki na, bee ki bun na, bee kitaal koo na, le ni joo toor kitork tii mi. Ni dak ke m ga gaa nimina ni chee ee?

ref: Instead of offering the acceptable animals you have promised, you bring me those that are unhealthy. I will punish you for this, because I am the great King, the Lord All-Powerful, and I am worshiped by nations everywhere.
text: Ujinjir u yaa joo ni kiwakork ki kaa bi tibaa ni na nan toor kitork tii mi na kan, m ga puun lii udaan pu, ba pu? u kpa kiwakork ki ŋan aan u puu ke u ga di tii mi na waapiih ni. M ye ubɔrkpaan la, le ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aanib san mi ijawaan.” Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina.

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have something else to say to you priests.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan bui bitotoorb ke, “Nkaal mumina ye nimi yoo la.

ref: You had better take seriously the need to honor my name. Otherwise, when you give a blessing, I will turn it into a curse. In fact, I have already done this, because you haven't taken to heart your duties as priests.
text: Ni li nyuŋni mi nimi aatun mɔmɔk ni. Ni yaa kaa pel maah len pu na kan, m ga puun lii ni pu. M ga puun lii baah tii nimi tiwan ni na pu. Mbamɔn, naah kaa joo maakaal mbamɔm pu na, m puen puun lii ni pu a.

ref: I will punish your descendants and rub your faces in the manure from your animal sacrifices, and then be done with you.
text: M ga daa nimi aabim aatafal, ki di naah kɔr tiwakor ti na aapor boon ninimbil wɔb, aan bi ga di nimi buen litapuln pu.

ref: I am telling you this, so I can continue to keep my agreement with your ancestor Levi.
text: Le ni ga bee ke min le tii nimi nkaal ngbaan, le maah puu tipuur ti tii Liifai aayaabitiib na aan bii.

ref: I blessed him with a full life, as I had promised, and he kept his part of the agreement by honoring me and respecting my name.
text: “M nan puu tipuur tii bi ke bi ga li kpa limɔfafɔfɔŋ ni laafee, ki nan sil tii bi tiwan ngbaan, ke bi li pak mi. N‑yaayoonn ngbaan na bi nan pak mi ki san mi.

ref: He taught the truth and never told lies, and he led a lot of people to turn from sin, because he obeyed me and lived right.
text: Bi nan joo ibamɔn le mɔk maanib, kaa mɔk bi tiwan ni kaa ŋan na. Bi nan kpa lifuur, ki dii mi mbamɔm, le ki ter binib pam ke bi di cha titunwanbir aatuln.

ref: You priests should be eager to spread knowledge, and everyone should come to you for instruction, because you speak for me, the Lord All-Powerful.
text: Ni ye bitotoorb aatuln le ke bi mɔk binib Uwumbɔr aah sil ye pu na. Bima chee le binib ga buen ki ti bae maah ban pu na, ba pu? bima le ye min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan aatutum.

ref: But you have turned your backs on me. Your teachings have led others to do sinful things, and you have broken the agreement I made with your ancestor Levi.
text: “Le nimi bitotoorb yii isan i ŋan na. Naah mɔk binib pu na cha bi yenn ki tun titunwanbir la. Ni bii tipuur ti m nan puu tii nimi aayaaja Liifai na.

ref: So I caused everyone to hate and despise you, because you disobeyed me and failed to treat all people alike. A Broken Agreement
text: Ni yii, kaa kii maa ban pu na. Ni yaa ji maanib tibɔr kan, ni ganni la. Nima pu na, m mu ga cha Israel yaab lik seen nimi.” Binib aah kaa kii tii Uwumbɔr pu na

ref: Don't you know that we all have God as our Father? Didn't the one God create each of us? Then why do you cheat each other by breaking the agreement God made with your ancestors?
text: Taa kpaan te la aa? Naa ye Uwumbɔr baan le naan ti mɔmɔk aa? Kina kan, ni ŋa kinye aan ti bii tipuur ti ti puu tii tɔb na, ki lik seen tipuur ti Uwumbɔr nan puu tii tiyaajatiib na?

ref: You people in Judah and Jerusalem have been unfaithful to the Lord. You have disgraced the temple that he loves, and you have committed the disgusting sin of marrying the worshipers of other gods.
text: Juda aanib bii tipuur ti bi nan puu tii Uwumbɔr na, ki tun titunwanbir kpaan Jerusalem aatiŋ ni, ni kitiŋ ngbaan mɔmɔk pu. Bi bii Uwumbɔr Aadichal li u gee na. Bijab yoor bipiib bi dooni ŋiwaa na.

ref: I pray that the Lord will no longer let those who are guilty belong to his people, even if they eagerly decide to offer the Lord a gift.
text: Uwumbɔr, nyan Israel aanib ponn ni binib bi tun kina aatun na, ki taa ki cha bi kpaan timi aatimbol aah joo ipiin i nan tii sin, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan na ni.

ref: And what else are you doing? You cry noisily and flood the Lord's altar with your tears, because he isn't pleased with your offerings and refuses to accept them.
text: Naah ki ŋani tiwan ni mu kpee na sɔ: Ni pu, le bipiib wii ki di tinyunyunn gbiin Uwumbɔr aatork aabimbiln pu, kina pu na le Uwumbɔr aa ki gaal nimi aapiin i ni joo nan tii u na.

ref: And why isn't God pleased? It's because he knows that each of you men has been unfaithful to the wife you married when you were young. You promised that she would be your partner, but now you have broken that promise.
text: Ni baa le ke ba ŋa? Naah ye pu na le ye ke u nyi ke aa bii tipuur ti aa nan laa ye unachipɔɔn ki puu ti tii upii u aa nan yoor na. Aa ni upii ngbaan nan kpaan la, le aa bii tipuur ti aa nan puu tii u na, ki nyi ke aa nan puu tipuur ngbaan Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni ke saan nya upuwɔb.

ref: Didn't God create you and your wife to become like one person? And why did he do this? It was so you would have children, and then lead them to become God's people. Don't ever be unfaithful to your wife.
text: Uwumbɔr nan di aa ni aapuu aawon ni kifuurk kpaan ŋa kibaa la. Ba nan cha u ŋa kina? Ni nan ye le ke ni kan mbim mu ye Uwumbɔr aanib na. Kina pu na, li nyi man, ubaa taa bii u ni upuu aah puu tipuur ti tii tɔb na.

ref: You have worn out the Lord with your words. And yet, you ask, “How did we do that?” You did it by saying, “The Lord is pleased with evil and doesn't care about justice.”
text: Ni cha Uwumbɔr ti kpaan bak naah len tibɔr pu na pu. Tɔ, le ni baa ke, “Ti ŋa kinye ki tii u tibakr?” Naah len tibɔr pu na, le ni tii u tibakr; ba pu? ni len ke “Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan dak ke titunwanbirdam mɔmɔk ŋan le na; ke mbamɔn, u gee bi la,” ki ki len ke, “Uwumbɔr u tii binib ibamɔn na bi la chee?”

ref: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send my messenger to prepare the way for me. Then suddenly the Lord you are looking for will appear in his temple. The messenger you desire is coming with my promise, and he is on his way. A Day of Change
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan gar ke, “M ga tun ni maatuun aan u nan toor nsan siin mi. Le Dindaan u ni ban na ga fuu ni libuul ngbaan ni, Waadichal ni. Ntuun mu ni neen sakpen ke ni kan mu na ga dan ki nan di maah puu tipuur ti na moon.”

ref: On the day the Lord comes, he will be like a furnace that purifies silver or like strong soap in a washbasin. No one will be able to stand up to him.
text: Tɔ, ŋma ga ŋmaa sil kina aawiin chee? U yaa nan fuu ni kan, ŋma ga ŋmar? U ga nan li bi ke bukiib bu pɔɔ na la, ki bi ke mmii mu wu nyani tijɔŋ tikur ni na la.

ref: The Lord will purify the descendants of Levi, as though they were gold or silver. Then they will bring the proper offerings to the Lord,
text: U ga nan ji tibɔr ibamɔn ni, ke unii u pu tikunabr mmii ni ki nyani tijɔŋ na la. Uchaa aah pu tikunabr ni salmaa mmii ni ki nyani tijɔŋ pu na, kina le Uwumbɔr aatuun ga nan toor bitotoorb, ki cha bi joo ni kitork bamɔnn nan tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: and the offerings of the people of Judah and Jerusalem will please him, just as they did in the past. Don't Cheat God
text: Le kitork aapiin i Juda ni Jerusalem aanib joo nan tii Uwumbɔr na ga piir usui, ke yaah nan piir usui n‑yaayoonn na pu na.

ref: The Lord All-Powerful said: I'm now on my way to judge you. And I will quickly condemn all who practice witchcraft or cheat in marriage or tell lies in court or rob workers of their pay or mistreat widows and orphans or steal the property of foreigners or refuse to respect me.
text: Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ki bui ke, “M ga dan ni chee ki nan ji nimi tibɔr, ki bii binib bi joo inyɔk tun lituln na, ni bi ye bidagoob na, ni bi geei inyamɔn paani biken na, ni bi ji baatutum pem pem na, ni bi kaa tii bikpopiib ni nkpobim baabamɔn na, ni bi ji biwɔwɔm na, ni bi kaa pak mi na. M ga mɔk bi mɔmɔk ke baabɔr bii la. Unii aah ga yakr waah tun ki kan pu na ligeln ki tii Uwumbɔr na

ref: Descendants of Jacob, I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I never change. That's why you haven't been wiped out,
text: “Min le ye Uwumbɔr, maa kpelni. Kina pu na, nimi, Jakob aayaabitiib aa kee kuln doo.

ref: even though you have ignored and disobeyed my laws ever since the time of your ancestors. But if you return to me, I will return to you. And yet you ask, “How can we return?”
text: Ni bi ke niyaajatiib la, le ki yii maakaal, kaa joo i. Fenn gir ni m chee man, aan m mu fenn gir ni ni chee. Min Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan le len kina. Le ni baa ke, ‘Ti ga ŋa kinye ki fenn gir ni aa chee?’

ref: You people are robbing me, your God. And, here you are, asking, “How are we robbing you?” You are robbing me of the offerings and of the ten percent that belongs to me.
text: Le m ga baa nimi ke ni ŋan ke unii ji Uwumbɔr pem pem aa? Mbamɔn, naa ŋan; le nima tee ji mi pem pem. Le ni ki baa ke, ‘Kinye aan ti ji si pem pem?’ Le m ga gar nimi ke naah yakr nimi aatuln aanyoor aageln li tii mi na, ni ipiin i ni tii mi na, le ni ji mi.

ref: That's why your whole nation is under a curse.
text: Litimbol mɔln ngbaan mɔmɔk aah ji mi pem pem pu na le m puun lii ni mɔmɔk pu.

ref: I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I challenge you to put me to the test. Bring the entire ten percent into the storehouse, so there will be food in my house. Then I will open the windows of heaven and flood you with blessing after blessing.
text: Ni li joo ni naah yakr tiwan ni ke ni ye min yaan na Maadichal ni, aan tijikaar li bi li ponn ni. Tɔŋ mi man aan ki kan ke m ga piir paacham aatakolu tiib waan, ki cha tijikaar gbiin nimi aatiŋ.

ref: I will also stop locusts from destroying your crops and keeping your vineyards from producing.
text: Maan cha tiwayukaan bii nimi aajikaar, le nimi aasubil aasui ga lu sakpen.

ref: Everyone of every nation will talk about how I have blessed you and about your wonderful land. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken!
text: Le ŋitimbol mɔmɔk aanib ga yin nimi ke mpopiindam, ba pu? nimi aatiŋ ga li ye kitinyaan tii binib ke bi li koo ki ponn ni.” Uwumbɔr aah puu ke u ga san waanib kinimbaak pu na

ref: You have said horrible things about me, and yet you ask, “What have we said?”
text: Uwumbɔr ki bui ke, “Ni len tibɔbir pam m pu. Le ni baa ke, ‘Ti len ba aabɔbir aa pu?’

ref: Here is what you have said: “It's foolish to serve the Lord God All-Powerful. What do we get for obeying God and from going around looking sad?
text: Ni bui ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aadiim aa kpa tinyoor tibaa. Ti yaa ŋani waah len pu na kan, naa kpa tinyoor; ti yaa ti ki bui Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan ke tisui bii taah tun pu na pu kan, naa kpa tinyoor tibaa.

ref: See how happy those arrogant people are. Everyone who does wrong is successful, and when they put God to the test, they always get away with it.” Faithfulness Is Rewarded
text: Taah nyi pu na le ye ke bigaadam le kpa mpopiin. Titunwanbirdam kani tinyoor, le ki joo titunwanbir tɔŋni Uwumbɔr ke bi lik ke u kpa limɔr aan waa kpa, le nibaa aa ŋani bi.’”

ref: All those who truly respected the Lord and honored his name started discussing these things, and when God saw what was happening, he had their names written as a reminder in his book.
text: Le binib bi san Uwumbɔr na len tɔb chee tibɔr, le Uwumbɔr pel, le ki ŋun baah len pu na. Bi ŋmee kigbaŋ ni binib bi san Uwumbɔr ki pak u na aayimbil bilni, unimbiin ni.

ref: Then the Lord All-Powerful said: You people are precious to me, and when I come to bring justice, I will protect you, just as parents protect an obedient child.

text: Ni yaa mee mi tiwan maayimbil pu kan, m ga ŋa naah ban pu na tii nimi.” Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aah ga fuu ni pu na

text: Baah nyan lipaal na, le u bui bi, “Israel yaab, ni li nyi naah ga ŋa bijab ngbaan pu na.

ref: Later, when the people of our nation were being counted, Judas from Galilee showed up. A lot of people followed him, but he was killed, and all his followers were scattered.
text: Uja umina aayoonn aah jer na, le Galilee aatiŋ aanii ubaa nan yoor ubaa paacham, bi yin u ke Judas. U nan bi buyoonn bi nan chuun kahn binib na. Kinipaak nan dii u. Le bijab ku u mu. Waadidiliib bimɔk dii u na mu yaa.

ref: So I advise you to stay away from these men. Leave them alone. If what they are planning is something of their own doing, it will fail.
text: Nima le m tuk nimi, nyan niŋaal bijab ngbaan aabɔr ni, ki taa ŋa bi nibaa. Baah kpokl pu na, ni baah tun lituln pu na, yaa ye binibɔm aatuln kan, li ga bee yɔli.

ref: But if God is behind it, you cannot stop it anyway, unless you want to fight against God. The council members agreed with what he said,
text: Ni yaa ye Uwumbɔr aatuln kan, naan ŋmaa nyaŋ bi. Ni yaa jan bi kijaak kan, ni li nyi man, nibaakan, ni ga kan ke ni jan Uwumbɔr le kijaak.” Bi nan kii Gamaliel aah len pu na.

ref: and they called the apostles back in. They had them beaten with a whip and warned them not to speak in the name of Jesus. Then they let them go.
text: Le bi yin Yesu aakpambalb ngbaan, ke bi gir koo ni, le ki gbaa bi, ki tuk bi ke bi taa ki tuk binib Yesu aabɔr daalbaadaal, ki taa ki pur waayimbil, le ki di bi lii.

ref: The apostles left the council and were happy, because God had considered them worthy to suffer for the sake of Jesus.
text: Le Yesu aakpambalb ngbaan siir bi chee, ki nan kpa mpopiin; ba pu? Uwumbɔr pak bi ke bi ye binib bi ga ŋmaa ji inimɔɔn Yesu aayimbil pu na.

ref: Every day they spent time in the temple and in one home after another. They never stopped teaching and telling the good news that Jesus is the Messiah.
text: Idaa mɔmɔk le bi chaa Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni, ni binib do, ki ti tuk binib Uwumbɔr aabɔr ki mooni tibɔnyaan tee, ke Yesu le ye Kristo u gaa binib lir na.

ref: A lot of people were now becoming followers of the Lord. But some of the ones who spoke Greek started complaining about the ones who spoke Aramaic. They complained that the Greek-speaking widows were not given their share when the food supplies were handed out each day.
text: Binib nan gaal Yesu ki keei idaa mɔmɔk ki kpae waadidiliib pu. N‑yoonn ngbaan le Juu yaab bi len Griik aaliin na ŋulni Juu yaab bi len Juu aaliin na pu, le ki bui ke baah yakr tijikaar idaa mɔmɔk na, bi sulni baakpopiib bɔr.

ref: The twelve apostles called the whole group of followers together and said, “We should not give up preaching God's message in order to serve at tables.
text: Le Yesu aakpambalb kipiik ni bilee na yin Yesu aadidiliib mɔmɔk, ki nan bui bi, “Naa ŋan ti li yakr tijikaar ki di cha Uwumbɔr aaliin.

ref: My friends, choose seven men who are respected and wise and filled with God's Spirit. We will put them in charge of these things.
text: Nnaabitiib, nima pu na, ni nyan ni ponn ni bijab bilole bi gbiin Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan, ki kpa nlan mbamɔm, ki kpa liyimbil na, ki cha bi li ye lituln ngbaan aaninkpiib.

ref: We can spend our time praying and serving God by preaching.”
text: Tima aanimbil ga li man limeel, ni Uwumbɔr aabɔr aamoon pu la.”

ref: This suggestion pleased everyone, and they began by choosing Stephen. He had great faith and was filled with the Holy Spirit. Then they chose Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and also Nicolaus, who worshiped with the Jewish people in Antioch.
text: Yesu aakpambalb aah len pu na, le ni piir bi mɔmɔk aasui. Le bi nyan uja ubaa, bi yin u ke Stiifen, u gaa Yesu ki kii mbamɔm ki gbii Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan na. Bi nan nyan Filip, ni Prokorus, ni Nikanor, ni Timonn, ni Pamenas, ni Nikolas, u nan ye Antiok aatiŋ aanii na mu. Nikolas aa nan ye Juu aanii. U nan kpeln le ki dii Juu yaab aasan.

ref: These men were brought to the apostles. Then the apostles prayed and placed their hands on the men to show they had been chosen to do this work.
text: Le bi nyan bijab bilole bimina, ki cha bi sil Yesu aakpambalb aanimbiin ni. Le bi mee Uwumbɔr tii bi, ki di biŋaal paan bi pu.

ref: God's message spread, and many more people in Jerusalem became followers. Even a large number of priests put their faith in the Lord. Stephen Is Arrested
text: Le Uwumbɔr aabɔr nan mooni ŋipepel mɔmɔk. Le binib moo gaal Yesu ki keei, ki kpae waadidiliib pu ki wiir, Jerusalem ponn ni. Uwumbɔr aatotoorb pam mu nan gaa Yesu aabɔnyaan tee ki kii. Baah chuu Stiifen mpɔɔn pu na

ref: God gave Stephen the power to work great miracles and wonders among the people.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ter Stiifen mbamɔm, ki tii u mpɔɔn sakpen, ki cha u tun lijinjiir aatun Juu yaab aakaasisik ni.

ref: But some men from Cyrene and Alexandria were members of a group who called themselves “Free Men.” They started arguing with Stephen. Some others from Cilicia and Asia also argued with him.
text: Le Juu yaab bibaa fii ki kpak u. N‑yoonn mubaa, Juu yaab ngbaan nan ye binaagbiib, ki nan gaa bibaa. Bi nyan ni Sairene aatiŋ ni, ni Aleksandria aatiŋ ni, ni Silisia aatiŋ ni, ni Asia aatiŋ ni. Bijab ngbaan le kpak Stiifen kinikpakpak.

ref: But they were no match for Stephen, who spoke with the great wisdom that the Spirit gave him.
text: Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aah tii Stiifen nlan sakpen pu na, baa ŋmaa len ki nyaŋ u.

ref: So they talked some men into saying, “We heard Stephen say terrible things against Moses and God!”
text: Nima pu le bi tii bijab bibaa ŋimombil ke bi mɔln inyamɔn paan u. Le bijab ngbaan len ke bi ŋun u sii Moses ni Uwumbɔr.

ref: They turned the people and their leaders and the teachers of the Law of Moses against Stephen. Then they all grabbed him and dragged him in front of the council.
text: Baah len pu na, le Juu yaab, ni baaninkpiib, ni Uwumbɔr aakaal aamɔmɔkb gee liŋuul Stiifen pu. Bi dan nan chuu u mpɔɔn, ki di u siin bibɔjirb aaninkpiib aanimbiin ni,

ref: Some men agreed to tell lies about Stephen, and they said, “This man keeps on saying terrible things about this holy temple and the Law of Moses.
text: le ki joo ni binib bi ga mɔln inyamɔn paan u na. Le bi len ke, “N‑yoonn mɔmɔk uja wee bii Moses aakaal, ki seei Uwumbɔr Aadichal.

ref: We have heard him claim that Jesus from Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses gave us.”
text: Ti ŋun u len ke Yesu, u ye Nasaref aatiŋ aanii na, ga gbaa wii Uwumbɔr Aadichal ngbaan, ki kpeln Moses aah nan tii timi ikaal i mɔmɔk na.”

ref: Then all the council members stared at Stephen. They saw that his face looked like the face of an angel.
text: Le bibɔjirb aaninkpiib mɔmɔk lik Stiifen ki kan ke unimbil wɔb wiin chain ke Uwumbɔr aatuun aanimbil wɔb na.

ref: The high priest asked Stephen, “Are they telling the truth about you?”
text: Uwumbɔr aatotoorninkpel nan baa Stiifen, “Baah len pu na, ti gbii ii?”

ref: Stephen answered: Friends, listen to me. Our glorious God appeared to our ancestor Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he had moved to Haran.
text: Le Stiifen bui ke, “Ntetiib ni nnaabitiib, ni li pel man. Uwumbɔr u nyuun na nan dan tiyaaja Abraham chee. Waah nan dan u chee na, u nan laa bi Mesopotamia aatiŋ ni, kaa kee buen Harann aatiŋ ni, ke u ti kal nima.

ref: God told him, “Leave your country and your relatives and go to a land that I will show you.”
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui u, ‘Nya aado yaab aatiŋ ni, ni saanib chee, ki li cha maah ga mɔk si kitiŋ ki na ponn ni.’

ref: Then Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After his father died, Abraham came and settled in this land where you now live.
text: Nima pu le u fii Kaldii yaab aatiŋ ni, ki buen Harann aatiŋ ni, ki nan ti bi nima. Waah bi nima na, le ute kpo. Ute aah kpo na, le Uwumbɔr nyan u nima chee, ki di u dan taah bi kitiŋ ki ponn ni dandana wee na.

ref: God didn't give him any part of it, not even a square meter. But God did promise to give it to him and his family forever, even though Abraham didn't have any children.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan, Uwumbɔr aa nan tii u kitiŋ kibaa do chee na. Waa nan po tii u lisaŋ libaa. U nan puu tipuur tii u ke u ga di kitiŋ kee tii u ni uyaabitiib. N‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur tee tii u na, Abraham aa nan kee kpa ubo.

ref: God said Abraham's descendants would live for a while in a foreign land. There they would be slaves and would be mistreated
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui u, ‘Aayaabitiib ga li ye bicham kitiyayaŋ ponn ni. Kitiŋ ngbaan aanib ga di bi ŋa binaagbiib, ki ŋa bi bakaa ŋibin ikui inaa.

ref: But he also said, “I will punish the nation that makes them slaves. Then later they will come and worship me in this place.”
text: Kitiŋ ngbaan aanib aah ga di bi ŋa binaagbiib na, le m ga daa bitafal. N‑yoonn ngbaan le aayaabitiib ga nya kitiŋ ngbaan ni, ki dan kitiŋ kee ponn ni, ki nan li dooni mi do chee na.’

ref: God said to Abraham, “Every son in each family must be circumcised to show you have kept your agreement with me.” So when Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him. Later, Isaac circumcised his son Jacob, and Jacob circumcised his twelve sons.
text: Le Uwumbɔr puu tipuur tii Abraham, ki tii u nkaal, ke u ni uyaabitiib mɔmɔk gii ŋichakpan, aan ni mɔk ke bi kii uma Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ti na. Le Abraham ma ubijabo, ki yin u ke Aisak, le ki gii uchakpaln, u nan laa ye iwiin iniin aabo la. Le Aisak ma waabo Jakob. Jakob mu ma japɔtiib kipiik ni bilee bi ye tiyaajaninkpiib na. Le bi mɔmɔk gii ŋichakpan.

ref: These men were our ancestors. Joseph was also one of our famous ancestors. His brothers were jealous of him and sold him as a slave to be taken to Egypt. But God was with him
text: “Le Jakob aajapɔtiib nan kpa lipiipoln binaal Josef pu, ki di u kooh binib pu, u li ye unaagbiija kitiŋ kibaa ponn ni, bi yin ki ke Ijipt. Le Uwumbɔr mu nan bi u chee,

ref: and rescued him from all his troubles. God made him so wise that the Egyptian king Pharaoh thought highly of him. The king even made Joseph governor over Egypt and put him in charge of everything he owned.
text: ki ter u, ki nyan u waafalaa mɔmɔk ponn ni. N‑yoonn ngbaan Faro nan ye Ijipt aatiŋ aabɔr. Le Uwumbɔr tii Josef nlan, ki cha Faro gee waabɔr. Le Faro di u ŋa kitiŋ ngbaan aayidaan, ni waachiln aayidaan.

ref: Everywhere in Egypt and Canaan the grain crops failed. There was terrible suffering, and our ancestors could not find enough to eat.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le nkon lir Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ni Kanaann aatiŋ ni. Binib nan kan falaa sakpen. Tiyaajatiib nan bi Kanaann aatiŋ ni. Baa nan kan tijikaar.

ref: But when Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he sent our ancestors there for the first time.
text: Le bite Jakob ŋun ke tijikaar bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni. Nima pu na, u nan cha ujapɔtiib buen nima chee bi ti daa tijikaar. Le bi buen ti daa, ki gir ni, ki ki buen lelee.

ref: It was on their second trip that Joseph told his brothers who he was, and the king learned about Joseph's family.
text: Baah buen lelee na, le Josef ti di ubaa mɔk bi, le ki di waamaal mu mɔk Ubɔr Faro,

ref: His father went to Egypt and died there, just as our ancestors did.
text: Le bi mɔmɔk buen u chee Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki nan bi nima kina ki ti kpo.

ref: Later their bodies were taken back to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor.
text: Baah kpo na, le bi yoor bi ki di dan Sekem aatiŋ ki bi do chee na ni, ki ti di bi sub. Bi nan sub bi nfal mu Abraham nan di ŋimombil daa Hamor yaab chee na ponn ni la.

ref: Finally, the time came for God to do what he had promised Abraham. By then the number of our people in Egypt had greatly increased.
text: “Tɔ, Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur tii Abraham. Le n‑yoonn mu u ga ŋa waah puu tipuur ti na peen ni. N‑yoonn ngbaan le Israel yaab too pɔr kpee Ijipt aatiŋ ni.

ref: Another king was ruling Egypt, and he didn't know anything about Joseph.
text: Ni nan yunn pam, le ubɔrkpaan u kaa nan nyi Josef aabɔr na jin nnaan Ijipt aatiŋ ni.

ref: He tricked our ancestors and was cruel to them. He even made them leave their babies outside, so they would die.
text: Le u nan ŋmanni tiyaajatiib ki ŋani bi bakaa, le ki tuk waanib ke bi di tiyaajatiib aabim mee timoor ni aan bi kpo.

ref: During this time Moses was born. He was a very beautiful child, and for three months his parents took care of him in their home.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le bi ma Moses, u nan ye ubo u ŋan sakpen na la. Le bi kpiin u ute do iŋmal itaa.

ref: Then when they were forced to leave him outside, the king's daughter found him and raised him as her own son.
text: Waah ŋa iŋmal itaa aabo na, le bi di u bil timoor ni. Le Faro aabisal ti kan u, ki yoor u, ki kpiin u, ki di u ŋa waabo.

ref: Moses was given the best education in Egypt. He was a strong man and a powerful speaker.
text: Le bi mɔk u Ijipt yaab aalan aabɔŋ aabɔŋ. Le u kpaln unii u nyi tibɔr na, ki tun lituln li kpa liyimbil na.

ref: One day he saw an Egyptian mistreating one of them. So he rescued the man and killed the Egyptian.
text: Le u mann bi, ki kan Ijipt aanii ubaa ŋa Israel aanii ubaa bakaa. Le u buen ti ter Israel yaab aanii ngbaan, ki gbaa Ijipt aanii ngbaan teen ki ku u.

ref: Moses thought the rest of his people would realize God was going to use him to set them free. But they didn't understand.
text: U nan dakl ke unaabitiib ga bee ke Uwumbɔr ga cha u nyan bi baadim aaŋaal ni. Le baa bee.

ref: The next day Moses saw two of his own people fighting, and he tried to make them stop. He said, “Men, you are both Israelites. Why are you so cruel to each other?”
text: Le ni woln le u ti kan Israel yaab bilee bi jaa. U nan ban ke u par bi, le ki bui bi, ‘Njɔtiib, ni ye naabitiib la. Ba ŋa ni ŋani tɔb bakaa?’

ref: But the man who had started the fight pushed Moses aside and asked, “Who made you our ruler and judge?
text: Le unii u ŋa uŋeen aatɔ bakaa na nan tur Moses foor bibaa chee, ki bui u, ‘Ŋma ŋa si timi aayidaan ni ubɔjir?

ref: Are you going to kill me, just as you killed that Egyptian yesterday?”
text: Aa ban ke aa ku mi ke saah fe ku Ijipt aaja na pu na la aa?’

ref: When Moses heard this, he ran away to live in the country of Midian. His two sons were born there.
text: Waah len kina na, le Moses san nyan Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki buen Midiann aatiŋ ni, ki nan ti ye uchaan nima. Le upuu ma mbijabim bilee nima.

ref: Moses was surprised by what he saw. He went closer to get a better look, and the Lord said,
text: Moses aah kan ni na, le ni gar u pam. Le u foor mal mmii ngbaan u ti lik. Waah foor mal mu na, le u ŋun Uwumbɔr aaneel len ke,

ref: “I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses started shaking all over and didn't dare to look at the bush.
text: ‘Min le ye aayaajatiib Abraham, ni Aisak, ni Jakob Aawumbɔr.’ Ijawaan chuu Moses, le uwon gbaa. Waa ki kaa u ki lik.

ref: The Lord said to him, “Take off your sandals, because the place where you are standing is holy.
text: Le Uwumbɔr bui u, ‘Saah si nin chee na ye kitiŋ ki bi chain na la. Chuu takl saanaatak ngbaan.

ref: With my own eyes I have seen the suffering of my people in Egypt. I have heard their groans and have come down to rescue them. Now I am sending you back to Egypt.”
text: M kan maanib Israel yaab aah bi ji falaa sakpen Ijipt aatiŋ yaab aaŋaal ponn ni pu na, ki ŋun baah wii pu na, le m sunn ni ke m nan gaa bi lii. Li pel, m ga tun si Ijipt aatiŋ ni, aa ti nyan bi nima chee.’

ref: This was the same Moses that the people rejected by saying, “Who made you our leader and judge?” God's angel had spoken to Moses from the bush. And God had even sent the angel to help Moses rescue the people and be their leader.
text: “Tɔ, Moses le ye unii u Israel yaab nan yii u, ki bui u ke, ‘Ŋma ŋa si timi aayidaan ni ubɔjir?’ Uma le Uwumbɔr nan tun waatuun u chee, busub bu bi ke bu aah gaal mmii le na pu, u ti tuk u ke u buen ti nyan ni waanib tinaagbiir ni, ki li joo ni bi.

ref: In Egypt and at the Red Sea and in the desert, Moses rescued the people by working miracles and wonders for
text: Uma Moses le nyan bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki tun lijinjiir aatun nima chee, ni Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem ni, le ki ti nin tun lijinjiir aatun timoor ni, ŋibin imonko ilee.

ref: Moses is the one who told the people of Israel, “God will choose one of your people to be a prophet, just as he chose me.”
text: Uma Moses le tuk Israel yaab, ‘Uwumbɔr ga tun ni ubɔnabr ubaa ni chee, ke waah tun ni mi pu na. U mu ga li ye ninaabitiib ponn ni ubaa la.’

ref: Moses brought our people together in the desert, and the angel spoke to him on Mount Sinai. There he was given these life-giving words to pass on to us.
text: Uma Moses, ni tiyaajatiib, ni Uwumbɔr aatuun nan bi nteersakpiin ni, Sainai aajool chee, le Uwumbɔr aatuun len u chee tibɔr lijool ngbaan paab, ki tuk u limɔfal aabɔr ke u nan tuk timi.

ref: But our ancestors refused to obey Moses. They rejected him and wanted to go back to Egypt.
text: “Le tiyaajatiib aa gee ke bi kii waamɔb. Bi yii u, ki ban ke bi ki labr buen Ijipt aatiŋ ni,

ref: Then they made an idol in the shape of a calf. They offered sacrifices to the idol and were pleased with what they had done.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le bi di salmaa mɔɔ unaabo, le ki toor kitork tii u. Baah mɔɔ unaabo ngbaan na, le bi jin njim ki mɔɔni sakpen.

ref: God turned his back on his people and left them. Then they worshiped the stars in the sky, just as it says in the Book of the Prophets, “People of Israel, you didn't offer sacrifices and offerings to me during those
text: Le Uwumbɔr daak bi chee, le ki siir cha bi, le bi dooni ŋiŋmabil ŋi bi kitaapaak na. Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr nan ŋmee tibɔr ngbaan Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni, ke Uwumbɔr len ke, ‘Israel yaab, ni nan kɔr tiwakor ki toor kitork ŋibin imonko ilee timoor ni. Naah toor kitork na, ni toor tii min aa? Aayii.

ref: Instead, you carried the tent where the god Molech is worshiped, and you took along the star of your god Rephan. You made those idols and worshiped them. So now I will have you carried off beyond Babylonia.”
text: Ni nan yoor liwaal li bi yin li ke Molek na aabool, ni liwaal Refann li ye liŋmabil aanaŋ na. Ni nan mɔɔ ŋiwaa ŋimina, ke ni li dooni ŋi. Nima pu na, m ga di nimi buen tinaagbiir ni, kitiŋ ki bi Babiloŋ aatiŋ aapuwɔb na ni.’

ref: The tent where our ancestors worshiped God was with them in the desert. This was the same tent that God had commanded Moses to make. And it was made like the model that Moses had seen.
text: “Tɔ, tiyaajatiib nan joo ngban aabool timoor ni. Uwumbɔr nan joo ubaa mɔk bi libool ngbaan ponn ni la. U nan tuk Moses waah ga ŋa pu ki ŋa libool ngbaan na. Le Moses ŋa li Uwumbɔr aah mɔk u pu na.

ref: Later it was given to our ancestors, and they took it with them when they went with Joshua. They carried the tent along as they took over the land from those people that God had chased out for them. Our ancestors used this tent until the time of King David.
text: Tiyaajatiib nan di libool ngbaan tii baabim. Baabim ni baayidaan Josua mu nan yoor libool ngbaan, le ki buen bi ti gaa kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr jenn binib nima na. Le libool ngbaan nan bi nima, ki ti saa Ubɔr David aayoonn.

ref: He pleased God and asked him if he could build a house of worship for the people of Israel.
text: Uwumbɔr nan gee Ubɔr David. Le David nan ban ke u maa lidichal tii Uwumbɔr, u nan ye uyaaja Jakob Aawumbɔr na. David mu aa nan maa lidichal tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: And it was finally King Solomon who built a house for God.
text: Ujapɔɔn Solomonn le nan maa lidichal tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: But the Most High God doesn't live in houses made by humans. It is just as the prophet said, when he spoke for the Lord,
text: “Tɔ, Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aa bi binib aah maa ŋidichal ŋi na ponn ni baanja. Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr nan len ke Uwumbɔr len ke,

ref: “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build for me? In what place will I rest?
text: ‘Kitaapaak le ye maabɔrjal, le kitiŋ ye ntaa aah taa ni pu na: ni ga maa ba aadichal aaboln ki tii mi? Ba aapaan ni ga kan tii mi aan m li koo nima?

ref: I have made everything.”
text: Min mbaa le nan naan tiwan nimina mɔmɔk.’”

ref: You stubborn and hardheaded people! You are always fighting against the Holy Spirit, just as your ancestors did.
text: Tɔ, Stiifen nan ki len ke, “Nitafal pɔɔ, naa dii Uwumbɔr aasan nisui ni, kaa pel waaliin. N‑yoonn mɔmɔk ni ban ni yii Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan, ke niyaajatiib aah nan yii mu pu na.

ref: Is there one prophet that your ancestors didn't mistreat? They killed the prophets who told about the coming of the One Who Obeys God. And now you have turned against him and killed him.
text: Niyaajatiib nan muk Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib mɔmɔk, le ki ku binib bi tuk bi ke Uwumbɔr Aatutunyaan ga dan na. U fuu ni, le ni kooh u, ki ku u.

ref: Angels gave you God's Law, but you still don't obey it. Stephen Is Stoned to Death
text: Uwumbɔr nan tun ni waatuuntiib bi nan tii nimi waakaal. Le ni yii, kaa kii nkaal ngbaan.” Baah mae Stiifen ŋitakpal ki ku u pu na

ref: When the council members heard Stephen's speech, they were angry and furious.
text: Stiifen aah len kina na, le liŋuul chuu binib ngbaan, le bi ŋmɔ ŋinyin.

ref: But Stephen was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked toward heaven, where he saw our glorious God and Jesus standing at his right side.
text: Le Stiifen u Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan gbii u na, waan lik paacham, le ki kan Uwumbɔr aah wiin chain pu na, le ki kan Yesu si uŋangii wɔb.

ref: Then Stephen said, “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right side of God!”
text: Le u bui ke, “Lik, m kan kitaapaak chuu piir, ki kan Unibɔn Aabo na si Uwumbɔr aaŋangii wɔb.”

ref: The council members shouted and covered their ears. At once they all attacked Stephen
text: Waah len kina na, le bi teen mpɔɔn pu, ki di biŋaal ŋeeb bitafal, le ki kpaan ber bi ti chuu u,

ref: and dragged him out of the city. Then they started throwing stones at him. The men who had brought charges against him put their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
text: ki nyan u kitiŋ ponn ni, ki di buen n‑gbaan, ki ti mae u ŋitakpal. Le biseeraadam ngbaan chuu peer baabɔkul, ki di bil unachipɔɔn ubaa chee, bi yin u ke Sɔɔl.

ref: As Stephen was being stoned to death, he called out, “Lord Jesus, please welcome me!”
text: Le bi mae Stiifen ŋitakpal u ti kpo. Baah bi mae u ŋitakpal na, le u mee Tidindaan ke, “Tidindaan Yesu, gaa maawiin,”

text: Le Herod siin nwiin mundaln bi ga kuun tɔb na. Liyaadaal le u di waabɔrkekeln peen, ki kal waabɔrjal pu, le ki len bi chee tibɔr.

ref: The people shouted, “You speak more like a god than a man!”
text: Waah len tibɔr pu na, le bi mɔmɔk tar ke, “Ni ye Uwumbɔr aaneel la, naa ye unibɔn.”

ref: At once an angel from the Lord struck him down because he took the honor that belonged to God. Later, Herod was eaten by worms and died.
text: Tɔ, libuul ngbaan ni le Tidindaan aatuun cha iween chuu u; ba pu? waa tii Uwumbɔr lisil. Le ŋikpaambil ŋman u, le u kpo.

ref: And after Barnabas and Saul had done the work they were sent to do, they went back to Jerusalem with John, whose other name was Mark.
text: Banabas ni Sɔɔl ma kan, baah nan di ŋimombil tii Yesu aanib aaninkpiib na, le bi di Jɔnn Mak nyan Jerusalem ni, ki labr buen Antiok aatiŋ ni.

ref: While they were worshiping the Lord and going without eating, the Holy Spirit told them, “Appoint Barnabas and Saul to do the work for which I have chosen them.”
text: Le bi mɔmɔk dooni Uwumbɔr ki lul bumɔb. Baah ŋani kina na, le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan tuk bi ke bi nya Banabas ni Sɔɔl bi ti tun waah siin bi lituln li na.

ref: Everyone prayed and went without eating for a while longer. Next, they placed their hands on Barnabas and Saul to show that they had been appointed to do this work. Then everyone sent them on their way. Barnabas and Saul in Cyprus
text: Le Yesu aanib lul bumɔb, ki mee Uwumbɔr, ki di biŋaal paan bi pu, le ki cha bi buen. Banabas ni Sɔɔl aah ŋa pu Saiprus aatiŋ ni na

ref: After Barnabas and Saul had been sent by the Holy Spirit, they went to Seleucia. From there they sailed to the island of Cyprus.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aah tun Banabas ni Sɔɔl pu na, le bi buen, ki ti fuu kitiŋ kibaa ni, bi yin ki ke Selusia, le ki koo buŋɔb ni, ki puur ki ti fuu lidikl pu, bi yin lidikl ngbaan ke Saiprus,

ref: Barnabas and Saul went all the way to the city of Paphos on the other end of the island, where they met a Jewish man named Bar-Jesus. He practiced witchcraft and was a false prophet.
text: Le bi ki buen lidikl ngbaan aapepel liken wɔb, ki ti fuu kitiŋ kibaa ni, bi yin ki ke Pafos. Baah ti fuu nima na, le bi kan ubɔɔ ubaa, bi yin u ke Bariyesu. U nan ye Juu yaab aanii le ki ŋmann ke u ye Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr la.

ref: He also worked for Sergius Paulus, who was very smart and was the governor of the island. Sergius Paulus wanted to hear God's message, and he sent for Barnabas and Saul.
text: Lidikl ngbaan aatim aaninkpel mu nan bi nima, bi yin u ke Sejius Pɔɔlus. U nan ye unii u kpa nlan na la. Ubɔɔ ngbaan aajɔ le nan bi na. Le uninkpel ngbaan yin Banabas ni Sɔɔl ke bi dan u chee, ki ban u ŋun Uwumbɔr aabɔr.

ref: But Bar-Jesus, whose other name was Elymas, was against them. He even tried to keep the governor from having faith in the Lord.
text: Ubɔɔ ngbaan aayimbil leler nan ye Elimas la. Elimas aatataa le ye ke ubɔɔ. Le u kpak Banabas ni Sɔɔl kinikpakpak, ki pɔɔni ubaa ke uninkpel ngbaan taa gaa Yesu ki kii.

ref: Then Saul, better known as Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
text: Le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan fir Sɔɔl, u bi duln u ke Pɔɔl na pu, le u lik Elimas mbamɔm,

ref: and said, “You son of the devil! You are a liar, a crook, and an enemy of everything that is right. When will you stop speaking against the true ways of the Lord?
text: le ki bui u, “Sin u ye kinimbɔŋ aajapɔɔn na, aa ye litunyaan mɔmɔk aadin la, ki ŋmanni binib n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki kpa mbiin sakpen, ki ban aa bii Tidindaan aasan mu tok na.

ref: The Lord is going to punish you by making you completely blind for a while.” Suddenly the man's eyes were covered by a dark mist, and he went around trying to get someone to lead him by the hand.
text: Uwumbɔr ga daa aatafal, ki cha aa jɔb, kaan ki li waa, ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu Uwumbɔr gee na.” Libuul ngbaan ni le likpakpal bɔmbɔln biin unimbil pu, le u jɔb, ki chuun mann gonni ki ban unii u ga chuu uŋaal ki dar u na.

ref: When the governor saw what had happened, he was amazed at this teaching about the Lord. So he put his faith in the Lord. Paul and Barnabas in Antioch of Pisidia
text: Uninkpel ngbaan aah kan kina, ki bae Tidindaan aah bi pu na, le ni gar u pam. Le u gaa Yesu ki kii. Pɔɔl aah moon Uwumbɔr aabɔr Antiok aatiŋ ni pu na

ref: The rest of them went on from Perga to Antioch in Pisidia. Then on the Sabbath they went to the synagogue and sat down.
text: Le bi nyan Pega aatiŋ ni, ki buen ti fuu Antiok aatiŋ ki bi Pisidia aapepel ni na. Juu yaab aakpaakool daal, le bi koo kal mmeen aadiik ni.

ref: After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the leaders sent someone over to tell Paul and Barnabas, “Friends, if you have anything to say that will help the people, please say it.”
text: Le unii ubaa karn Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni. U karn Moses ni Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib aah nan ŋmee pu na. Waah karn doo na, le mmeen aadiik aaninkpiib tun unii bi chee, ke u ti tuk bi ke bi yaa ban bi tuk binib tibɔr ti ga pɔɔk bitaakpab na kan, bi tuk bi.

ref: Paul got up. He motioned with his hand and said: People of Israel, and everyone else who worships God, listen!
text: Le Pɔɔl fii sil ki yoor uŋaal ki len ke, “Israel yaab, ni nimi bi kaa ye Israel yaab ki pak Uwumbɔr na, li pel man:

ref: The God of Israel chose our ancestors, and he let our people prosper while they were living in Egypt. Then with his mighty power he led them out,
text: Timi Israel yaab Aawumbɔr nan nyan tiyaajatiib. Bi nan ye bicham le Ijipt aatiŋ ni. Baah bi nima na, le Uwumbɔr ter bi, ki cha bi pɔr. Le Uwumbɔr nyan bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni, ki mɔk Ijipt aatiŋ aanib waapɔɔn sakpiin.

ref: Later, God removed Saul and let David rule in his place. God said about him, “David the son of Jesse is the kind of person who pleases me most! He does everything I want him to do.”
text: Nee aapuwɔb le Uwumbɔr nyan u bi chee, ki di David ŋa baabɔr, ki len ke, ‘David u ye Jese aajapɔɔn na bi maah gee pu na. U ga li ŋani maah gee pu na mɔmɔk.’

ref: God promised that someone from David's family would come to save the people of Israel, and this one is Jesus.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur ke u ga tun unii Israel yaab chee, ke u gaa bi lii. Yesu le u tun ni u bi chee, ke u gaa bi lii. Uma le ye Ubɔr David aayaabil ubaa.

ref: Then, when John's work was almost done, he said, “Who do you people think I am? Do you think I am the Promised One? He will come later, and I am not good enough to untie his sandals.”
text: Jɔnn aah kaa nan kee tun waatuln doo na, le u baa bi, ‘Ni dak ke m ye ŋma? Maa ye Kristo u ga gaa binib lii na. Uma le paan ni mpuwɔb. Maa ŋeer m chuu gbiln waanaatak aaŋmin.’”

ref: Now listen, you descendants of Abraham! Pay attention, all of you Gentiles who are here to worship God! Listen to this message about how to be saved, because it is for everyone.
text: Tɔ, Pɔɔl nan ki bui bi, “Nnaabitiib, Abraham aayaabitiib, ni binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab ki pak Uwumbɔr na, timi chee le Uwumbɔr nan tun ni tibɔnyaan ke u ga gaa timi lii.

ref: The people of Jerusalem and their leaders didn't realize who Jesus was. And they didn't understand the words of the prophets they read each Sabbath. So they condemned Jesus just as the prophets had said.
text: Binib bi bi Jerusalem ni na, ni baaninkpiib aa nyi ke Yesu le ga gaa bi lii. Likpaakool mɔmɔk daal, bi karni Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni, Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib aah nan len pu na, kaa bee naatataa. Le bi jin Yesu tibɔr ki len ke waabɔr bii. Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib nan len ke bi ga ŋa kina.

ref: They did exactly what the Scriptures said they would. Even though they couldn't find any reason to put Jesus to death, they still asked Pilate to have him killed. After Jesus had been put to death, he was taken down from the cross and placed in a tomb.
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni baah ga nan ŋa Yesu pu ki ku u na. Le bi nan ŋani naah ŋmee pu na mɔmɔk, le ki nyan u ndɔpuinkoo pu, ki di u sub kitakpaluŋ ni.

ref: But God raised him from death!
text: Le Uwumbɔr fikr u nkun ni.

ref: Then for many days Jesus appeared to his followers who had gone with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. Now they are telling our people about him.
text: Le u di ubaa mɔk binib bi nan dii u Galilee ki nan saa Jerusalem na. Le bi kan u iwiin pam. Dandana wee, bima le ye waaseeraadam, ki tuk Juu yaab waabɔr.

ref: When David was alive, he obeyed God. Then after he died, he was buried in the family grave, and his body decayed.
text: Ubɔr David aah nan bi na, u nan tun Uwumbɔr aatuln, le ki ti kpo. Le bi sub u uyaajatiib chee, le u bur.

ref: But God raised Jesus from death, and his body did not decay.
text: Yesu u Uwumbɔr fikr u nkun ni na, uma aawon aa bur.

ref: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to say more about these same things on the next Sabbath.
text: Pɔɔl aah len doo na, le u ni Banabas nyan ni mmeen aadiik ni. Baah nyan ni na, le binib bui bi ke likpaakool li choo na daal bi ki gir ni, ki nan ki tuk bi tibɔr ngbaan.

ref: After the service, many Jews and a lot of Gentiles who worshiped God went with them. Paul and Barnabas begged them all to remain faithful to God, who had treated them with undeserved grace.
text: Binib mɔmɔk aah nyan mmeen aadiik ni na, le Juu yaab, ni binib bi nan kpeln ki dii Juu yaab aasan na pam nan dii Pɔɔl ni Banabas. Le Pɔɔl ni Banabas len bi chee ki tuk bi ke Uwumbɔr aah san bi kinimbaak pu na, bi li beenin dii waasan.

ref: The next Sabbath almost everyone in town came to hear the message about the Lord.
text: Tɔ, likpaakool li paan ni na daal, le binib bimɔk bi kitiŋ ngbaan ni na nan kuun ni bi nan ŋun Tidindaan aabɔr. Ubaabaa baanja le nan gur linampal.

ref: When the Jewish people saw the crowds, they were very jealous. They insulted Paul and spoke against everything he said.
text: Juu yaab aah kan kinipaak ngbaan kuun kina na, le bi kpa lipiipoln sakpen, ki kpak Pɔɔl kinikpakpak, ki seei u.

ref: But Paul and Barnabas bravely said: We had to tell God's message to you before we told it to anyone else. But you rejected the message! This proves that you don't deserve eternal life. Now we are going to the Gentiles.
text: Le Pɔɔl ni Banabas kpa lipobil ki bui Juu yaab ngbaan, “Ni ŋan ke ti puen tuk nimi Uwumbɔr aabɔr. Le ni yii, kaa kii, kaa dak ke ni ŋeer ni kan limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na. Kina pu na, ti ga di cha nimi, ki tuk binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na Uwumbɔr aabɔr.

ref: The Lord has given us this command, “I have placed you here as a light for the Gentiles. You are to take the saving power of God to people everywhere on earth.”
text: Uwumbɔr tuk timi waagbaŋ ponn ni ke ti ŋa kina. U nan len ke, ‘M nyan si la, ke aa woln binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aanimbil, ki tii dulnyaa wee ni aanib mɔmɔk nsan ke bi ŋmar.’”

ref: This message made the Gentiles glad, and they praised what they had heard about the Lord. Everyone who had been chosen for eternal life then put their faith in the Lord.
text: Tɔ, binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aah ŋun baah len pu na, le bi kpa mpopiin sakpen, le ki bui ke Uwumbɔr aabɔr ŋan sakpen a. Le binib bi Uwumbɔr nyan bi ke bi kan limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na gaa Yesu ki kii.

ref: The message about the Lord spread all over this region.
text: Le Uwumbɔr aabɔr moon itingbaan mɔmɔk ni.

ref: But the Jewish leaders went to some of the important men in the town and to some respected women who were religious. They turned them against Paul and Barnabas and started making trouble for them. They even chased them out of this part of the country.
text: Le bipiib bi kpa mpɔɔn ki pak Uwumbɔr na bi kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni. Kitiŋ ngbaan aaninkpiib mu nan bi. Le Juu yaab ŋa, ki cha bi ŋma tijar Pɔɔl ni Banabas pu, ki ŋa bi falaa, ki nyan bi baatiŋ ni.

ref: Paul and Barnabas shook the dust from that place off their feet and went on to the city of Iconium.
text: Le Pɔɔl ni Banabas kpaar bitaa aatatan lii nima, ni ye nsurm le ki tii bi, ki nyan ni nima, ki buen kitiŋ kibaa ni, bi yin ki ke Ikonium.

ref: But the Lord's followers in Antioch were very happy and were filled with the Holy Spirit.
text: Le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan gbiin binib bi gaa Yesu ki kii Antiok aatiŋ ni na. Le bi nan kpa mpopiin pam.

ref: Paul and Barnabas spoke in the synagogue in Iconium, just as they had done at Antioch, and many Jews and Gentiles put their faith in the Lord.
text: Pɔɔl ni Banabas nan ti fuu Ikonium aatiŋ ni, ki koo mmeen aadiik ni, ki kpa mpɔɔn ki tuk binib Uwumbɔr aabɔr. Nima pu na, binib pam nan gaa Yesu ki kii, bi ye Juu yaab, ni bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu.

ref: But the Jews who did not have faith in him made the other Gentiles angry and turned them against the Lord's followers.
text: Le Juu yaab bibaa yii Uwumbɔr aabɔr, ki bii Yesu aanib, ki cha binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na bibaa gee liŋuul bi pu.

ref: Paul and Barnabas stayed there for a while, having faith in the Lord and bravely speaking his message. The Lord gave them the power to work miracles and wonders, and he showed that their message about his gift of undeserved grace was true.
text: Le Pɔɔl ni Banabas nan bi nima ki yunn, ki nan kpa lipobil ki tuk binib Tidindaan aabɔr, ke u gee bi. Le Tidindaan cha bi tun lijinjiir aatun, ki mɔk ke baah len pu na, ti gbii.

ref: The people of Iconium did not know what to think. Some of them believed the Jewish group, and others believed the apostles.
text: Le kitiŋ ngbaan aanib aa kpa kimɔbaan. Bibaa nan si Juu yaab aapuwɔb, biken mu si Yesu aakpambalb aapuwɔb.

ref: Finally, some Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, decided to make trouble for Paul and Barnabas and to stone them to death.
text: Le Juu yaab ni baaninkpiib, ni binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na bibaa kpokl ke bi ga ŋa Yesu aakpambalb bakaa ki mae bi ŋitakpal.

ref: In Lystra there was a man who had been born with paralyzed feet and had never been able to walk.
text: Uja ubaa nan bi Listra aatiŋ ni, le utaafar faan. Una aah nan ma u na, u nan ye uwɔb la. Waa nan chuun.

ref: The man was listening to Paul speak, when Paul saw that he had faith in Jesus and could be healed. So he looked straight at the man
text: U nan ka pel Pɔɔl aah len pu na, le Pɔɔl bee ke u gaa Yesu ki kii, nima le u ga ŋmaa tii u laafee. Le Pɔɔl lik u sulm,

ref: and shouted, “Stand up!” The man jumped up and started walking around.
text: ki len mpɔɔn pu, “Fii sil aataa pu.” Le uja ngbaan fii yuk sil, le ki chuun gonni.

ref: When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they yelled out in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have turned into humans and have come down to us!”
text: Le kinipaak ngbaan kan Pɔɔl aah ŋa pu na. Le bi teen Likonia aatiŋ aanib aaliin ponn ni, “Ŋiwaa le kpaln binib ki dan ti chee do.”

ref: The people then gave Barnabas the name Zeus, and they gave Paul the name Hermes, because he did the talking.
text: Le bi yin Banabas ke Seus. Pɔɔl nan len tibɔr jer Banabas. Nima pu le bi yin u ke Hemes.

ref: The temple of Zeus was near the entrance to the city. Its priest and the crowds wanted to offer a sacrifice to Barnabas and Paul. So the priest brought some bulls and flowers to the city gates.
text: Liwaal Seus aadichal nan bi kitiŋ ngbaan aagoln aabisamɔb chee la. Le unii u toor kitork tii liwaal ngbaan na joo ni inaaja ni nsupuun ki di dan kitiŋ ngbaan aagoln aabisamɔb chee. U ni kinipaak ngbaan nan ban ke bi toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr aakpambalb Banabas ni Pɔɔl la.

ref: When the two apostles found out about this, they tore their clothes in horror and ran to the crowd, shouting:
text: Le Banabas ni Pɔɔl ŋun baah ban bi ŋa pu na. Baah ŋun kina na, le bi chuu kar baabɔkur, le ki san koo kinipaak ngbaan aakaasisik ni, ki tar ke,

ref: Why are you doing this? We are humans just like you. Please give up all this foolishness. Turn to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
text: “Njɔtiib, ba pu ni ŋani kina? Ti po ye binibɔm ke naah ye pu na la. Ti dan ti nan tuk nimi tibɔnyaan la. Di cha man, ki taa ki dii ŋiwaa man. Ŋi ye fam la. Ni li dii Uwumbɔr u fu na. Uma le nan naan paacham ni kitiŋ, ni nnyusakpem, ni tiwan mɔmɔk.

ref: In times past, God let each nation go its own way.
text: N‑yaayoonn na, u nan cha ŋinibol mɔmɔk ŋani baah gee pu na.

ref: But he showed he was there by the good things he did. God sends rain from heaven and makes your crops grow. He gives food to you and makes your hearts glad.
text: N‑yoonn mɔmɔk u mu ŋani nimi tiŋann, ki tii nimi utaal, ki cha tijikaar ŋani, ki kpiini nimi, ki cha ni kpa mpopiin, u mɔk nimi ke u bi.”

ref: Even after Paul and Barnabas had said all this, they could hardly keep the people from offering a sacrifice to them.
text: Le Pɔɔl ni Banabas len kina ki pɔɔni bibaa ke bi taa cha kinipaak ngbaan toor kitork ngbaan tii bi, le baa ki toor ki tii bi.

ref: Some Jewish leaders from Antioch and Iconium came and turned the crowds against Paul. They hit him with stones and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead.
text: Le Juu yaab bibaa nyan ni Antiok aatiŋ ni, ni Ikonium aatiŋ ni, ki dan Listra aatiŋ ni, bi nan bii Pɔɔl ni Banabas ki cha binib gee liŋuul bi pu. Le bi mae Pɔɔl ŋitakpal, ki dar fuul u nyan kitiŋ ni, ki ti di bil, ki dak ke u kpo, le ki siir cha u.

ref: But when the Lord's followers gathered around Paul, he stood up and went back into the city. The next day he and Barnabas went to Derbe. Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch in Syria
text: Le Yesu aadidiliib dan nan sil gob u. Baah sil gob u na, le u fii sil, ki labr buen kitiŋ ngbaan ni. Pɔɔl mam aah labr buen Antiok aatiŋ ni pu na Kitaak aah woln na, le Pɔɔl ni Banabas siir buen Debe aatiŋ ni,

ref: Paul and Barnabas preached the good news in Derbe and won some people to the Lord. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch in Pisidia.
text: ki ti tuk nima chee aanib tibɔnyaan ngbaan. Le binib pam gaa ti, ki dii Yesu aasan. Le Pɔɔl ni Banabas nyan nima ki ki labr buen Listra aatiŋ ni, ni Ikonium aatiŋ ni, ni Antiok aatiŋ ki bi Pisidia aapepel ni na.

ref: They encouraged the followers and begged them to remain faithful. They told them, “We have to suffer a lot before we can get into God's kingdom.”
text: Baah dii ntim ngbaan ni na, le bi pɔɔk Yesu aanib aataakpab, ki toor tuk bi Uwumbɔr aabɔr, le ki tuk bi ke bi sil Yesu aachaŋ ni, ke binib yaa ban bi koo Uwumbɔr aanaan ni kan, bi ga ji falaa sakpen le ki nin koo ni.

ref: Paul and Barnabas chose some leaders for each of the churches. Then they went without eating and prayed that the Lord would take good care of these leaders who had trusted in the Lord.
text: Ntim mɔmɔk ni, bi nan leer Yesu aanib ponn ni bininkpiib ke bi li joo bi, le ki lul bumɔb, ki mee Uwumbɔr tii bi. Baah gaa Tidindaan ki kii na, le bi di bi ŋa uŋaal ponn ni, ke u li lik bi.

ref: Paul and Barnabas went on through Pisidia to Pamphylia,
text: Le bi bɔ dii Pisidia aatim ponn ni, ki ti ki fuu Pamfilia aapepel ni,

ref: where they preached in the town of Perga. Then they went down to Attalia
text: le ki ti fuu Pega aatiŋ ni, ki tuk binib Yesu aabɔr, le ki buen Atalia aatiŋ ni.

ref: After arriving in Antioch, they called the church together. They told the people what God had helped them do and how he had made it possible for the Gentiles to believe.
text: Baah fuu ni na, le bi yin Yesu aanib ke bi kuun ni, le ki tuk bi tiwan nimɔk Uwumbɔr cha bi ŋa na, ki tuk bi waah ŋa pu ki tii binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na nsan ke bi gaa Yesu ki kii na.

ref: Then they stayed there with the followers for a long time.
text: Pɔɔl ni Banabas nan ti bi nima, Yesu aadidiliib chee, ki yunn.

ref: Some people came from Judea and started teaching the Lord's followers that they could not be saved, unless they were circumcised as Moses had taught.
text: Tɔ, bijab bibaa nan nyan ni Judea aatiŋ ni, ki dan Antiok aatiŋ ni, le ki nan tuk Yesu aanib ke bi yaa kaa gii ŋichakpan, Moses aakaal aah mɔk pu na kan, baan ŋmar.

ref: This caused trouble, and Paul and Barnabas argued with them about this teaching. So it was decided to send Paul and Barnabas and a few others to Jerusalem to discuss this problem with the apostles and the church leaders. The Church Leaders Meet in Jerusalem
text: Le bijab ngbaan kpak Banabas ni Pɔɔl kinikpakpak sakpen tibɔr ngbaan pu. Nima pu na, bi mɔmɔk nan kii ke bi ga tun Pɔɔl ni Banabas ni binib bibaa aan bi buen Jerusalem, ki ti baa Yesu aakpambalb ni Yesu aanib aaninkpiib bi bi nima na, ki lik.

ref: The men who were sent by the church went through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling how the Gentiles had turned to God. This news made the Lord's followers very happy.
text: Yesu aanib nan ter bi, le bi gor ki buen. Baah cha na, le bi bɔ dii Fonisia aatim ni, ni Samaria aatim ni, ke bi ti mann Yesu aanib, ki tuk bi ke binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu gaa Yesu ki kii. Le ni tii bi mɔmɔk mpopiin sakpen.

ref: When the men arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, including the apostles and the leaders. They told them everything God had helped them do.
text: Le Pɔɔl ni Banabas ti fuu Jerusalem. Baah ti fuu nima na, le Yesu aanib ni baaninkpiib ni Yesu aakpambalb doon bi ni mpopiin. Le Pɔɔl ni Banabas tuk bi tiwan nimɔk Uwumbɔr cha bi ŋa na, ki tuk bi waah ter bi pu na.

ref: But some Pharisees had become followers of the Lord. They stood up and said, “Gentiles who have faith in the Lord must be circumcised and told to obey the Law of Moses.”
text: Le Farisii yaab bibaa, bi dii Yesu na, fii sil, le ki len ke binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na yaa dii Yesu kan, ni ŋan ke bi gii ŋichakpan, ki kii Moses aakaal.

ref: The apostles and church leaders met to discuss this problem about Gentiles.
text: Le Yesu aakpambalb ni Yesu aanib aaninkpiib kuun tɔb chee, ke bi kpokl tibɔr ngbaan.

ref: They had talked it over for a long time, when Peter got up and said: My friends, you know that God decided long ago to let me be the one from your group to preach the good news to the Gentiles. God did this so they would hear and obey him.
text: Baah kpokl ki ti yunn na, le Piita fii sil ki bui ke, “Nnaabitiib, ni nyi ke n‑yoonn mu jer na Uwumbɔr nan lee mi ni ponn ni, ke m buen binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na chee, ki ti tuk bi tibɔnyaan ngbaan, aan bi ŋun ki gaa Yesu ki kii.
