text: Le bi cha Jasonn mam pan ŋimombil ke bi di bi lii. Le bi pan, le bi di bi lii. Berea aatiŋ aanib aah gaa Yesu aabɔr pu na

ref: That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue.
text: Kinyeek ngbaan le Yesu aanib cha Pɔɔl ni Sailas siir buen Berea aatiŋ ni. Baah ti fuu na, le bi buen Juu yaab aameen aadiik ni.

ref: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
text: Le binib bi bi nima na pel Pɔɔl aah len pu na. Binib ngbaan ye binib ki jer Tesalonika aatiŋ ni yaab. Le binimbil man Pɔɔl aah len pu na pu. Idaa mɔmɔk bi nan kpar Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni, ki karni ke bi lik ke ti gbii aan taa gbii.

ref: Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
text: Nima pu na, bi ponn ni pam nan gaa Yesu ki kii. Griik yaab bi nan ye bininyuum na, bijab ni bipiib, mu gaa u ki kii ki wiir.

ref: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
text: Le Juu yaab bi bi Tesalonika aatiŋ ni na ŋun ke Pɔɔl bi Berea aatiŋ ni ki bi tuk binib Uwumbɔr aabɔr. Le bi mu buen nima ki ti cha kinipaak na ŋma tijar Pɔɔl pu.

ref: At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.
text: Libuul ngbaan ni, le Yesu aanib cha Pɔɔl siir buen ki dii nsan mu cha nnyusakpem aagbaan na. Sailas ni Timoti ma nan bee Berea aatiŋ ni.

ref: While Paul was waiting in Athens, he was upset to see all the idols in the city.
text: Le Pɔɔl ti bi Atens aatiŋ ni, ki ka kii Sailas ni Timoti. Waah bi nima na, le u kan ŋiwaa pam kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni. Le ni bii usui sakpen.

ref: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
text: Likpaakool daal le u koo mmeen aadiik ni, ki tuk Juu yaab, ni binib bi pak Uwumbɔr na Yesu aabɔr. Le bi gbaa tɔb chee tibɔr ngbaan. Idaa mɔmɔk u nan chaa kinyaŋ ni, ki ti tuk binib bi bi nima na Yesu aabɔr. Le u ni bi gbaa tɔb chee tibɔr ngbaan.

ref: Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him. People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?” Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
text: Binib bibaa mu nan bi kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni. Bi yin bibaa ke Epikurus aanib, ki yin bibaa mu ke Stoik aanib. Baah ŋun Pɔɔl aah len pu na, le bibaa baa tɔb, “Ulambidaan ngbaan len kinye?” Le bibaa mu bui ke bi dak ke u len ŋiwaa yayan ŋibaa aabɔr la. Pɔɔl ma nan bi len Yesu aabɔnyaan, ke u fikr nkun ni.

ref: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
text: Bi nan yin kitiŋ ngbaan aaninkpiib ke Areopagus aanib. Le bi di Pɔɔl buen bininkpiib ngbaan chee, le ki ti bui u ke waah tuk binib tibɔchann ti na, bi ban ke u tuk bi mu, bi bee,

ref: We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
text: ke waah len pu na, ni gar bi, bi ban ke u tuk bi mu taatataa.

ref: More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new.
text: Atens aatiŋ aanib, ni bicham bi nan bi nima na, nan gee ke bi li kuun ni ki gbaa tɔb chee tibɔchann n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Nima pu le bi ban bi ŋun Pɔɔl yaar mu.

ref: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
text: Le Pɔɔl sil bikaasisik ni, ki len ke, “Atens aatiŋ aanib, m bee ke nitafal bi ŋiwaa aabɔr ni pam.

ref: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
text: M chuun nimi aatiŋ ponn ni ki kan naah dooni ŋiwaa pu na, le ki kan bi nan ŋmee ŋŋmeen naah toor kitork nin chee na. Bi ŋmee ke, ‘Taah kaa nyi Uwumbɔr u na.’ Ni dooni Uwumbɔr, ki mu aa nyi u. Waabɔr le m ban m tuk nimi dandana wee.

ref: This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.
text: Uwumbɔr nan naan dulnyaa wee, ni tiwan nimɔk bi ni ponn ni na. Uma le ye paacham ni taab Aadindaan. Waa bi liwaal aadiik ni.

ref: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
text: Waah nan naan binib na, u ban ke bi li ban u. U dak ke nibaakan bi ga baa ki ban u, ki kan u. Waa daa unii ubaa chee. U po mal timi la.

ref: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
text: Uma pu le ti fu, ki chuun, ki bi. N‑yaayoonn na, nimi aalankpalb bibaa nan len ke, ‘Ti ye Uwumbɔr aabim la.’ Baah len pu na, ti gbii.

ref: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
text: Taah ye Uwumbɔr aabim na, taa cha ti li dak ke Uwumbɔr aabimbin bi ke ŋiwaa na. Ŋiwaa po ye ŋitakpal le bi kpii ŋi, bee salmaa, bee tikunabr le bi di mɔɔ ŋi.

ref: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
text: Binib aah kaa nan kee nyi Uwumbɔr aasan buyoonn na, waa nan gar baah ŋani pu na. Dandana wee le u len ke u ban ke binib bimɔk bi dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ponn ni na kpeln baabimbin ki dii waasan.

ref: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
text: Ba pu? u siin nwiin bundaln u ga ji binib mɔmɔk tibɔr na, ki ti saa baah ŋa ki ŋeer pu na. U nyan uja u ga ji binib tibɔr na. U nan fikr uja ngbaan nkun ni, nima le ye limɔkl tii binib mɔmɔk.”

ref: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
text: Binib ngbaan aah ŋun Pɔɔl len ke Uwumbɔr fikr unii nkun ni na, le bibaa ŋani u mbɔnyun. Le bibaa mu len ke bi ban bi ki ŋun tibɔr ngbaan.

ref: When Paul left the council meeting,
text: Le Pɔɔl siir nima ki buen.

ref: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
text: Le bijab bibaa gaa Yesu ki kii, ki kpaan Pɔɔl chee. Bi yin ubaa ke Dionisius, u nan ye Areopagus aanii ubaa na. Uken mu nan ye upii u bi yin u ke Damaris na. Binib biken mu nan gaa Yesu ki kii.

ref: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
text: Pɔɔl nan siir Atens aatiŋ ni, ki di buen Korint aatiŋ ni.

ref: where he met Aquila, a Jewish man from Pontus. Not long before this, Aquila had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Emperor Claudius had ordered the Jewish people to leave Rome. Paul went to see Aquila and Priscilla
text: Waah bi nima na, le u kan Juu yaab aaja ubaa, bi yin u ke Akuila. Bi nan ma u Pontus aatiŋ ni la. Bi yin upuu ke Prisila. Bi nan bi Itali aatisakpeŋ Rom ni. Le Ubɔrkpaan Klɔdius nan siin nkaal ke Juu yaab mɔmɔk nya Rom aatiŋ ponn ni. Nima pu le Akuila ni Prisila nan nyan nima, ki dan Korint aatiŋ ni. Bi nan fuu ni naa yunn, le Pɔɔl nan ti kan bi.

ref: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
text: Uja ngbaan ni upuu nan jab igban le ki gaal ŋiboo. Baatuln le nan bi na. Pɔɔl aatuln ni baatuln kpaa la. Nima pu le u nan ti bi bido. Le bi tun lituln ngbaan tɔb chee.

ref: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
text: Le bi kpak u kinikpakpak, ki seei u. Baah ŋa kina na, le Pɔɔl chuu waakekeln gbuk ki nyan kitangbaak, ni ye nsurm le ki tii bi, le ki bui bi, “Ni yaa kaa ŋmar kan, nimi aasin ga li bi nimi nibaa aaŋaal ni la, naa ye maataani. M ga di cha nimi, ki tuk binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na le Yesu aabɔr.”

ref: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
text: Le u siir cha bi, ki buen unii ubaa do, bi yin u ke Titius Justus, u nan ye unii u pak Uwumbɔr na. Udo ni mmeen aadiik si gbɔk tɔb la.

ref: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
text: Mmeen aadiik aaninkpel u bi yin u ke Krispus na, ni waachiln ni aanib mɔmɔk gaa Tidindaan ki kii. Le Korint aatiŋ aanib pam mu ŋun Yesu aabɔr, ki gaa u ki kii. Le bi muin bi nnyun ni.

ref: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
text: Kinyeek kibaa daal, le Pɔɔl daŋ tidaŋ, le Tidindaan bui u, “Taa ki san ijawaan. Aa li beenin tuk binib tibɔnyaan ngbaan. Taa di cha.

ref: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
text: M bi aa chee. Ubaa aan ŋmaa ŋa si nibaa. Kitiŋ kee ponn ni, binib pam ye maanib la.”

ref: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
text: Kina pu na, Pɔɔl nan bi nima ki ti saa libiln libaa ni ligeln, ki tuk binib Uwumbɔr aabɔr.

ref: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
text: Korint aatiŋ nan bi Akaya aapepel ni la. Akaya ngbaan mɔmɔk aaninkpel nan ye uja u bi yin u ke Galio na. Waayoonn ngbaan le Juu yaab kuun ki nan chuu Pɔɔl, ki di u buen uma Galio aanimbiin ni,

ref: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
text: ki len ke Pɔɔl tuk bi baah ga ŋa pu ki doon Uwumbɔr na, kaa tuk bi mbamɔm, ke u bii baatiŋ aakaal la.

ref: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
text: Pɔɔl aah ban ke u len na, le Galio tuk Juu yaab, “U yaa ba ŋa bakaa ni kinimbɔŋ kibaa kan, m ba ga ji u tibɔr. U mu aa ŋa nibaa.

ref: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
text: Nimi Juu yaab, ni kpak tɔb iliin pu, ni binib aabɔr pu, ni nimi aakaal pu la. Ni bi ni chee la, naa ye maabɔr. Maan ji tibɔr ngbaan.”

ref: Then he sent them out of the court.
text: Le u jenn nyan bi bibɔjirb aadiik ni.

ref: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
text: Le bi mɔmɔk chuu mmeen aadiik aaninkpel u bi yin u ke Sosenes na, le ki gbaa u libɔjil aadiik chee. Le Galio aatafal aa nan bi ni ponn ni. Pɔɔl mam aah gir buen Antiok aatiŋ ni pu na

ref: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
text: Pɔɔl nan bi Korint aatiŋ ni ki yunn. Waah bi nima ki yunn na, le u chɔi Yesu aanib. Le u ni Prisila ni Akuila buen Senkrea aatiŋ ni. Pɔɔl aah ti bi nima na, le u kuu uyikpir lii. Ni mɔk ke waah nan puu tipuur ti tii Uwumbɔr na le na. Le bi nan ti koo buŋɔb ni, ke bi puur nnyusakpem na ki buen Siria aatim ponn ni.

ref: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
text: Le bi ti fuu Efesus aatiŋ ni, ki nyan buŋɔb na ni. Le Pɔɔl buen mmeen aadiik ni. Le u ni Juu yaab ti gbaa tɔb chee Yesu aabɔr.

ref: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
text: Le bi ban ke u yunn bi chee. Le waa kii,

ref: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
text: ki ti yunn nima siib, le ki bɔ dii Galasia aatim ni, ni Frijia aatim ni, ki mann Yesu aanib, ki pɔɔk bitaakpab. Uja u bi yin u ke Apolos na aabɔr

ref: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
text: Juu yaab aanii ubaa nan bi, bi yin u ke Apolos. Bi nan ma u Aleksandria aatiŋ ni la. Le u dan Efesus aatiŋ ni. U nan ye unii u nyi tibɔr aalem na, ki nyi tibɔr ti ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni na mbamɔm.

ref: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
text: Binib nan tuk u Tidindaan Yesu aasan aabɔr, le unimbil man tibɔr ngbaan pu. U nan len binib chee, ki tuk bi Yesu aabɔr mbamɔm. U mu aa nyi Yesu aah gbiini binib Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan pu na. U po nyi Jɔnn aah nan muini binib nnyun ni pu na la.

ref: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
text: Le Apolos koo mmeen aadiik ni, ki tuk binib Yesu aabɔr ni lipobil. Le Prisila ni Akuila ŋun waah tuk bi pu na. Baah ŋun na, le bi di u di buen bido, ki ti toor tuk u Uwumbɔr aasan aabɔr mbamɔm.

ref: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
text: N‑yoonn mu Apolos nan laa bi Korint aatiŋ ni na, le Pɔɔl bɔ dii ŋijoo aatiŋ ni, ki ti fuu Efesus aatiŋ ni. Waah ti fuu nima na, le u kan Yesu aanib bibaa.

ref: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
text: Le u baa bi, “Naah gaa Yesu ki kii na, ni gbii Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aa?” Le bi bui u, “Taa kan, ki mu aa ŋun ke Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan bi.”

ref: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
text: Le Pɔɔl bui bi, “Jɔnn nan muin binib bi kpeln baabimbin na nnyun ni, ki tuk bi ke bi gaa unii u ga paan ni upuwɔb na ki kii. Uma le bi yin u ke Yesu.”

ref: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
text: Pɔɔl aah tuk bi kina na, le bi cha u muin bi nnyun ni, Tidindaan Yesu aayimbil pu.

ref: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
text: Le u di uŋaal paan bi pu. Le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan sunn ni bi pu. Le bi len iliin yayan, le ki nabr Uwumbɔr aah len pu na.

ref: There were about twelve men in this group.
text: Bi ga nan li fuu bijab kipiik ni bilee.

ref: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
text: Le bi ponn ni bibaa aatafal pɔɔ. Baa kii tii waaliin, le ki len tibɔr ti kaa ŋan na Tidindaan aasan pu, kinipaak aanimbil ni. Kina pu le Pɔɔl siir cha bi, ki di binib bi dii Yesu aasan na buen uja u bi yin u ke Tiranus na aadisakpeŋ ki ponn ni binib ŋmaa kuun ni na. Idaa mɔmɔk le u ni binib gbaa tɔb chee Yesu aabɔr nima.

ref: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
text: Uwumbɔr nan cha Pɔɔl tun lijinjiir aatun ki ti nyaŋ. Binib aa nan kee kan kina.

ref: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
text: Le bi yoor Pɔɔl aakekengen ŋi u joo per unimbil wɔb na, ni ŋikeken ŋi u joo biini unimbiin ni na, ki ti di paan bibum pu, ni tiyayaar aah joo bi na mu pu. Baah ŋani kina na, libuul ngbaan ni le bi pɔɔk.

ref: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
text: Le tiyayaar ngbaan bui bi, “M nyi Yesu, ki nyi Pɔɔl. Nimi ma kan, ŋma ye nimi?”

ref: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
text: Le uja u tiyayaar joo u na nan chuu bi, ki gbaa lakr bi, ki gaa baawanpeenkaan ki nyaŋ bi. Le bi mɔmɔk san biŋmeen ki nyan udo.

ref: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
text: Le Efesus aatiŋ aanib bi ye Juu yaab na, ni bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mɔmɔk ŋun tibɔr ngbaan. Le ijawaan chuu bi mɔmɔk. Le bi nyuŋ Tidindaan Yesu.

ref: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
text: Le Tidindaan aaliin moo moon ŋipepel mɔmɔk, ki moo kan mpɔɔn. Binib aah ŋma tijar Efesus aatiŋ ni pu na

ref: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
text: Nee aapuwɔb, le Pɔɔl nan ban ke u bɔ dii Masedonia aatim ni, ni Akaya aatim ni, ki nin buen Jerusalem. Le u ŋa nlandak ke u yaa buen Jerusalem aatiŋ ni kan, u ga ti buen Rom aatiŋ mu ni.

ref: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan, le Efesus aatiŋ aanib ŋma tijar Tidindaan aasan pu.

ref: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
text: Unii ubaa nan bi nima, bi yin u ke Demetrius. U nan di tikunabr le mɔɔ ŋidichal waatiir ŋi bi ke liwaal li bi yin li ke Atemis na aadichal na, aan ki joo kooh binib pu. Le binib pam mu tun lituln ngbaan, ki kan tinyoor pam.

ref: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
text: Le Demetrius kuun binib bimɔk tun lituln ngbaan na, ki bui bi ke, “Njɔtiib, ni nyi ke timi aatuln kpa tinyoor pam.

ref: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
text: Pɔɔl mu bi bii timi aatuln la. Ni kan aa? Ni ŋun waah len pu na. U len ke ŋiwaa ŋi binib mɔɔ ŋi na aa ye nibaa. Binib bi bi Efesus aatiŋ ni do, ni Asia aapepel mɔmɔk ponn ni na pam pak waah len pu na, kaa ki dii ŋiwaa.

ref: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
text: U yaa beenin ŋani kina kan, u ga bii timi aatuln. Atemis, li ye liwaal sakpeln na aadichal ga bee fam. Atemis li Asia aatim aanib, ni dulnyaa ni aanib mɔmɔk dooni li na, mu ga ŋa fam, kaan ki li bi tibɔr tibaa ni.”

ref: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
text: Binib ngbaan aah ŋun kina na, le bi gee liŋuul sakpen, ki tar ke, “Atemis li ye Efesus aatiŋ aanib aawaal na ye liwaal sakpeln la.”

ref: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
text: Le kitiŋ ngbaan aanib mɔmɔk kpa kifuuk ki ŋma tijar, le ki chuu Pɔɔl aajɔtiib bilee, Gayus ni Aristakus, ki di san mala buen binib aah kuuni nin chee na, mpaan sakpiin ni. Gayus ni Aristakus nan ye Masedonia aatiŋ aanib bilee bi dii Pɔɔl waasachuln ponn ni na la.

ref: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
text: Le Pɔɔl ubaa nan ban ke u buen kinipaak na aah kuun nin chee na, u ti len bi chee. Le Yesu aanib aa cha u buen.

ref: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
text: Kitiŋ ngbaan aaninkpiib ponn ni bibaa nan ye Pɔɔl aajɔtiib la. Bi mu nan tun unii Pɔɔl chee ke u ti tuk u ke u taa buen kinipaak ngbaan aah kuun nin chee na.

ref: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
text: Kinipaak ngbaan nan kpa kifuuk sakpen; bibaa nan tar ki len tibaa, bibaa mu nan tar ki len tiken. Baa nyi budabu pu bi kuun ni nima chee na.

ref: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
text: Le Juu yaab bi nan bi nima na nan nyan uja ubaa bi yin u ke Aleksanda, ke u sil kinipaak ngbaan aanimbiin ni. Nima pu na, binib bibaa mu nan dak ke ni ye uma Aleksanda aabɔr la. Le u yoor uŋaal ki nyii bi pu, ki ban ke u tuk bi ke naa ye Juu yaab aabɔr.

ref: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
text: Kinipaak ngbaan aah bee ke u ye Juu yaab aanii na, le bi kpaan ki teen nfumbaa ke, “Atemis li ye Efesus aatiŋ aanib aawaal na ye liwaal sakpeln la.” Bi nan tar kina ki ti saa tikur tilee.

ref: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
text: Le kitiŋ ngbaan aaninkpel ubaa dan nan nyii bi pu, ke bi di cha kifuuk. Baah di cha na, le u len ke, “Efesus yaab, binib mɔmɔk nyi ke nimi Efesus yaab lik Atemis ni laadichal pu la, ki nyi ke Atemis ye liwaal sakpeln li nyan ni kitaapaak ki sunn ni kitiŋ na.

ref: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
text: Ubaa aan ŋmaa nee ke taa gbii. Sɔŋ nisui man, ki taa tun lituln fam.

ref: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
text: Nimi le joo ni bijab ngbaan do chee na. Baa sun tiwan liwaal aadichal ponn ni, kaa sii timi aawaal.

ref: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
text: Demetrius mam ni unii ubaa yaa kpa tibɔr kan, bibɔjirb bi, libɔjil daal mu bi. Cha bi buen nima ki ti len.

ref: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
text: Nimi aaninkpiib mu yin binib ki kuun bi, ke bi nan ji tibɔr. Ni yaa kpa tibɔr kpee kan, bi ga len ti mu.

ref: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
text: Ni kpa kifuuk ki ŋma tijar din. Nibaakan, timi aatiŋ aaninkpiib ga ji timi tibɔr kifuuk ngbaan pu. Nibaa aa bi ni ponn ni, ni po kpa kifuuk fam la. Bi yaa baa timi kifuuk ngbaan pu kan, taa nyi taah ga len pu na.”

ref: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
text: Waah len kina na, le u cha bi mɔmɔk siir.

ref: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
text: Kifuuk ngbaan aah ti ŋmin na, le Pɔɔl yin Yesu aanib ke bi dan u chee, ki nan len bi chee tibɔr, ki pɔɔk bitaakpab, ki chɔi bi, le ki buen Masedonia aatiŋ ni.

ref: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
text: Le u bɔ dii ntim mu bi nima na ni, ki mann Yesu aanib bi bi nima na, ki len bi chee tibɔr pam, ki pɔɔk bitaakpab, ki ti fuu Griis aatiŋ ni,

ref: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
text: ki nan bi nima ki pii iŋmal itaa, le ki ban u koo buŋɔb ni, ki buen Siria aatiŋ ni. Le u ŋun ke Juu yaab kpokl ke u yaa koo buŋɔb na ni kan, bi ga ku u. Waah ŋun kina na, le waa buen, ki len ke u ga labr jer Masedonia aatim.

ref: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
text: Le binib bibaa nan dii u. Binib bi nan dii u na aayimbil nan ye Sopata, u nan ye Berea aatiŋ aanii, ki nan ye Pirus aajapɔɔn na; ni Aristakus, ni Sekundus, bi nan ye Tesalonika aatiŋ aanib na; ni Gayus, u nan ye Debe aatiŋ aanii na; ni Tikikus, ni Trofimus, bi nan ye Asia aatiŋ aanib na; ni Timoti.

ref: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
text: Le bi mɔmɔk loln nsan ki buen Troas aatiŋ ni, ki ti kii timi nima.

ref: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
text: Likpaakool ponn ni, njan aawiin daal, le ti kuun tɔb chee ke ti nan ji Tidindaan aajikaar. Le Pɔɔl len bi chee Uwumbɔr aabɔr le kitaak ti siir. U nan ban ke kitaak yaa woln kan, u buen cha bi. Nima le cha u len bi chee tibɔr kitaak ti siir.

ref: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
text: Taah kuun paacham aadiik ni na, karyaa mam nan wiir ki ponn ni.

ref: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
text: Unachipɔɔn ubaa nan bi nima, bi yin u ke Yutikus. U nan ka kiditatar aatakolu pu, le ngeen chuu u. Pɔɔl aah bi len tibɔr ki yunn na, le u geen, ki ker lir kitiŋ. Le bi mɔmɔk nyan ni, ki sunn ti yoor u. U mu kpo a.

ref: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
text: Le Pɔɔl mu nyan ni, ki sunn buen bi chee, ki ti doon paan u pu, le ki di uŋaal kpal u, le ki bui bi, “Chuu nibaa man. Waa kpo. U bi.”

ref: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
text: Le Pɔɔl gir koo paacham aadiik ngbaan ni, ki ti jin bi chee tijikaar, ki ki len bi chee tibɔr ki yunn, hali ki ti woln kitaak. Naah woln na, le u buen cha bi.

ref: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
text: Le bi yoor unachipɔɔn ngbaan di buen udo. Waah fikr na, le bisui sɔŋ mbamɔm. Taah buen Miletus aatiŋ ni pu na

ref: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
text: Le ti loln nsan ki koo buŋɔb ni, ki puur buen Asos aatiŋ ni. Pɔɔl ma nan chuun kitiŋ, ki mu buen nima, le ti ti keln tɔb. Pɔɔl nan tuk timi ke u mu ga koo buŋɔb na ni nima.

ref: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
text: Waah ti pii timi Asos aatiŋ ni na, le ti yoor u ŋa buŋɔb na ni, le ti di buen Mitilene aatiŋ ni.

ref: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
text: Ti nan nyan nima ki nabr buen. Naah woln kitaak na, le ti fuu lidikl libaa chee, bi yin li ke Kios, ki ki woln kitaak, le ti fuu lidikl liken chee, bi yin li ke Samos, ki ki woln kitaak le ti nan fuu Miletus aatiŋ ni.

ref: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
text: Le Pɔɔl ban u fuu Jerusalem mala. U nan ban ke u pɔɔn ubaa ki fuu nima Pentekost aawiindaal. Nima pu na, waa nan ban ke u yunn Asia aatiŋ ni. Le u bui ke u ga gɔln Efesus aatiŋ, waan dii nima. Pɔɔl aah chɔi Yesu aanib aaninkpiib pu na

ref: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
text: Le Pɔɔl tun unii ke u buen Efesus aatiŋ ni ki ti yin ni Yesu aanib aaninkpiib, ke bi dan u chee Miletus aatiŋ ni.

ref: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
text: Baah fuu ni u chee na, le u bui bi, “Maah nan fuu Asia aatiŋ ni, ki nan bi ni chee na, ni nan bee maabimbin aah nan bi pu n‑yoonn ngbaan mɔmɔk na.

ref: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
text: Ni nan bee ke m sunn mbaa taab, ki tun Tidindaan aatuln ni tinyunyunn, ki kan falaa Juu yaab chee, baah kpokl n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke bi ŋa mi bakaa pu na.

ref: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
text: M buen binib aah kuuni nin chee na, ki buen nido mu, ki tuk nimi Yesu aabɔr. M tuk nimi tibɔr timɔk ga ter nimi na, kaa gur tibaa.

ref: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
text: M sur Juu yaab ni binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu, ke bi kpeln baabimbin ki dii Uwumbɔr aasan ki gaa Tidindaan Yesu ki kii.

ref: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
text: Dandana wee m kii Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aamɔb le ki cha Jerusalem ni, kaa nyi baah ga ti ŋa mi nima chee pu na.

ref: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
text: M po nyi ke ntim mɔmɔk ponn ni, Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan sur mi ke bi ga di mi ŋa kiyondiik ni, ki ŋa mi falaa.

ref: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
text: Tɔ, m yaa kpo, bee m yaa bi kan, ntafal aa bi ni ni. Tidindaan Yesu tii mi lituln, ke m tuk binib tibɔnyaan ngbaan, ke Uwumbɔr gee bi. Ntafal bi lituln ngbaan ponn ni, ke m tun li ti doo.

ref: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
text: “Maah nan bi ni chee na, m nan chuun tuk nimi Uwumbɔr aanaan aabɔr. M nyi ke ni ponn ni ubaa aan ki kan mi.

ref: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
text: Din, m tuk nimi mbamɔn la, unii ubaa ni ponn ni yaa kaa kan limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na kan, naa ye maataani.

ref: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
text: M tuk nimi Uwumbɔr aabɔr mɔmɔk, kaa gur tibaa.

ref: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
text: Ni li nyi man, ki taa cha unii ubaa ŋmann nimi. Ni li ter Yesu aanib, ki taa cha unii ubaa ŋmann bi mu. Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan nan ŋa nimi waanib aaninkpiib. Ni li joo waanib ngbaan mbamɔm. Waabo nan dan nan kpo bi pu, ke bi kpaln waanib la.

ref: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
text: M nyi ke m yaa kaa ki bi ni chee kan, binib ga dan nan bii nimi, ke ŋisapol aah chuun chur ipiih pu na.

ref: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
text: Nima pu na, ni li nyi man, ki li teer ke ŋibin ŋitaa le na, m nan bi ni chee ki sur nimi ni tinyunyunn, nwiin pu ni kinyeek.

ref: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
text: “Nnaabitiib, m di nimi ŋa Uwumbɔr aaŋaal ni, ke u li lik nimi. M tuk nimi waaliin i mɔk timi waah gee timi pu na. Waaliin ngbaan ga ter nimi, ke ni dii waasan mbamɔm. U ga di lifaal tii nimi, ni binib bimɔk bi chain na.

ref: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
text: M ni njɔtiib yaa nan ban tiwan ni na kan, min mbaa le nan tun lituln, le ki kan taah ban tiwan ni na. Nimi nibaa nyi kina.

ref: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
text: Maah tun lituln kina na, m mɔk nimi ke ni mu li tun kina, ki ter bibum, ki li teer ke Tidindaan Yesu ubaa nan len ke, ‘Uwumbɔr aanyoor bi unii u tii na pu ki jer u gaa na pu.’”

ref: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
text: Pɔɔl aah len doo na, le bi mɔmɔk gbaan bitaŋaayil pu, ki mee Uwumbɔr.

ref: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
text: Waah tuk bi ke baan ki kan u na, le ni bii bisui sakpen. Le bi cheen u buen u ti gir koo buŋɔb ngbaan ni.

ref: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
text: Tɔ, ti nan chɔi bi, le ki koo buŋɔb ngbaan ni, le ki puur ki ti fuu lidikl libaa chee, bi yin li ke Kos; ki woln kitaak, le ti fuu Rodes aatiŋ ni, ki nyan nima, ki buen Patara aatiŋ ni,

ref: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
text: le ki ti kan buŋɔb bu ga buen Fonisia aatiŋ ni na. Le ti nyan ti koo bu ponn ni, ki cha.

ref: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
text: Taah cha na, le ti jer lidikl libaa bi yin li ke Saiprus, li bi ŋŋangan wɔb na, le ki ti fuu Taya, kitiŋ ki bi Siria aatiŋ ni na. Taah ti fuu nima na, le bi ban bi bi nima ni yunn siib, bi ti nyan ŋitun.

ref: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
text: Iwiin ilole ngbaan aah jer na, le ni ŋeer ti gir koo buŋɔb na ni. Taah gir cha ti ti koo buŋɔb ni na, le bi mɔmɔk, ni bipuutiib, ni baabim cheen timi, ki nyan ni kitiŋ ngbaan ni. Le ti mɔmɔk gbaan nnyusakpem na aagbaan, ki mee Uwumbɔr,

ref: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
text: ki chɔi tɔb. Le bi gir kun. Le ti mu koo buŋɔb na ni,

ref: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
text: Ti nan bi nima ki yunn siib. Le Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr ubaa nyan ni Judea ki fuu ni ti chee nima, bi yin u ke Agabus.

ref: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
text: Le u gaa Pɔɔl aagbapapaln, ki di buu ubaa aataa ni uŋaal, ki tuk Pɔɔl ke Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan bui ke Juu yaab bi bi Jerusalem na ga nan di udaan u yeh ligbapapaln ngbaan na buu utaa ni uŋaal kina, ki di u ŋa binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aaŋaal ni.

ref: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
text: Taah ŋun kina na, le ti ni binib bi bi nima na nan gaŋ Pɔɔl ke u taa buen Jerusalem.

ref: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
text: Le Pɔɔl baa bi, “Ni ŋani ba kina, ki wii, ki bii nsui? Bi yaa ga ti buu mi Jerusalem ni, bee bi yaa ga ti ku mi nima Tidindaan Yesu pu kan, m ga buen. Maan di cha.”

ref: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
text: Taa nan ŋmaa chuu u ke u taa buen, le ki len ke, “Cha Tidindaan ŋa waah gee pu na,” le ki ŋmin, kaa ki len tibaa.

ref: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
text: Ti nan bi nima ki yunn siib, le ki gor ke ti buen Jerusalem.

ref: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
text: Le Yesu aanib bi nyan ni Siisarea aatiŋ ni na bibaa mu dii timi, ki di buen Jerusalem, uja ubaa do, ki ti koo nima. Bi nan yin u ke Menasonn, u ye Saiprus aatiŋ aanii, ki nan dii Yesu ni yunn. Pɔɔl aah buen ti mann Jems pu na

ref: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
text: Taah ti fuu Jerusalem na, Yesu aanib nan gaa timi ki nan kpa mpopiin.

ref: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
text: Naah woln kitaak na, ti ni Pɔɔl nan buen ti ti doon Jems. Yesu aanib aaninkpiib mɔmɔk mu nan bi nima.

ref: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
text: Le Pɔɔl doon bi, ki ŋeer tuk bi Uwumbɔr aah ŋa tiwan nimɔk na, binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aakaasisik ni, uma Pɔɔl aatuln pu.

ref: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
text: Baah ŋun kina na, le bi mɔmɔk nyuŋ Uwumbɔr, ki bui Pɔɔl, “Tina aabo, aa nyi ke Juu yaab ŋichur pam le gaa Yesu ki kii. Bi mɔmɔk aanimbil man Moses aakaal pu.

ref: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
text: Le bi ŋun ke aa mɔk Juu yaab bimɔk bi Biniyayam aatim ni na ke bi taa ki dii Moses aakaal, ki taa ki geei baabim aachakpan, ki taa ki dii Juu yaab aakaal.

ref: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
text: Bi ga ŋun ke aa fuu ni. Ti ga ŋa kinye?

ref: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
text: Ti ga tuk si saah ga ŋa pu na. Bijab binaa bibaa bi do. Bi nan puu tipuur tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
text: Bi ga buen Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni, bi ti ŋa bibaa chain. Aa mu li dii bi cha, ki mu ti ŋa aabaa chain, ki tii bi ŋimombil, aan bi ti daa tiwan ki nan toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr, ki kuu baayikpir. Aa yaa ŋa kina kan, binib mɔmɔk ga bee ke aa mu dii Moses aakaal. Bi ga bee ke binib bi len ke saa dii Moses aakaal na aa len mbamɔn.

ref: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
text: Tɔ, binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab ki gaa Yesu ki kii na ma kan, ti nan ŋmee kigbaŋ tii bi, ki tuk bi taah kpokl pu na, ke bi taa ki ŋmɔ kitork aanann, ki taa ki ŋmɔ nsin, ki taa ki ŋmɔ tiwan ni bi tab ku ni na, ki taa ki gɔr kidagook.”

ref: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
text: Tɔ, Pɔɔl nan kii baah tuk u pu na. Ki woln kitaak le u yoor bijab binaa ngbaan, le u ni bi ti ŋa bibaa chain. Le u koo Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni, ki ti tuk Uwumbɔr aatotoor bundaln bi ga ŋa chain doo aan ki toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr na. Iwiin ilole daal, le bi ga ŋa chain doo. Binib aah chuu Pɔɔl Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni pu na

ref: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
text: Tɔ, iwiin ilole ngbaan aa nan kee fuu, le Juu yaab bibaa, bi nyan ni Asia aatim ni na, kan Pɔɔl Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni. Le bi cha kinipaak ŋma tijar Pɔɔl pu, ki chuu u mpɔɔn, ki tar ke,

ref: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
text: “Israel yaab, ter timi man. Uja wee ye unii u buen ŋipepel mɔmɔk na, ki tuk binib mɔmɔk ke bi taa li pak timi Juu yaab, ki taa li pak Moses aakaal, ki taa li pak Uwumbɔr Aadichal. U mu joo ni binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na, ki di bi koo ni Uwumbɔr Aadichal li ye chain na ni, ki bii li.”

ref: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
text: Le kitiŋ ngbaan aanib mɔmɔk ŋma tijar, ki san kuuni tɔb chee, ki chuu Pɔɔl ki dar nyan ni u Uwumbɔr Aadichal ni. Libuul ngbaan ni le Uwumbɔr Aadichal aakikiirb piin jaaleŋ mam.

ref: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
text: Le kinipaak na pɔɔn bibaa bi gbaa ku Pɔɔl. Le unii ubaa buen Rom aatɔb aajab aapol chee, le ki tuk u ke Jerusalem aanib mɔmɔk bi ŋmɔ tijar la.

ref: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
text: Libuul ngbaan ni le upol ngbaan di butɔb aajab bibaa ni baaninkpiib, ki san buen kinipaak ngbaan chee. Baah kan butɔb aajab ngbaan ni baapol na, le bi di cha Pɔɔl, kaa ki gbaa u.

ref: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
text: Le upol ngbaan buen Pɔɔl chee, ki ti chuu u, ki tuk waajab ke bi di tikululn tilee buu u, le ki baa ke, “Ŋma ye uja wee? U ŋa kinye?”

ref: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
text: Le bibaa tar baah gee pu na, le biken mu tar baah gee pu na. Kifuuk ngbaan pu, le upol ngbaan aa ŋmaa bee budabu ŋa na. Le u tuk waajab ke bi di Pɔɔl buen butɔb aajab aadichal ni.

ref: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
text: Le bi mɔmɔk paa bipuwɔb ki tar, “Ku u man.” Pɔɔl aah len waabamɔn pu na

ref: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
text: Le bi ti fuu lidichal ngbaan aabisamɔb chee, ki ban bi koo. Le Pɔɔl bui upol ngbaan Griik aaliin ponn ni, “Cha m tuk si tibɔr tibaa.” Le upol ngbaan baa u, “Aa ŋun Griik aaliin aa?

ref: “Aren't you that Egyptian who started a riot not long ago and led
text: M nyi ke aa ye Ijipt aatiŋ aanii u nan cha kinipaak tukni timi aatiŋ aaninkpiib, ki di binikurb ŋichur ŋinaa buen nteersakpiin ni na la.”

ref: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
text: Le Pɔɔl bui u, “M ye Juu yaab aanii la. Bi nan ma mi Tasus aatiŋ ki bi Silisia aatiŋ ni na; ki ye kitiŋ ki kpa liyimbil na la. Pɔɔk aabaa ki cha m len kinipaak ngbaan chee.”

ref: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
text: Le u kii ke u len. Le Pɔɔl sil ŋibimbin paab, ki di uŋaal nyii bi pu. Baah ŋmin na, le u len bi chee bima Juu yaab aaliin ponn ni.

ref: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
text: Libuln ni utaal aayoonn yaa ti fuu ni n‑yoonn mu na kan, naa ŋan ti li bi kiloloŋ ngbaan ponn ni. Nima le ti ponn ni binib pam bui ke ni ŋan ti nyan kiloloŋ ngbaan ponn ni, ki pɔɔk tibaa ke ti fuu Fiiniks, kitiŋ ki bi Krete aadikl paab na. Kiloloŋ bi nima mu. Libuln ni utaal yaa fuu ni n‑yoonn mu na kan, ni ŋan ke timi aaŋɔb li bi ki ponn ni. Kiloloŋ ngbaan aah bi liwilir wɔb pu na, nima le libuln aan ŋmaa pii timi nima. Libupɔpɔɔl aah muk timi buŋɔb ni pu na

ref: When a gentle wind from the south started blowing, the men thought it was a good time to do what they had planned. So they pulled up the anchor, and we sailed along the coast of Crete.
text: Le libuln li kaa pɔɔ na nyan ni ŋŋangii wɔb. Le bi bui ke ni ŋeer ke ti nyan kiloloŋ ngbaan ponn ni. Le bi chuu gbiln buŋɔb na, le ki di siir. Bi nan joo bu kpak Krete aadikl ngbaan chee la.

ref: days you have been so worried that you haven't eaten a thing.
text: Naah kpee siib na, le libupɔpɔɔl nyan ni ŋŋangan wɔb ki daar choo,

ref: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
text: ki daar yeŋni buŋɔb na, ki cha bu sil. Libuln daar tooh bu la. Nima pu na, bu aa nan ŋmaa chuun. Le ti cha bu jɔnn libuln.

ref: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
text: Le ti ti fuu lidikl libaa chee, bi yin li ke Kɔda, li bi ŋŋangan wɔb. Ti nan peŋ lidikl ngbaan, le libuln aa ki pii timi ki pɔɔ. Le timi aaŋɔsakpem dar buŋɔb waatiib bubaa. Taah peŋ lidikl ngbaan na, le ti chuu yoor buŋɔb waatiib na ŋa busakpem ni.

ref: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
text: Bi nan di iŋmin gbin punn punn busakpem na. Litambol nan dɔ nnyun ni, Libia aatiŋ chee, le bi dak ke nibaakan buŋɔb na ga dii litambol ngbaan paab. Nima pu na, bi nan chuu gbiln buŋɔb aakekeln li nan bi paacham na, ki cha bu jɔnn libuln.

ref: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
text: Libuln nan beenin daar ki pɔɔ, le buŋɔb na yeŋni. Naah woln kitaak na, le bi chuu nyan ni ŋitun na ki di mee lii nnyun ni;

ref: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
text: ki ki woln kitaak, le ti chuu nyan buŋɔb aawan mu ki di lii nnyun ni.

ref: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
text: Taah nan bi bu ponn ni na, ni nan yunn le taa ŋmaa kan nwiin, kaa waa ŋiŋmabil mu, ntaalangbam pu. Libuln mu nan beenin daar, ki pɔɔ. Taa nan ki dak ke ti ga ŋmar.

ref: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
text: Tɔ, baa nan ki ji tijikaar, ni ti yunn. Baah kaa ki ji tijikaar ni yunn na, le Pɔɔl fii sil binimbiin ni, ki bui bi, “Njɔtiib, ni yaa ba pel maah nan len pu na, ki yaa kaa ba nyan ni Krete aadikl ni kan, ni ba ga li ŋan. Timi aawan aa ba ga bii.

ref: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
text: Tɔ, m gaŋ nimi la, chuu nibaa man. Ti ponn ni unii ubaa aan kpo. Buŋɔb ngbaan baanja le ga bii.

ref: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
text: M ye Uwumbɔr aanii, le ki dooni u. Kinyeek na, le waatuun ubaa dan nan sil m chee,

ref: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
text: ki bui mi, ‘Pɔɔl, taa san ijawaan. Aa ga sil Ubɔrkpaan Siisa aanimbiin ni. Uwumbɔr ga cha binib bimɔk bi buŋɔb bue ponn ni na ŋmar, saanimbaak pu.’

ref: Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised.
text: Njɔtiib, nima pu na, chuu nibaa man. M pak ke Uwumbɔr ga ŋa waah tuk mi pu na.

ref: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
text: Libuln mu ga daa buŋɔb na ti tam lidikl libaa, ki bii bu.”

ref: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
text: Le bi chuu geei tikur na aaŋmin, le ti bee nnyun ni. Le bi chuu gbiln tiŋɔpann aaŋmin, ki nan di likekeln gbin liŋɔyil ndɔ pu paacham. Libuln aah daar na, le bi ban ke likekeln ngbaan li joo buŋɔb chuun cha nnyun aagbaan. Le bu chuun buen.

ref: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
text: Le biŋɔŋaab ban ke bi loon nyan buŋɔb na ni. Le bi chuu nyan buŋɔb waatiib na di deen nnyun pu, ki ŋmann ke bi chuu nyan tikur tibaa le liŋɔyil pu.

ref: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
text: Le bi dak ke nibaakan buŋɔb ngbaan ga duur ŋitakpal ki bii. Nima pu na, bi nan di tikur tinaa gbin iŋmin inaa pu, ki di gbin liŋɔjuul, le ti doon tam kitiŋ, ki joo bu. Bu aan ki ŋmaa chuun. Baah ŋa kina na, le bi mee Uwumbɔr ke u cha kitaak woln.

ref: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
text: Tɔ, Pɔɔl nan bee baah ban bi ŋa pu na, le ki bui butɔb aajab ni baaninkpel, “Biŋɔŋaab ngbaan yaa nyan buŋɔb ngbaan ponn ni kan, naan ŋmaa ŋmar.”

ref: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
text: Waah len kina na, le butɔb aajab chuu buŋɔb waatiib na aaŋmin gii, ki di bu lii, ki cha busakpem na.

ref: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
text: Ni pɔɔk nibaa ki ji pɔkaa man. Ni ga ter nimi, ni kan mpɔɔn. Nibaa aan ŋa unii ubaa do ponn ni.”

ref: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
text: Pɔɔl aah len kina na, le u yoor boroboro, ki doon Uwumbɔr bi mɔmɔk aanimbil ni, ki gii ki ŋman.

ref: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
text: Waah ŋa kina na, le bi mɔmɔk chuu bibaa, ki mu jin tijikaar.

ref: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
text: Le bi mɔmɔk ŋman ti bab. Baah ŋman bab na, le bi di tijikaar ti gur na di mee nnyun ni. Bi nan ban ke buŋɔb ngbaan yook la. Timi aaŋɔb aah bii pu na

ref: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
text: Kitaak aah woln na, le ti kan kitiŋ. Le biŋɔŋaab aa nyi kitiŋ ngbaan ni. Le bi kan kiloloŋ. Litambol mu dɔ kiloloŋ ngbaan aagbaan. Le bi len ke bi ga pɔɔn bibaa ki cha buŋɔb na ti nyal litambol ngbaan paab.

ref: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
text: Litambol libaa nan dɔ nnyun ponn ni, le baa waa li, ki di dii lipaab. Le liŋɔyil chɔb lipaab, kaan ki ŋmaa chuun. Tinyunkpenn nan gbaa buŋɔb na le liŋɔjuul ti wii.

ref: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
text: Butɔb aajab aaninkpel aa nan ban ke bi ku Pɔɔl, nima pu le waa kii. U nan tuk bi ke binib bi ŋmaa wo nnyun na puen yuk lir nnyun ponn ni, ki wo buen nnyun aagbaan, ki ti nyan;

ref: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
text: ke binib bi kaa ŋmaa wo nnyun na nyoon ŋikpan, ni ŋiŋɔbɔk, ki li cha nnyun aagbaan, ki ti nyan. Le ti ŋa kina. Le ti mɔmɔk ti nyan.

ref: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
text: Taah nyan nnyun ngbaan ni na, le bi tuk timi ke bi yin lidikl ngbaan ke Malta.

ref: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
text: Le kitiŋ ngbaan aanib gaa timi ki ŋa timi tiŋann pam. Le utaal piin ki bi nu, le tiwoor bi. Le bi tuur mmii tii timi.

ref: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
text: Le Pɔɔl ti peei ni idɔ nan di ŋa mmii ni. Waah di i ŋa mmii ni na, le i toŋ. Le uwaa nyan i ni, ki juu dab uŋaal, ki jɔn.

ref: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
text: Waah juu dab uŋaal ki jɔn na, le kitiŋ ngbaan ponn ni aanib kan, ki bui tɔb ke uja ngbaan ye unikur, le ki nyan ni nnyusakpem ni; Uwumbɔr mu aan cha u ŋmar.

ref: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
text: Tɔ, Pɔɔl nan gbɔk uŋaal, le uwaa na lir mmii ni. Naa ŋa u nibaa.

ref: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
text: Bi dak ke ni ga duun la, ni yaa kaa ye kina kan, u ga kpo. Bi nan lik le ni ti yunn, ki mu aa kan nibaa ŋa u. Le bi ki dak ke u ye liwaal la, le ki kpaln unii.

ref: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
text: Tɔ, kitiŋ ngbaan aanib aaninkpel mu nan bi. Bi yin u ke Publius. Waasaak aa nan daa taah bi nin chee na. Le u gaa timi, ki chann timi tichann ki ŋa timi tibulchinn iwiin itaa.

ref: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
text: Ute nan bun, ki dɔ kidiik ni. Uwon nan ton, le u peel nsin. Pɔɔl nan koo u chee kidiik ni, ki ti mee Uwumbɔr tii u, ki ti di uŋaal paan u pu, le u pɔɔk.

ref: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
text: Pɔɔl aah ŋa kina na, le bibum biken bi bi lidikl ngbaan aatiŋ ni na mu dan Pɔɔl chee, le u cha bi mu pɔɔk.

ref: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
text: Le bi tii timi ipiin pam. Taah nan ban ti buen na, bi nan ki tii timi, timi aasachuln aapiin. Taah nyan Malta aadikl pu ki buen Rom aatiŋ ni pu na

ref: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
text: Ti nan bi nima iŋmal itaa, le buŋɔb bubaa nan bi nima tiwoor ni libuln yoonn. Bu nyan ni kitiŋ kibaa ni, bi yin ki ke Aleksandria. Bi nan yin buŋɔb ngbaan ke “Bijaam.” Le ti koo bu ni, ki buen.

ref: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
text: Ti nan ti fuu kitiŋ kibaa ni, bi yin ki ke Sirakus, ki nan bi nima iwiin itaa,

ref: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
text: Ti nan kan Yesu aanib bibaa nima. Le bi gaŋ timi ke ti li bi bi chee ki ti saa iwiin ilole. Iwiin ilole ngbaan aah jer na, le ti chuun kitiŋ ki buen Rom aatiŋ ni.

ref: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
text: Yesu aanib bi nan bi Rom aatiŋ ni na nan ŋun ke ti choo. Le bi tooh ni timi nsan pu. Bibaa nan tooh ni timi Apius Aanyaŋ ponn ni, le bibaa mu tooh ni timi Tidir Daakaan Titaa na chee. Pɔɔl aah kan bi na, le u doon Uwumbɔr, ki kan lipobil. Pɔɔl aah moon Yesu aabɔr Rom aatiŋ ni pu na

ref: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
text: Tɔ, ti nan ti fuu Rom aatiŋ ni. Taah fuu nima na, le bi cha Pɔɔl koo kidiik kibaa ni, le butɔb aaja ubaa si kii u.

ref: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
text: Iwiin itaa aah jer na, le Pɔɔl yin Juu yaab aaninkpiib ke bi kuun ni u chee. Baah kuun ni u chee na, le u bui bi, “Nnaabitiib, maa ŋa timi aanib bakaa, kaa bii tiyaajatiib aakaal. Bi po chuu mi Jerusalem ni ki di mi ŋa Rom yaab aaŋaal ni.

ref: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
text: Bi nan jin mi tibɔr, le ki bee ke maa ŋa bakaa, naa ŋeer bi ku mi. Le bi ban ke bi di cha mi.

ref: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
text: Le Juu yaab aa kii ke bi di cha mi. Nima pu na, m len ke m ban ke Ubɔrkpaan Siisa le ji mi tibɔr ngbaan. Naa ye ke m ban ke m galn maanib u chee.

ref: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
text: Nima pu le m yin nimi ke ni dan m chee, aan ti nan len tɔb chee tibɔr. Timi Israel yaab kpa limakl ke unii u ga gaa timi lii na ga dan. Limakl ngbaan pu, le bi buu mi tikululn tee.”

ref: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
text: Le bi bui u, “Judea aatiŋ aanib aa ŋmee saabɔr kigbaŋ ni tii ni timi. Tina aabo ubaa aa nyan ni nima, ki nan tuk timi saabɔr, kaa len tibɔbir aa pu.

ref: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
text: Ti nyi ke bi len ntim mɔmɔk ponn ni ke saah dii nsan mu na aa ŋan. Nima pu na, ti ban ti ŋun tibɔr ti bi aamɔb ni na.”

ref: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
text: Le bi siin bundaln bi ga ki kuun Pɔɔl chee na. Liyaadaal aah fuu ni na, bi nan ki kuun ni waadiik ni, ki wiir pam. U nan len bi chee tibɔr kichakpiik ni ki nan saa kijook, ki tuk bi Uwumbɔr aanaan aabɔr, ke Moses ni Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib nan ŋmee Yesu aabɔr, Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni. Pɔɔl nan pɔɔni ubaa ke bi gaa Yesu ki kii.

ref: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
text: Juu yaab bibaa kii tii waah len pu na, bibaa mu aa kii tii.

ref: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
text: Le bi kpak tɔb kinikpakpak. Baah ban bi nyan Pɔɔl aadiik ni na, le u bui bi, “Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan nan cha waabɔnabr Aisaya tuk niyaajatiib mbamɔn.

ref: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
text: U nan tuk Aisaya ke, ‘Li cha ti tuk binib ngbaan ke Uwumbɔr len ke: Ni ga pel ki pel, kaan bee maaliin aatataa. Ni ga lik ki lik, kaan li waa.

ref: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
text: Binib ngbaan aasui aa bi nibaa ni. Bitafal kpaa la. Bi ŋub binimbil, kaa ban ke binimbil woln, kaa ban ke bitafal ŋun, kaa ban ke bisui bee maaliin aatataa, kaa ban ke bi kpeln baabimbin ki dii maasan, aan m tii bi laafee.’”

ref: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
text: Pɔɔl aah len kina na, le Juu yaab ngbaan nyan waadiik ni, ki beenin kpak tɔb kinikpakpak sakpen.]

ref: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
text: Pɔɔl nan bi kidiik ngbaan ponn ni ŋibin ŋilee. U nan pan ki pu, le ki bi ki ni. Le binib choo nan manni u nima. Le u gaa bi mɔmɔk ni mpopiin.

ref: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
text: U nan beenin tuk binib Uwumbɔr aanaan aabɔr, ni Tidindaan Yesu Kristo aabɔr, ki nan kpa lipobil ki len. Ubaa mu aa bui ke u di cha.

ref: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
text: Min Pɔɔl le ŋmee kigbaŋ kee. M ye Yesu Kristo aatutunn la. Uwumbɔr nan yin mi ke m li ye Yesu aakpambal, ki nyan mi ke m moon waabɔnyaan tee.

ref: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
text: N‑yaayoonn na, Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur ke u ga tii timi tibɔnyaan tee. Le waabɔnabtiib ŋmee ti waagbaŋ ki ye chain na ponn ni.

ref: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
text: Uwumbɔr nan fikr u nkun ni, le Waafuur Nyaan mɔk ke u ye uma Uwumbɔr Aajapɔɔn u kpa mpɔɔn na.

ref: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
text: U pu le Uwumbɔr ŋa tinyoor ŋa m pu, le ki ŋa mi waakpambal, ke m tuk ŋinibol mɔmɔk ke ni ŋan ke bi tii u naadii, ki kii waamɔb.

ref: You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
text: Nimi bi bi Rom aatiŋ ni na, Uwumbɔr yin ni mu, ke ni li ye Yesu Kristo aanib.

ref: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
text: Nima le m ŋmee kigbaŋ kee m tii nimi bimɔk bi Rom aatiŋ ni na. Uwumbɔr gee nimi ki yin nimi ke ni li ye waanib. Tite Uwumbɔr ni Tidindaan Yesu Kristo ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu, ki tii nimi nsuudoon. Idoon aameel

ref: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
text: Yesu Kristo pu, le m dooni Maawumbɔr ni mɔmɔk pu; ba pu? binib bimɔk bi dulnyaa ni na ŋun naah gaa Yesu Kristo ki kii pu na.

ref: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
text: M di nsui mɔmɔk tun lituln tii Uwumbɔr, ki tuk binib Ujapɔɔn Yesu Kristo aabɔnyaan ngbaan. Uma Uwumbɔr le nyi ke ni ye mbamɔn, m teer nibɔr maameen mɔmɔk ponn ni,

ref: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
text: ki mee u n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke ni yaa ye waageehn kan, u tii mi nsan ke m dan nan mann nimi dandana wee.

ref: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
text: M ban ke m kan nimi, ki ter nimi aan ni kan Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aapiin i ga pɔɔk nitaakpab na.

ref: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
text: Maah len pu na le ye ke m ni nimi aah gaa Yesu Kristo ki kii pu na, ti ga pɔɔk tɔb aataakpab.

ref: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
text: Nnaabitiib, m ban ke ni bee ke n‑yoonn mɔmɔk m nan ban ke m dan ni chee, le kaa kee ŋmaa dan. M ban ke m cha binib gaa Yesu ki kii Rom aatiŋ ni, ke maah ŋa pu ntim muken ponn ni na.

ref: I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
text: Maa san inimɔɔn Yesu aabɔnyaan tee pu. Tibɔnyaan ngbaan kpa Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn. Binib bimɔk ŋun ti ki gaa Yesu Kristo ki kii na ga ŋmar; njan, bi ye Juu yaab na ga ŋmar, le bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu ga ŋmar.

ref: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
text: Tibɔnyaan ngbaan mɔk timi ke unii yaa gaa Yesu Kristo ki kii kan, Uwumbɔr ga len ke waabɔr ŋan. Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Uninyaan aah gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii na, u ga li kpa limɔfal.” Unibɔn aataani

ref: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
text: Uwumbɔr mɔk binib ke u gee liŋuul titunwanbirdam pu; bi tun lituln li kaa ŋan na, kaa dii u. Baabiin pu le bi yii mbamɔn.

ref: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
text: Uwumbɔr gee liŋuul bi pu la; ba pu? waabɔr ti binib ga ŋmaa bee ti na bi mpaan pu. Uwumbɔr le di ti mɔk bi.

ref: God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse.
text: Buyoonn Uwumbɔr nan naan dulnyaa wee ki nan saa dandana wee na, binib kani waabimbin aah bi pu na. Naa ye ke binimbil le kan u. Bi kan tiwan ni u naan ni na, ki kan ke u kpa mpɔɔn mu kaan doo na, ki sil ye Uwumbɔr. Nima le baan ŋmaa len ke baa nyi.

ref: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
text: Bi nyi ke u bi, ki mu aa nyuŋni u waah ŋeer pu na, ki mu aa dooni u waaterm pu. Nima le baalandak bee fam. Bisui ni bɔɔn la, kaa kpa nlan.

ref: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
text: Bi len ke bi ye bilankpalb, le ki tee ye bijɔrb.

ref: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
text: Baa ki dooni Uwumbɔr u nyuun ki bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Bi ŋa binibɔm aanaŋ, ni inyoon aanaŋ, ni iwaa aanaŋ, ki dooni ŋiwaa ngbaan.

ref: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
text: Nima le Uwumbɔr di cha bi, le bi dii bisui aah ban pu na, ki tun tijɔŋ aatuln, ki tun lituln li jinni biwon inimɔɔn na. Bi yii Uwumbɔr u ye mbamɔn na, ki dii ŋiwaa.

ref: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
text: Bi dooni tiwan ni Uwumbɔr naan ni na, ki dii ni, kaa dooni Uwumbɔr u naan tiwan mɔmɔk na, kaa dii u. Uma Uwumbɔr le yeh mpakm n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Amii.

ref: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
text: Baah yii Uwumbɔr na, nima le u siir cha bi. Le bi tun inimɔɔn aatuln, bisui aah ban pu na. Bipiib di biŋeen aatɔtiib kpaln bijab, ki doo bi chee.

ref: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
text: Bijab mu yii bipiib, ki chuun ban bijab, ki di biŋeen aatɔtiib kpaln bipiib ki tun inimɔɔn aatuln, le Uwumbɔr daa bitafal, baatunwanbir aah ŋeer pu na.

ref: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
text: Baah kaa gee ke bi li nyi Uwumbɔr na, le u siir cha bi. Le bi dak ilandak i ye fam na, ki tun lituln li kaa ŋan na,

ref: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
text: ki gbii titunwanbir aabɔŋ mɔmɔk. Bi gɔr kidagook ki tun baka baka, ki kpa iniman, kaa gee tɔb, ki kpa lipiipoln, ki jaa kijaak, ki ku tɔb, ki ŋmanni tɔb, ki nan tɔb, ki bii tɔb libɔɔl ni,

ref: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
text: ni mpaan pu. Bi nan Uwumbɔr, le ki seei tɔb, ki kpa kalmbaani, ki puk kipupuk. Bi po dak baah ga ŋa pu ki moo tun titunwanbir na la. Bi yii bite ni bina aamɔi.

ref: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
text: Baa kpa nlan. Bi yaa puu tipuur kan, baa gbiini ti. Baa gee baamaal aanib, kaa cha pinni binib, kaa san binib kinimbaak.

ref: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
text: Bi nyi ke Uwumbɔr len ke binib bi ŋani kina na ŋeer nkun, le bi tee beenin ŋani kina, ki len ke binib yaa ŋani kina kan, naa bir.

ref: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
text: Tɔ, si u galni binib biken na, saan ŋmaa len tibaa ki nyan aabaa tibɔr ni Uwumbɔr chee; ba pu? aa mu ŋani kina la. Saah galni bi na, le ni mɔk ke saabɔr mu bii; ba pu? si u galni bi na, aa mu ŋani ke baah ŋani pu na la.

ref: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
text: Ti nyi ke Uwumbɔr yaa daa binib bi ŋani kina na aatafal kan, ni ŋan.

ref: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
text: Si u ŋani kina na, ki galni biken bi ŋani kina na, aa dak ke Uwumbɔr aan daa aatafal aa?

ref: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
text: U ŋa si tibulchinn sakpen, ki kpa limɔr ni suklaa aa pu. Ba ŋa aa lik u fam? Saa nyi ke Uwumbɔr ban ke aa kpeln saabimbin aa? Nima le cha u ŋa si tibulchinn.

ref: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
text: Le aatafal pɔɔ. Saa ban ke aa kpeln aasui. Nima le Uwumbɔr ga moo daa aatafal, bundaln u ga gee liŋuul binib aanimbil ni ki ji bi tibɔr mbamɔm na.

ref: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
text: U ga ŋa binib mɔmɔk baatuln aah ŋeer pu na.

ref: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
text: Binib bi kpa limɔr ki tun lituln li ŋan na, ki ban mpakm, ni nnyuŋ, ni limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na, bima le Uwumbɔr ga tii bi limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
text: Binib bi ban tibɔr, ki yii mbamɔn, ki dii nsan mu kaa ŋan na, bima le Uwumbɔr gee liŋuul sakpen bi pu.

ref: All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles.
text: Binib bimɔk tun titunwanbir na ga kan falaa ni limukl. Njan, Juu yaab ga kan, le binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu ga kan.

ref: But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
text: Binib bimɔk tun lituln li ŋan na, Uwumbɔr ga nyuŋ bi, ki pak bi, ki tii bi nsuudoon. Njan, u ga tii Juu yaab, le ki ga tii binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu;

ref: God doesn't have any favorites!
text: ba pu? Uwumbɔr aa pak ubaa ki jer uken.

ref: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
text: Binib bimɔk kaa nyi Moses aakaal ki tun titunwanbir na aan kan limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na. Uwumbɔr aan baa bi ke bi dii Moses aakaal aan baa dii. Binib bimɔk nyi Moses aakaal ki tun titunwanbir na, Uwumbɔr ga baa bi tibɔr nkaal ngbaan aah dii pu na, ki ga daa bitafal.

ref: God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
text: Uwumbɔr aan len ke binib bi nyi waakaal kaa dii mu na aabɔr ŋan. U ga len ke binib bi dii waakaal na le aabɔr ŋan.

ref: This proves that the conscience is like a law written in the human heart. And it will show whether we are forgiven or condemned,
text: Baah ŋani pu na, nima le mɔk ke Moses aakaal aah len pu na bi bisui ni. Bisui ponn ni, bi nyi ni ŋan na, ni ni kaa ŋan na. Nima le baalandak bii bi n‑yoonn mubaa, ki pak bi n‑yoonn mubaa mu.

ref: when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says. The Jews and the Law
text: Ni ga li bi kina le bundaln Uwumbɔr ga cha Yesu Kristo ji binib tibɔr, ki baa bi tibɔbɔrkaan ti bi bisui ni na aabɔr. Maah tuk binib tibɔnyaan ti na le mɔk kina. Juu yaab ni nkaal na

ref: Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God.
text: Tɔ, aa len ke aa ye Juu aanii la, ki dak ke saah nyi Moses aakaal na, nima le ga cha aa ŋmar; aa kpa kipupuk ke aa nyi Uwumbɔr,

ref: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
text: ki nyi waah gee pu na, ki bae Moses aakaal, ki nyi lituln li ŋan na, ni li kaa ŋan na,

ref: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
text: ki dak ke aa ye usanmɔkr le ki tii bijoom, ki ga ŋmaa woln binib bi kaa waa na aanimbil,

ref: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
text: ki ga ŋmaa mɔk bijɔrb nlan, ki ga ŋmaa mɔk mbim mmɔkm. Saah nyi Moses aakaal mu na, aa dak ke aa nyi tiwan mɔmɔk, ki dak ke saah len pu na mɔmɔk ye mbamɔn.

ref: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
text: Tɔ, si u mɔk biken na, ba ŋa saa mɔk aabaa? Si u tuk binib ke bi taa su kinaayuk na, ba ŋa aa su?

ref: You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples.
text: Si u len ke binib taa gɔr kidagook na, ba ŋa aa gɔr? Si u yii ŋiwaa na, ba ŋa aa su ŋaadir ni aawan?

ref: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
text: Si u kpa kipupuk Uwumbɔr aakaal pu ki bii nkaal ngbaan na, aa jinn u inimɔɔn la.

ref: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni ke, “Nimi Juu yaab aah ŋani titunwanbir pu na, nima le cha binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na len Uwumbɔr tibɔbir.”

ref: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
text: Tɔ, aa yaa joo Moses aakaal kan, lichakpangeei kpa tinyoor. Aa mu yaa gii lichakpaln ki bii Moses aakaal kan, ni mɔk ke saa gii le na.

ref: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
text: Binib bi kaa gii ŋichakpan na yaa joo Uwumbɔr aakaal kan, Uwumbɔr aan yii bi, ke baa gii ŋichakpan.

ref: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
text: Binib bi kaa gii ŋichakpan na yaa joo Uwumbɔr aakaal kan, bi ŋan jer nimi Juu yaab bi gii ŋichakpan Moses aakaal aah mɔk pu na, ki bii nkaal muken na.

ref: Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew.
text: Unii u ye Juu aanii mpaan pu baanja na aa ye Juu aanibamɔnn. Unii u gii lichakpaln kaa kpeln waabimbin na, naa ye lichakpangeei bamɔnn.

ref: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
text: Unii u gii lichakpaln, kaa kpeln waabimbin na aa piir Uwumbɔr aasui. Unii u dii Uwumbɔr usui ni na, uma le ye Juu aanibamɔnn. Unii u Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan bi u ni na, nima le ye lichakpangeei bamɔnn. Uwumbɔr le ga pak udaan, naa ye binib.

ref: What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised?
text: Lichakpangeei aanyoor ye ba? Juu yaab jer binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aa?

ref: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
text: Een, bi jer bi tiwan aabɔŋ ni la. Ni jer tiwan mɔmɔk na le ye ke Uwumbɔr nan di waabɔr ŋa bima le aaŋaal ni.

ref: It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith?
text: Bi ponn ni bibaa yaa kaa gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii kan, ni ye ba? Baah kaa gaa u ki kii na, Uwumbɔr aan gbiin waa puu tipuur ti na aa?

ref: No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God, “Your words will be proven true, and in court you will win your case.”
text: U ga gbiin ti. Binib mɔmɔk yaa ye binyamɔndam kan, Uwumbɔr ma ye mbamɔndaan la. Ni ŋmee waagbaŋ ni ke, “Bi ga kan ke saah len pu na ye mbamɔn, Aa yaa jin binib tibɔr kan, aa kpa mbamɔn la.”

ref: If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask.
text: Timi aatunwanbir yaa mɔk ke Uwumbɔr ŋani ni ŋan na kan, ti ga len ke Uwumbɔr yaa daa titafal kan, u ŋa ni kaa ŋan na aa? Binib bi kaa dii Uwumbɔr na le baa kina.

ref: But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
text: U ŋa ni ŋan na la; ba pu? ni yaa kaa ŋan kan, u ga ŋa kinye ki ji dulnyaa ni aanib tibɔr?

ref: Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner.
text: Ubaa ga baa ke, “Maah gee nnyamɔn na yaa mɔk ke Uwumbɔr ye mbamɔndaan ki ga cha binib nyuŋ u kan, ba ŋa u daa ntafal ke m ye titunwanbirdaan?”

ref: You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well. No One Is Good
text: Ti ga tun titunwanbir aan ni kpaln tiwan ni ŋan na aa? Taan ŋa kina kpala. Binib bibaa seei timi ki bui ke ti len kina la. Binib ngbaan ga kan ntafadaan mu ŋeer bi na. Ubaa aa ŋan Uwumbɔr chee

ref: What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said.
text: Tɔ, timi Juu yaab ŋan ki jer binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aa? Taa jer bi. M nan mɔk nimi ke binib bi ye Juu yaab na, ni bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mɔmɔk ye titunwanbirdam la.

ref: The Scriptures tell us, “No one is acceptable to God!
text: Ni ŋmee kina le Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Unii ubaa aa ye uninyaan,

ref: Not one of them understands or even searches for God.
text: ubaa aa kpa nlan, ubaa aa ban Uwumbɔr,

ref: They have all turned away and are worthless. There isn't one person who does right.
text: bi mɔmɔk di cha waasan, bi mɔmɔk bee fam la. Ubaa aa bi ki tun lituln li ŋan na, ubaa baanja aa bi.

ref: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
text: Baaliin po ye iliin i bir na la. Bi geei inyamɔn ki ŋmanni binib. Baaliin bii binib ke ujagen aaluul aah bii binib pu na la.

ref: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
text: Baamɔi gbii ŋisiibil ni kinanaŋ la.

ref: These people quickly become violent.
text: Bi yaa ban bi ku binib kan, naa pɔɔ.

ref: Wherever they go, they leave ruin and destruction.
text: Bi muk binib ki ŋani bi falaa n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la.

ref: They don't know how to live in peace.
text: Bi chuun ban tibɔr la.

ref: They don't even fear God.”
text: Baa san Uwumbɔr.”

ref: We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty.
