text: Tɔ, ti nyi ke nkaal aah len pu na mɔmɔk len binib bi bi mu chee na la. Nima le dulnyaa wee ni aanib mɔmɔk aabɔr bii Uwumbɔr chee. Ubaa aan ŋmaa len tibaa ke u nyan ubaa tibɔr ni Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
text: Ubaa aan ŋmaa len ke waah joo Uwumbɔr aakaal mbamɔm pu na, waabɔr ŋan Uwumbɔr chee. Uwumbɔr aakaal le mɔk binib ke bi ye titunwanbirdam la. Uwumbɔr aah cha ti ni uma tuuk pu na

ref: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
text: Dandana wee, Uwumbɔr mɔk timi waah ga ŋa pu ki len ke timi aabɔr ŋan na. Waakaal ni waabɔnabtiib aaliin le bi waagbaŋ ponn ni, ki mu tuk timi kina la. Naa ye ke ti dii waakaal mbamɔm le cha u len.

ref: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
text: binib mɔmɔk tun titunwanbir la, kaa gbiin Uwumbɔr aanimbil.

ref: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
text: Le Yesu Kristo daa timi, ki gaa timi lii. Timi bi kpaan u chee na, le Uwumbɔr len ke timi aabɔr ŋan. Waabulchinn pu le u len, naa ye ke ti ŋan la.

ref: God sent Christ to be our sacrifice. Christ offered his life's blood, so by faith in him we could come to God. And God did this to show that in the past he was right to be patient and forgive sinners. This also shows that God is right when he accepts people who have faith in Jesus.
text: Tɔ, dandana wee, u len titunwanbir aabɔr ki bui ke binib bi gaa Yesu ki kii na aabɔr ŋan u chee. Nimina le mɔk ke uma Uwumbɔr si chob.

ref: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.
text: Tɔ, ba pu aan ti ga li kpa kipupuk? Taan li kpa kipupuk nibaa pu. Ba pu? Naa ye ke ti dii Uwumbɔr aakaal mbamɔm le cha u gaa timi lii, taah gaa Yesu ki kii na, nima le cha u gaa timi lii.

ref: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
text: Nima pu na, ti bee ke ti yaa gaa Yesu ki kii kan, Uwumbɔr ga len ke timi aabɔr ŋan. Naa ye ke ti joo waakaal mbamɔm le cha u len kina.

ref: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
text: Uwumbɔr ye Juu yaab baanja Aawumbɔr la aa? Waa ye binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu Aawumbɔr aa? Mbamɔn, u ye.

ref: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
text: Ti yaa len ke binib yaa gaa Yesu ki kii ki ga ŋmar kan, ti yii Uwumbɔr aakaal aa? Naa bi kina kpala. Ti ŋa mu tibɔkpaan la.

ref: Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham?
text: Tɔ, cha ti lik tiyaaja Abraham aabɔr aah nan bi pu na:

ref: If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God.
text: Ni yaa ba ye waatunyaan pu le cha Uwumbɔr len ke waabɔr ŋan kan, u ba ga ŋmaa li kpa kipupuk. U mu aa ŋmaa li kpa kipupuk Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
text: Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ len ke, “Abraham nan gaa Uwumbɔr aamɔboln ki kii, kina pu na le Uwumbɔr gaa u ke u ye uninyaan u chee.”

ref: Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working.
text: Unii u tun lituln ki kan tipar na, tipar ngbaan aa ye ipiin, ni ye waapar la.

ref: But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him.
text: Tɔ, unii u kaa joo nkaal na yaa gaa Uwumbɔr u di cha pinn titunwanbirdam na ki kii kan, waah gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii na, nima le Uwumbɔr ga len ke waabɔr ŋan.

ref: In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
text: Ubɔr David mu nan len ke binib bi Uwumbɔr len ke baabɔr ŋan na le kpa mpopiin. Bi gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, nima le cha u len ke baabɔr ŋan, naa ye ke bi tun litunyaan le cha u len kina. Ubɔr David nan len ke,

ref: “What a blessing when God forgives our sins and our evil deeds. What a blessing when the Lord erases our sins from his book.”
text: Binib bi Uwumbɔr aan len ke baabɔr bii na, bima le kpa mpopiin.”

ref: Are these blessings meant for circumcised people or for those who are not circumcised? Well, the Scriptures say that God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.
text: U len ke Juu yaab baanja le kpa mpopiin ngbaan aa? Waa len kina. Binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu kpa. Ti len ke Abraham nan gaa Uwumbɔr aamɔboln ki kii, nima le cha Uwumbɔr gaa u ke u ye uninyaan u chee.

ref: But when did this happen? Was it before or after Abraham was circumcised? Of course, it was before.
text: Bayoonn Uwumbɔr len ke waabɔr ŋan? Buyoonn u nan gii lichakpaln na le aan buyoonn waa nan kee gii na? Buyoonn waa nan kee gii na.

ref: Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised.
text: Waah gii lichakpaln na, nima le nan ye limɔkl ki mɔk ke u gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, nima le Uwumbɔr gaa u ke u ye uninyaan u chee, buyoonn waa nan kee gii lichakpaln na. Nima pu le Abraham ye binib bimɔk gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, kaa gii ŋichakpan na aate. Baah gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii na, nima le Uwumbɔr gaa bi ke bi ye bininyaam u chee.

ref: This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised. The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
text: Binib bi gii ŋichakpan, ki tak Abraham aataabuu ponn ni, ki gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii ke Abraham aah nan gaa u ki kii pu, buyoonn waa nan kee gii lichakpaln na, bima mu le Abraham ye bite. Gaakii pu le ti ga kan Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ti na

ref: God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable.
text: Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur tii Abraham ni uyaabitiib, ke bima le ga li yeh dulnyaa. Naa ye ke bi joo Uwumbɔr aakaal le ga cha bi kan tipuur ngbaan. Bi gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii la, le u len ke baabɔr ŋan. Nima le ga cha bi kan tipuur ngbaan.

ref: If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa ba puu tipuur ke binib bi joo waakaal na le ga li yeh dulnyaa kan, naadii aa ba ga li kpa tinyoor. Tipuur ngbaan mu aa ba ga gbiin; ba pu? ubaa aan ŋmaa joo nkaal mɔmɔk mbamɔm.

ref: God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken.
text: Binib aah bii nkaal na, le Uwumbɔr gee liŋuul bi pu. Nkaal aah kaa bi nin chee na, binib aa bii nkaal.

ref: Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all.
text: Nima le Uwumbɔr puu tipuur tii binib bi gaa u ki kii na. Uwumbɔr aah gee binib pu na, nima le u tii Abraham aayaabitiib mɔmɔk waah nan puu tipuur ti na. U ga tii Abraham aayaabitiib bi ye Juu yaab ki gaa u ki kii na, ni binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab ki mu gaa u ki kii na ke Abraham aah nan gaa u ki kii pu na. Abraham ye timi bimɔk gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii na aayaaja la.

ref: The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni ke Uwumbɔr bui Abraham, “M ŋa si ŋinibol pam aayaaja la.” Abraham le ye tite Uwumbɔr chee. U nan tii Uwumbɔr naadii. Uma Uwumbɔr le fikr binib bi kpo na nkun ni, le ki yin binib bi kaa kee bi na, ke baah bi le na.

ref: God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations.
text: U nan puu tipuur tii Abraham ke u ga ŋa u ŋinibol pam aayaaja, ke uyaabitiib ga li wiir ke iŋmabi aah wiir pu na. Ni nan bi ke tipuur ngbaan aah kaan ŋmaa gbiin le na. Abraham mu nan tee kpa limakl ke ti ga nan gbiin.

ref: But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
text: Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ti tii u na, tima le gur ye waalandak. Le u pak tipuur ngbaan mbamɔm, kaa joo beeni ke ti ga gbiin bee taan gbiin? U nan moo gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii le ki nyuŋ u,

ref: Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised.
text: ki sil nyi ke Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ti na, u ga ŋmaa ŋa kina.

ref: They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life.
text: Ni ŋmee kina le Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni. Timi pu le bi nan ŋmee kina, naa ye Abraham baanja pu; ba pu? timi bi gaa Uwumbɔr u nan fikr Tidindaan Yesu nkun ni ki kii na, le u ga len ke timi aabɔr ŋan.

ref: God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
text: Yesu nan kpo timi aatunwanbir pu, le ki fikr nkun ni. Nima le Uwumbɔr len ke timi aabɔr ŋan.

ref: By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God.
text: Taah gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na, nima le u len ke timi aabɔr ŋan. Tidindaan Yesu Kristo pu le ti ni Uwumbɔr kpaan kijɔtiik.

ref: Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God.
text: Yesu Kristo pu, le Uwumbɔr len ke timi aabɔr ŋan. Le ti mɔɔni ki kpa limakl ke ti ga yakr u chee Uwumbɔr aamɔɔn.

ref: But that's not all! We gladly suffer, because we know that suffering helps us to endure.
text: Naa ye nima baanja pu le ti mɔɔni. Falaa mu pu le ti mɔɔni. Ba pu? falaa le tii timi suklaa.

ref: And endurance builds character, which gives us a hope
text: Suklaa mu tii timi mbimbinyaan. Mbimbinyaan mu tii timi limakl.

ref: that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
text: Limakl ngbaan aan jinn timi inimɔɔn. Ba pu? Uwumbɔr aah tii timi Waafuur Nyaan na, Nfuur Nyaan ngbaan le cha ti bee tisui ni waah gee timi sakpen pu na.

ref: Christ died for us at a time when we were helpless and sinful.
text: Naah nan ŋeer na, le Kristo nan kpo timi bi ye titunwanbirdam na pu, taah kaa kpa mpɔɔn buyoonn na.

ref: No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person.
text: Ni pɔɔ ke unii kpo ke u nyan unii u dii mbamɔm na nkun ni. Nibaakan, unii ubaa ga kaa ki kpo uninyaan pu.

ref: But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
text: Tima kan, buyoonn ti nan laa ye titunwanbirdam na le Kristo nan kpo ti pu. Nima le mɔk timi Uwumbɔr aah gee timi sakpen pu na.

ref: But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger.
text: Kristo aasin pu le Uwumbɔr len ke timi aabɔr ŋan. Ŋmaninkabaa taah ga nya ntafadaan mu ponn ni u pu na?

ref: Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son.
text: Buyoonn ti nan ye Uwumbɔr aadim na, le Ujapɔɔn nan kpo ti pu. U pu, le ti ni Uwumbɔr kpaan kijɔtiik. Ti ni Uwumbɔr aah kpaan kijɔtiik na, ŋmaninkabaa taah ga ŋmar waamɔfal pu pu na?

ref: And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us. Adam and Christ
text: Naa ye nima baanja pu le ti mɔɔni. Tidindaan Yesu Kristo pu le ti bee Uwumbɔr aah ŋan pu na, le ki mɔɔni. U pu le ti ni Uwumbɔr kpaan kijɔtiik. Adam pu le ti kpo, Kristo pu le ti kpa limɔfal

ref: Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die.
text: Unibaan le nan joo ni titunwanbir dulnyaa ni, le titunwanbir ngbaan joo ni nkun. Binib mɔmɔk aah tun titunwanbir na, le nkun yaa gaa dulnyaa mɔmɔk ni.

ref: Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law.
text: Buyoonn Moses aa nan kee tuk binib Uwumbɔr aakaal na, titunwanbir nan bi. Nkaal aah kaa bi nin chee na, Uwumbɔr aan len ke bi bii mu.

ref: Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did. In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later.
text: Adam aayoonn ki ti saa Moses aayoonn le nkun pii binib. Bi nan tun titunwanbir la. Baatunwanbir ni Adam u nan yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na aatunwanbir aa kpaan. Nkun mu pii bi la. Ti mɔmɔk kan Adam aatunwanbir aatafadaan. Kina le ti mɔmɔk yakr Kristo aatunyaan aanyoor mu.

ref: But the gift of God's undeserved grace was very different from Adam's sin. That one sin brought death to many others. Yet in an even greater way, Jesus Christ alone brought God's gift of undeserved grace to many people.
text: Uwumbɔr aah tii timi ipiin i na aa bi ke Adam aatunwanbir na. Ni ye mbamɔn ke unibaan aatunwanbir pu le nkun pii binib mɔmɔk. Yesu Kristo aanimbaasaln pu, le Uwumbɔr san binib mɔmɔk kinimbaak, ki tii bi ipiin i ye limɔfal na.

ref: There is a lot of difference between Adam's sin and God's gift. That one sin led to punishment. But God's gift made it possible for us to be acceptable to him, even though we have sinned many times.
text: Uwumbɔr aapiin aah ŋa timi pu na aa bi ke Adam aatunwanbir aah ŋa timi pu na. Adam aatunwanbirbaan pu, le binib aabɔr bii. Uninyaan ubaa u ye Yesu na pu, le Uwumbɔr di cha pinn titunwanbirdam pam, ki len ke baabɔr ŋan. Waapiin le na.

ref: Death ruled like a king because Adam had sinned. But that cannot compare with what Jesus Christ has done. God has treated us with undeserved grace, and he has accepted us because of Jesus. And so we will live and rule like kings.
text: Unibaan u bi yin u Adam na aatunwanbir pu, le nkun pii binib mɔmɔk. Unibaan Yesu Kristo na pu, le binib ga kan Uwumbɔr aaterm sakpen. U ga len ke baabɔr ŋan. Nima le ye waapiin. Bi ga li kpa limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na, ki kan linyaŋ.

ref: Everyone was going to be punished because Adam sinned. But because of the good thing that Christ has done, God accepts us and gives us the gift of life.
text: Unibaan aatunwanbir pu, le binib mɔmɔk aabɔr bii. Yesu aatunyaan pu, le Uwumbɔr ga len ke binib bimɔk gaa Yesu ki kii na aabɔr ŋan, ki ga tii bi limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: Adam disobeyed God and caused many others to be sinners. But Jesus obeyed him and will make many people acceptable to God.
text: Unibaan Adam aah nan yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na, nima le binib mɔmɔk aabɔr bii Uwumbɔr chee. Yesu aah nan kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na, nima le binib bimɔk gaa uma Yesu ki kii na aabɔr ŋan Uwumbɔr chee.

ref: The Law came, so that the full power of sin could be seen. Yet where sin was powerful, God's gift of undeserved grace was even more powerful.
text: Moses nan tuk binib Uwumbɔr aakaal. Nkaal ngbaan mɔk bi ke baatunwanbir wiir sakpen. Le titunwanbir aah wiir nin chee na Uwumbɔr aanimbaasaln wiir ki jer titunwanbir.

ref: Sin ruled by means of death. But God's gift of grace now rules, and God has accepted us because of Jesus Christ our Lord. This means that we will have eternal life.
text: Titunwanbir pu le binib kpo. Tidindaan Yesu Kristo pu, le Uwumbɔr san timi kinimbaak, ki len ke timi aabɔr ŋan, le ti kan limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: What should we say? Should we keep on sinning, so that God's gift of undeserved grace will show up even better?
text: Kina pu na, ti ga len kinye? Ti ga li beenin tun titunwanbir aan Uwumbɔr aanimbaasaln kpee ee? Taan li ŋani kina kpala.

ref: No, we should not! If we are dead to sin, how can we go on sinning?
text: Ti kpo ke titunwanbir taa ki li joo timi la. Ti yaa beenin tun titunwanbir kan, naa ŋan.

ref: When we were baptized, we died and were buried with Christ. We were baptized, so we would live a new life, as Christ was raised to life by the glory of God the Father.
text: Baah muin timi nnyun ni na, nima le mɔk ke ti kpo, le bi sub timi u chee. Uwumbɔr aapɔɔn pu le u fikr Kristo nkun ni. Waapɔɔn mu pu le ti kpa mbimbipɔm ki ŋani ni ŋan na.

ref: If we shared in Jesus' death by being baptized, we will be raised to life with him.
text: Ti ni u aah kpaan pu na, ti kpo ke waah kpo pu na. Ti mu ga fikr nkun ni, ke waah fikr pu na.

ref: We know that the persons we used to be were nailed to the cross with Jesus. This was done, so our sinful bodies would no longer be the slaves of sin.
text: Ti bee ke baah kpaa u ndɔpuinkoo pu na, bi kpaa timi aabimbikpok mu u chee, ke mbimbikpok mu kaa ŋan na taa ki li bi, aan ti taa ki li ye titunwanbir aanaagbiib.

ref: We know sin doesn't have power over dead people.
text: Unii u kpo na nyan titunwanbir ni.

ref: As surely as we died with Christ, we believe we will also live with him.
text: Taah kpo Kristo chee na, ti ŋa naadii ke ti ga li kpa limɔfal u chee.

ref: We know that death no longer has any power over Christ. He died and was raised to life, never again to die.
text: Ti nyi ke waah fikr nkun ni na, waan ki kpo. Nkun aa ki kpa mpɔɔn u chee.

ref: When Christ died, he died for sin once and for all. But now he is alive, and he lives only for God.
text: Waah kpo na, u kpo ke u kuln titunwanbir nfum mubaa, aan titunwanbir taa ki li joo timi. Waah kpa limɔfal dandana wee na, u bi ke u nyuŋ Uwumbɔr la.

ref: In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to the power of sin. But Christ Jesus has given life to you, and you live for God.
text: Kina pu na, ni mu li nyi ke ni kpo ke titunwanbir taa ki li joo nimi la. Naah kpaan Yesu Kristo chee pu na, le ni mu kpa limɔfal ke ni nyuŋ Uwumbɔr.

ref: Don't let sin rule your body. After all, your body is bound to die, so don't obey its desires
text: Nima pu na, ni taa ki cha titunwanbir li joo nimi aawon ti ga kpo na, ki taa ki kii tii tiwon aah ban pu na.

ref: or let any part of it become a slave of evil. Give yourselves to God, as people who have been raised from death to life. Make every part of your body a slave that pleases God.
text: Ni taa di nimi aawon tii titunwanbir, ki taa tun lituln li kaa ŋan na. Ni di nibaa tii Uwumbɔr, ke binib bi fikr nkun ni na, ki di nimi aawon tii Uwumbɔr, ke ni tun lituln li ŋan na ki tii u.

ref: Don't let sin keep ruling your lives. You are ruled by God's undeserved grace and not by the Law. Slaves Who Do What Pleases God
text: Nkaal aa ki joo nimi. Uwumbɔr aanimbaasaln le joo nimi. Nima le titunwanbir aan ki li ye nimi aadindaan. Li ye mbimbinyaan aanaagbiib man

ref: What does all this mean? Does it mean we are free to sin, because we are ruled by God's gift of undeserved grace and not by the Law? Certainly not!
text: Nkaal aah kaa ki joo timi aan Uwumbɔr aanimbaasaln joo timi na, ti ga tun titunwanbir aa? Taan ŋa kina kpala.

ref: Don't you know that you are slaves of anyone you obey? You can be slaves of sin and die, or you can be obedient slaves of God and be acceptable to him.
text: Aa yaa di aabaa tii unii aan ki kii waamɔb kan, aa ye waanaagbiija la. Naa bee kina aa? Aa yaa kii tii titunwanbir kan, aa ye titunwanbir aanaagbiija la, le ki ga kpo. Aa yaa kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb kan, u ga bui ke saabɔr ŋan.

ref: You used to be slaves of sin. But I thank God that with all your heart you followed the example set forth in the teaching you received.
text: N‑yoonn mubaa, ni nan ye titunwanbir aanaagbiib la. Ti dooni Uwumbɔr sakpen, ke baah mɔk nimi waasan pu na, ni dii nsan ngbaan nisui mɔmɔk ni,

ref: Now you are set free from sin and are slaves who please God.
text: ki nya ni titunwanbir aanaagbiir ni, ki ŋa litunyaan aanaagbiib.

ref: I am using these everyday examples, because in some ways you are still weak. You used to let the different parts of your body be slaves of your evil thoughts. But now you must make every part of your body serve God, so that you will belong completely to him.
text: M di binibɔm aabimbin ŋaŋ Uwumbɔr aabɔr ke ni bee maah len pu na aatataa mbamɔm la. Ni nan joo nimi aawon tun tijɔŋ aatuln, ni titunwanbir aabɔŋ mɔmɔk la. Dandana wee, ni di nimi aawon tun lituln li ŋan na man, aan ki ŋa binib bi bi chain na.

ref: When you were slaves of sin, you didn't have to please God.
text: Naah nan ye titunwanbir aanaagbiib na, nitafal aa nan bi litunyaan ni.

ref: But what good did you receive from the things you did? All you have to show for them is your shame, and they lead to death.
text: Ni yaa teer naah tun titunwanbir ti na kan, ni jinni nimi inimɔɔn dandana wee la. Tinyoor nan bi titunwanbir ngbaan ni ii? Aayii. Titunwanbir ngbaan aadoon ye nkun la.

ref: Now you have been set free from sin, and you are God's slaves. This will make you holy and will lead you to eternal life.
text: Uwumbɔr nyan nimi titunwanbir aanaagbiir ni la. Dandana wee, ni ye uma Uwumbɔr aanaagbiib la. Nimi aanyoor ye mbimbin mu bi chain na la. Naadoon ga li ye limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: Sin pays off with death. But God's gift is eternal life given by Jesus Christ our Lord.
text: Titunwanbir aapar ye nkun la. Tidindaan Yesu Kristo pu le Uwumbɔr aapiin ye limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: My friends, you surely understand enough about law to know that laws only have power over people who are alive.
text: Nnaabitiib, ni mɔmɔk nyi nkaal aah bi pu na. Nima le ga cha ni bee maah ga len pu na aatataa. Nkaal dii unii buyoonn u bi na baanja la. U yaa kpo kan, nkaal aa ki dii u.

ref: For example, the Law says that a man's wife must remain his wife as long as he lives. But once her husband is dead, she is free
text: Nkaal pu le upii u kpa chal na ye uchal yoo n‑yoonn mumɔk uchal bi na. Uchal yaa kpo kan, nkaal mu len ke u ye uchal yoo na aa ki dii u.

ref: to marry someone else. However, if she goes off with another man while her husband is still alive, she is said to be unfaithful.
text: Upii yaa ban uja uken buyoonn uchal bi na kan, bi ga len ke u ye upiidagoor la. Uchal yaa kpo kan, nkaal ngbaan aa ki dii u. U yaa mɔn uja uken kan, waa ye upiidagoor.

ref: That is how it is with you, my friends. You are now part of the body of Christ and are dead to the power of the Law. You are free to belong to Christ, who was raised to life so we could serve God.
text: Nnaabitiib, nimi aabɔr mu bi kina la. Kristo aah nan kpo ndɔpuinkoo pu na, ni mu nan kpo; nkaal aa ki dii nimi. Ni kpaan Kristo u fikr nkun ni na chee la, le ki dii Uwumbɔr aasan.

ref: When we thought only of ourselves, the Law made us have sinful desires. It made every part of our bodies into slaves who are doomed to die.
text: Taah kaa nan dii Uwumbɔr buyoonn na, tisui nan gee Uwumbɔr aakaal aah kɔ pu na, ki cha ti tun titunwanbir ki dii nkun aasan.

ref: But the Law no longer rules over us. We are like dead people, and it cannot have any power over us. Now we can serve God in a new way by obeying his Spirit, and not in the old way by obeying the written Law. The Battle with Sin
text: Dandana wee, taah kpo na, nkaal na aa ki dii timi, ki mu aa ki joo timi tinaagbiir. Le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan tii timi mbimbipɔm, ke ti tun lituln tii Uwumbɔr. Nkaal na aa ki joo timi. Nkaal ni titunwanbir

ref: Does this mean that the Law is sinful? Certainly not! But if it had not been for the Law, I would not have known what sin is really like. For example, I would not have known what it means to want something that belongs to someone else, unless the Law had told me not to do this.
text: Nima pu na, ti ga len ke Moses aakaal aa ŋan aa? Mu ŋan. Nkaal na yaa kaa ba bi kan, maa ba ga bee titunwanbir. Nkaal na yaa kaa ba len ke “Taa li kpa iniman” kan, maa ba ga bee ke iniman ye titunwanbir.

ref: It was sin that used this command as a way of making me have all kinds of desires. But without the Law, sin is dead.
text: Nkaal aah len kina na, le titunwanbir ti bi nsui ni na yii nkaal ngbaan, ki cha m kpa iniman aabɔŋ aabɔŋ. Nkaal yaa kaa bi kan, titunwanbir aa fu.

ref: Before I knew about the Law, I was alive. But as soon as I heard that command, sin came to life,
text: N‑yoonn mubaa m nan bi, kaa nyi nkaal aatataa mbamɔm. Buyoonn m bee nkaal aatataa mbamɔm na, le titunwanbir fikr nsui ni. Le m bee ke m ŋeer nkun.

ref: and I died. The very command that was supposed to bring life to me, instead brought death.
text: Uwumbɔr nan tii timi waakaal ke ti dii mu, aan ki kan limɔfal. Le m bee ke maah kaa ŋmaa joo waakaal mɔmɔk na, m ŋeer nkun.

ref: Sin used this command to trick me, and because of it I died.
text: Nkaal pu le titunwanbir ti bi nsui ni na nan kpa nsan ki ŋmann mi, ki cha m ŋeer nkun.

ref: Still, the Law and its commands are holy and correct and good.
text: Uwumbɔr aakaal bi chain la. Uwumbɔr aah tuk timi ke ti ŋa pu na le bi chain, ki bi mbamɔm, ki ŋan.

ref: Am I saying something good caused my death? Certainly not! It was sin that killed me by using something good. Now we can see how terrible and evil sin really is.
text: Waakaal mu ŋan na le ku mi ii? Aayii. Titunwanbir le ku mi. Nkaal mu ŋan na pu, le titunwanbir ku mi, ki cha ti bee ke titunwanbir aa ŋan. Nkaal na le mɔk timi titunwanbir aah bir sakpen pu na.

ref: We know that the Law is spiritual. But I am merely a human, and I have been sold as a slave to sin.
text: Ti bee ke Uwumbɔr aakaal mɔk timi Uwumbɔr aah ban pu na. M mu aa ŋani kina; ba pu? m ye titunwanbir aanaagbiija la.

ref: In fact, I don't understand why I act the way I do. I don't do what I know is right. I do the things I hate.
text: Maah ŋani pu na, maa kii kina nsui ni. Maah kaa gee ke m li ŋani tiwan ni na, m ŋani nima la. Maah nan tiwan ni na, nima le m tee ŋani.

ref: Although I don't do what I know is right, I agree that the Law is good.
text: M yaa ŋani maah kaa gee ke m li ŋani tiwan ni na kan, nima le mɔk ke m kii ke Uwumbɔr aakaal ŋan.

ref: So I am not the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
text: Naa ye ke min le ŋani kina, titunwanbir ti bi nsui ni na le cha m ŋani.

ref: I know that my selfish desires won't let me do anything that is good. Even when I want to do right, I cannot.
text: M bee ke tiwan ni ŋan na aa bi maabimbikpok ni; m ban ke m tun lituln li ŋan na, kaa ŋmaa tun.

ref: Instead of doing what I know is right, I do wrong.
text: Maah ban m tun litunyaan li na, maa tun kina. Maah kaa ban m tun titunwanbir ti na, m tun tima la.

ref: And so, if I don't do what I know is right, I am no longer the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
text: M yaa tun maah kaa gee m tun pu na kan, naa ye ke min le tun kina, titunwanbir ti bi nsui ni na le cha m tun.

ref: The Law has shown me that something in me keeps me from doing what I know is right.
text: Naah ye pu na, m yaa ban m tun lituln li ŋan na kan, titunwanbir bi m chee la.

ref: With my whole heart I agree with the Law of God.
text: M gee Uwumbɔr aakaal nsui ni.

ref: But in every part of me I discover something fighting against my mind, and it makes me a prisoner of sin that controls everything I do.
text: M mu kan nkaal muken maawon ni. Nkaal ngbaan jaa Uwumbɔr aakaal mu bi nsui ni na kijaak la. Nima le titunwanbir aakaal i bi maawon ni na joo mi tinaagbiir.

ref: What a miserable person I am. Who will rescue me from this body that is doomed to die?
text: M kpa kinimbaak. Titunwanbir bi tiwon tee ni, ki ga ku mi. Ŋma ga nyan mi titunwanbir ngbaan ni?

ref: Thank God! Jesus Christ will rescue me. So with my mind I serve the Law of God, although my selfish desires make me serve the law of sin.
text: M dooni Uwumbɔr u nyan mi titunwanbir ngbaan ni, Tidindaan Yesu Kristo pu na. Mma kan, maalandak baanja le dii Uwumbɔr aakaal. Maabimbikpok dii titunwanbir aakaal la.

ref: If you belong to Christ Jesus, you won't be punished.
text: Nima pu na, Uwumbɔr aan len ke binib bi kpaan Yesu Kristo chee na aabɔr bii.

ref: The Holy Spirit will give you life that comes from Christ Jesus and will set you free from sin and death.
text: Taah kpaan Yesu Kristo chee na, le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aapɔɔn tii timi limɔfal; Nfuur Nyaan aapɔɔn ngbaan le nyan mi titunwanbir ni nkun aapɔɔn ni.

ref: The Law of Moses cannot do this, because our selfish desires make the Law weak. But God set you free when he sent his own Son to be like us sinners and to be a sacrifice for our sin. God used Christ's body to condemn sin.
text: Nkaal aan ŋmaa ŋa kina; ba pu? binib aa kpa mpɔɔn ke bi joo nkaal ngbaan. Le Uwumbɔr ŋa waakaal aah kaa ŋmaa ŋa pu na; timi aatunwanbir pu le u nan tun ni Ujapɔɔn Yesu dulnyaa wee ni, ke u di tiwon ti naahn timi titunwanbirdam aawon na bii titunwanbir ti bi tisui ni na aapɔɔn,

ref: He did this, so that we would do what the Law commands by obeying the Spirit instead of our own desires.
text: ki tii timi bi dii Waafuur Nyaan kaa ki dii mbimbikpok na mpɔɔn ke ti li dii waakaal mbamɔm.

ref: People who are ruled by their desires think only of themselves. Everyone who is ruled by the Holy Spirit thinks about spiritual things.
text: Binib bi dii mbimbikpok na, bitafal bi mbimbikpok aabɔr ni la. Binib bi dii Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan na, bitafal bi Nfuur Nyaan aabɔr ni la.

ref: If our minds are ruled by our desires, we will die. But if our minds are ruled by the Spirit, we will have life and peace.
text: Binib bi aatafal bi mbimbikpok aabɔr ni na ga kpo la. Binib bi aatafal bi Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aabɔr ni na ga kan limɔfal, ni nsuudoon.

ref: Our desires fight against God, because they do not and cannot obey God's laws.
text: Binib bi aatafal bi mbimbikpok aabɔr ni na, bi ye Uwumbɔr aadim la; ba pu? baa dii waakaal, ki mu aa ŋmaa dii mu.

ref: If we follow our desires, we cannot please God.
text: Binib bi dii mbimbikpok aah ban pu na aan ŋmaa piir Uwumbɔr aasui.

ref: You are no longer ruled by your desires, but by God's Spirit, who lives in you. People who don't have the Spirit of Christ in them don't belong to him.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan yaa bi ni ni kan, naa dii mbimbikpok aah ban pu na, ni dii Nfuur Nyaan aah ban pu na la. Kristo Aafuur Nyaan yaa kaa bi unii ni kan, udaan ngbaan aa ye Kristo yoo.

ref: But Christ lives in you. So you are alive because God has accepted you, even though your bodies must die because of your sins.
text: Titunwanbir pu, le nimi aawon ga kpo. Kristo yaa bi ni ni kan, Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan tii nimi limɔfal; ba pu? u len ke nimi aabɔr ŋan.

ref: If you do, you will die. But you will live, if by the help of God's Spirit you say “No” to your desires.
text: Ni yaa dii unibɔn aabimbin aah ban pu na kan, ni ga kpo la. Ni yaa kuln nimi aawon aatunwanbir, Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aapɔɔn pu kan, ni ga li kpa limɔfal li kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: Only those people who are led by God's Spirit are his children.
text: Binib bimɔk dii Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan aah ban pu na, bima le ye Uwumbɔr aabim.

ref: God's Spirit doesn't make us slaves who are afraid of him. Instead, we become his children and call him our Father.
text: Nfuur Nyaan mu Uwumbɔr tii nimi na, mu aa joo nimi tinaagbiir ke ni san ijawaan. Waafuur Nyaan le ŋa nimi waabim, le ki cha ti yin u ke “Nte.”

ref: God's Spirit makes us sure that we are his children.
text: Waafuur Nyaan le kpaan timi aawiin chee, le ki ji seeraa ke ti ye Uwumbɔr aabim.

ref: His Spirit lets us know that together with Christ we will be given what God has promised. We will also share in the glory of Christ, because we have suffered with him. A Wonderful Future for God's People
text: Taah ye Uwumbɔr aabim na, ti ga kan Uwumbɔr aah di tiwanyaan ni bil kiir timi paacham na. Ti ni Kristo ga kpaan kan tiwanyaan ngbaan. Ti yaa ji falaa u pu kan, ti ni u ga nan kpaan ji mmɔɔn paacham. N‑yoonn mu choo na aanyuŋ

ref: I am sure what we are suffering now cannot compare with the glory that will be shown to us.
text: M nyi ke dandana aafalaa aan ŋmaa ŋaŋ mpopiin mu ti ga nan kan mu paacham na.

ref: In fact, all creation is eagerly waiting for God to show who his children are.
text: Tiwan ni Uwumbɔr naan ni na mɔmɔk aanimbil man ke ni kan bundaln Uwumbɔr ga nyan waabim mpaan pu na.

ref: Meanwhile, creation is confused, but not because it wants to be confused. God made it this way in the hope
text: Buyoonn Adam nan tun titunwanbir na, Uwumbɔr nan len ke tiwan ni u naan ni na, ni ga li bi, ki bi fam la. Waageehn pu, le u len kina. Naa ye tiwan ni u naan ni na aageehn.

ref: that creation would be set free from decay and would share in the glorious freedom of his children.
text: Uwumbɔr mu tii tiwan ni u naan ni na limakl ke ni ga ŋa tiwan ni kaan bur na, ki kan lifuur nyaan ke Uwumbɔr aabim aah kan pu na.

ref: We know that all creation is still groaning and is in pain, like a woman about to give birth.
text: Ti nyi ke Uwumbɔr aah naan tiwan nimɔk na wu ke imalween aah wu pu na, ki du ki nan saa dandana.

ref: The Spirit makes us sure about what we will be in the future. But now we groan silently, while we wait for God to show that we are his children. This means that our bodies will also be set free.
text: Naa ye tiwannaankaan baanja le wu; timi bi Uwumbɔr puen tii timi Waafuur Nyaan na, ti mu du tisui ni, ki kii bundaln Uwumbɔr ga mɔk ke ti sil ye waabim, ki ga tii timi tiwon ti kaan kpo na.

ref: And this hope is what saves us. But if we already have what we hope for, there is no need to keep on hoping.
text: Taah ŋmar pu na, le ti kpa limakl. Unii yaa kpa limakl ke u ga kan tiwan kan, ni mɔk ke waa kee kan la. U yaa kan ni kan, waan ki li kpa limakl ni pu.

ref: However, we hope for something we have not yet seen, and we patiently wait for it.
text: Tɔ, ti yaa kpa limakl ke ti ga kan tiwan ni tinimbil aa waa ni na kan, le ti ga li kpa limɔr ki kii bundaln ti ga kan ni na.

ref: In certain ways we are weak, but the Spirit is here to help us. For example, when we don't know what to pray for, the Spirit prays for us in ways that cannot be put into words.
text: Le Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan ter timi, timi aadabur ni. Taa nyi taah ga mee u mbamɔm pu na, le Waafuur Nyaan mee u tii timi, ki du, ubaa aah kaa ŋmaa len pu na.

ref: All of our thoughts are known to God. He can understand what is in the mind of the Spirit, as the Spirit prays for God's people.
text: Uwumbɔr u lik binib aasui ni aah bi pu na nyi Waafuur Nyaan aalandak aah bi pu na; ba pu? Nfuur Nyaan mee u tii waanib waah ban pu na.

ref: We know that God is always at work for the good of everyone who loves him. They are the ones God has chosen for his purpose,
text: Ti nyi ke tiwan nimɔk pii timi na, Uwumbɔr le cha ni mɔmɔk kpaln tiwan ni ŋan na ki tii binib bi gee u na. Waageehn pu le u nan yin bi.

ref: and he has always known who his chosen ones would be. He had decided to let them become like his own Son, so his Son would be the first of many children.
text: U nan nyi binib bimɔk ga kii tii u na, le ki nan nyan bi, ke bi kpaln Ujapɔɔn Yesu Kristo aah bi pu na, aan u li ye njan aabo, naabitiib pam ponn ni.

ref: God then accepted the people he had already decided to choose, and he has shared his glory with them. God's Love
text: Binib bi Uwumbɔr nyan bi na, le u yin bi. Binib bi u yin bi na, le u len ke baabɔr ŋan, ki nyuŋ bi. Uwumbɔr aah gee timi pu na

ref: What can we say about all this? If God is on our side, can anyone be against us?
text: Uwumbɔr aah ŋa kina mɔmɔk na, ti ga len kinye? Uwumbɔr aah si tichaŋ ni na, ubaa aan ŋmaa ŋa timi nibaa.

ref: God did not keep back his own Son, but he gave him for us. If God did this, won't he freely give us everything else?
text: Uwumbɔr aa yii ke waan tii timi Ujapɔɔn. U nan di Ujapɔɔn ŋa binib aaŋaal ni ke u ti kpo ti mɔmɔk aatunwanbir pu la. Waah tii timi Ujapɔɔn na, u ga ki tii timi tiwan mɔmɔk ki kpee.

ref: If God says his chosen ones are acceptable to him, can anyone bring charges against them?
text: Ŋma ga ŋmaa galn binib bi Uwumbɔr nyan bi na? Uwumbɔr ubaa len ke baabɔr ŋan.

ref: Or can anyone condemn them? No indeed! Christ died and was raised to life, and now he is at God's right side, speaking to him for us.
text: Nima le ubaa aan ŋmaa galn timi. Yesu Kristo nan kpo ti pu, ki fikr nkun ni, ki bi Uwumbɔr aaŋangii wɔb, ki mee u ki tii timi.

ref: Can anything separate us from the love of Christ? Can trouble, suffering, and hard times, or hunger and nakedness, or danger and death?
text: Ba ga ŋmaa nyan timi Kristo u gee timi na aaŋaal ni? Falaa aa? Tibɔr aa? Limukl aa? Nkon aa? Igiin aa? Linimaln aa? Nkun aa? Aayii.

ref: It is exactly as the Scriptures say, “For you we face death all day long. We are like sheep on their way to be butchered.”
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Sin pu le bi ku timi iwiin mɔmɔk, le ti naahn ipiih i bi ban bi ti kɔr i na la.”

ref: In everything we have won more than a victory because of Christ who loves us.
text: Tɔ, Yesu Kristo u gee timi na aapɔɔn pu, le ti kan linyaŋ kookoo.

ref: I am a follower of Christ, and the Holy Spirit is a witness to my conscience. So I tell the truth and I am not lying when I say
text: Tɔ, maah ye Kristo aanii na, m len mbamɔn la. Maa gee nnyamɔn. Maalandak ni Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan ji seeraa ke m len mbamɔn la.

ref: my heart is broken and I am in great sorrow.
text: M kpa mpombiin sakpen. Nsui bii n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, mmaal aanaabitiib Juu yaab pu la.

ref: I would gladly be placed under God's curse and be separated from Christ for the good of my own people.
text: M ga li ŋmaa ban ke m bee fam Kristo chee, bima taa bee.

ref: They are the descendants of Israel, and they are also God's chosen people. God showed them his glory. He made agreements with them and gave them his Law. The temple is theirs and so are the promises that God made to them.
text: Bi ye Israel yaab la. Uwumbɔr nan ŋa bi waabim, ki nyuŋ bi, ki puu tipuur tii bi, ki tii bi waakaal, ki mɔk bi baah ga li dooni u pu na, ki bui bi waah ga ŋa tinyoor pu ki ŋa bi pu na.

ref: They have those famous ancestors, who were also the ancestors of the Christ. I pray that God, who rules over all, will be praised forever! Amen.
text: Biyaajatiib ye tiyaajaninkpiib la. Kristo aah nan ŋa unibɔn na, u nan ye bi ponn ni ubaa la. Uma le yeh mpɔɔn mɔmɔk. Cha ti pak Uwumbɔr n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Amii.

ref: It cannot be said that God broke his promise. After all, not all of the people of Israel are the true people of God.
text: Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ti tii Israel yaab na, maa len ke waa gbiin tipuur ngbaan. Bi ye Israel aayaabitiib la. Ni mu aa ye bi mɔmɔk le ye Israel yaab bamɔm.

ref: In fact, when God made the promise to Abraham, he meant only Abraham's descendants by his son Isaac. God was talking only about Isaac when he promised
text: Nima le mɔk ke Abraham aayaabitiib ngem aa ye Uwumbɔr aabim. Mbim bi Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur ke Abraham ga maa na, bima le ye uyaabitiib bamɔm.

ref: Sarah, “At this time next year I will return, and you will already have a son.”
text: Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur tii u ke ni yaa nan ŋeer kan, u ga dan u chee, le upuu Sara ga maa ubijabo.

ref: Don't forget what happened to the twin sons of Isaac and Rebekah.
text: Naa ye nimina baanja. Rebeka aabijabim mulee nan kpa te ubaa, u ye tiyaaja Aisak la.

ref: Even before they were born or had done anything good or bad, the Lord told Rebekah that her older son would serve the younger one. The Lord said this to show he makes his own choices and it wasn't because of anything either of them had done.
text: Le Uwumbɔr nan bui Rebeka ke ubo u ye uwaatiir na ga jer ukpel. Buyoonn Uwumbɔr bui u kina na, waa nan kee ma mbim ngbaan. Baa nan kee ŋa ni ŋan na, bee ni kaa ŋan na. Uwumbɔr nyan mbim mulee ngbaan ponn ni ubaa, waageehn pu, naa ye baatuln pu. Nima le mɔk ke Uwumbɔr aageehn pu le u nyan waah ban unii u na.

ref: That's why the Scriptures say that the Lord liked Jacob more than Esau.
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ponn ni ke u len ke u gee Jakob ki jer Esɔ.

ref: The Lord told Moses that he has pity and mercy on anyone he wants to.
text: U nan bui Moses ke binib bi u ban u san bi kinimbaak na, u ga san bi kinimbaak la.

ref: Everything then depends on God's mercy and not on what people want or do.
text: Naa ye binib aageehn pu, kaa ye baatuln pu; Uwumbɔr aanimbaasaln pu, le u san bi kinimbaak.

ref: In the Scriptures the Lord says to the king of Egypt, “I let you become king, so that I could show you my power and be praised by all people on earth.”
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke Uwumbɔr nan bui Ubɔr Faro, “M ŋa si ubɔr ke m mɔk binib maah kpa mpɔɔn ki chiin si pu na, aan maayimbil nya paacham, dulnyaa aapepel mɔmɔk ni.”

ref: Everything depends on what God decides to do, and he can either have pity on people or make them stubborn. God's Anger and Mercy
text: Nima le binib bi u ban u san bi kinimbaak na, u san bi kinimbaak. Binib bi u ban ke u cha bi gaa biyil na, u cha bi gaa la. Uwumbɔr aaŋuul, ni waanimbaasaln

ref: Someone may ask, “How can God blame us, if he makes us behave in the way he wants us to?”
text: Nibaakan, aa ga baa mi, “Ni yaa ye kina kan, ba pu Uwumbɔr galn binib? Ŋma ga ŋmaa yii waageehn?”

ref: But, my friend, I ask, “Who do you think you are to question God? Does the clay have the right to ask the potter why he shaped it the way he did?
text: Njɔ, aa ye ŋma ki kpak Uwumbɔr? Tiwanaankaan aan baa unii u naan ni na, “Ba ŋa aa naan mi kina?”

ref: Doesn't a potter have the right to make a fancy bowl and a plain bowl out of the same lump of clay?”
text: Uyakmaal ga ŋmaa yakr tiyakr waageehn pu, ki di tibaa ti maa lisil aasambil, ki di tiken maa lisambil li kaa ye lisil aasambil na.

ref: God wanted to show his anger and reveal his power against everyone who deserved to be destroyed. But instead, he patiently put up with them.
text: Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu na, ni bi kina la. U nan ban ke u mɔk binib ke u gee liŋuul titunwanbir pu, ki ban ke bi bee waah kpa mpɔɔn pu na. Nima le u ji limɔr pam binib bi ŋa u liŋuul ki ŋeer ntafadaan na pu.

ref: He did this by showing how glorious he is when he has pity on the people he has chosen to share in his glory.
text: U mu ban ke binib bee waah ŋan sakpen pu na, ki san timi kinimbaak, ki ŋa timi mpopiin pam. U nan naan timi ke u ŋa timi kina la,

ref: Whether Jews or Gentiles, we are those chosen ones,
text: ki yin timi bi ye Juu yaab na, ni binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu.

ref: just as the Lord says in the book of Hosea, “Although they are not my people, I will make them my people. I will treat with love those nations that have never been loved.
text: Ni ŋmee Hosea aagbaŋ ni ke Uwumbɔr bui ke, “Binib bi kaa nan ye maanib na, m ga yin bi maanib. Ŋinibol ŋi maa nan gee ŋi na, m ga yin ŋi maanigeehm la.

ref: “Once they were told, ‘You are not my people.’ But in that very place they will be called children of the living God.”
text: Baah nan tuk bi ke baa ye maanib nin chee na, nima chee le bi ga yin bi ke min Uwumbɔr u fu na aabim.”

ref: And this is what the prophet Isaiah said about the people of Israel, “The people of Israel are as many as the grains of sand along the beach. But only a few who are left will be saved.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Aisaya nan len Israel yaab aabɔr; u nan len ke Israel yaab wiir ke nnyusakpem aatambol aah wiir pu na, le bi ponn ni, binib siib baanja ga ŋmar;

ref: The Lord will be quick and sure to do on earth what he has warned he will do.”
text: ba pu? Uwumbɔr ga daa dulnyaa aanib aatafal, waah nan len pu na, kaan taan.

ref: Isaiah also said, “If the Lord All-Powerful had not spared some of our descendants, we would have been destroyed like the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah.” Israel and the Good News
text: Ni bi ke Aisaya aah nan ki len pu na ke, “Uwumbɔr Mpɔɔnsakpiindaan yaa kaa ba gur timi yaabitiib siib kan, ti mɔmɔk ba ga kuln ke Sodom aatiŋ aanib ni Gomora aatiŋ aanib aah nan kuln pu na la.” Israel yaab ni tibɔnyaan ngbaan

ref: What does all of this mean? It means that the Gentiles were not trying to be acceptable to God, but they found that he would accept them if they had faith.
text: Nima pu na, ti ga len kinye? Binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aanimbil aa nan man ke Uwumbɔr len ke baabɔr ŋan. Dandana wee, baah gaa Yesu ki kii na, nima le Uwumbɔr len ke baabɔr ŋan.

ref: It also means that the people of Israel were not acceptable to God. And why not? It was because they were trying to be acceptable by obeying the Law instead of by having faith in God. The people of Israel fell over the stone that makes people stumble,
text: ba pu? baa gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii. Bi dak ke baatuln pu le Uwumbɔr ga len ke baabɔr ŋan. Bi yii Yesu Kristo le ki lir;

ref: just as God says in the Scriptures, “Look! I am placing in Zion a stone to make people stumble and fall. But those who have faith in that one will never be disappointed.”
text: bi gbeer lifaakuul li Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ len laabɔr na ke, “U di lifaakuul bil Sionn aatiŋ ni. Binib ga gbeer li ki lir. Le unii umɔk gaa u ki kii na aan ji inimɔɔn.”

ref: Dear friends, my greatest wish and my prayer to God is for the people of Israel to be saved.
text: Nnaabitiib, m mee Uwumbɔr tii maanib Israel yaab ke bi ŋmar. M ban kina le nsui mɔmɔk.

ref: I know they love God, but they don't understand
text: M ga ŋmaa ŋa bi seeraa ke binimbil man Uwumbɔr aatuln pu. Bi mu aa bee u mbamɔm.

ref: what makes people acceptable to him. So they refuse to trust God, and they try to be acceptable by obeying the Law.
text: Baa nyi Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu aan ki len ke binib aabɔr ŋan u chee na. Bi nan ban ke bi dii nkaal aan ki ŋmar, ki yii Uwumbɔr aah ŋa pu ki cha binib aabɔr ŋan u chee na.

ref: But Christ makes the Law no longer necessary for those who become acceptable to God by faith. Anyone Can Be Saved
text: Kristo fuu ni ke binib bi gaa u ki kii na aabɔr li ŋan. Naa ye ke baah dii nkaal pu na le cha baabɔr ŋan. Uwumbɔr ban ke u gaa binib mɔmɔk lii

ref: Moses said a person could become acceptable to God by obeying the Law. He did this when he wrote, “If you want to live, you must do all the Law commands.”
text: Moses nan ŋmee ke unii yaa kii nkaal aah mɔk pu na kan, Uwumbɔr ga len ke waabɔr ŋan. U nan ŋmee ke “Unii yaa ŋa nkaal aah mɔk pu na kan, u ga kan limɔfal.”

ref: But people whose faith makes them acceptable to God will never ask, “Who will go up to heaven to bring Christ down?”
text: Timi bi gaa Yesu ki kii na, Uwumbɔr len ke timi aabɔr ŋan. Nima pu le ti len ke, “Taa baa aabaa aasui ni ke, ‘Ŋma ga buen paacham u ti li joo ni Kristo?’

ref: Neither will they ask, “Who will go down into the world of the dead to raise him to life?”
text: ki taa baa ke, ‘Ŋma ga buen bitekpiib do ki ti fikr Kristo nkun ni?’”

ref: All who are acceptable because of their faith simply say, “The message is as near as your mouth or your heart.” And this is the same message we preach about faith.
text: Ti len ke, “Uwumbɔr aaliin aa daa aa chee. I bi aamɔb ni, ni aasui ni.” Iliin ngbaan le ti mooni ke aa gaa Yesu ki kii.

ref: So you will be saved, if you honestly say, “Jesus is Lord,” and if you believe with all your heart that God raised him from death.
text: Aa yaa len binib aanimbil ni ke Yesu le ye Aadindaan, ki yaa ŋa naadii aasui ni ke Uwumbɔr fikr u nkun ni kan, aa ga ŋmar.

ref: God will accept you and save you, if you truly believe this and tell it to others.
text: Ti gaa u ki kii tisui ni la, nima le Uwumbɔr len ke timi aabɔr ŋan. Ti len binib aanimbil ni ke ti gaa u ki kii, nima le ti ŋmar.

ref: The Scriptures say no one who has faith will be disappointed,
text: Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ len ke unii umɔk gaa u ki kii na aan ji inimɔɔn.

ref: no matter if that person is a Jew or a Gentile. There is only one Lord, and he is generous to everyone who asks for his help.
text: Binib bi ye Juu yaab na, ni binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mɔmɔk kpaan la. Uwumbɔr le ye bi mɔmɔk Aadindaan, ki ŋa tinyoor sakpen ŋa binib bimɔk mee u ke bi ŋmar na pu.

ref: All who call out to the Lord will be saved.
text: Waagbaŋ len ke unii umɔk mee Uwumbɔr ke u gaa bi lii na kan ga ŋmar.

ref: How can people have faith in the Lord and ask him to save them, if they have never heard about him? And how can they hear, unless someone tells them?
text: Bi yaa kaa gaa u ki kii kan, bi ga ŋa kinye aan ki mee u ke u gaa bi lii? Bi yaa kaa ŋun waaliin kan, bi ga ŋa kinye aan ki gaa u ki kii? Unii yaa kaa mooni waaliin kan, bi ga ŋa kinye aan ki ŋun?

ref: And how can anyone tell them without being sent by the Lord? The Scriptures say it is a beautiful sight to see even the feet of someone coming to preach the good news.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa kaa tun bi ke bi ti moon waaliin kan, bi ga ŋa kinye aan ki moon i? Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Binib bi joo ni tibɔnyaan ti tii timi nsuudoon na, bi tii timi mpopiin pam.”

ref: Yet not everyone has believed the message. For example, the prophet Isaiah asked, “Lord, has anyone believed what we said?”
text: Tɔ, naa ye binib mɔmɔk le kii tii tibɔnyaan ngbaan. Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Aisaya nan baa ke, “Uwumbɔr, ŋma pak taah len pu na?”

ref: But am I saying that the people of Israel did not hear? No, I am not! The Scriptures say, “The message was told everywhere on earth. It was announced all over the world.”
text: Le m baa ke, “Israel yaab aa nan ŋun aa?” Mbamɔn, bi ŋun. Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Bineel mu tee chaa dulnyaa wee mɔmɔk ni, le kitiŋ kee mɔmɔk pu ŋun.”

ref: Did the people of Israel understand or not? Moses answered this question when he told that the Lord had said, “I will make Israel jealous of people who are a nation of nobodies. I will make them angry with people who don't understand a thing.”
text: M ki baa ke, “Israel yaab aa nan bee ee?” Bi bee. Njan Moses nan len ke Uwumbɔr len ke, “M ga ŋa litimbol li kaa ye tibaa na tinyoor, le ki cha nimi Israel yaab li kpa lipiipoln li pu. M ga ŋa litimbol li aanib ye bijɔrb na tinyoor, le ki cha ni gee liŋuul bi pu.”

ref: Isaiah was fearless enough to tell that the Lord had said, “I was found by people who were not looking for me. I appeared to the ones who were not asking about me.”
text: Aisaya mu nan kpa lipobil pam ki len ke Uwumbɔr len ke, “Binib bi kaa chuun ban mi na kan mi la. M di mbaa mɔk binib bi kaa baa maabɔr na.”

ref: And Isaiah said about the people of Israel, “All day long the Lord has reached out to people who are stubborn and refuse to obey.”
text: Israel yaab ma kan, Uwumbɔr len baabɔr ke, “Iwiin mɔmɔk m kai ŋŋaal ki yin binib bi yii mi kaa kii maamɔb na.”

ref: Am I saying that God has turned his back on his people? Certainly not! I am one of the people of Israel, and I myself am a descendant of Abraham from the tribe of Benjamin.
text: Nima pu le m baa ke, “Uwumbɔr yii waanib Israel yaab aa?” Naa bi kina kpala. Min Pɔɔl mbaa ye Israel yaab aanii la. M ye Abraham aayaabil, ki ye Benjaminn aanibol aanii la.

ref: God did not turn his back on his chosen people. Don't you remember reading in the Scriptures how Elijah complained to God about the people of Israel?
text: Uwumbɔr aa yii waanib bi u nan lee bi njan na. Ni bee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ aah len Elaija aabɔr pu na. Elaija nan galn Israel yaab Uwumbɔr chee,

ref: He said, “Lord, they killed your prophets and destroyed your altars. I am the only one left, and now they want to kill me.”
text: le ki bui ke, “Uwumbɔr, bi ku saabɔnabtiib, ki gbaa wii saatork aabimbin. Min baanja le gur saabɔnabtiib ponn ni. Le bi ban bi ku m mu.”

ref: This means that only a chosen few of the people of Israel found what all of them were searching for. And the rest of them were stubborn,
text: Kina kan, ni bi kinye? Israel yaab aah ban pu na, baa kan. Binib bi Uwumbɔr nyan bi na le kan. Bi gur na gaa biyil.

ref: It is the same way now. God treated the people of Israel with undeserved grace, and so a few of them are still his followers.
text: Ni bi kina le dandana wee. Israel yaab ponn ni, binib siib baanja le ŋmar. Uwumbɔr lee bi waanimbaasaln pu.

ref: This happened because of God's undeserved kindness and not because of anything they have done. It could not have happened except for God's gift of undeserved grace.
text: Waah lee bi waanimbaasaln pu na kan, naa ye baatuln pu le u lee bi. Ni yaa ye baatuln pu kan, waanimbaasaln aan ki li ye linimbaasaln bamɔnn.

ref: just as the Scriptures say, “God made them so stupid that their eyes are blind, and their ears are still deaf.”
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Uwumbɔr chuu nyan nlan biyil ni ke binimbil taa woln, bitafal mu taa ŋun, ki nan saa dandana wee.”

ref: Then David said, “Turn their meals into bait for a trap, so that they will stumble and be given what they deserve.
text: Ubɔr David mu nan len ke, “Cha baajikaar aajim kpaln gaawɔb, cha bi kan ntafadaan ki lir.

ref: Blindfold their eyes! Don't let them see. Bend their backs beneath a burden that will never be lifted.” Gentiles Will Be Saved
text: Cha binimbil li bɔɔn, aan bi taa li waa, ki cha bi kan falaa sakpen.”

ref: Do I mean that the people of Israel fell, never to get up again? Certainly not! Their failure made it possible for the Gentiles to be saved, and this will make the people of Israel jealous.
text: Nima pu le m baa ke: Juu yaab lir ke bi taa ki fii ii? Naa bi kina kpala. Baah lir na, nima le cha binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na ŋmar, aan Juu yaab li kpa lipiipoln bi pu.

ref: I am now speaking to you Gentiles, and as long as I am an apostle to you, I will take pride in my work.
text: Tɔ, m ga len nimi bi kaa ye Juu yaab na chee tibɔr. Uwumbɔr aah tun mi ke m tuk nimi waabɔr na, le m pak lituln ngbaan;

ref: I hope in this way to make some of my own people jealous enough to be saved.
text: ba pu? m ban ke maanibol Juu yaab kan naah ŋmar pu na, aan ki li ban ke bi mu ŋmar.

ref: When Israel rejected God, the rest of the people in the world were able to turn to him. So when God makes friends with Israel, it will be like bringing the dead back to life.
text: Uwumbɔr aah yii Juu yaab na, le u ni binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na kpaan kijɔtiik. U yaa ki gaa Juu yaab kan, ni ga li ye limɔfal le ki tii binib. Nkun aan ki li joo bi.

ref: If part of a batch of dough is made holy by being offered to God, then all of the dough is holy. If the roots of a tree are holy, the rest of the tree is holy too.
text: Tɔ, bi yaa di njan aaboroboro tii Uwumbɔr kan, ni mɔk ke boroboro umɔk gur na mu ye uyoo la. Bi yaa di busub aanyaan tii Uwumbɔr kan, ni mɔk ke ibon mu ye uyaan la.

ref: You Gentiles are like branches of a wild olive tree made to be part of a cultivated olive tree. You have taken the place of some branches that were cut away from it. And because of this, you enjoy the blessings that come from being part of that cultivated tree.
text: Uwumbɔr nan gaa gii busunyaan aabon ibaa, le ki di timoor ni aasub aabon ki di toŋ bu pu. Juu yaab bi ke busunyaan na la. Nimi bi kaa ye Juu yaab na bi ke timoor ni aasub aabon na. Le Uwumbɔr chuu nyan ni binib bibaa Juu yaab ponn ni, ki di nimi koon Juu yaab ponn ni, ke ni yakr baanyoor, ni baawanyaan.

ref: But don't think you are better than the branches that were cut away. Just remember you are not supporting the roots of this tree. Its roots are supporting you.
text: Nima pu na, ni taa li kpa kipupuk ke ni jer bi. Ni ga ŋa kinye ki li kpa kipupuk? Ni po ye ibon la. Naa joo inyaan, inyaan le joo nimi. Juu yaab pu le ni ŋmar, naa ye nimi pu le cha Juu yaab ŋmar.

ref: Maybe you think those branches were cut away, so you could be put in their place.
text: Nibaakan, ni ga len ke, “Uwumbɔr chuu nyan ni binib bibaa Juu yaab ponn ni, ke u di timi koon bi ponn ni.”

ref: That's true enough. But they were cut away because they did not have faith, and you are where you are because you do have faith. So don't be proud, but be afraid.
text: Ni ye mbamɔn, Juu yaab aah kaa gaa Yesu Kristo ki kii na, nima le cha Uwumbɔr di bi lii. Nimi le gaa u ki kii. Nima le ni leŋ baaleleŋ. Ni taa li kpa kalmbaani. Ni li san Uwumbɔr.

ref: If God cut away those natural branches, couldn't he do the same to you?
text: U nan daa Juu yaab aatafal. Ni li nyi ke u ga ŋmaa daa ni mu aatafal.

ref: Now you see both how kind and how hard God can be. He was hard on those who fell, but he was kind to you. And he will keep on being kind to you, if you keep on trusting in his kindness. Otherwise, you will be cut away too.
text: Ni kan Uwumbɔr aah ŋan pu na, ki kan waah dar binib aatafal pu na. U dar binib bi kaa kii tii u na aatafal la, le ki ŋa nimi tiŋann. Ni yaa beenin dii u kan, u ga li beenin ŋani nimi tiŋann. Ni yaa kaa beenin dii u kan, u ga di ni mu lii la.

ref: If those other branches will start having faith, they will be made a part of that tree again. God has the power to put them back.
text: Juu yaab mu yaa kpeln ki yaa gaa Yesu Kristo ki kii kan, Uwumbɔr ga ki di bi toŋ waanib pu; u ga ŋmaa ŋa kina.

ref: After all, it wasn't natural for branches to be cut from a wild olive tree and to be made part of a cultivated olive tree. So it is much more likely that God will join the natural branches back to the cultivated olive tree. The People of Israel Will Be Brought Back
text: Nimi bi kaa ye Juu yaab na, ni bi ke timoor ni aasub aabon na, le Uwumbɔr gaa gii nimi ki di toŋ busunyaan pu, binib aah kaa ŋani pu na. Nima le naa pɔɔ u di Juu yaab, bi bi ke busunyaan aabon na, ki ki di toŋ busunyaan ngbaan pu. Uwumbɔr aanimbaasaln

ref: My friends, I don't want you Gentiles to be too proud of yourselves. So I will explain the mystery of what has happened to the people of Israel. Some of them have become stubborn, and they will stay like that until the complete number of you Gentiles has come in.
text: Nnaabitiib, m ban ke ni bee tibɔbɔrkaan tibaa, aan ki taa li dak ke ni kpa nlan sakpen. Juu yaab bibaa kpak tibɔnyaan tee la, ki ga kpak ti ki nan saa buyoonn binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab aan Uwumbɔr lee bi na ga ŋmar na.

ref: In this way all of Israel will be saved, as the Scriptures say, “From Zion someone will come to rescue us. Then Jacob's descendants will stop being evil.
text: N‑yoonn ngbaan le Juu yaab mɔmɔk mu ga ŋmar. Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “U gaal binib lir na ga nyan ni Sionn paacham, ki nyan Jakob aayaabitiib aatunwanbir.

ref: This is what the Lord has promised to do when he forgives their sins.”
text: Maah puu tipuur ti tii bi na le ye ke m ga nyan baatunwanbir bi chee.”

ref: The people of Israel are treated as God's enemies, so the good news can come to you Gentiles. But they are still the chosen ones, and God loves them because of their famous ancestors.
text: Tɔ, baah yii Yesu aabɔnyaan tee na, bi ye Uwumbɔr aadim la. Nima le ni kan tinyoor ki ŋmar. Uwumbɔr mu nan lee bi; waah lee bi na, biyaajatiib pu le u gee bi.

ref: God doesn't take back the gifts he has given or disown the people he has chosen.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa lee binib ki ŋa tinyoor ŋa bi pu kan, waan kpeln waalandak.

ref: At one time you Gentiles rejected God. But now Israel has rejected God, and you have been shown mercy.
text: Nimi bi kaa ye Juu yaab na, n‑yaayoonn na, ni nan yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb. Le dandana wee u san nimi kinimbaak, Juu yaab aah yii u na pu.

ref: And because of the mercy shown to you, they will also be shown mercy.
text: Uwumbɔr aah san nimi kinimbaak pu na, nima le ga cha u san Juu yaab bi kaa gaa Yesu ki kii dandana wee na kinimbaak.

ref: All people have disobeyed God, and that's why he treats them as prisoners. But he does this, so that he can have mercy on all of them.
text: U len ke Juu yaab ni binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mɔmɔk ye titunwanbirdam, aan u san bi mɔmɔk kinimbaak.

ref: Who can measure the wealth and wisdom and knowledge of God? Who can understand his decisions or explain what he does?
text: Uwumbɔr kpa nlan ni mbaem sakpen. Ubaa aan ŋmaa bee waah kpa sakpen pu na. Waah siin pu na, ubaa aan ŋmaa bee ŋitaa ŋi pu u siin kina na. Ubaa aan ŋmaa bee waah ŋani pu na.

ref: “Has anyone known the thoughts of the Lord or given him advice?
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Ŋma nyi Uwumbɔr aalandak? Ŋma ga ŋmaa tuk u waah ga ŋa pu na?

ref: Has anyone loaned something to the Lord that must be repaid?”
text: Ŋma tii u nibaa aan u giin tii u?”

ref: Everything comes from the Lord. All things were made because of him and will return to him. Praise the Lord forever! Amen.
text: Tiwan nimɔk bi na, ni nyan ni u chee la. U cha tiwan mɔmɔk beenin bi. Tiwan mɔmɔk bi, ke ni pak u. Uma le yeh mpakm n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Amii.

ref: Dear friends, God is good. So I beg you to offer your bodies to him as a living sacrifice, pure and pleasing. That's the most sensible way to serve God.
text: Nima pu na, nnaabitiib, Uwumbɔr aanimbaasaln pu le m gaŋ nimi, ni di nimi aawon tii Uwumbɔr, ki ŋa kitork ki fu, ki bi chain, ki ga piir usui na. Nimina le ye naah ga li dooni u mbamɔm pu na.

ref: Don't be like the people of this world, but let God change the way you think. Then you will know how to do everything that is good and pleasing to him.
text: Ni taa ki li bi ke dulnyaa wee aanib aah bi pu na. Kpeln nimi aalandak man aan ki kpeln nimi aabimbin. Nima le ni ga bee Uwumbɔr aah gee pu na. Ni ga bee naah ga ŋa pu ki li bi mbamɔm ki tun litunyaan ki piir usui na.

ref: I realize God has treated me with undeserved grace, and so I tell each of you not to think you are better than you really are. Use good sense and measure yourself by the amount of faith that God has given you.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr aah tii mi tininkpir pu na, nima le m bui unii umɔk bi ni ponn ni na, ke u taa li dak ke u ŋan jer waah ŋan pu na. U li dak suuna, Uwumbɔr aah cha unii mɔmɔk tii u naadii pu na.

ref: A body is made up of many parts, and each of them has its own use.
text: Ti kpa tiwon aawan ni wiir na tiwonbaan ponn ni la. Tiwon aawan mɔmɔk aatuln bi libaa libaa la.

ref: That's how it is with us. There are many of us, but we each are part of the body of Christ, as well as part of one another.
text: Ti mu bi kina la. Ti wiir, le taah kpaan Kristo chee na, ti kpaan tiwonbaan. Ti mɔmɔk toŋ tɔb pu ke tiwon aawan aah toŋ tɔb pu pu na la.

ref: God has also given each of us different gifts to use. If we can prophesy, we should do it according to the amount of faith we have.
text: Uwumbɔr tii timi Waafuur Nyaan aapiin ibaabaa ke i cha ti tun waatuln libaabaa na. Waah tii timi pu na, cha ti tun kina man. Unii aapiin yaa ye ke u nabr Uwumbɔr aah len pu na kan, u len iliin ngbaan waah ŋa naadii pu na.

ref: If we can serve others, we should serve. If we can teach, we should teach.
text: Uken aapiin yaa ye Uwumbɔr aatuln kan, u li tun lituln ngbaan. Uken yaa ŋmaa mɔk binib Uwumbɔr aabɔr kan, u li mɔk bi.

ref: If we can encourage others, we should encourage them. If we can give, we should be generous. If we are leaders, we should do our best. If we are good to others, we should do it cheerfully. Rules for Christian Living
text: Uken yaa ŋmaa pɔɔni binib aataakpab kan, u pɔɔk bitaakpab. Uken mu yaa ŋmaa tii bigiim kan, u li tii bi ki li kpa tibulchinn. Uken mu yaa ye Yesu aanib aaninkpel kan, utafal li bi bi ponn ni. Uken mu yaa ter binib baamukl ni kan, u li ter bi ki li kpa mpopiin.

ref: Be sincere in your love for others. Hate everything that is evil and hold tight to everything that is good.
text: Tɔ, ni li gee binib nisui ni. Ni li nan lituln li kaa ŋan na, ki li gee lituln li ŋan na.

ref: Love each other as brothers and sisters and honor others more than you do yourself.
text: Ni li gee tɔb mbamɔm, ke mmaalbaan ni aanib aah gee tɔb pu na, ki li pak biken ki jer nibaa.

ref: Never give up. Eagerly follow the Holy Spirit and serve the Lord.
text: Ni taa li san ligbanyakl man. Cha ninimbil li man Tidindaan aatuln pu,

ref: Let your hope make you glad. Be patient in time of trouble and never stop praying.
text: ki li kpa mpopiin nimi aamakl pu, ki li kpa limɔr falaa ponn ni, ki li mee Uwumbɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk,

ref: Take care of God's needy people and welcome strangers into your home.
text: ki yakr nimi aawan tii Uwumbɔr aanib bi lann ni na, ki chann bicham tichann.

ref: Ask God to bless everyone who mistreats you. Ask him to bless them and not to curse them.
text: Ni mee Uwumbɔr ke u ŋa tinyoor ŋa binib bi ŋani nimi falaa na pu. Ni bui bi ke, “Uwumbɔr ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni pu.” Ni taa sii bi.

ref: When others are happy, be happy with them, and when they are sad, be sad.
text: Ni li kpa mpopiin binib bi kpa mpopiin na chee, ki li wii binib bi wii na chee.

ref: Be friendly with everyone. Don't be proud and feel that you know more than others. Make friends with ordinary people.
text: Ni li kpaa kimɔbaan man. Ni li jɔnni bigiim man, ki taa li kpa kalmbaani. Ni taa li dak ke ni kpa nlan sakpen.

ref: Don't mistreat someone who has mistreated you. But try to earn the respect of others,
text: Unii yaa ŋa si bakaa kan, taa teen u. Ni li ŋani ni ŋan na binib mɔmɔk aanimbil ni.

ref: and do your best to live at peace with everyone.
text: Ni li pɔɔni nibaa man, ki li bi suuna binib mɔmɔk chee.

ref: Dear friends, don't try to get even. Let God take revenge. In the Scriptures the Lord says, “I am the one to take revenge and pay them back.”
text: Maanigeekaab, binib yaa ŋa nimi bakaa kan, ni taa teen bi. Cha Uwumbɔr le daa bitafal. Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke Uwumbɔr len ke, “Min baanja le kpa nsan ke m daa binib aatafal. Min le ga teen bi.”

ref: The Scriptures also say, “If your enemies are hungry, give them something to eat. And if they are thirsty, give them something to drink. This will be the same as piling burning coals on their heads.”
text: Ni ki ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Nkon yaa joo saadin kan, tii u tijikaar u ji. Nnyunyuu yaa joo u kan, tii u nnyun u nyu. Aa yaa ŋa kina kan, inimɔɔn ga ku u.”

ref: Don't let evil defeat you, but defeat evil with good.
text: Unii yaa ŋa si bakaa kan, taa cha bakaa ngbaan nyaŋ si. Cha tiŋann le nyaŋ bakaa.

ref: Obey the rulers who have authority over you. Only God can give authority to anyone, and he puts these rulers in their places of power.
text: Ni ŋan ke binib mɔmɔk li keei baatiŋ aayidam aamɔb. Uyidaan ubaa aa bi ubaa pu see Uwumbɔr le cha u bi. Biyidam bi bi na, Uwumbɔr le nyan bi siin.

ref: People who oppose the authorities are opposing what God has done, and they will be punished.
text: Nima pu na, unii yaa yii waatiŋ aayidam kan, u yii Uwumbɔr aah siin pu na la. Binib bi yii bi na ga kan ntafadaan.

ref: Rulers are a threat to evil people, not to good people. There is no need to be afraid of the authorities. Just do right, and they will praise you for it.
text: Biyidam aa bi ke bi li faani binib bi tun lituln li ŋan na. Bi bi ke bi li faani binib bi tun lituln li kaa ŋan na la. Aa ban ke aa li kaar biyidam aa? Tun lituln li ŋan na, nima le bi ga pak si.

ref: After all, they are God's servants, and it is their duty to help you. If you do something wrong, you ought to be afraid, because these rulers have the right to punish you. They are God's servants who punish criminals to show how angry God is.
text: Bi ye Uwumbɔr aatutum ke bi biin aa pu la. Aa mu yaa tun lituln li kaa ŋan na kan, li san ijawaan. Bi kpa mpɔɔn ke bi daa aatafal. Bi ye Uwumbɔr aatutum ke bi daa binib bi tun lituln li kaa ŋan na aatafal.

ref: But you should obey the rulers because you know it is the right thing to do, and not just because of God's anger.
text: Nima pu na, ni li keei nimi aatiŋ aayidam aamɔi, ki taa kan ntafadaan; nimi aalandak mu taa bii nimi.

ref: You must also pay your taxes. The authorities are God's servants, and it is their duty to take care of these matters.
text: Nima pu na, ni ŋan ke ni li pa lampoo mu. Bi ye Uwumbɔr aatutum bi u nan siin bi ke bi tun lituln ngbaan na la.

ref: Let love be your only debt! If you love others, you have done all that the Law demands.
text: Ni taa li joo unii ubaa aapɔln. Naah joo tɔb aapɔln li na le ye ke ni li gee tɔb. Unii u gee binib na, u gbiin Uwumbɔr aakaal mɔmɔk la.

ref: In the Law there are many commands, such as, “Be faithful in marriage. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not want what belongs to others.” But all of these are summed up in the command that says, “Love others as much as you love yourself.”
text: Ba pu? ikaal mɔmɔk nyan ni nkaal mu len ke, “Aa li gee binib biken ke saah gee aabaa pu na” ni la. Ikaal i len ke, “Taa gɔr kidagook, taa ku binib, taa su kinaayuk, taa gee nnyamɔn paani binib, taa li ban biken aawan” na, ikaal ngbaan, ni ikaal i gur na mɔmɔk nyan ni nkaal ngbaan ponn ni la.

ref: No one who loves others will harm them. So love is all that the Law demands. The Day When Christ Returns
text: Unii u gee binib na aa ŋani bi bakaa ubaa. Nima pu na, unii u gee binib na gbiin Uwumbɔr aakaal mɔmɔk aah len pu na la.

ref: You know what sort of times we live in, and so you should live properly. It is time to wake up. You know that the day when we will be saved is nearer now than when we first put our faith in the Lord.
text: Ni li ŋani kina man. Ba pu? n‑yoonn mumina ye linimaln aayoonn la. Ni ŋeer ke ni finn ngeen pu ki taa ki san ligbanyakl. Tidindaan aah ga gir ni bundaln na aan ki yunn. Le u ga nyan timi falaa mɔmɔk ponn ni.

ref: Night is almost over, and day will soon appear. We must stop behaving as people do in the dark and be ready to live in the light.
text: Naan yunn, kinyeek ga doo. Kitaak aawoln aa ki daa. Nima pu na, cha ti di cha mbɔmbɔɔn ni aatuln, aan ki li kpa mbimbinyaan mu ŋeer nwiihn na.

ref: So behave properly, as people do in the day. Don't go to wild parties or get drunk or be vulgar or indecent. Don't quarrel or be jealous.
text: Cha ti li bi mbamɔm, ke binib bi bi nwiihn ni na aah bi pu na, ki taa li ye bidanyurb, ki taa nyu ndaan ki gbii, ki taa gɔr kidagook, ki taa ŋani yɔl yɔl aatuln, ki taa jaa kijaak, ki taa li kpa lipiipoln.

ref: Let the Lord Jesus Christ be as near to you as the clothes you wear. Then you won't try to satisfy your selfish desires.
text: Ni li bi ke Tidindaan Yesu Kristo aah bi pu na, ki taa ki li ŋani nimi aabimbikpok aah ban pu na.

ref: Welcome all the Lord's followers, even those whose faith is weak. Don't criticize them for having beliefs that are different from yours.
text: Tɔ, unii u gaa Yesu ki kii, ki mu aa bee waasan mbamɔm na, ni gaa u man. Ni mu taa kpak u kinikpakpak waah joo beeni pu na pu.

ref: Some think it is all right to eat anything, while those whose faith is weak will eat only vegetables.
text: Ubaa ga pak ke tijikaar tibaa aa kɔ. Unii u kaa kee bee Yesu aasan mbamɔm na ga li kɔ tinann.

ref: What right do you have to criticize someone else's servants? Only their Lord can decide if they are doing right, and the Lord will make sure that they do right.
text: Aa ye ŋma ki galn uken aatutunn? U yaa sil kan, u sil ki tii uma ubaa Aadindaan la. U yaa ti ki lir kan, u lir ki tii uma ubaa Aadindaan la. Ni ye mbamɔn, u ga sil; ba pu? Uwumbɔr ga ŋmaa cha u sil.

ref: Some of the Lord's followers think one day is more important than another. Others think all days are the same. But each of you should make up your own mind.
text: Unii ubaa pak nwiin mubaa ki jer iken la. Ubaa mu len ke iwiin mɔmɔk kpaan la. Cha unii mɔmɔk li nyi waah dak pu na, ki li ŋani kina.

ref: Whether we live or die, it must be for God, rather than for ourselves.
text: Unii ubaa aa bi ubaa baanja pu, ubaa mu aakun aa ye uma baanja aabɔr.

ref: Whether we live or die, it must be for the Lord. Alive or dead, we still belong to the Lord.
text: Ti yaa bi kan, ti bi ke ti li pak Tidindaan la. Ti yaa kpo kan, ti kpo ke ti li pak Tidindaan la. Nima pu na, ti yaa bi, bee ti yaa kpo kan, ti ye Tidindaan yaab la.

ref: This is because Christ died and rose to life, so that he would be the Lord of the dead and of the living.
text: Kristo nan kpo ki fikr nkun ni, ke u li ye binib bi kpo na, ni binib bi fu na mu Aadindaan la.

ref: Why do you criticize other followers of the Lord? Why do you look down on them? The day is coming when God will judge all of us.
text: Sin, ba ŋa aa galn aana aabo? Sin, ba ŋa aa lik aana aabo fam? Ti mɔmɔk ga sil Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, le u ji timi tibɔr.

ref: In the Scriptures God says, “I swear by my very life that everyone will kneel down and praise my name!”
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke uma Uwumbɔr len ke, “Ni ye mbamɔn, binib mɔmɔk ga dan nan gbaan nnimbiin ni, ki pak mi, ke min le ye Uwumbɔr.”

ref: And so, each of us must give an account to God for what we do. Don't Cause Problems for Others
text: Nima pu na, ti mɔmɔk ga tuk Uwumbɔr taah ŋa pu na. Taa gbii aana aabo pu libuul

ref: We must stop judging others. We must also make up our minds not to upset anyone's faith.
text: Nima pu na, ti taa ki galni tɔb. Ni li nyi ki taa leŋ nina aabo Uwumbɔr aasan ni.

ref: The Lord Jesus has made it clear to me that God considers all foods fit to eat. But if you think some foods are unfit to eat, then for you they are not fit.
text: Maah kpaan Tidindaan Yesu chee na, le m sil bee ke tiwan nibaa aa kɔ nibaa pu. Unii mu yaa dak ke tiwan nibaa kɔ kan, ni kɔ u chee la.

ref: If you are hurting others by the foods you eat, you are not guided by love. Don't let your appetite destroy someone Christ died for.
text: Aa yaa ji tijikaar ti kɔ aana aabo chee na, ki bii usui kan, naa ye ke aa gee u le cha aa ŋa kina. Kristo le nan kpo u pu. Aa taa ŋa u fam saajikaar pu.

ref: Don't let your right to eat bring shame to Christ.
text: Ni taa ŋani tiwan ni ga cha binib bii nimi aasanyaan na.

ref: God's kingdom isn't about eating and drinking. It is about pleasing God, about living in peace, and about true happiness. All this comes from the Holy Spirit.
text: Uwumbɔr aanaan aa ye tijikaar ni tiwanyukaan. Mu ye mbimbinyaan, ni nsuudoon, ni mpopiin, Waafuur Nyaan aah tii timi pu na la.

ref: If you serve Christ in this way, you will please God and be respected by people.
text: Unii u dii Kristo ki bi kina na, u ga piir Uwumbɔr aasui. Binib mu ga pak u.

ref: We should try to live at peace and help each other have a strong faith.
text: Nima pu na, ni li pɔɔni nibaa aan ki li kpaan kimɔbaan, aan ki ter tɔb ke ni dii Uwumbɔr aasan mbamɔm.

ref: Don't let your appetite destroy what God has done. All foods are fit to eat, but it is wrong to cause problems for others by what you eat.
text: Ni taa bii Uwumbɔr aatuln tijikaar pu. Tijikaar tibaa aa kɔ. Aa mu yaa ji tijikaar ti ga bii uken aasui na kan, nima le aa ŋan.

ref: It is best not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything else that causes problems for other followers of the Lord.
text: Ni ŋan ke aa taa kiir aana aabo Uwumbɔr aasan ni; ni taa ŋmɔ kitork aanann, ki taa nyu ndaan, ki taa ŋa tiwan nibaa ni ga cha aana aabo tun titunwanbir ki lir na.

ref: What you believe about these things should be kept between you and God. You are fortunate, if your actions don't make you have doubts.
text: Aa yaa kɔ tijikaar tibaa, bee aa yaa kaa kɔ tibaa kan, cha ni li bi aa ni Uwumbɔr chee. Unii u ji tijikaar ti ŋan u chee na, kaa galni ubaa na, u kpa mpopiin la.

ref: But if you do have doubts about what you eat, you are going against your beliefs. And you know that is wrong, because anything you do against your beliefs is sin.
text: Unii u ji tijikaar, kaa pak ke ti ŋan na, waabɔr bii la; ba pu? waa ŋa naadii ke ni ŋan. Unii yaa kaa pak ke tiwan ŋan, ki ŋa ni kan, ni ye titunwanbir la.

ref: If our faith is strong, we should be patient with the Lord's followers whose faith is weak. We should try to please them instead of ourselves.
text: Timi bi gaa Yesu ki kii mbamɔm na, ni ŋan ke ti li ji limɔr, ki ter binib bi kaa gaa u mbamɔm na, ki taa ŋani tibaa aageehn baanja.

ref: We should think of their good and try to help them by doing what pleases them.
text: Cha ti mɔmɔk aatafal li bi tinaabitiib ponn ni, aan ki ter bi, bi dii Uwumbɔr aasan mbamɔm.

ref: Even Christ did not try to please himself. But as the Scriptures say, “The people who insulted you also insulted me.”
text: Kristo aa nan ban ke u li ŋani uma ubaa aageehn. Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Ŋisiibil ŋi ye sin yee na choo min chee la.”

ref: God is the one who makes us patient and cheerful. I pray that he will help you live at peace with each other, as you follow Christ.
text: Uwumbɔr u tii timi limɔr, ki pɔɔk timi aataakpab na tii nimi kimɔbaan Yesu Kristo aah ban pu na,

ref: Then all of you together will praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. The Good News Is for Jews and Gentiles
text: aan ni mɔmɔk li kpaan kimɔbaan ki nyuŋ Uwumbɔr, u ye Tidindaan Yesu Kristo aate na. Binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu ŋun tibɔnyaan ngbaan

ref: Honor God by accepting each other, as Christ has accepted you.
text: Ni gaa tɔb ke Kristo aah nan gaa nimi pu na, aan ki nyuŋ Uwumbɔr man.

ref: I tell you that Christ came as a servant of the Jews to show that God has kept the promises he made to their famous ancestors. Christ also came,
text: M tuk nimi la, Kristo nan ter Juu yaab ki gbiin Uwumbɔr aah nan puu tipuur tii biyaajatiib pu na, ki mɔk ke Uwumbɔr len mbamɔn la,

ref: so that the Gentiles would praise God for being kind to them. It is just as the Scriptures say, “I will tell the nations about you, and I will sing praises to your name.”
text: ki cha binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na mu nyuŋ Uwumbɔr waanimbaasaln pu, ke naah ŋmee waagbaŋ ponn ni ke, “M ga doon si binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aakaasisik ni, ki gaa ilahn ki pak si.”

ref: The Scriptures also say to the Gentiles, “Come and celebrate with God's people.”
text: Uwumbɔr ki len ke, “Nimi bi kaa ye Juu yaab na, ni li kpa mpopiin Uwumbɔr aanib chee,”

ref: Again the Scriptures say, “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles. All you nations, come and worship him.”
text: ki ki len ke, “Nimi bi kaa ye Juu yaab na, ni mɔmɔk pak Uwumbɔr man. Ŋinibol mɔmɔk, li pak u mbamɔm.”

ref: Isaiah says, “Someone from David's family will come to power. He will rule the nations, and they will put their hope in him.”
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔnabr Aisaya mu nan len ke, “Jese aayaabil ga fuu ni. Uwumbɔr ga tii u mpɔɔn u li ye binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na aayidaan. Le bi ga gaa u ki kii.”

ref: I pray that God, who gives hope, will bless you with complete happiness and peace because of your faith. And may the power of the Holy Spirit fill you with hope. Paul's Work as a Missionary
text: Uwumbɔr tii timi limakl la. Naah gaa u ki kii pu na, u gbiin nimi mpopiin ni nsuudoon mɔmɔk. Nima le ni ga li kpa limakl sakpen, Waafuur Nyaan aapɔɔn pu. Naah ŋa pu aan Pɔɔl ŋmee kina na

ref: My friends, I am sure that you are very good and that you have all the knowledge you need to teach each other.
text: Nnaabitiib, m nyi nsui ni ke nimi aabimbin ŋan pam. Ni bee Uwumbɔr aaliin mbamɔm, ki ga ŋmaa sur tɔb.

ref: But I have spoken to you plainly and have tried to remind you of some things. God treated me with undeserved grace!
text: Tɔ, m mu aah ŋmee kigbaŋ kimina tii nimi na, m kpa lipobil ki teer nimi tibɔr tibaa pu; ba pu? Uwumbɔr san mi kinimbaak,

ref: He chose me to be a servant of Christ Jesus for the Gentiles and to do the work of a priest in the service of his good news. God did this so that the Holy Spirit could make the Gentiles into a holy offering, pleasing to him.
text: ki ŋa mi Yesu Kristo aatutunn ke m tuk binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na Uwumbɔr aabɔnyaan, ki di bi tii Uwumbɔr, ke kitork na. Waafuur Nyaan le ŋa bi chain ke bi piir usui.

ref: Because of Christ Jesus, I can take pride in my service for God.
text: Maah tun lituln tii Uwumbɔr na, le m ga ŋmaa li kpa kipupuk Yesu Kristo pu.

ref: In fact, all I will talk about is how Christ let me speak and work, so that the Gentiles would obey him.
text: M ban m tuk nimi Kristo aah cha m tun lituln pu na la. Maan len biken aatuln pu. U cha m tuk binib bi kaa ye Juu yaab na waabɔr ki tun lijinjiir aatun, ke bi kii waamɔb.

ref: Indeed, I will tell how Christ worked miracles and wonders by the power of the Holy Spirit. I have preached the good news about him all the way from Jerusalem to Illyricum.
