text: Mak, ni Aristakus, ni Demas, ni Luk, bi ye maatutuŋeerb Uwumbɔr aatuln ponn ni na, bi mu dooni si.

ref: I pray that the Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you!
text: Tidindaan Yesu Kristo aaŋann li bi nisui ni. [Amii.]

ref: Long ago in many ways and at many times God's prophets spoke his message to our ancestors.
text: N‑yaayoonn na Uwumbɔr nan cha waabɔnabtiib tuk tiyaajatiib waabɔr ki di tiwan aabɔŋ aabɔŋ ŋaŋ waasan.

ref: But now at last, God sent his Son to bring his message to us. God created the universe by his Son, and everything will someday belong to the Son.
text: Kookoo aayoonn mue le u cha Ujapɔɔn tuk timi waabɔr. Uma le u nan cha u naan dulnyaa wee, ki len ke uma le ga li yeh tiwan mɔmɔk.

ref: God's Son has all the brightness of God's own glory and is like him in every way. By his own mighty word, he holds the universe together. After the Son had washed away our sins, he sat down at the right side of the glorious God in heaven.
text: U wiin chain ke Uwumbɔr aah wiin chain pu na, ki ye Uwumbɔr aanaŋ bamɔnn, ki di waabɔr ti kpa mpɔɔn na le joo tiwan mɔmɔk. U di ubaa toor kitork ki finn timi ki nyan timi aatunwanbir, le ki nin kal Uwumbɔr u yeh mpɔɔn mɔmɔk na aaŋangii wɔb paacham. Uwumbɔr Aajapɔɔn aapɔɔn jer waatuuntiib aapɔɔn

ref: He had become much greater than the angels, and the name he was given is far greater than any of theirs. God's Son Is Greater than Angels
text: Uwumbɔr tii u liyimbil li jer waatuuntiib aayimbil na. Waayimbil aah jer baayimbil pu na, kina le u jer bi.

ref: God has never said to any of the angels, “You are my Son, because today I have become your Father!” Neither has God said to any of them, “I will be his Father, and he will be my Son!”
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Ujapɔɔn ke, “Sin le ye Maabo, din wee le m ma si,” ki ki bui ke, “Min le ga li ye Ute, le u li ye Maabo.” Uwumbɔr aa nan bui waatuun ubaa kina.

ref: When God brings his first-born Son into the world, he commands all of his angels to worship him.
text: U nan tun ni Ujapɔɔn u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na dulnyaa wee ni, le ki bui waatuuntiib mɔmɔk ke bi gbaan unimbiin ni ki doon u.

ref: And when God speaks about the angels, he says, “I change my angels into wind and my servants into flaming fire.”
text: Uwumbɔr len waatuuntiib aabɔr, ke u cha waatuuntiib tun waatuln la, ke libuln ni mmiigaal aah tun waatuln pu na.

ref: But God says about his Son, “You are God, and you will rule as King forever! Your royal power brings about justice.
text: Le u len Ujapɔɔn aabɔr ke, “Uwumbɔr, saanaan ga li bi ki ti saa n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Aa joo saanaan ni aanib mbamɔm la.

ref: You loved justice and hated evil, and so I, your God, have chosen you. I appointed you and made you happier than any of your friends.”
text: Aa gee lituln li ŋan na, le kaa gee titunwanbir. Nima pu le Uwumbɔr u ye Saawumbɔr na lee si, ki tii si mpopiin ki jer aaŋeen aatɔtiib mɔmɔk.”

ref: The Scriptures also say, “In the beginning, Lord, you were the one who laid the foundation of the earth and created the heavens.
text: Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ki len ke, “Naah nan piin na, sin Uwumbɔr le nan naan kitiŋ, ni paacham mu.

ref: They will all disappear and wear out like clothes, but you will last forever.
text: Kitiŋ ni paacham ga doo, le aa ma ga li beenin bi. Kitiŋ ni paacham ga kpoi ke libɔkul na.

ref: You will roll them up like a robe and change them like a garment. But you are always the same, and you will live forever.”
text: Aa ga kpab kitiŋ ni paacham ke likekeln na, ki kpeln ni nipɔɔn, le sin ma beenin bi, kaan kpeln; saayoonn aan doo.”

ref: God never said to any of the angels, “Sit at my right side until I make your enemies into a footstool for you!”
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Ujapɔɔn ke, “Kal ŋŋangii wɔb, ki ti saa buyoonn m ga nyaŋ saadim mɔmɔk na.” Tɔ, Uwumbɔr aa nan bui waatuun ubaa kina.

ref: We must give our full attention to what we were told, so we won't drift away.
text: Nima pu na, ni ŋan ke titafal li bi tibɔnyaan ti ti ŋun ti na ponn ni, ti taa di ti lii.

ref: The message spoken by angels proved to be true, and all who disobeyed or rejected it were punished as they deserved.
text: Tibɔr ti Uwumbɔr nan cha waatuuntiib tuk waanib na sil mbamɔm la. Unii umɔk nan yii tibɔr ngbaan ki ŋa taah kɔ pu na nan kan ntafadaan mu ŋeer u na.

ref: So if we refuse this great way of being saved, how can we hope to escape? The Lord himself was the first to tell about it, and people who heard the message proved to us that it was true.
text: Nima pu na, ti yaa yii ŋŋmarkpaan ngbaan aaboln kan, taan nyan ntafadaan ni. Tidindaan ubaa le nan pue tuk binib ŋŋmarm ngbaan aabɔr. Le binib bi ŋun na mu tuk timi, ki mɔk timi ke ti gbii la.

ref: God himself showed that his message was true by working all kinds of powerful miracles and wonders. He also gave his Holy Spirit to anyone he chose to. The One Who Leads Us To Be Saved
text: Uwumbɔr mu cha bi tun lijinjiir aatun aabɔŋ aabɔŋ, waapɔɔn pu, ki tii bi Waafuur Nyaan aapiin waah gee pu na. Nima le mɔk ke bi len mbamɔn. Yesu u gaal timi lir na

ref: We know that God did not put the future world under the power of angels.
text: Ti len dulnyaa u choo na aabɔr la. Uwumbɔr aa nan di dulnyaa ngbaan ŋa waatuuntiib aaŋaal ni.

ref: Somewhere in the Scriptures someone says to God, “What makes you care about us humans? Why are you concerned for weaklings such as we?
text: Ni ŋmee Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Unibɔn ye ba aan aa teer ubɔr? Unibɔn ye ba aan aatafal bi u ni?

ref: You made us lower than the angels for a while. Yet you have crowned us with glory and honor.
text: Aa sunn u taab ki cha saatuuntiib jer u, ni yunn siib. Aa di kipak ni liyimbil le di tii u, ki di u ŋa saawanaankaan mɔmɔk aayidaan,

ref: And you have put everything under our power!” God has put everything under our power and has not left anything out of our power. But we still don't see it all under our control.
text: ki cha tiwan mɔmɔk kii umɔb.” Tɔ, saah cha tiwan mɔmɔk kii umɔb na, tiwan ni kaa kii umɔb na aa ki gur. Ti mu aa kee kan tiwan mɔmɔk kii umɔb;

ref: What we do see is Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels. Because of God's gift of undeserved grace, Jesus died for everyone. And now that Jesus has suffered and died, he is crowned with glory and honor!
text: ti kan Yesu la. Uwumbɔr nan sunn u taab ki cha waatuuntiib jer u, ni yunn siib, aan u ti kpo binib mɔmɔk pu, uma Uwumbɔr aanimbaasaln pu. Dandana wee ti kan ke waah jin nkun aafalaa na, Uwumbɔr di kipak ni liyimbil le di tii u.

ref: Everything belongs to God, and all things were created by his power. So God did the right thing when he made Jesus perfect by suffering, as Jesus led many of God's children to be saved and to share in his glory.
text: Uwumbɔr u nan naan tiwan mɔmɔk ki joo ni mɔmɔk na, ni ŋeer u ke u cha Yesu ji falaa, ki li joo ni Uwumbɔr aabim bi wiir na waanaan ni. Uma le gaa bi lii. Waah ji falaa pu na, nima le cha u ye timi aaŋmaŋmardaan bamɔnn.

ref: Jesus and the people he makes holy all belong to the same family. This is why he isn't ashamed to call them his brothers and sisters.
text: U ŋani binib chain la. U ni binib bi u ŋani bi chain na, bi mɔmɔk kpaan te ubaa la. Nima le inimɔɔn aa joo u ke u yin bi unaabitiib.

ref: He even said to God, “I will tell them your name and sing your praises when they come together to worship.”
text: Le u bui Uwumbɔr ke, “M ga tuk nnaabitiib saah tun pu na. M ga pak si baah kuun nin chee na,”

ref: He also said, “I will trust God.” Then he said, “Here I am with the children God has given me.”
text: ki ki len ke, “M ga tii Uwumbɔr naadii la,” ki ki len ke, “Lik, m ni mbim bi Uwumbɔr tii mi na sɔ.”

ref: We are people of flesh and blood. This is why Jesus became one of us. He died to destroy the devil, who had power over death.
text: Tɔ, timi waabim aah ye binibɔm pu na, nima le uma Yesu mu kpaln unibɔn, ke u nan kpo ki ŋa kinimbɔŋ ki nan kpa nkun aapɔɔn na fam,

ref: But he also died to rescue all of us who live each day in fear of dying.
text: le ki gaa binib bimɔk san nkun ijawaan na lii; baayoonn mɔmɔk nkun aajawaan nan joo bi.

ref: Jesus clearly did not come to help angels, but he did come to help Abraham's descendants.
text: Ni ye mbamɔn, naa ye Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib le u ter. Abraham aayaabil le u ter.

ref: He had to be one of us, so he could serve God as our merciful and faithful high priest and sacrifice himself for the forgiveness of our sins.
text: Ni ŋan ke u li naahn unaabitiib tiwan mɔmɔk ponn ni, aan ki li ye utotoorninkpel u san timi kinimbaak, ki tun Uwumbɔr aatuln mbamɔm, ki di ubaa toor kitork aan Uwumbɔr di cha pinn waanib baatunwanbir na.

ref: And now that Jesus has suffered and was tempted, he can help anyone else who is tempted.
text: Uma ubaa le kan ntɔŋ ki jin falaa, nima le u ga ŋmaa ter binib bi kan ntɔŋ na.

ref: My friends, God has chosen you to be his holy people. So think about Jesus, the one we call our apostle and high priest!
text: Nnaabitiib bi bi chain, aan Uwumbɔr yin bi na, ni li dakl lik Yesu aabɔr. Ti dii u ki len binib aanimbil ni ke ti dii u la. Uwumbɔr nan tun ni u, ke u nan li ye utotoorninkpel.

ref: Jesus was faithful to God, who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in serving all God's people.
text: U tun lituln mbamɔm tii Uwumbɔr u tii u lituln ngbaan na. Moses mu nan tun Uwumbɔr aatuln mbamɔm Uwumbɔr aamaal aanib aakaasisik ni.

ref: But Jesus deserves more honor than Moses, just as the builder of a house deserves more honor than the house.
text: Unii u ye mmaal aayaaja na le kani nnyuŋ ki jer mmaal aanii ubaa. Kina le Uwumbɔr len ke Yesu ŋeer nnyuŋ ki jer Moses.

ref: Of course, every house is built by someone, and God is really the one who built everything.
text: Mmaal mɔmɔk kpa yaaja la. Uwumbɔr le nan naan binib mɔmɔk.

ref: Moses was a faithful servant and told God's people what would be said in the future.
text: Ni ye mbamɔn, Moses nan tun Uwumbɔr aatuln mbamɔm, Uwumbɔr aamaal aanib aakaasisik ni. U nan ye Uwumbɔr aatutunn, ki tuk binib Uwumbɔr aah nan ban ke u tuk bi pu na.

ref: But Christ is the Son in charge of God's people. And we are those people, if we keep on being brave and don't lose hope. A Rest for God's People
text: Kristo ma kan, u ye Uwumbɔr Aajapɔɔn, le ki joo Uwumbɔr aamaal mbamɔm. Timi le ye waamaal ni aanib. Ti yaa kpa lipobil ni mpopiin ki ti saa ndoon kan, ki yaa kaa joo beeni kan, ti ye waamaal yaab la. Uwumbɔr aanib aafuur

ref: It is just as the Holy Spirit says, “If you hear God's voice today,
text: Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan nan bui Israel yaab ke, “Ni yaa ŋun Uwumbɔr aaneel din wee kan,

ref: don't be stubborn! Don't rebel like those people who were tested in the desert. *
text: ni taa cha nitafal li pɔɔ ke niyaajatiib aatafal aah nan pɔɔ pu buyoonn bi nan yii waamɔb nteersakpiin ni na.

ref: “Then God got tired of them and said, ‘You people never show good sense, and you don't understand what I want you to do.’
text: Nima pu le u nan gee liŋuul bi pu, le ki bui ke baalandak yenni n‑yoonn mɔmɔk la, baa bee waasan.

ref: God became angry and told the people, ‘You will never enter my place of rest!’ ”
text: Nima pu na, u nan gee liŋuul, ki puu tipuukpaan ke baan koo kitiŋ ki ponn ni u ba ga tii bi lifuur na.”

ref: My friends, watch out! Don't let evil thoughts or doubts make any of you turn from the living God.
text: Nnaabitiib, ni li nyi man, ni ponn ni ubaa aasui taa li bir aan u li joo beeni ki yii Uwumbɔr u ye limɔfadaan na.

ref: You must encourage one another each day. And you must keep on while there is still a time that can be called “today.” If you don't, then sin may fool some of you and make you stubborn.
text: Ni li pɔɔk tɔb aataakpab iwiin mɔmɔk, nsan aah laa bi pu buyoonn na, titunwanbir taa ŋmann unii ubaa aan utafal li pɔɔ.

ref: We were sure about Christ when we first became his people. So let's hold tightly to our faith until the end.
text: Ti yaa beenin tii u naadii ke taah nan tii u naadii njan pu na ki ti saa ndoon kan, ti ga ji waamɔɔn.

ref: Who were those people that heard God's voice and rebelled? Weren't they the same ones that came out of Egypt with Moses?
text: Ŋma ŋun Uwumbɔr aaneel ki yii waamɔb? Naa ye binib bimɔk Moses nan nyan bi Ijipt aatiŋ ni na aa?

ref: And who did God say would never enter his place of rest? Weren't they the ones that disobeyed him?
text: U nan puu tipuukpaan ke ŋma aan koo kitiŋ ki ponn ni u ba ga tii bi lifuur na? Naa ye binib bi nan yii waamɔb na aa?

ref: We see that those people did not enter the place of rest because they did not have faith.
text: Nima le ti bee ke baah kaa nan gaa u ki kii na, nima le baa nan ŋmaa kan lifuur ngbaan u chee.

ref: The promise to enter the place of rest is still good, and we must take care that none of you miss out.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ke u ga tii timi lifuur na, nsan laa beenin bi ke ti kan li. Nima na, ni li nyi man, ubaa taa lann lifuur ngbaan.

ref: We have heard the message, just as they did. But they failed to believe what they heard, and the message did not do them any good.
text: Ti mu ŋun tibɔnyaan tee ke binib ngbaan aah nan ŋun ti pu na. Bi nan ŋun ti, kaa gaa ti ki kii, nima le tibɔnyaan ngbaan aa ŋa bi tinyoor.

ref: Only people who have faith will enter the place of rest. It is just as the Scriptures say, “God became angry and told the people, ‘You will never enter my place of rest!’ ” God said this, even though everything has been ready from the time of creation.
text: Timi bi gaa Yesu ki kii na le kan lifuur ngbaan. Uwumbɔr nan len ke, “M nan gee liŋuul binib bi kaa gaa mi ki kii na pu, ki puu tipuukpaan ke baan koo kitiŋ ki ponn ni m ba ga tii bi lifuur na.” Waah nan naan dulnyaa wee doo na, waatuln doo le na.

ref: In fact, somewhere the Scriptures say that by the seventh day, God had finished his work, and so he rested.
text: Iwiin ilole daal aabɔr bi Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ ni ke, “Uwumbɔr nan fuur winlole daal ki di cha waatuln mɔmɔk.”

ref: We also read that he later said, “You people will never enter my place of rest!”
text: Ni ki ŋmee ke, “Baan koo kitiŋ ki ponn ni m ba ga tii bi lifuur na.”

ref: This means that the promise to enter is still good, because those who first heard about it disobeyed and did not enter.
text: Binib bi puen ŋun tibɔnyaan tee na, baa nan gaa ti ki kii, nima le baa kan lifuur ngbaan. Binib biken mu ga kan lifuur ngbaan.

ref: If Joshua had really given the people rest, there would not be any need for God to talk about another day of rest.
text: Tɔ, Josua yaa ba nan tii Israel yaab lifuur ngbaan kan, Uwumbɔr aa ba ga ki siin nwiin muken.

ref: But God has promised us a Sabbath when we will rest, even though it has not yet come.
text: Naah bi pu na, lifuur beenin bi ki tii Uwumbɔr aanib.

ref: On that day God's people will rest from their work, just as God rested from his work.
text: Unii u kan lifuur li Uwumbɔr tii u na, u di cha ubaa aatuln ke Uwumbɔr aah nan di cha waatuln pu na la.

ref: We should do our best to enter the place of rest, so none of us will disobey and miss going there, as they did.
text: Nima pu na, cha tinimbil li man ke ti kan lifuur ngbaan, ubaa taa yii Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki lir, ke Israel yaab aah nan lir pu na.

ref: God's word is alive and powerful! It is sharper than any double-edged sword. His word can cut through our spirits and souls and through our joints and marrow, until it discovers the desires and thoughts of our hearts.
text: Uwumbɔr aabɔr fu, ki kpa mpɔɔn, ki ka jer kijuk ki ka ŋipepel mɔmɔk ŋilee na, ki koo unii aasui ni, ni waawiin ni, ki lik usui ni aabɔbɔrkaan aah bi pu na, ki mɔk waalandak aah bi pu na, ki lik usui aah ban pu na, ke ni ŋan aan naa ŋan.

ref: Nothing is hidden from God! He sees through everything, and we will have to tell him the truth. Jesus Is the Great High Priest
text: Tiwan nibaa aa bi ki bɔr Uwumbɔr. Tibɔr mɔmɔk nyan ki dɔ mpaan pu, ki dɔ tiŋmeen unimbil ni. Uma le ti ga len timi aabɔr ki tuk u. Yesu le ye utotoorninkpekpaan

ref: We have a great high priest, who has gone into heaven, and he is Jesus the Son of God. This is why we must hold on to what we have said about him.
text: Tɔ, ti kpa utotoorninkpekpaan u bi Uwumbɔr do na. U ye Uwumbɔr Aajapɔɔn Yesu la. Nima pu na, cha ti li beenin dii u ki taa di waasan lii.

ref: Jesus understands every weakness of ours, because he was tempted in every way that we are. But he did not sin!
text: Utotoorninkpel ngbaan ga ŋmaa san timi kinimbaak timi aafalaa ponn ni. U kan ntɔŋ aabɔŋ aabɔŋ ke taah kan ntɔŋ mɔmɔk pu na. Uma le aa tun titunwanbir tibaa.

ref: So whenever we are in need, we should come bravely before the throne of our merciful God. There we will be treated with undeserved grace, and we will find help.
text: Timi aatotoorninkpel aah bi kina na, cha ti li kpa lipobil ki dan Uwumbɔr u kpa tibulchinn na aabɔrjal chee, aan u san timi kinimbaak, ki ter timi buyoonn ti ban nterm na.

ref: Every high priest is appointed to help others by offering gifts and sacrifices to God because of their sins.
text: Utotoorninkpel umɔk bi na, Uwumbɔr le lee u ki nyan u binib ponn ni siin, ke u ti sil baasisiiyaan Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni, aan ki tii u ipiin, ki toor kitork tii u binib aatunwanbir pu.

ref: A high priest has weaknesses of his own, and he feels sorry for foolish and sinful people.
text: Utotoorninkpel ubaa mu kpa titunwanbir la. Nima le u ga ŋmaa san binib bi tun titunwanbir kaa nyi na kinimbaak.

ref: This is why he must offer sacrifices for his own sins and for the sins of others.
text: Uma ubaa aah kpa titunwanbir pu na, ni ŋan ke u toor kitork uma ubaa aatunwanbir, ni bi mu aatunwanbir pu.

ref: But no one can have the honor of being a high priest simply by wanting to be one. Only God can choose a priest, and God is the one who chose Aaron.
text: Unii ubaa aan ŋmaa nyuŋ ubaa ki ŋa ubaa utotoorninkpel, see Uwumbɔr le lee u, ki ŋa u utotoorninkpel, ke waah nan lee utotoorninkpel Aaronn pu na.

ref: This is how it was with Christ. He became a high priest, but not just because he wanted the honor of being one. It was God who told him, “You are my Son, because today I have become your Father!”
text: Kina le Kristo aa nyuŋ ubaa ki ŋa ubaa utotoorninkpel. Uwumbɔr le bui u ke, “Sin le ye Maabo, din wee le m ma si,”

ref: In another place, God says, “You are a priest forever just like Melchizedek.”
text: le ki ki bui u ke, “Aa ye utotoor ke Melkisedek aah nan ye pu na, ki ga li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”

ref: God had the power to save Jesus from death. And while Jesus was on earth, he begged God with loud crying and tears to save him. He truly worshiped God, and God listened to his prayers.
text: Buyoonn Yesu nan ye unibɔn na, u nan wii tinyunyunn mpɔɔn pu, ki gaŋ Uwumbɔr u ga ŋmaa nyan u nkun ni na. Waah san Uwumbɔr na, le u ŋun waameel.

ref: Jesus is God's own Son, but still he had to suffer before he could learn what it really means to obey God.
text: U ye Uwumbɔr Aajapɔɔn la, le ki kii waamɔb, ki jin falaa, le ki bae naah pɔɔ pu aan u kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb ki jin falaa na.

ref: Suffering made Jesus perfect, and now he can save forever all who obey him.
text: Nima le cha u ye timi aaŋmaŋmardaan bamɔnn, ki gaa binib bimɔk kii waamɔb na lii n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: This is because God chose him to be a high priest like Melchizedek. Warning against Turning Away
text: Uwumbɔr len ke u ye utotoorninkpel ke Melkisedek aah nan ye pu na. Taa yii Uwumbɔr aasan man

ref: Much more could be said about this subject. But it is hard to explain, and all of you are slow to understand.
text: Ti ga ki ŋmaa len waabɔr ti wiir na, le nimi aalan par, nima le taatataa ga li pɔɔ ni chee.

ref: By now you should have been teachers, but once again you need to be taught the simplest things about what God has said. You need milk instead of solid food.
text: Naah dii Uwumbɔr ni yunn pu na, ni ba ga mɔk binib biken waasan. Le ni ban ke unii ki mɔk nimi Uwumbɔr aamɔkm mu diin na. Ni naahn binib bi ban nnaabiin kaa ban tijikaar bamɔnn na la.

ref: People who live on milk are like babies who don't really know what is right.
text: Unii umɔk nyu nnaabiin na ye ubopɔɔn la, kaa ŋmaa len nsanyaan aabɔr.

ref: We must try to become mature and start thinking about more than just the basic things we were taught about Christ. We shouldn't need to keep talking about why we ought to turn from deeds that bring death and why we ought to have faith in God.
text: Nima na, ti taa li beenin len Kristo aamɔkm mu diin na baanja aabɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk. Cha ti bae waamɔkm mu gur na mɔmɔk, aan ki chikr waasan ni. Naa ki ban ke ti li beenin tuk nimi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk ke, “Kpeln nimi aabimbin man, ki di cha ŋitukpok, ki tii Uwumbɔr naadii man.”

ref: And we shouldn't need to keep teaching about baptisms or about the laying on of hands or about people being raised from death and the future judgment.
text: Naa ki ban ke ti li beenin tuk nimi n‑yoonn mɔmɔk baah muini binib nnyun ni pu na, ni baah joo biŋaal paani binib pu pu na aabɔr, ni binib aah ga fikr nkun ni pu na aabɔr, ni ntafadaan mu kaa kpa ndoon na aabɔr. Timina mɔmɔk ye njan aabɔr le waasan ni.

ref: A field is useful to farmers, if there is enough rain to make good crops grow. In fact, God will bless such a field.
text: Kitiŋ ki gaa utaal aanyun mu lir ni ki pu, ki ŋani tijikaar ti ŋan na ki tii binib bi ko ti na, Uwumbɔr ŋani tinyoor ŋani kitiŋ ngbaan pu.

ref: But land that produces only thornbushes is worthless. It is likely to fall under God's curse, and in the end it will be set on fire.
text: Tɔ, kitiŋ ki po ŋani ikokon ni ichakpeejagar baanja na bee yɔli la. Naan yunn, le bi ga see ki mmii ki bii ki. Kitiŋ ngbaan aadoon le na.

ref: My friends, we are talking this way. But we are sure that you are doing those really good things people do when they are being saved.
text: Timi aanigeekaab, ti len kina la; ti mu aa dak ke ni bi ke kitiŋ ki bi ga see ki mmii na. Ti bee ke ni ŋmar ki ga kan tinyoor.

ref: God is always fair. He will remember how you helped his people in the past and how you are still helping them. You belong to God, and he won't forget the love you have shown his people.
text: Uwumbɔr ŋan la. Waan suln naah tun lituln pu ki ter waanib, ki beenin ter bi na, ki mɔk u naah gee u pu na bɔr.

ref: We wish each of you would always be eager to show how strong and lasting your hope really is.
text: Ti ban ke ni mɔmɔk pɔɔk nibaa ki li kpa limakl ki nan saa ndoon.

ref: Then you would never be lazy. You would be following the example of those who had faith and were patient until God kept his promise to them. God's Promise Is Sure
text: Ni taa li san ligbanyakl man. N‑yaayoonn na aanib bi nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii ki jin suklaa na, bi bi paacham ki kan waah puu tipuur ti ke u ga tii bi na. Ni mu li dii baah dii pu na. Uwumbɔr ga ŋa waah puu tipuur ti na

ref: No one is greater than God. So he made a promise in his own name when he said to Abraham,
text: Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ki tii Abraham na, u nan puu uma ubaa aayimbil pu la. Ubaa aa bi ki jer u, ke u puu waayimbil, nima le cha u puu uma ubaa aayimbil.

ref: Then after Abraham had been very patient, he was given what God had promised.
text: Abraham nan kpa limɔr, le ki nan kan Uwumbɔr aah nan puu tipuur ti na.

ref: When anyone wants to settle an argument, they make a vow by using the name of someone or something greater than themselves.
text: Binib yaa puu tipuur kan, bi puur unii u jer bi na aayimbil pu la. Binib yaa kpak kinikpakpak ki ti puu tipuur kan, ni doo le na.

ref: So when God wanted to prove for certain his promise to his people could not be broken, he made a vow.
text: Uwumbɔr nan ban ke u mɔk binib bi ga kan waah puu tipuur ti na, ke waan kpeln. Nima le u nan puu uma ubaa aayimbil pu.

ref: God cannot tell lies! And so his promises and vows are two things that can never be changed. We have run to God for safety. Now his promises should greatly encourage us to take hold of the hope that is right in front of us.
text: Waah nan puu tipuur ti na, waan kpeln. Waah puu uma ubaa aayimbil pu na, nima le sil mɔk ke waan kpeln. Waan ŋmaa mɔn nnyamɔn. Nima le timi bi san cha u chee ke ti ŋmar na aataakpab pɔɔ mbamɔm, le ti kpa limakl ke ti ga kan waah puu tipuur ti na.

ref: This hope is like a firm and steady anchor for our souls. In fact, hope reaches behind the curtain and into the most holy place.
text: Taah kpa limakl ngbaan na, nima le joo timi aasui ke ti taa di cha waasan. Yesu pu, le ti kpa limakl ngbaan. Limakl ngbaan pu, le Yesu u bi paacham na aalandak bi tisui ni.

ref: Melchizedek was both king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He was the one who went out and gave Abraham his blessing, when Abraham returned from killing the kings.
text: Melkisedek ngbaan nan ye Salem aatiŋ aabɔr, ki nan ye Uwumbɔr u kaa kpa ŋeen aatɔ na aatotoor la. Abraham aah nan ku bibɔrb bi ye waadim na ki gir ni na, le Melkisedek tooh u nsan pu ki ti ŋa Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa u pu.

ref: Then Abraham gave him a tenth of everything he had. The meaning of the name Melchizedek is “King of Justice.” But since Salem means “peace,” he is also “King of Peace.”
text: Le Abraham nan nyan tiwan nimɔk u nan gaa na nibaabaa kipiik mɔk ponn ni, ki di tii Melkisedek. Melkisedek aatataa le ye ke “ubɔr u kpa mbimbinyaan na.” U nan ye Salem aatiŋ aabɔr la. Salem aatataa le ye ke “nsuudoon.”

ref: We are not told he had a father or mother or ancestors or beginning or end. He is like the Son of God and will be a priest forever.
text: Baa ŋmee ute ni una ni uyaajatiib aabɔr, kaa ŋmee buyoonn bi nan ma u na, ki mu aa ŋmee buyoonn u doo waatuln na. Waamɔfal aayoonn mɔmɔk u nan ye Uwumbɔr aatotoor la. Nima le u naahn Uwumbɔr Aajapɔɔn u ye utotoor n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: Notice how great Melchizedek was! Our famous ancestor Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had taken from his enemies.
text: Dakl lik man uja ngbaan aah nan nyuun pu na; tiyaajaninkpel Abraham nan yakr waadim aawan tiwan nfum kipiik, ki nyan nibaa, ki di tii u, ki gur niwae.

ref: The Law teaches that even Abraham's descendants must give a tenth of what they possess. And they are to give this to their own relatives, who are the descendants of Levi and are priests.
text: Uwumbɔr aakaal len ke Israel yaab yakr baawan mɔmɔk nfum kipiik, ki nyan nibaa tii Liifai aayaabitiib, bi ye Uwumbɔr aatotoorb na. Bi ni Israel yaab nan ye binibaan la. Bi mɔmɔk nan ye Abraham aayaabitiib la.

ref: Although Melchizedek wasn't a descendant of Levi, Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had. Then Melchizedek blessed Abraham, who had been given God's promise.
text: Melkisedek aa nan ye Liifai aayaabil, le Abraham yakr waawan mɔmɔk nfum kipiik, ki nyan nibaa tii u. Le u ŋa tinyoor ŋa Abraham pu. Abraham le Uwumbɔr nan puu tipuur tii u.

ref: Everyone agrees a person who gives a blessing is greater than the one who receives the blessing.
text: Unii yaa kpa mpɔɔn ke u ŋa Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa uken pu kan, ni mɔk ke u jer u la. Ubaa aan kpak kina.

ref: Levi's descendants are now the ones who receive a tenth from people. We could even say that when Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth, Levi also gave him a tenth.
text: Abraham aah nan yakr waawan ki di tii u na, ti ga ŋmaa len ke uyaabitiib Liifai yaab bi gaal biken chee na, mu nan tii u la.

ref: This is because Levi was born later into the family of Abraham, who gave a tenth to Melchizedek.
text: Buyoonn Melkisedek nan tooh Abraham nsan ni na, Abraham aa nan kee ma uyaabil Liifai. Ti ga ŋmaa len ke Abraham nan sil uyaabil Liifai aasisiiyaan la.

ref: Even though the Law of Moses says the priests must be descendants of Levi, those priests cannot make anyone perfect. So there needs to be a priest like Melchizedek, rather than one from the priestly family of Aaron.
text: Uwumbɔr tii Israel yaab nkaal mu mɔk bi waatotoorb Liifai yaab aah ga li joo bi pu na. Bitotoorb ngbaan aatuln yaa ba gaa binib lii kan, Uwumbɔr aa ba ga li ban u tun ni Yesu u ye utotoor ke Melkisedek aah nan ye pu na. U ba ga ki tun ni utotoor u bi ke Aaronn aayaabitiib Liifai yaab aah nan bi pu na la.

ref: And when the rules for selecting a priest are changed, the Law must also be changed.
text: Waah tun ni utotoor uken aaboln na, see u kpeln nkaal ngbaan mu.

ref: The person we are talking about is our Lord, who came from a tribe that had never had anyone to serve as a priest at the altar.
text: Tidindaan u ti len waabɔr na, aa nan ye Liifai aanibol ponn ni aanii. U nan ye linibol liken ponn ni aanii la. Waanibol ponn ni aanii ubaa aa nan kee ye Uwumbɔr aatotoor.

ref: Everyone knows he came from the tribe of Judah, and Moses never said priests would come from that tribe.
text: Binib mɔmɔk nyi ke Tidindaan nan ye Juda aanibol ponn ni aanii la. Moses aa nan len ke linibol ngbaan aanib ga li ye bitotoorb. Utotoor yayan u bi ke Melkisedek na

ref: All of this becomes clearer, when someone who is like Melchizedek is appointed to be a priest.
text: Nima le mɔk timi chob ke utotoor yayan, u bi ke Melkisedek aah nan bi pu na, fuu ni.

ref: The Scriptures say about him, “You are a priest forever, just like Melchizedek.”
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui u, “Aa ga li ye utotoor n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na ke Melkisedek aah nan bi pu na.”

ref: because the Law cannot make anything perfect. At the same time, we are given a much better hope, and it can bring us close to God.
text: Moses aakaal aa nan kpa tinyoor, kaa nan kpa mpɔɔn, kaa ŋmaa ŋa bi binib bi ŋan ti doo na. Nima le Uwumbɔr di nkaal ngbaan lii, le ki tii timi limakl li ŋan ki jer nkaal ngbaan na. Limakl ngbaan pu le ti ga ŋmaa duun Uwumbɔr.

ref: God himself made a promise when this priest was appointed. But he did not make a promise like this when the other priests were appointed. The promise he made is, “I, the Lord, promise that you will be a priest forever! And I will never change my mind!”
text: Waah ŋa Yesu utotoor buyoonn na, u nan puu tipuur tii u, le ki bui u ke, “Min Uwumbɔr le puu tipuukpaan, kaan kpeln, ke aa ga li ye utotoor n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.”

ref: This means that Jesus guarantees us a better agreement with God.
text: Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuupɔln ti tii Yesu na, nima le mɔk ke tipuupɔln ngbaan le ŋan ki jer tipuukpokl na.

ref: There have been a lot of other priests, and all of them have died.
text: Israel yaab aatotoorb nan ye binib bi ga kpo na, le biken leŋni baaleleŋ. Nima le bi nan wiir.

ref: But Jesus will never die, and so he will be a priest forever!
text: Yesu ma kan, u ye utotoor u ga li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Ubaa aan ki nab waatuln pu ki toor kitork.

ref: He is forever able to save the people he leads to God, because he always lives to speak to God for them.
text: U bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na, u li mee Uwumbɔr tii binib bi dan Uwumbɔr chee u pu na. Nima le u ga ŋmaa gaa bi lii n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: Jesus is the high priest we need. He is holy and innocent and faultless, and not at all like us sinners. Jesus is honored above all beings in heaven,
text: Yesu le ye utotoorninkpel taah ban pu na. U bi chain, kaa kpa ngalm, kaa kpa titunwanbir tibaa. U ni titunwanbirdam aa kpaani. Uwumbɔr yoor u paacham ki jer bimɔk bi paacham na.

ref: and he is better than any other high priest. Jesus doesn't need to offer sacrifices each day for his own sins and then for the sins of the people. He offered a sacrifice once for all, when he gave himself.
text: Bitotoorninkpiib biken aah bi pu na, waa bi kina. Waa toor kitork uma ubaa aatunwanbir pu, u toor kitork binib aatunwanbir pu la. Waa toor kitork iwiin mɔmɔk. U nan di ubaa toor kitork nfum mubaa, kookoo aatork mu le na.

ref: The Law appoints priests who have weaknesses. But God's promise, which came later than the Law, appoints his Son. And he is the perfect high priest forever.
text: Bi nan leer bitotoorninkpiib Moses aakaal aah dii pu na. Bitotoorninkpiib ngbaan aa nan ŋan ti doo. Nkaal ngbaan aapuwɔb le Uwumbɔr puu tipuur, ki ŋa Ujapɔɔn utotoorninkpel. Uma le ye utotoorninkpel bamɔnn, ki ga li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: What I mean is we have a high priest who sits at the right side of God's great throne in heaven.
text: Maah len pu na aayil le ye ke ti kpa utotoorninkpel wee aaboln. Uma le ye Yesu Kristo u ka Uwumbɔr u yeh mpɔɔn mɔmɔk na aabɔrjal aaŋangii wɔb paacham na.

ref: He also serves as the priest in the most holy place inside the real tent there in heaven. This tent of worship was set up by the Lord, not by humans.
text: U tun utotoorninkpel aatuln paacham aadiik ki ye kidibamɔŋ ki bi chain na ponn ni. Uwumbɔr le maa ki, naa ye binib.

ref: If he were here on earth, he would not be a priest at all, because here the Law appoints other priests to offer sacrifices.
text: Bitotoorninkpiib bi dulnyaa wee ni ki toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr, Juu yaab aakaal aah dii pu na la. Yesu yaa ba laa bi dulnyaa wee ni kan, waa ba ga li ye utotoor.

ref: But the tent where they serve is just a copy and a shadow of the real one in heaven. Before Moses made the tent, he was told, “Be sure to make it exactly like the pattern you were shown on the mountain!”
text: Bitotoorninkpiib ngbaan aatuln ye paacham aatuln aanaŋ la. Moses yaan mu nan bi kina la. Waah nan ban ke u ŋa libool tii Uwumbɔr na, Uwumbɔr nan bui u ke u li nyi ki ŋa tiwan mɔmɔk ke waah mɔk u laanaŋ, lijool paab pu na.

ref: Now Christ has been appointed to serve as a priest in a much better way, and he has given us much assurance of a better agreement.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr nan tii Yesu lituln li jer bitotoorninkpiib ngbaan aatuln na. Kina le tipuupɔln ti Uwumbɔr puu tii waanib Yesu pu na jer tipuukpokl na, ki mɔk ke u ga tii timi tiwan ni ŋan jer tipuukpokl ngbaan aawan na.

ref: If the first agreement with God had been all right, there would not have been any need for another one.
text: Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ti njan na yaa kaa ba lann nibaa kan, waa ba ga li ban ke u ki puu tipuur lelee.

ref: But the Lord found fault with it and said, “I tell you the time will come, when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and the people of Judah.
text: Uwumbɔr nan kan ke waanib kpa taani, le ki bui ke, “Lik, n‑yoonn choo, le m ga nan puu tipuupɔln tii Israel yaab ni Juda yaab.

ref: It won't be like the agreement that I made with their ancestors, when I took them by the hand and led them out of Egypt. They broke their agreement with me, and I stopped caring about them!
text: Tipuur ngbaan aan li bi ke tipuur ti m nan puu tii biyaajatiib, buyoonn m nan chuu biŋaal ki daar nyan bi, ki cheen bi nyan Ijipt aatiŋ ni na. Baa nan joo tipuur ngbaan, nima le maa nan ki gar bi. Min Uwumbɔr le len kina.

ref: “But now I tell the people of Israel this is my new agreement: ‘The time will come when I, the Lord, will write my laws on their minds and hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
text: Maah ga puu tipuur ti tii Israel yaab n‑yoonn mu choo na na le ye ke: M ga di maakaal ŋa baalandak ni, ki ŋmee mu bisui ponn ni. M ga li ye Baawumbɔr, le bi li ye maanib.

ref: Not one of them will have to teach another to know me, their Lord.’ “All of them will know me, no matter who they are.
text: Bi ponn ni ubaa aan ki bui uŋeen aatɔ ke, ‘Bee Uwumbɔr.’ Ubaa mu aan ki bui una aabo ke, ‘Bee Uwumbɔr.’ Ba pu? bi mɔmɔk ga bee mi, biwaatiib ki ti saa bikpaam mɔmɔk ga bee mi.

ref: I will treat them with kindness, even though they are wicked. I will forget their sins.”
text: M ga di cha pinn baatunwanbir, kaan ki teer baataani.”

ref: When the Lord talks about a new agreement, he means that the first one is out of date. And anything that is old and useless will soon disappear.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr aah len ke u ga puu tipuupɔln na, u ŋa njan yaan tipuukpokl la. Tiwan yaa ye tiwankpok kan, naan yunn, naan ki li bi.

ref: The first part of the tent was called the holy place, and a lampstand, a table, and the sacred loaves of bread were kept there.
text: Bi nan ŋa libool lipepel libaa wɔb, ki yin li ke chain aapepel. Karyaa ni teebul ni boroboro u bi di tii Uwumbɔr na, nan bi li ponn ni.

ref: The gold altar for burning incense was in this holy place. The gold-covered sacred chest was also there, and inside it were three things. First, there was a gold jar filled with manna. Then there was Aaron's walking stick that sprouted. Finally, there were the flat stones with the Ten Commandments written on them.
text: Salmaa aatork aabimbiln nan bi ni ponn ni. Libimbiln ngbaan paab le bi seer tulalee aayon tii Uwumbɔr. Uwumbɔr aakaal aah nan bi dakaa u ponn ni na, mu nan bi ni ni. Bi nan di salmaa aakur le biin dakaa ngbaan pu. Tijikaar ti bi yin ti ke mana na, nan bi salmaa aasambil ponn ni, dakaa ngbaan ponn ni. Aaronn aadabil li nan ŋeen nsupuun na mu nan bi u ponn ni. Uwumbɔr aakaal aah nan ŋmee ŋitakpapapan ŋilee ŋi pu na, mu nan bi u ponn ni.

ref: On top of the chest were the glorious creatures with wings opened out above the place of mercy. Now isn't the time to go into detail about these things.
text: Tiwan ni kpa ifeen na nilee mu nan bi dakaa ngbaan paab. Nima chee le Uwumbɔr nan mɔk Israel yaab waah wiin chain pu na. Tiwan ngbaan aafeen nan biin dakaa ngbaan aabiil pu, Uwumbɔr aah san bi kinimbaak nin chee na. Taan ŋmaa len tiwan nimina mɔmɔk aatataa nibaabaa dandana wee.

ref: But this is how everything was when the priests went each day into the first part of the tent to do their duties.
text: Baah di tiwan nimina mɔmɔk siin kina na, le bitotoorb koo mɔb aadiik ni iwiin mɔmɔk, bi ti tun lituln tii Uwumbɔr.

ref: However, only the high priest could go into the second part of the tent, and he went in only once a year. Each time he carried blood to offer for his sins and for any sins that the people had committed without meaning to.
text: Utotoorninkpel baanja le koo ni chain chain aapepel li bi libool ngbaan ponn ni na. U koo ni nima chee libiln mɔmɔk nfum mbaa baanja la. U yaa koo ni kan, see u joo ni nsin nan tii Uwumbɔr, uma ubaa aatunwanbir ni binib aatunwanbir pu.

ref: All of this is the Holy Spirit's way of saying no one could enter the most holy place while the tent was still the place of worship.
text: Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan mɔk timi ke mɔb aadiik ngbaan aah nan laa bi na, binib aa nan kpa nsan ke bi koo ni chain chain aapepel ponn ni.

ref: This also has a meaning for today. It shows we cannot make our consciences clear by offering gifts and sacrifices.
text: Libool ngbaan le nan ye Yesu aabɔr aamɔkl ki tii bi. Libool ngbaan ponn ni, le bi joo ipiin, ni tiwakor toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr. Kitork ngbaan aa nan cha bisui doon titunwanbir pu.

ref: These rules are merely about such things as eating and drinking and ceremonies for washing ourselves. And rules about physical things will last only until the time comes to change them for something better.
text: Nkaalkpok ngbaan mɔk bi tijikaar ni tiwanyukaan ni kɔ na, ni ni kaa kɔ na, ki mɔk bi baah ga finn bibaa ki ŋa chain pu na. Ni nan mɔk ke see bi dii kina le ki nan saa buyoonn Yesu ga joo ni nsanpɔɔn mu ŋan na.

ref: Christ came as the high priest of the good things that are now here. He also went into a much better tent that wasn't made by humans and that doesn't belong to this world.
text: Dandana wee Kristo fuu ni a, ki ye utotoorninkpel, ki joo ni nsanyaan mu bi nan len ke mu ga fuu ni na. Waa koo ni libool li binib ŋa li dulnyaa wee ni na. U dii lipepel li jer dulnyaa wee aabool ngbaan na,

ref: Then Christ went once for all into the most holy place and freed us from sin forever. He did this by offering his own blood instead of the blood of goats and bulls.
text: le ki koo lipepel li ye chain na paacham, nfum mbaa kookoo. Uma ubaa aasin pu le u nan gaa timi lii n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na, naa ye tiwakor aasin pu.

ref: According to the Law of Moses, those people who become unclean are not fit to worship God. Yet they will be considered clean, if they are sprinkled with the blood of goats and bulls and with the ashes of a sacrificed calf.
text: Bi nan joo iŋoob ni inaaja aasin yɔkr binib bi kaa ye chain na pu, ki di unaasabo aafatan gbaa gbaa bi, le ni ŋa tiwon chain.

ref: But Christ was sinless, and he offered himself as an eternal and spiritual sacrifice to God. This is why his blood is much more powerful and makes our consciences clear. Now we can serve the living God and no longer do things that lead to death.
text: Nimina yaa nan ŋa tiwon chain kan, Kristo aasin ga ter timi, ki jer kina. Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan mu bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na aapɔɔn pu, u nan di ubaa toor kitork ki kaa kpa ngalm na tii Uwumbɔr. Waasin ga nyan titunwanbir ti ga ku timi na tisui ni, aan ti dii Uwumbɔr u ye limɔfadaan na.

ref: In fact, making an agreement of this kind is like writing a will. This is because the one who makes the will must die before it is of any use.
text: Unii yaa yakr waafaal ki laa ka kan, ubaa aan ŋmaa ji lifaal ngbaan, see ni puen mɔk ke u kpo.

ref: In other words, a will doesn't go into effect as long as the one who made it is still alive.
text: Buyoonn u laa beenin bi na, ubaa aan ŋmaa ji lifaal ngbaan, see u kpo.

ref: Moses told the people all the Law said they must do. Then he used red wool and a hyssop plant to sprinkle the people and the book of the Law with the blood of bulls and goats and with water.
text: Njan, Moses nan tuk binib mɔmɔk baah ga dii Uwumbɔr aakaal mɔmɔk pu na, le ki nin di tikumaman ni tifar ŋa inaabi ni iŋoob aasin, ni nnyun ni, ki di yɔk yɔk Uwumbɔr aakaal aagbaŋ pu, ni binib mɔmɔk pu,

ref: Moses also sprinkled blood on the tent and on everything else used in worship.
text: le ki di nsin ngbaan yɔk yɔk libool, ni baah joo tiwan nimɔk tun lituln tii Uwumbɔr na pu.

ref: The Law says that almost everything must be sprinkled with blood, and no sins can be forgiven unless blood is offered. Christ's Great Sacrifice
text: Nkaal ngbaan aah dii pu na, bi yaa nan ban ke bi ŋa tiwan chain kan, see bi di nsin yɔk yɔk ni pu le ki ŋa ni chain. Nsin yaa kaa nyan kan, Uwumbɔr aan di cha pinn titunwanbir. Yesu Kristo aatork nyani titunwanbir

ref: These things are only copies of what is in heaven, and so they had to be made holy by these ceremonies. But the real things in heaven must be made holy by something better.
text: Uwumbɔr Aabool, ni tiwan nimɔk nan bi li ponn ni na ye paacham aawan aanaŋ la. Le bi nan di tiwakor aasin ŋa ni mɔmɔk chain. Paacham aawan bamɔnn le ban nsin mu jer tiwakor aasin na, aan ni ŋa chain.

ref: This is why Christ did not go into a tent made by humans and was only a copy of the real one. Instead, he went into heaven and is now there with God to help us.
text: Kristo aa koo ni chain aapepel li ye paacham yaan aanaŋ li binib maa li na ponn ni. Paacham le u koo ni, ki si timi aasisiiyaan, Uwumbɔr aanimbiin ni.

ref: Christ did not have to offer himself many times. He wasn't like a high priest who goes into the most holy place each year to offer the blood of an animal.
text: Juu yaab aatotoorninkpel nan di nsin mu kaa ye uma ubaa aasin na le koo ni chain aapepel ni, libiln mɔmɔk. Yesu Kristo di ubaa toor kitork nfum mbaa baanja la.

ref: If he had offered himself every year, he would have suffered many times since the creation of the world. But instead, near the end of time he offered himself once and for all, so he could be a sacrifice that does away with sin.
text: U yaa ba nan joo ubaa toor kitork libiln mɔmɔk kan, u ba ga ji falaa n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, buyoonn dulnyaa wee piin ki joo cha na. Naah ye pu na, u fuu ni buyoonn ni ŋeer na, ki di ubaa toor kitork nfum mubaa, ke u kuln titunwanbir.

ref: We die only once, and then we are judged.
text: Uwumbɔr siin ke binib ga kpo nfum mubaa la, nee aapuwɔb le u ga ji bi tibɔr.

ref: So Christ died only once to take away the sins of many people. But when he comes again, it will not be to take away sin. He will come to save everyone who is waiting for him.
text: Kristo mu di ubaa toor kitork nfum mubaa, binib pam aatunwanbir pu. U ga ki fuu ni lelee. Naa ye titunwanbir pu le u ga ki fuu ni. U ga fuu ni ke u nan gaa binib bi kii waagirndaal na lii.

ref: The Law of Moses is like a shadow of the good things to come. This shadow isn't the good things themselves, because it cannot free people from sin by the sacrifices offered year after year.
text: Moses aakaal nan ye nsanyaan mu choo na aamɔkl la, naa nan ye nsanyaan ngbaan mbamɔm. Binib bi dii Moses aakaal na toor titorbaan ŋibin ŋibin, nima le aa ŋmaa ŋa bi binib bi ŋan ti doo na.

ref: If there were worshipers who already have their sins washed away and their consciences made clear, there would not be any need to go on offering sacrifices.
text: Nkaal ngbaan yaa ba nan nyan bi titunwanbir ni kan, baalandak aa ba ga ki li muk bi titunwanbir pu. Bi mu aa ba ga ki toor kitork ngbaan.

ref: But the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins. It only reminds people of their sins from one year to the next.
text: Inaaja aasin, ni iŋoob aasin aa ŋmaa nyan titunwanbir binib aasui ni.

ref: When Christ came into the world, he said to God, “Sacrifices and offerings are not what you want, but you have given me my body.
text: Nima pu na, Yesu Kristo aah nan ban ke u dan dulnyaa wee ni na, u nan bui Uwumbɔr ke, “Saa ban tiwakor ni tijikaar aatork. Aa naan tiwon tii mi la.

ref: No, you are not pleased with animal sacrifices and offerings for sin.”
text: Saa ban ke m di tiwakor aatork, ki di see mmii ni tii si, kaa ban ke m toor kitork ngbaan titunwanbir pu.

ref: Then Christ said, “And so, my God, I have come to do what you want, as the Scriptures say.”
text: Le m bui ke, ‘Uwumbɔr, m fuu ni ke m nan ŋa saageehn, ke baah ŋmee maabɔr pu saagbaŋ ni na.’”

ref: The Law teaches that offerings and sacrifices must be made because of sin. But why did Christ mention these things and say that God did not want them?
text: Njan, le u bui Uwumbɔr ke, “Saa ban tiwakor ni tijikaar aatork, kaa ban ke m di tiwakor aatork ki di see mmii ni tii si, kaa ban ke m toor kitork ngbaan titunwanbir pu.”

ref: Well, it was to do away with offerings and sacrifices and to replace them. This is what he meant by saying to God, “I have come to do what you want.”
text: Le u ki bui Uwumbɔr, “M fuu ni ke m nan ŋa saageehn.” Uma Yesu Kristo aah di ubaa toor kitork na, Uwumbɔr gaa waatork, le ki kuln kitorkpok ngbaan.

ref: So we are made holy because Christ obeyed God and offered himself once for all.
text: U ŋa Uwumbɔr aageehn, le ki di ubaa aawon toor kookoo aatork nfum mbaa, le ki ŋa timi waanib bi ye chain na.

ref: The priests do their work each day, and they keep on offering sacrifices that can never take away sins.
text: Juu yaab aatotoorb mɔmɔk tun lituln iwiin mɔmɔk tii Uwumbɔr. N‑yoonn mɔmɔk, bi toor kitork kichachaan le tii u. Kitork ngbaan aan ŋmaa nyan titunwanbir binib aasui ni.

ref: But Christ offered himself as a sacrifice that is good forever. Now he is sitting at God's right side,
text: Yesu Kristo toor kookoo aatork titunwanbir pu nfum mbaa, le ki kal Uwumbɔr aaŋangii wɔb.

ref: and he will stay there until his enemies are put under his power.
text: U bi nima ki kii bundaln Uwumbɔr ga nyaŋ waadim ki di bi ŋa utaapɔtan ni na.

ref: By his one sacrifice he has forever set free from sin the people he brings to God.
text: Kitork baan ngbaan pu, le u nyan titunwanbir binib aasui ni, ki ŋa bi binib bi ŋan ti doo ki cha n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: The Holy Spirit also speaks of this by telling us that the Lord said,
text: Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan mu tuk timi kina la. Mu nan bui

ref: “When the time comes, I will make an agreement with them. I will write my laws on their minds and hearts.
text: ke Uwumbɔr len ke, “Maah ga puu tipuur ti tii bi n‑yoonn mu choo na le ye ke m ga di maakaal ŋa bisui ni, ki ŋmee mu baalandak ni,”

ref: Then I will forget about their sins and no longer remember their evil deeds.”
text: ki ki len ke, “Maan teer baatunwanbir bɔr, kaan ki teer baah bii maakaal pu na.”

ref: When sins are forgiven, there is no more need to offer sacrifices. Encouragement and Warning
text: Kina pu na, Uwumbɔr yaa di cha pinn titunwanbir kan, baan ki toor kitork ti pu. Cha ti foor duun Uwumbɔr man

ref: My friends, the blood of Jesus gives us courage to enter the most holy place
text: Nnaabitiib, Yesu aasin pu le ti kpa lipobil ke ti koo ni chain aapepel ponn ni, Uwumbɔr aah bi nin chee na.

ref: by a new way that leads to life! And this way takes us through the curtain that is Christ himself.
text: Yesu aah di ubaa toor kitork tii Uwumbɔr na, u nyan tiwan nimɔk nan bi ti ni Uwumbɔr aakaasisik ni na, ki tii timi nsanpɔɔn mu ye nsanbamɔnn na, ke ti koo ni Uwumbɔr aah bi nin chee na.

ref: We have a great high priest who is in charge of God's house.
text: Ti kpa utotoorninkpel u joo timi bi ye Uwumbɔr aanib na.

ref: So let's come near God with pure hearts and a confidence that comes from having faith. Let's keep our hearts pure, our consciences free from evil, and our bodies washed with clean water.
text: Nima pu na, cha tisui li bi mbamɔm, aan ti duun Uwumbɔr chee, ki gaa u ki kii mbamɔm ki taa joo beeni; ba pu? Yesu Kristo aasin finn tisui ni aatunwanbir, timi aalandak taa ki li muk timi titunwanbir pu. Le bi finn timi aawon nnyun mu bi chain na ni.

ref: We must hold tightly to the hope we say is ours. After all, we can trust the one who made the agreement with us.
text: Taah bui ke ti kpa limakl na, cha ti li joo limakl ngbaan iŋaal ilee ki taa joo beeni. Ba pu? Uwumbɔr u puu tipuur tii timi na ga sil tii timi waah puu tipuur ti na.

ref: We should keep on encouraging each other to be thoughtful and to do helpful things.
text: Cha titafal li bi tɔb pu man, aan ki fiin tɔb aasui, aan ki li gee tɔb, ki tun lituln li ŋan na.

ref: Some people have given up the habit of meeting for worship, but we must not do that. We should keep on encouraging each other, especially since you know that the day of the Lord's coming is getting closer.
text: Cha ti li beenin kuuni tɔb chee ki ti dooni Uwumbɔr man, ki taa di cha, ke binib bibaa aah di cha pu na. Ni li pɔɔni tɔb aataakpab man. Ni kan ke bundaln Yesu Kristo ga gir ni na peen ni. Nima na, ni li moo pɔɔni tɔb aataakpab man.

ref: No sacrifices can be made for people who decide to sin after they find out about the truth.
text: Tɔ, unii yaa gaa Uwumbɔr aabɔr ki nyi waah ban pu na, ki yaa ki yii ki tun titunwanbir kigaak pu kan, kitork kibaa aa ki bi ki ga cha Uwumbɔr di cha pinn u.

ref: They are God's enemies, and all they can look forward to is a terrible judgment and a furious fire.
text: U ga kan ntafadaan mu kpa ijawaan na; ba pu? Uwumbɔr ga gee liŋuul pam, ki di waadim ŋa mmii mu ton sakpen na ponn ni.

ref: If two or more witnesses accused someone of breaking the Law of Moses, that person could be put to death.
text: Unii ubaa yaa nan yii Moses aakaal kan, biseeraadam bilee, bee bitaa, yaa len ke ti gbii kan, le bi ku u, kaa san u kinimbaak.

ref: But it is much worse to dishonor God's Son and to disgrace the blood of the promise that made us holy. And it is just as bad to insult the Holy Spirit, who shows us mercy.
text: Unii yaa lik Uwumbɔr Aajapɔɔn fam, ki yaa dak ke Yesu aasin mu ŋa u chain na ye fam, ki yaa sii Uwumbɔr Aafuur Nyaan mu san timi kinimbaak na kan, udaan ngbaan ŋeer ntafadaan sakpen ki jer unii u bii Moses aakaal na aah kan pu na.

ref: We know that God has said he will punish and take revenge. We also know that the Scriptures say the Lord will judge his people.
text: Ti nyi ke Uwumbɔr len ke uma le ga daa bitafal, uma le ga teen bi. U ki len ke u ga ji waanib tibɔr.

ref: It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
text: Aa yaa lir Uwumbɔr u ye limɔfadaan na aaŋaal ni kan, ni kpa ijawaan sakpen a.

ref: Don't forget all the hard times you went through when you first received the light.
text: Ni teer man n‑yoonn mu jer na. Buyoonn ninimbil nan woln njan na, ni nan jin falaa sakpen, ki nan kpa limɔr.

ref: Sometimes you were abused and mistreated in public, and at other times you shared in the sufferings of others.
text: N‑yoonn mbaa bi nan ŋa nimi bakaa, ki sii nimi binib aanimbil ni. N‑yoonn mbaa mu, ni yakr binib bi jin falaa kina na aafalaa la,

ref: You were kind to people in jail. And you gladly let your possessions be taken away, because you knew you had something better, something that would last forever.
text: ki san binib bi bi kiyondiik ni na kinimbaak. Binib aah gaa nimi aawan mpɔɔn pu na, le ni nan kpa mpopiin; ba pu? ni nyi ke ni kpa tiwan paacham ni jer baah gaa ni na, ke tiwan ngbaan ga li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: Keep on being brave! It will bring you great rewards.
text: Ni taa di nimi aapobil lii man; ba pu? nima le ga cha ni kan tinyoor sakpen.

ref: Learn to be patient, so you will please God and be given what he has promised.
text: Ni ban ni li kpa limɔr, aan ki ŋa Uwumbɔr aageehn, aan ki kan waah puu tipuur ti na.

ref: As the Scriptures say, “God is coming soon! It won't be very long.
text: Uwumbɔr Aagbaŋ len ke, “Naan yunn, u choo na ga fuu ni, kaan taan.

ref: The people God accepts will live because of their faith. But he isn't pleased with anyone who turns back.”
text: Uwumbɔr aaninyaam bi gaa u ki kii na ga li kpa limɔfal. Unii ubaa mu yaa gir puwɔb kan, waan piir Uwumbɔr aasui.”

ref: We are not like those people who turn back and get destroyed. We will keep on having faith until we are saved.
text: Tima kan, taa ye binib bi gir puwɔb aan ki beer yɔli na. Ti ye binib bi tii Uwumbɔr naadii aan ki ŋmar na la.

ref: It was their faith that made our ancestors pleasing to God.
text: N‑yaayoonn na aanib aah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii na, nima le u len ke baabimbin ŋan.

ref: Because of our faith, we know that the world was made at God's command. We also know that what can be seen was made out of what cannot be seen.
text: Ti gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, nima le cha ti bee ke u nan len ki naan kitiŋ ni paacham. U nan di tiwan ni tinimbil aa ŋmaa kani ni na naan tinimbil aah kani nimɔk na.

ref: Because Abel had faith, he offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. God was pleased with him and his gift, and even though Abel is now dead, his faith still speaks for him.
text: Abel nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, nima le cha u nan toor kitork ki ŋan ki jer ukpel Keenn aah toor pu tii Uwumbɔr na. Waah gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na, le Uwumbɔr len ke waabimbin ŋan, le ki gaa waah toor kitork ki tii u na. U kpo, le waah gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na pu, u beenin len.

ref: But without faith no one can please God. We must believe that God is real and rewards everyone who searches for him.
text: Unii yaa kaa gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii kan, waan ŋmaa piir Uwumbɔr aasui. Unii u dan Uwumbɔr chee na, see u pak ke u bi, ki pak ke u ŋani binib bi ban u na tinyoor.

ref: Because Noah had faith, he was warned about something that had not yet happened. He obeyed and built a boat that saved him and his family. In this way the people of the world were judged, and Noah was given the blessings that come to everyone who pleases God.
text: Uwumbɔr nan bui Nowa linimaln li nan choo na pu, le laa kee fuu ni. Nowa aah nan tii Uwumbɔr naadii pu na, le u nan pak waah len pu na, le ki kii waamɔb, le ki kpii buŋɔb bu, u ni waamaal koo ki ŋmar na. Nowa aah nan ŋa kina na, le ni mɔk ke dulnyaa ni yaab biken aabɔr bii Uwumbɔr chee. Nowa nan tii Uwumbɔr naadii, nima le nan cha Uwumbɔr len ke waabɔr ŋan u chee.

ref: Abraham had faith and obeyed God. He was told to go to the land that God had said would be his, and he left for a country he had never seen.
text: Uwumbɔr nan yin Abraham, ki bui u ke u buen kitiŋ ki u puu tipuur ke u ga di tii u na. Abraham aah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na le u kii waamɔb, le ki nyan waatiŋ ni, ki buen, kaa nyi waah cha nin chee na.

ref: Because Abraham had faith, he lived as a stranger in the promised land. He lived there in a tent, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who were later given the same promise.
text: U nan ti fuu kitiŋ ki Uwumbɔr puu tipuur ke u ga di tii u na ni. Le u pak Uwumbɔr aah len pu na, nima le u nan kal nima, ki nan ye uwɔwɔnja. U ni waabo Aisak, ni uyaabil Jakob nan bi nima, ŋiboo ponn ni. Bi mu nan yeh tipuur tichachaan ngbaan la.

ref: Abraham did this, because he was waiting for the eternal city God had planned and built.
text: U nan ban kitiŋ ki ga li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon aan Uwumbɔr maa ki na la.

ref: Even when Sarah was too old to have children, she had faith that God would do what he had promised, and she had a son.
text: Abraham aapuu Sara mu nan tii Uwumbɔr naadii, nima le nan cha u kan mpɔɔn ke u dek lipuul, buyoonn u jer timar na. Ba pu? u nan pak ke Uwumbɔr ga ŋa waah puu tipuur ti na.

ref: Her husband Abraham was almost dead, but he became the ancestor of many people. In fact, there are as many of them as there are stars in the sky or grains of sand along the seashore.
text: Nima pu na, ujabaan u nan bi ke waah kpo le na, nan ma binib bi wiir ke iŋmabi aah wiir pu na. Bi wiir ke litambol li dɔ nnyusakpem aagbaan na. Ubaa aa ŋmaa kahn bi.

ref: Every one of those people died. But they still had faith, even though they had not received what they had been promised. They were glad just to see these things from far away, and they agreed that they were only strangers and foreigners on this earth.
text: Binib ngbaan mɔmɔk nan tii Uwumbɔr naadii le ki ti saa baakundaal, kaa kan Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ti na. Bi nan bee ke n‑yoonn mu choo na, u ga nan ŋa waah puu tipuur ti na. Bi nan len ke bi ye bicham le dulnyaa wee ni.

ref: When people talk this way, it is clear they are looking for a place to call their own.
text: Binib bi len kina na mɔk chain ke bi ban bite do la.

ref: If they had been talking about the land where they had once lived, they could have gone back at any time.
text: Binimbil yaa ba man kitiŋ ki bi nyan ni ki ponn ni na pu kan, bi ba ga li kpa nsan ke bi gir buen nima.

ref: But they were looking forward to a better home in heaven. This is why God wasn't ashamed for them to call him their God. He even built a city for them.
text: Bi nan ban kitiŋ ki ŋan jer kitiŋ ngbaan na la. Bi nan ban paacham aatiŋ la. Nima pu na, inimɔɔn aa nan joo Uwumbɔr ke bi yin u ke Baawumbɔr. U nan toor kitiŋ tii bi.

ref: Later, when Jacob was about to die, he leaned on his walking stick and worshiped. Then because of his faith he blessed each of Joseph's sons.
text: Jakob nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, nima le nan cha u ŋa Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa waabo Josef aabim bilee pu buyoonn u nan ban u kpo na, le ki nyii waajaangbeedabil pu, ki doon Uwumbɔr.

ref: And right before Joseph died, he had faith that God would lead the people of Israel out of Egypt. So he told them to take his bones with them.
text: Josef nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, nima le waah nan ban u kpo na, u len ke Israel yaab ga nya Ijipt aatiŋ ponn ni, ki tuk bi ke bi yaa nan nyan kan, bi yoor waawon di buen.

ref: Because Moses' parents had faith, they kept him hidden until he was three months old. They saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid to disobey the king's orders.
text: Moses aate ni una aah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na, le bi nan di u bɔr iŋmal itaa. Bi nan kan ke u ye ubo u ŋan sakpen na, kina pu na, baa nan san Ubɔr Faro aah nan siin ke bi ku bima Israel yaab aabijabim pu na aakaal.

ref: Then after Moses grew up, his faith made him refuse to be called the king's grandson.
text: Moses nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, nima le waah nan chikr na, waa nan kii ke bi yin u ke Ubɔr Faro aabisal aabo.

ref: He chose to be mistreated with God's people instead of having the good time that sin could bring for a little while.
text: U nan kii ke u ni Uwumbɔr aanib kpaan ji falaa, ke ni soor ni u ji titunwanbir aamɔɔn mu kaa yunn na.

ref: Moses knew that the treasures of Egypt were not as wonderful as what he would receive from suffering for the Messiah, and he looked forward to his reward.
text: U nan bee ke u yaa kan ŋisiibil Kristo pu kan, u ga nan kan tinyoor ti jer Ijipt aatiŋ aawankpal mɔmɔk na. Ba pu? utafal nan bi tinyoor ti Uwumbɔr ga tii u na ni la.

ref: His faith also made him celebrate Passover. He sprinkled the blood of animals on the doorposts, so that the first-born sons of the people of Israel would not be killed by the destroying angel.
text: Waah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na le u nan bui Israel yaab ke bi kɔr ipihbi, ki di nsin gbaa gbaa ibisamɔi, aan Uwumbɔr aatuun u ga ku mbipolb na taa nan ŋa bi nibaa.

ref: Because of their faith, the people walked through the Red Sea on dry land. But when the Egyptians tried to do it, they were drowned.
text: Israel yaab aah nan ban ke bi puur Limɔɔkal Aanyusakpem, baah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na, le nnyun nan yakr ki cha nsan tii bi, le bi puur. Ijipt aatiŋ aanib aah nan ban bi mu puur na, bi nan bee nnyun ni la.

ref: God's people had faith, and when they had walked around the city of Jericho for seven days, its walls fell down.
text: Israel yaab nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, nima le baah nan chuun manni Jeriko aatiŋ aagon iwiin ilole na, ŋi nan lir.

ref: Rahab had been a prostitute, but she had faith and welcomed the spies. So she wasn't killed with the people who disobeyed.
text: Rahab, u nan ye upiidagoor na, nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, ki chann bipepekb tichann. Waah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na, le baa nan ku u buyoonn bi kuln waatiŋ aanib bi kaa kii Uwumbɔr aamɔb na.

ref: What else can I say? There isn't enough time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets.
text: Tɔ, m ga ki len ke ba? Maa kpa n‑yoonn ke m len Gideonn, ni Barak, ni Samsonn, ni Jefta, ni David, ni Samuel, ni Uwumbɔr aabɔnabtiib aabɔr.

ref: Their faith helped them conquer kingdoms, and because they did right, God made promises to them. They closed the jaws of lions
text: Baah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na, le bibaa nan nyaŋ ŋitimbol aajab, bibaa mu tun lituln li ŋan na, bibaa mu kan Uwumbɔr aah puu tipuur ti na, bibaa mu muib ichinn aamɔi, i taa ŋa bi nibaa.

ref: Some women received their loved ones back from death. Many of these people were tortured, but they refused to be released. They were sure they would get a better reward when the dead are raised to life.
text: Bipiib bibaa aah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na, le biyaab bi kpo na nan fikr nkun ni. Bibaa mu aah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na, le binib gbaa ku bi. Baa yii Uwumbɔr ke bi nyan bibaa nkun ni. Bi nan pak ke bi ga kan limɔfal li ŋan ki jer dulnyaa wee aamɔfal na paacham.

ref: Others were made fun of and beaten with whips, and some were chained in jail.
text: Bibaa mu aah nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii pu na, le binib nan ŋa bi mbɔnyun, ki lue bi ŋinaalab, ki buu bi tikululn, ki laŋ bi kiyondiik ni.

ref: The world did not deserve these good people, who had to wander in deserts and on mountains and had to live in caves and holes in the ground.
text: Bi nan ye biwɔwɔm, ki nan bi kipɔɔk ni, ni ŋijoo paab, ki koo titakpalunn ni, ni ibuu i bi kitiŋ ni na. Bi mu nan ye bininyaam ki jer dulnyaa wee aanib.

ref: All of them pleased God because of their faith! But still they died without being given what had been promised.
text: Binib ngbaan mɔmɔk nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii, nima le nan cha u len ke baabɔr ŋan. Bi mu aa kan tiwan ni u nan puu tipuur ke u ga tii bi na,

ref: This was because God had something better in store for us. And he did not want them to reach the goal of their faith without us.
text: Ba pu? u nan ban ke u ŋa ti mu tiŋann sakpen la. U nan ban ke u di timi, ni bi mu, kpaan ŋa binib bi ŋan ti doo na la.

ref: Such a large crowd of witnesses is all around us! So we must get rid of everything that slows us down, especially the sin that just won't let go. And we must be determined to run the race that is ahead of us.
text: Tɔ, n‑yaayoonn na aanib bi nan gaa Uwumbɔr ki kii na wiir pam, ki gonn timi, ki lik taah dii Uwumbɔr aasan pu na. Nima pu na, cha ti di tiwan nimɔk leŋ timi na lii, ki di cha titunwanbir ti dii timi na, ki li kpa limɔr, ki li dii Uwumbɔr aasan.

ref: We must keep our eyes on Jesus, who leads us and makes our faith complete. He endured the shame of being nailed to a cross, because he knew later on he would be glad he did. Now he is seated at the right side of God's throne!
text: Cha ti li lik Yesu chee man. Waapɔɔn pu le ti nan piin ki gaa u ki kii. Waapɔɔn mu pu, le ti ga tii u naadii, ki ti saa ndoon. Mpopiin mu u ga nan kan mu na pu, le u jin falaa ni inimɔɔn ndɔpuinkoo pu, ki lik inimɔɔn ngbaan fam. Dandana wee le u ka Uwumbɔr aabɔrjal aaŋangii wɔb.

ref: So keep your mind on Jesus, who put up with many insults from sinners. Then you won't get discouraged and give up.
text: Titunwanbirdam nan nan u, ki yii u. Le u nan kpa limɔr. Ni teer kina man, aan ki taa cha nitaakpab yɔl aan ni di waasan di lii.

ref: None of you have yet been hurt in your battle against sin.
text: Ni yii titunwanbir, le ki pɔɔni nibaa ke ni taa lir; ni mu aa kee kpo nsanyaan ngbaan pu.

ref: But you have forgotten that the Scriptures say to God's children, “When the Lord punishes you, don't make light of it, and when he corrects you, don't be discouraged.
text: Ni suln Uwumbɔr aah sur nimi pu na aa? U yin nimi waabim ki bui ke, “Maabo, Uwumbɔr yaa sak si kan, ŋun mbamɔm. U yaa cha falaa pii si ke u chiin si kan, taa cha aataakpab yɔl.

ref: The Lord corrects the people he loves and disciplines those he calls his own.”
text: Ba pu? Uwumbɔr sak binib bimɔk u gee bi na, ki dar binib bi u ŋa bi waabim na mɔmɔk aatafal.”

ref: Be patient when you are being corrected! This is how God treats his children. Don't all parents correct their children?
text: Tɔ, naah ji falaa pu na, Uwumbɔr mɔk nimi nlan le na. U ŋa nimi ke binib aah ŋani baabim pu na la. Ubo ubaa aa bi, kaa kan ntafadaan ute chee.

ref: God corrects all his children, and if he doesn't correct you, then you don't really belong to him.
text: Uwumbɔr yaa kaa daa nitafal, ke waah dar waabim mɔmɔk aatafal pu na kan, naa ye waabim, ni ye mbɔmbim le u chee.

ref: Our earthly fathers correct us, and we still respect them. Isn't it even better to be given true life by letting our spiritual Father correct us?
text: Titetiib bi ma timi na nan dar titafal la, le ti pak bi. Nima le ni ŋan ke ti kii Tite Uwumbɔr u bi paacham na aamɔb ki jer kina, aan ki kan limɔfal.

ref: Our human fathers correct us for a short time, and they do it as they think best. But God corrects us for our own good, because he wants us to be holy, as he is.
text: Taah nan ye mbim buyoonn na, titetiib nan dar titafal, baah gee pu na. Uwumbɔr ma kan, u dar titafal ke u ŋa timi tinyoor, aan ti yakr waabimbin mu bi chain na la.

ref: It is never fun to be corrected. In fact, at the time it is always painful. But if we learn to obey by being corrected, we will do right and live at peace.
text: Buyoonn ti kan ntafadaan na, ni wu la, naa ye mpopiin aawan. Binib mu yaa kan ntafadaan kan, nee aapuwɔb le bi kani nsuudoon ni mbimbinyaan. Mmɔkm ni nsurm kpaam

ref: Now stand up straight! Stop your knees from shaking
text: Nima pu na, ni li yoor iŋaal i bak na man, ki li pɔɔni nitaakpab,

ref: and walk a straight path. Then lame people will be healed, instead of getting worse. Warning against Turning from God
text: ki li beenin dii nsan mu tok na, aan binib bi joo beeni na taa yenn; bi mu li dii mbamɔm.

ref: Try to live at peace with everyone! Live a clean life. If you don't, you will never see the Lord.
text: Ni mɔmɔk pɔɔ nibaa ki li kpa kimɔbaan man, ki li bi chain. Unii umɔk kaa ye chain na aan kan Tidindaan.

ref: Make sure no one misses out on God's wonderful kindness. Don't let anyone become bitter and cause trouble for the rest of you.
text: Ni li nyi man, ubaa taa lann Uwumbɔr aanyoor. Ni li nyi man, ubaa taa cha usui li to, ki li muk nimi ki cha binib pam yenn.

ref: Watch out for immoral and ungodly people like Esau, who sold his future blessing for only one meal.
text: Ni li nyi man, ubaa mu taa gɔr kidagook. Ubaa mu taa lik Uwumbɔr fam ke Esɔ aah nan ŋa pu na. Tijikaar pu, le u nan di ubopol aafaal kooh.

ref: You know how he later wanted it back. But there was nothing he could do to change things, even though he begged his father and cried.
text: Nee aapuwɔb na, u nan ki ban lifaal li ye Uwumbɔr aanyoor ngbaan na, kaa kan. Waa nan ŋmaa kpeln waah nan ŋa pu na. U nan wii ki gaŋni ute ke u ŋa Uwumbɔr aanyoor ŋa u pu. Le ute yii.

ref: You have not come to a place like Mount Sinai that can be seen and touched. There is no flaming fire or dark cloud or storm
text: Tɔ, naa fuu ni dulnyaa wee ni aajool chee. Israel yaab nan fuu ni Sainai aajool chee, ki kan lijool ngbaan gaal mmii ki kpa iŋmanyuu i bɔɔn ki bɔln nima chee na. Bi nan ŋun kibuŋ ki daar na,

ref: or trumpet sound. The people of Israel heard a voice speak. But they begged it to stop,
text: ki ŋun kakaan wii mpɔɔn pu, ki ŋun nneel mu len mpɔɔn pu. Baah ŋun nneel ngbaan pu na, le bi gaŋ Uwumbɔr ke u taa ki len bi chee tibɔr.

ref: because they could not obey its commands. They were even told to kill any animal that touched the mountain.
text: U nan bui bi ke kiwakork kibaa yaa po meeh lijool ngbaan kan, bi mae ki ŋitakpal ki ti kpo. Nima le ijawaan nan joo bi sakpen.

ref: The sight was so frightening that Moses said he shook with fear.
text: Baah kan tiwan ni na nan kpa ijawaan pam. Moses mu nan len ke ijawaan joo u sakpen, le uwon gbaa.

ref: You have now come to Mount Zion and to the heavenly Jerusalem. This is the city of the living God, where thousands and thousands of angels have come to celebrate.
text: Naa fuu ni lijool ngbaan chee. Ni fuu ni Sionn aajool chee la. Nima chee le Uwumbɔr u ye limɔfadaan na aatiŋ bi. Kitiŋ ngbaan ye Jerusalem la, ki bi paacham. Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib churbaka bi ki ponn ni.

ref: Here you will find all of God's dearest children, whose names are written in heaven. And you will find God himself, who judges everyone. Here also are the spirits of those good people who have been made perfect.
text: Ni fuu ni Uwumbɔr aabipolb bi aayimbil ŋmee paacham na aakuun chee la. Ni fuu ni Uwumbɔr u ye binib mɔmɔk aabɔjir na chee. Ni fuu ni bininyaam aawiin mu Uwumbɔr ŋa mu, mu ŋan ti doo na chee.

ref: And Jesus is here! He is the one who makes God's new agreement with us, and his sprinkled blood says much better things than the blood of Abel.
text: Ni fuu ni Yesu chee la. U pu, le Uwumbɔr puu tipuupɔln tii timi. Uma Yesu aasin mu yaa ti pu na le ŋa timi chain. Mu pu, le Uwumbɔr di cha pinn timi. Waasin ngbaan len tibɔr ti ŋan jer Abel aasin aah nan len pu na.

ref: Make sure you obey the one who speaks to you. The people did not escape, when they refused to obey the one who spoke to them at Mount Sinai. Do you think you can possibly escape, if you refuse to obey the one who speaks to you from heaven?
text: Ni li nyi man, ki taa yii Uwumbɔr u len ni chee na. Buyoonn u nan sur Israel yaab dulnyaa wee ni na, le bi yii, le u daa bitafal. Ti yaa yii Yesu u nyan ni paacham ki nan sur timi na kan, u ga sil daa titafal.

ref: When God spoke the first time, his voice shook only the earth. This time he has promised to shake the earth once again, and heaven too.
text: N‑yaayoonn na waaneel nan cha kitiŋ deŋ. Dandana wee u puu tipuur ke u ga ki cha kitiŋ ni paacham mɔk deŋ.

ref: The words “once again” mean that these created things will someday be shaken and removed. Then what cannot be shaken will last.
text: Waah len kina na, ni mɔk timi ke u ga deŋ waah nan naan tiwan nimɔk na, ki nyan ni, ki cha tiwan ni kaan deŋ na.

ref: We should be grateful we were given a kingdom that cannot be shaken. And in this kingdom we please God by worshiping him and by showing him great honor and respect.
text: Ti ga ji nnaan mu ga li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Nima pu na, cha ti doon Uwumbɔr, ki tun lituln li ga piir usui na tii u, ki li pak u, ki li san u ijawaan.

ref: Keep being concerned about each other as the Lord's followers should.
text: Tɔ, ni li beenin gee tɔb man ke naabitiib na.

ref: Be sure to welcome strangers into your home. By doing this, some people have welcomed angels as guests, without even knowing it.
text: Ni li teer ki chann bicham tichann. Binib bibaa nan chann Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib tichann, kaa nyi ke Uwumbɔr aatuuntiib ye.

ref: Remember the Lord's people who are in jail and be concerned for them. Don't forget those who are suffering, but imagine you are there with them.
text: Ni teer man binib bi bi kiyondiik ni na, ke nimi le aah bi ki ni na, ki teer man binib bi ji falaa na. Ba pu? ni mu bi tiwon tee ni la.

ref: Have respect for marriage. Always be faithful to your partner, because God will punish anyone who is immoral or unfaithful in marriage.
text: Tɔ, chatiib ni puutiib, ni li nyi ke Uwumbɔr le di nimi kpaan, ki li pak kina, ki taa gɔr kidagook man. Binib bi chuun bɔɔni na, ni binib bi chuun gɔr kidagook na, Uwumbɔr ga ji bi tibɔr.

ref: Don't fall in love with money. Be satisfied with what you have. The Lord has promised that he will not leave us or desert us.
text: Ni taa cha ninimbil li man ŋimombil pu. Cha ninimbil gbiin naah kpa ni na pu. Ba pu? Uwumbɔr ubaa le bui ke waan di cha si. Waan di si lii.

ref: This should make you feel like saying, “The Lord helps me! Why should I be afraid of what people can do to me?”
text: Nima pu le ti ga li kpa lipobil ki bui ke, “Uwumbɔr ye maateter la. Maan san ijawaan. Ubaa aan ŋmaa ŋa mi nibaa.”

ref: Don't forget about your leaders who taught you God's message. Remember what kind of lives they lived and try to have faith like theirs.
text: Ni teer man nimi aayidam bi tuk nimi Uwumbɔr aabɔr na, ki li teer baamɔfal aah doo pu na, ki li beenin dii Yesu aasan ke baah nan dii pu na.

ref: Don't be fooled by any kind of strange teachings. It is better to receive strength from God's gift of undeserved grace than to depend on certain foods. After all, these foods don't really help the people who eat them.
text: Ni taa dii mmɔkm yayan aabɔŋ aabɔŋ ki yenn. Ni ŋan ke nisui doon Uwumbɔr aaterm pu, naa ye tijikaar pu. Binib bi kɔ tijikaar tibaa ki ji tiken na, naa ŋa bi tinyoor.

ref: But we have an altar where even the priests who serve in the place of worship have no right to eat.
text: Timi aatork aabimbiln le ye Yesu aadɔpuinkoo. Juu yaab aatotoorb aan ŋmaa ji timi aatork.

ref: After the high priest offers the blood of animals as a sin offering, the bodies of those animals are burned outside the camp.
text: Bi yaa toor kitork kan, le baatotoorninkpel di nsin koo ni chain aapepel ponn ni, titunwanbir pu. Le bi nyan tinann ngbaan kitiŋ ponn ni ki di buen n‑gbaan, bi ti di see mmii.

ref: Jesus himself suffered outside the city gate, so his blood would make people holy.
text: Nima pu le Yesu mu nan kpo kitiŋ aagbaan, ke waasin finn tisui, ki ŋa timi chain.

ref: This is why we should go outside the camp to Jesus and share in his disgrace.
text: Nima pu na, ti li cha u chee n‑gbaan nima, ki dii waasan, ki yakr u chee waanimɔɔn.

ref: On this earth we don't have a city that lasts forever, but we are waiting for such a city.
text: Tido u bi dulnyaa wee ni na aan li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Ti ban tido u bi dulnyaa u choo na ni la.

ref: Our sacrifice is to keep offering praise to God in the name of Jesus.
text: Yesu pu, cha ti pak Uwumbɔr n‑yoonn mɔmɔk, ki li dooni u waabulchinn pu. Nima le ye kitork ki tii u.

ref: But don't forget to help others and to share your possessions with them. This too is like offering a sacrifice that pleases God.
text: Ni teer man aan ki li tun lituln li ŋan na, ki yakr naah kpa ni na tii tɔb man. Nima le ye kitork ki ga piir Uwumbɔr aasui mbamɔm na.

ref: Obey your leaders and do what they say. They are watching over you, and they must answer to God. So don't make them sad as they do their work. Make them happy. Otherwise, they won't be able to help you at all.
text: Ni li keei nimi aayidam aamɔi man, ki taa kpak bi. Bitafal bi ni ponn ni, ke ni dii Uwumbɔr aasan mbamɔm. Bi nyi ke see bi mɔk Uwumbɔr baah nan joo nimi pu na. Ni yaa keei baamɔi kan, bi ga li kpa mpopiin, le ki joo nimi. Ni yaa kaa keei baamɔi kan, bi ga li kpa mpombiin, le ki joo nimi. Nima le aan ŋa nimi tinyoor.

ref: I especially want you to pray that I can visit you again soon. Final Prayers and Greetings
text: M gaŋ nimi ke ni li moo mee Uwumbɔr ki tii mi, ke u ter mi, aan m gir ni ni chee mala. Kookoo aameel

ref: God gives peace, and he raised our Lord Jesus Christ from death. Now Jesus is like a Great Shepherd whose blood was used to make God's eternal agreement with his flock.
text: Uwumbɔr nan fikr Tidindaan Yesu u ye waanib mɔmɔk aayidaan na nkun ni. Waasin pu, le Uwumbɔr puu tipuupɔln tii timi. Tipuur ngbaan ga li bi n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na.

ref: I pray God will make you ready to obey him and that you will always be eager to do right. May Jesus help you do what pleases God. To Jesus Christ be glory forever and ever! Amen.
text: Uwumbɔr, u tii timi nsuudoon na, toor nimi aabimbin mbamɔm, aan ni li ŋani waah gee pu na. Cha u ŋa nimi binib bi ga piir usui na Yesu Kristo pu. Uma le yeh mpakm n‑yoonn mu kaa kpa ndoon na. Amii. Kookoo aabɔr

ref: My friends, I have written only a short letter to encourage you, and I beg you to pay close attention to what I have said.
text: Nnaabitiib, m gaŋ nimi, ni li ji limɔr ki pel maah sur nimi kigbaŋ kee ponn ni pu na. Maah ŋmee pu na, ni ye siib la.

ref: By now you surely must know that our friend Timothy is out of jail. If he gets here in time, I will bring him with me when I come to visit you.
text: M ban ke ni bee ke bi nan di tina aabo Timoti di lii. U yaa fuu ni mala kan, m ni uma ga kan nimi.

ref: Please give my greetings to your leaders and to the rest of the Lord's people. His followers from Italy send you their greetings.
text: Ni doon nimi aayidam mɔmɔk, ni Uwumbɔr aanib biken mɔmɔk tii timi. Binib bi ye Itali aatiŋ aanib na dooni nimi.

ref: I pray that God will be kind to all of you!
text: Uwumbɔr ŋa tinyoor ŋa ni mɔmɔk pu. Amii.

ref: From James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ. Greetings to the twelve tribes scattered all over the world. Faith and Wisdom
text: Min Jems, u ye Uwumbɔr ni Tidindaan Yesu Kristo aatutunn na, m dooni Uwumbɔr aanib bi yaa ki bi itingbaan mɔmɔk ni na. Gaakii ni nlan

ref: My friends, be glad, even if you have a lot of trouble.
text: Nnaabitiib, ni yaa kan ntɔŋ mɔmɔk aabɔŋ kan, ni cha ni mɔmɔk li ye mpopiin ni chee.

ref: You know you learn to endure by having your faith tested.
text: Ba pu? ni bee ke ni yaa kan ntɔŋ, kaa koo mu ni kan, nima le tii nimi limɔr.

ref: But you must learn to endure everything, so you will be completely mature and not lacking in anything.
text: Ni mu li nyi man ki li kpa limɔr ki ti saa naadoon, ki taa di cha, aan ki li ye binib bi ŋan doo na, ki taa li kpa taani ubaa, ki taa lir.

ref: If any of you need wisdom, you should ask God, and it will be given to you. God is generous and won't correct you for asking.
text: Ni ponn ni ubaa yaa lann nlan kan, cha u mee Uwumbɔr, le u ga tii u; ba pu? Uwumbɔr tii binib mɔmɔk sakpen, kaa jinni ubaa inimɔɔn.

ref: But when you ask for something, you must have faith and not doubt. Anyone who doubts is like an ocean wave tossed around in a storm.
text: U mu yaa mee Uwumbɔr kan, u li pak ke u ga kan, ki taa joo beeni; ba pu? unii u joo beeni na naahn ke libuln aah daar kan, nnyusakpem aanyunkpuŋ feei pu na.

ref: If you are that kind of person, you can't make up your mind, and you surely can't be trusted. So don't expect the Lord to give you anything at all. Poor People and Rich People
text: Ulandak aa si tiwanbaan pu, u saa labr, ki nya do, ki ti saa do la. Igiin ni liwangol

ref: Any of God's people who are poor should be glad he thinks so highly of them.
text: Tɔ, Uwumbɔr aah nyuŋ tinaabitiib bi ye bigiim na, bi li kpa mpopiin.

ref: But any who are rich should be glad when God makes them humble. Rich people will disappear like wild flowers
text: Waah sunn tinaabitiib bi ye biwankpadam na taab na, bi mu li kpa mpopiin; ba pu? bi ga jer ke mmopuun aah gbaar mala pu na.

ref: scorched by the burning heat of the sun. The flowers lose their blossoms, and their beauty is destroyed. This is how the rich will disappear, as they go about their business. Trials and Temptations
