text: Le bi nan sɔb kugbɔŋ nan ki tun bi: Yisa a tooi nin biwonjiɛm a sanliib nin ban ye ni nabum le sɔb kugbɔŋ nan, Ki tenn nim yadadam ban kaa ye Juu yaab wee ki be Antiɛg nin Siriya nin Silisiya: Ti poor ni.

ref: We have heard that some people from here have terribly upset you by what they said. But we did not send them!
text: Ti gbir ke ti ni biba dan ni ban le naa ye tim le tun bi, ki jɔɔ tibɔr ti ba ki pag ni, le ni mugir ni ki ŋmarin ni potiɛl.

ref: So we met together and decided to choose some men and to send them to you along with our good friends Barnabas and Paul.
text: Ni bu le ti chee ki gann bininfob biba bi ma nin ti jɔtiib Banabasi nin Pɔɔl ke bin dan ni ban,

ref: These men have risked their lives for our Lord Jesus Christ.
text: ban junn bi miɛfol ti Yudaau Yisa Masiya a yinl bu-n.

ref: We are also sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you in person the same things that we are writing.
text: Nima bu le ti tun Judasi nin Silasi ke bin nan ta bi mɔb ki pag bei ni ta sɔb nan.

ref: The Holy Spirit has shown us that we should not place any extra burden on you.
text: Ni ŋan ki sei Kasi a Naaŋ nin tim wee ti laa che nin mug ni ki jo nsiim man sɔb nan ni:

ref: But you should not eat anything offered to idols. You should not eat any meat that still has the blood in it or any meat of any animal that has been strangled. You must also not commit any terrible sexual sins. If you follow these instructions, you will do well. We send our best wishes.
text: Ni laa ji tijiir tan wee bi ta mann ibawoli, ni laa ji nchami, ni laa ŋma kuwankobug kan wee bi ŋmaan ŋmaan ku a nann ni, wee ki laa tun iwanjaab toon lipiibanlin bee lijabanlin ni. Ni pɔɔn niba wee ki nya ni niɛ nan yaan na. Ni laan paara.

ref: The four men left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. Then they called the church members together and gave them the letter.
text: Le bi tun bi, le bi jon jir Antiɛg, nin yaan le bi lagin biwonjiɛm a laguŋin biɛn ki sei be kugbɔŋin.

ref: When the letter was read, everyone was pleased and greatly encouraged.
text: Baah karin kugbɔŋin nin, le ni ŋa bi nmɔn nin baah ta pɔɔninba a kpaan yan ki sei bin bu.

ref: Judas and Silas were prophets, and they spoke a long time, encouraging and helping the Lord's followers.
text: Judasi nin Silasi ban mu nan ye bilinlemin, nan pag takpem le ki pɔɔg biwonjiɛm nmɔn a gbanann nin bi sufu.

ref: The men from Jerusalem stayed on in Antioch for a while. And when they left to return to the ones who had sent them, the followers wished them well.
text: Baah nan yuur nin yaan wama-n, a bɔɔn bu, le biwonjiɛmin nan chiɛn bi nsan bu nin tikaar nin nposɔɔn, le bi jir kun ban tun bin ban.

ref: But Paul and Barnabas stayed on in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached about the Lord. Paul and Barnabas Go Their Separate Ways
text: Amaa le Pɔɔl nin Banabasi nan paar Antiɛg, le bi ma nin bi tab takpem nan mɔɔn tibɔŋann nin ki sei bininfob ki ji wɔɔn bi Uyudaan a bɔr. Pɔɔl nin Banabasi kaah yiɛr man

ref: Sometime later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let's go back and visit the Lord's followers in the cities where we preached his message. Then we will know how they are doing.”
text: Ni nan yuur wamau le Pɔɔl nan bei Banabasi ke, “Che ti jir tan gɔnn ti nabum ban biɛn be ntim man yaan wee ti nan mɔɔn Uyudaau a bɔr ki sei bi-n, ki kan baah tun man.”

ref: Barnabas wanted to take along John, whose other name was Mark.
text: Le Banabasi nan ban bin ta Jɔnn wan a yinl ji ye Mag ki kpiɛ bi bu,

ref: But Paul did not want to, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia and had stopped working with them.
text: amaa le Pɔɔl kaa chee ke bin ta Jɔnn Mag ki kpiɛ, nan bu-n u nan jiɛn bi le Pamfiliya ki labir kun kaa ji kpiɛg bi bu itoon nin yaan ni.

ref: Paul and Barnabas argued, then each of them went his own way. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus,
text: Bi mɔkpel nmɔn kaah nan pɔɔn bu le nan che Pɔɔl nin Banabasi yiɛr tab. Le Banabasi ta Jɔnn Mag, le bi kɔɔ kuŋaluŋ ki jon Saipuru.

ref: but Paul took Silas and left after the followers had placed them in God's care.
text: Amaa le Pɔɔl mu gann Silasi. Le biwonjiɛmin ta bi ki ŋa Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanlin le bi jon.

ref: They traveled through Syria and Cilicia, encouraging the churches.
text: Le u nɔɔ Siriya nin Silisiya a timin ki pɔɔgir biwonjiɛm a laginn a gbanann.

ref: Paul and Silas went back to Derbe and Lystra, where there was a follower named Timothy. His mother was also a follower. She was Jewish, and his father was Greek.
text: Le Pɔɔl foon Deba, le ki jon foo Lisitira, nan yaan wee u kan ubɔɔnɔɔr wan wee bi yi u ke Timoti. Wan a na nan ye Juu a ninfou ki ye yada daan ni, amaa le u baa ye Girig a ninfou.

ref: The Lord's followers in Lystra and Iconium said good things about Timothy,
text: Nnabum ban be Lisitira nin Ikoniɛm a timin nan pag Timoti pam.

ref: and Paul wanted him to go with them. But Paul first had him circumcised, because all the Jewish people around there knew that Timothy's father was Greek.
text: Pɔɔl nan ban un ta Timoti le jo nsan nmɔn, ni ma bu le u nan jii u punl Juu yaab ban nan be niin nin bu, nan bu-n bi biɛn nan nyi Timoti a baa kaah ye Girig a jau.

ref: As Paul and the others went from city to city, they told the followers what the apostles and leaders in Jerusalem had decided, and they urged them to follow these instructions.
text: Baah nan choon ntimin nin, le bi nan mɔɔn tibɔr tan wee itoon nin bisanliib ban be Jerusalam nan pag choo ki wɔɔn ke bi li nɔɔ-n.

ref: The churches became stronger in their faith, and each day more people put their faith in the Lord. Paul's Vision in Troas
text: Le biwonjiɛmin a yada nan pɔɔgir le bi kanl kpiɛg lidaal biɛn. Pɔɔl kaah nan kan zii Tirosi a tiŋin man

ref: Paul and his friends went through Phrygia and Galatia, but the Holy Spirit would not let them preach in Asia.
text: Kasi a Naaŋ kaah kaa nan chee ke bin mɔɔn tibɔrin nmɔn Asiya a yerin nin ni, le Pɔɔl nin u ninɔɔtabin nan nɔɔ Ferijiya nin Galantiya a tingbɔŋin.

ref: After they arrived in Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not let them.
text: Baah nan tan foo Misiya a timin a tarigin, bi ni nan ban bin kɔɔ Batiniya a timin le, amaa le Yisa a Naaŋ kaa chee ke bin kɔɔ.

ref: So they went on through Mysia until they came to Troas.
text: Mambu che bi nan lagir Misiya a tiŋ bu ki jon Tirosi.

ref: During the night, Paul had a vision of someone from Macedonia who was standing there and begging him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
text: Kunyiɛg kaah nan foo-n le Pɔɔl kan zii, u zii nmɔn a poolin le Masedoniya a jau uba si ki balin u ke, “Dan Masedoniya ki nan ter ti ni.”

ref: After Paul had seen the vision, we began looking for a way to go to Macedonia. We were sure that God had called us to preach the good news there. Lydia Becomes a Follower of the Lord
text: Pɔɔl kaah kan zii nmɔn a bɔɔn, le ti ŋa sili weem ke ti jo Masedoniya, nan bu-n ti nan biɛ ke Uwonbɔr le ke ti jo nin yaan ki tan mɔɔn tibɔŋann nin ki sei nin yaan a ninfob. Lidiya kaah nan kpenn u binbem Filipi man

ref: We sailed straight from Troas to Samothrace, and the next day we arrived in Neapolis.
text: Taah nan nyan Tirosi a tiŋin, ti nan jon limɔgilin le ki tan kɔɔ kuŋaluŋ ki jon Samotara, le ni won kutaag le ti foo Niɛpolisi.

ref: From there we went to Philippi, which is a Roman colony in the first district of Macedonia. We spent several days in Philippi.
text: Ti nan nyan nin yaan ki jon Filipi, kitiŋ nmɔn nan be Rom yaab a nɔɔn le ki ye kitiŋ takpeŋ Masedoniya a yerin nin. Ti nan be niin ki yuur wamau.

ref: Then on the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to a place by the river, where we thought there would be a Jewish meeting place for prayer. We sat down and talked with the women who came.
text: Likpakɔɔl daal le ti nɔɔ nyan kitiŋ nmɔn a timansanmɔnn ki jon nkpenn, ti nan ban nan yaan wee ti li miɛ Uwonbɔr le. Le ti kal ki piin ki pag tenn bipiib ban nan lagin niin nmɔn.

ref: One of them was Lydia, who was from the city of Thyatira and sold expensive purple cloth. She was a worshiper of the Lord God, and he made her willing to accept what Paul was saying.
text: Bipiib ban nan ka pelig tibɔr nmɔn, bi ni u ba a yinl le nan ye Lidiya, u nan nyan Tayatira le, ki choon kɔɔr ikinken man yan a daag pɔɔ, ki jiɛn Uwonbɔr. Le Uyudaan loor u sufu le u chee tibɔr tan wee Pɔɔl pagin.

ref: Then after she and her family were baptized, she kept on begging us, “If you think I really do have faith in the Lord, come stay in my home.” Finally, we accepted her invitation. Paul and Silas Are Put in Jail
text: Taah nan fun u ma nin u niin yaab Uwonbɔr a nyunfulin, le u gɔɔ ti ke ti jo u niin. Le ki ke, “Ni ye ni sin nyi ke n ŋa ti Yudaau yada ke, ni li chaan ki nan be n niin.” Le u balin ti le ti jon. Baah loon Pɔɔl nin Silasi Filipi a tiŋin man

ref: One day on our way to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl. She had a spirit in her that gave her the power to tell the future. By doing this she made a lot of money for her owners.
text: Weemba le ti nan chaa baah miɛ Uwonbɔr nan yaan nin, taah nan chaa-n, le kibisiɛg ki ba to ti nsan, u nan ye uyom le. Le kinaaŋ be u bu le ki ŋa u uninligir. Waah nan ye uninligir nbu, u nan ga ilig takpem ki tenn u dam.

ref: The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she kept yelling, “These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how to be saved.”
text: Le kibisiɛgin nɔɔ Pɔɔl nin tim ban gurin a bɔɔn ki tann papaab ke, “Bininfob nan ye Uwonbɔr wan kaa jɔɔ kpiɛg nan a toontum le, le ki bei ni naah li ŋa man ki kan nŋmarim.”

ref: This went on for several days. Finally, Paul got so upset that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I order you to leave this girl alone!” At once the evil spirit left her.
text: U le nan ŋaan man le lidaal biɛn. Waah ŋaan man ni le Pɔɔl a ŋuul nan fii, le u gbiɛ lig u le ki bei kinaaŋ kan be u ni nmɔn ke, “Yisa Masiya a yinl bu, n ke a nyam u ni.” Libol nmɔn le kinaaŋin nyan u ni.

ref: When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court.
text: Kiyom bisiɛg nmɔn a dam kaah nan biɛ ke baa ji li kan ilig kibisiɛgin ban nin, le bi choo Pɔɔl nin Silasi ki dar bi jon kitiŋ nmɔn a bɔjib ban kinyaŋin ban jɔɔ tininkper a pɔɔm ban.

ref: They are telling us to do things we Romans are not allowed to do.”
text: ki wɔɔn ke ti chee ki li ŋaan likaal lan wee Rom yaab a siim kaa chee.”

ref: The crowd joined in the attack on Paul and Silas. Then the officials tore the clothes off the two men and ordered them to be beaten with a whip.
text: Le kuninfogbaluŋin kpiɛ bibɔjibin bu, le bi bei bi ke bin pir Pɔɔl nin Silasi ki boo ba.

ref: After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully.
text: Baah nan boo bi nmɔn a bɔɔn le bi ta bi ki ŋa kuloondiigin, le ki bei uloondiiguurin ke u li mann guu bi nbamɔma.

ref: The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
text: Waah nan gbir man nin, le u ta bi ŋa kuloondiig kan be poolinpoolin nin, le ki baan bi tibaandaar.

ref: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing praises to God, while the other prisoners listened.
text: Le kunyiɛgtasiig le Pɔɔl nin Silasi nan miɛ Uwonbɔr ki gaa liwonpagil a lai-n ki pagir Uwonbɔr, le ban loo kpiɛ bi bu-n nin pelig.

ref: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
text: Libol nmɔn le kitiŋ dam, le kuloondiig nmɔn a fiɛl tɔɔl nan dam dam. Le tidir a timansanmɔɔŋi loor nba bu, le baah nan baan bi tibaandaar tan ni choo gɔgir lu.

ref: When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself.
text: Iyaayoo le wan guu kuloondiigin fii njiɛmin, ki miin tidir biɛn a timansanmɔɔŋi loor le ki yaa yaa, le u nyi ke baah loon ban nin biɛn guun na, le u nan fɔɔ u tɔb a jug ke un ku uba.

ref: But Paul shouted, “Don't harm yourself! No one has escaped.”
text: Amaa le Pɔɔl tiɛn ki ke, “Laa sei a baa kidaŋi! Ti biɛn be doo!”

ref: The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas.
text: Le uloondiiguurin ke bin sei nŋmi ni, le ki guun kɔɔ weem ki jegil, ki tan gbaan tum Pɔɔl nin Silasi a nintogil.

ref: After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
text: Le u nan ta bi ki nyan tan baan bi, “N yin ŋa ni wee ki kan feegabaa?”

ref: They replied, “Have faith in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved! This is also true for everyone who lives in your home.”
text: Le bi jiin bei u ke, “Ŋaam Uyudaan Yisa yada, wee ki kan feegab, fin nin a niin yaab biɛn.”

ref: Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord.
text: Le bi nan pag Uyudaan a bɔr ki sei u ma nin ban be u niin nmɔn biɛn.

ref: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
text: Lidaal a nyiɛg, le uloondiiguurin nan ŋunn bi biɛi; le u ma nin u niin yaab biɛn nan gaa Uwonbɔr a nyunful.

ref: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
text: Le u nan ta Pɔɔl nin Silasi ki kɔɔ u niin le ki sei bi tijiir; ni nan mɔŋ u le, nan bu-n u ma nin u niin yaab biɛn kaah nan ŋa Uwonbɔr yada nbu.

ref: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
text: Naah nan won kutaagin, le Rom yaab a bɔjib nan tun bi tooi uloondiiguurin ban ke: “Nyan bininfob nmɔn ki jaau.”

ref: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
text: Le uloondiiguurin bei Pɔɔl ke, “Bibɔjib tun bi tooi ni ke n che fin nin Silasi nya kuloondiigin n-yaan na, ni li fir n nya. Ni li chaa nin nposɔɔn na.”

ref: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
text: Amaa le Pɔɔl bei bi ke: “Baa la jin ti tibɔri, amaa bi won boo ti kuninfogbaluŋ a numin na, hali nin taah le ye Rom yaab nna, le ki won ta ti ki ŋa kuloondiigin, le daandaan nan bi nin ban bin woon ki nyan taa? Aai! See ke bi baantɔɔl dan ki nan nyan ti.”

ref: When the police told the officials that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, the officials were afraid.
text: Le itoon nin nan jir ki tan bei bibɔjibin man, baah nan gbir ke Pɔɔl nin Silasi ye Rom yaabin le bijawaam choo bi.

ref: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
text: Le bi jon Pɔɔl nin Silasi ban ki tan fa bi tisandann, le ki nyan bi kuloondiigin, ki balin bi ke, bin nya bi tiŋin na.

ref: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
text: Pɔɔl nin Silasi kaah nan nyan kuloondiig nmɔn a bɔɔn, bi nan jon tan kɔɔ Lidiya a niin le. Nin yaan le bi nan lagin biwonjiɛm ki pɔɔg bi sufu. Le bi nin fɔɔr kitiŋ nmɔn yaan.

ref: After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city.
text: Tɔ, le Pɔɔl nin Silasi nɔɔ Amfipolisi a tiŋin nin Apoloniya a tiŋin ki tan foo Tesalonika. Nin yaan le Juu yaab a wonjiɛndiig nan be.

ref: So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures
text: Le Pɔɔl tan kɔɔ niin ke waah pii ti kɔɔ man ni. U nan ta ipkakɔɔ itaa le ki be niin, ki wɔɔn bi Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin a taai,

ref: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
text: ki wɔɔn ni taai ke ni kpaa talar le ke Masiya nji fala ki kpo ki fii nkumin, “Yisa wan wee n pag u bɔr nan, u ma ye Masiya nmɔn.”

ref: Some of them believed what Paul had said, and they became followers with Paul and Silas. Some Gentiles and many important women also believed the message.
text: U nan pag ki kpenn Juu yaab biba a lam, le bi nin dan ki nan kpiɛ u ma Pɔɔl nin Silasi bu. Le Girig yaab ban jiɛn Uwonbɔr, nin bipiib ban jɔɔ jilima takpem nan kpiɛ bi bu.

ref: The Jewish leaders were jealous and got some troublemakers who hung around the marketplace to start a riot in the city. They wanted to drag Paul and Silas out to the mob, and so they went straight to Jason's home.
text: Amaa Juu yaabin nan ŋa u lipiiponl le; ki jin ki lagin kinyaŋ a ninfobir, ki nan mug kitiŋ nmɔn yaan nin tifur, ki tan leg Jasonn a niin, ki ban Pɔɔl nin Silasi, ke bin nyan bi dan kuninfogbaluŋin ban.

ref: But when they did not find them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the Lord's followers. They took them to the city authorities and shouted, “Paul and Silas have been upsetting things everywhere. Now they have come here,
text: Amaa baah kaa nan kan bi n-yonn man ni, le bi choo Jasonn nin nnabum biba, ki dar bi dan kitiŋin a ninkpeeb ban, ki tiɛn ke “Bininfob nan le nan mugir bininfob ntim biɛn nin, le ki nan dan do nan mu,

ref: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. All of them break the laws of the Roman Emperor by claiming that someone named Jesus is king.”
text: Le Jasonn gaa bi ki ŋa u niin. Le bi biɛn nan choon ki bii ubɔr Siiza a siim, ki ke ubɔr uba mu ji be le bi yi u ke Yisa.”

ref: The officials and the people were upset when they heard this.
text: Baah nan gbir man n-yonn man nin, le ni bii kuninfogbaluŋin nin biyudamin a sufu takpem.

ref: So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go. People in Berea Welcome the Message
text: Le biyudam nmɔn che Jasonn nin bi miɛnin yɔn ilig le bi ta bi jaa. Baah nan be Beriya man

ref: That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue.
text: Naah nan bɔŋ n-yonn man nin, le biwonjiɛmin nan chabir Pɔɔl nin Silasi le bi jon Beriya. Baah nan foo-n le bi kɔɔ Juu yaab a wonjiɛndiigin.

ref: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
text: Beriya a tiŋ a ninfob pel Pɔɔl a bɔrin ki jon Tesalonika yaaba, le ki gaa tibɔrin nin njiɛm takpem ki dibir imɔleen nmɔn lidaal biɛn ki lig njee Pɔɔl kaah pag nan nmɔn sin ye ibamɔn naa.

ref: Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
text: Le Juu yaab takpem nan ŋa yada ki kpiɛ Girig a piib ban jɔɔ liyinl nin Girig a jab takpem bu.

ref: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
text: Juu yaab ban be Tesalonika nan kaah gbir ke Pɔɔl be mɔɔn Uwonbɔr a bɔr le Beriya a tiŋin nin, le bi tɔɔl jon niin ki tan pag ki bii Pɔɔl, ki fiin kuninfogbaluŋin a ŋuui, ke bin ŋɔɔr wa.

ref: At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.
text: Libonl nmɔn le biwonjiɛmin nan chiɛn Pɔɔl nin biba ki tan jaa bi limɔgil a gbaam, amaa le Silasi nin Timoti ma paar Beriya.

ref: Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
text: Bininfob ban nan chiɛn Pɔɔl nan ta u foo Atensi le, ki nin jir kun, le Pɔɔl bei bi ke bin tan bei Silasi nin Timoti ke bin dan u ban weem. Baah nan be Atensi man

ref: While Paul was waiting in Athens, he was upset to see all the idols in the city.
text: Pɔɔl kaah la nan be Atensi ki guu Silasi nin Timoti nni, le u kan kitiŋin kaah gbee nin itingban, le ni bii u sufu takpem.

ref: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
text: Le u kɔɔ kuwonjiɛndiigin ki pag tenn Juu yaab nin ban kaa ye Juu yaab ki jiɛn Uwonbɔr nan tibɔr, ki ji chaa bi nyamin idaa biɛn, ki pag nin ban chaan nin yaan nmɔn tibɔr.

ref: Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him. People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?” Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
text: Le ban wɔɔnn wee bi yi biba ke Epikurusi, ki yi biba mu Sitoog nan, mu nan dan ki nan far limɔkpel nin Pɔɔl. Le bi ni biba nan pag nin tab ke, “Wan be jabin nan mu ke baa?” Le biba jiin ke, “Ni nann ke u pag iweenchaan iba a bɔr le-n.” Bi nan len man babu, Pɔɔl nan mɔɔn Yisa a bɔŋann nin le nin u kum a fiim.

ref: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
text: Le bi ta Pɔɔl ki jon bibɔjib a kikaabol nan yaan wee bi yi ke, Aropagusi nan, ki bei Pɔɔl ke, “Ti li fir biɛ tibɔchann tan wee a wɔɔn nan naa?

ref: We have heard you say some strange things, and we want to know what you mean.”
text: A pag tibɔchan le ti ban, le ti ban ti biɛ ti taai.”

ref: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
text: Le Pɔɔl fii sir Aropagusi a laguŋ nmɔn yaan, ki bei ke: “Atensi yaab! N kan ni binbemin, ni ban liwonjiɛnl pam.

ref: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
text: Nan bu-n maah gɔnn ni tiŋ nan, n dibir tiwann tan wee ni jiɛn nin le nbamɔm, hali ki nan kan libinbinl liba le ni sɔb libu ke, libinbinl nan si “NWEEN MAN WEE TAA NYI” nan a taalin le. Daandaan nan n ban n wɔɔn ni nween man wee ni jiɛn wee kaa sin nyi Win yaa bɔr le.

ref: This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.
text: “Nween man naan dulinya nin niwann nan biɛn be niin nin, u ma ye paab nin tum a yudaau, waa be tiwonjiɛndir tan wee bi ta bi nɔɔi maa yaan ni.

ref: From one person God made all nations who live on earth, and he decided when and where every nation would be.
text: Uninfo uba ni le u che ibol biɛn nyan, ki che bi be dulinya nan a gbanann biɛn nin, le u lol n-yonn man wee un nan siin bi nin baah na li be nan yaan.

ref: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
text: Uwonbɔr nan ŋa man le ke bininfobin ban u, nba ke bi ban u ke bi li kan u. Amaa u bol kaa fɔg nin ti ni uba ban ni.

ref: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
text: ‘Nan bu-n U ma bu le ti fo ki choon ki be.’ Ke ni tɔɔl a landam biba kaah nan len ke, ‘Tim ye Uwonbɔr a buwaab le.’

ref: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
text: “Mambu taah ye Uwonbɔr a buwaab nan, ti laa tiɛr ke Uwonbɔr ye kuwan naan waŋ ke salima, bee tikur ninann bee litangbagil lan wee uninfo ta u lam bee u biɛm ki naan li nni.

ref: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
text: Iyoo yan nan jon nin, wee bininfob kaa nan nyi Uwonbɔr nan, waa nan gar bi bir bu. Amaa daandaan nan, u ke uninfo biɛn nkpenn u binbema.

ref: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
text: Nan bu-n, u pii siin lidaal lan wee u na yin che uninfo gannkaau nmɔn nji dulinya yaab tibɔr ibamɔn a sam bu. U jin ni siɛra ki sei uninfo biɛn na le ki fiin u nkumin.”

ref: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
text: Baah gbir Pɔɔl pag nkum a fiim a bɔrin, le biba sɔɔl u, amaa le biba mu ke, “Ti ban ti mann gbir nan wee a wɔɔn nan le jigin.”

ref: When Paul left the council meeting,
text: Iyaayoo nmɔn le Pɔɔl fii ki jiɛn bi kulaguŋ nmɔn yaan.

ref: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
text: Bijab wama nan le nan ŋa Pɔɔl a bɔrin yada, le ki ŋa u bɔɔnɔɔb. Bi ni uba nan ye Dionasi, u nan ye bibɔjibin a ni uba le. Ki kpiɛ upii uba mu nan ŋa yada, le u yinl ye Damarisi, biba mu nan be ki kpiɛ.

ref: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
text: Ni bɔɔn bu, le Pɔɔl nyan Atensi ki jon Korenti a tiŋin.

ref: where he met Aquila, a Jewish man from Pontus. Not long before this, Aquila had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Emperor Claudius had ordered the Jewish people to leave Rome. Paul went to see Aquila and Priscilla
text: Nin yaan le u nan kan Juu yaab a ninfo uba, le u yinl ye Akula, amaa le bi nan ma u Pɔntusi, le u ma nin u poo Pirisila la nyan Itali ki dan Korenti, nan bu-n ubɔr yudaan Kuladiyasi le nan sei bi bimɔb ke Juu yaab biɛn nya Rom a tiŋin na. Le Pɔɔl jon ke un tan kan bi,

ref: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
text: u mu kaah nan ye ugbanjab ke baah pii ti tun man nin, mambu le che u nan paar bi ban ki tun nin bi.

ref: Every Sabbath, Paul went to the synagogue. He spoke to Jews and Gentiles and tried to win them over.
text: Le likpakɔɔl daal biɛn ke Pɔɔl n kɔɔ kuwonjiɛndiigin, ki far Juu yaab nin Girig yaab limɔkpel ki ban bin chee u bɔr tan wee u pag tenn bin.

ref: But after Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, he spent all his time preaching to the Jews about Jesus the Messiah.
text: Le Silasi nin Timoti nan nyan Masedoniya ki dan. Le Pɔɔl nin ta u toon yin ki jiɛn ki nin ta u saŋi biɛn ki sei Yisa a bɔr n-yaa mɔɔnim, ki wɔɔn Juu yaab ke Yisa le ye Masiya.

ref: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
text: Amaa le Juu yaabin kaa chee Pɔɔl a bɔr nmɔn ni, le ki sugir u. Le Pɔɔl gbagbag u wan yeewaŋ, le ki ke, “Ni cham li be ni tɔɔl a yuli bu! N tun maah ye n tun man le. Naah nyan dinan ki chaa, n yin jo ban kaa ye Juu yaabin ban le.”

ref: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
text: Le Pɔɔl nyan kuwonjiɛndiig nmɔn yaan ki jon tan kɔɔ Tatusi Jasitusi a niin, u nan ye uwonjiɛn le.

ref: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
text: Le kuwonjiɛndiig nmɔn a yudaau Kerepusi nin u niin yaab biɛn ŋa Uyudaan yada; le Korenti yaab takpem mu gbir u bɔr nmɔn le ki ŋa yada. Le bi fun bi Uwonbɔr a nyunful.

ref: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
text: Weemba a nyiɛg le Pɔɔl nan kan zii le Uyudaan pag nin u ke: “Laa san bijawaami; wee ki li mɔɔn n bɔŋann nmɔn na, ki laa ŋmin ni.

ref: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
text: N be niŋ, le uba kaa be ki li legiŋ ki seiŋ kidaŋi, nan bu-n n jɔɔ bininfob takpem kitiŋ nan yaan.”

ref: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
text: Mambu Pɔɔl nan be niin le libinl nin iŋmal iloob, ki wɔɔn bininfob Uwonbɔr a bɔr.

ref: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
text: N-yonn man wee Galio nan ye Akaya a tingbɔŋ a bɔr yudaau win, le Juu yaab nan lagin tab ki tan leg Pɔɔl, ki ta u jon bibɔjib ban.

ref: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
text: Ki tan bei ke, “Uja nan le lar bininfob le bi jiɛn Uwonbɔr nin nsan man kaa nɔɔ ti siimi.”

ref: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
text: Pɔɔl kaah ke un pag n-yonn man nin, le Galio bei Juu yaab nmɔn ke, “Nim Juu yaab, ni ye tibɔr nan ye tibɔbir bee limɔyiil le ke, ni bi ŋan n mann pel.

ref: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
text: Amaa naah ye ibinbaan ki jiin ni tɔɔl a mɔleen, nin ni yin, nin ni tɔɔl a siim paam nan ma, ni tɔɔl nmann tibɔr nmɔn na, maa li fir ji tibɔr nmɔn ni.”

ref: Then he sent them out of the court.
text: Le ki che bi ŋɔɔr bi nyan tibɔr a ji bol nmɔn.

ref: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
text: Le bi biɛn choo Sositenesi, wan ye kuwonjiɛndiig a yudaau ki boo u tibɔr a jibol, amaa le Galio a baga kaa be niin ni. Baah jirin Antiɛg a tiŋin man

ref: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
text: Pɔɔl nan be Korenti a tiŋin iyoo takpem. Le ki nan chabir biwonjiɛmin ki kɔɔ kuŋaluŋ ki jon Siriya. Le Pirisila nin Akula chiɛn u. Waah kaa la nan kɔɔ kuŋaluŋin nin, le u koo u yul Senkariɛ a tiŋin nan bu-n waah poo tipoor tan nin bu.

ref: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
text: Le bi nan chaa ki tan foo Efesusi, nan yaan wee Pɔɔl nan jaa Pirisila nin Akula nan, le u tɔɔl jon ki tan kɔɔ Juu yaab a wonjiɛndiigin, ki pag sei Juu yaab nmɔn.

ref: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
text: Le bi nan bei u ke un laan paar bi ban iweehn ilee, amaa le waa chee.

ref: Paul sailed to Caesarea, where he greeted the church. Then he went on to Antioch.
text: Waah tan foo Sizariya n-yonn man nin, le u don tan poor biwonjiɛm a laguŋ, le ki ji jiir Antiɛg.

ref: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
text: Waah jin n-yonn wama Antiɛg nmɔn a bɔɔn bu, le Pɔɔl ji nan nyan nin yaan ki choon ntim ntim Galantiya nin Ferijiya a tinbumin ki pɔɔgir bi bɔɔnɔɔbin a sufu. Apolosi kaah nan be Efesusi nin Korenti man

ref: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
text: Juu a jau uba le nan be, le u yinl ye Apolosi, amaa bi nan ma u Alɛgzandira le, le u nan dan Efesusi. U nan ye ubiɛndaan le, ki nyi Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋ nbamɔm.

ref: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
text: Bi pii nan wɔɔn u Uyudaan a sam ma, le u nan pag Yisa paam ke ni yeg, hali waah le nan nyi Jɔnn kaah nan fun bininfob Uwonbɔr a nyunfulin a binba-n nni.

ref: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
text: Le u piin ki pag Uwonbɔr a bɔr nin lipoobil, Juu yaab a wonjiɛndiigin. Le Pirisila nin Akula gbir u bɔr nmɔn, le ki nan ta u kun ki tan mann wɔɔn u Uwonbɔr a sam nbamɔm.

ref: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
text: Apolosi kaah nan ban un jo Akaya nan le biwonjiɛmin pɔɔg u gbanann ki sɔb kugbɔŋ ki sei bi bɔɔnɔɔb ban nan be niin nin ke, bin gaa mu kuchɔŋ. Waah tan foo niin n-yonn man nin, u sin nan jiir ban ŋa yada, Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl nbu le ki ye literil ki sei bi.

ref: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
text: Nan bu-n uma nin Juu yaab kaah nan far limɔkpel nin tabin, le u yuur Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋ, ki wɔɔn bi ke Yisa le sin ye Masiya, ki pag nin npɔɔn, ki nyaŋ bi kuninfogbaluŋin yaan.

ref: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
text: Apolosi kaah la na be Korenti nan, le Pɔɔl nan nyan niin ki nɔɔ kisanbig ki jon Efesusi. Nin yaan le u kan biwonjiɛm biba,

ref: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
text: le ki baan bi ke, “Naah nan ŋa yada-n ni nan gaa Kasi a Naaŋin waa?” Le bi jiin ke, “Aai. Taa pii la nyi ki gbir ke Kasi a Naaŋ be gbaa.”

ref: “Then why were you baptized?” Paul asked. They answered, “Because of what John taught.”
text: Le Pɔɔl baan bi ke, “Ke bi nan fun ni Uwonbɔr a nyunful nii?” Le bi bei u ke, “Bi nan fun ti Jɔnn a nyunfulin le.”

ref: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
text: Le Pɔɔl bei bi ke, “Jɔnn kaah nan fun bininfob Uwonbɔr a nyunfulin, ni wɔɔn ke bin kpenn bi binbem ki jiɛn bi toonbira. Le ki sin bei bi ke bin ŋaam wan yin ŋɔɔrin u bɔɔn nin yada, u ma ye Yisa.”

ref: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
text: Baah gbir man nin, le bi nin fun bi Uwonbɔr a nyunful, Uyudaan Yisa a yinl bu.

ref: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
text: Le Pɔɔl ta u nɔɔi ki paan bi bu, le Kasi a Naaŋ jiirin bi bu, le bi nin pag ileen pɔɔn, ki ji pag ilinlen leen.

ref: There were about twelve men in this group.
text: Bijab nmɔn biɛn nan ŋa bininfob piig nin bileeu.

ref: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
text: Pɔɔl nan be Juu yaab a wonjiɛndiigin iŋmal itaa le, ki pag Uwonbɔr a bɔr ki tenn bi nin lipoobil, ki pɔɔn uba ke un kpenn bi potiɛl ki jiin Uwonbɔr a naamin paam.

ref: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
text: Amaa bi ni biba nan ye tukangbirdam le; kaa chee Yisa a sam, ki pag tibɔbir kuninfogbaluŋin yaan ki jiin Uyudaan nmɔn paam. Le Pɔɔl fɔɔr jiɛn bi. Le ki ta biwonjiɛmin jon Tiranusi a wɔɔnim a diigin, le idaa biɛn ke u wɔɔn bi niin.

ref: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
text: Ni nan ye man le ki tan kpaa ibin ilee, mambu che Juu yaab nin Girig yaab ban biɛn nan be Asiya a tingbɔŋin nan gbir Uyudaan a bɔr nmɔn na. Sikefa a naachim a bɔr

ref: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
text: Le Uwonbɔr nan che Pɔɔl tun ligaril a toon gbingbemin yan be i binba,

ref: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
text: le bininfob yuur u numpirim nin u wan yɔɔr tan wee u yee gbaa, ki paag bibaarib bu le bi wiɛn diɛr, le nnaanbiim nyan ki jiɛn bi.

ref: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
text: Iyaayoo nmɔn Juu yaab biba mu nan be, ki choon nyan nnaanbiim bininfobin, bi nan yi Uyudaan Yisa a yinl le ke bin nyan nnaanbiim, ki bei nnaanbiimin ke, “Tim le sei ni bimɔb, Yisa wan wee Pɔɔl nan mɔɔn u bɔrin a yinlin bu, ni nyau.”

ref: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
text: Nbijabum bilile ban nan ye Juu yaab a minmanib a yudaau Sikefa a naachimin le nan tun man.

ref: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
text: Le weemba daal, le kinaanbiig nmɔn baan bi ke, “N nyi Yisa, ki nyi Pɔɔl, ke ni mu, ni ye ŋmam maa?”

ref: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
text: Le uja wan wee kinaanbiig be u bu nmɔn, fii ki choo bi, ki boo bi ki nyaŋ bi biɛn, le bi nan guun nyan iniin nmɔn yaan nin igbananbil le bi gbanann nya ncham.

ref: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
text: N-yonn man wee Juu yaab nin Girig yaab ban be Efesusi a tiŋin nin biɛn nan gbir man nin, le bijawaam choo bi, le bi sei Uyudaan Yisa a yinl jilima.

ref: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
text: Le ban nan ye biwonjiɛmin takpem nan nyan npaan ni ki nan kpiir bi toonbir.

ref: Some who had been practicing witchcraft even brought their books and burned them in public. These books were worth about
text: Le binyɔgdam nin ta bi sabi ki dan nan nyɔɔ nŋmi kuninfogbaluŋ n-yaan, le bi bigin isab nmɔn a ligi ki miin i ye tikur a ligibim turpiŋmu le.

ref: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
text: Ni ma nan che Uyudaan a bɔr nmɔn mann mɔɔn ki kɔɔ bininfobin, ki kpiɛ npɔɔn. Bininfob kaah gaa tijar Efesusi a tiŋin man

ref: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
text: Ni niɛ nan biɛn kaah tun jon a bɔɔn, le Pɔɔl lol ke un nɔɔ Masedoniya nin Akaya ki jo Jerusalam. Waah nan be niin nmɔn a bɔɔn bu, le Pɔɔl bei u ba ke, “See ke n gɔnn Rom mu.”

ref: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
text: U nan tun Timoti nin Erasitusi ban ye u toon terib bilee-n le, Masedoniya, amaa le u paar Asiya a tiŋin.

ref: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
text: Iyaayoo nmɔn le Efesusi yaab nan gaa tijar ki jiin Uyudaan Yisa a samin paam.

ref: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
text: Uja uba nan be le u yinl ye Dimitirusi, u ti jɔɔ tikur ninann le ki maa bi tigbann yan wee bi yi ke Atemisi nan a dir ki kɔɔr tenn bitoontumin. Le bitoontum n mu ta itoon nmɔn ki kan tinyɔɔr takpem.

ref: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
text: Le Dimitirusi nan yin bi biɛn ki lagin tab, nin ban biɛn tun itoon nmɔn a booli biɛn ki bei bi ke, “N jɔtiib, ni nyi taah ga tinyɔɔr tan itoon nan yaan.

ref: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
text: Ni tɔɔl kan ki gbir Pɔɔl nan a bol kaah kpenn bininfob takpem a lam ki lar bi ki kɔɔn kulɔŋ man Efesusi nin Asiya a tingbɔŋin biɛn. U ke tiwann naan wann tan wee bininfob maa-n kaa ye itingban ni.

ref: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
text: U ŋaan kidaŋ le u mɔleen nmɔn yaan, naa ye kidaŋ kan li bii ti nyaŋ a binba, amaa ti tingbanl takpenlin Atemisi a diigin a jilima yin war le, le litingbanlin tɔɔl, lan wee bi jiɛn Asiya a tingbɔŋin nin dulinya nan yaan a jilima li bii.”

ref: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
text: Baah gbir man nmɔn, le bi ŋuui fii, le bi piin ki tann ki ke: “Tim Efesusi yaab a tingbanl Atemisi ye litingbanl takpenl le!”

ref: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
text: Naa nan yuuri le kitiŋ nmɔn a ninfob fu, ki gaan tijar. Le ki bib Pɔɔl a ninɔɔtab bilee Gayɔsi nin Arisitakusi ban nyan Masedoniya nan, le kuninfogbaluŋin kpab tab ke ninfo uba a danin ki kɔɔ kinaakoog takpoŋin.

ref: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
text: Pɔɔl nan ban un kɔɔ kuninfogbaluŋin yaan le, amaa le biwonjiɛmin kaa nan chee un kɔɔ.

ref: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
text: Hali kitiŋ nmɔn a yudam nin Pɔɔl a jɔtiib nan tun itoon le ki balin u ke Pɔɔl nmɔra, ki laa kɔɔ kuninfogbaluŋin yaan ni.

ref: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
text: Iyaayoo kulaguŋ nmɔn nan jɔɔ kuŋmaruŋ le: Biba nan tann niba bu le biba mu tann nitɔ bu. Bininfob takpem kaa nan nyi nan bu wee bi be niin ni.

ref: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
text: Le Juu yaab nyan uja uba le bi yi u ke Alɛgzanda, ki siin u bi nintogil ke un pag bi bu, le Alɛgzanda don u nɔɔi papaab, ki ban un pag ki sei kuninfogbaluŋin, ki nyan bi limɔkpel nmɔn yaan.

ref: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
text: Amaa baah nan nan biɛ ke u ye Juu a ninfou le-n, le bi biɛn tann ki pag bɔr tiba ke, “Tim Efesusi yaab a tingbanl Atemisi ye litingbanl takpenl le!” Bi nan tiɛn man ki tan kpaa tikur tilee le gbaa.

ref: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
text: Ni joorimin le kitiŋ nmɔn a gbansɔbiru uba nan che kuninfogbaluŋin ŋmin, le u baan bi ke: “Nim Efesusi yaab, uba be kutingbɔŋ nan yaan wee kaa nyi ke nim Efesusi yaab le guu Atemisi a diig nan nin litingbanl lan nyan papaab ki nan lu nan naa?”

ref: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
text: Nima bu uba kaa be ki li fir niɛ ni nan a bamɔn bu. Ni ŋan nin ni mɔr ki laa ban jegjegi.

ref: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
text: Ni ta bininfob nan dan doo, amaa baa sun ti wonjiɛndiig a wan ni, bee ki sug ti tingbanl li.

ref: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
text: Ni ye Dimitirusi nin u toontun tabin jɔɔ tibɔr nin uba ke, tibɔr a ji bol be, bibɔjib mu be. Bi li fir jo ki tan poor tab bi ban.

ref: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
text: Amaa ni ye ni jɔɔ tibɔr tan kaa ye ni ta ti jo bibɔjib nmɔn ban ke, ni ŋan nin ni jo ni tɔɔl a yudam ban.

ref: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
text: Ke naah ye man nin, ti be kidaŋin le, bi li ji tim tibɔr kufuug kan wee ti ŋa dinan nan bu. Le taa yin fir wɔɔn kufuug nmɔn a taai, taa yin nyi taah li len man ni.”

ref: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
text: Waah len man nmɔn, le u che bi biɛn fɔɔr.

ref: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
text: Kufuug nmɔn kaah nan ŋmin nin, le Pɔɔl yin biwonjiɛm, le ki pɔɔg bi gbanann, ki chabir bi, le ki jon Masedoniya a tingbɔŋin.

ref: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
text: U nan chonn ntim man be niin nmɔn le, ki wɔɔn biwonjiɛm ban be niin nmɔn Uwonbɔr a bɔr takpem, ki pɔɔg bi sufu, ni joorimin le u tan foo Giresi,

ref: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
text: ki be niin iŋmal itaa. U nan ŋa u sili le ke un jo Siriya, amaa le ki gbir ke Juu yaab lolig nlolbirim le u bu, le u lol ke, un jir nɔɔ Masedoniya paam le.

ref: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
text: Pirusi wan nyan Beriya a bija Sopata, nin Arisitakusi nin Sekondusi, ban nyan Tesalonika, nin Gayɔsi wan nyan Deba, nin Timoti nin Tachikusi nin Tirofimusi ban nyan Asiya a tingbɔŋin nin, bi ma nan nɔɔ Pɔɔl ki jon.

ref: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
text: Le bijab nan, nan liir nsan ki tan guur ti Tirosi a tiŋin.

ref: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
text: Amaa Kuchiig kan wee bi ti ŋma boroboro kan kaa jɔɔ nnyɔg nni a bɔɔn bu le ti kɔɔ kuŋaluŋ, ki nyan Filipi ki chaa Tirosi. Ni ween iŋmu daal le ti foo bi ban Tirosi, ki paar be niin ki tan kpaa iweehn ilile. Tirosi a tiŋ a bɔr

ref: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
text: Likpakɔɔl a weemba daal le ti lagin tab, ke ti ji ti yudaau a jiir. Le Pɔɔl pag Uwonbɔr a bɔr digdig nin kunyiɛgtasiig, nan bu-n u nan ban ni won ke un jo ni ba yaan le.

ref: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
text: Bi nan nyɔɔ filaam le takpem kudiititɔrug kan yaan wee ti nan lagin nin a poolin.

ref: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
text: Le Unaachipɔɔn uba nan be niin, le u yinl ye Itikusi, le u ka kudiititɔrug a takorobonl bu. Le Pɔɔl pag Uwonbɔr a bɔr ki yuur, le u ka pelig, le njiɛm nan choo u, le u nyan kudiititɔrug kan kpiɛ titaa-n a paab ki tan lu tum. Le bi jiir ki tan yuur u, ki miin u kpou.

ref: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
text: Le Pɔɔl nyan kudiititɔrugin a paab, ki jiir ki nan wugin u bu, ki ta u nɔɔi bib u, ki len ke, “Ni laa che ni sufu n bii, u fo!”

ref: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
text: Le ki jir don kudiititɔrugin a paab ki tan jin tijiir. Ni bɔɔn bu le u ji pag Uwonbɔr a bɔr hali nin naah nan won, le u jaa bi ki jon.

ref: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
text: Le bi nan yuur unaachipɔɔn nmɔn ke u fo, le bi ta u ki kun nin npopeen takpem. Pɔɔl kaah nyan Tirosi ki jon Miletusi man

ref: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
text: Le ti chinn jon ki tan kɔɔ kuŋaluŋ, ki jon Asosi. Nin yaan le ti nan tan yin yuur Pɔɔl, u nan ŋa man a sili le, nan bu-n, u nan ban un choon tum le ki foo niin.

ref: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
text: Waah nan kenn ti Asosi n-yonn man ni, le ti yuur u ki ŋa kuŋaluŋin yaan ki jon Mitilene.

ref: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
text: Le ni won kutaag le ti nyan niin ki foo Kiosi. Le ni nan won kutaag le ti foo Samosi, ki ji won kutaag le ti foo Miletusi.

ref: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
text: Pɔɔl kaa nan ban un sir Efesusi, nan bu-n waa nan ban un yuur Asiya a tiŋin ni, le ki ban weem ke u bi li fir ke, un bin foo Jerusalam, lidaal lan wee bi yi ke, Pentikosi nan a daal. Pɔɔl kaah chabir Efesusi a wonjiɛn ninkpeeb man

ref: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
text: Le Pɔɔl tun ntoon, ke bin nya Miletusi a tiŋin, ki jo Efesusi ki tan yin biwonjiɛn ninkpeebin ni.

ref: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
text: Baah tan foo n-yonn man nin, le u bei bi ke: “Ni nyi n binbem kaah nan ye man, maah nan be ni ban nin, maah foon Asiya a tingbɔŋ nan yaan lidaal lan ki nan kpaa dinan.

ref: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
text: N tun Uwonbɔr a toon le nin jiininba takpem nin tinyinyinn, nin nima biɛn ni n kan limagil takpem Juu yaab ban na.

ref: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
text: Ni nyi maah pag Uwonbɔr a bɔr, ki wɔɔn ni bininfobin nin ni niin yin. N nan pag ni tibɔr tan biɛn li ter ni le kaa gur tiba.

ref: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
text: N bei Juu yaab nin Girig yaab biɛn ke bin kpenn bi binbema ki jir Uwonbɔr ban, ki ŋa ti Yudaau Yisa yada.

ref: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
text: “Tɔ, daandaan nan Kinaaŋin le che n chaa Jerusalam, amaa maa nyi nan ta li ŋaam nin yaan ni.

ref: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
text: Amaa maah choon ntim man biɛn nin, Kasi a Naaŋ ti chinn beim le ke kuloondiig nin fala be n nintogil ki guum.

ref: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
text: Amaa n tiɛr ki n miɛfol ye yɔli ki seim, amaa nan kpaa le ye n tun itoon yan wee Uyudaan Yisa nan ta seimin ki diɛ, itoon nmɔn le ye n wɔɔn bininfob tibɔŋann nmɔn Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl bu.

ref: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
text: “Daandaan nan n nyi ke maah nan choon ki mɔɔn Uwonbɔr a naam a bɔrin ki tenn nim ban nin, ni ni uba kaa ji li kan mi.

ref: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
text: Mambu le n bei ni dinan ke, nnɔɔ kaa be uninfosaal biɛn a chamin ni.

ref: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
text: Nan bu-n n pag ni Uwonbɔr a bam a bɔrin biɛn ki wɔɔn na, kaa gur tiba.

ref: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
text: Ni li ŋmag niba nbamɔm nin ipee yan biɛn wee Kasi a Naaŋ ta ŋubin ni nɔɔn ke ni li guu-n. Ni li guu Uwonbɔr a ninfobin na, ban wee U ta U cham ki daa-n.

ref: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
text: N nyi ke maa nan be a bɔɔn ke, tibɔkardam ban nann igbingbelin na li dan ni sisiigin, ki bii Uwonbɔr a ninfob.

ref: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
text: Ni bu, ni li guu ni ba! Ki li tiɛr ke ibin itaa sɔ le n le kpaan ni biɛn nan nin tinyinyinn, nween nin kunyiɛg.

ref: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
text: “Daandaan nan, n jɔɔ ni ki ŋubin Uwonbɔr a nɔɔn nin U nyunyunbasanl a mɔleen yin bu, U bɔr nmɔn le li fir che ni nɔɔ nbamɔm, ki li fir sei nim ban biɛn wee u ŋa ni u kasi a ninfobin lifaal.

ref: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
text: Ni tɔɔl nyi ke min tɔɔl a nɔɔi le n jɔɔ tun, ki lig nba nin n ninɔɔtab.

ref: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
text: Maah tun man nmɔn n wɔɔn ni le ke see ke ti tun takpem wee ki ter bilanjiim, ni li tiɛr Uyudaan Yisa kaah nan len ke: ‘Tikaar be wan pu bu ki jon wan gaan na.’ ”

ref: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
text: Pɔɔl kaah nan pag u bɔr nmɔn ki diɛ n-yonn man nin, le uma nin bi ma biɛn lagin ki gbaan tum ki miɛ Uwonbɔr.

ref: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
text: Bi biɛn nan mɔr le, ki yuur bi nɔɔi paab ki poor u.

ref: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
text: Nan nan bii bi sufu ye waah nan len ke baa ji li nyi ki kan u num paamin bu. Le bi chiɛn u ki jon limɔgilin ke un tan kɔɔ kuŋaluŋ.

ref: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
text: Baah nan chabir ti a bɔɔn bu, le ti kɔɔ kuŋaluŋ ki don limɔgil ki tan foo Kosi. Le ni won kutaag le ti jon Rodesi, ki ji nyan niin ki jon Patara.

ref: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
text: Niin le ti kan kuŋaluŋ kan chaa Fonisiya, le ti kɔɔ kuŋaluŋin ki chaa.

ref: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
text: Taah nan tan ga Saipuru n-yonn man ni, le ti nɔɔ nnɔɔganpaam ki jon Siriya. Le ki tan foo Taya nan yaan wee bi nan tan yin nyan kuŋaluŋin a wan yɔɔr.

ref: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
text: Amaa le ti chaam a yonn nan foo, le biwonjiɛmin nin bipiib nin bi buwaab chiɛn ti ki tan nyan kitiŋ n yaan. Le ti biɛn gbaan limɔgilin a gbaam ki miɛ Uwonbɔr.

ref: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
text: Taah nan chabir tab a bɔɔn, le ti jon tan kɔɔ kuŋaluŋin ki chaa, le bi biɛn jir kun.

ref: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
text: Le ti nyan Taya ki foo Tolemasi, ki jon tan poor biwonjiɛmin, le ki paar bi ban weemba.

ref: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
text: Le ni won kutaag le ti nyan Tolemasi, ki foo Sizariya, ki jon Filib wan ye umɔleenmɔɔn a niin ki tan be. U nan ye bijab bilile ban wee bi nan gann bi ke bi li tol tijiir n-yaa ni u ba le.

ref: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
text: U nan jɔɔ nbisiɛm mina le ke maa la kun bijabi, le bi pag ilinlen leen.

ref: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
text: Ti nan be niin ki yuur wamau, ni bɔɔn bu le Uwonbɔr a linlenu wan wee bi yi u ke Agabu nan nyan Judiya ki dan.

ref: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
text: Le ki nan ta Pɔɔl a changbam, ki lol u tɔɔl a taai nin u nɔɔi, le ki len ke, “Kasi a Naaŋ len ke, Juu yaab ban be Jerusalam yin lol nchangban nan daan man le ki ta u ŋubin ban kaa ye Juu yaab a nɔɔn.”

ref: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
text: Taah nan gbir man nmɔn, le tim nin ban biɛn nan be niin nin, balin Pɔɔl ke u laa ji chaa Jerusalami.

ref: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
text: Amaa le Pɔɔl jiin ke, “Ba ŋa wee ni mɔr ki ku n gbanann naa? Naa ye ba tan yin lolimin a binba bu le n chaa, amaa n ŋa sili nin n tan kpo Jerusalam Uyudaan Yisa a yinl buu.”

ref: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
text: Waah len man ni, le ti jir ŋmin, amaa le ki len ke, “Che Uyudaan a bam n tun.”

ref: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
text: Ni bɔɔn bu, le ti ŋa sili ki jon Jerusalam.

ref: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
text: Le biwonjiɛm ban nyan Sizariya a ni biba chiɛn ti jon Minason a niin nan yaan wee ti nan tan yin be. Minason nmɔn mu pii nan ye Yisa a bɔɔnɔɔru le, u nan ye Saipuru a ninfou le ki ye chinchinn a wonjiɛmin a ni uba. Pɔɔl kaah gɔnn Jemisi man

ref: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
text: Taah foo Jerusalam n-yonn man nin, le biwonjiɛm ban nan be niin nin gaa ti nin npopeen.

ref: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
text: Le ni won kutaag, le Pɔɔl nin tim ban gurin jon ke ti tan poor Jemisi. Biwonjiɛn ninkpeebin mu nan be niin.

ref: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
text: Le Pɔɔl poor bi, ki wɔɔn bi Uwonbɔr kaah tun nan ki sei ban kaa ye Juu yaabin u ma Pɔɔl a toon yin.

ref: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
text: Baah gbir u bɔr nmɔn nin, le bi biɛn pag Uwonbɔr. Le ki bei Pɔɔl ke: “Ti na a big, a kan Juu yaab turtur kaah ŋa yada man na, bi biɛn ji ŋmag nsiimin le kenken.

ref: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
text: Biba nan bei bi ke, a wɔɔn Juu yaab ban be ban kaa ye Juu yaab a timin nin, ke bin yii Moziz a siimin na, ki ji bei bi ke, bi laa jiil bi buwaab a pun yi, ki laa nɔɔ Juu yaab a kaali.

ref: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
text: Ti yin ŋa nii? Bi le li gbir ke a foon na,

ref: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
text: ni bu ti beiŋ man ke, a tum man. Bijab bina le be ti ban do ki poo tipoor.

ref: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
text: Ta bijab nan wee fin nin bi ma li chaa ki tan mann ni bau, wee a yɔ baah jin lipɔnl lan biɛn, wee bin koo bi yuli, wee bininfob biɛn biɛ ke baa pag man ki jiin a paamin kaa ye ibamɔn ni, nan bu-n, fin tɔɔl nɔɔ nsiimin le.

ref: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
text: Amaa ban kaa ye Juu yaab wee ki ye biwonjiɛm nan ma, ti pii sɔb kugbɔŋ sei bi ki wɔɔn bi ke, bi laa ji tijiir tan wee bi ta mann libawoli, bee ki ŋman nchami, bee kuwankobug kan wee bi ŋmaan ŋmaan ku, ki laa tun iwanjaab toon lipiibanlin bee lijabanlin ni.”

ref: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
text: Le ni won kutaag le Pɔɔl ta bijab nmɔn, le u ma nin bi ma mann biba, le ki kɔɔ iwonjiɛn niin, ke bin wɔɔn bi idaa yan wee bi yin be ki tan kpaa lidaal lan wee biba a manim na li diɛ wee bin mann kumanug ki sei bi biɛn. Baah nan choo Pɔɔl iwonjiɛn niin man

ref: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
text: Iweehn ilile nmɔn kaah nan nan mal ndiɛmin, le Juu yaab ban nyan Asiya ki dan nin kan Pɔɔl iwonjiɛn niin. Le ki fiin kuninfogbaluŋin a ŋuui Pɔɔl bu le ki choo u,

ref: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
text: le ki ji tann ke “Iziral yaab, ni ter ti ni! Uja nan le choon ilog biɛn, ki pag ki bii ti ninfob ki bii ti siim nin iwonjiɛn niin nin paam, nan ji kpiɛ ye ti jɔɔ ban kaa ye Juu yaabin chaan tiwonjiɛn niin nan yaan, ki bii ti kasi a niin nmɔn.”

ref: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
text: Le kitiŋin yaab biɛn a ŋuui nan fii, le bininfobin biɛn guun ki nyan ilog biɛn. Ki nan leg Pɔɔl, ki choo u, ki dar u nyan iwonjiɛn niin n-yaan. Libol nmɔn le bi loon iwonjiɛn niin ni a timansanmɔɔŋi.

ref: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
text: Le bininfobin nin ban bin ku Pɔɔl, iyaayoo le Rom a tɔtogib a yudaau wan nan ŋmag bitɔtogib tur nan gbir ke Jerusalam yaab biɛn be gaan tijar le.

ref: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
text: Le u ŋa weem ki fii ki ta bitɔtogib ninkpeeb biba nin bitɔtogib, le bi daa jon kuninfogbaluŋin ban. Bininfobin kaah kan u ma nin bitɔtogibin n-yonn man ni, le bi jiɛn Pɔɔl a boor.

ref: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
text: Le bitɔtogib nmɔn a yudaau jon ki tan choo Pɔɔl, ki sei bi mɔb ke bin ta tikulor tilee ki baan mu. Le ki baan bi uninfo nmɔn waah ye wan nin waah galin nan.

ref: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
text: Le kuninfogbaluŋin yaan biba tann Pɔɔl bu balbal, balbal, bi ŋmaruŋ nmɔn bu che bitɔtogib a yudaau win kaa nan biɛ ni taai nbamɔmi. Mambu le u sei bimɔb ke bin ta u ŋa bitɔtogib a niin na.

ref: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
text: Baah nan tan foo ntisamɔn a nan yaan wee bi tɔɔg kɔɔ-n, le bitɔtogibin yuur Pɔɔl papaab, nan bu-n, kuninfogbaluŋin nan ban bin ku u le.

ref: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
text: Le bi nin nɔɔ bitɔtogib a bɔɔn ki tann ke, “Kum uja nan na!” Pɔɔl kaah jin uba a siɛra man

ref: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
text: Bitɔtogibin kaah nan tan yin ta u kɔɔ bi niin n-yonn man nin, le u baan bitɔtogib nmɔn a yudaau ke, “Npaan be nin n pag niba ki sei ŋaa?” Le u jiin ki baan u ke, “A fin pag Girig yaab a leen yaa?”

ref: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
text: Le Pɔɔl jiin u ke, “N ye Juu a ninfou le, n nyan Tarsusi kan be Silisiya a tingbɔŋin nin le, n ye kitintakpeŋ a ninfou le, n baliŋ le, che n pag ki sei bininfob nan.”

ref: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
text: Le bitɔtogib a yudaan win sei npaan. Le Pɔɔl sir bitɔtogibin a diig a tisanmɔnn nan yaan wee bi tɔɔg ki kɔɔ-n, ki don u nɔɔ bininfobin bu ke bin ŋmin na. Baah ŋmin n-yonn man nin, le u pag sei bi Juu yaab a leen yin, ke:

ref: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
text: Baah gbir u pag bi tɔɔl a leen yin ni, le bi ŋmin soon. Le Pɔɔl len ke,

ref: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
text: “N ye Juu a ninfou le, bi mam Tarsusi kan be Silisiya a tingbɔŋin nin le, amaa n nan ŋa uninfo Jerusalam nan le. Gamaliɛl le nan wɔɔnim. U nan wɔɔnim ti yaajam a siim le chib chib, le n nɔɔ Uwonbɔr nin linunmanl, ke ni biɛn nan kaah nɔɔ U dinan man nan.

ref: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
text: N nan mugir ki ku ban nɔɔ Yisa a samin le, ki ji chor bijab nin bipiib ki loog kuloondiigin,

ref: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
text: “Maah chaa ki tan mal Damasiko nwosisiigin le nwonween takpem nyan papaab ki nan won n bu ki jim.

ref: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
text: Le n lu tum, ki gbir likukɔl yin ke, ‘Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, ba ŋa wee a mugirim man naa?’

ref: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
text: “Le n jiin ki baan u ke, ‘Uyudaan a ye ŋmiɛ?’ “Le u beim ke, ‘Min Nazarif a ninfou Yisa le a mugir nmɔn.’

ref: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
text: Bininfob ban nan chiɛmin nan kan nwonween nin na, amaa baa nan biɛ wan nan pag ki tenn min a niɛn ni.

ref: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
text: “Le n baan u ke, ‘Uyudaau n yin ŋa nii?’ “Le Uyudaan beim ke, ‘Fiim paab ba ki li chaa Damasiko. Bi ta li wɔɔniŋ nan biɛn wee Uwonbɔr ke a ŋa.’

ref: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
text: N ninɔɔtab le nan ŋmag n nɔɔ ki dam foo Damasiko, nan bu-n nwonween man nan nyagir n num paamin nan jɔɔn ma.

ref: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
text: “Uja uba mu a yinl ye Ananiɛsi nan dan ke un nan kam. U nan ŋmag Uwonbɔr a siimin nbamɔm, ni bu Juu yaab ban nan be Damasiko nan tenn u jilima le takpem.

ref: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
text: Le u nan sir n ban ki ke, ‘N nabig, Sɔɔl, ligira.’ Libonl nmɔn le n ligir ki kan u.

ref: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
text: “Le u len ke, ‘Uwonbɔr wan ye ti yaajam a Weemin pii ganiŋ le, ke a biɛ u bam, ki kan U ninfo Buchiu, ki ji gbir u mu a mɔnn.

ref: You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard.
text: A li ŋa u siɛradaau, ki li pag tenn bininfob biɛn ŋaah kan nan nin ŋaah gbir nan.

ref: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
text: “Maah nan jir Jerusalam, ki tan kɔɔ iwonjiɛn niin n-yaan, ki miɛ Uwonbɔr nan le n kan zii,

ref: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
text: zii nmɔn yaan le n kan Uyudaan, le u beim ke. ‘Ŋa weema! Nya Jerusalam libol libol nan na, nan bu-n ni ye a bei Jerusalam yaab n bɔr ke, baa yin gaa tibɔr nmɔn ni.’

ref: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
text: “Le n jiin u ke, ‘Uyudaau, bininfob pii nyi ke min le nan chonn kɔɔ tiwonjiɛndirin ki chor bininfob ban nɔɔ a samin, ki boo bi ki kɔɔn bi tiloondirin.

ref: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
text: Le baah nan ke bin ku a siɛradaau Sitifin nin, n tɔɔl nan be niin, ki chee ke bin ku mu. Min le ji nan ŋmag ban nan ku win a wan yɔɔr.’

ref: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
text: “Le Uyudaan beim ke, ‘Fin le li chaau; min le yin tuŋ nan fɔg bininfob ban kaa ye Juu yaabin ban.’ ”

ref: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
text: Baah nan be tann ki pir bi daalam gabir, ki liɛr titann ki kur kutangbaag jaar paabin,

ref: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
text: le bitɔtogib a yudaau n sei bimɔb ke bin ta Pɔɔl ki kɔɔn bitɔtogib a niin na ki ji bei bi ke, bin boo mu, wee ki baan u wee win biɛ tibir tan wee u tun wee Juu yaab tann titintann nmɔn.

ref: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
text: Le bi tann u ki ke bin boo, le Pɔɔl baan bitɔtogib a sanliiru wan nan ŋmag bitɔtogib kobig wee ki si u ban nin ke, “Ni ŋan nin ni boo Rom a tinbig wee baa la jin u tibɔr ki kan u galin yaa?”

ref: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
text: Bitɔtogib a ninkpelu nmɔn kaah gbir man ni, le u jon bi yudaau n ban, ki tan baan u ke, “A ni yin ŋa nii?” Rom a ninfou le ye uja nmɔn.”

ref: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
text: Le bitɔtogib a yudaau nmɔn mu fii, ki tan baan Pɔɔl ke, “Beim ni a ye Rom a ninfou lee?” Le Pɔɔl chee ke “Nn.”

ref: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
text: Le bitɔtogib a yudaau nmɔn bei u ke, “Min nan yɔn ilig takpen le, ki kpann Rom a ninfou.” Amaa le Pɔɔl bei u ke, “Min bu ke n ye Rom a tinbig le.”

ref: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
text: Libol nmɔn le bitɔtogib ban nan ban bin baan u ibinbaan nin fɔr ki jir bi bɔɔn. Bitɔtogib a yudaau win tɔɔl a lam nan yug le, waah nan nan biɛ ke Pɔɔl ye Rom a tinbig wee u che bi lol u tikulorin bu. Juu yaab a yudam kaah jin Pɔɔl tibɔr man

ref: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
text: Naah nan won kutaag wee bitɔtogib a yudaau nmɔn nan ban un biɛ igalin yan wee Juu yaab pag ki jiin Pɔɔl paam nan a bamɔn chib chibin, le ni nan won kutaag, le u che bi lor u, le ki sin sei bimɔb ke, kumanug a ninkpeeb nin Juu yaab a yudamin biɛn lagin ni, le ki che Pɔɔl dan ki nan sir bi nintogil.

ref: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
text: Le Pɔɔl lig Juu yaab a yudam nmɔn chiir ki nan len ke, “N nabum, maah be ki nan kpaa dinan, n biɛ n sufu ni ke n tun ki gbeen n toon kaah ye man Uwonbɔr ban na.”

ref: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
text: Waah len man nmɔn, le kumanug a yudaau Ananiɛsi bei ban si ki mal Pɔɔl ke, bin faa Pɔɔl a mɔba.

ref: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
text: Le Pɔɔl bei u ke, “Uwonbɔr li faaŋ, a be le ke ligonl lan kaa ŋan wee bi ta nfatam pɔn li nan le! A ka do le ki ji min tibɔr, nsiim kaah wɔɔn man, amaa le fin tɔɔl bii nsiim nmɔn ki ke bin faam!”

ref: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
text: Le ban nan si mal Pɔɔl n nan tiɛn u bu ke, “A ye ŋmiɛ ki nan sugir kumanug a yudaau waa?”

ref: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
text: Le Pɔɔl jiin bi ke, “N nabum, maa nyi ke u ye kumanug a yudaau wi. Ni sɔb Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin ke, ‘Naa ŋan nin a pag tibɔbir ki jiin bininfob a yudaau paami.’ ”

ref: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
text: Pɔɔl kaah biɛ ke Juu yaab a yudam nmɔn biba ye Sadusim yaab, wee biba mu ye Farasiimin, le u pag npɔɔn ke, “N nabum, n ye Farasii a ninfou le, le ki ye Farasii a big. Le baah jim tibɔr tan bu ye maah jɔɔ tama ke bitakpiib naah li fii nkumin nin bu.”

ref: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
text: Waah pag man nmɔn le limɔkpel dan Sadusi yaab nin Farasii yaabin a sisiigin, le bi laguŋ nmɔn bɔgir.

ref: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
text: Le bi tintann nin nan mann ki do ki kpiɛg. Le ban wɔɔnn Uwonbɔr a siim ki ye Farasiim nan a ni biba fii sir, ki pag nin linunmanl ke, “Taa kan uja nan a biri. “Naa nyi ke nba ke kinaaŋ bee malaka le pag ki sei waa?”

ref: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
text: Le limɔkpel nmɔn nan fii takpem, hali ke bijawaam nan choo bitɔtogib a yudaau, u nan nyi ke bin yin choo Pɔɔl dar bɔgir le. Mambu le u sei bimɔb ke bitɔtogibin tan nyan Pɔɔl npɔɔn bi ban ni wee ki nan ta u ŋa bi niin na.

ref: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
text: Le niwonn ki nan be kunyiɛg, le Uyudaan dan nan sir Pɔɔl ban ki ke, “Che a sufu li pɔɔu, ke ŋaah pii jin siɛra man Jerusalam, man le a yin ji n siɛra Rom mu.” Baah nan lolig bin ku Pɔɔl man

ref: The next morning more than
text: Ban nan lol man nmɔn nan yab jon bininfob pinau.

ref: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
text: Le bi jon kumanug a yudam nin bininkpeeb ban ki bei bi ke, “Ti poo tipoor tan pɔɔ le ke taa yin ji niba see ke ti nan ku Pɔɔl.

ref: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
text: Daandaan nan ti ban nim le n sir Juu yaab a yudam a taalin ki tun u ba wee un jo bitɔtogib a yudaau n ban, ki tan bei u ke un ta Pɔɔl dan ni ban, ke ni ban ni baan u le ki mann biɛ u bɔr nmɔn nbamɔm. Amaa ti li ku u ke waa la foon do.”

ref: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
text: Amaa Pɔɔl a ninsa a big kaah gbir bi lol nmɔn nin, le u jon bitɔtogib a niin nmɔn yaan ki tan bei Pɔɔl.

ref: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
text: Le Pɔɔl yin bitɔtogib a sanliiru uba, ki bei u ke, “Ta Unaachipɔɔn nan ki jo ni yudaau ban, u jɔɔ tibɔr tiba le ki yin bei u.”

ref: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
text: Le u ta u jon bitɔtogib a yudaau ban. Le ki tan bei u ke, “Pɔɔl wan ye uloondiikɔɔrin le ke n ta Unaachipɔɔn nan ki dan a ban ke u jɔɔ tibɔr tiba le ki yin beiŋ.”

ref: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
text: Le bitɔtogib a yudaau choo Unaachipɔɔn nin a nɔɔ ki ta u nyan ngbaan, ki tan baan u ke, “Ba a bɔr wee a yin beim maa?”

ref: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
text: Le u ke: “Juu yaab le kpaag bimɔb ki ban a won nyan Pɔɔl ki che bin ta u ki dan Juu yaab a yudam ban, ke bi ban bin mann ki baan u le ki biɛ u bɔr a sam nbamɔm.

ref: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
text: Le bitɔtogib a yudaau nan chabir Unaachipɔɔn nmɔn ki kpaan u ke, “Laa bei u ba ke a poor tibɔr nan ki seim mi.” Baah nan ta Pɔɔl jon ubɔr Fɛlisi ban man

ref: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
text: Ni ta utaan ki sei Pɔɔl wee un jig, ki ta u ki jo ubɔr Fɛlisi ban soon ki laa che un kan kidaŋi.”

ref: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
text: Min Kuladiyasi Lisiɛ le sɔb kugbɔŋ nan, ki poor jilimadaan ubɔr Fɛlisi.

ref: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
text: Juu yaab le nan choo uja nan, ki yin ku u, le n gbir ke u ye Rom a ninfou le. Ni ma bu le n ta bitɔtogib ki jon tan fee u.

ref: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
text: N nan ban n biɛ nan bu wee bi choo u le, mambu le n nan ta u ki jon bi ma Juu yaa a yudam ban.

ref: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
text: N biɛ ke ni ye bi tɔɔl a siim bu le bi galin u nmɔn, amaa naa ye u galin niba le wee ni kpaan nin un kpo, bee bin loon u n diin ni.

ref: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
text: Le bi beim ke Juu yaab lolig le ke bin ku u, mambu le n ke bitɔtogib nan n ta u ki dan a ban weem, n bei ban galin u nmɔn ke, bin dan a ban ki nan wɔɔŋ u bir kaah ye tan.

ref: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
text: Le bitɔtogib nmɔn nan tun ke bi yudaau kaah wɔɔn bi man ni, ki ta Pɔɔl kunyiɛg nmɔn ki jon kitiŋ kan wee bi yi ki ke Antipatirisi nan.

ref: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
text: Le ni won kutaag, le bitanjigibin ta u ki jon, le ban nan choon tumin ma nan jir kun bi niin.
