ref: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
text: Bitanjigibin kaah tan foo Sizariya n-yonn man nin, le bi ta kugbɔŋin sei ubɔr, ki ta Pɔɔl ŋubin u.

ref: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
text: Le ubɔr karin kugbɔŋin le ki baan u waah nyan nan yaan. Le ki biɛ ke u nyan Silisiya le,

ref: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
text: Le u bei u ke, “Ban galiŋin foon n-yonn man ke, n li gbir a bɔr nmɔn.” Le ki sei bimɔb ke ban guun li ŋmag u ubɔr Herɔd a bɔr naakoon na.

ref: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
text: Iweehn iŋmu daal, le kumanug a yudaau Ananiɛsi, nin bininkpeeb, nin Rom yaab a bɔjiru wan wee bi yi u ke Tetulusi nan, foo Sizariya ki pag galin Pɔɔl ubɔr Fɛlisi ban.

ref: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
text: Baah nan yin Pɔɔl kɔɔn n-yonn man nin, le Tetulusi nan pag Pɔɔl a bɔr ki wɔɔn Fɛlisi ke: “Ubɔr Fɛlisi fin bu le ti kan nposɔɔn kitiŋ nan, nin ŋaah tiɛr wonbu le a jɔɔ ki mann ki tiŋ nan.

ref: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
text: Jilima daan Fɛlisi, ti jɔɔ npopeen nan yaan biɛn nin niwann biɛn nin, ki tenniŋ kunɔɔpoog takpem ni bu.

ref: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
text: Amaa maa ban n bii a saŋiyi, n baliŋ le ke a mɔr ki gbir ti bɔr nan wamau.

ref: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
text: “Ti kan uja nan le n miin u ye kuŋmaruŋ daan le, ki jɔɔ limɔyiil Juu yaab a tingbɔŋ nan yaan biɛn. U ye bikɔnbam a sanliiru le ki be Nazarif yaab a wonjiɛmin,

ref: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
text: Ni ye a tɔɔl baan uja nan ke, a li biɛ nan biɛn bu wee ti pag ki galin u nan a bamɔn.”

ref: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
text: Le Juu yaab nmɔn kpiɛ u bu ki ke waah pag man nmɔn sin ye ibamɔn le. Pɔɔl kaah nan jin uba a siɛra Fɛlisi ban man

ref: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
text: Ubɔr nmɔn kaah wɔɔn Pɔɔl nnɔɔ ke un fii ki pagin: Le Pɔɔl ke, “N nyi ke ŋaah ŋa ubɔjir ti tingbɔŋ nan yaan, ni ŋa ibin takpem ma. Mambu, ni ŋaam npopeen pam nin maah yin ji min tɔɔl a siɛra a ban.

ref: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
text: A li fir ki feen ki biɛ ke naah laa jon iweehn piig nin ilee le n nan jon Jerusalam ke n tan jiɛn Uwonbɔr.

ref: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
text: Ban galin min kaa kan maah far bininfob limɔkpel iwonjiɛn niin man ni, bee ki fiin bi ŋuui tiwonjiɛndirin ni, bee kitiŋ nmɔn yaan ni.

ref: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
text: Le bi mu kaa ji li fir pag wɔɔniŋ n galin kaah ye nan ni.

ref: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
text: Amaa, n che ke, n jiɛn Uwonbɔr wan ye ti yaajam a weemin le, ki nɔɔ u siimin, man wee bi ke maa ye ibamɔn nin. N ŋa nan sɔb nsiim a gbɔŋin nin nan sɔb Uwonbɔr a linlem a gbann nin yaan biɛn yadau,

ref: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
text: le n jɔɔ tama uba le nin Uwonbɔr ke baah jɔɔ man nin, ke nkum a fiim na li be ki sei bininfoŋam nin bipootondam.

ref: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
text: Mambu, n pɔɔn n baa le iyoo biɛn ke n tun nan kpaan, wee n sufu li be nbamɔm nin Uwonbɔr nin uninfosaal ban.

ref: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
text: “Maah nyan Jerusalam ni yuur pam, le n nan jir niin ki ŋmag ipiin ke n ta sei n ninfob ban ye bilanjiimin, ki sin mann kumanug.

ref: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
text: Bi nan nan kam ki miin n nan mann nba le ki be kasi iwonjiɛn niin ki mann kumanug nmɔn. Iyaayoo nmɔn bininfob takpem kaa nan be niin ni, le tifur mu kaa nan be.

ref: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
text: Amaa Juu yaab biba nan nyan Asiya a tingbɔŋin ki be iwonjiɛn niin nan yaan. Ni bi ye bi kan n bir ke, ni kpaa talar le nin bin dan ki nan pag biim.

ref: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
text: Bee ban be do nan, che bin wɔɔn tibir tan wee bi nan kan n tun, maah nan sir Juu yaab a yudam a nintogilin.

ref: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
text: See limɔbonl liba lan wee n nan tiɛn ki pag bi sisiigin ke, “Bitakpiib na li fii nkumin nin bu le n si a nintogil dinan nan.”

ref: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
text: Fɛlisi ma kaah nan nyi Yisa a san nmɔn a nɔɔm nbamɔmin bu le u jiɛn tibɔrin, le ki ke, “Bitɔtogib a yudaau Lasiya nan foon n-yonn man ke, n li ji ni bɔr nmɔn.”

ref: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
text: Le ki nan bei bitɔtogib a sanliiru uba ke u li guu Pɔɔl, ki che u li be u wiiba, ki che Pɔɔl a jɔtiib li tenn u nan wee u ban na. Pɔɔl kaah nan pag sei Fɛlisi nin u poo man

ref: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
text: Ni bɔɔn bu, le Fɛlisi dan tibɔr a ji bol, u ma nin u poo Dirusila, wan nan ye Juu a bisiɛg nan, le ki che bi yin Pɔɔl ki dan bi ban. Le Pɔɔl pag uninfo kaah li ŋa Yisa Masiya yada man, le u pelig.

ref: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
text: Pɔɔl kaah nan pag ki wɔɔn nbuchin binben nin ba a ŋmagim nin tibɔr a jidaal a yonn kaah yin foon man nin, le bijawaam choo Fɛlisi, le u ke, “Ni li kpaan man daandaan nan! Li chaau. Amaa ni ye n kan isaŋ ke n ji li yiŋ.”

ref: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
text: Fɛlisi nan ban Pɔɔl n kɔɔ u bu nin ilig le, ni ma bu le u nan gbaa yi u ki pag nin u.

ref: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
text: Ibin ilee kaah jon a bɔɔn le Posiɛ Fetusi mu gaa Fɛlisi a ninkper nmɔn. Fɛlisi kaah nan yin fii lijalin bu-n, u nan ban un penn Juu yaab a pooi le, mambu le u che Pɔɔl be kuloondiigin.

ref: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
text: Fetusi kaah nan foo Sizariya iweehn itaa daal le u nyan nin yaan ki jon Jerusalam,

ref: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
text: niin le biminmanib a yudam nin Juu yaab a yudam dan Fetusi ban ki nan pag ki galin Pɔɔl.

ref: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
text: Le ki balin Fetusi nin linunmanl ke un chee ki tun baah ban man nin sei ba wee ki nyan Pɔɔl Sizariya a tiŋin ki ta u dan Jerusalam, amaa bi nan ban bin woon ku Pɔɔl le nsann.

ref: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
text: Le Fetusi jiin bi ke, “Bi la ŋmag Pɔɔl Sizariya a tiŋin, min tɔɔl chaa niin le daandaan nan.

ref: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
text: Che ni sanliib biba n nɔɔm ki jo, ni ye u tan jɔɔ igalin ke ni galin mu.”

ref: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
text: Fetusi kaah nan be bi ban ki tan kpaa iweehn iniin bee piig nan, ni bɔɔn bu le u jir Sizariya, ki won kutaag, le u kal u bɔr binbinl bu ki che bi ta Pɔɔl dan u ban.

ref: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
text: Pɔɔl kaah foon n-yonn man nin, le Juu yaab ban nan nyan Jerusalam nan fii sir ki gɔɔn u, ki pag galin Pɔɔl tibɔr tan wee baa li fir ji ti siɛra.

ref: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
text: Le Pɔɔl jin uba a siɛra ki ke, “Maa tun niba ki bii Juu yaab a siimi, bee ki bii iwonjiɛn niin ni bee ubɔr Siiza.”

ref: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
text: Fetusi kaah nan ban un sɔŋ Juu yaab a sufu nni, le u baan Pɔɔl ke, “A li ban a jo Jerusalam wee n tan ji a bɔr tan wee bi pag ki galiŋ nan niin naa?”

ref: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
text: Le Pɔɔl jiin ke, “N le la si ubɔr Siiza a nintogil le u naakoon, nan yaan ŋan ki kpaan ni ji n bɔr. Maa tun niba ki bii Juu yaabi, ke fin tɔɔl kaah nyi ni nbamɔm man nin.

ref: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
text: Ni ye n bi jɔɔ niba a galin yan wee n tun wee ni kpaan nin n kpo ke, maa yii nkumi. Amaa ni ye bi por tibɔkar le seim ke, uba kaa li fir taam ki ŋubin bi nɔɔn ni. N balin ubɔr Siiza le ke un ji n bɔr nmɔn!”

ref: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
text: Le Fetusi ta tibɔr nmɔn ki gbeer u ninkpeeb, le ki bei Pɔɔl ke, “A balin ubɔr Siiza ke Siiza ban le a li jo.” Pɔɔl kaah sir ubɔr Agiripa nin u ninsa Bɛnisi a nintogil man

ref: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
text: Le ni ŋa iweehn ilee le ubɔr Agiripa nin Bɛnisi dan Sizariya ke bin nan poor ubɔr Fetusi.

ref: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
text: Baah nan be niin idaa takpem nmɔn nan che Fetusi nan wɔɔn ubɔr Agiripa Pɔɔl a bɔr kaah ye man na, ki ke: “Uja uba be do le Fɛlisi nan jiɛn u ŋa kuloondiigin.

ref: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
text: Maah nan jon Jerusalam n-yonn man ni, le biminmanib a yudam nin Juu yaab a ninkpeeb nan pag ki galin u, ki ke u kpaan nin nkum le.

ref: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
text: Le n bei bi ke, “Tim Rom yaab a kaal kaa chee man ni, ni ye bi pag ki galin uninfo uba ke, ti che bi lagin tab le ki gbir baah pag ki galin u nan bu, ki che u mu n len u bamɔn kaah ye man.

ref: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
text: Baah dan n ban nin tibɔr nmɔn, maa bii isaŋi, ni nan won kutaag le n che bi lagin n naakoon, le ki che bi ta Pɔɔl kɔɔn.

ref: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
text: Ban nan pag ki galin u nan kaah fii bin pag, baa nan fir pag ki galin u ki jiin tibir tan paam wee n bi tiɛrin ni.

ref: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
text: Amaa bi le far u limɔkpel le ki jiin bi wonjiɛnl paam, nin utakpiir wan wee bi nan yi u ke Yisa nan, wee Pɔɔl ke u be u miɛfolin nin bu.

ref: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
text: N sufu nan ŋmarin le maah li ji tibɔr nmɔn man; mambu le che n baan u ke un bin chee ki jo Jerusalam wee n tan ji u bɔr nmɔn niin.

ref: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
text: Le Pɔɔl balin ke bi li ŋmag u ki nan kpaa lidaal lan wee Siiza na li ji u bɔr. Mambu le n che bi guu u ke n nan ta u jo ubɔr Siiza ban.”

ref: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
text: Le ubɔr Agiripa bei Fetusi ke, “Min tɔɔl ban n gbir uja nmɔn a mɔn.” Le u jiin bei u ke, “Won nan, a wo li gbir u mɔn.”

ref: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in

text: Le bitɔtogibin nan ban bin ku ban wee bi nan ta ŋa kuloondiigin nin biɛn, ke ni ba ke bi ni uba n nan wo nnyum do ki guun ŋmar.

ref: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
text: Amaa le bitɔtogibin a sanliiru n ma nan ban un ŋmiɛn Pɔɔl le, le kaa chee bi lol nmɔn ni. Amaa le ki sin jaa bi ke wan nyi linyunwol wee ki li fir wo do ke, un chinn yug ki lu ki li wo chaa likpengonla.

ref: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
text: Ban gur kaa nyi linyunwol nan mu n choo kuŋaluŋ a daag bee iŋalinbɔg ki kpab ki wo do. Ti biɛn nan ŋa man le ki ŋmar.

ref: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
text: Le Pɔɔl tan pii tidagingann ki piɛn pii kijageŋ ki nan ŋa nŋmi-n, le nŋmi-n a tom gbir uwa-n le u nyan ki nan finfin Pɔɔl a nɔɔ ki junn ki jɔn.

ref: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
text: Ligungonl nmɔn a paab a ninfob kaah kan uwa-n kaah jɔn Pɔɔl a nɔɔ bu man nin, le bi bei tab ke, “Uja nan ye uninfokur le, nin waah le ŋmar limɔgil nan a poolin nan biɛn yɔli, bitakpiib kaa yin jiɛn un be u miɛfolin ni.”

ref: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
text: Le Pɔɔl gbag u nɔɔ le uwa-n lu nŋmi-n yaan, amaa le naa ŋa Pɔɔl niba hali wama.

ref: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
text: Le bininfobin ni nan ka ki tiɛr ke u nɔɔ li duun bee u li nyan lu ki kpo. Baah pel pel ki nan bag kaa kan niba ŋa Pɔɔl nan, le bi ji kpenn bi potiɛl ki ke u ye litingbanl le.

ref: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
text: Nin yaan kaa nan fɔg nin ubɔr Pubilisi a kpaabin ni, u ma nan ye ligungonl nmɔn a bɔru. Le u gaa ti kuchɔŋ ki tan kpaa iweehn itaa.

ref: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
text: Kugbanantuntoŋ nin kupoomarug le nan jɔɔ Pubilisi a baa le u dɔ. Le Pɔɔl kɔɔ u ban ndiin ki tan ta u nɔɔ ki paan u bu ki miɛ Uwonbɔr sei u le u pɔɔg.

ref: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
text: Naah nan tun man nmɔn le bibaarib ban nan gur ki be ligungonl nmɔn yaan biɛn dan le u teb bi.

ref: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
text: Ti nan be Malita iŋmal itaa le, ni bɔɔn bu le ti kɔɔ kuŋaluŋ kan nan be niin tiwar nin kufaag a yonn nin, kuŋaluŋ nmɔn nan nyan kitiŋ kan wee bi yi ki ke, Alɛgzandira nle, bi nan yi kuŋaluŋ nmɔn ke, “Tijaann a weem.” Ti nan kɔɔ kuŋaluŋ nmɔn le ki jon.

ref: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
text: Ki tan foo kitiŋ kiba bi yi ki ke, Sarakuse, ti nan be niin iweehn itaa le.

ref: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
text: Le ki tɔɔr jon Regiɛm a tiŋin. Le ni won kutaag le ntafaam yaan ti nan nyan nnɔɔganpaam ki daar ti, le iweehn ilee daal le ti foo Putoli a tiŋin.

ref: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
text: Nin yaan le ti kan nnabum biba. Le bi bei ti ke, ti li be bi ban ki tan kpaa iweehn ilile. Le ti be bi ban ki nan nyan jon Rom.

ref: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
text: Nnabum man be niin nin nan gbir taah chaan na, le bi fii ki kenn ti Apiu a nyaŋin, le bi ba mu kenn ti ichanniin yan kpiɛ itaa ki mal Rom a tiŋin ni. Pɔɔl kaah kan bi n-yonn man ni, le ni sei u ngbananpɔɔn, le u poor Uwonbɔr. Pɔɔl kaah be Rom a tiŋin man

ref: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
text: Taah foo Rom n-yonn man nin, le bi jaa Pɔɔl le u be iniin le utɔtogir guu u.

ref: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
text: Ni ween itaa a bɔɔn le Pɔɔl yin Juu yaab a yudam ki lagin tab. Baah lagin tab n-yonn man ni, le Pɔɔl bei bi ke: “N nabum, maa tun niba ki bii ti ninfob bee ti yaajam a kaali, amaa le bi nan choom ki taam ŋa kuloondiigin Jerusalam, le ki nan taam ŋubin Rom yaab a nɔɔn.

ref: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
text: Le bi baanim ibinbaan, ki nan ban bin jaam, nan bu-n baa nan kan n galin yan kpaan nin bin ku mi.

ref: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
text: Amaa le Juu yaab ban kaa nan chee bin jaamin bu, le n nan ke n balin ubɔr Siiza le, amaa naa ye n ban n pag galin n ninfob le.

ref: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
text: Mambu le n ke bin che n kan ni ki bei ni tibɔr nmɔn. Iziral yaab biɛn kaah jɔɔ tama wan nin bu le bi lolim tikulor nan.”

ref: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
text: Le bi jiin u ke, “Taa kan tigbann nyan Judiya ki pag a bɔri, le ti nabum ban nyan niin nan kaa pag niba ti ban ki bii ŋi.

ref: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
text: Amaa ti ban ti biɛ a potiɛl le, ti pii nyi ke nwonjiɛn san man wee a nɔɔ nan, bininfob takpem li pag ki bii mi iyag biɛn.”

ref: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
text: Le bi nan siin lidaal lan wee bi li jir u ban, le bininfob takpem nan lagin u niin kɔɔ kaai nmɔn yaan le u piin ki wɔɔn bi Uwonbɔr a naam a bɔr njakpanyiɛn ki tan kpaa kujɔɔg, ki wɔɔn bi Yisa a bɔr tan be Moziz a siimin yaan, nin Uwonbɔr a linlem a sɔbimin kaah ye man ki gbaar un kpenn bi potiɛl wee bin ŋa Yisa yada.

ref: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
text: Biba a potiɛl nan kpenn u bɔr nmɔn buu, amaa biba mu kaa nan ŋa ti yada.

ref: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
text: Le limɔkpel nan dan bi sisiigin le bi piin ki worin, baah gbir Pɔɔl a mɔboi joor kaai n-yaa bɔɔn ke. “Kasi a Naaŋ nan pag ibamɔn le ki sei ulinlenn Azaya, le u pag ki sei ni Yaajam:

ref: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
text: ‘Li chaa ki tan bei bininfob nan ke, Ni le yin gbir le kaa yin biɛ ni taai yi; ni le yin lig le kaa sin yin kan ni.

ref: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
text: Bininfobin a sufu le pɔɔ; le bi kpaa bi tuli ke bi laa gbiri, ki ji dabin bi num. Naa bi ye man ke, bi bi li kan nin bi num, ki gbir nin bi tuli, ki biɛ ni taai bi sufu ni, ki kpenn bi binbem wee n teb bi.’

ref: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
text: Pɔɔl kaah nan len man nmɔn a bɔɔn, le Juu yaab nan fɔɔr niin ki far tab limɔkpel.

ref: For two years Paul stayed in a rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
text: Pɔɔl nan be kudiig nmɔn yaan ibin ilee le ki yɔ ku bu. Le uninfo wan biɛn dan u ban ke un gaa u nbamɔm.

ref: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
text: U nan mɔɔn Uwonbɔr a naamin a bɔr le, ki wɔɔn bininfob Uyudaan Yisa Masiya a bɔr nin lipoobil le uba kaa ŋɔɔr wi.

ref: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
text: Pɔɔl, wan ye Masiya a toontunnu, wee U yim ki gannim ki ŋaam ntoon ke n mɔɔn Uwonbɔr a bɔŋann nin,

ref: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
text: tibɔŋann tan wee U nan chinn siin limɔsiinl lan nyan u linlemin ban wee ki sɔb Uwonbɔr a kasi a Gbɔŋin nin,

ref: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
text: ki jiin u wonaaŋ paam mu ke, Uwonbɔr a Kasi a naaŋin nan wɔɔn nin npɔɔn ke u ye Uwonbɔr a bija le u kum a fiimin bu: U ma ye ti Yudaau Yisa Masiya.

ref: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
text: U ma nin U yinlin bu, le Uwonbɔr san ti kunyunyunbaag, le ki ŋa ti itoon ke ti yin bininfob ban kaa ye Juu yaabin a booli biɛn ke bi li jɔɔ limɔcheel bi yada kan wee bi jɔɔ-n bu.

ref: You are some of those people chosen by Jesus Christ.
text: Le ni mu kpiɛ ban wee Yisa Masiya yin bin a kanlin na.

ref: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
text: N poor nim ban biɛn be Rom wee Uwonbɔr jiɛ ni ki yin ni wee ni ye U ninfogann kaabin: Ti Baa Uwonbɔr nin ti Yudaau Yisa Masiya a nyunyunbasanl nin nposɔɔn li be nin ni. Ipoor a wonmiɛl

ref: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
text: Chinchinn, Yisa Masiya bu le n poor n Wonbɔru ni biɛn nan bu, nan bu-n dulinya nan yaan biɛn bi pag ni yada buu.

ref: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
text: Uwonbɔr wan wee n jiɛn nin n sufu biɛn ki mɔɔn U bija-n a bɔŋann nin, U ma ye n siɛra daau ki jiin maah tiɛr ni bu man isaŋ biɛn,

ref: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
text: n wonmiɛlin n-yonn biɛn; n miɛ Uwonbɔr le ke ni ye U bam ke Un loor nsan seim wee n dan ni ban.

ref: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
text: N ban n kan ni le wee ki ta kinaaŋin a piini ibam ki sei ni wee yin sei ni npɔɔn,

ref: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
text: ni ma ye, nan li pɔɔg tab a yada nim nin min a gbanann pɔɔmin.

ref: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
text: N nabum, maa ban ni laa nyi ke iyoo takpem n lolig le ke n dan ni ban naah li ŋa man wee n fir ki kan bininfob takpem ni sisiigin, ke maah pii kan man ban kaa ye Juu yaabin a sisiigin biba-n.

ref: It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome. The Power of the Good News
text: Ni ma bu le n numan ke n mɔɔn tibɔŋann nmɔn ki sei nim ban be Rom nan mu. Tibɔŋann nin kaah jɔɔ npɔɔn man

ref: I am proud of the good news! It is God's powerful way of saving all people who have faith, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
text: Ifa kaa jɔɔm tibɔŋann nin a mɔɔnim bu, nan bu-n ti ye Uwonbɔr a pɔɔm le ki sei ban biɛn ŋa yada ke bin kan feegab: Juu yaab li yin chinn kan feegab le ban kaa ye Juu yaabin mu nin paan.

ref: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
text: Tibɔŋann nin yaan le nbuchin binben man nyan Uwonbɔr ban nin kpiir npaan ni, nbuchin binben man nyan ti yada-n npiinimin nin ndiɛmin, ke naah sɔb man Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin ke: “Ubuchin li kan limiɛfol yada bu.” Uninfosaal a galin

ref: From heaven God shows how angry he is with all the wicked and evil things that sinful people do to crush the truth.
text: Uwonbɔr a ŋuufiiŋ nyan papaab ki kpiir ban kaa jɔɔ Uwonbɔr nin bipootondam buu, ban jɔɔ bipootom ki deginn ibamɔn nin bu-n,

ref: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
text: bininfosaalib kaah bi ye bi li nyi Uwonbɔr man nin ni dɔ npaan ni le ki sei bi, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr le che ni dɔɔn npaan ni ki sei bi.

ref: God's eternal power and character cannot be seen. But from the beginning of creation, God has shown what these are like by all he has made. That's why those people don't have any excuse.
text: Uwonbɔr kaah nan naan dulinya n-yonn man nin, le bininfob kan Uwonbɔr wan kaa ga-n a binbem, nin U Pɔɔm man kaa jɔɔ diɛmin, le U wonaaŋin ji che bininfob biɛ U, ni bu baa jɔɔ nan wee bi li ta pag ke baa nyi.

ref: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
text: Nin ni ma biɛn ni bi nyi Uwonbɔr, le kaa tenn U jilima kaa tenn u kunɔɔpoog mu, amaa le baa tiɛr nan ye nlam a wan ni, le bi sufu gbee nin ijɔrig nin libunbɔnl.

ref: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
text: Hali nin baah pag ke bi ye bilandam nan biɛn ni, bi kpann tijɔri le

ref: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
text: ni ma che bi kpenn Uwonbɔr wan kaa kpegin a jilima ki ta sei tiwann mann wan tan wee bi mann wee ti nann uninfo wan kpeg nin nnɔɔm nin tiwankor nin tiwann tan fuul.

ref: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
text: Mambu che Uwonbɔr nyan U num le ki jiɛn bi le bi tun bi sufu a bam a toon, yan ye lipiibanl bee lijabanl lan kaa be kasi ki ye ifa a wan ki tenn tab bi tɔɔl a gbanann nin.

ref: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
text: Bi kpenn Uwonbɔr a bamɔn n le ki ŋa ti tibɔkar, le ki jiɛn tiwann naan kaar ki tun ki tenn ti, le ki yii kaa jiɛn Uninaan nin tɔɔl li, U ma kpaan npagim iyoo biɛn. Ibamɔn.

ref: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
text: Ni niɛ nan bu, Uwonbɔr nyan U num ki jiɛn bi per bi fai a kɔlisa nmɔn. Hali gbaa bi yaa piib kpenn le ki dɔɔ nin bi piitab ki jiɛn bijab.

ref: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
text: Man mu jigin le bijab mu yii kaa dɔɔ nin bipiibi le ki jɔɔ bi kɔlisa nmɔn dɔɔ nin bijatab. Bijab tun tijaginn a toonl le nin bijatab, le ki gaa litudaril lan kpaan bi ki jiin bi toonbirin bu.

ref: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
text: Nan kpiɛ, baah yii kaa ban bi li nyi Uwonbɔr a bamɔn yin bu le U nyan U num ki jiɛn bi per bi potiɛkpiinn nin, le bi tun nan kaa kpaan nin bin tun ni.

ref: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
text: Bi sufu gbee nin npooton a booli le, nin titoonbir nin kujaŋuuŋ nin nan kaa jɔɔ bu. Bi gbee nin linunchɔril le, nin lininfo kul, ki kɔnn nin tab, ki lar tab, ki nan tab. Bi ye bi bɔɔn sub le,

ref: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
text: nin bitingbiib, ki nan Uwonbɔr, ki sugir tab, ki jɔɔ kalanbaani, ki far igbingban; ki tiɛr baah li ŋa man ki mann tun titoonbir; ki yiin bi baam nin bi nam a mɔɔŋi;

ref: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
text: Baa jɔɔ nlami, baa ye ban wee bi li fir ŋa bi yada, bi sufu kaa be bi tabin ni, kaa san tab kunyunyunbaagi.

ref: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
text: Bi nyi Uwonbɔr a buchin siimin kaah len ke bininfob ban tun man nmɔn kpaan nin nkum le, baa nan tun man a binba amaa le ki sin chee sei bitab ke bi li tun man na.

ref: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
text: Mambu, fin, wan jin a kpiɛ tibɔr nan, ŋaa jɔɔ nsan man wee a li nɔɔ ki ke ŋaa nyi, ni ma bu ŋaah nɔɔ nsan man bu wee ki jin a kpiɛg tibɔrin, a tɔɔl jɔɔ igalin, nan bu-n fin wan jin a kpiɛg tibɔrin tɔɔl tun man le.

ref: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
text: Daandaan nan ti nyi ke Uwonbɔr kaah ji ban tun man nmɔn tibɔrin ni nɔɔ ibamɔn a sam bu le.

ref: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
text: Ke ni ye fin, uninfosaal mu, jin bi tibɔr wee ki mu ji tun man ke, a tiɛr ke a li fir ŋmar Uwonbɔr a bɔjilin naa?

ref: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
text: Bee a ziɛn Uwonbɔr a binben ŋamin a yabim nin U chee sei nin U mɔril nlee, kaa nyi ke Uwonbɔr kaah jɔɔ nbinben ŋan man nin ban a kpenn a binbem lee?

ref: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
text: Amaa ni tukangbiril nin naah kaa ban ni kpenn ni sufu-n bu, le ni kpiɛg U ŋuufiiŋ lan yab ki tenn ni ba lidaal man wee Uwonbɔr a ŋuufiiŋ nin U buchin bɔjilin na yin degirin nin.

ref: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
text: Uwonbɔr “Na li sei uninfo biɛn nin waah nan tun man.”

ref: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
text: Le ban si iyoo biɛn ki tun itoon ŋan ki ban kupag nin jilima a binbem nin limiɛfol lan kaa kpegin, U li sei bi limiɛfol lan kaa jɔɔ ndiɛmin.

ref: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
text: Amaa ban ban niwann biɛn li ye bi yaan, wee ki yii ibamɔn wee ki nɔɔ titoonbir a samin, Uwonbɔr a ŋuul yin fii bi bu le.

ref: All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles.
text: Tibɔmugkaar nin nton li dan bininfob ban biɛn tun titoonbir nan bu. Chinchinn ni yin foo Juu yaab ban le ki nin foo ban kaa ye Juu yaab n mu ban;

ref: But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
text: amaa kupag nin jilima nin nposɔɔn le Uwonbɔr yin ta sei ban tun nan ŋan nin: Chinchinn ni na yin foon Juu yaab ban le wee ki nin foo ban kaa ye Juu yaabin ban.

ref: God doesn't have any favorites!
text: Nan bu-n, Uwonbɔr kaa gann ni.

ref: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
text: Ban biɛn kaa jɔɔ Uwonbɔr a siim wee ki tun titoonbirin, bi yin kpo le kaa jɔɔ nsiimi, ban biɛn jɔɔ Uwonbɔr a siimin, amaa wee ki tun titoonbirin, Uwonbɔr yin ta nsiim nmɔn le ki ji bi tibɔr.

ref: God accepts those who obey his Law, but not those who simply hear it.
text: Nan bu-n naa ye ban gbir nsiimin le ye bibuchim Uwonbɔr ban ni, amaa ban chee sei nsiimin bi ma le bi na li yin bi bibuchim.

ref: when God appoints Jesus Christ to judge everyone's secret thoughts, just as my message says. The Jews and the Law
text: Ni niɛ nan na yin tun lidaal lan wee Uwonbɔr na yin ji bininfob a bɔwoonkaar Yisa Masiya bu, ke n bɔŋann nin kaah wɔɔn man nin. Juu yaab nin nsiim a bɔr

ref: Some of you call yourselves Jews. You trust in the Law and take pride in God.
text: Daandaan nan fin, ni ye a ke a ye Juu a ninfou; wee ki nɔɔ nsiimin, ki far a gbingbanl ŋaah jɔɔ nɔɔ nin tab nin Uwonbɔr man;

ref: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
text: ni ye a nyi Uwonbɔr a bam, wee ki chee sei nan jon ni biɛn nan bu-n nsiimin kaah wɔɔn ni man ni-n;

ref: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
text: ni ye a ke a ye wan wɔɔnn bijɔɔm le nsan, ki ye nwonween ki sei ban be libunbɔnlin,

ref: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
text: ki ye wan kpaan tijɔri, ki ye wan wɔɔnn nbuwaab tirim, nan bu-n ni jɔɔ nnyinyin nin ibamɔn nin kaah sɔb man nsiimin a gbɔŋin,

ref: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
text: fin wan wɔɔnn a tabin, ba ŋa wee ŋaa wɔɔn a baa? A wɔɔn bi ke bi laa su, ke fin suu?

ref: You say people should be faithful in marriage. But are you faithful? You hate idols, yet you rob their temples.
text: Fin wan wɔɔnn ke bininfob laa tun iwanchɔgin toon nin, a tun iwanchɔgin toon naa? Fin wan kaa ban libawomanil a bɔrin ŋaa su kuwonjiɛndiig a wan naa?

ref: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
text: Fin wan jɔɔ nsiimin ki far ligbingbanlin, ŋaa tenn Uwonbɔr le jilima le ki bii U siimin naa?

ref: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
text: Ke naah sɔb Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin man nin: “Ban kaa ye Juu yaabin sugir Uwonbɔr le nim Juu yaab bu.”

ref: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
text: Lipunjiil jɔɔ bu ni ye ni ŋmag nsiimin ke, amaa ni ye ni bii nsiimin ke, ni yin be le ke ban kaa jii-n.

ref: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
text: Ni ye ban kaa jii bi pun yin ŋmag nsiimin kaah wɔɔn man nin ke, Uwonbɔr kaa yin ŋmag bi le ke ban jii bi pun yin naa?

ref: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
text: Wan kaa jii u punl tigbanann nin amaa wee ki sin ŋmag nsiimin li fir pag ki biiŋ, hali nin ŋaah le jɔɔ nsiim nmɔn wee min sɔb dɔ nmɔn biɛn nin lipunjiilin, a ye wan bii nsiim le.

ref: Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew.
text: Wan ye Juu a ninfou npaan ni a binba kaa ye Juu a ninfo wi, le lipunjiil bamɔnl mu kaa ye nan ŋaan tigbanann nin a binba le.

ref: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
text: Aai wan ye Juu a ninfou ke u ye Juu a ninfou u sufu ni le, le lipunjiil bamɔnl mu be sufu ni le, ki ye kinaaŋin, naa ye nan sɔb dɔ kugbɔŋin nin a binba, u yaa daan gaa u pag Uwonbɔr ban le naa ye uninfo ban ni.

ref: What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised?
text: Juu yaab ma ta ba ki jon ban kaa ye Juu yaabin naa, bee lipunjiil a nyɔɔr ye baa?

ref: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
text: Juu yaab jɔɔ isan a booli takpem ni wan biɛn ni; chinchinn, Uwonbɔr nan ta U bɔrin ŋubin Juu yaab a nɔɔn le.

ref: It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith?
text: Ni ye bi ni bibam kaa si bogiliba ke, bi kaa si bogiliba nmɔn li fir bii Uwonbɔr mu wee U laa si bogilibaa?

ref: No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God, “Your words will be proven true, and in court you will win your case.”
text: Naa ye man ni! Che Uwonbɔr ma le ye ubamɔndaan na, wee uninfosaal biɛn mu le ye tibɔkardaan na. Ke naah sɔb Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin man nin: “Na li ŋa man wee bin ke fin Uwonbɔr a bɔr ŋan ni ye a pag ke le uba mu kaa yin fir faaŋ limɔkpel a bɔr a jimin ni.”

ref: If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask.
text: Amaa ni ye ti kaa jɔɔ nbuchin binben bu che Uwonbɔr a buchin binbemin nyan npaan nin ke, ti ji yin len ke baa? Ti li fir len ke Uwonbɔr galin nin waah fiin U ŋuul ti buu?

ref: But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
text: Naa ye man ni! Ni bi ye man ke, Uwonbɔr na yin ŋa nii ki ji dulinya yaab tibɔraa?

ref: Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner.
text: Nba ke uba ma li faam limɔkpel, “Ke ni ye n bɔkarin kpiir Uwonbɔr a bamɔn nbu ki che Uwonbɔr a jilima mann kpiɛ ke, ke ni ŋa ni wee Uwonbɔr ji yin jim tibɔr ki ke n ye tibirdaan naa?”

ref: You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well. No One Is Good
text: Ba ŋa taa li fir len, ke bitingbiib kaah len man wee bibam sin chee-n, ke, “Ni che ti tun tibir wee niwann ŋann nnyan naa”? Bi li ji bi tibɔr naah kpaan man. Uba kaa be ki ye u buchin Uwonbɔr ban ni

ref: What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said.
text: Ni joorimin ti yin len ke nii? Tim pii ŋan jon bi lee? Naa ye man ni! Ti pii wɔɔn ni ke Juu yaab nin ban kaa ye Juu yaabin biɛn be tibir a poolin.

ref: Not one of them understands or even searches for God.
text: Uba kaa be ki biɛ ni taai yi, uba kaa be ki ban Uwonbɔr a boli.

ref: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
text: “Bi mɔɔŋi yaa le ke tikar tan logir ki yaa-n; le bi lanbili pag nan kaa ye ibamɔn ni.” “Le bi mɔgbai gbee nin liwaataal a labir.”

ref: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
text: “Bi mɔɔŋi gbee nin imɔpoo le nin npooton.”

ref: These people quickly become violent.
text: Le bi taai ton nin ncham a nyam;

ref: Wherever they go, they leave ruin and destruction.
text: Le bi ŋaar biɛn ke, bi tenn bininfob ndam ki che bin ji fala,

ref: They don't know how to live in peace.
text: le kaa nyi nposɔɔn a ŋaari.”

ref: They don't even fear God.”
text: “Le baa san Uwonbɔr bijawaami.”

ref: We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty.
text: Daandaan nan ti nyi Uwonbɔr a siimin a poolin kaah len man biɛn, mi pag tenn bininfob ban nɔɔ nsiim nmɔn le, wee uba nlaa nan kan bimɔb ki fir pag niba, wee Uwonbɔr n nan ji dulinya biɛn tibɔr.

ref: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
text: Ni ma bu uba kaa li fir len ke waah ŋmag Uwonbɔr a siimin bu u ye ubuchin Uwonbɔr ban ni; amaa nsiimin le che ti biɛ tibir kaah ye nan. Uwonbɔr kaah ŋa ti bibuchim man

ref: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
text: Amaa daandaan nan nbuchin binben man nyan Uwonbɔr ban, wee U che ti biɛ mi-n, maa nyan nsiim a ŋmagimin ni, ni ma le nsiim a gbɔŋ nin bilinlem jin mi siɛra-n.

ref: God treats everyone alike. He accepts people only because they have faith in Jesus Christ.
text: Nbuchin binben man nyan Uwonbɔr ban nmɔn nyan yada kan wee bi jɔɔ nin Yisa Masiya nle, ki tenn ban biɛn ŋa u yada-n. Naa jɔɔ nbɔgirimi,

ref: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
text: nan bu-n, ti biɛn nan ye tibirdam le ki par Uwonbɔr a pag,

ref: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
text: le Masiya daa ti ki che ti be ti wiib U nyunyunbasanlin bu ki ke tibɔr ŋan.

ref: God sent Christ to be our sacrifice. Christ offered his life's blood, so by faith in him we could come to God. And God did this to show that in the past he was right to be patient and forgive sinners. This also shows that God is right when he accepts people who have faith in Jesus.
text: U nan ŋa man ki wɔɔn U bamɔn le n-yonn man wee ti be nan, ke U li ye ubamɔndaan wee ki ŋa ban ŋa Yisa yada-n mu bibamɔndam.

ref: What is left for us to brag about? Not a thing! Is it because we obeyed some law? No! It is because of faith.
text: Ligbingbanfaal ye baa? Laa kpiɛ niin ni. Ba bu che naa kpiɛ niin naa? Taah ŋmag nsiimin buu? Aai, amaa taah ŋa yada-n bu.

ref: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
text: Ni ma bu tim le si le ke uninfosaal a yada le che u bɔr ŋan Uwonbɔr ban amaa naa ye waah ŋmag nsiimin bu.

ref: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
text: Uwonbɔr ye Juu yaab a binba a Uwonbɔr u lee? Waa ye ban kaa ye Juu yaabin ma a Uwonbɔr waa? Nn U ye ban kaa ye Juu yaab tɔɔl a weem le,

ref: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
text: Ti wɔɔn ke yada a ŋaam bii nsiimin lee? Aai naa ye man ni! Ti le mann ŋmag nsiimin le.

ref: Well then, what can we say about our ancestor Abraham?
text: Ti yin pag ke nii ki jiin ti yaaja Abiraham nin waah nan kan nan nin paam maa?

ref: If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God.
text: Ni ye Abiraham a toon bu le Uwonbɔr nan ke u bɔr ŋan ke, u nan jɔɔ nan wee u li ta faa u gbingbanl, amaa naa ye Uwonbɔr a nintogili.

ref: The Scriptures say, “God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.”
text: Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin len ke nii? “Abiraham ŋa Uwonbɔr le yada, le Uwonbɔr kan u yada nmɔn kpiɛ u buchin binbem bu.”

ref: Money paid to workers isn't a gift. It is something they earn by working.
text: Ni ye uninfo tun litoonl ki gaa tiyɔr ke, baa kaan u yɔr nmɔn ke ti ye ipiin ni, amaa ni kpaan un gaa le.

ref: But you cannot make God accept you because of something you do. God accepts sinners only because they have faith in him.
text: Amaa, uninfo wan kaa nɔɔ itoon ŋan a tum bu, wee ki gaa Uwonbɔr wan che bipootondam kpann bibuchim jin nin, u yada nmɔn bu le Uwonbɔr ke u bɔr ŋan u buchin binbem bu.

ref: In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
text: Defid tɔɔl nan len man le, waah nan pag ke Uwonbɔr a kaar be uninfo bu u buchin binbem bu ki kpiɛ u toon bu-n:

ref: “What a blessing when God forgives our sins and our evil deeds. What a blessing when the Lord erases our sins from his book.”
text: Tikaar be uninfo wan wee Uwonbɔr kaa li nyi kan u bir ki bil guun win bu.”

ref: Are these blessings meant for circumcised people or for those who are not circumcised? Well, the Scriptures say that God accepted Abraham because Abraham had faith in him.
text: Tikaar nan ye ban jii bi pun a binba yaar le bee, ban kaa jii n mu kpiɛ nii waa? Ti le gbaa pag le ke Abiraham a yada-n nan wɔɔn u buchin binbem le.

ref: Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised.
text: U punjiilin nan ye siɛra le ki wɔɔn ke u pii ŋa Uwonbɔr yadau, le Uwonbɔr ta U buchin binbem a daagim ki daag u, u yada bu, n-yonn man wee waah laa nan jii u punlin. Le ki ŋa u yadadam ban kaa jii bi pun biɛn a baa, na li ŋa man wee bin kanh bi kpiɛ ban jɔɔ nbuchin binben nin.

ref: This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised. The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
text: U ma ji ye ban jii bi pun wee kaa be lipunjiil a binba bu amaa wee ki nɔɔ yada a tabogi yan wee ti baa Abiraham nan jɔɔ n-yonn man wee waah laa nan jii u punlin. Yada bu le ti gaa Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinlin

ref: God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable.
text: Naa nan ye nsiimin a ŋmagim bu le Uwonbɔr nan siin limɔsiinl ki sei Abiraham nin u yaabili ke bi li ji dulinya nan a faalin ni, amaa nbuchin binben man nyan yada-n nin bu.

ref: If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
text: Ni ye Uwonbɔr bi ke ban ŋmag nsiimin le yin ye dulinya nan a faajib ke, yada a ŋaam kaa bi jɔɔ tinyɔɔri le limɔsiinl kaa jɔɔ tinyɔɔri,

ref: God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken.
text: nan bu-n nsiimin a biim le jɔɔ Uwonbɔr a ŋuufiiŋ chaan. Nan yaan wee nsiim kaa be-n uba mu kaa jɔɔ igalin ni.

ref: Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all.
text: Mambu Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinlin nɔɔ nin yada le, ki ye Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl ki si guu Abiraham a yaabili biɛn, naa ye ban ŋmag nsiimin a binba, amaa ban jɔɔ Abiraham a yada-n. U ma ye ti biɛn nan a baa.

ref: The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
text: Ke naah sɔb man Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin nin: “Min le ŋaaŋ ibol takpem a baa.” U ye ti baa le Uwonbɔr ban, wan wee u ŋa u yada, U ma ye Uwonbɔr wan tenn bitakpiib limiɛfol wee ki che tiwann tan kaa nan be-n nin be ke ti pii nan be le-n.

ref: God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations.
text: Nin tama kaah kaa le nan be nmɔn biɛn ni, Abiraham nan jɔɔ tama le ki ŋa Uwonbɔr yada le ki nan ŋa ibol takpem a baa ke Uwonbɔr kaah nan bei ke, “A yaabili na yin yab man le.”

ref: But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
text: Nin ni ma biɛn ni, waa nan biɛnn Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinlin ni, amaa u yada nan mann sei u npɔɔn le u sei Uwonbɔr kupag.

ref: Abraham was certain that God could do what he had promised.
text: U num nan gbee ke Uwonbɔr jɔɔ npɔɔn ki li fir tun waah nan siin limɔsiinl ke U li tun man nin.

ref: just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham.
text: Imɔbon yan len ke, “Bi nan kan u kpiɛ-n,” kaa nan sɔb dɔ u binba bu le,

ref: They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life.
text: amaa tim tɔɔl, ban wee Uwonbɔr li kan kpiɛ ban jɔɔ nbuchin binben nin. Taah ŋa yada nin U ma Uwonbɔr wan fiin ti yudaau Yisa nkumin nin bu.

ref: God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
text: Ti toon bir bu le Uwonbɔr nan ta Masiya sei nkum amaa le U fiin u nkumin ke Un ŋa ti bininfoŋam Uwonbɔr ban.

ref: By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God.
text: Mambu, ti yada kan che ti ŋa bininfoŋam Uwonbɔr ban nin, li che ti be Uwonbɔr ban nin nposɔɔn ti yudaau Yisa Masiya bu,

ref: Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God.
text: wan a yada bu wee ti kan Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl lan yaan wee ti nin be nan. Le ni mɔ ti nin tama kan wee ti jɔɔ-n ke ti na li por Uwonbɔr a pag.

ref: But that's not all! We gladly suffer, because we know that suffering helps us to endure.
text: Naa ye man a binba, amaa ti fala a jimin gbaa ni mɔ ti le, nan bu-n fala a jim le jɔɔ nnyiginim chaan;

ref: And endurance builds character, which gives us a hope
text: nnyiginim li tenn ti nbinben le nbinben tenn ti tama.

ref: that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
text: Le tama kaa li che ti ji ifa, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr nan che U Kasi a Naaŋ kan wee U ta sei ti-n le kpaar U jiɛmin ki ŋa ti sufu ni.

ref: No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person.
text: Ni li pɔɔ takpem nin uninfo uba n chee ki kpo uninfo buchin bu, amaa niba ke uba li chee ki kpo uninfo ŋan bu.

ref: But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
text: Amaa Uwonbɔr kaah mag ki wɔɔn ti U tɔɔl a jiɛm man wee U jiɛ ti-n ye nan le: Taah le la nan ye tibirdamin, le Masiya kpo ki sei ti.

ref: But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger.
text: Waah ta U chamin ki ŋunn ti ki ŋa ti bininfoŋam nan, nan jon man le ye, U bu le ti yin kan nŋmarim ki nya Uwonbɔr a ŋuufiiŋin yaan;

ref: Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son.
text: Taah nan ye Uwonbɔr a duntiibin, le U bija a kumin bu tim nin U ma jir ki mɔŋ nin tab, nan jon man le ye taah jir mɔŋ nin Uwonbɔr nan, U bija a miɛfolin bu ti li kan fee gab.

ref: And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us. Adam and Christ
text: Naa ye ni yaa binba, amaa ni ye nmɔn le ki sei ti Uwonbɔr ban nin ti Yudaau Yisa Masiya wan che tim nin Uwonbɔr jir ki mɔŋin bu. Adam nin Masiya a bɔr

ref: Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die.
text: Mambu, tibir kaah nan nɔɔ uninfo uba bu ki kɔɔn dulinya nan yaan nin, wee u bir nmɔn ta nkum ki dan nin, ni ma che nkum dan bininfob biɛn bu, nan bu-n ti biɛn tun tibira.

ref: Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law.
text: Le nsiim nan nan foon ki miin tibir pii be dulinya ni. Amaa baah kaan tibir nan yaan wee nsiim kaa be.

ref: Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did. In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later.
text: Amaa nin ni ma biɛn ni, nkum li le ŋmag na nyan Adam a yonn ki nan kpaa Moziz a yonn, hali ki nyaŋ ban kaa tun tibir ke Adam kaah nan tun tibir ki nan bii Uwonbɔr a siimin, Adam nan jɔɔ wan yin ŋɔɔrin nin a nunaŋ le.

ref: But the gift of God's undeserved grace was very different from Adam's sin. That one sin brought death to many others. Yet in an even greater way, Jesus Christ alone brought God's gift of undeserved grace to many people.
text: Amaa Uwonbɔr a piin yin kaa nann Adam a birin ni. Ni ye bininfob takpem kpo uninfo uba nmɔn a bir bu ke, man ke Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanlin ma li jo man, le U piin yan nyann uninfo uba wan ye Yisa Masiya a nyunyunbasanlin nin ma li yab ki tan lagir le Un ta sei bininfob takpem!

ref: There is a lot of difference between Adam's sin and God's gift. That one sin led to punishment. But God's gift made it possible for us to be acceptable to him, even though we have sinned many times.
text: Jigin, Uwonbɔr a piin yin kaa nann uninfo uba a birin ni: Tibɔr a jim nɔɔ uba a bir bu le ki ta nkum dan, amaa ipiin yan wee Uwonbɔr ta sei ti-n ma nɔɔ bininfob takpem a toonbir bu le, le Uwonbɔr ke ti bɔr ŋan.

ref: Death ruled like a king because Adam had sinned. But that cannot compare with what Jesus Christ has done. God has treated us with undeserved grace, and he has accepted us because of Jesus. And so we will live and rule like kings.
text: Ni ye uninfo uba a bir bu, le nkum nɔɔ uninfo uba nmɔn bu ki dan ke, man ke Uwonbɔr a buchin piin yan yab ki san ti kunyunyunbaagin ma jon man na, U ma ye Yisa Masiya wan sei ti limiɛfolin.

ref: Everyone was going to be punished because Adam sinned. But because of the good thing that Christ has done, God accepts us and gives us the gift of life.
text: Mambu uninfo uba a bir bu kaah nan che Uwonbɔr bii bininfob biɛn nin, man mu le uninfo uba a buchin binbem bu mu le che Uwonbɔr bei bininfob biɛn ke bi bɔr ŋan le ki sei bi limiɛfol.

ref: Adam disobeyed God and caused many others to be sinners. But Jesus obeyed him and will make many people acceptable to God.
text: A li ke naah nan ye uninfo uba a mɔyiil bu le nan che bininfob takpem kpann tibirdamin, man mu le uninfo uba a mɔcheel bu mu yin che bininfob takpem n kpann bibuchim.

ref: The Law came, so that the full power of sin could be seen. Yet where sin was powerful, God's gift of undeserved grace was even more powerful.
text: Nsiimin nan kpiɛ le ki che titoonbir pɔr. Amaa le titoonbir kaah pɔr man nmɔn linyunyunbasanlin pɔr jon man na,

ref: Sin ruled by means of death. But God's gift of grace now rules, and God has accepted us because of Jesus Christ our Lord. This means that we will have eternal life.
text: naah ŋa man wee titoonbir che nkum nyaŋ bininfob biɛn nin, man mu le nbuchin binben mu yin che linyunyunbasanl mu n sei ti limiɛfol lan kaa jɔɔ ndiɛmi ti Yudaau Yisa Masiya bu.

ref: What should we say? Should we keep on sinning, so that God's gift of undeserved grace will show up even better?
text: Ti ni yin len ke nii? Ti le li mann tun tibira wee nin che Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl npɔr bee?

ref: No, we should not! If we are dead to sin, how can we go on sinning?
text: Naa li fir ye man ni! Tibir bu ke, ti kpou; ke ni yin ŋa nii wee ti gbaa be tibir nmɔn yaan naa?

ref: Don't you know that all who share in Christ Jesus by being baptized also share in his death?
text: Bee naa nyi ke tim ban biɛn nan fun Uwonbɔr a nyunful Masiya bu-n nan fun u kum a nyunful mu waa?

ref: When we were baptized, we died and were buried with Christ. We were baptized, so we would live a new life, as Christ was raised to life by the glory of God the Father.
text: Mambu ti nan kpo nin Yisa le bi pii ti nin u ma, Uwonbɔr a nyunfulin bu, a li ke Masiya kaah nan fii nkumin nin u Baa a pagin, man le ti mu yin be limiɛfol pɔnlin yaan.

ref: If we shared in Jesus' death by being baptized, we will be raised to life with him.
text: Ni ye tim nin Yisa lagin kpo man ke, man le ti le ji na yin lagin fii nin U.

ref: We know that the persons we used to be were nailed to the cross with Jesus. This was done, so our sinful bodies would no longer be the slaves of sin.
text: Ti nyi ke ti binben kpegimin nan lagin kpaa nin Masiya u, na li ŋa man ki bii tibir a gbanann, wee ti laa ji be tibir a yomirin ni;

ref: We know sin doesn't have power over dead people.
text: Nan bu-n, wan biɛn kpo ke, u nyan tibir a yomirin na.

ref: As surely as we died with Christ, we believe we will also live with him.
text: Daandaan nan ni ye ti kpo nin Masiya ke, ti jɔɔ yada ke ti na li lagin be nin u.

ref: We know that death no longer has any power over Christ. He died and was raised to life, never again to die.
text: Nan bu-n ti nyi ke Masiya kaah nan fii nkumin nin, waa ji yin kpo jigin ni; nkum kaa jɔɔ npɔɔn ki li fir nyaŋ wi.

ref: When Christ died, he died for sin once and for all. But now he is alive, and he lives only for God.
text: Nkum man wee u kpe-n, ti yaa bir bu le u kpo taaliba ki sei ti biɛn; amaa limiɛfol lan wee u nin jɔɔ-n, u nin be ki sei Uwonbɔr le.

ref: In the same way, you must think of yourselves as dead to the power of sin. But Christ Jesus has given life to you, and you live for God.
text: Man nmɔn jigin, ni kan ni ba ki kpiɛ ban kpo ki sei tibirin na, amaa Masiya ni, ni jɔɔ limiɛfol ki sei Uwonbɔr.

ref: Don't let sin rule your body. After all, your body is bound to die, so don't obey its desires
text: Mambu ni laa ji che tibir ŋmag ni gbanann tan kpeg nan ni, ki laa chee sei tibir a gbanann nmɔn a bami.

ref: or let any part of it become a slave of evil. Give yourselves to God, as people who have been raised from death to life. Make every part of your body a slave that pleases God.
text: Laa ta a gbanann a bɔgi ki sei tibir ke npooton a toontunn tiɛri, amaa ta a baa ki sei Uwonbɔr, ki li be ke bininfob ban nyan nkumin ki be limiɛfolin nin; wee ki nin ta a gbanann a bɔgi ki sei Uwonbɔr ke tibuchinn a toontunn tiɛrin.

ref: Don't let sin keep ruling your lives. You are ruled by God's undeserved grace and not by the Law. Slaves Who Do What Pleases God
text: Tibir kaa ji yin ye a yudaau wi, nan bu-n, nsiim kaa ŋmag ŋi, amaa Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanlin bu le a be. Nbuchin binben a yomir

ref: What does all this mean? Does it mean we are free to sin, because we are ruled by God's gift of undeserved grace and not by the Law? Certainly not!
text: Ni nin ye nii? Ti li tun tibir ki ke nsiim kaah kaa ji ŋmag ti wee ti be Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanlin nin buu? Naa li fir ye man ni!

ref: You used to be slaves of sin. But I thank God that with all your heart you followed the example set forth in the teaching you received.
text: Amaa n tenn Uwonbɔr kunɔɔpoog, nin nim ban nan ye titoonbir a yomi wee ki nan nɔɔ nwɔɔnim man wee ni nan gaa nin ni sufu biɛn nin bu.

ref: Now you are set free from sin and are slaves who please God.
text: Ni ŋmar ki nyan tibirin na le ki nin ŋa nbuchin binben a yomi.

ref: I am using these everyday examples, because in some ways you are still weak. You used to let the different parts of your body be slaves of your evil thoughts. But now you must make every part of your body serve God, so that you will belong completely to him.
text: N ta bininfosaalib a binbem le ki pag nan bu-n ni tɔɔl a won naaŋin ni jɔɔ idaburig le. A li ke naah nan jɔɔ ni gbanann a bɔgi ki ŋaan tijaginn a toon a yomirin, nin npooton man mann kpiɛgin, daandaan nan ni ta ni gbanann ki ŋa nbuchin binben a yomirin na wee ki li be kasi.

ref: When you were slaves of sin, you didn't have to please God.
text: Naah nan be tibir a yomirin nin, ni nan be ni wiib le nbuchin binben kaa nan ŋmag ni.

ref: But what good did you receive from the things you did? All you have to show for them is your shame, and they lead to death.
text: Ba a nyɔɔr wee ni kan n-yonn nmɔn nin naah ni nan san nan ifa daandaan nan naa? Ni ma biɛn nan a joorim nan ye nkum le!

ref: Now you have been set free from sin, and you are God's slaves. This will make you holy and will lead you to eternal life.
text: Amaa daandaan nan wee Uwonbɔr fee ni jaa ni tibirin wee ni nin ye Uwonbɔr a yomi nan, tinyɔɔr tan wee ni kan ye kasi a binbem le, le ni joorim ye limiɛfol lan kaa jɔɔ ndiɛm.

ref: Sin pays off with death. But God's gift is eternal life given by Jesus Christ our Lord.
text: Titoonbir a nyɔɔr ye nkum le, amaa le Uwonbɔr a piin ye limiɛfol lan kaa jɔɔ ndiɛm ti Yudaau Masiya ni.

ref: My friends, you surely understand enough about law to know that laws only have power over people who are alive.
text: N nabum, n pag ki tenn bininfob ban nyi nsiimin le, naa nyi ke nsiimin jɔɔ tininkper a pɔɔm ki ŋmag uninfo n-yonn man wee u la fo be nlee?

ref: For example, the Law says that a man's wife must remain his wife as long as he lives. But once her husband is dead, she is free
text: Ni che n mag wɔɔn ni, nsiim ŋmag chaldaan n-yonn man wee u chal la be nle, amaa ni ye u chal kpo ke, lijakunl nmɔn a siim kaa ji ŋmag wi.

ref: That is how it is with you, my friends. You are now part of the body of Christ and are dead to the power of the Law. You are free to belong to Christ, who was raised to life so we could serve God.
text: Ni bu, n nabum, ni tɔɔl kpo ki sei nsiimin na, Masiya a gbanann nin bu, ke ni fir ŋa Masiya wan nan fii nkumin nin kaah ye ban, na li ŋa man wee ti lo iloon ŋan ki sei Uwonbɔr.

ref: When we thought only of ourselves, the Law made us have sinful desires. It made every part of our bodies into slaves who are doomed to die.
text: Tigbanann a bam kaah la nan ŋmag ti n-yonn man nin, le nsiimin nan che kɔlisa birug fii ti gbanann nin, ki che ti lo iloon ki sei nkum.

ref: But the Law no longer rules over us. We are like dead people, and it cannot have any power over us. Now we can serve God in a new way by obeying his Spirit, and not in the old way by obeying the written Law. The Battle with Sin
text: Amaa daandaan nan, taah nan kpo ki sei niwann nan nan ŋmag ti, ti nyan nsiimin yaan na, ti ni yin tun ki sei Kinaaŋ a binben pɔŋin le, naa ji ye nsiim kpegim man nan sɔb dɔ-n ni. Nsiim nin tibir

ref: Does this mean that the Law is sinful? Certainly not! But if it had not been for the Law, I would not have known what sin is really like. For example, I would not have known what it means to want something that belongs to someone else, unless the Law had told me not to do this.
text: Ti ni yin len ke nii? Nsiimin ye tibir lee? Naa ye man ni! Ibamɔn buu maa bi yin nyi tibir kaah ye nan ni, nsiimin le che n biɛ. Maa bi yin nyi linunchɔril kaah jann ye nan ni, ni ye nsiimin kaa bi be ke, “Laa jɔɔ linunchɔrili.”

ref: It was sin that used this command as a way of making me have all kinds of desires. But without the Law, sin is dead.
text: Amaa le tibir kan npɔɔn nsiimin yaan, ki che linunchɔril a booli pɔr n sufu ni. Ni bu nsiimin kaa bi be ke, tibir ma bi kpou.

ref: Before I knew about the Law, I was alive. But as soon as I heard that command, sin came to life,
text: Maah kaa la nan nyi nsiimin n-yonn man nin; n nan jɔɔ limiɛfol, amaa nsiim kaah nan nan foo nin, le tibir fii ki kan npɔɔn n gbanann nin le n kpo.

ref: and I died. The very command that was supposed to bring life to me, instead brought death.
text: Le n kan ke nsiim man bi ye min sei limiɛfolin, nin ta nkum le dan.

ref: Sin used this command to trick me, and because of it I died.
text: Tibir kan npɔɔn nsiimin yaan le ki larim, le nsiim nan bu, le tibir kum.

ref: Still, the Law and its commands are holy and correct and good.
text: Ni bu nsiimin be kasi, le maah wɔɔn man nin be kasi, ki jɔɔ tibuchinn ki ŋan.

ref: Am I saying something good caused my death? Certainly not! It was sin that killed me by using something good. Now we can see how terrible and evil sin really is.
text: Ke ni wɔɔn ke niwann ŋan ke, ni labir nkum le ki dan n buu? Aai naa ye man ni! Amaa tibir nɔɔ nan ŋan bu le ki che nkum pɔr nni, na li ŋa man wee ti biɛ tibir kaah ye nan, nsiimin le che ti biɛ tibir kaah bir kaa tan jɔɔ magim man. Likɔnl lan be ti ni

ref: We know that the Law is spiritual. But I am merely a human, and I have been sold as a slave to sin.
text: Ti nyi nsiimin ye kinaaŋ a binbem le; amaa min le jɔɔ tigbanann a bam, le bi kɔɔrim sei tibir ke uyomin.

ref: In fact, I don't understand why I act the way I do. I don't do what I know is right. I do the things I hate.
text: Maa biɛ nan n tun nmɔn a taai yi. Nan bu-n, nan wee n bi ban n tun nin maa tun ni ma, amaa niwann nan wee n nan nin, ni ma le n tun.

ref: Although I don't do what I know is right, I agree that the Law is good.
text: Tɔ le ni ye n tun nan wee maa bi ban n tun nin ke, n chee ke nsiimin ŋan.

ref: So I am not the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
text: Naah ye man nmɔn, naa ji ye min tɔɔl le tun man ni, amaa tibir tan be n sufu-n nin, le tun man.

ref: I know that my selfish desires won't let me do anything that is good. Even when I want to do right, I cannot.
text: N nyi ke niwaŋann niba kaa be n sufu-n ni, ti ma ye n binben biimin yaan. Nan bu-n, n bi ban n tun nan ŋan, amaa maa yin fir tun ni.

ref: And so, if I don't do what I know is right, I am no longer the one doing these evil things. The sin that lives in me is what does them.
text: Daandaan nan ni ye n tun maah kaa bi ban n tun man nin le ke, naa ji ye min le tun ni, amaa tibir tan be n sufu-n nin le tun man.

ref: The Law has shown me that something in me keeps me from doing what I know is right.
text: N kan ke nsiim nmɔn tun itoon: Ni ye n ban n tun nan ŋan ke, nan bir be n ban.

ref: With my whole heart I agree with the Law of God.
text: Nan bu-n, n potiɛmin ni mɔm le nin Uwonbɔr a siim;

ref: But in every part of me I discover something fighting against my mind, and it makes me a prisoner of sin that controls everything I do.
text: amaa n kan nsiim miba mu kaah be n gbanann nin, ki kɔnn nsiim man be n potiɛmin ni, ki ŋaam tibir tan be n gbanann ni a bɔgi a loondikɔɔru.

ref: What a miserable person I am. Who will rescue me from this body that is doomed to die?
text: Ba a nyunyunbaag a ninfobol ye maa! Ŋma yin feem ki nyam nkum a gbanann nan yaan naa?

ref: Thank God! Jesus Christ will rescue me. So with my mind I serve the Law of God, although my selfish desires make me serve the law of sin.
text: N tenn Uwonbɔr kunɔɔpoog, ti Yudaau Yisa Masiya bu! Ni ma bu, min tɔɔl a potiɛmin n ye Uwonbɔr a siimin a yomu le, amaa le n binben biimin mu ye tibir a siimin a yomu.

ref: If you belong to Christ Jesus, you won't be punished.
text: Mambu, daandaan nan Uwonbɔr kaa yin bii bininfob ban be nin Masiya nni,

ref: The Holy Spirit will give you life that comes from Christ Jesus and will set you free from sin and death.
text: nan bu-n, Masiya bu le limiɛfol a naaŋ a siim feem ki jaa tibirin nin nkumin a siimin.

ref: The Law of Moses cannot do this, because our selfish desires make the Law weak. But God set you free when he sent his own Son to be like us sinners and to be a sacrifice for our sin. God used Christ's body to condemn sin.
text: Uwonbɔr tun nan wee nsiimin kaa fir tun nna nan bu-n uninfosaal a gbanann kaa nan fir ŋmag nsiim nmɔn ni, le U tun U tɔɔl a big le ki nann uninfosaal wan ye tibirdaan nin ke un nan mann tibir a manug. Le ki bii tibir tan be uninfosaal a gbanann nin ni-n,

ref: He did this, so that we would do what the Law commands by obeying the Spirit instead of our own desires.
text: na li ŋa man wee nin gbeen ti buchin a binbem kaah ye man nsiimin yaan, nan bu-n taah kaa ji be tigbanann a wiib a bamin wee ki nin be Uwonbɔr a Kasi a naaŋ kaah ye ti man nin.

ref: People who are ruled by their desires think only of themselves. Everyone who is ruled by the Holy Spirit thinks about spiritual things.
text: Ban nɔɔ tigbanann a bamin a potiɛl be tigbanann nmɔn kaah ban man nin yaan le; amaa ban nɔɔ Kasi a Naaŋ a bamin mu a potiɛl be Kinaaŋin a bamin yaan le.

ref: If our minds are ruled by our desires, we will die. But if our minds are ruled by the Spirit, we will have life and peace.
text: Wan ta u potiɛl ŋa tigbanann a bamin yaan ke ni ye nkum le, amaa lipotiɛl lan mu wee Kasi a Naaŋin ŋmagin ye limiɛfol le nin nposɔɔn;

ref: If we follow our desires, we cannot please God.
text: Ban wee tigbanann a bam ŋmagin kaa li fir gbee Uwonbɔr a numi.

ref: You are no longer ruled by your desires, but by God's Spirit, who lives in you. People who don't have the Spirit of Christ in them don't belong to him.
text: Nim, ma ke, tigbanann a bamin kaa ji ŋmag ni amaa Kinaaŋin le ni ŋmag ni, ni ye Uwonbɔr a Naaŋ be ni ni ke. Wan mu kaa jɔɔ Masiya a Naaŋin ke, waa ye Masiya yaa wi.

ref: But Christ lives in you. So you are alive because God has accepted you, even though your bodies must die because of your sins.
text: Amaa ni ye Masiya be ni ni ke, ni gbanann kpo tibir buu, nin ni ma biɛn ni, ni naaŋin fo nbuchin binben bu.

ref: Yet God raised Jesus to life! God's Spirit now lives in you, and he will raise you to life by his Spirit.
text: Ni ye wan a Naaŋ fiin Yisa nkumin nin be ni ni ke, wan nan fiin Masiya nkumin nin mu li sei ni gbanann tan kpegin limiɛfol u Naaŋin a pɔɔm man be ni nin bu.

ref: If you do, you will die. But you will live, if by the help of God's Spirit you say “No” to your desires.
text: Ni ye ni nɔɔ tigbanann a bamin kaah wɔɔn ni man nin ke, ni li kpo; amaa ni che Uwonbɔr a Naaŋin ku tigbanann a bam a toon yin ke, ni li fo,

ref: Only those people who are led by God's Spirit are his children.
text: nan bu-n, ban wee Uwonbɔr a Naaŋin lii bi samin, bi ye Uwonbɔr a naachim le.

ref: God's Spirit makes us sure that we are his children.
text: Uwonbɔr a Naaŋin tɔɔl le jin siɛra ti naaŋin ke ti sin ye Uwonbɔr a buwaab le.

ref: His Spirit lets us know that together with Christ we will be given what God has promised. We will also share in the glory of Christ, because we have suffered with him. A Wonderful Future for God's People
text: Daandaan nan ni ye ti sin ye Uwonbɔr a buwaab ke, man ke ti ye U faajib le, tim nin Masiya le lagin ki ye Uwonbɔr a faajib, ni ye tim nin Masiya lagin ki jin U fala-n ke tim nin U ma ji na yin lagin kan U pag. Kupag kan la chaan

ref: I am sure what we are suffering now cannot compare with the glory that will be shown to us.
text: N chee ke fala kan wee ti ji daandaan nan kaa foo ti ta bigin kupag kan wee Uwonbɔr na yin kpiir ti ni nni.

ref: In fact, all creation is eagerly waiting for God to show who his children are.
text: Niwann nan wee Uwonbɔr naan nan biɛn le guu le bi sufu ŋa sili ki lig lidaal lan wee Uwonbɔr na yin kpiir U naachimin ni.

ref: that creation would be set free from decay and would share in the glorious freedom of his children.
text: ke tiwann naan wann tɔɔl li nya nburim a yomirin, ki kɔɔ Uwonbɔr kaah ta wiib kan jɔɔ kupag ki sei U buwaabin yaan.

ref: We know that all creation is still groaning and is in pain, like a woman about to give birth.
text: Ti nyi ke tiwann naan wann biɛn le dun le ke nmarwiɛn kaah wu man nin hali nin daandaan nan.

ref: The Spirit makes us sure about what we will be in the future. But now we groan silently, while we wait for God to show that we are his children. This means that our bodies will also be set free.
text: Naa ye ni yaa binba, amaa tim ban wee Uwonbɔr chinn sei ti U Kasi a Naaŋin a looi yin tɔɔl dun le ti sufu ni ki guu n-yonn man wee Uwonbɔr na yin ta ti kpann U tɔɔl a buwaab, ki sei ti nkpenim a manug ti gbanann nin.

ref: And this hope is what saves us. But if we already have what we hope for, there is no need to keep on hoping.
text: Tama nan bu le ti kan feegab. Amaa tama kan wee ti ga-n kaa ye tama kolibi. Ŋma a tama be niwann nan wee u pii jɔɔ-n buu?

ref: However, we hope for something we have not yet seen, and we patiently wait for it.
text: Amaa ni ye ti jɔɔ tama taah kaa la jɔɔ tiwann tan nin bu ke, ti jɔɔ limɔril le ki guu ti.

ref: In certain ways we are weak, but the Spirit is here to help us. For example, when we don't know what to pray for, the Spirit prays for us in ways that cannot be put into words.
text: Man le ye ni, Kinaaŋin ter ti le ti daburigi yin. Taa nyi taah yin miɛ Uwonbɔr ki ban nan ni, amaa Kasi a Naaŋin tɔɔl le gaa ki miɛ Uwonbɔr ki tenn ti nin ndundun man wee imɔleen kaa li fir pag wɔɔn ni.

ref: All of our thoughts are known to God. He can understand what is in the mind of the Spirit, as the Spirit prays for God's people.
text: Le Uwonbɔr wan feen ki lig ti sufu-n nin nyi Kasi a Naaŋin a potiɛl, nan bu-n Kasi a Naaŋin le gaan ki miɛ tenn Uwonbɔr a ninfob gannkaabin Uwonbɔr a bam kaah wɔɔn man.

ref: We know that God is always at work for the good of everyone who loves him. They are the ones God has chosen for his purpose,
text: Le ti nyi ke niwann biɛn nin, Uwonbɔr tun le ki tenn bininfob ban jiɛ win naah li ŋan ki sei bi man, U jɔɔ nan bu wee U yin bi.

ref: and he has always known who his chosen ones would be. He had decided to let them become like his own Son, so his Son would be the first of many children.
text: Ban wee Uwonbɔr pii nan nyi ki bon ke bi na li chee ki kpenn ki li be ke u bija-n kaah be man nin, wee nin che U bija nmɔn nŋa kibininkpeeg u nabum takpem a sisiigin.

ref: What can we say about all this? If God is on our side, can anyone be against us?
text: Ti ni yin len ke nii ki jiin ni niɛ nan paam maa? Ni ye Uwonbɔr si ti chaŋ ke, ŋma li fir kɔnn taa?

ref: God did not keep back his own Son, but he gave him for us. If God did this, won't he freely give us everything else?
text: Uwonbɔr wan kaa nan yii U tɔɔl a bija a kum bu, amaa le ki ta u mann kumanug ki sei ti biɛn, ke ni yin ŋa nii wee waa ji li fir ta U ki kpiɛ tiwann tan biɛn gurin bu ki sei taa?

ref: If God says his chosen ones are acceptable to him, can anyone bring charges against them?
text: Ŋma li fir galin bininfob ban wee Uwonbɔr gann nan naa? Uwonbɔr le len ke bi bɔr ŋan.

ref: Or can anyone condemn them? No indeed! Christ died and was raised to life, and now he is at God's right side, speaking to him for us.
text: Ŋma li fir bii baa? Masiya le nan kpo, le nan jon man le ye u nan fii nkumin na, ki ka Uwonbɔr a nɔɔjiim paam ki miɛ Uwonbɔr ki tenn ti.

ref: Can anything separate us from the love of Christ? Can trouble, suffering, and hard times, or hunger and nakedness, or danger and death?
text: Ŋma li fir bɔgir ti nyan Masiya a jiɛm nan yaan naa? Tibɔmugkaar bee nton bee limugil bee nkom bee nnan bee kidaŋ bee bitɔb a jugaa?

ref: It is exactly as the Scriptures say, “For you we face death all day long. We are like sheep on their way to be butchered.”
text: A li ke naah sɔb Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin ke: “Fin bu le ti be nkum a daŋin lidaal biɛn; ki nann upee wan wee bi ŋa sili bin kɔrin.”

ref: In everything we have won more than a victory because of Christ who loves us.
text: Aai nin ni ma biɛn ni, ti jon ban nyaŋa Masiya a jiɛmin bu.

ref: I am sure that nothing can separate us from God's love—not life or death, not angels or spirits, not the present or the future,
text: N nyi kaa biɛn ni ke naa ye nkum bee limiɛfol, kaa ye malakam bee npɔniimi, kaa ye tiwann yɔɔr tan be daandaan nan bee tiwann yɔɔr tan la yin dan ni, kaa ye ipɔɔn iba,

ref: and not powers above or powers below. Nothing in all creation can separate us from God's love for us in Christ Jesus our Lord!
text: kaa ye nkpikper bee nnyunyɔɔni, kaa ye tiwann yɔɔr tan be tiwann naan wann nin biɛn ni, ni ba kaa be ki li fir bɔgir ti nyan Uwonbɔr a jiɛm man be ti Yudaau Masiya ni-n yaan ni.

ref: I am a follower of Christ, and the Holy Spirit is a witness to my conscience. So I tell the truth and I am not lying when I say
text: N pag ibamɔn le Masiya bu, maa por tibɔkari, le n potiɛl jin siɛra Kasi a naaŋin,

ref: my heart is broken and I am in great sorrow.
text: n jɔɔ npoobiin le nin nan wu kan kaa jɔɔ diɛm n sufu ni.

ref: I would gladly be placed under God's curse and be separated from Christ for the good of my own people.
text: N bi ban ke Uwonbɔr a mɔpoolin bin jim wee min nin Masiya n yiɛr nin tab min tɔɔl a nabumin bu, ban wee min nin bi ma piɛ libolin,

ref: They are the descendants of Israel, and they are also God's chosen people. God showed them his glory. He made agreements with them and gave them his Law. The temple is theirs and so are the promises that God made to them.
text: bi ma ye Iziral yaab. Bi ma le Uwonbɔr nan ta bi kpann U bimarim; ki che bi jɔɔ U tɔɔl a pag, ki poo tipoopɔnn sei bi, ki sei bi U siim, ki wɔɔn bi baah li jiɛn U man iwonjiɛn niin, le ki siin bi limɔsiinl.

ref: They have those famous ancestors, who were also the ancestors of the Christ. I pray that God, who rules over all, will be praised forever! Amen.
text: Bi yaab le ye ti yaajam ninkpeebin, ban nyan ti yaajamin a bolin nin Masiya tɔɔl nyan niin le u ninforin nin bu, U ma ye Uwonbɔr wan jon niwann biɛn, U ma kpaan npagim man kaa jɔɔ diɛm! Ibamɔn.

ref: It cannot be said that God broke his promise. After all, not all of the people of Israel are the true people of God.

text: Ni laa chee sei dulinya nan yaab a binbem jigin ni, amaa ni mann pɔŋ ni potiɛla wee ni binbemin kpenn. Ni ma le ni li fir mag ki chee Uwonbɔr a bam kaah ye man. U bam man ŋan ki jɔɔ linungbeel ki be chasi-n.
