ref: Titus, because of our faith, you are like a son to me. I pray that God our Father and Christ Jesus our Savior will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! What Titus Was To Do in Crete
text: N sɔb kugbɔŋ nan ki tenn fin Tatusi wan ye n big bamɔŋin, nin taah lagin ki jɔɔ yada kiba kan nin bu. Ti ba Uwonbɔr nin Masiya wan ye ti feeru win a nyunyunbasanl nin nposɔɔn li be niŋ. Tatusi a toonl kaah ye nan Kereti

ref: I left you in Crete to do what had been left undone and to appoint leaders for the churches in each town. As I told you,
text: Nan bu wee n nan jiɛn niŋ Kereti a tiŋin nin nan ye nan le, n nan ban a gbaar itoon yan nan gur kaa diɛ n le ki sin gann bininkpeeb ntim biɛn nin ke maah nan wɔɔniŋ man nin.

ref: they must have a good reputation and be faithful in marriage. Their children must be followers of the Lord and not have a reputation for being wild and disobedient.
text: Naa ŋan nin uninkpel li jɔɔ igalin ni, u li ye wan jɔɔ upii uba kpeŋileŋ, le u buwaab mu li ye ban jɔɔ yada, ki laa ye tukangbirdami.

ref: Church officials are in charge of God's work, and so they must also have a good reputation. They must not be bossy, quick-tempered, heavy drinkers, bullies, or dishonest in business.
text: Nibu, uwonjiɛn sanliir kaah ŋmag Uwonbɔr a toon yin ni, naa ŋan nin u li jɔɔ igalin bee ki mugir u tabi, ki laa ye wan a ŋuul fii yɔli yɔli, ki laa ye udanyugbeeri, ki laa ye ukɔnban bee ki laa ban tinyɔɔr tan kaa jɔɔ jilima.

ref: Instead, they must be friendly to strangers and enjoy doing good things. They must also be sensible, fair, pure, and self-controlled.
text: Amaa ni kpaa talar le nin u li gaan bicham, ki li ye wan ban nan ŋan, ki li ye wan fir chor u ba, ki li ye wan jɔɔ lasaab, ki li be kasi nin uba a ŋmagimin.

ref: They must stick to the true message they were taught, so their good teaching can help others and correct everyone who opposes it.
text: Ki li ŋmag ibamɔn a bɔr tan wee bi nan wɔɔn win kenken, wee ki fir pɔɔg u kpiɛtiib a gbanann nin ibamɔn a wɔɔmin, wee ki fir nyaŋ ban biɛn kaa cheel tibɔŋann nmɔn nin.

ref: There are many who don't respect authority, and they fool others by talking nonsense. This is especially true of some Jewish followers.
text: Nan bu-n, limɔyiil a ninfob yaba, ban pag yɔli yɔli nin kularug a ninfob, nin ban jann nɔɔ lipunjiil a kaalin.

ref: But you must make them be quiet. They are after money, and they upset whole families by teaching what they should not.
text: Ni kpaa talar le nin bin ŋmin, nan bu-n bi choon kɔɔ bininfob biɛn a niin yin le ki wɔɔn nwɔɔm man kaa kpaan nin bi li wɔɔn ni, bi wɔɔn man ki ban tinyɔɔr tan kaa jɔɔ jilima le.

ref: It is like one of their own prophets once said, “The people of Crete always tell lies. They are greedy and lazy like wild animals.”
text: Hali bi yaa linlenn uba len ke, “Kereti yaab ye tibɔkardam le iyoo biɛn, bi nann tiwankor le, ki ye bigbanyagdam nin bijijib.”

ref: This surely is a true saying. And you should be hard on such people, so you can help them grow stronger in their faith.
text: Siɛra nan ye ibamɔn le. Ni ma bu fuun bi bu choba, wee nin che bin mann sir bi yada-n nbamɔm,

ref: Don't pay any attention to any of those senseless Jewish stories and human commands. These are made up by people who won't obey the truth.
text: ki laa pelig Juu yaab a wɔɔnim man kaa ye ibamɔn nin bee bininfob ban yii ibamɔn a siimin ni.

ref: Everything is pure for someone whose heart is pure. But nothing is pure for an unbeliever with a dirty mind. That person's mind and conscience are destroyed.
text: Bininfob ban be kasi-n, bi wan biɛn be le kasi, amaa bininfob ban kaa be kasi wee kaa jɔɔ yada-n ma ban, niba kaa be ki be kasi. Nan bu-n bi sufu nin bi potiɛri biɛn ŋmarin na.

ref: Such people claim to know God, but their actions prove they really don't. They are disgusting. They won't obey God, and they are too worthless to do anything good.
text: Bi len ke bi nyi Uwonbɔr, amaa le bi toon yin wɔɔn ke bi yii wa. Uwonbɔr nan bi binbem nmɔn. Bi ye tukangbirdam le kaa li fir tun litoon ŋanli.

ref: Titus, you must teach only what is correct.
text: Ni kpaa le nin fin Tatusi n wɔɔn bi ibamɔn a wɔɔm.

ref: Tell the older women to behave as those who love the Lord should. They must not gossip about others or be slaves of wine. They must teach what is proper,
text: Man mu jigin, wɔɔn bipiininkpeeb wee bi li jɔɔ jilima bi binbemin, ki laa ye bitingbiibi, ki laa ye bidanyubi, amaa wee ki li wɔɔn nan ŋan.

ref: so the younger women will be loving wives and mothers.
text: Ni ye man ke, bi li tinn bipiisapɔm wee bi li ban bichiɛb nin bi buwaab,

ref: Each of the younger women must be sensible and kind, as well as a good homemaker, who puts her own husband first. Then no one can say insulting things about God's message.
text: ki li chor biba, ki li be kasi, ki li jɔɔ inunman bi niin yin, ki li be nbamɔm, ki li ye ban cheel bi chiɛb a mɔɔŋi, ni ma li che uba kaa li fir pag ki bii Uwonbɔr a bɔri.

ref: Tell the young men to have self-control in everything.
text: Man mu jigin, pɔɔg binaachipɔm mu a gbanann wee bi li chor bi ba.

ref: Always set a good example for others. Be sincere and serious when you teach.
text: Nin niwann biɛn ni ŋaam limagil ki sei bi ki li tun nan ŋan na. A wɔɔm a poolin ke, a wɔɔn bi tininforin nin inunman na.

ref: Use clean language that no one can criticize. Do this, and your enemies will be too ashamed to say anything against you.
text: Ki li pag ibamɔn yan wee uba kaa li fir pag bii ti, wee ban kaa chee a wɔɔm nmɔn n ji ifa, nan bu-n baa jɔɔ niba a bɔbir ki li fir pag sei ti.

ref: Tell slaves always to please their owners by obeying them in everything. Slaves must not talk back to their owners
text: Wɔɔn ban ye biyom wee bi li cheel bi yudam a mɔɔŋi niwann biɛn nin, ki li pɔɔn bi ba ki li be nbinben man li gbee bi yudam a num, ki laa far bi imɔkpeli,

ref: or steal from them. They must be completely honest and trustworthy. Then everyone will show great respect for what is taught about God our Savior. God's Kindness and the New Life
text: ki laa su bi wan yɔɔri, amaa wee ki wɔɔn ke bi sin ye ban wee bi li ŋa bi yada le, wee niwann biɛn nin bin che Uwonbɔr wan ye ti feeru win a wɔɔmin li jɔɔ kɔlisa.

ref: God has shown us undeserved grace by coming to save all people.
text: Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl lan ta feegab dan ni, kpiir uninfo biɛn bu-u.

ref: He taught us to give up our wicked ways and our worldly desires and to live decent and honest lives in this world.
text: U nyunyunbasanl nmɔn wɔɔn ti ke ti yiim nan kaa ye nwonjiɛn binben nin dulinya nan a kɔlisa birug biɛn, wee ki li chor ti ba ki li ye ban jɔɔ lasaab, ki li jɔɔ nwonjiɛn binben n-yonn man wee ti be nan yaan.

ref: We are filled with hope, as we wait for the glorious return of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ.
text: A li ke taah le jɔɔ tama ki guu ti kaar a daalin, le ti lig lidaal lan wee ti Wonbɔr gbingbemilin nin ti feegabdaan Yisa Masiya kaah na yin degirin nin kupag man,

ref: He gave himself to rescue us from everything evil and to make our hearts pure. He wanted us to be his own people and to be eager to do right.
text: wan ta uba ki ŋa nkpenim a manug ki sei ti, ki nyan ti titoonbir biɛn a yomirin, le ki ŋa ti u baantɔɔl a ninfob ban be kasi ki jɔɔ linunmanl nin itoon ŋan a tum.

ref: Teach these things, as you use your full authority to encourage and correct people. Make sure you earn everyone's respect.
text: Ni niɛ nan le ye nan wee a li wɔɔn bi. Ki li jɔɔ npɔɔn man wee bi ta seiŋin biɛn ki pɔɔg bi gbanann ki li kpaan bi. Ki laa che uba nlig ziɛŋi.

ref: Remind your people to obey the rulers and authorities and not to be rebellious. They must always be ready to do something helpful
text: Tiɛr bininfob nmɔn ke bi li nɔɔ biyudam nin bibɔrtiib a siim kaah wɔɔn man nin, ki li cheel bi mɔɔŋi, ki ŋa sili nin bin tun niwann nan ŋan biɛn,

ref: and not say cruel things or argue. They should be gentle and kind to everyone.
text: bi laa jɔɔ kutingbiig u ba bu, ki li be nin nposɔɔn, ki li jɔɔ nbinben ŋan, ki li tenn bininfob biɛn ibamɔn a jilima.

ref: We used to be stupid, disobedient, and foolish, as well as slaves of all sorts of desires and pleasures. We were evil and jealous. Everyone hated us, and we hated everyone.
text: Isaŋ iba ti mu nan ye tijɔri le nin tukangbirdam, le ni lar ti ki ta ti ŋa tiyomir, ki jɔɔ kɔlisa birug nin dulinya nan a wan ŋan. Le ti jɔɔ kininaŋ nin linunchɔril, le bi nan ti le ti mu nan bitab.

ref: God our Savior showed us how good and kind he is.
text: Amaa Uwonbɔr wan ye ti feeru nan a ŋam nin U bam kaah nan degirin nin,

ref: He saved us because of his mercy, and not because of any good things we have done. God washed us by the power of the Holy Spirit. He gave us new birth and a fresh beginning.
text: le U fee ti gab, naa ye ibuchin toon le ti tun ni, amaa U nyunyunbasanl bu. U fee ti gab waah nan fun ti nnyum ki sei ti nmaal pɔɔn nin kinaaŋ pɔŋ Kasi a Naaŋ a pɔɔm bu,

ref: God sent Jesus Christ our Savior to give us his Spirit.
text: Kasi a Naaŋ nmɔn le U nan kpaar takpem ki jaa uninfo biɛn bu Yisa Masiya wan ye ti feegabdaan nin bu,

ref: Jesus treated us much better than we deserve. He made us acceptable to God and gave us the hope of eternal life.
text: U nyunyunbasanl bu le U ke tibɔr ŋan, ti na li ŋa Uwonbɔr a faajib ki jɔɔ limiɛfol lan kaa jɔɔ diɛmin a tama.

ref: This message is certainly true. These teachings are useful and helpful for everyone. I want you to insist that the people follow them, so that all who have faith in God will be sure to do good deeds.
text: Tibɔr nan ye ibamɔn le. Le n ban ni li jɔɔ ti ki wɔɔn bi iyoo biɛn wee nin che ban ŋa Uwonbɔr yada-n n choo biba ki ta bi saŋi ki tun itoon ŋan. Ni ma ye nan ŋan ki jɔɔ tinyɔɔr ki sei uninfo biɛn.

ref: But don't have anything to do with stupid arguments about ancestors. And stay away from disagreements and quarrels about the Law of Moses. Such arguments are useless and senseless.
text: Amaa ni nyam ijɔrig nin nmaal a ninkpeeb a yin a bɔrin nin imɔkpel a famin nin ikɔn ki ta jiin Uwonbɔr a siim paam, nan bu-n ni ye yɔli le kaa jɔɔ tinyɔɔri.

ref: Warn troublemakers once or twice. Then don't have anything else to do with them.
text: A kpaan kumabiyiɛrugdaan taaliba bee itaa ilee wee waa kpenn ke, a nyam udaan a bɔrin ki laa ji kan u ki kpiɛ ni kanlin ni.

ref: You know their minds are twisted, and their own sins show how guilty they are. Personal Instructions and Greetings
text: A nyi ke man a ninfou ye kuŋmaruŋ le nin tibirdaan, u bii u bau. Nwɔɔm man joor

ref: I plan to send Artemas or Tychicus to you. After he arrives, please try your best to meet me at Nicopolis. I have decided to spend the winter there.
text: N tun Atemasi bee Tachikusi a ban ke, a pɔɔn a ba ki dan n ban Nikopolisi, nan bu-n n bon ke n be niin le kufaag a yoo.

ref: When Zenas the lawyer and Apollos get ready to leave, help them as much as you can, so they won't have need of anything.
text: Pɔɔn a ba ki ter Zenasi wan ye Rom yaab a bɔjiru win nin Apolosi bi sanchonlin ki laa che baah ban nan npar bi.

ref: Greetings to you from everyone here. Greet all of our friends who share in our faith. I pray that the Lord will be kind to all of you!
text: Ban biɛn be n ban nin poor ni. Poor ban ban ti, bi yada bu-n na. Linyunyunbasanl li be ni biɛn bu.

ref: From Paul, who is in jail for serving Christ Jesus, and from Timothy, who is like a brother because of our faith. Philemon, you work with us and are very dear to us. This letter is to you
text: Min Pɔɔl, wan ye uloondiikɔɔr Masiya bu-n, nin ti na a big Timoti le sɔb kugbɔŋ nan, Ki tenn ti jɔ kpaarimɔɔn, Filemɔɔn wan ye ti toontunn kpiɛgin,

ref: and to the church that meets in your home. It is also to our dear friend Apphia and to Archippus, who serves the Lord as we do.
text: nin ti ninsa Apifiɛ, nin Achipusi wan ye ti tɔtogkpiɛg nin biwonjiɛm a laguŋ ban lagin a niin nin:

ref: I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! Philemon's Love and Faith
text: Ti Baa Uwonbɔr nin ti Yudaau Yisa Masiya a nyunyunbasanl nin nposɔɔn li be ni bu. Filemɔɔn a jiɛm nin u yada a bɔr

ref: Philemon, each time I mention you in my prayers, I thank God.
text: Iyoo biɛn n le poor n Wonbɔru le ki tiɛr a bu n wonmiɛlin,

ref: I hear about your faith in our Lord Jesus and about your love for all God's people.
text: nan bu-n n gbir ŋaah ŋa Uyudaan Yisa yada wee ki jiɛ Uwonbɔr a ninfogannkaab biɛn man na.

ref: As you share your faith with others, I pray they may come to know all the blessings Christ has given us.
text: N miɛ Uwonbɔr le ke a li tun nin linunmanl ki li por yada kan wee a jɔɔ-n, wee nin che a biɛ nbamɔm niwann ŋan nan biɛn wee ti jɔɔ Masiya ni-n.

ref: My friend, your love has made me happy and has greatly encouraged me. It has also cheered the hearts of God's people. Paul Speaks to Philemon about Onesimus
text: A jiɛm nmɔn seim nmɔn le takpem nin ngbananpɔɔn, nan bu-n fin n nabig, a pɔŋ Uwonbɔr a ninfogannkaab a sufuu. Pɔɔl kaah miɛ Onesemosi man

ref: Christ gives me the courage to tell you what to do.
text: Mambu, hali maah bi ye n li jɔɔ lipoobil Masiya bu ki li fir wɔɔniŋ ŋaah bi ye a tun nan nin,

ref: But I would rather ask you to do it simply because of love. Yes, as someone in jail for Christ,
text: amaa n baliŋ le njiɛm bu. Min Pɔɔl, wan ye uninkpel wee daandaan nan ki ye uloondiikɔɔr Yisa Masiya bu-n,

ref: I beg you to help Onesimus! He is like a son to me because I led him to Christ here in jail.
text: n baliŋ le, n bija Onesemosi bu, wan kpann n bija, n-yonn man wee bi nan lolim tikulorin.

ref: Before this, he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.
text: N-yonn nba waa nan jɔɔ tinyɔɔr a ban ni, amaa daandaan nan u jɔɔ tinyɔɔr ki sei min nin fin biɛn.

ref: Sending Onesimus back to you makes me very sad.
text: Uma wan ye n poobil a ninfou win le n jɔɔ u jiin a ban.

ref: I would like to keep him here with me, where he could take your place in helping me while I am here in prison for preaching the good news.
text: Baah lolim tikulorin tibɔŋann nin a mɔɔnim bu, n bi li ban u li be n ban do ki si a taalin ki terim.

ref: But I won't do anything unless you agree to it first. I want your act of kindness to come from your heart, and not be something you feel forced to do.
text: Amaa maa ban n ŋa niba wee ŋaa nyi man bu, wee a yin ter nan ke ni laa ye limugili, amaa wee ni li ye a tɔɔl a bam.

ref: Perhaps Onesimus was taken from you for a little while so you could have him back for good,
text: Niba ke waah nan fɔr a ban wama-n, nan ye le ke u nan jirin ke u li be a ban isaŋ biɛn,

ref: but not as a slave. Onesimus is much more than a slave. To me he is a dear friend, but to you he is even more, both as a person and as a follower of the Lord.
text: kaa ji ye uyomi, amaa wan jon uyom, ki ye kinabig jiɛkaag. N jiɛ u kaga amaa fin le jann jiɛ u ki jom, waah ye uninfosaal ki ye kinabig Uyudaan ni-n bu.

ref: If you consider me a friend because of Christ, then welcome Onesimus as you would welcome me.
text: Ni ma bu ni ye a nyi ke n ye a toontunn kpiɛg ke, gaa mu ke ŋaah bi li gaam man nin.

ref: If he has cheated you or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
text: Ni ye u nan galiŋ bee u jin a pɔnl le ke, che ni li nɔɔ min na.

ref: With my own hand I write: I, PAUL, WILL PAY YOU BACK. But don't forget you owe me your life.
text: Min Pɔɔl, tɔɔl a nɔɔ le n ta sɔb nan. N li yɔ, kaa yin tiɛr ke min le ye fin tɔɔl gbaa.

ref: My dear friend and follower of Christ our Lord, please cheer me up by doing this for me.
text: N na big, n bi ban ke n kan tinyɔɔr tiba le a ban ti yudaau bu; pɔŋ n sufuu Masiya ni.

ref: Please get a room ready for me. I hope your prayers will be answered, and I can visit you.
text: Nan kpiɛ: Mann kuchandiig ki guun ma, nan bu-n n jɔɔ tama ke Uwonbɔr li taam ki jiin nin ni ban, ke naah miɛ Uwonbɔr man nin. Ipoor yan joor

ref: Epaphras is also here in jail for being a follower of Christ Jesus. He sends his greetings,
text: Epafarasi, wan ye n loondiig kɔɔ kpiɛg Masiya bu-n pooriŋ.

ref: and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, who work together with me.
text: Le Mag, nin Arisitakusi, nin Demasi, nin Lug, ban ye n toontunn kpiɛtiibin mu poorin.

ref: I pray that the Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you!
text: Ti yudaau Yisa Masiya a nyunyunbasanl li be nin ni naam.

ref: Long ago in many ways and at many times God's prophets spoke his message to our ancestors.
text: Yaayoo nni, Uwonbɔr nan taar isaŋ takpem nin isan balbal le ki che bilinlem pag tenn ti yaajam,

ref: But now at last, God sent his Son to bring his message to us. God created the universe by his Son, and everything will someday belong to the Son.
text: amaa idaa yan joor nan, u che U bija le pag sei ti, wan wee U ŋau niwann biɛn a faajiru win, nin wan bu wee U nan naan dulinya nan nin.

ref: God's Son has all the brightness of God's own glory and is like him in every way. By his own mighty word, he holds the universe together. After the Son had washed away our sins, he sat down at the right side of the glorious God in heaven.
text: Uwonbɔr a pag le che U bija-n nyagin, ki jɔɔ Uwonbɔr a nunaŋ, ki ji ye wan ŋmag niwann biɛn u mɔleen a pɔɔm bu. Ni bɔɔn bu waah nan ban tibir a ŋunnim ki sei ti-n, le u kal Jilimadaan Uwonbɔr a nɔɔjiim paam papaab. Uwonbɔr a bija kaah jon Malakam man

ref: He had become much greater than the angels, and the name he was given is far greater than any of theirs. God's Son Is Greater than Angels
text: Le Masiya yab jon malakam biɛn, ke liyinl lan wee Uwonbɔr ta sei win kaah yab jon malakam a yin man nin.

ref: God has never said to any of the angels, “You are my Son, because today I have become your Father!” Neither has God said to any of them, “I will be his Father, and he will be my Son!”
text: Malaka u la ba wee Uwonbɔr la nyi len ke, “Fin le ye N bijaa; dinan a daal N ŋa a Baa”? Bee, “N li ŋa u Baa, wee u mu n ŋa n bijaa”?

ref: When God brings his first-born Son into the world, he commands all of his angels to worship him.
text: Uwonbɔr kaah nan ta U bininkpeegin ki dan dulinya nan yaan nin, U ji nan len ke, “Che Uwonbɔr a malakam biɛn n jiɛn u.”

ref: And when God speaks about the angels, he says, “I change my angels into wind and my servants into flaming fire.”
text: U nan len ke malakamin paam ke, “U ŋa U malakam le bi be ke ntafaamin, Le u toontum mu be ke nŋmipeen nin.”

ref: But God says about his Son, “You are God, and you will rule as King forever! Your royal power brings about justice.
text: Amaa U bija-n ma paam U nan len ke, “A naangbɔŋin, Uwonbɔr aa, a yin gbaa be le hali nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛmi, le a buchin li ye a naam a jaangbiɛg

ref: You loved justice and hated evil, and so I, your God, have chosen you. I appointed you and made you happier than any of your friends.”
text: Ŋaah ban nbuchin binben ki nan npooton ni; mambu Uwonbɔr, wan ye a weemin, nan kpaar nmɔn a kpam ki jaa a bu ki seiŋ tininkper tan yab jon a kpiɛtiib a ninkper.”

ref: The Scriptures also say, “In the beginning, Lord, you were the one who laid the foundation of the earth and created the heavens.
text: Uwonbɔr ji len ke, “Npiinimin, Uyudaan aa fin le nan fiɛ dulinya nan a fiɛl, le paab mu ye a nɔɔi kaah tun nan.

ref: They will all disappear and wear out like clothes, but you will last forever.
text: Bi biɛn na li kpo, amaa fin le yin gbaa be le; bi na li char ke tiwanyee wan kaah char man nin.

ref: You will roll them up like a robe and change them like a garment. But you are always the same, and you will live forever.”
text: A na li kpab bi ke likinkenlin; bi biɛn na li kpenn ke likinkenlin. Amaa fin kaa yin kpenn ni, le a bi-n mu kaa jɔɔ diɛmi.”

ref: God never said to any of the angels, “Sit at my right side until I make your enemies into a footstool for you!”
text: Malaka u la ba wee Uwonbɔr la nyi ki bei u ke, “Kalim n nɔɔjiim paam, hali nin maah na li che, a dataam n kpann a taai a tɔɔnbol laa”?

ref: Angels are merely spirits sent to serve people who are going to be saved.
text: Naa ye malakam biɛn ye nnaam ban tun itoon le ki tenn ban biɛn yin kan nŋmarimin naa?

ref: We must give our full attention to what we were told, so we won't drift away.
text: Mambu ni kpaa talar le nin ti li ŋmag ibamɔn yan wee ti nan gbirin, wee niba laa ta ti ki nya ibamɔn nmɔn yaan ni.

ref: The message spoken by angels proved to be true, and all who disobeyed or rejected it were punished as they deserved.
text: Nan bu-n Malakam kaah nan pag tibɔr tan sei ti yaajamin nan wɔɔn ke ni ye ibamɔn le, le ban nan yii tibɔr nmɔn nan kan litudaril lan kpaan bi ke,

ref: So if we refuse this great way of being saved, how can we hope to escape? The Lord himself was the first to tell about it, and people who heard the message proved to us that it was true.
text: ti yin ŋa nii wee ki ŋmara, ni ye ti yii nŋmarim man polig nan ke naa? Nŋmarim man wee Uyudaan nan chinn pag mi bɔrin, le ban nan gbir U bɔr nmɔn jin ti siɛra ti ban.

ref: God himself showed that his message was true by working all kinds of powerful miracles and wonders. He also gave his Holy Spirit to anyone he chose to. The One Who Leads Us To Be Saved
text: Uwonbɔr tɔɔl nan jin mi siɛra nin ligaril a siɛra nin lijinjeel a toon nin ligaril a toon balbal, nin waah nan ta U kasi a Naaŋ a piini ki tol bi waah ban man. Wan lii ti sam ki chaa nŋmarimin

ref: We know that God did not put the future world under the power of angels.
text: Uwonbɔr kaa len ke malakam le ye dulinya kan wee ti pag nan a yudaau wi.

ref: Somewhere in the Scriptures someone says to God, “What makes you care about us humans? Why are you concerned for weaklings such as we?
text: Amaa uba mu nan jin siɛra Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋin ke: “Uninfo ye baa wee a potiɛl be u ni, Uninfosaal a bija wan wee a baga be u ni-n naa?

ref: You made us lower than the angels for a while. Yet you have crowned us with glory and honor.
text: A nan ŋa u le ki che u jilima waar kaa foo malakam yaali; le a sei u jilima nin kupag a yuchigirig

ref: And you have put everything under our power!” God has put everything under our power and has not left anything out of our power. But we still don't see it all under our control.
text: ki ta niwann biɛn ki ŋa u nɔɔn.” Uwonbɔr kaah ta niwann biɛn ki ŋa Yisa a nɔɔn nin, Uwonbɔr kaa nan che niba gur kaa ye u yaan ni. Amaa daandaan nan taa kan waah ye niwann biɛn man ni.

ref: What we do see is Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels. Because of God's gift of undeserved grace, Jesus died for everyone. And now that Jesus has suffered and died, he is crowned with glory and honor!
text: Amaa ti kan Yisa, wan wee Uwonbɔr nan jiin u tum wama malakam ban nin, daandaan nan, u chig kupag nin jilima a yuchigirig le waah jin nkum a fala-n bu, wee Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl bu u nan che u kpo uninfo biɛn bu-n.

ref: Everything belongs to God, and all things were created by his power. So God did the right thing when he made Jesus perfect by suffering, as Jesus led many of God's children to be saved and to share in his glory.
text: Waah yin ta nbuwaab takpem ki kɔɔn kupagin nin, ni nan kpaan ke Uwonbɔr wan nan naan niwann biɛn, nin wan bu wee niwann biɛn be-n, Un ŋa bi feegab a daau kasi u fala a jim bu.

ref: Jesus and the people he makes holy all belong to the same family. This is why he isn't ashamed to call them his brothers and sisters.
text: Yisa le che bininfob be kasi, le kasi dam nmɔn nin Yisa ye iniin yaab. Ni bu ifa kaa jɔɔ Yisa nin un yin bi ke u nabumi.

ref: He even said to God, “I will tell them your name and sing your praises when they come together to worship.”
text: U len ke, “N li mɔɔn a yinl ki sei n nabum; biwonjiɛm a nintogil n li gaah ilan ki don a yinl.”

ref: He also said, “I will trust God.” Then he said, “Here I am with the children God has given me.”
text: Le ki ji len ke, “N li gaa Uwonbɔr ki ji.” Le ki ji nan len ke, “Min sɔ do, nin n buwaab ban wee Uwonbɔr ta seimin.”

ref: We are people of flesh and blood. This is why Jesus became one of us. He died to destroy the devil, who had power over death.
text: Baah ye nbuwaab ki jɔɔ tigbanann nin nchamin, ni bu le Yisa mu nan kpann uninfo ke uma nin bininfob li jɔɔ tigbanann tiba, wee u kumin ke u nan bii Sintani wan ŋmag nkum a pɔɔmin,

ref: But he also died to rescue all of us who live each day in fear of dying.
text: wee ki fee ban a binbem biɛn ŋa bi tiyomir nkum bu dulinya nan yaan nin ki gab.

ref: Jesus clearly did not come to help angels, but he did come to help Abraham's descendants.
text: Ni ye ibamɔn le, naa ye malakam le U teri, amaa Abiraham a yaabili le U ter.

ref: He had to be one of us, so he could serve God as our merciful and faithful high priest and sacrifice himself for the forgiveness of our sins.
text: Ni nan bu ni nan kpaa talar le u li be ke u nabum kaah be man nin niwann biɛn nin, wee ki fir kpann biminmanib a yudaau wan yab ki si nba bu nin wan ye unyunyunbasann u toon yin ki sei Uwonbɔr, ki ta uba ki mann tibir a manug ki sei bininfob.

ref: And now that Jesus has suffered and was tempted, he can help anyone else who is tempted.
text: Yisa tɔɔl kaah nan kan nbiginim ki jin fala nbu, u li fir ter ban wee nbiginim kan bin.

ref: My friends, God has chosen you to be his holy people. So think about Jesus, the one we call our apostle and high priest!
text: Mambu, n nabum ban be kasi nan, wee ki kpiɛ Uwonbɔr a yimin yaan nin, ni li tiɛr Yisa buu, wan ye ntoon nin biminmanib a yudaau wan wee ti ŋa u yada tiwonjiɛn samin nin.

ref: Jesus was faithful to God, who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in serving all God's people.
text: U nan si nba bu le ki sei wan gann win, a li ke Moziz kaah nan si nba bu u toon yin ki sei Uwonbɔr a ninfob biɛn man nin.

ref: But Jesus deserves more honor than Moses, just as the builder of a house deserves more honor than the house.
text: Yisa le ye wan kpaan jilima ki jon Moziz, a li ke uniinmaar kaah jɔɔ jilima ki jon iniin nin tɔɔl man nin.

ref: Of course, every house is built by someone, and God is really the one who built everything.
text: Iniin biɛn jɔɔ wan maa i le, amaa Uwonbɔr le ye wan maa niwann biɛn.

ref: But Christ is the Son in charge of God's people. And we are those people, if we keep on being brave and don't lose hope. A Rest for God's People
text: Amaa Masiya ma si nba bu le Uwonbɔr a ninfob biɛn bu ki ye U bija, tim le ye Uwonbɔr a niin yaab, ni ye ti li jɔɔ lipoobil le nin tama kan wee ti far ligbingbanl ki bu-n. Uwonbɔr a ninfob a foorim

ref: It is just as the Holy Spirit says, “If you hear God's voice today,
text: Ke Kasi a Naaŋ kaah len ke: “Dinan, ni ye ni gbir U kukɔl ke,

ref: don't be stubborn! Don't rebel like those people who were tested in the desert. *
text: ni laa ta niba ŋa tukangbirdami, wee ki kɔnn bininkpeeb ke ni yaajam kaah nan mag u n-yonn man wee bi nan be kukunkɔɔg a paabin ni,

ref: For forty years your ancestors tested God and saw the things he did.
text: nan yaan wee ni yaajam nan magim ki tan kpaa ibin pina, wee bi num kan nan wee N tun ni.

ref: “Then God got tired of them and said, ‘You people never show good sense, and you don't understand what I want you to do.’
text: Mambu le N ŋuul nan fii bi nɔɔm nmɔn bu, le N len ke, ‘Bi sufu ŋmarin le iyoo biɛn, le baa nyi N san yi.’

ref: God became angry and told the people, ‘You will never enter my place of rest!’ ”
text: Le N nan poo tipoor N ŋuufiiŋin bu ki ke, ‘Baa li kan lifooril N ban ni.’

ref: My friends, watch out! Don't let evil thoughts or doubts make any of you turn from the living God.
text: N nabum, ni li nyi wee ni ni uba laa jɔɔ sufu birug kan li che un fɔɔr ki jiɛn Uwonbɔr wan ye limiɛfol daan nin ban ni.

ref: You must encourage one another each day. And you must keep on while there is still a time that can be called “today.” If you don't, then sin may fool some of you and make you stubborn.
text: Amaa ni li pɔɔgir tab a sufu idaa biɛn na, taah la be Dinan nin, wee ni ni uba laa ye tukangbirdaan tibir a larug bu.

ref: We were sure about Christ when we first became his people. So let's hold tightly to our faith until the end.
text: Nan bu-n ni ye ti ŋmag ti chinchinn a dindann nbamɔm ki tan kpaa ti miɛfol a joorim ke, tim nin Masiya na yin ye nba le.

ref: Who were those people that heard God's voice and rebelled? Weren't they the same ones that came out of Egypt with Moses?
text: Ŋmam le nan gbir Uwonbɔr a kukɔl, wee ki yii nnaa? Naa ye ban biɛn wee Moziz nan nyan bi Ijibir nnaa?

ref: And who did God say would never enter his place of rest? Weren't they the ones that disobeyed him?
text: Ke ŋmam wee U nan poo tipoor ke baa li kan lifooril U ban nin na, wee naa ye ban yii U mɔb nnaa?

ref: We see that those people did not enter the place of rest because they did not have faith.
text: Ni bu, ti kan ke baa nan fir kɔɔ lifooril nmɔn yaan ni, nan bu-n bi kaa jɔɔ yada-n bu.

ref: The promise to enter the place of rest is still good, and we must take care that none of you miss out.
text: Mambu, Uwonbɔr kaah siin limɔsiinl ke U li sei ti lifooril lan nin kaah la si nbu, ni che ti choo tiba wee uba laa nan lann lifooril nmɔn ni.

ref: We have heard the message, just as they did. But they failed to believe what they heard, and the message did not do them any good.
text: Ti mu gbir tibɔŋann nmɔn ke baah nan gbir ti man nin le; amaa baah nan gbir tibɔŋann nmɔn taa nan jɔɔ tinyɔɔr ki sei bi, nan bu-n baa nan ta tibɔŋann nmɔn ki kpiɛ bi yada ni.

ref: Only people who have faith will enter the place of rest. It is just as the Scriptures say, “God became angry and told the people, ‘You will never enter my place of rest!’ ” God said this, even though everything has been ready from the time of creation.
text: Daandaan nan, tim ban ŋa yada nan kan lifooril nmɔn na, a li ke Uwonbɔr kaah len ke, “Mambu le N poo bimɔb N ŋuul kaah fii-n bu ki ke, ‘Baa li kan lifoorili.’ ” Nin ni ma biɛn na U pii nan diɛ U toon yin dulinya nan a piinimin le.

ref: In fact, somewhere the Scriptures say that by the seventh day, God had finished his work, and so he rested.
text: Ni ma bu, niba yaan U pag ki jiin iweehn ilile nmɔn paam ke, “Iweehn ilile daal le Uwonbɔr nan nan diɛ U toon biɛn le ki foor.”

ref: We also read that he later said, “You people will never enter my place of rest!”
text: Le Uwonbɔr ji nan len nkarim nmɔn yaan ke, “Baa li kan lifooril N ban ni.”

ref: This means that the promise to enter is still good, because those who first heard about it disobeyed and did not enter.
text: Ni le la biɛn nin ye man le ke biba na li kɔɔ lifooril nmɔn yaan, amaa ban nan chinn ki gbir tibɔŋann nmɔn nin kaa nan kɔɔ lifooril nmɔn yaan ni, nan bu-n bi mɔyiil nbu.

ref: If Joshua had really given the people rest, there would not be any need for God to talk about another day of rest.
text: Nan bu-n ni ye Josuwa nan bi sei bi lifooril ke, Uwonbɔr kaa ji nan bi li pag lifooril daal a bɔr ni bɔɔn bu.

ref: But God has promised us a Sabbath when we will rest, even though it has not yet come.
text: Mambu lifooril daal le la si le ki sei Uwonbɔr a ninfob;

ref: On that day God's people will rest from their work, just as God rested from his work.
text: Wan kɔɔ Uwonbɔr a foorilin ke, udaan tɔɔl kan u tɔɔl a lifooril la, a li ke Uwonbɔr kaah nan foor man ni.

ref: We should do our best to enter the place of rest, so none of us will disobey and miss going there, as they did.
text: Ni ma bu, ni che ti pɔɔn tiba wee ki kɔɔ lifooril nmɔn yaan, wee ti ni uba laa nɔɔ limɔyiil a sam ki nan lu.

ref: God's word is alive and powerful! It is sharper than any double-edged sword. His word can cut through our spirits and souls and through our joints and marrow, until it discovers the desires and thoughts of our hearts.
text: Uwonbɔr a mɔbonl fo le ki tun itoon. Ki ka ki jon ijumɔɔŋ ilee, ki fin jiil uninfosaal ki piir u naaŋ nin u miɛfol, ki kɔɔ for u tugiri nin u kpabi a nsugirim, tibɔr nmɔn le ji feen ki biɛr usaal a sufu a binbem, nin u potiɛl kaah be man.

ref: Nothing is hidden from God! He sees through everything, and we will have to tell him the truth. Jesus Is the Great High Priest
text: Uwonbɔr kaah naan nan biɛn niba kaa be wee ki woo wee waa ga ni. Niba kaa degi, niwann biɛn dɔ npaan ni le Uwonbɔr a numin, wan wee ti biɛn na yin kpiir ta tun nan ki wɔɔni. Yisa le ye biminmanib a yudaau

ref: We have a great high priest, who has gone into heaven, and he is Jesus the Son of God. This is why we must hold on to what we have said about him.
text: Mambu taah jɔɔ biminmanib a yudaau wan ye Uwonbɔr a Bija Yisa wan nan don paabin, ni che ti li ŋmag ti yada kan ti ŋa nan kenken na.

ref: Jesus understands every weakness of ours, because he was tempted in every way that we are. But he did not sin!
text: Taa jɔɔ biminmanib a yudaau wan kaa li fir jogir ti, ti daburigin ni, amaa ti jɔɔ wan nan kan nbiginim niwann biɛn nin, a li ke taah be man nin, amaa waa nan jɔɔ tibiri.

ref: So whenever we are in need, we should come bravely before the throne of our merciful God. There we will be treated with undeserved grace, and we will find help.
text: Ni bu ni che ti fɔɔr mal Uwonbɔr wan ye unyunyunbasann nin a naangbɔŋin ban nin tidindann, wee ti kan linyunyunbasanl n-yonn man wee ti ban.

ref: Every high priest is appointed to help others by offering gifts and sacrifices to God because of their sins.
text: Bi gann biminmanib a yudaau biɛn bininfob a sisiigin le, ki ta siin u kpiɛtiib a taai Uwonbɔr ban, ke u jɔɔ ipiin nin bi bir a manug ki tenn Uwonbɔr.

ref: A high priest has weaknesses of his own, and he feels sorry for foolish and sinful people.
text: U li fir ŋmag ban kaa nyi-n, nin ban borin soon, nan bu-n u tɔɔl ye wan jɔɔ idaburig le.

ref: This is why he must offer sacrifices for his own sins and for the sins of others.
text: Ni ma bu le ni kpaa talar nin un mann u tɔɔl a bir a manug, nin bininfobin a bir a manug.

ref: But no one can have the honor of being a high priest simply by wanting to be one. Only God can choose a priest, and God is the one who chose Aaron.
text: Uba kaa li fir ta biminmanib a jilima nmɔn ki sei ubaantɔɔli; amaa see ke Uwonbɔr yin udaan, a li ke waah nan yin Arɔnn man nin.

ref: This is how it was with Christ. He became a high priest, but not just because he wanted the honor of being one. It was God who told him, “You are my Son, because today I have become your Father!”
text: Masiya mu kaa nan taa kupag nmɔn ubaantɔɔl a bam bu ke un ŋa biminmanib a yudaau wi. Amaa Uwonbɔr le nan bei u ke, “A ye N Bija le; dinan le N kpann a Baa.”

ref: God had the power to save Jesus from death. And while Jesus was on earth, he begged God with loud crying and tears to save him. He truly worshiped God, and God listened to his prayers.
text: Yisa kaah nan be dulinya nan yaan n-yonn man nin, u nan miɛ Uwonbɔr le ki bei U waah ban nan, ki mɔr nkukɔpɔɔn nin tinyinyinn ki ŋaan U, Uwonbɔr wan li fir fee u nkumin nin, waah nan jɔɔ jiininba ki tenn Uwonbɔr nin limɔcheelin bu le U nan gbir u miɛm.

ref: Jesus is God's own Son, but still he had to suffer before he could learn what it really means to obey God.
text: Hali nin waah le nan ye Uwonbɔr a Big nmɔn biɛn ni u nan tinn limɔcheel le u fala a jimin,

ref: Suffering made Jesus perfect, and now he can save forever all who obey him.
text: waah nan nan ŋa nan kpaan ki diɛ-n, le u nin ye feegabdaan ki sei ban biɛn chee u mɔbin,

ref: This is because God chose him to be a high priest like Melchizedek. Warning against Turning Away
text: le Uwonbɔr gann u ki ŋa u biminmanib a yudaau wan a toon be ke Melikizɛdɛg a toon kaah nan be man nin. Ikpaan ki ta jiin Yada a ta gab Paam

ref: Much more could be said about this subject. But it is hard to explain, and all of you are slow to understand.
text: Ti jɔɔ tibɔr takpem ki bi li pag ki jiin tibɔr nan paam, amaa le ni pɔɔ nin ti mann wɔɔn ni taai nan bu-n naa tinn ki biɛr weemi.

ref: By now you should have been teachers, but once again you need to be taught the simplest things about what God has said. You need milk instead of solid food.
text: Ibamɔn buu n-yonn nan, ni kpaan ni li ye ban wɔɔnn le, amaa le ni ji ban uba n wɔɔn ni Uwonbɔr a bɔr a piinimin a bamɔn. Ni ban nbiim le, naa kpaan nin tijiir tan kpiɛgi!

ref: People who live on milk are like babies who don't really know what is right.
text: Wan la mɔɔ nbiim ke, udaan la ye kiwatirig le, wan a lam kaa la gɔnn ni, nin tibuchinn a wɔɔmin paami.

ref: Solid food is for mature people who have been trained to know right from wrong.
text: Amaa ban chegir le kpaan nin tijiir tan kpiɛg, bi ma ye ban nan gbaa tinn ki biɛ nan ŋan nin nan bir a bɔgirim.

ref: We must try to become mature and start thinking about more than just the basic things we were taught about Christ. We shouldn't need to keep talking about why we ought to turn from deeds that bring death and why we ought to have faith in God.
text: Mambu ni che ti jiɛn Masiya a bɔr tan ye npiinim a wɔɔnimin, wee ki ta nninkpelam ki wɔɔn ki jo nintogil, naa ji kpaa talar nin ti ji mann bil lifiɛl a bɔr tan wɔɔn ke ni jiɛn titoonbir tan ye nkum a samin a nɔɔma, amaa wee ki ŋa Uwonbɔr yada,

ref: And we shouldn't need to keep teaching about baptisms or about the laying on of hands or about people being raised from death and the future judgment.
text: nin Uwonbɔr a nyunful a wɔɔnim, nin inɔɔ a paanim bininfob bu, nin n kum a fiim, nin litudaril lan kaa jɔɔ diɛmi.

ref: Let's grow up, if God is willing.
text: Ni ye Uwonbɔr chee ke, ti li ŋa man.

ref: But what about people who turn away after they have already seen the light and have received the gift from heaven and have shared in the Holy Spirit? What about those who turn away after they have received the good message of God and the powers of the future world? There is no way to bring them back. What they are doing is the same as nailing the Son of God to a cross and insulting him in public!
text: ni ye bi lu bi yada ni ke, baa ji li fir kan nsan man wee bi li nɔɔ ki kpenn bi binbemi. Nan bu-n bi lum nmɔn bu bi ji jiin Uwonbɔr a Bija-n le ki kpaag lidapunpunl bu ki jinn u ifa npaan ni.

ref: A field is useful to farmers, if there is enough rain to make good crops grow. In fact, God will bless such a field.
text: Nkpatam man nyu utaal a nyum man lur mi bu-n wee ki ŋaan tijiir ki tenn ban ko nan, Uwonbɔr le ŋaan tinyɔɔr ŋaan nkpatam nmɔn bu.

ref: But land that produces only thornbushes is worthless. It is likely to fall under God's curse, and in the end it will be set on fire.
text: Amaa nkpatam man wee ikunkon nin ijakpiɛgar pa-n mi dɔ le yɔli, limɔpool a daŋ li be nkpatam nmɔn bu. Le njoorimin nŋmi n nan gaa npaan nin nmɔn.

ref: My friends, we are talking this way. But we are sure that you are doing those really good things people do when they are being saved.
text: N nabum hali nin taah le pag man nan biɛn na, ni biɛn yɔli ti jɔɔ tidindann, ti nyi ke ni jɔɔ tiwann ŋann tan nyan ni feegabin.

ref: God is always fair. He will remember how you helped his people in the past and how you are still helping them. You belong to God, and he won't forget the love you have shown his people.
text: Uwonbɔr ye wan ŋan le, Waa li tam ni toon nin naah jiɛ U man ki ter U ninfob ki la biɛ nin ter bin bu.

ref: We wish each of you would always be eager to show how strong and lasting your hope really is.
text: Ti ban ni biɛn li jɔɔ inunman le hali nin ndiɛm, wee nin che naah jɔɔ tama nan bu-n nin sin ŋa ibamɔn.

ref: Then you would never be lazy. You would be following the example of those who had faith and were patient until God kept his promise to them. God's Promise Is Sure
text: Taa ban ni ŋa bigbanyagdami, amaa ni toog ban nan ŋa yada wee ki jɔɔ limɔrilin na, wee nin che ni kan lifaal lan wee Uwonbɔr nan siin limɔsiinlin. Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinbamɔnl

ref: No one is greater than God. So he made a promise in his own name when he said to Abraham,
text: Uwonbɔr kaah nan yin siin limɔsiinl ki sei Abiraham, wee uba kaa nan be ki jon U wee U li poo udaan a yinl bu-n, U nan jir poo Ubaantɔɔl a yinl bu le,

ref: “I, the Lord, will bless you with many descendants!”
text: Ki len ke, “Ibamɔn, N sin li kaab tikaar ki jaa a bu, ki seiŋ iyaabil takpem.”

ref: Then after Abraham had been very patient, he was given what God had promised.
text: Abiraham kaah nan jɔɔ limɔril ki guurin, ni bɔɔn bu le u nan kan nan wee Uwonbɔr nan siin limɔsiinlin.

ref: When anyone wants to settle an argument, they make a vow by using the name of someone or something greater than themselves.
text: Bininfob poog ban jon bi a yinl bu le, le tipoor nmɔn cheel ki ku limɔkpel biɛn.

ref: So when God wanted to prove for certain his promise to his people could not be broken, he made a vow.
text: Nan bu-n Uwonbɔr kaah nan ban Un wɔɔn ban na yin kan U mɔsiinlin a gbeemin, ibamɔn ke waa yin kpenn waah bon man nin bu, le U nan poo tipoor.

ref: God cannot tell lies! And so his promises and vows are two things that can never be changed. We have run to God for safety. Now his promises should greatly encourage us to take hold of the hope that is right in front of us.
text: Uwonbɔr ŋa tiwann tilee nan le taa jɔɔ kpenimi, ti ma ye limɔsiinl nin tipoor tan bu wee ni li pɔɔ nin Uwonbɔr n por tibɔkar. Mambu tim ban kan wunwoon bol u ban ni, ni ŋan nin ti li ŋmag ti tama kan be ti nintogilin nin lipoobil kenken.

ref: This hope is like a firm and steady anchor for our souls. In fact, hope reaches behind the curtain and into the most holy place.
text: Tama kan wee ti jɔɔ nmɔn li ŋmag ti sufu le ki baa kenken. Tama nmɔn le jon lagir likinkenl lan gɔɔn nin bu, ki kɔɔ kasi a diig n-yaan ke uninfosaalin,

ref: Melchizedek was both king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He was the one who went out and gave Abraham his blessing, when Abraham returned from killing the kings.
text: Melikizɛdɛg nmɔn nan ye Salem a bɔru le nin Uwonbɔr wan be paab a minmanu. Abiraham kaah nan jon ki tan ton ki nyaŋ bibɔrtiib wee ki chaa kun nin, le Melikizɛdɛg nan to u nsan bu le ki kaab Uwonbɔr a kaar ki jaa u bu,

ref: Then Abraham gave him a tenth of everything he had. The meaning of the name Melchizedek is “King of Justice.” But since Salem means “peace,” he is also “King of Peace.”
text: le Abiraham nan nyan waah jɔɔ nan biɛn piig a poolin libaba ki sei u. Chinchinn, Melikizɛdɛg a yinl a taai le ye “Tibuchinn a bɔru”; le ki ji ye “Salem a bɔru” le li mu a taai ye “Nposɔɔn a bɔru.”

ref: We are not told he had a father or mother or ancestors or beginning or end. He is like the Son of God and will be a priest forever.
text: Waa nan jɔɔ baa bee na, kaa jɔɔ yaajasan, kaa jɔɔ maa daali bee kum daali, u nann Uwonbɔr a Bija le, ki ye u minmanu hali nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm.

ref: Notice how great Melchizedek was! Our famous ancestor Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had taken from his enemies.
text: Ni tiɛr ki lig uja nmɔn kaah nan ye lininfo takpenl man: Hali ke ti yaaja Abiraham nan nan nyan waah to bitɔb ki fee nan biɛn a piig a poolin libaba le ki ta sei u!

ref: The Law teaches that even Abraham's descendants must give a tenth of what they possess. And they are to give this to their own relatives, who are the descendants of Levi and are priests.
text: Uwonbɔr nan siin nsiim ke ban ye Liifai a yaabili wee ki ye biminmanibin li gaan bi tɔɔl a ninfob Juu yaab kaah jɔɔ nan biɛn piig a poolin libabau, hali nin bi nabum nmɔn kaah le ye Abiraham a yaabili yin na.

ref: Although Melchizedek wasn't a descendant of Levi, Abraham gave him a tenth of what he had. Then Melchizedek blessed Abraham, who had been given God's promise.
text: Uja nmɔn kaa nan kpinn Liifai yaabi, amaa le u nan gaa niwann biɛn piig a poolin libaba Abiraham ban, ki kaab tikaar jaa uma wan nan gaa Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinlin bu.

ref: Everyone agrees a person who gives a blessing is greater than the one who receives the blessing.
text: Naa jɔɔ nbiɛnimi, wan kaab tikaar jon wan wee u kaab jaar u bu nan na.

ref: Priests are given a tenth of what people earn. But all priests die, except Melchizedek, and the Scriptures teach that he is alive.
text: Biminmanib ban gaan niwann biɛn piig a poolin libaba bininfob ban nin nan kpeg le; amaa Melikizɛdɛg ma kaa kpo, u be u miɛfolin ke Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋ kaah len man nin.

ref: Levi's descendants are now the ones who receive a tenth from people. We could even say that when Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth, Levi also gave him a tenth.
text: Uba li fir len ke Liifai, ban nan gaan piig a poolin liba-n, Abiraham le bi nan ti for le u jɔɔ tenn bi,

ref: This is because Levi was born later into the family of Abraham, who gave a tenth to Melchizedek.
text: nan bu-n Melikizɛdɛg kaah nan to Abiraham nsan bu n-yonn man nin, ki miin baa laa nan ma Liifai.

ref: Even though the Law of Moses says the priests must be descendants of Levi, those priests cannot make anyone perfect. So there needs to be a priest like Melchizedek, rather than one from the priestly family of Aaron.
text: Ni ye Liifai a bol ban ye biminmanibin a toon yin nan bi ŋan ke , ba ŋa wee ni ji nan kpaa talar ke uminmann uba n ji dan ki ye wan be ke Melikizɛdɛg, kaa ye Arɔnn a maalimin naa?

ref: And when the rules for selecting a priest are changed, the Law must also be changed.
text: Ni bu ni ye bi kpenn biminmanibin ke, see ke nsiim mu kpenn.

ref: The person we are talking about is our Lord, who came from a tribe that had never had anyone to serve as a priest at the altar.
text: Tibɔr nan kaah pag ki jiin ti yudaau wan paamin, waa ye wan nyan Liifai a bolin ni, le u bol a ninfo uba kaa la nan nyi ki tun kumanug a toon Uwonbɔr a manug a binbinl bu.

ref: Everyone knows he came from the tribe of Judah, and Moses never said priests would come from that tribe.
text: Ti nyi ke ti yudaau nmɔn nan nyan Juda a maalimin le, amaa Moziz kaa pag niba ki jiin bi bol nmɔn paam ke bi ye biminmanibi. Uminmann uba wan nann Melikizɛdɛg

ref: All of this becomes clearer, when someone who is like Melchizedek is appointed to be a priest.
text: Ni ye biminmanib a yudaau wan nann Melikizɛdɛg degirin ke, nan wee ti pag nmɔn li mann wonn binum,

ref: That person wasn't appointed because of his ancestors, but because his life can never end.
text: ki ye wan kpann uminmann kaa ye wan nɔɔ u yaajam a siim kaah wɔɔn man nin amaa ki ye limiɛfol lan kaa jɔɔ ndiɛmin a pɔɔm.

ref: In this way a weak and useless command was put aside,
text: Uwonbɔr tir nsiim kpegimin le ki tabin ngbaan mi daburigi nin mi kaa jɔɔ nyɔɔr n bu,

ref: because the Law cannot make anything perfect. At the same time, we are given a much better hope, and it can bring us close to God.
text: , mambu le Uwonbɔr wɔɔn ti tama kan ŋan, nan che ti fɔɔr mal Uwonbɔr.

ref: God himself made a promise when this priest was appointed. But he did not make a promise like this when the other priests were appointed. The promise he made is, “I, the Lord, promise that you will be a priest forever! And I will never change my mind!”
text: amaa Yisa nan ŋa biminmanib a yudaau nin tipoorin le, n-yonn man wee Uwonbɔr nan bei u ke, “Uyudaan poo tipoora le kaa yin kpenn U potiɛli ‘A ye uminmann wan a toon kaa jɔɔ diɛm le.’”

ref: This means that Jesus guarantees us a better agreement with God.
text: Tipoor nan bu, le Yisa ta uba ki siin ke tipooŋann n tun.

ref: There have been a lot of other priests, and all of them have died.
text: Biminmanib nmɔn yaba, nan bu-n nkum gen bi toon le baa fir tun chaari;

ref: But Jesus will never die, and so he will be a priest forever!
text: amaa Yisa kaah be nin n-yonn man kaa jɔɔ diɛmin, u minmanug a toon nmɔn yin gbaa be le.

ref: He is forever able to save the people he leads to God, because he always lives to speak to God for them.
text: Mambu u li fir fee ban dan Uwonbɔr ban u ma bu-n iyoo biɛn ki gab, nan bu-n iyoo biɛn u be le ki miɛ ter bi.

ref: Jesus is the high priest we need. He is holy and innocent and faultless, and not at all like us sinners. Jesus is honored above all beings in heaven,
text: Biminmanib a yudaau nmɔn le tenn ti taah ban nan, ki ye wan be kasi, kaa jɔɔ igalin ni, kaa jɔɔ tijaginn ni, le Uwonbɔr che u be u binba kaa ŋmar nin tibirdamin ni, ki don u yinl ki jon ban biɛn be paab a naamin yaan.

ref: and he is better than any other high priest. Jesus doesn't need to offer sacrifices each day for his own sins and then for the sins of the people. He offered a sacrifice once for all, when he gave himself.
text: Waa be ke ban nan ye biminmanib a yudamin ni, waa nan chinn mann kumanug lidaal biɛn u tɔɔl a bir bu, wee ki nin mann bitab a bir bu. U nan mann kumanug nba bu le ki sei bi biɛn bi bir bu waah nan ta uba ki mann kumanugin.

ref: The Law appoints priests who have weaknesses. But God's promise, which came later than the Law, appoints his Son. And he is the perfect high priest forever.
text: Ni ma bu nsiimin nan gann ndaburim le ki ŋaan bi biminmanib a yudam; amaa tipoor, tan nan ŋɔɔrin nsiimin a bɔɔn nin, nan gann Uma Uwonbɔr a Bija, wan bi ŋa u kasi hali nin isaŋ yan kaa jɔɔ diɛmin le.

ref: What I mean is we have a high priest who sits at the right side of God's great throne in heaven.
text: Nan bu wee ti len ni niɛ nan ye nan le: Ti jɔɔ biminmanib a yudaau, wan kal paab a naamin a naangbɔŋ nbu Jilimadaan a nɔɔjiim paamin,

ref: He also serves as the priest in the most holy place inside the real tent there in heaven. This tent of worship was set up by the Lord, not by humans.
text: wan tun wonjiɛn bol, ibamɔn a wonjiɛn nanboŋ kan wee Uyudaan baantɔɔl tii ki-n, wee naa ye usaal le tii-n.

ref: If he were here on earth, he would not be a priest at all, because here the Law appoints other priests to offer sacrifices.
text: Ni ye u nan bi be dulinya nan yaan ke, waa nan bi li ye biminmanib a yudaau wi, nan bu-n bininfob pii nan be ki mann nsiim nmɔn kaah wɔɔn man nin le.

ref: But the tent where they serve is just a copy and a shadow of the real one in heaven. Before Moses made the tent, he was told, “Be sure to make it exactly like the pattern you were shown on the mountain!”
text: Wonjiɛn bol kan yaan wee bi tun ibamɔn a toon yin ki nann le ke paab a naamin a jinjiimin. Ni niɛ bu le bi nan kpaan Moziz n-yonn man wee u na yin tii kuwonjiɛn nanboŋin ke: “Che niwann biɛn n ŋa ke maah nan wɔɔniŋ kuwonjiɛn nanboŋ kan lijɔɔl a paabin.”

ref: Now Christ has been appointed to serve as a priest in a much better way, and he has given us much assurance of a better agreement.
text: Amaa itoon yan wee Yisa gaa-n yab jon bi yaa toon ke, tipoopɔnn tan wee Yisa si bininfob nin Uwonbɔr a sisiigin nin kaah jon tipookpegirin man nin, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinl ŋanl nmɔn tɔɔ lifiɛŋanlin bu le.

ref: If the first agreement with God had been all right, there would not have been any need for another one.
text: Ni ma bu ni ye chinchinn a poor nmɔn kaa nan bi jɔɔ kuŋmaruŋ ke, baah ji nan bi li ban tipoor tiba jigin ni.

ref: But the Lord found fault with it and said, “I tell you the time will come, when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and the people of Judah.
text: Amaa Uwonbɔr nan kan bininfob a galin le ki len ke: “Uyudaan le len ke, n-yonn chaan, le N na li poo tipoopɔnn ki sei Iziral Yaab nin Juda yaab.

ref: It won't be like the agreement that I made with their ancestors, when I took them by the hand and led them out of Egypt. They broke their agreement with me, and I stopped caring about them!
text: Uyudaan len ke tipoor nmɔn kaa na yin nann, tan wee N nan poo sei bi yaajam n-yonn man wee N nan da bi nyan Ijibir a tingbɔŋin nni, nan bu-n baa nan ŋmag tipoor nmɔn nbamɔmi, le N nan labir ki jiɛn bi, Uyudaan le len.

ref: “But now I tell the people of Israel this is my new agreement: ‘The time will come when I, the Lord, will write my laws on their minds and hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
text: N-yonn nmɔn nan jon ke, maah li poo tipoor tan sei Iziral yaab sɔ, Uyudaan le len. N li ta n siim ki ŋa bi potiɛrin le ki sɔb nsiim nmɔn ŋa bi sufu ni. Le n na li ye bi Wonbɔru, le bi mu na li ye n ninfob.

ref: Not one of them will have to teach another to know me, their Lord.’ “All of them will know me, no matter who they are.
text: Uba kaa ji na li wɔɔn u kunkɔɔn tau bee u nabig ki ke, ‘Li nyi Uyudaan ni,’ nan bu-n bi biɛn na yin nyim le, naah nyan nbuwaabin ki tan kpaa bininkpeebin.

ref: I will treat them with kindness, even though they are wicked. I will forget their sins.”
text: Nan bu-n N na li jiɛn bi pootomin ki per bi le kaa ji li tiɛr bi bir bu jigin ni.”

ref: When the Lord talks about a new agreement, he means that the first one is out of date. And anything that is old and useless will soon disappear.
text: Uwonbɔr kaah nan yin tipoor nan ke, “Tipoopɔnn nin” le U ŋa tipoor tan chinn nin tipookpegir tan kaa ji tun ni; le niwann nan mu ŋa niwann kpegin ki por li bor kaa li yuuri.

ref: The first promise included rules for worship and a tent for worship here on earth.
text: Chinchinn a poorin nan jɔɔ liwonjiɛnl a siim le nin dulinya nan a wonjiɛn bol.

ref: The first part of the tent was called the holy place, and a lampstand, a table, and the sacred loaves of bread were kept there.
text: Bi nan tii kunanboŋ le. Ki yi ki poolin niba yaan ke kasi a bol nan yaan wee fila a titɔɔnbol nin teebul nin kasi a boroboro kan wee bi jɔɔ tenn liwonseil a mann bolin nan be.

ref: The gold altar for burning incense was in this holy place. The gold-covered sacred chest was also there, and inside it were three things. First, there was a gold jar filled with manna. Then there was Aaron's walking stick that sprouted. Finally, there were the flat stones with the Ten Commandments written on them.
text: kunanboŋ nmɔn a poolin nan jɔɔ salima a binbinl nan yaan wee bi nan nyɔɔr nnyɔgkusim ki tenn Uwonbɔr, le Uwonbɔr a poor adaka kan wee salima nan tab ki bu-n mu be niin. Adaka nmɔn a poolin nan jɔɔ salima a binbog kan gbee nin tijiir tan wee bi yi maana nan, nin Arɔnn a jaangbiɛg kan nan bunn tifarin, nin itangbag ilee yan wee bi nan sɔb nsiim ki paan i bu-n nan kpee niin.

ref: On top of the chest were the glorious creatures with wings opened out above the place of mercy. Now isn't the time to go into detail about these things.
text: Le tiwann naan wann tan jɔɔ jilima ki nann bininfob nin tikpinkpann nan tɔɔ adaka nmɔn bu, le bi kpinkpann nmɔn deg nan yaan ye tibir a jiɛnper a bolin. Amaa taa li fir pag tibɔr nmɔn biɛn daandaan nan ni.

ref: But this is how everything was when the priests went each day into the first part of the tent to do their duties.
text: Ni ye niwann biɛn a sili nan ti ŋa ke, biminmanib nan ti kɔɔ le iyoo biɛn chinchinn a nanboŋ n-yaan ki tan tun bi wonjiɛnl a toon.

ref: However, only the high priest could go into the second part of the tent, and he went in only once a year. Each time he carried blood to offer for his sins and for any sins that the people had committed without meaning to.
text: Amaa biminmanib a yudaau a binba le nan ti kɔɔ kunanboŋ kan be poolin nin taaliba libinl a poolin, u nan ti ŋmag ncham le ki kɔɔ, nan wee u li ta mann ubaantɔɔl a bir bu, nin bininfob kaah tun tibir tan wee kaa nyi.

ref: All of this is the Holy Spirit's way of saying no one could enter the most holy place while the tent was still the place of worship.
text: Kasi a Naaŋ nan wɔɔn ni niɛ le ke, nsan man chaa kasi mu a kasi a bolin kaa la loori, chinchinn a wonjiɛn nanboŋin kaah la si n bu.

ref: This also has a meaning for today. It shows we cannot make our consciences clear by offering gifts and sacrifices.
text: Ni niɛ le ye nan mag ki wɔɔn n-yonn man wee ti be daandaan nan, ni wɔɔn ke ipiin nin kumanug kan wee bi nan mann nin kaa nan fir ŋunn uwonjiɛn a potiɛli.

ref: These rules are merely about such things as eating and drinking and ceremonies for washing ourselves. And rules about physical things will last only until the time comes to change them for something better.
text: Ni nan ye tijiir, nin tiwann nyuwann, nin kuchiig daal a kaal nin dulinya nan a siim kaah wɔɔn man hali ki nan kpaa tipoopɔnn nin a yoo.

ref: Christ came as the high priest of the good things that are now here. He also went into a much better tent that wasn't made by humans and that doesn't belong to this world.
text: Masiya kaah nan dan wee ki ye biminmanib a yudaau wan ye tiwann ŋan tan pii nan be-n, u nan kɔɔ kuwonjiɛn nanboŋ kan yab ki ŋan jon kan be dulinya nan yaan, wee naa ye bininfob le tii ki-n yaan le.

ref: Then Christ went once for all into the most holy place and freed us from sin forever. He did this by offering his own blood instead of the blood of goats and bulls.
text: Waa nan ŋmag iŋɔɔb nin nnaabum a cham le ki kɔɔ nin yaan ni; amaa nba bu le u nan kɔɔ kasi mu a kasi a bolin ki ta u tɔɔl a cham ki mann kumanug kan ye nkpenim a manug kan kaa jɔɔ diɛm Uwonbɔr ban ki sei ti.

ref: According to the Law of Moses, those people who become unclean are not fit to worship God. Yet they will be considered clean, if they are sprinkled with the blood of goats and bulls and with the ashes of a sacrificed calf.
text: Bi minmanib nan ti taar iŋɔɔb nin inaaja a cham le nin kinaasiɛg kan bi nyɔɔ ki a fatam le ki jɔgin bininfob bu ban jɔɔ tijaginn bi kaal bu-n wee nin ŋa bi kasi bi gbanann nin.

ref: But Christ was sinless, and he offered himself as an eternal and spiritual sacrifice to God. This is why his blood is much more powerful and makes our consciences clear. Now we can serve the living God and no longer do things that lead to death.
text: Mambu ke, Masiya ma a chamin tun nan jon man na, uma wan kaa jɔɔ igalin wee kinaaŋ kan be u ni kaa jɔɔ diɛmin nan che u ta uba ki mann kumanug ki sei Uwonbɔr, ki ŋunn ti potiɛri a toon yan yin liin ti kɔɔn nkumin nin, wee nin che ti fir jiɛn Uwonbɔr wan foo-n!

ref: Christ died to rescue those who had sinned and broken the old agreement. Now he brings his chosen ones a new agreement with its guarantee of God's eternal blessings!
text: Ni ma bu le Masiya ye ti sandanfaaru tipoopɔnn n-yaan, ke nin che ban wee Uwonbɔr yin bin kan Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinl lan ye lifaal lan kaa jɔɔ diɛmi. Nan bu-n Masiya pii nan kpo ke un da ban nan tun tibir n-yonn man wee tipookpegirin la nan si-n le, ki nyan bi tibir nmɔn a tudarilin.

ref: In fact, making an agreement of this kind is like writing a will. This is because the one who makes the will must die before it is of any use.
text: Ni ye uninfo por u faal waah nan kpo ke u faalin ji man ke, naa tun itoon ni, see ke u nan kpo,

ref: In other words, a will doesn't go into effect as long as the one who made it is still alive.
text: Nan bu-n uba kaa li fir ji uninfo a faal wee udaan la fo; amaa see ke udaan nan kpo.

ref: Blood was also used to put the first agreement into effect.
text: Ni nan bu le che hali chinchinn a poorin kaa nan bi li fir tun itoon wee ncham kaa be.

ref: Moses told the people all the Law said they must do. Then he used red wool and a hyssop plant to sprinkle the people and the book of the Law with the blood of bulls and goats and with water.
text: Moziz kaah nan ta Uwonbɔr a siimin biɛn ki wɔɔn bininfobin biɛn n-yonn man nin, le u ta nnaabum a cham nin nnyum, nin tipeekormann nin iduufala ki lol tabin tab ki ta bɔ ncham nin nnyumin yaan ki jɔg jɔg Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋ kpabkaagin nin bininfobin biɛn bu.

ref: He told the people, “With this blood God makes his agreement with you.”
text: Le ki len ke, “Ni niɛ le ye tipoorin a cham, tan wee Uwonbɔr ke ni li ŋmagin.”

ref: The Law says that almost everything must be sprinkled with blood, and no sins can be forgiven unless blood is offered. Christ's Great Sacrifice
text: Ibamɔn buu nsiimin wɔɔn ke ncham le ye min ŋunn niwann biɛn, ni bu ncham kaa nyan ke tibir a jiɛnper kaa be. Masiya a manug le nyann tibir

ref: These things are only copies of what is in heaven, and so they had to be made holy by these ceremonies. But the real things in heaven must be made holy by something better.
text: Ni nan kpaa talar le, nin bi li mann kumanug ki ŋunn tiwann tan nann paab a wan yɔɔrin, amaa paab a wan yɔɔrin tɔɔl jɔɔ kumanug kan ŋan jon ti niɛ nan.

ref: This is why Christ did not go into a tent made by humans and was only a copy of the real one. Instead, he went into heaven and is now there with God to help us.
text: Nan bu-n Masiya kaa nan kɔɔ bininfob kaah maa wonjiɛn bol lan nan nann wonjiɛn bol bamɔnlin yaan ni; paab baantɔɔl le u nan don, le ki si ti taalin Uwonbɔr a nintogil.

ref: Christ did not have to offer himself many times. He wasn't like a high priest who goes into the most holy place each year to offer the blood of an animal.
text: Waa nan don paab nmɔn ke u ta li gbaa jɔɔ uba ki mann kumanug ke biminmanib a yudaau kaah ti kɔɔ kasi mu a kasi a bol ibin biɛn ki ŋmag ncham man kaa ye u tɔɔl a cham ki tan mann man nin ni.

ref: If he had offered himself every year, he would have suffered many times since the creation of the world. But instead, near the end of time he offered himself once and for all, so he could be a sacrifice that does away with sin.
text: Ni bi ye man ke Masiya nan bi li ji fala n-yonn takpem naah nyan dulinya a piinimin. Amaa daandaan nan u degirin ti bu nba bu le, iyoo nan a diɛmin ki ta uba ki mann kumanug ki nyan tibir.

ref: So Christ died only once to take away the sins of many people. But when he comes again, it will not be to take away sin. He will come to save everyone who is waiting for him.
text: man mu le Masiya a manugin nan mann nba bu ki nyan bininfob takpem a bir; le u ji li jirin, kaa ye u nan ji tibir a fala, amaa u li ŋmag feegab ki nan sei ban guu win.

ref: The Law of Moses is like a shadow of the good things to come. This shadow isn't the good things themselves, because it cannot free people from sin by the sacrifices offered year after year.
text: Nsiimin ye tiwann ŋann tan chaan nin a jinjiim le, amaa naa ye tiwann ŋann bamɔn nmɔn tɔɔl le ye ni. Ni ma bu kumanug kan gbaa mann ibin biɛn kaa diɛrin, kaa yin fir ŋa ban fɔɔr mal bin jiɛn Uwonbɔrin kasi.

ref: If there were worshipers who already have their sins washed away and their consciences made clear, there would not be any need to go on offering sacrifices.
text: Ni ye biminmanib nmɔn nan bi li fir ke, baa nan bi li ta kumanug ki jiɛn naa? Ni ma bu na biwonjiɛmin bi kan nŋunnim nba buu le nin diɛ, le bi sufu kaa ji bi li bii bi toonbir bu.

ref: But the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins. It only reminds people of their sins from one year to the next.
text: nan bu-n inaaja nin iŋɔɔb a cham kaa li fir nyan tibiri.

ref: When Christ came into the world, he said to God, “Sacrifices and offerings are not what you want, but you have given me my body.
text: Mambu Masiya kaah dan dulinya nan yaan nin, u nan bei Uwonbɔr ke: “Ŋaa ban kumanug nin ipiin nin, amaa tigbanann le a ŋa ti sili ki seim;

ref: No, you are not pleased with animal sacrifices and offerings for sin.”
text: A num kaa nan gbee kumanug kan wee bi nan mann ki nyɔɔr ti nŋmi ni nin tibir a manugin ni.

ref: Then Christ said, “And so, my God, I have come to do what you want, as the Scriptures say.”
text: Le n nan len ke, ‘Min sɔ, ni sɔb Uwonbɔr a gbɔŋ kpabkaagin ki jiin n paam ke, “N dan n nan tun a bam le, Uwonbɔr aa.’ ”

ref: The Law teaches that offerings and sacrifices must be made because of sin. But why did Christ mention these things and say that God did not want them?
text: Chinchinn u nan len ke, “Ŋaa ban kumanug nin ipiin nin tiwankor tan wee bi nyɔɔ nŋmi, nin tibir a manug kan wee bi ti mann tibir bu-n nni” .

ref: Well, it was to do away with offerings and sacrifices and to replace them. This is what he meant by saying to God, “I have come to do what you want.”
text: Le u len ke, “Min sɔ, N dan n nan tun ŋaah ban man le.” Le Uwonbɔr ta chinchinn a manugin ki gab, le ki siin kumanug kan kpiɛ milee nan.

ref: So we are made holy because Christ obeyed God and offered himself once for all.
text: Uwonbɔr a bam nmɔn bu le U ŋa ti kasidam Yisa Masiya kaah nan ta u gbanann ki mann kumanug nba bu ki sei ti-n bu.

ref: The priests do their work each day, and they keep on offering sacrifices that can never take away sins.
text: Biminmanib biɛn si le lidaal biɛn ki tun bi wonjiɛn toon; ki le gbaa sagir ki mann kumanug kuba nmɔn, kan kaa li fir nyan tibiri.

ref: But Christ offered himself as a sacrifice that is good forever. Now he is sitting at God's right side,
text: Amaa uminmann u niɛ man nan mann kumanugin nba bu le kpeŋileŋ tibir bu, le ki kal Uwonbɔr a nɔɔjiim paam.

ref: and he will stay there until his enemies are put under his power.
text: Ki guu iyoo yan wee Uwonbɔr na li che u dataam n kpann u taai a tɔɔn bol,

ref: By his one sacrifice he has forever set free from sin the people he brings to God.
text: nan bu-n kumanug kiba nmɔn le u che ban wee u nyan bi tibirin ki ŋaan bi kasi hali nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm.

ref: The Holy Spirit also speaks of this by telling us that the Lord said,
text: Kasi a Naaŋin mu jin kumanug nmɔn a siɛra ki sei ta. Chinchinn u len ke:

ref: “When the time comes, I will make an agreement with them. I will write my laws on their minds and hearts.
text: Uyudaan len ke, “Tipoor tan wee N yin poo sei bi sɔ n-yonn man chaan nan a bɔɔn bu, N li ta N siimin ki ŋa bi sufu ni, le ki sɔb nsiim nmɔn ki ŋa bi potiɛrin.”

ref: Then I will forget about their sins and no longer remember their evil deeds.”
text: Le u ji len kpiɛ ke: “Bi bir nin bi tukangbir a toon yin, maa ji li tiɛr i bu.”

ref: When sins are forgiven, there is no more need to offer sacrifices. Encouragement and Warning
text: Nan yaan wee tibir a jiɛn per be-n, naa kpaa talar nin tibir a manug ji li be. Ni che ti fɔɔr mal Uwonbɔr

ref: My friends, the blood of Jesus gives us courage to enter the most holy place
text: Mambu, n nabum, taah jɔɔ tidindann ke ti na li kɔɔ kasi mu a kasi a bolin Yisa a chamin bu-n,

ref: by a new way that leads to life! And this way takes us through the curtain that is Christ himself.
text: nsanpɔɔn man fo wee ti kan likinkenlin loor ki sei ti-n, n ma ye, Yisa a gbanann,

ref: We have a great high priest who is in charge of God's house.
text: nin taah jɔɔ uminmann wan yab ki ŋmag Uwonbɔr a niin nin,

ref: So let's come near God with pure hearts and a confidence that comes from having faith. Let's keep our hearts pure, our consciences free from evil, and our bodies washed with clean water.
text: ni che ti fɔɔr mal Uwonbɔr nin sufu ŋaŋ nin yada kan gbee nin ibamɔn na, waah jɔgin ki ŋunn ti sufu nyan kasi, wee ti nyan igalin ti potiɛlin ni, wee ki fun tigbanann mu nnyum ŋami.

ref: We must hold tightly to the hope we say is ours. After all, we can trust the one who made the agreement with us.
text: Ni che ti li ŋmag taah jɔɔ tama kan ki pag ki bɔrin wee ki laa yeŋi, nan bu-n wan siin limɔsiinlin nmɔn ye yada daan le.

ref: Some people have given up the habit of meeting for worship, but we must not do that. We should keep on encouraging each other, especially since you know that the day of the Lord's coming is getting closer.
text: Ni laa che ti ta tab ban a lagim ki jiɛn ni, a li ke bibam kaah ŋaan man nin ni, amaa ni che ti li mann pɔɔg tab a gbanann, a li ke naah kan Uyudaan a dan daalin kaah fɔɔr maligin man nin.

ref: No sacrifices can be made for people who decide to sin after they find out about the truth.
text: Taah biɛ ibamɔn yan wee bi wɔɔn ti nan a bɔɔn bu, ni ye ti ji be ki tun titoonbir ke, kumanug kuba kaa ji gur ki li ŋunn tibir nmɔn ni,

ref: They are God's enemies, and all they can look forward to is a terrible judgment and a furious fire.
text: amaa taah guu tibɔr a jim nin nŋmi takpen man na yin gaa Uwonbɔr a dataamin a jawaam le be.

ref: If two or more witnesses accused someone of breaking the Law of Moses, that person could be put to death.
text: Ni ye uninfo nan ti yii Moziz a siimin ke, wee bininfob bilee bee bita jin u siɛra ke, bi nan ti ku udaan le kaa san u kunyunyunbaagi.

ref: But it is much worse to dishonor God's Son and to disgrace the blood of the promise that made us holy. And it is just as bad to insult the Holy Spirit, who shows us mercy.
text: Mambu, ni tiɛr ke baa a tudaril kpaan nin uninfo wan taah Uwonbɔr a bija a taal bu nan n kan naa, wan ŋa ncham man ye Uwonbɔr a poorin tijaginn a ŋaar, wee ncham nmɔn ŋunn udaan, wee udaan ji sug Uwonbɔr a nyunyunbasanl a Naaŋin naa?

ref: We know that God has said he will punish and take revenge. We also know that the Scriptures say the Lord will judge his people.
text: Nan bu-n ti nyi wan nan len ke, “Ni ye min le nkɔn jiin; n li yɔ,” ki ji len ke, “Uyudaan li ji u ninfob tibɔr.”

ref: It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
text: Ni jɔɔ bijawaam le nin uninfo n lu Uwonbɔr wan ye limiɛfoldaan nan a nɔɔn.

ref: Don't forget all the hard times you went through when you first received the light.
text: Ni tiɛr iyoo yan nan chinn nin, wee ni nan gaa nwonween nin a bɔɔn bu, wee ni nan ye fala a jim nin linunmanlin, amaa naa nan nyaŋ ni.

ref: Sometimes you were abused and mistreated in public, and at other times you shared in the sufferings of others.
text: Iyonn iba bi nan ti sugir ni le ki mugir ni npaan ni; le iyonn iba mu ke ni ti kpiɛg ban wee bi mugir nbu le ki ji fala.

ref: You were kind to people in jail. And you gladly let your possessions be taken away, because you knew you had something better, something that would last forever.
text: Ni nan jogir biloondiikɔɔbin le, le ki chee sei ban yug ni wan yɔɔrin nin nmɔn, nan bu-n ni tɔɔl nyi naah jɔɔ nan nin kaah ŋan kaa jɔɔ diɛmi.

ref: Keep on being brave! It will bring you great rewards.
text: Mambu ni laa ta ni dindanin ki gabi; nan bu-n ni nyɔɔr na li yab.

ref: Learn to be patient, so you will please God and be given what he has promised.
text: Ni ŋan nin ni li jɔɔ limɔril wee ni nan fir tun Uwonbɔr a bam ke, ni li kan nan wee U nan siin limɔsiinl ke U li sei nin.

ref: As the Scriptures say, “God is coming soon! It won't be very long.
text: Ni ma bu n-yonn wama nan yaan, “Wan chaan nin li dan kaa li yuuri.”

ref: The people God accepts will live because of their faith. But he isn't pleased with anyone who turns back.”
text: Amaa N yaa ninfo buchin win li be u yada ni. Ni ye u jir bɔɔn ke, N num kaa li gbee wi.”

ref: We are not like those people who turn back and get destroyed. We will keep on having faith until we are saved.
text: Amaa tim kaa ye ban sul jir bɔɔn wee ki gab yɔli nni, amaa ti ye ban ŋa yada nin ban kan feegabin le.

ref: Faith makes us sure of what we hope for and gives us proof of what we cannot see.
text: Yada a ŋaam ye taah kaa jɔɔ nbiɛnim nin nan wee ti jɔɔ tama ni bu-n, wee ti num kaa ga nin.

ref: It was their faith that made our ancestors pleasing to God.
text: Ni niɛ nan bu le yaaja yonn a ninfob nan jɔɔ kupag.

ref: Because of our faith, we know that the world was made at God's command. We also know that what can be seen was made out of what cannot be seen.
text: Yada bu le ti biɛ ke Imɔleen le Uwonbɔr nan ta naan dulinya, ni bu naa ye nan wee ti ga nan le Uwonbɔr nan ta naan dulinya.

ref: Because Abel had faith, he offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. God was pleased with him and his gift, and even though Abel is now dead, his faith still speaks for him.
text: Yada bu le Ebiɛl nan mann kumanug ŋaŋ ki sei Uwonbɔr ki jon Kenn a manug. Yada bu le Uwonbɔr nan pag u ke u ye ubuchin le, Uwonbɔr kaah nan pag nan ŋan ki jiin u manugin paamin. Yada bu le u le la pag, hali nin waah le kpo nan.

ref: But without faith no one can please God. We must believe that God is real and rewards everyone who searches for him.
text: Naa ye yada ke uba kaa li fir tun wee nin gbee Uwonbɔr a numi, nan bu-n wan biɛn dan Uwonbɔr ban ke ni ŋan udaan li jɔɔ yada ke Uwonbɔr be, ki ye wan tenn ban ban u nin inunman tinyɔɔr.

ref: Because Noah had faith, he was warned about something that had not yet happened. He obeyed and built a boat that saved him and his family. In this way the people of the world were judged, and Noah was given the blessings that come to everyone who pleases God.
text: Yada bu le Nowa, Uwonbɔr kaah nan kpaan u ikpaan ki ta jiin tiwann tan paam wee u num kaa la nan kan nin, le kasi a jawaam nan che u kpee kuŋaluŋ kan fee uma nin u niin yaab gabin. U yada bu le Uwonbɔr nan bii dulinya le Nowa kpann ufaajir u buchin tan nyan u yada nin.

ref: Abraham had faith and obeyed God. He was told to go to the land that God had said would be his, and he left for a country he had never seen.
text: Yada bu, Abiraham nan chee Uwonbɔr a yim ki jon kitiŋ kan wee Uwonbɔr nan siin limɔsiinl ke U li ta kitiŋ kan ki sei win, u nan chee Uwonbɔr a mɔb le ki jon, hali nin waah kaa le nan nyi kitiŋ nmɔn yaan ni, ni biɛn yɔli u nan jon na.

ref: Because Abraham had faith, he lived as a stranger in the promised land. He lived there in a tent, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who were later given the same promise.
text: Yada bu le u nan ŋa u kukɔɔbol limɔsiinl a tiŋin n-yaan ki be ke uchaan kaah ŋaan man kitinchaŋin nin, u nan be Tinanbonn nin le uma nin Azig nin Jekɔb ban mu nan ye limɔsiinl nmɔn a faajibin.

ref: Abraham did this, because he was waiting for the eternal city God had planned and built.
text: Nan bu-n u nan lig nintogil le ki guu kitiŋ kan a fiɛl wee Uwonbɔr nan loon wee ki maa ki-n.

ref: Even when Sarah was too old to have children, she had faith that God would do what he had promised, and she had a son.
text: Yada bu le Abiraham nin u poo Sɛra wan nan ye upiiŋɔɔb ki ji porin nan kan npɔɔn ki ma ki big, nan bu-n bi nan ŋa Uwonbɔr wan nan siin limɔsiinlin le yada.

ref: Her husband Abraham was almost dead, but he became the ancestor of many people. In fact, there are as many of them as there are stars in the sky or grains of sand along the seashore.
text: Hali nin Abiraham kaah kaa ji nan fɔg nin nkumin gbaa, uma uja uba nmɔn a yaabili le nan yabig ke iŋmabil yan be titalangbann nin ni, ki ji yab ke limɔgil a gbaam a tanbiidil yan kaa jɔɔ kanlin.

ref: Every one of those people died. But they still had faith, even though they had not received what they had been promised. They were glad just to see these things from far away, and they agreed that they were only strangers and foreigners on this earth.
text: Bininfob nan biɛn la nan be nin bi yada le ki kpo. Baa nan gaa tiwann tan wee Uwonbɔr nan siin limɔsiinlin ni; amaa bi nan kan tiwann nmɔn dindanl le ki jɔɔ npopeen. Bi nan chee ke bi ye kitiŋ kiba a ninfob le ki ye bicham dulinya nan yaan.

ref: When people talk this way, it is clear they are looking for a place to call their own.
text: Bininfob ban pag man nin nmɔn wɔɔn ke bi ban kitiŋ kan ye bi tɔɔl yaag le.

ref: If they had been talking about the land where they had once lived, they could have gone back at any time.
text: Ni ye bi nan bi tiɛr kitiŋ kan yaan wee bi nan fiin nbu ke, na bi nan bi kan nsan ki jira.

ref: But they were looking forward to a better home in heaven. This is why God wasn't ashamed for them to call him their God. He even built a city for them.
text: Amaa bi nan ban kitiŋ kan ŋan le, ki be papaab. Mambu naa jɔɔ Uwonbɔr ifa nin bin yin U ke bi Wonbɔr wi, ni ma bu U mann kitiŋ le ki guu bi.

ref: Abraham had been promised that Isaac, his only son, would continue his family. But when Abraham was tested, he had faith and was willing to sacrifice Isaac,
text: hali nin Uwonbɔr kaah le nan bei u ke, “Azig bu le bi na li tiɛr a yaabili bu-n.”

ref: because he was sure that God could raise people to life. This was just like getting Isaac back from death.
text: Abiraham nan tiɛr ke Uwonbɔr li fir fiin utakpiir nkumin, pag wonn a poolin, u sin nan gaa Azig ki nyan nkumin.

ref: Isaac had faith, and he promised blessings to Jacob and Esau.
text: Yada bu le Azig nan kaab tikaar jaa Jekɔb nin Isɔɔ bu ki jiin iyoo yan la chaan nin paam.

ref: Later, when Jacob was about to die, he leaned on his walking stick and worshiped. Then because of his faith he blessed each of Joseph's sons.
text: Yada bu Jekɔb, kaah nan yin kpe-n, u nan kaab tikaar ki jaa Josef a naachim bu ubaba, le ki nyii u jaangbiɛg bu ki jiɛn Uwonbɔr.

ref: And right before Joseph died, he had faith that God would lead the people of Israel out of Egypt. So he told them to take his bones with them.
text: Yada bu Josef a kum kaah nan malin, u nan pag Iziral yaab a nyam Ijibir a tiŋin, ki ji wɔɔn bi waah kpo ke bin ŋa u kpabi man.

ref: Because Moses' parents had faith, they kept him hidden until he was three months old. They saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid to disobey the king's orders.
text: Yada bu le Moziz a baa nin u na nan ta u ki woon iŋmal itaa, baah nan maa u a bɔɔn. Bi nan kan ke Moziz ye kibiŋiŋaŋ kan kaa jɔɔ kpiɛg le, mambu baa nan san ubɔr a siimin ni.

ref: Then after Moses grew up, his faith made him refuse to be called the king's grandson.
text: Yada bu Moziz kaah nan yabig, u nan yii le kaa ban bin ke u ye ubɔr Faro a bisa a bigi.

ref: He chose to be mistreated with God's people instead of having the good time that sin could bring for a little while.
text: U nan chee nin un ji fala nin Uwonbɔr a ninfobin, ki jon nin un ji tibir a mɔm man kaa yuurin na.

ref: Moses knew that the treasures of Egypt were not as wonderful as what he would receive from suffering for the Messiah, and he looked forward to his reward.
text: U nan tiɛr ke u jin ifa Masiya bu ke ni jɔɔ tinyɔɔr jon Ijibir a jɔɔma, nan bu-n u num nan tɔɔ u nyɔɔr tan be nintogilin bu le.

ref: Because of his faith, Moses left Egypt. Moses had seen the invisible God and wasn't afraid of the king's anger.
text: Yada bu Moziz nan nyan Ijibir, kaa san bijawaam ubɔr a ŋuul bu; u nan jɔɔ limɔril le, nan bu-n u nan kan Uwonbɔr wan wee baa ga-n le.

ref: His faith also made him celebrate Passover. He sprinkled the blood of animals on the doorposts, so that the first-born sons of the people of Israel would not be killed by the destroying angel.
text: Yada bu le u nan ŋmag Yuglagir a chiigin, ki nan che bi ta ncham ki jɔg jɔg inaangan bu ke nkum a malaka wan ku nbininkpeemin nan foon ke, un laa ku Iziral yaab a bininkpeemin ni.

ref: Because of their faith, the people walked through the Red Sea on dry land. But when the Egyptians tried to do it, they were drowned.
text: Yada bu le Iziral yaab nan don limɔgmanlin ke kitinkooŋin; amaa Ijibir yaab ma kaah nan bigin ke bin do-n, nnyum nan jin ba.

ref: God's people had faith, and when they had walked around the city of Jericho for seven days, its walls fell down.
text: Yada bu Iziral yaab kaah nan choon jin Jeriko a goi a lapoob iweehn ilile-n, ni bɔɔn bu i nan lur le.

ref: Rahab had been a prostitute, but she had faith and welcomed the spies. So she wasn't killed with the people who disobeyed.
text: Yada bu baah nan ku ban ye limɔyiildamin, baa nan ku Rahab wan nan ye lipiijagɔɔrilin ki kpiɛ bi bu, nan bu-n waah gaa Iziral a ninfob ban jon bin pigir kitiŋin ki ligin ki woon u niin nin bu.

ref: What else can I say? There isn't enough time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets.
text: Ke n ji yin len ke baa? Maa jɔɔ isaŋ nin n pag ni Gidion, nin Barag, nin Samisin, nin Jafita, nin Defid, nin Samɔɔl nin bilinlemin biɛn a bɔri,

ref: Their faith helped them conquer kingdoms, and because they did right, God made promises to them. They closed the jaws of lions
text: ban a yada bu wee bi nan kɔn ki nyaŋ ntim a bɔrtiib, ki tun ibamɔn a itoon, ki kan nan nan ye Uwonbɔr a mɔsiinlin; ki ye ban nan loon igbegin a mɔɔŋi,

ref: and put out raging fires and escaped from the swords of their enemies. Although they were weak, they were given the strength and power to chase foreign armies away.
text: le ki junn nŋmipeen a tuntom, le ki guun ŋmar takoobi a kumin; ban a daburigi nan kpann npɔɔn, le ki nan to bitɔb nin npɔɔn ki nyaŋ itindoo a tɔtob.

ref: Some women received their loved ones back from death. Many of these people were tortured, but they refused to be released. They were sure they would get a better reward when the dead are raised to life.
text: Bipiib biba a takpiib le Uwonbɔr nan fiin bi nkumin, le bi ji be nin bi miɛfol. Biba nan kan limugil, amaa le baa chee bin guun nin, naah li ŋa man wee bin kan nkum a fiim man ŋan.

ref: Others were made fun of and beaten with whips, and some were chained in jail.
