text: liŋmabil nmɔn a yinl le nan ye Kpajarig. Le nnyum nmɔn a bɔgirim mitaa-n a kerim nba kpann kunyuntuntoŋ, le kunyuntuntoŋ nmɔn nan ku bininfob takpem.

ref: When the fourth angel blew his trumpet, a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck. They each lost a third of their light. So during a third of the day there was no light, and a third of the night was also without light.
text: Le malaka wan kpiɛ mina-n mu pee u naatuŋ, le bi faa nween nin uŋmal nin iŋmabil biɛn le bi wonweem a bɔgirim nkerim mitataa a kerim nbaba bɔŋ. Lidaal a bɔgirim a kerim mitaa, nkerim nba kaa nan jɔɔ nwonween ni, kunyiɛg mu a bɔgirim a kerim mitaa-n, nkerim nba mu nan ye man le.

ref: Then I looked and saw a lone eagle flying across the sky. It was shouting, “Trouble, trouble, trouble to everyone who lives on earth! The other three angels are now going to blow their trumpets.”
text: Iyaayoo le n lig, ki gbir libaanweenl kaah be paab ki laan ki mɔr nkukɔpɔɔn ki ke: “Ni li bir! Ni li bir! Ni li bir ki sei dulinya, nan bu-n malakam bita ban gur wee ki la yin pee bi naatunn nbu!”

ref: When the fifth angel blew his trumpet, I saw a star fall from the sky to earth. It was given the key to the tunnel that leads down to the deep pit.
text: Le malaka wan kpiɛ miŋmu mu pee u naatuŋ, le n kan liŋmabil kaah nyan kitilangbɔŋ bu ki nan lu tum. Le bi sei liŋmabilin libogil lan nyɔɔ kaa jɔɔ tarig nmɔn a piim.

ref: As it opened the tunnel, smoke poured out like the smoke of a great furnace. The sun and the air turned dark because of the smoke.
text: N-yonn man wee u loor libogil lan nyɔɔ kaa jɔɔ tarigin, le tikpinnyir nyan niin ki nann nŋmi takpen a kpinnyir, le tikpinnyir nmɔn nan bɔŋ nween nin titilangbann.

ref: Locusts came out of the smoke and covered the earth. They were given the same power that scorpions have.
text: Le itɔɔn nan nyan tikpinnyir nmɔn yaan ki lunn tum, le Uwonbɔr sei bi npɔɔn ke inɔɔn kaah jɔɔ npɔɔn man dulinya nan yaan nin.

ref: The locusts were told not to harm the grass on the earth or any plant or any tree. They were to punish only those people who did not have God's mark on their foreheads.
text: Uwonbɔr nan bei bi ke bi laa sei dulinya nan a mɔɔr bee tiwann bu wan bee isiigi kidaŋi, amaa bin sei bininfob ban kaa jɔɔ Uwonbɔr a daagim bi yutun bu-n a binba.

ref: The locusts were allowed to make them suffer for five months, but not to kill them. The suffering they caused was like the sting of a scorpion.
text: Uwonbɔr kaa nan sei bi npɔɔn ke bin ku bininfobi, amaa ke bin mugir bi ki tan kpaa iŋmal iŋmu. Ntiton man wu ke unɔɔn kaah jun uninfo ke ni wu man nin.

ref: In those days people will want to die, but they will not be able to. They will hope for death, but it will escape from them.
text: Iyaayoo bininfob na li ban nkum, amaa le kaa li kan ni; bi na li ban bin kpo amaa le nkum na li guun ki jiɛn bi.

ref: These locusts looked like horses ready for battle. On their heads they wore something like gold crowns, and they had human faces.
text: Itɔɔn nmɔn nan nann itaan yan wee bi ŋai bitɔb a sili-n le. Bi nan chig niba bi yuli bu le ni nann salima a naam a yuchigirig, le bi num paam nann bininfosaalib a num paam.

ref: Their hair was like a woman's long hair, and their teeth were like those of a lion.
text: Bi kor nan nann bipiib a yukper le, le bi nyin mu nann igbegin a nyin.

ref: On their chests they wore armor made of iron. Their wings roared like an army of horse-drawn chariots rushing into battle.
text: Bi nan jɔɔ ngbingban tegirim man nann tikur a gbingban tegirim le, le bi kpinkpann fu ke itaan takpem kaah dar torokom ki chaa bitɔb a tom ke ni fu man nin le.

ref: Their tails were like a scorpion's tail with a stinger that had the power to hurt someone for five months.
text: Bi jɔɔ ijoo le ki junn ke inɔɔn nin, bi jɔɔ npɔɔn bi jo-i nmɔn yaan ki li fir mugir bininfob iŋmal iŋmu.

ref: Their king was the angel in charge of the deep pit. In Hebrew his name was Abaddon, and in Greek it was Apollyon.
text: Bi nan jɔɔ wan ye ubɔr le u ye libogil nmɔn yaan a malaka, ki ye ubiir.

ref: The first horrible thing has now happened! But wait. Two more horrible things will happen soon.
text: Chinchinn a nan bir ma jon na; nan bir milee la chaan.

ref: Then the sixth angel blew his trumpet. I heard a voice speak from the four corners of the gold altar that stands in the presence of God.
text: Le malaka wan kpiɛ miloob mu pee u naatuŋ, le n gbir likukɔl liba nyan salima a binbinlin lan be Uwonbɔr a nintogilin.

ref: The voice spoke to this angel and said, “Release the four angels who are tied up beside the great Euphrates River.”
text: Le likukɔl nmɔn bei malaka wan kpiɛ miloob ki jɔɔ kunaatuŋin ke, “Lor malakam bina ban wee bi lol bi nkpen takpen man wee bi yi ke Yufiratiisi n yaan ki jaau.”

ref: The four angels had been prepared for this very hour and day and month and year. Now they were set free to kill a third of all people.
text: Le u nan lor malakam ban pii nan ŋa sili ki guu isaŋ, nin lidaal, nin li ŋmalu, nin libinl nmɔn ke bin ku bininfob a bɔgirim nkerim mitaa a kerim nba-n.

ref: In my vision their riders wore fiery-red, dark-blue, and yellow armor on their chests. The heads of the horses looked like lions, with fire and smoke and sulfur coming out of their mouths.
text: Maah nan kan itaan nin bitanjigib nmɔn nin, n zii ni, ni nan nann nan le: Bitanjigibin nan jɔɔ bigbingban tegirim man man ke nŋmi-n, ki be ke buginu, ki ye nduuyom a li ke lichibilin. Le itaan nin a yuli nann igbegin a yuli, le nŋmi nin tikpinnyir nin lichibil nyan bi mɔɔŋin ni.

ref: One third of all people were killed by the three terrible troubles caused by the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur.
text: Le imag itaa yan ye nŋmi nin tikpinnyir nin lichibil yan nyan itaan a mɔɔŋi ni nan ku bininfob a bɔgirim nkerim mitaa a kerim nba.

ref: The horses had powerful mouths, and their tails were like poisonous snakes that bite and hurt.
text: Itaan nin a pɔɔm nan be bi mɔɔŋin nin bi joi ni le, nan bu-n bi joi nan nann iwaa le, ki jɔɔ iyul, le bi jɔɔ junn bininfob.

ref: The people who lived through these terrible troubles did not turn away from the idols they had made, and they did not stop worshiping demons. They kept on worshiping idols that were made of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood. Not one of these idols could see, hear, or walk.
text: Le bininfob ban gur wee imag nan kaa ku bi nan, kaa nan chee ke bin kpenn ki ta bitɔɔl kaah maa nan nin ki gabi, baa nan ta npɔniim a jiɛnim ki jiɛn ni, nin ibawol yan wee bi ta salima ki maa i, nin salima nin tikur ninann nin tikurdiin nin itangbag nin tidaar, kaa chee bin ta bi bawoli yan kaa gaa bee kaa gbiri bee kaa choon nin gabi.

ref: No one stopped murdering or practicing witchcraft or being immoral or stealing.
text: Le kaa chee kpenn bi binben ki jiɛn lininfokuli, nin inyɔg a toon, nin iwanchɔgin toon, nin nnaayigimin.

ref: I saw another powerful angel come down from heaven. This one was covered with a cloud, and a rainbow was over his head. His face was like the sun, his legs were like columns of fire,
text: Le n ji kan malaka takpeŋ uba kaah nyan paab ki chaa jiirin. U nan yee kitilangbɔŋ le ke likinkenlin, le uwaakpajatooŋ be u yul a paab; le u num paam nann nween, le u taai mu nann nŋmipeen.

ref: and with his hand he held a little scroll that had been unrolled. He stood there with his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land.
text: U nan ŋmag kigbanbig kpabkaag le, le ki kpar ki be u nɔɔn, le u ta u nɔɔjiim a taal ki siin limɔgilin, le u nɔɔgam a taal mu si limɔgil nmɔn a dool.

ref: Then he shouted with a voice that sounded like a growling lion. Thunder roared seven times.
text: Le u tiɛn paab takpem ke ugbegin nin. Waah tiɛn man ki diɛ, le utaal a tintann a kukɔli nkerim milile-n pag.

ref: After the thunder stopped, I was about to write what it had said. But a voice from heaven shouted, “Keep it secret! Don't write these things.”
text: Utaal a tiɛm kerim milile nmɔn kaah pag ki diɛ, le n ŋa sili ke n sɔb; amaa le n ji gbir likukɔl liba nyan paab ki len ke, “Li ŋmag utaal kaah tiɛn nkerim milile man nin a sufu-n na, wee ki laa sɔb ti ki bili.”

ref: The angel I had seen standing on the sea and the land then held his right hand up toward heaven.
text: Le n kan malaka wan a taaliba tɔɔ limɔgil a nyum bu wee litɔ mu tɔɔ limɔgil a doolin kaah don u nɔɔjiim paab.

ref: He made a promise in the name of God who lives forever and who created heaven, earth, the sea, and every living creature. The angel said, “You won't have to wait any longer.
text: Le u poo Uwonbɔr wan be ki le gbaa be-n ke, wan nan naan paab nin nan biɛn be bi ni, nin dulinya nin nan biɛn be dulinya ni, nin limɔgil nin nan biɛn be limɔgilin ki len ke, “Nguurim kaa ji be!

ref: God told his secret plans to his servants the prophets, and it will all happen by the time the seventh angel sounds his trumpet.”
text: Amaa idaa yan wee malaka wan kpiɛ bilile-n na yin pee u naatuŋ ke, Uwonbɔr a wool a bɔr li gbee, a li ke waah nan bei u toontum bilinlemin man nin.”

ref: Once again the voice from heaven spoke to me. It said, “Go and take the open scroll from the hand of the angel standing on the sea and the land.”
text: Le likukɔl lan wee n bi gbir wee li nyan paabin ji beim ke, “Li chaa, ki tan gaa kugbɔŋ kpabkaag kan kpar ki be malaka a nɔɔn wee u tɔɔ nyum nin limɔgil a dool bu-n.”

ref: When I went over to ask the angel for the little scroll, the angel said, “Take the scroll and eat it! Your stomach will turn sour, but the taste in your mouth will be sweet as honey.”
text: Le n jon malaka nban ki tan bei u ke un ta kigbanbig kpabkaag nmɔn ki seim ni. Le u beim ke, “Gaa ki ki ŋman na. Ni yin mɔ a mɔnn le ke tiseerin, amaa le ki mɔŋ a poolin.”

ref: I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and ate it. The taste was sweet as honey, but my stomach turned sour.
text: Le n gaa kigbanbig kpabkaag nmɔn u nɔɔn ki ŋman. Le ki sin mɔ n mɔnn ke tiseerin, amaa maah nan ŋman diɛ le ki mɔŋ n poolin.

ref: Then some voices said, “Keep on telling what will happen to the people of many nations, races, and languages, and also to kings.”
text: Le bi nan beim ke, “Ni kpaa le nin a pag ilinlen leen ki jiin bininfob, nin ibol, nin ileen balbal, nin bibɔrtiib paam takpem.”

ref: But don't measure the courtyard outside the temple building. Leave it out. It has been given to those people who don't know God, and they will trample all over the holy city for
text: Amaa laa mag iwonjiɛn niin a loobin ni, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr ta nloob nmɔn ki sei ban kaa ye biwonjiɛmin na. Bi na li chonn ki taan kasi a tiŋ nmɔn bu ki tan kpaan iŋmal pina nin ilee.

ref: These two witnesses are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand in the presence of the Lord who rules the earth.
text: Siɛradam bilee nmɔn le ye Olif a siigi ilee-n nin fila a tutɔɔnbol a kerim milee-n, yan si kutingbɔŋ a Yudaau a nintogilin.

ref: They have the power to lock up the sky and to keep rain from falling while they are prophesying. And whenever they want to, they can turn water to blood and cause all kinds of terrible troubles on earth.
text: Siɛradam nmɔn jɔɔ npɔɔn man li fir choo utaal ke waa li nu n-yonn man wee bi be ki pag ilinlen leen nin; ki ji jɔɔ npɔɔn man li fir che nnyum nkpann ncham, ki ji li fir che imag a booli biɛn dan dulinya bu baah ban man nin.

ref: After the two witnesses have finished preaching God's message, the beast that lives in the deep pit will come up and fight against them. It will win the battle and kill them.
text: N-yonn man wee bi nan diɛ bi siɛra a toon nmɔn ke, kuwanbiigin na li nyann libogil lan nyɔɔ wee kaa jɔɔ tarigin yaan ki to bi bitɔb ki nyaŋ ki ku bi.

ref: Their bodies will be left lying in the streets of the same great city where their Lord was nailed to a cross. And this city is spiritually like the city of Sodom or the country of Egypt.
text: Bi gbanann na li dɔɔn kitintakpeŋ a sanjal bu, ntim man wee pag woon a poolin bi yi mi ke Sodom nin Ijibir, nan yaan mu jigin wee bi nan kpaa bi Yudaau lidapunpunl bu-n.

ref: For three and a half days the people of every nation, tribe, language, and race will stare at the bodies of these two witnesses and refuse to let them be buried.
text: Le bininfob na li nyan imaal biɛn, nin ileen balbal biɛn, nin ibol biɛn nin, ki nan lig bi gbanann nmɔn iweehn mun itaa nin ligenl amaa kaa yin chee bin pii tigbanann nmɔn ni.

ref: Everyone on earth will celebrate and be happy. They will give gifts to each other, because of what happened to the two prophets who caused them so much trouble.
text: Kutingbɔŋ nan a ninfob a pooi na li penn bi bilee nmɔn a kum bu, ki gel igel ki sei bi kpiɛtiib ipiin, nan bu-n bilinlem bilee nmɔn che ban be dulinya nan yaan jin fala pam.

ref: But three and a half days later, God will breathe life into their bodies. They will stand up, and everyone who sees them will be terrified.
text: Iweehn itaa nin ligenl nmɔn kaah nan jon a bɔɔn, le kufoorug kan ye limiɛfolin nyan Uwonbɔr ban ki nan kɔɔ bi, le bi fii sir paab, le bijawaam choo ban kan bin takpem.

ref: The witnesses then heard a loud voice from heaven, saying, “Come up here.” And while their enemies were watching, they were taken up to heaven in a cloud.
text: Le siɛradam bilee nmɔn gbir nkukɔpɔɔn kaah nyan paab ki bei bi ke, “Ni donn paab do.” Le bi don kitilangbɔŋin ki jon paab, le bi dataam nan si ki lig bi.

ref: At that same moment there was a terrible earthquake that destroyed a tenth of the city. Seven thousand people were killed, and the rest were frightened and praised the God who rules in heaven.
text: Iyaayoo nmɔn le kutingbɔŋ dam takpem, le kitiŋ nmɔn a niin piig a poolin nkerim nbaba lu, le bininfob turilile nan kpo kutingbɔŋ nmɔn a damim ni, le bijawaam nan choo ban gurin, le bi sei Uwonbɔr wan be paabin kupag.

ref: The second horrible thing has now happened! And the third one will be here soon. The Seventh Trumpet
text: Ni lig! Niwanbirin nan kpiɛ milee-n jon na; niwanbirin nan kpiɛ mitaa-n li foon ke naa yuuri. Kunaatuŋ kan kpiɛ milile

ref: At the sound of the seventh trumpet, loud voices were heard in heaven. They said, “Now the kingdom of this world belongs to our Lord and to his Chosen One! And he will rule forever and ever!”
text: Le malaka wan kpiɛ milile mu pee u naatuŋ, le ikukɔpɔɔr be paab ki tann ki len ke: “Dulinya a naam kpann ti Yudaau nin U Masiya yaala, le u li ŋmag u naam hali nin isaŋ yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm.”

ref: They said, “Lord God All-Powerful, you are and you were, and we thank you. You used your great power and started ruling.
text: ki len ke: “Ti tenniŋ kunɔɔpoog, Uyudaan Uwonbɔr wan jɔɔ npɔɔn biɛn, Wan pii nan be ki le la biɛ nin be, nan bu-n a gaa a pɔɔm man yaba le ki piin a naam a ŋmagim.

ref: When the nations got angry, you became angry too! Now the time has come for the dead to be judged. It is time for you to reward your servants the prophets and all your people who honor your name, no matter who they are. It is time to destroy everyone who has destroyed the earth.”
text: Le ibol a ŋuui fii; le A ŋuufiiŋ foon. Isaŋ foou nin bitakpiib a bɔr a jima nin A yɔ A toontum ban ye bilinlemin, nin A ninfogannkaab nin ban tenn A yinl jilima-n, ban gbee bininfob, nin ban kaa gbee bininfobi, ki bii ban bii dulinya.”

ref: The door to God's temple in heaven was then opened, and the sacred chest could be seen inside the temple. I saw lightning and heard roars of thunder. The earth trembled and huge hailstones fell to the ground.
text: Le Uwonbɔr a wonjiɛn niin yan be paabin loor, le n kan Uwonbɔr a kaal adaka iwonjiɛn niin a poolin. Le utaal a jugin nyagin ki dun ki tann, le kutingbɔŋ dam, le itanyunbɔl gbingbem nan lunn.

ref: She was about to give birth, and she was crying because of the great pain.
text: U nan jɔɔ lipool le ki kuun imariwiɛn kaah choo u nbu.

ref: Something else appeared in the sky. It was a huge red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, and a crown on each of its seven heads.
text: Le siɛra liba mu ji degirin paab a naamin ni: Ki ye kutunwiɛŋ kan man ki jɔɔ iyul ilile nin iyinh piig, le nnaam a yuchigirig milile chig iyul nmɔn bu.

ref: With its tail, it dragged a third of the stars from the sky and threw them down to the earth. Then the dragon turned toward the woman, because it wanted to eat her child as soon as it was born.
text: Le kutunwiɛŋ nmɔn ta u jool ki tigin iŋmabil a bɔgirim a poolin mitaa nkerim nba ki jaa kutingbɔŋin, le kutunwiɛŋ nmɔn jon tan si upii wan yin maa nmɔn a nintogil ki guu, ke upii nan maa ke un ŋman kibiliɛgin.

ref: The woman gave birth to a son, who would rule all nations with an iron rod. The boy was snatched away. He was taken to God and placed on his throne.
text: Le upii nmɔn nan maa kibijag, kibijag kan na yin ta kukurug a jaangbiɛg ki ŋmag dulinya yaab biɛn ni. Le Uwonbɔr ta u don paab u naangbɔŋin bu.

ref: The woman ran into the desert to a place that God had prepared for her. There she would be taken care of for
text: Le upii nmɔn guun ki jon kukunkɔɔg a paab, nan yaan wee Uwonbɔr nan mann npaan ki bil guur upii nmɔn ke bi li lig u ki tan kpaa iweehn turil nin iweehn kobilee nin iweehn piloob.

ref: A war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels were fighting against the dragon and its angels.
text: Bitɔb le nan be paab. Le Maakil nin u malakam nan ton kutunwiɛŋ, le kutunwiɛŋ nin u mu a malakam ton jiin.

ref: But the dragon lost the battle. It and its angels were forced out of their places in heaven
text: Amaa kutunwiɛŋ a pɔɔm kaa nan yabi, le bi nyaŋ bi, le bi lann binbebol paab.

ref: and were thrown down to the earth. Yes, that old snake and his angels were thrown out of heaven! That snake, who fools everyone on earth, is known as the devil and Satan.
text: Le bi nyan kutunwiɛŋ takpeŋ nmɔn gab, u pii ye uwaa wan nan be le yaayoo-n, wee bi yi u ke ulinlaril bee Sintani, wan liir dulinya yaab a sam ki che bi borin, le bi nyan uma nin u malakam ki gabin dulinya nan yaan.

ref: Then I heard a voice from heaven shout, “Our God has shown his saving power, and his kingdom has come! God's own Chosen One has shown his authority. Satan accused our people in the presence of God day and night. Now he has been thrown out!
text: Iyaayoo le n gbir nkukɔpɔɔn miba nyan paab ki ke: “Daandaan nan feegab nin npɔɔn nin ti Wonbɔru a naam dan na, nin U Masiya a naam a ninkper a pɔɔm foona. Nan bu-n wan nan galin ti nabumin, wan nan galin bi ti Wonbɔru a numin nween nin kunyiɛgin, bi nyan u gabin tuma.

ref: “Our people defeated Satan because of the blood of the Lamb and the message of God. They were willing to give up their lives.
text: Bi nyaŋ wa kipeebig a cham bu nin bi siɛram bu baa nan jiɛ bi miɛfolin ki tan kaagi ki sul jir bɔɔn ki nyan nkumin ni.

ref: “The heavens should rejoice, together with everyone who lives there. But pity the earth and the sea, because the devil was thrown down to the earth. He knows his time is short, and he is very angry.”
text: Mambu, ni che ni li mɔn na! Paab nin nan biɛn be niin ni! Amaa tibɔbir be dulinya nin limɔgil bu, nan bu-n ulinlaril kaah jiirin ni ban nin! U gbee nin kiŋuufiiŋ le, nan bu-n u nyi u saŋi kaah kaa yabi.”

ref: When the dragon realized it had been thrown down to the earth, it tried to make trouble for the woman who had given birth to a son.
text: Kutunwiɛŋ nmɔn kaah nan kan baah nyan u jaa dulinya nan yaan nin, le u nin nɔɔ ke un choo upii wan maa kibijagin.

ref: But the woman was given two wings like those of a huge eagle, so she could fly into the desert. There she would escape from the snake and be taken care of for a time, two times, and half a time.
text: Le Uwonbɔr nan ta libaanweenl takpenl a kpinkpann tilee ki sei upii nmɔn ke un yug ki jo kukunkɔɔg a paab nan yaan wee Uwonbɔr mann npaan ki guun win ke bi li jin u ki tan kpaan ibin itaa nin ligenl ki jiɛn uwaa-n wee u laa pii wi.

ref: The snake then spewed out water like a river to sweep the woman away.
text: Le uwaa nmɔn nan sii nnyum u mɔnn a li ke nkpenn a nyumin, ke nnyum nmɔn npuu ki tan ta upii nmɔn.

ref: But the earth helped her and swallowed the water that had come from the dragon's mouth.
text: Amaa le kutingbɔŋ nan ter upii nmɔn ki yaar u mɔb ki ta nnyum man wee kutunwiɛŋ sii u mɔn nin ki nyun.

ref: This made the dragon terribly angry with the woman. So it started a war against the rest of her children. They are the people who obey God and are faithful to what Jesus did and taught.
text: Iyaayoo le kutunwiɛŋ nmɔn a ŋuul nan fii upii nmɔn bu, le u lol bitɔb ki jon ke un tan tob upii nmɔn a buwaab ban gurin, ban chee Uwonbɔr a siim wee ki jɔɔ Yisa a siɛra-n.

ref: I looked and saw a beast coming up from the sea. This one had ten horns and seven heads, and a crown was on each of its ten horns. On each of its heads were names that were an insult to God.
text: Le kutunwiɛŋ nan sir limɔgil a dool. Le n kan kuwanbiig kaah chaa nyan limɔgilin. Ku nan jɔɔ iyinh piig le nin iyul ilile, ki chig nnaam a yuchigirim piig u yin bu, le iyin yan sugir Uwonbɔr nan sɔb paa u yuli nmɔn biɛn bu.

ref: The beast I saw had the body of a leopard, the feet of a bear, and the mouth of a lion. The dragon handed over its own power and throne and great authority to this beast.
text: Maah nan kan kuwanbiig kan nmɔn nan nann unamuun le, amaa le u taai nann ke ubakar a taai, le u mɔb nann ligbeginl a mɔb. Le kutunwiɛŋ ta u pɔɔm, nin u naangbɔŋ nin tininkper a pɔɔm ki sei kuwanbiigin.

ref: One of its heads seemed to have been fatally wounded, but now it was well. Everyone on earth marveled at this beast,
text: Kuwanbiig nmɔn a yul liba bu nan nann le ke li kan kidaŋ takpem le-n, amaa kidaŋ takpeŋ nmɔn a biɛl nan bugira. Ni nan gar dulinya yaab le bi nɔɔ kuwanbiig nmɔn.

ref: and they worshiped the dragon who had given its authority to the beast. They also worshiped the beast and said, “No one is like this beast! No one can fight against it.”

Everyone on earth whose names were not written in the book of life before the time of creation will be amazed. They will see this beast that used to be and no longer is, but will be once more.
text: Kuwanbiig kan wee a kan nin, nan be le, le kaa ji be daandaan nan ni, le ki na li nyan libogil lan nyɔɔ n-yaan ki jo nan yaan wee bi li bii u. Le kutingbɔŋ yaab ban a yin kaa sɔb be limiɛfol a gbɔŋin n-yaan dulinya a piinimin nin, bi nan kan kuwanbiig nmɔn ke ni li gar bi, nan bu-n u pii nan be, le kaa ji be daandaan nan nin, le ki ji na li dan.

ref: Anyone with wisdom can figure this out. The seven heads that the woman is sitting on stand for seven hills. These heads are also seven kings.
text: “Ni niɛ nan ban npotiɛm le nin nlamgɔrikaam. Iyul ilile-n ye igungon ilile yan wee upii-n ka-n le.

ref: Five of the kings are dead. One is ruling now, and the other one has not yet come. But when he does, he will rule for only a little while.
text: I mu ji ye bibɔrtiib bilile le. Biŋmu luu, uba be, wan gurin kaa la dan nin; amaa u nan dan ke, ni kpaa le nin un be n-yonn wama.

ref: You also saw a beast that used to be and no longer is. That beast is one of the seven kings who will return as the eighth king, but only to be destroyed.
text: Kuwanbiig kan pii nan be wee kaa jin nan be-n, le ye ubɔr wan kpiɛ biniin nin. U ye bibɔrtiib bilile-n a ni uba le, le ki chaa u biim a bol.

ref: The ten horns you saw are ten more kings, who have not yet come into power, and they will rule with the beast for only a short time.
text: “Iyinh piig yan wee a kan nin le ye bibɔrtiib piig ban kaa la gaa bi naamin, amaa kukurug kiba a poolin bi li gaa tininkper a pɔɔm ke bibɔrtiibin ki kpiɛ kuwanbiig nmɔn bu.

ref: They all think alike and will give their power and authority to the beast.
text: Lol liba le bi jɔɔ ki na li ta bi pɔɔm nin bi ninkper a pɔɔm ki sei kuwanbiigin.

ref: These kings will go to war against the Lamb. But he will defeat them, because he is Lord over all lords and King over all kings. His followers are chosen and special and faithful.
text: Bi na li to Kipeebigin bitɔb, amaa Kipeebigin na li nyaŋ bi, nan bu-n kipeebig nmɔn le ye biyudam a yudaau nin bibɔrtiib a bɔru, le ban na li be u ban ye ban wee u yin ki gann bi, wee bi ye yadadam ki nɔɔ win.”

ref: The oceans you saw the prostitute sitting on are crowds of people from all races and languages.
text: Le malaka nmɔn beim ke, “Nnyum man wee a nan kan nin, wee lipiijagɔɔrilin ka mi bu-n, ye bininfob le, kuninfogbaluŋ, ibol nin ileen balbal.

ref: The ten horns and the beast will start hating the shameless woman. They will strip off her clothes and leave her naked. Then they will eat her flesh and throw the rest of her body into a fire.
text: Kuwanbiigin nin iyinh piig yan wee a nan kan nin na li nan lipiijagɔɔrilin, ki fee u faal biɛn wee ki jaa u lijakpalomil, bi na li ŋman u gbanann ki nyɔɔ u nŋmi.

ref: God is the one who made these kings all think alike and decide to give their power to the beast. And they will do this until what God has said comes true.
text: Nan bu-n Uwonbɔr le nan ta ibon nmɔn ki ŋa bi potiɛmin ke bin tun Uma Uwonbɔr kaah lol man, ni bu le U che bi ŋa mɔbiba ki ta npɔɔn sei kuwanbiigin, hali nin Uma Uwonbɔr a bɔr kaah na li gbeen.

ref: The woman you saw is the great city that rules over all kings on earth.
text: Upii wan wee a nan kan nin, n ye kitintakpeŋ kan ŋmag dulinya nan a bɔrtiib le.”

ref: I saw another angel come from heaven. This one had great power, and the earth was bright because of his glory.
text: Ni bɔɔn bu le n ji kan malaka kaah nyan paab ki chaa jiirin. U nan jɔɔ tininkper a pɔɔm takpem. Le u wonweem man nyan u ni wonn dulinya biɛn bu.

ref: The angel shouted, “Fallen! Powerful Babylon has fallen and is now the home of demons. It is the den of every filthy spirit and of all unclean birds, and every dirty and hated animal.
text: Le u tiɛn paab nin nkukɔpɔɔn ke, “Ki lu! Babilɔnn kan ye kitintakpeŋin luu! Babilɔnn kpann npɔniim a binben bola nin nan yaan wee nnaanbiim gɔɔr nin nan yaan wee nnɔɔm man jɔɔ tijaginn kaa kpaan binib le gaa i gɔɔr.

ref: Babylon's evil and immoral wine has made all nations drunk. Every king on earth has slept with her, and every merchant on earth is rich because of her evil desires.”
text: Nan bu-n kutingbɔŋ nan a ninfob pii nyun ndapɔɔrim ke u wanchɔgin toon yin. Dulinya a bɔrtiib tun iwanchɔgin toon nin wa, le kpoŋkpoŋ dam kpann biwandam u wanŋan banl nmɔn bu.”

ref: Then I heard another voice from heaven shout, “My people, you must escape from Babylon. Don't take part in her sins and share her punishment.
text: Le n ji gbir likukɔl liba nyan paab ki len ke: “Ni nya u ban na, n ninfob, wee u bir nmɔn laa tabin ni, wee u magil liba laa kan ni;

ref: Her sins are piled as high as heaven. God has remembered the evil she has done.
text: Nan bu-n u birin paan paan le ki tan pii paab, le Uwonbɔr tiɛr u galin nmɔn bu.

ref: Treat her as she has treated others. Make her pay double for what she has done. Make her drink twice as much of what she mixed for others.
text: Ni jiin sei u waah sei ni nan nin; Ni yɔ waah ŋa nan ki sei ni a kerim mileeu. Ni ŋmarin ndapɔɔrim nkerim milee u tɔɔl a yiinyɔɔgin ki sei wa.

ref: That woman honored herself with a life of luxury. Reward her now with suffering and pain. “Deep in her heart Babylon said, ‘I am the queen! Never will I be a widow or know what it means to be sad.’
text: Ni sei mu limugil nin npoobiin takpema, a li ke kupag nin liwanŋanl banl lan wee u ti jɔɔ tenn u baantɔɔlin. U far ligbingbanl le u sufu ni ki ke, ‘N ka le ke upiibɔrin; maa ye lipukɔɔli, le maa li nyi mɔɔ tikpemɔri.’

ref: And so, in a single day she will suffer the pain of sorrow, hunger, and death. Fire will destroy her dead body, because her judge is the powerful Lord God.”
text: Mambu weemba daal u magil nmɔn na li nyaŋ u: Nkum, nin tikpemɔr nin nkom na li choo u. Nŋmi le na li gaa u, nan bu-n Uyudaan Uwonbɔr wan ye npɔɔn daan le ji u tibɔr.

ref: Every king on earth who slept with her and shared in her luxury will mourn. They will weep, when they see the smoke from that fire.
text: “N-yonn man wee kutingbɔŋ nan a bɔrtiib ban tun iwanchɔgin toon nin upii nmɔn nin ki jin u wanŋan banlin a mɔmin nan kan nŋmi man gaan win a kpinnyir kaah dug ke, bi li mɔɔ tikpemɔr upii nmɔn bu.

ref: Her sufferings will frighten them, and they will stand at a distance and say, “Pity that great and powerful city! Pity Babylon! In a single hour her judgment has come.”
text: U fala nmɔn a jim na li choo bi bijawaam, bi na li sir nan yaan fɔg ki mɔr: ‘Woo! Woo, Kitintakpeŋaa, Babilɔnn aa, kitiŋ kan jɔɔ npɔɔn! Kukurug kiba a poolin le a tudaril foon!’

ref: Every merchant on earth will mourn, because there is no one to buy their goods.
text: “Dulinya a kpoŋkpoŋ dam na li mɔɔ tikpemɔr u bu, nan bu-n uba kaa ji na li be ki daa bi tugi jigin ni,

text: itug yan ye salima, nin tikurninann, nin itangbag yan a daag pɔɔ, nin nliɛm man nyagin, nin ikinken ŋan, nin itan man geuŋ nin itan yan ŋaan bolbol nin itan man a wan yɔɔr, nin tidaar tan ŋan, nin tiwann tan wee bi ta uloob a nyin ki naan ni, nin tidaar tan a daag pɔɔ, nin tikurdiin, nin tikurpɔɔr, nin ichabpeen;

ref: No one will buy their cinnamon, spices, incense, myrrh, frankincense, wine, olive oil, fine flour, wheat, cattle, sheep, horses, chariots, slaves, and other humans.
text: itug yan ye ilanjobon nin tiwann tan tenn tikpinn nbaam, tiwann tan nyɔɔr ki jɔɔ nbaam, nin isiig a nyinyinn nin nnyɔgkusim, nin ndaam nin Olif a kpam, nin n-yom ŋam nin idi, nin inaa nin ipee; itaan nin i torokom; nin tigbanann nin bininfob a naam.

ref: Babylon, the things your heart desired have all escaped from you. Every luxury and all your glory will be lost forever. You will never get them back.
text: “Bi na li len ke, ‘Iloon yan wee a ban nin bor a ban na. A jɔɔm nin tiwann tan ŋan niŋ biɛn bora, kaa ji li fir kan ni.’

ref: The merchants had become rich because of her. But when they saw her sufferings, they were terrified. They stood at a distance, crying and mourning.
text: Le kpoŋkpoŋ dam ban kɔɔr tiwann nmɔn kitiŋ nmɔn yaan wee ki kpann biwandamin upii nmɔn bu-n, na li sir nan fɔg, le nin ŋa bi bijawaam upii nmɔn a fala a jim bu. Bi na li mɔɔ tikpemɔr,

ref: Then they shouted, “Pity the great city of Babylon! She dressed in fine linen and wore purple and scarlet cloth. She had jewelry made of gold and precious stones and pearls.
text: ki mɔɔ paab ke, ‘Woo! Woo, kitintakpeŋaa, kan nan yee ikinken ŋan nin itan man geuŋ nin itan man, le ki nan nyagin nin salima, nin itangbag yan jɔɔ kudaag, nin nliɛm!

ref: Yet in a single hour her riches disappeared.” Every ship captain and passenger and sailor stood at a distance, together with everyone who does business by traveling on the sea.
text: Kukurug kiba a poolin njɔɔm takpem biɛn bor!’ “Le ban donn tiŋalin a yudam nin ban kɔɔ tiŋalin nin biŋalindom nin ban biɛn ji limɔgil nmɔn yaan nin, na li sir nan fɔg.

ref: They cried loudly, and in their sorrow they threw dust on their heads, as they said, “Pity the great city of Babylon! Everyone who sailed the seas became rich from her treasures. But in a single hour the city was destroyed.
text: Bi na li minn titann ki gabir bi yuli bu, le ki mɔr tikpemɔr ki kunn ke: ‘Woo! Woo, kitintakpeŋaa, nan yaan wee ban biɛn nan donn tiŋalin nan kpann biwandam upii a jɔɔm bu-n! Le kukurug kiba a poolin le u jɔɔm nmɔn nan bor!

ref: A powerful angel then picked up a huge stone and threw it into the sea. The angel said, “This is how the great city of Babylon will be thrown down, never to rise again.
text: Le malaka wan pɔɔ yuur litangbagil lan polig ke linaal takpenlin, ki gab limɔgilin ki len ke: “Nin limugil nmɔn Bi na li tir Babilɔnn kitintakpeŋ nmɔn ki jaa tum, le baa ji li kan ki.

ref: The music of harps and singers and of flutes and trumpets will no longer be heard. No workers will ever set up shop in that city, and the sound of grinding grain will be silenced forever.
text: Bibiɛfaab nin bilangaab nin binaakpaapeeb nin binaatunpeeb a lai-n kaa ji na li gbir a ban ni. Kpoŋkpoŋ daan uba kaa ji na li be a ban ni. Linaal a mɔr kaa ji na li gbir a ban ni.

ref: Lamps will no longer shine anywhere in Babylon, and couples will never again say wedding vows there. Her merchants ruled the earth, and by her witchcraft she fooled all nations.
text: Le fila a wonweem kaa ji na li won a bu jigin ni. Lipiichanil daan nin u bɔɔnh a kukɔl kaa ji na li gbir a ban ni. A kpoŋkpoŋ damin nan ye dulinya a ninfob gbingbemin le. A nyɔgimin kɔɔn ibol biɛn kulɔŋa.

ref: On the streets of Babylon is found the blood of God's people and of his prophets, and everyone else.”
text: Babilɔnn nmɔn ni, le bi nan kan bilinlem nin Uwonbɔr a ninfob gannkaabin a cham nin ban biɛn wee bi nan ku kutingbɔŋ nan yaan nin.”

ref: After this, I heard what sounded like a lot of voices in heaven, and they were shouting, “Praise the Lord! To our God belongs the glorious power to save,
text: Ni bɔɔn bu le n gbir niba a mɔr, le ni nann ke kuninfogbaluŋ a kukɔlin ki nyan paab ki tann ke: “Ti don Uwonbɔr a yinl! Feegab nin kupag nin npɔɔn ye ti Wonbɔru yaan le,

ref: because his judgments are honest and fair. That filthy prostitute ruined the earth with shameful deeds. But God has judged her and made her pay the price for murdering his servants.”
text: nan bu-n U bɔjil ŋan le ki ye ibamɔn. U bii lipiijagɔɔril takpenlin na, wan ta iwanchɔgin toon ki boon kutingbɔŋin. U dar u tul ki jiin U toontumin a cham buu.”

ref: Then the crowd shouted, “Praise the Lord! Smoke will never stop rising from her burning body.”
text: Le kuninfogbaluŋin ji kunn ki len ke: “Ti don Uwonbɔr a yinl! Tikpinnyir tan nyan u nin do paab le hali nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm.”

ref: From the throne a voice said, “If you worship and fear our God, give praise to him, no matter who you are.”
text: Le likukɔl nyan kunaagbɔŋin yaan ki len ke: “Ni don ti Wonbɔru, nim ban biɛn ye u toontum, wee ki san u, ban kaa gbee bininfob nin ban gbee bininfob!”

ref: Then I heard what seemed to be a large crowd that sounded like a roaring flood and loud thunder all mixed together. They were saying, “Praise the Lord! Our Lord God All-Powerful now rules as king.
text: Iyaayoo le n ji gbir nan nann kuninfogbaluŋ a fur, le ki nann nnyum puukaam a fur bee utaal kaah tann a fur ki len ke, “Ti don Uwonbɔr a yinl! Nan bu-n ti Yudaau Uwonbɔr wan ye Npɔɔn biɛn daan nin le ŋmag ti.

ref: So we will be glad and happy and give him praise. The wedding day of the Lamb is here, and his bride is ready.
text: Ni che ni li mɔ ta wee ti pooi li peen na wee ti sei U kupag! Nan bu-n Kipeebigin a piichanil a yoo foou, le u bɔɔnh ŋa u ba siliu.

ref: She will be given a wedding dress made of pure and shining linen. This linen stands for the good things God's people have done.”
text: Le Uwonbɔr sei u bɔɔnh nmɔn itan ŋan yan nyagin ki be chasi, ke un yee.”

ref: Then the angel told me, “Put this in writing. God will bless everyone who is invited to the wedding feast of the Lamb.” The angel also said, “These things God has said are true.”
text: Le malaka-n beim ke, “Sɔb ke: ‘Tikaar be ban wee bi yin bi ke bi nan ji Kipeebigin a piichanil a jiir nan bu!’ ” Le ki ji len ke, “Ni niɛ nan le ye Uwonbɔr a mɔleen ibamɔn.”

ref: I knelt at the feet of the angel and began to worship him. But the angel said, “Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you and everyone else who tells about Jesus. Don't worship anyone but God. Everyone who tells about Jesus does it by the power of the Spirit.” The Rider on the White Horse
text: Iyaayoo le n lu u taatum ki jiɛn u. Amaa le u beim ke, “Laa ŋa man ni! N ye a toontum kpiɛg le nin a nabum ban ŋmag Yisa a siɛra-n. Li jiɛn Uwonbɔr a! Nan bu-n Yisa a siɛra ye Kinaaŋ a linlen leen le.” Utanpeen jigir nan a bɔr

ref: He had eyes like flames of fire, and he was wearing a lot of crowns. His name was written on him, but he was the only one who knew what the name meant.
text: Le u numbili nann nŋmipeen, le nnaam a yuchigirim takpem chig u yul bu. Liyinl liba nan sɔb paa u bu le uba kaa nyi li taai, see uma a binba.

text: Le u wan yee wan man nin ncham, le u yinl ye Uwonbɔr a Mɔbonl.

ref: He was followed by armies from heaven that rode on white horses and were dressed in pure white linen.
text: Le paab a tɔtogib nɔɔ u, ki jig itanpeen ki yee itan ŋan yan peen ki be chasi.

ref: From his mouth a sharp sword went out to attack the nations. He will rule them with an iron rod and will show the fierce anger of God All-Powerful by trampling the grapes in the pit where wine is made.
text: Le takoobi kan ka nyan u mɔn, le u li ta ki kɔn nyaŋ ibol. “U li ta kukurug a jaangbiɛg ki ŋmag bi.” Ki li taan bi ke baah taan isiloon a daam man nin, ni ma ye Uwonbɔr wan ye npɔɔn biɛn daan a ŋuul nin u ŋuufiiŋ.

ref: On the part of the robe that covered his thigh was written, “KING OF KINGS AND Lord OF LordS.”
text: U wann yeewann nin u panl bu, le liyinl liba nan sɔb paa ke: BIBƆRTIIB BIƐN A BƆRU NIN BIYUDAM BIƐN A YUDAAU.

ref: I then saw an angel standing on the sun, and he shouted to all the birds flying in the sky, “Come and join in God's great feast!
text: Le n kan malaka kaah si nween, ki kunn nkukɔpɔɔn ki yi nnɔɔm man yugir paab ki ke, “Dan, ni lagin taba wee ki nan ji Uwonbɔr a jɔɔg a jiir takpen nan,

text: wee ni fir ŋman bibɔrtiib, nin bitɔtob a yudam, nin bipɔɔndam, nin itaan nin bitanjigib, nin bininfob biɛn ban ye bi ba nin ban ye biyom, ban gbee bininfob nin ban kaa gbee bininfob a nann.”

ref: I also saw the beast and all kings of the earth come together. They fought against the rider on the white horse and against his army.
text: Le n kan kuwanbiigin nin kutingbɔŋ nan a bɔrtiib nin bitɔtogib kaah lagin bin to utaan jigirin nin u tɔtogib bitɔb.

ref: But the beast was captured and so was the false prophet. This is the same prophet who had worked miracles for the beast, so he could fool everyone who had the mark of the beast and worshiped the idol. The beast and the false prophet were thrown alive into a lake of burning sulfur.
text: Amaa bi nan choo kuwanbiig nmɔn na nin tibɔkar a linlenu wan nan sir u taalin wee ki tun ligaril a siɛra-n. Siɛram nan le u nan ta bii ban nan gaa kuwanbiigin a daagim a potiɛl le bi jiɛn u nunaŋin. Bi bilee nmɔn la nan fo le bi ta bi jaa lichibil a ŋmiim a mɔgilin yaan.

ref: But the rest of their army was killed by the sword that came from the mouth of the rider on the horse. Then birds stuffed themselves on the dead bodies.
text: Takoobi kan nan nyan utaan jigirin a mɔn nin, le u nan ta ku ban gurin biɛn, le nnɔɔm biɛn jin bi gbanann kpiinn ki nan gbee.

ref: I saw thrones, and sitting on those thrones were the ones who had been given the right to judge. text: Iyaayoo le n kan tinaangbann, le bi sei ban ka ti bu-n tininkper a pɔɔm ke bi li ji tibɔr. Le n kan baah nan tugir ban a yuli yin a naam, baah nan jin Yisa a siɛra nin Uwonbɔr a mɔleen n bu. ref: Then the devil who fooled them will be thrown into the lake of fire and burning sulfur. He will be there with the beast and the false prophet, and they will be in pain day and night forever and ever. The Judgment at the Great White Throne
text: Le Sintani wan lar bin, Uwonbɔr ta u ki gab lichibil lan gaan nŋmi-n ni a mɔgilin yaan, nan yaan wee bi nan ta kuwanbiigin nin tibɔkar a linlemin ki gabin. Ni yaan le bi yin ji fala nween nin kunyiɛg hali nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ diɛm. Libɔjil lan joor

ref: I saw a great white throne with someone sitting on it. Earth and heaven tried to run away, but there was no place for them to go.
text: Le n kan kunaangbɔŋ pɔŋ takpoŋ, nin wan ka ki bu-n. Le kutingbɔŋ nin kitilangbɔŋ nan guun fɔɔr u ban kaa ji jɔɔ binbeboli.

ref: I also saw all the dead people standing in front of that throne. Every one of them was there, no matter who they had once been. Several books were opened, and then the book of life was opened. The dead were judged by what those books said they had done.
text: Le n kan bitakpiib, ban gbee bitakpiib nin ban kaa gbee bitakpiib kaah si kunaangbɔŋin a nintogil, le tigbann kpaar. Le kugbɔŋ kuba mu ji kpaar, ki ma ye limiɛfol a gbɔŋ. Le bi jin bi tibɔr baah tun nan wee Uwonbɔr sɔb ŋa tigbann nmɔn yaan nin.

ref: The sea gave up the dead people who were in it, and death and its kingdom also gave up their dead. Then everyone was judged by what they had done.
text: Le limɔgil nan nyan bitakpiib ban be li ni ki jaa, le nkum nin kitakpiin tiŋ nyan bitakpiib ban be bi ni ki jaa. Le bi jin bi biɛn tibɔr baah tun nan bu.

ref: Afterwards, death and its kingdom were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
text: Le u ta nkum nin kitakpiin tiŋ ki gab nŋmi a mɔgilin yaan. Nŋmi a mɔgil nmɔn le ye nkum man kpiɛ milee.

ref: Anyone whose name wasn't written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
text: Ni ye wan a yinl kaa nan sɔb ŋa limiɛfol a gbɔŋin yaan ke, bi nan ti ta u le ki gab nŋmi a mɔgilin yaan.

ref: I saw a new heaven and a new earth. The first heaven and the first earth had disappeared, and so had the sea.
text: Le n kan paab pɔŋ nin kutingbɔŋ pɔŋ, nan bu-n chinchinn a papaab nin chinchinn a tumin nan fɔɔra, le limɔgil kaa ji be.

ref: I heard a loud voice shout from the throne: God's home is now with his people. He will live with them, and they will be his own. Yes, God will make his home among his people.
text: Le n gbir likukɔl kaah nyan nnaam a gbɔŋin yaan ki len ke, “Daandaan nan Uwonbɔr a binben bol be bininfob ban, le U li be nin bi. Bi li ŋa U ninfob, le Uwonbɔr mu tɔɔl li be nin bi ki ye bi Weem.

ref: He will wipe all tears from their eyes, and there will be no more death, suffering, crying, or pain. These things of the past are gone forever.
text: Uwonbɔr na li pir bi num a nyinyinn biɛn. Iyaayoo nkum bee tikpemɔr bee timɔr bee nan wu kaa ji na li be, nan bu-n niwann kpegin nin biɛn fɔɔra”

ref: Then the one sitting on the throne said: I am making everything new. Write down what I have said. My words are true and can be trusted.
text: Le wan nan ka kunaangbɔŋ bu-n len ke, “Lig, n ŋaan niwann biɛn niwann pɔnn le!” Le ki ji len ke, “Sɔb ki bila, nan bu-n imɔleen nmɔn ye ibamɔn le ki ye gaa ji.”

ref: Everything is finished! I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will freely give water from the life-giving fountain to everyone who is thirsty.
text: Le u beim ke: “Ni ŋau. Min le ye Wan chinn nin Wan joor, Npiinim nin Ndiɛm. Nnyunyum kaah jɔɔ ban nin, n li sei bi limiɛfol a nnyum, man ye nnyunbunkaamin yɔli.

ref: All who win the victory will be given these blessings. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
text: Wan fir ki nyaŋ ke udaan li kan lifaalin biɛn, le N li ye u Wonbɔru le u mu li ye N big.

ref: But I will tell you what will happen to cowards and to everyone who is unfaithful or dirty-minded or who murders or is sexually immoral or uses witchcraft or worships idols or tells lies. They will be thrown into that lake of fire and burning sulfur. This is the second death. The New Jerusalem
text: Amaa ban kaa jɔɔ lipoobil, nin ban kaa jɔɔ yada, nin bipootondam, nin bininfokub, nin ban tun iwanchɔgin toon lipiibanl nin lijabanl, nin ban ye binyɔgdam, nin bibawomanib, nin tibɔkardam biɛn na yin be lichibil a ŋmiim a mɔgilin yaan. Ni niɛ le ye nkum man kpiɛ milee.” Jerusalam pɔŋ a bɔr

ref: I saw one of the seven angels who had the bowls filled with the seven last terrible troubles. The angel came to me and said, “Come on! I will show you the one who will be the bride and wife of the Lamb.”
text: Le malakam bilile ban ŋmag tiyir tilile wee ti gbee nin imag ilile-n yan joorin a ni uba beim ke, “Dan wee n wɔɔniŋ ujakunn nin, wan ye kipeebig nmɔn a bɔɔnh.”

ref: Then with the help of the Spirit, he took me to the top of a very high mountain. There he showed me the holy city of Jerusalem coming down from God in heaven.
text: Le u nan taam Kinaaŋin ki don lijɔɔl takpenl lan kper a paab, ki tan wɔɔnim Jerusalam kan ye Kasi a Tiŋin, le ki nyan paab Uwonbɔr ban ki chaa jiirin tum.

ref: The glory of God made the city bright. It was dazzling and crystal clear like a precious jasper stone.
text: Ki nyagin nin Uwonbɔr a pag, ki ŋan ki nyagin ke nliɛm man a daag pɔɔ, ki be ke sataŋin, le ki ji ween ke niɛnu a maarin.

ref: The city had a high and thick wall with twelve gates, and each one of them was guarded by an angel. On each of the gates was written the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
text: Le kitiŋ nmɔn jɔɔ ligonl takpenl, lan kper ki jɔɔ itimansanmɔn piig nin ilee, le malakam piig nin bilee ka guu itimansanmɔnn piig nin ilee nmɔn. Bi nan sɔb Iziral yaab a boli piig nin ilee-n a yin le ki tabin itimansanmɔn nmɔn bu.

ref: Three of these gates were on the east, three were on the north, three more were on the south, and the other three were on the west.
text: Itimansanmɔnn itaa le nan be liwonpɔɔnl paam, le itaa be nnɔɔjiinpaam, le itaa be nnɔɔgan paam, le itaa mu be liwonlul paam.

ref: The city was built on twelve foundation stones. On each of the stones was written the name of one of the Lamb's twelve apostles.
text: Kitiŋ nmɔn a gonl nan maa tɔɔn ifiɛ piig nin ilee bu le, le Kipeebigin a tooi piig nin bilee-n a yin nan sɔb ki paa ifiɛ nmɔn bu.

ref: The angel who spoke to me had a gold measuring stick to measure the city and its gates and its walls.
text: Malaka wan nan beim man nin, nan ŋmag salima a jaangbiɛg kan wee u jɔɔ magir tiwann yɔɔr, ke un mag kitiŋ nmɔn nin ki timansanmɔnn nin igon.

ref: The city was shaped like a cube, because it was just as high as it was wide. When the angel measured the city, it was about
text: Kitiŋ nmɔn bi nan loon ki nann kitinmɔg le, le ki fufɔgim nin ki yinyalim ye nba. Le u nan ta u salima a jaangbiɛgin ki mag kitiŋ nmɔn, le ki fufɔgim ye maal turil piig nin turil bilee, ki fufɔgim nin ki yinyalim nin ki kpikperim biɛn nan ye nba.

ref: The wall was built of jasper, and the city was made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
text: Sataŋ le bi nan ta maa ligonl nmɔn, le kitiŋin baantɔɔl ye salima bamɔn, ki nyagin ke niɛnu a maar.

ref: Each of the twelve gates was a solid pearl. The streets of the city were made of pure gold, clear as crystal.
text: Le itimansanmɔn piig nin ilee nmɔn nan ye nliɛm piig nin milee le, le ntimansanmɔn nba biɛn nan ye nliɛm nba le. Kitiŋ nmɔn a sanjal nan ye salima bamɔnl le ki ga ke niɛnu-n.

ref: I did not see a temple there. The Lord God All-Powerful and the Lamb were its temple.
text: Maa nan kan iwonjiɛn niin kitiŋ nmɔn yaan ni, nan bu-n Uyudaan Uwonbɔr Npɔɔn biɛn daan nin Kipeebigin le ye ki wonjiɛn niin.

ref: And the city did not need the sun or the moon. The glory of God was shining on it, and the Lamb was its light.
text: Kitiŋ nmɔn kaa ban nween bee uŋmal a wonweem li nyagin ki bu, nan bu-n Uwonbɔr a pagin le tenn ki nwonween, le Kipeebigin ye nin yaan a fila.

ref: Nations will walk by the light of that city, and kings will bring their riches there.
text: Ibol biɛn na li choon kitiŋ nmɔn a wonweemin, le dulinya a bɔrtiib na li ta bi ŋinŋam ki kɔɔ niin.

ref: Its gates are always open during the day, and night never comes.
text: Lidaal kaa be wee ki timansanmɔn li loon ni, nan bu-n kunyiɛg kaa na yin be niin ni.

ref: The glorious treasures of nations will be brought into the city.
text: Le ibol biɛn na li ta bi pag nin jilima ki kɔɔ niin.

ref: But nothing unworthy will be allowed to enter. No one who is dirty-minded or who tells lies will be there. Only those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life will be in the city.
text: Le niwann nan biɛn jɔɔ tijaginn bee ban biɛn tun ifa bee kularug a toon kaa na li kɔɔ kitiŋ nmɔn yaan ni, amaa ban a yin sɔb be Kipeebigin a miɛfol a gbɔŋin a binba.

ref: The angel showed me a river that was crystal clear, and its waters gave life. The river came from the throne where God and the Lamb were seated.
text: Iyaayoo le malaka nan wɔɔnim nkpen man ye limiɛfol a nyum, ki ween ke niɛnu a maarin, ki puu nyan Uwonbɔr nin Kipeebigin a naangbɔŋin,

ref: Then it flowed down the middle of the city's main street. On each side of the river are trees that grow a different kind of fruit each month of the year. The fruit gives life, and the leaves are used as medicine to heal the nations.
text: ki jiir kitiŋin a sanjal a sisiigin. Le limiɛfol a siigi nan si ikpengon ilee nmɔn biɛn bu, le isiig nmɔn lon iloon itaa piig nin ilee, uŋmal biɛn ke i lo le. Le isiig nmɔn a far ye kutebug ki sei ibol biɛn.

ref: God's curse will no longer be on the people of that city. He and the Lamb will be seated there on their thrones, and its people will worship God
text: Limɔpool kaah ji na li be niin ni, Uwonbɔr nin Kipeebigin a naangbɔŋ na li be kitiŋ nmɔn yaan, le U toontum na li tun tenn u.

ref: and will see him face to face. God's name will be written on the foreheads of the people.
text: Bi na li kan u num paam, le u yinl na li paa bi yutun bu.

ref: Never again will night appear, and no one who lives there will ever need a lamp or the sun. The Lord God will be their light, and they will rule forever. The Coming of Christ
text: Kunyiɛg kaa ji na yin be nin yaan ni. Baa ji na li ban fila a wonweemi, bee nween a wonweemi, nan bu-n Uyudaan Uwonbɔr na li sei bi nwonween. Le bi na li ji nnaam ki li be hali nin iyoo yan kaa jɔɔ ndiɛm. Yisa a dam a bɔr

ref: Then I was told: These words are true and can be trusted. The Lord God controls the spirits of his prophets, and he is the one who sent his angel to show his servants what must happen very soon.
text: Le malaka nan beim ke, “Imɔleen nan ye ibamɔn le ki ye gaa jin. Uyudaan wan ye bilinlem a naam a Wonbɔru tun U malakam bin tan wɔɔn U toontumin nan kpaa nin lin tun daandaan nan.”

ref: Remember, I am coming soon! God will bless everyone who pays attention to the message of this book.
text: “Ni lig, n chaan le daandaan nan! Tikaar be ban ŋmag ilinlen leen a mɔboi yan be kugbɔŋ nan yaan nin bu.”

ref: My name is John, and I am the one who heard and saw these things. Then after I had heard and seen all this, I knelt down and began to worship at the feet of the angel who had shown it to me.
text: Min, Jɔnn, le ye wan gbir ki kan ni nan biɛn. N-yonn man wee n nan gbir wee ki kan ni-n, le n sɔɔn malaka wan gbaa wɔɔnimin a taatum ki jiɛn u.

ref: But the angel said, Don't do that! I am a servant, just like you. I am the same as a follower or a prophet or anyone else who obeys what is written in this book. God is the one you should worship.
text: Amaa le u beim ke, “Laa ŋa ni! N ye fin nin a nabum ban ye bilinlemin a toontunn kpiɛg le, nin ban biɛn nɔɔ kugbɔŋ nan kaah len man nin. Li jiɛn Uwonbɔr a!”

ref: Don't keep the prophecies in this book a secret. These things will happen soon.
text: Le u beim ke, “Laa ta tiwann tabin wann ki tabin ilinlen leen a mɔboi yan be kugbɔŋ nan yaan bu, nan bu-n iyoo mala.

ref: Evil people will keep on being evil, and everyone who is dirty-minded will still be dirty-minded. But good people will keep on doing right, and God's people will always be holy.
text: Che wan tun tibir li gbaa tun tibira; che wan tun tijaginn li gbaa tun u jaginn na; che wan tun ibuchin toon li gbaa tun ibuchin toon na; le wan be kasi u li gbaa be kasiu.”

ref: Then I was told: I am coming soon! And when I come, I will reward everyone for what they have done.
text: “Ni lig! N chaan le daandaan nan! N nyɔɔr be n ban, le n li ta sei uninfo biɛn nin waah tun nan.

ref: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
text: Min le ye Alifa nin Omega, Chinchinn nin Njoorim, Npiinim nin Ndiɛm.

ref: God will bless all who have washed their robes. They will each have the right to eat fruit from the tree that gives life, and they can enter the gates of the city.
text: “Tikaar be ban ŋunn bi wann yɔɔr bu, bi na li kan nsan limiɛfol a siigin ki nɔɔ itimansanmɔnn nin yaan ki kɔɔ kitiŋ nmɔn yaan.

ref: But outside the city will be dogs, witches, immoral people, murderers, idol worshipers, and everyone who loves to tell lies and do wrong.
text: Ban kaa na yin be kitiŋ nmɔn a poolin ye: Ibɔ, nin ban tun inyɔg a toon, nin ban tun iwanchɔgin toon lipiibanl nin lijabanl, nin bininfokub, nin bibawomanib, nin ban jiɛ ki sin tun tibɔkar a toon.

ref: I am Jesus! And I am the one who sent my angel to tell all of you these things for the churches. I am David's Great Descendant, and I am also the bright morning star.
text: “Min, Yisa, le tun n malaka ke u nan sei biwonjiɛm a laginn siɛra nan. N ye Defid a tuŋ le ki ye u yaabil, ki ye kutaayɔg a ŋmabil lan ween.”

ref: The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” Everyone who hears this should say, “Come!” If you are thirsty, come! If you want life-giving water, come and take it. It's free!
text: Le Kinaaŋ nin ki bɔɔnh nin len ke, “Dan!” Wee ki che wan gbir nlen ke, “Dan!” Nnyunyum jɔɔ wan ke, ni che un dan; le wan ban ke ni che un gaam limiɛfol a nyum sei kaam man ye yɔli. Ndiɛm

ref: Here is my warning for everyone who hears the prophecies in this book: If you add anything to them, God will make you suffer all the terrible troubles written in this book.
text: N kpaan wan biɛn gbir ilinlen leen a mɔboi yan be kugbɔŋ nan yaan ke: Ni ye uba ta niba ki kpiɛ imɔleen nmɔn bu ke, Uwonbɔr tɔɔl li kpiɛ imag yan a bɔr sɔb be kugbɔŋ nan yaan udaan bu.

ref: If you take anything away from these prophecies, God will not let you have part in the life-giving tree and in the holy city described in this book.
text: Le wan mu nyan niba ilinlen leen a mɔboi a gbɔŋ nan yaan ke, Uwonbɔr li nyan udaan a tol lan be limiɛfol a siigin nin kasi a tiŋ kan a bɔr sɔb be kugbɔŋ nan yaan nin.

ref: The one who has spoken these things says, “I am coming soon!” So, Lord Jesus, please come soon!
text: Wan jin ni niɛ nan biɛn a siɛra len ke, “Nn, n chaan le daandaan nan.” Ibamɔn. Dan, Uyudaan Yisa.

ref: I pray that the Lord Jesus will be kind to all of you.
text: Uyudaan Yisa a nyunyunbasanl li be nin Uwonbɔr a ninfob. Ibamɔn.
